Article.Title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
Article.Authors: Small C.; Kumar D.; Abbas A.; Sánchez Fructuoso A.; Yamanaga S.; Pérez González V.; Karakizlis H.; Nissen M.; Gyun Choe P.; Paloschi V.; Chadban S.; Hailemariam H.; Gerard C.; David M.; Descamps D.; Vandermeulen C.; Oluwayi K.; Hulstrøm V.; N/A N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one ( n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart ( n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years ( n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [ n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [ n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

Article.Title: Percolation and site energy distribution jointly control Li+ transport in disordered rocksalt positive electrodes
Article.Authors: Liao J.; Li Z.; Chen H.; Xie Y.; Man Z.; Tan S.; Qu Y.; Zhao S.; Lun Z.; Hou T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Disordered rocksalt positive electrodes are promising candidates for high-energy batteries, yet their ion transport kinetics is constrained by an incomplete understanding of Li transport in disordered environments. Conventional percolation theory focuses on topological connectivity but often overlooks the critical role of the energy landscape. Here, leveraging actively fine-tuned machine learning interatomic potentials combined with experimental validation, we quantitatively resolve the interplay between Li percolation connectivity and the Li-site energy distribution. We reveal a trade-off whereby increasing cation disorder enhances topological connectivity but concurrently broadens the site energy distribution, inducing a rugged energy landscape that suppresses overall diffusion. To reconcile these conflicting factors, we construct a design map spanning the full Li–Mn–Ti–O composition space, establishing a Li-site energy rectified percolation metric that transforms their interaction into a quantifiable descriptor. This framework enables the identification of Li 1.3 Mn 0.4 Ti 0.3 O 2 , which delivers a specific capacity of 294 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we demonstrate that inducing a phase transition toward a partially disordered spinel-like state simultaneously enhances percolation connectivity and narrows the energy landscape, achieving a specific capacity of 316 mAh g −1 . This work provides insights into the ion transport mechanisms in disordered electrode materials and offers practical design principles for battery systems.

Article.Title: Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
Article.Authors: Park Y.; Kim T.; Baek J.; Park S.; Kim D.; Shin C.; Sam S.; Kim W.; Dongbang S.; Kim D.; Choi Y.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Here, using alkanethiolate-based molecular junctions, we show that the carrier itself can drive conformational reorganization once the applied bias brings backbone-delocalized molecular orbitals into the transmission window. Combined electrical and in situ structural measurements resolve a threshold-activated transition to a gauche-defect state coincident with the onset of orbital-mediated transport. We rationalize this coupling through a quantum resonance scattering framework in which accessible orbitals act as scattering potentials that transiently host the injected charge, depositing energy into nuclear motion with an efficiency set by molecule–electrode coupling and Franck–Condon overlap. The framework quantitatively reproduces the measured response and predicts the enhanced behavior of amide-containing junctions. Together, these results suggest that charge-transport–structure feedback can be understood in terms of microscopic parameters governing resonance-mediated energy transfer, and that these parameters may be tuned through chemical design.

Article.Title: miProbe: microbial peptide repository of biological embeddings
Article.Authors: Yao P.; Wu D.; Zhu R.; Long Q.; Yang B.; Jiao N.; Pu X.; Zhang G.; Wang W.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: Microbial peptides represent a vast yet largely underexplored component of microbial dark matter, offering a valuable reservoir of bioactive molecules. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized peptide mining, demonstrating high-throughput screening capabilities in tasks such as functional prediction and de novo design. To fully unlock the potential of microbial resource, we present miProbe (https://www.biosino.org/iMAC/miProbe), an integrative platform hosting 1.08 × 109 microbial peptides from disparate habitats. Uniquely, miProbe bridges the gap between raw sequences and AI applications by providing 8 TB of precomputed protein language model embeddings (e.g., ESM2-650M and ProtT5-XL-U50). Our analysis reveals substantial variation in peptide diversity and functional properties across habitats and microbial taxonomic groups, and highlights the utility of large-scale embedding resources in functional peptide mining. Equipped with robust APIs for seamless model integration, miProbe establishes a diverse and scalable data resource to accelerate AI-driven exploration of microbial dark matter and the rational design of novel therapeutics. Authors present miProbe, a platform aimed to consolidate peptide data and functional characterisation, and presenting a resource to accelerate AI-driven exploration of microbial dark matter.

Article.Title: CCR8-depleting antibodies restore response to radiotherapy plus anti-PD1 therapy in head and neck cancer by targeting intratumoral CCR8+ regulatory T cells
Article.Authors: Olimpo N.; Van Court B.; Yu J.; Neupert B.; Kumar H.; Knitz M.; Gadwa J.; Hodgson C.; Nguyen A.; Beynor J.; Abdelazeem K.; Sun J.; Weiskpof T.; Puram S.; Rankin A.; Pierce N.; Osbourne D.; Karam S.
Article.Abstract: Despite advances in immunotherapy (IO) and radiation therapy (RT), anti-PD-1 (aPD-1) therapy has provided only modest benefit in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) for reasons that remain poorly understood. CCR8 is a chemokine receptor selectively enriched on tumor infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs), making it an attractive candidate for therapeutic targeting. Given our knowledge that immunosuppressive T-regulatory cells are associated with resistance to RT and IO, but have no effective targeting strategy in HNSCC, we investigate the depletion of tumor specific Treg subsets on tumor growth in female mice. In human and murine HNSCC, we characterize a subset of CCR8+ Tregs that are an immunosuppressive cell population associated with incomplete response to RT and IO. In preclinical models of HNSCC, we find that RT drives CCR8+ Treg infiltration into the primary tumor to promote tumor growth and recurrence, which can be reversed with administration of CCR8-depleting antibodies (aCCR8). Finally, we show that resistance to RT+aPD1 combination therapy is mediated by aPD1 activation of CCR8+ Tregs to facilitate tumor growth, which can be reversed with aCCR8. These findings reveal the immunosuppressive profile of CCR8+ Tregs in HNSCC and pave the way for novel combination strategies of IO in HNSCC. Previous evidence has implicated regulatory T cells (Tregs) in treatment resistance in head and neck cancer. Here the authors report that radiotherapy and anti-PD1 therapy drive the accumulation and activation of intratumoral CCR8+ Tregs, promoting tumor growth and recurrence, which can be reversed with administration of CCR8 depleting antibodies.

Article.Title: Dynamic chlorine vacancies enable X-ray-specific afterglow
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Shang Y.; Zhao Q.; Li D.; Gao P.; Hao S.; Zhou J.; Yang C.
Article.Abstract: Afterglow luminescence in inorganic materials is conventionally attributed to pre-existing static defects that trap and gradually release charge carriers. However, the observation of afterglow activated only by specific types of excitation sources, such as X-ray-specific afterglow in certain phosphors, highlights an opportunity to move beyond this static trap model. Here we show that Bi3+ doped Cs2ZrCl6 crystals exhibit afterglow exclusively under X-ray excitation, with no such effect under ultraviolet illumination. We demonstrate that this behavior arises from the in-situ generation and self-healing of metastable chlorine vacancies (VCl) specifically driven by X-ray irradiation, directly correlating with afterglow kinetics. Advancing beyond previous vague attributions to Frenkel defects, our multimodal evidence unambiguously pinpoints VCl as the operative defect species. This discovery challenges the paradigm that afterglow requires static pre-existing traps, establishing a dynamic mechanism where metastable defects are created by the probing radiation and gradually disappear when radiation is removed. We further manipulate the afterglow kinetic through Sn4+ induced modulation of vacancy formation energy, extending the afterglow duration to multiple hours while maintaining a high light yield of 55670 photons MeV−1 and a low detection limit of 30.81 nGyair s−1. Finally, we integrate these crystals into a flexible PDMS composite film for X-ray imaging, achieving a high spatial resolution of 23.6 lp mm−1 that enables high-fidelity imaging of curved objects via time-resolved readout. Our findings open an avenue for designing smart scintillators with programmable, radiation-specific responses, with implications for flexible radiography and beyond. Afterglow is thought to arise from permanent charge-trapping defects, yet radiation-specific responses defy this model. Liu et al. reveal that X-rays create transient chlorine vacancies and control their formation for prolonged, high-resolution flexible imaging.

Article.Title: Chirality inversion in DNA-assembled nanorod superlattices via site-specific asymmetric anchoring of single nanospheres
Article.Authors: Xu X.; Song J.; Deng M.; Dong B.; Hu H.; Wang Y.; Mo X.; Jiang S.; Fan Z.; Lan X.
Article.Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) chiral superlattices of plasmonic nanoparticles have attracted considerable interest due to their broad potential across various fields. However, achieving facile control over their handedness without compromising structural integrity remains a persistent challenge. Here, we report a distinct class of 2D superlattices, 4-arm pinwheel arrays with tunable configurations, through defined patch size mismatch in DNA origami-templated assembly. A superlattice framework possessing preconfigured mirror-image units is created and utilized as a platform for DNA programming of chirality. We demonstrate a single-degree-of-freedom strategy that controls the handedness of the entire superlattice through DNA-enabled site-selective and asymmetric binding of a single gold nanoparticle into the mirror-image units. These local minimal perturbations preserve long-range crystalline order while generating opposite chiroptical responses via altered plasmonic near-field coupling. Our work expands the design scope of programmable materials toward chiral functional metasurfaces, and establishes a chirality-engineering approach that circumvents global structural reconstruction. Chiral 2D plasmonic superlattices are hard to tune without global redesign. Here, the authors use DNA-origami-templated 4-arm pinwheel lattices of gold nanorods to demonstrate that site-specifically adding one gold nanosphere per unit inverts handedness while preserving long-range order.

Article.Title: Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Yu J.; Xu J.; Zhang Y.; Chen H.; Ho M.; Kam K.; Young A.; Ip P.; Pang C.; Tham C.; Yam J.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early-life nutritional conditions may influence biological aging and age-related health, but the long-term associations of early exposure to sugar rationing remain unclear. Here we investigate the associations of early-life exposure to sugar rationing with biological aging and age-related diseases among 54,201 participants in the UK Biobank, taking advantage of the abrupt end of post-war sugar rationing as a natural experiment. Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life is associated with lower biological age acceleration, with stronger associations observed among participants with longer exposure durations. The association is more pronounced in females and remains consistent across strata of genetic susceptibility. Early-life exposure to sugar rationing is also associated with lower risks of age-related cataract and chronic kidney disease, but not with several other age-related diseases examined. Overall, these findings suggest that early-life exposure to a population-level nutritional policy is associated with biological aging and several age-related diseases in later life, highlighting the potential long-term relevance of early-life nutritional environments for healthy aging.

Article.Title: Directional motility of crystallizing cholesterol on supported lipid bilayers
Article.Authors: Tae H.; Choe Y.; Jiang D.; Gnanasekaran L.; Park S.; Zhu J.; Bazan G.; Zhdanov V.; Parikh A.; Cho N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cholesterol crystallization within phospholipid bilayers necessarily remodels the surrounding membrane, creating dynamic feedback between growing crystallites and locally changing membrane. Using fluorescence microscopy, we show that lipid-coated, cholesterol-rich crystallites self-propel on the bilayer surface along directional trajectories, including circular, unidirectional, and reciprocating motion. We hypothesize that crystallite motilities arise from local cholesterol depletion in the underlying bilayer, generating gradients in composition, rigidity, and thus adhesion, which induce directional forces analogous to those involved in haptotaxis and/or durotaxis. Fluorescence lifetime imaging with a mechanosensitive probe reveals time-resolved changes in membrane packing, consistent with this mechanism. Single particle tracking and mathematical modeling support the mechanical plausibility of a working model in which crystallization-induced cholesterol redistribution may generate dynamic rigidity gradients at crystallite–membrane interface. Tuning membrane states yields a quantitative operating map that relates composition to motility, providing model-dependent design guidance for controlling cholesterol crystallite transport on lipid interfaces.

Article.Title: LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish luteal cell identity
Article.Authors: Gagnon F.; Brunelle M.; Morin F.; Sharifi E.; Garneau D.; Murphy B.; Gévry N.
Article.Abstract: Despite advances in assisted reproductive technology, success rates remain modest, largely due to implantation failure and inadequate support of early pregnancy. Corpus luteum function and consequent progesterone secretion are essential for these processes. Large luteal cells are the primary source of progesterone production, yet the transcriptional programs that define their identity remain unclear. Here, we identify the nuclear receptor Liver receptor homolog-1 as a key regulator of large luteal cell function. Loss of Liver receptor homolog-1 disrupts lipid droplet accumulation and downregulates key steroidogenic genes. Mechanistically, Liver receptor homolog-1 undergoes chromatin-binding reprogramming during luteinization, establishing regulatory regions that couple lipid metabolism to steroidogenesis. Large luteal cells integrate energy metabolism with steroid hormone production and promote nuclear acetyl-coenzyme A synthesis via Acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2, linking metabolic reprogramming to epigenetic control. These findings establish Liver receptor homolog-1 and Acyl-CoA synthetase short-chain family member 2 as key regulators coordinating lipid homeostasis, chromatin regulation and fertility. Gagnon et al. show that LRH-1 coordinates metabolic and epigenetic programs that establish large luteal cell identity, progesterone production and fertility.

Article.Title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
Article.Authors: Frumento N.; Porter C.; Euden J.; Varley M.; Raisanen L.; Adams R.; Bodman C.; Carroll M.; Choy E.; Cicconi P.; Dagley V.; Govender M.; Griffin S.; Harris D.; Hill A.; Hood K.; Jeffery K.; Knapper S.; Laidlaw S.; Meacham G.; Nixon L.; Ottensmeier C.; Pringle S.; Rolt J.; Shier S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

Article.Title: A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria
Article.Authors: Agrawal S.; Chandramouli A.; Mohela K.; Ganie H.; Puthalath I.; Mony B.; Jenal U.; Kamat S.; Hallez R.; Radhakrishnan S.
Article.Abstract: Mechanisms interlinking metabolic cues with cell cycle programs remain unknown. We show that an oscillating cytosolic redox critically governs cell cycle transitions in Caulobacter crescentus. By integrating evolutionary genetics with metabolic flux tracing, we uncover temporally orchestrated shifts in core metabolic pathways that remodel cytosolic redox across the cell cycle. Early stages channel carbon flux toward unsaturated fatty-acid synthesis and a reverse-TCA to drive cytosolic oxidation-coupled G1-to-S transition. The later stages depend on an enhanced forward-TCA cycle that promote cytosolic reduction-driven proliferation. Strikingly, perturbing fatty-acid synthesis or reverse/forward-TCA cycle uncouples growth from proliferation. Intriguingly, a biphasic glucose uptake program dictates the cell cycle-stage-specific metabolism. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized metabolic-redox circuitry that coordinates cell cycle progression in bacteria. They further unveil several metabolic branchpoints as promising targets for chemical intervention to disrupt critical and conserved cell cycle events, with potential applicability to bacterial pathogens. How cells coordinate growth and division with their metabolic state is poorly understood. Here, Agrawal et al. describe changes in glucose uptake and central metabolism that alter cytosolic redox balance and drive cell cycle progression in the bacterial model Caulobacter crescentus.

Article.Title: Humanized yeast ORC drives R-loop dependent transcription-replication conflicts and global gene dysregulation
Article.Authors: Lee C.; Lalonde M.; Straub T.; Zheng M.; Márquez-Gómez E.; Riepl M.; Dong B.; Tsirkas I.; Sajid A.; Werner M.; Janeva A.; Karypidou X.; Scialdone A.; Schmoller K.; Palancade B.; Tye B.; Hamperl S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) recruits Mini-Chromosome Maintenance (MCM) hexamers to initiate eukaryotic DNA replication. While yeast ORC binds specific DNA motifs, human ORC binds sequence-agnostically nucleosome-depleted promoter regions. Here, using a mutant yeast model that recapitulates the human ORC binding landscape, we demonstrate that pervasive and unscheduled ORC binding at promoters in the compact yeast genome generates R-loop associated transcription-replication conflicts and disrupts gene expression across thousands of genes. Unexpectedly, we also uncover that substituting endogenous gene promoters with a replication origin sequence maintains robust transcription. We reveal that this intrinsic, promoter-like function relies on the ability of origins to form a nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) encoded within the origin’s sequence composition. However, origin-substituted loci reposition the +1 nucleosome which drives the transcription machinery to select alternative transcription start sites (TSSs). Thus, origins and promoters share an intrinsic chromatin structure-controlled ability to drive transcription initiation. Together, our results show that origin licensing in compact genomes relies on sequence-specific, coupled origin licensing to insulate transcription from the replication machinery.

Article.Title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
Article.Authors: Liu A.; Kaeser B.; Pereira J.; Taylor-Kearney L.; Hammel M.; Nogales E.; Adams P.; Shih P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proteins often assemble as higher order complexes, underlying a diversity of molecular structures and biological functions. The emergence of protein-protein interactions between binding partners is generally considered to be the primary driver of oligomerization. However, ligand binding has also been demonstrated to affect higher-order assembly, though this phenomenon is not widely considered as a primary driver of oligomerization. Here, we describe the mechanism by which different rubisco oligomeric states are induced via ligand binding. By expanding the phylogenetic sampling of a unique clade of rubisco, we discover a range of oligomeric responses to ligand binding across the phylogeny and identify the structural features responsible for shifts in the oligomeric state that ultimately provide a path to evolving new quaternary structures. Here, we identify a ligand-dependent mechanism giving rise to new protein assemblies, in contrast with the typical process of evolving new protein-protein interfaces directly. Our findings describe a means by which binding and entrenchment of a ligand enables an increase in structural complexity.

Article.Title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
Article.Authors: Kim C.; Kim S.; Song J.; Lee J.; Kim L.; Im S.; Ju H.; Jung Y.; Kim G.; Cho J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: neuromorphic hardware; autapses; leaky integrate-and-fire neurons

Article.Title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Yang J.; Wang L.; Zhang J.; Xu S.; Wang S.; Xu X.; Lv L.; Tao P.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial pangenomes provide a shared reservoir of antiphage defenses, yet the ecological and functional constraints shaping this reservoir remain unclear. Here, we combine comparative genomics of 206 Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) genomes with cross-infection assays of 50 strains against 36 phages and heterologous expression of 24 defense systems in a phage-sensitive Xoo chassis. The Xoo pan-defensome comprises a conserved core of 9 subtypes and a variable layer of 35 accessory and cloud subtypes structured by host phylogeography. Phages are more infectious on sympatric than allopatric hosts, consistent with local adaptation. Variable systems show stronger apparent activity than core systems, whereas resistance breadth is not predicted by defense system number. Co-expression of representative co-occurring and mutually exclusive system pairs reveals synergistic and antagonistic interactions underlying non-random repertoire assembly. Together, these findings extend the pan-immunity framework by showing that population-level immune reservoirs are shaped by both ecological structure and functional compatibility. In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

Article.Title: SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
Article.Authors: Caro T.; Ibarra Arriaga J.; Solini G.; Shivji Z.; Grossman E.; Jhatro A.; Stewart B.; Fu X.; Sessions A.; Karthikeyan S.
Article.Abstract: Soil microbial activity, and the balance of anabolic (carbon assimilating) and catabolic (CO2-releasing) processes, control the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. Soil hydration controls this activity, and with hydroclimate volatility increasing across many regions, microbial responses to drought-rewetting cycles urgently require quantification. We conducted rainfall exclusion experiments at two Mediterranean-type field sites, coupling isotope labeling with multi-omics, to link microbial growth, greenhouse gas fluxes, and the carbon sources driving both. Rehydration shortened apparent cell generation times from years to days within minutes. High-intensity drought lengthened the lag before growth resumed, yet metagenomic inference indicated post-drought enrichment of rapid-growth phenotypes. Drought and rehydration shifted the soil metabolome, implicating specific osmolytes in the microbial response and suggesting metabolite diversity modulates microbial function. These results constrain soil microbial activity rates and mechanisms underlying drought-rewetting responses and motivate further study of carbon cycling under increasingly volatile hydroclimates. This study demonstrates that soil microbial growth rates are extremely slow under dry conditions, with rehydration causing a rapid increase in anabolic activity within days. These findings refine our understanding of microbial contributions to soil carbon cycling with a warming climate.

Article.Title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
Article.Authors: Tang W.; Wei Z.; He T.; Huang H.; He X.; Wu S.; Liu J.; Yu C.; Fu H.; Hu W.; Wang S.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform in next-generation integrated optoelectronics and on-chip/chip-chip interconnection due to its attractive optical property and versatility. However, integration of conventional-material-based photodetectors on TFLN platforms still faces multiple challenges. Herein, a high-bandwidth TFLN-based waveguide-integrated lateral WSe 2 p-i-n photodetector is presented. The localized self-aligned doping process eliminates slow carrier diffusion and defect trapping in doped regions which further boosts modulation bandwidth. Secondly, n-type and p-type Ohmic contacts, along with a high-quality p-n junction, are achieved through Se vacancy defect engineering and high-work function molybdenum oxide buffer layer, respectively. Furthermore, combined with the high dielectric constant of lithium niobate suppressing ionized impurity scattering, carrier mobilities exceeding 350 cm 2 /V·s are achieved for both electrons and holes, significantly accelerating carrier drift. The device features a measured bandwidth of 1.12 GHz and a data rate up to 10 Gbit/s in visible light. Separately, the device achieves a responsivity of ~492 mA·W −1 and a near-unity external quantum efficiency of 95.6% at 638 nm. This combination of two-dimensional homostructure and TFLN nano-waveguides provides a basis for high-speed photodetectors and visible-light interconnections in future TFLN integrated optoelectronics and optical input/output applications.

Article.Title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
Article.Authors: Wan N.; Zhao H.; Hatfield J.; Pielke R.; Kirkham M.; Welch S.; Zhang L.; Liu Z.; Yang H.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maize yield responses to climate change differ seasonally and regionally, with both positive and negative impacts shaped by local climate trends and management decisions. Here, using a phenology-aligned moving crop-season framework and the Hybrid-Maize model (1991–2024) across five U.S. Corn Belt states, we quantify climate-driven yield contributions and show that they transition from southern declines to northern gains, reflecting the persistent influence of the central U.S. summer warming hole characterized by cooling maximum temperatures and increasing rainfall. A systematic thermal mismatch between environmental heat availability and hybrid growing degree day requirements is observed, particularly south of 42°N, where thermal matching declined despite favorable thermal conditions. Contrasting trends in thermal matching and reproductive duration help explain the latitude-dependent structure of climate-driven yield contributions. Our findings highlight how hybrid selection modulates the impacts of temperature, precipitation, vapor pressure deficit, and radiation trends on maize yield gains across the U.S. Corn Belt.

Article.Title: Epigenetic gatekeeping enables genome-scale horizontal gene transfer in eukaryotic cells
Article.Authors: Aoki R.; Nishihara H.; Sakamoto T.; Sato Y.; Kuramoto T.; Fukuda M.; Matsunaga T.; Uehara A.; Slane D.; Kawanishi Y.; Mori S.; Nagaoka D.; Hirakawa M.; Gao H.; Maejima D.; Minoura Y.; Suto Y.; Ishii K.; Anthony C.; Ishiyama S.; Kato S.; Inui Y.; Wada N.; Mogi Y.; Yoshida Y.
Article.Abstract: Horizontal gene transfer drives rapid evolutionary innovation, yet well-substantiated cases are largely confined to prokaryotes. Eukaryote-to-eukaryote transfer remains exceptionally rare, and direct genome-scale demonstrations are absent. Here, inspired by endosymbiotic genome acquisition, we show that mammalian cells can initiate genome-scale horizontal gene transfer through phagocytic uptake of intact algal cells, albeit at a much lower frequency than cell fusion. Live-cell imaging captures the early nuclear appearance of transferred algal DNA after fusion, while genome sequencing and cytogenetic analyses reveal stable retention of chromosome-scale algal DNA in mammalian cells. Hybrid cells maintain more than 16 Mb of algal DNA, including intact chromosomes, as telomere-linked structures that persist for 95 generations without selection. Transferred algal DNA shows a progressive increase in DNA methylation together with enrichment of repressive histone modifications, forming heterochromatic domains that physically associate with host chromosomes. Notably, mammalian cells deficient in a de novo DNA methyltransferase show reduced stable establishment and retention of transferred algal DNA, supporting a gatekeeping role for DNA methylation in the stable accommodation of foreign genomes. Our findings reveal an epigenetic mechanism that contributes to the stable accommodation of large-scale foreign DNA between distantly related eukaryotes.

Article.Title: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
Article.Authors: Peres P.; Sellers K.; Sutton T.; Bracken-Grissom H.
Article.Abstract: As the global biodiversity crisis accelerates across terrestrial and shallow marine systems, the extent of this collapse remains unknown within the deep sea. Despite encompassing most of the ocean, deep-sea ecosystems remain the planet's final frontier. Within this vast realm, the mesopelagic zone represents a critical yet poorly understood habitat, particularly in terms of its conservation status. Here, we integrate genomic data with ecological niche modeling to assess and forecast the conservation status of five mesopelagic species in the Gulf of Mexico. Samples were collected from 2011 to 2023, representing one of the longest time-series datasets for mesopelagic fauna in oceanographic history. All species exhibit current effective population sizes below the minimum thresholds for long-term viability. Genomic diversity declined over a decade in some species at rates comparable to or exceeding those reported for threatened and endangered species. Demographic modeling indicates historical population declines across all species. Ecological niche models predict declining Gulf habitat suitability for most species under future climate change scenarios. Together, our results identify indicators associated with elevated extinction risk in Gulf mesopelagic species and raise the possibility of a broader, unnoticed crisis, challenging assumptions of stability and resilience in mesopelagic ecosystems.

Article.Title: Cobalt based anode for highly stable alkaline water electrolysis under operation conditions beyond industrial requirements
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Qiu T.; Zhang S.; Han C.; Xu W.; Feng S.; Chen H.; Wen Y.; Tian X.; Dai S.; Lu Z.
Article.Abstract: Alkaline water electrolysis is the most established route to electrochemical hydrogen production, but the limited lifetime of anode catalysts makes long-term equipment investment costly and hinders miniaturization. Here we show that, unlike the extensively investigated nickel- and nickel–iron-based hydroxides, the long-neglected cobalt–nickel hydroxides are promising anode catalysts whose stability exceeds current industrial requirements. A cobalt–nickel layered double hydroxide anode enables stable alkaline water electrolysis for more than 8,000 hours at 1 A cm–2 in 6 M sodium hydroxide at 80 °C. This stability arises from the strengthened metal–oxygen bonding of the in-situ-formed cobalt–nickel oxyhydroxide, which raises the energy barrier for lattice-oxygen loss during the oxygen evolution reaction. In a practical electrolyzer, the anode achieves an energy consumption of ~4.2 kWh per normal cubic metre of hydrogen at 1 A cm–2 and operates stably for thousands of hours. The design of high-current-density alkaline electrolyzers should therefore prioritize robust anode stability under industrial conditions in addition to activity optimization. Hydrogen production by alkaline water electrolysis is limited by anode durability under industrial conditions. Here, the authors demonstrate a cobalt–nickel layered double hydroxide anode that sustains operation for over 8,000 h at 1 A cm⁻² in 6 M NaOH at 80 °C, enabling durable hydrogen production.

Article.Title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Liu Q.; Zhang S.; Qin G.; Gu Y.; Jin Y.; Preston S.; Xu Y.; Kiblawi S.; Yim W.; Ossowski T.; Naumann T.; Wei M.; Poon H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. We introduce Universal Report Generation (UNIRG), which adopts reinforcement learning to directly optimize clinically meaningful quality criteria. With this framework, we developed UNIRG-CXR, an 8-billion-parameter vision–language model trained on four public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient-160k and IU-Xray) by supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning (group-relative policy optimization) against a composite lexical, semantic and clinical-error reward. We evaluated held-out test sets and an external proprietary dataset, with RadCliQ as primary metric and expert radiologist validation. Here we show that our method improves report quality and generalization: UNIRG-CXR surpasses prior models on the ReXrank benchmark across four datasets and two generation settings, exceeding the previous best score by over 50% on two test sets, and produces fewer clinically significant errors while maintaining performance on unseen data sources and across demographic subgroups.

Article.Title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
Article.Authors: Yi X.; Wei M.; Yu T.; Xu W.; Wu Y.; Wang Q.; Gu X.; Wang Y.; Cheung H.; Zhang T.; Cao Q.; Zhang Y.; Li H.; Wang L.; Yuan P.; Xu T.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Threat learning requires rapid adaptation, but how the brain weights successive aversive experiences remains unclear. Here we show that many male mice exhibit delayed freezing acquisition during auditory fear conditioning. A trial-wise discount reinforcement learning model captured these dynamics through transient attenuation of early associative updating. Medial prefrontal neurons projecting to the periaqueductal gray constrained acquisition and subsequent cue-evoked freezing: inhibition increased freezing, whereas activation reduced it. Calcium imaging of individual neurons identified a subpopulation with delayed post-shock responses that declined during learning and predicted the model-derived discount-like variable. Temporally restricted inhibition implicated activity extending beyond the shock in constraining early acquisition. Local somatostatin interneurons showed increasing shock-evoked activity and provided inhibitory input to these projection neurons, suggesting a mechanism for relaxing this constraint. These findings link the trial-wise weighting of aversive experience to a prefrontal inhibitory microcircuit and provide a framework for understanding individual differences in threat memory formation. Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

Article.Title: Evolution of the molybdenum and vanadium cycles through time and their impact on ancient nitrogen fixation
Article.Authors: Hao W.; Robbins L.; Anbar A.; Rucker H.; Chen N.; Sun W.; Alessi D.; Dong H.; Stüeken E.; German C.; Lyons T.; Kaçar B.; Konhauser K.
Article.Abstract: Biological nitrogen (N2) fixation is crucial for incorporating atmospheric N2 into the biosphere. However, its evolutionary trajectory remains enigmatic, particularly given the presumed scarcity of molybdenum (Mo) in Archean seawater prior to oxidative weathering and the apparent early emergence of Mo-based nitrogenase over its vanadium (V)-based alternatives. Here, we integrate partitioning experiments with an extensive analysis of iron-rich sediments through time to investigate the behavior of Mo and V in ancient seawater. Our results suggest that, during the Archean to Paleoproterozoic, dissolved V was removed from seawater more efficiently than Mo, primarily through preferential incorporation into banded iron formations (BIF). Consequently, Mo was likely more available in seawater than commonly assumed, with Archean seawater characterized by higher Mo/V ratios than today. Greater Mo availability relative to V provides a compelling explanation for the earlier evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase despite the absence of widespread oxidative weathering, and helps resolve the apparent paradox surrounding the early evolution of biological N2 fixation. Partitioning experiments and Fe-rich sediments show V was removed from Archean– Paleoproterozoic seawater more efficiently than Mo, enriching seawater in Mo relative to V and helping explain the early evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase.

Article.Title: ISG15 promotes PARP inhibitor resistance in BRCA1-deficient cells by facilitating DNA replication and repair
Article.Authors: Dagg R.; Paulsen T.; Prasad B.; De Gregoriis G.; Seung Y.; Groelly F.; Draganov S.; Pedretti F.; Herencia-Ropero A.; Serra V.; Pinto-Fernández A.; Tarsounas M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) has proven largely successful in targeting BRCA1/2 -mutated tumours. However, the emergence of PARPi-resistant disease can reduce the efficacy of this treatment, posing significant challenges in the clinic. Here, we use multiple models of BRCA1 -/- cells and patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) that have been treated with PARPi until they no longer responded to the drug, to characterise genomic and transcriptomic alterations specific to PARPi resistance. We find that abrogation of TP53BP1 expression occurs spontaneously during prolonged PARPi treatment, alongside TP53BP1 genomic deletions and promoter methylation. Additionally, innate immune response genes, including ISG15 and factors of the ISGylation machinery are upregulated in PARPi-resistant cells and tumours. We demonstrate that ISG15 inhibition re-sensitises PARPi-resistant cells to the drug and, conversely, that ISG15 overexpression in BRCA1 -/- cells promotes PARPi resistance. Mechanistically, BRCA1 -/- PARPi-resistant cells rely on ISG15 for replication fork progression and restart of stalled forks and for DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair via homologous recombination (HR). Our results indicate that complex ISG15 interactions with DNA replication/repair factors can drive PARPi resistance in BRCA1-deficient cancer cells and that targeting ISG15 has the potential to overcome PARPi resistance.

Article.Title: Engineering CAR-Vδ2 T cells to boost persistence and anti-tumor function
Article.Authors: Leong L.; Narula M.; Englisch J.; Ou C.; Mamonkin M.; Watanabe N.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-modified Vδ2 T cells are an attractive therapeutic cell platform for cancer immunotherapy. However, their clinical efficacy is limited by short in vivo persistence due to insufficient cytokine support and high susceptibility to activation-induced cell death (AICD). Through comparison of membrane-bound (mb) cytokines, we identified mbIL-18 to support superior anti-tumor activity of CAR-Vδ2 T cells in vitro and in vivo. To reduce constitutive surface exposure of IL-18 and enable antigen-driven signal 3, we fused MyD88 - the key IL-18R signaling mediator - to an extracellular domain of Fas (Fas88). Antigen stimulation-induced FasL engagement of Fas88 triggered IL-18 signaling while simultaneously protecting Vδ2 T cells from AICD. Fas88-armed human CAR-Vδ2 T cells produced superior yet stimulation-dependent in vivo expansion and functional persistence in xenograft models of hematologic and solid malignancies. Together, these findings highlight the importance of IL-18 signaling and AICD resistance for CAR-Vδ2 T cell activity, enabling a single-transgene modification to limit inflammatory risk and facilitate clinical translation. Article.Title: Emergent stoichiometric host-guest recognition on ligated colloidal surfaces via dynamic ligand reorientation
Article.Authors: Li W.; Yang Z.; Tiwari V.; Liu J.; Wang Y.; Xie Y.; Huang H.; Chen R.; Ke J.; Lin S.; Karmakar T.; Li S.; Lan Y.; Xie J.; Cao Y.
Article.Abstract: Physical adsorption on ligand-protected colloidal nanoparticles is central to their properties and applications, yet adsorption events on dynamic ligand shells are rarely defined, counted, or quantified with molecular precision. Here we show that on a native ligand shell without pre-designed receptor-like motifs, molecular adsorption can trigger stoichiometric host-guest recognition through dynamic ligand reorientation. In aqueous dispersion, atomically precise [Au25(p-MBA)18]− (p-MBA = para-mercaptobenzoic acid) nanoclusters accommodate tetraalkylammonium ions within transient aromatic pockets formed by three to four neighboring p-MBA ligands. NMR titration and diffusion-ordered spectroscopy reveal an apparent saturated binding number of six guests per nanocluster, with an apparent association constant of ~3.5 × 104 M−1 and ΔG of ~−25 kJ•mol−1 for tetrapropylammonium binding. Molecular simulations and free-energy analysis rationalize this stoichiometry through a cooperative yet self-limiting mechanism, in which ligand reorientation creates bowl-like pockets stabilized by multiple CH···π interactions while steric constraints limit further guest accommodation. The guest-size- and surface-dependent binding behaviors further reveal the adaptive nature of emergent pockets. These findings change the role of the ligand shell from a stabilizing layer or diffuse adsorption medium to an active supramolecular interface capable of producing molecularly defined recognition, paving the way for adaptive nanomaterials, selective sensing, and stimuli-responsive colloidal systems. Here the authors show that molecular adsorption can trigger stoichiometric host-guest recognition through dynamic ligand reorientation.

Article.Title: Constructing exclusive Pt@WOx interfacial sites enables selective C–O bond activation
Article.Authors: Zou J.; Zhou D.; He Q.; Zhao B.; Zhu C.; Liu L.; Dong J.
Article.Abstract: Precisely constructing exclusive metal-oxide interfacial active sites while eliminating non-interfacial species represents a longstanding challenge in heterogeneous catalysis. Here we construct catalysts featuring exclusively isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites via a controlled electrostatic adsorption strategy, thereby eliminating non-interfacial Pt species, enabling controlled reaction pathways. We identify that selective C–O bond activation is governed by the availability of interfacial reactive hydrogen, where isolated Pt sites drive deep hydrogenolysis, while Pt@WOx interfacial sites control reaction pathways by constrained hydrogen availability. This principle is validated in glycerol hydrogenolysis, achieving a high 1,3-PDO selectivity of 73.5% at a low temperature of 130 °C. Experiments reveal that 1,3-PDO selectivity is not enhanced by increasing active site density, but by eliminating intrinsically unselective sites, thereby reshaping the reaction energy landscape to suppress thermodynamically driven over-hydrogenolysis. This architecture provides an ideal platform for disentangling interface effects from contributions arising from non-interfacial metal species. Precisely constructing metal–oxide catalysts with exclusively interfacial active sites remains challenging. Here, glycerol is selectively converted to 1,3-propanediol over catalysts in which Pt exists solely as isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites.

Article.Title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis

Article.Abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) regulate plant development, stress responses and genome stability by guiding ARGONAUTE (AGO) proteins to their targets. AGO1 is the major effector of microRNA (miRNA) and 21/22-nucleotide (nt) secondary small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways in Arabidopsis thaliana. However, how AGO1 subcellular dynamics shape sRNA loading and silencing remained unclear. Here, we validate a functional nuclear localization signal (NLS) in the N-terminal extension of AGO1 and identify IMPORTIN α2 (IMPα2) as a nuclear import factor acting within a larger importin α network. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that AGO1 spatial partitioning itself quantitatively shapes the efficiency and specificity of sRNA loading and the silencing outputs. Article.Title: scMomer: a pretraining framework for inferring robust cellular representations from single-cell transcriptomes
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Zou Q.; Su R.; Wei L.
Article.Abstract: High-quality cellular representations are important for understanding complex biological systems. Here, we propose scMomer, a multistage pretraining framework designed to infer robust cellular representations by integrating multimodal knowledge into scRNA-seq-only inputs. The framework progressively learns through three stages. Firstly, it pretrains unimodal encoders on single-modality datasets to obtain modality-specific representations. Secondly, it aligns these modalities using paired data to learn joint representations. Thirdly, it applies knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge of the missing modality (scATAC-seq) into a cross-modal student encoder, enabling the inference of multimodal-aware representations from scRNA-seq-only inputs. We perform extensive experiments show that the representations learned by scMomer achieve superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods across diverse tasks, including cross-modality translation, cell annotation, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and gene property prediction, demonstrating its robustness and versatility. Overall, we demonstrate that scMomer enables unimodal data to yield robust cellular representations, providing an effective solution to missing-modality modeling. Here, the authors develop scMomer, a pretraining framework that infers multimodal-aware cellular representations from scRNA-seq data alone. By distilling chromatin accessibility knowledge, the authors show that this method can be applied to different downstream single-cell tasks.

Article.Title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
Article.Authors: Zhao G.; Mou B.; Zheng X.; Liu S.; Sheng D.; Wang S.; Zhu L.; Yang W.; Huang Z.; Song S.; He S.; Zhu L.; Ning Y.; Cui F.; Wang J.; Sun W.
Article.Abstract: Numerous E3 ubiquitin ligases regulate plant immunity through mediating protein homeostasis, yet how homeostasis of E3 ligases is finely regulated per se remains poorly understood. Article.Abstract: Abstract This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Article.Title: High-pressure synthesis of a polymeric N3H2 solid stabilized by hydrogen bonds
Article.Authors: Ranieri U.; Geneste G.; Weck G.; Bolton S.; Spender J.; Liang A.; Massani B.; Garbarino G.; Laniel D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polymeric nitrogen represents a long-sought class of high energy density materials, in which single-bonded nitrogen networks release large amounts of energy upon decomposition to molecular N 2 . However, polymeric nitrogen allotropes require extreme pressures to synthesize and cannot be recovered at ambient conditions due to surface instabilities. Hydrogen has been proposed as a key element to stabilize such frameworks, yet polymeric nitrogen–hydrogen solids have until now remained the realm of theoretical calculations. Here, we report the high-pressure synthesis of polymeric N 3 H 2 at 134(3)–139(1) GPa from N 2 –H 2 mixtures. Synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and first-principles calculations reveal a fully single-bonded framework of 1-dimensional chains of N 6 rings, each decorated by four H atoms. The chains of N 6 H 4 units are cross-linked through hydrogen bonds. Employing modern synchrotron sources, hydrogen positions are directly resolved from diffraction data at 139(1) GPa. At ambient conditions, N 3 H 2 exhibits an estimated energy of decomposition of 7.98 kJ/g, highlighting hydrogen-stabilized polymeric nitrogen as a promising class of energetic materials.

Article.Authors: Wyborski P.; Paralikis A.; Metuh P.; Jacobsen M.; Ruiz Madera C.; Gregersen N.; Munkhbat B.
Article.Abstract: Single-photon sources operating at telecom wavelengths are fundamental components for long-distance optical quantum communication and information processing. These results establish MoTe2 as a viable platform for tunable, low-noise, high-purity single-photon sources for quantum photonics. Article.Abstract: Abstract Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are widely utilised in RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) technologies to eliminate polymerase chain reaction (PCR) duplicates, thereby improving the accuracy of molecular quantification. While various computational methods have been developed for error correction, the lack of a unified benchmarking and validation framework impedes systematic evaluation and optimisation. Here, we present UMIche, an open-source, UMI-centric computational platform designed to enhance UMI-assisted molecular quantification. Its application to collapsing monomer and homotrimer UMIs across multiple bulk and single-cell sequencing protocols demonstrates effective PCR-duplicate removal. Article.Abstract: RHOA, a RAS superfamily member, is frequently mutated in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). Directed attention uniformly amplifies surround suppression across the visual hierarchy, consistent with a distributed suppressive field, whereas modulation of target-related activity increases hierarchically from V1 to hV4. Critically, modulation of surround suppression, but not target enhancement, predicts behavioral performance. These findings dissociate the mechanisms of target enhancement and surround suppression and reveal the computational architecture underlying biased competition in the human cortex, converging with recent primate electrophysiology research. Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

Article.Authors: Nakano K.; Tsuruta T.

At higher fields, the response was consistent with field-assisted charge injection across the molecular junction. This approach requires no pre-derivatisation of the DNA backbone and provides a versatile strategy for post-synthetic functionalisation. Here, the authors develop a chemically defined DNA–ferrocene conjugate through covalent modification of a DNA duplex and demonstrate an enhanced electrical response. Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). Article.Title: Processing-induced self-organised triboelectric interfaces enable event-responsive cementitious composites
Article.Authors: Cai J.; Sun H.; Li D.; Huang J.; Cai G.; Wu J.; Fei H.; Wu C.; Ma L.; Wang L.; Zhang Y.; Zhang R.; Guo T.
Article.Abstract: Structural materials are commonly designed to bear loads passively, whereas sensing and energy-harvesting functions are typically implemented using externally attached devices that are vulnerable to damage and interfacial failure. Here we report a processing-induced strategy for forming self-organised triboelectric interfaces directly within fibre-reinforced cementitious composites during vibration-assisted casting. Through fresh-state flow, fibre migration, and grid-assisted interception, conductive and dielectric constituents assemble into local fibre-enriched contact regions, enabling intrinsic electromechanical transduction without post-fabrication assembly. Microstructural characterisation reveals local fibre enrichment and fibre-grid interweaving around the embedded coated grid, while first-principles calculations support the interfacial charge redistribution between polyvinyl alcohol and polytetrafluoroethylene. The composites retain high mechanical toughness while exhibiting stable electrical responses under low-frequency mechanical excitation, with signal amplitude scaling with load and contact configuration. After cracking, newly created internal interfaces continue to provide functional output, demonstrating damage-tolerant electromechanical activity. We further demonstrate an event-triggered sensing system in which the embedded interfaces serve as self-powered signal sources for wake-up and alert operations. Article.Title: Single photon reflection from a quantum dot in a waveguide
Article.Authors: Patel T.; Pennacchietti M.; Gangopadhyay S.; Dalacu D.; Poole P.; Hughes S.; Reimer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Single-atom waveguide-QED systems have emerged as a leading platform for demonstrating non-linear optics in the few-photon regime. Devices with such non-linear behavior are necessary for developing deterministic gates for photonic quantum computing. Artificial atoms coupled to nanophotonic or superconducting waveguides can be used to engineer highly efficient light-matter interfaces for such non-linear interactions, where every photon in the system interacts with the quantum emitter. However, it has been a challenge to access the reflection port of the waveguide due to the inability of rejecting stray electromagnetic fields that do not interact with the artificial atom. Here, we show coherent reflection of single photons from a semiconductor quantum dot strongly coupled to the fundamental waveguide mode of a nanowire. We utilize the tapered end of the nanowire for ideal mode-matching in a vertical geometry, enabled by the extinction technique developed. This mode-matching allows for efficient transfer of photons from the input to the reflection port while having all interacted with the quantum dot. Such a high-efficiency scalable photonic platform opens up applications in few-photon quantum nonlinear optics and has been proposed for creating key resource states for universal photon-based quantum computing.

Article.Title: Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
Article.Authors: Raghuram A.; Blondell F.; Mortlock J.; Maddox B.; Dasgupta S.; Middleton-Spencer H.; Hazzard K.; Price H.; Gregory P.; Cornish S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

Article.Title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Ma Y.; Jin Q.; Gan C.; Zhang J.; Rong H.; Liu T.; Wang N.; Yuan Y.
Article.Abstract: Sustainable uranium supply is critical for nuclear energy, yet its practical recovery is severely hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium in natural waters. In dynamic aqueous environments, uranium continuously shifts between large, cationic hydrolyzed clusters (acidic/neutral) and compact, anionic carbonate complexes (alkaline). Conventional static adsorbents fail to accommodate these contrasting charges and geometries. Here, we report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework (COF), TAM-DTDA-AMM, to overcome this speciation barrier. Featuring a three-fold interpenetrated dia topology, the functional COF enables environment-driven reversible −COO−···NH4+ ion-pair reconfiguration, coupling adaptive pore-surface chemistry with dynamic spatial confinement. Under alkaline environments, cationic microdomains stabilize [UO2(CO3)3]4− via electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions, whereas under near-neutral to acidic conditions, protonated carboxyl groups directly coordinate hydrolyzed uranyl clusters. This dual-adaptive mechanism enables rapid, selective, and high-capacity uranium extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries and offers a general strategy for recognizing multiple metal species in complex environments. Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

Article.Title: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Cao M.; Liu R.; Song L.; Zhang Z.; Zhang F.; Yao R.; Yang L.; Shen D.; Zhu Y.; Sun E.; He X.; Li F.; Bu Z.; Sheng X.; Zhao D.
Article.Abstract: Numerous viruses have evolved diverse strategies to counteract host antiviral responses. African swine fever virus (ASFV), a large double-stranded DNA virus that threatens the global swine industry and food security, is thought to employ highly complex yet poorly understood mechanisms to facilitate infection. Article.Abstract: Abstract Four-electron iodine redox chemistry offers a high theoretical specific energy of ~1324 Wh kgI −1 , yet its practical realization is fundamentally limited by the conflicting demands of rapid I 0 /I + oxidation, effective suppression of iodine shuttling, and stabilization of highly reactive I + species. Upon electrochemical oxidation, electrophilic phthalimide δ+ strongly interacts with nucleophilic iodine and polyiodide species, concurrently suppressing polyiodide shuttling and promoting their conversion to I + . The consecutively generated phthalimide δ− acts as a nucleophilic stabilizer for the resulting I + species. Article.Title: Robust optical skyrmion arising from randomness
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Lu X.; Shi P.; Lu X.; Xia Z.; Zhan Q.; Cai Y.; Yuan X.; Zhao C.
Article.Abstract: Optical skyrmions, known as topological quasiparticles, have emerged as a distinct photonic degree of freedom with great potential and promising prospects for broad applications. Prior studies have predominantly focused on skyrmions in fully coherent light fields. In this paper, we show that incoherent optical skyrmions can arise from an ensemble of random modes whose statistical correlations are deliberately engineered. Under external obstacles, the engineered statistical correlations enable reconstruction of the focal field, while the skyrmion topology provides a quantized global measure of the structural robustness. Beyond enabling programmable control over skyrmion topology by tailoring these correlations, the statistical construction suppresses the fixed-phase interference between neighboring skyrmion units inherent in coherent superpositions. The demonstrated robustness under obstacles, enhanced skyrmion density resolution, and flexible generation of programmable arrays extensively expand the skyrmion family and offer insights into optical quasiparticles, with potential applications in photonics. Article.Authors: Zeng J.; Chen T.; Liu H.; Shang Y.; Wang F.; Huang X.; Hao S.; Zhou J.; Yang C.
Article.Abstract: Lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles exhibit multicolor emission through discrete, narrowband transitions, enabling applications in bioimaging, lasers, and displays. Here, we address this by introducing a core@shell cascaded transition strategy that selectively populates Ho3+ high-lying states via engineered energy relays at a key intermediate level, Ce3+-mediated cross-relaxation control, and precise spatial ion arrangement. Our design achieves a ∼1500-fold boost in blue emission versus conventional architectures, enabling balanced red, green and blue output at 10 W/cm2 (10 mg/mL suspension). This white-light system surpasses mixed-nanoparticle media in stability, producing white lasers for photonics. Our approach provides a versatile route to high-lying states activation in lanthanide systems, with potential implications for multicolor imaging, displays, and anti-counterfeiting. The authors develop triply doped upconversion nanoparticles with cascaded energy transition pathways via precise spatial ion arrangement, which enables balanced RGB multicolor output and white lasing.

Article.Title: Pigment repression protects fungus from ferroptosis to maintain virulence
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Ma T.; Zhou J.; Sun K.; Zhou Z.; Li Y.; Chen X.; Huang-Fu X.; Haas H.; Ma Z.; Yin Y.
Article.Abstract: Fungal pathogens must adapt to host-derived stresses to establish infection, yet how secondary metabolite regulation contributes to this process remains poorly understood. Article.Authors: Ostapenko D.; Li H.; Trier I.; Shamby R.; Wang Y.; Zagoren E.; Sabrera C.; Sumigray K.; Alarcón C.; Kabeche L.

We further characterize their ecosystem distributions and predict associations with bacteria and other eukaryotes. This study provides a global, cultivation-independent resource for targeted sampling and downstream genomic, ecological and experimental characterization. Article.Authors: Park S.; Zolfaghar M.; Russin J.; Miller D.; O’Reilly R.; Boorman E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent work has shown that the brain abstracts non-spatial relationships between entities or task states into representations called cognitive maps. These representational motifs also emerge with distinct temporal profiles over the course of training in the recurrent neural network, with map-like representations appearing first. We further show that increasing control demands due to incongruence (conflicting responses) between current task-relevant and irrelevant dimensions impact the geometry of subjective representations, and the degree of this effect further accounts for individual differences in cognitive control. The baseplate core is formed by DTPs and BHPs, with terminal TTPs making direct proximal contacts with DTPs and contributing to overall structure. Surrounding the conserved cores are diverse baseplate accessory proteins (BAPs), including upper baseplate proteins (BppUs), central fiber proteins (CFPs), and others, which assemble into distinct peripheral architectures and give rise to two baseplate-opening mechanisms. These structures reveal a conserved baseplate core complex diversified by BAPs, a feature potentially shared across mycobacteriophage siphophage families. Article.Abstract: Battery materials supply chains for plug-in electric vehicles face vulnerabilities to disruptions from geopolitical disputes and natural disasters. Through industry interviews, we identify scenarios that could disrupt materials supply by 2030. We find year-long disruptions can have large impacts: trade restrictions that reduce processed lithium supply from China by 30% and disasters shutting down the three largest cobalt mines increase average new vehicle prices (including conventional vehicles and plug-in electric vehicles) by $1,100-1,600, costing consumers $14-17 billion. This approach allowed imaging of Escherichia coli both expressing O-antigen and fully lacking lipopolysaccharide (LPS) oligosaccharides, revealing that AFM contrast depends on LPS complexity and confirming previously observed outer membrane domains as LPS-enriched islands. It also enabled imaging of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii outer membranes, which lack the characteristic protein trimers observed in model E. coli . Finally, we discovered growth-phase dependent alterations in E. coli pole morphology, where trimer networks typical of exponential-phase cells were unresolved and morphological defects appeared.

Article.Title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"
Article.Authors: Sibatov R.; Ksenofontova P.
Article.Abstract: Self-assembled networks of nano-objects have attracted growing interest as physical substrates for brain-inspired computation. The work of Milano et al. 1 is a valuable study of the dynamics of memristive networks of nanowires. The experimental data presented by the authors are comprehensive and of high quality, providing extensive material for validating stochastic conductance models in such systems. The compact Markovian model proposed in ref. 1 , formulated as a stochastic differential equation of the Itô type that combines deterministic return to equilibrium with random components (Gaussian noise and jumps), allows for the description of certain aspects of the dynamics and an assessment of the impact of stochasticity on computational capabilities within the reservoir computing paradigm. However, closer examination of the data from ref. 1 reveals that each key aspect of the conductance dynamics (deterministic relaxation, jump process, and Gaussian fluctuations) exhibits non-Markovian properties, which calls into question the original stochastic model and suggests a need for its fundamental revision.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Anaerobic methanotrophic (ANME) archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments, yet their physiology remains poorly understood due to the lack of axenic cultures. Here, we show that cultivation on poised electrodes yields near-axenic cultures (95.8% relative abundance) of a freshwater ANME, for which we propose the name ‘ Candidatus Methanoperedens vercellensis’. We identified key physiological properties of ‘ Ca . M. vercellensis’: doubling times of 4.6 days at 30 °C, menaquinone as respiratory electron carrier, the inability to oxidize ethane, and preferential reduction of iron oxides over nitrate after cultivation on electrodes. Notably, in contrast to bacterial OmcZ, archaeal OmcZ-type nanowires do not form interconnected networks, and hemes are less solvent-exposed, which can protect them from the environment. Surprisingly, these archaea assemble OmcZ into nanowires even in the apparent absence of prolyl isomerase involved in folding bacterial OmcZ. Article.Title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
Article.Authors: Ueda H.; Maeda M.; Okada S.; Noguchi R.; Dasgupta B.; Yamamoto R.; Furuta M.; Nishi A.; Nagao A.; Sakaguchi Y.; Miyauchi K.; Suzuki T.
Article.Abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) link mRNA codons to amino acids during translation. Here, we develop an end-to-end deep learning model, termed nano tRNA classifier, that directly uses nanopore-DRS ionic current signals to classify tRNAs without basecalling. Using an equimolar mixture of native tRNAs as a ground-truth reference, we correct read-count bias, enabling absolute quantification and profiling under diverse culture conditions. Article.Authors: Langenmayr U.; Schuler J.; Slednev V.; Fichtner W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Article.Abstract: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and climate. Peptide-functionalized nanoparticles exhibit pronounced and tunable responses to CO2 across orders of magnitude changes in gas flow rate, with sensitivity governed by site- and sequence-specific changes in peptide structure. The aggregation sequence-dependence is described by six design principles while quantitative modeling show that aggregation rate scales with flow rate rather than cumulative CO2 dose. This gas-controlled response translates from colloidal nanoparticles to cm-scale biocompatible hydrogels that reversibly and colorimetrically respond to CO2. Leveraging this responsiveness, we further demonstrate spatial patterning of a hydrogel through a gas-permeable mask using CO2 as a lithographic stimulus. Consequently, this work establishes gas-mediated control as a general and scalable strategy for programming responsive materials across length scales. Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Fan Z.; Mei Y.; Yu Y.; Zhong C.; Li Q.; Zhuang X.; Wang L.; Zhou D.; Zhu C.; Yang J.; Ding H.; Zhang Z.; Zhang S.; Cao J.

Here, we show that a single dose of propofol rapidly and persistently reduces alcohol consumption in mice for approximately six days. This effect is mediated by sustained hyperactivity of the habenular ensemble activated by propofol. Furthermore, this ensemble is enriched in 5-HT2C receptors, and we identify the V209 site as the specific binding site through which propofol induces ensemble activation. Article.Authors: Bruderer M.; Li J.; Kaczmarczyk A.; van Vliet S.; Schleicher K.; Girish R.; Manfredi P.; Thürkauf N.; Klotz A.; Kuhn M.; Khanna N.; Persat A.; Laventie B.; Jenal U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. Article.Title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Singh M.; Mendez K.; Ayers B.; Wang S.; Takahashi A.; Teodorescu D.; Mill J.; Albors C.; Escher A.; Fan Y.; Ozturk C.; Sheridan E.; Rutherford E.; Camara O.; Chakravarty T.; Roche E.
Article.Abstract: Atrial fibrillation poses significant challenges because the complex geometry of the left atrial appendage complicates personalized interventions for stroke prevention. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. Article.Authors: Wang H.; Ye Y.; Zhang T.; Li B.; Hayward A.; Wang Y.; Xiao Y.; Kong Y.; Zhong J.; Li C.; Zuo K.; Wang S.; Nauen R.; Shi Y.; Wang X.; Bass C.; Ma S.; Zhou S.
Article.Abstract: Insecticide resistance poses a growing threat to global human health and food security. Article.Title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
Article.Authors: Kim K.; Lee J.; Kim H.; Sim H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

Article.Authors: Lee H.; Sung J.; Park S.; Kim D.; Lee S.; Lim J.; Ko K.; Wang D.; Wang D.; Lee Y.; Moon J.; Park S.

Article.Abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is the second largest source of plastic wastes. An ideal solution is to chemically convert PET back into its monomers.
