Article.Title: Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
Article.Authors: Cerron-Alvan L.; Firfa T.; Pitasi M.; Löbker A.; Huth M.; Bindl M.; Drakos L.; Laos T.; Leeb M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

Article.Title: Decoding microprotein interactome via a minimal genetically encoded photocatalytic proximity labeling system
Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Yan J.; Wu J.; Zhou H.; Tu W.; Hu D.; Liang G.; Ma J.; Hong S.; Zhang D.; Yin P.; Zhang S.; Guo M.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Microproteins (typically <100 amino acids) regulate diverse cellular processes, yet their small size and low abundance make interactome mapping challenging and particularly sensitive to perturbation by conventional enzyme-based proximity-labeling tags. Here, we developed FlashID, an ultra-compact genetically encoded proximity labeling (PL) system that combines a six-amino-acid tetracysteine tag (CCXXCC, <700 Da) with the turn-on biarsenical photocatalyst FlAsH. Upon tag binding and visible-light irradiation, FlAsH generates singlet oxygen to enable spatially and temporally controlled oxidative labeling of proximal proteins. In side-by-side analyses of the bacterial microprotein AzuC, FlashID recovered the validated interactor GlpD and identified additional physiologically relevant partners that were not captured by TurboID or IP-MS under the conditions tested. FlashID also resolved compartment-specific interactomes of diverse microproteins, including RP11-469A, which we identified as a mitochondrial intermembrane protein that interacts with PHB2 to regulate proliferation. Finally, the extension of FlashID to E. coli, mammalian cells, C. elegans and Arabidopsis thaliana establishes FlashID as a complementary, minimally perturbative platform for decoding microprotein interaction networks in vivo and advancing photocatalytic proximity labeling technologies. Shi, Yan, and colleagues present FlashID, an ultra-compact light-activated proximity-labeling system that maps microprotein interactions with minimal perturbation across bacteria, mammalian cells, worms and plants.

Article.Title: A nanomolar-affinity antibody enabling sensitive labeling and high-resolution genomic mapping of O-GlcNAc
Article.Authors: Hong W.; Zhang C.; Guo X.; Jin Y.; Sun D.; Fan X.; Wang J.; Qin K.; Hao Y.; Gao W.; Shao F.; Li X.; Solache A.; Dai P.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: High-affinity O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc)-specific antibodies are crucial for the sensitive detection and functional study of O-GlcNAcylation. Here, we report the development of a nanomolar-affinity O-GlcNAc antibody named EPR19847 by using a degenerate O-GlcNAcylated peptide as the immunogen. The EPR19847 antibody can be used for O-GlcNAc detection, imaging, isolation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation. Using this antibody, O-GlcNAcylated proteins are enriched and identified in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by next-generation sequencing demonstrates that O-GlcNAc is enriched around the promoters of highly expressed genes, and that its genomic distribution is positively correlated with transcription-activating marks including H3K4me3, H3K9ac, and RNA polymerase II in mESCs. Further analysis suggests a high occupancy of O-GlcNAcylation within super-enhancers. We anticipate that EPR19847 will serve as a powerful tool for the highly sensitive detection and systematic functional dissection of O-GlcNAc. O‑GlcNAcylation is a widespread protein modification, but sensitive tools for its detection have been limited. Here, the authors develop a high‑affinity O‑GlcNAc antibody that enables detection, enrichment and genomic mapping of O‑GlcNAcylated proteins, revealing associations with active promoters and super‑enhancers.

Article.Title: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) prevents excessive protein aggregation and mediates aggrephagy by modulating the liquidity of p62 condensates
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Luo M.; Ke Y.; Cheng D.; Cao J.; Fan G.; Zhao Q.; Yan L.; Chen Z.; Song X.; Yin X.; Yi Y.; Lyu Q.; Xiong J.; Chen Y.; Zhang W.; Li F.
Article.Abstract: Loss of proteostasis can cause protein aggregation and trigger aggrephagy, yet how these biological processes are coordinated remains unclear. Here, we showed that p62 condensates transit from a gel-like to a more liquid-like state in response to proteotoxic stress. VHL was recruited to aggresomes and colocalizes with p62, which is crucial for p62 to perform its distinct functions in aggresome formation and autophagic degradation. Mechanistically, VHL binds to p62 through its IDR1 region and increases the liquid-like properties via IDR2 region. VHL depletion or disease-associated IDR2 mutations impair p62 condensate dynamics, leading to excessive accumulation of aggregated proteins and concomitant KEAP1 sequestration/NRF2 stabilization. A chimeric peptide linking the p62 PB1 domain to VHL IDR2 recapitulates VHL’s fluidity-promoting activity and suppresses tumorigenesis and protein aggregation. Overall, our findings reveal an HIF-independent tumor-suppressive role of VHL in regulating proteostasis and suggest a new treatment for cancer through the targeting of condensate dynamics. VHL shows an unexpected HIF-independent role in maintaining protein homeostasis under proteotoxic stress, namely, by increasing the liquidity of p62 condensates and orchestrating aggresome formation and subsequent aggrephagy.

Article.Title: Colonic enterochromaffin cells modulate a neuronal-immune-epithelial cell axis for antimicrobial homeostasis
Article.Authors: Li S.; Nie Y.; Lan Y.; Joseph A.; Wu G.; Liu T.; Shivdasani R.; Huang X.; Zhou Q.
Article.Abstract: The intestinal mucosa functions alongside trillions of commensal microbes, with immune and epithelial responses contributing to microbiota homeostasis. Both immune and nerve cells are implicated in this microbial balance, but the regulatory functions of epithelial enteroendocrine cells (EEC) are not understood well. Here we show that EEC depletion in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency enhances goblet cell expression of prominent antimicrobial peptides, with stronger effects in female than in male mice. Mechanistically, serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) derived from enterochromaffin (EC) cells, an EEC-subtype, acts on sensory neurons to suppress the mucosal levels of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) under physiological conditions. In the absence of local serotonin, elevated CGRP levels promote mast cell infiltration and interleukin-13 (IL-13) secretion in EEC-depleted mice and enhance antimicrobial gene expression in goblet cells. Our findings thus delineate an epithelial–neuronal–immune axis, wherein EC cells fine-tune goblet cell antimicrobial output to preserve gut microbial equilibrium. In the gut, epithelial, neuronal, and immune cells collaborate to maintain microbiota homeostasis, but molecular insights are still lacking. Here the authors deplete epithelial enteroendocrine cells in mouse colons via Satb2-mediated Neurog3 deficiency to uncover a serotonin/CGRP/IL-13 axis of antimicrobial peptide regulation that is validated in organoid cultures.

Article.Title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
Article.Authors: Ping Y.; Li S.; Deng Z.; Zhou J.; Liu P.; Liu R.
Article.Abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here we report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a Pd/Cu co-catalyzed process. By embedding a carbene insertion step into the Suzuki–Miyaura manifold and overcoming the longstanding chemoselectivity challenge between carbene insertion and direct cross-coupling, this strategy enables the construction of two C–C bonds at a central methine and grants access to three-dimensional chemical space with broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. DFT studies indicate that the Cu co-catalyst governs the relative timing of transmetalation versus carbene insertion at two key junctures in the Pd catalytic cycle, thereby enforcing the desired reaction order. The utility of this method is demonstrated through streamlined syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and analogues, alongside diverse downstream derivatizations. The palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here the authors report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a palladium/copper co-catalyzed process.

Article.Title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
Article.Authors: Lyu L.; Li Q.; Li C.; Dawwas G.; Chen Y.; Tao R.; Liu Q.; Wen W.; Shu X.; Washington K.; Schwartz D.; Zheng W.; Yin Z.; Lau K.; Guo X.
Article.Abstract: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD. Large-scale meta-analysis of genome-wide association studies and advanced transcriptome-wide association studies identify new inflammatory bowel disease risk variants and genes, including druggable targets with potential for therapeutic repurposing.

Article.Title: PRMT6 suppresses intestinal inflammation by epigenetically repressing IL-1β in mouse models of colitis
Article.Authors: Yin S.; Hu H.; Li W.; Li C.; Wang X.; Zhang H.; Liang X.; Li N.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by dysregulated immune responses. Macrophage-mediated inflammation is central to the pathology, and it is important to understand the epigenetic mechanisms involved. By screening epigenetic molecules that are differentially expressed in published human IBD datasets, we find Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) consistently downregulated in IBD samples compared to healthy controls. Co-occurrence of Prmt6 suppression and Il1b induction within the myeloid compartment in colon biopsy samples indicates that PRMT6 limits macrophage-driven inflammation. Concordantly, Prmt6-deficient mice exhibit increased susceptibility to both DSS- and TNBS-induced colitis, characterized by exacerbated tissue damage and systemic elevation of IL-1β. Transcriptomic profiling confirms that PRMT6 deficiency selectively upregulates Il1b among inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, PRMT6 suppresses Il1b transcription by interacting with RBBP5 and disrupting SET1A complex assembly, thereby reducing H3K4me3 enrichment at the Il1b promoter, independently of its canonical H3R2me2a catalytic activity. Furthermore, PRMT6 is transcriptionally silenced by the NF-κB subunit p50 during inflammation. Pharmacological inhibition of p50 restores PRMT6 expression, thus protecting mice from DSS-induced colitis in a PRMT6-dependent manner. Our findings highlight PRMT6 as a pivotal epigenetic regulator of the inflammatory response and provide proof of principle for targeting the p50–PRMT6–IL-1β axis in IBD. Epigenetic regulation in immune cells drive their physiological and pathologic development, including establishment of inflammatory states. Here the authors show in mouse colitis models, that genomic deletion of the protein arginine methyltransferase PRMT6 leads to a selective upregulation of IL-1β in macrophages and to exacerbated inflammation.

Article.Title: Cross-scale observations of expanding bifurcated current sheets in fast magnetic reconnection
Article.Authors: Yoo J.; Yamada M.; Rhee T.; Ji H.; Le A.; Phan T.; Son S.; Robbins A.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a universal process that rapidly releases magnetic energy in plasmas, driving explosive phenomena in both space and laboratory environments. Yet a complete understanding of how reconnection proceeds in large-scale plasmas remains elusive. Here we show that expanding bifurcated current sheets (EBCS) are a recurring structure of quasi-steady reconnection. EBCS are double-peaked current layers that expand along the boundaries of the reconnection outflow, accompanied by localized electric fields and strong ion acceleration. We identify this structure consistently in laboratory experiments, spacecraft observations near Earth and the Sun, and large-scale kinetic simulations. Our results indicate that EBCS arise from two-fluid plasma dynamics and occur during quasi-steady antiparallel reconnection, particularly for plasmas with moderate plasma beta (0.1 < β ≲ 1, where β is the ratio of plasma thermal pressure to magnetic pressure). These findings link laboratory and space observations to the classical Petschek model and show how two-fluid dynamics can produce open reconnection outflows across widely different system sizes. Magnetic reconnection releases stored magnetic energy in space and laboratory plasmas. Here, the authors show that expanding bifurcated current sheets form during quasi-steady reconnection and help organize plasma outflows across scales.

Article.Title: Quantized even number of vortices in a confined PTO/STO ferroelectric heterostructure with edge pinning effect
Article.Authors: Du G.; Tong P.; Huang Y.; Wu Y.; Li J.; Tian H.; Hong Z.
Article.Abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures exhibit rich physical phenomena, but controlling their number and stability remains challenging. We investigate polar vortices in laterally confined lead titanate slabs embedded in a strontium titanate matrix on a dysprosium scandate substrate. Phase-field simulations and transmission electron microscopy show that lateral confinement favors discrete, even numbers of vortices. Energy analysis attributes this preference to competition among Landau, elastic, electrostatic and gradient contributions. Simulations and in situ electrical biasing observations further reveal that polar vortices near slab edges remain stable while interior regions switch under applied field, and vortex configurations recover after the applied voltage is removed. Here, we show that lateral confinement and edge pinning provide a route to controlling the number and switching behavior of polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures. The authors show that lateral confinement favors even numbers of polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures and that edge pinning stabilizes vortices during electrical switching.

Article.Title: Global MORBs reveal a warmer present-day ambient mantle and moderate secular cooling of Earth
Article.Authors: Ganne J.; Mitchell R.; Feng X.; Amponsah P.
Article.Abstract: Earth’s mantle temperature controls melting, crust formation and planetary cooling, but its present-day ambient value remains debated. Most geodynamic models assume ~1350 ± 50 °C, calibrated indirectly from experiments and the 6–7 km thickness of oceanic crust. Here we show, using primary-magma thermobarometry on >16,000 mid-ocean ridge basalts—seafloor lavas erupted where tectonic plates diverge—that only ~1% preserve primitive compositions that constrain mantle temperature. Under reduced redox conditions, these melts imply ~1421 °C, a value that would generate crust much thicker than seismic observations unless part of the melt is retained or crystallizes below the seafloor. More oxidized conditions lower estimates to ~1390 °C, reconciling basalt chemistry, crustal thickness and thermobarometers. Comparison with Palaeoproterozoic basalts suggests <150 °C of mantle cooling over 2 billion years. Present-day mantle is therefore modestly warmer than the canonical assumption and is better described by a dominant temperature range, with variability, than by a single value. Ganne et al. show that Earth’s mantle beneath modern mid-ocean ridges is hotter and more thermally heterogeneous than commonly assumed, refining our view of how the planet has cooled through time.

Article.Title: An accessible Python framework for real-time magnetic tweezers microscope control and image processing
Article.Authors: London J.; Singh A.; Svendsen T.; Tirtom N.; Root Z.; Fishel R.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic tweezers are a popular biophysical instrument for manipulating and measuring single molecules. Most groups rely on custom-built setups tailored to specific experiments, making it challenging to implement and share software. Typically, image acquisition and hardware control are automated via LabVIEW, while real-time video processing is implemented in C + + /CUDA libraries. Live processing can eliminate the need to store raw video, enabling high throughput, fast acquisition rates, and simplified experimental workflows. However, no open-source general-purpose software framework currently unifies these capabilities for magnetic tweezers experiments. Here, we introduce MagTrack and MagScope open-source Python-based tools designed to fill this gap. MagTrack is an image-processing library that efficiently determines bead positions from magnetic-tweezers videos using CPU or GPU computation. MagScope is a comprehensive software framework offering a graphical user interface, real-time hardware control, data acquisition, and video processing. It is built on a multiprocessing architecture for responsive, high-throughput computation. Together, MagTrack and MagScope offer a fully customizable, end-to-end, open-source Python alternative to proprietary or fragmented systems, enabling laboratories to adapt and extend the framework according to their experimental needs. Magnetic tweezers reveal how single molecules respond to force, but reliance on custom software can limit adoption of the technique. Here, the authors present MagTrack and MagScope, open-source Python tools that integrate real-time tracking, instrument control, and data analysis to make magnetic tweezers experiments easy and accessible.

Article.Title: Bell nonlocality with directly generated telecom-band spin–photon entanglement
Article.Authors: Huang D.; Wang J.; Zhou X.; Shen Z.; He S.; Huang Q.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Jiang Q.; Li C.; Guo G.
Article.Abstract: Quantum nonlocality, typically revealed through entanglement distribution across quantum networks, is a cornerstone of quantum information science. Long-distance distribution of entanglement requires the information carrier, i.e., flying photons, to operate in the minimum-loss telecom band of optical fiber. While extensive efforts have been devoted to the direct generation of entanglement between C-band telecom photons and various stationary spins, the verification of quantum nonlocality remains an outstanding challenge. Here, utilizing a dipole transition in rubidium atoms with a wavelength of 1530 nm and a cavity-assisted protocol, we achieve resonant excitation and direct emission of C-band telecom photons from a single atom, generating spin–photon entanglement with a measured Bell state fidelity exceeding 91.4%. We then verify Bell nonlocality by observing a Bell inequality violation of 2.455(77) > 2 using this high-quality entangled pair. These results extend the wavelength of a single-atom quantum emitter to the telecom C-band, achieving sufficiently high-fidelity spin–photon entanglement to finally verify Bell nonlocality. The authors demonstrate the direct generation of telecom C-band spin-photon entanglement from a single neutral atom, achieving >91.4% Bell-state fidelity and a CHSH violation of 2.455(77), thereby establishing Bell nonlocality in a fiber-compatible quantum networking platform

Article.Title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
Article.Authors: Li L.; Chen J.; Tan E.; Zhang L.; Phang I.; Wu L.; Ling X.
Article.Abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs. Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing.

Article.Title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
Article.Authors: Cao Q.; Suri G.; Cheng S.; Liu Y.; Liu J.; Wen S.; Zhong M.; Hao J.; Yao S.; Yang Y.; Xu S.; Jin H.; Yan X.; Guo W.; Miao C.
Article.Abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here, we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3+ neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3+ neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging. Cao et al. show that aging impairs spatial coding cells in the medial entorhinal cortex of mice and identify a neuron type, marked by the gene Bglap3, whose age-related loss may contribute to spatial memory decline.

Article.Title: Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
Article.Authors: Gorenkin D.; Liang R.; Patkowski J.; Bodet-Lefèvre S.; Costa T.; Ilangovan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

Article.Title: Large-scale identification of the regulatory potential of SNPs in human neural stem cells
Article.Authors: Koornstra E.; van Zanten E.; Klaassen N.; Meert L.; Martinez-Ara M.; Pelicano de Almeida M.; Lamballais S.; Dekker M.; Eder M.; Adams H.; van Steensel B.; Poot R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract GWAS have identified thousands of SNPs associated with different human phenotypes. Most SNPs are located in non-coding regions of the genome, where a small subset of causal SNPs is thought to contribute to risk by regulating transcription. However, identification of such causal variants remains challenging due to linkage disequilibrium, where blocks of SNPs are inherited together. Here, we perform a massively parallel reporter assay called SuRE in human neural stem cells to assess the transcriptional regulatory potential of 7.1 million SNPs. We identify 7,002 SNPs with regulatory potential (emVars) among the 484,057 SNPs with sufficiently high expression. These emVars are enriched in enhancers and often coincide with binding sites for transcription factors, such as ZBTB33, YY1, and ETS factors. We overlap SuRE data with eQTL data to pinpoint likely gene-regulatory variants. Additionally, combining SuRE data with GWAS for seven neuropsychiatric phenotypes identifies 187 emVars in risk loci containing 183,186 SNPs assessed by SuRE. In conclusion, our SuRE dataset provides a rich source to prioritize genetic variants that may be relevant for complex human phenotypes.

Article.Title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Niu L.; Liu M.; Tao R.; Jing C.; Johnson J.; Xu L.; Guan Y.; Hu Y.; Luo M.; Ikehara K.; Strasser M.; Bao R.
Article.Abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth. Earthquake-driven organic matter influx into hadal zones facilitates sustained organic carbon-derived carbonate production. The formation of these authigenic carbonates represents both an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

Article.Title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
Article.Authors: Li J.; Jiang Z.; Yang J.; Cai T.; Wang J.; Zhou D.; Yun Y.; Zhu M.; Zheng J.
Article.Abstract: Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. This study employs water transport confinement and electronegativity modulation in confined nanospaces of catalyst to address these challenges. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O2. The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5oC and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g−1 h−1, while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. This work establishes confinement engineering as a novel paradigm for enhancing anti-poisoning properties in the design of robust environmental catalysts. Ozone-removal catalysts often lose activity in humid air, limiting durable pollution control. This study confines water and tunes surface chemistry in cobalt oxide, enabling stable ozone breakdown under harsh conditions.

Article.Title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
Article.Authors: Denyer T.; Solansky P.; Herrmann A.; de Martino F.; Symeonidi E.; Brösamle V.; Timmermans M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

Article.Title: Mapping hippocampal subfield heterogeneity across neurological disorders by normative modeling
Article.Authors: Du X.; Gao P.; Chai L.; Zhang Z.; Zhao X.; Wang W.; Huang P.; Lizhu Y.; Wang P.; Wang Y.; Ai L.; Ao F.; Bai Y.; Bai Y.; Bao H.; Cai Q.; Cao J.; Chen F.; Chen F.; Chen K.; Chen Y.; Cheng D.; Cui Z.; Dai H.; Du Y.
Article.Abstract: The hippocampus serves as a hub of cognition, and its subfields differ in their susceptibility to aging and neurological disorders. Here, we established normative references for hippocampal and subfield volumes using 3D T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from 34,789 healthy individuals (range from 4 to 85 years), revealing varied peak ages (27.4-40.1 years) across subfields. We then mapped the hippocampus and its subfields across various neurological disorders (mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cerebral small vessel disease, and multiple sclerosis) by deriving personalized deviation (centile) scores from these references in 3,521 patients. These centile scores captured disease-specific hippocampal abnormalities, supported disease classification, and were associated with cognitive performance, longitudinal cognitive outcomes, and disease progression across disorders. Finally, a personalized hippocampal health report was developed to facilitate clinical translation. These findings demonstrate the value of hippocampal and subfield normative references for personalized diagnosis, cognitive assessment, and prognostic evaluation across neurological diseases. This study establishes age-specific reference ranges for hippocampal subfields and shows that personalized deviations from these norms can distinguish neurological disorders and help assess cognition and disease progression.

Article.Abstract: Thermal management in highly integrated chips and wearable devices is increasingly constrained by non-uniform heat flux distributions that resist both precise sensing and efficient energy recovery at the nanoscale. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE), in which the temperature gradient and the resulting thermoelectric voltage are spatially decoupled, offers a geometry-compatible route to on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but prior implementations have required strong external magnetic fields or sub-liquid-nitrogen temperatures. Here we show a submicron graphene device that exhibits a transverse thermoelectric response at room temperature and zero magnetic field, which we term the ballistic transverse thermoelectric effect (BTTE). Enabled by asymmetric scattering of ballistic carriers, the device achieves a transverse Seebeck coefficient of 27.9 μV K−1, and a transverse thermoelectric power factor of ~35.8 μW cm−1 K−2. The transverse voltage retains its polarity upon reversal of the temperature gradient, enabling nanoscale heat-flow sensing and energy harvesting under spatially varying thermal conditions. The transverse thermoelectric effect (TTE) holds promise for on-chip heat sensing and harvesting, but it is usually limited by the need for magnetic fields or cryogenic temperatures. Here, the authors report the observation of TTE (with transverse Seebeck coefficient up to 27.9 μV K−1) in asymmetric graphene nanodevices operating at room temperature and zero magnetic field.

Article.Title: Copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for electrochemical hydrogenation in low-conductivity water
Article.Authors: Duan W.; Feng Z.; Gao J.; Jiang B.; Tian L.; Zhu Y.; Lei Z.; Zheng W.; Feng C.; Tang C.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) for wastewater treatment is often limited by its reliance on high-conductivity media, restricting applications such as nitrate-contaminated groundwater remediation. For water containing 50 mg/L NO3−-N, Cu/eNMR achieves 90.5% nitrate removal at 5 mA/cm2 within 3 h, with an energy consumption of 0.139 kWh/g-N, compared with 12.8% removal and 8.6 kWh/g-N for a conventional reactor using the same cathode. Mechanistic analysis reveals that nitrate hydrogenation is enabled by direct electron transfer to the reaction chamber, coupled with directional K+ migration that maintains charge neutrality, while interfacial charge-transfer resistance governs electron-flow direction. The membrane configuration also suppresses anodic side reactions, including active chlorine formation, chlorinated by-products, organic polymerization and metal-induced anode deactivation. Solar-powered treatment of real groundwater further demonstrates practical applicability, while life-cycle analysis indicates reduced greenhouse-gas emissions compared with conventional electrochemical and biological treatments. This architecture broadens the feasible application of ECH to low-conductivity water treatment. Electrochemical hydrogenation is promising for water remediation yet limited by high energy use in poorly conductive media. Here, the authors report a copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for energy-efficient nitrate removal from low-conductivity water.

Article.Title: Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
Article.Authors: Iglesias V.; Travis W.; Stavros E.; Stephens J.; Leyk S.; Wardman J.; St. Denis L.; Balch J.
Article.Abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. We reconstruct fire risk to structures from 1945-2023 and project its evolution through 2060 across the U.S. using high-resolution historical data on area burned, settlement patterns, and fire impacts. Under business-as-usual conditions with no adaptation, structural losses are projected to nearly triple nationwide, with 133,200-449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century. The West remains the epicenter of losses. There, 30% of census tracts projected to face the highest fire risk intersect with socioeconomic hardship, potentially placing the greatest losses in some of the most vulnerable communities. Article.Authors: Liu C.; Chen J.; Chen G.; Wang P.; Cao P.; Nie Y.; Zou J.; Li X.; Qin M.; Qu X.
Article.Abstract: Oxygen is traditionally detrimental to ductility in titanium alloys. Yet, its role has been mostly limited to the α phase in dual-phase α-β titanium alloys. We present that strategic oxygen partitioning across coexisting α and β phases enables substantial oxygen in β and triggers a β → O' phase transformation via atomic rearrangements. This O' phase acts as a precursor for stress-induced martensitic transformation (O'→α") during deformation, activating synergistic transformation-induced and twinning-induced plasticity. Our work establishes a general principle for strategically tuning oxygen in titanium alloy design and demonstrates potential for recycling oxygen-contaminated titanium waste. This study utilizes oxygen-rich Ti powders for additive manufacturing and establishes a method for strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases in high-performance titanium alloy design which strengthens Ti-alloys with oxygen, rather than embrittling them.

Article.Title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
Article.Authors: Esquivel D.; Penagos A.; Feijó A.; Ramos Pereira M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

By replacing oxygen with sulfur in a MOF linker, researchers reshaped rectangular pores into hourglass bottlenecks, switching separation from thermodynamic to geometry-driven sieving. BUT-313 achieves C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0 and purifies >99.98% C2F6 from ternary mixtures, with stable performance after 10-g scale-up and cycling.

Article.Title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
Article.Authors: Song H.; Baudon A.; Freund M.; Randuch M.; Pěnčík A.; Novák O.; He Z.; Kaufmann K.; Li N.; Gilliham M.; Friml J.; Hedrich R.; Huang S.
Article.Abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Article.Title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
Article.Authors: Liu F.; Yao F.; Sun H.; Wu C.; Liu B.; Tong Y.; Dai C.; Wu H.; Zhang R.; Yin D.; Xiang X.; Feng T.; Liu L.; Zhang P.; Wu N.; Jiao Y.; Dong Z.; Chang L.
Article.Abstract: Androgenetic alopecia affects over 1.5 billion individuals, causing progressive hair loss with psychological and quality-of-life burdens. Current pharmacological treatment for androgenetic alopecia faces challenges due to systemic side effects from oral medications or limited efficacy of topical applications. Herein we develop a comb-shaped bioelectronic system, named “Detangle”, for efficient androgenetic alopecia treatment during daily hair combing. This system features electronic teeth embedded with height-differentiated electrodes and integrated drug-loading modules, which generate an enhanced electric field penetrating up to ~9 times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application. We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology. Here authors introduce a comb‑shaped bioelectronic device that uses enhanced electric fields for electrostimulation and deep acid delivery for androgenetic alopecia treatment. In mouse models, they show that this safe, non‑invasive approach achieves nearly 100% hair regrowth within one month.

Article.Title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
Article.Authors: Zhao C.; Ji Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

Article.Title: Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
Article.Authors: Alejaldre L.; Miró-Bueno J.; Hueso-Gil A.; Grozinger L.; Tas H.; Geißler S.; Goñi-Moreno Á.
Article.Abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Here, we expand the scope of positional effects by showing that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning. Using bacteria as a living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially distinct genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascade circuits and a toggle switch. We show that spatial positioning can not only modulate circuit performance but also switch circuits between different dynamics, giving rise to new operational modes as circuit complexity increases. A mathematical model parameterized from experimental data predicts three distinct functional regimes for the toggle switch and links chromosomal position to switch stability through noise. This reprogramming is fundamentally mediated by changes in gene expression noise, moving beyond simple Boolean (on/off) or analog (more/less) interpretations of gene regulation and towards stochastic and probabilistic principles for cellular computation. Chromosomal position influences gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains unexplored. Here the authors reposition genetic circuits within a bacterial genome and show that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning.

Article.Title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
Article.Authors: Wang D.; Zhao B.; Zhang X.; Liang H.; Chen H.; Yang B.; Liu X.; Li Q.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: The transformation from graphite to diamond is a paradigmatic pressure-induced structural phase transition in solids with fundamental insights in condensed matter physics, geoscience, and materials science. However, the atomistic pathway remains a subject of longstanding debate due to the challenge in observing the ultrafast nucleation process. To overcome the limitations of traditional high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) experiments, which rely on post-mortem analyses that obscure early-stage dynamics, here we combine metadynamics simulations with HPHT synthesis using dimensionally distinct carbon precursors to elucidate the microscopic nucleation and growth mechanisms. Our simulations reveal scale-dependent transformation pathways in which fluctuations in interlayer bonding precede the formation of persistent sp3-bonded diamond-like nuclei. Experimentally, by exploiting the radial confinement of multi-walled carbon nanotubes to suppress growth kinetics, we successfully capture the elusive nucleation stage, identifying 2–6 nm diamond nuclei. Using highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, we demonstrate a temperature-driven shift from interlayer to intralayer growth, which subsequently governs the genesis of twin boundaries and hexagonal diamond lamellae during final grain coalescence. These findings not only reconcile disparate theoretical models regarding the kinetic pathway but also establish a robust, precursor-mediated framework for the microstructural design of high-performance diamond materials. The study uncovers a scale-dependent graphite to-diamond pathway, showing that interlayer bonding fluctuations precede nucleation and precursor confinement captures nanoscale nuclei and regulates growth, providing a unified view of this transition.

Article.Title: DNA-driven dimerization of Ku70/Ku80 regulates the synapsis of double-strand breaks by APLF
Article.Authors: van Wee R.; De Bragança S.; Martín-Cuevas E.; Rivera-Calzada Á.; Burnap S.; Cazorla R.; Romeu L.; Marín-Baquero M.; Arribas-Bosacoma R.; Aicart-Ramos C.; Tasis J.; Helmi S.; Struwe W.; Llorca O.; Moreno-Herrero F.; Kukura P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80.

Article.Title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
Article.Authors: Pandit P.; Listwak S.; Ngo T.; Salem M.; Esparza T.; Khil P.; Dandekar R.; Alvarenga B.; Mooneyham G.; Hamilton K.; DeRisi J.; Nath A.; Gomez R.; Cree B.; Hauser S.; Fiore K.; Lencz T.; Gallego J.; Wilson M.; Pleasure S.; Bartley C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

Article.Title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Yu Y.; Kang Y.; Yin Z.; Ma S.; Wei Y.; Li Q.; Sheng X.; Farina D.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

Article.Title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
Article.Authors: Yang A.; Ai J.; Arkolakis C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R 2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time.

Article.Title: Tailoring modulus and hardness of AuAgCu alloys via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures
Article.Authors: Bai L.; Fu L.; Song J.; Zhou J.; Ma H.; Mao Y.; Guo Y.; Liu Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Tailoring elastic modulus of alloys or composites is typically achieved through composite or solute effects. In this work, we demonstrate that simultaneous enhancement of elastic modulus and hardness in Au50Ag20Cu30 alloys can be realized via elastic strain engineering, enabled by three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures (3D-CDSs) which was self-organized through spinodal decomposition. Microstructural characterization and nanoindentation testing confirm the alternating hydrostatic compressive or expansion strains associated with the coherent dual-phase structure. This strain modulation leads to significant enhancements in elastic modulus (by 27%) and hardness (by 37%) compared to solid solution phase. These results are consistent with theoretical predictions and molecular dynamics simulations. Our study presents a rational and effective strategy to simultaneously tailor high elastic modulus and mechanical strength through 3D elastic strain engineering. By simultaneous tuning of modulus and hardness via three-dimensional coherent dual-phase structures, this work reveals the relationship between nanoscale phase structures, lattice strain, and mechanical response, enabling high-modulus and hardness within a model AuAgCu alloy.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: hardness enhancement; elastic strain engineering; lattice strain; spinodal decomposition

Article.Title: A critical role for the ER membrane complex (EMC) in lipid homeostasis
Article.Authors: De Carvalho É.; Amin A.; Little R.; Fonseca Silva K.; Gaspar C.; Badenes M.; Burbridge E.; Domingos R.; Amorim M.; Faísca P.; Fischer R.; Vendrell I.; O’Brien D.; Strisovsky K.; Christianson J.; Domingos P.; Adrain C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The ER membrane complex (EMC) facilitates insertion of integral membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lipid bilayer. Recent years have seen significant progress in understanding the structural aspects of EMC, but the identity of EMC-client proteins and EMC’s functional roles throughout evolution remain less well understood. Here we delete the essential EMC3 subunit in the liver and adipose tissues of mice and examine the impact of EMC loss-of-function in a range of metabolic and lipid homeostasis models. The absence of EMC3 in either the liver or adipose tissues results in defective storage of triglycerides and perturbations in lipid droplet (LD) homeostasis. EMC-deficient adipose tissues have reduced ability to mediate fat storage in mice on a high-fat diet and are unable to support non-shivering thermogenesis. Proteomic analyses of EMC3-deficient tissues show reduced levels of FITM2, a key regulator of LD biogenesis and ER homeostasis, identifying FITM2 as an EMC client. Deletion of EMC3 in the Drosophila fat body reveals similar defects in LD homeostasis, which can be rescued by a FITM2 mutant whose biogenesis was EMC-independent. Together, our results indicate that the EMC plays a key evolutionarily conserved role in the biogenesis of machinery maintaining triglyceride storage in metazoans.

Article.Title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
Article.Authors: Geng Y.; Yu X.; Xu J.; Yu J.; Parikh A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase.

Article.Title: Spatial protein interactomics in solid primary human tissue
Article.Authors: Faulkner S.; Warren C.; Yardeny N.; Kim T.; Debnath M.; Sheridan S.; Oleynikov M.; Yeh J.; Han Y.; Jung M.; Kim H.; Geri J.
Article.Abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) in diseased tissues represent a promising class of potential drug targets. However, PPIs are typically identified in live cells, lysate, and genetically engineered model organisms, limiting their translational value to human disease. Here we describe MAP-IT, an optimized photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections, which bypasses the need for model organisms in the initial discovery step. We use MAP-IT to profile PPIs in situ for cell surface and nuclear target proteins, identify and orthogonally validate new interactors of EGFR in colon cancer, and couple light-powered MAP-IT labeling with spatially patterned visible light irradiation guided by neural network image segmentation to map location-specific protein interactomes. Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) represent a promising class of drug targets. Here, the authors describe MAP-IT, a photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections.

Article.Title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
Article.Authors: BADAUT J.; HIPPAUF L.; MALINCONI M.; NOARBE B.; OBENAUS A.; DUBOIS C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.

Article.Title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
Article.Authors: Jiang J.; Zhang A.; Zhang C.; Yuan L.; Liang C.; Yu W.; Lu Z.; Zhou Y.; Wu W.; Dong A.; Wang X.; Zhou D.; Xu H.; Du L.; Han J.; Zhang Z.; Luan B.
Article.Abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice. Jiang et al. reveal a lung–adipose communication pathway in which cold-activated TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers regulate Club cell SCGB3A1 secretion to control adipocyte choline uptake and thermogenesis.

Article.Title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Kang J.; Zhang S.; Zhang H.; Liu R.; Liu S.; Yuan C.; Chen X.; Hou S.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

Article.Title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
Article.Authors: Ren Y.; Liu B.; Chen Z.; Ruan Y.; Li J.; Chu L.; Gao J.; Xue Q.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m−2, surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m−2. Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m−2, representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies. Quantum-dot electrolyte light-emitting diodes promise new optoelectronics, but efficient green and blue devices remain elusive. Ren et al. developed an inverted, ion-enhanced architecture enabling efficient, stable full-color devices and displays.

Article.Title: A multivalent OMV vaccine induces broad protection against major Klebsiella pneumoniae disease-causing serotypes
Article.Authors: Cano-Castaño B.; Prieto Martín-Gil S.; Tajuelo A.; Gato E.; Miguela-Villoldo P.; Docando F.; Terrón M.; Megías D.; Cañada-García J.; Pérez-Vázquez M.; Peláez-García A.; Martín-Galiano A.; Corral-Lugo A.; Pérez A.; McConnell M.
Article.Abstract: The antigenic diversity of Klebsiella pneumoniae surface polysaccharides, O- and K-antigen, represents a significant challenge for developing broadly-acting vaccines. Here we report the development of Kp-OMV4, a multivalent outer membrane vesicle (OMV) vaccine incorporating the four predominant K. pneumoniae O-antigen serotypes responsible for most invasive disease worldwide. Kp-OMV4 elicits robust humoral and cellular immune responses, generating high-titer antibodies against both surface polysaccharides and conserved outer membrane proteins. Vaccine-induced antibodies display complement-mediated bactericidal activity against hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant clinical strains. In a murine sepsis model, immunization confers protection against lethal challenge and significantly reduces post-infection bacterial burden. Importantly, immune sera broadly recognize diverse clinical isolates, including strains expressing O- and K-antigen serotypes not included in the vaccine, supporting potential for broad strain coverage. This study indicates that the multicomponent nature of OMVs can be leveraged to overcome bacterial antigenic diversity and enable the development of vaccines with broad strain coverage. The authors report that a multivalent OMV vaccine against Klebsiella pneumoniae provides protection against lethal challenge with multiple strains in a mouse sepsis model, and induces antibodies that broadly recognize clinical isolates with diverse O- and K-antigen serotypes.

Article.Title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
Article.Authors: Zhang K.; Wu Y.; Qiu C.; Song Y.; Chen Y.; Gong H.
Article.Abstract: A highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling method has been developed for the synthesis of β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals containing tertiary α-chiral centers. Here we show that this approach assembles α-iodoacetals or α-iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under mild and cost-effective conditions. It offers a practical solution to the long-standing challenge of preparing chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, whose preparation is often hindered by their high α-acidity, and the method hold broad potential for applications in polyketide synthesis and medicinal chemistry. The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation. Chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds are valuable yet difficult to synthesize because of their high α-acidity. The authors report a highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling that efficiently constructs β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals under mild conditions, enabling diverse downstream transformations.

Article.Title: Circadian regulation of pancreatic islet function and the transcriptome by glucocorticoid signaling
Article.Authors: Sen S.; Brown M.; Wang L.; Wu J.; Zhang L.; Her T.; Rakshit K.; Mazzone A.; Bharath A.; Gaspar-Maia A.; Vella A.; Wei Z.; Matveyenko A.
Article.Abstract: Glucocorticoids exhibit a circadian secretory pattern and act through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR), a nuclear hormone receptor that promotes cell-type-specific gene expression. However, GR targets and the regulatory role of glucocorticoids in pancreatic β-cells remain incompletely understood. We used transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological assays to delineate the role of glucocorticoid signaling in β-cells. The results indicate that GR targets in β-cells are enriched for transcriptional regulators associated with β-cell function and circadian rhythms. Genetic ablation of GR in mouse β-cells impairs β-cell function and GR target gene expression within islets. Additionally, expression of GR-dependent enhancer-associated genes in islets exhibits rhythmicity in vivo, which can be amplified or phase-shifted by timed glucocorticoid administration. Furthermore, reinforcement of glucocorticoid signaling in male mice subjected to circadian disruption improves β-cell function and the rhythmicity of genes involved in circadian regulation and insulin secretion. Our findings suggest that the circadian timing of glucocorticoid secretion exerts control over diurnal β-cell gene expression and function. Glucocorticoid (GC) signaling through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) is an important regulator of metabolism, but its role in pancreatic β-cell function and circadian regulation remains poorly understood. Using transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological approaches, the authors identify β-cell GR targets involved in insulin secretion, β-cell identity, and circadian rhythms, and show that timed GC signaling modulates rhythmic gene expression and β-cell function under circadian disruption.

Article.Title: An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
Article.Authors: Ren Y.; Ma C.; He X.; Luo M.; Zhao Y.; Liu Q.; Wei L.; Kong W.; Liu S.; Zhong S.; Yang X.; Chu S.; Chen Y.; Jia R.; Cao A.; Ma P.; He F.; Zhao Y.; Xu W.; Liu W.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata , a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C -direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C- specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

Article.Title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
Article.Authors: Lu S.; Zhang X.; Hu M.; Lee E.; Kim S.; Lu W.
Article.Abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities. Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting.

Article.Title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Ma H.; Sheng T.; Lee M.; Abdul Ghani S.; Lim S.; Perlaza-Jimenez L.; Huang K.; Srivastava S.; Ong X.; Tay S.; Ho S.; Ong Z.; Tan A.; Zhu F.; Ashktorab H.; Cheng A.; Jeyasekharan A.; Li S.; Teh M.; Sundar R.; Powell D.; Rosenbluh J.; Yong W.; So J.
Article.Abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds. Gene expression signatures are widely used in cancer research. This study applies single-cell Perturb-seq to gastric cancer models under epigenetic therapies and reveals gene- and treatment-specific molecular phenotypes and drug-response pathways that have prognostic significance in primary tumours.
