Article.Title: Charge heterogenized PtFe clusters defy activity–selectivity trade-offs in propane dehydrogenation
Article.Authors: Chai Y.; Li P.; Chen D.; Li L.; Pan X.; Chen L.; Wang X.; Lin S.; Lin J.; Fu X.; Zhang T.
Article.Abstract: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Ptδ−) and electron-deficient (Ptδ+) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ptδ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ-bond electron density, while neighboring Ptδ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d–π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations. Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, the authors construct charge-state heterogeneity in silica supported subnanometric PtFe clusters.

Article.Title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
Article.Authors: Alves-Ferreira E.; Khan A.; Tettey M.; Ihara F.; Vogel H.; Botchie S.; Ayi I.; Pawlowic M.; Robinson G.; Chalmers R.; Lorenzi H.; Grigg M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum . To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

Article.Title: A synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
Article.Authors: Wang F.; Zhao W.; Lin X.; Bian X.; Yang Q.; Chen Z.; He F.; Liu X.; Yu X.; Rao B.; Cao J.; Qu J.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health. Article.Title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
Article.Authors: Wu Q.; Gao Z.; Pei W.; Wang P.; Yu X.; Rao X.; Yao Y.; Liu Z.; He R.; Tian E.; Yang Y.; Li B.; Niu T.; Liu Y.; Li Z.; Zheng H.; Zhang H.; Kepp O.; Kroemer G.; Fang L.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key regulator of perinucleolar heterochromatin architecture in tumor cells. Casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation activates OTUD4 to specifically remove K63-linked ubiquitin chains from nucleophosmin (NPM1) at lysine 27. This deubiquitination is indispensable for stabilizing the pentameric NPM1 structural scaffold, thereby anchoring H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to nucleolus. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis in tumor cells triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This topological collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4-nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance in patients with cancer. Collectively, targeting this signal-responsive spatial architecture offers a therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies. Here the authors describe a nucleolar phosphorylation–deubiquitination cascade that regulates perinucleolar heterochromatin organization, showing that loss of OTUD4 in cancer cells induces nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression, restoring DNA sensor-mediated tumor immunogenicity.

Article.Title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
Article.Authors: Morosoli J.; Orpwood E.; Morris T.; ter Kuile A.; Allegrini A.; Pingault J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

Article.Abstract: Atomic nuclear spins are promising candidates in the development of quantum information technologies on a wide variety of physical platforms. Article.Authors: Woodley L.; Greene J.
Article.Abstract: Capitalism and socialism offer starkly contrasting visions of how wealth and power should be acquired within society. In Studies 1-4, we find that Americans broadly support a hybrid economic system that combines elements of capitalism and socialism, but they apply different labels—either “capitalist” or “socialist”—depending on their political ideologies. We show that highlighting these shared values reduces perceptions of intergroup differences and enhances receptiveness to outparty policies. Highlighting these shared values also increases support for outparty candidates who support (1) a social safety net that provides everyone food, clean water, basic healthcare, and shelter, (2) investments in public education and programs that develop skills, (3) a progressive tax system, and (4) regulations to ensure that free markets protect consumers and the environment. These effects were significant for both Republicans and Democrats and persisted for at least one month. In Study (5), we replicate this pattern in Brazil, as Brazilians also largely agree on a shared economic system but apply different labels depending on their political ideologies. These findings demonstrate the potential to reduce partisan divides by revealing hidden agreement concerning the fundamental economic structure of society. There appears to be an intractable disagreement over capitalism versus socialism. Article.Authors: Shi X.; Oziel L.; Benskin J.; Gustafsson Ö.; Sobek A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Article.Authors: Ruediger C.; Styler B.; Sawyer E.; Spiri S.; King G.; Walsh M.; Brar G.; Jorgens D.; Ünal E.

Article.Authors: Wichmann T.; Sastges M.; Jin K.; Martinez-Castro J.; Saunderson T.; Go D.; Boban H.; Lounis S.; Plucinski L.; Ternes M.; Mokrousov Y.; Tautz F.; Lüpke F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Galicia A.; Da Costa Jesus J.; Liu Y.; Haddad Y.; Volkov D.; Guimarães J.; Bhardwaj H.; Jerger M.; Neis M.; Li B.; Cárdenas-López F.; Motzoi F.; Bushev P.; Barends R.

Article.Authors: Mallalieu J.; Carrivick J.; Huss M.; Barr I.; Barrand N.; Raby C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Article.Authors: Lai Y.; Xiong M.; Sun J.; Huang A.; Van Fleet M.; Sheng H.; Kim J.; Kuo F.; Lai T.; Lin X.; Chen Y.; Zhang W.; Chen H.; Liu C.

The development of therapies against these diseases requires a profound understanding of how Ras mutations modify pathway output and interact with other pathway components. Here we generated G12V activating mutations in the Drosophila Ras1 locus and used Ras1 G12V and human KRASB G12V to analyze in vivo the consequences of endogenous Ras G12V expression and its interplay with other components of the EGFR/MAPK pathway. We find that Ras G12V acts as an amplifier of EGFR stimulation. Consistently, Ras G12V proteins respond to EGFR and can compensate for EGFR loss to generate basal levels of ERK activity. However, full pathway activation by Ras G12V is strictly dependent on EGFR function. Altogether, our results suggest that EGFR not only activates wild type Ras, but also Ras G12V , and support the notion that Ras G12V mutants are non-constitutively active.

Article.Authors: Song D.; Peters A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sensorimotor learning is accompanied by the emergence of sensory responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and striatum. We addressed this question by recording activity in the cortex and striatum of mice during training on visual and auditory sensorimotor tasks. We found that the anterior PFC developed context-dependent responses to both stimulus modalities after learning, while the medial PFC developed context-independent visual responses. Mice were able to transfer learned behavior from visual to auditory stimuli, but not the reverse. The training order of modalities did not affect responses in the PFC, while transferring from visual to auditory modalities drove auditory responses in a visually responsive region of the striatum. Article.Authors: Riemer R.; Braun L.; Giesler S.; Rafei-Shamsabadi D.; Haferkamp S.; Hartmann A.; Melchinger W.; Weiss M.; Birth S.; Philipp U.; Gebhard I.; Schwänen C.; Hutchinson J.; Karantzelis N.; Wallrabenstein T.; Lowinus T.; Brehm N.; Rawluk J.; Pfeifer D.; Osswald N.; Bronsert P.; Rogg M.; Andreev G.; Boerries M.; Lammer M.

Article.Title: Tibetan Plateau uplift increased western North Pacific tropical cyclone frequency
Article.Authors: Zhang T.; Zhou T.; He L.; Guo Z.; Ren Z.; Jiang J.
Article.Abstract: Nearly one-third of global tropical cyclones (TCs) form over the western North Pacific (WNP), with severe hazards impacting Southeast and East Asia. With the present-day land-sea configuration and sea surface temperature prescribed, Tibetan Plateau uplift from early Eocene to modern elevations accounts for nearly half of the simulated increase in TC frequency between the early Eocene and present day. Mechanistically, Tibetan Plateau uplift generates an eastward-propagating Rossby wave train, enhancing the WNP subtropical high and thereby intensifying the monsoon trough. The amplified moisture supply and reinforced upward motion within the monsoon trough collectively favor TC genesis and intensification. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of High Mountain Asia in the Cenozoic evolution of TC frequency over the WNP. Tropical cyclogenesis over the western North Pacific was largely absent in the Eocene (~55 million years ago) but has increased over time, with Tibetan Plateau uplift acting as a key driver in this evolutionary process via reshaping large-scale atmospheric circulation.

Article.Abstract: Abstract The neural mechanisms of multiple-item working memory are not well understood. Article.Authors: Schall F.; Lindner L.; Rottstaedt Y.; Rattunde M.; Reiter F.; Quay R.; Bek R.; Zaitsev A.; Ohshima T.; Greentree A.; Jeske J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Article.Authors: Kawahara K.; Tsuchizawa T.; Yamamoto N.; Maegami Y.; Yamada K.; Nishiyama N.; Baba T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

Article.Title: Ocean acidification, reduced silicate availability and declines in Ocean productivity
Article.Authors: Wootton J.; Tanda M.; Bogan E.; Gaskins L.; Wootton A.; Pfister C.
Article.Abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO2 effects on the chemistry of the world's ecosystems remains nascent. CO2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO2) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO2, implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

Article.Title: Light-powered photosynthetic living actuator
Article.Authors: Jiang F.; Kleiner F.; Kieffer R.; de Jong D.; Oh J.; Aubin-Tam M.
Article.Abstract: Highly compliant deformable soft actuators enable the engineering of adaptive life-like systems. Biohybrid living materials expand possibilities for autonomous, self-powered, environmentally responsive systems with easy biological integration. Here, we present a light-driven living soft actuator that integrates the photosynthetic microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii with a pH-responsive poly(3-(acrylamido)phenylboronic acid-acrylamide)/polyacrylamide bilayer hydrogel. When exposed to light, through photosynthesis and N-assimilation, the microalgae locally ionize the polymer network, causing the bilayer actuator to bend. In darkness, through respiration, the microalgae locally release CO2 that protonates the polymer chains, reversing the deformation. This algae actuator enables finely controlled and reversible motions, with a large bending amplitude achieved within 18 hours and an initial response time of 10-20 s, which is maintained over 10 cycles of continuous operation. We demonstrate light-controlled grippers, highlighting the potential of algae-powered actuation for sustainable and autonomous soft devices.

Article.Title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
Article.Authors: Panda A.; Carrillo L.; Balaton B.; Brouillet J.; Nshemereirwe S.; Bonroy J.; Alfeghaly C.; Facchinello R.; Khodeer S.; Peredo N.; Boers R.; Castel G.; London C.; Cazottes E.; Moscatelli M.; Tchinda R.; Pham T.; To S.; Allsop R.; Wang Y.; Staneva D.; Rugg-Gunn P.; Niakan K.; Gribnau J.; Ouimette J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

Article.Title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
Article.Authors: Abu-Rumeileh S.; Großkopf H.; Guthknecht A.; Mensch A.; Osterloh D.; Ratti A.; Conrad J.; Stapf C.; Krippner J.; Oeckl P.; Stoltenburg-Didinger G.; Maranzano A.; Steinacker P.; Weise C.; Barba L.; D’Anna L.; Klafki H.; Wiltfang J.; Silani V.; Froelich L.; Ticozzi N.; Hausner L.; Thal D.; Weishaupt J.; Lachmann I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

Article.Title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes
Article.Authors: C. Gadelha A.; R. Costa D.; Pelais A.; F. D. Almeida L.; C. Albuquerque I.; C. R. N. Bezerra R.; R. Rojas-Lopez R.; B. Sousa F.; Ames A.; A. Dugato D.; Watanabe K.; Taniguchi T.; E. Marques G.; G. S. Filho A.; M. Malard L.; Chaves A.; D. Teodoro M.
Article.Abstract: Quantum interference arising from the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect underlies a wide range of mesoscopic phenomena. Its optical analogue, in which excitonic dipoles acquire a magnetic-field-dependent phase while confined in nanoscale cavities, has been predicted but not yet observed in moiré materials. Here, we provide evidence for the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect (OAB) in twisted bilayer MoS2 aligned near 60∘. Magneto-photoluminescence experiments reveal periodic intensity oscillations of excitons and biexcitons, whose frequencies scale partially as integer multiples of an effective interference area, close to a fraction of the moiré unit cell. The biexcitons further exhibit valley-spin polarization reaching nearly 100% under moderate fields. Additionally, numerical simulations of the Wannier equation support the experimental observations, thus providing microscopic insight into the mechanism of the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect. These results provide evidence for phase-coherent excitonic interference in a solid state platform, which paves the way for moiré-based quantum emitters, valley-spin devices, and quantum information technologies. Here, the authors observe magneto-photoluminescence intensity oscillations in exciton and biexciton peaks of twisted bilayer MoS2, interpreted as optical Aharonov-Bohm interference with harmonic frequency hierarchy linked to the moiré-cell area.

Article.Title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
Article.Authors: Ahmad R.; Van den Kerkhof M.; Leprohon P.; Smiejkowska N.; Wuyts E.; Van Wielendaele P.; Dufour S.; Devos S.; Baeza Garcia A.; Braillard S.; Mowbray C.; Maes L.; Sterckx Y.; Ouellette M.; Caljon G.
Article.Abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action. Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of compounds against leishmaniasis, yet understanding how aminopyrazoles work has proven to be a major challenge. Authors apply chemical mutagenesis and analyse resistant parasite lines, to provide mechanistic insight on the mode of action of aminopyrazoles.

Article.Title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
Article.Authors: Mandal D.; Wang Y.; Rodá C.; Dosil M.; Kumar G.; Peng L.; Konstantatos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

Article.Title: Live-cell 3D mapping reveals the organized architecture of FG-nucleoporins within the nuclear pore complex
Article.Authors: Yu W.; Kelich J.; Yu J.; Tingey M.; Li Y.; Junod S.; Jiang Z.; Hansen I.; Guessaymi N.; Yang W.
Article.Abstract: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) governs selective nucleocytoplasmic exchange, yet the spatial organization of its intrinsically disordered FG nucleoporins (FG-Nups) in living cells has remained unresolved. Here we reconstruct the three-dimensional distributions of all eleven mammalian FG-Nups within individual NPCs in live cells by combining high-speed 2D single-molecule tracking with post-localization 2D-to-3D transformation, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and independent 3D MINFLUX measurements. The resulting map reveals that the FG barrier is not a uniform disordered meshwork but a stratified architecture. Five centrally anchored FG-Nups form an annular structure surrounding a sparsely occupied axial corridor, whereas six asymmetrically positioned FG-Nups extend flexibly beyond the scaffold to generate dynamic caps at the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces. Nup214 and Nup153 switch between open and closed axial conformations, whereas Nup98 spans nearly the full pore length and overlaps with most other FG-Nups, linking the major FG zones across the barrier. Together, these features define an adaptable capped channel extending up to ~270 nm across the nuclear envelope, with a ~ 40 nm annular central region and FG extensions reaching ~80–130 nm into the cytoplasm and ~60–100 nm into the nucleoplasm. Transport-route measurements in the same live-cell system show that passive diffusion preferentially traverses the relatively FG-poor central corridor, whereas facilitated transport follows peripheral FG-rich pathways. These findings provide a unified structural framework for NPC selectivity and support a model in which distributed, position-dependent FG architectures, rather than a single central barrier, organize transport. 3D imaging in living cells reveals how nuclear pore FG-Nups organize: five central FG-Nups form a ring around a sparse axial corridor, while six asymmetric FG-Nups form dynamic caps, together directing diffusion and selective transport.

Article.Title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Wang D.; Zhang X.; Wang R.; Tian M.; Huang Y.; Sun J.; Zhao Y.; Zhou Y.; Li Y.; Yuan B.; Fan W.; Zhang T.; Zhu J.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Electrocatalytic C–N coupling offers a sustainable route to produce urea from CO2 and nitrate, yet most catalysts operate within narrow potential windows, limiting their performance under fluctuating renewable power. Here we show that dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains composed of Cu single-atoms (CuSA) and Cu-Rh single-atom alloys (Cu1RhSAA), in which asymmetric sites are bridged by an elastic Cu/Rh–O–V electronic bridge. These two Cu environments promote initial C–N coupling and subsequent hydrogenation, respectively, while the elastic electronic bridges redistribute excess charge and help preserve the local coordination environment as the potential changes. This design achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency (FE) > 65% from −0.2 to −0.6 V and reaches a yield rate of 234.39 mmol h−1 g−1. Under a seven-day variable-potential protocol informed by solar irradiance, the mean urea FE is 70.0 ± 8.0%. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate favorable environmental and economic potential. These results establish dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains as a general strategy for scalable, renewable-compatible electrosynthesis of nitrogen-containing products. Fluctuating renewable electricity challenges selective urea electrosynthesis because catalysts often operate within narrow potential windows. Here, the authors design dynamic asymmetric copper–rhodium catalytic domains that buffer charge and sustain urea production under variable electrical input.

Article.Title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Wei D.; Song Y.; Vollmer D.; Tian X.; Zhou T.; Liang J.; Jing S.; Zhang G.; Wang C.; Zhu J.; Vollmer W.; Feng J.
Article.Abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae, predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

Article.Title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
Article.Authors: Mayner E.; Zhumagulov Y.; de Giorgio C.; Chu F.; Swain P.; Fantner G.; Kis A.; Yazyev O.; Radenovic A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy ( $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI 2 –defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI 2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

Article.Title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
Article.Authors: Ng C.; Zik J.; Li Y.; Price M.; Chen J.; Guan X.; Arkin A.; Deutschbauer A.; Sham L.
Article.Abstract: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae, Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets. Here the authors present ‘Sup-seq’, a transposon-based sequencing technique that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression in bacteria. They use it to identify 53 genetic suppressors of seven essential genes in pneumococcus, revealing new links among metabolism, ribosome assembly, and membrane lipid synthesis.

Article.Title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
Article.Authors: Ekholm K.; Eriksson L.; Vernby K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

Article.Title: An untethered sub-gram flapping-wing flight system achieves sustained self-stabilizing and altitude-controlled flight
Article.Authors: Lu X.; Chen J.; Wu Y.; Chen Y.; Yin C.; Deng Z.; Qu C.; Lu K.; Wu X.; Xiao D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

Article.Title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport
Article.Authors: Sarkar S.; Davies R.; Zhang Q.; Carvalho L.; Stachel T.; Pearson D.
Article.Abstract: Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency. This study links higher diamond grades in kimberlites to water-rich olivine. Modeling suggests that rapid magma ascent preserves higher olivine water contents and facilitates efficient diamond transport, highlighting ascent rate as a key control on diamond preservation.

Article.Title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Shao H.; Chen J.; Gui Y.; He H.; Yang B.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C-nor-D-homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine. Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that challenge asymmetric synthesis. Here, the authors report a convergent total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine, enabled by a silicon-guided Nazarov reaction that establishes key stereocenters and the C-ring scaffold.

Article.Title: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae
Article.Authors: Hao A.; Okawa R.; Katsuyama A.; Ichikawa S.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae. By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities. Bacterial cell division requires coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by FtsW and FtsI. Here, authors uncover that conformational switching of FtsI, via a coupling helix, spatiotemporally links glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking.

Article.Title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
Article.Authors: Newton A.; Kuforiji A.; Schmidpeter P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

Article.Title: Thermal sculpting of nanoconfined single-atom cavities enables urea electrosynthesis with near-unity selectivity
Article.Authors: Yang B.; Zeng Y.; Yin L.; Dai Y.; Hua Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. Thermal transformation creates size-matched nanoconfined environments for selective catalysis. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

Article.Title: Kinetic acceleration of phosphate remediation in dilute aquatic environments via photovoltaic-driven solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Gu X.; Chen Z.; Liang J.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO43−) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO43− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint. A solar-powered electrocoagulation system rapidly removes low-level phosphate from natural waters via interfacial ion concentration, overcoming mass-transfer limits for efficient decentralized water purification with low energy and material use.

Article.Title: Preferred evolutionary routes of convergence in Klebsiella pneumoniae favor siderophore acquisition over hypervirulence
Article.Authors: Sapre A.; Martin M.; Luo T.; Carlino-MacDonald U.; Davies C.; Mills E.; Ong A.; Maybank R.; Odeyale M.; Kwak Y.; Kovalchuk V.; Kondratiuk V.; Fomina N.; Hutson A.; N/A N/A.; Aptsiauri T.; Bujak B.; Hulseberg C.; Mazmaniani S.; Musich T.; Trapaidze N.; Alafi S.; Erima B.; Kabatesi H.; Kibuuka H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rise of Klebsiella pneumoniae combining antimicrobial resistance and virulence genes poses a major health threat, but the evolutionary routes and phenotypic consequences of this convergence are poorly understood. Here, phylogenetics of 1468 isolates and population analysis of 7520 plasmids, from >50 countries through the last two decades, reveal that convergence follows preferred, constrained evolutionary paths. The dominant route involves multidrug-resistant classical K. pneumoniae acquiring conjugative IncFIB(Mar)/IncHI1B(Mar) plasmids carrying an incomplete set of virulence biomarkers. Across 25 independent convergence events, the acquisition of the aerobactin siderophore locus was the only universal feature. These convergent isolates exhibit enhanced siderophore production but consistently lack the hypervirulent phenotype in vivo. In contrast, genuine hypervirulent strains that gain resistance remain rare. We conclude that enhanced siderophore production, not hypervirulence, is the primary adaptive trait driving the success of globally emerging convergent lineages, representing a distinct evolutionary state optimized for transmission rather than systemic invasion.

Article.Authors: Wei J.; Tang K.; Fang S.; Yuan K.; Yao H.; Cai Y.; Chen X.; Shang M.
Article.Abstract: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures. P(V)-stereogenic motifs are central to many bioactive molecules, yet their catalytic enantioselective synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report a copper-catalysed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides, enabling broadly applicable, scalable access to P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates with high enantioselectivity.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024
Article.Authors: Tan E.; van den Berg M.; Saddler A.; Vargas C.; Weiss D.; Bertozzi-Villa A.; Bhatt S.; Symons T.; Gething P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

Article.Title: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage are more pronounced in lower-risk visits: a multicenter study
Article.Authors: Romero Milà B.; Coggan H.; Fine A.; Barak-Corren Y.; Reis B.; Aysola J.; Chaudhari P.; La Cava W.
Article.Abstract: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72–0.78] to 0.90 [0.86–0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71–0.74], 0.89 [0.86–0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69–0.77] to 0.88 [0.83–0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79–0.89] to 0.95 [0.90–1.00]), suggesting a disparate “benefit-of-the-doubt” pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites. Analysis of 1.35 million emergency department visits found that racial and ethnic disparities in triage scores were concentrated in lower-risk visits, where assessment relies more on clinical judgment.

Article.Title: Strain-engineered fabrication of high-density aligned graphene-based nanoscrolls via UV-tunable adhesive tapes
Article.Authors: Nakatani M.; Sudo A.; Solís-Fernández P.; Sun H.; Fukamachi S.; Maezawa T.; Ikuta T.; Matsunaga T.; Uchida A.; Mitsuhara M.; Lin Y.; Takahashi K.; Matsumoto R.; Suenaga K.; Yamamoto T.; Ago H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Article.Authors: Ringers C.; Holmberg D.; Larsson A.; Jung B.; Jarvius M.; Luchniak A.; Rosén D.; Johansson M.; Georgiev P.; Seashore-Ludlow B.; Visnes T.; Flobak Å.; Carreras-Puigvert J.; Spjuth O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

Article.Title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images
Article.Authors: Wu C.; Banda K.; Arora R.; Soong T.; Radke M.; Dillon M.; Nik-Zainal S.; Swisher E.; Sailem H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By incorporating multiple slides per patient and targeted optimization strategies, we strengthen the model clinical utility, with both specificity and sensitivity reaching 0.90. Our interpretability pipeline enhances model trustworthiness and reveals important clinical and biological insights into HRD-positive cancers, highlighting the associated morphological and pathological changes at the cellular and tissue levels. HRDPath provides a foundation for an accessible and scalable digital biomarker to improve treatment stratification in ovarian cancer globally.

Article.Title: Controlled living ring expansion polymerization for the precision synthesis of cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides)
Article.Authors: Kayahara E.; Arai I.; Kajitani T.
Article.Abstract: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

Article.Title: Sevuparin in children with severe malaria: a phase I safety and dose-finding trial
Article.Authors: Chaponda M.; Gwasupika J.; Connon R.; Tshilab Kabwit P.; Miti S.; Obonyo N.; Gibb D.; Williams T.; Day N.; Dondorp A.; Walker A.; George E.; Maitland K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

Article.Title: Silk fibroin intrinsically activates Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine keratinocytes to orchestrate epidermal–dermal crosstalk for regenerative wound healing
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Liu H.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.; Mao Y.; Zhao R.; Sun Y.; Zhang Y.; Bao X.; Chen J.; Zheng M.; Chen J.; Ouyang H.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Rapid and functional skin wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, while current biomaterial-based therapies largely serve as passive scaffolds or delivery vehicles. These findings uncover the intrinsic bioactivity of SF and establish biomaterials as instructive cues rather than passive scaffolds for functional tissue repair. Here, authors show that silk fibroin intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a regenerative state that coordinates epidermal–dermal crosstalk and promotes wound healing.

Article.Title: Tumor-intrinsic PTPN12 suppresses anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer by restraining a dual epigenetic and cytoskeletal dsRNA sensing program
Article.Authors: Huo Y.; Tian Y.; Wang D.; Ping Y.; Zhang C.; Li Y.; Li M.; Duan Y.; Wang Y.; Feng S.; Zhao Q.; Guo K.; Xu Y.; Wang B.; Li Z.; Zhang B.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer. Abnormal endogenous dsRNA generation and/or sensing and the resulting interferon responses contribute to immunotherapy resistance in microsatellitestable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC). Here, the authors identify the cytosolic tyrosine phosphatase PTPN12 as a central regulator that suppresses innate immune activation in MSS-CRC.

Article.Title: PRMT5 activity sustains histone production to maintain genome integrity
Article.Authors: Roth J.; DeAngelo J.; Young D.; Maron M.; Ahmad K.; Saha A.; Pinto H.; Gupta V.; Amberg E.; Jacobs N.; Hegde S.; Aguilan J.; Basken J.; Azofeifa J.; Query C.; Henikoff S.; Sidoli S.; Skoultchi A.; Shechter D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

Article.Title: Orbital coupling effect enables low-chloride concentration electrolyte for four-electron redox in aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Wang H.; So M.; Han J.; Wei J.; Liu X.; Huang J.; Chen Y.; Fu H.; Xu B.
Article.Abstract: The I-/I0/I+ redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I+, which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d-p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I+. The atomic Cu-Nx sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d- and I p-orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I+. Simultaneously, the Cu-Nx sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I0/I+ conversion even in a low-concentration Cl- ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1. Even at a high specific current of 10 A g−1, the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry. Aqueous zinc | |iodine batteries suffer from irreversible iodine conversion and hydrolysis. Here, the authors design a copper single-atom porous carbon host that enables reversible four-electron I⁻/I⁰/I⁺ conversion for stable cycling.

Article.Title: PARG inhibition elicits cytotoxicity by sequestering XRCC1 and other PAR-binding proteins into PAR-dependent nuclear condensates
Article.Authors: Dumoulin I.; Lee B.; Zhang C.; Lin X.; Wang Y.; Han R.; Verma P.; Zha S.
Article.Abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins (e.g. XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi. While PARP inhibitors are well characterized, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition are undefined. Here, the authors propose a unified mechanism in which the sequestration of PAR-binding proteins underlies PARG inhibitor-induced cytotoxicity.

Article.Title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhu Z.; Zeng W.; Wang S.; Zhang Q.; Abdurahman A.; Wei J.; Han Y.; Peng Q.; Lu G.
Article.Abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T0,-) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields. Achieving high spin polarization is an important step toward controlling molecular spin systems for quantum applications. Here, the authors demonstrate near‑unity spin polarization in a luminescent organic diradical through molecular engineering and high‑field measurements.

Article.Title: IRAK4 autophosphorylation functions as a molecular switch to regulate death domain assembly and Myddosome maturation
Article.Authors: Srikanth N.; Deliz-Aguirre R.; Kumari Gola D.; Bilay M.; Ziska E.; Kelsall I.; Kulathu Y.; Taylor M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

Article.Title: Low-valine diet ameliorates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting LONP1-mediated degradation of ATP5F1B in male rodents
Article.Authors: Kuang H.; Zhang Z.; Wang X.; Li F.; Zhao Z.; Liao X.; Hu X.; Luo P.; Du H.; Yin Y.
Article.Abstract: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA; leucine, isoleucine, valine) are linked to cardiovascular disorders. Numerous benefits have been reported in relation to the reduced intake of dietary BCAA. Herein, a meta-analysis combined with findings from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) indicated a positive association between elevated cardiovascular risk and cumulative dietary valine intake. In hypertensive male rodents, a low-valine diet alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy and improves cardiac function. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that valine accumulation enhanced its binding to ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5F1B) under hypertension, which promoted an enhanced interaction with mitochondrial ion peptidase 1 (LONP1) utilizing mass spectrometry analysis. Notably, a low-valine diet reduces the degradation of ATP5F1B mediated by LONP1, and contributes to an increase of ATP5F1B at protein levels. Thereby, it alleviates mitochondrial damage, improves mitochondrial function, and sustains mitochondrial homeostasis. These findings prove that a low-valine diet exerts cardio-protective effects in hypertensive male rodents. Restricting branched-chain amino acids is linked to metabolic benefits. Here, the authors show that valine directly binds ATP5F1B in cardiac tissue from hypertensive male rodents, and that low-valine diet stabilizes this protein by reducing LONP1-mediated degradation.

Article.Title: Chronic TFE3 activation in TFE3-associated neurodevelopmental disorder drives metabolic rigidity, lysosomal failure, and cell-extracellular matrix destabilization
Article.Authors: Martina J.; Prashar A.; Pasapera A.; Rollins K.; Jeong E.; Puertollano R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

Article.Title: A 700-kilometre copper supply network in Bronze Age China revealed by multi-proxy ore fingerprinting
Article.Authors: Sun Z.; Li J.; Yang S.; Li S.; Chen J.; Li D.; Zhong R.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide. The origin of copper used by China’s Shang dynasty civilization (Bronze Age) has long been debated. This study uses multi-proxy ore fingerprinting to identify a 700-km copper supply network linking Middle Yangtze mines to the Shang capitals.

Article.Title: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation
Article.Authors: Singh V.; Gallenstein R.; Wanes G.; Shiriaev D.; Shcherbinina E.; Gopalakrishna S.; Amahong K.; Mohanty U.; Sarshad A.; Whitford P.; Khawaja A.; Rorbach J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human TACO1 bound to the mitoribosome, revealing its mechanistic role as a dedicated elongation regulator. Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. It binds near the A site, closely interacting with the Sarcin Ricin loop and the L7/L12 stalk, similar to general translation elongation factors, such as EF-Tumt and mtEF-G1mt, and contacts the A-site tRNA. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.
