Article.Title: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions
Article.Authors: Garrels C.; Myers J.; Souza S.; Jarodsky J.; Reichow S.
Article.Abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel–channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations. The interfaces lack extensive protein–protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function. Gap junction channels assemble into plaques that coordinate communication across tissues. Here, authors show how neighboring Cx46/50 channels pack within membranes and identify ordered lipids as major components of their interfaces

Article.Title: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
Article.Authors: Yu C.; Zhang J.; Liu Y.; Jia Y.
Article.Abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems. Here, the authors develop a tensor-based framework for jointly optimizing communication topology and role assignment in multi-agent systems. They establish theoretical guarantees for the proposed optimization and demonstrate improved scalability and performance over combinatorial approaches.

Article.Title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
Article.Authors: Tateishi M.; Otsuka Y.; Matsuoka R.; Asayama K.; Zenkoh J.; Nakagawa T.; Murata Y.; Kobayashi N.; Sato Y.; Hizawa N.; Tsubochi H.; Endo S.; Hagiwara K.; Niki T.; Fukushima N.; Inamura K.; Kanai A.; Suzuki Y.; Matsubara D.; Suzuki A.
Article.Abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC. Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is an aggressive lung cancer whose biological diversity remains poorly understood. Here, the authors combine genomic, epigenomic and spatial transcriptomic analyses to show that LCNEC cells can shift between neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine states, identifying intermediate cell states and immune microenvironment features that may influence prognosis and treatment responses.

Article.Title: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Hui J.; Dal Grande F.; Li Q.; Chen P.; Wang C.; Taylor J.; Wei X.; Gao C.
Article.Abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. This dataset enables us to test two hypotheses: (H1) HGT-acquired genes exhibit partner-specific functional profiles consistent with functional differentiation between the major symbiotic partners, and (H2) inter‑symbiont HGT has occurred across the fungal–algal interface. Consistent with H1, putative HGT‑acquired genes in mycobionts show greater representation of functions related to cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, transcription, and defense mechanisms, whereas putative HGT‑acquired genes in photobionts show greater representation of functions related to amino acid transport and metabolism, signal transduction, and translation. Consistent with H2, we detect 31 putative inter‑symbiont HGT-acquired genes (16 inferred from mycobionts to photobionts and 15 inferred from photobionts to mycobionts), including multiple photobiont genes inferred to encode RfeF transcription factors with putative mycobiont origin, suggesting a potential contribution of HGT to regulatory evolution. These findings are consistent with a potential role of HGT in functional specialization and potential gene flow across fungal–algal boundaries, offering insights into the eco‑evolutionary dynamics of symbiotic systems. Horizontal gene transfer may shape how lichen symbionts adapt, but its role remains unclear. Across 197 lichen MAGs, this study identified 1,882 putative horizontally transferred genes and 31 potential transfers between fungal and algal symbionts, with distinct functional patterns.

Article.Title: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage
Article.Authors: Kang T.; Zhou Z.; Mohammed S.; Makris Y.; Bleris L.
Article.Abstract: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems. DNA is a dense and durable storage medium for digital information but its use in living cells remains difficult to scale and protect. Article.Title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation
Article.Authors: Ansorge R.; Romano S.; Frioux C.; Korcsmáros T.; Yoou M.; Juge N.; Sidorczuk K.; Hildebrand F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

Article.Authors: Lomeli E.; Kundu S.; Siewierska K.; Kusch M.; Böhm T.; Sahel-Schackis S.; Chuang Y.; Zhuo Z.; Chen K.; Xi X.; Shen L.; Dakovski G.; Geprägs S.; Moritz B.; Devereaux T.; Kling M.; Vinson J.; Huang E.; Jost D.

Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Article.Title: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
Article.Authors: Lingg R.; Johnson S.; Hinz D.; Mohamed A.; Skog T.; Lizarazu M.; Romig-Martin S.; LaLumiere R.; Narayanan N.; Radley J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Article.Title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
Article.Authors: Korolev V.; Lettau T.; Krishna V.; Croy A.; Thümmler M.; Zürch M.; Spielmann C.; Wächtler M.; Peschel U.; Gräfe S.; Soavi G.; Kartashov D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale. Article.Title: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
Article.Authors: Gao L.; Yuan Z.; Huang T.; Li P.; Zhong Y.; Gao J.; Luo Y.; Li B.; Pan H.; Ye K.; Guan M.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysregulation under nutrient stress disrupts bone homeostasis. Maladaptive ACSS1 accumulation enforces excessive acetyl-CoA production from either exogenous or glucose/ethanol-derived endogenous acetate, promoting mitochondrial protein hyperacetylation specifically inactivating ME2 via lysine 94 acetylation. This ACSS1-triggered ME2 inactivation disturbs the malate-aspartate shuttle, leading to a self-perpetuating cycle of redox imbalance and oxidative stress that exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic impairment. Importantly, genetic deletion of Acss1 or AAV-delivered non-acetylatable ME2 mutant in osteoprogenitor cells restores mitochondrial resilience, osteogenic capacity, and bone formation, protecting against osteoporosis or osteonecrosis in male mouse models of type 2 diabetes and chronic alcohol consumption. These results unveil an essential role for ACSS1 in controlling metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis, identifying ACSS1 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic stress-related bone disorders. Targeting ACSS1 preserves bone integrity in diabetic and alcoholic mice by sustaining bone formation.

Article.Authors: Kida N.; Togashi T.; Tono K.; Ikemoto Y.; Sawada K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. Article.Authors: Haque S.; Cross M.; Rajpurohit S.; Haber J.; Ciccarino C.; Zimmerman A.; Sealey I.; Kulichenko V.; Tie M.; Wang H.; Philip S.; Seo C.; Koralek J.; Balicas L.; Ozerov M.; Smirnov D.; Tan L.; da Jornada F.; Ogitsu T.; Hoffmann M.; Heinz T.; Lindenberg A.

Article.Authors: Jiang F.; Chen S.; Dayimu A.; Gopinath B.; Dong Q.; Jayakody D.; Wang S.; Jia Y.; Ssemata A.; Opondo C.; Louw Q.; Shang S.; Yao Y.; Fu X.; Wang H.; Feng J.; Zhang H.; Xu L.
Article.Abstract: Over-the-counter hearing aids may improve access to hearing care, but the level of support older adults need remains uncertain. In this multicenter, three-arm, pragmatic randomized controlled trial at ten community health centers in three Chinese cities, 322 adults aged 50 years or older with untreated bilateral hearing loss were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to self-fitting (n = 108), primary care physician support (n = 107), or remote audiologist support (n = 107). Outcome assessors and statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was hearing aid benefit on the Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit at 3 months. Here we show that both supported models produce greater benefit than self-fitting, with adjusted mean differences of 12.20 (95% confidence interval 7.18 to 17.22) for remote support and 9.71 (4.74 to 14.67) for primary care physician support. Hearing-related quality of life, satisfaction, speech recognition and device use also favor supported care, and differences persist at 12 months. One participant in the self-fitting group died of stroke. No intervention-related serious adverse events occurred. At 12 months, incremental costs per quality-adjusted life-year gained are $167.16 for physician support and $361.17 for remote support. Structured support improves the effectiveness of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400086117. In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

Article.Title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
Article.Authors: Summers P.; Robel A.; Jackson R.; King M.; Amundson J.; Burton J.
Article.Abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise. This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

Article.Title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
Article.Authors: Yu D.; Wang N.; Hassani A.; Perri S.; Peng Y.; Chen S.; Peng J.; Shangguan Y.; Zhang C.; Dong J.; Zhang G.; Shi Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

Article.Title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
Article.Authors: Li S.; Zhao X.; Yang F.; Wang Y.; Zhao Y.; Tang H.; Yao X.; Zhang K.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Gasdermin pores formed by the processed N-terminal domain of gasdermin family members induce pyroptotic cell death and are involved in multiple diseases. Gasdermin B (GSDMB) is cleaved by granzyme-A (GZMA) from killer lymphocytes, triggering pyroptosis in targeted cancer cells to enhance antitumor immunity. Previous research has indicated that the substrate specificity of GZMA is determined by interactions outside the catalytic site, but the molecular mechanism by which the exosite of GZMA recognizes GSDMB is not well understood. Here we report the cryo-EM structure of human GSDMB in complex with GZMA, revealing the specific recognition of GSDMB-CTD by GZMA. Several association interfaces between GSDMB-CTD and the GZMA monomer or the GZMA dimeric interface were uncovered, in addition to the cleavage sequence bound to the GZMA active site. These contacts function as exosites and present GSDMB substrate to the adjacent GZMA for trans-cleavage. Our results suggest that GZMA specifically recognizes and cleaves GSDMB in a GZMA dimerization interface-dependent manner, implying that a similar mechanism may be applicable to other physiological substrates of granzymes. Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

Article.Title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
Article.Authors: Schuurmans J.; Claros M.; Savino E.; Lukas F.; Slattery A.; Noël T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

Article.Title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
Article.Authors: Kim T.; De Franco M.; Dosil M.; Oh J.; Bera R.; Martos Valverde M.; Kumar G.; Konstantatos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

Article.Title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
Article.Authors: Van Tricht L.; Huss M.; Zekollari H.; Aguayo R.; Beer J.; van Tiel M.; von der Esch A.; Farinotti D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

Article.Title: Mosquito repellency mediated by skin commensal Bacillus species via volatile metabolite reprogramming
Article.Authors: Gu Z.; Gao H.; Guo H.; Fan Z.; Zhang W.; Xing D.; Zhou X.; Yu H.; Zhao T.; Wu J.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Individual variation in human attractiveness to mosquitoes critically influences vector-borne disease transmission, and this phenomenon arises from multiple underlying factors. This study integrated human skin microbiome profiling, non-human primate in situ intervention, and volatilomics to uncover a microbial-mediated mechanism underlying host-specific mosquito repellency. Bacillus species were identified as a microbial signature associated with reduced mosquito attraction in humans. Targeted Intervention of B. licheniformis and B. paralicheniformis on primate skin was sufficient to significantly reduce mosquito attraction, thereby establishing a causal microbial contribution beyond descriptive correlations. Mechanistic analyses revealed that Bacillus enrichment reprogrammed the skin volatilome, specifically increasing the abundance of aromatic and fatty acid-derived effectors, such as p-Cresol and decanoic acid, which are associated with repellency phenotypes. Together, these findings revealed a potential role of skin commensals in shaping mosquito host-seeking behavior, providing a molecular basis for microbiome-informed and bio-inspired strategies for mosquito disease control.

Article.Title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
Article.Authors: Bouchet P.; Brosse S.; Toussaint A.
Article.Abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies.

Article.Title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
Article.Authors: Heintz E.; Dantas W.; Taylor A.; Zunica E.; Belmont K.; Slone J.; Mey J.; Beyl R.; Vandanmagsar B.; Parry H.; Ajayi P.; Glancy B.; Axelrod C.; Kirwan J.
Article.Abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Du H.; Sun H.; Huang X.; Wang D.; Chen X.; Chen J.; Zhang X.; Zhou L.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

Article.Authors: Guo R.; Norford K.; Xu L.; Wei M.; Wang W.; Halene S.; Pyle A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. Here, we report small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly activate the RIG-I receptor protein. These agonists stimulate the first step in RIG-I signaling by triggering release of the signaling domains (CARDs) from an autorepressed form of the protein. This was achieved by developing a sensitive high-throughput screening (HTS) assay that directly monitors CARD expulsion through optical methods. The resulting screen hits were refined and optimized, leading to a specific RIG-I agonist that induces a robust interferon response. This study establishes a pharmacophore and assay for development of small molecules that precisely modulate RIG-I signaling.

Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; Huang Z.; Wang S.; Xu X.; Cheng Y.; Guo J.; He T.; Liu Y.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. Article.Authors: Ma J.; Wang T.; Zheng Y.; Ren T.; Zhu D.; Qiu Y.; Yang Y.; Jiang L.; Shen S.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4–68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation. Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

Article.Authors: Cheng J.; Zhai H.; Sun R.; Liu T.; Chen Q.; Yu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Article.Title: Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system
Article.Authors: Skolc L.; Chattopadhyay S.; Marijanović F.; Li Q.; Keeling J.; Lev B.; Demler E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Extending these ideas to solid-state electron systems could enable continuous-wave optical control of electronic order, but is impeded by the mismatch between optical wavelengths and electronic length scales. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

Article.Title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
Article.Authors: Kim W.; Chung M.; Asress S.; Trautwig A.; Dammer E.; Fournier C.; Seyfried N.; McEachin Z.; Glass J.; Thomas E.
Article.Abstract: Predictive biomarkers are increasingly used to guide clinical trial design, diagnosis, and management of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. Using large-scale plasma proteomics, Kim et al. identify proteins altered in ALS and develop a 10-protein model with high classification accuracy, supporting development of a blood-based tool to facilitate earlier ALS diagnosis.

Article.Title: Crystallization-mediated twisting of supramolecular nanoribbons from plant-derived triterpenes
Article.Authors: Niu X.; Wan Z.; Tao H.; Mao Y.; Lu X.; Ye Y.; Ko F.; Madden J.; Zhou C.; Rojas O.
Article.Abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). By interrupting classical nanolayer restacking and coupling interfacial dynamics with amphiphilic balance, surfactant- and salt-mediated antisolvent crystallization perturbs growth symmetry and biases directional molecular packing. The resulting twisted nanoribbons exhibit defined dimensions (width ~200 nm, thickness ~50 nm and ∼3.6 μm pitch) and aligned BT nanolayers with ~1.3 nm interlayer spacing. Polarization-resolved optical coherence tomography reveals depth-resolved mesoscale polarization anisotropy and links ribbon topology to effective refractive index and linear and circular birefringence. Molecular dynamics simulations support cooperative twisting driven by hydrophobic interactions and London dispersion forces. This crystallization-mediated strategy enables multiscale periodicity and tunable optical anisotropy, expanding opportunities for sustainable soft photonic and optoelectronic materials derived from biomolecules. Controlling the crystallization conditions allows to tailor the properties of crystals, but achieving directed supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging. Here the authors demonstrate direct supramolecular twisting and hierarchical organization in a triterpene system by directing the self-assembly of betulin into nanoribbons.

Article.Title: Towards scalable DNA data storage with DNA-SaM codec system
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Xu J.; Wang Y.; Nie Z.; Huang J.; Li M.; Wu Y.; Sun Y.; Chen S.; Mei H.; Qin Z.; Dai J.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: The exponential growth of global data volume is driving an urgent need for novel storage medium. Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA), nature’s genetic repository, presents a transformative solution with data storage density and lifespan orders of magnitude higher than conventional media. However, scaling DNA storage has been hindered by the complexity of codec algorithms, the generation of biochemically problematic sequences, and the absence of robust architecture for large-scale data. We present DNA-SaM, a system integrating highly efficient encoding, stringent biochemical constraint checks, and a storage unit distribution paradigm facilitated by a two-tiered indexing architecture. DNA-SaM demonstrates linear encoding time complexity and substantially reduced encoding time compared with representative approaches by in silico analysis. Critically, it proactively excludes sequences such as homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, and potential promoter motifs that could interfere with downstream biochemical processes, showing improved compatibility with in vitro and in vivo applications. It is further validated by practical data storage both in vitro and in vivo with a 100% success rate. On the basis of its encoding scheme and sequence design space, DNA-SaM could theoretically store data exceeding 270 petabytes (PB), marking an advancement in the scalability of DNA-based data storage. Scaling DNA storage is limited by complex codecs, biochemically problematic sequences, and insufficient architecture for large-scale data. Here, the authors present DNA-SaM, integrating efficient encoding, biochemical checks, and a storage unit distribution with a two-tiered indexing architecture.

Article.Title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
Article.Authors: Julian L.; Crozier L.; Lukow D.; Swamy A.; Mishra S.; Hagenson R.; Sennhenn P.; Sausville E.; McGeoch A.; Thompson S.; Mendelson B.; Chuaqui C.; Qiao L.; Vasudevan A.; Lin K.; Bhatia S.; Bertomeu T.; Chatr-aryamontri A.; Zhang L.; Rees M.; Ronan M.; Roth J.; Nottoli T.; Bai S.; Lakshmipathi J.
Article.Abstract: The cyclin-dependent kinase CDK11 is an understudied kinase that has been the subject of conflicting reports regarding its function in cancer. Here, we combine genetic and pharmacological approaches to demonstrate that CDK11 is a critical regulator of cancer cell survival that is required for RNA splicing and the expression of homologous recombination genes. Inhibition of CDK11 disrupts genome stability, promotes the retention of intronic sequences in mature mRNAs, and induces synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors. Through integrative analysis of functional genomics datasets, we identify heterozygous deletions of chromosome 1p36 - which encompasses CDK11 and its activating cyclin CCNL2 - as a recurrent and predictive biomarker of sensitivity to CDK11 inhibition. To assess the therapeutic potential of CDK11, we establish a genetically-engineered mouse model that allows us to differentiate between the on-target and off-target effects of CDK11 inhibitors in vivo. Using this platform, we demonstrate that MEL-495R, an orally bioavailable CDK11 inhibitor, induces widespread on-target toxicity, revealing a narrow therapeutic index. Experiments with a chemically distinct CDK11 inhibitor similarly reveal minimal anti-cancer activity at tolerable doses. Together, these findings define CDK11 as a core cancer dependency, uncover a chromosomal deletion that sensitizes tumors to CDK11 inhibition, demonstrate that on-target toxicity limits the efficacy of CDK11-targeting therapies, and provide a generalizable strategy for deconvolving drug efficacy and toxicity in vivo for novel oncology targets. CDK11 encodes a poorly-characterized cyclin-dependent kinase. Here, the authors demonstrate that CDK11 is essential for cancer proliferation, but the function(s) of CDK11 in normal tissue limits the efficacy of CDK11 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

Article.Title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
Article.Authors: Wan C.; Mu X.; He Z.; Liu H.; Pinson P.; Ju P.; Xu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

Article.Title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Voyer J.; Yu C.; Sajbel K.; Lu K.; Wang L.; Shi M.; Yang J.; Li J.; Xia S.; Fu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

Article.Title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
Article.Authors: Gregory C.; Elizondo U.; Guinaldo T.; Frölicher T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

Article.Title: Spatially resolved host and microbiota RNA profiling in the mouse gut using microDBiT
Article.Authors: Tao B.; Song D.; Dong M.; Li G.; Wang S.; Wang D.; Di X.; Gao F.; Lin L.; Yu X.; Xu J.; Liu M.; Zhang D.; Kelley M.; Feng A.; Jin Y.; Du J.; Kluger Y.; Palm N.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Hosts and their microbiomes coexist in a shared environment, engaging in dynamic interactions that are essential to maintaining health and modulating disease processes. Here, we present microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomic platform that enables simultaneous, high-resolution profiling of host and bacterial RNAs, including both mRNA and rRNA. We observed location-specific transcriptomic alterations in both host and bacterial cells in response to colonization and during inflammation. These results demonstrate the utility of microDBiT for dissecting host-microbiome interactions at high resolution and provide new insights into immune responses, spatial microbial localization, and microbiome-associated disease processes. This study introduces microDBiT, a spatial transcriptomics method that maps host and bacterial RNA together in gut tissue, revealing how microbes and host responses vary across intestinal regions and during inflammation.

Article.Title: Discovering network resilience formulas with symbolized reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Ding J.; Jin D.; Gao J.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Many complex networks display remarkable resilience under external perturbations, internal failures and environmental changes, yet they can swiftly deteriorate into dysfunction upon the removal of a few keystone nodes. Discovering formulas that measure network resilience offers the potential to prevent catastrophic collapses—from species extinctions to financial crises—with profound implications for real-world systems. Existing resilience metrics are typically designed to characterize topological properties, whereas in many real systems resilience is defined by the dynamics imposed on the network; consequently, metrics that explicitly incorporate dynamical state information are expected to be better suited for identifying keystone nodes in such settings. Here, we report an automatic method for resilience metric discovery, which learns from how machine learning model solves a complicated network dismantling problem and symbolizes its network attack strategies into mathematical formulas. This proposed self-inductive approach discovers a resilience formula that accounts for both topology and dynamics, highlighting how the correlation between node degree and state shapes overall network resilience. Additionally, our approach discovers formulas that refine existing well-established resilience metrics with over 37.5% improvement in accuracy, significantly advancing human understanding of complex networks with machine learning. Complex networks can fail when a small number of critical components are lost. Here, the authors use symbolized reinforcement learning to derive interpretable formulas that identify these components and quantify network resilience.

Article.Title: Alkali hydrides catalyze hydrogenolysis of polystyrene to alkylbenzenes under mild conditions
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Cai Y.; Tan K.; Liu B.; Zhang S.; Zhang S.; Guo J.; Pei Q.; Yu Y.; Wu A.; He T.; Chen P.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a highly efficient, transition-metal-free method for upcycling polystyrene (PS) waste using alkali metal hydrides, specifically KH, as a catalyst. Operating under mild conditions (130 °C, 1 bar H₂, 3 hours), KH achieves an impressive 93.2% yield of gaseous products and alkylbenzenes, with 95.8% selectivity toward alkylbenzenes. The production rate of 313.3 mmolcarbon/gKH/h is approximately 2.6 times higher than noble-metal catalysts operating at much higher temperatures (280 °C). This versatile approach is effective on diverse real-life PS waste. Mechanistically, depolymerization is driven by a synergy between direct hydride-induced Hδ+(C) abstraction and K+···π interactions with adjacent phenyl rings. This interaction elongates the C(sp³)–C(sp³) bonds, facilitating targeted cleavage into alkylbenzenes. Ultimately, this work establishes hydride catalysis as an energy-efficient platform for plastic depolymerization, providing crucial insights for designing mild-condition catalysts to address the global plastic waste crisis. Catalytic hydrogenolysis has been explored for polystyrene degradation, but its dependence on transition-metal catalysts and harsh conditions reduces its practicality. Here, the authors report the selective hydrogenolysis of polystyrene into alkylbenzenes under mild conditions (low temperature and hydrogen pressure) using alkali metal hydrides.

Article.Authors: Brault A.; Herry F.; Mazzilli S.; Cristancho-Fajardo L.; Froidefond M.; Epinoux M.; Berot M.; Soler M.; Lapostolle A.; Camaglia F.; Charniga K.; Cholin T.; Jean M.; Fouere T.; Ahmed A.; Niang M.; Paireau J.; Lessler J.; Azman A.; Bosetti P.; Balicchi J.; Cauchemez S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Article.Title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
Article.Authors: Ankur A.; Upadhya R.; Doosti M.; Ferreira D.; Miller S.; Xie L.; Hung I.; Lodge J.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. In C. neoformans , chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

Article.Authors: Ghosh G.; Bachmann J.; Nyenhuis M.; Krüger T.; Fernández Z.; Coelho J.; Albers A.; Köyer M.; Doltsinis N.; Fernández G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

Article.Abstract: Fatty acid (FA) availability for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis depends in part on lipolysis of lipid droplet (LD) triglycerides. BAT-specific AnkB deficiency caused excess lipid accumulation, enlarged LDs, and BAT whitening without altering mitochondrial oxidative capacity or thermogenesis in the fed state in male mice. Mechanistically, AnkB promoted basal lipolysis by recruiting hormone-sensitive lipase to LDs. However, AnkB loss compromised thermoregulation during cold exposure with fasting, linking AnkB-dependent FA release to thermogenesis under energetic stress. Unexpectedly, BAT AnkB deficiency protected male mice from high-fat diet-induced obesity (DIO), hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, and insulin resistance. This protection was associated with enhanced BAT mitochondrial oxidative capacity, oxidative remodeling of white adipose tissue, and increased circulating FGF21. Together, these findings establish AnkB as a previously unrecognized regulator of BAT lipid mobilization that coordinates thermogenic fuel availability with mitochondrial oxidative adaptation during metabolic stress. Article.Abstract: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify’s intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. Article.Title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
Article.Authors: Tang Q.; Chen H.; Chen Y.; Wu H.; Meng X.; Jin W.; Jiang P.; Zhang Y.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

Article.Abstract: HIV-1 uses the accessory protein Nef to enhance the infectivity of newly produced virus particles, but the host defenses counteracted by Nef remain incompletely defined. Article.Title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
Article.Authors: Zhang F.; Yu X.; Wu Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N-terminal fatty acid chains (C6–C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics. Authors present their chain-as-prompt deep learning framework, which identifies antimicrobial lipopeptides that show efficacy against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens in laboratory and animal model.

Article.Title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
Article.Authors: Moloney M.; Paterson R.; Yan B.; Eyres A.; Newell C.; Vorng J.; Pirkl A.; Watts J.; Gilmore I.; Trindade G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many biologically important molecules are structural isomers that share the same molecular mass yet differ in shape, bonding and function. This creates an ambiguity for mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), where chemically distinct species can be indistinguishable on the mass-to-charge ( m/z) scale and therefore cannot be reliably mapped in heterogeneous materials. Here we demonstrate that Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) can provide an orthogonal contrast that enables both identification and spatial separation of isomeric molecules directly on surfaces. By exploiting structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation and gas-phase collisional effects during ion transmission, we discriminate isomeric trisaccharides raffinose, maltotriose and melezitose and spatially resolve raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures. We benchmark these measurements against ion mobility spectrometry and observe consistent trends between OrbiSIMS transmission behaviour and ion mobility separation. These results establish OrbiSIMS as an approach for isomer-resolved MSI at surfaces and interfaces, opening opportunities to map isomeric biomolecules in complex systems where spatial distribution is central to function.

Article.Title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
Article.Authors: Xiong Y.; Lu L.; Wu Q.; Wang H.; Hu H.; Zhao H.; Santos H.; Shahbazi M.; Mi B.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds. Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

Article.Title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Kim T.; Kim J.; Oh J.; Kang S.; Kim S.; Kim J.; Han M.; Kim Y.; Pak C.; Park J.; Lim H.
Article.Abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.

Article.Title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
Article.Authors: Hu L.; Huang W.; Huang J.; Zhang J.; Qiu X.; Cheng B.; Pan L.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non-catalytic tri-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side-chains. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N-terminal domains, which can interact with family-defining ATP-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex. The remaining central multi-helix and C-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone-like function in RiPP biosynthesis. Graspetides are ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides. Here, TIGR04500 family proteins are shown to guide graspetide biosynthesis as non-catalytic chaperone-like partners through a likely widespread recognition mechanism.

Article.Title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
Article.Authors: Sepic S.; Gottemukkala K.; Du J.; Maiwald S.; Chrustowicz J.; Papadopoulou E.; Stier L.; von Gronau S.; Schulman B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLH MKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLH MKLN1 -dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

Article.Title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
Article.Authors: Jiang M.; Wang A.; Thissen J.; Nelson K.; Pipes L.; Kantor R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

Article.Title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
Article.Authors: Farago M.; Mucha B.; Samudra V.; Zhang S.; Pytel D.; Abbas A.; Phillips-Mason P.; Cavero D.; Shimonosono M.; Henick B.; Nakagawa H.; Wong K.; Rustgi A.; Koumenis C.; Ruggero D.; Fan Y.; Fuchs S.; Diehl J.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) occurs in cancer and is targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) including palbociclib (PD). CDK4/6i triggers quiescence (reversible) which transitions to senescence (irreversible) following prolonged exposure. Resolving the program that directs this transition is critical to overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We demonstrate that CDK4/6i predominantly triggers PERK, a shared kinase between the unfolded protein response (UPR) and integrated stress response (ISR). Inhibition of PERK combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR adaptive signaling instructing early commitment to senescence. Early senescence commitment reflects accelerated senescence markers, dephosphorylation of the Retinoblastoma (RB), and engagement of a senescence specific gene signature. Combined treatment with CDK4/6i and ISRIB (ISR inhibitor) reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents through increased senescence and immune cell surveillance. This work highlights CDK4/6i+ISRIB as a potential therapy for a range of cancers with an intact CDK4/6-RB1 axis. CDK4/6 inhibitors can trigger stress responses that alter tumor outcomes. Here, the authors show that PERK signaling shapes cell fate after CDK4/6 inhibition and influences response to therapy.

Article.Title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
Article.Authors: Kwon S.; Hoshi D.; Nagase T.; Sugiyama D.; Mukai H.; Takemura K.; Kojima R.; Zhou Y.; Watabe S.; Yoshihara F.; Tsai J.
Article.Abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform. Kerr parametric oscillators provide a route to protected bosonic quantum states through engineered energy gaps. Here, the authors realize a three-photon Kerr parametric oscillator and demonstrate coherent control of a bosonic qutrit, observing three photon Rabi oscillations, three-component cat states, and an energy gap that suppresses leakage from the qutrit manifold.

Article.Title: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Fei Z.; Huang W.; Liu M.; Tang J.; He Q.; Wang S.; Li F.; Zheng C.; Xie H.; Tao S.; Xu Z.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most adults worldwide and usually persists without symptoms, yet in some individuals it is associated with malignancies such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). How antibody responses to specific regions of EBV proteins differ between healthy individuals and patients with NPC remains incompletely understood. Here we show that epitope-resolved profiling of EBV antibodies reveals serological patterns associated with NPC development and clinical outcomes. We developed EBVScan, a quantitative phage-display platform covering 42 EBV isolates, to map IgA and IgG responses across the viral proteome. Multi-centre validation identified an antibody response to the TK139-194 region that distinguished NPC from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97. We also identified antibody-reactive regions enriched in healthy individuals that overlapped known viral receptor-interaction interfaces, and selected peptides from these regions reduced EBV infection in vitro. In patients with NPC, baseline antibody signatures were additionally associated with chemotherapy response and progression-free survival. Together, these findings provide an epitope-resolved view of EBV-host immune interactions and identify serological features with potential applications in NPC detection and patient stratification. Here, the authors map antibody responses to Epstein-Barr virus protein regions, identifying signatures associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma detection, chemotherapy response and progression-free survival.

Article.Title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Kim J.; Yang Y.; Song X.; Koo D.; Xu K.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.
