Article.Title: Trustworthiness in pain research is essential. Developing and implementing the ENTRUST-PE framework
Article.Authors: O'Connell N.; Belton J.; Cashin A.; Eccleston C.; Ferraro M.; Keefe F.; Knaggs R.; Norris E.; Pogatzki-Zahn E.; Palermo T.; Pickering G.; Rice A.; Segelcke D.; Sharma S.; Smart K.; Soliman N.; Toelle T.; Stewart G.; Vollert J.; Wainwright E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trustworthy pain research is essential for developing a deeper understanding of the phenomena, how it is experienced, its many impacts and how it might be reduced, prevented or managed to improve the lives of those who live with pain. Recognising multiple critical challenges that undermine trust in health research, an international, interdisciplinary network was convened to create an integrated framework for enhancing the trustworthiness of research in pain. The ENTRUST-PE framework was launched in 2024 with a call to action, proposing that trustworthiness in pain research is multidimensional and underpinned by 7 Core Values: Integrity and Governance; Equity, Diversity and Inclusivity; Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement; Methodological Rigour; Openness and Transparency; Balanced Communication and Data Authenticity. The framework includes specific recommendations for a range of interest holders and resources to support those recommendations. In this paper, we summarise the framework, reflect on the response to the framework from the pain research community, consider challenges and opportunities in the evolving research landscape and suggest how we might move towards deeper implementation to enhance the trustworthiness of pain research.

Article.Title: Exercise therapy for chronic pain: an updated perspective on mesocorticolimbic system function
Article.Authors: Senba E.; Minami K.; Habata S.; Kami T.; Kouda K.; Tajima F.; Kami K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patients with chronic pain often experience behavioral issues linked to pain, depression, and other emotional disorders. These problems stem from dysfunction in the mesocorticolimbic system, and exercise offers a safe, accessible, and effective alternative. It not only reduces pain but also activates multiple neural pathways, helping restore normal function. First, in the periphery, exercise promotes the release of myokines, which are essential for the body-brain connection and influence neural activity. IGF-1, released from muscles during exercise, can cross the blood-brain barrier and affect the brain. IGF-1 specifically targets orexin neurons in the hypothalamus, which then stimulate dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area, triggering the reward system. Second, exercise can reshape neural circuits and restore mesocorticolimbic function, reducing chronic pain and related issues. We showed that exercise activates neurons in the basal nucleus of the amygdala that project to the nucleus accumbens, supporting patients' goal-directed behavior. Moreover, inhibiting GABAergic neurons in the central nucleus of the amygdala decreases freezing behavior. Third, chronic pain often leads to depression, mainly due to reduced activity of serotonin (5-HT) neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus, which impairs the brain’s reward system. Exercise boosts activity of 5-HT neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus. Furthermore, exercise can modify gene expression through epigenetic mechanisms, leading to long-lasting improvements in brain function and behavior. Overall, exercise can restore brain function, helping individuals overcome chronic pain and lead healthier lives. These findings support exercise therapy as a key component of chronic pain management and suggest mesocorticolimbic mechanisms underlying its effects.

Article.Title: Under pressure: lessons from and beyond entrapment neuropathies
Article.Authors: Schmid A.; Chang P.; Camerone E.; Sierra-Silvestre E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Entrapment neuropathies are the most prevalent focal neuropathic pain conditions globally and impose a substantial individual and socioeconomic burden. Traditionally conceptualised as purely mechanical compression syndromes, this view is increasingly challenged by converging evidence from human tissue analyses, advanced neuroimaging, and deep clinical phenotyping. Entrapment neuropathies are now recognised as biologically dynamic disorders shaped to different extents by microvascular compromise, demyelination, axonal degeneration, immune dysregulation, neuroinflammation, central nervous system adaptations, and psychosocial influences. Varying combinations and dominance of biopsychosocial processes give rise to marked clinical heterogeneity even within the same diagnostic label. This mechanistic diversity helps explain common diagnostic discordances, including extraterritorial symptom spread, normal electrodiagnostic findings despite clinical symptoms indicative of entrapment neuropathies, and imaging–clinical presentation mismatch. It also challenges one-size-fits-all treatment approaches, which have largely failed in entrapment neuropathies. Uniquely, entrapment neuropathies provide a natural human model of focal nerve injury in the context of neuropathic pain. Surgical decompression allows integration of tissue-level biology with precise clinical phenotypes and offers time-locked insights into recovery. Lessons derived from this model extend beyond entrapment neuropathies and can inform broader understanding of neuropathic and nerve-related musculoskeletal pain conditions. Here, we synthesise contemporary mechanistic insights, examine how biological heterogeneity translates into distinct clinical phenotypes, and discuss potential implications for mechanism-informed management.

Article.Title: Brain sites involved in endogenous analgesia
Article.Authors: Henderson L.; Crawford L.; Kang J.; Keay K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pain modulation is a fundamental survival mechanism that prioritises, shapes, and suppresses nociceptive inputs to optimise behaviour. Although acute pain signals potential or actual tissue damage, sustained pain can impair essential behaviours, necessitating modulatory circuits that dynamically regulate nociception according to context and motivational state. These systems are deeply conserved, embedded within primitive spinal and brainstem structures, and capable of powerful modulation independent of cortical input, although higher regions such as the prefrontal cortex can influence their function. Decades of work have sought to identify these core modulatory circuits to advance basic understanding and develop strategies for clinically meaningful hypoalgesia. More recently, dysfunction within these circuits has been implicated in chronic pain, driving efforts to characterise how their organisation and function change during persistent pain states. Although most mechanistic insights come from animal studies, human neuroimaging, particularly since the advent of functional magnetic resonance imaging, has begun to map their location and engagement during pain modulation. Early work focused on forebrain regions due to the limited spatial resolution of standard MRI, but ultra-high-field functional magnetic resonance imaging now enables mm 3 -scale investigation of brainstem nuclei. This review synthesises evidence from animal and human studies to outline the best-characterised modulatory pathway, consisting of projections from the midbrain periaqueductal gray to the rostral ventromedial medulla and onward to the dorsal horn/spinal trigeminal nucleus, and highlights recent work detailing its organization.

Article.Title: Advances in research on combination therapy for the management of pain
Article.Authors: Gilron I.; Peterson C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pharmacotherapy remains an important component of multidisciplinary, multimodal pain treatment. Based on a well-established understanding of multiple concurrent mechanisms of nociceptive transmission and modulation, the demonstrated potential for synergistic interactions of drug combinations seen in preclinical studies supports the hypothesis of superior analgesia, and possibly also, fewer side-effects as compared with monotherapy. Likely related to this hypothesis and rationale, real-world evidence shows that approximately half of all patients with chronic pain, and even more with acute pain, concurrently receive 2 or more drugs from different mechanistic classes. To date, many dozens of randomized controlled trials have evaluated various analgesic combinations for the treatment of postoperative, neuropathic, back, arthritis, fibromyalgia, pelvic, and cancer-related pain conditions. Despite this growing area of research, most analgesic drug combinations are currently administered without rigorous evidence, thus exposing patients to the added cost or risk of some combinations that are not necessarily superior to monotherapy. As such, we propose future efforts to more efficiently exploit the potential benefits of combination therapy including: (1) expansion and coordination of translational collaborations to prioritize the most beneficial and clinically relevant combinations; (2) ensuring that preclinical combination studies evaluate multiple drug dosages and multiple relevant adverse effects; (3) ensuring that clinical trials include comparisons with each and every monotherapy component of the combination; (4) conducting further real-world studies of clinically beneficial combinations to ensure safety and efficacy in broader clinical settings; and (5) the application of these principles also to the evaluation of nonpharmacological treatment combinations.

Article.Title: Molecular histochemical analysis of neuroplasticity-related gene expression in pain pathway
Article.Authors: Noguchi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract I am deeply honored to receive the 2026 John Bonica Prize for distinguished lifetime achievement in the basic science of pain. Reflecting on 40 years of research, this review paper will summarize my key findings to date. For the past four decades, my research has focused on elucidating the molecular mechanisms of pain using animal models. By integrating morphological techniques with molecular biology, behavioral analysis, and electrophysiological recordings, I have sought to clarify how pain signals are modulated and sustained under chronic pain conditions. Since the early stages of my career, I have been particularly interested in the diverse molecular dynamics within pain pathways and their functional significance. This long-term research has been driven by the conviction that a detailed analysis of gene expression changes within pain pathways—particularly those associated with neuroplasticity—is essential to understanding the mechanisms underlying intractable pain. This review provides a comprehensive overview of our investigation into the molecular and cellular mechanisms of chronic pain, focusing on gene expression analyses related mainly to dorsal root ganglion and spinal cord plasticity, alongside historically significant contributions from the global pain research community. Finally, I will also discuss recent methodological advances and their applications, as well as the challenges and future directions facing basic pain research.

Article.Title: Prediction and prevention of pain after surgery
Article.Authors: Pogatzki-Zahn E.; Pradier B.; Segelcke D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative pain is common and has substantial clinical consequences for patients, their families, and society. Acute pain is not the only problem: a meaningful subset of patients develops chronic postsurgical pain, which is associated with considerable functional and psychosocial burden. Because established chronic postsurgical pain is difficult to treat, prevention is a key clinical objective, but it depends on the early identification of vulnerable patients and timely mechanism-informed interventions. This review examines mechanisms of postsurgical pain, as well as the prediction and prevention of unfavorable outcomes, from a translational perspective that integrates clinical evidence with mechanistic insights from preclinical models. After briefly summarizing recent developments, we outline current challenges and argue that progress requires alignment of outcome constructs across species, rigorous selection and reporting of experimental models, and identification of shared intermediate phenotypes linking mechanisms to patient trajectories. We then summarize the perioperative risk architecture underlying the transition from acute to chronic postsurgical pain, focusing on bio-psycho-social patient-related and surgical factors. Because current risk assessment tools do not yet provide sufficiently precise, reliable, and generalizable prediction, we discuss emerging evidence, including biological signatures that may refine prediction and risk stratification. We further argue that risk emerges dynamically through interactions across pre-, intra- and postsurgical phases. Building on this multi-stage, interactive framework, we propose a strategy integrating bio-psycho-social factors into clinically relevant prognostic models. Finally, we outline how this may not only help identify patients at risk, but also support mechanism-based, personalized prevention in vulnerable patients.

Article.Title: Chloride dysregulation: the next target for chronic pain therapeutics
Article.Authors: De Koninck Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic pain affects a substantial fraction of the population, yet pharmacological management remains deeply inadequate. This failure likely reflects the focus on developing analgesics suppressing normal nociceptive signalling rather than correcting the pathological substrates distinguishing chronic from acute pain. Here we review how the identification of injury-induced downregulation of the potassium-chloride cotransporter KCC2 in spinal dorsal horn neurons represents a landmark. It first provided a mechanistic, long-term substrate for spinal inhibitory failure. This form of disinhibition had the potential to explain several cardinal symptoms of neuropathic pain; not just hyperalgesia, through spinal hyperexcitability, and tactile allodynia, through cross-talk between sensory modalities, but also spontaneous pain, through enabling spontaneous bursts of activity in spinal nociceptive output to emerge. A second landmark is that chloride dysregulation as a substrate of disinhibition yields non-linear, non-intuitive predictions of neural circuit behaviours that shed light on several features of chronic pain and its therapeutic challenges. One is paradoxical pro-excitatory actions of tapping into normally endogenous inhibitory neurotransmission, potentially explaining failures of benzodiazepines analgesia and of conditional pain modulation. Others include degradation of sensory processing, possibly explaining diffuse pain, and leaky plasticity, predisposing to catastrophic sensitization. In turn, mechanisms regulating KCC2 itself emerge as substrates of chronification, as well as substrates of opioid-induced maladaptive paradoxical hyperalgesia. Finally, divergent yet convergent signaling cascades underlying KCC2-downregulation reveal a form of pathway degeneracy across sexes with lessons for therapeutics. All-in-all, these findings position KCC2 as a key novel target, not just for analgesia, but also for disease modification.

Article.Title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity
Article.Authors: Lampert A.; Tigerholm J.; Stiehl T.; Kurth I.; Haag N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neuropathic pain arises from dysfunction of the peripheral or central nervous system and affects up to 10% of the population worldwide. Aberrant activity in injured sensory nerve fibers, particularly spontaneous firing and altered conduction properties of nociceptors, is tightly linked to pain, yet its molecular underpinnings in humans have long remained elusive. Over recent years, major technological advances have transformed both functional and molecular analyses of sensory neurons. High-resolution single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have produced detailed atlases of sensory neuron diversity, while traditional electrophysiological approaches such as patch-clamp and microneurography have provided unparalleled insight into nerve fiber properties. Despite their individual strengths, molecular and functional classifications of sensory neurons have largely evolved in parallel. This review focuses on emerging strategies that bridge these approaches to achieve an integrated, mechanistic understanding of neuropathic pain. We discuss how microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks, such as activity-dependent slowing, recovery cycle signatures, and following frequency, can be transferred into in vitro patch-clamp paradigms, enabling direct functional comparison with dissociated human and large-animal sensory neurons. The incorporation of Patch-seq approaches has further enabled the assignment of molecular identity to functionally defined nociceptor subtypes, exemplified by the characterization of the mechano-insensitive “sleeping” nociceptors. Finally, we highlight how multimodal datasets combining electrophysiology, transcriptomics, and computational modeling provide new opportunities to unravel the ion channel mechanisms, particularly sodium channel subtypes, that shape pathological firing states. By directly linking human nerve fiber function to molecular programs, this integrative framework paves the way toward stratified, mechanism-based therapies for neuropathic pain.

Article.Title: Toward precision pediatric pain care: integrating mechanistic science, real-world measurement, and patient partnership
Article.Authors: Simons L.; Aghaeepour N.; Cashman C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pediatric pain science is at an inflection point. Advances in neuroscience, behavioral science, digital health technologies, and patient engagement are rapidly expanding how chronic pain in youth can be understood, measured, and treated. Yet despite these advances, many children and adolescents continue to experience persistent pain-related disability and limited access to effective care, reflecting a gap between scientific discovery and real-world clinical practice. In this perspective, we propose the BRIDGE framework (Biobehavioral Research Integrated with Digital Monitoring and Guided Engagement) as a model for advancing pediatric pain research and care. Mechanistic science is increasingly identifying neural, behavioral, and contextual processes that contribute to pain persistence and recovery, creating opportunities to target modifiable mechanisms underlying pain-related disability. At the same time, digital health technologies including wearable sensors and ecological momentary assessment enable continuous measurement of activity, physiology, and patient-reported experiences in daily life, offering new insights into the dynamic nature of pain and the potential to develop digital biomarkers of risk, recovery, and treatment response. Central to this framework is meaningful partnership with youth and families, ensuring that innovations in measurement and intervention remain aligned with patient priorities and lived experience. Integrating these domains can support precision behavioral interventions, adaptive treatment strategies, and scalable models of care that expand access to evidence-based pediatric pain treatment.

Article.Title: Spontaneous neuropathic pain
Article.Authors: Zeng X.; Woolf C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spontaneous pain is a highly prevalent and disabling consequence of neuropathic disorders, yet it remains mechanistically underdefined and therapeutically underserved. Historically, preclinical animal models and clinical trials have been overwhelmingly biased toward stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity, relegating spontaneous pain to a secondary manifestation. Emerging evidence now challenges this view. Converging data from pharmacology, neural recordings, and systems-level causal manipulations indicate that spontaneous and stimulus-evoked pain arise from substantially dissociable molecular, cellular, and circuit substrates. Injured-fiber–derived ectopic activity within specific sensory neuron subtypes serves as a dominant peripheral generator of spontaneous pain, whereas cellularly distinct, intact spared-fiber pathways mediate stimulus-evoked hypersensitivity. At spinal and supraspinal levels, spontaneous pain preferentially engages affective–salience networks during pain chronification and may ultimately become stabilized within higher-order circuitry—while remaining dynamically coupled to afferent input. This mechanistic delineation carries critical translational implications. Current diagnostic and treatment guidelines rarely differentiate symptom domains, and most therapies have been validated primarily using stimulus-evoked or overall pain intensity endpoints—potentially contributing to a mechanism–therapy mismatch and variable efficacy. We argue that spontaneous neuropathic pain should be defined as a separate symptom domain rather than considered as a spontaneous manifestation of evoked pain mechanisms. This recognition demands longitudinal, biomarker-informed phenotyping to capture its persistent and fluctuating nature, and thereby enable robust mechanistic dissection at peripheral, spinal, and cortical nodes. Reframing spontaneous neuropathic pain along these lines will provide a foundation for precision therapeutics that target defined cell types, specific molecular drivers, and maladaptive network states—enabling mechanism-based, symptom-aligned treatments.

Article.Title: Advancing equitable pain care worldwide requires progress in low- and middle-income settings: priorities for practice, research, and policy
Article.Authors: Sharma S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Equitable, high-value pain care remains out of reach for many populations worldwide, particularly for people living in low- and middle-income countries and cultural minority groups in high-income settings. Despite carrying a disproportionate burden of chronic pain, these populations remain underrepresented in high-quality pain research, underserved by existing health systems, and constrained by social, political, environmental, and commercial determinants of health. The lack of locally generated evidence forces clinicians and policymakers to rely on externally produced research that may not translate to local cultural, linguistic, or health-system contexts. This invited viewpoint synthesizes key contributors to pain inequity—including limited prioritization of chronic pain in low- and middle-income countries, underdeveloped rehabilitation capacity, poor access to essential treatments, commercial exploitation, and misalignment between culturally shaped pain beliefs and Western-derived assessment and treatment models. I highlight opportunities to strengthen equity in clinical care through improved education of health professionals and the public, culturally and linguistically responsive assessment, and contextually adapted self-management and treatment strategies. Equitable research requires standardized collection of sociodemographic variables, deliberate inclusion of underrepresented groups, and global partnerships that avoid colonizing practices. I propose principles for fair and impactful North–South collaborations focused on co-creation of research agendas, shared leadership, sustainable capacity building, and transparent governance. Advancing equitable global pain care and research will require collective action from clinicians, researchers, institutions, policymakers, journals, funders, and communities. A coordinated shift toward culturally grounded, contextually adaptable, and ethically collaborative approaches is essential to meaningfully reduce global pain disparities and ensure all individuals benefit from scientific progress.

Article.Title: Life course trajectories of musculoskeletal pain
Article.Authors: Ahacic K.; Raices Cruz I.; Kåreholt I.; Bartels S.; Oksanen A.; Wicksell R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A life course perspective can help identify critical periods and high-risk groups for musculoskeletal pain. However, how musculoskeletal pain develops over the adult life course and the extent to which this development varies among individuals remain largely unexplored. This Swedish population-representative survey followed a sample of 6328 individuals over 7 waves and 42 years, from ages 15 to 101 years, including about 25,000 observations. Reported musculoskeletal pain in the joints, back, or shoulders over the past year was categorized as follows: no pain (0), light pain in 1 to 3 sites (1), severe pain in one site (2), and severe pain in 2 to 3 sites (3). Age-related pain trajectories were identified through a sex-stratified latent class growth analysis. For both women and men, 2 distinct trajectories emerged. In the high-risk group, pain increased consistently throughout working age before declining postretirement. In the other group, pain levels were generally low, surpassing light pain only after retirement age. Although the trajectory patterns were similar for women and men, the high-risk group was twice as large among women (20%) as among men (9%). The general increase in pain towards the end of the life course likely reflects normal ageing processes, including disease onset and frailty, while the trajectory of the high-risk group may indicate the cumulative effect of risk factors associated with working life. Average trends across the entire sample mask the unique experience of this high-risk group and obscure the distinct effects of ageing on the development of musculoskeletal pain.

Article.Title: Fatigue links sociodemographic risk to pain intensity and spread in 2 surgical cohorts
Article.Authors: Sun M.; Ansari B.; Clauw D.; Harris R.; Sluka K.; Kaplan C.; Brummet C.; Lindquist M.; Wager T.; N/A N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Why some surgical patients develop pain that extends beyond the original site of injury while others do not remains poorly understood. The recently proposed Risk of Pain Spread (ROPS) framework integrates multiple psychosocial risk factors associated with widespread pain, but its generalizability to surgical populations has not been established. Using 2 large presurgical cohorts of participants undergoing total knee arthroplasty or thoracic surgery, we evaluated the generalizability of the ROPS framework and examined relationships among psychosocial and sociodemographic factors, surgical-site pain, nonsurgical-site pain, and widespread pain using complementary latent-variable, regression, Bayesian network, and mediation analyses. Across cohorts and analytical approaches, fatigue emerged as the most consistent correlate of pain outcomes, independent of other measured risk factors. Fatigue also occupied a central position within the conditional dependency structure of psychosocial and pain variables and accounted for substantial shared variance linking sleep disturbance, depressive symptoms, neuroticism, adverse childhood experiences, and socioeconomic disadvantage with pain intensity. Nonsurgical-site pain consistently occupied a position linking pain intensity with widespread pain across complementary analyses. Together, these findings externally validate the ROPS framework in clinically relevant surgical populations and identify fatigue as a central correlate linking biopsychosocial vulnerability with pain burden.

Article.Title: Astrocyte Orai1 signaling promotes spinal excitatory synaptic potentiation and neuropathic pain after nerve injury in male mice
Article.Authors: Tsujikawa S.; Shetti A.; Grant R.; Novakovic M.; Prakriya M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neuropathic pain after peripheral nerve injury is a multifactorial condition mediated partly by inflammation in the spinal cord that results in potentiation of excitatory synaptic transmission in nociceptive circuits. Glial cells including astrocytes are key mediators of the underlying inflammation, but the signaling checkpoints that regulate astrocyte-driven spinal cord inflammation and sensitization of nociceptive circuits are not well understood. Here, we identify Orai1-mediated store-operated Ca 2+ entry (SOCE) as an important regulator of spinal astrocyte cytokine production, metabolic reprogramming, and pain hypersensitivity in mice. Conditional deletion of Orai1 in astrocytes attenuated mechanical allodynia after nerve injury in male but not female mice, despite comparable SOCE suppression in both sexes. Orai1 deficiency also attenuated production of proinflammatory cytokines after SOCE activation, including TNFα, IL-6, and IL-33, both in vivo and in vitro. Electrophysiological recordings revealed that astrocyte Orai1 deletion prevented injury-induced enhancement of glutamatergic synaptic transmission in dorsal horn neurons, linking astrocytic Ca 2+ signaling to central sensitization. Metabolomic profiling showed that Orai1 loss disrupted glycolysis and TCA cycle intermediates while promoting accumulation of immunomodulatory metabolites such as itaconate, consistent with a less inflammatory astrocyte metabolic state. These findings identify Orai1 channels as integrators of astrocyte Ca 2+ signaling, immunometabolism, and excitatory synaptic potentiation after nerve injury, and identify a sexually dimorphic astrocyte mechanism governing neuropathic pain pathogenesis. Targeting astrocyte Orai1 channels may provide a selective therapeutic strategy for male-predominant chronic pain.

Article.Title: Mineralocorticoid receptor signaling reduces somatostatin expression in developing sensory neurons and drives neonatal pain after early-life stress
Article.Authors: Eid F.; Serafin E.; Muniz M.; Woodke S.; Booher J.; Zhang J.; Baccei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early-life stress (ELS) causes pain hypersensitivity in neonatal mice and alters the transcriptional profile of the immature dorsal root ganglia (DRG), highlighted by a marked reduction in the expression of a neuropeptide, somatostatin (Sst), which is known to constitutively suppress peripheral nociceptive transmission during adulthood. However, the mechanisms that drive plasticity in gene expression within the developing DRG and neonatal pain after ELS remain unclear. Here, we investigated the degree to which ELS-induced neonatal pain was mediated by corticosterone signaling onto sensory neurons and potential changes in peripheral Sst transmission. The conditional knockout of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR), but not the glucocorticoid receptor, from immature DRG neurons prevented ELS-evoked neonatal pain. In contrast, the systemic administration of the selective MR antagonist eplerenone failed to acutely influence pain after ELS, thus suggesting that MR activation enhances pain during the neonatal period via canonical effects on gene transcription. Meanwhile, hind paw injection of the Sst receptor antagonist cyclo-somatostatin increased spontaneous nocifensive behaviors in control pups, but not in pups previously subjected to ELS, raising the possibility that a disruption in tonic antinociception mediated by peripheral Sst contributes to neonatal pain after ELS. Furthermore, administration of the peripherally restricted Sst analog octreotide reversed noxious cold and pressure hypersensitivity in neonatal mice after ELS. Finally, the selective deletion of MR from sensory neurons prevented the ELS-induced decrease in Sst expression. Collectively, these results provide novel mechanistic insight into the effects of chronic early-life adversity on nociceptive processing in the developing nervous system.

Article.Title: Targeting GPR183 to reduce peripheral sensitization: evidence from rodent and human tissue analyses
Article.Authors: Oberkrom K.; Braden K.; Li E.; Shah S.; Maric D.; Mannes A.; Pacifico P.; Jayaraj N.; Arnatt C.; Menichella D.; Sapio M.; Salvemini D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peripheral sensitization is a key process in the development of painful inflammatory conditions, driven in part by immune-cell mediator release following tissue injury. The G protein–coupled receptor, GPR183, predominantly expressed on immune cells, regulates their migration, positioning, and mediator production. However, its role in peripheral sensitization and the specific immune cells involved remains insufficiently understood. In rats, intraplantar injection of 7α,25-dihydroxycholesterol (7α,25-OHC), the most potent endogenous GPR183 ligand, produced long-lasting nociception that was prevented by the selective GPR183 antagonist SAE-14. As GPR183 activates extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling, which influences pain pathways including nitric oxide synthase (NOS) activity and NO formation, we used NOS inhibitors and knockout animals to test the contribution of inducible and neuronal NOS isoforms to 7α,25-OHC-induced sensitization. We found that both isoforms influence this response, independent of cyclooxygenases. In a well-characterized rat incisional injury model, GPR183 protein expression increased in injured paw tissue, and SAE-14 reversed hypersensitivity. Meta-analysis of human postsurgical skin samples similarly showed elevated GPR183 expression and transcriptional changes favoring 7α,25-OHC production after injury. We identified macrophages, Langerhans cells (LCs), and T cells as the principal GPR183 -expressing cell types in human skin. Ablation of LCs and removal of mature B and T cells revealed that 7α,25-OHC-evoked hypersensitivity does not depend on these cell types, leaving GPR183 + macrophages as the most likely drivers of GPR183-induced hypersensitivity. Overall, our findings define the cellular and molecular pathways linking GPR183 to peripheral sensitization and highlight GPR183 antagonism as a promising strategy for pain management.

Article.Title: Circulating HSPCs enhance their self-renewal by augmenting the endocytosis and lysosomal acidity via MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis
Article.Authors: Xu Y.; Lu J.; Zhang M.; Teng Y.; Wang X.; Lai X.; Huo D.; Tie R.; Zeng X.; Chen Y.; Shan W.; Shi C.; Wen R.; Jiang P.; Li H.; Yu X.; Pei S.; Qian P.; Huang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human circulating hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (cHSPCs) in steady-state blood are a rare, underutilized resource limited by poor ex vivo expansion and unclear regulation. Using an immune-cell screening platform, we found that monocytes most effectively promote cHSPC expansion while preserving long-term hematopoietic reconstitution in serial transplantation. Mechanistically, cHSPCs engage the MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis to enhance endocytosis and lysosomal acidification, which upregulates CD34 + CXCR4 + cells, reduces ROS, stabilizes HIF-1α, and maintains glycolytic activity and stemness. Monocyte co-culture or pathway agonizts (MIF, EN6) also expanded HSPCs from cord blood, bone marrow, and poor-graft-function patient samples. Thus, cHSPC self-renewal is driven by an MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A-dependent mechanism modulating endocytosis, lysosomal function, and metabolism. This offers a universal expansion strategy for diverse clinical sources, including steady-state peripheral blood, cord blood, and functionally compromised hematopoietic cells.

Article.Title: Low-frequency phase in early visual cortex gates prefrontal influence on perception
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Hu X.; Tan Q.; Li K.; Han B.; Shen L.
Article.Abstract: Perceptual experience depends on interactions between sensory inputs and top-down predictions, yet how intrinsic cortical rhythms shape this interaction remains unclear. Here, we use rare human intracranial recordings from the prefrontal and early visual cortices during bistable motion perception, including two patients with simultaneous coverage of both regions, to investigate how oscillatory phase shapes perceptual outcomes. We show that prestimulus low-frequency phase in early visual cortex and prestimulus theta phase in prefrontal cortex are each associated with subsequent perceptual reports. Crucially, directed connectivity and cross-frequency coupling analyses, conducted in the two patients with simultaneous prefrontal and early visual cortex coverage, show that prefrontal theta phase modulates visual high-frequency activity preferentially at specific phases of early visual low-frequency activity, consistent with a probabilistic, phase-dependent gating of top-down influence. A computational model implementing low-frequency-phase–dependent gating successfully reproduces these empirical dynamics, suggesting a unifying mechanism by which cortical state constrains top-down modulation. Together, these findings provide preliminary human intracranial evidence that ongoing low-frequency phase in early visual cortex is associated with the efficacy of top-down influence from prefrontal cortex, and thereby with perceptual interpretation under ambiguity.

Article.Title: Volitional stopping is preceded by a transient motor cortex EEG beta oscillation
Article.Authors: Doutel Figueira J.; Ojala R.; Vasilev D.; De Miguel A.; Jeay-Bizot L.; Iwai R.; Raposo I.; Safaei N.; de Sardenberg Schmid L.; Maoz U.; Watanabe M.; Totah N.
Article.Abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) beta (15-30 Hz) oscillations undergo power modulations during volitional movements. The prevailing view is that beta oscillations are involved in inhibitory control, but their timing relative to movement cancellation is highly variable across studies. This variability has hindered understanding the function of beta oscillations in movement. The variability arises from use of the stop-signal task, in which movement cancellation time is covert. We recorded 32-electrode cortex-wide EEG along with the velocity of a treadmill while head-fixed rats stopped in-progress running. We show that a single beta oscillation cycle occurred in the left motor cortex around 200 msec before movement cancellation with consistent across-trial timing. Using information theory, we show that beta power was informative about velocity 200 msec in the future, but only during planning to stop. By introducing artificial temporal jitter to mimic the estimation of a covert stopping time used in prior work, we show that this brain-action relationship fails with even small jitter. Finally, we use machine learning methods to show that, despite EEG beta oscillations being a clear neural correlate of stopping, it has limited utility for real-time action decoding. Our work suggests a new conceptual model for neural control of overt action stopping.

Article.Title: Dual HDAC6 and HDAC8 inhibition enhances STING mediated innate immune responses
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Yim J.; Jang Y.; Kim S.; Lee M.; Jung M.; Park J.; Kim J.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Despite the critical role of Stimulator of Interferon Genes (STING) in innate immune regulation, the isoform-specific epigenetic mechanisms that regulate its activation remain poorly understood because of the lack of suitable chemical tools. Here, we identify SEH002, a mechanistically informative dual HDAC6 and HDAC8 inhibitor that amplifies STING activation and reveals the complementary roles of HDAC6 and HDAC8 in innate immune signaling. STING-induced innate immunity proceeds through an intrinsic cell-autonomous phase, followed by a non-cell-autonomous paracrine phase. HDAC6 inhibition promotes the early cell-autonomous phase by increasing α-tubulin acetylation and facilitating endoplasmic reticulum-to-Golgi trafficking, thereby enhancing STING signaling. In contrast, HDAC8 inhibition sustains the later non-cell-autonomous phase by limiting STAT1 dephosphorylation and prolonging interferon signaling. These findings establish HDAC6 and HDAC8 as regulators of distinct phases of STING-mediated immune response. SEH002 provides an isoform-aware chemical handle to probe this cross-talk and suggests a general strategy for defining how epigenetic mechanisms orchestrate the magnitude and duration of STING-mediated innate immune responses.

Article.Title: ADAMTS7 impairs endothelial angiogenic function via suppressing POSTN-mediated VEGFR2 activation in pre-eclampsia
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Xu H.; Xu Y.; Tang Q.; Wang L.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Angiogenic imbalance-induced endothelial dysfunction is central to pre-eclampsia (PE) pathogenesis. A disintegrin and metalloprotease with thrombospondin motif, member 7 (ADAMTS7) is upregulated in PE placentas and suppresses trophoblast function; however, its role in systemic endothelial dysfunction during PE remains unclear. Here we show a higher placental secretion and plasma level of ADAMTS7 in PE patients. ADAMTS7 circulating levels are positively correlated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure of pregnant women. Besides, hypoxia stimulates ADAMTS7 expression in human trophoblast and vascular cells by a HIF1α-dependent way. Pregnant rats with ADAMTS7 overexpression by adenovirus injection exhibits PE-like symptoms and impaired placental development. Functionally, ADAMTS7 significantly inhibits endothelial angiogenic activity and suppresses vessel formation as evidenced by proliferation, migration, angiogenic assays. Mechanistically, ADAMTS7 binds to and decreases periostin (POSTN), reducing VEGFR2 expression and phosphorylation. This study identifies ADAMTS7 as a pathogenic factor in PE that impaired endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting that targeting ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for PE. Angiogenic imbalance drives endothelial dysfunction in pre-eclampsia (PE). Here, the authors show the metalloprotease ADAMTS7 is elevated in the circulation of PE patients and impairs endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting the ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis as a therapeutic target for PE.

Article.Title: Nanobody mimicry of a GPCR recognition site disrupts human C5a-C5aR1 signaling
Article.Authors: Santos-López J.; Querol-García J.; de la Paz-García K.; Sierra-Filardi E.; Camero S.; Navas-Yuste S.; Ajona D.; Pereda A.; Tapia-Agudo G.; Harasimowicz H.; Vincke C.; Pio R.; Cañada F.; Pantoja-Uceda D.; Muyldermans S.; Rodríguez de Córdoba S.; Fernández F.; Vega M.
Article.Abstract: The human anaphylatoxin C5a is a potent proinflammatory mediator generated during complement activation. C5a acts through the G-protein-coupled receptors C5aR1 and C5aR2, which are implicated in many immune-inflammatory diseases, and blocking C5a-C5aR1 signaling is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here we generate and characterize nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments, that bind human and mouse C5a with high affinity and fall into two families recognizing non-overlapping epitopes. In cell assays, these nanobodies block C5a-induced receptor activation and downstream signaling. Crystallography shows that the antigen-binding loop of the highest-affinity nanobody mimics a turn in the extracellular amino-terminal region of C5aR1 and C5aR2, so that the nanobody competes with the receptor for the same surface of C5a. An antibody loop and a cell-surface receptor thus converge on analogous solutions for engaging the same ligand. These results inform our understanding of antibody-mediated inhibition of receptor agonists and identify nanobody-based C5a inhibitors as candidates to modulate C5a-driven inflammation.

Article.Title: Amyloid pathology compresses dynamic range and degrades spatial coding in an Alzheimer’s mouse model
Article.Authors: Go M.; Clarke K.; Li Y.; Prado S.; Teixeira B.; Gao M.; Yu J.; Schultz S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupts neural circuits vital for memory and cognition. Using two-photon calcium imaging in behaving 5xFAD mice, we examined how amyloid pathology alters hippocampal CA1 activity and spatial coding. We found elevated baseline activity but reduced locomotion-driven firing, leading to a diminished neuronal dynamic range. To our knowledge, this is the first direct experimental evidence for reduced dynamic range in an AD model. These abnormalities were strongest near amyloid plaques and became more widespread with age. We also observed altered network synchrony, degraded spatial coding, and increased neuronal response variability. Furthermore, place fields emerged more slowly in both familiar and novel environments, indicating impaired recall and learning. By showing a link between local plaque pathology and impaired flexible modulation of CA1 activity and progressive deficits in spatial memory coding, our study offers new insights into the circuit basis of cognitive decline in AD.

Article.Title: Artificial skyglow at night disrupts chronobiology and physiology in Crassostrea gigas
Article.Authors: Botté A.; Payton L.; Geerebaert Y.; Tran D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial skyglow at night (ASAN) is widespread in coastal environments, with consequences beginning to be highlighted but still understudied. Long-term ASAN field studies are needed to better understand the real challenge that nocturnal light poses to coastal organisms. To fill this gap, we investigated during one year in Arcachon Bay (France), ASAN’s impact on the oysters’ biological rhythms and major physiological parameters: behavior, growth, and gametogenesis. Results show that ASAN affects oysters’ behavioral valve activity rhythms, whether they are directly driven by light cycles (daily, lunar, and annual) or not (tidal and semi-lunar), suggesting a disruption of the oyster’s internal clock functioning. Our study also reveals that ASAN affects oyster physiology at the annual scale by inducing a phase advance in body weight and shell length growth, and gametogenetic cycle. These chronobiological and physiological effects of ASAN could lead to a disruption of the oyster’s fitness.

Article.Title: In planta-specific transcriptional regulatory circuit regulates expression of MoHTR1, a nuclear effector gene of Magnaporthe oryzae
Article.Authors: Yoon Y.; Lee H.; Kim S.; Chung H.; Khang C.; Lim Y.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract During host-pathogen interactions, fungal pathogens secrete effectors into host cells to manipulate the host immune system and facilitate infection. Although many effector genes are highly expressed during infection stages, there is limited information on the mechanisms regulating their in planta expression. Here, we characterize the promoter of MoHTR1 , a nuclear effector gene of the rice blast pathogen, to elucidate its in planta -specific expression. Article.Authors: Storer K.; Hawthorne S.; Lovell C.; Mahmood F.; Kenna D.; Zhu T.; Graystock P.; Gill R.

Article.Title: Loss of confidence in commercial antibody validation threatens biomedical research integrity
Article.Authors: Lim T.
Article.Abstract: Recent independent investigations conducted have identified thousands of apparently manipulated validation images across the online catalogues of more than a dozen commercial antibody suppliers. The greatest trait variability and resilience arise when antagonistic and environmental selection pressures are symmetrical. In species-rich communities, fluctuating selection emerges naturally, while dominance of antagonistic pressure consistently dampens trait directionality. Coupled ecological and evolutionary processes favour trait matching and generate both nested and modular network structures. Compared with bipartite antagonistic networks, network architecture plays a weaker role in shaping trait coevolution in three-guild systems. Together, these results show how trade-offs among antagonistic, mutualistic and environmental selection pressures govern trait evolution and resilience in complex ecological networks.

Article.Title: A dichotomous family of Cache domain proteins evolved through c-type heme acquisition
Article.Authors: Deshpande M.; Xing J.; Gumerov V.; Dunleavy R.; Castillo H.; Crane B.; Zhulin I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract PAS domains often bind cofactors, whereas related Cache domains are thought to function exclusively as ligand-binding modules. We identify and characterize a large family of Cache domains containing covalently bound c-type heme. Sequence, phylogenetic and structual analysis of the DUF3365/Tll0287 family reveals conservation of a canonical CXXCH heme-binding motif, establishing c-type heme binding as a defining feature of this family. Despite previous annotation as PAS-like, these proteins share a distinct heme-binding insertion into a pre-existing Cache scaffold, representing the first documented recruitment of an intact cofactor-binding motif into a bacterial sensor domain. Domain architecture further divides the family into two subclasses: one exhibiting fusions to signaling domains and another comprised of standalone proteins. Spectroscopic analyses indicate that a representative signaling protein acts as a nitric oxide sensor, whereas a stand-alone representative exhibits redox-related properties and weak nitric oxide binding. Article.Title: Dynamic climate and ecological expansion drive body morphology evolution in fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Fang Z.; Liu B.; Ding Z.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Cephalopods originated in the Cambrian approximately 500 million years ago, evolving from externally shelled ancestors to forms with diverse morphologies. Despite their morphological diversity, the macroevolutionary patterns and drivers of their diversification remain incompletely understood. Here, we construct a time-calibrated phylogenetic framework for fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods and quantify evolutionary rates and morphological disparity over ~490 million years. We identify five peaks in morphological diversification, indicating rapid evolutionary phases during historical periods. Morphological disparity exhibits a time-lagged response to evolutionary rate shifts. Sea surface temperature and ecological factors are macroevolutionary drivers shaping evolutionary rates and morphological disparity. Major environmental perturbations, including the end-Permian and end-Triassic mass extinctions and Early Triassic and Toarcian hyperthermal events, are associated with reduced evolutionary rates, whereas post-Cretaceous conditions correspond to elevated rates driven by ecological release and adaptive radiation. Our results show that cephalopod morphological evolution is governed by coupled environmental and ecological processes that structure evolutionary dynamics over deep time.

Article.Title: Glutathione S transferase assembled gold silver nanoclusters activate cGAS STING immunity in breast cancer
Article.Authors: Li J.; Bai Z.; Yang R.; Liu Y.; Lian B.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer often returns or spreads after treatment, and therapies that can destroy tumors while also engaging the immune system are urgently needed. However, it remains difficult to design safe nanomaterials that both heat tumors under light and turn dying cancer cells into signals that support long-lasting antitumor immunity. Here we show that glutathione S-transferase guided self-assembly produces ultrasmall glutathione-stabilized gold-silver nanoclusters for laser-assisted breast cancer treatment. Under near-infrared light, these nanoclusters efficiently generate heat and oxidative stress, killing breast cancer cells and releasing immune-stimulating signals. The treatment activates the cGAS-STING immune signaling pathway, promotes dendritic cell maturation, increases tumor-killing T cell infiltration, and strengthens memory T cell responses. In mouse models of primary and metastatic breast cancer, the nanoclusters preferentially accumulate in tumors and suppress tumor growth, metastasis, and relapse with limited signs of toxicity. This protein-guided nanocluster strategy provides a potential route for combining localized light-based treatment with systemic antitumor immunity and may support the future development of safer and more durable cancer nanomedicines. GST-mediated self-assembly of gold-silver nanoclusters activates cGAS-STING signaling and remodels antitumor immunity, enabling photothermal-immunotherapy to inhibit breast cancer growth, metastasis and recurrence.

Article.Title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
Article.Authors: Pogorevc N.; Upadhyay M.; Simčič M.; Sandoval-Castellanos E.; Horvat S.; Medugorac I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Introgression is increasingly documented, yet its detection remains challenging because patterns used to infer gene flow may reflect multiple processes, including the persistence of ancestral polymorphism under balancing selection. Domestic species, like goats, and their wild relatives provide informative models for testing the biological feasibility and genomic consequences of interspecific gene flow. We analyze whole-genome sequences from 164 individuals of the genus Capra , including 36 newly generated, to investigate hybridization and signatures of introgression within the genus. Genomic analyses confirm a goat–ibex hybrid and identify two backcross offspring, providing evidence of male F1 fertility. We identify 8 candidate regions with shared haplotypes consistent with ancient introgression predating domestication and enriched for genes involved in olfaction and immunity. However, some regions show signatures compatible with balancing selection. Overall, our results show that hybridization between domestic and wild Capra is biologically possible, that most shared haplotypes likely predate domestication, and highlight the importance of distinguishing introgression from balancing selection when interpreting shared genomic variation across species.

Article.Title: Predicting discrete traits in evolving systems
Article.Authors: Prall J.; Surya K.; Bender E.; Feigin L.; Meade A.; Organ C.
Article.Abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. Predictions using discrete data are central to imputation, forecasting, and hypothesis testing in biology. How much accuracy and confidence they deliver together, and how this varies across scenarios and taxa, has not been quantified systematically. Here, using accuracy and log loss, we benchmark these models across scenarios varying in tree size, evolutionary rate, and trait coevolution. Against non-phylogenetic baselines, they increase accuracy by 23 percentage points and lower log loss by 92% on average; different Markov implementations perform similarly. Log loss rises as terminal branch lengths elongate, a direct consequence of the Markov process. Last, we provide a tutorial and empirical demonstration for the evolution of unexpected character states (outliers). Our study provides a framework for imputing missing data, reconstructing ancestral traits, and testing evolutionary hypotheses.

Article.Title: Biofilm selection activates c-di-GMP synthesis by the bifunctional enzyme MbaA
Article.Authors: Lorentzen Ø.; Abel S.; Johnsen P.; Frøhlich C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Article.Authors: Osborne A.; Hayward S.; Colby E.; Andag U.; Kalra P.; Koziell A.; Radresa O.; Skroblin P.; Taal M.; Welsh G.; Saleem M.; Campbell C.

Article.Authors: Carson K.; Roy R.; Stern J.

Morphometric analyses reveal that AP capillaries are significantly larger than those in the NTS, providing a structural basis for this flow asymmetry. Despite these geometric differences, capillary flow velocities are preserved across regions, indicating active regulation of perfusion within the shared network. These findings reveal directional blood flow within a shared AP-NTS capillary network, identifying a potential vascular route by which diffusible signals generated in one region may preferentially reach the other.

Article.Authors: Zhu M.; Wang Y.; Pei Y.; Liu Y.; Wang X.; Dai X.

We further identify the transition-state regulator AbrB as a key modulator that integrates growth and sporulation, promoting growth under favorable conditions while facilitating sporulation under poor nutrients. On good carbon sources, AbrB optimizes cellular resource allocation by directly suppressing the unnecessary expression of adaptive pathways. In contrast, on poor carbon sources, where the Spo0A-signaling pathway is strongly activated, AbrB promotes sporulation by repressing the expression of a plasmid-encoded Rap-family phosphatase gene, which otherwise interferes with the Spo0A signaling pathway. Article.Authors: Olmo F.; Hesketh A.; Hage H.; Monneuse J.; Taylor M.; Costa F.; Da Silva C.; Bequet F.; Escudié F.; Mercer D.; Saliou A.; Chatelain E.; Kelly J.; Abi-Ghanem J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chagas disease is caused by infection with the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi . Despite triggering a strong immune response, infections are typically life-long and can result in severe cardiac and/or digestive tract pathology. Current drugs have limited efficacy, and treatment failure is a common outcome. Eliminating a non-replicating T. cruzi sub-population that can persist after therapy has been a key challenge for the drug-development community. Here, we describe the transcriptome and proteome profiles of a low-proliferative sub-population of epimastigote forms of the parasite isolated from exponentially growing cultures on the basis of reduced turnover of transiently-induced red fluorescent protein. These data provide a resource that can be exploited to dissect the mechanistic basis of quiescence, as a step towards refining the drug-development screening cascade.

Article.Authors: Hirsch M.; Ergun J.; Chin S.; Graff C.; Yee D.; Perez-Guijarro E.; Merlino G.; Day C.; Przytycka T.

These subclones interact with each other and the immune system to shape tumor progression. In the experimental models, admixtures of proliferative and invasive subclones of varying proportions were implanted into immunocompromised and immunocompetent mice. Tumor growth and subclone composition were tracked over time. In parallel, we built a computational model to capture the system dynamics. By estimating parameter values of our mathematical model using experimental measurements, we found that, while the proliferative subclone outgrew the invasive subclone, T cell activities selected for the invasive subclone. Initial subclonal proportion in this dynamic system determines the overall tumor sensitivity to immune response. The key interactions identified in this study provide insights into how intratumor heterogeneity and immune pressure influence melanoma progression, suggesting strategies for optimizing individualized therapy.

Article.Title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
Article.Authors: Lengerer B.; Bertemes P.; Szucs A.; Ladurner P.; Mertens B.; Grosbusch A.; Wattiez R.; Flammang P.
Article.Abstract: Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive sea star footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens, comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. Here, we generated a high-quality de novo genome assembly of the starlet cushion star, Asterina gibbosa, enabling full-length gene identification of Sfps. Proteomics of deposited footprint material identified 34 candidates; in situ hybridization localized 10 to the tube foot adhesive epidermis. Nine (designated Agib-Sfps) were homologous to known A. rubens Sfps, and one encoded a trypsin-like proteinase. Anti-peptide antibodies revealed distinct footprint labeling patterns for Agib-Sfp7 and Agib-Sfp8, although mostly associated to the thin layer in contact with the substrate. Comparative analyses indicate a conserved core adhesive toolkit and domain repertoire between species, alongside species-specific reshuffling of domains across Sfps. These results refine the molecular model of asteroid adhesion and provide targets for sequence recombinant production toward seawater-compatible biomimetic adhesives. The study highlights a conserved core adhesive toolkit across sea star species, with species-specific reshuffling of single protein domains. Detailed analyses revealed distinct roles for adhesive proteins in forming cohesive and surface-binding layers. These findings refine the molecular understanding of sea star adhesion, emphasizing evolutionary conservation and functional diversity of adhesive proteins. The research provides a foundation for further studies into how these proteins enable strong yet reversible adhesion in marine environments.

Article.Title: Disruption of arn lipid A aminoarabinosylation confers AmpCmediated cephalosporin resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: Hardie Boys M.; Wardell S.; Pletzer D.
Article.Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in chronic cystic fibrosis infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa is shaped by pathogen-specific adaptation, yet the mechanisms driving cephalosporin resistance in epidemic clinical lineages remain incompletely defined. Here, we used in vitro experimental evolution to generate ceftazidime-resistant P. aeruginosa LESB58 strains, revealing loss-of-function mutations in the arnBCADTEF-ugd operon, encoding the L-Ara4N lipid A modification system (aminoarabinosylation). Transcriptome sequencing and an ampC-promoter reporter fusion demonstrated strong upregulation of ampC, encoding a β-lactamase, following ceftazidime treatment in the arn deletion strain. Deletion of ampC in the arn mutant restored cephalosporin susceptibility to wild-type levels, confirming AmpC as the primary resistance mechanism. This arn-linked resistance was also observed in LESB65 but absent in laboratory strains PAO1 and PA14. These findings identify a connection between lipid A modification loss and AmpC-driven cephalosporin resistance in clinically relevant P. aeruginosa lineages. Article.Title: COX2 contributes to the spatial reorganization of B7H4+ and CD44v6+ niches promoting therapy resistance in ER- breast cancer

Inflammatory stimulation increased and spatially reorganized COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ populations. While COX2+ cells occupied oxygenated-to-intermediate zones, B7H4+ populations were enriched in intermediate-to-hypoxic regions, and CD44v6 remained broadly distributed. Diclofenac disrupted this organization and reduced clustering of COX2+, B7H4+, and COX2+CD44v6+ phenotypes. Poor-outcome patients showed high COX2 at the tumor-stroma interface as well as altered COX2+, B7H4+, and CD44v6+ clustering phenotypes. Article.Title: Friend advice influences mate choice through brain-to-brain synchrony and computational decision processes
Article.Authors: Huang R.; Jiang J.; Liu J.; Zhang C.; Wang H.; Zhang X.; Wang H.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Individuals often rely on friends’ advice when making mate-choice decisions under uncertainty, yet how such advice is integrated into decision-making remains unclear. Using fNIRS hyperscanning, we simultaneously recorded neural and behavioral activity from 66 adult friend dyads (33 female dyads) during interactive advice phases. Only the bidirectional Social Information Processing (SIP) computational model best fit the behavioral data, indicating that social influence arises from reciprocal interaction rather than one-way transmission. Behaviorally, positive advice from in the relationship advisors increased mate-choice intention, whereas negative advice from single advisors more strongly influenced decision-making. Both conditions elicited enhanced interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), linked to risk evaluation, and in the left superior and middle temporal gyri (l-STG, l-MTG), associated with semantic processing and value transformation. Machine learning analyses showed that task-level INS robustly forecasted overall advice influence. Together, these findings demonstrate that friend advice influence emerges from dynamic brain-to-brain alignment in control and semantic networks—reflecting emotional sharing during positive advice and risk re-evaluation during negative advice. This study extending SIP theory to interactive decision-making and revealing how friend advice influence mate-choice decision.

Article.Title: Analysis of structural modifications and metagenomic sequencing during the ensiling of Caragana korshinskii provides insights into how extrusion pretreatment promotes lignocellulose degradation
Article.Authors: Bai B.; Ge G.; Qiu R.; Bao J.; Liu M.; Zhao M.; Ma W.; Sheng P.; Jia Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: In this study, to address the problems of poor silage fermentation quality and difficulty degrading lignocellulose interfering with resource utilization of Caragana korshinskii biomass, the effects of extrusion pretreatment (temperature 140°C and screw speed of 400 rpm) on its ensiling process were investigated. Results showed that pretreatment significantly improved silage quality, with lactic acid and water-soluble carbohydrate content increasing significantly ( P < 0.05), neutral detergent fiber content decreasing significantly ( P < 0.05), and hemicellulose degradation rate increasing by 31.64 ± 1.20% compared with the normal silage group. Microstructure analysis showed that pretreatment destroyed the dense biomass structure, increased specific surface area and porosityenhanced hydrophilicity, and reduced crystallinity, thus promoting the degradation of hemicellulose and cellulose. Metagenomic analysis further showed that extrusion pretreatment remodeled the microbial community structure, increasing the proportion of lactic acid bacteria such as Weissella and Companilactobacillus , and significantly increased the abundance of genes encoding debranching enzymes (CE3 and CE12) involved in hemicellulose degradation as well as main chain hydrolases (GH43 and GH8) ( P < 0.05). This study provides insights into the mechanisms by which extrusion pretreatment improves Caragana korshinskii silage in terms of physical and chemical structure and microbial functions, and this in turn may provide a technical and theoretical basis for understanding how efficient ensiling can be achieved more broadly in high-lignocellulosic feedstocks.

Article.Abstract: This review examines the expanding role of PARP inhibitors in cancer therapy, moving beyond the traditional model of single-strand break repair inhibition and BRCA-dependent synthetic lethality. Article.Title: iTBS and cTBS to an individualized dlPFC target produce differential working memory improvement and session-dependent putamen deactivation
Article.Authors: Sun I.; Gregory D.; Abd-Elmoniem N.; Patel M.; Casalvera A.; Gura H.; Rodriguez C.; Brighter G.; Rueda Mora S.; Chandrashekar S.; Makhoul W.; Lynch K.; Oathes D.; Sheline Y.; Balderston N.
Article.Abstract: We evaluated the effects of individualized left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) theta-burst stimulation (TBS) on working memory performance and task-related BOLD activity in 115 healthy adults (iTBS: n = 63; cTBS: n = 52). Participants completed the Sternberg Working Memory paradigm at baseline and approximately 24 hours after each visit. Groups were well-matched at baseline on all behavioral and neural measures. iTBS produced a significant improvement in working memory accuracy across sessions while cTBS did not, with a significant Group × Session interaction confirming differential trajectories. Both groups showed reaction time speedup across sessions, consistent with a shared practice effect. Despite these behavioral differences, BOLD activity at the dlPFC stimulation site showed no significant effects of Group, Session, or their interaction. Whole-brain analyses revealed significant session-dependent attenuation of bilateral putamen deactivation during the retention interval in both stimulation groups, with greater putamen deactivation at baseline correlating negatively with working memory accuracy. These results demonstrate that individualized task-based fMRI targeting can link TBS to circuit-level behavioral change, and that downstream subcortical responses may be more sensitive indices of TBS effects than activation at the stimulation site. Article.Title: Cortex-wide neuronal dynamics underpin quasi-periodic patterns in resting-state fMRI
Article.Authors: Mandino F.; Shen X.; Horien C.; Papademetris X.; Strittmatter S.; Keilholz S.; Xu N.; Lake E.
Article.Abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) captures whole-brain activity fluctuations non-invasively in humans and animals. Beyond task/stimuli-locked responses, fMRI measures large-scale patterned activity during rest. Among these, quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) represent recurring waves of activity that unfold over seconds and exhibit consistent spatiotemporal characteristics. Notably, certain fMRI-QPPs are well-preserved across species and altered in various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, our collective understanding of their neural underpinnings is limited given the indirect nature of the blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) fMRI signal. Simultaneous measures of local field potentials have provided some affirmation that fMRI-QPPs have neural origins, but these point-measurements are limited to a handful of sites. Here, we use a unique multimodal implementation of simultaneous wide-field calcium (WF-Ca2+) imaging and fMRI to investigate the neural origins of fMRI-based QPPs. We uncover a robust time-locked correlation between QPPs detected by cortex-wide fluorescent WF-Ca2+ imaging of neural activity and QPPs of BOLD-fMRI. These data validate the hypothesis that BOLD-fMRI QPPs derive from preceding slow waves of neural activity with regional and temporal precision. We use simultaneous wide-field Ca2+ imaging and fMRI to uncover the neural origins of quasi-periodic patterns (QPPs) in fMRI. Cortex-wide Ca2+ activity closely tracks and predicts fMRI-QPPs, revealing a direct link between neuronal dynamics and fMRI.

Article.Title: Epigenetic regulation of cancer drivers and EMT revealed by genome-wide methylome profiling in NSCLC
Article.Authors: Chwialkowska K.; Niemira M.; Ostrowska A.; Zeller A.; Reszec-Gielazyn J.; Kozlowski M.; Mroz R.; Naumnik W.; Sierko E.; Moniuszko M.; Niklinski J.; Kretowski A.; Kwasniewski M.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

Article.Title: Chronic exercise induces a pathway-dependent electrophysiological signature in the mouse hippocampus
Article.Authors: Muela P.; Makarova J.; Muñoz-Arnaiz R.; Aballay J.; Cintado E.; Herreras O.; Trejo J.
Article.Abstract: Chronic physical exercise enhances hippocampal function, yet its impact on network activity remains poorly defined. Schaffer Collateral and Lacunosum-Moleculare generators showed changes that did not achieve statistical significance. Exploratory spatial transcriptomics identified a coordinated enrichment of calcium signaling and long-term potentiation programs in the dentate gyrus. These findings demonstrate that exercise-induced plasticity is not a global shift but a localized remodeling of specific synaptic inputs, with changes detectable at both circuit and molecular levels. These durable, pathway-specific imprints persist in the absence of active task engagement, suggesting a reorganization of the brain’s memory circuitry.

Article.Authors: Li X.; Jia X.; Sun Z.; Li T.; Xu B.; Cao X.; Ding K.; Wang Y.; Shi Y.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: The bone marrow (BM) vascular network drives bone development and hematopoiesis, but the mechanisms governing its specialized sinusoidal architecture remain poorly characterized. Article.Title: Evolutionary genomics of ancient and endangered Achnatherum breviaristatum on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Zhang X.; Su X.; Wu G.; Yang Y.; Liu J.; Yuan L.; Ren G.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Climate change and human activities threaten biodiversity on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), renowned for its endemic species. We examined genomic diversity and evolution of Achnatherum breviaristatum, an endangered grass species endemic to the QTP. A. breviaristatum diverged from its sister lineage ~15 million years ago, and contrasts with two widespread and ecologically dominant monotypic genera within the same lineage—Neotrinia splendens and Psammochloa villosa—which thrive in arid northwestern China. All species experienced parallel demographic declines since the Quaternary glaciation, with reductions during the Pleistocene. The endangered status of A. breviaristatum likely results from weaker clonal reproduction relative to its relatives, combined with Pleistocene vegetation shifts and anthropogenic activities. A reduced genetic load in A. breviaristatum may mitigate the effects of its low genetic diversity and contribute to its persistence. This study highlights interactions among climatic shifts, reproductive strategy, and human impact in shaping endemic species’ fates, providing genetic insights for conservation in vulnerable ecosystems. A comparative genomics study on grasses from the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau reveals how demographic decline, reduced clonal reproduction, and Pleistocene climate shifts have driven low diversity in an endangered endemic species, while reduced genetic load may have enabled its persistence.

Article.Title: Developmental restriction of the jaw skeletal muscle cardiogenic potential
Article.Authors: Díaz-Díaz C.; Ocaña O.; Isern J.; Muñoz-Cánoves P.; Torres M.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of mortality worldwide and heart failure remains an end-stage disease with no other treatment than transplantation. A promising field to tackle heart failure is cardiomyocyte implantation. Whereas cardiomyocyte generation from pluripotent cells has shown promising results, direct derivation of cardiomyocytes from somatic stem cells is still challenging. Skeletal muscle progenitors have been extensively studied as a source of cardiac cells, due to their cellular and functional similarities. During development, the right ventricular myocardium and jaw skeletal muscles derive from a common pool of myogenic mesodermal progenitors. Previous studies have reported the derivation of cardiomyocyte-like cells specifically from adult mouse jaw muscle stem cell populations, but not from other skeletal muscles, suggesting that developmental origin endows cardiogenic potential. Here we evaluated the cardiogenic potential of satellite cells and mesenchymal progenitor cells from the masticatory muscle by reproducing, optimizing and diversifying previously described protocols. We consistently found that stem cells from masticatory muscles are unable to differentiate into cardiac cells under any tested cardiogenic environment. Furthermore, pharmacological erasing of repressive epigenetic marks did not activate cardiogenic potential, suggesting that barriers restraining lineage plasticity are profound and unlikely to be reversed by simple exposure to cardiogenic environments.

Article.Authors: Carvalho A.; Falcón-Pérez J.; Beck H.; Matthiesen R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, yet their proteomic profiling remains confounded by massive co-isolation. Article.Abstract: Breast cancer endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, systemically disrupts estrogen receptor signaling and increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk in women. Hyperplastic adipose tissue expansion, especially in subcutaneous depots, facilitates nutrient storage and attenuates inflammation during a chronic positive energy balance and is impaired in the absence of estrogen. Article.Title: Assessing whole-cortex excitability from electromagnetic brain signals
Article.Authors: Pellegrino G.; Duma G.; Schuler A.; Daub M.; Marinazzo D.; Arcara G.; Soddu A.; Rasero J.
Article.Abstract: Cortical excitability is a core feature of brain function shaped by microcircuitry, large-scale networks, and neurochemistry. In humans, it can be inferred from indirect electrophysiological measures, yet it remains unclear whether these capture a single construct or multiple processes. Aperiodic and alpha-band measures were strongly coupled and most spatially aligned with stimulus responses, while temporal, complexity, and synchronization metrics were largely independent. Article.Authors: Batista R.; Semedo T.; Beck R.; Bittencourt P.; Ceríaco L.; Cuadros-Espinoza S.; da Silva M.; de Melo F.; Deo R.; de Vries D.; Farh K.; Farias I.; Gibson M.; Goodhead I.; Gubili C.; Hermosilla-Albala N.; Hrbek T.; Janiak M.; Kuderna L.; Mahabir D.; Marqués-Bonet T.; Melin A.; Mendoza A.; Mittermeier R.; Nash S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Complex ecological and evolutionary patterns shaped the rich biodiversity of the Neotropics. Article.Authors: Cecconello C.; Claria-Ribas P.; Cartagena García C.; Busnel J.; Dalli J.; Perretti M.; Norling L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Article.Authors: Molina M.; Zhang Y.; Steenbergen R.; Melchers W.; Du J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

The stochastic nature of these models and the typically limited throughput of most experimental designs challenge the automatic inference of latent variables. Here, we combine high-throughput behavioral assays in larval zebrafish with drift-diffusion modeling, revealing that larvae progressively develop more persistent, self-reinforcing integration dynamics during early development. This effect is reduced in fish carrying mutations in genes linked to human epilepsy and schizophrenia.
