Article.Authors: Lemaire J.; Mangione R.; Loveland J.; Fusani L.; Canoine V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The capacity to regulate corticosterone release following a stressful event is an essential component of the physiological flexibility required to maintain homeostasis and ensure adaptive responses to environmental change. Hg blood concentrations were negatively correlated with corticosterone responsiveness, suggesting impairment of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis function. These results demonstrate that environmental Hg contamination is associated with reduced stress responsiveness and physiological flexibility, which likely limits the ability of Hg-contaminated individuals to cope with novel environmental stressors. Article.Title: PDE10A identified by cross-hemisphere visual cortex proteomics restores adult ocular dominance plasticity involving cAMP/CREB signaling

Importantly, paracrine signaling alone is insufficient, highlighting a requirement for direct epithelial–mesenchymal interaction. Under these conditions, we observed activation of mechanotransduction-associated and developmental signaling programs together with structural and transcriptional changes consistent with more mature alveolar-like epithelial states. This platform establishes a physiologically relevant model for human alveologenesis and provides a foundation for disease modeling and regenerative applications. hPSC-derived distal bud tip organoids that resemble fetal alveolar progenitors are developed and used to show that air-liquid interface culture and cyclic stretch enhance alveolar epithelial maturation and increased segregation of AT1- and AT2-associated cell states.

Article.Title: Targeting central thalamus with transcranial ultrasound reduces arousal in healthy volunteers
Article.Authors: Hopkins A.; Cain J.; White E.; Abakians S.; Monti M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Using low-intensity focused transcranial ultrasound stimulation, we test the causal roles of the central thalamus in arousal and the pulvinar in visuospatial attention in the healthy human brain. In a within-subjects, counterbalanced design, 27 healthy volunteers (two females) complete a vigilance task (Psychomotor Vigilance Task) and a visuospatial attention task (Egly-Driver Task) before and after sham, central thalamic, and pulvinar sonication. Targeting the central thalamus slows responses and increases lapses in attention during the vigilance task, indicating reduced arousal. Pulvinar sonication reduces (and slows) responses to visual stimuli presented contralaterally, suggesting a disruption of contralateral visuospatial attention. These results provide causal evidence linking the pulvinar to visuospatial attention and the central thalamus to arousal in the healthy human brain and demonstrate that ultrasound can elicit distinct behavioral changes in healthy volunteers when delivered to close but functionally distinct thalamic regions, underscoring its potential as a tool for noninvasive brain mapping.

Article.Title: Whole brain modeling reveals subtype specific regulation for adolescent major depressive disorder
Article.Authors: Zeng X.; Zhang G.; Wang F.; Xiong Y.; Zhang T.; Zhou C.; Biswal B.; Yao D.; Guo D.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder exhibits substantial intrinsic subtype heterogeneity, necessitating the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Using the Boston Adolescent Neuroimaging of Depression and Anxiety dataset, we identified two subtypes with distinct clinical features. For each subtype, we constructed a whole-brain model and performed virtual stimulation to assess regulatory effects at global (whole-brain) and regional (classical depression-related targets) levels. Here we show that the two subtypes require different but stable stimulation modalities, excitatory or inhibitory, to normalize brain activity. Optimal stimulation intensities for restoring static and dynamic features vary across targets and subtypes, whereas the stimulation modality remains consistent within each subtype. Notably, localized stimulation of subtype-specific targets within classical depression-related regions produces more effective and stable outcomes than whole-brain stimulation. These findings provide a computational framework for identifying subtype-specific regulatory strategies in adolescent major depressive disorder, bridging whole-brain modeling with potential clinical translation.

Article.Title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
Article.Authors: Dai X.; Wu J.; Liu L.; Song W.; Wu H.; Gao S.; Zhang L.; Liu D.; Zhou Y.; Tian B.; Zhang P.; Chen S.; Chen D.; Zhang P.; Mei W.; Tang Z.
Article.Abstract: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Results show that CMT Vglut2 neuron activity revealed a reduction during the loss of consciousness and a subsequent elevation upon recovery of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Chemogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons delays induction and hastened recovery from sevoflurane anesthesia. Moreover, during sustained sevoflurane anesthesia at steady state, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons facilitates cortical activation and behavioral recovery. During burst suppression under sevoflurane, this stimulation elicits cortical arousal and declines the burst-suppression ratio. Conversely, inhibiting CMT Vglut2 neurons via chemogenetic or optogenetic methods produces greater sensitivity to sevoflurane anesthesia and deepens cortical suppression, respectively. Monosynaptic connections from CMT Vglut2 neurons to red nucleus glutamatergic neurons (RN Vglut2 neurons) are identified using combined retrograde and anterograde tracing. During sevoflurane anesthesia, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 -RN terminals triggers cortical activation. Overall, these findings identify the CMT Vglut2 -RN pathway as a neural circuit regulating cortical activation and behavioral arousal under various stages of sevoflurane-induced anesthesia.

Article.Title: Efficient structural information integration into protein language models with implicit mixture-of-experts ProBEiT
Article.Authors: Li M.; He S.; Sang T.; Li R.; Jiang Y.; Ren Y.; Zhao Y.; Yao S.; Yang G.; Wang X.; Lu H.
Article.Abstract: Protein language models can now predict function and mutational effects directly from sequence, yet only a few incorporate function-deciding structural information with minimal additional effort. We introduce ProBEiT, a multimodal architecture that jointly encodes amino-acid sequences and discrete, tokenized structures via a parameter-efficient implicit mixture-of-experts scheme with deterministic routing. Trained on 1.7 million AlphaFoldDB proteins, the 400 million-parameter model surpasses larger baselines across six tasks of fitness prediction and functional annotation, demonstrating enhanced understanding of sequence-structure-function relationships. Unlike existing billion-scale models, ProBEiT attains strong accuracy early in continual training period, reducing computational cost. In an experimental thermostability engineering task on glycerol-3-phosphate oxidase, it correctly identifies optimized variants with positive epistatic effects. These results show that tightly coupling structural context with sequence modeling in a modality-specialized framework enables efficient, high-performance protein engineering. ProBEiT integrates protein sequence and tokenized structure with deterministic implicit MoE routing, enabling efficient sequence structure modeling and strong performance in fitness prediction and thermostability engineering.

Article.Title: Hierarchical distortions in structure-function coupling linked to multiscale neurobiological characteristics in autism
Article.Authors: Kim T.; Namgung J.; Park Y.; Kim C.; Yoo K.; Satterthwaite T.; Di Martino A.; Bernhardt B.; Park B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder is associated with widespread alterations in brain connectivity, but how structural and functional networks are jointly reorganized remains unclear. Here, we show that autism is associated with altered structure-function coupling, particularly in the hierarchical organization of sensory and association systems. Using brain imaging data from 91 individuals with autism and 67 typically developing controls, we model functional connectivity from structural networks using Riemannian optimization and examine communication across multiple steps. In the resulting simulated networks, hierarchical organization is comparable between groups at lower communication steps but becomes less differentiated in autism as communication extends across multiple steps. These alterations are associated with excitation/inhibition alterations, neurotransmitter distributions, gene expression, and multisensory processing. We also identify atypical connectivity involving the thalamus and putamen. Importantly, greater hierarchical distortion predicts more severe autistic symptoms, linking macroscale network organization with neurobiology and behavior. These findings highlight hierarchical structure-function coupling as a potential framework for understanding biological and behavioral characteristics in autism.

Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomic insights into conserved and divergent oligodendrocyte lineage programs across species
Article.Authors: Han X.; Zuo L.; Zhang Z.; Yu Y.; Hu J.; Long Q.; Tian X.; Wei J.; Zhang R.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLLCs) are essential for myelination and neuronal homeostasis, yet the evolutionary conservation of their transcriptional programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated approximately one million hippocampal single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomes from humans, rhesus macaques, cynomolgus macaques, and mice. OLLCs emerged as among the most evolutionarily conserved neural cell populations, with oligodendrocyte precursor cells exhibiting highly conserved transcriptional identities, whereas mature oligodendrocytes displayed greater species-specific diversification We identified evolutionarily divergent genes, including the primate-specific gene CNDP1, and uncovered a species-specific temporal shift of the transcription factor ETV1 during oligodendrocyte differentiation. Cross-species analysis of aging revealed conserved chromatin-regulatory programs together with species-specific aging signatures, including coordinated remodeling of a primate-specific Wnt regulatory network in primate OPCs, whereas aged mouse OPCs were enriched for ribosome biogenesis. Disease-risk signatures further underscore the involvement of OLLCs in neurological disorders. Together, these findings provide a comparative framework for understanding mammalian myelin biology, brain aging, and disease.

Article.Title: A role for the BBSome in restricting the entry of non-ciliary proteins into cilia
Article.Authors: Cevik S.; Yenisert F.; Kantarci H.; Pucak D.; Gallrein C.; Stöckl S.; Dünninger X.; Cakici O.; Stigloher C.; Kirstein J.; Kaplan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cilia possess the inherent ability to restrict the entry of non-ciliary components through the ciliary gate. Mutations in genes encoding components of the ciliary gate result in various cilia-related diseases known as ciliopathies. Yet, how non-ciliary residents are prevented from accumulating in cilia remains unclear. Here, we observe ciliary accumulation of non-ciliary proteins in BBSome-deficient mutants (Bardet-Biedl syndrome), a phenotype reminiscent of ciliary gate-defective mutants such as mks-5 and nphp-4 . Time-lapse imaging shows that these non-ciliary proteins move bidirectionally along cilia at IFT velocities, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) reveals that the non-ciliary protein ELMD-1 associates with the IFT component IFT-43 in BBSome-deficient mutants, indicating that they are mis-loaded onto IFT trains. This misloading allows them to bypass the ciliary gate. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) suggests the gate remains largely functional, supporting a potential two-step model of ciliary composition control: cargo selection/loading and ciliary gating. We propose that defects in cargo selection/loading (and potentially export) alter ciliary composition, allowing unintended protein entry.

Article.Title: Inhibition of spinal astrocytic GPR177 attenuates neuropathic pain by modulating C3/C3aR signaling in male rats
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Yang M.; Li A.; Liu Y.; Guo K.; Yang Y.; Yao Y.
Article.Abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) remains refractory to conventional therapy partly because its pathogenesis is incompletely understood. G protein-coupled receptor 177 (GPR177), a multi-pass transmembrane protein, regulates Wnt trafficking and secretion. Here, we use a chronic constriction injury model in male rats and find GPR177 predominantly expresses in spinal astrocytes and co-localizes with complement component 3 (C3). Gpr177 silencing with siRNA alleviates nerve injury-associated hypersensitivity and reduces the increases in GPR177, glial fibrillary acidic protein, C3, and C3aR. Intrathecal administration of the C3 inhibitor compstatin and the C3aR antagonist SB290157 reduces hypersensitivity and suppresses C3/C3aR activation, supporting the involvement of C3/C3aR signaling in NP development. These findings demonstrate that spinal GPR177 contributes to NP by activating astrocytes and regulating the C3/C3aR signaling pathway, suggesting the GPR177/C3/C3aR axis as a potential therapeutic target for NP.

Article.Title: Anatomical differences in the brain organization between Australopithecus and early Homo based on computational neuroanatomy
Article.Authors: Amano H.; Tanabe H.; Bruner E.; Ogihara N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Encephalization is a hallmark of human evolution, but how regional brain morphology changed during early hominin evolution remains unclear. Here, we show regional brain morphological differences between sampled Australopithecus and early Homo specimens. Using computed tomography and endocranial casts, we generated brain models for Australopithecus africanus , Homo habilis , and Homo ergaster using an anatomically homogeneous cross-species interpolation technique. Our reconstructions suggest that the posterior cerebellum was enlarged in early Homo compared with the sampled A. africanus specimens. In contrast, relative frontal lobe volume remains largely unchanged among the sampled fossils. We also identify enlargement of temporoparietal regions that, in modern humans, are associated with functions including social communication and tool use. By integrating fossil endocranial morphology with comparative neuroanatomical information from extant primates, the present approach provides a quantitative framework for generating and testing hypotheses about regional brain evolution in extinct hominins.

Article.Title: Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity
Article.Authors: Yeo J.; Chae J.; Kwon S.; Han J.; Kusen I.; Lim J.; Lee H.; Kim H.; Haam S.; Cheong J.; Kim T.; Moon S.; Jung Y.; Lee J.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: Wnt proteins regulate adult tissue homeostasis and repair by driving stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. High-performance Wnt preparations have enormous therapeutic potential, especially alongside various stem cell technologies. Currently, a major limitation of most Wnt preparations is that they inevitably require fetal bovine serum (FBS) or detergents to maintain Wnt solubility and activity. Recently, afamin (AFM) was identified as a serum factor that solubilizes Wnt3a in conditioned media (CM), obviating the requirement for animal sera. Here, we show that serum albumin (SA) helps maintain the activity and stability of AFM-solubilized Wnt3a in CM, likely through a stabilizing effect. We further demonstrate, using test-tube assays, that SA alone efficiently solubilizes purified Wnt3a (pWnt3a) independently of AFM. This approach enables the conversion of conventional detergent-solubilized pWnt3a (CHAPS-pWnt3a) into SA-pWnt3a through dialysis-mediated detergent removal. Together, these findings define a simple and robust SA-based strategy for preserving Wnt3a activity, addressing a long-standing challenge in both experimental and therapeutic settings.

Article.Title: Dysregulation of the Hippo pathway enhances PD-L2 transcription to promote immune evasion in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ando T.; Okamoto K.; Sato K.; Goto Y.; Izumi H.; Kataoka N.; Ueda Y.; Kobayashi Y.; Omachi K.; Maeda Y.; Furusho H.; Iglesias-Bartolome R.; Yoshimoto T.; Shintani T.; Yanamoto S.; Miyauchi M.; Gutkind J.; Kajiya M.

YAP/TAZ predominantly contribute to PD-L2 expression, which is associated with Stat3 activation, partially enhancing PD-L1 transcription. YAP/TAZ-activated cells can be targeted by antigen-specific T cells but evade them through PD-L2. These findings suggest that Hippo pathway alterations and associated YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may serve as potential prognostic factors for stratifying patients undergoing ICI therapy. Targeting YAP/TAZ/TEAD could offer a promising treatment avenue for cancers harboring YAP/TAZ hyperactivation.

Article.Title: Hdac3 shapes adipocyte size, death susceptibility, macrophage turnover, and vascular remodeling in a mouse model of obesity
Article.Authors: Coppi L.; Severi I.; Bonacina F.; Villa S.; Peri C.; Longo R.; Senzacqua M.; Perugini J.; Galli C.; Pedretti S.; Mitro N.; Catapano A.; Norata G.; Giordano A.; De Fabiani E.; Crestani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The crosstalk between adipocytes and macrophages is crucial in adipose tissue biology. Here we show that adipocyte-specific deletion of Hdac3 gene in mice affects the response to high-fat overload, by reducing fat mass and adipocyte size in visceral fat of knockout mice. This is coupled with increased crown-like structures and adipocyte death in visceral fat of knockout mice, exacerbated by high-fat feeding. Hdac3 silencing in cultured adipocytes and inactivation in mice promotes a pro-apoptotic microenvironment, as assessed by positivity to Annexin V and cleaved Caspase 3. In conclusion, we propose that Hdac3 acts as a rheostat in visceral fat, differentially affecting lipid accumulation and adipocyte size during the progress of high fat diet (HFD) feeding, and limiting cell death, vascularization, and macrophage proliferation, in a mouse model of obesity.

Article.Title: Relationship between X chromosome mosaicism, neuroanatomy and cognitive performance in females
Article.Authors: Karipidis I.; Klabunde M.; Jordan T.; Chromik L.; Hosseini S.; Reiss A.; Hong D.
Article.Abstract: Females have two X chromosomes, one of which is inactivated early in development with specific regions and genes ‘escaping’ inactivation. Thus, X chromosome loss putatively results in decreased ‘dosage’ of X chromosome escapee and pseudoautosomal genes, impacting downstream pathways. Evidence from Turner syndrome (TS) indicates that X chromosome monosomy results in consistent neuroanatomical and cognitive phenotypes. However, it remains unclear whether mosaic karyotypes, with mixed proportions of 45X and 46XX cells, attenuate these phenotypes. Using support vector regression, we examined whether X chromosome mosaicism is predicted by features derived from structural brain MRI and neurocognitive assessments of 48 pre- and early pubertal girls with monosomic TS, with mosaic TS, and without TS. Higher proportion of 46XX cells was significantly predicted by structural properties in somatosensory, motor, visual, and language brain areas, and by performance in visuospatial, fine-motor, and language tasks. Thus, mosaicism partially ‘rescues’ phenotypes linked to full 45X monosomy and may explain the role of the X chromosome not only across heterogeneous phenotypic expression in females, but also in sex differences observed in neuropsychiatric conditions. X chromosome mosaicism in Turner syndrome partly mitigates the brain and cognitive effects of X monosomy. Higher proportions of 46XX cells predict more typical brain structure and better visuospatial, motor, language, and cognitive performance.

Article.Title: FLASHS reveals multiscale spatial gene programs at atlas scale
Article.Authors: Yang C.; Zhang X.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue architecture, but detecting spatially variable genes at atlas scale remains difficult because biologically relevant patterns are multiscale, sparse, and often non-parametric. Here we show that FLASHS, a frequency-domain kernel test using random Fourier features, sparse sketching, and a kurtosis-corrected null, retains Gaussian-kernel flexibility at near-linear per-gene cost without permutation. Across 50 benchmark datasets spanning 9 spatial transcriptomics platforms, FLASHS achieves the highest ranking accuracy among 14 compared methods while maintaining calibrated inference under simulation and full-atlas permutation. In human heart tissue, it recovers a mitochondrial biogenesis program that co-localizes with ventricular cardiomyocytes. On the Allen Brain MERFISH atlas containing 3.94 million cells, FLASHS completes in minutes on a single workstation and separates biological signal from negative-control barcodes even when p -values saturate.

Article.Authors: Patel K.; Zhao X.; Xie Z.; Zhi D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

Article.Authors: Girnius N.; Vallius T.; Chen W.; Launonen I.; Palomino-Echeverria S.; Lin J.; Mills C.; Kauppila S.; Kronqvist P.; Ellonen A.; Perala M.; Withnell E.; Chen Y.; Secrier M.; Santagata S.; Sorger P.; Färkkilä A.

Article.Title: Anatid herpesvirus 1 US10 recruits TRIM13 to ubiquitinate STING for autophagic degradation and immune suppression
Article.Authors: Tian Y.; Tian B.; Xiao Z.; Ran R.; Cai D.; Wang M.; Wu Y.; Yang Q.; Zhang S.; Zhu D.; Liu M.; Zhao X.; Sun D.; Huang J.; Ou X.; Wu Z.; He Y.; Pan Y.; Jia R.; Chen S.; Cheng A.

Here we show that AnHV-1 tegument protein US10 suppresses innate immunity by targeting stimulator of interferon genes (STING) for autophagosome-lysosome degradation. US10 associates with STING and binds the autophagy-related protein microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B), enhancing delivery to lysosomes. Mechanistically, US10 recruits E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing protein 13 (TRIM13) and induces stress in the endoplasmic reticulum through the Protein kinase R-like Reticulum Kinase (PERK). These synergistic actions inhibit type I interferon (IFN-I) production and IFN-stimulated gene expression. Deletion of US10 reduces viral replication and pathogenicity while enhancing immune activation in cells and animals. Our findings uncover a dual autophagy-based mechanism of immune evasion and highlight potential therapeutic targets against AnHV-1 and related alphaherpesviruses.

Article.Title: Individualized morphometric-similarity deviations in autism linked to cortical hierarchy and microarchitecture
Article.Authors: Mamat M.; Chen Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows marked interindividual variation that complicates efforts to identify coherent neuroanatomical signatures. Here we combine subject-wise morphometric-similarity networks with hierarchical Bayesian normative regression to map per-region, per-subject departures from expected cortical organization across 308 parcels in a large multisite cohort. Normative z-maps reveal that ASD individuals have a higher prevalence of extreme, spatially focal deviations than controls, yet fewer than 12% of cases show extreme deviation in any single region. These deviations are not random: they preferentially redistribute morphometric similarity from association and heteromodal cortex toward sensory and visual territories and align with canonical cortical gradients. Network-level analyses identify a spatially localized subnetwork of altered similarity (dominant in occipito-temporal/visual nodes). Semi-supervised clustering of individual z-maps resolves a reproducible continuous axis of deviation whose opposite ends carry opposite global polarity and distinct cortical-molecular couplings revealed by transcriptomic and neurotransmitter-receptor density maps, as well as divergent cognitive meta-analytic associations. Together, these findings reframe ASD neuroanatomy as gradient-constrained and molecularly tethered at the individual level and support normative, subject-wise approaches for mechanism-informed stratification. Normative models of morphometric similarity across 1,344 brains map where each autistic individual’s cortex departs from expectation. Article.Title: Maltreatment predicts centiles of individual variation from normative brain growth in children
Article.Authors: Mohn J.; Bauer M.; Hoffmann F.; Rasmussen J.; Tietze A.; Entringer S.; Winter S.; Buss C.; Heim C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to maltreatment in childhood is posited to profoundly disrupt brain development with adverse consequences for cognitive development and health across the lifespan. Here we use “brain charts” from the largest available neuroimaging database to quantify individual brain volumes relative to normative brain growth distributions in 299 children, aged 3 to 13 years, including 123 children with clinically verified maltreatment exposure. Using magnetic resonance imaging, we obtain volumes of cortical grey, total white, and subcortical grey matter and derive chart-based centiles for each child and tissue type. Associations of greater maltreatment severity with lower brain centiles do not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Article.Title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Aziz N.; Kortagere S.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

Article.Title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang Z.; Huang Z.; Yu X.; Wang Z.; Qiu H.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. Yet it remains difficult to quantify, at genome scale, how histone-modification landscapes encode these burst kinetics. Here we show that DeepBurst, a deep learning model, predicts gene-specific burst-frequency and burst-size regimes from histone-modification profiles around transcription start sites. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

Article.Title: Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
Article.Authors: Janshoff S.; Sirkinti L.; Nocke M.; Bechtel T.; Gömer A.; Brüggemann Y.; Steinmann E.; Brown R.; Todt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

Article.Title: Identification of candidate key genes involved in natural rubber biosynthesis in Periploca sepium
Article.Authors: Lu G.; Yong J.; An Y.; Lang S.; Zhang H.; Chen R.
Article.Abstract: Natural rubber is a critical industrial material facing supply shortages. Periploca sepium has emerged as a promising alternative for producing the rubber component cis-polyisoprene. To investigate its biosynthesis, we performed genome and transcriptome sequencing. Our results indicate that this plant possesses complete mevalonic acid (MVA), 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate/2-C-methyl-D-erythritol-4-phosphate (DXP/MEP), and polyisoprene pathways, as well as contains corresponding rubber particle membrane proteins. Using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, we identified 11 key genes positively correlated with levels of cis-polyisoprene and precursor allylic diphosphates (IPP/DMAPP, GPP, FPP, GGPP). Overexpressing acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, and 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate reductoisomerase genes from the MVA and DXP/MEP pathways in P. sepium increased IPP/DMAPP levels. Molecular docking and enzyme assays indicated that cis-prenyltransferase exhibits the highest affinity for FPP, suggesting it is the dominant initiator of IPP condensation in cis-polyisoprene biosynthesis. Overexpressing the FPP synthase gene enhanced FPP levels, leading to increased cis-poly7isoprene content. Overexpressing cis-prenyltransferase, small rubber particle protein, and rubber elongation factor genes, especially in combination, significantly raised cis-polyisoprene content and high-molecular-weight proportions. These findings demonstrate that targeted gene up-regulation can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium. The candidate key genes involved in rubber biosynthesis in P. sepium were identified via genome and transcriptome sequencing combined with WGCNA. Up-regulation of the key genes by overexpression, especially in combination, can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium.

Article.Title: In vivo replication of a fully functional nerve net in a clonally reproducing animal
Article.Authors: Sakib E.; Hofacker L.; Noack C.; Ströbel F.; Giez C.; Wittlieb J.; Klimovich A.; Bosch T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nerve nets are considered the evolutionarily oldest form of nervous system. How such networks develop and how complex nervous systems become fully functional is largely unknown. In a phylogenetically ancient animal, the freshwater polyp Hydra , we demonstrate how a nerve net consisting of distinct neuronal populations is precisely replicated over the course of asexual proliferation by budding. During this process, precursor cells first accumulate at the site of the emerging neural network, followed by a stepwise formation of functional neural circuits composed of distinct neuronal populations. These circuits become arranged according to an accurately controlled spatiotemporal pattern and take control of behaviors independently of the existing parental network. Since similar processes also govern the formation of more complex nervous systems in other invertebrates and vertebrates, we suggest that the basic requirements for a neuronal network to replicate were already in place at the beginning of the evolution of the nervous system.

Article.Title: Evolution towards higher unitary conductance in mammals makes BK channels more efficient and precise
Article.Authors: Hepburn I.; Hellemans S.; Taniguchi T.; Bourguignon T.; De Schutter E.
Article.Abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. We show that mammalian BK channels are activated more efficiently by calcium and generate stronger repolarizing currents than lower unitary conductance channels. Channels with lower unitary conductance require greater channel density in the cell membrane, leading to stronger competition for calcium and reduced activation. In contrast, high unitary conductance channels minimize competition, enabling more effective activation and repolarization. Incorporating these channel properties into a neuronal model revealed that mammalian-type BK channels enhance spike-timing precision, consistent with the evolution of fine motor control and advanced neuronal processing in mammals.

Article.Authors: Brosseau N.; Pincez T.; Lo K.; Lo C.; Beaudoin M.; Lettre G.

Article.Authors: Klaourakis K.; Kulkarni S.; Zvonickova K.; Kalisch-Smith J.; Smart N.; Sparrow D.; Jackson D.; Riley P.; Vieira J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The genetic mouse model Lyve1 Cre is widely used to study lymphatic endothelial cells, but its activity in the embryonic heart has not been comprehensively defined. Article.Authors: Wang H.; Kroeschell G.; Zhu Y.; Mumm J.; Yi J.

Article.Authors: Krishna N.; Menon A.; Kumaran M.; Kesireddy D.; Venkatesh I.
Article.Abstract: Adult central nervous system neurons fail to regenerate after injury, in part due to epigenetic constraints that maintain a growth-restrictive chromatin state. Nucleosome eviction at these sites likely helps in enhancer activation, establishing a mechanistic link between chromatin reorganization and transcriptional reprogramming. Such efforts are critical to establish a robust consensus of scientific data to support effective management of reef deoxygenation. Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid droplet (LD) size is a key determinant of hepatic lipid metabolism, yet the molecular programming routing size-defined subpopulations to distinct fates remains unclear. Moreover, comparative proteomics of fasted livers reveals a clear ‘division of labor’: Large LDs (L-LDs) function as specialized mitochondrion-coupled ‘putative fueling hubs’, whereas small LDs (S-LDs) serve as lysosome-coupled ‘putative trafficking and turnover hubs’. This interaction map is highly plastic; metabolic stress (fasting or steatosis) triggers a programmatic remodeling where lysosomal machinery is inducibly recruited to S-LDs. Crucially, in vivo stress recruits mitochondria to both pools, supporting a ‘parallel programs’ model where S-LD-associated mitochondria are hypothesized to power the energy-intensive degradative machinery. These findings establish that metabolic state leverages LD size to direct organelle partnerships, nominating the small-LD lysosomal axis as a critical regulatory node in metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD).

Article.Title: Vascular tree structure-based perfusion phantom fabrication using modified Hele-Shaw cell method
Article.Authors: Das S.; Rakshe M.; Sarkar S.; Paul R.; Marathe S.; Abraham N.; Gandhi P.; Varma H.
Article.Abstract: Tissue phantoms mimicking microvasculature and perfusion are essential for vasculature modelling and calibrating imaging systems, which require faithful replication of vascular geometry and flow. Conventional fabrication methods, including lithographic micromachining and additive manufacturing remain constrained by predefined designs, rectangular channel cross-sections, limited scalability, and high production costs. Here we present a lithography-free approach based on a modified lifted Hele-Shaw cell method where, unlike above-mentioned methods, random fractal-like vascular structures emerge naturally. This results in channels of widths 100-1000 μ m with smooth Gaussian cross-section and natural diameter tapering. We demonstrate this with four phantom designs: a planar vascular tree, a cerebral vasculature-mimicking guided tree network, a conformable curved substrate and a retinal vasculature-mimicking network. Flow visualisation with laser speckle contrast imaging shows close agreement with in vivo observations and consistency with the generalized Murray’s law. This approach uniquely combines fractal-like network formation leading towards realistic vascular geometry and flow characteristics, offering an in vitro alternative to small animal vascular models.

Article.Title: FOXO3 induces chromatin changes in a model of DNA damage-induced senescence
Article.Authors: Brown A.; Arevalo J.; Holcom A.; Finch A.; Maybury-Lewis S.; McNamara A.; Webb A.
Article.Abstract: FOXO transcription factors are critical for cellular homeostasis and the stress response and have been implicated in longevity in several species. Yet, how these factors function at the chromatin level in differing conditions in human cells is poorly understood. Here, we take an integrated multi-omics approach to identify the chromatin-level mechanisms by which FOXO3 coordinates transcriptional programs in replicating cells and in a model of cellular senescence. In a DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 levels are elevated early in senescence entry. Increased FOXO3 expression induces expression of chromatin remodeling factors, and impacts chromatin accessibility across the genome together with SWI/SNF chromatin remodelers. As cells enter DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 is essential for chromatin remodeling and reprogramming of a genomic network that functions to modulate cell stress and lineage-specific cellular functions. Altogether, we identify a FOXO3-SWI/SNF network that regulates key cellular processes including metabolism, proteostasis, epigenetics, and cell lineage, and is dynamically controlled under DNA damaging conditions.

Article.Title: Large-scale functional overlap between dorsal and ventral object-responsive networks
Article.Authors: Simmons C.; Behrmann M.; Ayzenberg V.
Article.Abstract: The processes of acting on and recognizing objects have traditionally been attributed to dorsal and ventral visual pathways, respectively. Although extensive evidence suggests that the two pathways interact, the extent and the strength of these interactions across whole-brain networks remain unclear. In two experiments, we characterized the whole-brain network connections of object-selective regions in each pathway using functional magnetic resonance imaging data acquired while participants viewed objects. Here, we show substantial spatial overlap in connectivity networks generated from the dorsal and the ventral seed region—with greater similarity between object networks within an individual than each network shows across individuals. This overlap persists across viewing of tools and non-tools and even after controlling for the shared variance between pathways. Together, these findings reveal that dorsal and ventral pathways form highly overlapping and distributed networks in the service of object perception.

Article.Title: Estradiol deficiency aggravates AngII-induced vascular remodeling by failing to inhibit GRK2 through ERα-mediated autophagy
Article.Authors: Ji M.; Song N.; Adu-Amankwaah J.; Liu C.; Wang G.; Zhou W.; Hao Y.; Shi Y.; Wu J.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension acts as a critical cardiovascular risk factor that drives vascular remodeling, which manifests as vascular media thickening triggered by excessive proliferation and migration of vascular smooth muscle cells. Angiotensin II promotes vascular remodeling by upregulating G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2. Estradiol deficiency, particularly among postmenopausal individuals, increases susceptibility to hypertension by overactivating the renin-angiotensin system, while the precise mechanism remains unkown. Here we show that estradiol inhibits G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 to ameliorate hypertensive vascular remodeling. Ovariectomy in spontaneously hypertensive rats exacerbate hypertension, while estradiol supplementation significantly reduced blood pressure and attenuated vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, Estradiol downregulated G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 expression, leading to decreased β-arrestin2 recruitment and ERK signaling, thereby reducing vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration. Additionally, Autophagy or estrogen receptor α blockade abolishes the effects of estradiol on G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 degradation. This study provides a potential therapeutic strategy for hypertensive vascular remodeling. Ji and colleagues show that estradiol (E2) enhances autophagy and ERalpha-AMPK signaling in a mouse model of hypertension and vascular remodeling.

Public functional genomics data revealed downregulation of LPLAT7/LPGAT1 gene expression in failing human hearts and murine cardiomyocytes. Article.Title: A Colletotrichum orbiculare-based fungal model recapitulates conserved cellular defects of Niemann–Pick type C disease and enables therapeutic evaluation
Article.Authors: Sano H.; Takezawa S.; Saomoto N.; Chiba A.; Tanaka C.; Kato N.; Nishiuchi T.; Nishisaka H.; Kitatani K.; Kodama S.; Kubo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Niemann–Pick type C disease is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in NPC1 or NPC2 , leading to lipid accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration. Current mammalian models recapitulate major pathological features but are limited by long disease courses and low throughput. Here, we establish the plant-pathogenic fungus Colletotrichum orbiculare as a scalable eukaryotic model of Niemann–Pick type C disease. Introduction of disease-associated mutations into fungal NPC1 or NPC2 homologs abolishes pathogenicity, showing that NPC dysfunction compromises lipid-dependent morphogenesis required for host penetration. Conversely, human NPC1 partially restores fungal infection. Together, these findings support functional conservation of NPC-dependent cellular processes across kingdoms. Miglustat and 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin restore pathogenicity through distinct lipid pathways. These complementary modes of rescue indicate that NPC1 and NPC2 dysfunction converges on lipid-dependent morphogenesis closely linked to actin organization. By connecting lipid metabolism, actin organization, and pharmacological rescue to a measurable infection outcome, this fungal model provides a tractable and scalable platform for mechanistic and therapeutic exploration.

Article.Title: Microglial Transmembrane 119 (Tmem119) is Protective in Ischemic Stroke
Article.Authors: Misrani A.; Xu Y.; Wang J.; Tanifum E.; McCullough L.; Liu F.; Ngwa C.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Microglial responses to cerebral ischemia are tightly regulated by inhibitory pathways that limit excessive post‐stroke inflammation. Transmembrane protein 119 (Tmem119) has emerged as an important regulator of microglial activation and neuroinflammatory signaling. We investigated the role of microglial Tmem119 during acute ischemic stroke using primary microglia and a young adult mouse model. Primary microglia were transfected with Tmem119‐siRNA and subjected to oxygen–glucose deprivation (OGD) alone or combined with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation. In vivo, young adult male mice received stereotaxic injection of lenti‐Tmem119 or lenti‐GFP for 4 weeks before 60 min of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Tmem119 expression and inflammatory responses were assessed by qPCR, Western blotting, and ELISA at 1 and 3 days after stroke. Infarct volume and neurobehavioral outcomes were also evaluated. Tmem119 silencing significantly increased IRAK4, IRF5, and CD68 mRNA expression in primary microglia. Ischemic injury reduced microglial Tmem119 protein expression and increased IRAK4 signaling in vivo. In contrast, lenti‐Tmem119 treatment before MCAO decreased phosphorylated IRAK4 protein expression and increased IL‐10 levels in both plasma and ischemic brain tissue compared with lenti‐GFP controls. Tmem119 overexpression also significantly reduced infarct volume and improved neurobehavioral outcomes. These findings demonstrate that microglial Tmem119 exerts a protective anti‐inflammatory role during the acute phase of ischemic stroke by suppressing IRAK4‐mediated inflammatory signaling and enhancing IL‐10 production. Collectively, Tmem119 limits microglial activation, reduces ischemic brain injury, and improves functional recovery, identifying Tmem119 as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

Article.Title: Plcg2 Deficiency Leads to Sex‐Associated Divergent Effects on Glial Transcriptomes
Article.Authors: Hartigan K.; Dabin L.; Kersey H.; Jury‐Garfe N.; Sharify A.; Kim B.; Lamb B.; Bissel S.; Lasagna‐Reeves C.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Plcg2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase C signaling enzyme expressed predominately in microglia in the brain. Article.Title: Reactive Astrocyte‐Associated IL‐33 Signaling Contributes to a Protective Neuroimmune State During Chronic Toxoplasma gondii – Plasmodium berghei Coinfection
Article.Authors: Leleu I.; Keswani T.; Herbert F.; Picavet C.; Arnaud M.; Marion S.; Glineur C.; Pied S.

Our findings identify reactive astrocytes as key components of a regulated neuroimmune environment associated with protection against ECM during chronic T. gondii coinfection. These results highlight astrocyte‐associated IL‐33/ST2 signaling and ILC2 recruitment as components of a multicellular neuroimmune network that contribute to disease tolerance during polymicrobial CNS infections.

Article.Authors: Xu J.; Wang H.; Yang S.; Zhang K.; Liao X.

Article.Authors: Adachi T.; Suyama K.; Ito S.; Isogai E.; Sone M.; Hoshino M.

Article.Title: A Glial Interplay Regulates Junctional Architecture at the Blood–Brain Barrier of Drosophila
Article.Authors: Contreras E.; Naffin E.; Collins‐Ramírez M.; Surina N.; Rothermel M.; Salazar‐Tirado J.; Schirmeier S.; Klämbt C.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Neurons require a tightly controlled ion and metabolite homeostasis, which is maintained by an effective blood–brain barrier (BBB). In contrast, in PG‐ablated pupae, moody expression is impaired in SPG and pSJs progressively split, producing ectopic junctional strands. Article.Authors: Manrique‐Castano D.; ElAli A.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The pathobiology of ischemic stroke is associated with the activation of brain platelet‐derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) β + perivascular cells. Moving beyond the qualitative descriptors, we sought to develop point pattern analysis (PPA) and topological data analysis (TDA) workflows to generate robust and reusable mathematical models to assess spatial cell responses and tissue scar topological changes. Notably, the conditional attenuation of KLF4 expression specifically in reactive PDGFR β + cells does not alter spatial cellular distribution nor scar organization. This suggests that, in contrast to peripheral PDGFR β + cells upon ischemic insults, KLF4 is not a main regulator of the reactivity of brain cells in response to ischemic stroke. Ultimately, our findings supported by open‐source spatiotemporal models indicate that the reactivity of brain PDGFR β + perivascular cells is highly heterogeneous and fundamentally distinct from peripheral PDGFR β + cells.

Article.Title: sox17 Mutagenesis Reveals Compounding Effects ofMaternal and Zygotic Contribution on Microglia Abundance
Article.Authors: Spring C.; Dennen J.; Gan D.; Li J.; Smith C.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Embryonic development is shaped by maternal and zygotic factors but how the interplay between these factors contributes to phenotypic variability and impacts specific populations of brain cells, and subsequently neurodevelopment, remains largely unknown. We demonstrate that microglia deficits are exacerbated in homozygous offspring from homozygous parents compared to homozygous offspring from heterozygous parents, suggesting a compounding effect of maternal and zygotic sox17 mutation on microglia abundance. We observe that sox17 is expressed in microglia and yolk sac precursors and is maternally contributed. Transcriptional and mutant analyses with these genes suggest sox17 positively regulates mpp1 transcription. These results demonstrate that microglia are susceptible to additive effects of maternal and zygotic sox17 mutation, and that offspring greatly differ in their susceptibility to microglia deficits depending on the mother's genotype. Article.Title: Disruption of Lactate Metabolism in the Peripheral Nervous System Leads to Motor‐Selective Deficits
Article.Authors: Bloom A.; Tendulkar S.; Hackett A.; Strickland A.; Sato‐Yamada Y.; Yuan L.; Dong W.; Ippolito J.; Schmidt R.; Sasaki Y.; DiAntonio A.; Milbrandt J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Schwann cells (SCs) myelinate and provide trophic support to axons in the peripheral nervous system (PNS). Disrupted SC metabolism can lead to demyelination and axon degeneration, cardinal deficits in peripheral neuropathy. The lactate shuttle hypothesis proposes that glycolytic support cells supply lactate to axons to sustain their high metabolic demands. This transfer requires lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to interconvert lactate and pyruvate in both SCs and neurons. To test the importance of lactate metabolism in the PNS, we selectively knocked out both LDHA and LDHB in ChAT‐positive neurons, including motor neurons (MNs), Nav1.8‐lineage sensory neurons (SNs), or SCs. Interestingly, motor axons and their synapses progressively degenerate when LDH is deleted from either MNs or SCs, but defects in Nav1.8‐lineage sensory axons and their terminals are not observed when LDH is excised from either SNs or SCs. Deletion of LDH in SCs leads to decreased ATP in peripheral nerves despite marked accumulation of pyruvate and glycolytic intermediates, consistent with energetic deficits due to failed conversion of pyruvate to lactate. Cholinergic neuron‐specific gene expression using ribosome affinity profiling (RiboTag) identified a strong response to metabolic compromise by activating axon‐injury stress programs in LDH‐deficient neurons. Finally, blocking axon degeneration in LDH‐deficient mice by SARM1 deletion preserves axon morphology without ameliorating behavioral and electrophysiological defects, demonstrating functional decline of lactate‐deprived axons that remain physically intact. These results show a differential requirement for SC‐derived lactate by motor vs. sensory axons, suggesting that lactate availability could influence the course of motor neuron diseases.

Article.Title: Astrocytic <scp>EAAT</scp> ‐2 Upregulation Supports Neuro‐Axonal Homeostasis in Chronic Inflammatory <scp>CNS</scp> Lesions
Article.Authors: Reukauf L.; Margineanu A.; Muinjonov B.; Chen J.; Cui Y.; Rosiewicz K.; Radbruch H.; Munro I.; Alisch M.; Siffrin V.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Neuronal loss in multiple sclerosis (MS) is a key factor in the progression of disability. Axonal degeneration within MS lesions is central to progressive MS pathology, yet its mechanisms are not fully understood. Excess extracellular l‐glutamate (GLUT) is neurotoxic due to overstimulation of GLUT receptors. Excitotoxicity, driven by GLUT, is a suspected contributor to several central nervous system (CNS) diseases. Astrocytic glutamate transporters EAAT‐1 and EAAT‐2 play crucial roles in managing extracellular GLUT, yet their role in chronic MS remains underexplored. Using the animal model experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and advanced microscopy in live anesthetized mice, we examined GLUT‐mediated neurotoxicity and protective mechanisms in chronic CNS lesions. By employing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors, we visualized extracellular GLUT levels and axonal Ca 2+ dynamics within the live mouse brain during EAE. In acute EAE, extracellular GLUT levels were high, while in chronic lesions, normalized GLUT levels together with sustained EAAT‐2 upregulation were consistent with a protective astrocytic response. EAAT‐2 inhibition in chronic lesions led to higher intra‐axonal Ca 2+ levels and morphological changes consistent with neuroaxonal injury, indicating that EAAT‐2 upregulation may counter excitotoxicity and support neuroprotection. Post‐mortem MS brain tissue analysis provided complementary evidence, showing elevated EAAT‐1 and EAAT‐2 expression in chronic MS lesions with expression patterns varying according to lesion type and cellularity. This study highlights astrocytic mechanisms that may contribute to neuroaxonal protection in MS tissue and suggests targeting GLUT transporters as a promising strategy to limit neurodegeneration in progressive MS.

Article.Title: Single‐Cell Integration of Mouse Models of Autism Reveals Conserved Transcriptomic Signatures of Excitatory‐Inhibitory Imbalance and Glial Dysfunction
Article.Authors: Nani J.; Duque V.; Muotri A.; Mecawi A.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The etiological heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) complicates identifying core molecular mechanisms. We systematically integrated scRNA‐seq data from 11 diverse genetic and environmental mouse ( Mus musculus ) models, encompassing > 300,000 cells across multiple brain regions and developmental stages. Using advanced computational harmonization (RPCA), we identified robust convergent transcriptomic signatures that transcend model‐specific variability. Our findings reveal widespread alterations in neuronal communication pathways, specifically increased excitatory‐inhibitory signaling involving PTN, SLIT, and PTPR pathways. Furthermore, cell–cell communication analysis via NicheNet prioritized ligand‐receptor pairs associated with altered circuit excitability, offering a predictive blueprint of dysregulated intercellular crosstalk. Crucially, we identified significant glial involvement characterized by astrocyte function inhibition, marked by Aqp4 and Kcnj10 downregulation related to impaired water/potassium homeostasis and mature oligodendrocyte metabolic dysregulation through Olig family upregulation and enhanced oxidative phosphorylation. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) significantly overlapped with SFARI‐listed high‐confidence risk genes, particularly within excitatory neuronal subtypes. Comparison with human postmortem single‐nucleus data from the prefrontal and parietal cortices demonstrated conserved signatures related to impaired synaptic protein synthesis (GRIN2B, CAMK2A) and oligodendrocyte‐mediated neurodevelopmental deficits (NRXN, DLGAP). This study confirms that E/I imbalance and glial dysfunction are universal cellular pathologies in ASD, providing a robust, large‐scale reference for identifying novel therapeutic targets with single‐cell resolution.

Article.Title: A Müller Glia‐Retinal Pigment Epithelium Apical Network Surrounding Cone Outer Segments in Fish and Mouse
Article.Authors: Sharkova M.; Housset M.; Boudreau S.; Dworkind C.; Amidian S.; Cayouette M.; Hocking J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Homeostasis of the vertebrate retina critically depends on two non‐neuronal cell populations, Müller glia and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Their opposing apical surfaces delineate the subretinal space, a specialized extracellular compartment housing the light‐detecting outer segments of photoreceptors. Although the individual interactions between these supporting cells and photoreceptors have been extensively characterized, Müller glia and the RPE have long been presumed to remain physically separate in the healthy retina. Here, we challenge this assumption and present a revised model of the subretinal space architecture based on detailed FIB‐SEM and confocal microscopy imaging of the zebrafish and mouse outer retina. We demonstrate that both Müller glia and the RPE extend long apical processes that not only contact one another but also collectively ensheath cone outer segments, forming a previously unrecognized tripartite interface. These contact regions are highly elaborated in fish and, while comparatively sparser, are still present in mouse. Developmentally, the growth and interdigitation of Müller glial and RPE apical processes follow the emergence of the outer segment in both species and, in mouse, coincides with the onset of visual function. Although glial–RPE interactions are enriched at cone‐associated sites, their presence is not strictly dependent on cone localization in either species, suggesting they represent a fundamental feature of the vertebrate subretinal space. Together, these findings revise our understanding of the subretinal space cytoarchitecture and reveal a previously unappreciated structural interaction between Müller glia, RPE, and photoreceptors that is conserved across vertebrate species.

Article.Title: <scp>CD47</scp> – <scp>SIRPα</scp> Axis as a Target for Neuroprotection
Article.Authors: Gómez‐López A.; Manich G.; Penas C.; Pampalona J.; Villacampa N.; Almolda B.; Viennois E.; Rojas S.; González B.; Castellano B.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Microglial “Off” signaling is crucial for maintaining microglia in a homeostatic state through the interaction of “Off” neuronal ligands with their corresponding microglial receptors. Dysregulation of “Off” signaling has been reported in both acute and chronic neuroinflammation; however, the influence of inflammatory mediators on this pathway remains underexplored. Here, we investigated whether chronic IL‐6 or IL‐10 overexpression modulates microglia–neuron “Off” signaling after FNA, thereby accounting for the previously observed differences in facial motoneuron (FMN) survival and microglial reactivity in transgenic mouse models (GFAP‐IL6Tg and GFAP‐IL10Tg). To this end, we examined the expression of the neuronal “Off” ligands CD200, CX3CL1, CD47, and CD22, as well as their corresponding microglial “Off” receptors CD200R, CX3CR1, SIRP‐α, and CD45 in non‐lesioned and axotomized GFAP‐IL6Tg, GFAP‐IL10Tg, and WT mice across multiple time points. Our analyses revealed the dynamic regulation of “Off” signaling in both neurons and microglia during microgliosis and FMN phagocytosis and showed temporally restricted strain‐specific differences in CD47 expression across genotypes. Chronic IL‐6 overproduction promoted a more phagocytic microglial phenotype, defined by downregulation of SIRPα and CX3CR1 alongside upregulated CD45 in the microglial population. In contrast, chronic IL‐10 overproduction did not alter the expression of microglial “Off” receptors but induced an IL‐10 dependent accelerated upregulation of neuronal CD47. Our findings highlight the CD47‐SIRPα axis as a key regulator of FMN death via microglial phagocytosis and emphasize IL‐10's neuroprotective potential role through enhanced neuronal CD47 signaling. Overall, this work positions the CD47‐SIRPα axis as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate neuroinflammation‐induced neuronal loss.

Article.Title: Microglial Labeling in Mouse Spinal Cord Injury: A Review of Timing, Efficacy, and Specificity
Article.Authors: Colbert R.; Di Stefano J.; Dooley D.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is a complex and disabling condition with no curative therapy currently available. The mechanical damage of the primary injury phase is followed and exacerbated by a secondary injury phase, characterized by the release of free radicals and pro‐inflammatory cytokines that lead to chronic inflammation. Microglia, as the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, play a critical role in orchestrating this inflammatory response. Studying their dynamics after SCI not only deepens our understanding of injury pathology but also advances the development of microglia‐targeted immunotherapies. However, trauma‐induced transcriptional and phenotypic changes mean that markers used to identify homeostatic microglia may be unreliable when applied to their reactive counterparts. Another major challenge lies within discriminating resident microglia from infiltrating monocyte‐derived macrophages (MDM), which permeate the blood‐spinal cord barrier (BSCB) after injury. In this review, we examine three key variables for selecting appropriate strategies for labeling microglia in mice: (i) time (in relation to injury); (ii) efficacy (within the chosen murine SCI model); and (iii) specificity (to microglia). We discuss the transcriptional landscape of murine microglia pre‐injury and its alteration post‐injury, evaluate the strengths and limitations of commonly used markers, and highlight emerging tools and approaches for studying microglia in preclinical murine SCI research.

Article.Title: Ifi27l2a Facilitates the Recruitment of Pathogenic T Cells by Retinal Microglia in the Initiation Phase of Experimental Autoimmune Uveoretinitis
Article.Authors: Gao W.; Wu P.; Xie K.; Zhou P.; Jin B.; Zhu H.; Li F.; Wang Y.; Lei B.; Jin X.; Du L.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The mechanisms by which pathogenic T cells enter the immune‐privileged retina at the onset of uveitis remain unclear. To identify regulatory targets that promote retinal inflammation, we established an experimental autoimmune uveoretinitis (EAU) model by immunizing C57BL/6J mice with IRBP 651–670 and dynamically evaluated retinal inflammation after induction; fundus lesions were prominent, with the first 14 days representing the initiation phase, Days 14–28 the amplification phase, Days 28–35 the peak phase, and Days 35–42 the regression phase. We characterized retinal cellular alterations from the pre‐inflammatory stage to the peak stage using single‐cell transcriptomic analysis, and found that retinal immune cells changed in parallel with EAU severity, while immune‐cell interactions were strongest on Day 14, especially between microglia and T cells through multiple chemokine‐related pathways. We then identified key cell populations and candidate targets through integrated analyses and functional validation, and Ifi27l2a emerged as a core gene associated with inflammatory and immune responses in retinal microglia on Day 14. In vitro knockdown of Ifi27l2a in LPS‐activated BV‐2 cells reduced inflammatory mediator production and abolished Th1/Th17 induction. In vivo targeting of Ifi27l2a attenuated EAU severity and restored the balance of T‐cell subsets. These findings indicate that microglia are highly activated before retinal inflammation becomes prominent and that Ifi27l2a regulates this early pathogenic process.

Article.Title: Neuronal Overexpression of Glycogen Synthase Kinase‐3β Accelerates Age‐Related Glial, Vascular, and Inflammatory Remodeling of the Murine Dentate Gyrus
Article.Authors: Prádanos‐Senén A.; Rodríguez‐Moreno C.; Llorens‐Martín M.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN)—the lifelong generation of new neurons in the dentate gyrus (DG)—depends on the integrity of the subgranular zone (SGZ) neurogenic niche, which comprises astrocytes, microglia, oligodendroglial cells, and a dense vascular network. Although AHN declines during aging and is impaired in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the cell‐type‐specific alterations within the DG underlying this decline remain poorly characterized. Given the critical role of glycogen synthase kinase‐3β (GSK‐3β) in AD pathogenesis and AHN regulation, we studied how the overexpression of this kinase in dentate granule cells (DGCs) remodels the cellular and vascular composition of the DG throughout life. Using a layer‐resolved approach (SGZ vs. granule cell layer (GCL)) and mice of distinct ages (4–30 months), we quantified glial densities, cellular contacts, vascular architecture, and cytokine profiles in wild‐type (WT) and GSK‐3β‐overexpressing (GSK‐3β‐OE) mice. In the former, aging was associated with a layer‐specific reorganization, characterized by progressive astrocyte loss in the SGZ, midlife increases in GCL microglia, a reduction in oligodendroglial progenitors, and enhanced SGZ vascularization. GSK‐3β overexpression accelerated age‐related changes, triggering premature SGZ astrocyte depletion by 4 months, broader disruption featuring reduced SGZ microglial and mature oligodendrocyte densities accompanied by increased microglial morphological complexity, vascular restructuring, and a shift toward a pro‐inflammatory environment. Therefore, neuronal GSK‐3β overexpression promoted a non‐cell‐autonomous reorganization of the DG, consistent with premature remodeling of the neurogenic niche. These results provide mechanistic insights into AHN failure in AD and point to the modulation of GSK‐3β activity as a strategy to preserve DG integrity.

Article.Title: Formulation and Characterization of Coenzyme Q10-Loaded Emulsions Based on Natural Gums
Article.Authors: Veskov J.; Krstonošić V.; Nemeš T.; Ćirin D.; Mikulić M.; Kladar N.; Krstonošić M.
Article.Abstract: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is a highly lipophilic antioxidant with poor aqueous solubility, making its incorporation into delivery systems challenging. Oil-in-water emulsions containing 0.4% CoQ10, 10% olive oil, 0.5% tragacanth gum (TG) and gum arabic (GA) (0–3.0%) were formulated. Their physicochemical characteristics, CoQ10 content, antioxidant activity, rheological properties, and physical stability were investigated. The Sauter mean diameter D (3,2) ranged from 5.22 to 7.15 µm, with the smallest droplets observed in formulations containing 0.25–1% GA. CoQ10 content ranged from 84.07% to 95.93% of the theoretical amount throughout 14 days, without significant changes. DPPH radical inhibition ranged from 57.55% to 66.17%, with no significant differences among formulations. Increasing GA decreased apparent viscosity and consistency index, increased the flow behaviour index, and reduced the hysteresis loop area, indicating less pronounced shear-thinning and thixotropic behaviour. Physical stability decreased at higher GA concentrations, as evidenced by greater creaming and separation under centrifugation. The 3% GA formulation exhibited the greatest instability. These findings show that GA concentration influences rheological behaviour and physical stability, and that increasing GA does not necessarily improve emulsion stability. Overall, the results provide a basis for the design and optimization of TG/GA-based emulsions for pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food applications.

Article.Title: Transmembrane Domain-Mediated Dimerization Regulates Matrix Metalloproteinase-7-Dependent Shedding of Syndecan-2
Article.Authors: Jang Y.; Hwang J.; Yang H.; Cho S.; Un Y.; Oh E.
Article.Abstract: Syndecan-2 (SDC-2) is a cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycan whose transmembrane domain (TMD)-mediated dimerization regulates colon cancer cell behavior. In addition to functioning as a membrane receptor, SDC-2 undergoes matrix metalloproteinase-7 (MMP-7)-mediated ectodomain shedding, producing soluble fragments that promote angiogenesis and tumor progression. However, the mechanistic link between TMD-mediated dimerization and ectodomain shedding has remained unclear. Here, we show that different SDC family members exhibit distinct propensities for SDS-resistant dimer formation, which correlate with their susceptibility to MMP-7-mediated cleavage. Notably, the dimeric forms of both SDC-2 and SDC-4 were cleaved more rapidly by MMP-7, whereas dimerization-defective mutants of SDC-2 (S2GL) and SDC-4 (S4GL) displayed significantly reduced proteolytic cleavage in vitro. Conditioned media from cells expressing wild-type SDC-2 (HT29-S2W) contained elevated levels of shed SDC-2 and promoted increased migration of HT29 colon cancer cells and macrophages. In contrast, this effect was diminished in media from cells expressing the dimerization-defective S2GL mutant. Furthermore, a TMD mutant of SDC-2 identified in colon cancer patients showed impaired dimerization and decreased ectodomain shedding. Together, these findings demonstrate that TMD-mediated dimerization is required for MMP-7-dependent shedding of SDC-2 and drives tumor progression by enhancing cancer cell migration and immune cell recruitment.

Article.Title: Plant ER Proteostasis Through a Framework of Protein Load, Processing Capacity and Clearance
Article.Authors: Yoo J.; Ko K.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) must coordinate protein entry, maturation and removal to sustain plant growth and stress adaptation. Although unfolded protein response (UPR) signaling and quality control pathways are well characterized, their activation alone does not reveal which process limits ER function. Here, we propose a Load, Capacity and Clearance (LCC) framework that organizes these mechanisms by their effects on protein flux. The Load module regulates protein influx, Capacity supports productive folding, maturation, assembly and export, and Clearance removes misfolded proteins and selected portions of the ER. We examine transcriptional remodeling, translational regulation, regulated RNA decay, ER-associated degradation and selective autophagy, distinguishing mechanisms demonstrated during plant ER stress from those established in other stress responses. How these processes are coordinated, and how much each contributes to ER recovery, remain to be quantified. We outline testable predictions and experimental approaches to determine which processes limit recovery, how the timing of influx restoration affects recovery, and whether combined measurements of influx, processing and clearance explain or predict stress outcomes better than UPR markers alone. This framework may guide strategies to improve plant stress resilience and recombinant protein production.

Article.Title: 5-HT7–TrkB Heteroreceptor Complexes: A Novel Molecular Pathway May Contribute to the Antidepressant-like Effects of 5-HT7 Receptor Activation
Article.Authors: Ilchibaeva T.; Tsybko A.; Eremin D.; Shalagina M.; Naumenko V.
Article.Abstract: Serotonin receptor 5-HT7 and tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) are both key regulators of neuroplasticity implicated in the pathophysiology and treatment of depression. Although functional crosstalk between these receptors has been suggested, the underlying molecular mechanism remains unknown. Here, we investigated the physical and functional interaction between 5-HT7 and TrkB receptors at behavioral, biochemical, and molecular levels. Using males of the antidepressant-sensitive cataleptic (ASC) mouse model of depressive-like behavior, we demonstrated that repeated (9 days) activation of 5-HT7 receptors with the selective agonist LP-211 produced antidepressant-like effects in the sucrose preference test. These behavioral effects were dependent on TrkB signaling, as it was prevented by pretreatment with the TrkB antagonist ANA12. Both acute and repeated 5-HT7 receptor activation increased TrkB phosphorylation in the mouse brain, although this long-term effect was brain region- and amino acid residue-specific. To determine if these functional interactions were mediated by a direct physical association, we used co-immunoprecipitation and FRET assays. We found that 5-HT7 and TrkB form heteroreceptor complexes in vitro in neuroblastoma cells and in vivo in the mouse frontal cortex, hippocampus, and midbrain. Collectively, our findings support an oligomerization between 5-HT7 and TrkB receptors and suggest that this association may contribute to the antidepressant-like effects of 5-HT7 receptor activation.

Article.Title: Exploratory Metabolomic Characterization of HbA1c-Defined Glycemic Groups in the Qatar Biobank Cohort
Article.Authors: Bacha R.; Al Saady R.; Sumon M.; Chowdhury M.; Al-Mansoori L.; Pedersen S.
Article.Abstract: Glycemic status is commonly defined using glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), classifying individuals as normoglycemic, prediabetic, or diabetic. However, these categories may not fully capture the underlying metabolic complexity associated with early dysglycemia and disease progression. This study aimed to investigate metabolomic alterations across HbA1c-defined glycemic groups using a bioinformatics-guided approach. Targeted metabolomic profiling of EDTA plasma samples from 1752 Qatar Biobank participants was performed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS). Participants were classified as normoglycemic (NG), prediabetic (PD), or diabetic (DM) according to established HbA1c criteria. Metabolite data were integrated with clinical variables and analyzed using multivariate modeling, ROC analysis, and pathway enrichment to identify discriminatory metabolic features across glycemic states. Distinct metabolomic profiles were observed across the glycemic spectrum. The NG–PD comparison showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.64–0.69), with alterations primarily involving steroid-conjugated, lipid-related, and amino acid-associated metabolites, indicating early metabolic alterations beyond glucose metabolism. In contrast, the PD–DM comparison demonstrated stronger discrimination (AUC ~0.90), driven predominantly by carbohydrate-related metabolites, including meta_glucose, mannose, mannonate, fructose, and reduced 1,5-anhydroglucitol (1,5-AG), reflecting progressive glucose-centric metabolic dysregulation. Metabolomic profiling revealed distinct patterns of metabolic alterations across HbA1c-defined glycemic groups, with modest differences between normoglycemia and prediabetes involving steroid-, lipid-, and amino acid-related metabolites, and more pronounced carbohydrate-related differences in diabetes. These findings provide exploratory insights into the metabolic heterogeneity associated with early dysglycemia and warrant further investigation in independent and longitudinal cohorts.

Article.Title: Fungicidal Activity of N-Chlorotaurine Against Candidozyma auris
Article.Authors: Grimus T.; Coraça-Huber D.; Lass-Flörl C.; Nagl M.
Article.Abstract: N-chlorotaurine (NCT) is a well-tolerated antiseptic and anti-infective that originates from innate immunity and can be applied for topical treatment of infections of different body areas. The aim of this study was to investigate its fungicidal activity in vitro against the emerging pathogen Candidozyma auris. Five representative strains of C. auris were grown overnight in broth culture and subjected to quantitative killing assays in NCT solution. Fungal biofilms were cultivated on metal discs (A2-steel) for 1–2 weeks and incubated in NCT solution, followed by quantitative cultures and scanning electron microscopy. All strains in planktonic form were killed by NCT. At standard test conditions (1% NCT at 37 °C) at pH 7, there was a more than 3 log10 reduction in colony-forming units after 4–5 h, whereas at pH 5 the same reduction was achieved after just 2 h, with a more than 2 log10 reduction after 1 h. The addition of 5% peptone further reduced the killing time to less than 15 min (>3 log10 reduction). The viability of biofilms of C. auris was impaired in a similar way, with a 2 log10 reduction of colony-forming units after 4 h incubation time and up to 3 log10 after 6 h. At these times, no morphological changes in fungal cells were visible in electron microscopy. NCT has demonstrated fungicidal activity against C. auris similar to other yeasts. Topical application of NCT for the treatment of infections by these species, too, is conceivable, above all for wound and complicated urinary tract infections.
