Article.Title: Aberrant single-subject cortical morphological networks and their associations with multiple symptoms in generalized anxiety disorder
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Hu X.; Deng R.; Cao L.; Chai S.; Wang Y.; Li H.; Gao Y.; Gong Q.; Qiu C.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is a prevalent disorder associated with disrupted topological organization of large-scale brain networks. However, the morphological basis for network disruption and its clinical relevance remains unexplored. We constructed single-subject cortical morphological networks for 58 drug-free GAD patients and 86 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) separately based on cortical thickness, surface area, cortical volume, mean curvature, sulcal depth and local gyrification index. Between-group differences in local morphology and network topology were analyzed using general linear models. Partial correlation analyses were conducted to examine the relationship between brain alterations and clinical characteristics in GAD patients, while controlling for age, sex, education years and intracranial volume. Compared with HCs, GAD patients showed increased thickness in the left middle temporal gyrus and decreased local gyrification index in the left superior frontal gyrus. At the network level, GAD patients exhibited increased local efficiency, normalized clustering coefficient, and small-worldness, alongside decreased characteristic path length in cortical volume-based networks. Local morphology and network topological properties were associated with clinical characteristics such as illness duration, age of onset, anxiety severity, and personality traits. Our findings revealed both region-specific cortical abnormalities and global network reorganization in GAD patients. In particular, the shift toward stronger small-world configurations suggests enhanced local integration and global communication efficiency. These results highlight that GAD is associated not only with focal cortical alterations but also with systemic structural network changes that ma y underlie excessive anxiety and personality traits associated with the disorder.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of long-acting injectable aripiprazole in bipolar disorder: a multinational real-world target trial emulation
Article.Authors: Hsu C.; Hung K.; Carvalho A.; Berk M.; Tseng P.; Lai Y.; Lin Y.; Liang C.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Long-acting injectable (LAI) aripiprazole is approved for maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder (BD), but real-world efficacy and safety evidence remains limited. Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a target trial emulation among patients with BD who initiated oral aripiprazole between 2017 and 2023. Patients switching to LAI within one month were compared with those continuing oral therapy. After 1:1 propensity score matching on demographics, comorbidities, prior treatments, and laboratory data, hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for nine efficacy and safety outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with prespecified sensitivity and subgroup analyses. After matching, 1814 LAI and 1814 oral aripiprazole users were followed for a mean of 1.6 years. LAI use was associated with reduced all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.77, 95%CI 0.69–0.85) and emergency department visits (0.88, 0.79–0.98), with no difference in suicidal ideation or behavior (0.90, 0.75–1.08) or all-cause mortality (0.86, 0.55–1.37). Article.Title: Cyclopurine DNA lesions and repair in individuals with bipolar disorder and their unaffected siblings
Article.Authors: Arat Çelik H.; Tuna G.; Akşahin İ.; Yılmaz S.; Fettahoğlu İ.; Eslami Abriz A.; Gör C.; Çörekli E.; Kök Kendirlioğlu B.; Dal Bekar N.; Çelik Ö.; Yorguner N.; Ceylan D.
Article.Abstract: Oxidative stress plays a key role in bipolar disorder (BD). 8,5’-cyclopurine-2’-deoxynucleosides (cPUs), including R- and S-cdA, are tandem oxidative lesions that distort the DNA helix, impair replication and transcription, and are primarily repaired by the nucleotide excision repair (NER) pathway. XPB, XPF , and CSB levels were significantly higher in siblings than in the BD group, whereas XPD expression was increased in the BD group compared to both siblings and HCs. Article.Authors: Ellul P.; Marchand-Martin L.; Salmon F.; Ancel P.; Pierrat V.; Letouzey M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maternal immune activation (MIA) and preterm birth have both been associated with increased risk of autism spectrum disorder but their combined impact in preterm children is unclear. Article.Authors: Lugo V.; Güthoff Y.; Ulaganathan S.; Franzen A.; Balfanz S.; Baumann A.; Ullah G.; Fahlke C.
Article.Abstract: Vesicular glutamate transporters (VGLUTs) harness proton gradients to load glutamate into synaptic vesicles while mediating luminal chloride efflux through a channel-like conductance. Article.Title: Hippocampal CA1 neuronal ensembles efficiently discriminate routes during foraging- and homing-like task
Article.Authors: Altamira-Camacho M.; Lopez-Hidalgo M.; Olivares-Moreno R.; Carrillo-Reid L.; Rojas-Piloni G.
Article.Abstract: In natural conditions, rodents continuously explore their environment and form spatial representations that enable them to navigate and locate relevant sites. Additionally, rodents rely on a route-based navigation strategy, consisting of well-defined paths that enhance efficiency and confer survival advantages. However, the contribution of the hippocampus to route-based navigation during continuous exploration—such as searching for resources and returning home—remains largely unexplored, particularly regarding its onset and the mechanisms of route discrimination. Here, we address this gap by investigating when and how hippocampal CA1 activity differentiates between overlapping trajectories in a continuously explored environment. Using calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked neural activity as animals self-initiated routes in search of water. Our findings show that CA1 neurons rapidly establish an accurate global spatial map upon second exposure to the task. With increasing familiarity, route-specific representations progressively emerge and are maintained over the long term. Article.Title: CASCADE is an agentic AI framework for trustworthy biomarker discovery in precision oncology
Article.Authors: Yaacov A.; Gillis R.; Pomerantz A.; Purim O.; Katz D.; Peled N.; Grinshpun A.; Asna N.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous AI agents can now run end-to-end scientific analyses, yet no general method ensures those analyses are correct, and one upstream error can propagate across hundreds of downstream results at machine speed. We present CASCADE, an agentic validation framework built on mandatory, quantitatively gated analytical steps. Its central principle, specification-implementation separation, fixes what must be validated and to what standard while leaving how to the agent, so conclusions depend on the protocol rather than the model executing it. Every analysis is preserved as human-readable code with a complete decision log. Derived from a ∼25,000-patient clinical cancer genomics cohort and applied unmodified across three settings (13,424 patients), CASCADE recovered established signal, reported insufficient power instead of a false result where data were inadequate, and reversed a clinically consequential artifact (hazard ratio 0.84, corrected to 1.25). Findings were replicated in two independent multi-institutional cohorts, and three AI systems reproduced them with high fidelity.

Article.Authors: Laitifi-Navid H.; Akhavan M.; Jalali P.; Barzegar Behrooz A.; Vakili S.; Vitorino R.; Beheshti I.; Menon A.; Mutalik V.; Schroth R.; Chelikani P.; Ghavami S.
Article.Abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) progression has been increasingly linked to dysbiosis of the oral microbiome. We then applied principal component analysis, permutation testing, and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to interrogate network topology. This framework revealed an outlier-dominated rather than binary PCA structure: Fusobacterium nucleatum and Streptococcus mitis were the most separated taxa, while the remaining bacteria formed a compact central cluster. Pathobiont-associated networks emphasized inflammatory-metabolic autophagy signatures, whereas commensal-associated networks emphasized kinase-homeostasis signaling. Permutation testing and degree-preserving randomization confirmed that the explained-variance structure was non-random ( p < 0.001; Z = 19.13). Leave-one-out and bootstrap analyses supported variance robustness and recurrent gene contributions without establishing a stable signature. The Dysbiosis Index distinguished the bacterial cohorts but requires independent validation. Clinical datasets provided supportive but indirect relevance and showed concurrent activation of pathogenic and homeostatic programs. Collectively, these findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework requiring mechanistic and clinical validation.

Matched blood and tumor samples showed associations between circulating TIPARP -positive ( TIPARP +) classical monocytes, intratumoral TIPARP + macrophages, and M2-like signatures. Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Liang Z.; Xing F.; Wang X.; Chen S.; Liu J.; Xing N.; Wang Z.; Cao J.; Yuan J.
Article.Abstract: This study explores the role of histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in chronic pain-related cognitive impairment following chronic constriction injury (CCI). Moreover, HDAC2 upregulation suppressed potassium-chloride cotransporter 2 (KCC2) expression, suggesting that HDAC2 modulates synaptic plasticity through epigenetic repression of KCC2. Restoration of KCC2 expression or inhibition of HDAC2 rescued dendritic abnormalities and behavioral impairments. Restoration of KCC2 activity via the specific agonist CLP257 rescued dendritic spine abnormalities, normalized ACC neuronal hyperexcitability, and alleviated both pain and cognitive impairment in CCI mice. These findings indicate that HDAC2 contributes to neuropathic pain-related cognitive dysfunction by epigenetically suppressing KCC2, which in turn impairs synaptic plasticity and disrupts neuronal excitability in the ACC.

Article.Authors: da Silva Mazzarini Baldinotti R.; Tolstenkov O.; Kauffman P.; Aasjord A.; Chourrout D.; Chatzigeorgiou M.
Article.Abstract: Threat detection and evasion are fundamental challenges across the animal kingdom. Here, we examine threat detection and avoidance behaviors in two planktonic tunicates, Ciona intestinalis larvae and Oikopleura dioica adults, by quantifying locomotion and ecologically relevant behaviors in the presence of copepods. Both species exhibited marked increases in swimming speed, distance traveled, and roaming behavior upon predator exposure, whereas conditioned water alone had no effect. Pharmacological manipulations revealed species-specific effects of compounds targeting monoaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic signaling: in C. intestinalis , bioamine, glutamatergic, and GABAergic perturbations disrupted threat-induced movement patterning, whereas in O. dioica they suppressed motility increases. Whole-brain calcium imaging suggested that these cues engage widespread yet structured neural activity across the larval brain, recruiting distributed neuronal populations with distinct temporal response motifs. Circuit-level analysis further indicated that sensory inputs propagate through a hierarchical sensorimotor network linking peripheral neurons to central interneurons and motor outputs, supporting a distributed transformation of threat-related information into behavior. These findings uncover conserved yet mechanistically distinct antipredator strategies in two evolutionarily distant tunicates.

Article.Authors: Calzoni A.; Sans-Dublanc A.; Kühn N.; Remans D.; Fernandez de Cuevas Lopez F.; Reinhard K.; Farrow K.
Article.Abstract: The location of visual stimuli influences the actions animals select, reflecting the distinct ecological and behavioral significance of the upper and lower visual fields. Whether these circuits are repeated across visual space or are specialized by visual-field position remains unclear. Dual-color rabies tracing demonstrated that wide- and narrow-field neurons receive input from a largely shared set of brain regions, whereas upper- and lower-field domains sample these inputs differently. Multiplexed analysis of projections by sequencing (MAPseq) showed that most superficial collicular neurons project to a single downstream target, but target probabilities differ between upper- and lower-field populations. Together, these findings identify visual-field position as a major organizing principle of input and output connectivity in the superficial superior colliculus.

Article.Title: When one letter matters: Distinguishing VGF from VEGF in biomedical research
Article.Authors: Anjum A.; Jabbari Shiadeh S.; Åkesson E.; Mallard C.; Cocco C.; Ardalan M.
Article.Abstract: Scientific communication relies heavily on abbreviations to simplify complex terminology. When abbreviations are similar yet represent biologically distinct molecules; however, confusion can arise with consequences for literature interpretation, data retrieval, and scientific communication. One example is the recurring visual similarity between vascular growth factor (VGF; or proVGF), a neuroprotein precursor implicated in neuronal development, synaptic plasticity, metabolism, and neuropsychiatric disease, and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a key regulator of angiogenesis and vascular function. Although these proteins belong to entirely different biological systems, their near-identical abbreviations create a structural risk of misreading among students, researchers, reviewers, and clinicians, a risk that may grow as literature search and screening increasingly rely on automated and AI-based tools. Here, we discuss the origins of this naming overlap, contrast the distinct biological roles of VGF and VEGF, and propose practical recommendations to reduce ambiguity in scientific communication.

Article.Title: Epidemic waves and cytokine signatures of seven respiratory pathogens after COVID-19 restrictions
Article.Authors: Qin K.; Tong Z.; Zhu J.; Zhong J.; Tong Y.; Bian T.; Xu M.; Gao Q.; Zhao L.; Bao Z.; Zhao J.; Qian F.
Article.Abstract: Background: Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during COVID-19 created population-level immunity debt. Following NPI lifting in China (May 2023), clinicians face unprecedented resurgence patterns of respiratory pathogens with altered age distributions and co-infection dynamics, but comprehensive comparative cytokine profiling across diverse pathogens remains limited. Methods: We conducted a 20-month prospective-retrospective surveillance study (June 2024-January 2026) of 54,902 febrile patients, with nested cytokine profiling (n=187) across 11 groups using a 47-analyte multiplex panel. Random forest machine learning with 10-fold stratified cross-validation identified optimal cytokine panels for pathogen discrimination. Results: Three sequential epidemic waves emerged: Wave 1 (July-August 2024, SARS-CoV-2, n=1,988), Wave 2 (December 2024-March 2025, IAV, n=5,373), and Wave 3 (November 2025-January 2026, IAV+HRV, n=8,567). The 9.5% co-infection rate (2,986 cases) fell within the upper pre-pandemic range. G-CSF and IL-1Ra were universally elevated across all pathogens (1.4- to 100.2-fold and 1.8- to 41.7-fold vs. healthy controls, respectively), serving as broad inflammatory markers. Machine learning classification using five cytokines (MIF, IP-10, RANTES, G-CSF, IL-1Ra) achieved 87.3% cross-validated accuracy (95% CI 82.1-92.4%) for pathogen-group discrimination. IAV exhibited a unique IL-4-dominant profile (105.8-fold elevation, η²=0.84), while MP demonstrated distinct immune suppression (IL-16 and PDGF-BB suppressed 0.5-fold). Co-infections generated supra-additive cytokine amplification (e.g., MIG 36.6-fold in HRV+MP vs. 4.2- to 7.3-fold in single infections) and dysregulated IL-10 anti-inflammatory feedback. Conclusions: Pathogen-specific cytokine signatures enable rapid etiological inference from single plasma samples. G-CSF and IL-1Ra serve as universal ARI screening markers, while IAV-specific IL-4 elevation and MP-specific immune suppression offer diagnostic and therapeutic targets for precision medicine in respiratory infectious diseases.

Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Zhang Y.; Wang M.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer (OVCA) is one of the most common gynecological tumor and is the eighth most common cause of cancer death in women. Sex comb on midleg-like 1 (SCML1) plays an important role in the regulation of embryonic development, but its role in OVCA has not been detected. SCML1 was identified to be associated with cisplatin resistance in OVCA. The expression of SCML1 in OVCA tissues was verified by testing clinical samples. The effect of SCML1 on the proliferation and drug resistance of OVCA cells was investigated in vivo and in vitro. The expression of SCML1 is significantly lower in OVCA cisplatin-resistant tissues. Article.Title: Chronotherapy for retinopathy: Unraveling the mystery of Rev-erbα in the circadian rhythm
Article.Authors: Qu C.; Wu H.; Huang Z.; Wang Y.; Wang K.; Li S.; Pu N.; Zhang J.; Ding S.; Zhang C.; Song Z.; Tao Y.
Article.Abstract: Disruption of the retinal circadian rhythm is a common manifestation of various retinal diseases, characterized by abnormal expression of clock genes and impaired light signaling in intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs). This review aims to elucidate the mechanisms of circadian disruption in retinal pathologies, explore the interrelationship between clock genes and ipRGCs, and delineate the therapeutic potential and directions of chronotherapy for retinopathies. Through a systematic retrieval and analysis of literature on retinal diseases and circadian rhythms from databases including PubMed and Web of Science, this review reveals that Rev-erbα and melanopsin form an antagonistic system within the retina, regulating the intraocular dopamine-melatonin rhythm and maintaining retinal homeostasis. Disruption of this rhythmic system leads to oxidative stress, inflammation, and dysregulation of emotional responses. Moreover, chronotherapy, as an intervention leveraging intrinsic temporal patterns, holds significant promise for treating retinopathies associated with circadian misalignment.

Bioinformatics has shifted research into cisplatin resistance in HNSCC. Article.Title: Impact of GCR and SPE on space radiation shielding: OLTARIS simulation and quantum optimization of material selection using quantum algorithms
Article.Authors: Lalwani K.; Sreedevi V.; Gakhar M.; Agrawal D.; Tinker D.
Article.Abstract: During long-term deep-space missions, a key challenge to the human and spacecraft is the space radiation, which is coming from the three different sources: Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs), Solar Particle Events (SPEs), and trapped particles in regions of Van Allen belts. High-energy particle radiation can have harmful effects on the spacecraft systems, sensors, electronic components, and astronauts, compromising mission reliability. This makes effective shielding a critical requirement. Traditionally, passive shielding materials such as aluminum have been used, but their limitations, especially in generating secondary radiations, necessitate the search for more efficient alternatives. In this study, the performance of various shielding materials, such as Lithium hydride (LiH), Polyethylene (C2H4), Lithium borohydride (LiBH4), Beryllium borohydride (Be(BH4)2), and Ammonia borane (NH3BH3) is systematically evaluated in the GCR and SPE environment using On-Line Tool for the Assessment of Radiation in Space (OLTARIS), a NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)-developed simulation tool. Further, the effect of SPEs (October 1989) on the performance of shielding materials is studied and evaluated through particle flux distributions (energy spectrum) and equivalent dose distributions for these materials. The relative shielding effectiveness of these materials in the SPE environment varied from that in the GCR environment, suggesting that material performance is dependent on the radiation environment. Beryllium borohydride (Be(BH4)2) emerges as the best material in the SPE environment, while lithium hydride (LiH) gives the least dose equivalent in the GCR environment. The particle-wise dose equivalent and flux contributions reveal that, in the SPE environment, the material performance is directly linked to the hydrogen content of the material. In addition, the effect of solar modulation on dose equivalent in the GCR environment is studied. As solar modulation increases, the GCR intensity reduces and hence dose equivalent also reduces. As the space radiation environment consists of complex particle radiation of high energies, in order to validate the large sample of materials for space radiation shielding, the combinatorial complexity of possible configurations presents a major computational challenge. To address this challenge, the material selection problem is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model and is solved using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). By mapping OLTARIS dose-equivalent data to the Ising model and utilizing the quantum-classical hybrid approaches of VQE and QAOA, optimal shielding configurations that minimize radiation dose are identified, demonstrating the potential of Quantum Algorithms in advancing space radiation protection strategies. Our results are in agreement between OLTARIS and Quantum Optimization in the SPE environment.

Article.Title: Enabling climate action: A nexus approach for delivering co-benefits across biodiversity, water, food, and health
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Gupta H.; Díaz-José J.; McElwee P.; Tirado M.; Cherubini F.; Duchková H.; Llope M.; Vale M.; Khan S.; Ito A.; Hori M.; Eriksen S.; Tiwari L.; Phang S.; Mason-D’Croz D.; Xu X.; van Huysen T.; Herrero M.; Ricketts T.; Harrison P.; Smith P.

These patterns do not arise from technical design alone. By integrating nexus governance with Earth System Justice, the analysis indicates how cross-sectoral coordination, distributive equity, procedural inclusion, accountable finance, and knowledge pluralism can shape legitimacy and durability. Climate action is more likely to deliver sustained system-wide benefits when institutions align ecological interdependencies with social rights and responsibilities. Otherwise, promising interventions may remain partial, contested or short-lived.

Article.Title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Chen R.; Ding S.
Article.Abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

Article.Title: An integrated framework for agroclimatic, salinity, and groundwater assessment in the Jizzakh Region, Uzbekistan

Article.Abstract: Climate change, salinization, and water scarcity increasingly threaten irrigated agricultural landscapes in arid regions. Integrated assessment scores ranged from 11 to 16 points, classifying most districts as unsatisfactory in 2021 and satisfactory during 2022-2024. Zafarabad and, occasionally, Sh. Rashidov exhibited the lowest overall scores. The framework provides a practical tool for monitoring landscape vulnerability and supporting irrigation, reclamation, and salinity-management decisions.

Article.Abstract: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby defining the hydraulic niche for colonization. In contrast to previous reviews focusing on single factors, this review constructs an integrated framework linking soil hydrology with microbial ecology, supported by emerging comparative evidence. Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Fournier L.; Wymann B.; Talbot K.; Luisier R.; Patani R.
Article.Abstract: O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase (OGT) catalyzes the O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification to proteins and has been implicated in a range of diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a rapidly progressive and currently incurable neurodegenerative disorder. However, the precise mechanisms by which OGT influences ALS pathogenesis remain largely unresolved. In this study, we used human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived spinal motor neurons (hiPSC-MNs), the principal cell type that undergoes degeneration in ALS, to systematically reveal that OGT-related mechanisms regulate RNA-binding protein (RBP) nucleocytoplasmic compartmentalization. Using a combination of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) technology and small molecular pharmacology, we reveal two distinct regulatory mechanisms of RBP compartmentalization, including by intron-retaining transcript-mediated sequestration and O-linked N-acetylglucosaminylation (O-GlcNAcylation)-mediated nuclear transport. We finally examine the tractability of manipulating OGT activity in the ALS context but demonstrate that the OGT-related mechanisms governing RBP localization in healthy hiPSC-MNs are impaired in the context of ALS-causing VCP and TARDBP mutations.

Article.Title: CD8+ T cell transcriptional reprogramming toward TCF7-low cytotoxicity drives immune aging in viral ARDS
Article.Authors: Li K.; Ainiwaer K.; Song L.; Hu J.; Yang Y.; Liu Y.; Li H.; Xu S.; Wang Y.; Yin J.; Li L.; Wang X.; Hong X.; Xie L.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Viral acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) exhibits distinct clinical outcomes across age groups, but the immune mechanisms underlying this disparity remain unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic profiling, T cell receptor repertoire analysis, serum proteomics, and functional validation to characterize age-dependent T cell remodeling in influenza-associated ARDS. Adult ARDS was characterized by reduced T cell receptor diversity, expansion of CD8+ effector memory T cells, and enhanced cytotoxic programs marked by increased granzyme B (GZMB) expression compared with pediatric ARDS. At the transcriptional level, adult CD8+ effector memory T cells displayed a TCF7-low state associated with activation of a TGFB1-related RUNX3/PRDM1 program. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that TGFB1 promoted cytotoxic programming in CD8+ effector memory T cells and increased epithelial injury in a co-culture model. These findings identify age-associated CD8+ T cell remodeling as a potential mechanism contributing to immune dysregulation in viral ARDS.

Article.Title: CB1 receptor inhibition restores synaptoneurosomal alternative splicing landscape in fragile X syndrome mice
Article.Authors: Reyes-Ramírez L.; Ciaran-Alfano L.; Reixachs-Solé M.; Bergadà-Martínez A.; Galera-López L.; Martínez-Torres S.; Navarro-Romero A.; Maldonado R.; Eyras E.; Ozaita A.
Article.Abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most frequent heritable cause of intellectual disability and autism, involves impaired cognition and synaptic plasticity. Preclinical studies show that inhibition of the cannabinoid type-1 receptor (CB1R) restores key phenotypic traits in Fmr1 knockout (FX) mice. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain undefined. We analyzed the hippocampal synaptoneurosomal transcriptome and confirmed that synaptoneurosomes are an accurate representation of synaptic composition and function. Then, we analyzed this transcriptome after pharmacological CB1R inhibition in male FX mice and found that rimonabant had limited impact at the gene expression level. Notably, detailed in silico analysis of alternative splicing (AS) revealed that rimonabant reverts numerous AS events in FX mice to wild-type levels. These changes in synaptoneurosomal AS landscape suggest a novel mechanism by which CB1R targeting may restore specific AS patterns. Altogether, our results reveal new molecular alterations in FXS context that are sensitive to pharmacological treatment related to cognitive alleviation.

Article.Title: Quantifying land transfer in China: Integrating its impacts on urban economy
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang T.; Hu S.; Feng Y.
Article.Abstract: In China's hierarchical land-governance system, the central government establishes the regulatory framework, while provincial and municipal authorities adapt the implementation according to local fiscal capacity, development priorities, and spatial constraints. Despite the importance of land transfer in shaping urban economic development processes, empirical research has long relied on fragmented samples or single-scale observations, and a unified long-term dataset spanning multiple administrative levels remains unavailable. To address this gap, this study constructs a multi-level spatiotemporal dataset of land transfer in China covering the period 2000-2024 at the national, provincial, and city levels. The dataset integrates seven standardized indicators, including land supply area, transaction price, gross floor area (GFA), payment amount, floor area ratio (FAR), building density, and greenery rate. Data are compiled from official land-market disclosure platforms and verified administrative transaction records and undergo systematic quality-control procedures, including cross-source reconciliation, unit harmonization, coverage diagnostics, and outlier screening to ensure temporal consistency and spatial comparability. The resulting database supports analyses of long-term land transfer dynamics, regional heterogeneity, and multi-level governance patterns. In addition, an illustrative empirical application demonstrates the analytical utility of the dataset for examining associations between land allocation and urban economic development indicators. This dataset provides a comprehensive empirical foundation for future research on land governance, land finance, urban spatial development, and regional transformation in China.

Article.Title: LncRNA Arsa-DT is required for spermatogenesis and male fertility by regulating G2/M progression
Article.Authors: Choi H.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Lee H.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Male infertility is a major reproductive health burden worldwide, yet its molecular etiology remains largely unknown. The testis expresses numerous long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), although their involvement in the pathophysiology of male infertility remains unexplored. Here, we identified Arsa-DT, a testis-predominant divergent lncRNA of Arsa, and demonstrated its essential role in maintaining male fertility. Loss of Arsa-DT leads to subfertility, characterized by reduced sperm production, increased sperm abnormalities, and decreased serum testosterone levels. Notably, Arsa-DT deficiency alters the testosterone-to-estradiol ratio through upregulation of aromatase expression. Specifically expressed in the nuclei of spermatogonia and spermatocytes, Arsa-DT regulates spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules. Mechanistically, Arsa-DT regulates G2/M phase progression and chromosome segregation in male germ cells. Collectively, our findings identify Arsa-DT, a testis-predominant lncRNA, as a regulator of spermatogenesis by controlling G2/M phase progression of male germ cells. This study provides mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of male infertility.

Article.Title: Diversity of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates of Staphylococcus aureus and its role in membrane potential
Article.Authors: Asada Y.; Nishihama S.; Kawada-Matsuo M.; Ohdan K.; Aikawa T.; Yanamoto S.; Komatsuzawa H.
Article.Abstract: Staphylococcus aureus colonizes human skin, nasal cavity, and oral mucosa and causes opportunistic infections. Host-derived fatty acids exhibit antibacterial activity against S. aureus, but the diversity and determinants of fatty acid susceptibility among clinical isolates remain unclear. Here, we evaluated seven C14-C18 fatty acids selected from a physiologically relevant range of host-associated lipids. Linoleic acid (LA), palmitoleic acid (POA), and γ-linolenic acid (GLA) demonstrated significant antibacterial activity. We then analyzed LA and POA susceptibility in 253 clinical isolates. LA minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranged widely from 18.75 to 1,200 μM, whereas POA MICs clustered between 37.5 and 150 μM. Low-LA-susceptibility strains showed higher baseline membrane potential-associated signals and weaker LA-induced depolarization. Anaerobic culture and srrA inactivation reduced both of these signals and LA MICs. These findings indicate that membrane potential contributes to the heterogeneity of LA susceptibility and provide insight into host fatty acid-mediated control of S. aureus.

Article.Title: Minibeam radiation therapy supports CAR T therapy in a rat model of CNS lymphoma
Article.Authors: Iturri L.; Potiron S.; Sun L.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Espenon J.; Anegon I.; Ménoret S.; Soussain C.; Amigorena S.; Alcantara M.; Prezado Y.
Article.Abstract: Radiotherapy is increasingly combined with CAR T cell therapy in B cell lymphomas, but treatment outcome may depend on the irradiation modality. We evaluated minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) as a partner for CD19 CAR T cells in an orthotopic primary central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma model in immunodeficient rats. CAR T therapy prolonged survival compared with untreated controls. MBRT at 30 Gy followed by CAR T cells five days later produced the longest median survival among radiotherapy-containing regimens and improved outcome compared with conventional radiotherapy (CRT) based combinations. Histopathological findings were consistent with these survival differences. However, MBRT plus CAR T therapy did not significantly outperform CAR T monotherapy. These results indicate that MBRT provides a favorable, non-antagonistic radiotherapy context for CAR T therapy and suggest that radiation modality should be considered when designing combinations of radiotherapy with adoptive cellular therapies.

Article.Title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer’s disease using electronic records
Article.Authors: Katsuhara Y.; Khan U.; Miller Z.; Allen I.; Oskotsky T.; Sirota M.; Tang A.
Article.Abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Multi-omics profiling reveals molecular features of visceral adiposity in autonomous cortisol secretion
Article.Authors: Nakao H.; Yokomoto-Umakoshi M.; Fujita M.; Nakatani K.; Kitamura Y.; Ogasawara R.; Kaneko H.; Iwahashi N.; Nakano Y.; Fukumoto T.; Ogasawara T.; Takayanagi H.; Matsumoto T.; Izumi Y.; Eto M.; Bamba T.; Umakoshi H.; Ogawa Y.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous cortisol secretion (ACS) from adrenal adenomas increases cardiometabolic risk. Visceral adiposity is a hallmark of ACS. RNA-seq deconvolution and immunohistochemistry indicated increased macrophage infiltration. Plasma steroid metabolomics identified 11-deoxycorticosterone (11-DOC), a mineralocorticoid metabolite, as positively associated with VSR in premenopausal ACS women independent of cortisol. Mendelian randomization showed genetically predicted plasma Cer(d18:1/16:0) was positively associated with trunk fat mass. Article.Title: Probing the role of left inferior frontal gyrus in vocal motor control: Evidence from TMS and causal inference analysis
Article.Authors: Chang Y.; Guo Q.; Zhao S.; Li T.; Wu X.; Liu D.; Dai G.; Zhu X.; Chen X.; Wang L.; Liu P.; Yan N.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Beyond an established role in speech initiation and planning, the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) may contribute to sensorimotor control of speech production. A causal inference analysis (CIA) framework was developed to characterize source-space network organization. cTBS over both left aIFG and pIFG reduced vocal responses and enhanced P2 responses to pitch feedback perturbations, with no significant differences between two active stimulations. However, global dissimilarity analysis revealed greater P2-related topographic deviation from sham stimulation following aIFG stimulation than following pIFG stimulation. CIA further identified different source-space network patterns associated with aIFG and pIFG stimulation. These findings demonstrate the causal involvement of the left IFG in auditory-vocal integration and highlight the potential of CIA for characterizing distributed network organization underlying vocal motor control.

Article.Title: Development of a predictive model and nomogram using CTPA parameters for the identification of group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension
Article.Authors: Yuan H.; Cheang I.; Liang G.; Zhu X.; Xing Y.; Li W.; Liao S.; He J.; Cao Y.; Li X.; Xu Y.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to identify computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-derived predictors of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and to develop a prediction model and nomogram for non-invasive diagnosis. We retrospectively analyzed CTPA datasets from 203 patients in the training cohort and 98 patients in the validation cohort, stratified into PAH (confirmed by right heart catheterization) and non-PAH groups. Pulmonary vascular and cardiac structural metrics were measured. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression identified interventricular septal angle (IVSA), interventricular septal thickness (IVST), and right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness (RVOTW) as independent predictors. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964 and 0.969 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively, with excellent calibration and clinical utility. Article.Title: Repeated visual adaptation induces persistent behavioral and neural biases in body size perception
Article.Authors: Sang X.; Dong X.; Bao M.
Article.Abstract: Body size and shape misperception, notably body size overestimation, is prevalent among young people. It has been proposed that such a bias may stem from adaptation aftereffects caused by exposures to distorted bodies, yet whether adaptation can persistently alter daily body perception remains unclear. This study explored the long-term impacts of body size adaptation by having participants repeatedly view thin or large body images for 7 daily sessions, or comparing participants with varied experiences of exposure to the thin-ideal in life. Behavioral results revealed that repeated exposure to distorted body images persistently shifted participants' perception of body normality toward the adapting shape. ERP data showed that repeated adaptation to thin bodies or higher endorsement of the thin-ideal could enhance the early brain response bias to enlarged bodies. These findings collectively suggest that repeated exposure to distorted bodies contribute to the development of perceptual and neural response bias toward body shapes.

Article.Title: Reconstructing the genetic ancestry of the archaeological site in Amiternum: From Roman Imperial to early medieval times in Central Italy
Article.Authors: Moroni E.; Agostini V.; Ciabini D.; Colombo G.; Di Gerlando R.; Rambaldi Migliore N.; Zarivi O.; Semino O.; Achilli A.; Forgione A.; Poma A.; Olivieri A.
Article.Abstract: Central-southern Italy is pivotal for reconstructing the population history of the peninsula, yet the genetic impact of the complex demographic past in the Abruzzo region remains largely unexplored. The sample comprises one adult male from the Roman Imperial period and 15 subadults mainly from the early medieval period. Genome-wide data reveal a sharp genetic discontinuity between the two epochs. The Roman individual mirrors other Italians from the same period, characterized by significant Near Eastern ancestry. Overall, the medieval genetic structure differs from the Roman one and closely resembles that of modern Central and Southern Italians.

Article.Authors: Pan X.; Kang Y.; Zhong J.; Yu T.; Zheng L.; Wei Y.; Tan J.; Nie L.; Zhang M.; Chen N.; Zhou Q.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) are single-stranded non-coding RNAs found in eukaryotic nucleolus, and their aberrant expression is closely related to tumorigenesis. Article.Title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
Article.Authors: La Manna G.; Merella M.; Crobu A.; Pansini A.; Ceccherelli G.
Article.Abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. Most studies examine short-term, individual-level responses, limiting inference on long-term effects. Impacts vary widely by stressor, taxon, and biological outcome. Invertebrates often show positive responses linked to reef effects, though key functional traits are vulnerable. Fish responses are largely neutral except under noise, while marine mammals exhibit the most consistent negative impacts. The impact score developed here highlights taxon-specific vulnerability and offers a scalable risk-assessment tool for data-poor regions. The review calls for standardized, long-term field monitoring to support OWF expansion while safeguarding biodiversity.

Article.Title: Targeting BCL11B-mediated JAK2/STAT3 activation: A novel therapeutic strategy for Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Chen W.; Zhang Y.; Zhou X.; Yan J.; Song Y.; Shen J.; Gu X.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is driven in part by neuroinflammation. BCL11B knockdown attenuated dopaminergic neuron loss, reduced apoptosis, improved motor deficits, and partially blocked JAK2/STAT3 pathway activation in both inflammatory and MPTP-induced PD models. Mechanistically, BCL11B mediated neurotoxicity through the JAK2/STAT3 pathway, with acetylation modifications potentially modulating its activity. Article.Authors: Rajeshkumar L.; Ramesh M.; Arulmozhivarman J.; Dinesh Kumar M.; Sathishkumar M.
Article.Abstract: The accelerated global shift to EVs is revolutionizing the field of materials science, thereby making polymeric materials indispensable to all subsystems in EVs. In this context, this review provides a critical analysis of the evolution, classification, and applications of polymeric materials within the different EV subsystems, including structural composites, battery housing, thermal systems, insulation, and interior parts. Building on this classification, this review further highlights the latest advances made in the fields of fiber-reinforced polymer composites, engineering thermoplastic polymers, elastomers, bio-based, and recyclable polymers with specific performance criteria and associated challenges. Beyond their technical role, this review also focuses on aligning the technological advancements of such materials with the United Nations sustainable development goals (UN SDGs). This review also highlights relevant knowledge gaps in scaling up bio-based polymer production, the longevity of polymer housings for batteries subjected to thermal cycling, and the lack of a universally agreed-upon EV polymer recycling protocol.

Article.Title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
Article.Authors: Halling A.; Goodson B.; Hirschmann A.; Wing B.; Simpson C.
Article.Abstract: During the 70-million-year Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity over 3-fold. Unicellular eukaryotes in this environment would have faced severe constraints on movement and nutrient uptake, while nascent multicellular organisms, with larger size and collective mobility, could have gained an adaptive advantage. We experimentally tested whether viscosity-induced metabolic constraints could have selected for multicellular phenotypes, potentially driving the origin or early diversification of multicellularity. Under Snowball Earth-like viscosities, populations of unicellular green algae evolved motile multicellular forms, along with other phenotypes that optimize size and speed. As oceans warmed and viscosities decreased, the diversity of multicellular phenotypes may have allowed early multicellular organisms to exert novel physical control over their local environments. This pivotal period in Earth's history could have shaped the emergence and eventual dominance of certain multicellular lineages, highlighting a potential ecological driver of one of life's major evolutionary transitions.

Article.Title: The circulating lipidome in severe obesity
Article.Authors: Anwar M.; Highland H.; Palmer A.; Duong T.; Lin Z.; Zhu W.; Sprinkles J.; Kim D.; Young K.; Chen H.; Krishnan M.; Gutierrez A.; Roshani R.; Frankel E.; Landman J.; Gordon-Larsen P.; Fried S.; Lee M.; Fisher-Hoch S.; McCormick J.; Curran J.; Blangero J.; Meikle P.; Giles C.; Below J.
Article.Abstract: Severe obesity (SevO; BMI ≥ 40 kg/m2) is rising globally yet remains understudied mechanistically. To characterize lipidomic alterations at the species level, we analyzed Border Health Research Cohort participants with fasting plasma lipidomics and genetic data, comparing SevO (n = 185) to non-obese controls (18.5 ≥ BMI < 25; n = 393). We quantified 830 lipid species across 49 classes and assessed associations using logistic regression, orthogonal projections to latent structures discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), and network deconvolution Mendelian randomization (NDMR). SevO participants showed more adverse cardiometabolic traits. Lipidomics revealed broad dysregulation: shorter, saturated, and monounsaturated triacylglycerols were elevated in individuals living with SevO compared to controls, while lysophospholipids, plasmalogens, cholesteryl esters, and long-chain species were reduced. OPLS-DA identified over 300 lipids strongly predictive of SevO, and NDMR implicated specific triacylglycerols as potentially contributing to SevO status. Using pupillometry across three counting-task experiments, we found a dissociation between inner and overt speech. While overt speech consistently elicited pupil dilation across conditions, inner speech produced a variable dilation profile relative to baseline: pupil constriction (simple counting), no deviation (noun-phrase counting), and clear dilation (step counting; high cognitive load). Importantly, pupil size during inner speech remained smaller than that during overt speech despite task-dependent dynamics. These findings suggest that task-elicited inner speech is accompanied by lower pupil-linked arousal than overt speech, adding a state-level physiological dimension to cortical accounts of verbal processing.

Article.Abstract: Groundwater-level prediction supports water-resource management in overexploited aquifers, yet conventional data-driven models often struggle to represent pumping disturbances and contrasting shallow- and deep-aquifer responses. Deep-well performance depended on the pumping-response window, with 60-day averaged pumping providing a stable configuration. These incremental gains show that incorporating pumping disturbances and aquifer-specific response differences as process guidance can improve groundwater-level representation and provide a modeling approach for groundwater management in agricultural abstraction areas.

Article.Title: A source-target transfer learning framework with physics priors for subsurface chlorophyll reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific Ocean

Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. The framework first learns large-scale spatiotemporal vertical representations from long-term CMIP6 simulations and then adapts them using reconstructed fields constrained by BioGeoChemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) observations, reducing simulation biases while preserving regional variability. By integrating dual-attention, residual learning, and convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) architectures, ST-CoupleNet substantially improves reconstruction accuracy over a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN). Article.Title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
Article.Authors: Farhadzadeh F.; Borji A.; Aram C.; Alishvandi A.; Kamali M.; Rahimi M.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

Article.Authors: Smith Z.; Vonhoff F.
Article.Abstract: The physiological functions of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) remain unclear due to genetic redundancy and complex phenotypes. Article.Authors: Slobodian P.; Riha P.; Hausnerova B.
Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl acetate (PVAc) is a highly polar, fluorine-free polymeric adhesive that combines strong interfacial adhesion with good processability. Article.Title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
Article.Authors: Vahedi L.; Pradhan S.; Zaidi S.; Brizuela V.; Rashid S.; El Adawy M.; Hajjeh R.; Gaffey M.; Bhutta Z.
Article.Abstract: This scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). As climate shocks intensify, advancing a mechanistic understanding will be critical to designing responsive, inclusive, and sustainable systems of protection.

Article.Authors: Xu X.; Zhou C.; Zhang R.; Fan C.; Wang Q.
Article.Abstract: Kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC) carries substantial clinical challenges. Article.Abstract: Socioeconomic health inequality among reproductive-age populations remains insufficiently characterized globally. Article.Title: EGaIn-based thermal management for high heat flux electronics
Article.Authors: Joung J.; Na H.; Yoon S.; Jeong Y.; Lee M.; Majidi C.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: The increasing power density of modern electronic systems makes efficient thermal management essential for maintaining device performance, reliability, and operational lifetime. Among emerging thermal management materials, eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) has attracted attention because it uniquely combines metallic thermal conductivity with room-temperature fluidity, enabling efficient heat transfer and conformal contact with interfaces. In this review, we examine EGaIn as an adaptive thermal management platform and connect its material properties with the thermal functions they enable, their implementation in cooling systems, and the associated engineering challenges. We discuss how EGaIn enhances heat dissipation through interfacial heat transfer, liquid metal cooling, and thermally conductive composites, and review applications in batteries, high-performance electronics, electronic packaging, and flexible devices. We discuss challenges including oxidation, leakage, corrosion, electrical insulation, and long-term reliability, together with engineering strategies to address them. Finally, we provide perspectives for developing reliable EGaIn-based thermal management technologies for next-generation electronic and energy systems.

Article.Title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli
Article.Authors: Deodato M.; Melcher D.
Article.Abstract: Neural oscillations support cognition and perception by organizing information across oscillatory cycles. Article.Title: Offensive unpredictability and defensive tracking in intergroup conflict show sex-differentiated patterns
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Zhang C.; Widjaja A.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Intergroup conflict poses asymmetric strategic demands: acquiring resources through offense benefits from behavior that opponents cannot easily anticipate, whereas protecting resources through defense requires monitoring opponents and adjusting to threats. Article.Authors: Meski S.; Mojsoska B.; Krogfelt K.; Cruz-Paredes C.
Article.Abstract: Soils support a varied range of microbial communities and are important repositories of antimicrobial resistance genes. Sequence-based techniques, such as quantitative polymerase chain reaction and shotgun metagenomics, have substantially aided soil-resistome cataloging. This review contends that better clinical inference requires tying presence-based signals to function, mobility, and exposure routes, rather than just increasing survey volume. We offer a four-tiered evidentiary paradigm that distinguishes between detection, functional or expression-based evidence, mobile genetic element context, and exposure-linked evidence in environmental, animal, and human compartments. Because activity, mobility, and cross-compartmental similarity support several claims, layered, claim-aligned approaches are required for careful One Health interpretation.

Article.Title: Intestinal microbiota-associated LysoPC(16:0) promotes endometriosis via PPARγ-mediated M2 macrophage polarization and IL-10 secretion
Article.Authors: Li N.; Yuan M.; Jin X.; Jiao X.; Wang S.; Zhong Z.; Guan H.; Le X.; Ren Q.; Liu Y.; Dong X.; Li Q.; Wang M.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Both gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered pelvic immune microenvironment have been linked to endometriosis (EM), but the metabolites connecting the two remain undefined. Clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion blocked LysoPC(16:0)-driven lesion growth. LysoPC(16:0) further induced PPARγ-dependent IL-10 transcription, and IL-10 neutralization in vivo reduced lesion weight. Conditioned medium from LysoPC(16:0)-stimulated THP-1 macrophages promoted migration of primary endometrial stromal cells from patients with EM, an effect reversed by GW9662 or IL-10 neutralization. Article.Title: Negative regulation of TH17-mediated inflammation by the nuclear receptor REV-ERBβ
Article.Authors: Campbell S.; Mosure S.; Amir M.; Chuck J.; Lu Q.; Solt L.
Article.Abstract: TH17 cells play a central role in several human autoimmune diseases. We and others reported the nuclear receptor, REV-ERBα, as a cell-intrinsic repressor of TH17-mediated pathogenicity. REV-ERBβ, REV-ERBα's closely related family member, is thought to be functionally redundant to REV-ERBα, which we sought to explore in TH17-mediated immunity. Our data indicate that deletion of REV-ERBβ enhances TH17-mediated pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and exacerbated disease in mouse models of multiple sclerosis and colitis. RNA-sequencing indicates REV-ERBβ and REV-ERBα do not have similar transcriptional profiles in TH17 cells. REV-ERBβ does not appear to strongly rely on interaction with the classic co-repressor NCoR1 to regulate gene expression, which is in contrast to REV-ERBα in TH17 cells, nor does it utilize heme, its known endogenous ligand for its repressive functions. Our results establish that while REV-ERBβ also acts as a negative regulator of TH17-cell function and pathogenicity, it does so in a manner that is non-redundant, independent, and unique to REV-ERBα.

Article.Abstract: The olfactory epithelium (OE) is a dynamic and complex sensory tissue in which continuous regeneration, neuronal differentiation, and tissue maintenance depend on coordinated molecular and cellular signaling. Article.Authors: Zheng W.; Yang Z.; Chen Z.; Yang S.; Lin Z.; Zhang Y.; Zhang J.; Wu H.; Peng X.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Complex underwater terrains require robots that can maneuver efficiently through confined, vegetation-rich spaces while minimizing hydrodynamic disturbance. Article.Title: Antibiotic resistance genes in aquaculture: Molecular detection, environmental dynamics, and biological control strategies
Article.Authors: Loveymi H.; Roomiani L.; Tadayoni M.
Article.Abstract: Antibiotic resistance in aquaculture is a major threat to sustainable fish production and global public health. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of studies on antibiotic resistance in aquaculture published between 2005 and 2025, identified through a systematic and reproducible literature search. Evidence is organized into thematic domains encompassing molecular mechanisms, environmental reservoirs and drivers, diagnostic and surveillance tools, and biological alternatives to antibiotics. In parallel, vaccines, probiotics, and bacteriophage therapy show promising, context-dependent potential when embedded in multifaceted biocontrol frameworks. This review highlights priorities including protocol standardization, rapid farm-deployable diagnostics, and optimized synergistic biocontrol strategies, supported by artificial intelligence and big data analytics, to facilitate a transition from reactive treatment to preventive, system-level resistance management in aquaculture.

Article.Title: Effect of the end-of-life care education program on improving oncology nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors: A quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: Yu W.; Hou X.; Guo R.; Wang Y.; Ma X.; Pang D.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Education can strengthen nurses' capabilities in end-of-life care. Intra-group comparisons showed the training group exhibited superior knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors than at baseline (p < 0.05). The end-of-life care education program effectively enhanced oncology nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors.

Article.Title: Epidemiological modeling of African swine fever in wild boars—A systematic review
Article.Authors: Hirwa F.; Tanveer M.; Ntakiyisumba E.; Won G.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a viral disease that poses a major threat to swine production, with wild boars contributing to virus persistence and transmission. Article.Title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Rao D.; Zhang J.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Senescent cells, which exert context-dependent tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects, are central to this progress and engage in complex crosstalk with tumor proliferation. This review critically examines the multidimensional interplay between aging and cancer by synthesizing genetic, cytokine signaling, and tissue microenvironment evidence. We discuss how senescent cells influence immune surveillance, therapy response, tumor progression, metastasis, and age-related cancer risk, while cellular diversity, molecular complexity, immune balance, tumor heterogeneity, treatment resistance, and individual aging variability further complicate this relationship. We conclude that aging and cancer are intertwined through dynamic, context-specific mechanisms. By integrating these insights, this review aims to inspire novel research directions and transformative advances in cancer therapy and healthy longevity.

Article.Title: Distinct electrophysiological correlates of low- and high-level visual consciousness with minimized post-perceptual processing
Article.Authors: Hense A.; Peters A.; Dellert T.; Bruchmann M.; Straube T.
Article.Abstract: Conscious visual phenomenology comprises multiple representational levels, from basic features to integrated percepts, raising the question of how the neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) differentiate accordingly. Event-related potential (ERP) studies identified early occipitotemporal negativities as reliable NCC; yet, it remains unclear whether these capture conscious content beyond low-level features and extend to higher-order representations. Moreover, whether later ERP components index higher-level conscious percepts independent of task-related processing remains contested. The present study addresses this question using an inattentional blindness (IB) paradigm that isolates three representational levels of conscious perception (no, low- or high-level awareness) for an identical stimulus under minimized post-perceptual processing. Across 85 healthy participants, low-level line perception was indexed by an enhanced early occipital negativity, whereas high-level face perception additionally recruited a right-lateralized occipitotemporal negativity, followed by medial posterior positivities. These findings reveal systematic spatiotemporal differentiation of awareness-related potentials across representational levels of consciousness under task-irrelevant conditions.

Article.Authors: Choi E.; Nichols E.; Tomfohr-Madsen L.; Giesbrecht G.; Manning K.; Lebel C.; Duerden E.

Article.Title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
Article.Authors: Paraskevopoulos E.; Bamidis P.
Article.Abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

Article.Authors: Krapf P.; Heidbreder P.; Bruijning M.; Meirmans P.; Stankowski S.; Kulmuni J.
Article.Abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Article.Authors: Ou Y.; Allen E.; Kay K.; Oxenham A.
Article.Abstract: Pitch and timbre, two fundamental perceptual attributes of sound, are critical for both speech and music. Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Feng X.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To date, experimental development biology still faces challenges to efficiently model the morphogenesis of cross-species vertebrates, spanning from the embryonic development to postnatal growth. Article.Abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of solids is hindered by strong scattering, which violates assumptions underlying the Beer-Lambert (BL) law. Article.Title: Early-warning signals of critical transitions in global ecoregions
Article.Authors: Hirsch E.; Koren I.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecoregions represent coherent ecological units shaped by shared environmental conditions and biological communities. As ecosystems approach critical transitions, their resilience declines, showing slower recovery from perturbations and increasing temporal autocorrelation. By combining spatial clustering, vegetation trend analysis, and resilience indicators, we identify ecoregions exhibiting both vegetation change and declining resilience. We find that approximately one-quarter of ecoregions, covering over one-third of Earth's land surface, show consistent signals of emerging structural transitions. Many of these occur in regions with low direct human modification, suggesting a strong role for large-scale environmental drivers. The detected patterns reveal increasing internal fragmentation within ecoregions and highlight regions potentially approaching critical transitions. This framework provides a scalable approach for identifying ecosystems at risk and supports targeted monitoring and conservation planning.

Article.Abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD), ischemic stroke (IS), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and lower-extremity vascular disease are leading causes of disability in Western Europe and North America, but their diet-attributable burden remains unclear. Article.Abstract: The Himalayan ibex (Capra sibirica), a prized trophy and crucial prey species of the snow leopard (Panthera uncia), has increased in abundance alongside snow leopard populations due to ongoing conservation efforts. Article.Title: Periodontitis as a potential contributor to lung cancer: Epidemiological evidence, proposed mechanisms, and clinical implications
Article.Authors: Dong H.; Xin H.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis has been proposed as a potential contributor to lung cancer (LC), but the epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. This structured narrative review evaluates the association between periodontitis and LC, the directness of proposed biological mechanisms, and the implications for risk assessment and supportive care. Observational studies generally report positive associations, although effect estimates vary according to periodontal ascertainment, study population, and adjustment for smoking. Clinically assessed periodontitis, self-reported or administrative diagnoses, tooth loss, periodontal-associated microbial markers, and general oral microbiome profiles represent distinct exposure domains and should not be interpreted interchangeably. The absence of a clear association among lifelong never smokers and the lack of supportive Mendelian randomization evidence further limit causal inference. Human studies demonstrate oral-lower airway microbial overlap, while experimental LC models support microbiota-related inflammatory and oncogenic signaling; however, periodontal origin, directional microbial transmission, and a continuous causal pathway from periodontitis to LC have not been established. Clinically, periodontitis should not modify current eligibility for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, and oral or respiratory microbiome biomarkers remain investigational. Perioperative oral care has comparatively stronger evidence for reducing postoperative pulmonary infectious complications, but this benefit should not be extrapolated to tumor recurrence or survival. Overall, current evidence supports an observational association and biological plausibility, whereas independent causality and an oncologic benefit of periodontal treatment remain unproven.

Article.Abstract: In rotating machinery fault diagnosis, the original feature space often suffers from anomalous outliers, limited sample availability, and imbalanced class distributions. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid method of HCAB-SMOTE-LOF for diagnosing imbalanced fault diagnosis under outlier contamination. The core idea is not a simple combination of Local Outlier Factor (LOF) and Hybrid Clustering Affinity Synthesis Minority oversampling technique (HCAB-SMOTE), but a coupling mechanism in which LOF-based majority-class purification constrains the boundary region of HCAB-SMOTE, so that synthetic samples are generated in reliable minority-class clusters. To extract the fault-relevant time-frequency features, high-pass filtering is applied to the raw vibration signals to remove low-frequency components. The LOF is introduced to eliminate samples that are clearly abnormal or mislabeled in the feature space. On this basis, the HCAB-SMOTE algorithm is employed to synthetically generate minority-class fault samples, thereby improving the quality and distributional plausibility of the generated samples and alleviating the adverse impact of data imbalance on classifier performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using both a laboratory dataset and the Ottawa motor dataset. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted between the proposed method and several oversampling strategies applied during data processing, including the use of original data, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and HCAB-SMOTE. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms all existing oversampling methods across all evaluation metrics, confirming its marked advantages in outlier removal and sample-distribution optimization and thus its capability to effectively detect rotating machinery faults.

Article.Title: Recurrent latent dynamics in spinal circuits enable a digital twin of autonomic state transitions
Article.Authors: Choo M.; Cho M.; Lee J.; Oh C.; Hong S.; Heo C.; Shon Y.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Physiological signals underlying homeostasis, such as blood pressure, are dynamic and nonlinear, shaped by interactions among diverse neurons. In the spinal intermediolateral nucleus (IML), neurons show heterogeneous, monotonic firing changes during blood pressure transitions, intrinsic to control yet difficult to decode. We introduce a manifold-based model reconstructing internal state dynamics from IML activity, beyond prior descriptive frameworks. Brief spinal stimulation lowering blood pressure showed that single-neuron responses could not explain the nonlinear trajectory, so we derived a low-dimensional circular manifold capturing its cyclical evolution. Embedding the manifold as a dynamic reservoir in a recurrent neural network reconstructed trial-to-trial variability and nonlinear blood pressure dynamics generated by the manifold, without a readout. Our results establish the neural manifold as a generative computational substrate for autonomic physiology, a capability that remains largely unexplored in spinal circuits, and a step toward closed-loop spinal neuromodulation.

Article.Title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation
Article.Authors: Tawk C.; Saab G.; Abdallah G.; El Khoury J.; Aouad R.
Article.Abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.

Article.Title: Critical analysis of the new European framework for non-fossil flexibility and the questions left unanswered
Article.Authors: Mastropietro P.; Rodilla P.; Chaves Ávila J.
Article.Abstract: The 2024 Electricity Market Design Reform introduced a new European framework for non-fossil flexibility. The first national flexibility needs assessments were published in July 2026, and indicative objectives and support schemes for non-fossil flexibility will soon be introduced. However, we argue that this new framework, which will influence the development of European power systems as they transition to low-carbon resources, is based on a flawed theoretical foundation and exhibits significant overlap with the European resource adequacy framework. No flexibility metric has been defined for the flexibility needs assessment. No flexibility standard/target has been calculated based on the economic equilibrium between the cost of additional flexibility and the cost of not relying on it. We identify three underlying metrics for flexibility needs, we present alternative approaches to define flexibility products and identify open questions that need to be addressed before the new flexibility framework moves to the implementation phase.

Article.Authors: Yu Z.; Wang H.; Zhuo Y.; Zuo Z.

These findings identify a frequency-dependent bottleneck in VPL-to-S1FL transfer, rather than local cortical responsiveness, as a constraint on sustained cortical expression of temporally dense sensory input.

These findings provide a mechanistic basis for understanding drought impacts on vegetation WUE across contrasting frozen-soil environments.

Article.Abstract: Cell type deconvolution algorithms have significantly advanced in recent years. Article.Title: Unrealized optimal designs challenge models of constraint in early vertebrate evolution
Article.Authors: Leflaëc E.; Ballell A.; Sanisidro O.; Ferrón H.
Article.Abstract: Jawed vertebrates dominate modern vertebrate diversity, whereas most jawless vertebrate lineages disappeared during the Devonian. Recent photocatalytic systems are examined, including TiO2-based materials, S-scheme and Z-scheme heterojunctions, laddered architectures, metal-organic frameworks, and g-C3N4 composites. Combining photocatalysis with renewable energy and water treatment could offer a practical route to microplastic management, provided catalyst recovery, toxicity, and scale-up challenges are addressed.

Conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches remain poorly suited to early detection and timely intervention. This paper analyzes the development of BCI technology, from the first detection of electroencephalogram (EEG) signals to the parallel development of invasive and non-invasive systems, and outlines the basic principles of signal acquisition, processing, and decoding, together with the relative advantages and limitations of different approaches. It then focuses on the use of BCI in Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), covering early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation. The article also discusses the difficulties encountered by BCI technology in terms of technological realization, clinical translation, and ethical considerations, as well as several future research directions, including multimodal fusion, adaptive algorithms, closed-loop control systems, and personalized treatment so as to drive the applications of BCI in precision medicine and in neurological diseases.

Our findings demonstrate mechanistic insights surpassing conventional tests, a valuable intermediate step to guide material development prior to in vivo experiments.

Article.Title: Sequence of aerobic and resistance exercise influences short- and long-term glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: A randomized trial

Compared with pre-exercise levels, mean glucose (p = 0.043) and HbA1c (p = 0.007) decreased only in AR group. Article.Title: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in Drosophila
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim A.

Article.Title: Quantum-enhanced trusted execution with dynamic policy optimization for zero-trust edge computing
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Zhou Y.

Article.Abstract: Olfactory dysfunction and anosmia are associated with disruptions in sleep.
