Article.Title: How Habitual Language Mode Shapes Self-Stigma Perception Process in Deaf Individuals: Evidence from an Event-Related Potentials Study
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Li Y.; Wang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deaf individuals often experience public stigma from the hearing majority due to communication barriers, which may further evolve into internalized self-stigma. However, how habitual language mode shapes self-stigma-related processing remains unclear. In the present study, 20 signing deaf and 21 oral deaf individuals completed a semantic priming task while event-related potentials (ERPs) were recorded. Deaf-identity (“I am deaf”) primes were presented subliminally or supraliminally before positive and negative trait words. Among oral deaf participants, negative words elicited a larger N400 than positive words under supraliminal priming, while a negative-over-positive LPC effect emerged in the no-priming and subliminal conditions but disappeared under supraliminal priming. Signing deaf participants showed no N400 valence effect but exhibited a negative-over-positive LPC effect across all conditions. These findings provide no clear evidence of self-stigma in either group. Instead, they suggest that habitual language mode and conscious accessibility of deaf identity jointly shape the temporal dynamics of self-evaluative processing, potentially reflecting different ways of resisting the internalization of negative societal evaluations. Signing deaf individuals may derive protection from a culturally and collectively grounded Deaf identity, whereas oral deaf individuals may rely more on individualized, self-protective processing to prevent negative evaluations from being incorporated into the self.

Article.Title: Understanding Audiovisual Affective Processing: Behavioral Effects and Neural Underpinnings
Article.Authors: Gao C.; Green J.; Shinkareva S.; Yan R.; Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emotional signals are typically conveyed jointly through vision and audition. This article reviews behavioral, electrophysiological, and neuroimaging evidence on audiovisual affective processing, addressing what its core effects are, when they unfold, and where they occur in the brain. Congruent audiovisual cues often facilitate emotion recognition, although benefits vary across emotions, tasks, measures, and unimodal comparisons. Audiovisual input can also shape affective appraisals and subjective emotional experience. Modality dominance is context-dependent, varying with cue reliability and the affective dimension judged. Cross-modal influences can persist when one modality is task-irrelevant, suggesting limited goal dependence. Electrophysiological findings reveal audiovisual affective interactions at both early and later stages of neural processing. Neuroimaging work implicates posterior superior temporal cortex (pSTC) within a distributed network of sensory, subcortical, and frontal regions. Building on this evidence, we consider Anderson's information integration theory as a computational framework for characterizing modality-related and value-dependent contributions to affective judgments. We propose a hypothesis-generating dual-pathway framework predicting that reliability-related changes in cue influence will covary with sensory-pSTC interactions, whereas value-dependent changes will additionally involve amygdala and prefrontal systems. These hypotheses concern relative rather than exclusive network contributions and require direct testing through independent manipulations of cue reliability and affective value.

Article.Title: When Fakes Feel Real: Behavioral and Neural Mechanisms of Deepfake Hyperrealism in Younger and Older Adults
Article.Authors: Washburn S.; Lin T.; Zhu M.; Faulkner R.; Cahill B.; Lighthall N.; Ebner N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deepfakes are designed to mimic real people and constitute an emerging exploitation threat. They are potent methods of fraud as humans detect deepfake images at near or below chance levels, and deepfakes are frequently perceived as more real even than real images (deepfake hyperrealism). Anterior insula (aINS) function is implicated in processing salient, untrustworthy cues suggesting that low aINS recruitment during deepfake perception may underlie experiences of deepfake hyperrealism. Further, aging may confer increased experiences of deepfake hyperrealism, given increased susceptibility to deception and reduced aINS sensitivity to deceptive stimuli with age. Here, 156 participants (62 younger: 18-37 years, 94 older: 60-89 years) evaluated the realness of real and deepfake face images while undergoing fMRI. Behavioral results revealed deepfake hyperrealism in both age groups, with these effects more pronounced in older adults. Our imaging results indicated lower aINS activation was associated with higher realness ratings and aINS activity was also lower for deepfake than real images in both younger and older adults. These findings provide additional support for deepfake hyperrealism in perception, underscoring the threat of deepfakes as a method of exploitation across adulthood. Results also support that muted aINS response to deepfakes constitutes a neuromechanism in deception vulnerability.

Article.Title: mPFC-Dependent Valuation Shapes Information Sharing: Causal Evidence from tDCS and a Dyadic Social Media Paradigm
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Information sharing drives the spread of both accurate and misleading content, yet its psychological and neural mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether perceived self- and social relevance influence sharing through downstream content evaluations, and whether this process depends on medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) function. In a dyadic social media paradigm, 186 participants were assigned to anodal, cathodal, or sham tDCS over the mPFC. Senders judged 30 science news items (15 true and 15 false) on truthfulness, self-relevance, social relevance, interestingness, and importance before deciding whether to share each item with a real receiver. Structural equation modeling showed that self- and social relevance predicted sharing indirectly through evaluations of interestingness, importance, and truthfulness. mPFC stimulation did not reliably change sharing rates, but altered evaluative processing: it reduced perceived interestingness, and anodal stimulation produced a significant negative indirect pathway to sharing through reduced interestingness. Multi-group analyses indicated that these valuation pathways were invariant across true and false news. On the receiver side, social endorsement increased reading of shared items but had little effect on post-reading evaluations. Together, these findings support a causal contribution of mPFC-targeted neuromodulation to evaluative processing relevant to sharing, with limited evidence for a direct effect on sharing behavior.

Article.Title: Social relationship is associated with distinct patterns of inter-brain synchrony and directed connectivity during interpersonal coordination
Article.Authors: Han H.; Zhao Z.; Lin L.; Li C.; Jin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract How social relationship and effector pairing relate to behavioral coordination and inter-brain interaction during joint timing remains unclear. Using functional near-infrared spectroscopy hyperscanning during a dyadic synchronization-continuation task, we examined 21 romantic couples and 23 stranger dyads performing hand-hand and hand-foot coordination. Romantic partners showed smaller tapping deviations than strangers during continuation, while hand–foot coordination was associated with greater tapping variability. Motor-region inter-brain synchrony (IBS) was greater in romantic partners than in strangers. True-dyad IBS exceeded the pseudo-dyad baseline in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, corresponding differences were not detected in the motor cortex or left temporoparietal junction. Dynamic IBS analysis identified two recurrent configurations differing in synchrony strength and global efficiency, but state-transition frequency did not differ significantly between relationship groups. Granger-causality-based directed connectivity was stronger overall in stranger dyads, with female-to-male values exceeding those in the reverse direction. Together, these findings indicate that social relationship is associated with contrasting patterns of motor-region synchrony and directed connectivity, while effector pairing is associated with behavioral variability.

Article.Title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
Article.Authors: O’Brien C.; Gunturkun F.; Deng Y.; Ruaysungnoen R.; Chang D.; Khanijo S.; Barnett C.; Kapil S.; Daly A.; Goffi A.; Stavi D.; Carrier F.; Ennehas Y.; Fiza B.; Patterson A.; Daubert T.; Moll V.; Castellucci C.; Zekhtser M.; Burgara N.; Mayette M.; Courchesne K.; Thompson S.; Parikh R.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

Article.Title: Human adipose derived mesenchymal stem cell extracellular vesicles ameliorate ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 expression in premature ovarian insufficiency mice
Article.Authors: Arjmand F.; Mirsanei J.; Mehdizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a major cause of infertility and long-term health complications in young women and can result from gonadotoxic chemotherapy. Current management alleviates symptoms but does not restore ovarian reserve. Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (hAD-MSC-EVs) have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical POI models. Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hAD-MSCs) were expanded and characterized by morphology and flow cytometric immunophenotyping. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated from conditioned medium by sequential centrifugation and ultracentrifugation and characterized using dynamic light scattering, transmission electron microscopy, the Bradford assay, and Western blotting for CD63, TSG101, and calnexin. POI was induced in mice using cyclophosphamide and busulfan. Animals received hAD-MSC-EVs via tail vein injection. Serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and estradiol (E2) levels were measured, and ovarian histology was evaluated using hematoxylin and eosin staining. Ovarian messenger RNA (mRNA) levels of Bmp15 , Gdf9 , Foxo3 , and Mapk3 , encoding bone morphogenetic protein 15 (BMP15), growth differentiation factor 9 (GDF9), forkhead box O3, and mitogen-activated protein kinase 3, respectively, were quantified, together with ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels. EV treatment partially ameliorated POI-associated endocrine alterations, reducing FSH and increasing LH and E2 levels compared with untreated POI mice. Histological analysis showed improved ovarian architecture and reduced stromal abnormalities. Ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels were higher in EV-treated mice than in untreated POI mice and did not differ significantly from control levels. However, Bmp15 and Gdf9 mRNA levels increased only modestly and remained below control levels, whereas Foxo3 and Mapk3 mRNA levels did not differ significantly among groups. hAD-MSC-EV treatment was associated with partial endocrine and histological improvement and increased ovarian BMP15 and GDF9 protein levels in mice with chemotherapy-induced POI. These findings support further investigation of hAD-MSC-EVs as a potential approach to ovarian recovery, while the mechanisms underlying these associations remain to be established.

Article.Title: Association between social networks and central sensitization-related symptoms among residents of a Japanese community: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Abe Y.; Endo M.; Kono K.; Iwata N.; Haruyama Y.; Kobashi G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social networks may be associated with central sensitization-related symptoms, but community-based evidence is limited. We examined associations of total, family, and friend network scores with elevated symptom burden among 1813 residents of Mibu Town, Japan, in a cross-sectional study. The Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) and six-item Lubben Social Network Scale (LSNS-6) were used; CSI ≥ 40 indicated elevated symptom burden rather than a clinical diagnosis. Overall, 135 participants (7.4%) met this threshold. Participants with CSI ≥ 40 had lower social network scores than those with CSI < 40. In multivariable analyses, higher total network scores were associated with lower odds of CSI ≥ 40 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85–0.92), as were family (aOR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.76–0.87) and friend scores (aOR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.82–0.93). All three networks showed inverse trends across score categories (P for trend < 0.001). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses excluding self-reported CSI Part B conditions from the adjustment set. These findings highlight the relevance of family and friend relationships to symptom burden but do not establish causality.

Article.Title: Application of Raman spectroscopy to the first actual fuel debris retrieved from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Unit 2
Article.Authors: Ueno K.; Yomogida T.; Kumagai Y.; Kitagaki T.; Ikeuchi H.; Mizokami M.; Mizokami S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Following the successful first trial retrieval of fuel debris from Unit 2 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (FDNPS), a Raman spectroscopic assessment was conducted to investigate the chemical states of the debris. The powdered fuel debris sample, prepared via a vibratory mill, was analyzed using micro-Raman spectroscopy and was compared with simulated debris synthesized under controlled conditions. The average Raman spectrum revealed characteristic bands corresponding to tetragonal ZrO₂, spinel-type oxides originating from stainless-steel structural components, and a cubic (U, Zr)O₂ solid solution. The Raman spectrum of the retrieved fuel debris differed significantly from that of uranium-containing particles (UP1) previously sampled from stagnant water at torus room of Unit 2 of the FDNPS, indicating that further sampling and analysis are required to fully understand the overall chemical complexity of the fuel debris. Raman spectroscopy proved effective for identifying oxidative products in the fuel debris, requiring only minimal sample amounts and no vacuum or coating pretreatments. This study highlights the method’s potential as a valuable tool in nuclear decommissioning efforts, especially for the characterization of uranium bearing compounds in fuel debris.

Article.Title: Techno-economic optimization of a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system with an EV charging station at a university campus​
Article.Authors: Nazir K.; Biswas B.; Shimul A.; Solre G.; Al-Humaidi J.; Aljazzar S.; Benghanem M.; Elboughdiri N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in developing economies, combined with the growing imperative to decarbonize campus energy systems, necessitates novel planning frameworks that reconcile grid-interactive microgrid design with probabilistic economic validation. This study presents a techno-economic planning framework for a grid-integrated hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) co-designed with an EV charging station at university campus​. Unlike prior studies that treat EV loads as static inputs, this work constructs a behaviorally-informed, regulated-charging EV load profile by characterizing the actual EV fleet accessible within the study area, yielding a demand model grounded in local mobility patterns. Four HRES configurations integrating PV arrays, WT, a Bio-Gen, BESS, and utility grid support are optimized through HOMER Pro. The optimal configuration achieves a NPC of $2,403,816 and a COE of $0.069/kWh at a RF of 70.04%, while attaining significantly reduced emissions of CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , and CO compared to the more grid-reliant configurations (Cases III and IV), and demonstrating environmental performance akin to Case II. Critically, this study couples system-level optimization with a probabilistic Monte Carlo simulation framework consisting of 10,000 stochastic trials over uncertain techno-economic parameters to produce probabilistic financial performance distributions. The analysis yields a 99.03% probability of achieving a positive NPV, a mean payback period of ~ 11.5 years, and a mean IRR of 10.98%, closely aligned with the project discount rate, collectively indicating favorable financial performance under the considered uncertainty. A local multivariate sensitivity analysis further indicates that, within the evaluated parameter ranges, solar irradiance exhibits the greatest influence on system performance, followed by wind speed, whereas Bio-Gen availability demonstrates comparatively low sensitivity. These findings provide useful guidance for technology prioritization in climate-variable south-central region.

Article.Title: Multilayer feed-forward neural network-based mobile app for photovoltaic module parameter estimation
Article.Authors: Taibin M.; Islam M.; Hussan M.; Rahman M.; Al-Subhi A.; Shafiullah M.; Hossain M.; Islam A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate parameter estimation of photovoltaic (PV) cells and modules is essential for the modeling, simulation, and optimization of PV systems. However, this task involves solving a complex nonlinear optimization problem, which often suffers from slow convergence and entrapment in local minima. The objective of this research is to contribute finding an efficient and software-independent approach to predict the parameters of the single diode model for polycrystalline and monocrystalline PV cells and modules from only the datasheet parameters at Standard Test Conditions (STC). To accomplish this task, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) approach is used, which resulted in the ability to estimate instantly without the need of commercial software. The developed model is additionally implemented in an Android application, which offers a user friendly and accessible instrument for PV system designers. The model was further evaluated through comparisons of reconstructed I–V and P–V characteristics with available reference characteristics, Simulink library modules, manufacturer datasheet values, and recently published algorithms. The results demonstrate high reliability, with RMSE, MAE and U95 values of 1.3610e−04, 6.8160e−05 and 2.659820e−04 respectively. Furthermore, the model reliably reproduced P–V and I–V characteristics under varying environmental conditions, closely aligning with the datasheet specifications of the four modules.

Article.Title: Maintenance and termination of the embryonic diapause in the univoltine damselfly Lestes sponsa Hansemann
Article.Authors: Norling U.; Sniegula S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Embryonic diapause and its termination are key to seasonal timing in the univoltine damselfly Lestes sponsa , ensuring that eggs overwinter and hatch in spring. Following summer oviposition—typically in plants above water—diapause begins after 2–3 weeks. We investigated diapause termination in eggs from southern Sweden (~ 55°N) using combinations of chilling in darkness and subsequent exposure to photoperiods at elevated temperatures. Diapause development—a physiological process underlying termination—was fastest at 10 °C, slower at 5 °C, and slowest (possibly stagnating) at 20–21 °C. Longer chilling enhanced the terminating effects of long photoperiods and high temperatures, resulting in faster, more synchronous hatching and a shorter critical photoperiod. At immediate 21 °C and solstice-like photoperiods (LD 19.5:4.5), hatching began 1–2 weeks after diapause initiation and continued for weeks, but synchrony improved with prior exposure to diapause-maintaining conditions (< LD 17:7). LD 18:6 was only weakly effective in terminating diapause without chilling. After 19–21 weeks at 5 °C, virtually complete hatching occurred within 2–4 days independently of photoperiod. If diapause was not terminated immediately at 21 °C after chilling, diapause development appeared to reverse, restoring pre-chill photoperiodic responses. In contrast, 10 °C post-chill accelerated diapause development and reduced late outliers, but some effects of photoperiod on hatching time still persisted after 19–21 weeks chilling. Post-diapause development was 3-3.5 times slower at 10 °C and ~ 20 times slower at 5 °C compared to 21 °C. Hatching was successful at 5 °C, and larvae survived two weeks near 0 °C, suggesting potential for winter hatching under a warmer climate. Eggs from Poland (~ 54°N) and northern Sweden (~ 66°N) differed in critical photoperiods, with a weaker diapause at higher latitudes. This system, adapted to latitude, ensures early and synchronous spring hatching, with hatchlings resistant to cold spells and prevents premature hatching during untimely warm periods via short-day inhibition.

Article.Title: Integrating UAV-assisted blow sampling and photo-identification in common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
Article.Authors: Ceolotto L.; Fiore E.; Ferraresso S.; Andrés-Hervías C.; Genov T.; Gonzalvo J.; Lokar K.; Pesce G.; Dugény E.; Mazzariol S.; Centelleghe C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-invasive genetic sampling can improve the study and conservation of cetaceans by reducing disturbance while providinsg information on population structure, connectivity, and other parameters. In this study, we evaluated the feasibility of UAV-assisted blow sampling for obtaining DNA from free-ranging common bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in two Mediterranean areas: The Gulf of Ambracia (Greece) and the Gulf of Trieste (off Piran, Slovenia). Blow samples were linked to photo-identified individuals and assessed through UAV video review. Mitochondrial DNA amplification was successful for at least one mitochondrial locus in 78% of Greek and 100% of Slovenian samples, whereas a nuclear marker amplified only in samples of animals under human care, used as a control, indicating that the mitochondrial assays used here performed more consistently than the single nuclear assay tested for blow-derived low-template DNA. Fifteen individuals were sequenced for up to six mitochondrial loci, and 13 were retained in the final concatenated dataset. Phylogenetic, haplotype network, and multivariate analyses showed that the recovered mitochondrial sequences could be used for genetic comparisons between the two study areas. Video-assessment categories were associated with molecular success, suggesting that UAV video assessment is particularly useful for identifying sampling attempts with a low likelihood of molecular success. Overall, our results support UAV-assisted blow sampling integrated with photo-ID as a promising approach for individual-based molecular monitoring of small cetaceans.

Article.Title: From waste to worth: Green valorization of food waste into a sustainable fluorimetric nanoprobe for chemical and bioanalytical sensing
Article.Authors: Abdel-Monem M.; Eid M.; Aly F.; Abdallah N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Overripe plant materials represent a major source of organic agricultural waste and are highly susceptible to rapid microbial decomposition due to their high moisture and sugar content. Improper disposal of such waste leads to the release of greenhouse gases and contributes to environmental pollution. Therefore, adopting sustainable recycling approaches is essential to minimize their environmental impact and promote efficient resource utilization. Herein, overripe goldenberry fruits, typically discarded as waste, have been successfully recycled and utilized for the first time as a convenient, renewable eco-friendly carbon source for engineering multi-doped CQDs that exhibit outstanding fluorescence characteristics (λex/em of 340/420 nm). These naturally derived nanodots were fabricated in only two min using a straightforward, one-pot microwave-assisted process offering rapid, and eco-friendly aspects arising from the utilization of bio-based carbon material and preparation strategy. The fabricated nanosensor was utilized for quantification of the veterinary NSAID Flunixin (FXN). The studied drug induced fluorescence quenching of these CQDs via both inner filter effect and dynamic quenching. This work showcases transforming discarded biomass into profitable nanomaterials. Beyond introducing the first CQD-based fluorescent assay for FXN, this study demonstrates an innovative strategy for converting discarded biomass into high-value nanomaterials. The method exhibited outstanding performance, including remarkable selectivity, a broad linear range, and a low detection limit, highlighting its sustainability, and applicability to pharmaceutical, food, and environmental water samples.

Article.Title: Postoperative evaluation of Achilles tendon using short echo time MRI and artificial intelligence
Article.Authors: Ciszkowska-Łysoń B.; Borowiec A.; Witkowska J.; Paśnik M.; Śmigielski R.; Borucki B.; Kapiński N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The objective was to identify the optimal MRI sequence to evaluate postoperative Achilles tendon (AT) healing. We compared T2 gradient sequence with 4.1ms (TE4) and 16ms (TE16) echo time with PD (proton density-weighted) through signal intensity (SI) measurements and correlated them with tendon-specific biomarkers. Additionally, the study assessed agreement between radiologists and AI in evaluating tendon-specific biomarkers. A total of 45 patients (mean age 36 ± 6 years; 36 men, 9 women) underwent nine consecutive MRI examinations at intervals from 1 to 52 weeks after surgery. SI in all postoperative MRI examinations was measured in AT in TE4, TE16 and PD. SI in the operated AT appears normal in PD and TE16 sequences around week 39. However, TE4 still shows high signals, indicating ongoing remodeling. Significant correlations were found between biomarkers and SI in the TE4 sequence ( p < 0.001 for structural changes and tendon edema, and p = 0.002 for tissue edema). High SI values were associated with poor biomarker outcomes. The mean absolute errors (MAE) between AI model scores, obtained using only axial TE4 scans, and radiologist evaluations ranged from 0.12 to 0.63. In conclusion, TE4 demonstrated greater sensitivity to persistent postoperative signal and structural abnormalities and may be useful in postoperative assessment of AT. AI scores showed relatively small absolute differences from the reference radiologist scores.

Article.Title: More choices improve behavioral risk measures but surveys remain more reliable
Article.Authors: Heinke S.; Schürmann O.; Andraszewicz S.; Rieskamp J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract It is essential for researchers and practitioners advising decision-makers to understand and measure precisely individual risk preferences. Behavioural risk- preference elicitation tasks have several advantages over self-report measures, including reducing biases and providing objective assessments. However, their low test–retest reliability limits their predictive value and overall measurement quality. This study investigates whether increasing the number of decisions within behavioural risk-elicitation tasks can improve their reliability. We hypothesise that adding multi-items to behavioural tasks can reduce decision noise and improve test–retest reliability. To test this hypothesis, we compared an enhanced multi-item behavioural risk elicitation task with standard behavioural- and self-report risk measures. Our results show that, although increasing the number of decisions improves reliability relative to traditional behavioural risk-preferences elicitation tasks, well-established multi-item self-report psychological questionnaires still demonstrate superior test–retest consistency.

Article.Title: LLM-agent-based cross-modal retrieval method for detecting clues of ecological environment damage
Article.Authors: Zhao M.; Bai L.; Lu S.; He X.; Chen L.; Ben F.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Within Ecological Conservation Redline zones, ecological environmental damage caused by non-compliant production and construction activities has become increasingly severe. Existing methods typically leverage remote sensing imagery and deep learning techniques to automatically identify unauthorized construction, or retrieve clues of ecological environmental damage from textual information such as public complaints and official circulars. The former often relies on professional experiential knowledge, while the latter remains at the level of passive retrieval; both rely on predefined rules and professional experience and suffer from a time lag. Recently emerging Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents, which possess both natural language understanding and multi-step task execution capabilities, make it possible to acquire and fulfill users’ retrieval demands in a fast and flexible manner through human–machine dialogue. Inspired by this, this paper constructs a multimodal clue retrieval agent for ecological environmental damage based on a multi-agent framework. The agent interacts with users who lack computer professional and technical backgrounds through natural language via LLMs to clarify their retrieval demands regarding specified regions, time periods, and damage types. It then orchestrates different sub-agents to automatically retrieve textual clues and remote sensing image clues within the corresponding spatiotemporal scope in a cross-modal manner, and aggregates and presents textual and image evidence to users to support the review and analysis of problem clues. Testing and evaluation conducted by researchers in the field of procuratorial case handling show that the proposed method achieves satisfactory retrieval performance and usability, and is simple and easy to learn. It can provide technical support for the screening and assessment of ecological environmental damage issues.

Article.Title: Identification and mechanistic elucidation of neutrophil migration-related biomarkers in bladder cancer based on single-cell and transcriptomic sequencing data
Article.Authors: Zhang N.; Sang W.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This research comprehensively explores the role of neutrophils in bladder cancer (BLCA), aiming to clarify underlying molecular mechanisms, identify key genes and biomarkers, and develop a reliable prognostic prediction model to provide new insights for clinical diagnosis and treatment strategies. Multiple datasets from GEO and TCGA databases were collected. Single-cell RNA sequencing data underwent processing with Seurat, including quality control, cell clustering, and annotation. Differential abundance, expression, and enrichment analyses were performed. WGCNA screened neutrophil migration-related genes. Ten machine-learning algorithms constructed 116 prognostic models; molecular mechanisms were explored via database and network construction. RT-qPCR validated key gene expression. To explore EMP1 roles, overexpression and knockdown experiments were conducted using human peripheral blood neutrophils, with migration assessed via transwell assays. Neutrophil abundance was notably increased in tumor tissue. Among eight neutrophil subtypes, neutro4 showed highest migration-related activation. Through comprehensive analyses, we identified 28 candidate genes associated with neutrophil migration. The stepCox + RSF composite model was selected as optimal (average C-index = 0.7, AUC > 0.7), incorporating EMP1 and RBP7 biomarkers involved in specific biological processes with complex non-coding regulatory networks. These biomarkers correlated with bladder cancer clinical phenotypes. RT-qPCR confirmed RBP7 and EMP1 were significantly downregulated in tumors ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, functional experiments revealed that EMP1 overexpression significantly enhanced neutrophil migration. This study provides a better understanding of neutrophil roles in bladder cancer. The identified biomarkers and constructed prognostic model offer potential clinical value for diagnosis and prognosis assessment, which may contribute to more effective treatment strategies. Functional experiments validate EMP1’s biological significance in neutrophil migration, supporting its potential as a therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Source informed dual expert machine learning combining Gaussian and Boltzmann representations for sequential twin tunnel settlement prediction
Article.Authors: Rostami A.; Mahdevari S.; Shahriar K.; Rostami J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sequential excavation of twin tunnels creates a staged settlement problem because the second drive acts on ground already affected by the first. We developed VF, a source informed dual expert machine learning surrogate that learns first stage settlement (S1) and incremental second stage settlement (ΔS = S2 − S1) from separately trained Gaussian and Boltzmann derived representations and reconstructs cumulative settlement S2 exactly. In nested five fold evaluation of 52 staged HSsmall numerical scenarios, VF predicted ΔS with R 2 = 0.839 and RMSE = 0.2315 cm, nearly identical to the Gaussian expert (0.2324 cm) and lower than the Boltzmann expert (0.2578 cm). Additional conventional baselines showed that a raw design ExtraTrees model achieved lower RMSE for S1 and S2 (0.9492 and 1.0592 cm) than VF (1.0761 and 1.1856 cm), whereas VF retained the lowest ΔS RMSE among the added baseline set (next lowest 0.2379 cm for gradient boosting). Thus, the evidence supports response dependent representation use rather than universal ensemble dominance. Blocked family testing exposed poor extrapolation for Isfahan S1 and S2 when complete response families were absent from training. VF is supported as a leakage controlled numerical surrogate within the audited HSsmall domain; independent field validation remains required before physical predictive use.

Article.Title: Molecular epidemiology of tuberculosis in Tétouan, Morocco: insights into strain diversity and genetic clustering
Article.Authors: Ez-Zari A.; Wałpuska P.; Mezzoug N.; Herrador Z.; Bouti K.; Bakuła Z.; Mokrousov I.; Elmtili N.; Jagielski T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Morocco. We investigated the diversity, lineage distribution, and clustering of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) isolates from pulmonary TB patients in Tétouan (2020–2023). In a prospective cross-sectional study, 103 MTBC isolates were characterized using 24-locus MIRU-VNTR genotyping. Genetic diversity was assessed using the Hunter–Gaston discriminatory index, while UPGMA and minimum spanning tree analyses evaluated genetic relatedness. Associations between demographic characteristics and double-locus-variant clonal complex membership were assessed using binary logistic regression. The 24-locus scheme showed high discriminatory power (HGDI = 0.9896). Among genotyped isolates, LAM was predominant (29.1%), followed by Beijing (9.7%), Ghana (3.9%), S (2.9%), Haarlem (1.9%), West African 1 (1.9%), and West African 2 (1​%); 49.5% of isolates were unassigned. UPGMA identified five identical-profile clusters comprising 17 isolates (16.5%), corresponding to an estimated recent transmission rate of 11.6%. Ten double-locus-variant clonal complexes included 40 isolates (38.8%). Old Medina residence was independently associated with clonal complex membership (AOR = 6.020, 95% CI 2.158–16.683; p = 0.001). The findings indicate high MTBC diversity and substantial genotypic heterogeneity, with greater likelihood of clonal-complex membership in a socioeconomically vulnerable urban area. Whole-genome sequencing and broader epidemiological sampling are needed to resolve transmission pathways and clarify the significance of genetically related isolates.

Article.Title: Aversive conditioning prevents perceptual habituation, but not cortical adaptation to odors
Article.Authors: Oleszkiewicz A.; Riedel F.; Sinding C.; Hummel T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To save attentional resources, the human brain learns to decrease its response to non-threatening stimuli. The decreased behavioral response is known as habituation, while the decreased peripheral and central neural response is called adaptation. In this investigation, we were interested in whether initially non-threatening olfactory stimuli, when paired with aversive shock, may become less prone to habituation and adaptation. To this end, in 46 individuals (24 females; M age =24.8 ± 5.7 years), we examined changes in cortical response and perceptual assessments of three odors, of which one was conditioned (i.e. paired with electric shock) and the remaining two were unconditioned. The conditioned odor was randomized across the participants. We report that aversive conditioning can prevent odor habituation, but we did not find support for the hypothesis that aversive conditioning prevents odor adaptation. We propose that aversive conditioning can be a method of maintaining olfactory alertness in those, who remain at risk of malodor exposure and may unintentionally get used to it, inflating the risk of negative consequences of this exposure.

Article.Title: The sulfur budget and composition of arc magmas and cumulates
Article.Authors: Hehn P.; Keith M.; Strauss H.; Kutzschbach M.; Haase K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subduction zones play an important role in the global S cycle, because recycling of altered oceanic crust and overlying sediments transfers different S species, particularly sulfide and sulfate, into the mantle. These affect the S contents, the S isotope composition and possibly the redox conditions in the mantle, as reflected by arc magmas along subduction zones. We compiled S and Cu contents together with ​ δ 34 S data of arc magmas and associated sulfides and show that ascending magmas in arcs typically become sulfide-saturated at Mg# ~ 55, evidenced by decreasing S and Cu concentrations. This effect may promote Ni-Cu sulfide deposit formation by removing > 70% of the S and Cu budget of mafic magmas in the deep arc crust. Sulfur isotope data of sulfide-bearing cumulates imply that most primitive magmas in Phanerozoic and Precambrian arcs have low δ 34 S values (− 2 to + 3‰) that overlap with mid-ocean ridge basalt (− 0.9 ± 0.5‰). Sulfide segregation drives positive δ 34 S shifts in residual melts by preferentially sequestering isotopically light S into magmatic sulfides, particularly in relatively oxidized magmas. Greater S isotope variability in Phanerozoic than Proterozoic arc magmas probably reflect the more variable δ 34 S of subducted sediments, whereas slab-derived sulfate has little effect on magma redox state.

Article.Title: Assessment of potential bias mechanisms in the analysis of large electronic medical record datasets
Article.Authors: Janssens A.; Crèvecoeur J.; Libin P.; Van Pottelbergh G.; Vaes B.; Neyens T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electronic medical records aid general practitioners in the follow-up of their patients. The vast amounts of patient data that are being collected through such electronic medical records offer opportunities to use them for other purposes such as epidemiological and (pre)clinical research. But the use of electronic medical record data for research purposes raises concerns about potential biases, since these data are typically not collected within a study design specifically developed to address a predefined research question, which may instead emerge during or after data collection. In addition, data collection practices and reporting behaviours can vary between general practitioners, while patients themselves differ in their likelihood of seeking care or reporting symptoms. Although a large patient population may mitigate some of these random variations through the law of large numbers, systematic biases related to the non-randomized sample of the participating practices and heterogeneity in patient characteristics may persist. If not appropriately accounted for, these sources of heterogeneity and potential bias can lead to different or potentially conflicting research findings. Using a large electronic medical records dataset from Flanders, Belgium, we assess how simple statistical approaches, such as adding practice-level random effects and changing the analytical entity, can help identify potential bias mechanisms and assess the sensitivity of estimated associations to them.

Article.Title: SRSF3-mediated post-transcriptional regulation of SERPINH1 promotes tumor growth and immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Yan H.; Zhu L.; Liu B.; Liu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by aggressive progression and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 3 (SRSF3) is a key regulator of alternative splicing, yet its role in shaping the immune microenvironment and fibrotic remodeling in HCC remains poorly understood. SRSF3 expression was examined in human HCC tissues and cell lines by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, and Western blot. Gain- and loss-of-function approaches were used to evaluate the effects of SRSF3 on HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and cytokine secretion in vitro. RNA immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the interaction between SRSF3 and SERPINH1 mRNA. Tumor growth, immune cell infiltration, and fibrosis were analyzed in mouse tumor models with SRSF3 manipulation or overexpression of distinct SERPINH1 isoforms using flow cytometry, histology, and immunofluorescence. SRSF3 was markedly upregulated in HCC tissues and correlated with poor prognosis, reduced cytotoxic immune infiltration, increased regulatory T cells, and elevated PD-L1 expression. Functionally, SRSF3 promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and secretion of immunosuppressive cytokines. In vivo, SRSF3 accelerated tumor growth and reshaped the TME toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. Mechanistically, SRSF3 directly bound to SERPINH1 mRNA and enhanced its expression. Among SERPINH1 isoforms, the short isoform exerted the strongest pro-tumorigenic and pro-fibrotic effects, promoting collagen deposition, tumor proliferation, and immune exclusion. Our findings identify SRSF3 as a critical driver of HCC progression by orchestrating tumor growth, fibrosis, and immune evasion through regulation of SERPINH1, particularly its short isoform. Targeting the SRSF3–SERPINH1 axis may represent a promising strategy to simultaneously inhibit tumor progression and improve antitumor immune responses in HCC.

Article.Title: Genotype by environment interaction and yield stability of common bean genotypes in western Ethiopia using AMMI analysis
Article.Authors: Bacha T.; Ali U.; Belissa S.; Tolani T.; Mendera J.; Barwant M.; Ogidi O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is a vital source of dietary protein and income for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia, yet productivity is severely limited by strong genotype × environment interaction (G×E). This study aimed to quantify G×E on grain yield and identify high-yielding, stable genotypes for western Oromia. Eleven common bean genotypes (white and red seeded types) were evaluated at four contrasting locations (Haru, Bure, Dabo Hana, and Tole) during the 2024 main cropping season using a randomized complete block design with three replications. Data on grain yield (kg/ha⁻¹) were subjected to combined analysis of variance (ANOVA) and additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) analysis using GenStat 18th edition and the R package ‘metan’. AMMI stability value (ASV) and Yield Stability Index (YSI) were computed to rank genotypes. The overall mean yield was 3115.88 kg/ha⁻¹. Genotype, environment, and G×E were highly significant ( p < 0.01), accounting for 14.34%, 28.14%, and 24.00% of the total sum of squares, respectively. The first interaction principal component (IPCA1) captured 64.25% of the G×E sum of squares. Based on ASV, the most stable genotypes were Dinkinesh (ASV = 16.30), Nasir (16.86), and SCR 15 (17.89). However, Nasir combined the highest mean yield (3807.25 kg/ha⁻¹) with excellent stability, while Awash 2 (3206.25 kg/ha⁻¹) showed above-average yield and moderate stability (ASV = 24.37). The AMMI1 biplot confirmed Nasir and Awash 2 as high-yielding, stable genotypes, whereas Tole and Dabo Hana were identified as highly interactive, high-yielding environments. Due to its yield superiority and stability, Nasir is provisionally recommended for the target agro-ecologies, with Awash 2 as a reliable alternative. The single-year data underscore the necessity of multi-season validation before large-scale deployment. These findings provide a basis for enhancing common bean productivity and food security in western Ethiopia.

Article.Title: Traumatic PVR prevention and treatment via composite drug film
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu Y.; Liu J.; Zhu T.; Nan K.; Chen M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to develop a composite sustained-release drug film by incorporating triamcinolone acetonide (TA) and daunorubicin (DNR) into a poly-L-lactide caprolactone (P(LLA-CL)) matrix, and to evaluate its in vitro release characteristics, in vivo biocompatibility, and therapeutic efficacy in the treatment of traumatic proliferative vitreoretinopathy (TPVR). P(LLA-CL) was dissolved in hexafluoroisopropanol, weighed TA and DNR powder, and added it to the P(LLA-CL) solution, and then electrospinning was performed on these materials to prepare P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug films. In vitro release experiments were performed on drug films (4 × 8 mm) and corresponding drug powders placed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). At fixed time points, samples were collected and drug content was calculated by HPLC to record the cumulative drug release curve. The in vivo safety of the drug films was evaluated by suturing the drug films onto the rabbit eyes sclera, 5 mm away from the limbus, and then observing slit-lamp biomicroscopy, intraocular pressure (IOP), and histopathological changes at fixed time points from 1 week to 6 months after suturing. TPVR was constructed by scleral injury and autologous blood injection, and the rabbits were randomly divided into model, control, P(LLA-CL)-TA, P(LLA-CL)-DNR, and composite drug film groups. The observation indices were fundus photography, HE staining, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis of inflammatory factors TNF-α and TGF-β. In vitro release experiment results showed that the P(LLA-CL)-TA and P(LLA-CL)-DNR drug films released the drugs for 156 and 135 days, and the cumulative drug release rates reached 88.41% and 92.68%, respectively. The composite P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR drug film released TA and DNR for 141 days (91.54%) and 129 days (89.31%) respectively, which were greatly prolonged compared with the release time of the drugs powders (48 days and 4 days for TA and DNR, respectively). In vivo experiment results showed that no ocular toxicity or IOP elevation was induced by the drug films. The gradual degradation of drug films was observed during the six-month observation period. In therapeutic application, the composite drug film reduced the retinal folding, preretinal membrane formation and TNF-α mean optical density at 2 weeks [(0.426 ± 0.036) vs. (0.518 ± 0.043) in the model group, P < 0.0001] and at 4 weeks [(0.460 ± 0.040) vs. (0.537 ± 0.029), P = 0.0003], and improved the vitreous hemorrhage ( P = 0.0402). P(LLA-CL)-TA-DNR composite drug film can achieve sustained release of therapeutic agents for up to five months. The drug film exhibits a good safety profile, and showed preliminary therapeutic potential to attenuate TPVR progression via suppressing inflammatory response and cellular proliferation. Compared with single-drug films, the composite film showed marginal improvement of vitreous hemorrhage absorption and reduced retinal proliferation.

Article.Title: Biliary bile acid profiling reveals diagnostic signatures for cholangiocarcinoma and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Arif M.; Braadland P.; Larsson E.; Darwich L.; Natali L.; Burza M.; Hedenström P.; Hov J.; Henricsson M.; Sadik R.; Molinaro A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The early diagnosis of biliopancreatic cancers, including cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), remains challenging because currently available serum biomarkers have limited diagnostic accuracy. Bile acids are bioactive signaling molecules implicated in carcinogenesis and may reflect disease-specific alterations within the biliary microenvironment. We aimed to characterize biliary bile acid profiles in patients with PDAC and CCA and evaluate their diagnostic potential. Bile samples were prospectively collected from the common bile duct during endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) in 71 individuals, including noncancer controls (CTRL, n = 41), patients with PDAC ( n = 14), and patients with CCA ( n = 16). Quantitative bile acid profiling was performed with ultra-performance liquid chromatography‒tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC‒MS‒MS/MS). Random forest, stability selection, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, and elastic net algorithms were used as feature-selection methods to identify diagnostic bile acid signatures, which were evaluated using five-fold cross-validated receiver operating characteristic analysis. PDAC was associated with higher total and primary bile-acid concentrations than CCA, including higher cholic acid concentrations. Compared with controls, CCA was associated with lower total secondary bile-acid concentrations ( p = 0.009), including lower deoxycholic acid ( p = 0.013), lithocholic acid ( p = 0.021), and ursodeoxycholic acid ( p = 0.023) concentrations. After adjustment for bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, glycocholic acid, taurochenodeoxycholic acid, and taurohyocholic acid were selected by all four feature-selection methods. Their combined model achieved a cross-validated area under the curve of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.79–0.90), compared with 0.67 (95% CI, 0.58–0.76) for CA19-9 and 0.61 (95% CI, 0.51–0.71) for CEA. A separate bile-acid model distinguished CCA from PDAC with an area under the curve of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.72–0.99), 85.7% sensitivity, and 87.5% specificity. CCA and PDAC patients exhibit distinct biliary bile acid profiles. Bile acid signatures identified after adjustment for cholestasis may complement conventional serum biomarkers during ERCP-based evaluation of indeterminate biliary strictures.

Article.Title: The systemic immune-inflammation index is associated with prevalent chronic kidney disease in adults with hypertension
Article.Authors: Duan H.; Zhao Z.; Zhang J.; Li M.; Lou T.; Yin Y.; Ma S.; Zhao M.; Zhang Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypertension and chronic kidney disease (CKD) interact bidirectionally, forming a vicious cycle, while chronic low-grade inflammation represents a central pathway mediating hypertensive renal injury. The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), calculated from routine complete blood count parameters, comprehensively reflects systemic inflammatory and immune imbalance. However, evidence from large-scale stratified analyses and robust validation remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between SII and prevalent CKD in adults with hypertension in a nationally representative sample and to assess the consistency of the findings across multiple propensity score weighting approaches. This cross-sectional study included 18,675 adults with hypertension from the 2001–2020 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Analyses accounted for NHANES examination weights, strata, and primary sampling units. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and stratified interaction analyses were performed. The consistency of the findings was assessed using propensity score weighting approaches targeting the average treatment effect (ATE), the average treatment effect among the treated, and the average treatment effect in the overlap population. After full adjustment, each 1-standard-deviation increment in log1p-transformed SII was associated with higher odds of CKD (OR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.04–1.17, P = 0.002). Compared with the lowest SII quartile, the highest quartile had higher odds of CKD (OR = 1.23; 95% CI, 1.03–1.47, P = 0.023). The fully adjusted spline showed a significant overall association ( P = 0.002), whereas the test for nonlinearity was not significant ( P = 0.267). The association was stronger among participants younger than 60 years ( P for interaction = 0.017). Overlap weighting yielded an OR of 1.192 (95% CI, 1.064–1.334, P = 0.002) for high versus low SII. Higher SII was associated with greater odds of CKD among individuals with hypertension. SII may serve as an auxiliary inflammatory biomarker associated with CKD in individuals with hypertension.

Article.Title: Context-aware forecasting of inter-firm competitive dynamics with graph learning and multi-agent reasoning
Article.Authors: Park D.; Kwon Y.; Han S.; Yoo P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evolution of competitive dominance in technology-intensive industries is shaped by complex interactions among research activity, media visibility, strategic disclosures, public attention, and market signals. Understanding these dynamics is critical for strategic intelligence, yet existing predictive models often treat firms as isolated entities and provide limited support for contextualizing long-horizon firm-to-firm competitive forecasts. Here, we introduce an integrated framework that captures the relational nature of market competition by extending our prior Bayesian Multivariate Time-series Graph Neural Network with a newly designed, post hoc, lookahead-free multi-agent reasoning layer. The framework infers inter-firm relational dependencies endogenously from multimodal signals to forecast latent firm competitiveness and pairwise competitive gap trajectories with quantified predictive uncertainty. To evaluate strategic plausibility, specialized persona-driven language model agents critique the forecasted trajectories across technological, financial, and regulatory lenses using retrieved evidence. Evaluated under a rigorous date-based temporal protocol with strictly withheld test horizons, the framework consistently outperforms competitive structural baselines and yields well-calibrated prediction intervals. When applied to thirty leading AI-oriented technology firms, the framework uncovers asymmetric competitive momentum, contested market leadership, and emerging challenger dynamics. By bridging relational time-series forecasting with structured multi-agent deliberation, this study advances competitive dynamics analysis from purely accuracy-centric prediction toward context-aware, uncertainty-informed strategic intelligence.

Article.Title: Hill-based reformulation of the Hodgkin-Huxley model for mapping gating changes to neuronal excitability
Article.Authors: Saab B.; Fahs J.; Daou A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conductance-based models link ion-channel gating to neuronal excitability, but mutation reports often provide steady-state voltage shifts without sufficient kinetic measurements to specify a unique model. We introduce a Hill-based reformulation of selected Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) gating relationships and evaluate its usefulness under this low-information constraint. The hybrid formulation retains canonical HH-like spike waveforms and frequency–current behavior after a modest remapping of applied current, while providing an explicit mapping from reported activation descriptors to model parameters under specified assumptions. An A863P kinetic-sensitivity analysis shows how steady-state constraints and kinetic assumptions jointly shape excitability predictions in both classical HH and Hill-based implementations. The Hill formulation makes this mapping reproducible through explicit parameter relations, whereas refitting classical HH rates requires additional fitting choices; both approaches still require kinetic assumptions. Retrospective benchmarks using the Nav1.7 mutations A863P, F1449V, and A1632G show that the Hill-based model captures the qualitative increase in excitability but overestimates the magnitude of threshold reduction. Classical HH comparisons for A863P demonstrate that similar qualitative predictions can also be obtained under specified kinetic assumptions. These findings support the Hill formulation as a reproducible framework for mapping reported gating changes onto HH-like excitability, without establishing superior quantitative prediction of mutation effects. Quantitative transfer to mutation-specific neuronal behavior requires additional kinetic and cellular constraints.

Article.Title: Cost-effectiveness and carbon footprint of cystoscopic surveillance schedules in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repeated cystoscopy for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer incurs costs and greenhouse-gas emissions, but fewer examinations may delay recurrence detection. We compared nine surveillance schedules in a 15-year monthly cohort model stratified by European Association of Urology risk group. We used 2021 United States costs and an international emissions inventory. In low-risk patients, ending scheduled surveillance after the three-month examination, while retaining investigation of symptoms, reduced modelled costs by 24.0% and inventoried emissions by 13.0% compared with guideline follow-up. Time spent with undetected recurrence increased. In 5,000 paired simulations, the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years for this low-risk comparison was 0.009 per patient (95% uncertainty interval, -0.260 to 0.291). Clinical results depended on progression before recurrence detection and diagnosis prompted by symptoms; less favourable assumptions increased progression and bladder-cancer deaths. Recurrence treatment accounted for most inventoried emissions, limiting the carbon savings from fewer cystoscopies. Selected reductions in low-risk surveillance warrant prospective evaluation, but the model does not establish the safety of stopping scheduled surveillance after one examination.

Article.Title: Cortical activation during hand grasping in Parkinson’s disease with different motor onset sides: an fNIRS study
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Guo J.; Liu D.; Wu Q.; Qiao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motor symptom asymmetry is a key feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD), but how onset side affects cortical activation during motor tasks remains unclear. This study used functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to investigate cortical activation and task-related lateralization during hand grasping in left-onset PD (LPD, n = 29), right-onset PD (RPD, n = 35), and healthy controls (HC, n = 14). During the left-hand task, both PD groups showed lower mean ΔHbO in the right primary somatosensory cortex than HC (LPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.027; RPD vs. HC: pFDR = 0.022), with altered peak timing in the right frontal eye field (pFDR = 0.004 and 0.011). During the right-hand task, the RPD group showed lower activation in the right somatosensory association cortex (vs. HC pFDR = 0.039; vs. LPD pFDR = 0.024) and reduced peak activation (pFDR = 0.021), with shortened full width at half maximum in bilateral S1, M1, and SMA (all pFDR < 0.05). Lateralization analysis showed reversed task-related lateralization in the right primary somatosensory cortex in LPD (deltapeak: pFDR = 0.047) and altered task-related lateralization of timing in the right frontal eye field in both PD groups (pFDR = 0.034). In an exploratory analysis, longer disease duration was associated with shorter R-SAC time-to-peak in RPD but not LPD ( p = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵, q = 2.4 × 10⁻³ globally). Motor onset side is associated with distinct sensorimotor cortical dysfunction, with RPD showing more widespread deficits, whereas delayed FEF timing is a shared alteration independent of onset side. Temporal-domain metrics were more consistently affected than amplitude-based measures and may capture cortical changes missed by intensity indices.

Article.Title: Low-frequency noise reduction in laser-induced graphene devices by noble metal nanoparticles decoration
Article.Authors: Drozdowska-Czubek K.; Smulko J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sensors or contact paths in wearable electronics due to their elastic properties, and their inherent noise impacts their performance. The simple NPs modification of the LIG surface resulted in a noise-reduction effect, which increased in the following order: Pt<Ag<Au for the devices investigated here.​ Au-decorated LIG exhibited a 32-times reduction of normalized voltage noise. This result was observed independently of photoactivation or plasmonic resonance induction in the NPs. The most significant effect was observed for Au-decorated LIG. We propose the interpretation that AuNPs occupy the LIG surface, which may create a damping effect on phonon vibrations, thereby decreasing the intensity of mobility fluctuations responsible for flicker noise generation as reported for other materials. The weaker effect observed for Ag-/Pt-decorated LIGs can be ascribed to differences in contact forces existing between these nanoparticles and graphene compared to AuNPs. Our work points out that Au-decorated graphene has high potential for use in low-noise electronics and that low inherent noise is required to employ graphene and graphene-like structures in practical sensing applications.

Article.Title: Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Tang W.; Du H.; Xu R.; Huang C.; Zhang W.; Luo Q.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract China contributes to approximately 20% of the global burden of hypertension; however, a nationwide epidemiological survey on the prevalence of hypertension among older adults is lacking. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension among older adults in China. The data were derived from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) in 2015. We included 7,733 participants aged 60 years and older. The prevalence of hypertension was 53.1% (95% CI 51.7–54.6%), which is equivalent to 140 million adults aged 60 years or older with hypertension in China. Among the participants with hypertension, 74.1% (95% CI 72.5–75.8%) were aware of their condition, 54.5% (95% CI 52.5–56.5%) were treated, and only 33.7% (95% CI 31.8–35.6%) were controlled. Systolic blood pressure increased with age ( r = 0.504, P < 0.001), whereas diastolic blood pressure decreased with age ( r = − 0.175, P < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension increased with age (P for trend < 0.001). The prevalence of hypertension was observed to be higher in urban areas (57.0%, 95% CI 53.7–60.3%) than in rural areas (51.2%, 95% CI 49.8–52.6%) ( P = 0.002), along with the prevalence being higher in northern areas (56.8%, 95% CI 54.7–58.8%) than in southern areas (50.7%, 95% CI 48.8–52.7%) ( P < 0.001). Spanning from the western provinces to the central provinces to the eastern areas, the prevalence of hypertension was 50.8% (95% CI 48.6–53.1%), 52.6% (95% CI 50.4–54.8%), and 55.6% (95% CI 52.7–58.5%) (P for trend < 0.001), respectively. Multivariable analysis revealed that older age (65–69 years group: OR = 1.292, 95% CI 1.105–1.512; 70–74 years group: OR = 1.482, 95% CI 1.235–1.779; 75–79 years group: OR = 1.922, 95% CI 1.569–2.355; ≥ 80 years group: OR = 2.192, 95% CI 1.739–2.764), living in northern areas (OR = 1.197, 95% CI 1.054–1.360), drinking more than once a month (OR = 1.187, 95% CI 1.000–1.410), obesity (OR = 2.568, 95% CI 1.977–3.336), diabetes (OR = 1.694, 95% CI 1.443–1.989), and dyslipidaemia (OR = 1.378, 95% CI 1.218–1.559) were positively correlated with hypertension, whereas being married (or cohabitating) (OR = 0.772, 95% CI 0.668–0.892) was negatively correlated with hypertension. The prevalence of hypertension was high in people aged 60 years or older in China; however, the rates of control of hypertension remain low. Efforts are needed to prevent hypertension and improve the treatment and control of hypertension.

Article.Title: Explainable IoT intrusion detection via bio-inspired encoding and interpretable AI models
Article.Authors: AL Ibaisi T.; Kazim M.; Ur Rehman M.; Kaiiali M.; Kuhn S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We introduce an explainable Internet of Things (IoT) intrusion detection framework built on a bio-inspired Amino Acid encoding of network flows. The flow features are first transformed with the Yeo–Johnson transformation, the most informative ones are selected, and their values are encoded as Amino Acid sequences, which are then summarized by ten protein structural properties (e.g., $$\beta $$ -Turn, Isoelectric Point and Molecular Weight). In this way every flow is described by the same compact set of ten properties, whatever the feature set of the original dataset. The models are explained with SHAP, LIME and ELI5, complemented by Captum Integrated Gradients and Alibi anchors for the neural models, and the attributions are linked back to the raw traffic features through measured correlations. On a balanced 50,000-flow subset of CICIoT2023 that covers all 33 attack classes, most of the 12 classical and 5 deep models reach 98.4–98.5% accuracy on a held-out test set (MCC up to 0.97). The recurrent neural network (RNN), used for the in-depth explainability study, reaches 98.5% accuracy with a false-alarm rate of 0.02%, has fewer than 15,000 parameters and needs about 0.1 ms per flow on a CPU. An ablation experiment shows that encoding the selected features keeps detection close to the full 39-feature raw representation (MCC 0.970 against 0.979), while giving a fixed ten-property input that can be explained. All explanation methods agree that $$\beta $$ -Turn and Isoelectric Point drive most decisions, and both properties correlate strongly with the packet count and packet size of the flows.

Article.Title: Geotechnical characterization and foundation competence evaluation using shallow seismic refraction: a case study from Ain Sokhna, Gulf of Suez, Egypt
Article.Authors: Farag M.; Shebl S.; Soliman S.; Shazly T.; Abed M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evaluation of subsurface conditions and foundation competence is essential for sustainable infrastructure development in the Ain Sokhna area along the Gulf of Suez, Egypt. This study applies shallow seismic refraction surveys to characterize the geotechnical properties of near-surface materials and assess their suitability for engineering and construction. Seismic P-wave (Vp) velocities obtained from twenty survey sites were integrated with measured S-wave (Vs) velocities and density values to derive a comprehensive set of dynamic geotechnical parameters, including Poisson’s ratio, shear modulus, Young’s modulus, bulk modulus, material index, concentration index, stress ratio, ultimate bearing capacity, and allowable bearing capacity. Results reveal pronounced spatial variations in subsurface engineering characteristics. P-wave velocities range from 677 to 2330 m/s, while S-wave velocities vary between 376 and 1355 m/s. Velocity distributions show a systematic decrease from the northeastern to the southwestern sector, reflecting reduced density, stiffness, and rock-mass competence. This trend is corroborated by elastic parameters: shear modulus ranges from 224 to 3954 MPa, Young’s modulus from 571 to 9842 MPa, and bulk modulus from 427 to 6420 MPa. The northeastern sector exhibits higher velocities and moduli, indicating compacted, mechanically competent foundation materials, whereas the southwest shows lower values, suggesting increased fracturing, weathering, and diminished geotechnical quality. Bearing-capacity analyses are consistent with this zonation, with ultimate values between 2.0 and 85.4 kg/cm 2 and allowable values from 0.7 to 28.5 kg/cm 2 . The highest capacities occur in the northeast, while progressively weaker conditions dominate toward the southwest. The integrated results delineate two broad geotechnical zones, with comparatively competent materials in the northeastern, eastern, and central sectors and moderately competent materials toward the southwest.

Article.Title: Machine-learning-assisted prediction and optimization of tensile strength in particulate-filled polymer composites
Article.Authors: Fuxian Z.; Wen Z.; Bailiang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Particulate-filled polymer composites (PFPCs) are characterized by high specific strength, good formability, and considerable design flexibility, making them key materials for rapid tooling in aerospace equipment manufacturing. In this study, metal-powder/resin composites were investigated, and a tensile-strength dataset comprising 45 independent experimental conditions was established. Three machine-learning regression algorithms, namely linear least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR), were employed to develop tensile-strength prediction models. A fixed outer five-fold cross-validation procedure was used to obtain out-of-fold (OOF) predictions, while hyperparameters were selected through inner five-fold cross-validation within each outer training fold; a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently used to further optimize the SVR hyperparameters. The OOF RMSE, MAE, and R² values of SVR were 1.67 MPa, 1.32 MPa, and 0.882, respectively, and those of GA-SVR were 1.54 MPa, 1.21 MPa, and 0.901. With increasing particle volume fraction and particle size, the tensile strength initially increased and then decreased, whereas ball-milling time had a relatively limited effect. Single-parameter analysis yielded predicted peak positions of approximately 34.80%, 30.92 μm, and 2.68 h for particle volume fraction, particle size, and ball-milling time, respectively. Continuous searching within the experimental domain identified a high-strength parameter combination of f = 34.63%, D = 30.67 μm, and t = 2.65 h, corresponding to a predicted tensile strength of 61.33 MPa. The measured strengths of three independent validation specimens prepared using a nominal particle size of 31 μm were 61.12, 60.93, and 60.56 MPa, with a mean of 60.87 ± 0.28 MPa, a coefficient of variation of 0.47%, and a relative deviation of 0.75% between the experimental mean and model prediction. Within the current experimental domain, the proposed framework can provide a quantitative reference for PFPC tensile-strength prediction and formulation/process-parameter screening, and offers an efficient strategy for accelerating formulation design and optimization while reducing experimental cost. Its implementation also provided students with practical experience in applying machine-learning algorithms to material-strength prediction and parameter design.

Article.Title: Polygenic associations with COVID-19 severity across two danish cohorts: relationships with pre-infection health
Article.Authors: Quinn L.; Geller F.; Feenstra B.; Vestergaard L.; Hjalgrim H.; Kaspersen K.; Didriksen M.; Dinh K.; Nissen J.; Hindhede L.; Schwinn M.; Saekmose S.; Werge T.; Bruun M.; Aagaard B.; Sørensen E.; Erikstrup C.; Ullum H.; Schork A.; Ostrowski S.; Christoffersen L.; Pedersen O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract COVID-19 severity varies widely between individuals, reflecting a combination of demographic, clinical, and genetic risk factors. Although polygenic scores (PGS’s) are increasingly used to study susceptibility to infectious disease, it remains unclear to what extent these associations are sensitive to health characteristics present before infection. We examined PGS associations across four disease domains with COVID-19 severity outcomes in two complementary Danish cohorts: 14,364 participants from the Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS), with self-reported bedridden COVID-19, and 115,515 participants from the Copenhagen Hospital Biobank (CHB), with register-defined COVID-19 severity among individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. PGSs surviving false-discovery-rate correction were examined across sequential models adjusting for pandemic period, measured pre-infection health and vaccination status at infection. Associations were quantified using population-standardised risk differences with 5,000 bootstrap iterations used to generate 95% CIs for risk estimates. Eight PGSs were associated with bedridden COVID-19 in DBDS and nine with register-defined COVID-19 severity in CHB, with seven associations shared across cohorts and showing concordant directions. In our nested sequential adjustment models adjustment for pre-infection health resulted in heterogeneous changes across PGSs. In DBDS, the risk difference per 1-SD higher ADHD PGS decreased from 1.75% points after adjustment for pandemic period to 1.31 after additional adjustment for pre-infection BMI and physical and mental health, whereas the corresponding influenza PGS association changed from 2.00 to 1.83% points. In CHB, ADHD PGS decreased from 0.49 to 0.40% points following adjustment for pre-pandemic comorbidity, while the COVID-19 severity PGS remained stable (0.19 to 0.19% points). Vaccination adjustment generally produced comparatively little additional attenuation. In our study, polygenic liabilities across multiple disease domains were associated with COVID-19 severity outcomes, but their associations showed varying sensitivity to adjustment for measured pre-infection health across two distinct cohort settings and two distinct pre-infection health measures. These findings suggest that cross-trait polygenic associations with COVID-19 differ in their relationships with pre-existing health highlighting the importance of pre-existing health when interpreting genetic associations with infectious disease outcomes.

Article.Title: A cue-locality audit framework for attributing spurious temporal shortcuts in deep sequence models
Article.Authors: Cho Y.; Kim D.; Kim Y.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High accuracy on independent and identically distributed (IID) test data does not reveal which temporal cue a sequence model uses. A directional process can leave a cue in individual frames, so out-of-distribution (OOD) failure alone does not establish temporal-order use. We propose a six-gate audit that attributes failure to a nuisance and distinguishes frame-local, order-invariant multi-frame, and order-encoded cues. A companion controlled benchmark provides the factor-level probes and interventions the audit requires. Applied to this benchmark, the audit revealed that a variant designed to encode temporal order was instead solvable from individual frames. In the strict order-encoded variant (OE-Strict), direction is readable only from interior frame order. With nuisance direction aligned with the label with probability 0.97 during training, a gated recurrent unit (GRU) trained by empirical risk minimization (ERM) selects the shortcut in thirty of thirty seeds (0.970 IID and 0.030 OOD accuracy). Channel-selective interventions attribute the collapse to nuisance frame ordering. The audit distinguishes which process supports a prediction and whether using that process requires temporal order.

Article.Title: Sociodemographic correlates of physical literacy among urban adults aged 20–59 years: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; He J.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical literacy (PL) is widely regarded as a cornerstone of lifelong physical activity (PA) participation. However, empirical research on PL and its sociodemographic correlates in adult populations remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the sociodemographic correlates of PL among Chinese urban adults aged 20–59 years. We used convenience sampling to recruit 731 participants, of whom 80.4% held a bachelor’s degree or higher. PL was measured using a previously developed assessment tool for Chinese adults, covering three domains: PA cognition, PA-related behavior, and physical competence. Univariate analyses and hierarchical multiple linear regression were conducted to identify correlates of PL. Univariate analyses showed significant differences in the total PL scores across age, health status, city, education level, personal monthly disposable income, and frequency of health checkups ( P < 0.05). After controlling for city, the final regression model revealed that PL was significantly associated with age ( β = -0.15, P < 0.001), health status ( β = 0.11, P = 0.002), holding a bachelor’s degree or higher (β = 0.15, P = 0.007), a personal monthly disposable income exceeding 9000 yuan ( β = 0.08, P = 0.05), and undergoing annual or biennial health checkups ( β = 0.26, P = 0.001; β = 0.10, P = 0.04). Notably, the models explained a modest proportion of variance in total PL (adjusted R² = 0.27) and a very small proportion for the PA cognition domain (adjusted R² = 0.02). PL among urban Chinese adults with relatively high education levels is associated with age, health status, education, income, and regular health checkups. However, the limited explanatory power of these sociodemographic factors suggests that future research should incorporate broader psychosocial and environmental determinants to inform more effective intervention design.
