Article.Title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy across acute and post-acute phases after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a multi-cohort randomized controlled pilot study (HOT-RESUS 1)
Article.Authors: Schnaubelt S.; Snijders E.; Strouven C.; Janssens E.; Verdonck P.; Lateur J.; Peeters M.; Vermeersch G.; De Paep R.; Saenen J.; Snoeckx A.; Sulzgruber P.; De Maeyer C.; Schlager O.; Jorens P.; Monsieurs K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains untested in humans despite promising preclinical evidence. We thus evaluated feasibility, tolerability, observed treatment-related adverse events, and early biological signals of HBOT across three distinct clinical cohorts and exposure subgroups. This prospective, single-centre, randomized, controlled, open-label pilot study enrolled (i) Intensive Care Unit (ICU) patients with sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) within the preceding 24 h, (ii) long-term OHCA survivors, and (iii) healthy volunteers. Within each cohort, participants were randomized to no HBOT, one HBOT session, or five HBOT sessions. Assessments included serial laboratory biomarkers, vascular function, neurocognitive testing, and patient-reported outcomes. Analyses were primarily descriptive, with additional between-group comparisons considered exploratory. The prespecified recruitment target was achieved (45/45 participants), all assigned HBOT sessions were completed (90/90; 100%), and all scheduled blood samples were obtained. No HBOT-related adverse events occurred. In ICU patients, serial biomarkers demonstrated pronounced temporal changes during the acute post-cardiac-arrest phase across inflammatory, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, neuronal injury, and myocardial injury domains, whereas direct comparison of trajectories between HBOT groups were generally inconclusive. In long-term OHCA survivors and healthy volunteers, exploratory analyses suggested reductions in arterial stiffness and, particularly among survivors, favourable changes in neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Given the small subgroup sizes, extensive multiplicity, and generally inconclusive direct between-group comparisons, these findings remain exploratory. HOT-RESUS 1 demonstrated that the prespecified recruitment and HBOT procedures could be completed as planned, including treatment of selected acute post-ROSC ICU patients in a specialised hyperbaric centre, with no HBOT-related adverse events observed. Exploratory analyses showed dynamics of inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, arterial stiffness, and neurocognitive and patient-reported outcomes, with several favourable numerical patterns observed in HBOT-exposed groups. Although the small pilot sample, extensive multiplicity, and largely inconclusive direct between-group comparisons preclude attribution of these changes to HBOT or conclusions regarding biological or clinical efficacy, the findings identify possible biological and functional outcomes for further investigation in adequately powered randomized trials.

Article.Title: Nano-curcumin-mediated antibacterial photodynamic therapy activated by blue diode laser or blue LED against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals
Article.Authors: Sherif H.; Abdelgawad L.; Zaki D.; Sherief M.; Eissa S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the antibacterial efficacy of nano-curcumin activated by a 450-nm diode laser or a blue light-emitting diode (LED) against Enterococcus faecalis biofilms in infected root canals. Sixty-six extracted human single-rooted teeth were prepared, sterilized, inoculated with Enterococcus faecalis , and incubated at 37 °C for three weeks. Six specimens were used to confirm biofilm formation by scanning electron microscopy (SEM; n = 3) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM; n = 3). The remaining 60 specimens were randomly allocated into six experimental groups ( n = 10 per group): Group 1, 2.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl); Group 2, diode laser alone; Group 3, LED alone; Group 4, nano-curcumin; Group 5, nano-curcumin + diode laser; and Group 6, nano-curcumin + LED. Antibacterial efficacy was evaluated by colony-forming unit (CFU) counts and CLSM-based live/dead biofilm assessment. Data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Tukey’s post hoc test ( p < 0.05). Significant reductions in Enterococcus faecalis CFU counts were observed in all treatment groups compared with baseline ( p < 0.05), except for Groups 2 and 3. Group 1 exhibited the greatest antibacterial efficacy (99% CFU reduction), followed by Group 5 (70.02%) and Group 6 (68.29%), whereas Group 4 demonstrated a modest antibacterial effect (27.86% CFU reduction). CLSM findings were consistent with the CFU results, with Group 1 exhibiting the greatest reduction in biofilm viability, followed by Groups 5 and 6. Within the limitations of this in vitro study, activation of nano-curcumin with either a 450-nm diode laser or a blue LED enhanced its antibacterial activity and may have potential as an adjunctive approach to conventional root canal disinfection.

Article.Title: Distribution and genetic relatedness of multidrug-resistant E. coli in poultry farms: a One Health perspective
Article.Authors: Wafa A.; Bakr W.; Omran E.; Elsenduony M.; ElSayed N.; Reda O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The prevalence of pathogens, including multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, especially extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing E. coli (ESBL-EC), in poultry farms is a matter of public health and One Health significance. This cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the distribution and genetic relatedness of MDR and ESBL-producing E. coli from different reservoirs in poultry farms. A total of 90 samples were collected from five poultry farms: 60 chicken samples (66.7%), 15 farm-worker stool samples (16.7%), and 15 pooled environmental samples (16.7%), comprising five pooled litter samples, five pooled farm-soil samples, and five pooled agricultural-soil samples. Chickens were selected using a simple random technique (12 samples from each of the five farms), and all available farm workers were included. E. coli was isolated and identified, and the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of the isolates was determined. All isolates were genotyped using Enterobacterial Repetitive Intergenic Consensus polymerase chain reaction (ERIC-PCR) to assess similarity and genetic relatedness among isolates from the different compartments. Out of the total 90 samples, 52.2% ( n = 47) were MDR and 40.0% ( n = 36) were ESBL-producing E. coli . Among the 60 chicken samples, 63.3% ( n = 38) were MDR and 50.0% ( n = 30) were ESBL producers. Among the 15 pooled environmental samples, 46.7% ( n = 7) were MDR-positive and 26.7% ( n = 4) were ESBL-positive. Relatively lower ESBL positivity was observed among farm workers (2/15; 13.3%). Similar ERIC-PCR fingerprint patterns were observed among isolates from chickens, workers, and environmental compartments. Chicken isolates showed higher observed MDR and ESBL positivity than isolates from the pooled environmental samples and farm workers. Similar ERIC-PCR profiles across sources suggest genetic relatedness and potential epidemiological connectivity. These findings underscore the value of integrated One Health surveillance strategies.

Article.Title: The Cdh23tm2a mouse allele causes progressive hearing loss that is not improved by postnatal Cdh23 gene expression
Article.Authors: Pentland D.; Blackburn J.; Altiti B.; Ingham N.; Kirwin D.; Steel K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cdh23 encodes cadherin related 23, a cadherin which is an essential component of the tip link of stereocilia on the sensory hair cells of the inner ear. Mutations in human CDH23 lead to either non-syndromic deafness or Usher syndrome, while mutations in mouse Cdh23 lead to hearing impairment with or without balance defects. Here we characterise the Cdh23 tm2a mouse mutant and show that the mutation causes reduced transcription of Cdh23 and early-onset progressive hearing loss in Cdh23 tm2a/tm2a homozygotes. Cdh23 +/tm2a heterozygotes also exhibit progressive hearing loss but only at high frequencies, and this was dependent on the presence of the Cdh23 ahl allele which is present in the background C57BL/6N strain. Scanning electron microscopy revealed stereocilia bundle defects in homozygous mutants but stereocilia appeared normal in heterozygotes. To investigate whether hearing loss could be reversed by inducing expression of the gene, we removed the transcription disruption cassette within the Cdh23 tm2a mutant allele using tamoxifen-inducible Flp recombinase at either 4 days or 21 days old, but no improvements in Auditory Brainstem Response thresholds or stereocilia bundle appearance were detected. These findings suggest that any treatments for Cdh23 -associated hearing loss would probably need to applied very early in development, before stereocilia are fully formed.

Article.Title: Intraspecific differentiation in metabolite diversity of a monotypic endemic Indianthus in the Western Ghats
Article.Authors: Bhat K.; Pandi V.; Gayathri R.; Mahim B.; Udupa S.; Muthusamy A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Indianthus virgatus (Marantaceae), a monotypic genus endemic to the Western Ghats–Sri Lanka Biodiversity Hotspot, represents an evolutionarily distinctive lineage for which intraspecific metabolomic variation remains poorly documented. Such variation can provide insights into biochemical differentiation among populations and potential environmental interactions. We used untargeted high-resolution liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (HR-LC-MS) to characterize metabolomic diversity across nine geographically distinct populations of I. virgatus in the Western Ghats. A total of 3,673 metabolite features were detected, of which 214 putative plant-derived metabolites were annotated and retained for downstream analyses following quality filtering. Multivariate analyses revealed differences in metabolomic profiles among the sampled population composites. Principal component analysis showed that the first two components explained 51.2% of the total variation. Variable importance in projection analysis highlighted glutamyl derivatives, amino acid intermediates, and phenolic compounds as important contributors to the observed separation. Distance-based redundancy analysis identified precipitation during the coldest quarter as the only individually significant environmental predictor ( P < 0.05), although the overall model was not statistically significant ( P > 0.05). KEGG pathway analysis indicated nominal enrichment of pyrimidine metabolism, which did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction (FDR = 0.0539). This preliminary metabolomic characterization provides a biochemical foundation for future multi-omics investigations integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic data to elucidate the ecological and evolutionary processes underlying intraspecific diversity in I. virgatus . It also suggests a basis for further research into its phytochemical composition, bioactive compounds, and potential pharmacological applications.

Article.Title: Multifunctional isoliquiritigenin-loaded chitosan/alginate hydrogels with antibacterial and antifibrotic potential for wound dressing applications
Article.Authors: Tymetska S.; Wnuk D.; Bernasik A.; Brzychczy-Włoch M.; Drożdż K.; Targosz‐Korecka M.; Ozimek J.; Szajna K.; Krok F.; Raczkowska J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic wounds present complex healing challenges due to bacterial infection, persistent inflammation, and dysregulated extracellular matrix remodeling. Although isoliquiritigenin (ISL) exhibits potent anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifibrotic properties, its low aqueous solubility hinders direct hydrogel incorporation. Here, alginate (Alg)- and chitosan/alginate (Cht/Alg)-based hydrogels were developed for localized ISL delivery, using Tween 20 (Tw20) or decyl glucoside (DecGlu) as non-ionic surfactants to enhance compound release. Polymer composition and surfactant addition significantly influenced hydrogel morphology, swelling, surface chemistry, micromechanical properties, and porosity. Surfactant-enriched Alg formulations increased ISL release by 52–76% within 24 h. In vitro assays demonstrated high cytocompatibility for Cht/Alg systems (>80% viability in MTT and >90% in crystal violet/LDH assays at 144 h), whereas the Alg/Tw20 formulation exhibited cytotoxicity. ISL-containing extracts significantly attenuated TGF-β 1 induced fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, reducing α-SMA-positive cells by 50% for Alg and 29% for Cht/Alg, with DecGlu further reducing them to 15.0% and 20.0%, respectively. ISL also reduced total collagen I and fibronectin protein levels. Furthermore, Cht/Alg hydrogels exhibited marked antibacterial activity, achieving 4- and 5-log reductions in Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , respectively. Overall, ISL-enriched Cht/Alg-DecGlu hydrogels represent a promising multifunctional wound-contact platform combining localized bioactive delivery, excellent cytocompatibility, antibacterial efficacy, and potent modulation of profibrotic responses.

Article.Title: Aligning clinical decisions with patient values: a quantitative analysis of patient and physician preferences in liver cancer treatment decisions
Article.Authors: Winkelmann C.; Bengart P.; Vogt B.; Wacker F.; Neumann T.; Dewald C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract When several liver-directed treatments are feasible, patients and physicians may weigh survival benefit, treatment-related risk, and short-term physical burden differently. We used choice-based conjoint analysis with hierarchical Bayes estimation and preference-share simulations to compare preferences of 69 patients with hepatic malignancies and 40 gastroenterologists in Germany across three scenarios describing early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (Case 1), an isolated colorectal liver metastasis (Case 2) and metastatic uveal melanoma with diffuse hepatic involvement (Case 3). Lifetime extension was the most important attribute for both groups in all scenarios. Patients assigned greater relative importance to well-being after the intervention in Cases 1 and 2 (25.2% vs 10.9% and 22.3% vs 12.1%, posterior probability of direction [pd] ≥ 99%), whereas gastroenterologists assigned greater importance to tumor-removal probability in Case 1 (24.3% vs 17.2%, pd 95.8%). In Case 2, the simulated ablation share was higher among patients (86.6% vs 71.8%, p < 0.01), with the complementary resection share higher among gastroenterologists. In Case 3, simulated shares did not differ significantly. Whether and in which attributes the two groups differed thus depended on the clinical scenario. Patient priorities should therefore not be inferred from general assumptions but addressed explicitly during shared decision-making.

Article.Title: The brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge for establishing correspondence between pre-operative and follow-up MRI scans of diffuse glioma patients
Article.Authors: Baheti B.; Chakrabarty S.; Akbari H.; Bilello M.; Wiestler B.; Schwarting J.; Calabrese E.; Rudie J.; Abidi S.; Mousa M.; Villanueva-Meyer J.; Fields B.; Kofler F.; Shinohara R.; Iglesias J.; Mok T.; Chung A.; Wodzinski M.; Jurgas A.; Marini N.; Atzori M.; Müller H.; Großbröhmer C.; Siebert H.; Hansen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Registration of longitudinal brain MRI scans containing pathologies remains a challenging problem, due to substantial changes in tissue appearance. While medical image registration methods have advanced considerably, they often lack the required precision and robustness. To address this gap, we introduced the brain tumor sequence registration (BraTS-Reg) challenge, the first public benchmark specifically designed for deformable registration between pre-operative and follow-up scans of patients with adult-type diffuse gliomas. Conducted in conjunction with ISBI-2022 and MICCAI-2022, BraTS-Reg provides de-identified, multi-institutional, multi-parametric MRI data accompanied by expert-annotated landmark points across time. Training data with ground truth annotations were publicly released for algorithm development, while validation data without annotations enabled pre-testing. Submitted containerized algorithms were evaluated on hidden testing cases. Quantitative evaluation was based on median Euclidean error (MEE), Robustness, and the determinant of Jacobian of the displacement field. Top-ranked methods demonstrated comparable performance and shared key features, including pre-alignment of scans, deep neural networks, inverse consistency analysis, and per-case test-time optimization. The best method achieved MEE comparable to inter-rater variability for 63% of landmarks, underscoring the need for further improvements in accuracy and robustness relative to human experts. BraTS-Reg serves as a three-fold active resource for research on image registration, providing a publicly available dataset, a framework for a community benchmark, and online evaluation tools, accessible at https://bratsreg.github.io/ .

Article.Title: Process evaluation showing the importance of co-located, high-intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support in a lung cancer screening setting
Article.Authors: McCutchan G.; Quinn-Scoggins H.; Tong H.; Smith P.; Quaife S.; Callister M.; Thorley R.; Baldwin D.; Beeken R.; Copeland H.; Crosbie P.; Lewis S.; Rogerson S.; Wu Q.; Murray R.; Brain K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evidence regarding optimal integration of smoking cessation is needed to inform implementation of lung cancer screening (LCS) and reduce smoking-related inequalities. The Yorkshire Enhanced Stop Smoking Randomised Controlled Trial tested opt-out, co-located standard best practice (SBP) smoking cessation support (control) versus SBP enhanced with theory-informed, personalised risk information derived from participants’ lung scan results to boost quit motivation (intervention). The intervention was tailored to degree of lung/heart damage, and designed to optimise self-efficacy and response-efficacy for quitting smoking 1 . Smoking cessation practitioners (SCPs) received bespoke intervention training in delivering theory-informed behaviour change techniques (BCTs). We conducted a nested process evaluation to evaluate the implementation of optimised smoking cessation support compared to SBP. Semi-structured interviews were carried out with 45 trial participants and eight SCPs at 4-, 12- and 52-weeks after screening (participants) or training (SCPs). Interviews were analysed thematically to assess intervention fidelity, exposure, context, contamination and theory. Observations of SCP consultations on the mobile screening unit (n = 84; 4%) and 4-weeks after screening (n = 132; 13%) were analysed to test fidelity, context and contamination. Intervention context was paramount: participants in both trial arms described benefits of co-located and ongoing high-intensity smoking cessation support, with immediate provision of pharmacotherapy. Tailored, non-judgemental care was considered key to initiating and sustaining quitting, particularly for participants at various points along their quit pathway and awaiting a possible lung cancer diagnosis. Fidelity was high (97%) on the screening unit and moderate (75%) 4-weeks after screening, and moderate for the enhanced intervention (77%) 4-weeks after screening. SBP and the intervention was flexibly delivered according to time constraints, participant motivation to quit, anxiety about screening and screening and/or booklet results. There was variation in how participants used and shared their booklets (exposure). Contamination of SCP intervention training was observed, with SCPs delivering theory-informed BCTs across both trial arms e.g. using the LCS context to boost response-efficacy beliefs. Provision of co-located, high intensity and person-centred smoking cessation support was vital, irrespective of trial arm. Investment in specialist LCS smoking cessation practitioners may harness the benefits of LCS as a teachable moment for cessation. Trial registration : www.clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03750110 (registered 21/11/2018).

Article.Title: Broad-spectrum antimicrobial white light preserves cellular and tissue homeostasis without detectable cytotoxic or genotoxic damage in primary human skin models
Article.Authors: Bartolocci V.; Capone A.; Di Meo E.; Arcano S.; Dellambra E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has stimulated the development of non-pharmacological approaches for microbial control in healthcare and other occupied environments. Antimicrobial white light (aWL) inactivates microorganisms through photoexcitation of endogenous chromophores while providing environmental illumination, but its photobiological effects on human skin require characterization. Here, we evaluated the acute photobiological effects of a broad-spectrum aWL source (peak 400–420 nm) under a conservative close-proximity exposure scenario using primary human keratinocytes, dermal fibroblasts, and reconstructed three-dimensional skin equivalents, with UV-B irradiation as a phototoxic reference. Cellular responses were assessed by clonogenic survival, tissue architecture, intracellular ROS generation, antioxidant enzyme modulation, oxidative DNA damage, cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs), and p53/p21 pathway activation. Unlike UV-B, which reduced clonogenic ability, increased ROS, induced CPDs, and activated p53/p21 signaling, aWL preserved cell survival and tissue structure without detectable DNA damage or stress-pathway activation. Acute aWL exposure did not induce detectable ROS accumulation, although modulation of antioxidant enzyme expression was observed, consistent with a possible redox-regulatory response. Overall, broad-spectrum aWL preserves cutaneous cellular and tissue homeostasis without detectable cytotoxic or genotoxic effects under the acute conditions investigated. These findings support further evaluation, including long-term and cumulative exposure studies, to define the broader safety profile.

Article.Title: Real-time predictive control of fusion plasmas with an adaptive digital twin
Article.Authors: Morishita Y.; Kenmochi N.; Murakami S.; Funaba H.; Osakabe M.; Motojima G.; Mizuno Y.; Nagahara K.; Okuno A.; Ueno G.; Nakanishi H.; Tokunaga S.; Ishii Y.; Yokoyama M.; Sakamoto R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fusion plasma control requires real-time coordination of multiple actuators under partial observations and model uncertainty. Here we demonstrate predictive control of a fusion plasma on the Large Helical Device using an adaptive digital-twin system that combines data assimilation with physics-based integrated modeling. The digital twin was dynamically synchronized with experimental observations, while heating and fueling inputs were optimized from its predictions to drive the plasma toward target states. Real-time adaptation and control estimation were performed on a remote supercomputer located approximately 1,000 km from the experimental device, using up to 10,000 CPU cores. Multivariate control of electron density, electron temperature, and ion temperature was demonstrated in five representative target cases. These results establish a closed loop between an adaptive digital twin and a physical fusion plasma. They provide a route toward digital-twin-based control of fusion reactors and other partially observed complex systems.

Article.Title: Micron-precision depth control in automated volumetric laser ablation with ultrashort laser pulses
Article.Authors: Holder D.; Buser M.; Weber R.; Onuseit V.; Graf T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. To overcome measurement artifacts arising from the evolving surface morphology and local fluctuations of the OCT depth signal, two complementary correction strategies were implemented. First, a morphology-dependent initial OCT depth offset is determined by extrapolating the stabilized depth progression and subsequently compensated. Second, a pixel-wise moving average of the OCT depth measurements provides a robust termination criterion for local laser processing. The developed processing system with the advanced control software enabled precise and reproducible laser ablation of volumetric structures in AISI 304 stainless steel with a depth accuracy of 1 μm to 2 μm regardless of the investigated initial surface states and process parameters for target depths ranging from 50 μm to 500 μm.

Article.Title: Disinformation-aware decision-making in supply chains using support vector machines
Article.Authors: Dolly B.; Jindal S.; Kumar N.; Kumar V.; Dwivedi S.; Nandal A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Supply chain decision-making is increasingly vulnerable to disinformation—false or misleading information that triggers demand forecasting errors, inventory mismanagement, and procurement disruptions. This study presents a systematic evaluation of five machine learning classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost—for automated supply chain disinformation detection. A hand-verified dataset of 141 labeled statements spanning 12 supply chain topic areas was constructed from professional fact-checking organizations. All classifiers were evaluated using nested stratified 5-fold cross-validation with TF-IDF feature extraction. Linear classifiers substantially outperform ensemble tree methods: LR achieves the highest F1-score (82.2%) and precision (89.0%); SVM achieves the highest AUC-PR (0.925) and ROC-AUC (0.918); NB achieves the highest recall (84.2%). RF and XGBoost lag on F1 (72.4% and 72.5%). A Friedman test (χ 2 (4) = 7.435, p = 0.115) finds no statistically significant difference at the current dataset size; however, Cohen's d effect sizes up to 2.16 indicate a practically meaningful advantage for linear classifiers. A sensitivity analysis on the 104-row supply-chain-only subset confirms results are robust to source-domain confounding. SVM is recommended when threshold flexibility is required; LR when minimising false positives is the priority.

Article.Title: Development of an anti-GM1 antibody-specific glycomimetic for Guillain-Barré syndrome and multifocal motor neuropathy
Article.Authors: Bialic A.; Aliu B.; Pang L.; McGonigal R.; Seydoux E.; Demeestere D.; Salhi S.; Boucraut J.; Delmont E.; Steck A.; Herrendorff R.; Willison H.; Ernst B.; Hänggi P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multifocal motor neuropathy (MMN) is a chronic autoimmune neuropathy predominately affecting motor neurons, caused by IgM antibodies that target the ganglioside GM1. These pathogenic autoantibodies trigger complement-mediated nodal disruption and axonal injury at paranodes and neuromuscular junctions. Similar anti-GM1 antibodies also drive acute forms of peripheral neuropathy, such as Guillain-Barré-Syndrome (GBS), in which molecular mimicry following infection induces cross-reactive immune responses. Antibodies generated against microbial GM1-like glycans bind endogenous GM1, leading to severe neurological symptoms which requires intensive care. Current therapies, such as plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulins (IVIG), can be effective, however, they lack selectivity and can cause adverse effects. We hypothesize that selective depletion of autoreactive anti-GM1 antibodies could provide a targeted therapeutic strategy. This antibody removal can be achieved through multivalent presentation of carbohydrate mimetics of pentasaccharide on a biodegradable poly- l -lysine scaffold. Here we report the development of a lead compound that successfully inhibits binding of anti-GM1 antibodies from patients’ sera to GM1 and effectively prevents binding of anti-GM1 antibodies on terminal axonal networks in vitro and ex vivo.

Article.Title: AI-based non-destructive food screening for detecting calcium carbide (CaC2)-treated bananas
Article.Authors: Alam E.; Hossain M.; Islam M.; Mahmud A.; Tariq F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial fruit ripening using calcium carbide (CaC 2 ) poses a significant food safety concern because prolonged consumption may expose consumers to harmful chemicals. Existing detection methods typically require destructive laboratory analysis, specialized equipment or expert interpretation, limiting their use for rapid on-site screening. Although several AI-based approaches have recently been proposed, they are generally evaluated on individual banana images under controlled conditions, with limited investigation of robustness, computational efficiency and realistic deployment scenarios. This study presents an AI-based framework for the non-destructive detection of calcium carbide-treated bananas using conventional smartphone captured images. Two complementary AI frameworks, Deep Classification with a Frozen Backbone (DCF) and Deep Feature-Based Shallow Classification (DFS), were systematically compared using seven state-of-the-art convolutional and transformer backbones. Unlike previous studies, the proposed framework was evaluated under realistic inspection scenarios containing multiple bananas with different proportions of naturally ripened and calcium carbide-treated fruits, together with comprehensive robustness, explainability and computational efficiency analyses. The DCF-based MobileNet-v2 achieved the highest hold-out classification accuracy of 99.74%, whereas the DFS-based MobileNet-v2​ + Logistic Regression (LR) framework provided the best trade-off between predictive performance and computational efficiency. The MobileNet-v2 + LR framework achieved 95.46% hold-out accuracy, 95.40% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy and correctly classified all 20 images (99.9% mean prediction confidence) in realistic multi-banana inspection, while requiring only 0.65 Giga Floating-Point Operations (GFLOPs) and 0.177 seconds per image. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirmed that the model learned meaningful fruit-specific representations. These findings demonstrate that DFS models combined with smartphone imaging provide an efficient and practical solution for non-destructive food adulteration screening.

Article.Title: Environmental DNA captures ecological communities' dynamics along natural and anthropogenic gradients in a mediterranean lagoon ecosystem
Article.Authors: Zangaro F.; Ismailaj M.; Mercuri E.; Sota D.; Bakaj A.; Specchia V.; Pinna M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mediterranean lagoons are vital ecosystems that provide essential services such as water filtration, carbon sequestration, and habitat support. Despite their high ecological and socio-economic value, transitional waters naturally experience strong environmental variability, including atmospheric phenomena like sea level rise and temperature fluctuations, and are vulnerable to human pressures such as invasive species, pollution, and human activities, emphasising the need for effective conservation strategies. In this study, we employed multiple marker genes and eDNA metabarcoding to characterise the micro-eukaryotic and zoobenthic community structure of lagoon ecosystems and to assess its variation in relation to natural and anthropogenic gradients. Our research focused on a large Albanian lagoon, which, like other Mediterranean lagoon systems, plays a significant role in mitigating climate change. Given the importance of effective management and conservation strategies for these ecosystems, our findings highlight the potential of eDNA metabarcoding as an innovative tool for monitoring biodiversity and informing sustainable practices in Mediterranean lagoon environments. Furthermore, this study demonstrated that analysis through eDNA, simultaneously investigating multiple marker genes and targeting benthic and micro-eukaryotic communities, indirectly highlights the potential influence of an urbanised area on their structure, opening up possibilities for the use of this approach in monitoring and prevention activities.

Article.Title: Carcass traits and sensory properties of five different strains of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) reared in brackish water ponds
Article.Authors: Moses M.; Chauka L.; Palaiokostas C.; Mtolera M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Five introduced strains of Nile tilapia O. niloticus in Tanzania were evaluated to gain insights regarding their carcass quality and sensory properties and used as basis for setting up a breeding program. One-year-old tilapia strains, identified as BIG NIN, Chitralada, GIFT, ¨Ruvu Farm¨ and Silver YY harvested from brackish water lined ponds with mean live average weight (±standard deviation) of 634.89 ± 107.34, 601.56 ± 144.90, 687.13 ± 161.46, 535.80 ± 123.49 and 466.56 ± 134.01, respectively were used in this experiment. To estimate the carcass traits, fish body offal were removed and then each individual fish was separated into three sections namely; front cut, interior cut and rear cut. The 9-point Hedonic Scale was used to assess the sensory properties of the fish. Overall, the total edible fillet yields (%) were 42.5, 40.2, 40.0, 36.2 and 34.7 for the Chitralada, GIFT, BIG NIN, ¨Ruvu Farm¨ and Silver YY strains, respectively. The higher muscle area was recorded at interior cut, followed by the front cut and the rear cut. The Silver YY, BIG NIN and GIFT scored significantly higher ( p < 0.05 ) than Chitralada in overall acceptability of sensory properties. All of these disparities are likely to be related to each strains breeding and farming history. Therefore, any future breeding design could benefit from the studied traits.

Article.Title: S2O-SARUNet: SAR-to-optical self-attention Res-UNet for grayscale images colorization
Article.Authors: Abdelaziz A.; AboRizka M.; Maghraby F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery provides all weather, day and night Earth observation but lacks the spectral richness of optical imagery, which limits interpretability in many applications. This work presents an enhanced SAR-to-Optical (S2O) translation model architecture based on a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) with a Residual U-Net generator augmented self-attention, which we will call S2O-SARUNeUsing the SEN1–2 dataset, comprising globally distributed, multi-season SAR–optical pairs, and integrating VGG-based perceptual loss, cosine-annealed learning rates, and early stopping to maximize structural and spectral normalization in the discriminator on GPU hardware (RTX A2000, 4 GB).dB, with a peak SSIM of 0.961 and best case PSNR of 27.5 dB, with LPIPS of 0.302, FID of 114.67, SAM of 8.60°, and ERGAS of 36.59. The proposed configuration outperformed the evaluated baseline U-Net, transformer-augmented, and diffusion-refined variants in terms of SSIM and PSNR. However, comparisons with literature-reported methods revealed metric-dependent trade-offs, and uniform superiority across all metrics is not claimed. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed local–global–adversarial configuration for SAR-to-optical translation under the reported resource-constrained setting.

Article.Title: Neurophysiological correlates of interoceptive compassion training for depression
Article.Authors: Anzolin A.; Ellis S.; Kim E.; Joss D.; Marin F.; Gawande R.; Comeau A.; Bumpus C.; Phillips J.; Cahn B.; Kim M.; Napadow V.; Schuman-Olivier Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depression is often linked to interoceptive dysfunction and self-critical thinking. The Heart-Smile Training-Intensive Introduction Program (HST-IIP) integrates interoceptive attention training with compassion-based practices to support emotional well-being. This pilot study randomized 23 individuals with depression to either HST-IIP or a waitlist control group. Participants completed EEG recordings and clinical assessments before and after a 4-week intervention. The primary outcome was heartbeat-evoked potentials (HEPs), while depression severity was our main clinical outcome, assessed using the Computerized Adaptive Test-Mental Health (CAT-MH). Exploratory outcomes included Delta power spectral density (PSD) during guided meditation, as well as psychological measures of interoceptive awareness (MAIA-2) and self-compassion (SCS). Compared to the control group, participants assigned to HST-IIP showed greater improvements in depression scores (Hedges’ g = –1.422, p = 0.028) and increases in interoceptive awareness. EEG analyses revealed attenuated (less negative) HEP amplitude in right frontal electrodes during attention-focused meditation and reduced Delta power during compassion-focused meditation. Changes in these neural markers were associated with improvements in depression outcomes. This exploratory pilot study provides preliminary evidence that HST-IIP is associated with improvements in depressive symptoms together with changes in HEP and Delta activity. These findings suggest that interoceptive compassion training may influence neurophysiological processes relevant to depression and support further research into interoceptive compassion training as a treatment for depression.

Article.Title: Enhancing illness communication between patients with stroke and their spouses: a dyadic coping intervention programme
Article.Authors: Lv X.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To develop a dyadic coping intervention program tailored to illness communication between patients with strokes and their spouses, with the aim of enhancing their ability to communicate effectively while coping with the disease together. Following an evidence-based approach, relevant domestic and international literature was reviewed. Guided by the Systemic-Transactional Model, an initial draft of the dyadic coping intervention program was developed through group discussions. The final version of the program was established after two rounds of expert consultations using the Delphi method. A total of 15 experts from two regional medical centres participated in two rounds of consultation, with a 100% response rate for both rounds. The authority coefficient of the experts was 0.933. The coefficient of variation for all items ranged from 0 to 0.116. The Kendall’s coefficient of concordance was 0.299, indicating low to moderate agreement among the experts ( P < 0.001). The finalized intervention program comprised 8 primary indicators, 19 secondary indicators, and 24 tertiary indicators. The dyadic coping intervention program developed in this study was systematically constructed and refined through expert consultation. The final program reflects a moderate level of expert agreement and may provide a structured reference for future clinical practice and empirical evaluation in supporting illness communication among patients with stroke and their spouses.

Article.Title: Robust low-light object detection and classification via hybrid feature fusion and synthetic data augmentation
Article.Authors: S K.; Sethi S.; J S G.; Vasudevan A.; Manimaran S.; Raj R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Robust visual navigation in low-light environments remains a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems due to severe illumination degradation, low signal-to-noise ratio, reduced texture information, and loss of discriminative visual cues. These primary conditions significantly impact the reliability of conventional handcrafted descriptors to detect objects on training on well-illuminated datasets through deep learning models. To improve low-light image object detection and classification by overcoming above limitation, we proposed a low-light visual recognition framework that combines image enhancement, complementary handcrafted and pretrained deep feature representations, dimensionality reduction, and synthetic low-light data augmentation. In the pre-processing stage, we had applied Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), followed by gamma correction, to enhance local contrast while preserving structural information. To improve generalization across varying illumination levels, a pseudo low-light image synthesis pipeline was introduced, combining gamma-based exposure reduction, Poisson photon noise modeling, and intensity bias simulation. The resulting pseudo low-light images provide realistic illumination degradations for data augmentation. Feature extraction was done using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), which captures local edge and gradient structures that are comparatively robust to intensity variations, followed by deep convolutional embeddings that provide high-level semantic representations. For image classification, HOG descriptors and pre-trained features of ResNet-18 model was evaluated both individually and as a fused representation with PCA-based dimensionality reduction, using Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifiers. Separately, for object detection, synthetic low-light images generated from COCO images were used to augment ExDark training images, and their effect is evaluated with YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 object detection models. Extensive experiments were performed on the ExDark benchmark dataset to evaluate the proposed hybrid feature fusion strategy in terms of feature discriminability, detection accuracy, recall, and robustness across varying illumination conditions, in comparison with conventional handcrafted and deep feature baselines. The results show that complementary feature representations and synthetic low-light augmentation improve classification and detection performance under challenging low-light conditions, supporting improved robustness to illumination variation of low-light images.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based computer-aided detection of cerebral microbleeds achieves high sensitivity with a low false-positive rate in a confirmatory clinical trial
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Lee E.; Yoon J.; Yeo I.; Lee J.; Lee M.; Jo S.; Song D.; Jang H.; Kim D.; Lee K.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are small, focal brain lesions recognized as critical biomarkers of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive decline. Despite advances in MRI technology, detecting CMBs remains challenging, highlighting the need for automated tools. This study aimed to evaluate the standalone performance of Neurophet SCALE MRI for automated CMB detection. The model was trained on 201 SWI and phase examinations. Neurophet SCALE MRI employs a two-stage deep learning pipeline with preprocessing steps, including reorientation, resampling, and data augmentation. In the first stage, CMB candidates are generated using a multiscale backbone and bidirectional convolutional Long Short-Term Memory. The second stage reduces false positives through a Squeeze-and-Excitation ResNet-based classifier and brain tissue segmentation. In this retrospective, single-center clinical trial, the model was tested on 457 MRI examinations. The primary endpoints were lesion-wise sensitivity (> 85.7%) and false positive rate (< 2.35 per patient). In addition, patient-wise and group-wise analyses were conducted. A total of 456 participants (224 CMB-positive, 232 CMB-negative) with 515 CMB lesions were included for the statistical analysis. The device exceeded all predefined performance criteria, demonstrating a lesion-wise sensitivity of 88.35% (95% CI: 86.61–90.17) and a false positive rate of 0.95 per patient (95% CI: 0.83–1.07). Patient-wise sensitivity and specificity were 1.0 (95% CI: 0.98–1.0) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.81–0.90), respectively. For group-wise classification (0–4 vs. ≥5 CMBs), sensitivity and specificity were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.88–0.93) and 0.95 (95% CI: 0.74–1.0). Neurophet SCALE MRI demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity along with a low false-positive rate, supporting its potential clinical utility. Further validation by expert readers in a broader population is warranted.

Article.Title: Long-term trends and COVID-19 pandemic–era changes in the incidence of cancers with established screening strategies in the United States: a population-based SEER study
Article.Authors: Mali B.; Mali A.; Mali A.; Abdulrazzak M.; Jobran A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer screening and prevention constitute essential components of cancer control, although their influence on population-level incidence varies across cancer types and is shaped by patterns of healthcare access and utilization. Large-scale public health emergencies can disrupt the delivery of routine preventive, diagnostic, and oncologic services. The present study examines long-term incidence trends and evaluates changes in cancer incidence patterns during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were sourced from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) 21 registries database. Age-adjusted incidence rates for lung and bronchus, colon and rectum, breast, and cervix uteri cancers among adults aged 40 years and older were analyzed separately from 2000 to 2022. Joinpoint regression analysis was conducted to assess long-term incidence trends. Pre-pandemic trends from 2000 to 2019 were extrapolated to estimate expected incidence rates for 2020–2022, which were compared with observed rates. Long-term incidence declined significantly for lung and bronchus (AAPC, − 1.81%), colorectal (AAPC, − 1.94%), and cervical cancers (AAPC, − 1.48%) from 2000 to 2022, whereas breast cancer incidence showed no significant overall change (AAPC, − 0.32%). Descriptive subgroup analyses demonstrated heterogeneous patterns across age, sex, race/ethnicity, and stage. Stage distribution among diagnosed cases showed only modest year-to-year variation across the four cancer sites. Over the past two decades, lung and bronchus, colorectal, and cervical cancer incidence declined, whereas breast cancer incidence remained relatively stable among adults aged ≥ 40 years. During 2020–2022, observed incidence rates for several cancer types deviated from those expected based on pre-pandemic trends, with the largest reductions generally observed in 2020 and variable patterns thereafter. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining accessible and resilient cancer screening and diagnostic services during future public health emergencies to minimize potential disruptions in timely cancer detection and care.

Article.Title: Environmental and innovation outcomes following China’s Zero-Waste City program
Article.Authors: Niu L.; Wu Q.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract China’s Zero-Waste City (ZWC) program bundles source reduction, resource utilization, controlled disposal, hazardous-waste compliance and public disclosure in a city-level solid-waste governance framework. Using a balanced panel of 297 prefecture-level cities from 2005 to 2023 and a corrected designation map, we estimate two-way fixed-effects, cohort-specific, and group-time difference-in-differences models. The baseline ln(PM 2.5) is -0.012 and statistically indistinguishable from zero in all specifications with year effects. Baseline associations for industrial ln(CO 2 ), ln(SO 2) and the municipal harmless-treatment rate lose significance under province-by-year effects, pretreatment covariate by year controls, or city-specific trends. The coefficients of ln(invention-patent) grants is significantly higher than ln(utility-model) grants. But this contrast is fragile that the invention estimate is concentrated in the 11 cities designated in 2019, whose pre-designation test is borderline, and a group-time DID gives an aggregated invention ATT of 0.026. Invention applications do not increase and science spending does not change. Industrial solid-waste utilization and broad city science and technology spending outcomes are also null. Because city-level waste-source effects are likely masked by the broader atmospheric setting, these null estimates do not imply policy ineffectiveness. The results might be interpreted as a provisional difference in observed patent-grant composition across patent types.

Article.Title: Association between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum
Article.Authors: Karakullukcuoglu Z.; Oke D.; Gulec M.; Ozkan C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between ultrasonographic diaphragm thickness and pulmonary function in children with pectus excavatum compared with healthy controls. In this prospective study, 32 children with pectus excavatum and 29 healthy controls were included. Diaphragm thickness was measured ultrasonographically at functional residual capacity (FRC) and total lung capacity (TLC). Spirometry assessed forced vital capacity (FVC), forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV 1 ), and FEV 1 /FVC ratio. Correlations between diaphragm thickness and spirometric parameters were analyzed using Pearson’s test, with significance set at p < 0.05. In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FVC % predicted ( r = 0.421, p = 0.016), while no correlation in the controls ( r = 0.070, p = 0.719). In the pectus group, inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive correlation with FEV 1 % predicted ( r = 0.421, p = 0.016), whereas no significant correlation between these parameters was observed in controls ( r = 0.070, p = 0.719). Mean expiratory thickness at FRC was 1.60 ± 0.38 mm versus 1.64 ± 0.47 mm, respectively ( p = 0.709). Regarding spirometric values, mean FVC % predicted was 82.62 ± 9.00 vs. 87.10 ± 10.58 ( p = 0.079), mean FEV 1 % predicted was 83.31 ± 11.16 vs. 88.72 ± 11.64 ( p = 0.069), and mean FEV 1 /FVC ratio was 88.28 ± 8.52 versus 91.34 ± 6.42, respectively ( p = 0.121). Inspiratory diaphragm thickness at TLC showed a modest positive association with FEV 1 % predicted in children with pectus excavatum. Given the cross-sectional design, small sample size, and multiple exploratory comparisons, this finding requires confirmation in larger studies. Article.Title: Causal admissibility of earthquake triggering laws
Article.Authors: D’Alessandro A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Statistical earthquake-triggering models allow previous events to influence later seismicity immediately across space, satisfying temporal ordering but not finite-speed physical reachability. Here I show that causal admissibility can be imposed by restricting triggering probability to the domain reached after the earliest permitted arrival from a point source or evolving finite rupture, and define causal leakage as the excluded pre-arrival probability. Dimensionless analysis identifies the propagation-to-triggering timescale ratio and the temporal and spatial kernel exponents as its controls. Synthetic experiments show that timing uncertainty can erase the distance–time dependence distinguishing retarded from instantaneous formulations and induce compensating parameter bias. In the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence, causal leakage is $$2.31 \times 10^{ - 5}$$ and enforcement produces negligible predictive change. Across four selected Southern California earthquake families, predictive gains vary in sign without exhibiting a consistent monotonic relationship with leakage magnitude. Physical admissibility and predictive superiority are therefore distinct model properties.

Article.Title: Combined infrared thermography and 3D scanning for evaluation of FDM‑printed PETG components
Article.Authors: Chwał M.; Jabłońska M.; Stawiarski A.; Grylewicz M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing availability of shipboard additive manufacturing (AM) enables on-board repair through the rapid fabrication of temporary polymer spare parts. This preliminary study assesses the thermo-geometric stability of FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling)-printed PETG components intended for short-term service. First, cylindrical PETG pipe specimens with wall thicknesses ranging from 1 to 2 mm were manufactured using different layer heights and printing speeds and subsequently evaluated under steady heating. Passive infrared thermography (IRT), combined with pre- and post-heating 3D scanning, was employed for analysis. Next, a reverse-engineered PETG replica of a flanged tee connector used in shipboard piping systems was fabricated and tested under the same thermal conditions. IRT revealed moderate temperature gradients associated with the vertical heating configuration; nevertheless, 3D deviation maps indicated only minor dimensional changes, comparable to those observed in the pipe specimens. The experiments suggested that rapid thermal and thermo-mechanical loading may lead to layer separation in FDM-printed specimens. Infrared thermography provided information on the thermal response of the specimens, while delamination was identified through post-test visual inspection. Under steady heating conditions, the investigated specimens exhibited stable thermal and geometric behavior, with only minor dimensional deviations observed. Overall, the results suggest that PETG parts printed using time-efficient process parameters may have potential for use as temporary components under steady-state thermal conditions. The study further suggests that passive IRT can be a practical tool for monitoring temperature distribution and assessing the thermal behavior of AM polymer components under operating-like thermal loads.

Article.Title: An exploratory survey of student perceptions of generative artificial intelligence at a Saudi maritime studies faculty
Article.Authors: Aljahdali B.
Article.Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is widely used in higher education, but evidence from safety–critical disciplines such as maritime studies, where graduates must exercise independent judgement, remains limited, particularly in Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East. This exploratory cross-sectional survey described how undergraduates at one Saudi maritime studies faculty used GenAI and judged its value and risks for learning. All 224 enrolled undergraduates were invited, and 48 returned complete responses (21.4%). The questionnaire, reviewed by five experts and piloted with eight students, contained four background questions and 20 five-point perception items, and agreement was reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). Agreement was higher for learning support than for reliance on GenAI: 68.8% (95% CI 54.7–80.1%) endorsed easier comprehension, whereas 33.3% (21.7–47.5%) would rely on GenAI to solve a real-world maritime problem. Study use and homework-writing assistance were endorsed by 56.2% and 50.0%, and concerns about privacy, critical thinking and academic integrity by 60.4%, 54.2% and 50.0%. In exploratory comparisons, agreement with learning improvement rose with self-assessed proficiency, whereas critical-thinking concern was most frequent at medium proficiency. The findings give maritime educators in the region an early, discipline-specific reference point and support the evaluation of supervised activities in which students verify generated claims, disclose assistance and explain decisions unaided.

Article.Title: HierWoodNet: HierStyle multi-scale semantic style transfer method for Chinese woodblock painting
Article.Authors: Qiao J.; Fan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Woodblock painting, a traditional Chinese intangible cultural heritage, is known for its vivid colors and distinctive textures. However, modern lifestyles and declining cultural inheritance have led to risks of style loss and discontinuity. AI-based image style transfer offers a promising avenue for preserving and creating woodblock art. However, existing methods struggle with semantic feature extraction, style consistency, and color modeling in this domain. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical woodblock style transfer network. Our approach introduces a Content-Aware Positional Encoder based on the Transformer architecture, which enhances multi-scale feature representation and global structural perception. This helps preserve content during style transfer. We further present a HierStyle Encoder that learns rich, hierarchical style features from data, enabling fine-grained control over the transfer process and improving semantic and textural coherence. A progressive decoder integrates multi-stage upsampling with cross-layer connections to preserve semantic structure while injecting detailed style features. Finally, the ChromaNova Color Decoder dynamically optimizes color representation through a multi-dimensional color loss function that considers both color contrast and distribution differences. Quantitative experiments show that our method achieves the best PSNR, FID, LPIPS, and NIMA scores among the evaluated methods, supported by qualitative comparisons on multi-color woodblock style transfer. The source code and trained models will be released after acceptance at https://github.com/LPDLG/HierWoodNet .
Article.Topic: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

Article.Title: Secular trends (2001–2019) in the body build of physiotherapy students
Article.Authors: Lewandowski A.; Siedlaczek M.; Kryst Ł.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to identify secular changes in the body types of physiotherapy students and their potential sociodemographic determinants. A total of 1,232 students (347 men and 885 women) in Bydgoszcz, Poland, were assessed in 2001–2011 and 2016–2019. Anthropometric measurements were used to calculate five indices and classify body build according to the Wanke/Kolasa typology into I, A, V/Y, and H elements. Data recorded using a standardized study record form included age, place of residence, and parental education. Temporal changes and potential determinants were evaluated using non-parametric tests and linear regression models. Mixed types predominated, particularly profiles dominated by V/Y and I. Among women, elements A and H decreased and Y increased. Among men, evidence for a decrease in A was inconsistent across analytical approaches. The contribution of individual elements fluctuated between annual cohorts despite significant overall temporal trends, while place of residence and parental education did not substantially alter these trends. The hypothesis of progressive leptosomization among future physiotherapists was therefore not unequivocally confirmed. Overall, body build remained relatively stable, and unmeasured factors may have contributed to the observed year-to-year variation.

Article.Title: Tomato maturity assessment via region-consistency constrained learning
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Dong R.; Zhou S.; Liang F.; Lou J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate tomato maturity assessment based on visual appearance is essential for quality control in agricultural production, yet remains challenging under complex visual conditions due to background clutter and ambiguous maturity cues. Many existing methods can suppress background interference to some extent, but lack explicit mechanisms to ensure that classification decisions are formed within maturity-relevant fruit regions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a region-consistency constrained learning framework for tomato maturity assessment. The framework integrates decision-relevant regions characterized by Class Activation Maps (CAM) with saliency-based spatial priors and enforces consistency between them during training, thereby regulating where classification decisions are formed without modifying the input or intermediate feature representations. Experiments conducted on a real-world tomato dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves classification performance across multiple backbone architectures. Statistically significant gains are achieved without introducing additional computational cost during inference, indicating that the proposed framework provides an effective way to enhance the reliability of visual maturity assessment under complex agricultural conditions.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware planning of hybrid renewable and conventional distributed generation using a novel optimization framework
Article.Authors: Saleh A.; Magdy G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the increasing integration of distributed generation (DG) units based on renewable energy into power distribution networks, advanced planning models are required to guarantee smooth integration and enhanced network performance. In order to reduce investment costs while lowering line losses and improving voltage stability, this study proposes an optimization planning model for the optimal placement and sizing of DG units. A novel hybrid algorithm, the Improved Genetic Moth Swarm Algorithm (IGMSA), combining the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and an improved Moth Swarm Algorithm (MSA), is introduced to address the complex DG placement problem under renewable-generation uncertainty. This method considers systems with variable renewable energy sources (RESs), including photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WT), and their combinations with fuel cells (FC), with uncertainties modeled using the Point Estimate Method (PEM). Three hybrid configurations; namely PV/WT/FC, PV/FC, and WT/FC, are simulated and optimized on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 119-bus distribution systems. Comparative analysis demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed IGMSA against the standard GMSA and other optimization algorithms, yielding competitive Pareto-optimal solutions with an improved balance between exploration and exploitation. Results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively reduce power losses, optimize operating costs, improve voltage profiles, and support the reliable and cost-effective integration of hybrid RESs into radial distribution networks.

Article.Title: Association between diagnosis to treatment interval and survival outcomes in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma using a causal inference approach
Article.Authors: Alem A.; Mohanty I.; Pati N.; Wellard C.; Chung E.; Hawkes E.; McQuilten Z.; Wood E.; Opat S.; Niyonsenga T.
Article.Abstract: Timely care is an important aspect of health care quality, particularly for aggressive malignancies like diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). However, the prognostic impact of diagnosis-to-treatment interval (DTI) in DLBCL remains inconclusive. Thus, we evaluated the impact of DTI on survival outcomes using causal inference methods. A total of 2610 DLBCL patients treated with immunochemotherapy from the Lymphoma and Related Diseases Registry were included. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores estimated via generalized boosted models was applied to adjust for differences in adverse prognostic factors between DTI cohorts. The median DTI was 15 days, with an interquartile range of 8–28 days. Patients who received treatment within 14 days had adverse clinical characteristics, including stage III/IV, poor performance status, elevated LDH, B-symptoms, bulk disease, > 1 extranodal sites involved and anaemia. In univariable analyses, shorter DTI (≤ 14 days) was associated with worse overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). However, after IPTW adjustment, shorter DTI was significantly associated with improved OS (adjusted hazard ratio = 0.68; 95% CI: 0.52, 0.88). our study suggest that short DTI should be interpreted primarily as a marker of disease severity rather than as an adverse prognostic factor itself.

Article.Title: Doggybone DNA vaccine provides long lasting immunity against SARS CoV 2 than Covaxin
Article.Authors: Dutta A.; Chatterjee K.; Masid A.; Jena R.; Das S.; Singh S.; Caproni L.; Chattopadhyay S.; Bhaumik M.
Article.Abstract: Durable and balanced immune responses are critical for effectual SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We compared the immunogenicity of a novel linear doggybone DNA vaccine encoding the full length membrane anchored spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein (S-dbDNA) with that of a licensed inactivated whole-virion vaccine, Covaxin, in a murine model. S-dbDNA induced significantly higher anti-S1 IgG titres with strong reactivity to the RBD (receptor-binding domain) and superior neutralization of virulent SARS-CoV-2. S-dbDNA also elicited higher frequencies of mono- and polyfunctional CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, along with cytokine-producing NK and NKT cells, compared with Covaxin. Importantly, S-dbDNA generated more durable immune memory, with sustained antibody, neutralization, and T-cell responses detectable up to 120 days post-immunization. These findings support linear DNA vaccines as a promising platform for SARS-CoV-2 and emerging pathogens.

Article.Title: Multiscale transition field and temporal trend fusion for multivariate time series forecasting
Article.Authors: Lei Y.; Zhong H.
Article.Abstract: Multivariate time-series forecasting requires models to represent state transitions, temporal dependence, and distributional drift without conflating their roles. We propose VTTF-Net, a role-separated multiresolution framework organized by resolution before modality. At each shared temporal resolution, a transition-field branch encodes regularized variable-wise Markov transition fields, a local–global branch combines dilated convolution with self-attention, and a trend-aware branch couples adaptive smoothing with an autoregressive anchor. Each modality first learns its own scale allocation; an input-conditioned gate then routes the three aggregated representations to a factorized horizon–variable decoder. On Traffic, ETTh1, and Exchange-Rate, VTTF-Net achieved the lowest MSE and MAE among the protocol-aligned evaluated models in all 12 dataset–horizon settings. The unweighted mean of the 12 five-seed setting means was 0.383/0.357 for MSE/MAE, compared with 0.392/0.368 for a fixed reference using PatchTST on Traffic and ETTh1 and DLinear on Exchange-Rate. Controlled fusion-order and component analyses support the proposed organization under the evaluated protocol. Synthetic perturbations, modality-routing coefficients, and scale-allocation coefficients are reported only as diagnostic sensitivity and descriptive internal allocation statistics, not as evidence of causal importance or robustness to naturally occurring distribution shifts.

Article.Title: Serum trace element profiles and gallbladder cancer risk in an Indian population: evidence from a case–control study
Article.Authors: Chauhan M.; Schilling K.; Patil O.; Pirjade S.; Singh P.; Jadhav K.; Kadam S.; Bharmal K.; Gurav R.; George G.; Agivale D.; Kadam K.; Sagare S.; Manjrekar A.; Gupta S.; Dikshit R.; Chaturvedi P.; Mhatre S.
Article.Abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC), a rare yet aggressive biliary tract malignancy, exhibits marked geographic variation in incidence, with particularly high rates reported across northern and eastern India (including the gangetic plain) as well as parts of north-eastern India. This spatial distribution suggests that environmental exposures and region-specific risk factors play a significant role in GBC etiology. This study aimed to investigate the association of serum essential and non-essential trace elements, individually and as mixtures, with GBC risk. In this hospital-based case–control study, a total of 912 GBC cases and 1140 visitor controls were enrolled at Tata Memorial Hospital, India. The concentration of non-essential (Cr, Ni, As, Cd, Pb, U) and essential elements (Mn, Cu, Se) were measured in serum samples, following acid digestion with trace metal-grade nitric acid (50-fold dilution), using ICP-MS. With highly right-skewed distributions, trace element concentrations were log-transformed for statistical and sensitivity analysis. Individual effects were presented using logistic regression model adjusting for prespecified confounders, while joint metal mixture effects were obtained using WQS and qgcomp methods. In addition to primary logistic regression analysis, two-part and winsorization models were performed to assess the robustness of findings. A strong non-linear association for Cu, Mn, Cd and U (P-overall ≤ 0.05 ; P-nonlinear ≤ 0.05 ) was observed. The strongest inter-metal correlation was observed for Mn-U. Exposure to metal mixture showed one-unit increase in the WQS index with increased GBC risk (OR = 6.19; 95% CI 4.84–7.95; P ≤ 0.001 ), with the highest weight contributed by Cu (~ 60%), followed by Cd (~26 %) and Mn (~ 13%). A DAG-informed confounder set, applied to an internal validation dataset generated from the training-validation split, confirmed a significant WQS-GBC association (OR = 2.71; 95% CI 2.26–3.25; P ≤ 0.001 ), supporting the robustness of the primary metal mixture findings. An exploratory mediation analysis indicated no statistically significant evidence of mediation through gallstone (β ACME : 0.01; 95% CI − 0.00–0.03; P = 0.064). Metal mixtures might be significantly associated with GBC and identification of the source of exposure, particularly in the high-risk areas of the GBC, would be useful in primary prevention.

Article.Title: Effect of silicon carbide (SiC) nanomaterials on the performance of the disc brake pads in vehicles: an experimental study
Article.Authors: El Daheb H.; Mosbah M.; Ali A.; Saleh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Composite materials are used in many industries, and one of the most important industries in which composite materials are used is the automobile industry. One of the parts whose performance depends most on composite materials in vehicles is the brake pads. The wear rate, friction rate, cooling rate, and overall brake performance depend on it. This study investigates the enhancement of brake pad performance by incorporating silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles as an abrasive additive. Testing was conducted on a specialized rig utilizing a standard grey cast iron ventilated disc (outer diameter of 241 mm and nominal thickness of 19 mm), consistent with the specifications of a 2005 Hyundai Excel. Four experimental formulations with SiC concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1.5, and 3 wt% were evaluated. The results demonstrate that the 0.5 wt% SiC concentration achieved the most significant improvement, increasing the average brake force by up to 19% and enhancing the friction coefficient compared to unmodified pads. Furthermore, the SiC-infused samples exhibited superior thermal stability and fade resistance at temperatures up to 130 °C, outperforming all other tested formulations and demonstrating more consistent reliability under different operating conditions.

Article.Title: A point-of-care lateral flow assay for semiquantitative detection of vitamin A deficiency for low-resource settings
Article.Authors: Pinto L.; Shettigar K.; Mahesh H.; Hebbar S.; Rao G.; Upadhya D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vitamin A is essential for vision, neurodevelopment, immunity and other functions. Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) remains prevalent in low-resource settings and vulnerable populations, particularly during pregnancy and lactation and in children, due to the unavailability of advanced detection methods. An inexpensive point-of-care semi-quantitative method could support early detection of VAD in such conditions. This study used a gold nanoparticle (AuNP)- based lateral flow assay (LFA) to detect VAD, with retinol-binding protein (RBP) as a Marker. The Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis and NanoDrop were used to characterize AuNPs conjugated with anti-RBP antibody and to determine the optimal conjugation pH, respectively. Antibody concentrations were optimized on nitrocellulose membranes to achieve reproducible, semi-quantitative visual signals. The values obtained from the LFA semiquantitative kit were confirmed and validated by ELISA, and the developed color chart was evaluated for sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Optimal conditions for antibody conjugation were achieved at pH 8.5, and 0.5–1 µg of the capture antibody resulted in the formation of the test line. The LFA demonstrated good agreement with ELISA in distinguishing low RBP from normal RBP levels, enabling classification into normal (> 19 µg/mL), subclinical (12–19 µg/mL), and clinical deficiency (< 12 µg/mL) categories, with 93.70% accuracy, 93.95% sensitivity, and 92.73% specificity. The presented semiquantitative LFA demonstrates promising results for a rapid, simple, economical, and point-of-care screening for VAD, suitable for limited-resource settings. While clinical verification is needed to validate the clinical cutoffs and the test’s feasibility for Point-of-care screening, this kit provides an opportunity to develop several semiquantitative kits for other biomarker proteins.

Article.Title: Predicting awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed among women in Ethiopia using explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Alemu E.; Aragie F.; Tsegaw T.; Demoze L.; Yitageasu G.; Hailemeskel H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Access to safe abortion care remains a significant public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, where unsafe abortion contributes substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. In Ethiopia, although abortion is legally permitted under specific circumstances and facility-based abortion services are available, awareness of where these services can be accessed remains limited. Evidence on predictors of such awareness remains scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to predict women’s awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed in the community and identify its key predictors using nationally representative data. Data from 8,894 women participating in the 2019 Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia survey were analyzed. The data were stratified into development (80%) and independent test (20%) sets. Within each training fold, imputation, categorical encoding, Boruta feature selection, and SMOTENC were performed before model fitting to minimize information leakage. Eight supervised machine learning algorithms were developed and compared using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation with five repeats. Grid-search hyperparameter tuning was performed for the selected model using the development data. The final model was refitted on the full development set and evaluated on the independent test set using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, balanced accuracy, F1-score, precision, Brier score, and calibration measures. SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used to identify features contributing to the final model’s predictions. XGBoost was the top-performing algorithm and, on the independent test set, achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.856 (95% CI 0.835–0.878), balanced accuracy of 0.784 (95% CI 0.761–0.804), and Brier score of 0.178 (95% CI 0.167–0.188), with a calibration intercept of − 0.003 and calibration slope of 0.959. SHAP analysis identified knowledge of legally permitted abortion circumstances (rape, risk to the mother’s life, and incurable fetal disease), media exposure to family planning information, family planning method use, region (Tigray), age, and parity as influential features in model predictions. The XGBoost model showed good predictive discrimination for women’s awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed, with consistent performance between model development and independent test evaluation. SHAP analysis identified knowledge of legally permitted abortion circumstances, media exposure to family planning information, family planning method use, region, age, and parity as influential features in model predictions. These findings highlight potentially relevant domains for further research and for the development and evaluation strategies to improve awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed in the community and related reproductive health information. However, these features represent predictive contributions within the fitted model and should not be interpreted as causal effects or independent determinants of awareness.

Article.Title: Nanoclay-enhanced shear thinning gelatin/alginate hydrogels with tunable physicochemical properties for cytocompatible scaffolds
Article.Authors: Shahedi Aliabad F.; Tamjid E.; Tavakoli M.; Najafi P.; Alipour H.
Article.Abstract: The development of cytocompatible hydrogels with tunable mechanical and degradation properties is important for cell growth and tissue-mimetic scaffolds. This study fabricated and characterized gelatin/alginate hydrogels containing 0, 1, and 2 wt% laponite to evaluate their potential for cell-based applications. Their morphological, mechanical, physicochemical, and biological properties were assessed using FTIR, XRD, SEM, swelling and degradation analyses, compression and rheological testing, MTT assay, and cell attachment studies. Laponite incorporation reduced the average pore size in freeze-dried SEM cross-sections from 46 ± 9 μm for Lap 0% to 42 ± 8 μm and 26 ± 7 μm for Lap 1% and Lap 2%, respectively. Compared with Lap 0%, the 360-min swelling ratio decreased by approximately 29% for Lap 1% and 47% for Lap 2%, while the 7-day mass loss decreased from 57% to 48% and 16%, respectively. Lap 1% exhibited more than twice the compressive strength of Lap 0%, while the non-crosslinked precursor formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior. The hydrogels maintained high hydration (> 90%) and supported L929 fibroblast metabolic activity and initial human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (hBMSC) attachment, demonstrating cytocompatibility under the tested conditions and potential for further cell-based studies.
