Article.Title: Physiological and molecular responses to transport stress in European sea bass: evaluating less-invasive and non-invasive monitoring methods
Article.Authors: Simó-Mirabet P.; Rodríguez-Viera L.; Molina-Roque L.; Sánchez-Ruiz D.; Mancera J.; Martínez-Rodríguez G.; Martos-Sitcha J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transport exposes fish to considerable stress, threatening their health, well-being, and overall farming productivity. Assessing fish welfare requires a deep understanding of physiological and molecular stress responses. While plasma cortisol is the standard biomarker, blood collection itself induces stress. Therefore, identifying less-invasive or non-invasive monitoring matrices is essential. This study evaluated the metabolic, neuroendocrine, and immunological effects of acute transport stress in European sea bass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ), focusing on cortisol levels across different matrices (plasma, skin mucus, scales, and water). To assess this, sea bass juveniles were transported for 4 h and sampled either immediately after transport (TRANSP group) or after a 24-hour recovery period (RECOV group), alongside undisturbed control groups (CTRL1 and CTRL2). Typical short-transport responses were observed, including water acidification, increased haemoglobin, and reduced haematocrit. Cortisol levels increased significantly across all evaluated matrices in the transported fish. Positive correlations between cortisol levels in mucus, scales, and water relative to plasma confirm these alternative matrices as reliable, less-invasive tools for stress evaluation. Secondary stress responses in transported fish were evidenced by higher levels of plasma glucose, triglycerides, and lactate, alongside depleted liver glucose and muscle lactate, reflecting the high energy demand of coping with acute stress. Additionally, transport produced consistent transcriptional changes across tissues, characterized by the upregulation of cxcr4 , il10 , and hsp70 in the head kidney, and crhbp and hsp70 in the brain. In conclusion, transporting sea bass triggers clear physiological and molecular stress responses that can be detected by less-invasive and non-invasive monitoring methods.
Article.TopicFields: Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Aquaculture disease management and microbiota; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Animal Science and Zoology > Animal Behavior and Welfare Studies; Environmental Science > Ecology > Physiological and biochemical adaptations

Article.Title: Venetoclax combined with multi-frequency decitabine, vincristine and dexamethasone (VDVD) as induction therapy for patients with de novo acute leukaemia of ambiguous lineage
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Suo X.; Bai G.; Bai Y.; Zheng F.; Liu J.; Li L.; Mi Y.; Sun R.; Lu X.; Zhang J.; Zhao X.; Liu K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute leukaemia of ambiguous lineage (ALAL) is a rare and heterogeneous leukaemia with unsatisfactory outcomes from conventional chemotherapy. Venetoclax (VEN) has shown potential efficacy in ALAL. Our pilot study demonstrated that VEN combined with multi-frequency decitabine (DEC) was safe and effective in elderly acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) patients. We therefore designed VDVD regimen (VEN, multi-frequency DEC, vincristine, dexamethasone) as induction therapy for de novo ALAL. VDVD comprised VEN (100 mg d1, 200 mg d2, 400 mg d3-11), DEC (20 mg/m² every 8 hours d4-6), vincristine (2 mg/d d1,8), and dexamethasone (10 mg/m² d1-4,8–11). Dasatinib was added for BCR::ABL1-positive patients. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) was recommended upon achieving complete remission (CR) or complete remission with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi). The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS) and disease-free survival (DFS). This multicenter retrospective study included 19 patients with de novo ALAL (median age 58 years, range 15–71) from 8 hospitals in China, all of whom were treated with the VDVD regimen.After one induction cycle, ORR(CR + morphologic leukaemia-free state, MLFS + partial remission, PR) was 94.73% (18/19), with CR rate of 84.21% (16/19). No induction deaths occurred. At median follow-up of 11 months (range 2–36), 3 (15.79%) patients underwent HSCT. Median OS was 11 months (range 2–36), median EFS and DFS were both 9.5 months (range 1–31​). In conclusion, the VDVD regimen demonstrates promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile as induction therapy for de novo ALAL.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Hematology > Acute Myeloid Leukemia Research; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Retinoids in leukemia and cellular processes; Medicine > Hematology > Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia research

Article.Title: First-principles investigation of half-metallicity and physical properties of cubic XEuO$$_3$$ (X = K, Rb, Cs, Fr) perovskites for potential opto-spintronic applications
Article.Authors: Biswas M.; Khanom M.; Banik B.; Hossain M.; Ahmed F.
Article.Abstract: The development of structurally stable half-metallic perovskites with coupled magnetic and optoelectronic functionalities is highly desirable for next-generation opto-spintronic devices. In this study, we performed first-principles calculations to systematically investigate the structural, magnetic, mechanical, thermal, electronic, optical, and dynamical properties of cubic XEuO \(_3\) (X = K, Rb, Cs, Fr) perovskites. The investigated compounds exhibit an energetically favorable ferrimagnetic (FiM) ground state relative to the competing magnetic configurations, while the negative formation energies and positive cohesive energies support their thermodynamic stability and strong lattice cohesion. Spin-polarized electronic band structures reveal intrinsic half-metallic behavior with complete spin polarization at the Fermi level. Nearly integer total magnetic moments of approximately \(4 \mu _{\textrm{B}}\) and high estimated Curie temperatures demonstrate robust ferrimagnetic behaviour. All compounds satisfy the Born stability criteria, with Young’s moduli ranging from 80.12 to 130.58 GPa and Vickers hardness values from 4.19 to 13.14 GPa. The mechanical indicators further classify KEuO \(_3\) , RbEuO \(_3\) , and CsEuO \(_3\) as ductile, whereas FrEuO \(_3\) exhibits brittle behavior. The calculated Debye temperatures span 288.2-338.7 K, while the minimum thermal conductivity remains low at 0.506-0.598 Wm \(^{-1}\) K \(^{-1}\) . The constant-volume heat capacity ( \(C_V\) ) approaches approximately 29.5-30 cal/(cell \(\cdot \) K) near 600 K, consistent with the classical Dulong-Petit limit. Strong dielectric response, pronounced infrared and ultraviolet absorption, high optical conductivity, and substantial reflectivity highlight broad optoelectronic activity. Moreover, the absence of imaginary phonon modes throughout the Brillouin zone confirms their dynamical stability. These combined characteristics suggest that XEuO \(_3\) (X = K, Rb, Cs, Fr) perovskites are potentially suitable for opto-spintronic applications.
Article.Topic: Magnetic and transport properties of perovskites and related materials
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials > Magnetic and transport properties of perovskites and related materials; Materials Science > Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials > Heusler alloys: electronic and magnetic properties; Materials Science > Electronic, Optical and Magnetic Materials > Multiferroics and related materials

Article.Title: Artifact-aware lightweight dermoscopic lesion segmentation with reproducible corruption robustness evaluation
Article.Authors: Gong H.; Yin C.; He J.; Guo H.; Tang M.; Meng L.; Gong C.
Article.Abstract: Automated dermoscopic lesion segmentation is a key step in computer-aided skin cancer analysis, yet lightweight models for resource-constrained dermoscopic image analysis can be unstable when images contain acquisition artifacts such as hair, specular highlights, skin lines, and air bubbles. This paper addresses this problem by proposing an artifact-aware lightweight U-shaped segmentation framework together with a reproducible corruption benchmark for robustness evaluation. The proposed framework first estimates artifact-prone regions through a multi-cue stem that combines Laplacian, bright-region, dark-region, and learned responses. It then uses efficient multi-scale encoder blocks with depthwise separable operations and channel gating to preserve lesion-relevant features under a limited parameter budget. During decoding, a mask-guided skip-fusion module integrates coarse lesion predictions with propagated artifact cues, reducing the direct transfer of contaminated shallow features while retaining boundary information. To evaluate robustness beyond clean ISIC images, we construct fixed corrupted subsets from ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018 by applying four clinically motivated artifact categories at two severity levels, with unchanged ground-truth masks and recorded artifact metadata. Experiments compare clean-only training, direct artifact augmentation, and curriculum-based artifact exposure against representative lightweight baselines. The results show that the proposed framework maintains competitive clean-domain accuracy, improves corrupted-domain robustness, benefits from curriculum training under stronger artifact severity, and transfers better to PH2 without fine-tuning. Ablation studies further verify the complementary effects of artifact-aware input modeling, robust encoder design, and mask-guided skip fusion. Overall, this work provides a lightweight segmentation framework and a reproducible evaluation protocol for studying artifact robustness in dermoscopic image segmentation. Our code is available at: https://github.com/28001736/ARL-UNet .
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: depthwise separable convolution; lightweight segmentation model; artifact robustness; curriculum learning; ISIC
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Oncology > Cutaneous Melanoma Detection and Management; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Medical Image Segmentation Techniques; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection

Article.Title: From brittle to ductile: synergistic effects of EPS waste and polypropylene fibers in reduced-density concrete with strength–density optimization
Article.Authors: Abdi F.
Article.Abstract: The incorporation of expanded polystyrene (EPS) waste into concrete reduces density but typically compromises compressive strength due to increased porosity and weak interfacial transition zones. This study investigates a hybrid modification strategy combining EPS (5–20% fine aggregate replacement) and polypropylene (PP) fibers (0.9% by cement weight) to mitigate strength degradation while enhancing tensile performance. Thirty cylindrical specimens (150 × 300 mm) were tested at 28 days for compressive and split tensile strength. Results indicate that compressive strength decreased moderately from 27 MPa (control) to 24.13–25.32 MPa. Corrected split tensile strength values ranged from 0.69 to 0.92 MPa, which are physically consistent with concrete of this compressive strength range and do not indicate enhancement over control (0.72 MPa). Density reduction reached 5.95% at 20% EPS, which classifies the material as reduced-density normal-weight concrete rather than lightweight concrete, since all densities (2213–2353 kg/m³) exceed the ACI 213R lightweight threshold of 1850 kg/m³. One-way ANOVA confirmed significant differences among mix types ( p < 0.05); however, because the control contained no fiber while all EPS mixes contained fiber, the individual effects of EPS and PP fiber cannot be statistically separated in this design. A multi-objective strength–density optimization index (SPI) was developed to quantify performance efficiency, identifying 5% EPS as the first-peak optimum in the strength–density trade-off. The findings demonstrate that fiber reinforcement may contribute to crack control through bridging mechanisms, though the confounding of EPS and fiber in the mix design prevents isolation of this effect. The proposed hybrid approach provides a sustainable pathway for plastic waste valorization in non-structural and semi-structural concrete applications.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Innovative concrete reinforcement materials; Engineering > Building and Construction > Recycled Aggregate Concrete Performance; Engineering > Building and Construction > Materials Engineering and Processing

Article.Title: Modelling the drivers of modular construction adoption in Australia: a hybrid interpretive and classification approach
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Aloshan M.
Article.Abstract: Modular construction (MC) is increasingly promoted in Australia as a pathway toward more sustainable and efficient building delivery; however, adoption remains limited because the conditions shaping implementation are not yet fully understood. Existing studies largely identify or rank adoption drivers independently, with limited integration of hierarchical structural modelling and data-driven classification in the Australian context. This study investigates drivers of MC uptake through a mixed-method approach integrating qualitative evidence with quantitative modelling. A targeted literature scan and semi-structured interviews with 15 professionals, 11 based in Australia and four New Zealand-based comparative experts produced and refined an inventory of 79 drivers. Interview-occurrence analysis and category-specific Pareto evaluation prioritised the drivers; TISM-MICMAC modelled relationships among eight categories; and an ANN assessed how consistently occurrence and structural attributes reproduced the Pareto-defined classification. Social, technological, and supply-chain considerations occupied the strongest structural positions. A five-member content-review panel drawn from the remaining survey volunteer pool provided favourable ratings on 27 of 30 item responses (90%), with item-level favourable proportions of 60–100%. This supports face and content credibility only. Because the framework was developed from one small purposive dataset and the classifier target was occurrence-derived, the computational results remain internal-consistency evidence rather than independent causal or predictive validation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: modular construction; housing demand; supply chain coordination; socio-technical factors; digital capabilities
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Building and Construction > BIM and Construction Integration; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Construction Project Management and Performance; Engineering > Building and Construction > Sustainable Building Design and Assessment

Article.Title: Team-level differences in central defenders’ performance across the Premier League, LaLiga, and Serie A (2019–2022)
Article.Authors: Prieto-González P.; Alkhamees N.; Martín V.; Marcelino R.; Yagin B.; Yagin F.; Sal-de-Rellán A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined whether central defenders from elite teams present different performance profiles than those from mid- and bottom-tier teams, and whether their individual metrics are associated with collective success across the Premier League (EPL), LaLiga, and Serie A. Using a quantitative, observational, retrospective design, 657 player-season entries were initially screened; after removing 18 entries that did not meet the study’s club-season eligibility criteria (e.g., players who were not with the same club for the full season), 639 player-season entries remained, of which 623 entries from 339 unique central defenders who played at least 855 min between 2019 and 2022 were retained for analysis. Team tier was defined by final league ranking (Top, Mid, Bottom), and the hierarchical structure of the data, including repeated players across seasons and clustering within team-seasons, was addressed using a team-season-level regression ( n = 156 of 175 team-seasons with complete predictor data) and a linear mixed-effects model with player and team-season as crossed random effects ( n = 623 player-season observations). Tier was associated with distinct performance profiles, with defenders from higher-tier teams showing greater passing volume and differences in several defensive and possession-related metrics. The team-season regression (tier excluded from the primary specification to avoid circularity) showed that team possession and assists per 90 min were positively associated with seasonal team points, whereas opponent’s expected goals (xG) per 90 min with the player on the field, yellow cards per 90 min, and successful dribbles % showed negative associations after controlling for league; the model explained 68.9% of the variance in team points (adjusted R²), rising to 83.1% when tier was added in a sensitivity analysis. In the mixed-effects analyses (additive League + Tier models), League and Tier main effects emerged for 17 and 12 of the 30 performance variables, respectively, under the Wald test (17 and 10 under the likelihood-ratio test) after false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction. Two of the 30 League × Tier interactions survived FDR correction: opponent’s xG per 90 min with the player on the field and net xG per 90 min (Wald q = 0.001 for both; likelihood-ratio test q = 0.002 for both), both showing a steeper Bottom- to Top-tier gradient in Serie A than in the Premier League and LaLiga; the remaining 28 did not (smallest q = 0.123, Wald; 0.120, likelihood-ratio test). These findings indicate that central defenders are associated with both offensive build-up and defensive processes, with selected performance metrics showing meaningful associations with collective success across elite European football.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Orthopedics and Sports Medicine > Sports Performance and Training; Economics, Econometrics and Finance > Economics and Econometrics > Sports Analytics and Performance; Psychology > Developmental and Educational Psychology > Sport Psychology and Performance

Article.Title: Pixel-oriented prediction of soil moisture using graph neural network and remote sensing data- a case study in Karnataka, India
Article.Authors: Sudhakara B.; Pais S.; Bhattacharjee S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Forecasting soil moisture (SM) is challenging because of its spatial and temporal variability and its sensitivity to changing environmental and climatic conditions. Accurate SM forecasting is important for water-resource management and agricultural sustainability. In this study, we present a graph-based approach to forecast SM using graph neural networks (GNNs) for Karnataka, India, using multi-source data from April 2015 to December 2021. We developed static and dynamic temporal SM GNN (T-SM-GNN) variants by integrating graph convolutional network (GCN), graph attention network (GAT), combined graph convolutional and attention network (GCAT, and GACN) architectures with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for spatiotemporal SM forecasting. The proposed models were evaluated against six baseline models from the literature. Among the evaluated models, GAT-based T-SM-GNN achieved the best overall performance, with the dynamic variant attaining an RMSE of $$0.022 \pm 0.000$$ $$m^3$$ / $$m^3$$ and $$R^2$$ of $$0.919 \pm 0.003$$ , corresponding to a 4.34% reduction in RMSE compared with the strongest baseline, convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM). These results highlight the potential of graph-based spatiotemporal modelling for regional-scale SM forecasting.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Hydrological Forecasting Using AI; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Soil Moisture and Remote Sensing; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil Geostatistics and Mapping

Article.Title: ACTBR: safety-projected adaptive bitrate and logical chunk-duration control for HTTP adaptive streaming
Article.Authors: Chatri Y.; Akbari B.
Article.Abstract: HTTP Adaptive Streaming (HAS) typically adapts video bitrate while using a fixed chunk duration. However, short chunks provide faster adaptation at the cost of more HTTP requests, whereas long chunks reduce request frequency but respond more slowly to network changes. This paper proposes Safety-Projected Factorized ACTBR, an application-layer framework that adapts both video quality and logical chunk duration. The video is divided into aligned 2-s Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH) media units, which can be combined to form logical requests of 2, 4, 6, or 10 s. A source bitrate-only Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) controller is first trained using fixed 2-s requests. Its quality actor is then transferred and frozen, while a separate duration actor is trained. A conservative safety projection limits unsafe duration choices before each request is executed. The simulator uses exact variable-bit-rate media-unit sizes and measured mobile bandwidth traces. The proposed framework is evaluated using 40 mobile bandwidth traces, three DASH videos, fixed training–validation–test splits, and five independent training seeds. Compared with the source Adaptive Bitrate (ABR)-only controller using fixed 2-s requests, ACTBR reduces the number of HTTP requests by 6.55% while changing the mean time-weighted nominal representation bitrate by only $$-\,0.0099$$ Mbps. This request reduction is accompanied by a 0.8528-point decrease in mean quality of experience (QoE) and a 0.1341-s increase in mean rebuffering. Fixed-duration experiments show that D4, D6, and D10 reduce requests more strongly but cause progressively larger QoE losses. Additional variable-bit-rate (VBR)–constant-bit-rate (CBR), shared-bottleneck, and runtime analyses show that the observed trade-off remains consistent and that central processing unit (CPU) inference is sub-millisecond. Overall, ACTBR provides a conservative balance between streaming QoE and HTTP request efficiency.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Image and Video Quality Assessment; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Traffic and Congestion Control; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Caching and Content Delivery

Article.Title: Crustal-scale rheological segmentation of the Irpinia Fault system, southern Apennines: insights from integrated seismic and structural-geological observations
Article.Authors: Amoroso O.; Bello S.; Napolitano F.; Andrenacci C.; Palmucci A.; Capuano P.; Palo M.
Article.Abstract: Fault segmentation strongly influences earthquake rupture behaviour, yet the physical controls governing persistent along-strike variations in active fault systems remain poorly understood. In the Irpinia Fault System (Southern Apennines, Italy), previous studies have documented contrasts in elastic properties, seismic clustering, source parameters, and fault-network complexity, but it remains unclear whether these observations reflect independent local variations or the expression of a coherent crustal-scale architecture. Here, we integrate attenuation imaging, elastic properties, focal mechanisms, repeating earthquakes, and a combined structural geological–seismological stress analysis to test the hypothesis that the Senerchia Fault marks a crustal-scale rheological boundary within the fault system. Peak-delay and coda attenuation analyses derived from microseismicity recorded between 2008 and 2025 reveal a persistent contrast across the Senerchia Fault, separating a northwestern low-scattering, mechanically coherent crustal domain from a southeastern heterogeneous and highly dissipative crustal volume. Independent structural geological and seismological stress inversions performed on either side of the fault identify systematic differences in stress-tensor geometry and stress ratios, indicating distinct mechanical behaviour despite a common regional extensional regime. These observations are consistent with independent variations in Vp/Vs ratio, seismic clustering, and focal-mechanism distributions. The spatial coincidence of these contrasts indicates that the Senerchia Fault represents the surface expression of a first-order transition between mechanically distinct crustal domains. Our results suggest that crustal-scale rheological segmentation may influence fault coupling, seismic clustering, stress-field organization, and rupture propagation within the Irpinia Fault System. This rheological segmentation provides a unifying framework for interpreting seismic behaviour across scales, from background microseismicity to the segmented rupture of the 1980 Mw 6.9 Irpinia earthquake, and contributes to a broader understanding of fault segmentation and rupture propagation in similar tectonic settings.
Article.TopicFields: Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geophysics > earthquake and tectonic studies; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geophysics > Geological and Geophysical Studies Worldwide; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geology > Geological and Geophysical Studies

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of future desertification hotspots under climate and land-use change in arid Iran
Article.Authors: Farahi M.; Boali A.
Article.Abstract: Desertification is a major environmental hazard threatening ecosystems, natural resources, and human communities worldwide, with its impacts expected to intensify under climate and land-use change. This study aimed to predict future desertification hazard hotspots under climate and land-use change scenarios in southeastern Iran, using an integrated framework that combines the Iranian Model for Desertification Potential Assessment (IMDPA), a standardized desertification assessment framework, with remote sensing, Google Earth Engine, and machine learning techniques. Field observations and satellite-derived datasets were integrated to improve the reliability of desertification assessment and spatial prediction. Six machine learning algorithms were used and evaluated using the Area Under the Curve (AUC), Kappa coefficient, True Skill Statistic (TSS), F1-score and Deviance metrics. Future land-use changes for 2040 were simulated using a Markov chain model under the SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5 climate scenarios. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC = 0.94, Kappa = 0.72, TSS = 0.82, F1-score = 0.86). Spatial predictions identified Zahedan, Khash, Fanuj, Nikshahr, Chabahar, and Saravan major cities in the study area as future desertification hazard hotspots. The projections indicated an expansion of approximately 88,678 ha of desertified land by 2040, highlighting the increasing environmental risk associated with climate and land-use change. These findings provide valuable support for hazard mitigation, climate adaptation, and sustainable land management in arid regions.
Article.TopicFields: Earth and Planetary Sciences > Earth-Surface Processes > Aeolian processes and effects; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil erosion and sediment transport; Environmental Science > Global and Planetary Change > Land Use and Ecosystem Services

Article.Title: Stability analysis of ultra-high arch dams under temperature-stress coupling and cumulative temperature damage
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Yu Y.; Wang C.; Wang Z.; Qian J.
Article.Abstract: In the high-altitude regions of southwestern China, large diurnal and annual temperature fluctuations impose substantial thermal loads on ultra-high arch dams. Given their marked sensitivity to thermal variations, these structures face considerable threats to their safety and stability. To investigate the coupling effect between the temperature and stress fields of the dam body under high‑altitude and large temperature difference conditions, and to assess the influence of cumulative thermal damage on the structural response of the arch dam, this study takes a 217 m high asymmetric double curvature concrete arch dam as the research object. A thermo‑mechanical coupled numerical model is established using the ANSYS finite element method, incorporating self‑weight, hydrostatic pressure, silt pressure, and thermal loads. The displacement and stress field distributions of the dam under two operating conditions—sudden temperature rise and sudden temperature drop at normal storage level—are comparatively analyzed. The results indicate that the total displacement on the upstream face exhibits a symmetrical arc‑shaped distribution centered at the crown of the dam crest. It slightly increases under cooling and slightly decreases under warming, with magnitudes remaining within the normal elastic range. A temperature decrease causes the dam crest to deflect downstream, whereas a temperature increase causes it to deflect upstream. In the direction perpendicular to the river channel, significant torsional deformation is observed due to thermal regulation: clockwise torsion under cooling and counterclockwise torsion under warming, with consistent deformation patterns on both upstream and downstream faces. Under the cooling condition, compressive stresses dominate in the dam body, with tensile stress concentration occurring at the upstream arch abutments. Under the warming condition, the upstream stress distribution is more uniform, while tensile stress in the downstream restraint zone increases. Finally, the stability of the dam foundation and the arch abutments on both banks is analyzed using the non‑uniformity coefficient. Thermal loads significantly alter the deformation patterns and stress distributions of the arch dam through thermal expansion and contraction effects. These findings can provide a theoretical basis and model reference for temperature control design and safety evaluation of high arch dams.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Dam Engineering and Safety; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Concrete Properties and Behavior; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling

Article.Title: Numerical design and optimization of bifacial CIGS solar cell with Cu2O transparent back contact using SCAPS-1D
Article.Authors: Mishra V.; Sharma A.; Bhardwaj P.; Sengar B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bifacial solar cells must operate efficiently under both front and rear illumination, yet their performance is often constrained by the low conductivity of p-type transparent conductive oxides used for rear contacts. Cu 2 O offers a promising alternative due to its favorable electrical and optical characteristics. CIGS-based bifacial devices are strong candidates for high-efficiency photovoltaic operation, and this work presents a theoretical evaluation of their dual-sided performance. A device structure consisting of Al-doped ZnO/i-ZnO/n-ZnSe/CIGS/Cu 2 O was designed and simulated using SCAPS-1D, with the CIGS absorber layer thickness optimized for balanced operation. At an absorber thickness of 1 µm, ratio of rear-illumination performance to front-illumination performance parameters J SC , V OC , FF and PCE reach 96%, 100%, 97% and 94%, respectively. The optimized front-side performance yields a PCE of 23.25%, with J SC of 25.78 mA cm −2 , V OC of 1.06 V and FF of 84.35%. Rear-side illumination results in a PCE of 21.93% with J SC of 24.89 mA cm −2 , V OC of 1.06 V and FF of 82.54%. Analysis across multiple albedo levels highlights the strong influence of reflected light on bifacial output. A transparent Cu 2 O back-contact layer, a Cd-free ZnSe buffer layer, and a thorough optimization of bifacial functioning under both front and rear illumination are the innovative aspects of this study.

Article.Title: Refining functional outcome prediction for proximal femoral fractures: a hierarchical machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Tanaka I.; Maki S.; Shiga Y.; Inage K.; Inoue M.; Eguchi Y.; Hozumi T.; Nakamura J.; Kawarai Y.; Ohtori S.; Orita S.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to develop a refined machine learning model to predict the functional prognosis of patients with proximal femoral fractures (PFF). Given the difficulty of directly classifying all nine ADL categories, we adopted a hierarchical classification (HC) approach that decomposes the nine-class prediction problem into stepwise classification tasks. Using data from the Japan Association of Rehabilitation Database, we analyzed 2,959 patients with PFF from an initial cohort of 3,088 cases, after excluding 129 cases with missing discharge ADL outcomes. We sought to optimize rehabilitation planning tailored to individuals. The target variable was the 9-class functional prognosis at discharge. The HC framework first classified patients into five major ADL categories (Normal, J, A, B, and C), followed by binary subclassification within the J, A, B, and C categories. We evaluated 16 machine learning models and one deep learning model (TabNet). Model performance was assessed using accuracy, and interpretability was evaluated via SHapley Additive explanations (SHAP). The final HC model achieved an accuracy of 0.345 in the internal holdout cohort. This refined model has the potential to enhance preoperative assessment and facilitate more effective early postoperative recovery.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Surgery > Hip and Femur Fractures; Medicine > Orthopedics and Sports Medicine > Bone fractures and treatments; Health Professions > Health Information Management > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

Article.Title: Innovative design of a power transmission system for a multi-function machine tool
Article.Authors: Kumar B.; Yong X.; Rao S.; Poungthong P.; Murali G.
Article.Abstract: This study presents the design, analysis, and validation of a compact power transmission system for a multifunctional tabletop CNC machine capable of performing turning, drilling, and milling operations using a single motor. Three distinct gear cases are used in this study and are clearly distinguished throughout: the proposed transmission design (pinion 18 teeth/gear 51 teeth, module 6 mm), a replicated reference case used solely to benchmark the contact-stress methodology (“Case B”: 20 teeth/20 teeth, module 4 mm), and a design-sizing calculation (23/92 teeth, module 3 mm) used to determine the module and face width of the actual gear train. Spur gear design for the proposed transmission was carried out using AGMA and Lewis equations and validated through Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in ANSYS. The analytical bending stress of the pinion was 31.38 MPa, closely matching the FEA result of 31.11 MPa, while the gear exhibited analytical and FEA stresses of 23.51 MPa and 21.14 MPa, respectively. For the Case B reference study, contact stress analysis based on ISO 6336–2:2006 produced an analytical value of 1302.34 MPa, compared with 1274.1 MPa from FEA, showing a deviation of approximately 2.2%. Parametric analysis demonstrated that increasing the face width from 20 to 30 mm reduced bending stress from 275.95 MPa to 183.96 MPa and improved the factor of safety from 5.89 to 9.30. A functional prototype integrating turning, drilling, and milling operations was successfully developed. The single-motor transmission architecture is expected to reduce energy consumption relative to separate single-purpose machines, and results in a compact machine design; this expectation is design-based rather than measured, as no efficiency measurements were recorded on the fabricated prototype. The proposed methodology confirms that analytical design combined with FEA provides a reliable framework for developing high-performance multifunctional CNC systems suitable for modern precision manufacturing.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Gear and Bearing Dynamics Analysis; Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Engineering Technology and Methodologies; Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Mechanical Engineering Research and Applications

Article.Title: Target-selective MG53-containing extracellular vesicles delivery in acute and chronic kidney injury
Article.Authors: Duann P.; Li H.; Zhang M.; Rovin B.; Lin P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a sudden loss of kidney function associated with high morbidity and mortality, and effective therapy remains an unmet need. We previously showed that MG53, a muscle-predominant protein, confers kidney protection against ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-mediated kidney fibrosis. Here, we show that limb remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) partially attenuates tubular apoptosis alongside a trend toward functional renal improvement against I/R-AKI, an event accompanied by a systemic surge of circulating MG53-containing extracellular vesicles (EVs). While the exact systemic trafficking kinetics and precise tissue origins of this native endogenous pool remain a proposed working hypothesis, a stark, exclusive 2.3-fold upregulation of MG53 cargo occurs exclusively within the injured renal microenvironment. To evaluate the translational utility of this axis, we characterized exogenous MG53-containing EVs derived from C2C12 myotubes (EV C2C12 ) or engineered NIH3T3 cells (EV MMT ). Upon intravenous administration, these vehicles exhibited rapid, injury-dependent accumulation within damaged proximal tubules. Utilizing a chronic injection regimen, sustained delivery of these payloads successfully mitigated baseline renal functional defects (Scr and UPCR) in mg53 -/- mice. Finally, in vitro assays demonstrate that MG53-containing EVs uptake is closely associated with intracellular AKT activation and enhances proximal tubule cell metabolic activity during hypoxia/reoxygenation stress. In summary, this work underscores the reparative capacity of endogenous MG53 accumulation while establishing that exogenous vesicular delivery serves as a viable translational strategy within an integrated muscle-kidney crosstalk axis.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Extracellular vesicles in disease; Medicine > Nephrology > Acute Kidney Injury Research; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cell Biology > Mesenchymal stem cell research

Article.Title: SimpleYOLO for ultra-lightweight object detection in edge-based driver monitoring systems
Article.Authors: Fu S.; Zhang W.; Chen Y.; Guo H.; Li J.; Xue P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Driver monitoring systems (DMSs) impose strict computational and memory constraints on edge devices, making real-time perception challenging. Existing lightweight detectors often rely on aggressive network scaling, which weakens feature representation and reduces robustness for fine-grained driver behaviors. To address this issue, we propose SimpleYOLO, an ultra-lightweight object detector for edge-based driver monitoring. The backbone is reconstructed using Ghost-based feature generation to reduce computational redundancy, while a Multi-dimensional Compensatory Attention Module (MCAM) is introduced to partially compensate for accuracy loss under excessive compression. MCAM applies multiplicative spatial, height-wise, width-wise, and channel gates. Experiments on 6,284 images from the public driving-fvsg3 DMS benchmark show that SimpleYOLO achieves 95.46% mAP@0.5 with only 0.35M parameters and 2.1 GFLOPs. The INT8-deployed model on the Canaan K230 RISC-V edge platform has a 0.844-MiB kmodel and a mean KPU latency of 64.96 ms. Under the detector-core timing protocol, it achieves 10.32 FPS. Its measured whole-board power is 1.43 W, corresponding to 7.22 FPS/W.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Engineering > Automotive Engineering > Autonomous Vehicle Technology and Safety; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning

Article.Title: Flood simulation study of the lower tumen river based on a hydrological-hydrodynamic coupled model
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Quan H.; Jin R.; Zhu W.; Cui Y.; Jin G.
Article.Abstract: Climate change has profoundly altered global hydrological regimes and significantly intensified the occurrence of extreme flooding. Although discharge constitutes the dominant driver of flood genesis, flood propagation is also strongly controlled by channel and surface roughness conditions. Nevertheless, the magnitude of roughness impacts on flood responses, and their interactive effects with climate change, remain inadequately explored, especially in transboundary river basins with limited observational data. This paper uses a coupled hydrological-hydrodynamic model to simulate flood inundation patterns in the lower part of Tumen River under different climatic conditions and main channel roughness scenarios. The findings show: (1) Under the same roughness condition in the main channel, the SSP5-8.5 climate scenario shows more severe flooding. At roughness coefficients of 0.03 and 0.045, the total inundated area differs by 0.19 km 2 and 0.08 km 2 between the two climate scenarios, with corresponding differences of 0.02 and 0.01 percentage points in the inundation area ratio, respectively. (2) Under the same climate scenario, an increased roughness coefficient in the main channel results in more severe flooding. For the SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, increasing roughness from 0.03 to 0.045 raises the total inundated area by 0.39 km 2 and 0.28 km 2 , and increases the inundation area ratio by 0.04 and 0.03 percentage points, respectively. These findings advance the quantitative understanding of how climate change and channel hydraulic properties jointly shape flood behavior, and underscore the non-negligible role of channel roughness in modulating flood risk under a warming climate. Beyond supporting targeted local flood prevention and climate adaptation strategies for transboundary river reaches, this study provides a valuable analytical framework and reference for flood risk assessment in other data-constrained river basins worldwide.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Global and Planetary Change > Flood Risk Assessment and Management; Environmental Science > Water Science and Technology > Hydrology and Watershed Management Studies; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Earth-Surface Processes > Hydrology and Sediment Transport Processes

Article.Title: User-centered augmented reality design of BaDuanjin exercise: integrating Kano model and strategic experiential modules (SEMs)
Article.Authors: Wen X.; Liu F.; Cai J.; Ping Y.; You F.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the user-centered design of an augmented reality (AR) BaDuanjin application by combining the Kano model with Strategic Experiential Modules (SEMs). Employing a mixed-methods approach—comprising expert interviews, focus group discussions, and quantitative Kano-informed requirement analysis—the research identifies and categorizes user needs into must-be, one-dimensional, attractive, and indifferent attributes. Based on these findings, a prototype was developed with real-time posture feedback, customizable training scenes, personalized training records, and culturally resonant interaction strategies. Preliminary empirical evaluation using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and the short version of the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ-S) indicates that the prototype was perceived as acceptably usable and positively experienced by participants; these findings are formative and do not establish movement-learning effectiveness or health outcomes. The study provides a design-oriented framework for applying the Kano model and SEMs to AR fitness applications and offers practical insights into translating traditional exercise requirements into AR interaction design.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Augmented Reality Applications; Computer Science > Human-Computer Interaction > Innovative Human-Technology Interaction; Computer Science > Human-Computer Interaction > Usability and User Interface Design

Article.Title: Unravelling capacity fading in valve regulated lead acid battery pack for e-Rickshaw applications
Article.Authors: Mayavan S.; Nagarjuna N.; Prasad V.; Seenichamy P.; Arumugasamy K.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the electrical degradation behaviour of a 48 V valve-regulated lead–acid (VRLA) battery pack designed for e-rickshaw applications. The pack was subjected to continuous cycling under a severe duty profile derived from the IEC 63,193 standard, representing long-range operation under heavy load and steep-gradient driving conditions. The battery pack achieved peak performance corresponding to a maximum running time of approximately 162 min between cycles 110 and 150. However, after 164 cycles, the running time collapsed abruptly from 137 min to only 6 min, indicating sudden catastrophic failure. Several precursor warning signatures were identified prior to this collapse, including reduced charge acceptance, progressive suppression of rebound voltage, accelerated decline in energy efficiency, and a pronounced transformation of the discharge voltage profile. These degradation indicators consistently converged around the ~ 117th cycle, marking a clear inflection point at which aging transitioned from gradual to accelerated behaviour. The systematic evolution of the discharge voltage profile serve as a distinctive electrochemical fingerprint of positive active material (PAM) degradation. Based on these observations, a Dual-Regime Discharge behaviour is proposed to describe the transition from high-voltage-dominated discharge to low-voltage-dominated discharge as degradation progresses.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: valve-regulated lead-acid batteries; e-rickshaw; energy efficiency; battery degradation; capacity fade; charge acceptance

Article.Title: Advancing patient-centered hospital care through latent service quality modeling: a longitudinal analysis of HCAHPS data
Article.Authors: Hu L.; Zantedeschi D.; Varki S.
Article.Abstract: Monitoring hospital patient experience requires interpretable summaries of ordered ratings. We analyzed ten CMS HCAHPS domain star ratings for 384 hospitals across 2017–2019 and 2021–2022 (1,920 observations), combining a graded response model (GRM) with calendar-time growth modeling and 1,000 hospital bootstrap refits of both stages. Mean fitted latent scores for the sample declined from 2019 to 2021 ( \(-0.106\) ; 95% interval [ \(-0.159\) , \(-0.057\) ]), rebounded from 2021 to 2022 (0.195 [0.152, 0.238]), and exceeded the 2019 mean (0.089 [0.038, 0.138]). Alternative longitudinal models and observed-score analyses showed the same pattern. Overall rating, care transition, and nurse communication had the highest discrimination estimates; their point-estimate ordering is directional. Rank agreement with aggregate scores was high but depended on the comparator. Teaching- and ownership-related contrasts suggested differences in change, but these were inconclusive after adjustment for multiple tests in the primary model. An exploratory model assuming shared earlier trends showed a more negative 2022 deviation from projected trends for for-profit than government hospitals. Overall rating and recommendation remained associated beyond the common score, showing that it does not fully capture relationships among domains. The approach supports patient-experience monitoring by making measurement assumptions and uncertainty explicit; the temporal findings describe associations across study years.
Article.TopicFields: Health Professions > General Health Professions > Patient Satisfaction in Healthcare; Medicine > Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health > Healthcare Quality and Management; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Psychometric Methodologies and Testing

Article.Title: Temporal transcriptomic and physiological analyses reveal salinity-dependent adaptation in Tripolium pannonicum
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Hu Y.; Hu Q.; Ma X.; Feng L.; Zhang X.; Zheng J.
Article.Abstract: Tripolium pannonicum , a salt-tolerant halophyte, is a useful system for investigating plant responses to salinity. Here, we integrated physiological measurements with transcriptome profiling across six NaCl concentrations (0–16‰) and multiple time points. Based on growth responses, treatments were classified as low (3‰ and 6‰), moderate (8‰), or high (12‰ and 16‰) salinity. Salt exposure altered osmotic adjustment and antioxidant-enzyme activities in concentration- and time-dependent manners. Under low salinity, soluble osmolyte contents and antioxidant-enzyme activities changed gradually and remained comparatively stable. Moderate salinity produced a transient increase in soluble protein and sustained peroxidase activity. High salinity induced early osmolyte accumulation and a rapid increase in catalase activity at 0.5 h, followed by declining antioxidant-enzyme activities during prolonged exposure. Transcriptome analysis revealed salinity-dependent gene-expression responses, with differentially expressed genes enriched in MAPK signalling, plant hormone signal transduction, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and flavonoid biosynthesis. Temporal clustering identified early, intermediate, and late response patterns associated with hormone-related signalling, metabolic adjustment and genome maintenance, and transcriptional adaptation, respectively. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified modules correlated with soluble sugar content and catalase activity. Together, these results provide a time-resolved description of physiological and transcriptional responses to salinity in T. pannonicum and nominate candidate pathways for functional validation.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant Stress Responses and Tolerance; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Seed Germination and Physiology; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant-Microbe Interactions and Immunity

Article.Title: Chronic kidney disease is associated with reduced satellite cell number and impaired muscle regeneration in mice
Article.Authors: Sasaki H.; Kondo S.; Motohashi N.; Yonehara S.; Yamada M.; Isaji M.; Nakagawa T.; Horiuchi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is often associated with muscle wasting and impaired regeneration, but the underlying cellular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To better understand how CKD compromises muscle regeneration, we investigated the effects of uremic toxins on muscle satellite cells (SCs), which are indispensable for myofiber formation. CKD was induced in mice by feeding them an adenine-containing diet. As expected, the CKD mice exhibited lower muscle mass and weaker grip strength than the control mice. Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry revealed a significant decrease in the number of SCs in CKD mice. Conversely, the ratio of propidium iodide-positive SCs increased in CKD mice, indicating increased cell death. Muscle regeneration processes appeared normal after injury in CKD mice; however, muscle mass did not fully recover to baseline levels. Exposure of primary SCs to the uremic toxin indoxyl sulfate in vitro led to increased apoptosis and reduced cell viability. Notably, despite the reduced number of SCs, indoxyl sulfate did not obviously impair myotube formation in vitro, suggesting that SCs retain their myogenic capacity under CKD conditions. These findings suggest that uremic toxins primarily impair SC survival rather than differentiation, and that defective muscle regeneration is due, at least in part, to a reduced number of SCs in CKD mice. Our results suggest that maintaining the SC pool is crucial for preserving muscle regeneration capacity in CKD patients.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Muscle Physiology and Disorders; Medicine > Nephrology > Dialysis and Renal Disease Management; Nursing > Nutrition and Dietetics > Muscle metabolism and nutrition

Article.Title: Prediction of soil selenium content and model optimization for a watershed in the Taihang Mountains based on machine learning models
Article.Authors: Lufei Z.; Le L.; Furong D.; Xianglei Z.; Weiming X.; Shixiong T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate spatial prediction of soil selenium (Se) in mountainous regions is constrained by limited field sample sizes and unreasonable model validation strategies, which complicates co‑management of selenium‑rich agricultural production and heavy‑metal ecological risk mitigation. In this work, we investigated a metamorphic mountain watershed on the eastern Taihang Mountains, Hebei Province. A total of 107 topsoil samples were collected, and 17 soil geochemical indicators were measured. Two geostatistical models (ordinary kriging, OK; regression kriging, RK) alongside four machine-learning algorithms: Elastic-Net, radial-basis-function support vector machine (RBF-SVM), Honest Random Forest (Honest RF), and XGBoost were benchmarked. We adopted a dual nested cross-validation scheme to separate model-fitting performance from spatial extrapolation capacity. The results indicated that our spatial‑block cross‑validation avoids inflated accuracy caused by random sample division. Among all competing models, Honest RF achieved the optimal performance, exhibiting minimal residual spatial aggregation and stable predictive performance for unmeasured watershed areas. Permutation feature importance (PFI) and non‑linear response curves consistently identify soil organic matter (SOM), lead (Pb), and mercury (Hg) as dominant correlative predictors closely associated with spatial variation in soil Se, with distinct threshold-saturation responses for each driving factor. We put forward a tentative tri‑element coupling hypothesis explaining Se–Hg–Pb co‑enrichment driven by rock weathering, atmospheric deposition and organic‑colloid interfacial reactions. Our combined analytical pipeline—multi‑model comparison, spatial cross‑validation and interpretable driver analysis—offers a practical reference for point-wise out-of-sample prediction of soil elements in mountain catchments with limited sample sizes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: lead; LASSO; random forest; soil selenium; cadmium; soil organic matter; mountain catchments; Taihang Mountains; support vector machine; small sample prediction
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Soil Science > Soil Geostatistics and Mapping; Environmental Science > Pollution > Heavy metals in environment; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geochemistry and Petrology > Geochemistry and Geologic Mapping

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and multi-scenario simulation of urban flood resilience: a case study of five major urban agglomerations in China
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Hu Q.; Zhang L.; Chen Y.; Xiang X.
Article.Abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization intensify flood risk in urban agglomerations. Using data from 92 cities in five Chinese urban agglomerations during 2006–2022, this study assesses the capacities supporting urban flood resilience (UFR) through 19 indicators across four dimensions. Spatial analysis, inequality decomposition, obstacle diagnosis and interpretable machine learning are combined to examine resilience patterns and compare five development scenarios. The results show that mean UFR increased from 0.443 to 0.516, while the inter-city Gini coefficient declined by 19.29%, indicating that overall improvement coincided with narrowing relative disparities, although gains differed among agglomerations. Further diagnosis of local supporting conditions revealed prominent relative shortfalls in flood-protection and drainage indicators and regional differences in vegetation-related constraints. SHAP analysis of the XGBoost model further highlighted the importance of topography and population distribution, with mean slope and population density together accounting for 51.04% of mean absolute SHAP contributions. Under the specified development pathways, the coordinated development scenario yielded the highest projected UFR, whereas the population agglomeration scenario showed only a small additional gain over business as usual. These findings provide a basis for urban agglomerations to develop resilience plans that account for local conditions and address both flood-control infrastructure and ecological capacity.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Global and Planetary Change > Flood Risk Assessment and Management; Social Sciences > Sociology and Political Science > Disaster Management and Resilience; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Urban Stormwater Management Solutions

Article.Title: Early multibiomarker machine-learning prediction of in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with heart failure and atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Alioglu C.; Ay N.; Isleyen H.
Article.Abstract: Early prognostic assessment in critically ill patients with heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) may benefit from multidomain biomarkers, but composite ratios and machine-learning models require direct benchmarking against simpler alternatives. We used MIMIC-IV v3.1 for development and eICU-CRD v2.0 for external validation. Adults with HF and AF and valid lactate, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and hemoglobin within 6 h of ICU admission entered a fixed 6-hour landmark cohort; deaths or discharges at or before 6 h were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause post-landmark in-hospital mortality. MIMIC included 3,925 patients (760 deaths; 19.4%) and eICU 403 (125 deaths; 31.0%). Adjusted lactate-to-hemoglobin ratio was associated with mortality in both cohorts, whereas BUN-to-hemoglobin ratio was imprecise externally. Locked XGBoost achieved external AUC 0.668 (95% CI 0.610–0.723); its AUC was 0.053 higher than clinical plus LHR (95% CI 0.002–0.101) but showed no clear discrimination advantage over clinical plus raw lactate/BUN/hemoglobin logistic regression (AUC 0.672; delta AUC − 0.004, 95% CI -0.042 to 0.034). Removing both ratios changed XGBoost AUC by 0.0005.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Critical Care and Intensive Care Medicine > Sepsis Diagnosis and Treatment; Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > Heart Failure Treatment and Management; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Machine Learning in Healthcare

Article.Title: Inter-rater reliability, agreement and measurement error of CT-based three-dimensional proximal femoral morphometry in dry cadaveric femora
Article.Authors: Ghannam M.; Arfian N.; Faisal A.; Sakti Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Computed tomography (CT)-based three-dimensional (3D) morphometry is widely used to describe the proximal femur, yet the measurement properties of individual parameters are rarely reported. We quantified the inter-rater reliability, agreement and measurement error of ten proximal femoral parameters measured independently by two blinded raters on 3D models of 20 adult dry cadaveric femora. Reliability was quantified with the intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC(2,1)], measurement error with the standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change, and agreement and systematic bias with Bland–Altman analysis and paired t-tests. Six linear dimensions and the distal canal diameter (FCD2) showed excellent reliability (ICC 0.936–0.995; SEM 0.32–1.31 mm). The neck-shaft angle showed good reliability (ICC 0.778), and femoral anteversion (FAA; ICC 0.676) and the proximal canal diameter (FCD1; ICC 0.705) moderate reliability. Significant systematic differences between raters occurred for FAA (4.55°), FCD1 (1.13 mm) and FCD2 (0.49 mm), the latter despite excellent reliability. FAA had the largest measurement error (SEM 4.90°; limits of agreement − 9.0° to + 18.2°). These results describe agreement between two raters under one protocol; they do not establish anatomical accuracy, which requires comparison with a reference standard.
Article.TopicFields: Decision Sciences > Statistics, Probability and Uncertainty > Reliability and Agreement in Measurement; Medicine > Surgery > Hip disorders and treatments; Medicine > Surgery > Shoulder Injury and Treatment

Article.Title: Exploring the effect of instant controlled pressure drop pretreatment on bioactive compound recovery from acalypha pilosa, a traditionally used medicinal plant
Article.Authors: González-Padilla D.; Cardador-Martínez A.; Téllez-Pérez C.; Alonzo-Macías M.
Article.Abstract: Acalypha pilosa Cav. is an underexplored medicinal species traditionally used in Mexico for the treatment of chronic wounds and skin lesions, although its phytochemical composition remains poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effect of Instant Controlled Pressure Drop (DIC) pretreatment on the recovery of phenolic compounds and antioxidant capacity from A. pilosa leaves as preliminary indicators of its potential application in cutaneous regeneration. Dried leaves were subjected to 13 DIC conditions combining saturated steam pressure (0.1–0.3 MPa) and treatment time (10–35 s), followed by extraction with 70% ethanol. Total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), relative flavonoid content (RFC), and antioxidant capacity determined by DPPH and ABTS assays were evaluated using response surface methodology, global ANOVA, Pearson correlation analysis, and principal component analysis (PCA). Treatment time was the main factor affecting TPC, TFC, and antioxidant capacity, whereas pressure significantly influenced RFC. The highest TPC was obtained under DIC 11 (0.10 MPa, 23 s), reaching 63.88 mg GAE/g dw, while DIC 6 (0.27 MPa, 14 s) produced the highest TFC (17.69 mg RE/g dw), DPPH AC (722.49 mg TE/g dw), and ABTS AC (685.57 mg TE/g dw). Strong positive correlations were observed among TPC, TFC, DPPH AC, and ABTS AC ( r = 0.837–0.883), whereas RFC showed weak associations with antioxidant responses. PCA revealed distinct treatment distributions associated with differences in phytochemical and antioxidant responses. These findings show that phytochemical recovery and antioxidant capacity in A. pilosa varied according to DIC processing conditions, with specific treatments producing higher responses than the untreated material. These results provide a phytochemical basis for further characterization of this traditionally used medicinal species and evaluation of its biological properties.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Biochemistry (medical) > Phytochemicals and Antioxidant Activities; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Agricultural and Biological Research; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Food Drying and Modeling

Article.Title: A comprehensive analytic framework for wave solutions and stability in perturbed Gardner equations
Article.Authors: Rabie W.; Ramadan M.; Ahmed H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This work advances the mathematical analysis of the perturbed Gardner equation—a key model for nonlinear waves in plasmas, hydrodynamics, and optics. We introduce the improved modified extended tanh-function method (IMETFM), a robust analytical framework that generates exact traveling wave solutions, including bright/dark solitons, singular solitons, periodic waves, and rational forms. Unlike conventional techniques, IMETFM handles high-order nonlinearities and perturbation terms without restrictive assumptions. Linear perturbation theory and phase-plane portraits confirm the structural and dynamical stability of all obtained wave profiles. The dispersion triplet is shown to critically govern the nonlinearity-dispersion-perturbation balance, dictating distinct wave regimes. Analytical predictions align excellently with numerical simulations, validating both mathematical consistency and physical relevance. This study enriches the analytical toolkit for nonlinear evolution equations and offers actionable insights for fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and optical communications.
Article.TopicFields: Physics and Astronomy > Statistical and Nonlinear Physics > Nonlinear Waves and Solitons; Mathematics > Mathematical Physics > Advanced Mathematical Physics Problems; Physics and Astronomy > Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics > Dust and Plasma Wave Phenomena

Article.Title: A parameterized block LU preconditioning for double saddle point problems
Article.Authors: Aslani H.; Kalyani M.; Salkuyeh D.
Article.Abstract: We present a biparametric preconditioning technique for large, sparse, non-symmetric, and non-singular double saddle point problems. The preconditioner is induced using a stationary iteration method. It is also based on a two-parameterized block LU factorization of the coefficient matrix. To begin with, some convergence results of the iteration method are derived. Moreover, the spectral features exhibited by the preconditioned matrix are given. Finally, the presented preconditioner is conjuncted with the GMRES method. Numerical results demonstrate the satisfactory performance of the preconditioner.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: GMRES; Krylov subspace methods; convergence analysis

Article.Title: ECP-YOLO11n: a lightweight insulator defect detection algorithm
Article.Authors: Jiang B.; Li P.; Wang Y.; Wu D.; Tian E.; Zhang H.; Huang L.; Zheng X.
Article.Abstract: Facing the dual carbon goal and the demands of power grid intelligent upgrading, UAV-based inspection technology has been widely adopted for power equipment operation and maintenance. However, restricted by UAV load capacity and the complexity of insulator defect detection, existing methods struggle to balance real-time performance and reliable inspection for small defective targets. We improved the recognition performance of small defective targets by embedding an efficient multi-scale attention mechanism. A lightweight C3Ghost-based feature fusion layer was constructed to eliminate redundant computational overhead. For the backbone network, a progressive channel compression strategy was designed to cut network parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with the YOLO11n baseline, the proposed ECP-YOLO11n reduces the parameter count by 59.7% and computational cost by 23.8%. Meanwhile, it retains 99.5% and 95.1% of the original model’s mAP50 on the CPLID-2000 and IDID datasets respectively, satisfying the requirements of real-time and high-reliability detection.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Power Line Inspection Robots; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Infrastructure Maintenance and Monitoring

Article.Title: Machine and deep learning assessments for multi-scale wind power prediction: evidence from real-world SCADA datasets
Article.Authors: Bousla M.; Bafail A.; Haddi A.; Essaouini H.; El Mourabit Y.; Taj M.; Mosaad M.; Bossoufi B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for improving grid stability, optimizing energy management, and facilitating the large-scale integration of renewable energy. However, forecasting based on real-world SCADA measurements remains challenging because of the stochastic and nonlinear nature of wind generation. This study presents a comprehensive and reproducible benchmarking framework for short-term wind power forecasting by comparing fifteen forecasting approaches spanning statistical baselines, machine learning, and deep learning paradigms. The evaluated models include Persistence, Linear Regression, ARIMA, SARIMA, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, ExtraTrees, ANN, DNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, CNN, and Informer. The comparison is conducted using a 24-month industrial SCADA dataset (2024–2025) collected at 10-min intervals from an operational wind farm in northern Morocco. All models are evaluated under a common chronological protocol with the same forecasting target, horizon, test period, and evaluation criteria, while model-specific input representations and optimization procedures are adopted according to the requirements of each forecasting paradigm. All models perform one-step-ahead forecasting at the native 10-min SCADA resolution. The resulting power predictions are subsequently aggregated into daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly accumulated energy quantities for multi-scale evaluation, rather than being generated as independent direct forecasts at these horizons. Performance is then assessed using multiple statistical metrics, a MeanRankScore framework, and formal statistical significance tests (Diebold–Mariano and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests). The results show that the Persistence model provides the highest forecasting accuracy under the investigated conditions, while XGBoost is the best-performing learning-based model, consistently outperforming the remaining machine learning and deep learning approaches. In contrast, complex recurrent and Transformer-based architectures, including GRU and Informer, exhibit substantially larger prediction errors, particularly during low-power operating periods. These findings demonstrate that increasing model complexity does not necessarily improve forecasting accuracy for structured industrial SCADA datasets and highlight the value of rigorous benchmarking for selecting reliable forecasting models in practical wind energy applications.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Energy Load and Power Forecasting; Energy > Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment > Solar Radiation and Photovoltaics; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Stock Market Forecasting Methods

Article.Title: Designing a next-generation Chikungunya virus vaccine through integrated immunoinformatics and computational approaches
Article.Authors: Hayat C.; Gul N.; D’Elia M.; Almaary K.; Bibi H.; Zakir S.; Sadiq M.; Tesemma M.; Alyami E.; Zohaib H.; Alghamdi O.
Article.Abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a mosquito-borne alphavirus that can cause fever, severe joint pain and neurological complications. Although vaccines against CHIKV are available in some regions there is still a need for additional vaccine strategies. In this study we used a computational immunoinformatic approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate from the CHIKV structural polyprotein. B-cell epitopes and MHC-I and MHC-II epitopes were identified and screened for antigenicity, immunogenicity, allergenicity and toxicity. The selected epitopes were joined using suitable linkers and a 50 S ribosomal L7/L12 protein was added as an adjuvant. The final construct showed favourable predicted physicochemical and structural properties with an antigenicity score of 0.524. It was also predicted to be non-allergenic and non-toxic. Molecular docking showed favourable interaction with TLR-9, and a 200 ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated stability of the modelled vaccine–receptor complex. Immune simulation predicted both humoral and cellular immune responses. Overall, this study provides a computationally designed CHIKV multi-epitope vaccine candidate that can be considered for further experimental evaluation. In vitro and in vivo studies are needed to confirm its safety, immunogenicity and protective efficacy.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > vaccines and immunoinformatics approaches; Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Immunotherapy and Immune Responses; Chemistry > Organic Chemistry > Chemical Synthesis and Analysis

Article.Title: Preoperative anxiety and associated factors among adult patients undergoing elective surgery in Eastern Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Hashi S.; Seifu W.; Bayou F.; Semahegn A.
Article.Abstract: Preoperative anxiety refers to an unpleasant emotional state characterized by fear, tension, and nervousness among patients admitted for surgical procedures. It can cause negative psychological and physiological consequences, such as elevated blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, and constriction of arterial vessels. There was scarce evidence on preoperative anxiety in the Somali region, particularly in the study area. This study aimed to assess the proportion of preoperative anxiety and associated factors among adult elective surgical patients at Jigjiga University Sultan Sheik Hassan Yabare Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (JUSSHYCSH) in the Somali region, Eastern Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 422 adult patients scheduled for elective surgery. Proportional allocation and consecutive sampling were used to identify study participants. Preoperative anxiety status was assessed using the Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale (APAIS). The data were collected by a structured questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS version 23. Logistic regression was employed to identify factors associated with the outcome variable. The strength of the statistical associations was measured using adjusted odds ratios with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and statistical significance was indicated at p value < 0.05. In this study 414 completed the questionnaire, giving a response rate of 98.1%. The median and interquartile range of the APAIS score were 11 and 3, respectively. The proportion of patients with preoperative anxiety was 49.3% (95% CI: 44.4%, 54.2%). Being female (AOR = 3.3; 95% CI: 2.0, 5.2), having no formal education (AOR = 3.0; 95% CI: 1.7, 5.2), having a primary school (AOR = 3.1; 95% CI: 1.6, 6.0), having fear of death (AOR = 2.8; 95% CI: 1.8, 4.6), having fear of unexpected results of surgery (AOR = 3.3; 95% CI: 2.1, 5.3), having fear of physical disability (AOR = 2.0; 95% CI: 1.1, 3.5), and having fear of complications (AOR = 2.8; 95% CI: 1.7, 4.1) were significantly associated with preoperative anxiety. This study revealed a high proportion of preoperative anxiety among the study participants. Being female, having lower educational status, fear of death, fear of unexpected operation results, fear of physical disability, and fear of complications were significantly associated with higher likelihood of developing preoperative anxiety. Routine preoperative anxiety assessment and comprehensive patient education should be considered during pre-anesthetic evaluation.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Social Psychology > Music Therapy and Health; Psychology > Experimental and Cognitive Psychology > Anxiety, Depression, Psychometrics, Treatment, Cognitive Processes; Medicine > Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine > Anesthesia and Pain Management

Article.Title: Gill mucosal architecture and immune signatures in Atlantic salmon reared in different smolt production regimes
Article.Authors: Berg M.; Johansson G.; Brenne H.; Lourenço A.; Vaadal M.; Helland-Riise S.; Hansen M.; Kolarevic J.; Fernandes P.; Ytteborg E.; Rodger H.; Timmerhaus G.; Andersen L.; Lazado C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Production environments strongly influence the health, welfare, and robustness of Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ). Challenges related to gill health in particular have emerged as a major welfare and production issue in salmon aquaculture. Suboptimal rearing conditions can disrupt epithelial integrity, alter mucous cell dynamics, impair immunity, and compromise gas-exchange efficiency, ultimately resulting in reduced growth performance and greater susceptibility to disease. In this study, salmon were reared using three land‑based production regimes: a flow‑through system (FTS), recirculating aquaculture system (RAS), and partial reuse system (PRS). Fish were followed through smoltification, an extended land‑based post‑smolt phase, and a seawater period that simulated transfer to seawater. Gill health was evaluated using histopathology, machine learning-based quantitative image analysis, targeted gene expression profiling, and measurements of systemic immune markers. The functional effects of freshwater rearing history were assessed by subjecting fish to two experimental challenges with Neoparamoeba perurans , the aetiological agent of amoebic gill disease. The results showed that growth performance was broadly comparable across production regimes, although PRS-reared fish exhibited slightly lower final weight and length than RAS-reared fish at trial termination. Significant differences were observed in gill morphology, mucous cell composition, and immune‑related transcriptional profiles, but these patterns were predominantly explained by temporal progression rather than by clear effects of the rearing environment. Fish reared in RAS showed modulation of gill mucosal features and altered expression of genes associated with immune regulation and structural remodelling over time, which were accompanied by differences in circulating immune markers. Following repeated N. perurans challenge, gross gill scores and parasite loads were generally low across all groups, and RAS and PRS rearing did not increase the susceptibility to parasitic infection or associated gill pathology. The results indicate that land‑based production regimes influence gill structure and immune function in Atlantic salmon, but the detected differences were modest and largely time‑dependent. While system‑specific effects were measurable, they were not clearly distinguishable between production regimes.
Article.TopicFields: Immunology and Microbiology > Immunology > Aquaculture disease management and microbiota; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Aquatic Science > Aquaculture Nutrition and Growth; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Environmental Toxicology and Ecotoxicology

Article.Title: Biological sex influences the biodistribution and absorbed dose of 131I (iodide) in mice
Article.Authors: Elvborn M.; Ytterbrink C.; Shubbar E.; Spetz J.; Langen B.; Forssell-Aronsson E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biological sex can influence radiation response, but sex is rarely considered in biodistribution studies of radionuclides. 131 I is used clinically and may be released at nuclear accidents. The aim was to investigate differences in biodistribution and dosimetry of 131 I (iodide) between male and female mice. C57BL/6N mice received 170 kBq 131 I i.v. and separate groups were euthanised at seven time points from 1 h to 7 days after administration. 131 I concentration was determined in various collected organs and tissues, and mean absorbed dose per injected activity, D/A inj , was calculated. Results showed higher 131 I concentration and D/A inj in most organs in females than males except for kidneys, where males received fourfold higher D/A inj after 7 days (120 versus 31 mGy/MBq). The D/A inj in most organs in females was about up to approximately twofold higher than in males, while thyroid D/A inj was also higher in females, at 180,000 versus 140,000 mGy/MBq. In conclusion, sex-related differences in 131 I biodistribution between males and females were found in all investigated tissues at one or more time points, but the magnitude and timing of these differences varied between tissues. These findings support consideration of biological sex as a variable in preclinical biodistribution and dosimetry studies of radionuclides.
