Article.Title: Synchronization independent three-dimensional localization of LEO satellites using passive distributed ground antennas and staged dimensionality reduction
Article.Authors: Khorshidi M.; Samimi H.; Orvatinia M.; Karimzadeh Baee R.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a novel synchronization-free method for three-dimensional (3D) positioning of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites using a network of distributed passive ground antennas. By combining improved relative Received Signal Strength (RSS) measurements with Apollonius circle geometry, the proposed method leverages a multi-stage dimensionality reduction technique to enhance the precision of target estimation in multi-receiver systems. The initial stage estimates the projection of the satellite’s position onto the two-dimensional (2D) XY plane through an improved relative RSS algorithm. In the second stage, the satellite altitude is estimated by minimizing a cost function formulated from the Rician channel amplitude model. A multi-snapshot averaging strategy is utilized to mitigate Rician fading and additive noise, reducing the amplitude estimation variance by a factor of N through the coherent averaging of N independent snapshots. Theoretical results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 3D positioning median accuracy of approximately 31.41 km and a 3D angular error of 6.55 degree over 200 Monte Carlo trials with randomly distributed satellite positions spanning altitudes from 100 to 500 km. The robustness and sensitivity of the proposed algorithm are further evaluated under variations in receiver height, SNR, receiver antenna gain, shadowing and Rician channel parameters. Notably, these performance levels are attained without the need for inter-receiver synchronization, complex hardware, complex computational burden or prior knowledge of satellite ephemeris.

Article.Title: Green synthesis of carbon and nitrogen-containing tin oxide hierarchical nanostructures using apricot tree gum extract for selective isopropanol vapor sensing
Article.Authors: Mohammadzadeh Kakhki R.; Yaghoobi Rahni S.; Naghavi Moghaddam E.
Article.Abstract: In this work, carbon and nitrogen-containing tin oxide (C, N-SnO₂) hierarchical nanostructures were synthesized using apricot tree gum extract and was used for construction a resistive-type gas sensor for the selective detection of isopropanol vapor. Structural and compositional analyses confirmed the formation of phase-pure tetragonal SnO₂ with no detectable secondary phases. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed a hierarchical morphology consisting of tubular microstructures decorated with spherical nanoparticles, creating enhanced surface accessibility. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) detected the presence of carbon and nitrogen, suggesting dopant incorporation. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis confirmed the tetragonal SnO₂ structure and identified vibrational bands associated with Sn–O bonds and carbon- and nitrogen-related functional groups, providing evidence for dopant- derived species within the nanostructure. The vapor sensing performance of the fabricated sensor was systematically evaluated toward isopropanol vapor under varying operating temperatures, with an optimal temperature of 350 °C yielding the highest response. At this condition, the sensor exhibited a maximum response of 32.4 toward 0.1095 mol% isopropanol, with a response time of 24.34 s and a recovery time of 11.19 s, indicating fast and largely reversible sensing behavior. The effect of humidity on the sensor response also was investigated. Repeatable behavior was observed over ten consecutive dynamic injection-recovery cycles with negligible signal fluctuation, indicating good short-term operational stability. Furthermore, the sensor response showed a strong linear relationship with the logarithm of isopropanol concentration over a detection range of 0.0073–1.46 mol%, enabling reliable quantitative analysis. Based on the baseline variation and extrapolation of the calibration relationship, an estimated limit of detection (LOD) of approximately 3.6 ppm was obtained. Preliminary selectivity tests against individually tested interfering gases revealed lower responses compared to isopropanol, indicating favorable cross-sensitivity under the tested conditions. The enhanced sensing performance is proposed to be associated with the presence of carbon and nitrogen-containing species, which may modify the surface and electronic properties of SnO₂ and promote surface reaction kinetics, together with the hierarchical tubular–nanoparticle morphology that increases the active surface area available for gas adsorption. These results indicate that C, N-SnO₂ hierarchical nanostructures are a promising platform for selective isopropanol gas detection.

Article.Title: Prevalence, risk factors, comorbidities and awareness of chronic kidney disease in Bangladesh: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Shamim A.; Miah A.; Chowdhury S.; Hossen M.; Aziz M.; Shuvo F.; Barek M.; Rashid M.; Islam M.
Article.Abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an increasing public health concern worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Bangladesh. This systematic review and meta-analysis of CKD in Bangladesh examines its prevalence, risk factors, comorbidities, and awareness. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley, a comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, BanglaJOL, BMC, Wiley Online Library, SpringerLink, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect. Studies published between 2010 and 2025 were considered for inclusion in the review. Data on CKD prevalence were analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA) software v3.0. A total of 30 studies published between 2010 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. The study estimated the pooled prevalence of CKD in Bangladesh across population-based and hospital-based studies, with high heterogeneity. The pooled prevalence was 21.89% (95%CI 16.59–27.18) in population-based settings and 26.22% (95%CI 16.18–36.25) in hospital-based settings. Rural populations showed numerically higher population-based prevalence (25.46%) than urban populations (17.05%), whereas hospital-based prevalence was numerically higher in urban populations (29.69%) than in rural–urban groups (12.17%). The findings suggest that CKD burden is high in Bangladesh. In addition, the present study identified several factors associated with CKD in Bangladesh, such as diabetes mellitus, hypertension, lower economic and educational status, older age, and high dietary salt intake. Awareness of CKD was generally poor, particularly in rural populations. These findings indicate that CKD represents a significant and largely preventable health burden in Bangladesh for improved screening, awareness, and preventive strategies.

Article.Title: A context-token transformer framework for multi-resident smart home human activity recognition with comparative evaluation against recurrent architectures
Article.Authors: Khanna U.; Kala P.; Sharma A.; Perumal T.; Sharma V.; Bansal S.
Article.Abstract: Human Activity Recognition has emerged as a key enabling technology for context-centric intelligent home environments, facilitating applications such as ambient intelligence, healthcare monitoring, assisted living, and elderly residents monitoring. Despite substantial advancements in conventional Human Activity Recognition strategies as well as intelligent learning-based Human Activity Recognition mechanisms, reliable and robust activity recognition in real-world intelligent home environments remains challenging due to contextual ambiguity, overlapping activity patterns, and significant inter- and intra-subject variability, typically in multi-resident situations. In this paper, we present a comprehensive investigation of a unified context-aware Human Activity Recognition architecture for intelligent smart home environments, explicitly evaluated both single-resident and multi-resident activity recognition. In this work, four representative Deep Learning architectures, specifically Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention, Cascading Long Short-Term Memory, TransformerHAR, and the Patch and Context-Token-Transformer-based framework, were comprehensively investigated across single-resident and multi-resident smart home environments to measure their effectiveness under varying levels of activity complexity and resident interactions. The extensive experiments, validated through cross-validation and repeated-trial robustness analysis, are conducted using MARBLE and CASAS-Kyoto datasets to investigate performance under both single-resident and multi-resident smart home environments. These experimental results indicate that the Patch and Context Based Token Transformer framework accomplishes competitive performance in single-resident multiple activity recognition settings while significantly enhancing activity recognition performance in multi-resident settings, attaining an average accuracy of 69.38% compared with 58.66% (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention), 58.96% (TransformerHAR), and 60.41% (Cascading Long Short-Term Memory with Attention) for these competing baselines. Further, comprehensive class/activity-wise, confusion-matrix, and convergence investigations validate that the context-token conditioning competently assists in improving activity disambiguation, learning/training stability, and generalization, typically in multi-resident scenarios characterized by overlapping sensor patterns, concurrent activities, and complex contextual interactions.

Article.Title: Diversity and population dynamics of mammalian species across different habitat types in Chebera Churchura National Park, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Chere T.; Tessema Z.; Asefa A.; Kebede F.; Debeshu G.
Article.Abstract: Ecological data in protected areas are crucially important for improving management effectiveness and policy decision. Hence, this study was conducted to determine the diversity, abundance and distribution of mammalian species across major habitat types (i.e. Montane Forest, Wooded Grassland, Woodland and Riverine Forest), and between dry and wet seasons in Chebera Churchura National Park (CCNP), Ethiopia. We tested the hypothesis that the diversity and population dynamics of mammalian species in CCNP vary across habitat types and between seasons due to differences in availability and heterogeneity of resources. We counted mammals along with sighting distance transects across habitat types, both in wet season and dry season, using the naked-eye and a 8 × 40 Bushnell ® binoculars. We recorded a total of 19 mammalian species in the CCNP including the endangered African Elephant ( Loxodonta africana ), the Vulnerable Leopard ( Panthera pardus ), Lion ( Panthera leo ), and the Near Threatened African Buffalo ( Syncerus caffer ). We found a significant effect of habitat types ( P < 0.05) on species richness, species composition, and population density of mammals, but the effect of season was non-significant. Species richness was highest in the Montane Forest (16 species), due to its thick tree canopy with multilayered structure, and diverse micro-habitats, providing good protection. However, both Shannon diversity index ( H : 1.88) and evenness ( H’ : 0.71) were highest in the Woodland habitat, with greater plant diversity, supporting mammalian species with varying feeding strategies. Riverine forest had the lowest richness (11 species), Shannon diversity index ( H : 1.20), and evenness ( H’ : 0.50), due to its less vegetation cover, supporting low mammalian security and breeding sites. Median population densities of 8 of the 10 species occurring in more than two habitat types demonstrated significant difference among habitat types ( P < 0.05). Our findings showed that CCNP an important conservation site for threatened mammalian species in Ethiopia, with diverse habitat types acting as drivers of mammalian diversity, abundance and distribution.

Article.Title: Development and characterization of a larp7 knockout zebrafish model for alazami syndrome
Article.Authors: Zhao P.; Zhang X.; Hu S.; Hu Y.; Zhang L.; Tan L.; He X.
Article.Abstract: Alazami syndrome (AS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe growth restriction, significantly impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, and distinctive facial features, caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the LARP7 gene. However, the phenotype remains poorly defined due to the limited number of reported cases and the impact of its defects on human health is not yet fully understood. We reported a case with AS, reviewed all previously reported 48 AS patients, and generated a zebrafish knockout of the l arp7 gene. This patient was compound heterozygous for two pathological variants. Among these AS patients, the main clinical manifestations included intellectual disability (56/56), motor developmental delay (55/55), facial dysmorphism (50/50), short stature (50/54), low weight (36/45), and microcephaly (28/46). More than half also exhibited fetal growth retardation and behavioral abnormalities. These affected individuals all had bi-allelic pathogenic, loss-of-function variants in LARP7 . The larp7 -/- zebrafish showed reduced body length, smaller eye intervals at 3, 4 and 5 days post-fertilization and decreased distance and average velocity. Larval locomotion tests indicated impaired activity and response to stimuli, while open field tests revealed elevated anxiety levels. Transcriptome analysis identified increased aberrant splicing events in larp7 -/- zebrafish, linked to AS patient phenotypes. AS is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with severe growth restriction and microcephaly. This study establishes and validates the larp7 -/- zebrafish as an animal model to study AS in vivo, offering a valuable tool for further elucidation of larp7 precise mechanism in the development of this disease and the identification of potential therapeutic targets.

Article.Title: Predicting chemotherapy response in small cell lung cancer using habitat imaging and peritumoral radiomics: a dual-center study
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Xiao F.; Li T.; Gan T.; Long Y.; Li Y.; Liao M.
Article.Abstract: This study developed and validated a CT-based model combining habitat imaging and peritumoral radiomics to predict platinum-based chemotherapy response in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), and determined the optimal peritumoral margin. This dual-center retrospective study enrolled 315 SCLC patients receiving first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, divided into chemotherapy-sensitive and chemotherapy-resistant groups based on RECIST 1.1. Patients from Center 1 ( n = 212) were split into training and internal validation sets (8:2), and those from Center 2 ( n = 103) formed the external validation set. Clinical-imaging features were selected via univariate and multivariate logistic regression to build the Clinical model. Three peritumoral margins (0–3 mm, 0–6 mm, -3 to + 3 mm) and intratumoral habitats were analyzed. Features were selected via LASSO regression. Finally, an integrated model was built by combining habitat features, peritumoral features, and clinical-imaging factors. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test to assess discrimination, clinical utility, and calibration. The 0–3 mm peritumoral margin was optimal, with the model achieving AUCs of 0.851, 0.790, and 0.750 in the training, internal validation, and external validation sets, respectively. The habitat model showed promising performance with AUCs of 0.978, 0.873, and 0.882. The nomogram combined clinical-imaging, 0–3 mm peritumoral, and habitat features, achieving AUCs of 0.987, 0.909, and 0.911 across the three datasets. This nomogram shows promise for predicting SCLC chemotherapy response and may facilitate clinical translation.

Article.Title: Energy-efficient flexible job shop scheduling under time-of-use electricity pricing using a reinforcement learning-assisted evolutionary algorithm
Article.Authors: Guo S.; Li S.; Zhang G.; Zhao J.; Kou X.; Yu N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the difficulty of jointly optimizing production efficiency and electricity cost in flexible job shop scheduling under time-of-use electricity pricing, a bi-objective scheduling model is established to minimize the makespan and total electricity cost. An energy-aware hybrid reinforcement optimization algorithm (EAHROA) is proposed. The algorithm adopts a two-segment OS-MS encoding scheme to represent operation sequencing and machine selection. During decoding, a time-of-use electricity price-aware mechanism is introduced to calculate processing and idle electricity costs, guiding operations to avoid peak-price periods when possible. Three neighborhood structures, namely critical-machine reassignment, tariff-aware neighborhood search, and critical-operation insertion/swap, are designed to enhance local optimization for critical operations and high-cost operations. Furthermore, a Q-learning controller selects a joint search policy, including the crossover probability, mutation probability, neighborhood type, and maximum waiting limit, according to the search stage, the proportion of solutions in the first Pareto front, and the recent search trend. Simulation experiments on Brandimarte benchmark instances show that EAHROA provides competitive trade-offs between makespan and total electricity cost and achieves improved IGD, HV, and SC results in the comparative studies.

Article.Title: Eco-friendly synthesis of silver nanoparticles from Teucrium stocksianum extract and their effect on tomato salinity tolerance
Article.Authors: Aghaei Dargiri S.; Samsampour D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity stress is a major environmental constraint that limits the productivity of agricultural crops, especially in salt-sensitive tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ). This study evaluated the effects of greenly synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), produced using Teucrium stocksianum extract, at concentrations of 0, 20, 40 and 60 ppm under salinity stress of 0, 50, 100 and 150 mM NaCl. The antioxidant activity of biosynthesized AgNPs was dependent on the concentration of AgNPs in both DPPH and ABTS •+ radical scavenging assays. The involvement of phytochemicals in the reduction and stabilization of AgNPs was confirmed by FTIR analysis. Structural analysis performed using XRD showed that the AgNPs had a face-centered cubic structure. FE-SEM, EDS and DLS enabled the successful biosynthesis of homogeneous AgNPs with a predominant silver content. The results showed that, seedling length (79.98%), leaf length (31.01%) and root fresh weight (36.46%) increased in AgNPs 40, 20 and 60 ppm, respectively, compared to the control under 150 mM salinity stress. Also, AgNPs 40 and 20 ppm led to a 16.87% increase in leaf relative water content and a 16.23% decrease in ion leakage under 150 mM salinity stress, respectively. The application of AgNPs 60 ppm increased antioxidant activity by 61.90% compared to the control under 150 mM salinity stress. The total carbohydrate and anthocyanin content increased by 8.98% and 73.39%, respectively, compared to the control under 150 mM salinity stress with the application of 40 and 60 ppm AgNPs. AgNPs 20 ppm reduced the content of hydrogen peroxide and malondialdehyde by 4.9 and 61.89%, respectively, under 150 mM salinity stress conditions compared to the control. Likewise, catalase activity increased by 11.53, 33.99 and 31.41% compared to the control with the application of 20, 40 and 60 ppm AgNPs, respectively. In addition, peroxidase, polyphenol oxidase and superoxidase activities in 40, 20 and 40 ppm AgNPs increased by 98.29, 22.68 and 110.22% under 150 mM salinity stress compared to the control. Overall, greenly synthesized AgNPs at 20–40 ppm reduced salinity-induced oxidative stress and improved growth and physiological performance in tomato plants, indicating their potential in enhancing salinity tolerance.

Article.Title: Comparative study on the reinforcement bond performance and ecological properties of graphite tailings concrete and ordinary concrete
Article.Authors: Zeng Q.; Xu Y.; Li T.; Yao S.; Lv J.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the feasibility of applying Graphite Tailings Concrete (GTC) in reinforced concrete structures. The bond performance of GTC was systematically evaluated and compared with that of Normal Concrete (NC). The effects of concrete strength grades and reinforcement types were considered, with NC used as the benchmark. Through 24 central pull-out tests and life cycle assessment, the differences between the two concretes in terms of bond performance, constitutive relationship, failure mode, and environmental impact were comprehensively analyzed. The results indicate that, in terms of bond performance, the bond strength of GTC with ribbed reinforcement at the C40 grade decreased by 12.93% compared with NC, while the peak slip increased by 39.4%. When the strength grade increased to C60, the bond strength of the two concretes were basically equivalent, with a decrease of only 0.86%, and the increase in peak slip narrowed to 61.9%, indicating that a high-strength matrix can effectively suppress the negative effects of graphite tailings. In terms of failure mode, GTC and NC exhibited complete consistency. At the C40 grade, both concretes showed pull-out failure, while at the C60 grade, all ribbed reinforcement specimens exhibited yielding failure. Regarding the interfacial ultimate fracture energy, the value of GTC with ribbed reinforcement at the C60 grade increased by 33.3% compared with NC, demonstrating superior energy dissipation capacity. Environmental assessment results show that although all environmental impact indicators of GTC were slightly higher than those of NC, the increases were limited, and the GWP at the C60 grade was only 0.40% higher than that of NC.

Article.Title: Clinicopathological significance of cuproptosis-related genes DLD, LIAS, and PDHA1 in bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Homayoon S.; Ariafar A.; Ramezani A.; Salehi Z.; Faghih Z.; Entezam M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bladder cancer (BC) is the most common malignancy of the urinary tract, with high recurrence rates and frequent progression. Cuproptosis is a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death and a potential contributor to tumorigenesis; however, clinical evidence regarding the role of cuproptosis-related genes in BC remains limited. This study investigated the expression of DLD , LIAS , and PDHA1 in BC tissues. Gene expressions were quantified by RT-qPCR in 62 BC and 38 non-neoplastic bladder tissues. Clinicopathological associations were assessed, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Analyses revealed that LIAS expression was significantly lower in tumor tissues than in non-neoplastic tissues, showing a 1.59-fold reduction ( P = 0.036), whereas DLD and PDHA1 showed no significant differences. All three genes were significantly downregulated in muscle-invasive (MIBC) compared to non-muscle-invasive (NMIBC) tumors ( DLD , P = 0.001; LIAS , P < 0.001; PDHA1 , P = 0.030). Furthermore, lower DLD and LIAS expressions were significantly associated with advanced pathological stages and higher tumor grades ( P < 0.05). Individually, the genes showed limited discriminatory performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.54 to 0.63. However, their combined model showed improved performance, yielding an AUC of 0.81. Collectively, these findings indicate that DLD , LIAS , and PDHA1 expression levels are associated with tumor status and clinicopathological features in BC. Such patterns may reflect metabolic changes that alter tumor cell susceptibility to copper-dependent cell death, although the underlying biological mechanisms remain to be determined. The combined expression profile may have preliminary utility as an exploratory discriminatory panel for BC. However, this study did not directly evaluate cuproptosis activity or establish a mechanistic or causal relationship between these genes and copper-dependent cell death; validation in larger, independent cohorts is required.

Article.Title: Climate-smart dairy technology adoption profiles and multidimensional food security among smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Hussen Y.; Ayalew Z.; Nigussie Z.; Yitayew A.; Chekol Y.; Abawa M.; Gidelew G.; Aragaw A.; Abele S.
Article.Abstract: This study examines associations between climate-smart dairy technologies and practices (CSDTPs) adoption profiles and multidimensional food security (MDFS) among 734 smallholder dairy households in Northwest Ethiopia using cross-sectional survey design. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified three profiles: selective (19.5%), intermediate (45.9%), and intensive-diversified adoption (34.6%). Augmented-inverse probability weighting (AIPW) estimated the adjusted counterfactual contrast, with inverse-probability weighting regression adjustment (IPWRA) and inverse-probability weighting (IPW) estimators as a robustness checks. Compared with selective adoption, both adoption profiles had lower food insecurity deprivation scores across the four MDFS dimensions. The intensive-diversified adoption generally showed larger estimated differences relative to the selective profile mean: 23.46% for quantity, 10.35% for quantity, 27.22% for acceptability, and 16.62% for stability. Sensitivity analysis broadly supported the findings, although the quality contrast of intermediate profile was not robust to kebele-clustered standard errors. For binary MDFS, compared to selective adoption, intermediate and intensive-diversified adoption profiles were associated with 11.70% and 12.20% lower probabilities of food insecurity, respectively; their difference however, was not statistically significant. These findings highlight the relevance of context-specific combinations of CSDTPs in relation to MDFS. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, longitudinal and experimental studies are needed to establish causal effects and investigate underlying mechanisms.

Article.Title: Non-invasive milk-based immunological profiling identifies TGF-β and haptoglobin as candidate biomarkers for repeat breeding in Jersey cattle
Article.Authors: Kharb V.; Umar S.; Mir M.; Shah R.; Ganai N.; Shah S.; Kumar D.; Kashoo Z.; Shah S.; Pandit A.
Article.Abstract: Repeat breeding drains smallholder dairy farms economically, but there is still no practical cow-side test that can flag the condition early. In this study, we asked a simple question: does the milk of repeat-breeder Jersey cows carry an immunological signature that sets it apart from that of healthy animals? We enrolled 47 Jersey cattle at the Mountain Livestock Research Institute, SKUAST-Kashmir, allocated to three groups: healthy controls ( n = 18), treatment-naive repeat breeders ( n = 17) and cows with chronic reproductive disorders under-treatment ( n = 12). Milk cytology and composition were evaluated in 42 animals (cytology-evaluable subset: healthy n = 18, repeat breeders n = 17, chronic n = 7; five Group 3 smears were excluded due to preparation damage). Biomarker quantification by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was performed on a balanced subset of 36 animals ( n = 12 per group, a randomly selected subset limited by ELISA kit capacity and cost and blind to the biomarker values); these two datasets are overlapping subsets of the same 47-animal cohort. We measured 18 parameters in total and performed Kruskal–Wallis tests, pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction, Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across the primary outcomes, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Among all these parameters, transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) was the most notable. Its concentration climbed steadily from 11.76 pg/mL in healthy cows to 34.58 in repeat breeders and 90.12 in the chronic group ( p = 0.0001), and at a candidate cut-off of 24.09 pg/mL it picked up diseased animals with 79.2% sensitivity (95% CI: 58.3–95.8%) and 91.7% specificity (95% CI: 75.0–100.0%; area under the curve (AUC) = 0.873, 95% CI: 0.740–0.974) In the primary contrast of healthy versus treatment-naive repeat breeders, TGF-β gave an AUC of 0.799 at the same 24.09 pg/mL cut-off, with the pooled 0.873 retained as an exploratory measure of broader reproductive compromise. Haptoglobin told a similar story (AUC = 0.708 (95% CI: 0.625–0.812); p = 0.037, with most values below the assay detection limit), though haptoglobin was only nominally significant and did not survive multiple-testing correction (exploratory), and the two markers showed a moderate positive correlation (ρ = 0.562). Meanwhile, fat, protein, solids-not-fat (SNF), somatic cell count (SCC), and leukocyte counts barely changed across groups, which ruled out mastitis as a confounder. The separation of treatment-naive repeat breeders from healthy animals was borderline after correction for multiple testing (TGF-β p = 0.018; haptoglobin p = 0.035), and the clearest separation involved the chronic, under-treatment animals, so these results are candidate associations rather than validated biomarkers. Taken together, milk TGF-β with haptoglobin as a supportive marker emerges as a promising non-invasive candidate for laboratory-based milk assessment of reproductive status. The reported cut-offs are internally derived and require external, multi-breed validation before any clinical application. The TGF-β AUC held up on internal validation (optimism-corrected: 0.872), though sensitivity and specificity at the Youden cut-off are modestly optimistic by approximately 4–7% points.

Article.Title: BSIDM: secure IoT data management using blockchain, AW-DAG consensus, and HABE encryption
Article.Authors: Mishra A.; Mishra K.; Ahamad R.; Singh G.
Article.Abstract: Today, more than 55 billion IoT devices generate about 79.4 zettabytes of data per year, highlighting the growing gap between centralized cloud architectures and the security, scalability, and access-control needs of Internet of Things (IoT) applications. At the moment, blockchain solutions for managing IoT data remain fragmented: lightweight blockchains neglect access control, permissionless DAGs fail to provide fine-grained access control, and permissioned blockchains trade off throughput for Byzantine fault tolerance. In this paper, we propose a BSIDM (Blockchain-enabled Secure IoT Data Management) architecture that consists of four planes: IoT Sensing, Edge Preprocessing, Blockchain Coordination, and Cloud Storage that communicate via smart contracts. BSIDM architecture utilizes two novel ideas: an AW-DAG reputation-weighted, DAG-based Byzantine Fault Tolerance consensus protocol with sub-second finality due to parallel tip validation, and Hierarchical Attribute-Based Encryption (HABE), a hierarchical ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption with fine-grained access control in O(m + log k) complexity, where m is the number of attributes matched by the access policy and k is the number of authorities in the hierarchy, so decryption cost grows linearly with m and only adds a small O(log k) hierarchical-delegation term that can be applied to edge computing devices. Dynamic sharding through consistent hashing ensures cloud storage load balancing, and blockchain-secured migrations ensure auditability. The security of the BSIDM is formally proved, as it provides IND-CCA2 security, Byzantine fault tolerance for f < n/3, and prevention of Sybil attacks. The experiments performed on the 500-node CloudLab testbed, for comparison with IOTA Tangle, Hyperledger Fabric v2.4, the IPFS storage system, and AWS IoT Core, demonstrate that BSIDM achieves 5,847 TPS throughput, an average latency of 320 ms, and 0.8 s finality. Thus, BSIDM has a 5.97 × (5,847 vs. 980 TPS) improvement in throughput and a 90.1% reduction in average latency compared with IOTA, using just 0.23 mJ per transaction, 1.7% more than AWS IoT Core energy usage. Comparative analysis across nine aspects demonstrates BSIDM’s dominance.

Article.Title: Characterization of circumferential flux distributions in parabolic trough receivers using adaptive gaussian representations
Article.Authors: Waghmare S.; Cardona G.; Pujol-Nadal R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The solar flux on the receiver of a Parabolic Trough Collector (PTC) is highly non-uniform, which makes it hard to describe with a single mathematical function. Gaussian curves have long been used for solar irradiance and optical errors, but rarely for receiver flux. This study presents a systematic Gaussian characterization framework for circumferential flux distributions on the receiver of a modified LS-III PTC. Spectral Monte Carlo Ray Tracing (MCRT) generated flux profiles for wavelength-independent and wavelength-dependent materials, circumsolar ratio, receiver diameter, receiver height, and rim angle. The framework fits ten Gaussian descriptors, both individually and in combination, and selects the best fit using six statistical metrics, while flagging non-identifiable fits. A single Gaussian rarely described the full profile, and multi-component or two-region descriptors were usually needed. The selected descriptor varied consistently with the conditions tested, and the framework also represented asymmetric flux from a tilted beam. The fitted parameters showed physically interpretable behavior. A consistent spread asymmetry across independent sweeps quantifies the rise-decline shape of PTC flux profiles. The shadowing-region baseline varied differently with optical efficiency depending on the design variable, consistent with distinct physical mechanisms. This gives a compact, reproducible methodology for classifying and comparing PTC flux distributions.

Article.Title: Theory of mind predicts conversational success in early right hemisphere stroke recovery
Article.Authors: Suazo A.; Blake M.; Schnur T.
Article.Abstract: Those living with right hemisphere damage (RHD) often struggle with engaging in aspects of conversation that require understanding what a speaker means. There is growing evidence that conversation relies on deducing the speaker’s perspective, an ability known as theory of mind (ToM). However, whether individual differences in conversation after RHD relate to ToM deficits is unknown. Here, we related individual differences in conversational success to ToM in 31 speakers during the early stages of RHD (median 5 days post-stroke) in comparison to 16 age- and education-matched controls. We measured conversational success as the number of differences identified between two images while participants conversed with study coordinators. A non-verbal false belief task measured ToM abilities. Baseline cognitive tasks assessed visual inattention, inhibitory control/visual selective attention and working memory. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed that the ToM ability to explicitly infer others’ perspectives while managing conflict with one’s own reliably predicted conversational success (β = 0.42, p = .023; β’s = 0.44 − 0.64 across sensitivity models). Adding false belief ToM substantially increased model fit (ΔR 2 = 0.115, Cohen’s f 2 = 0.15), independent of baseline cognitive abilities and demographic factors. These findings provide the first empirical evidence in unilateral RHD that the ability to reason about a partner’s knowledge and manage conflict with one’s privileged perspective is critical for successful conversation. Results support theoretical models of ToM as a cognitive basis for everyday conversation. The clinical implications underscore the importance of socio-cognitive screening and ToM-based interventions to enhance communication outcomes in stroke rehabilitation.

Article.Title: Effects of plant growth regulators on seed yield, quality, and physiological traits of seed-producing sugar beet
Article.Authors: Zhao L.; Wang B.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: During sugar beet seed production, excessive stem elongation and lodging can adversely affect seed yield and quality. However, the effects of plant growth regulators (PGRs) on lodging resistance, physiological traits, and seed production performance remain insufficiently understood. A 2 year field experiment (2023–2024) was conducted to evaluate the effects of 1,1-dimethyl piperidinium chloride [DPC; 300 (D1), 500 (D2), and 900 g ha −1 (D3)] and chlormequat chloride [CC; 600 (C1), 1000 (C2), and 1800 g ha −1 (C3)] on plant architecture, physiological traits, seed yield (SY), and seed quality of sugar beet. Correlation analysis and Random Forest modeling were used to identify variables associated with SY and germination percentage (GP), and entropy weight–TOPSIS was used for comprehensive evaluation. Both PGRs reduced plant height (PH) and lodging rate (LR) without reducing the number of effective branches. Compared with CK, PH under D3 and C3 was reduced by 13.6% and 17.5%, respectively. LR reductions under D3 and C3 were 45.8% and 55.9% in 2023 and 33.7% and 63.7% in 2024, respectively. Both PGRs also increased total chlorophyll content, antioxidant enzyme activities, and soluble regulatory compounds, while reducing relative electrical conductivity and H 2 O 2 content; however, these responses were not accompanied by significant changes in MDA. Across the two growing seasons, C3 increased SY, thousand-seed weight, GP, and kernel plumpness rate by 32.1%, 32.9%, 19.8%, and 25.9%, respectively, compared with CK. Correlation analysis and Random Forest modeling identified APX, soluble reducing sugar content, and LR as variables associated with variation in SY and GP rather than direct causal determinants. C3 had the highest TOPSIS score in both years, but C2 and C3 showed comparable responses for several important yield and quality traits. Thus, the TOPSIS result represents a relative comprehensive ranking rather than evidence of an agronomic optimum.

Article.Title: Trajectory tracking of SSMR using backstepping control with neural estimation for logistics applications
Article.Authors: Alattas K.; Boubaker S.; Rossomando F.
Article.Abstract: The control of Skid Steering mobile robots (SSMRs) in logistics applications is challenging due to their nonlinear dynamics, nonholonomic constraints, payload variations, and sensitivity to disturbances and wheel slip. These factors make accurate, fast, and robust trajectory tracking essential for ensuring safe and efficient operation in dynamic logistics environments. Additionally, this class of robots is known to be underactuated in nature which may limit the ability of classical controllers to ensure sufficient performance. To address the above-cited challenges, this work presents the development of a nested control system for trajectory tracking of an SSMR. The proposed architecture consists of an outer loop for kinematic posture control and an inner loop for robust control based on backstepping and a neural estimator. The central challenge addressed is the underactuated nature of the robot, which has three states but only two physical control inputs, preventing direct control of the lateral error. To address the unmodeled uncertainties in lateral friction, longitudinal resistive force, and opposition torque, which vary significantly depending on the terrain, a neural estimator based on radial basis function neural networks (RBF-NN) is integrated. This estimator is combined with a robust backstepping technique that uses a virtual control law to indirectly stabilize the lateral error through kinematic coupling with angular velocity. The practical stability of the nested system is rigorously demonstrated using Lyapunov theory, ensuring that the longitudinal, lateral, and angular tracking errors are Uniformly Ultimately Bounded (UUB). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive neural robust controller achieves improved tracking accuracy and reduced error residuals compared to conventional feedback linearization and pure backstepping controllers within the evaluated operating scenarios. The robustness of the scheme is confirmed numerically under simulated external disturbances and parameter uncertainties.

Article.Title: RGVT: retrieval-guided Vision Transformer for CT-based kidney lesion classification and segmentation
Article.Authors: CH V.; Rao N.; Aljarbouh A.; Karim F.; Mostafa S.
Article.Abstract: Kidney lesion classification and segmentation from computed tomography images remain challenging because cysts, stones, tumors, and normal renal tissue may show overlapping visual characteristics, low-contrast boundaries, and inter-patient variability. This study proposes RGVT, a retrieval-guided Vision Transformer framework for CT-based kidney lesion classification and segmentation. The proposed framework extracts global image features using a Vision Transformer encoder and retrieves visually similar reference-case embeddings from a training-set memory bank. These retrieved embeddings are fused with current-case image features through cross-attention to improve lesion representation before classification and segmentation. The framework was evaluated on a CT kidney lesion dataset 1 containing cyst, normal, stone, and tumor classes and was compared with U-Net, U-Net + HC, and Swin Transformer baselines. In the original image-level evaluation, RGVT achieved an accuracy of 96.40%, precision of 96.20%, recall of 96.00%, F1-score of 96.10%, and macro-AUC of 0.977. For binary kidney-stone segmentation on KSSD2025, RGVT achieved a Dice score of 94.20% and an IoU of 89.50%. An additional group-disjoint analysis was performed using the same RGVT architecture and is reported in the Supplementary Information to examine the effect of examination-level separation on classification performance. The retrieval memory was restricted to training-group representations in this additional analysis. These results are intended to provide complementary evidence regarding the behavior of retrieval-guided visual feature fusion under different data-partitioning conditions.

Article.Title: GAB-Seg: a task-specific boundary-aware framework for irregular multi-scale spot-like target segmentation in anterior segment images
Article.Authors: Fu Z.; Luo L.; Zhou H.
Article.Abstract: The automated segmentation of localized spot-like anomalies on the bulbar conjunctiva presents a specific image processing challenge. While anterior segment images generally maintain high overall clarity without severe lighting interference, the visual data in this domain is strictly characterized by scattered, irregularly shaped targets with extreme scale variations and ambiguous boundary transitions. Compounded by data scarcity and severe foreground-background class imbalance, we propose GAB-Seg, a task-tailored generative boundary-aware segmentation framework exclusively designed for these morphological attributes. To overcome limited training samples, conditional generative adversarial networks provide data augmentation. Crucially, a Cross-Domain Gradient Orthogonal Decoupling (CGOD) module resolves optimization conflicts, preventing synthesized images from disrupting the learning of real edge gradients. To tackle boundary ambiguity, a Multi-Contour Predictive Map Auxiliary (MC-PMA) module constructs structural priors via polygon approximation, guiding the network to capture core target trajectories. Finally, a newly designed Multi-scale Smooth Distance-aware Synergistic Loss (MSDS-Loss) mitigates missed detections intrinsic to long-tailed distributions while suppressing local high-frequency noise. Experimental results on our internal test set suggest that GAB-Seg provides an effective, task-tailored engineering solution for this specific segmentation scenario.

Article.Title: Glutamate-binding protein from Corynebacterium glutamicum as fluorescence probe for glutamate detection in artificial cerebrospinal fluid
Article.Authors: Ferrara G.; Varriale A.; Milosevic I.; Radonic V.; D’Auria S.; Staiano M.
Article.Abstract: L-Glutamate (L-Glu) is the primary excitatory neurotransmitter in the mammalian central nervous system. In neurobiology, monitoring L-Glu accumulation is critical to track the neurodegeneration process, since excessive extracellular levels are caused by acute events like stroke, brain injuries, or malignant tumors. Conventional analytical methods are widely used to quantify L-Glu. Recently, alternative approaches based on biosensors have been developed for monitoring L-Glu in biological systems. In this work, we explored the use of the glutamate-binding protein (GluB), isolated from Corynebacterium glutamicum , as a specific probe to design a fluorescence biosensor for L-Glu detection. For this purpose, one of the three cysteine residues of GluB was labeled with the environment-sensitive fluorescence dye acrylodan. The stability of the labeled protein was assessed through thermal stability experiments. The binding of L-Glu to the GluB-acrylodan was investigated by steady-state and time-resolved fluorescence measurements. The results indicate the capability of the biosensor to effectively intercept the concentration values of L-Glu that are characteristic of acute clinical emergencies and tumor microenvironments before they can reach extreme neurotoxic levels. To explore the clinical potential application of the assay, GluB-acrylodan was tested through time-resolved fluorescence measurements in artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF). The results showed a LoD of 19.70 µM, a threshold value that is compatible with the pathological concentrations of L-Glu. The results suggest that GluB-acrylodan could represent a potential tool for future applications in neurobiological research and cellular excitotoxic events.

Article.Title: Insights into potential health risk of heavy metals from farmed fish and fish feed in renowned fish-growing region of Bangladesh
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Kanta A.; Khan M.; Rahman M.; Salam A.; Jiang J.; Aziz A.; Gautam S.; Min B.
Article.Abstract: Toxic elements can be accumulated into human body through fish chain as fish is exposed to metals through water, sediment and contaminated feeds. Therefore, the study was conducted to determine the heavy metal content of fish species and their feeds, as well as the potential health risks associated with them. Forty-five fish samples were collected from fifteen fish farms whereas thirty feed samples were collected from three upalizas of Mymensingh district during June to August 2022. The collected samples were digested with an acid mixture, and concentrations of twelve heavy metals were measured by ICP-MS. Fe predominates over the other metals in almost all samples. All three fish species contained the higher concentration of Fe, Ni, Zn and Cr. The concentrations of Fe, Ni, Zn and Cr are 20.84, 9.4, 6.60, 1.86 mgkg -1 for Pangasius, 25.8, 13.82, 8.91 and 2.00 mgkg -1 for Rui and 27.58, 7.08, 7.92 and 2.09 mgkg -1 for Tilapia, respectively. The WHO/EU standard limits for Cr, Mn, Ni, and Pb were exceeded in feed samples from farmers and in commercial feeds. Tilapia fish species had a strong propensity to acquire As, Co, and Ni from farmer-supplied feeds and As and Se from commercial feeds as BFAF value was higher than 1. The degree of contamination across all species can be characterized as follows: Tilapia > Rui > Pangasius. The mean estimated daily intake of the heavy metals was lower than the recommended daily allowance. Except for Fe, the THQ values for fish species were less than 1. Conversely, HI in all species was higher than the allowable threshold of 1. Carcinogenic risks from Ni and Pb consumption were present in all fish species. Antibiotics, especially oxytetracycline and tetracycline, were detected in various fish samples. The results suggest that the authority should take appropriate precautions to ensure feed quality and prevent significant heavy metal exposure from farmed fish.

Article.Title: SiO₂-modified bacterial nanocellulose (BNC) for efficient COD removal from petrochemical wastewater: characterization, removal performance and mechanistic insights
Article.Authors: Zamani W.; Rastgar S.; Hedayati A.
Article.Abstract: Petrochemical wastewater contains high concentrations of refractory organic pollutants, resulting in elevated chemical oxygen demand (COD) and serious environmental concerns. In this study, a SiO₂-modified bacterial nanocellulose (SiO₂–BNC) nanocomposite was synthesized via the sol–gel method and evaluated for COD removal from petrochemical wastewater. Material characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of SiO₂ and the formation of a porous, high-surface-area architecture. Process evaluation using response surface methodology (RSM) identified temperature and adsorbent dosage as the most influential operating parameters. Under the optimized conditions (pH 6.5, adsorbent dosage of 250 mg/L and temperature of 30 °C), the nanocomposite achieved an exceptional COD removal efficiency of 98.2%, displaying reasonable correspondence with experimental trends, although quantitative model predictions should be interpreted cautiously due to the significant lack-of-fit. The superior adsorption performance was attributed to the synergistic effects of intraparticle diffusion, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic attraction, and surface complexation. Furthermore, the adsorbent retained 89.4% of its initial removal efficiency (preserving approximately 91.0% of its initial adsorption capacity) after five consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. These findings demonstrate that the SiO₂–BNC nanocomposite represents an efficient, robust and recyclable adsorbent for advanced industrial wastewater remediation.

Article.Title: Integrated mechanical earth modeling and finite-element assessment of casing-collapse mitigation strategies in high-stress salt-bearing caprocks
Article.Authors: Elahifar B.; Hosseini E.
Article.Abstract: Casing collapse in wells penetrating salt-bearing caprocks is a significant well-integrity concern because anisotropic in-situ stresses and mechanical contrasts between geological formations can produce non-uniform loading. This study integrates a Mechanical Earth Model (MEM) with finite-element analysis (FEA) to evaluate the mechanical response of alternative casing configurations in a deep well. Acoustic and density logs from 3050 to 3618 m were used to estimate formation elastic properties and in-situ stresses. These estimates were applied to models of the formation–cement–casing system. The baseline 9.625-in production casing was compared with four alternatives: a thicker-wall T-95 casing configuration, a thick-wall L-80 casing, a 7-in inner liner installed within the existing casing, and a standalone 7-in casing. The predicted maximum von Mises stress and radial displacement were used as the primary response indicators. The baseline configuration produced a maximum von Mises stress of 1010.2 MPa and a displacement of 4.574 cm in Gachsaran Section 2. The corresponding values were 871.4 MPa and 3.821 cm for the T-95 configuration, and 618.2 MPa and 2.918 cm for the thick-wall L-80 configuration. The combined 9.625-in casing and 7-in liner exhibited the lowest reported response, with a maximum von Mises stress of 78.6 MPa and a displacement of 0.694 cm in the same section. The standalone 7-in casing showed a less favorable response than the combined configuration. These results indicate that, within the modeled conditions, increasing wall thickness and incorporating an inner liner may reduce predicted stress and displacement more substantially than upgrading steel grade alone. The findings are specific to a single-well static numerical assessment and require further numerical verification and independent field validation. Because time-dependent salt creep was not explicitly modeled, the results do not establish long-term casing performance.

Article.Title: A gradient multi-isocenter VMAT strategy for efficient craniospinal irradiation on an intelligent couch-shifting accelerator
Article.Authors: Li S.; Gao Y.; Wang J.; Dai N.; Li X.; Zhao Y.; Chi Z.; Zhang R.; Bai W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Delivering high-quality craniospinal irradiation (CSI) remains challenging because of the need to achieve adequate target coverage across ultra-extended volumes while minimizing dose to normal tissue and maintaining clinically practical treatment efficiency. Although helical tomotherapy (HT) provides excellent dose conformity for CSI, prolonged delivery time and increased low-dose exposure may limit its clinical applicability. This study aimed to investigate whether increasing the number of isocenters in a gradient multi-isocenter volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) strategy could enhance modulation capability for extended target volumes and provide a clinically feasible alternative to HT. Sixteen patients who received CSI at The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University between January 2022 and March 2026 were retrospectively selected. For each patient, two VMAT strategies using an intelligent couch-shifting accelerator (TaiChiPro) were generated: a conventional multi-isocenter configuration (Group A) and an increased-isocenter configuration (Group B). HT plans delivered on a Radixact™ system were generated as reference plans (Group C). Dosimetric parameters of the planning target volume (PTV), organs at risk (OARs), low-dose exposure of normal tissue, monitor units (MU), delivery time, and patient-specific quality assurance results were evaluated. All plans met clinical dose constraints. Increasing the number of isocenters improved the dose modulation capability of VMAT for extended target volumes. Compared with the conventional VMAT approach, the increased-isocenter VMAT strategy achieved lower V 5 , V 10 , and D mean values for selected OARs, including the parotid glands and kidneys, as well as reduced low-dose exposure to normal tissue ( P < 0.05). Compared with HT, both VMAT strategies substantially reduced delivery time by approximately 78% (1355.98 ± 219.63 s vs. 301.08 ± 27.56 s vs. 302.30 ± 19.02 s, P < 0.001) and decreased low-dose exposure to selected normal tissue. HT maintained advantages in target conformity index (CI), homogeneity index (HI), as well as in reducing D max to selected central nervous system structures. However, no significant differences were observed between conventional and increased-isocenter VMAT regarding target coverage. Both VMAT strategies achieved clinically acceptable dose continuity across the target junction regions. Patient-specific quality assurance (QA) further demonstrated reliable delivery accuracy, with gamma passing rates exceeding 97% across all evaluated plans. A gradient multi-isocenter VMAT strategy implemented on an intelligent couch-shifting accelerator offers improved dose modulation for craniospinal irradiation while substantially improving delivery efficiency and reducing low-dose exposure to normal tissue. Increasing the number of isocenters may further improve OARs sparing without substantially increasing treatment time, while maintaining clinically acceptable target dose distributions. This approach provides a practical option for complex ultra-extended field radiotherapy, particularly in institutions without dedicated tomotherapy systems.

Article.Title: Fitness-for-purpose of hospital clinical data warehouses for oncology real-world evidence generation: a PICOTS-informed feasibility assessment
Article.Authors: Choi E.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Yu S.; Seong H.; Kim Y.; Ryu M.; Kim K.; Hyung J.; Kim K.; Han E.
Article.Abstract: We assessed the fitness for purpose of routinely collected data from hospital clinical data warehouses (CDWs) for a predefined oncology real-world evidence (RWE) study. We examined 159 prespecified variables for availability, completeness, data format, and capture frequency, linked the variable-level findings to Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes, Timing, and Setting (PICOTS) components and key covariates, and assessed system-level CDW implementation. Of 159 variables, 127 (79.9%) were directly captured, 2 (1.3%) were objectively derivable from structured data, 21 (13.2%) were ascertainable from composite clinical information, and 9 (5.7%) were unavailable. Population and Comparator eligibility, Timing, Setting, and key covariates were feasible; Intervention was feasible with caveats, whereas Outcomes had limited feasibility, particularly for clinically interpretive endpoints requiring composite clinical ascertainment. System-level implementation was high across assessed domains, whereas studyspecific variable-level limitations remained in completeness and ascertainment. Broad availability of relevant clinical information did not consistently translate into direct analytic readiness, particularly for clinically interpretive variables, indicating the need for studyspecific assessment and, where necessary, targeted clinical ascertainment, external data linkage, or validation to support the intended analysis.

Article.Title: Populations from Indian Himalayan and adjoining regions share their associated lactase persistence variants with the Tibetans and South Asians
Article.Authors: De S.; Rai D.; Mandal K.; Subba S.; Mahapatra A.; Mitra N.; Chorol U.; Desai S.; Singh P.; Basu Mallick C.; Thangaraj K.; Chaubey G.; Tamang R.
Article.Abstract: The geographic distribution of lactase persistence (LP) within the global population demonstrates considerable variability. LP is linked to multiple independent mutations in a 100 bp enhancer region located 14 kb upstream of the Lactase ( LCT ) gene. Among these mutations, the -13910C>T variant was found to be identical by descent in both Europeans and Indians. Notably, the Indian Himalayan and adjoining populations (HAAPs) possess distinct genetic characteristics and share a significant proportion of ancestry with Tibetans. Previous studies identified the -13838G>A variant as the primary determinant of LP in Tibetans. In light of this, we investigated the spectrum of LP-associated variants within the HAAPs, who also have a long-standing tradition of cattle herding. Our examination of the 100 bp enhancer region of the 13th intron of MCM6 , situated 14 kb upstream of the LCT gene, among 19 HAAPs revealed one known variant (-13910C>T) and three variants, reported for the first time in Indian populations; -13838G>A, -13906T>A, and -13908C > T. We observed that both -13838G>A and -13910C>T variants in HAAPs occurred at considerable proportions, compared with other mainland Indian populations, which largely possess the -13910C>T. This further testifies that leveraging multiple populations across time helps us to understand the spread and prevalence of LP worldwide.

Article.Title: Gravitational pinning and commensurability constrain a rigid-sheet thermo-magnetic mechanism for laser-driven levitating graphite
Article.Authors: Liu Q.; Yi B.; Liu K.
Article.Abstract: Pyrolytic-graphite sheets levitating above checkerboard magnet arrays can be translated by a scanned laser, but the origin of this motion remains undetermined. In the standard thermo-magnetic explanation, local heating weakens the diamagnetic susceptibility and pulls the sheet toward the beam. Here we test this explanation at the level of transport by combining the checkerboard field, heat flow on the sheet, Curie-law susceptibility and self-consistent levitation height in a driven-washboard model without fitted transport parameters. The central result is gravitational pinning, i.e. after vertical re-equilibration the leading barrier scale is set by weight and geometry and is independent of the magnetic-energy prefactor, and uniform heating stiffens the barrier ( \(+11.2\%\) for a 300 K overheat at the enhanced coupling). The photothermal perturbation contains only the lattice harmonics of the magnet array, so it reshapes the wells but supplies neither an incommensurate trap nor a dc tilt. Across a 700-point operating map at a thousand-fold enhanced coupling, the model produces pinning, intra-well libration and occasional impulsive kicks, but no sustained beam-following transport, and matching the barrier force alone requires effective Curie constants of 37.9–48.7 K. Sheet deformation, current-driven forces and gas-mediated actuation remain candidate mechanisms, and we propose direct tests of each.

Article.Title: Quantum metrology via multipartite non-Gaussian states
Article.Authors: Isaac I.; Nha H.
Article.Abstract: We study quantum phase estimation using multimode non-Gaussian states to investigate quantum enhancement of measurement precision due to the characteristics of multipartite quantum entanglement. We consider two prototypical classes of multipartite entangled states, namely, GHZ-type and W-type entangled states of N optical modes and obtain an optimal configuration for each case by dividing N modes into two parts, one sent to phase-region and the other to empty region. In the lossless regime, both classes exhibit the Heisenberg scaling of quantum Fisher information (QFI) with input energy while the metrological advantage using larger-mode multipartite entanglement appears only in W-type states. Article.Authors: Diers A.; Rudloff S.; Singh V.; Hausmann H.; Agulló V.; Moreno D.; Wagner A.; Stricker S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Celiac disease (CD) is a gluten-dependent chronic inflammatory disease. Anthocyanins (ACN) like cyanidin-3-glucoside (C3G) and delphinidin-3-glucoside (D3G) may possess anti-inflammatory properties. Article.Title: Combined Saussurea costus and doxorubicin suppresses breast cancer cell migration and proliferation through MMP2/MMP9 downregulation: in vitro and molecular docking evidence
Article.Authors: Youssef M.; Warda A.; Hasanen J.; Ragab A.; Mohsen E.; El-Far A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer (BC) is still a major cause of cancer-related death in women and requires new strategies for treatment. Saussurea costus (COS) has been reported to exhibit anticancer activity, and doxorubicin (DOX) is a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent. The docking and dynamics study of major compounds with MMP2 and MMP9 was performed. The effects of COS, DOX, and their combination on MCF7 and MDA-MB-231 cells were assessed for cytotoxicity, proliferation, migration (wound healing and transwell), colony formation, apoptosis (annexin-V), cell cycle, and MMP2/MMP9 mRNA expression. Luteolin had the most negative value for protein binding (MMP2: − 8.90 kcal/mol; MMP9: − 9.50 kcal/mol) and medioresinol for mRNA binding. COS demonstrated dose-dependent cytotoxicity (IC 50 : 106.8 ± 1.43 μg/mL for MCF7; 116.8 ± 5.66 μg/mL for MDA-MB-231). The COS + DOX combination significantly reduced proliferation, migration, and colony formation, and increased apoptosis (MCF7: 34.85 ± 1.84%, MDA-MB-231: 45.56 ± 7.74%), and induced G2/M arrest in MDA-MB-231 cells. The expression of MMP2 and MMP9 mRNA was significantly downregulated. The COS + DOX treatment had a combinatorial effect in suppressing BC cell growth and migration, which was associated with downregulation of MMP2/MMP9 and induction of apoptosis. Article.Abstract: In this paper, a new adaptive critic learning approach is proposed to solve the safety tracking control issue for nonlinear systems with unmatched uncertainties, in which these uncertainties are converted into the management of tracking error dynamics, handling both transient and steady-state behaviors. The proposed strategy integrates an approximate optimal controller to manage transient dynamics and a conventional controller to handle steady-state behavior. To ensure the system states within safety boundaries under unmatched disturbances, a new cost function is integrated with the Control Barrier Function (CBF). Based on a comprehensive safety analysis, the proposed controller is then developed using adaptive control theory. Unlike traditional actor-critic methods, the proposed approach of this paper utilizes the adaptive-critic scheme to solve the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Finally, the stability, Uniformly Ultimately Bounded (UUB) property, and feasibility of the designed controller are validated through theoretical analysis and two simulation experiments.

Article.Authors: Nair S.; Anand N.; Andrushia D.; Varghese A.
Article.Abstract: The purpose of this research is to examine M25 grade concrete which incorporates unsoaked Light Expanded Clay Aggregate (LECA) as a substitute at 0% – 50% levels. Performance of freshly mixed concrete was evaluated based on slump test. Hardened concrete was tested for density, compressive strength, split tensile strength and flexural strength at 28 days. The mixes were also assessed for durability through acid and sulphate mass loss, water absorption and Rapid Chloride Penetration Testing (RCPT). Micro-structural characteristics were evaluated using Scanning Electron Microscopy-Energy Dispersive X-ray (SEM–EDX) analysis and sustainability was evaluated using both embodied energy and carbon (CO₂) emissions. The results also showed that a strong linear relationship exists between compressive strengths and densities (R 2 ≈ 0.98). Based on the experimental results, LECA replacement levels of 20–25% gave the most favourable trade-off between compressive strength retention and concrete density reduction, giving compressive strengths of 17–19 MPa (compared to 31.45 MPa for the control mix) while reducing concrete density by 15–20%. In terms of durability, although indications of increased water absorption, chloride penetration ability and mass loss were noted as the LECA content increased these levels exhibited acceptable levels of performance as per the American Concrete Institute (ACI) 213R-14. SEM–EDX analysis showed that the interfacial transition zone became more refined. There was less accumulation of calcium hydroxide, which helped create stronger mechanical bonding between the aggregate and the paste. The use of LECA increases the embodied energy of concrete but reduces its density, thereby lowering the dead load on the structure and may contribute to long-term sustainability benefits such as reduced operational and structural demand.

Article.Title: A regulatory node in the transcriptional network underlying multiple senescence subtypes in WI-38 human fibroblasts
Article.Authors: Turkki T.; Suda K.; Moriyama Y.; Ishida R.; Chiu Y.; Hasegawa H.; Razali N.; Kono K.
Article.Abstract: Cellular senescence is a stable cell cycle arrest accompanied by inflammatory responses that contribute to aging, age-related diseases, and cancer. Establishment of the senescent state requires extensive transcriptomic reprogramming; however, identifying transcriptional regulators that contribute to this process remains challenging. To address these challenges, we applied an in silico approach based on upstream regulator analysis using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis to systematically infer candidate transcriptional regulators from transcriptomic data. By analyzing datasets from WI-38 human fibroblasts exposed to distinct senescence-inducing stresses, including DNA damage, plasma membrane damage and calcium influx, we identified MYBL2 as a transcriptional regulator consistently implicated across multiple cellular senescence subtypes. Experimental validation demonstrated that MYBL2 downregulation is sufficient to induce several features associated with cellular senescence hallmarks and that MYBL2 overexpression suppresses these responses, consistent with its role in cell cycle progression. Taken together, these findings position MYBL2 as a shared regulatory node whose downregulation drives sustained cell cycle arrest in WI-38 cells.

Article.Title: Effects of pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo L.) flesh waste flour on the technological, textural, and sensory properties of bread
Article.Authors: Türkoğlu M.; Gerçekaslan K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined pumpkin flesh waste flour (PF) from pumpkin cultivated for seed production ( Cucurbita pepo L.) in bread production, aiming to determine the maximum PF substitution level achievable without compromising bread’s technological performance and consumer acceptability, rather than to affirm nutritional superiority. Physical, textural, and sensory attributes were evaluated in bread with PF at 2.5%, 5%, 10%, and 20%, including crumb texture changes during 5-day storage. PF level significantly affected all measured bread properties ( p < 0.05). Loaf volume and specific volume did not differ significantly between the control and 2.5% PF bread ( p > 0.05). Both decreased progressively from 5% PF onward, reaching 36% (254.17 vs. 397.83 ml) and 37% (1.91 vs. 3.04 ml/g) reductions at 20% PF. Loaf weight was lowest at 5% PF (129.87 g) and highest at 20% PF (134.53 g). Baking loss increased slightly at 2.5-5% PF (up to 23.20%, from 22.13% in the control) and then decreased significantly at 20% PF (to 18.94%). Crust and crumb color changed significantly with PF level, reflecting progressive crust darkening and crumb yellowing. On day 1, PF addition increased crumb hardness (7.59–18.80 N) and chewiness (5.11–9.44 N) while reducing springiness (0.988 − 0.912) and cohesiveness (0.688 − 0.556), with these differences becoming more pronounced during storage. Sensory scores did not differ significantly between the control and PF levels up to 5%, whereas 10% and 20% PF significantly reduced crust and crumb color, porosity, taste-aroma, odor, and overall acceptability ( p < 0.05). Up to 5% PF substitution produced bread with technological and sensory properties comparable to the control. These findings indicate that pumpkin flesh, discarded during seed pumpkin processing, can be valorized as a bread ingredient at moderate substitution levels, supporting sustainable waste utilization. Confirming its nutritional and functional benefits, however, will require compositional analyses of the baked product.

Article.Title: GRU-based temporal modeling of ECG derived physiological features for eclampsia outcome classification
Article.Authors: R. S.; N. K.; S. S.
Article.Abstract: Early detection of instability in the neurological and cardiovascular systems is imperative for the prevention of severe maternal complications such as eclampsia. Because of the increased occurrence of eclampsia during pregnancy weeks 20 or later, the importance of physiological monitoring is vital during the second and third trimesters. The findings clearly indicate the ability of temporal deep learning to classify physiological patterns related to eclampsia-related outcomes. In this regard, the suggested approach has been assessed on 10,000 instances of pregnancy-related ECG and clinical data, generated from clinically significant features obtained from various biomedical databases such as Kaggle, as well as the current clinical literature. The employed dataset includes multiple lead ECG signals along with the maternal clinical and demographic features. In the preprocessing step, data normalization and noise management were performed on the dataset. The Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN) method was utilized to overcome class imbalance. Some of the significant ECG features, such as RR interval, QRS interval, and ECG axis, were extracted from the ECG signals to be able to use them as a feature vector representing unstable physiology. Furthermore, temporal relations between extracted features were modeled using the Gated Recurrent Unit network. The model presented in this paper was evaluated against Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM. The experimental results show that the GRU model outperforms all other comparison methods by scoring 97.2% for accuracy, 96.8% for precision, 97.0% for recall, and 96.9% for F1-score, while the ROC-AUC is 0.989, and PR-AUC scores 0.98. From these results, one can see how efficient temporal deep learning is in detecting physiological behavior and how it can be used in early warnings of instability from eclampsia. Further investigation involving independent subjects, clinical validation of results, and prospective ECG data collection would be necessary for the proposed method to apply to the clinical setting.

Article.Title: An energy-efficient and explainable green AI framework for student dropout prediction with a rule-based decision support module
Article.Authors: Almazroei E.; Andijani D.
Article.Abstract: Student dropout is a persistent issue in massive open online and blended learning environments, and identifying vulnerable learners early is essential. Although deep learning (DL) techniques have increased prediction accuracy, they often have substantial computational overheads and insufficiently transparent operations, thus hindering their implementation in resource-scarce educational settings. This work presents a green AI and explainable learning approach for the prediction of student dropout using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). A small multilayer perceptron model, GreenMLP, is constructed to capture the behavioral pattern of learners by analyzing their demographic information and virtual learning environment logs. The GreenMLP model is trained under a low-resource setting on CPUs only, where energy expenditure during training is tracked using CodeCarbon, allowing the direct calculation of the carbon footprint. In addition, eXplainable AI (XAI) approaches such as SHAP and LIME are used to provide global and local explanations for the prediction task. The experimental results on the OULAD demonstrate that the proposed GreenMLP model achieves an AUC of 0.8361 and an accuracy of 0.7584 while using only 2,753 parameters and producing 2.08 × 10⁻⁵ kg of CO₂ during training. The explainability analysis reveals that student engagement features, particularly total and peak interaction levels, dominate dropout risk, whereas demographic factors play secondary roles. The rule-based decision layer reduces false alerts and increases intervention precision. These results show that energy-efficient and XAI methods can achieve competitive results and help maintain transparency and sustainability in the assessment of dropout risk in digital education.

Article.Title: Biotechnological enhancement of l-asparaginase production by mutant Aspergillus flavus against MCF-7 breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Zrieq R.; Kelany A.; El-Aziz N.; Al Qtaish N.; Ali A.; Ibrahim S.; Abdelghani H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to concentrated on isolating the best fungal strain with the highest l -ASNase activity; strain l -ASNase-4 recorded 296.68 U/mg, was sequenced the genomic region/gene used for molecular identification, identified as Aspergillus flavus AFK3 using PCR and ITS region gene sequencing and submitted into NCBI accession no. OK086056. Sequential mutation induction using Acridin Orange (AO) and Ethidium Bromide (EtBr) were used in successive mutagenesis to increase strain A. flavus AFK3 l -ASNase production. The most successful mutant that produced l -ASNase was A. flavus AO-22, which showed l -ASNase activity two times (622.47 U/mg) over the wild type strain A. flavus AFK3. This study aimed to enhance enzyme production by employing a two-phase optimization strategy. The initial phase employed the One Factor at a Time (OFAT) approach to identify key process parameters (different carbon and nitrogen sources) influencing enzyme activity. OFAT analysis revealed that the best carbon and nitrogen source showed the highest levels of l -ASNase activity in the medium containing glucose and malt extract. In the subsequent phase, Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used for further optimization, involving 30 experiments to assess the combined effects of multiple factors. The Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used to identify the ideal conditions for l -ASNase expression. With a pH of 7, 1.5% glucose (a carbon source), 1.5% malt extract (a nitrogen source), and 3 days of incubation, the maximum l -ASNase activity for mutant A. flavus AO-22 was 1923.04 U/mg. Ammonium sulfate precipitation (35–75%), DEAE-cellulose ion exchange chromatography, and Sephadex G100 gel filtration were used to completely purify l -ASNase for the wild type A. flavus AFK3 and its mutant A. flavus AO-22.The purification process raised the purification fold of the purified l -ASNase by 12.79 and 13.09 times, resulting in protein yields of 34.70 and 36.26%; respectively, for the wild type A. flavus AFK3 and its mutant A. flavus AO-22. According to SDS-PAGE analysis, the partially purified l -ASNase in this investigation had a molecular weight of roughly 53 kDa. Under ideal circumstances, a peak specific activity of 8455.83 and 4456.78 U/mg was obtained the purified l -ASNase for the wild type A. flavus AFK3 and its mutant A. flavus AO-22 at 20 min at 30 °C, pH 8.0, using l -asparagine as substrate. Both purified l -ASNase from wild type A. flavus AFK3 and mutant A. flavus AO-22 demonstrated concentration-dependent cytotoxicity in MCF-7 breast cancer cells, as assessed using the MTT assay. Notably, purified l -ASNase from mutant A. flavus AO-22 showed slightly higher cytotoxic potency, with an IC₅₀ of 61.92 µM compared to 64.02 µM for purified l -ASNase from wild type A. flavus AFK3. Overall, both purified l -ASNase from wild type A. flavus AFK3 and mutant A. flavus AO-22 exhibited significant antiproliferative activity, while purified l -ASNase from mutant A. flavus AO-22 showing a marginally stronger effect. According to these results, mutant A. flavus AO-22 seemed to be very future promising effective of l -ASNase a diverse array of clinical uses such as on MCF-7 breast cancer cytotoxicity.
