Article.Title: Dietary diversity, nutritional status, and health-related quality of life among adults living with HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy in ilu Ababor Zone, South-West Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Gemechu E.; Lemma T.; Abate K.
Article.Abstract: Malnutrition, low dietary diversity, and reduced health-related quality of life remain common among people living with HIV/AIDS in Ethiopia, yet most previous studies have relied on body mass index alone, missing clinically significant muscle wasting. This facility-based cross-sectional study conducted from December 2020 to August 2021 assessed dietary diversity, comprehensive nutritional status using both BMI and sex-specific mid-upper arm circumference cut-offs, health-related quality of life, and clinical outcomes among 384 adults on antiretroviral therapy in Ilu Ababor Zone, South-West Ethiopia. Only 39.3% achieved good dietary diversity. While 55.5% had normal nutritional status, 12.2% had isolated low MUAC—muscle wasting that would be missed by BMI alone. Combined undernutrition was significantly associated with detectable viral load (35.7% vs. 18.3%), low CD4 count (58.6% vs. 24.4%), and opportunistic infections (47.1% vs. 20.7%). Factors independently associated with poor dietary diversity included low income, lack of formal education, detectable viral load, and CD4 count < 350 cells/µL. Combined undernutrition was the strongest negative predictor of health-related quality of life. Routine MUAC measurement should be integrated into ART clinics to identify individuals with isolated muscle wasting, and nutritional interventions should be prioritised for patients with uncontrolled viraemia and immunosuppression.

Article.Title: Impact of HIV infection, immune status, and integrase inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy on the gut microbiota in men who have sex with men with and without HIV
Article.Authors: Rosas Cancio-Suárez M.; Díaz-Álvarez J.; Díaz-García C.; Nieto-Salas L.; Sánchez-Conde M.; Moreno E.; García-Ruiz de Morales A.; Martín-Pedraza L.; Crespillo-Andújar C.; Fons-Contreras M.; Ron R.; del Amo-de Palacios A.; González-Sanz M.; Moreno S.; Serrano-Villar S.
Article.Abstract: HIV infection and antiretroviral therapy (ART) influence gut microbiota, affecting immune function and systemic inflammation. However, isolating the effects of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based ART on gut microbiota is challenging due to confounding by HIV status, immunosuppression, and behavioral factors. We examined three cohorts of men who have sex with men (MSM) (n = 62): (1) HIV-negative individuals using post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) (n = 22), (2) people with HIV (PWH) with < 350 CD4 cells/µL sampled before and 48 weeks after ART initiation (n = 23), (3) PWH on long-term INSTI-based ART with immune recovery (n = 17). Fecal samples were collected longitudinally in cohorts 1 (at baseline and after 4 weeks of PEP) and 2 (at baseline and 48 weeks after ART initiation), and at a single timepoint in cohort 3. Microbiota composition was analyzed by 16 S rRNA sequencing, and functional profiling inferred with PICRUSt2. Differential abundance was assessed using ANCOM-BC2. HIV-negative participants showed significantly lower alpha diversity than PWH, and beta diversity differed by HIV status. Short-term INSTI-based ART in PEP users was associated with limited microbiota changes. Pro-inflammatory taxa, such as Prevotellaceae , were enriched in PWH. Functional predictions indicated enrichment of pathways related to cell envelope structure, membrane transport, and stress response. Long-term ART was associated with modest taxonomic and functional shifts, including enrichment of Barnesiella in individuals with immune recovery (ANCOM-BC2, LFC = 3.6, adjusted p = 0.02). HIV infection and immune suppression are the main drivers of gut microbiota alterations in MSM, whereas INSTI-based ART is associated with comparatively modest changes. These findings support a limited impact of INSTI-based ART on microbiota composition and function.

Article.Title: Run-to-run variability of large language models extracting structured data from Turkish colorectal cancer pathology report summaries
Article.Authors: Bilgiç E.; Karacan E.
Article.Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to convert free-text pathology reports into structured data, but validation usually relies on a single query. We submitted an identical zero-shot prompt containing 75 semi-structured, single-centre Turkish colorectal cancer pathology report summaries to ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek through public web interfaces, ten times each in new conversations at two time points, and compared eight extracted variables with a manually curated reference standard. Accuracy was at ceiling: 14,972 of 15,000 fields (99.8%) were correct across direct-extraction runs, and a regular-expression program written by Gemini was equally accurate, showing that the task is solvable by pattern matching and cannot discriminate between models on comprehension. Repeated querying nevertheless revealed variability invisible in single runs. In one of ten runs, ChatGPT left tumour differentiation empty in 28 records; within that run, omission was strongly associated with source-text spelling (28/29 versus 0/26 records). In five of ten runs, Gemini generated and executed parsing code, with output indistinguishable from direct extraction. Output layout varied between runs and over time. These findings establish that such instability occurs, not its frequency. Single-query accuracy does not establish reproducibility. For structured data extraction, outputs from public chat services should not be used without verification.

Article.Title: Accuracy of suprasternal ultrasonography compared with fluoroscopy for assessing endotracheal tube depth in preschool children with congenital heart disease
Article.Authors: Chintabanyat O.; Konateerakul P.; Waitayawinyu P.; Vijarnsorn C.; Raksamani K.
Article.Abstract: Endotracheal tube (ETT) malposition may occur in children with congenital heart disease because of shorter tracheal length and growth restriction. This prospective diagnostic accuracy study evaluated suprasternal ultrasonography for confirming ETT depth in 116 preschool children (0–6 years) undergoing elective cardiac catheterization under general anesthesia. Microcuff ETTs were inserted using the vocal cord depth mark. Ultrasonographic visualization of the cuff at the suprasternal notch (SSN), a prespecified surrogate for correct tip position, was compared with fluoroscopic tip position as the reference standard. Fluoroscopy showed correct tip position in 99 patients (85.3%). Using cuff visualization at the SSN as the criterion, sensitivity was 40.4% (95% CI, 30.7–50.7), specificity 70.6% (95% CI, 44.0–89.7), and overall agreement 44.8%, with negligible agreement beyond chance. In post hoc exploratory analyses, extending the threshold to 1.1–1.3 cm above the SSN increased sensitivity to above 80% but reduced specificity to 20%. The size-dependent distance between the cuff and the tube tip may explain part of this discordance. The SSN-based cuff criterion has limited accuracy for confirming ETT depth in this population and should not be used alone; revised ultrasonographic criteria require prospective validation. Clinical trial registration The study was registered in the Thai Clinical Trials Registry before data collection process (TCTR20230218001).

Article.Title: Tear fluid interleukin-6 concentrations in healthy individuals: pooled estimates and between-study heterogeneity
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Datta A.; Enriquez-de-Salamanca A.; Mergen B.; Agrawal R.; Lee B.; Travé-Huarte S.; Sharma N.; van de Sande N.; Raymond D.; Atkinson S.; Boychev N.; Gijs M.
Article.Abstract: This study is aimed to establish pooled estimates for interleukin-6 (IL-6) in tear fluid of healthy individuals and to identify key sources of variability influencing reported concentrations. Mean tear fluid IL-6 concentrations, along with methodological and demographic information were extracted. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to obtain pooled estimates of IL-6 concentrations. Meta-regression analyses were used to evaluate the effect of the definition of healthy, age, sex, sample type, collection method, and assay techniques. Across all included studies ( n = 76), the pooled estimate for tear fluid IL-6 concentrations was 20.02 pg/mL (95% CI, 13.09–30.64). A pooled estimate of basal tear fluid collected using capillary tubes (29 studies) was 23.16 pg/mL (95% CI, 10.91–49.19). In univariable and multivariable meta-regression, the collection method was significantly associated with pooled estimates of tear fluid IL-6 concentrations ( p < 0.05) but only accounted for part of the observed heterogeneity. The substantial heterogeneity observed across studies remained unexplained, underscoring the need for standardized approaches to the collection, processing, and analysis of tear fluid biomarkers.

Article.Title: Experimental and DFT investigation of a novel chromen-alanylglycine nonionic surfactant for enhanced oil recovery under harsh reservoir conditions
Article.Authors: Hosny R.; Khowdiar M.; Elhenawwy A.; Zahran A.; Abou-alfitooh S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To overcome the severe technical limitations of chemical enhanced oil recovery (CEOR) in hostile, high-salinity, and high-temperature reservoirs, this study introduces a novel molecular architecture based on a chromen-amino acid hybrid nonionic surfactant: 2-(7-hydroxy-2-oxo-2H-chromen-4-yl) acetyl alanylglycine (2HCAA). While conventional surfactants suffer from phase separation and precipitation under extreme ionic strengths, the newly synthesized 2HCAA displays exceptional structural resilience. Interfacial tension (IFT) evaluations demonstrate a distinct reduction from 18.4 to 1.9 mN/m. Crucially, contact angle profiling confirms a profound wettability alteration of the authentic sandstone substrate, successfully reversing the mineral matrix from a strongly oil-wetting state (132°) to a highly favorable water-wetting configuration (45.6°) at the critical micelle concentration (CMC). The definitive performance of 2HCAA was successfully validated through dynamic core-flooding experiments executed under rigorous, real-field simulated conditions (70 °C, 3000 psi pressure, and an extreme salinity of 116,000 ppm). The surfactant slug propagation successfully mobilized trapped capillary oil in porous media, providing a substantial incremental tertiary oil recovery that raised the ultimate recovery factor from 22.0 to 37.6% of the original oil in place (OOIP). To establish an atomistic-level understanding of this performance, quantum chemical Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were seamlessly integrated. The calculated HOMO–LUMO energy gap of 3.14 eV provides molecular-level evidence of a relatively stable yet electronically responsive molecular framework, complementing the experimentally observed interfacial activity. These findings position 2HCAA as a highly promising, structurally robust, and ecologically sound candidate for sustainable chemical flooding in challenging oil reservoirs.

Article.Title: Pupil baseline trends on ~ 10-s timescales track near-term task performance
Article.Authors: Yamashita J.; Terashima H.; Yoneya M.; Maruya K.; Kumada T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human task performance fluctuates on infraslow timescales, including a putative ~ 20-s cycle of task-positive/default-mode switching, yet a continuously computable biomarker remains scarce. Task-evoked pupil dilation tracks momentary facilitation of performance, but links between slow baseline dynamics and performance are inconsistent. Because prior research used demanding vigilance and working memory tasks, we tested whether upward 10-s baseline trends were associated with faster responses in a relatively simple, low-error go/no-go task. We quantified baseline “pupil trends” as slope-like changes at predefined timescales using two independent pipelines: moving-average smoothing and wavelet-based scale isolation. Upward trends were associated with faster responses across several smoothing windows, including 10 s, while the scale-isolated analysis identified the prespecified ~ 8-s dyadic component; downward trends were linked to slower responses (fastest vs. slowest quartile). These associations were supported by the strictly pre-target 10-s precursor and by trial-level analysis of the ~ 8-s component controlling for canonical pupil–behavior covariates. Timescale-specific pupil dynamics may provide a continuously computable index of local fluctuations in near-term task performance, with potential utility for monitoring in ecologically valid settings.

Article.Title: Multi-rank non-negative matrix factorization reveals myeloid-centered co-expression remodeling and prioritizes MMP9 as a candidate therapeutic target in kawasaki disease
Article.Authors: Liu D.; Sun Y.; Huang X.; Liu B.; Li G.; Duan Y.; Song M.
Article.Abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) causes coronary artery aneurysms in up to 25% of untreated children, but its transcriptomic resemblance to common febrile illnesses complicates early diagnosis. Current treatments are not directed at a defined disease mechanism, and 10–20% of patients do not respond to initial intravenous immunoglobulin. Using three GEO whole-blood cohorts covering KD, bacterial and viral infection, Henoch-Schönlein purpura, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, we combined multi-rank non-negative matrix factorization with differential gene correlation analysis to identify hub genes whose co-expression with partner genes differs in KD. KD shared far more differentially expressed genes with bacterial infection (Jaccard index 0.504) than with viral (0.155) or autoimmune (0.017) mimics. Five MCC-ranked hub genes (ITGAM, MMP9, HK3, FCER1G, and CSF3R) were upregulated in KD and showed significant co-expression pairs in KD that were absent in mimics; immune deconvolution hub-gene expression correlated positively with estimated neutrophil fractions and negatively correlated with estimated CD8 + T-cell fractions (HK3: Spearman r = − 0.81). A 5-gene classifier built with TabPFN-V2.5 reached an AUC of 0.889 in external validation. Molecular docking gave S-3304 the most favourable predicted binding energy for MMP9 (− 10.21 kcal/mol), and can used as a candidate drug for the treatment of coronary artery injury and be used in biochemical and preclinical evaluations.

Article.Title: A digital-driven deep learning framework for text–image multimodal machine translation with gated cross-modal fusion
Article.Authors: Li N.
Article.Abstract: Text-only neural machine translation (NMT) models can struggle with lexical, gender, and referential ambiguities when textual cues alone are insufficient. This paper presents a digital-driven deep-learning framework for text–image multimodal machine translation that integrates visual context through gated cross-modal fusion and contrastive text-image alignment. The architecture combines a frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 vision encoder with a trainable linear projection and a pretrained MarianMT text encoder-decoder. An adaptive sample-level scalar gate regulates the contribution of visual information according to cross-modal relevance. On the Multi30K EN–DE Test 2016 benchmark, the proposed framework achieves 40.9 BLEU and 0.867 COMET, improving upon text-only MarianMT by 2.2 BLEU and 0.025 COMET and outperforming the evaluated multimodal baselines across seven translation metrics. Paired bootstrap resampling with 1,000 iterations indicates statistically significant improvements ( \(p < 0.001\) , Cohen’s \(d = 0.72\) , 95% CI [1.2, 3.2]). Analysis of gate activations further examines how visual contribution varies across samples with different linguistic characteristics, without assuming token-level gating. The framework introduces an additional inference latency of 21.7 ms over the text-only baseline and is further evaluated under multiple visual degradation and image-relevance conditions. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive gated fusion for incorporating visual evidence into multimodal machine translation while maintaining computational efficiency.

Article.Title: β12 borophene as a next-generation platform for PFAS adsorption: a DFT investigation
Article.Authors: Alshammari B.; Otaif H.; Aldawsari N.; Mahmoud A.; Ibrahim M.
Article.Abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) have garnered significant attention owing to their extreme persistence, bioaccumulation potential, and harmful effects on both human health and ecosystems. In the current work, the adsorption capability of the β 12 nanosheet toward toxic PFASs, namely PFAS = PFBA, PFBS, PFOA, and PFOS, was systematically investigated, using density functional theory calculations. The β 12 nanosheet exhibited adsorption behavior toward all investigated PFASs, with adsorption strength increasing with PFAS carbon-chain length in the order PFBA < PFBS < PFOA < PFOS, reaching the most negative adsorption energy ( E ads ) of −13.93 kcal/mol for PFOS. Among the investigated configurations, adsorption was generally most favorable in the parallel orientation, followed by the head and tail orientations, as reflected by the corresponding E ads values. Bader charge findings revealed a small net electron transfer between the β 12 nanosheet and the adsorbed PFASs, as evidenced by small negative Q t values. Furthermore, variations in the E LUMO and E HOMO values following adsorption demonstrated that PFAS adsorption induces changes in the electronic structure of the β 12 . The calculated recovery times provided a theoretical indication of the desorption behavior of PFASs from the β 12 nanosheet within the framework of the applied computational model. Implicit solvent calculations were also performed using aqueous solvation, yielding the same trend of stronger adsorption for the long-chain PFASs. As a fundamental adsorption study, the present work provides molecular-level insights into the interactions of PFASs with the β 12 nanosheet, establishing a theoretical basis for further experimental evaluation of its adsorption behavior.

Article.Title: Fault-tolerant multi-leg inverter-fed roadway-powered dynamic wireless power transfer charging system
Article.Authors: Santhakumar C.; Aganti M.; Chokkalingam B.; Twala B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resonant Inductive Power Transfer is an advanced wireless technology offering a practical and safe solution for charging Electric Vehicle batteries, especially in dynamic highway environments. The proposed system integrates a Random Forest Control Algorithm for intelligent switching and fault management, ensuring continuous power delivery even in the event of faults. Each transmitter (Tx) coil is connected to an individual inverter leg configured as a half-bridge circuit, enabling efficient power transfer and precise control. In the case of a leg fault, the FPGA executes a rapid fault detection and redirection algorithm, using changeover switches to reassign the Tx coil to an adjacent healthy leg while isolating the faulty leg. This approach guarantees uninterrupted operation. To enhance safety, protection mechanisms such as fuses and circuit breakers are embedded in each leg. Fault logs, leg configurations, and system parameters are stored in an EEPROM for diagnostics and recovery purposes. Sensors on each Tx coil activate charging when the receiver coil is detected, optimizing energy transfer. The system’s performance is validated through MATLAB simulations, demonstrating its reliability, cost-effectiveness, and practical feasibility. This study focuses on ensuring continuous operation through intelligent fault management, excluding misalignment effects in the analysis.

Article.Title: Explainable federated blockchain framework for privacy preserving medical image analysis in smart healthcare systems
Article.Authors: Murala D.; UM F.; Bagalkot S.; Shaik S.; Mohamud A.
Article.Abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has revolutionized smart healthcare by enabling continuous, distributed patient monitoring and real-time clinical data acquisition. However, the sensitive nature of medical imaging data including CT scans, MRI sequences, and histopathological slides raises critical concerns around data privacy, model transparency, and regulatory compliance. Existing centralized deep learning frameworks for medical image analysis fail to address these multidimensional challenges simultaneously. This paper proposes XFedChain-IoMT, a novel integrated framework that synergistically combines Federated Learning (FL), Blockchain technology, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and edge computing to deliver privacy-preserving, secure, and interpretable medical image analysis across distributed IoMT environments. Our framework introduces a Hierarchical Federated Aggregation Protocol (HFAP) in which edge nodes perform local model training on medical image datasets without raw data leaving the devices. Gradient updates are cryptographically signed and committed to a permissioned blockchain ledger, where a smart-contract-enforced validation gate, Proof-of-Medical-Integrity (PoMI), applies established Byzantine-robust filters (gradient-norm clipping and cosine-directional consistency checks related to Krum and FoolsGold) before global aggregation, making these checks auditable via an immutable on-chain log. A multi-modal XAI layer integrating SHAP, Grad-CAM++, and LIME provides clinician-interpretable saliency maps, attribution scores, and decision explanations at inference time. Experiments on the LIDC-IDRI (lung CT), LiTS (liver tumor), and ISIC-2020 (skin lesion) benchmark datasets demonstrate that XFedChain-IoMT achieves a classification accuracy of 97.3%, an AUC-ROC of 0.984, and an F1-score of 0.971, outperforming state-of-the-art federated and centralized baselines by 3.1–6.8%. The blockchain overhead remains below 2.3% on model convergence time, while the XAI layer adds only 12 ms inference latency. The proposed framework advances trustworthy, privacy-aware AI for We additionally quantify, for the first time in this combination to our knowledge, how differential-privacy noise degrades the fidelity of gradient-based explanations in a federated medical-imaging pipeline, revealing a substantial privacy–interpretability trade-off at the framework’s chosen operating point ( \(\varepsilon = 0.5\) ).

Article.Title: Surrogate-assisted multi-objective structural optimization of a permanent-magnet bridged reluctance actuator
Article.Authors: Sun J.; Xu Y.; Jiang X.; Sun Y.; Zhou H.
Article.Abstract: Structural optimization of permanent-magnet bridged reluctance actuators (PMBRAs) requires costly repeated finite-element analysis (FEA). Multimodal optimization must also preserve structurally distinct designs with comparable objective values. Here, we develop a surrogate-assisted multimodal multi-objective optimization framework combining a deep neural network (DNN) force-per-unit-depth surrogate with SPD-enhanced DN-NSGA-II. A full-factorial dataset of 4096 two-dimensional FEA samples from four structural variables, \(N_c\) , \(N_n\) , \(d_e\) , and g , was used to train a 64-32-16 DNN to predict \(q_F\) in \(\mathrm {kN/m}\) , with actuator thrust calculated as \(F=q_F w_m\) . The surrogate was evaluated using a fixed hold-out test, deterministic five-fold cross-validation, and a 168-point intermediate-grid validation. Over a stack-depth range of 37.6–60.0 mm, the five-fold MAE and RMSE were 10.04–16.03 N and 13.20–21.06 N, while the intermediate-grid errors were 3.95–6.30 N and 5.74–9.17 N. The DNN also outperformed five low-complexity surrogate baselines in MAE and RMSE under both validation protocols. The surrogate was coupled with SPD-DN-NSGA-II, where an FE-adaptive SPD offspring branch improves preservation of multiple Pareto-set branches in decision space. On 22 CEC2019 benchmark problems under equal function-evaluation budgets, significant suite-level differences were observed for rPSP, rHV, IGDX, and IGDF, with the clearest gains in rPSP and IGDX. Applied to the mixed-integer PMBRA problem, the framework revealed trade-offs between thrust density and the copper-loss-based force-to-power ratio while retaining alternative structural solutions under different air-gap and performance constraints.

Article.Title: Sex differences in colorectal cancer incidence and survival vary by age and tumor subsite in a nationwide Korean cohort
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Jang J.; Kang S.; Choi Y.; Choi M.; Cho E.; Park H.; Lee W.; Chung S.; Kim N.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, and sex differences in its incidence and survival have been consistently reported. However, whether these disparities vary according to age, anatomical subsite, and disease stage remains incompletely understood. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using linked Korean cancer registry and mortality data. Among 215,830 individuals aged ≥ 20 years diagnosed with CRC during 2012–2020, directly age-standardized incidence rate ratios (IRRs) comparing males with females were estimated, and overall survival was evaluated using multivariable Cox models. The IRR increased from 1.17 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.14–1.21) at < 50 years to 1.94 (95% CI, 1.92–1.96) at 50–74 years. Male predominance was most pronounced in rectal and left-sided colon cancers, whereas right-sided colon cancer showed modest sex differences. Among individuals aged < 50 years, left-sided colon cancer showed female predominance (IRR, 0.92). Males had poorer overall survival, with the greatest disadvantage at 50–74 years (hazard ratio [HR], 1.34), in localized disease (HR, 1.50), and in rectal cancer (HR, 1.31). These findings indicate age-dependent and anatomically heterogeneous sex differences in CRC incidence and survival and support further investigation of sex- and age-informed prevention, screening, and management strategies.

Article.Title: Toward stable laser weapon systems via vibration control and structural decoupling
Article.Authors: Park S.; Yun J.; Jang H.
Article.Abstract: As defense technologies advance, laser weapon systems (LWSs) are emerging as next-generation armaments. However, structural vibrations—primarily those originating from cooling systems such as pumps, compressors, and condensers—pose a critical challenge that causes jitter at the emission assembly, thus compromising targeting accuracy. In this study, we focus on addressing vibration problems in LWSs. Thus, we analyze the vibration characteristics of our recently constructed LWS and identify its primary vibration sources and dynamic transmission paths through platforms, including floor structures and frames. Subsequently, we propose a three-stage strategy that considers vibration-transmission paths from the sources, through the platform and transport trailer, to the emission assembly, as follows: (1) isolating vibrations at the source, (2) decoupling floor structures to simplify the transmission path through the platform, and (3) applying isolation mounts between the platform and transport trailer. The effectiveness of each stage is examined through numerical simulations and experiments, and the overall performance is then assessed to determine the amount of vibration that reaches the emission assembly. Experimental results show an attenuation of approximately 36 dB along the vibration-transmission path from the vibration source to the trailer in the fully integrated LWS, resulting in a final vibration level within the ultra-low-vibration regime.

Article.Title: Effect of liposomal bupivacaine for intraoperative intercostal nerve block on postoperative atelectasis and regional ventilation synchrony following video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy: a randomised controlled trial
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhou S.; Ke C.; Zhang Y.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Postoperative atelectasis is a common complication after thoracic surgery. Postoperative pain impairs respiratory function and represents a modifiable risk factor for atelectasis. Clinical evidence regarding the analgesic superiority of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) remains inconsistent. Given the subjective nature of pain scores, the incidence of atelectasis and postoperative ventilatory function may better reflect the clinical efficacy of LB.This randomised controlled trial included patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy with intraoperative intercostal nerve block, who were randomised to receive either liposomal bupivacaine or ropivacaine (R). A total of 74 patients were enrolled, all of whom completed the primary endpoint evaluation. The LB group had a lower incidence of atelectasis than the R group at 48 h postoperatively (13.5% vs. 35.1%, RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.15–0.97, P = 0.03). Regional ventilation delay (RVD) at 48 h was lower in the LB group[median (IQR), 2.96 (0.00–5.55) vs. 4.80 (1.52–8.95), P = 0.02]. Additionally, the increase in RVD from baseline to 48 h was smaller in the LB group [2.16 (0.00–4.36) vs. 4.11 (0.89–8.22), P = 0.02], accompanied by a greater reduction in RVD during the 24–48 h postoperative period [− 3.83 (− 13.73–0.00) vs. 0.00 (− 5.33–2.98), P = 0.04]. Global inhomogeneity index (GI) and centre of ventilation (CoV) did not differ between groups across time points. Furthermore, the LB group had significantly lower pain scores for time-weighted sum of pain intensity difference (TW-SPID) 0–72 h and late-phase TW-SPID 48–72 h ( P = 0.014 and P = 0.005, respectively). In patients undergoing thoracoscopic lobectomy, liposomal bupivacaine for intraoperative intercostal nerve block was associated with a lower incidence of early postoperative atelectasis and a lower 48-hour regional ventilation delay, with a potential late analgesic advantage.

Article.Title: The role of PDCD4 in the peripheral T cell immune microenvironment of non-valvular atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Zheng M.; Zhou J.; Yang Y.; Wulasihan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The immune and inflammatory mechanisms underlying non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) are not fully understood. Programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) is a transcriptional and translational inhibitor associated with pro-inflammatory activity and fibrotic remodeling in cardiac tissues. This study assessed the regulatory role of PDCD4 in T lymphocyte responses in the peripheral blood of NVAF patients. We utilized an open single-cell transcriptome dataset containing peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples from patients with drug-related paroxysmal atrial fibrillation during the medication period and the withdrawal period, combined with bioinformatics analysis, to preliminarily explore the role of PDCD4 in inflammatory response, cytokine secretion, and immune regulation. We collected peripheral blood from patients and matched non-AF controls and performed flow cytometry to (1) quantify PDCD4 expression in T-cell subsets, (2) determine the percentage of cytokine-positive PDCD4 + and PDCD4– T cells, and (3) quantify the expression of surface co-stimulatory and co-inhibitory receptors after in vitro stimulation with or without PDCD4-IN-1. T cell vitality was measured using the CCK-8 assay, and cytokine secretion was assessed by ELISA. Single-cell transcriptome analysis revealed that PDCD4 was highly expressed in activated CD8 + T cells from AF group. PDCD4-expressing cells exhibited strong enrichment for T-cell receptor signaling, cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction, and complement activation. Flow cytometry showed that PDCD4 expression was significantly higher in CD4 + T cells, CD8 + T cells, and Treg cells in the NVAF group (all P < 0.001). The secretion of IL-4, IL-17 A, IL-10, and IFN-γ was significantly higher in PDCD4 + T cells than in PDCD4 − T cells ( P < 0.05). PDCD4 inhibition reduced the percentage of CD8 + CD137 + T cells ( P < 0.001), T cell vitality ( P < 0.01), and the secretion of the proinflammatory cytokines IFN-γ and TNF-α ( P < 0.001). PDCD4 affects the immune microenvironment in NVAF by promoting peripheral T cell activation, and inflammatory cytokine secretion.

Article.Title: Scenario-dependent projections of brown planthopper immigration intensity under CMIP6 climate pathways
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Su Y.; Xue Y.; Lu Y.; Bao Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate change reshapes the dynamics of agricultural pests by altering temperature, wind, vertical airflows, precipitation and humidity. Brown planthopper, Nilaparvata lugens (Stål), is among the most destructive migratory pests in Asian rice, and its dynamics are tightly coupled to climate. Clarifying how the different emission pathways affect this pest is essential for forward-looking management. We combined 2001–2023 light-trap records from 11 Chinese stations with the Norwegian Earth System Model version 2 low-resolution configuration (NorESM2-LM) from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Lower-tropospheric temperature showed the strongest marginal associations at most representative stations. Random forest (RF), k-nearest neighbors (KNN) and linear regression (LR) were compared using temporally ordered development and independent 2019–2023 validation. Source qualification retained 8,428 station-pentads. Development annual-log RMSE averaged 0.744 for LR, 0.758 for KNN and 0.807 for RF; RF300 remained the projection reference. Across 42 independent station-years, exact-grade accuracy was 92.9%, matching an always-Grade-1 baseline. Mann–Kendall tests with false-discovery-rate control identified nine significant station–scenario trends, six retained after trend-free pre-whitening; none was significant under SSP1-2.6. Projections from all 11 stations showed marked spatial heterogeneity rather than uniform northward expansion. These conditional projections support climate-adaptive monitoring.

Article.Title: A geometry-tunable MWIR multispectral plasmonic filter based on a Dy-doped cadmium oxide bull’s-eye structure
Article.Authors: Razavinia S.; Karami M.; Vaez-Zadeh M.
Article.Abstract: We propose a compact bull’s-eye plasmonic filter based on Dy-doped cadmium oxide (Dy: CdO), an ENZ-capable transparent conducting oxide with low optical losses in the mid-wave infrared (MWIR). The design combines the plasmonic response of Dy: CdO beyond its ENZ wavelength with extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) enabled by the concentric bull’s-eye geometry. Two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations performed at a carrier concentration of 3.7 × 10²⁰ cm⁻³ demonstrate that systematic tuning of the corrugation period enables geometry-controlled multispectral resonances covering the 3–5 μm MWIR atmospheric window. To further tailor the spectral response, a SiO₂ dielectric encapsulation is incorporated to modify the local dielectric environment, while the geometrical parameters are systematically optimized to enhance resonant transmission and spectral selectivity. The encapsulated structure achieves a maximum transmission of 58% with a minimum FWHM of 400 nm, while increasing the average peak transmittance from approximately 45% to 50% and the average quality factor from 7.85 to about 9 (≈ 15%) compared with the unencapsulated design. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the proposed Dy: CdO bull’s-eye architecture outperforms its conventional Au-based counterpart in terms of transmission efficiency and spectral selectivity, providing a promising low-loss platform for compact MWIR multispectral filters. The proposed design offers significant potential applications in MWIR multispectral imaging and infrared spectroscopy.

Article.Title: Layer-specific effects of an ultra-speed sintering protocol on translucency and microstructure of yttria-gradient zirconia
Article.Authors: Shin H.; Cho M.; Seol H.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the effects of an experimental ultra-speed (US) sintering protocol on the translucency and microstructure of yttria-gradient zirconia. Eighty specimens were prepared from two laboratory yttria-gradient zirconias (5 mol% yttria-stabilized incisal and 4 mol% yttria-stabilized cervical layers). Each layer underwent conventional (CS) or experimental US sintering. Translucency ( TP 00 ) was measured spectrophotometrically ( n = 10/group). Microstructure, grain size, and phase composition were analyzed using field-emission scanning electron microscopy ( n = 4/group) and Rietveld refinement ( n = 2/group). Translucency was analyzed using three-way ANOVA, and grain size using a generalized linear model (α = 0.05). Under CS, the incisal layer ( TP 00 : 8.01–8.12) was more translucent than the cervical layer (7.27–7.45), whereas this relationship was reversed after US, with the incisal layer ( TP 00 : 5.12–5.23) being less translucent than the cervical layer (7.52–7.79). This reversal reflected a significant reduction in TP 00 in the incisal layer (Δ TP 00 : 2.78–3.00), exceeding the translucency acceptability threshold for Δ TP 00 , while cervical changes remained within the translucency perceptibility threshold for Δ TP 00 . Residual pores were more evident in the incisal layer after US sintering, with grain size increasing from 1.11 to 1.13 to 2.95–2.97 μm. After US sintering, the yttria-rich t’ -phase fraction was higher, whereas the t -phase fraction was lower under US than under CS in both layers. These findings provide further insight into the potential layer-specific response of yttria-gradient zirconias to US sintering protocol.

Article.Title: Recorded campus running is associated with temperature and background air pollution at two Beijing campuses
Article.Authors: Peng J.; Zhang X.; Chang Z.; Feng B.; Fan Z.; Dai S.
Article.Abstract: In this retrospective observational study, we examined associations of background temperature and PM2.5 with campus running under semester distance requirements. We linked 651,606 quality-screened runs by 19,255 students at two Beijing campuses across six semesters, 2023–2025 to hourly environmental data; timing analyses used daily means. Joint nonlinear models included student-by-campus fixed effects and weather and calendar covariates, with two-way clustering by student and date. Compared with 15 °C, time per kilometer was 1.28% longer at 5 °C (95% confidence interval 0.97–1.59%; approximately 4.8 s/km at the observed median pace) and 1.05% shorter at 25 °C (0.72–1.38%). The global temperature–pace test remained significant after Holm adjustment, whereas the primary PM2.5–pace test was inconclusive (Holm P = 0.140). Distance was 3.60% shorter at 5 °C than at 15 °C (2.83–4.36%). Among 636,181 observed student-campus-days, the proportion of first starts in the evening (≥ 18:00) was 6.87% points lower at 5 °C than at 15 °C (4.62–9.12 lower). Daily PM2.5 of 75 versus 25 µg/m³ was associated with a 2.23-percentage-point lower evening proportion (0.61–3.85 lower). Both global timing tests remained significant after exploratory adjustment. Analyses of common samples examined alternative environmental assignments and timing definitions. These modest associations describe recorded campus activity, and their magnitude varied with model adjustment.

Article.Title: Identity leadership in sport predicts healthy adolescent functioning across 11 countries
Article.Authors: Butalia R.; Boen F.; van Dick R.; Cruwys T.; Haslam S.; Steffens N.; Arvaja M.; Bespomoshchnov V.; Biśta Z.; Bruner M.; Damentka K.; Darpatova-Hruzewicz D.; de Cruz N.; Dhillon M.; Dipaola G.; Ghorbani A.; Gokduman Ç.; Healy L.; Hirokazu M.; Inagaki K.; Inoue Y.; P. Johnston J.; Kartal M.; Leo F.; López-Gajardo M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adolescence is marked by identity disruption, which can challenge young people’s mental and social health. Team sport provides a context in which adolescents navigate these challenges, yet sport environments can involve bullying and social exclusion. The quality of these environments is therefore likely to depend on how leaders shape them – particularly identity leaders, who represent, advance, create, and embed a shared sense of identity among those they lead. Using data from 3,540 athletes ( N = 395 teams) across 11 countries, this study examined whether coaches’ and peer leaders’ identity leadership supports adolescents’ healthy functioning (well-being and team commitment) by strengthening team identification. The results showed that identity leadership predicted stronger team identification, which in turn predicted higher well-being and greater team commitment. This effect was consistent across countries, genders (boys and girls), and age groups (12–17 years). Study findings suggest that identity leadership in sport may support healthy adolescent development.

Genotype interaction x harvest time had a significant effect on all the traits. The highest number of leaves per plant was recorded in G 4 H 1 , while the longest vines were recorded in G 6 H 6 , as in G 7 H 6 . Leaf area was the maximum in G 7 H 3 and was comparable to G 7 H 4 , G 5 H 6 , G 7 H 6 , and G 7 H 5 . In the physiological aspect, the nitrogen balance index was the highest in G 2 H 2 , the flavonoid index was the highest in G 3 H 5 , and the chlorophyll and anthocyanin indices were the highest in G 7 H 6 . The highest tuberous root weight and total yield were recorded from G 5 H 6 , followed by G 4 H 6 with the highest harvest index. The highest tuberous roots per plant, root length, root diameter, dry matter content, and total soluble solids content were recorded in G 1 H 4 , G 4 H 3 , G 5 H 6 , G 3 H 4 , and G 2 H 4 , respectively. Correlation and multivariate analyses revealed significant associations among morpho-physiological, yield and quality-related traits of sweet potato. Article.Title: Recolorized financial time series imaging: a multi-dimensional analysis of MTF, GAF, and recurrence plots for imbalanced stock trend classification
Article.Authors: Pandey V.; Ahmed T.; Sahoo G.; Bharti A.; Sayeed M.
Article.Abstract: Stock price prediction is a difficult task. The work proposed in this article takes on this issue and proposes a recolorized image encoding approach to classify the directional trend in a stock’s price. To this end, raw prices are complemented via technical and statistical features and projected by UMAP into a compact five dimensional space. This is then converted into three different image sets: 1) the Gramian Angular Field; 2) Markov Transition Field; 3) Recurrence Plot. We experiment with these methods to compare which method produces the best performance while preserving the temporal structure of the markets. For each image, the values are then recolorized, and a pretrained vision transformer is used to extract spatial features. Subsequently to classify the images, we use four layer bidirectional LSTM to model how these features evolve across time. In this paper, and for our experiments, we have also used SMOTE to correct the dominance of one particular class in the dataset. Finally, we experiment with seven downstream classifiers. Experimentation is performed on twenty companies of the National stock exchange spanning seven sectors. We have found that recolorized RP generalizes best at sector level. To be specific, sector wise number for accuracy is 0.7708 for RP, MTF at 0.7702 and GAF at 0.7535. Furthermore, without sector consideration, the numbers stand at: 0.7626 for RP, 0.7645 for MTF, 0.7410 for GAF. Lastly using statistical testing, we have found that the overall performance for RP and MTF is near identical (0.7626 vs. 0.7645; Cohen’s d = −0.0184), at the same time, both outperform GAF in rank based comparison (0.7410; Cohen’s d = −0.8028). These differences are confirmed by the Friedman test (p = 0.0211). Lastly, through the work presented in this article, we also try to show that the choice of recolorization, rather than the choice of classifier, could serve as a new benchmark for visual-temporal stock trend classification.

IV-treated glaucomatous eyes showed significantly lower IOP: G-evs–Brimonidine and G-Ms–Latanoprost vs. healthy eyes, and higher ERG b-wave amplitudes (both p < 0.001). All glaucomatous eyes exhibited dioptric power loss vs. healthy. G-evs–Brimonidine stabilized refraction and preserved RGC layer thickness (both p < 0.05). Conversely, G-Ms–Latanoprost caused greater myopization ( p = 0.011) but increased central retinal volume ( p < 0.001) and pRNFL thickness, exceeding even healthy eyes ( p = 0.001). A single IV brimonidine injection stabilized refraction and preserved RGC integrity, whereas repeated IV latanoprost injections induced myopization while enhancing central retinal and pRNFL thickness. Article.Authors: Duse D.; Haurand J.; Alde K.; Ophoff N.; Marjani K.; Georgy J.; Okkasian M.; Helten C.; Mourikis P.; Angendohr S.; Masyuk M.; Nienhaus F.; Kahle A.; Zaharia O.; Erkens R.; Bönner F.; Wischmann P.; Cramer M.; Gerdes N.; Meyer C.; Wagner R.; Roden M.; Polzin A.; Jung C.; Kelm M.

Among 833 SYSTEMI patients (74% male; mean age 64 years), 24.5% presented with cardiogenic shock and 23.4% with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Within SYSTEMI, CKD, admission CRP, and admission glucose were associated with in-hospital mortality after multivariable adjustment.

Article.Title: Interpretable neuro-affective language understanding for psychological and psychometric assessment towards clinical-support applications
Article.Authors: Faria D.
Article.Abstract: Human language conveys interacting semantic, affective, behavioral, psychological and risk-related information that is commonly modeled through isolated natural-language-processing tasks. This paper presents NALU (Neuro-Affective Language Understanding), an interpretable multi-task language-representation framework designed to jointly model multiple complementary dimensions of psychologically relevant language. The framework combines a shared Transformer encoder with specialized prediction heads, element-level supervision masks, validation-based threshold calibration and an auditable deterministic interpretation layer. The study was developed in two experimental stages. The initial configuration used 205,109 samples and eight specialized prediction heads comprising exactly 45 scalar outputs. The framework was then extended and evaluated on an audited corpus containing 589,155 unique samples, including 395,417 Brazilian-Portuguese and 193,738 English records. The expanded multilingual configuration uses XLM-RoBERTa and twelve specialized heads covering sentiment, emotion, valence–arousal–dominance, psychological constructs, behavior, mental-health risk, neurodevelopmental-language indicators, psychiatric-language indicators, addiction/eating/cognition-related language, electronic-risk indicators, psychometric items and psychometric scores. For the initial eight-head configuration, the calibrated model achieved a composite test score of 0.761 with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of [0.754, 0.767]. Macro-F1 reached 0.874 for psychological constructs, 0.783 for mental-health risk and 0.769 for clinical-language markers. Validation-tuned thresholds significantly improved emotion, psychological, behavioral, clinical and overall composite performance relative to a fixed 0.5 threshold ( p < 0.001), whereas the improvement for the risk head was positive but not statistically significant ( p = 0.096). The expanded 589,155-sample XLM-R configuration achieved a sentiment Macro-F1 of 0.7912 and emotion Macro-F1 of 0.6858. Threshold-free discrimination was high for several multi-label heads, with AUROC values of 0.9659 for emotion, 0.9838 for psychological constructs, 0.9694 for behavior, 0.9810 for mental-health risk, 0.9899 for psychiatric-language indicators and 0.9963 for addiction/eating/cognition-related language. Continuous prediction errors were MAE = 0.1009 for valence–arousal–dominance, MAE = 0.0109 for psychometric items and MAE=0.0280 for psychometric scores. Outcomes without sufficient positive held-out support are explicitly reported as not estimable rather than interpreted as validated zero performance. NALU is not presented as a diagnostic instrument. Psychometric outputs are interpreted as questionnaire-associated or language-derived latent estimates, and clinical-support outputs are intended for screening-oriented research and human-in-the-loop analysis.

Article.Title: Personality traits and their associations with psychological symptoms in patients with non-functioning pituitary neuroendocrine tumor
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Jung W.; Han Y.; Lee B.; Kong D.
Article.Abstract: Although personality traits influence emotional responses and illness adaptation, data regarding untreated patients with non-functioning pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (NF-PitNET) remain limited. This study investigated personality traits in NF-PitNET patients and examined their associations with anxiety, depression, and social interaction anxiety. This cross-sectional study included 48 pre-surgical NF-PitNET patients recruited between June and November 2025, and 48 healthy controls (HC) frequency-matched for age, gender, and education. Personality traits were assessed using the 50-item International Personality Item Pool. Psychological symptoms were measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, alongside shortened Korean versions of the Social Interaction Anxiety and Social Phobia Scales. Patients with NF-PitNET exhibited significantly higher levels of neuroticism, anxiety, and depression than HC; however, no significant group differences were found in other traits or social interaction anxiety. Among patients, extraversion correlated positively with longer post-diagnosis follow-up duration, and female patients showed higher agreeableness and neuroticism than males. Notably, higher neuroticism was positively associated with greater anxiety. NF-PitNET patients demonstrate elevated neuroticism, anxiety, and depression, with neuroticism being specifically associated with anxiety. Personality assessments may help identify patients who may benefit from individualized psychosocial support.

Article.Title: Petrogenesis, tectonomagmatic and remote sensing investigations on Um Rus gabbroic intrusion, Central Eastern Desert, Egypt
Article.Authors: Salem I.; Abd El-Wahed M.; Atef M.; Thabet I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated remote sensing, structural, and geochemical study of the Um Rus gabbroic intrusion, Eastern Desert, Egyptian Nubian Shield. The study is based on multispectral satellite data (Landsat 9 OLI, ASTER), field, petrographic, and geochemical analyses to decipher the petrogenesis and tectonomagmatic evolution of the intrusion and mineralization potential. Remote sensing techniques like FCC, PCA, MNF, Band Ratios and CEM has provided detailed lithological mapping and delineation of the hydrothermal alteration zones. There is a strong spatial relationship between the alteration halos, high lineament density, and alteration zones, especially along structural corridors controlled by the Wadi Mubarak shear belt and Najd Fault System. Geochemical and mineral chemistry data indicate that the Um Rus gabbros are late Neoproterozoic calc-alkaline to tholeiitic bodies derived from subduction modified mantle sources and emplaced in an active continental margin setting. Petrographic studies revealed six dominant rock types, with evidence of magmatic differentiation and a cumulate origin. Structural analysis indicates that the localization of magmatism and mineralization is controlled by thrust and strike-slip faulting. The integration of these multidisciplinary datasets brings new insights on the multiphase magmatic evolution, the tectonic setting and the mineral potential of the arc-related complexes in the Arabian-Nubian Shield. The study highlights the significance of integrating remote sensing data with geochemical and structural methods in mineral exploration and in better understanding the tectonomagmatic evolution of the Egyptian Nubian Shield.

Article.Title: Adaptive traffic signal control model for a single isolated intersection using deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Naeem D.; Abohashima H.; Eltawil A.; Gheith M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traffic congestion has major social, environmental, and economic consequences, and adaptive traffic signal control is one approach for improving intersection performance under changing demand. This study presents a reinforcement-learning-based controller for a single isolated intersection and compares its performance with a firefly-based heuristic. The main contribution is a normalized composite reward that combines queue length and vehicle waiting time. These measures are correlated, but they describe different operational aspects of intersection performance: queue length reflects spatial occupancy and potential spillback, whereas waiting time reflects the temporal delay experienced by vehicles. A weighting parameter (β) is used to vary the relative emphasis assigned to the two measures. The proposed reward was compared with queue-only and waiting-time-only rewards under the tested simulation conditions. The results indicate that the composite reward can provide a tunable compromise between the two measures, although it does not consistently outperform the single-metric rewards for every performance indicator and traffic-demand level.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based image classification and estimation of hazelnuts with potential implications for marketing efficiency and producer income
Article.Authors: Kadirhanoğulları İ.; Gülsoy E.; Gülbe A.; Kuş E.
Article.Abstract: Hazelnut classification and quality assessment are critical stages of post-harvest management that directly influence product quality, market value, and commercialization. Conventional grading methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and highly dependent on expert evaluation, limiting their efficiency and consistency in large-scale applications. This study aimed to develop an image-based artificial intelligence framework for automated hazelnut variety classification and weight estimation to improve post-harvest management, marketing efficiency, and producer income. A dataset comprising 700 images of five commercially important hazelnut varieties (Çakıldak, Koca Kulak, Palaz, Yağlı, and Yomra) was acquired under controlled imaging conditions. Due to their superior performance, the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model was selected for hazelnut variety classification, while the Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model was preferred for weight estimation. The dataset was divided into three subsets: 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing. The ANN model achieved 100% classification accuracy, while the GPR model achieved an R 2 value of 0.72. These findings suggest that image-based machine learning approaches may offer reliable and efficient solutions for automated hazelnut characterization. The proposed framework has the potential to reduce labor requirements, minimize subjective grading errors, and support quality-based classification and pricing. It may also facilitate weight estimation for logistics and inventory management and potentially contribute to improved producer profitability through more efficient resource allocation. The proposed system may support the digital transformation of agricultural production and post-harvest operations by providing a potentially practical and scalable approach for precision agriculture. In the longer term, such applications could contribute to value chain optimization, sustainable agricultural economics, improved marketing efficiency, and enhanced competitiveness in domestic and international hazelnut markets. However, these potential benefits require further validation under commercial and large-scale field conditions.

Article.Title: Worker-independent multimodal physiological fatigue detection in industrial workers using a domain adaptation network with multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy
Article.Authors: Paul S.; Verma R.
Article.Abstract: Occupational fatigue is a critical safety concern in industrial environments, where substantial inter-worker variability in physiological responses can limit the generalization of conventional fatigue-detection models. This study presents a Domain Adaptation Network (DAN) with Multi-Scale Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) for worker-independent multimodal fatigue classification using physiological and environmental measurements collected from 50 industrial workers during occupational activities. The framework integrates convolutional neural network-based feature extraction, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) temporal modeling, multi-head self-attention over the temporal sequence, Gradient Reversal Layer (GRL)-based adversarial learning, and Multi-Scale MMD-based domain alignment to learn representations that are more robust to inter-worker variability. A total of 60,000 windowed instances were generated from the synchronized multimodal recordings, using an 85-feature multimodal representation, and fatigue was classified into Low, Moderate, and High categories. A strictly worker-independent evaluation protocol was adopted, with previously unseen workers reserved for testing. Five models were comparatively evaluated: LightGBM, CNN, CNN+BiLSTM, CNN+BiLSTM+Attention, and the proposed DAN, achieving test accuracies of 84.81%, 87.96%, 96.72%, 96.35%, and 97.08%, respectively. The proposed DAN achieved the highest accuracy by combining temporal multimodal representation learning with adversarial and distribution-alignment mechanisms to address inter-worker variability. SHAP and LIME analyses were further employed to provide complementary global and local interpretability of the proposed model’s predictions. Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of multimodal temporal representation learning combined with domain adaptation for robust and interpretable worker-independent fatigue assessment in industrial environments.

Article.Title: Study on water–heat dynamics and structural characteristics of soil undergoing freeze–thaw cycles in typical cultivated areas of Heilongjiang Province, China
Article.Authors: Kong F.; Zhang Z.; Li T.; Fu Q.; Zhou L.; Zheng M.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: In order to explore the water, heat, and structural characteristics of soil undergoing freeze–thaw cycles in typical cultivated areas of Heilongjiang Province, paddy and dryland soils from six representative stations in the Sanjiang Plain and Songnen Plain were studied. Soil temperature, water content, soil moisture characteristic curve, total porosity, and water-stable aggregates were measured. The results showed that the temperature change in the surface soil was the most severe, and it gradually weakened with an increase in soil depth. The temperature change pattern of the paddy field soil was basically consistent with that of the dry field soil. During the freeze–thaw period, the soil temperature in paddy fields was lower than in dry fields, while during the crop growth period, the soil temperature in the paddy fields was higher than that in the dry fields. Overall, the soil water content gradually increases from the surface to the bottom layer. The soil moisture characteristic curves of each representative station show similar trends in each suction stage. The soil moisture characteristic curve of the Sanjiang Plain shows less water loss in the low suction stage, while the high suction stage has more water loss. The soil moisture characteristic curve of the Songnen Plain shows more water loss in the low suction stage than in the Sanjiang Plain. In the low suction stage, the water loss of paddy soil is similar to that of dry field soil, while in the high suction stage, the water loss is greater than that of dry field soil. Therefore, the water storage capacity of dry field soil is better. The total porosity of soil gradually decreases with an increase in soil depth, and the total porosity of paddy field soil is greater than that of dry field soil. The proportion of soil water stable aggregates with a particle size of less than 0.053 mm is the highest, and there is no significant difference in the distribution of different particle sizes between soil layers. The stability of paddy soil at the same depth is better than that of dry soil. The structural condition of the surface soil is better than that of the bottom layer, the soil structural condition in the Songnen Plain is better than that in the Sanjiang Plain, and the soil structural condition in paddy fields is better than that in dry fields with non-significant overall differences. Tillage regimes and regional variations synergistically modulate the hydrothermal dynamics and structural traits of farmland soils across freeze–thaw cycles in cold regions. This research will provide theoretical support for the optimal exploitation and sustainable management of soil resources in these agroecosystems.

Article.Title: Dosage, exposure timing and immune cell status affects immunomodulatory properties of platelet-rich plasma in knee osteoarthritis in vitro
Article.Authors: Sengprasert P.; Hengtrakool P.; Leearamwat N.; Pimthanom S.; Ngarmukos S.; Tanavalee A.; Reantragoon R.
Article.Abstract: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is an alternative treatment for knee osteoarthritis (OA) patients. However, studies have shown controversial results from using this blood-derived product. This may be due to the lack of in-depth understanding of the molecular mechanisms of PRP. Immunologically, PRP normally reduces inflammation, but have been shown to increase inflammation in high doses. Therefore, in our study, we evaluated the effects of PRP on monocytes and T cells, predominant immune cells in synovial fluid of knee joints exposed to PRP. Using a direct in vitro assessment approach, we tested on various conditions of PRP usage by evaluating PRP dosage, timing of PRP exposure, immune cell subpopulation phenotype after PRP exposure and the state of immune cells prior to exposure to PRP. We show that PRP effects immune cells differently depending on the parameter evaluated. Our results demonstrate in vitro conditions that affect outcome of PRP exposure, in which knee OA patients may benefit from optimizing PRP treatment conditions as well as precautions and limitations of PRP usage.

Article.Title: A novel two-parameter fractal-fractional model for crimean-congo hemorrhagic fever: stability analysis, optimal control, and data calibration
Article.Authors: Alyobi S.; Shafee A.; Zahir A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is a severe tick-borne zoonosis with a high case-fatality rate, an expanding geographic range and no licensed vaccine. We develop an eight-compartment tick–host–human model with an exposed (incubating) human class and formulate it with a Caputo-type, power-law fractal-fractional operator. In this operator the fractional order $$\alpha$$ encodes hereditary memory, and the fractal dimension $$\vartheta$$ acts as a power-law “fractal clock” that rescales all process rates. We give corrected definitions of the operator and its inverse, show how they relate to the Caputo, Atangana–Baleanu and Hausdorff operators, and identify the admissible domain $$\alpha +\vartheta>1$$ . A reference time makes the formulation dimensionally consistent. Using an extremum principle for the Caputo derivative, we prove positivity, invariance and boundedness directly in fractional form, and we prove global existence and uniqueness of solutions. We classify all equilibria and prove global stability of the endemic equilibrium with Volterra-type Lyapunov functions for every value of the human-to-human reproduction number. The bifurcation analysis identifies a forward transcritical bifurcation at $${\mathcal {R}}_{l0}=1$$ , an imperfect bifurcation of the human threshold caused by spillover, damped multi-year oscillations, and flip and Neimark–Sacker bifurcations of the discretised system. The model is calibrated to the 2017–2024 series of confirmed cases in Türkiye ( $$R^2=0.93$$ , MAPE $$6.6\%$$ , RMSE 93 cases). The estimated host-cycle reproduction number is $${\mathcal {R}}_{l0}=1.12$$ (95% CI 1.02–1.21), and the result is robust to the fractional orders, to the zoonotic route shares and to the choice of incidence function. Global sensitivity analysis (LHS–PRCC, Sobol) identifies the host-cycle parameters and tick mortality as the main drivers of human incidence. An optimal control problem with a derived fractional adjoint system shows that combined tick control and treatment would have averted about $$42\%$$ of cases and $$59\%$$ of deaths over 2017–2024. Tick control is the most cost-effective way to prevent infections, and treatment is the main lever for preventing deaths.

Article.Title: Food insecurity is associated with increased food environment interactions and lower dietary adequacy among peri-urban Tanzanian households
Article.Authors: Ambikapathi R.; Verissimo C.; Kariathi V.; O’Malley S.; Mangara A.; Mosha D.; Patil C.; Shively G.; Wiegel J.; Gunaratna N.; Kennedy G.; Leyna G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Africa is disproportionately burdened by food insecurity and HIV, yet few tools examine how food environments influence diets. Understanding urban food acquisition patterns is essential for designing targeted interventions, particularly in rapidly urbanizing East Africa. This observational study (2019–2020) examined associations between food insecurity, household food purchases, and dietary adequacy among 312 adults living with HIV in peri-urban Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Using an adapted 49-item food purchase tool, we conducted seven-day food purchase assessments and validated findings against 24-hour dietary recalls and micronutrient adequacy. Food environment interactions were defined as the frequency and diversity of purchases from formal, semi-formal, and informal vendors. Food-insecure households purchased more frequently than food-secure ones, and top purchases across households were tomatoes (62%), sugar (57%), beans (52%), carrots (50%), rice (48%), and maize flour (44%). Formal vendors dominated staples, while semi-formal and informal vendors provided the nutrient-dense foods. Meat purchase diversity predicted better zinc (OR: 1.2, P < 0.039) and vitamin A adequacy (OR: 1.2, P < 0.023). Latent class analysis identified three purchasing groups with differential associations with micronutrient adequacy. Findings highlight food-insecure households’ reliance on informal vendors and the need to preserve access to these critical sources.

Article.Title: Fano resonances in plasmonic gold gratings within a coupled-oscillator and diffraction framework
Article.Authors: Hashemi M.; Naderi N.; Ansari N.
Article.Abstract: Plasmonic gold gratings supporting Fano resonances are promising candidates for sensing, filtering, and surface-enhanced spectroscopy, yet the lack of a rigorous analytical framework connecting their coupled-oscillator description to grating diffraction physics has made it difficult to design structures tailored to specific applications. Here, we establish this connection for gold gratings on a silica substrate under transverse magnetic illumination, and derive analytical relations between the Fano asymmetry parameter and the oscillator parameters, which we use to interpret the geometry dependence of the line shape. We develop a two-oscillator model in which the continuum mode is driven directly by the external field and the discrete mode is excited through coupling, and show analytically that the Fano resonance emerges near the natural frequency of the discrete oscillator due to its \(\pi \) phase transition, while the overall spectral envelope follows the continuum oscillator. Intermediate values of oscillator damping produce asymmetric Fano profiles, with the asymmetry type (dip–peak or peak–dip) governed by the coupling strength: for real coupling a dip–peak profile arises when the discrete oscillator frequency exceeds that of the continuum, while for imaginary coupling the condition is reversed. Applying this framework to gold gratings, we identify the propagating zero-order diffraction as the continuum channel and evanescent higher diffraction orders beyond the Rayleigh wavelength as the discrete resonance, which appears as surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) localized predominantly at the metal–substrate interface. Momentum matching and the phase of \(H_z\) are consistent with an SPP at this interface: the phase difference between the fields at the Fano dip and peak is nearly uniform along the interface and close to \(\pi /2\) , whereas on the air side it is not. Parametric sweeps show that the ribbon width changes the resonance type (antiresonance, asymmetric Fano or Lorentzian), while the grating period and ribbon height tune the spectral position, quality factor and contrast. Fits of the simulated spectra show that the discrete-mode damping is finite, so that the Fano minima are finite. These qualitative trends provide guidelines for Fano-based plasmonic sensors, narrowband filters and surface-enhanced spectroscopy substrates.

Article.Title: Detecting dark web mirror sites on the ClearNET using encrypted traffic classification
Article.Authors: Jeon J.; Ryu S.; Ha J.; Han J.; Han M.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: Dark Web Mirror sites accessible through ordinary browsers may expose users to phishing attacks, malicious content, and illicit material while falling outside the scope of monitoring approaches focused on Tor traffic. We investigated whether such access could be identified at the session level using packet-direction information alone. We collected 4,600 sessions from 23 Clear Web Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) and 23 Dark Web Mirror site URLs, with 100 repeated 20-second visits to each URL. Traffic retained after Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), Transport Layer Security (TLS), and Quick UDP Internet Connections (QUIC) filtering was represented as fixed-length sequences of client-to-server, server-to-client, and padding symbols, excluding payloads, network addresses, page content, packet sizes, and timing from the model input. We evaluated observation windows, median-derived sequence lengths, removal of the initial 20-packet segment, sequence-length reduction, and ten sequence classifiers. Under session-level stratified 5-fold evaluation with a sequence length of 526 selected from the 3-second observation window, the baseline receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) was \(0.9847 \pm 0.0016\) . Under session-level stratified 5-fold evaluation with an input length of 526 including the initial 20 packets, one-dimensional Residual Network (ResNet1D) achieved an accuracy of \(0.9260 \pm 0.0057\) , an F1 score of \(0.9264 \pm 0.0055\) , and a ROC-AUC of \(0.9813 \pm 0.0016\) . These values are the means and sample standard deviations across the five final seeds, and the mean total processing time was 7.6808 ms. In the additional registrable-domain-disjoint Group-aware 5-fold evaluation, ResNet1D achieved a ROC-AUC of \(0.9431 \pm 0.0069\) . Interpretation of this result is restricted to domain-disjoint evaluation within the existing dataset. These results support the feasibility of early session-level detection of access to Dark Web Mirror sites in ordinary browser environments.

Article.Title: Variable elephant population trends lead to a mosaic of change across the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Conservation Area
Article.Authors: Guldemond R.; Ferreira S.; Ernst Y.; Henley M.; Balfour D.; Clegg B.; Engelen C.; von Dürckheim K.; Fletcher R.; Giddey B.; Mandinyenya B.; Manhiça E.; McCleery R.; Ntumi C.; O’Connor T.; Peel M.; Swanepoel B.; Coetzee B.
Article.Abstract: A challenge for conservation is understanding population dynamics when wildlife is shared across international borders among multiple institutions and when monitoring happens at different times. This is the case with African savanna elephants ( Loxodonta africana ) in the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Conservation Area (GLTFCA). The GLTFCA comprises 19 protected areas and 21 subpopulations across Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and South Africa. We sought to determine whether these subpopulations can regulate their numbers without management interventions. We collated and modelled a 30-year time series for each by fitting growth models and evaluating trends in density-dependent effects. Over this time period, we found that 20 subpopulations increased in size. For eight of them, the exponential model received the most support, whereas the density-dependent Ricker and theta-logistic models described the trends for two and nine subpopulations, respectively, and two had insufficient data for this assessment. Regressing annual growth on population size favoured a density-dependent model for five time series and a density-independent model for nine; six comparisons were indeterminate, and one lacked a complete model comparison. Our regional synthesis estimated that there were 64,051 elephants (95% CL: 58,532–70,040) in the GLTFCA in 2024. The elephant population is increasing, although not uniformly across space, with dispersal opportunities restored and resource availability and risks likely shaping population regulation.

Article.Title: Satellite-assisted wildfire propagation under environmental uncertainty: Huygens-based front evolution
Article.Authors: Dehkordi H.; Kumar A.
Article.Abstract: Wildfire propagation results from the complex interaction of fuel characteristics, atmospheric and environmental conditions, and terrain topography. This work proposes a satellite-assisted wildfire propagation model that integrates remote sensing observations with a front-propagation approach based on Huygens’ principle. The model combines thermal data, vegetation indices, and meteorological information to estimate directional rates of spread and generate evolving wildfire perimeters. The proposed framework is based on generalized directional wave fronts, which extend elliptical wildfire wave fronts by incorporating an additional geometric drift parameter. Satellite products provide key environmental variables, such as wind conditions and live fuel moisture content, from which head fire and backing fire spread rates are estimated. Successive applications of Huygens’ principle then generate anisotropic and spatially heterogeneous fire propagation, allowing the reconstruction of evolving fire fronts. Position-dependent propagation parameters naturally account for heterogeneous fuels, non-burnable barriers, and locally varying environmental conditions. Two examples based on measured environmental settings are used to illustrate the proposed methodology. The first considers wildfire spread initialized from satellite-derived fire perimeters under different environmental configurations, while the second uses satellite-derived fire images to illustrate the approach in a realistic wildfire-inspired setting. Both examples are a methodological proof of concept conditioned on measured environmental inputs; no quantitative validation against observed perimeters is claimed. Together, these examples highlight the flexibility of the framework for modeling spatially heterogeneous and anisotropic wildfire propagation, including directional elongation, asymmetric expansion, localized deformation, and complex fire front evolution under varying environmental conditions.

Article.Title: Impaired skin microvascular function and prevalent coronary atherosclerosis and cardiac function in a general population
Article.Authors: Bergstrand S.; Jonasson H.; Festin K.; Kylhammar D.; Strömberg T.; Östgren C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the association between skin microvascular function, coronary atherosclerosis and left ventricular dysfunction in a general population. The study included 3,809 individuals aged 50–65, derived from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS). Skin microvascular function was assessed using combined laser Doppler flowmetry and white light diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. Coronary artery calcium score (CACS) was assessed by non-contrast enhanced cardiac computed tomography and coronary artery plaques were assessed by coronary computed tomography angiography. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography. Individuals with coronary calcification (CACS > 0) were more likely to have lower peak oxygen saturation (OxyP) levels than those without coronary calcification (odds ratio (OR) 0.95, p < 0.001, 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.94–0.96​). Similar findings were observed when individuals with moderate to severe coronary calcification (CACS ≥ 100) were compared to those with lower levels of calcification after adjustment for age, sex, current smoking, body mass index (BMI), and hsCRP. Individuals with plaque in four 4 or more coronary segments, were more likely to have lower OxyP levels than individuals with plaque in fewer segments, (OR: 0.98, p = 0.035, CI: 0.95–1.00). Individuals with an elevated E/e’ ratio was also more likely to have lower OxyP levels than those with a normal E/e’ ratio (OR: 0.97, p = 0.003, CI: 0.95–0.99) after adjustment for age, sex and current smoking. However, these associations were no longer statistically significant when BMI and hsCRP was added to the model. In a middle-aged population-based setting, impaired skin microvascular function was associated with the presence of coronary atherosclerosis and cardiac dysfunction. Assessment of skin microvascular function could be a non-invasive, easily accessible indicator of cardiovascular organ damage.

Article.Title: Seasonal reorganization of marine metazoan communities in the Yellow Sea revealed by combined bulk and environmental DNA metabarcoding
Article.Authors: Choi J.; Kim S.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: The semi-enclosed Yellow Sea is a temperate continental shelf ecosystem characterized by strong seasonal hydrographic variability and indirect influence from Kuroshio-derived warm currents. Such environmental variability may drive seasonal restructuring of marine communities, yet detecting these dynamics at high taxonomic resolution remains challenging using conventional sampling approaches. Here, we investigated seasonal patterns of marine metazoan assemblages using integrated COI metabarcoding of meso bulk DNA (200 μm mesh), micro bulk DNA (40 μm mesh), and seawater-derived environmental DNA (0.45 μm pore size). A total of 373 samples collected during five research cruises between 2018 and 2022 were analyzed. Across all datasets, 398 metazoan taxa were identified at species or higher taxonomic levels, including 107 taxa shared among the three sampling matrices. Fifty-four taxa had no previous records from Korean waters based on the available reference databases, several of which are primarily distributed in lower-latitude regions such as the East China Sea and the Northwest Pacific. Higher taxonomic richness was observed during late summer and autumn surveys than during spring surveys, accompanied by differences in community composition characterized by a greater contribution of diverse invertebrate taxa. Co-occurrence network analyses further revealed seasonal turnover of key taxa and restructuring of community connectivity. These results indicate that integrated metabarcoding can effectively resolve seasonal community reorganization and suggest that the Yellow Sea may become seasonally connected with adjacent warm-current systems at the biological level.
