Article.Title: Follow-up investigation into the combined detection of inhibitors of the activin receptor signaling pathways (IASPs) by LC-HRMS/MS for doping control
Article.Authors: Sakellariou P.; Walpurgis K.; Thomas A.; Thevis M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cytokines of the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) superfamily, including myostatin (MSTN), activin A (ActA), and growth differentiation factor-11 (GDF-11), regulate biological processes such as muscle growth, erythropoiesis, and tissue repair through activin type II receptors A and B (ActRIIA/ActRIIB). Inhibitors of activin receptor signaling pathways (IASPs) are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) due to their potential performance-enhancing effects. Building on a previously published multiplexed liquid chromatography-high resolution (tandem) mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) assay for the detection of nine IASPs in serum and plasma, this study expanded the method to include five additional IASPs: the therapeutic antibodies Emugrobart and Trevogrumab, and the fusion proteins Taldefgrobep alfa, Efmitermant alfa and Cibotercept. Sample preparation involved ammonium sulfate precipitation, multi-ligand (immuno-)affinity purification with magnetic beads, and tryptic digestion. Target analytes were detected based on two to four proteospecific peptides per analyte. This work reports the first LC-HRMS/MS detection strategy for these analytes in an anti-doping context. The method was validated and proved to be specific and sensitive (LODs: 22-85 ng/mL). The assay is suitable for routine anti-doping testing as an initial testing procedure, is readily adaptable to easily include novel analytes and potentially enables retrospective analysis for newly emerging IASPs.

Article.Title: Event-triggered fault tolerant control of discrete-time switched systems subject to cyber deception attacks with application to a two tank system
Article.Authors: Mariappan G.; Shanmugam M.; Rajarathinam V.; Gunasekaran N.; H. Alsharif M.; Kim M.
Article.Abstract: In this work, the problem of fault tolerant event-triggered control with time-varying delay and actuation saturation subject to stochastic deception attack is investigated for a class of discrete-time switched systems. To reduce the network communication load, an event-triggered mechanism is employed independently. By choosing a standard Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF), stochastic deception attack, and average dwell time, novel inequality techniques are presented for the designed controller that guarantees exponentially mean square stable of the closed-loop system. Additionally, a fault tolerant event-triggered control scheme is established based on linear matrix inequalities (LMI) for the considered system. The proposed approach is established stability and event-triggered control performance that permit larger admissible delays while providing tolerance against higher faults. Finally, by using the MATLAB LMI toolbox, the effectiveness of the controller is verified through two numerical examples and an application of the two-tank process with simulations. Comparative results demonstrate its accuracy in control and its reduction in communication requirements while maintaining computational efficiency.

Article.Title: Machine learning model development for predicting pulmonary tuberculosis in symptomatic patients from Ethiopia’s Mid-Rift Valley
Article.Authors: Bekele D.; Nigussie H.; Abdulkadir M.; Dejene T.; Diriba G.; Gutema G.; Melese Sisay D.; Mezemir M.; Wolday D.; de Wit T.; Siu G.; Tafess K.
Article.Abstract: Tuberculosis continues to pose a serious health threat to high-burden countries, including Ethiopia. Complex interactions among multiple risk factors challenge disease control. Conventional epidemiological methods often fail to capture the complex interactions among risk factors; as a result, targeted interventions to control and prevent the disease are often less effective. The present study attempted to develop and test eight supervised machine learning models to address the methodological gap using comprehensive data collected from tuberculosis-suspected individuals attending public hospitals in the Mid-Rift Valley area of Ethiopia. A cross-sectional study using consecutive sampling was carried out between December 30, 2023, and January 2025 at five hospitals in the Mid-Rift Valley, Ethiopia. The required sociodemographic, clinical, and behavioral data, along with sputum samples, were collected from study subjects with signs and symptoms suggestive of TB using a structured questionnaire. Sputum samples collected from 2025 individuals suspected of having TB at OPDs were tested using the GeneXpert MTB/RIF assay for TB diagnosis. Data were split into training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%) sets before applying the models. Eight supervised ML models were trained and tuned. Model performance was assessed using metrics: Area Under the Curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. 95% confidence intervals were computed using bootstrap resampling (1000 replicates; percentile interval method) for AUC and F1-score, and the Wilson score interval for binomial proportions. We interpreted the best model using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and permutation importance. The data were analyzed using Jupyter Notebook, Python Version 3.12.4. Tuberculosis was diagnosed in 280 (13.8%) of the 2025 participants in the study. The Random Forest model performed best at predicting tuberculosis positivity. The final test set showed an AUC of 0.94 (95% CI 0.90–0.97), with an accuracy of 0.88 (95% CI 0.84–0.91), sensitivity of 0.83 (95% CI 0.69–0.92), and specificity of 0.89 (95% CI 0.84–0.92). HIV status, age, Body Mass Index (BMI), Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination history, night sweats, and weight loss were identified as strong predictors of tuberculosis disease in the Random Forest model. The Random Forest algorithm showed the best performance in predicting tuberculosis status, based on actual patient data in a high-burden setting. It also showed good promise as a clinical decision-support tool. However, further external validation in independent populations is required before routine clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Bilateral difference versus mean brachial–ankle pulse wave velocity after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with normal ankle–brachial indices
Article.Authors: Cho J.; Byoun J.; Joo D.; Jo S.; Yun K.
Article.Abstract: Bilateral brachial–ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) measurements provide a mean value and an absolute bilateral difference (ΔbaPWV). We compared their associations with 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after percutaneous coronary intervention. Among 1586 patients in two prospective multicenter stent registries, 1181 had bilateral ankle–brachial indices of 0.90–1.40 and complete baPWV measurements. Greater ΔbaPWV was associated with older age, higher body mass index, higher mean baPWV, and lower ankle–brachial index. During follow-up censored at 400 days, 61 patients experienced MACE, comprising all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or any revascularization. Crude incidence increased across ΔbaPWV tertiles (3.3%, 4.6%, and 7.7%; log-rank P = 0.013), but the adjusted highest-versus-lowest tertile comparison was nonsignificant (hazard ratio, 1.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.91–3.56; P = 0.092). Adding raw linear ΔbaPWV, but not mean baPWV, improved clinical-model fit (likelihood-ratio P = 0.026 and P = 0.439). The optimism-corrected C-index gain with ΔbaPWV was 0.007; bootstrap intervals for discrimination differences included zero. The spline association was nonsignificant ( P = 0.133), and continuous estimates were sensitive to extreme-value handling. The two summaries showed different patterns of association in the fitted models, but these findings do not establish robust incremental prognostic value for ΔbaPWV and do not support its routine use for risk stratification.

Article.Title: Using cellulose nanofibers as the sole binder for cement-free construction materials
Article.Authors: Szafraniec M.; Li L.; Landis E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cellulose nanofibers (CNF), fibrils extracted from wood, bind through hydrogen bonding and have served as the sole binder in wood-based panels, but to the authors’ knowledge they have not been used as the sole binder for un-sintered mineral sand without any hydraulic cement. Here we report an exploratory, proof-of-concept study in which an aqueous CNF gel (3.00–5.87 wt% solids) was the only binder for sand. Twelve compositions combined four gel solids contents with three gel-to-sand mass ratios (25:75, 40:60, 50:50), corresponding to 1.0–5.5 wt% dry cellulose in the dried composite. Cohesive solids formed at about 1 wt% dry cellulose and above, with dry compressive strengths of 0.42–3.73 MPa, comparable to rammed earth and adobe. Strength increased with both the gel fraction and the gel solids content, which interacted, so dry cellulose content alone does not describe the behaviour. Water saturation reduced strength to about 6% of the dry value; re-drying restored it (110 ± 22%), which is consistent with, but does not prove, a reversible physical binding mechanism. The results provide a preliminary composition-property map of cement-free CNF-sand composites and identify moisture sensitivity and the energy cost of drying as the main barriers to practical application.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of a lactiplantibacillus plantarum and bifidobacterium bifidum complex for dry eye disease: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Article.Authors: Son Y.; Shin Y.; Jang S.; Han S.; Jung M.; Kim D.; Park C.
Article.Abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a prevalent ocular condition associated with systemic inflammation, and the gut–eye axis has emerged as a potential therapeutic target. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of LB-101, a probiotic complex comprising Lactiplantibacillus plantarum NK151 and Bifidobacterium bifidum NK175, in adults with DED. Eighty participants were randomized to LB-101 or placebo once daily for 8 weeks, of whom 62 participants completed the study and were included in the final efficacy analysis. After 8 weeks, the LB-101 group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in tear break-up time compared to placebo (mean difference: 1.01 s, 95% CI 0.01–2.01, p = 0.047). Significant improvements were also observed in certain individual symptom-level Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) items. However, total OSDI scores and most other objective ocular surface endpoints did not differ significantly between the groups. Exploratory gut microbiota analysis revealed a significant increase in Carnobacteriaceae and a decrease in the endotoxin-producing bacterial family Oxalobacteraceae in the LB-101 group. No serious adverse events occurred. In conclusion, oral administration of LB-101 for 8 weeks improved tear film stability and certain symptom-level OSDI items, although total OSDI and most objective endpoints remained nonsignificant, with exploratory microbiome findings supporting the therapeutic relevance of the gut–eye axis in DED.

Article.Title: Tailoring selective laser melting parameters of CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys through volume energy density optimization
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Yang X.; Ma Q.; Ren Z.; Wu J.; Zhao J.; Liu Y.; Xu Y.
Article.Abstract: In this study, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys (HEAs) were fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) to investigate the effects of volumetric energy density (VED) on densification behavior, microstructural evolution, and mechanical properties. Three processing conditions were employed using laser powers of 300, 350, and 400 W and scanning speeds of 400, 430, and 460 mm/s, respectively, while the hatch spacing and layer thickness were fixed at 0.12 and 0.03 mm, corresponding to VED values of 208, 226, and 242 J/mm 3 . The microstructures were characterized by optical microscopy (OM), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and the mechanical properties were evaluated by room-temperature tensile tests. All samples exhibited a single FCC structure with characteristic columnar/equiaxed grains and dislocation-rich substructures. With increasing VED, the relative density and tensile properties first increased and then decreased. The sample fabricated at 226 J/mm 3 exhibited the highest relative density of 99.11 ± 0.56% and the best tensile performance, with an ultimate tensile strength of 733 ± 1.2 MPa, a yield strength of 608 ± 2.8 MPa, and an elongation of 18.1%. The superior mechanical properties at this condition were associated with reduced processing defects, grain refinement, and enhanced dislocation strengthening. These results demonstrate that appropriate optimization of VED can effectively regulate the forming quality, microstructure, and mechanical properties of SLM-fabricated CoCrFeMnNi HEAs.

Article.Title: A simple pathway for predicting the electrical performance of polymer carbon black nanoparticle system
Article.Authors: Soudmand B.; Munir M.; Arefian M.; Zare Y.
Article.Abstract: In the present article, Hui-Shia model is modified and progressed to estimate the conduction of nanocomposites with carbon black (CB) nanofiller. The advanced model supposes the concentration of CB/interphase networks as well as the tunneling resistance as the key term influencing the electron transfer. The effects of all factors like CB size, tunneling characteristics, interphase depth, network concentration and percolation onset on the conductivity are analyzed and clarified. Furthermore, the measured conductivity of several examples is provided to evaluate the predictions of the advanced model. Both tunneling length ( λ ) and polymer resistivity ( p ) inversely govern the conduction. λ = 1 and p = 50 Ω·m boost the conduction to 3.4 S/m, while only λ > 7 nm produces a poor conductivity of 0.08 S/m. Also, less CB radius ( R ) and higher interphase depth ( t ) can yield a higher conductivity. R = 15 nm and t = 25 nm grow the conductivity to 2 S/m, while R > 27 nm or t < 11 nm produce an insulated example. Additionally, both network amount (ϕ N ) and contact diameter ( d ) directly govern the electron transfer and the supreme conduction is reached as 1 S/m at ϕ N = 0.15 and d = 60 nm, whereas ϕ N < 0.01 or d < 20 nm poorly increase the conductivity to 0.002 S/m.

Article.Title: Juvenile coral assemblages reflect adult coral composition after a marine heatwave on the Great Barrier Reef
Article.Authors: Doherty M.; Browne I.; Coughlan E.; Foster N.; Leray M.; Preziosi R.; Reverter M.; Wilson A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coral reefs on the southern Great Barrier Reef experienced widespread bleaching during the 2024 marine heatwave, but the structure of juvenile coral assemblages following this event remains poorly resolved. We surveyed juvenile and adult scleractinian corals across 14 lagoonal patch reefs at One Tree Island in July 2025 to quantify post-disturbance juvenile abundance, taxonomic composition and life-history strategy representation. Juvenile abundance was positively associated with adult abundance across taxa, but the strength of this association differed among taxa, with significant positive relationships detected for Acropora spp., Goniastrea spp., Isopora spp., Lobophyllia spp., Pocillopora spp. and Merulinidae. Juvenile abundance also varied strongly across taxa and was highest in Porites spp., although pairwise contrasts indicated partial overlap among the most abundant taxa: Porites spp. overlapped with Pocillopora spp., while Pocillopora spp. also overlapped with Acropora spp., Isopora spp., Favites spp. and Merulinidae. Stress-tolerant taxa had higher total juvenile density than competitive taxa, but this pattern reversed when taxa were weighted equally, indicating that it was driven by abundant taxa such as Porites spp. rather than a consistent strategy-level effect. Genus/family-level composition did not differ detectably between adult and juvenile assemblages, and life-history strategy composition showed a similar pattern. Together, these results indicate that the juvenile assemblage structure at One Tree Island following the 2024 marine heatwave was associated with the identity and abundance of the observed adult coral assemblage, ​highlighting the need for repeated demographic surveys to determine recruitment, survival and recovery trajectories.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of limited access to drinking water services among households using improved water sources in East Africa: evidence from recent DHS data
Article.Authors: Teshome E.; Mengistu A.; Nibretie K.; Enatu E.; Berihun G.
Article.Abstract: Globally, more than 2.1 billion people lack access to improved drinking water services. Limited access to drinking water services has become one of the most critical challenges in developing countries, especially in East Africa. Despite this huge public health burden associated with limited water access, policymakers have given less attention to improving water service accessibility, and less research has been done among those households using improved water sources. Identifying the key predictors of limited access to drinking water can help to design targeted interventions. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models for predicting limited access to drinking water services among households using improved water sources in East Africa. This cross-sectional study employed machine learning models using the most recent DHS data from 146,120 households with improved drinking water sources. Data preprocessing involved handling missing data using k-Nearest Neighbors and mode imputation, encoding categorical features, and hybrid feature selection. Class-weighting, SMOTE, and SMOTEENN were compared to address class imbalance. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors, CatBoost, Support Vector Machine, Naïve Bayes, ANN, and XGB were trained on 80% of the data, with 20% reserved for testing. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AP, and ROC-AUC. SHAP was used to interpret feature contributions to predictions, while the Apriori algorithm was used to identify co-occurring patterns. The study found that in East Africa, among households using improved water sources, 22.1% (95% CI: 21.4%–22.8%) had limited access to drinking water services. The CatBoost model demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUC = 80.8% and AP = 49.8%). SHAP analysis identified responsibility for water collection by a male child under 15 years, household wealth status, community-level electricity access, country, and place of residence as the strongest contributors to model predictions. Apriori association rule mining identified household poverty, low community education, and poor water treatment practices in the community as the strongest co-occurring predictors of limited access to drinking water services. CatBoost with Bayesian optimization showed the strongest performance and was selected as the final model for interpreting predictors. These findings provide valuable insights for targeted interventions, including improving the proximity and availability of drinking water services, reducing the burden of water collection on children and women, addressing socioeconomic and infrastructure-related barriers, and strengthening community-level capacity to improve equitable access to drinking water services.

Article.Title: Design and experimental validation of an integrated cable driven robotic arm and gripper with 10 degrees of freedom
Article.Authors: Zhu B.; Shi P.; Zhang M.; Chow W.; Chen I.; Stanley S.; Cassoni R.
Article.Abstract: Cable-driven robotic manipulators can reduce distal mass by relocating actuators proximally, but increasing the number of remotely actuated degrees of freedom (DoFs) introduces complex cable-routing coupling and challenges in integrating payload capability with dexterous manipulation. In this study, we present LYNX-10, a lightweight 10-DoF cable-driven manipulator comprising a six-DoF arm and a four-DoF gripper. The arm combines a tower-type lifting mechanism, a selective compliance assembly robot arm (SCARA)-type positioning module, and a three-DoF quasi-spherical wrist. The design combines an elbow cable-routing decoupling mechanism with a geometry-based quasi-static compensation model implemented in the controller to compensate for deterministic cable-length redistribution during joint motion. The proposed compensation model substantially suppressed parasitic yaw motion during elbow rotation and parasitic pitch motion during combined elbow and wrist-yaw rotation. Coordinate-wise end-effector repeatability remained below 0.4 mm ( \(3\sigma\) ) at three tested positions. The 6 kg manipulator assembly handled payloads of up to 6 kg within shoulder and elbow operating ranges that narrowed as the payload increased. The four-DoF gripper generated a mean sustained pinch force of approximately 30 N over five measurements and enabled a page-turning task through coordinated thumb–index-finger, wrist, and arm motion. These results demonstrate a compact cable-driven architecture combining load-carrying capability, geometric coupling compensation, and dexterous end-effector manipulation.

Article.Title: Next-location prediction from sparse tourist trajectories with long-tailed destination distributions
Article.Authors: Song R.; He Y.; Wang Z.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Next-location prediction is commonly studied using long and repetitive mobility histories, whereas tourist trajectories are short and their destination frequencies are strongly imbalanced. We present a unified neural framework that combines a mixture-of-experts mobility encoder, retrieval-based trajectory context, and two domain-derived spatio-temporal signals, with auxiliary supervision for location category and visiting hour. Across the two datasets, the framework improves Top-1 accuracy and mean reciprocal rank over recurrent, attention-based, graph-based, and recent representation-learning baselines. Short-history analysis in Suzhou and frequency-stratified results in both cities further show higher reported scores when the observed context is limited or the destination is infrequently visited. Component comparisons show the largest aggregate reductions when the spatio-temporal signals or expert encoder are removed, while retrieval provides its clearest contribution on the tail subset. These findings support the utility of integrating behavioural heterogeneity, trip-level context and population-level trajectory evidence when individual observations are limited.

Article.Authors: Chi X.; Shang M.; Guo B.; Yan G.; Quan L.; Jiang S.; Ma L.; Han G.; Shi F.; Xia Y.; Han J.; Zhang M.; Liu F.; Dun W.
Article.Abstract: Regional neurofluid alterations after mild ischemic stroke (MIS) remain poorly understood. We investigated multiple neurofluid-related MRI markers and cognitive associations in unilateral atherosclerotic MIS. This cross-sectional study included 29 patients with left-lesional MIS (L_MIS), 26 patients with right-lesional MIS (R_MIS), and 31 healthy controls (HCs) undergoing multimodal MRI and neuropsychological assessments (MoCA, DST, TMT). MRI-derived measures included choroid plexus volume (CPV), perivascular space (PVS) counts, regional diffusion tensor imaging–along-the-perivascular-space (DTI-ALPS) index and blood-oxygen-level-dependent and cerebrospinal fluid (BOLD-CSF) coupling across anterior, middle, and posterior regions. Patients with MIS had lower MoCA scores (P = 0.002) and higher PVS counts than HCs (P = 0.004/<0.001, L_MIS/R_MIS). R_MIS showed BOLD-CSF decoupling except in contra-anterior/ipsi-posterior regions (P = 0.009–0.032) and increased global/left CPV (P = 0.043). L_MIS showed reduced DTI-ALPS except globally and ipsi-anteriorly after WMH/eTIV adjustment (P = 0.007–0.024). Mediation revealed indirect associations of PVS counts with DST-backward through ipsi-anterior/middle DTI-ALPS in L_MIS (β = −0.199, 95% CI −0.364 to − 0.044), and of CPV enlargement with MoCA through ipsi-posterior BOLD-CSF coupling in R_MIS (β = −0.249, 95% CI: −0.606 to − 0.029). Multiple neurofluid-related MRI markers exhibited region-specific alterations and associations with cognitive performance in MIS. Article.Title: Engineering spin-wave spectra through longitudinal compositional interfaces
Article.Authors: Sarria F.; Saavedra E.; Pereira A.; Escrig J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Engineering spin-wave spectra without modifying device geometry remains a central challenge in magnonics. Here, we investigate how longitudinal compositional interfaces reshape the equilibrium magnetic configurations and spin-wave dynamics of homogeneous and multisegmented Co/CoNi/Ni nanowires using micromagnetic simulations. Our results show that longitudinal compositional architecture modifies the magnetic energy landscape, giving rise to distinct equilibrium magnetization textures and changes in the spatial distribution of spin-wave excitations. The calculated dynamic susceptibility spectra reveal substantial changes in resonance frequencies and spectral amplitudes across the investigated architectures. While homogeneous Ni and Co nanowires exhibit dominant resonances in the C and Ku microwave bands, respectively, several multisegmented configurations display their strongest response within the technologically relevant X band. These findings demonstrate that tailoring the longitudinal distribution of magnetic material parameters provides a route to modifying the spin-wave resonance spectrum without changing the external nanowire geometry, offering a basis for the design of compositionally engineered magnonic nanostructures.

Article.Title: Biomechanical effects of posterior attachment design on mandibular incisor intrusion with clear aligners: a three-dimensional finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Çakır N.; Durmaz M.; Kadıoğlu M.; Rübendiz M.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the initial biomechanical effects of different posterior attachment designs during mandibular incisor intrusion with clear aligners using three-dimensional finite element analysis. A mandibular half-arch finite element model was constructed from computed tomography data. Five models were evaluated: no attachment (NA), horizontal rectangular attachment (HRA), gingivally beveled horizontal rectangular attachment (GB-HRA), occlusally beveled horizontal rectangular attachment (OB-HRA), and modified dome-shaped attachment (MDA). Attachments were placed on the mandibular canines and premolars. A 0.2-mm intrusive activation was simulated through an interference fit between the mandibular central and lateral incisors and the corresponding internal surfaces of the clear aligner. Directional dental displacement, aligner displacement and Von Mises stress, attachment stress, contact pressure, aligner–attachment contact area, and periodontal ligament stress were evaluated. Posterior attachment design influenced the initial biomechanical responses of the mandibular teeth and clear aligner. The HRA model produced substantial incisal-edge displacement in the intrusive direction with relatively limited reactive extrusion in the canine–premolar region. The MDA model exhibited the greatest incisal-edge displacement in the intrusive direction, the lowest aligner displacement, the highest aligner–attachment contact ratio, and the lowest attachment stress. However, it also produced the highest aligner and periodontal ligament Von Mises stresses and pronounced reactive canine–premolar extrusion. The GB-HRA model exhibited the highest attachment stress and contact pressure. Posterior attachment designs produced distinct initial biomechanical responses during simulated mandibular incisor intrusion. The HRA model demonstrated a more favorable balance between anterior incisal-edge displacement in the intrusive direction and limited posterior extrusion, whereas the MDA model exhibited reduced aligner displacement and increased aligner–attachment contact accompanied by higher stress concentrations and reactive extrusion. These findings characterize initial mechanical behavior and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of clinical retention, stability, or treatment effectiveness.

Article.Title: Explainable AI-driven neural activity analysis in Parkinsonian rats under electrical stimulation
Article.Authors: Choi H.; Kim G.; Yang S.; Baeg E.; Kim D.; Jin S.; Byun S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by motor dysfunction and abnormal neural oscillations. This study combined graphene-based cortical stimulation with an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework to investigate spatial and frequency-related features contributing to pre- and post-stimulation classification in Parkinsonian rats. Electrocorticogram (ECoG) signals were recorded before and after stimulation and classified using EEGNet and DeepConvNet. Layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) and DeepLIFT were applied to identify frequency bands and recording channels contributing to the classification. The anatomical locations of these channels were mapped onto a cortical map. XAI analyses were performed separately for each animal to examine individual attribution patterns. Our XAI analysis revealed frequency-band- and region-specific contributions to pre- and post-stimulation classification in Parkinsonian rats. Our approach provided complementary insights into the features contributing to pre- and post-stimulation ECoG classification alongside PSD-based analyses. These findings highlight the potential of combining graphene-based cortical stimulation with explainable deep learning to identify classification-relevant features across frequency bands and cortical areas in pre- and post-stimulation recordings.

Article.Title: Comparative effects of combined behavioral intervention and ericksonian hypnotherapy in alcohol use disorder: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Çınaroğlu M.; Yılmazer E.; Hızlı Sayar G.
Article.Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic, relapsing condition associated with psychological, behavioral, and social impairment. Individualized, experiential psychotherapies such as Ericksonian Hypnotherapy (EH) have a limited randomized evidence base in AUD. This three-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial compared Combined Behavioral Intervention (CBI), EH, and a psychoeducational control condition (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06916754). Ninety adults meeting DSM-5 criteria for AUD were randomized 1:1:1; both active interventions were delivered individually over 12 weekly sessions. Prespecified primary outcomes were three Timeline Follow-Back indices covering the preceding 30 days: drinking days, heavy drinking days, and drinks per drinking day. Craving, depressive and anxiety symptoms, quality of life, and readiness for change were secondary and exploratory. The primary analysis was an intention-to-treat linear mixed-effects model including all randomized participants, with completer and multiple-imputation analyses as sensitivity analyses; multiplicity was controlled across the confirmatory family of primary outcomes. Both active interventions produced significantly greater improvement than control across all primary alcohol-use outcomes and across the exploratory secondary domains, with moderate-to-large between-group effects. Contrasts between the two active treatments favored EH on craving-related cognitions, obsessive craving, and anxiety severity, but these comparisons were exploratory, were not powered a priori, and are reported as preliminary. Differences between the active treatments on alcohol-use outcomes were not statistically significant, which should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence. The findings support structured psychotherapy for AUD and identify Ericksonian Hypnotherapy as a treatment package warranting adequately powered comparative evaluation.

Article.Title: Effect of rhGH on IVF-ET outcomes in advanced-age women with different ovarian responsiveness during GnRH agonist long protocol ovulation induction
Article.Authors: Jiang F.; Liang Y.; Chen J.; Yang X.; Song J.; Li D.; Meng Y.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of recombinant human growth hormone (GH) during ovulation induction with a GnRH agonist long protocol on IVF-ET (in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer, IVF-ET) outcomes in female infertile patients (aged ≥ 35) with different ovarian responsiveness. A total of 148 female patients aged ≥ 35 group during controlled ovarian hyper-stimulation (COH) with a GnRH agonist long protocol were selected. The GH group was given in a daily injection of 4.5 IU of recombinant growth hormone co-COH, initiated from the starting day of gonadotropin and lasting 5 days. The group without GH co-treatment was used as the control group. The E 2 on HCG day, the thickness of the endometrium on HCG day, the number of eggs obtained, the number of mature eggs, the number of 2PN (2 pronucleus, 2PN) fertilization, the number of cleavage embryos, the high-quality embryos rates, the pregnancy rates and the implantation rates were used as the observational indexes. The participants were divided into two subgroups: normal ovarian response (the number of eggs obtained ≥ 4) and ovarian hyporesponsiveness (the number of eggs obtained < 4), further explored the IVF-ET outcomes of patients of different age groups (aged 35–37; aged 38–40; aged ≥ 41). In the normal ovarian response group with the number of eggs obtained ≥ 4, there was no statistically significant difference in all IVF outcomes observations in patients aged 35–37 group ( p > 0.05). The number of 2PN fertilization and the number of cleavage embryos in patients aged 38–40 group was significantly higher in the GH group than in the control group ( p < 0.05). The number of eggs obtained, the number of mature eggs and the number of cleavage embryos in patients aged ≥ 41 group was significantly higher in the GH group than in the control group ( p < 0.05). In the ovarian hyporesponsive group with the number of eggs acquired < 4, there was no statistically significant difference in all observed indicators of IVF outcomes in patients aged 35–37 group ( p > 0.05). The number of 2PN fertilization, the number of cleavage embryos and the high-quality embryos rates in patients aged 38–40 group was significantly higher in the GH group than in the control group ( p < 0.05). The thickness of the endometrium on HCG day, the number of 2PN fertilization, and the high-quality embryos rates were significantly higher in the GH group than in the control group in patients aged ≥ 41 group ( p < 0.05). Clinical pregnancy rates and implantation rates, among different ovarian response groups, were somewhat improved in GH group compared with the control group, but there was no statistical difference ( p > 0.05). The use of GH in combination with ovulation induction with a GnRH agonist long protocol can increase the number of 2PN fertilization and the high-quality embryos rates. To a certain extent, it improves the outcomes of IVF-ET in advanced-age infertile patients aged ≥ 38 years, whether they have normal ovarian response or low ovarian response. However, due to the relatively small sample size of the group aged 38 or above with a normal ovarian response (> 4 oocytes retrieved) in this study, in the future we need to additional data from a larger cohort in order to obtain more solid conclusions.

Article.Title: Interindividual variability in trunk function across body mass index in young men using exploratory cluster analysis
Article.Authors: Cepková A.; Cepka R.; Šooš Ľ.; Zemková E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trunk function is important for postural control and spinal loading; however, individuals with similar body mass index (BMI) may differ in trunk endurance and back muscle strength. The extent to which BMI reflects functional trunk capacity therefore remains unclear. This study investigated the relationships between BMI, plank endurance, maximal isometric back extensor strength, and sagittal spinal posture, and explored interindividual variability in trunk function using cluster analysis. A total of 199 male university students were assessed for BMI, maximal isometric back extensor strength, plank-based trunk endurance and sagittal spinal posture. K-means cluster analysis with z-score standardization was used to examine variability in trunk function and to identify functional profiles. Differences between groupings were analyzed in relation to physical activity, plank test termination and sagittal spinal posture. BMI demonstrated a moderate negative association with plank endurance (ρ = − 0.36, p < 0.001) and a weak positive association with maximal isometric back extensor strength (ρ = 0.22, p = 0.002).Cluster analysis identified three exploratory functional profiles, although separation was limited (silhouette = 0.280). The clusters differed in self-reported physical activity frequency ( p = 0.006). Separate comparisons did not detect differences in thoracic kyphosis or lumbar lordosis (Holm-adjusted p = 0.506 and 0.695, respectively), or in reasons for plank test termination ( p = 0.068). Plank endurance and maximal isometric back extensor strength represent distinct but complementary aspects of trunk function that are only partly associated with BMI. Individuals with similar BMI may exhibit different functional capacities, highlighting the importance of multidimensional assessment.

Article.Title: Pre-synthesis theoretical screening of pristine and B- and Si-doped C24 fullerene and coronene nanostructures for aqueous santenol adsorption in wastewater-remediation applications
Article.Authors: Almojil S.; Almohana A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this work, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations were used to investigate Santenol (Pollutant present in wastewater) adsorption on two carbon frameworks containing the same number of carbon atoms but differing substantially in topology, hydrogen termination, strain, electronic structure, and overall composition: C24 fullerene and coronene (COR), as well as their B- and Si-doped derivatives. We used geometry optimization, adsorption energy, cohesive energy, recovery time, electronic descriptors, a gap-derived electronic-response index, UV–Vis response, NBO, MEP, DOS, HOMO-LUMO, ELF, LOL, and NCI/RDG analyses to evaluate adsorption behavior and potential sensing properties. Adsorption-energy calculations indicated that B-C23 and SiC23 exhibit the strongest STN adsorption, with Eads values of – 51.83/– 54.77 and − 42.80/– 46.82 kcal.mol⁻¹ at the B97D/ωB97X-D levels, respectively. Thermodynamic analyses, including ΔHads and ΔGads, confirmed the favorable adsorption conditions for these structures. This suggests their potential as strong molecular adsorption candidates for STN under continuum-aqueous conditions and supports their further evaluation in wastewater-remediation-oriented studies. Thermodynamic analysis further showed that B-C23@STN exhibits the most favorable adsorption, with ΔGads = – 39.28 kcal.mol⁻¹, whereas COR@STN shows a slightly positive ΔGads = + 0.76 kcal.mol⁻¹ under the adopted standard-state computational conditions. In contrast, COR and B-COR showed weaker adsorption and comparatively small nominal τ values within the simplified desorption model, consistent with more reversible adsorption behavior. Electronic and optical analyses revealed adsorption-induced changes in the HOMO-LUMO gap, gap-derived electronic-response index, and λmax, particularly for B-COR, Si-COR, and B-C23. The large red shifts observed for B-COR@STN and B-C23@STN suggest a possible optical response toward STN. The combined NBO, MEP, ELF/LOL, NCI/RDG, and QTAIM analyses indicate that the extended adsorption interfaces contain substantial π-related, dispersion, and electrostatic contributions, whereas selected dopant–nitrogen contacts, particularly in B-C23@STN and Si-C23@STN, exhibit stronger localized donor–acceptor interactions with appreciable partial-bonding character. Overall, these computational results suggest that C24- and COR-based systems may serve as theoretical candidate platforms for guiding future experimental STN (as a model drug-like contaminant) adsorption and response-screening studies.

Article.Title: Applying ranked set sampling to Gaussian mixture models of Glasgow Coma Scale scores in intracerebral hemorrhage
Article.Authors: Ahmed E.; Rahman A.; Yusuf A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clinical severity scales like the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) exhibit heterogeneous distributions reflecting latent patient subgroups. Finite mixture models capture this heterogeneity, but component overlap limits interpretability. Ranked set sampling (RSS) incorporates auxiliary ranking information during sample selection, potentially improving separability. This empirical study evaluated whether RSS enhances component separability in Gaussian mixture models of GCS scores compared to simple random sampling (SRS). Admission GCS scores from a full consecutive cohort ( $$\:N=504$$ ) of primary intracerebral hemorrhage patients were analyzed. A retrospective ranked set subsampling ( $$\:n=300$$ ) and simple random subsampling ( $$\:n=300$$ ) were evaluated using Gaussian mixture models. A composite auxiliary variable (age and diabetes mellitus) was used for RSS ranking. Component numbers were selected via the Bayesian Information Criterion and bootstrap likelihood ratio tests. Parameters were estimated using the expectation-maximization algorithm, and separability was quantified via normalized overlap coefficients. A three-component model was selected under both schemes, aligning with established GCS severity categories. Compared to SRS, the retrospective RSS-based subsampling yielded more concentrated mixture components and substantially reduced overlap between adjacent components. A retrospective RSS-based subsampling design produced lower component overlap in Gaussian mixture models for clinical severity data without increasing model complexity. RSS represents a practical, underutilized strategy to potentially enhance mixture-based analyses of heterogeneous medical outcomes.

Article.Title: Physics-regularized neural network and multi-objective optimization for sustainable multi-binder concrete mix design
Article.Authors: Almutairi A.; Alrowais R.; Bashir M.; Makobero B.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: This study examined multi-age compressive-strength prediction and multi-objective mixture selection for concrete containing fly ash, ground-granulated blast-furnace slag, and silica fume. The dataset comprised 112 mixture-age mean strengths from 28 formulations tested at 3, 7, 28, and 90 days (336 cylinders). Complete mixture groups were assigned to training (20), validation (4), and testing (4) partitions. The physics-regularized neural network (PRNN) yielded an R² of 0.962 and an RMSE of 4.84 MPa on the 16 held-out mixture-age observations; the data-only multilayer perceptron yielded 0.790 and 11.42 MPa, respectively. Additional ridge, SVR-RBF, random forest, and gradient boosting models were evaluated using mixture-grouped validation and nine composition-and-age inputs. Random forest achieved a held-out R² of 0.743 and RMSE of 12.62 MPa; Gradient Boosting achieved 0.740 and 12.69 MPa. NSGA-III was used to examine candidate proportions under strength, cost, and global-warming-potential objectives. Three candidate laboratory mixtures yielded 90-day compressive strengths of 31.8, 41.5, and 51.2 MPa. The findings demonstrate the value of grouping formulations during evaluation and provide a comparative benchmark for predictive modeling of multi-binder concrete. Model evaluation was limited to four held-out formulations, and economic and environmental comparisons depend on their constituent inventories.

Article.Title: UCHL3 stabilizes ENO1 through deubiquitination to promote glycolysis and tumor growth in bladder cancer
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Wu Y.; Liao Z.; Liu Q.; Hu S.
Article.Abstract: Bladder cancer (BCa) is one of the most common malignant tumors of the urinary system and represents an increasingly serious public health problem worldwide. Dysregulated glycolysis is a key feature of metabolic reprogramming in BCa, and aberrant expression of enolase 1 (ENO1) is closely associated with tumor progression. This study aimed to identify novel deubiquitinases that regulate ENO1 ubiquitination and stability in BCa. We found that the deubiquitinating enzyme ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L3 (UCHL3) is highly expressed in BCa tissues (TCGA–GTEx and tissue microarray) and positively correlates with ENO1 levels, and that high UCHL3 expression predicts poor prognosis in patients with BCa in the GSE13507 cohort. Functionally, UCHL3 knockdown markedly reduced ENO1 protein levels and impaired glycolysis. Mechanistically, the C-terminal domain of UCHL3 directly interacted with the triose-phosphate isomerase (TIM) barrel domain of ENO1 and stabilized ENO1 by suppressing its ubiquitination. Moreover, UCHL3 knockdown inhibited BCa cell proliferation, migration and glycolysis. Crucially, phenotypic rescue experiments demonstrated that these malignant behaviors driven by UCHL3 were largely dependent on ENO1. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that UCHL3 activates glycolysis by deubiquitinating ENO1, and that its high expression promotes BCa cell proliferation, migration, glycolysis, and tumor growth. These results suggest that targeting UCHL3 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for BCa.

Article.Title: Green and simple rrs spectroscopic strategy based on xanthene-based dye; Acid Red 51 for eletriptan quantification in pharmaceuticals and biological samples
Article.Authors: Abu-hassan A.; Batakoushy H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Eletriptan tablets are a targeted pharmaceutical agent that acts as an agonist for the 5-hydroxytryptamine1 receptor subclassification, mostly employed to alleviate acute migraine episodes. As a member of the triptan class, Eletriptan functions by constricting cerebral blood vessels and decreasing the release of chemicals that cause light and sound sensitivity, nausea, and headache discomfort. Its efficacy in alleviating migraine symptoms makes it a valuable option for individuals seeking rapid and effective relief. A sustainable, rapid, one-pot resonance Resonance Rayleigh Scattering spectrometric technique was created for estimating out Eletriptan in pharmaceutical tablets and biological matrices. Upon mixing Eletriptan with the fluorescent ligand Acid Red 51 in an acidic buffer, a marked increase in resonance Resonance Rayleigh Scattering intensity was immediately observed. This phenomenon was ascribed to the selective formation of an ion-pair complex between the cationic Eletriptan drug and the anionic dye, which amplified the Resonance Rayleigh Scattering signal through enhanced scattering interactions. The RRS intensity showed a straight-line connection with Eletriptan concentration between 50 and 1500 ng/mL, allowing for accurate measurement. Key experimental parameters, including pH, ligand concentration, and buffer volume, were systematically optimized to maximize the sensitivity of the Eletriptan –Acid Red 51 system. The method adhered to International Council for Harmonisation validation criteria, achieving detection and quantification limits of 15.7 ng/mL and 47.8 ng/mL, respectively. Effective implementation to pharmaceutical and biological samples confirmed the method’s accuracy and reproducibility, with recovery rates aligning with acceptable analytical standards. Notably, the approach minimizes solvent consumption and hazardous waste generation, aligning with green analytical principles. By integrating simplicity, environmental sustainability, and high sensitivity, this Resonance Rayleigh Scattering-based technique emerges as a robust alternative for routine analysis of Eletriptan in quality control and biomedical research.

Article.Title: Comprehensive molecular and clinical analysis of human electron transfer flavoprotein variants in multiple Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
Article.Authors: Mangiavillano-Suleiman S.; Khan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human electron transfer flavoprotein (hETF) is a critical mitochondrial enzyme essential for fatty acid β-oxidation and amino acid catabolism. Genetic variations in hETF subunits cause Multiple Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency (MADD), a severe metabolic disorder. This study integrates computational analyses with clinical variant classification to propose a mechanism of pathogenicity and explore its diagnostic applicability. We investigated three naturally occurring single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) at the critical α/β-subunit interface—hETF-βE165K, hETF-αN259S, and hETF-αN259D—using comprehensive in-silico analyses including homology modeling, interprotein interaction profiling, stability predictions (ΔΔG), and theoretical small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). Concurrently, we applied the ACMG/AMP framework to classify three clinical variants: rs1441796075, rs897415970, and rs1371983074. Our findings reveal a mechanistic model: all three interface SNPs disrupt native inter-subunit interactions (hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and van der Waals contacts), driving the protein toward an "open" conformational state. This structural shift significantly increases solvent accessibility of the FAD cofactor pocket (> 15% ΔSASA), rendering it susceptible to pathogenic oxidation to 8-formyl-FAD (8f.-FAD). Stability predictions using multiple methods (DynaMut, mCSM, DUET) revealed variant-specific profiles: αN259S showed consensus destabilization across 3/3 methods, while βE165K showed consensus destabilization across 2/3 methods, while αN259D predictions were mixed, indicating uncertain energetic consequences. SAXS analysis revealed subtle conformational differences consistent with increased flexibility. Clinical classification identified rs1441796075 as Likely Pathogenic (PM2 + PP3 + PP5), while rs897415970 and rs1371983074 remain Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS) despite extreme rarity and deleterious predictions, highlighting the critical gap that molecular evidence can fill. This integrated approach provides strong computational evidence for a structure–function-disease model: interface destabilization → open conformation → FAD vulnerability → MADD pathology. Our methodology demonstrates potential as a high-throughput in silico screening approach for prioritizing VUS for further investigation and suggests a testable therapeutic strategy—small-molecule interface stabilizers—that warrants preclinical evaluation for MADD patients carrying interface-destabilizing variants.

Article.Title: Influence of spreader dispersion on rumour propagation in complex networks
Article.Authors: Ramrakhiyani M.; Tiwari M.; Vadivel Murugan S.
Article.Abstract: In social systems, information and misinformation can enter the underlying interaction network through multiple independent sources. Their cumulative reach depends not only on the influence of the sources but also on how they are collectively positioned in the network. Here, we study how the spatial dispersion of multiple initial spreaders influences rumour propagation on complex networks. This setting differs from epidemic spreading because rumour spreaders may become inactive after contacting already informed nodes. Hence, the placement of the initial spreaders affects not only initial coverage but also the timing of deactivation. We consider classical three-state rumour dynamics with interaction-driven stifling and compare dispersion-based initial spreader selection strategies, constructed using farthest-first traversal and a hybrid local-connectivity refinement, with non-dispersion-based strategies. Numerical simulations on Erdös-Rényi, Barabási-Albert and Watts-Strogatz networks, together with six real-world network datasets, show that dispersed initial spreaders generally increase both the final rumour size and the peak fraction of active spreaders. This occurs because dispersion reduces overlap among spreading regions and delays deactivation caused by contacts with already informed nodes. The hybrid strategy, which combines topological separation with local connectivity, typically outperforms degree-based seeding over a broad range of spreading and stifling probabilities. Our results show that in multi-source rumour spreading, a combination of broad separation between the initial spreaders and strong local connectivity is crucial for maximizing rumour reach and intensity.

Article.Title: Adaptive structural fusion for dielectric constant prediction using physics-guided graph neural networks
Article.Authors: Shetty J.; Krishna R.; Prabhu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of dielectric response is essential for improving the discovery of materials for electronic, energy-storage, radio-frequency, sensing, and optoelectronic applications. However, dielectric datasets are typically dominated by materials with low to moderate dielectric response, while high-dielectric materials are severely under-represented, making reliable prediction across the full property range challenging. This work proposes a physics-guided extension of the Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN) for total dielectric constant prediction through Adaptive Structural Fusion (ASF). This refines learned atomic representations using five physically motivated local descriptors: coordination number, mean bond length, bond-angle variation, local electronegativity difference, and atomic polarizability. A context-dependent Knowledge-Guided Graph Aggregation (KGGA) module is subsequently evaluated both independently and in combination with ASF to investigate whether adaptive graph aggregation depends on the quality of the underlying node representations. Four controlled architectures -the baseline CGCNN, CGCNN with KGGA, CGCNN with ASF, and the proposed model CGCNN with both ASF and KGGA- were evaluated on an identical frozen split of a curated benchmark containing 5,874 inorganic crystalline materials. Relative to the baseline CGCNN, the proposed framework – CGCNN with both ASF and KGGA- reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) from 11.139 to 8.828, decreased the root mean square error (RMSE) from 53.315 to 42.275, and increased the coefficient of determination (R²) from 0.214 to 0.506, corresponding to approximately 21% reductions in MAE and RMSE. Paired material-level statistical analysis further demonstrated a mean absolute-error reduction of 2.311 (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.960–3.736) and lower prediction error for 68.4% of the 588 held-out test materials. Regime-wise evaluation showed that the proposed model achieved the lowest MAE in five of six predefined dielectric regimes, a descriptive observation that should be interpreted cautiously given the sparse high-dielectric test samples. Representative material analysis further illustrated substantial error reductions for selected chemically and structurally diverse inorganic compounds. These results indicate that physics-guided representation refinement and adaptive graph aggregation are complementary strategies for improving dielectric property prediction while highlighting the importance of regime-aware evaluation for long-tailed materials datasets.

Article.Title: Numerical simulation of water-sediment two-phase erosion in a split-frame aqueduct and comparison of pier geometry schemes
Article.Authors: Bai J.; Zhang Z.; Xu C.; Wang Z.; Hou H.; Yang B.; Zhang H.; Lan Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate local erosion in split-frame aqueducts under sediment-laden flow, a three-dimensional water–sediment two-phase numerical model was developed using the RNG k–ε turbulence model, the Discrete Phase Model (DPM), and the Neilson–Gilchrist erosion model. The model was validated against flume-test data for pier erosion. The effects of discharge, sediment concentration, and particle size on erosion at different aqueduct sections were then examined, and pier-end aspect-ratio schemes were compared in terms of velocity distribution and erosion response. The mean relative error between simulated and measured erosion thicknesses under four benchmark inlet velocities was 6.76%. The inlet split-frame pier region, upstream aqueduct body, and turning zones of the outlet transition section were identified as the main high-erosion regions. Within the tested range, erosion generally increased with discharge, sediment concentration, and particle size. A combined scheme with AR₁ = 1.5 at the inlet and AR₂ = 2.0 at the outlet produced a smoother velocity transition, reduced the outlet wake-affected region, and yielded lower model-predicted erosion rates than the original semi-circular configuration in most cases. These results provide numerical support for erosion-risk identification and preliminary pier-geometry selection in similar water-conveyance structures.

Article.Title: Adequacy of control strategies in a selected sample of contemporary high-impact medical studies
Article.Authors: Goulart Xande J.; Maselli-Schoueri J.; del Giglio A.
Article.Abstract: To classify the control strategies used in contemporary high-impact medical studies using an adapted framework originally proposed by Ross. We conducted a cross-sectional methodological assessment of therapeutic studies published in 2025 in a deliberately restricted, non-systematic sample of selected high-impact medical journals. Articles were identified through structured keyword-based searches within journal platforms. Eligible studies were classified into four categories (fully controlled, incompletely controlled, control absent, or control not feasible) based on predefined criteria. Among 151 included studies, 113 (74.8%) were classified as fully controlled, 20 (13.2%) as incompletely controlled, and 18 (11.9%) as control absent. No studies were classified as control not feasible. Psychiatry had the highest observed proportion of fully controlled studies (86.4%), whereas oncology had the lowest (64.3%) and the highest proportion without control (33.3%). In this restricted, non-systematic sample of selected high-impact journals, most included therapeutic studies were classified as fully controlled, although the observed proportions varied across clinical domains. These findings are descriptive and should not be interpreted as population-level estimates or as evidence of systematic differences between specialties. Comparison with Ross’s 1951 findings is qualitative because differences in sampling and classification preclude direct quantitative comparison.

Article.Title: Ms4a6d in macrophages accelerated the progression of AAA via modulating SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING signaling induced inflammation and MMPs expression
Article.Authors: Zhuang J.; Huang J.; Wang J.; Lin L.; Shan Z.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the role of Ms4a6d in the formation of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) in mice and explore its underlying mechanism. Bioinformatic approaches were applied to comprehensively analyze transcriptomic and single-cell sequencing data obtained from AAA lesions and normal abdominal aortic tissues in mice. In vivo, 36 male ApoE⁻/⁻ mice were randomly divided into Sham, Model, Model+Ms4a6d-OE, and Model+Ms4a6d-KD groups ( n = 9/group). Aneurysm size was assessed by Masson staining, and macrophage infiltration by F4/80 immunohistochemistry. Dual immunofluorescence staining was performed to detect whether Ms4a6d is specifically expressed in macrophages. In vitro, RAW264.7 macrophages were transduced with Ms4a6d-OE or Ms4a6d-KD lentivirus and stimulated with Ang Ⅱ under hypoxia. A sequential pharmacological intervention strategy was employed using Piceatannol (SYK inhibitor), Activator 1 (PI3K/Akt/CREB activator), 666 − 15 (CREB inhibitor), and SR-717 (STING agonist). Protein expression was detected by Western blot; secretion of IL-1β, IL-18, MMP-2, and MMP-9 was measured by ELISA; MMP-2/9 enzymatic activities were assessed by gelatin zymography; and cell invasion was evaluated by Transwell assay. Co-immunoprecipitation was used to assess CREB-STING interaction. Bulk RNA‑seq analysis revealed widespread upregulation of genes related to immune inflammation and matrix remodeling in AAA at the tissue level, and further demonstrated a co‑expression network involving Ms4a6d, SYK, PI3K, CREB, STING, and MMPs. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis further revealed that the above alterations predominantly occurred within macrophage subpopulations, indicating that macrophages in AAA underwent metabolic reprogramming, exhibited enhanced differentiation potential and dysfunction, and showed shifted pseudotime differentiation trajectories. These findings also suggest that Ms4a6d may participate in these processes by regulating CREB. In vivo, Ms4a6d is predominantly expressed in macrophages. Ms4a6d overexpression increased AAA diameter and macrophage infiltration, while Ms4a6d knockdown reduced both. In vitro, Ms4a6d overexpression upregulated p-SYK, p-PI3K, p-CREB, p-STING, NLRP3, IL-1β, MMP-2, and MMP-9, enhanced IL-1β, IL-18, MMP-2, and MMP-9 secretion, increased MMP-2/9 gelatinolytic activities, and promoted macrophage invasion. Piceatannol blocked these effects, which were sequentially rescued by activator 1, suppressed by 666 − 15, and again enhanced by SR-717, confirming the hierarchical Ms4a6d/SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING axis. Co-IP demonstrated direct CREB-STING interaction. Ms4a6d in macrophages accelerates AAA progression by regulating the SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING signaling pathway, inducing inflammation and MMP expression.

Article.Title: Hybrid Markov Regime-Switching and Hurdle modeling of last-mile livestock logistics in Ukraine under systemic volatility
Article.Authors: Korniietskyi O.; Orel V.; Orel A.; Nitsenko V.; Perevozova I.; Jurgelane-Kaldava I.; Hudenko J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that integrates Random Forest Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) for preliminary predictor screening, a two-state Markov Regime-Switching (MRS) model for identifying latent logistics regimes, and a two-part Hurdle model for separately estimating disruption probability and conditional freight-cost intensity. The empirical analysis uses a verified monthly panel dataset covering 2023–2025 across three contrasting regional logistics nodes - Kyiv, Vinnytsia, and Lviv - and incorporates energy, security, market, transport, and infrastructure-related indicators. The MRS results identify two statistically distinct and persistent freight-cost regimes, with the systemic-crisis regime characterized by a 21.8% higher mean Freight Cost Per Ton and a longer expected duration than the operational-stability regime. The Hurdle estimates show that Security Alerts and Power Outage Hours are positively associated with the probability of logistics disruption, while Power Outage Hours and Fuel Price Volatility are positively associated with conditional freight-cost intensity; regional comparisons further reveal heterogeneous exposure to systemic shocks. Counterfactual technological scenarios further indicate that combining AI-assisted dynamic routing with decentralized autonomous and light electric transport solutions could reduce the estimated sensitivity of freight costs to energy disruptions by approximately 24.2%. The findings demonstrate the value of combining latent-regime identification, sequential disruption modeling, and technological scenario analysis for assessing the resilience of livestock last-mile logistics under persistent infrastructure and security shocks.

Article.Title: Association of tooth length and crown-root ratio with transverse expansion efficiency in clear aligner therapy
Article.Authors: Cengiz S.
Article.Abstract: The predictability of transverse expansion with clear aligner therapy (CAT) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the association between dental panoramic radiograph (DPR)-derived posterior tooth length, crown–root ratio (CRR), and transverse expansion efficiency in patients treated with CAT. Twenty-five patients treated with Invisalign involving transverse expansion in both arches were retrospectively evaluated. Planned expansion was obtained from the ClinCheck digital treatment setup, whereas achieved expansion was measured on pre-treatment and post-treatment digital models using OrthoAnalyzer software. Tooth morphology measurements, including DPR-derived total tooth length and CRR, were obtained from pre-treatment DPRs using ImageJ software. Associations between these morphologic variables and expansion efficiency were analyzed using correlation and multivariable regression analyses. Achieved expansion values were significantly lower than planned values in all evaluated dental regions ( p < 0.05). Expansion efficiency ranged from 80.03% to 91.08%. No significant correlations were identified between expansion efficiency and either total tooth length or CRR ( p > 0.05). Multivariable analyses likewise revealed no significant independent effects of tooth morphology variables on expansion efficiency. DPR-derived posterior tooth length and crown–root ratio were not significant predictors of crown-level transverse expansion efficiency during CAT, indicating that expansion outcomes are influenced by factors beyond the specific tooth morphology variables evaluated in the present study.

Article.Title: Three-dimensional reconstruction and evolutionary distribution characteristics of coal wall fractures in a large-mining-height longwall face
Article.Authors: Guo W.; Cheng R.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: The development and spatial distribution of fractures within the coal wall of large-mining-height longwall faces are important factors affecting coal-wall stability and spalling risk. To investigate the fracture characteristics of the coal wall under different stages of mining influence, the No. 22,523 working face of Halagou Coal Mine was selected as the engineering background. Different mining-affected zones ahead of the coal wall were identified through theoretical analysis of advance abutment pressure combined with FLAC3D numerical simulation, and coal samples were collected at distances of 1, 4, 6, and 40 m from the coal wall for industrial CT scanning. Based on CT image preprocessing, binary fracture extraction, and three-dimensional reconstruction using Avizo, the two-dimensional CT fracture area fraction, spatial fracture morphology, and dominant fracture orientations of coal samples from different positions were analyzed. The results show that, with decreasing distance from the coal wall, the overall degree of mining disturbance increases and the internal fractures become progressively more developed. The mean CT fracture area fractions of samples collected at 1, 4, 6, and 40 m from the coal wall were 1.18%, 0.62%, 0.56%, and 0.01%, respectively. Significant differences were observed in the three-dimensional fracture morphology among samples from different positions, together with corresponding variations in dominant fracture orientations. These findings indicate pronounced spatial differences in fracture characteristics under different degrees of mining influence and provide a basis for understanding coal-wall fracture development and its relationship with mining-induced disturbance in large-mining-height longwall faces.

Article.Title: Quantum otto and Carnot cycles via skew Ising model
Article.Authors: Valizadeh N.; Saghavaz N.; Ebadi Z.; Mohammadzadeh H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate the thermodynamic performance of quantum heat engines and refrigerators based on a two-spin system subject to a skew magnetic field. The working substance is described by an interacting spin model that incorporates both spin–spin coupling and anisotropy induced by a tilted magnetic field. We analyze and compare quantum Carnot and Otto cycles, showing that the Carnot cycle exhibits a universal, entropy-driven behavior with smooth phase boundaries, while the Otto cycle displays a much richer structure governed by the interplay between the energy spectrum and nonequilibrium population differences. In particular, we identify a crossover in both efficiency and coefficient of performance as a function of the interaction strength, which arises from the competition between the interaction energy scale and the magnetic field. We further demonstrate that the skew angle induces state hybridization, modifying both the energy levels and occupation probabilities. Our results highlight that interactions and anisotropy, when properly tuned, can enhance thermodynamic performance, and emphasize the importance of multi-level effects in the design of quantum thermal machines.

Article.Title: Dietary selenium intake, hypertension, and screening-defined mild cognitive impairment among older adults in Zhejiang, China: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: He M.; Zou Y.; Xu P.; Su D.; Zhao D.; Ding G.; Zhang R.
Article.Abstract: To explore association of dietary selenium intake and hypertension with screening-defined mild cognitive impairment (MCI) among community-dwelling older adults. We conducted a multicenter, cross-sectional study in 2020. The study recruited a total of 1084 community-dwelling adults aged 55 years or older from four regions across Zhejiang Province, China. The collection of study data included a range of variables: demographic profiles, evaluation of cognition using standardized scales, dietary intake using Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ), and parameters obtained from physical examinations. Of 1084 eligible participants aged 55 years or older, 1033 with complete information for the specified regression variables were included in the primary analysis. Dietary nutrients intake, including selenium, was calculated based on the converted FFQ-specific Food Composition Table. Modified Poisson regression with a log link and robust variance was used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals for the individual and joint associations of dietary selenium intake and hypertension with screening-defined MCI. Screening-defined MCI was present in 251 participants (24.3%). Compared with Q1 of dietary selenium intake, the adjusted PRs were 0.51 (95% CI 0.37–0.71) for Q2, 0.37 (95% CI 0.25–0.54) for Q3, and 0.30 (95% CI 0.18–0.50) for Q4. Hypertension was associated with a higher prevalence of screening-defined MCI (PR = 1.40, 95% CI 1.12–1.76 ). In the joint analysis, participants with hypertension and selenium intake < 100 µg/day had a higher prevalence than participants without hypertension and with intake < 100 µg/day (PR = 1.82, 95% CI 1.31–2.51). Higher dietary selenium intake was associated with a lower prevalence of screening-defined MCI, whereas hypertension was associated with a higher prevalence. In the exploratory joint analysis, the prevalence of MCI was highest among participants with hypertension and dietary selenium intake < 100 µg/day.

Article.Title: Multi-criteria ranking of open automatic speech recognition models under alternative deployment priorities
Article.Authors: Bafail O.; Miski A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automatic speech recognition (ASR) models differ in accuracy, throughput, and parameter count, so choosing a model involves trade-offs. This study ranks 69 license-eligible open ASR model configurations from the July 2026 open ASR leaderboard, which covers eight short-form English test sets. Criterion weights were derived with the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (fuzzy AHP) under three illustrative scenarios, each prioritizing one criterion: word error rate (WER), inverse real-time factor (RTFx), or parameter count. The models were then ranked with the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS). NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT-CTC-110M ranked first in the WER-prioritized scenario, and NVIDIA FastConformer-CTC-large ranked first in the other two. The sensitivity analysis tested three further ranking methods (VIKOR, MABAC, and ARAS), classical AHP and entropy weights, stronger dominance ratings, min–max normalization, 171 weight combinations, and alternative WER measures. Across the four ranking methods and three scenarios, the top rank was always held by one of three NVIDIA models: Parakeet-TDT-CTC-110M, FastConformer-CTC-Large, or Conformer-CTC-Small. Classical AHP weights produced nearly identical rankings (Spearman rank correlation of at least 0.998), and Parakeet-TDT-CTC-110M or FastConformer-CTC-Large ranked first in 163 of the 171 TOPSIS weight combinations. However, under the strongest WER priority tested, the more accurate but larger NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v2 ranked first in the WER-prioritized scenario, and ARAS favored the smallest models. The rankings are specific to this benchmark rather than validated recommendations for particular sectors, and any model’s suitability must be verified on representative audio and target hardware before deployment. The framework offers a transparent, reproducible way to compare ASR models under different deployment priorities.

Article.Title: Biochemical fingerprinting of peritoneal dialysis effluent according to PET-defined transport characteristics using FTIR spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Poonvivatchaikarn U.; Phatthanakun R.; Siriwong S.; Thumanu K.; Pechbooranin A.; Kreepala C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peritoneal equilibration test (PET) assesses peritoneal membrane transport but provides limited information on the biochemical composition of peritoneal dialysis (PD) effluent. This study used Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy to characterize effluent across PET-defined D 4 /D 0 glucose-based and peritoneal solute transport rate (PSTR) categories. In this single-center, cross-sectional study, effluent was collected from routine dialysis exchanges immediately preceding PET, rather than from the PET dwell itself, and analyzed using FTIR spectroscopy. PET was performed separately using a modified protocol with 4.25% glucose. Six predefined functional-group regions—O–H/N–H stretching, C–H stretching, amide I, amide II, C-H bending, and carbohydrate-associated vibrations—were quantified as normalized integral-area ratios and compared across transport categories. Fifty-three patients receiving continuous ambulatory PD were enrolled (mean age 55.4 ± 13.6 years; mean PD vintage 39.4 ± 30.0 months). Visual differences in mean spectral intensity were observed, with low-average and low groups generally showing higher absorbance than high-average and high groups. However, none of the six regions differed significantly among categories under either classification. These descriptive spectral patterns did not establish the ability of FTIR spectroscopy to discriminate among PET-defined transport groups. Further whole-spectrum multivariate and longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate its clinical utility.

Article.Title: Dynamic accommodative stress testing for early detection of anterior segment deformation patterns in subclinical keratoconus
Article.Authors: Başkan B.; Evcimen Y.
Article.Abstract: To investigate dynamic anterior segment alterations during accommodative effort in subclinical keratoconus (SKC) using combined Scheimpflug-Placido imaging and anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT), and to establish a dynamic stress test for early ectasia detection. In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study, 180 participants (one eye each) were allocated to three age-matched groups: bilateral subclinical keratoconus (SKC, n = 60), very asymmetric ectasia with clinically unaffected fellow eyes (VAE-NT, n = 60) and healthy controls ( n = 60). Anterior segment imaging was performed under standardised mesopic conditions at accommodative stimuli of 0, 3 and 6 D delivered through a Badal optometer. Primary outcomes were the accommodation-induced changes in anterior chamber depth (ΔACD) and maximum keratometry (ΔKmax). Two composite indices, the Dynamic Ectasia Index (DEI) and the Corneal Thickness Redistribution Index (CTRI), were derived from the present dataset after data collection and were not prespecified. At 6 D, SKC eyes deformed more than controls in every primary outcome: ΔACD − 0.114 ± 0.021 mm versus − 0.069 ± 0.015 mm, and inferotemporal curvature change 1.76 ± 0.27 D versus 0.66 ± 0.17 D (both p < 0.001). DEI separated SKC from control eyes with 98.3% sensitivity and 96.7% specificity (AUC 0.995, 95% CI 0.989–1.000), and the bivariate DEI + CTRI rule with 96.7% and 98.3%. The Belin/Ambrósio D-index reached an AUC of 1.000, but because its thresholds defined group eligibility this separation is an artefact of the sampling frame and not a measure of performance. All estimates were derived and evaluated in the same dataset and are therefore optimistic. Accommodative stress testing reveals anterior segment deformation patterns that distinguish SKC eyes from healthy controls. DEI and CTRI provide an empirically derived screening framework and should be interpreted as screening composites rather than biomechanical parameters. External validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: ASIA: adaptive single-diffusion-stage inference acceleration for diffusion-based virtual try-on
Article.Authors: Mansour S.; Elemry E.; Osman A.; Abdelwahab R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Virtual try-on synthesises an image of a person wearing a chosen garment. Diffusion models give the most realistic results, but remain too slow for interactive use. The leading method, TPD, runs its diffusion network twice: a first pass predicts a pair-specific mask locating where the garment belongs, and a second pass renders the garment into that region. Each pass takes about 100 denoising steps, so one image needs roughly 200, half of them producing only a binary shape. This first stage does not justify a diffusion model. We propose Adaptive Single-Diffusion-Stage Inference Acceleration (ASIA), which replaces diffusion-based mask generation with a lightweight convolutional network. Using DensePose and the flat garment mask as structural priors, ASIA predicts the pair-specific mask in one forward pass, reducing that stage from seconds to milliseconds. Try-on then needs a single diffusion stage, whose input block alone is finetuned to the new mask distribution. On VITON-HD, inference falls from 15.4 to 7.5 seconds per image, a 2.05-fold speedup. Under a controlled reproduction of TPD, paired structural (SSIM) and perceptual (LPIPS) similarity both improve while the Fréchet Inception Distance rises slightly (9.04 against 8.78). Removing an entire diffusion stage thus trades a small FID increase for a large speedup and improved paired fidelity.
