Article.Title: Effectiveness of a tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir (TLD)-based regimen among people with HIV-1 attending the Bamenda Regional Hospital Treatment Centre, Cameroon: a retrospective observational study
Article.Authors: Tah R.; Jingi A.; Pianta M.; Ngum E.; Bittaye S.; Ndongo F.; Donfack J.; Bissek A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Improving current and future antiretroviral treatment is crucial to ending AIDS by 2030. Treatment failure, drug toxicity and resistance remain major obstacles to durable viral suppression. In 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommended a dolutegravir-based regimen (DTG) as preferred first- and second-line antiretroviral therapy to help address these challenges. However, data on its effectiveness among people with HIV-1 (PLHIV) receiving routine care remain scarce, particularly in Central Africa. This study evaluated virologic suppression among a cohort of adherent, comorbidity-free PLHIV receiving DTG at a regional treatment centre in Cameroon. This retrospective observational study reviewed the medical records of PLHIV aged above 18 years attending the Bamenda Regional Hospital HIV Treatment Centre, who had an adherence rate of at least 95% by pill count, had no recorded comorbidities, and were receiving dolutegravir as part of combination antiretroviral therapy (cART); 99.4% of participants were specifically on tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir (TLD) and 0.6% on abacavir/lamivudine/dolutegravir. Both ART-naïve patients started on DTG-based first-line therapy and ART-experienced patients switched to a DTG-based regimen following the 2019 WHO recommendation were eligible. Eligible patients had initiated DTG-based cART between January 2020 and May 2021, early enough to have completed at least 12 months of follow-up before the close of the data-collection period in May 2022. The primary outcome was virologic suppression (< 1000 copies/mL) at 6 and 12 months, and the secondary outcome was 12-month DTG discontinuation due to a clinical switch to a non-DTG regimen. Because suppression was high (> 90%) with very few unsuppressed participants (7 at 6 months, 1 at 12 months), associations at 6 months were analyzed using crude risk ratios and Fisher’s exact tests. Multivariable adjustment was not possible, leaving the 6-month comparative analyses underpowered for small effect sizes, while formal 12-month statistical testing was omitted. Of 368 records screened, 157 participants met the eligibility criteria (105 treatment-naïve, 52 treatment-experienced) and had viral load data available at both 6 and 12 months. At 6 months, 150/157 participants (95.5%) were virologically suppressed; 7/157 (4.5%) were not. At 12 months, 156/157 participants (99.4%) were suppressed; 1/157 (0.6%) was not, and this participant was switched to a second-line regimen after confirmed virologic failure. No baseline factor examined sex, age, marital status, education, smoking, WHO clinical stage, treatment status, or HIV duration was significantly associated with 6-month suppression; given only 7 events, these null findings reflect limited statistical power rather than confirmed absence of association. Alcohol use at baseline was associated with a higher rate of 6-month suppression (risk ratio 1.14, 95% CI 1.02–1.28; Fisher’s exact p = 0.002); given the wide confidence interval, the small number of events, and the absence of adjustment for confounding, this finding should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. By 12 months (week 48), the median weight change in the study population was + 2.0 kg (interquartile range [IQR] 0 to 4). In this adherent, comorbidity-free sub-population receiving routine HIV care in Cameroon, DTG-based cART was associated with high rates of virologic suppression at both 6 months (week 24) and 12 months (week 48), in both treatment-naïve and treatment-experienced participants. Because of the selective eligibility criteria, small sample, single-centre design and short follow-up, these findings should not be generalised to the broader population in routine HIV care, and do not by themselves establish comparative or causal effectiveness relative to other regimens; they add descriptive, real-world observations to the existing trial-based evidence for DTG-based regimens in a Central African setting.

Article.Title: Electronic origin of the chromic response of Eriochrome Black T upon Co(II)/Co(III) coordination: a DFT and TD-DFT study
Article.Authors: Samandarova S.; Matrasulova N.; Eshchanov K.; Baltaeva M.; Smanova Z.; Abdullaev I.; Ibragimov S.; Bobrowski M.
Article.Abstract: Eriochrome Black T (EBT) is one of the most widely used metallochromic indicators in complexometric titrimetry, yet the electronic origin of its diagnostic blue-to-wine-red colour change upon metal coordination has not previously been established at the level of molecular orbital theory. In this work, density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations were performed at the B3LYP/6–31 + G**/CPCM(water) level, with benchmarking against the TPSSh functional, an SDD effective core potential on cobalt, and microsolvated models bearing explicit water ligands, to characterise the geometry, frontier molecular orbitals, molecular electrostatic potential, and electronic absorption spectra of EBT and its cobalt complexes. The neutral dye adopts a planar, fully trans-azo configuration (N = N = 1.268 Å) stabilized by an intramolecular O–H···N hydrogen bond that pre-organises an o, o′–O, N, O chelate pocket. Deprotonation to the analytically relevant dianion (HIn 2− ) liberates a free phenolate donor 2.70 Å from the proximal azo nitrogen, narrows the Kohn–Sham HOMO–LUMO gap from 2.72 to 2.38 eV, and concentrates negative electrostatic potential over the O, N, O pocket, indicating an enhanced electronic predisposition of the dianion toward metal coordination. The free dianion is more stable in the hydrazone tautomer by 19.1 kcal/mol, and this form reproduces the experimental maximum to within 3 nm; tridentate coordination nevertheless requires the azo tautomer, since the azo nitrogen is protonated in the hydrazone and cannot donate to the metal. TD-DFT reproduced the experimental absorption of the free dye (calculated 613 nm; blue) through a HOMO–LUMO intramolecular charge-transfer transition. Coordination of Co 2+ at the O, N, O site blue-shifts this band by 116–497 nm (wine red), reproducing the direction of the titration colour change although overestimating its magnitude relative to the measured shift of 49 nm, whereas high-spin Co 3+ produces only an 11 nm bathochromic shift, leaving the band essentially where it is in the free dye. This contrast shows that the magnitude of the chromic response depends on the oxidation state and electronic configuration of the coordinated metal, and not merely on the presence of a bound cation.

Article.Title: Context-less lightweight phishing domain detection for mobile and edge devices via INT8-quantized low-parameter transformer classifiers
Article.Authors: Narayan Y.; Jain A.; Dubey A.; Vishwakarma D.; Kaur A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mobile devices constitute the front door for billions of users to gain access to the internet, but are also extremely susceptible to phishing attacks launched via adversarial domain creation. The current transformer based Domain classifiers provide high accuracy, but have a large number of parameters more than 86.9 M, which is too large for edge devices with memory and battery constraints. We propose a context-less phishing detection framework which classifies domains based on the analysis of only the domain string itself, avoiding the risk of downloading malicious page content, and saving network bandwidth. All 4 variants of the lightweight transformer classifiers: PhishNet-10M, PhishNet-20M, PhishNet-45M and PhishNet-85M are trained and evaluated, with INT8 post training quantization for maximum edge efficiency. Validation with early stopping up to 20 epochs of training shows that the INT8 quantized version of the PhishNet-10M model achieves a validation accuracy of 95.72% and PhishNet-85M model achieves a validation accuracy of 96.20%. The 10.8 M (PhishNet-10M) configuration represents an ideal point of deployment. We benchmark all PhishNet variants against established sequence models (LSTM, GRU, CNN) and strong distilled transformer baselines (TinyBERT), demonstrating superior accuracy and efficiency for resource-constrained mobile and IoT edge devices.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: INT8 quantization; mobile devices; post-training quantization; resource-constrained deployment; edge devices

Article.Title: Clinically interpretable video-derived movement quality metrics for rehabilitation monitoring in breast cancer survivors
Article.Authors: Chung S.; Yang E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Markerless motion analysis enables quantitative extraction of movement information from standard video recordings; however, the measurement properties of video-derived movement metrics in cancer rehabilitation remain uncertain. This study was a secondary measurement-property analysis of data collected within a prospective, multicenter randomized wait-list controlled trial and included 71 breast cancer survivors from seven university hospitals in Korea. Four ReMAP-derived metrics were evaluated: mediolateral sway, trajectory variability, lateral correction rate, and energy ratio. Within-session task-segment consistency varied across metrics, with lateral correction rate showing the highest ICC (0.94, 95% CI 0.92–0.96) and mediolateral sway the lowest (0.17, 95% CI 0.04–0.30). Baseline associations with conventional rehabilitation outcomes were generally weak; the strongest association with TUG was observed for lateral correction rate (ρ = 0.353, p = 0.003). In baseline-adjusted analyses, trajectory variability (adjusted difference=-20.92, 95% CI -30.34 to -11.50, p < 0.001; d = 0.64) and energy ratio (-12.80, 95% CI -21.27 to -4.33, p = 0.003; d = 0.50) showed between-group differences in change. These findings indicate heterogeneous measurement properties and limited cross-domain overlap in this sample, but do not establish construct independence, complementary clinical utility, longitudinal test–retest reliability, or individual-level monitoring capability. Further validation using independently repeated acquisitions, external anchors, and reference biomechanical measurements is required.

Article.Title: Associations between sleep regularity indexed from wearable device data and mental health symptoms in the TemPredict longitudinal cohort study
Article.Authors: Soltani S.; Hartogensis W.; Dilchert S.; Hecht F.; Smarr B.; Mason A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Sleep Regularity Index (SRI) is an emerging sleep metric associated with health outcomes. We tested whether SRI derived from wearable device data correlated with self-reported depression, anxiety, and loneliness symptoms cross-sectionally in the TemPredict Study ( N = 22,894). We computed SRI using all available days with sufficient data ( All Days ) and a 7-day period before COVID-related restrictions ( Typical Week ). We used t -tests to compare SRI across mental health severity categories and logistic regression to estimate odds of worse severity before and after covariate adjustment. Lower SRI was associated with greater depression, anxiety, and loneliness severity in a graded pattern. In All Days analyses, mean SRI was lower among participants with severe depression (74.93 vs. 83.74; p <.0001), severe anxiety (78.94 vs. 83.67; p <.0001), and elevated loneliness (81.79 vs. 83.75; p <.0001) than within normal limits. Standardized effect sizes comparing SRI in participants with mild/moderate/severe mental health symptoms to those within normal limits were − 0.18 to -1.32 (depression), -0.13 to -0.69 (anxiety), and − 0.27 (loneliness). Logistic models showed greater odds of greater symptom severity per 5-point SRI decrease. Results were similar for Typical Week analyses. Sleep regularity metrics derived from wearable devices may represent modifiable risk factors to be evaluated in intervention studies.

Article.Title: MODWT-driven explainable spatio-temporal IDS for securing EV charging infrastructures
Article.Authors: Subran A.; Sankaran S.; Venkitasubramaniam P.; Achuthan K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid deployment of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCS) has introduced significant cybersecurity challenges, as these infrastructures are increasingly targeted by adversaries seeking to disrupt charging services, manipulate billing, or compromise user privacy. Conventional intrusion detection systems often fail to detect attacks due to the dynamic and non-linear nature of EVCS power consumption data. To address this, we propose a Host-based Intrusion Detection System (HIDS) integrating Maximum Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT) feature extraction with deep learning architectures – LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and ModWaveMLP- to enable multi-resolution analysis of power consumption signals, effectively decomposing consumption patterns to reveal subtle anomalies overlooked in raw time-series data. Explainable AI techniques such as SHAP and LIME are incorporated to interpret model decisions with quantified stability, fidelity, and sparsity metrics. Experimental evaluation on the CICEVSE2024 dataset demonstrates that the GRU combined with db1 wavelet decomposition achieves the highest AUC of 0.9937, representing a 38.9% point improvement over baseline models without wavelet preprocessing. A comprehensive ablation study confirms SMOTE as the optimal class imbalance strategy, achieving 0.9945 AUC compared to 0.9738 for class-weighted training, establishing a transparent, wavelet-driven IDS framework tailored for next-generation EV charging infrastructure security.

Article.Title: Occurrence patterns, disinfectant-source water interactions, and multi-dimensional health risk assessment of DBPs in a province in northwest China
Article.Authors: Yang W.; Ning L.; Pu D.; Zhe W.; Liu Y.; Li J.; Wusiman K.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the distribution characteristics and occurrence patterns of drinking water disinfection by-products (DBPs) in a province in northwest China, analyzed the interactive effects of disinfection processes and water source types on DBP formation, and conducted multi-dimensional population health risk assessments stratified by age and gender. Significant differences in DBPs concentrations were found across seasons, water sources, regions, and disinfection methods. TCM and TBM varied widely, while other DBPs remained stable. High-purity chlorine dioxide yielded notably low THM levels, whereas liquid chlorine produced DCAA and TCAA at 21.00 µg/L and 12.00 µg/L 6–10 times higher than other techniques. Disinfection methods and water sources interacted strongly: high-purity chlorine dioxide and bleaching powder reduced THM/HAA formation in surface water, while liquid chlorine increased BDCM and DCAA risks. Sodium hypochlorite best controlled DBPs in groundwater, though other methods aggravated TCM/DBCM accumulation. DBCM posed risks to 2–3-year-olds and adults, while BDCM, DCAA, and TCAA were carcinogenic across all ages (higher in females). All hazard indices were < 1, indicating no non-carcinogenic risk. Disinfection patterns and water-source types exerted prominent interactive effects. High-purity chlorine dioxide may reduce THM and HAA risks for surface-water supplies, and sodium hypochlorite could be considered for groundwater in the studied province of Northwest China. Carcinogenic risks of individual DBPs varied among populations, and combined exposure to DBPs may bring potential carcinogenic hazards. No obvious non-carcinogenic risks were observed for all DBPs under this study’s exposure levels.

Article.Title: Foliar biostimulants with nano-chelated Zn-B-Si reduce rind disorders and improve yield and fruit quality in ‘Washington’ Navel orange
Article.Authors: Munir M.; Alrashidi A.; Ghattas H.; Ramadan K.; Ali S.; Saad R.
Article.Abstract: Preharvest rind disorders, particularly fruit cracking and creasing, are major causes of yield loss and export downgrading in ‘Washington’ Navel orange. These disorders are associated with impaired peel calcium, boron, and silicon nutrition, cell-wall degradation, and rind turgor imbalance. Although biostimulants and nano-nutrients have shown individual benefits in fruit crops, their combined effectiveness against citrus rind disorders has not been systematically evaluated or compared with the industry-standard Ca + GA₃ program. This two-season field study (2024–2025) evaluated melatonin, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and 24-epibrassinolide (EBR), applied individually or combined with a nano-chelated Zn-B-Si formulation, together with a standalone nano-silicon treatment and the conventional Ca + GA₃ program in a randomized complete block design. GABA + nano (Zn-B-Si) (T10) ranked first for most traits, and EBR + nano (Zn-B-Si) (T9) was statistically comparable to it for several traits (e.g., fruit number, fruit set and chlorophyll). Both combinations generally surpassed their individual applications and the conventional Ca + GA₃ standard in vegetative growth, yield and fruit quality across both seasons. T10 reduced fruit cracking by up to 65.5%, creasing by up to 66.8% and fruit drop by up to 53% compared with the untreated control. Biostimulant–nanonutrient co-application, particularly GABA combined with nano-chelated Zn-B-Si, is a promising candidate strategy for reducing rind-disorder incidence and improving yield and fruit quality in ‘Washington’ Navel orange. Costs, total active-ingredient input and packinghouse grading outcomes were not assessed and require further study.

Article.Title: Advancing Grammar Error Correction in informal digital communication: a hybrid CNN-BART approach with adaptive noise modeling
Article.Authors: Kehkashan T.; Abdullah M.; Al-Shamayleh A.; Ahmed N.; Shahzad M.; Elsaed M.; Ahmed A.; Ahmad S.; Akhunzada A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Grammar Error Correction (GEC) has emerged as a critical natural language processing task with applications in educational technology, automated proofreading, and digital communication enhancement. Although current transformer-based methods have shown remarkable results in formal textual settings, they struggle to handle the linguistic diversity and situational ambiguity of informal digital communication, including purposeful abbreviations, code-switching, and intentional grammatical violations. This study presents a hybrid CNN-BART model that effectively merges local pattern recognition with transformer-based contextual understanding for robust text error correction. The proposed system integrates curriculum-based noise injection, multi-scale convolutional encoding, and a comprehensive feature selection pipeline to address the challenges of informal text processing. Experimental validation on three benchmark datasets demonstrates consistent absolute $$F_{0.5}$$ improvements of $$+6.5$$ points over Pillars of GEC on CoNLL-2014, $$+10.5$$ points over T5 on ErAConD, and $$+2.4$$ points over Pillars of GEC on BEA-2019, representing statistically significant advances ( $$p < 0.05$$ , bootstrap resampling, 95% CI). This work offers a practical framework for automated writing assistance in both academic and industry contexts.

Article.Title: Deep neutrosophic-embedded fusion-based deep learning for underwater benthic substrate classification
Article.Authors: Fernando N.; Seneviratne L.; Weerasinghe N.; Rathnayake N.; Hoshino Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning based benthic substrate mapping is essential for large scale marine monitoring and automated seafloor analysis. However, model performance degrades in real underwater environments due to noise, mixed substrates, overlapping classes, variations in depth, illumination, and sensing conditions. Conventional deep learning models typically assume clean, well separated classes. When applied to real world classification and mapping tasks, their accuracy decreases, resulting in high misclassifications rates. This highlights their difficulty in effectively representing uncertainty and ambiguity in benthic imagery which leads to increased misclassification. To address this limitation, we propose a Deep Neutrosophic-embedded Fusion framework for uncertainty-aware benthic classification. The proposed approach explicitly models truth, indeterminacy, and falsity within deep feature representations and is integrated convolution-based, state-space-based, and Transformer-based architectures, demonstrating its adaptability across fundamentally different feature learning paradigms. Specifically, we introduce a learnable deep Neutrosophic fusion strategy implemented in intermediate level of the deep learning architectures, that applies uncertainty-aware gating directly at the patch level feature representation stage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Neutrosophic framework consistently improves the performance of convolution-based (ResNet18), state-space-based (Mamba), and Transformer-based (SAEViT) architectures, demonstrating its adaptability across fundamentally different feature learning paradigms. Among the evaluated models, N-SAEViT achieved the largest relative improvement over its corresponding baseline, increasing the test accuracy from 80.72% to 97.60% (20.91%), whereas N-ResNet18 achieved the highest absolute predictive performance, including the highest test accuracy, Macro-F1 score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). N-Mamba also improved its baseline performance, demonstrating the adaptability of the proposed framework across diverse backbone architectures. Correlation analysis further revealed that $$H_{\text {mean}}$$ , $$Edge_{\text {density}}$$ , and $$LBP_{\text {energy}}$$ provide complementary color, structural, and texture information, improving class separability under uncertainty and demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed deep Neutrosophic fusion framework for robust benthic substrate classification.

Article.Title: Improving rock fragmentation in rock blasting through geomechanical-based burden prediction
Article.Authors: Hasanipanah M.; Rezaei M.
Article.Abstract: Rock fragmentation is a key determinant of blasting efficiency, excavation productivity, and downstream processing costs in mining and civil engineering. Achieving optimal fragmentation depends strongly on accurate burden ( B ) selection, yet B estimation remains challenging because of the complex interactions between rock-mass characteristics and blasting behavior. Previous studies have demonstrated the feasibility of using geomechanical parameters for B prediction; however, their integration with optimized ensemble learning, uncertainty quantification, and model interpretability remains insufficiently explored. To address this gap, this study develops a hybrid machine-learning framework for predicting B using rock blastability index ( BI ), rock quality designation ( RQD ), unconfined compressive strength ( UCS ), density ( D ), and cohesive strength ( C ). Extremely Randomized Trees (ERT) were optimized using four metaheuristic algorithms: Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO), and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Among the developed models, ERT-GWO achieved the highest prediction accuracy and the lowest prediction uncertainty on the available testing dataset. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified C as the most influential parameter, followed by RQD and UCS , highlighting the importance of geomechanical properties for B estimation. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of an accurate and interpretable decision-support approach for B estimation under the geological and operational conditions represented by the Mouteh dataset. However, its applicability to other geological and mining environments requires external validation using larger and geographically diverse datasets.

Article.Title: Effects of mimicry style, identity positioning, and description style on trust and usage intention in AI pet healthcare platforms
Article.Authors: Qian T.; Li Y.; Liu T.; Zhang D.; Zhang N.
Article.Abstract: With the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence applications in the field of pet healthcare, AI pet medical platforms have gradually become important tools for pet health management. However, in contexts characterized by high emotional involvement and high uncertainty, users’ trust in and adoption of such platforms still face significant challenges. Based on trust calibration theory, uncertainty management theory, and the Computers Are Social Actors paradigm, this study adopts a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design to examine the effects of mimicry style (anthropomorphic design versus zoomorphic design), identity positioning (expert-authoritative versus friendly-companion), and description style (lay terminology versus professional terminology) on users’ cognitive trust, affective attachment, and usage intention. A total of 400 valid samples were collected, and the hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance and mediation analysis. The results indicate that zoomorphic design significantly enhances affective attachment and usage intention and exerts a partial mediating effect on usage intention through affective attachment and cognitive trust. Expert-authoritative identity positioning significantly increases cognitive trust and usage intention, whereas the mediating role of affective attachment is not significant. Descriptive style shows no significant direct effect on usage intention, but professional terminology exerts a mediating effect on usage intention through cognitive trust. In addition, a significant interaction effect is found between mimicry style and identity positioning. The findings suggest that user adoption of AI pet medical platforms is jointly driven by both affective and cognitive pathways, with cognitive trust playing a more central role in high-risk decision-making contexts. This study extends the application of the Computers Are Social Actors paradigm and trust calibration theory in the pet healthcare context and provides practical implications for the interface and communication design of AI pet medical platforms.

Article.Title: Nutrient dynamics and bioremediation potential of lignocellulosic biomatrix in climbing perch aquaculture systems
Article.Authors: Padhan S.; Waikhom G.; Singh S.; Debbarma R.; Debbarma S.; Biswas P.; Paul T.
Article.Abstract: Cultivating climbing perch, Anabas testudineus , in culture ponds has often linked with eutrophication. Inorganic nitrogen and phosphorus are the major drivers of algal proliferation in such environments. The objective of this study was to assess the use of coconut coir pith, rice husk, and their composite blend (40:60 ratio) as biomatrix in climbing perch ( A. testudineus ) culture systems, with the aim of improving water quality, managing nutrient accumulation, and enhancing fish growth and survival. The experiment followed completely randomized designed comprised of three treatments: 50 mg L − 1 coconut coir pith, 50mg L − 1 rice husk, and the 50mg L − 1 composite mixture, and a control without the addition of any biomatrix with three replicate each. Advanced fingerlings (average weight = 50.61 g ± 0.19) were introduced into cement tanks at a density of 10 m − 2 and were provided with commercial feeds containing 32% protein. Water quality parameters were recorded at 15 days interval. Growth, survivability, feed utilization and haematological indices were recorded at the end of the experiment. The result showed that combined biomatrix (coconut coir pith + rice husk) significantly reduced nutrient accumulation ( p < 0.05), with total ammonia, nitrate and phosphate level 0.46 ± 0.00 mg L⁻¹,0.17 ± 0.00 b mg L⁻¹, and 0.26 ± 0.01 c mg L⁻¹respectively. This treatment achieved the highest specific growth rate 1.59 ± 0.06% d⁻¹, with 96 ± 0.00% survivability and an improved apparent feed conversion ratio of 0.96 ± 0.04 ( p < 0.05).In addition, plasma glucose levels were significantly reduced p < 0.05), indicating improved physiological condition. This study demonstrates that the composite biomatrix of coconut coir pith and rice husk is an effective and sustainable nutrient management strategy. It significantly reduces eutrophication risks, improves water quality, and enhances fish growth and survival, making semi-intensive climbing perch culture systems more productive and eco-friendly.

Article.Title: Reef resilience and demise on the NW shelf of Australia during the warm Miocene
Article.Authors: Petrick B.; Reuning L.; Bialik O.; Schwark L.; Pfeiffer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract During the Miocene, sea surface temperature (SSTs) and CO 2 exceeded modern levels. Given the current decline of coral reefs due to rising summer temperatures, it is unclear how extensive reef systems developed and thrived in a warm Miocene world. This problem is exacerbated by a lack of SST reconstructions. Here, we use TEX 86 H to reconstruct summer SSTs between 5.0 and 17.4 Ma from a sediment core (IODP Site U1464) within the Miocene NW Australian shelf Barrier Reef system. During the Miocene Climate Optimum, summer SSTs reached up to 34 °C. However, stable arid conditions and low subsidence rates allowed the reef to expand. Around 6 Ma, SSTs were ideal for coral reef growth, but increased terrestrial input and subsidence caused the relatively rapid collapse of almost all reefs. Multiple environmental stressors culminated in reef drowning. Therefore, a barrier reef system formed at > 30 °C SSTs, but this was only possible under otherwise ideal conditions.

Article.Title: A blockchain-secured multi-agent GNN–XGBoost framework for intelligent energy coordination in IoT-enabled sustainable smart grids
Article.Authors: Kommerla S.; Bhukya B.; Kuchibhatla S.; Vaadaala V.; Munaganuri R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing deployment of distributed energy resources and intelligent devices has transformed conventional power networks into highly decentralized smart grid ecosystems. While this evolution offers significant opportunities for improving energy efficiency and sustainability, it also introduces challenges related to real-time energy coordination, dynamic load balancing, secure data exchange, and adaptive decision-making. Traditional energy management approaches often struggle to capture complex interactions among interconnected grid components and are limited in their ability to respond effectively to rapidly changing operating conditions. To address these challenges, this paper presents an intelligent energy management framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, blockchain-enabled security, multi-agent coordination, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), and XGBoost-based predictive analytics. In the proposed architecture, distributed agents representing energy producers, consumers, and prosumers collaborate to monitor grid conditions and exchange operational information. The GNN module learns structural relationships among interconnected nodes, enabling a comprehensive understanding of network dynamics. Based on the extracted graph representations, the XGBoost model supports efficient decision-making for energy dispatch, demand response, and load distribution. A blockchain layer is incorporated to ensure data integrity, transparency, and trust among participating entities without relying on centralized control. The proposed framework is evaluated in a smart city energy environment using integrated simulation and edge-computing platforms. Experimental analysis demonstrates its capability to improve energy coordination, enhance system adaptability, reduce transmission inefficiencies, and support secure decentralized operation. The findings indicate that the proposed approach provides a reliable and scalable solution for sustainable smart grid management, contributing to the development of resilient and energy-efficient urban infrastructures.

Article.Title: A two-stage waveform-driven cross-differential protection scheme for PV-integrated parallel transmission lines
Article.Authors: Hojjatoleslami A.; Sadeghkhani I.
Article.Abstract: The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation in modern power systems introduces significant challenges to the protection of parallel transmission lines, primarily due to limited and highly variable fault current characteristics. Conventional cross-differential relay (CDR) schemes provide fast and selective protection for parallel transmission lines, but their reliance on current-magnitude comparison can limit their discrimination capability in PV-integrated systems. An enhanced CDR approach has addressed this limitation by incorporating remote-end voltage information to estimate the grid-voltage angle. However, this estimation relies on voltage measurement at the PV bus, the line impedance, and the equivalent grid impedance determined using voltage and current measurements at the grid bus. To address these measurement requirements, this paper proposes a two-stage waveform-driven cross-differential protection scheme for PV-integrated parallel transmission lines that relies solely on the currents of the parallel lines measured at the PV bus. In the first stage, internal fault detection is achieved using a normalized cross-correlation (NCC)-based fault detection index that captures waveform similarity between parallel line currents, thereby reducing the dependence on current amplitude under challenging operating conditions. In the second stage, faulty line identification is performed using the polarity of the fault-imposed positive-sequence current extracted via a delta filtering approach, enabling reliable direction-sensitive decision-making without requiring voltage measurements or communication links. The proposed method is extensively evaluated on a modified IEEE 39-bus system under diverse scenarios, including high-resistance faults, measurement noise, line parameter asymmetry, varying fault inception angles, PV generation intermittency, grid-code compliant reactive power support, and external faults. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves fast, robust, and accurate fault detection and identification across a wide range of operating conditions.

Article.Title: Effect of a multicomponent perioperative education and support program on adaptation after hysterectomy a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Amouseni Z.; Khalesi Z.; Rahnavardi M.; Maroufizadeh S.
Article.Abstract: Hysterectomy is one of the most frequently performed major gynecological procedures for benign uterine conditions. Although advances in surgical techniques have improved preoperative safety, many women continue to experience challenges in physical, psychological, social, and functional recovery after surgery. This study evaluated whether a structured multicomponent perioperative education and support program was associated with improved post hysterectomy adaptation. This parallel-group randomized controlled trial enrolled 62 women undergoing elective hysterectomy for benign gynecological conditions at a tertiary referral hospital in Rasht, Iran. Participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to receive either routine preoperative care alone (n = 31) or routine care plus a structured multicomponent perioperative education and support program consisting of three individualized face-to-face educational sessions, a standardized educational booklet, and weekly telephone follow-up for eight weeks after surgery (n = 31). The specified primary outcome was post hysterectomy adaptation, measured eight weeks after surgery using the validated Persian version of the Hysterectomy Adaptation Scale (HAS). Between-group comparisons were performed using appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistical methods according to data distribution. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between groups. At eight weeks after surgery, participants receiving a structured multicomponent perioperative education and support program had significantly higher post hysterectomy adaptation scores than those receiving routine care (mean ± SD, 76.2 ± 5.5 vs. 47.3 ± 4.7), corresponding to a mean difference of 28.9 points (95% CI, 26.3–31.5; P < 0.001). Improvements were consistently observed across all six HAS domains, including activity/rest pattern, psychological status, marital relationship, emotional communication, role performance, and urinary function (all P < 0.001). The standardized between-group effect size for the primary outcome was large (Cohen’s d = 5.65). A structured multicomponent perioperative education and support program was associated with higher post hysterectomy adaptation scores than routine preoperative care among women undergoing hysterectomy for benign conditions. However, because the intervention combined educational and supportive components, participant blinding was not feasible, outcomes were self-reported, and an attention matched compactor was not included, the independent contribution of individual intervention components cannot be determined. Moreover, the exceptionally large observed effect size likely reflects the combined effect of the multi component intervention package plus nonspecific contact effects (e.g., increased professional attention and therapeutic interaction), and therefore warrants cautious interpretation. Confirmation in adequately powered multi center randomized controlled trials with longer follow-up and attention matched control groups is required before definitive conclusions regarding effectiveness can be drawn. Trial Registration Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20250701066314N1); prospectively registered.

Article.Title: Floristic and ecological diversity of vascular plants in the Cherat region, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
Article.Authors: Ullah K.; Majeed A.; E.Mahmoud E.; Ahmad B.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the floristic and ecological diversity of vascular plants in the Cherat region of Tehsil Pabbi, District Nowshera, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Seasonal field surveys were conducted from November 2023 to September 2024 across ecologically contrasting habitats, and collected specimens were identified using standard taxonomic references and herbarium protocols. Ecological characterization was performed using habitat distribution, life-form, leaf-size, lamina, and growth-habit spectra, and chi-square goodness-of-fit tests were applied to evaluate differences in categorical patterns. A total of 177 plant species belonging to 46 families were recorded, including 174 angiosperms (98.31%) and 3 pteridophytes (1.69%). Poaceae was the most species-rich family (15.82%), followed by Asteraceae (12.43%), Brassicaceae (8.47%), Papilionaceae (7.34%), and Lamiaceae (5.65%). Habitat analysis showed that 123 species (69.49%) occurred in dry habitats, 33 species (18.64%) in wet habitats, and 21 species (11.86%) in both habitat types, with the distribution differing significantly from an equal expectation (χ 2 = 105.36, df = 2, p < 0.001). Therophytes were the dominant life form (50.28%; χ 2 = 256.58, df = 7, p < 0.001), while nanophylls (42.37%) and microphylls (32.20%) dominated the leaf-size spectrum (χ 2 = 205.39, df = 6, p < 0.001). Simple lamina (76.84%; χ 2 = 256.24, df = 3, p < 0.001) and herbaceous growth habit (77.97%; χ 2 = 270.12, df = 3, p < 0.001) were also predominant. These findings show that the flora of Cherat is strongly structured by semi-arid conditions, seasonal stress, disturbance, and habitat heterogeneity. The study provides a novel ecological baseline by integrating floristic inventory with habitat-specific and trait-based analysis, and offers useful reference data for biodiversity conservation, habitat monitoring, restoration planning, and future ecological research in semi-arid regions of Pakistan.

Article.Title: Load-following control based on extended point kinetic model for VVER-1200 reactor
Article.Authors: Salman A.; Elkhatib H.; Roman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an extended control-oriented framework for load-following operation of a VVER-1200 reactor, incorporating cladding temperature as an explicit dynamic state within a coupled neutronic–thermal model. The proposed formulation enhances conventional point kinetics approaches by enabling direct monitoring of the fuel–cladding–coolant thermal interactions, thereby improving the physical resolution of reactor transient behavior. The system is evaluated under three progressively demanding load-following power ramps (0.1%/s, 0.2%/s, and 0.25%/s). A state observer is employed to reconstruct unmeasured states, enabling implementation of an LQR-based full-state feedback controller without requiring complete direct measurement of all internal variables. The closed-loop performance is assessed in terms of power tracking, thermal response, and control rod dynamics. The model is verified against the nonlinear six-group point-kinetics formulation, VVER-1200 design data and published steady-state core thermal-hydraulic results, and it is compared quantitatively with the conventional two-node formulation. A sensitivity analysis further quantifies the effects of uncertainties in gap conductance, reactivity coefficients and control-rod worth and of the control-rod speed limit. Simulation results demonstrate stable and consistent performance across all scenarios, with maximum power overshoot reaching 8.9% under the most aggressive transient. Corresponding fuel temperature deviations reach 5.49%, while cladding temperature deviations are captured explicitly with peak values of 0.0086%, 0.16%, and 1.19% across the three ramps. The control rod drive system remains within its physical limit of 2 cm/s, although saturation is observed under high ramp rates, indicating actuator-limited operation during severe transients. The results confirm strong coupling between neutronic power and thermal response, while highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling cladding dynamics for improved assessment of thermal margins. The proposed framework provides a more detailed and physically consistent representation of reactor behavior under load-following conditions, supporting enhanced safety-oriented analysis and operational flexibility in pressurized water reactors.

Article.Title: Design of a novel dual-source III–V material-based junctionless line TFET for performance assessment
Article.Authors: Mubarak N.; Loan S.; Bansal D.; Afzal N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a dual-source III–V material-based junctionless line TFET (III–V JL-LTFET) aimed at improving device performance. The incorporation of a dual-source configuration increases the effective tunneling area, which enhances the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) probability and boosts the ON-state current. Furthermore, the junctionless configuration is employed to eliminate the requirement for abrupt doping profiles, thereby reducing fabrication complexity while mitigating random dopant fluctuations (RDFs). To boost the ON-state current while simultaneously suppressing the ambipolar current, a heterojunction design is implemented using narrow-bandgap GaSb at the source and wider-bandgap GaAs for the channel and drain regions.The results demonstrate that the proposed III–V JL-LTFET achieves an ON-state current (I ON ) of 7.22 × 10 − 6 A/µm, an I ON /I OFF ratio of 1.32 × 10 12 with an average subthreshold swing (AVSS) of 13.21 mV/dec at V GS = 0.5 V. Additionally, the device exhibits promising radio-frequency (RF) characteristics, including a transconductance (gm) of 40 µS, a cut-off frequency ( f T ) of 5.87 GHz, a gain-bandwidth product (GBW) of 1.16 GHz, and a transconductance–frequency product (TFP) of 32.6 GHz.

Article.Title: Differences in sugar satiety and short neuropeptide F signalling correlate with foraging specialization in honey bees
Article.Authors: Arenas A.; Roldán M.; Estivalis J.; de Brito Sanchez M.; Farina W.
Article.Abstract: Nutritional physiology plays a critical role in division of labour in honey bees, yet the mechanisms linking carbohydrate satiation and short neuropeptide F (sNPF) signalling to its foraging specialization remain unclear. Here, we assessed sugar satiety in nectar and pollen foragers before and after collecting their preferred resource, and examined its association with sNPF signalling by topically applying exogenous short neuropeptide F (sNPF) and quantifying brain expression of sNPF, sNPF receptor (sNPFR) and NPF . Nectar foragers ingested more sucrose upon arrival than upon departure from the food source, whereas pollen foragers showed similar ingestion levels. Nectar foragers required lower sNPF doses than pollen foragers to alter ingestion. At a lower dose, sNPF treatment increased the volume of sucrose ingested by nectar foragers captured at the end of the visit and extended the visit duration, with no detectable effect on pollen foraging. Expression of NPF and sNPFR was higher in arriving than in departing foragers. Furthermore, sNPFR expression level was higher in nectar foragers than in pollen foragers. Altogether, these findings suggest that dynamic regulation of internal sugar satiety via sNPF signalling underlies foraging motivation and specialization in honey bees.

Article.Title: Interpretable fuzzy decision stability modeling for decision engineering under measurement and benchmark uncertainty
Article.Authors: Rustam N/A.; Usman K.; Bordin C.; Iftikhar A.; Alsmadi H.; Fuad A.; Sani A.; Darem A.; Alhashmi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fuzzy decisions may vary with measurement errors and admissible benchmark choices, including thresholds, weights, membership shapes, and aggregation rules. Existing fuzzy uncertainty representations and post-hoc sensitivity analyses do not generally certify decision invariance under their joint variation. This study proposes Benchmark-Multiverse Robustness-Certified Fuzzy Learning (BM-RCFL), integrating benchmark-conditioned fuzzy inference, conservative class-score bounds, object-level robustness certification, fragility diagnostics, and safe benchmark pruning. The evaluated implementation uses a fixed prototype-based reference model rather than end-to-end certificate-aware training. On synthetic data, BM-RCFL achieved an accuracy of $$1.0000$$ , a mean certified radius of $$0.3538$$ , and a certified decision rate of $$99.29\%$$ at $$\rho _i \ge 0.20$$ . On a Statistics Indonesia welfare panel with constructed reference classes, reference agreement was $$0.6404$$ , the mean certified radius was $$0.2028$$ , and $$57.02\%$$ of cases met the same threshold. No sampled perturbations within the certified regions changed decisions, providing an empirical implementation-consistency check rather than a mathematical proof. Full-enumeration verification using the same conservative bounds produced identical certificates, while benchmark pruning accelerated certification by factors of $$1.93$$ and $$3.14$$ on the respective datasets. Adversarial search identified decision reversals beyond the certified regions, and sensitivity analyses demonstrated dependence on benchmark widths and perturbation-metric scaling. BM-RCFL therefore provides an interpretable, assumption-dependent decision-stability assessment rather than a guarantee of decision correctness.

Article.Title: Quantum gate optimization in hybrid neural networks for deepfake audio detection
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Khan W.; Siddiqa A.; Ul Haq Q.
Article.Abstract: Audio deepfakes challenge automated authenticity assessment and motivate the investigation of hybrid quantum-classical approaches to speech classification. This study evaluates quantum-circuit design for deepfake audio detection through gate-configuration screening, finite-shot inference analysis, resource estimation, and qubit-scaling experiments. In the exploratory configuration screening of 5 gates, CNOT+S achieved the highest screening score and was subsequently incorporated into a five-qubit Hybrid Quantum-classical Neural Network (HQNN). Across five initialization seeds on DEEP-VOICE, the HQNN achieved \(98.77\%\pm 0.38\%\) accuracy and Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC-AUC) of \(0.9985\pm 0.0011\) , compared with \(95.98\%\pm 0.85\%\) and \(0.9927\pm 0.0014\) , respectively, for a closely parameter-matched classical Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Zero-shot transfer to ASVspoof 2019 was poor, whereas ASVspoof-specific training produced comparable HQNN and CNN discrimination. Under simulated finite-shot measurement sampling, inference at 100–10,000 shots remained close to analytic expectation-value inference. Logical resource analysis showed rapidly increasing generic amplitude-state-preparation requirements with qubit count, and a controlled five-seed expansion from five to ten qubits did not improve mean classification performance. These results characterize gate-level design, measurement sensitivity, and resource–performance trade-offs in simulated hybrid quantum-classical deepfake audio classification.

Article.Title: Advanced exergy analysis of a low GWP propane and ethane cascade refrigeration system for cold thermal energy storage applications
Article.Authors: Zadeh A.; Maghsoudniazi M.; Alfilh R.; Kholiyarov E.; Sardor S.; Salavat A.
Article.Abstract: Cold thermal energy storage applications at very low temperatures require a refrigeration unit that can provide cooling efficiently while limiting the environmental effect of the working fluids. This study evaluates the refrigeration subsystem of a cascade vapor compression system using propane (R290) in the high temperature cycle and ethane (R170) in the low temperature cycle. The analysis is performed under steady state conditions using energy, exergy, and advanced exergy methods. The base case uses a 5 kW cooling load and an evaporation temperature of − 80 °C. The real operating case gives a coefficient of performance (COP) of 0.6035, total power input of 8.285 kW, and total exergy destruction of 6.671 kW. The compressors account for 2.350 kW, or 35.2% of the total exergy destruction, followed by the cascade heat exchanger with 1.600 kW, or 24%. The unavoidable and ideal cases give COP values of 1.044 and 1.71, respectively. The selected refrigerants have zero ozone depletion potential and very low global warming potential. The present model evaluates the refrigeration cycle that can be coupled with a cold thermal energy storage unit; transient charging, discharging, storage sizing, and storage material behavior are outside the scope of this work. The results therefore identify improvement priorities for the refrigeration subsystem rather than the dynamic performance of a complete storage system.

Article.Title: Structural phase transition and breakdown of monoclinic tridymite as a new shock indicator from shock recovery experiments on eucrite
Article.Authors: Kanemaru R.; Yamaguchi A.; Yusa H.; Mikouchi T.; Miyahara M.; Kimura M.; Imae N.; Yamazaki S.; Fujioka S.; Honda R.; Ishii A.; Koike M.; Usui T.; Abe M.; Kobayashi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Shock-induced progressive changes in petrological and mineralogical features observed in laboratory shock recovery experiments provide important constraints on the shock histories of meteorites. In this study, we investigated the response of MC (monoclinic) tridymite to dynamic shock compression using cathodoluminescence imaging combined with Raman spectroscopy. Although tridymite modifications have been reported as accessory minerals in various meteorite groups, their formation processes remain poorly understood. Shock recovery experiments were conducted on the basaltic eucrite NWA 15,289, which contains MC tridymite as the dominant tridymite modification, using a single-stage propellant gun at pressures ranging from 10.9 to 30.4 GPa. At relatively low shock pressures (~ 10–16 GPa), MC tridymite partially transformed into MX (monoclinic-X, incommensurate monoclinic) and PO (pseudo-orthorhombic) tridymite. At pressures exceeding ~ 20 GPa, MC tridymite began to transform into silica glass (i.e., diaplectic tridymite glass), and the transformation was nearly complete at ~ 30 GPa. These results provide experimental evidence that tridymite modifications may serve as new indicators for evaluating the shock degrees of meteorites.

Article.Title: Flexible negative-pressure suction ureteral access sheath-assisted flexible ureteroscopy for renal stones in patients with initially positive preoperative urine cultures
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Xu B.
Article.Abstract: Patients with renal stones and an initially positive preoperative urine culture have increased infection risk during flexible ureteroscopy. We assessed associations between a flexible negative-pressure suction ureteral access sheath and stone-free outcomes, intrarenal pressure, complications, and cultures. Adults treated from August 2022 to August 2025 were screened retrospectively. After introduction in January 2024, concurrent cases were propensity-score matched 1:1 by surgeon and calendar half-year, yielding 173 pairs. Surgery followed susceptibility-guided antimicrobials and a negative repeat culture. The primary outcome was single-session stone-free status (residual fragments ≤ 3 mm) on 1-month noncontrast computed tomography. Matched-pair tests and prespecified generalized estimating equations were used. Single-session stone-free status was more frequent with suction (89.0% vs. 75.7%; risk difference, 13.3%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.8%–20.8%; P = 0.001), as was complete clearance (74.0% vs. 59.0%; P = 0.001). Mean and peak pressures and high-pressure exposure were lower (all P < 0.001). Complications were less frequent (15.0% vs. 26.6%; risk difference, − 11.6%; 95% CI, − 19.9% to − 3.2%; P = 0.010); adjusted odds ratio (OR), 0.46 (95% CI, 0.26–0.82). Fever without sepsis was less frequent; urosepsis and septic shock did not differ. Culture positivity declined; the group-by-time interaction was nonsignificant, and average odds were lower with suction (OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31–0.90). Suction-sheath use was associated with higher stone-free rates, lower pressure, and fewer complications; causal effects require confirmation in multicenter randomized trials.

Article.Title: MFSD2A, the major transporter of omega-3 DHA in the central nervous system, is expressed in the neural cells of the retina
Article.Authors: Ruiz-Pastor M.; Sánchez-Sáez X.; Lax P.; Cuenca N.
Article.Abstract: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is an essential omega-3 fatty acid indispensable for neural tissue, with anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. Numerous dietary supplements enriched in omega-3 fatty acids were tested in patients with neurodegenerative diseases, as decreased levels of DHA were demonstrated in the central nervous system and plasma of patients and animal models. However, these therapies did not fully report a positive effect. The transport mechanism of DHA to neural tissue remains poorly understood. It was described that the endothelium of the blood–brain and blood-retina barriers expresses the protein major facilitator superfamily domain 2A (MFSD2A), described as the major transporter for DHA. Nevertheless, how neurons incorporate the fatty acid is unknown. Herein, we hypothesized that neurons could express MFSD2A to internalize DHA. We studied the expression of MFSD2A in neural and non-neural retinal cells of humans and other animals. We are the first to demonstrate that the major transporter for the omega-3 fatty acid is expressed not only in retinal blood vessels but also in retinal cells of all animals studied. We performed immunofluorescence in retinal sections of human and other representative non-human animals from different taxonomic orders using three commercial anti-MFSD2A antibodies. To test the specificity of antibodies, pre-absorption control and Western blot were performed. We also did double immunostaining with specific cell markers to identify the different populations of retinal cells. The anti-MFSD2A antibodies tested reported a similar pattern of immunostaining. We confirmed the expression of MFSD2A in the retinal vessels, but we also described the expression of the transporter in both neural and non-neural cells in the retina. Expression of MFSD2A was demonstrated in both rod and cone photoreceptor cells, bipolar cells, horizontal cells, amacrine cells, and ganglion cells of all vertebrates studied. Concerning the non-neural retinal cells, we emphasized the expression of the transporter in Müller cells, because of their known role in retinal homeostasis. Retinal pigment epithelium​, which is involved in nutrient supply to photoreceptors, was immunopositive for MFSD2A in frogs, cats, and dogs. Human Iba-1 + microglial cells did not express the transporter. This is the first study that describes the expression of MFSD2A in the neural retina. Both neural and non-neural retinal populations expressed MFSD2A, being conserved in all the animal species studied, regardless of their phylogenetic distance to Homo sapiens .

Article.Title: Platform, creator, and engagement patterns in BPH health information on chinese short-video platforms: A cross-sectional study of TikTok and Bilibili
Article.Authors: Li W.; Zhang J.; Guo J.; Wang L.; Ma Y.; Hou J.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patients increasingly encounter benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) information on short-video platforms, but the practical adequacy of this content for evaluation and treatment decisions may differ across platform and creator ecosystems. We compared TikTok and Bilibili to characterize structural quality, clinically relevant content coverage, and quality-engagement relationships. We conducted a cross-sectional search on March 12, 2026, retrieving the top 100 videos from each platform with the Chinese keyword for BPH. After excluding unrelated and duplicate content, 171 videos were analyzed (TikTok n = 98; Bilibili n = 73). Two urologists independently assessed structural reliability with modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), educational quality with the Global Quality Score (GQS), and content coverage with a study-specific Completeness Score (CS) spanning Definition, Symptoms, Risk factors, Evaluation, Management, and Outcomes. Inter-rater agreement was excellent for all scored domains (Cohen’s κ > 0.80). Creator composition differed substantially between platforms: professional individuals accounted for 96.9% of TikTok videos, whereas professional and non-professional institutions accounted for 32.8% of Bilibili videos (p < 0.001). TikTok videos had higher median engagement but shorter duration (62 vs. 116 s, p < 0.001). Platform CS and GQS distributions were similar, while TikTok had a slightly higher median mDISCERN score (3 vs. 2, p = 0.002). Institutional videos were longer and had higher CS and GQS values, although institutional subgroups were small. Risk factors and Evaluation were the least covered clinical domains. On TikTok, view count remained weakly associated with lower CS after adjustment for duration and uploader type (partial rs = -0.21, p = 0.032); no corresponding association was observed on Bilibili. BPH videos on both platforms provided incomplete clinical coverage, and engagement was not a dependable proxy for educational value. The underrepresentation of risk factors and evaluation, together with the greater completeness of longer institutional videos, identifies practical targets for clinician- and institution-led digital education in China. Because the data are cross-sectional, the observed associations do not establish algorithmic effects or patient outcomes.

Article.Title: Phylodynamic analysis of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in the Gambia: a 2-year genomic surveillance investigation
Article.Authors: Kanteh A.; Sanyang B.; Jallow H.; Badjie A.; Manneh J.; Jagne S.; Sanneh B.; Samateh A.; de Silva T.; Kampmann B.; D’Alessandro U.; Mohammed N.; Amambua-Ngwa A.; Roca A.; Hué S.; Sesay A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 viral spread are well documented in high income countries. However, limited sequence data in low-and middle-income countries have hampered our understanding of the virus’s spatiotemporal circulation within Sub-Saharan Africa. We used Bayesian phylogeographic inference to reconstruct the origin and migration pattern of SARS-CoV-2 sequenced in The Gambia during the pandemic. Our findings suggest high and continuous rates of viral imports, with at least 94 independent introductions between March 2020 and January 2022. Viral import was mostly associated with countries in Southern Europe, Western Africa, and Southern Asia. Gambia transmission clusters initiated prior to lockdown persisted longer during the pandemic, while clusters that emerged around the introduction of COVID-19 vaccines in The Gambia had shorter persistent times. The higher number of inferred introduction events suggests that international and regional travel continued to contribute substantially to viral movement into The Gambia despite the implementation of border control measures. Thus, a well-defined protocol at entry points, coupled with a well-structured genomic surveillance system, is essential for monitoring lineages and enabling early detection and control.

Article.Title: Fingerprinting of magnetic nanoparticle stability in superimposed static and dynamic magnetic fields
Article.Authors: Günther J.; Markert S.; Beierl J.; Reichl T.; Rückert M.; Kampf T.; Rosenfeldt S.; Schenk A.; Schüler D.; Behr V.; Mickoleit F.; Vogel P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) are promising agents for biomedical applications ranging from imaging to therapy. Among them, magnetosomes (MAGs) biosynthesized by magnetotactic bacteria represent a particularly complex and well-defined system. However, their structural complexity requires monitoring of colloidal stability and dynamic particle behavior, especially in multi-compound environmental media. While conventional methods like dynamic light scattering or sedimentation assays provide indirect information on stability, they do not directly reflect the magnetization dynamics, which is crucial for applications like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), magnetic particle imaging (MPI), or magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS). Here, we intentionally use MAGs as a demanding model system to demonstrate a simpler evaluation strategy by comparing fingerprints of the sensitive measurement technique COMPASS (critical offset magnetic particle spectroscopy). Demonstrating this concept on MAGs, we highlight that the comparative approach can be particularly powerful for rapidly assessing structural changes of MNPs in physiological fluids. This enables sensitive, fast and intuitive monitoring of MNP behavior for early detection of instability effects in biomedical formulations.

Article.Title: Investigating designers’ perceptions of thermal comfort: a Q-methodology study in residential design
Article.Authors: Tohidi M.; Fatahi K.; Omranipour A.; Beigi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employs a robust mixed methods approach—anchored in Q-methodology and semi-structured interviews—to explore how architects in Ilam, Iran, conceptualize thermal comfort as both technical and cultural discourse. A concourse of 78 statements, refined to 43, was sorted by 20 senior designers. Factor analysis using PQMethod revealed four distinct perception types: (1) passive climate responsiveness, (2) reliance on smart HVAC systems, (3) prioritization of insulation materials, and (4) management of natural light and solar exposure. These viewpoints highlight methodological hybridity, combining subjective discourse with analytical rigor, and reveal how cultural and professional logics shape design priorities. Findings indicate that thermal comfort is a cultural and cognitive construct, shaped by professional judgment, local climate, and social expectations. Q-methodology integrates qualitative interpretation with quantitative categorization to reveal subjective viewpoints with analytical rigor. By situating comfort within cultural and cognitive frameworks, this study demonstrates how Q-methodology enriches sustainability research, guiding climate-responsive design and fostering critical dialogue on energy efficiency and occupant well-being.

Article.Title: Social instability distinctly shapes fear memory retention and amygdala function in adolescents and adults
Article.Authors: Parker R.; Padival M.; Montes R.; Ferrara N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adolescence is marked by heightened fear-related behaviors relative to other age groups. The gradual decline in fear into adulthood corresponds to a number of functional changes in the amygdala. Social experiences in group living play an important role in buffering stress responses as well as fear learning and memory. These social experiences are developmentally regulated, where social structure itself is plastic in adolescence and stabilizes into adulthood. This stabilization of social structure, however, is disrupted with social instability. Social instability has negative consequences on amygdala function that supports fear memory formation and retention, often resulting in increased fear expression. Whether social disruptions affect the amygdala uniquely or produce the same fear-related changes seen in other elevated fear states remains unclear. This distinction is critical for understanding how social experience shapes fear during development. To address this gap, we used a social instability protocol in adolescents and adults and compared fear memory retention to that of fear elevation, a process through which fear expression is increased. We found that social instability increased adult fear memory retention while adolescent fear remained high between instability and control conditions, indicating that adult social instability interferes with the regulation of adult fear. We then collected amygdala tissue, and found opposite patterns of amygdala glutamatergic receptor expression connected to degree of freezing in adolescents and adults in control housed and instability groups, with a positive adult but a negative adolescent AMPA receptor correlation to freezing. These correlations were disrupted in those with elevated fear states. Therefore, functional changes within the amygdala may correspond with developmental differences in degree of fear expression that rely on stability in social structure in a manner that is distinct from elevated fear states. Our results collectively demonstrate developmental differences in fear memory retention are supported by age-related changes in amygdala function, which is shaped by social instability in adults.

Article.Title: Large language model agents with simulation-trained surrogates retrieve multi-objective reservoir development plans from hierarchical knowledge graphs
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Zhou F.
Article.Abstract: Optimizing oilfield development is a high-dimensional, multi-objective decision problem: candidate plans must balance hydrocarbon recovery against economic return while satisfying operational constraints. Retrieval methods that rank evidence by textual or structural similarity cannot express such trade-offs or reject infeasible plans, whereas full-physics simulation is too costly to run inside an interactive search. We present PHARAOH, a framework in which a large language model agent retrieves development plans over a multi-resolution knowledge graph, guided by a simulation-trained surrogate model that estimates objectives such as ultimate recovery and net present value. The agent combines global anchoring with type-filtered hierarchical refinement and aggregates parallel search trajectories into a set of diverse recommendations; its policy is then distilled into a compact student model. PHARAOH screens and ranks candidates within a pre-built decision space rather than solving a continuous optimization problem. On PetroGraph, a benchmark built from three public reservoir simulation models, PHARAOH attains the best average performance among the compared baselines, improving Hit@1 by 8.8 and Recall@20 by 7.1 over a surrogate-guided non-agentic search. Full-physics re-simulation shows that 14 of 15 top-ranked plans satisfy the operational constraints, although near-boundary plans remain sensitive to surrogate error. The distilled 7B student retains about 85% of the teacher’s Hit@1 at a fraction of the inference cost. These findings are limited to three simulation benchmarks; field-scale validation remains future work.

Article.Title: Species substitution and tissue adulteration in commercial beef hawawshi sandwiches revealed by histological and molecular analyses
Article.Authors: Farghaly O.; Abd El-Aziz D.; Elbarbary N.; Fotouh A.; Abd El-Malek A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Meat adulteration in processed products represents a major concern for food safety, quality, and consumer trust. Hawawshi, a popular Egyptian ready-to-eat meat product, is particularly susceptible to adulteration due to its minced and seasoned nature. This study aimed to assess the authenticity of commercially available beef hawawshi sandwiches collected from restaurants in Assiut Governorate, Egypt, by detecting meat species substitution and the presence of unauthorized animal tissues using complementary histological examination and PCR-based molecular identification. Unlike previous studies that applied these techniques independently, the present study integrated histological and molecular analyses to simultaneously evaluate tissue composition and species authenticity, providing a more comprehensive approach for detecting meat adulteration in commercially available hawawshi. The study further sought to evaluate the extent of meat adulteration across different price categories to support food fraud detection, consumer protection, and regulatory compliance. A total of 90 commercially available beef hawawshi sandwiches were randomly collected from restaurants in Assiut Governorate, Egypt, during March and April 2026 and stratified into three price categories (low, medium, and high; n = 30 each). Samples were aseptically transported to the laboratory in insulated containers under chilled conditions and stored at 4 °C until analysis. Histological examination was performed using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining to identify tissue composition, while PCR targeting the mitochondrial cytochrome b gene was used for molecular identification of animal species. Histological examination demonstrated significant differences among the three price categories. Low-priced hawawshi contained connective tissue (90.0%), adipose tissue (83.3%), plant materials (73.3%), lung tissue (36.7%), cartilage (26.7%), and bone fragments (23.3%), whereas high-priced samples consisted predominantly of skeletal muscle (93.3%). Molecular analysis revealed an overall adulteration rate of 73.3% (66/90). Beef DNA was detected in 60.0%, 80.0%, and 100.0% of low-, medium-, and high-priced samples, respectively, while chicken DNA was detected in 100.0%, 90.0%, and 50.0%, respectively. Pig DNA (26.7% overall) and donkey DNA (13.3% overall) were detected primarily in low- and medium-priced samples, whereas dog DNA was not detected. Adulteration was most prevalent in low-priced sandwiches (100.0%) and least prevalent in high-priced sandwiches (50.0%). Commercial hawawshi sandwiches had a 73.3% meat adulteration rate, with the highest rate (100.0%) observed in low-priced goods. Both histological and PCR methods were successful in detecting unapproved tissues and undeclared animal species. The results underscore the necessity for greater market surveillance by the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) in Egypt, and for periodic authenticity testing to counter food fraud and safeguard consumers. The use of complementary histology and molecular techniques in regular market monitoring is proposed to combat food fraud, protect consumer health, and improve customer confidence.

Article.Title: CC-GCN: enhancing graph convolutional networks using neighborhood interactions
Article.Authors: Saxena R.; Jadeja M.; Verma A.
Article.Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are a class of deep learning approaches designed for graph based data inference that have made noteworthy strides in handling graphical datasets in past few years. Notably, graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have demonstrated strong performance even with limited training data, often surpassing traditional state-of-the-art models across various tasks, including semi-supervised node classification, link prediction, graph classification, as well as applications in natural language processing and computational chemistry. In this work, we suggest sampling the training set nodes based on their clustering tendency rather than using a conventional random sample selection method. Then, we input the sampled nodes into GCN to carry out semi-supervised node classification tasks. Additionally, we provide a mathematical justification for how our suggested sample selection method leads to the creation of improved GNN models. This leads to better training and consequently better node embeddings and better outputs. Based on this unique training technique, the performance of GCN model over three benchmark networks—Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed has been examined. Following the implementation of the GCN model, classification accuracies of $$90.12\%$$ for CORA, $$89.20\%$$ for PubMed, and $$77.0\%$$ for Citeseer were achieved. CC-GCN attains the best accuracy among the evaluated methods on CORA and PubMed and remains competitive on Citeseer, indicating the effectiveness of structurally informed training-node selection. We also acquired an accuracy of $$91.85\%$$ on Amazon Computers dataset and $$84.04\%$$ on WikiCS dataset. We have also detailed how GCN based multimedia evaluation works for social networks and we have proved this by applying it to hostility classification of Hindi tweets. We have obtained weighted F1-score of 0.64, which is competitive with reported systems for this task. Our findings are generic and task-independent. Additionally, the suggested method can yield positive outcomes for other tasks, such as community detection and connection prediction.

Article.Title: Exploring the influence of multisensory human-plant interactions on attention, emotion, and learning-related reflections of elementary school children
Article.Authors: Hsieh C.; Huang C.; Chin W.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Interaction with natural environments alleviates mental fatigue by engaging involuntary attention and recovering directed attention. However, urbanization and reduced access to green spaces pose challenges for children, especially those at risk for attention-deficit disorders. Our study explores how various modes of plant-based experiences, categorized by environmental setting (indoor vs. outdoor) and format (touch vs. view), influence the attention, emotion, and learning-related reflections of elementary school students. A total of 120 fifth-grade elementary school students participated in one of four experimental groups: indoor-touch, indoor-viewing, outdoor-viewing, or outdoor-touch. We focused on two comparisons across four dimensions: (1) a comparison of pre- and post-activity emotion and attention of participants in each group, and (2) a cross-comparison of the improvement between the four groups based on the measurement using closed-ended questionnaires and the Necker Cube Pattern Control. On the other hand, we conducted a content analysis of students’ learning-related reflections using an open-ended questionnaire. Our results showed that direct contact with real plants indoors, in a multisensory manner, has the potential to outperform other modes in improving attention and emotional states, enhancing learning-related reflections, and fostering pro-environmental attitudes. While directly touching plants outperformed digitally viewing them, the effectiveness can be inconsistent across environmental settings and measurement tools. Our findings suggest that multisensory, hands-on interactions with plants enhance the cognitive and emotional well-being of children. Thus, we provide insight into integrating plant-based education into urban schools and practical alternatives for attention restoration when green space is limited.

Article.Title: Optimization of initiation sequence and delay times for metro‑tunnel blasting balancing gas pipeline safety and blasting performance
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Liu J.; Liu J.; Tian C.; Li Z.; Liang L.; Liu Z.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenge of controlling blast-induced vibration near gas pipelines in urban underground excavations, this study takes the B-entrance of Shanshi East Road Station on Jinan Metro Line 4 as the engineering background. Through field monitoring, numerical simulation and engineering application, the joint optimization of the dynamic response of gas pipelines and rock fragmentation is investigated under three initiation Sequences—simultaneous dual-hole blasting, lateral sequential blasting and longitudinal sequential blasting and under inter-hole delay times of 5, 10, 15 and 20 ms with longitudinal sequential blasting. The results show that longitudinal sequential blasting is the optimal scheme: it reduces the peak surface vibration velocity by about 38.5% compared with simultaneous dual-hole blasting while achieving better rock fragmentation. The inter-hole delay of 5 ms is optimal, yielding the minimum von Mises stress and resultant velocity of 1.25 MPa and 1.62 cm/s, respectively, with the most ideal rock fragmentation. This scheme reduces the pipeline dynamic response while improving blasting performance, providing a reference for similar sensitive environments.

Article.Title: Dynamic interactions between action generation and body-related multisensory integration
Article.Authors: Italia B.; Zampese C.; Poles K.; Garbarini F.; Rossi Sebastiano A.
Article.Abstract: Integrating multisensory stimuli that occur on the body into coherent perceptions (i.e., multisensory integration; MSI) and controlling one’s own actions (i.e., sense of agency) are both fundamental aspects of a coherent bodily-self awareness. Here, we investigate how body-related MSI and action generation interact by designing a combined task that merges two behavioural paradigms traditionally used to study them separately (i.e., MSI and sensory attenuation tasks). We asked participants to rate the perceived intensity of self- or other-generated stimuli, as in the sensory attenuation paradigm. Stimuli could be unimodal (i.e., sounds) or bimodal (i.e., sounds coupled with tactile stimuli on the hand), as in MSI task. Sounds were set at three above-threshold intensities. Beyond replicating MSI (i.e., increased perceived intensity of bimodal than unimodal stimuli) and sensory attenuation (i.e., reduced perceived intensity of self- than other-generated stimuli) effects, we found that the multisensory enhancement varied as a function of both the agent and the stimulus intensity. Specifically, as sensory attenuation emerged at increasing stimulus intensities, MSI was boosted for the attenuated self-generated stimuli. This pattern is consistent with the inverse effectiveness principle and may suggest that action-related predictions optimize the integration of afferent signals by shaping their perceived intensity.
