Article.Title: Spatial variability of GNSS –derived ionospheric total electron content over Ethiopia during 17–18 March 2015 geomagnetic storm
Article.Authors: Shiferaw Y.; Ali S.; Getahun E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ethiopia’s location within the equatorial ionization anomaly region renders its ionosphere highly vulnerable to storm-driven spatial ionospheric total electron content variability, although dense-network investigations of storm-time TEC response remain limited. This study assesses spatial variability of ionospheric total electron content over Ethiopia during the 17–18 March 2015 geomagnetic storm using GNSS -derived vTEC data from nine Ethiopia stations. The intense geomagnetic storm of 2015 were analyzed, the 17–18 March G4-class storm with Disturbance storm time (Dst) index − 234 nT. Concurrent Dst index, planetary Kp index and interplanetary magnetic field z component (IMF Bz) data were integrated with spatially continuous vertical total electron content (vTEC) map were done using ordinary kriging interpolation to characterize the storm-time ionospheric response over Ethiopia. A persistent east–west asymmetry was also identified with western and central sector such as Addis Ababa recording consistently higher vTEC than eastern sector such as Nazret (Adama) and with storm-time enhancements during the storm- time confined almost entirely to the 34–41°E sector within a specific local-time window, indicating that the longitudinal response is governed by local-time-dependent electrodynamic force rather than a spatially uniform disturbance. Positive ionospheric storm phases dominated the main and early recovery periods, while negative ionospheric storm phases emerged during later recovery intervals as disturbance dynamo-driven westward electric fields suppressed the equatorial electrojet (EEJ) and equatorial ionization anomaly (EIA). The leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) results quantitatively shows that the reliability of Kriging-derived TEC maps varies over time, with greater interpolation uncertainty during periods characterized by pronounced spatial TEC gradients.

Article.Title: Sepsis transcriptomics and validation identify PFKFB2 as a regulator of early inflammation and later lactate-dependent M2-like programming in LPS-stimulated macrophages
Article.Authors: Zhang T.; Dou D.; Zhang Y.; Li X.; Liu Q.; Xu D.; Cui B.; Yu M.; Wang S.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis involves dynamic immune dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming, but the role of lactylation-associated metabolic genes in macrophage responses remains unclear. We integrated four peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and four machine-learning algorithms. Thirty candidate genes were identified, and a 12-gene signature was obtained; PFKFB2 was selected for functional validation based on its consistent upregulation across sepsis cohorts and previous evidence linking PFKFB2-mediated glycolytic regulation to lactate production and macrophage functional adaptation. In LPS-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages, PFKFB2 silencing reduced extracellular lactate at 6 and 24 h. At 6 h, silencing attenuated TNF and IL1B induction, and sodium L-lactate did not restore this response. At 24 h, silencing increased TNF and IL1B while decreasing MRC1 and IL10 ; these changes were partially reversed by sodium L-lactate. Thus, PFKFB2 supports early pro-inflammatory gene induction and later sustains a lactate-dependent M2-like transcriptional program. These findings connect multi-cohort sepsis transcriptomics with functional evidence and identify PFKFB2 as a metabolic regulator of macrophage inflammatory transitions.

Article.Title: A machine learning based node influence analysis using isolating and betweenness centrality measures
Article.Authors: Chiranjeevi M.; Dhuli V.; Enduri M.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying node influence in complex networks is essential for exploring diffusion dynamics and identifying key spreaders. Traditional centrality measures, which rely primarily on network topology, often fail to accurately capture information propagation and neglect the interplay between local and global structural properties. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a machine learning-based framework incorporating a novel Isolating-Betweenness Centrality (ISBC) measure that integrates both local and global network information. The proposed ISBC combines local and global topological features to enable a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of the influence of nodes. Furthermore, the framework incorporates the infection rate as a crucial feature to better reflect the diffusion behavior in the real-world. The proposed approach formulates node influence estimation as a classification problem. Feature vectors are constructed using conventional centrality measures along with ISBC, while node labels are derived from diffusion models, particularly the Susceptible–Infected–Recovered (SIR) and Independent Cascade (IC) models. Various machine learning algorithms are applied to learn the relationship between structural features and spreading capability. Extensive simulations on multiple real-world networks demonstrate that the proposed framework improves prediction accuracy over traditional centrality methods. While machine learning models perform well when trained and tested on the same network, ISBC shows superior generalization in cross-network scenarios, consistently surpassing conventional methods.

Article.Title: Mult omics analysis reveals the characteristics and changes in gut microbiota, metabolism, and transcription in two breast cancer models
Article.Authors: Tian Z.; Wang Z.; Zhang Y.; Chen X.; Zheng X.; Gao X.; Pan Y.; Yan T.; Li D.; Xu Y.; Li Y.; Li P.; Zhang W.; Feng Y.; Tian Z.; Zuo Y.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer frequently involves the skeleton, but the systemic molecular changes associated with tumor growth in a vertebral implantation model remain incompletely characterized. To compare gut microbiota, metabolite, and tumor-transcriptome profiles between orthotopic breast tumors and tumors established by direct vertebral implantation, and to identify cross-omics associations for hypothesis generation. Orthotopic breast tumor, direct vertebral implantation, and sham-operated nude mouse groups were established. Fecal and tumor samples were analyzed by 16 S rRNA gene sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, and transcriptomics. Differential, enrichment, correlation, and exploratory feature-selection analyses were integrated. Glycerophospholipid-related features were consistently altered across fecal and tumor compartments. LysoPC 22:6 was selected as a cross-compartment candidate metabolite. Subdoligranulum and six genes (Cd300lb, Nrros, Enho, Fgf10, Zic1, and 9930111J21Rik2) showed exploratory associations with LysoPC and with one another. This study supports the hypothesis that “changes in the tumor-associated microenvironment regulate adaptive changes in systemic metabolism, transcription, and microbiome composition,” and constructs a multi-omics association network centered on LysoPC.

Article.Title: CTNNB1 activation attenuates neuronal apoptosis and improves functional recovery after spinal cord injury via the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Qin C.; Lin Y.; He Y.; Chen H.; Jin Z.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Neuronal apoptosis following spinal cord injury (SCI) critically contributes to neurological deficits. This study integrates bioinformatics and experimental validation to explore therapeutic targets and elucidate the protective role of CTNNB1 (encoding β-catenin) in SCI. Differential expression analysis and WGCNA were performed on GEO datasets to identify hub genes. In vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) models and in vivo rat Allen’s impact models were established. CTNNB1-overexpressing HT22 cells were generated using lentivirus, with Wnt/β-catenin agonist (WCA3) and inhibitor (CCT036477) for rescue experiments. Apoptosis and pathway activity were assessed via Western blot, CCK-8, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence. SCI rats received intraperitoneal injection of agonist, and functional recovery was evaluated by BBB scoring, footprint analysis, HE, and TUNEL staining. CTNNB1 was identified as a significantly downregulated hub gene post-SCI. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments confirmed that CTNNB1/β-catenin expression decreased as early as 6 h after injury. CTNNB1 overexpression in OGD models increased cell viability, reduced Cleaved Caspase-3 and Bax, and elevated Bcl-2 levels, effects reversible by Wnt/β-catenin inhibition. In vivo, agonist-mediated pathway activation improved motor function recovery, reduced spinal cord cavitation, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis. CTNNB1 exerts neuroprotection against neuronal apoptosis after SCI by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. The CTNNB1/Wnt/β-catenin axis represents a promising therapeutic target for SCI repair.

Article.Title: A study of marathon performance in elite amateur runners based on continuous glucose monitoring technology: an observational study
Article.Authors: Gu Z.; Zhang P.; Lv J.; Chen G.; Xu K.; Dai J.
Article.Abstract: This observational study aimed to characterize glycemic dynamics and their association with exercise performance in elite amateur runners during a marathon race using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). CGM was used to continuously monitor interstitial glucose concentration and exercise data of 26 elite amateur runners (24 males, 2 females) participating in the 2023 Wuxi Marathon. Generalized linear mixed models and linear mixed models were employed to examine differences across 10‑kilometer race segments, with runner as a random intercept. Correlation analyses assessed associations between glycemic variables and running speed. The mean interstitial glucose concentration during the race was significantly higher than the baseline value. Generalized linear mixed models revealed significant differences in interstitial glucose concentration across 10 kilometer segments, with decline in the 31–40 km and 41–42 km segments compared to the first 10 km. Speed analysis showed significant variations across segments, with a significant decrease during the 21–30 km, 31–40 km, and 41–42 km segments compared to the first 10 km. Correlation analysis between speed and interstitial glucose concentration indicated no significant linear relationship, either for the entire race or within individual 10‑kilometer segments. Pre‑race carbohydrate intake was not significantly associated with runners’ speed or interstitial glucose concentration during the first 10 km. A higher mean carbohydrate (CHO) intake rate during the race was associated with longer race completion time, whereas no significant correlation was found with the mean interstitial glucose concentration. The study highlights that marathon runners experience a significant increase in interstitial glucose concentration during the race, with declines in the later stages. Speed decreases significantly in the latter half of the race, particularly between 31 and 40 km. However, no significant linear correlation was found between interstitial glucose concentration and speed, and pre-race carbohydrate intake was not significantly associated with performance or glucose dynamics. These findings suggest that marathon fatigue is multifactorial, with interstitial glucose being only one of several contributing physiological factors.

Article.Title: Epistasis detection and fitness valleys in SARS-CoV-2 evolution
Article.Authors: Likhachev I.; Rouzine I.
Article.Abstract: Probabilistic prognosis of virus evolution, vital for the design of effective vaccines and antiviral drugs, requires the knowledge of adaptive landscape including epistatic interactions. Although epistatic interactions can, in principle, be inferred from abundant sequencing data by various methods, it has been shown previously that genetic linkage between evolving sites obscures their signature and requires averaging over several independent populations. Here we probe the limits of epistasis detection based on pairwise correlations conditioned on the state of a third site on synthetic sequences evolved in a Monte Carlo algorithm with known epistatic pairs in two scenarios: an initially-diverse population in the presence of recombination and mutation, with a uniform epistatic network, and an initially–uniform population in the presence of mutation and a fitness valley. In either scenario, the detection error decreases with the number of independent populations and increases with the sequence length. In the first scenario, the accuracy is enhanced by moderate recombination and is maximal, when epistasis magnitude approaches the point of full compensation. In the second scenario, simulation predicts the spontaneous crossing of a fitness valley and forming a new large strain. The method is then applied to several thousands of sequences of SARS-CoV-2. Results obtained under equal sampling from world regions are consistent with the existence of fitness valleys connecting groups of viral variants.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fitness valleys; SARS-CoV-2 evolution; epistasis detection; fitness landscape; recombination; genetic linkage

Article.Title: Research on anti-disturbance adaptive control strategy of power electronic converters based on deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Han Z.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: DC-DC boost converters are widely used in renewable-energy interfaces, energy-storage systems, electric vehicles, microgrids, and regulated DC supplies, but their voltage response can deteriorate under load changes, input-voltage fluctuations, and circuit-parameter uncertainty. This study develops an offline-trained state-dependent anti-disturbance controller based on twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) for an averaged continuous-conduction-mode boost-converter model. The actor maps normalized electrical observations to a bounded duty-cycle command, and the reward contains three independent normalized terms for tracking error, error variation, and duty-cycle smoothness. The numerical environment is integrated with fourth-order Runge–Kutta substeps and is evaluated against proportional-integral (PI), anti-windup PI (PI-AW), sliding-mode control (SMC), and an independently trained deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) controller. In the representative median-seed run, TD3 limits peak overshoot to 2.41%, 4.17%, and 2.02% in the load, input-voltage, and parameter-mismatch tests, respectively, while all reported trajectories remain below the numerical state guards. SMC attains lower RMSE in the load and parameter-mismatch tests, whereas TD3 provides a lower peak excursion and competitive tracking. Matched six-seed TD3/DDPG experiments show overlapping uncertainty and no statistically significant paired difference at the 0.05 level. These results support a balanced finite-horizon disturbance-rejection benefit of the state-dependent TD3 policy under the stated simulation assumptions, rather than universal superiority or a hardware-level stability guarantee.

Article.Title: Experimental study on differential rockburst characteristics of granite with single and parallel double structural planes
Article.Authors: Yan X.; Wei H.; Luo J.; Xiao H.; Wei Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The effect of structural planes on rockburst is a core issue in deep rock mechanics, yet the differential failure mechanisms induced by parallel double structural planes remain poorly understood. This study performs biaxial compression tests on granite specimens with a circular hole, combined with synchronized video monitoring and acoustic emission detection, to systematically compare rockburst characteristics under three conditions: intact rock, a single 45° structural plane, and parallel double 45° structural planes. Specimens with a single 45° structural plane exhibit progressive rockburst failure characterized by early damage initiation and slow evolution. The single structural plane imposes strong geometric constraints and significantly restrains the radial expansion of rockburst pits. In contrast, specimens with double structural planes present sudden rockburst failure with late initiation and rapid development. Stress superposition at crack tips and cooperative crack propagation attenuate the boundary constraint effect and promote the deep radial expansion of rockburst pits. AE analysis reveals that tensile cracks dominate the failure process of intact specimens. The shear crack proportion rises sharply to 33.6% in double-structural-plane specimens, indicating that shear crack coalescence drives the radial expansion of rockburst pits. These findings enrich the mechanism of structure-type rockbursts and support risk assessment for deep fractured tunnels.

Article.Title: Effect of ulnar fingers’ position on the stability of the index metacarpophalangeal joint during precision pinching
Article.Authors: Kurauchi K.; Date S.; Koike Y.; Sunagawa T.
Article.Abstract: This study quantitatively investigated how ulnar (middle, ring, and little) fingers’ position affects index metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint stability during precision pinching in response to perturbations. Twenty-nine right-handed asymptomatic adults performed a thumb–index precision pinch under two ulnar fingers’ positions (flexion, extension) and four force conditions (0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 kg, and 70% of maximum voluntary force). Under each condition, a perturbation was applied to the radial side of the index proximal phalanx. Acceleration amplitude and settling time were calculated from an accelerometer attached to the index proximal phalanx. Muscle activities of the extensor indicis proprius (EIP), extensor digitorum communis of the index and ring fingers (EDC-index, EDC-ring), flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS), first dorsal interosseous, and first lumbrical were recorded. Acceleration amplitude was significantly smaller with ulnar fingers’ extension than flexion at 0.3 kg (7.4 vs. 10.7 m/s²), 0.5 kg (7.5 vs. 10.3 m/s²), and 70% MVF (7.1 vs. 9.0 m/s²), whereas settling time did not differ between positions. Extensor muscle activities (EIP, EDC-index, EDC-ring) increased significantly during ulnar fingers’ extension, while FDS activity decreased (all p < 0.05). These findings suggest that ulnar fingers’ extension suppresses index MCP joint sway in response to perturbations through increased extensor muscle activity.

Article.Title: Longitudinal monitoring of motor symptoms in Parkinson’s disease using smartwatch and smartphone app digital biomarkers
Article.Authors: Chacko S.; Garcia-Gancedo L.; Batzu L.; Rota S.; van Wamelen D.; Zinzalias P.; Barwick N.; Reith A.; Williams S.; Hamy V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As part of a case–control study investigating Parkinson’s disease (PD) progression through clinical imaging and wet biomarker techniques, we utilised smartwatch and smartphone technology to identify potential markers of PD and evaluate their validity in terms of sensitivity to symptom severity and progression. Digital outcome measures were passively (smartwatch) and actively (task assessments) recorded and processed with cross-sectional, longitudinal (up to 24 months), and bivariate analyses. 26 patients with idiopathic PD on dopamine-replacement therapy and 18 healthy controls (HC) participated. 18 passive and 21 active measures could significantly distinguish PD from HC. Measures associated with tremor, daily walking, active motion tasks, and voice-related tasks were the most sensitive. Free living during early morning and OFF-medication assessment measures were able to effectively track symptom deteriorations. Overall, these findings show that smartwatch/smartphone technology can be used to surface candidate digital measures that characterize PD, and that voice changes, as well as motion measures, may be suitable for assessing longitudinal, symptom-related change in individuals with idiopathic PD on dopamine-replacement therapy.

Article.Title: Semi-supervised colonoscopy depth estimation via lighting adjustment model-driven soft labels
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Zhang Z.; Xu Z.; Liu E.; Chen D.; He B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate polyp size measurement during colonoscopy is essential for colorectal cancer diagnosis; however, monocular depth estimation is significantly affected by complex lighting variations, including mucus reflections, exposure inconsistencies, and synthetic-to-real domain gaps. To address these challenges, we propose LAM-Soft, a semi-supervised framework that integrates a dynamic Lighting Adjustment Model (LAM) with confidence-aware learning. The proposed LAM converts rigid pseudo-labels into soft constraints by modeling near-field light attenuation and surface reflection, facilitating the alignment between synthetic per-pixel shading features and real clinical grayscale distributions. A teacher–student architecture is adopted to jointly exploit hard labels from synthetic datasets and LAM-refined soft labels from clinical data, while a confidence decoder suppresses low-quality frames caused by motion blur or contamination. Experimental results on the C3VD dataset demonstrate that LAM-Soft achieves state-of-the-art performance with an L1 error of 0.1789 mm and a δ-accuracy of 57.19%. For polyp size estimation on the SUN database, the proposed method reduces the mean absolute error to 0.819 mm. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness of the proposed components. In addition, the lightweight architecture supports real-time inference at 71 FPS, indicating its potential for practical clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Thymol-rich Ajwain essential oil attenuates EMT-related features associated with the PTEN–AKT2 axis in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Hemmati M.; Rezazadeh D.; Mostafaei A.; Yavari P.; Mansouri K.
Article.Abstract: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) has a fundamental role in carcinoma metastasis. The PI3K/AKT signaling pathway makes an imperative contribution to EMT progression, with PTEN and AKT being its main inhibitor and effector, respectively. AKT and PTEN function can be regulated by phosphorylation. Ajwain essential oil (AEO) is rich in thymol. Thymol is a natural compound with well-studied anticancer effects; however, data on its anti-metastatic potential remain limited. This study investigated the potential of AEO in reversing EMT linked to modulation of the PTEN–AKT2 axis, along with its anti-proliferative properties, in MDA-MB-231 cells. Chemical profiling of AEO by GC/MS was provided, followed by an evaluation of its anticancer features using MTT, colony formation, and flow cytometry. Moreover, attenuation of EMT properties and its effect on PTEN and AKT2 were assessed using wound-healing, Transwell/invasion, and Western blot assays. Phytochemical profiling of AEO identified thymol as the major constituent (≈ 43%). Treatment led to a dose-dependent decrease in proliferation and clonogenic potential. Aside from apoptosis induction, AEO also led to accumulation of cells at the G2/M phase and reduced their migration and invasion potential. In response to treatment, the protein abundance of p-PTEN (Thr366) and p-AKT2 (Ser474) was decreased without significant changes in total PTEN and AKT2. Moreover, N-cadherin and Snail were downregulated; conversely, E-cadherin was upregulated. Collectively, these findings suggest that thymol-rich AEO could attenuate EMT properties, associated with a decrease in p-PTEN (Thr366) and p-AKT2 (Ser474) in MDA-MB-231 cells. Therefore, thymol-rich AEO merits further studies on its anti-metastatic properties.

Article.Title: Analysis of coupled prevention and control strategies for slope stability and hydrogeological conditions in coal mine fire-affected areas
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Yang Z.; Wang Y.; Yang F.; Li J.; Zhou J.; Liu T.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: The Zhundong Basin is a typical arid desert region in Northwest China characterized by abundant coal deposits. The widely distributed low-metamorphic Jurassic coal seams are prone to spontaneous combustion disasters. High-temperature burning of these coal seams has formed pyrolytic rocks that have altered the structural composition of original rock formations and groundwater distribution patterns, creating a unique hydrogeological pattern of "local fracture enrichment and belt-like water conduction and storage" specific to arid mining areas. This phenomenon induces complex geological hazards such as slope failures, water outburst, and collapses, significantly compromising safe and efficient open-pit coal mining. Using a large-scale open-pit mine in Zhundong as the study case and leveraging detailed geophysical survey data covering 19.065 km2, this study integrates multi-source exploration techniques—including high-precision magnetic methods, transient electromagnetic methods (TEM), and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT)—to systematically investigate geological, hydrogeological, and geophysical characteristics. The research standardized the entire workflow from field data acquisition to data calibration and interpretation. By analyzing stratigraphic structures, coal seam distribution patterns, and primary water inflow factors, the study elucidated the distinct geophysical response mechanisms between pyrolytic rocks and water-bearing rock masses. Through localized optimization of geophysical parameters and inversion algorithms for arid Gobi mining areas, precise boundaries of coal fire zones and spatial distributions of water-rich zones in main coal seams B5 and B2 were identified. Results accuracy was validated through engineering borehole tests and water extraction experiments, providing comprehensive insights into the geological consistency and underlying mechanisms of multi-source geophysical data. The research findings indicate that the study area features two extensive coal seam fire zones: a patchy distribution in the north and a linear belt pattern in the west. The magnetism of burned metamorphic rocks shows significant enhancement, while their resistivity exhibits distinct high-low variations; water-bearing burned metamorphic rocks demonstrate pronounced low-resistivity anomalies. Three strongly water-rich zones and six weakly water-rich zones were identified across the entire area, with the western crescent-shaped contiguous water-rich zone exhibiting optimal hydraulic connectivity and serving as the primary risk zone for water hazards and slope instability in the mining area. The multi-source geophysical exploration approach proves suitable for the complex conditions of arid Gobi regions in Northwest China, achieving an 83.3% verification accuracy for fire boundary drilling and meeting the precision requirements for geological water control projects in open-pit mines. Based on these findings, spatial distribution patterns of fire-affected and water-rich zones have been summarized, along with targeted recommendations for water hazard prevention and slope stabilization. The research provides theoretical foundations and practical insights for geological exploration, water management, and safety operations in similar arid self-igniting open-pit coal mines across Northeast and Northwest China.

Article.Title: A deep semantic and channel-spatial attention network for ultrasound uterine fibroid segmentation
Article.Authors: Zhou Q.; Ding X.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of uterine fibroids in ultrasound images is of great importance for computer-aided diagnosis and clinical assessment. However, this task remains difficult because ultrasound images often suffer from speckle noise, weak tissue contrast, indistinct lesion boundaries, and considerable variations in fibroid morphology. To improve segmentation accuracy under these challenging conditions, this study proposes DSCA-Net, a deep semantic and channel-spatial attention network for uterine fibroid segmentation. Specifically, the proposed network follows an encoder-decoder framework and incorporates several dedicated feature enhancement components. Firstly, a deep semantic attention gate module (DSAGM) is introduced into the deeper encoding stages to strengthen high-level semantic representation and guide the network to focus on fibroid-related regions. Secondly, a channel-spatial attention refinement module (CSARM) is embedded in the skip pathways to selectively refine encoder features before feature fusion, thereby reducing the interference of irrelevant background information. In the decoder, a residual feature refinement module (RFRM) is designed to enhance the recovery of spatial details and improve the fusion of multi-level features. In addition, a weighted efficient channel attention module (WECAM) is applied near the prediction layer to further recalibrate informative channel responses and stabilize feature activation. Experimental results on the uterine fibroid ultrasound dataset collected from Quzhou Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, the public brain tumor dataset, and the digital database thyroid image (DDTI) dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of DSCA-Net across different medical imaging tasks. On the uterine fibroid ultrasound dataset, DSCA-Net achieved Dice, Mcc, and Jaccard scores of 0.9174, 0.9140, and 0.8479. On the public brain tumor dataset, the corresponding scores were 0.8473, 0.8464, and 0.7509, while on the DDTI dataset, DSCA-Net obtained Dice, Mcc, and Jaccard values of 0.7767, 0.7417, and 0.6371. In addition, comprehensive ablation experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness of each key component in the proposed network. Computational efficiency was also evaluated by comparing model parameter counts and inference times with those of representative segmentation methods. DSCA-Net contains 15.07 million parameters and requires 163 ms per inference step under the reported experimental setting. These results demonstrate the segmentation performance of DSCA-Net across three medical imaging datasets and provide a quantitative assessment of its computational cost.

Article.Title: Incremental value of wearable digital phenotypes for anxiety under real-world missingness
Article.Authors: Meng X.; Cai M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wearable sensing may enable low-burden digital phenotyping of anxiety, but its incremental value beyond brief symptom questionnaires remains uncertain under real-world missingness. We analyzed a public 4-week dataset from 49 adults with two 14-day participant-windows aligned to week-2 and week-4 GAD-7 assessments (98 windows; 22 with GAD-7 ≥ 5). XGBoost models based on demographic/lifestyle, wearable, questionnaire, and combined feature sets were evaluated by participant-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, with uncertainty estimated by participant-level cluster bootstrap. QUESTIONNAIRE models achieved the highest classification performance (AUC 0.888; average precision 0.826; Brier 0.085), whereas WEARABLE alone remained near chance (AUC 0.501). Adding wearables to QUESTIONNAIRE did not improve performance (ΔAUC − 0.045; ΔBrier 0.025). In the high-compliance subset (34 participants; 68 windows), wearable-only discrimination remained weak; questionnaire-plus-wearable point estimates were more favorable, but confidence intervals included the null. Continuous GAD-7 analyses showed improved prediction beyond demographic/lifestyle variables but little added value beyond questionnaires. These findings indicate baseline-dependent incremental value: wearable-derived features may provide adjunctive information when questionnaire data are unavailable or sparse, but their added value was limited once baseline symptom questionnaires were available.

Article.Title: Diagnostic hyperspectral signatures of boron minerals for the identification of jadarite-type (LiNaSiB3O7(OH)) volcano-sedimentary lithium mineralization
Article.Authors: Corrado F.; Putzolu F.; Thiele S.; Armstrong R.; Gloaguen R.; Sorrentino A.; Mondillo N.; Herrington R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Volcano-sedimentary (VS) deposits host Li resources associated with clays and boron minerals (i.e., borates and borosilicates). Jadarite-type (LiNaSiB 3 O 7 (OH)) mineralization exhibits high Li grades; however, the textural and chemical overlaps between boron minerals hinder the field recognition and the differentiation of jadarite from unmineralized species. This study presents a systematic appraisal of the Visible and Near-Short-Wave Infrared (VSWIR; 380–2500 nm), Mid-Wave Infrared (MWIR; 2700–5300 nm), and Long-wave Infrared (LWIR; 7700–12300 nm) hyperspectral features of jadarite and associated boron minerals, to facilitate rapid identification of Li-rich species in VS deposits. Hyperspectral reflectance data were systematically collected on representative samples from the Jadar deposit and from reference materials. Results show that MWIR-LWIR spectroscopy can feasibly differentiate borosilicates from borates through the detection of the Si-O vibrational modes at ~ 4500 nm, ~ 8650 nm and ~ 9500 nm. However, MWIR-LWIR spectroscopy is not suitable to identify diagnostic features linked to Li-rich borosilicates, and hence cannot confidently differentiate jadarite from similar borosilicates such as searlesite (NaBSi 2 O 5 (OH) 2 ). The VSWIR signatures of boron species are ascribable to the OH and B-OH groups; however, jadarite exhibits a diagnostic doublet at 2041 nm and 2077 nm. Comparative analysis with Li-, B-, and Na-bearing reference compounds and spectral modelling indicate that the VSWIR signature of jadarite results from its distinctive Li-bearing crystal structure, which favors the vibrational coupling between BO 3 and OH to yield diagnostic doublets that uniquely distinguishes jadarite from searlesite, borate minerals and Li-smectite.

Article.Title: Blood based multi biomarker panel discriminates Alzheimer disease from healthy controls in a single center nested cross validation
Article.Authors: Li D.; Sun J.; Jin W.; Chen S.; Li Z.; Ma P.; Fu X.; Chen Q.; Wang M.; Qu C.; Pan R.; Sun Y.; Lin P.
Article.Abstract: AD involves complex pathological pathways that are poorly characterized by conventional univariate analyses. This study aimed to screen discriminatory blood biomarkers and evaluate their performance in differentiating patients with established AD from HCs using multimodal integrated analytical strategies. We recruited 200 participants (100 AD, 100 HCs) and measured 12 blood biomarkers, including neurotrophic factors, tau proteins, neuronal injury markers and peripheral inflammatory indices. PCA and OPLS-DA were applied for exploratory visualization. Nested stratified ten-fold cross-validation was used to avoid data leakage. L1-penalized LASSO logistic regression served as the primary feature selection method, with a stacking ensemble model constructed for benchmarking. Under lambda.1se criterion, eight predictive biomarkers were retained. BDNF, NGF, NFL and pTau217 were robust markers consistently selected by both pipelines; pTau231 and S100β represented second-tier stable markers. PLR and SII were excluded by LASSO-1se but occasionally selected in stacking, while Lym was retained only in LASSO-1se. Age, gender, neutrophil and platelet counts were eliminated in both models. Core AD neuropathology markers exhibited better cross-model reproducibility than non-specific systemic inflammatory indices. The LASSO-derived model achieved out-of-fold AUROC of 0.9999 and AUPRC of 0.9999; the stacking model reached AUROC = 0.999 and AUPRC = 0.999. All performance metrics were derived from single-centre internal cross-validation. External multi-cohort validation is mandatory before clinical application. This multimodal framework identifies multi-pathway blood biomarkers reflecting tau pathology, axonal injury, neurotrophic deficiency and peripheral immune perturbation, providing insights into AD pathogenesis.

Article.Title: Digital twin–guided graph-transformer with meta-reinforcement learning for real-time adaptive cyber-attack mitigation in smart grids
Article.Authors: Manogaran N.; Berkmans Y.; Nandagopal M.; Surulivel A.; Aseervatham J.; Das S.; Kumar G.
Article.Abstract: Smart grids are rapidly changing the current face of power systems by the use of state-of-the-art sensing and communication technology and renewable energy resources to improve the efficiency, reliability and sustainability of the transmission system. However, with the growing cyber–physical connectivity, new and more advanced cyber–physical attacks are emerging, and a rules-based approach or an offline learning process is not effective to counter them. To mitigate cyber-attacks in real-time for smart grids, a digital-twin guided graph-transformer architecture with meta-reinforcement learning is proposed, namely DT-GXTNet. The architecture is designed to produce interactive graphs of the communication in intrusion-detection traffic and is based on the use of spatial–temporal attention to identify changing relationships between the components of the grid. The learned representations are incorporated into a predictive digital twin, which simulate the propagation of the attack, vulnerability analysis and prediction of future grid states for the various threats. A meta-reinforcement learning agent views mitigation as a sequential decision-making process, enabling the agent to quickly and adaptively adjust its policy to the novel and evolving attacks, as well as previously unseen attacks. Experimental testing on public smart-grid intrusion data yields a detection accuracy ranging from 98.25% to 99.1%, and precisions and recalls are between 96% and 99% with an F1-score between 96% and 99%. Another unique feature of DT-GXTNet is that it provides a much lower real-time inference latency of 22ms, a 67.6% reduction fromDL-based digital-twin baseline (68ms). In addition, ablation and prediction analyses are provided, further illustrating the complementary benefits of graph-transformer learning, digital-twin simulation, and adaptive policy optimization. DT-GXTNet is an adaptive, scalable infrastructure for overall responsive and resilient smart-grid cyber-defense.

Article.Title: Vertical mesh-mediated fascial traction is associated with higher fascial closure rates than vacuum-assisted wound closure with mesh-mediated traction in open abdomen therapy
Article.Authors: Schaaf S.; Dohmen J.; Zago M.; Mones T.; von Websky M.; Berrevoet F.; Barbosa E.; Ioannidis O.; Willms A.; N/A N/A.; Bulian D.; Vilz T.; Kölbel B.; Beltzer C.; Kurpierz A.; Petersson U.; Lock J.; De Deken J.; Stavrou G.; Fuckert O.; Ulmer C.; Shaheen Y.; Schoen F.; Nickel B.; Kivillis M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Open abdomen treatment (OAT) is a critical surgical strategy for managing severe intra-abdominal conditions. Early definitive fascial closure (DFC) reduces complications and mortality. While the vacuum-assisted wound closure with mesh-mediated fascial traction (VAWCM) technique is considered the current standard, novel methods such as vertical mesh-mediated fascial traction (VMMFT) with devices like Fasciotens® Abdomen offer a promising alternative. This retrospective, registry-based, propensity score–matched cohort study compared fascial closure outcomes between VAWCM and VMMFT in patients undergoing OAT, utilizing data from the European Hernia Society Open Abdomen Registry (2015–2024). Patients were matched based on sepsis at OAT initiation and initial fascial defect width. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, Chi-square and Mann–Whitney U tests, and logistic regression. Of 1119 OAT cases, 39 (3.5%) received VMMFT and 675 (60.3%) VAWCM. After matching, each cohort included 28 patients. In the matched cohorts, higher DFC rates were observed with VMMFT than with VAWCM in both the ITT-like (89.3% vs. 60.7%; p = .01) and PP-like analyses (100.0% vs. 69.6%; p = .01). Logistic regression in the matched cohort showed an association between VMMFT and higher odds of fascial closure (OR 5.39, 95% CI 1.31–22.25; p = .02), although the confidence interval was wide. ICU stay and ventilation duration were longer in the VMMFT group, while enteroatmospheric fistula occurred in 0% versus 10.7% of patients, respectively (p = .08). In this retrospective registry-based analysis, VMMFT was associated with higher fascial closure rates compared with VAWCM. Given the limited number of VMMFT cases, wide confidence intervals, and residual imbalance after propensity-score matching, these findings should be interpreted as observational, exploratory, and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Larger prospective studies using standardized treatment protocols are required to confirm this association. Article.Title: An adaptive bio-inspired secure routing framework with ECC encryption and intrusion detection for MANET communication
Article.Authors: Rathod V.; Shukla V.; Sable N.; Patil U.; Kale B.; Pise G.; Workie M.
Article.Abstract: This research addresses a critical gap in MANET security, where secure routing, trust management, energy efficiency, and IDS are often treated separately, leading to suboptimal performance under dynamic and adversarial conditions. Conventional cryptographic methods introduce high computational overhead, while trust- and learning-based approaches often overlook end-to-end security, adaptive routing, and receiver-side intrusion validation. To address these gaps, this paper proposes Sec-BIO, a unified secure routing framework that integrates bio-inspired optimization, lightweight cryptography, and machine-learning-based intrusion detection into a single adaptive architecture. EHO is embedded in the AODV routing procedure to create an intrusion-aware, energy-efficient routing framework that uses trust, residual energy, and congestion as routing metrics. DSA-based node authentication enables secure participation in the network, while ECC provides lightweight end-to-end data confidentiality. The receiver-side K-means clustering-based IDS also dynamically classifies traffic behaviour and updates node trust, enabling the system to mitigate real-time attacks and reconfigure routes as needed. To evaluate the framework, we tested it in NS2 across different node densities and mobility scenarios and compared it against AODV, E-AODV, S-AODV, EA-AODV, and traditional IDSs. The results show that Sec-BIO provides statistically significant improvements in the networking and security metrics. Compared with the baseline protocols, the proposed framework increases PDR by up to 15.20%, reduces E2E delay by 16.30%, reduces routing overhead by 9.20%, and reduces energy consumption by 18.23%. For IDS, the K-Means-based Sec-BIO framework achieves 96.70% precision, 97.44% recall, 96.08% accuracy, and 96.85% F1-score, whereas SVM, Random Forest, and Naïve Bayes classifiers perform worse. Overall, the results show that Sec-BIO improves routing efficiency, energy usage, and security under the examined MANET conditions, providing insights into its possible applications in dynamic and sensitive environments. However, further studies using wireless, realistic testbeds are needed for practical implementation.

Article.Title: Benchmarking hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for power grid optimization problems
Article.Authors: Gaidai I.; Mukherjee R.
Article.Abstract: Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow Unit Commitment (AC-OPF-UC) is a difficult mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem that combines binary generator commitment decisions with nonconvex continuous AC power-flow constraints. In this work, we investigate whether hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithms can improve the solution of single-period AC-OPF-UC relative to classical approaches. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to directly evaluate quantum or hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for single-period AC-OPF-UC with explicit binary commitment variables and the full nonlinear AC power-flow formulation. We consider two candidate algorithms for improving AC-OPF-UC solution quality relative to purely classical methods on ideal quantum hardware. The first applies QAOA directly to a fully discretized formulation of the problem, with equality and inequality constraints incorporated through penalty terms and slack variables. Although conceptually straightforward, this approach requires a prohibitively large number of qubits even for small instances. The second, qubit-efficient approach encodes only the binary generator status variables on a quantum computer, while optimizing the continuous power-flow variables classically for each sampled bitstring. We benchmark this method on randomly generated AC-OPF-UC instances with 5–13 generators and compare it against SCIP, SMAC, and uniform random sampling. Our simulations show that the qubit-efficient hybrid method does not outperform uniform sampling. These results suggest that in order to establish potential advantage of the variational hybrid strategy considered here over the best classical algorithms, if any, much larger system sizes (24+ generators) need to be tested, which is beyond our computational capacity. Alternatively, different approaches, such as quantum versions of branch-and-bound methods, may be more promising.

Article.Title: A neuro-symbolic framework for cross-hospital glaucoma detection from fundus images
Article.Authors: Hemrajani P.; Aggarwal K.; Himthani V.; Bohra M.; Kushwaha S.
Article.Abstract: In 2020, an estimated 79.6 million people were affected by glaucoma, which is expected to increase to 111.8 million by 2040. Early identification is critical, but most automatic detection systems do not generalize well across hospitals and imaging devices. In this paper, we present the neuro-symbolic glaucoma detection framework (NSC), which combines an efficient network (EfficientNet-B4) using dual spatial-channel attention, a six-node anatomical graph attention network (GAT-GNN), and a differentiable symbolic constraint module that applies four clinical fuzzy logic rules involving cup-to-disc ratio (CDR), rim thinning, defects in retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), and vessel density. The framework is trained on 9100 fundus images drawn from a curated corpus of 12,619 images across eight datasets and eight countries. The 12,134 non-holdout images were split 75%/12.5%/12.5% into 9100 training, 1517 validation and 1517 test images; the 485-image RIM-ONE DL set was held out entirely as a never-seen cross-hospital test set. Augmentation is applied during training and does not alter the number of distinct images in any split. Among the evaluated variants the highest cross-hospital AUC is obtained by EfficientNet-B4+Symbolic (B4, 0.6997, 95% CI 0.649–0.750); the differences between B2, B3 and B4 on the cross-hospital holdout are small and not statistically significant. EfficientNet-B4+GAT-GNN (B3) is proposed as the deployment configuration on the basis of in-distribution performance and inference cost rather than cross-hospital AUC. The full NSC model achieves a test AUC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.934–0.958) and sensitivity of 0.900, while B3 achieves the highest in-distribution AUC among the evaluated variants at 0.9612 (95% CI 0.951–0.972). Ablation studies show that adding the GAT-GNN to EfficientNet-B4 improved in-distribution test AUC by 1.4 percentage points in the single-seed ablation (0.9472–0.9612) and the performance of GNN-symbolic interaction in terms of cross-hospital AUC is reduced by 8.1 points (z = − 3.08, p = 0.002). Across three independent training runs (seeds 42, 1337, and 2024), B3 achieved a mean test AUC of 0.9602 ± 0.0002, compared with 0.9492 ± 0.0015 for B2. On images excluded from training, agreement between the CDR proxy and expert-measured cup-to-disc ratio is weak and inconsistent across datasets ( \(\rho = 0.549\) , \(n = 26\) on DRISHTI-GS; \(\rho = 0.081\) , \(n = 100\) on REFUGE2), so anatomical grounding of the CDR proxy is not established. Validation of the CDR, RNFL, rim and vessel latent representations against segmentation ground truth remains future work. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first neuro-symbolic framework for glaucoma detection from fundus images, combining differentiable fuzzy constraints with anatomical graph reasoning, evaluated in a strict cross-hospital holdout setting (Canon CR-2 to Nidek AFC-210) without using segmentation masks.

Article.Title: Novel application of artificial intelligence based astronomical centroiding to small particle tracking
Article.Authors: Fetescu C.; Giltinan A.; Chullipalliyalil K.; Maryam S.; Smith N.; Sleator R.
Article.Abstract: Quantitative assessment of aerosol particle size distribution is an important variable for evaluating barrier mask efficacy and mitigating airborne pathogen transmission. However, real world aerosol imaging is compromised by optical noise, such as light scatter, background interference and variable illumination, limiting the reliability of conventional testing approaches. Herein, we propose a novel solution to this issue centred on star centroiding, an astronomy-derived approach built on two deep learning models, MobileUNet and ELUNet. These models were originally trained on noisy images to detect celestial objects, which resemble aerosol particles. The models were applied without retraining to laser-illuminated aerosol images acquired during mask efficacy experiments. These images were generated by laser illumination of aerosol produced from a 10% NaCl-in-water solution and exhaled through a medical mannequin connected to an artificial lung, with the dataset comprising both constant and plume emission conditions. Across 41 images containing 7,123 manually annotated aerosol particles, MobileUNet detected 99% (model-to-manual ratio) of all manually annotated aerosol particles and achieved 98% for precision, recall, and F1-score, whereas ELUNet detected 97% of particles with precision, recall, and F1-score of 98%, 96%, and 97%, respectively. MobileUNet additionally reduced computation time by approximately four-fold compared to ELUNet. These findings demonstrate that astronomical centroiding models can be directly translated to aerosol analysis maintaining high performance in real life uncontrolled and high-noise environments. This interdisciplinary approach provides a robust framework for aerosol quantification and objective assessment of mask efficacy, with potential applications in pandemic preparedness and airborne infection control.

Article.Title: Prospective evaluation of automated KU F40 fecal analysis versus microscopy for intestinal protozoa and illustrative labor costs
Article.Authors: Tunali V.; Turgay N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stool ova-and-parasite (O&P) microscopy remains widely used but is labor-intensive and constrained by expert availability. AI-assisted automated fecal analyzers can digitize stool microscopy workflows and generate images that may support remote expert review; however, evaluations should distinguish algorithm-only output from clinically deployable workflows that incorporate human verification. In a prospective diagnostic study at a tertiary-care parasitology laboratory in Izmir, Türkiye (November 2024–October 2025), 1000 consecutive, unselected adult human stool specimens submitted for routine testing were assessed in parallel by routine microscopy and the KU-F40 automated fecal analyzer. All 1,000 specimens contributed paired entries to the analysis tables. KU-F40 was evaluated as automated diagnosis (AD; algorithm call before human review) and AD plus expert user verification (AD + UV; expert review of KU-F40-generated images). The diagnostic AD + UV analysis was kept distinct from the labor-cost model, which evaluated illustrative 30%-verification and universal-verification scenarios. Relative to routine microscopy, KU-F40 AD showed positive/negative percent agreement (PPA/NPA) of 100%/99.8% for Entamoeba histolytica/dispar , 100%/98.6% for Giardia spp ., and 67.3%/97.7% for Blastocystis spp. Expert verification removed the 14 microscopy-negative Giardia AD calls and reduced microscopy-negative Blastocystis calls from 22 to 12; the two microscopy-negative E. histolytica/dispar calls remained UV-supported but were not independently adjudicated. Coccidia ( Cryptosporidium spp., Cyclospora cayetanensis ) fell outside the KU-F40 classifier panel and were identified only by conventional microscopy. The illustrative labor model assumed 35 min/specimen for microscopy and 2 min/specimen for AD, with 10 min of specialist time per verified specimen; no formal time-and-motion study was performed. The resulting modeled direct labor costs (USD/specimen) for microscopy, AD and illustrative 30%-verification AD + UV were Türkiye 4.56/0.20/0.72, Germany 21.87/0.91/3.46 and UK 27.21/0.79/4.66. KU-F40 provided a digitized screening workflow. Under the specified assumptions, the illustrative labor model yielded lower estimated hands-on labor inputs and direct labor costs than conventional microscopy; these were model outputs, not observed operational performance. Expert verification improved agreement for selected organisms, but UV-supported discordant calls were not an independent confirmation of infection. KU-F40 did not cover Cryptosporidium or Cyclospora in this evaluation; conventional and dedicated methods therefore remain necessary whenever these organisms fall within the requested diagnostic scope. Multi-site studies with measured workflow times and independent discordance adjudication are required before implementation or cost-effectiveness claims.

Article.Title: Attribute-typed Gamma transformations in fuzzy soft sets for benefit, cost, linguistic and threshold criteria in multi-criteria clinical decision-making
Article.Authors: Saeed M.; Razaq F.; Salameh W.; Saeed M.; Habib M.; Ullah M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gamma soft set models convert raw attribute data into fuzzy memberships through a single transformation for all attributes, so they cannot express attributes whose desirability peaks at a target value. We propose the attribute-typed fuzzy Gamma soft set (AT-FGSS), in which a typing map assigns each attribute one of four types (benefit, cost, linguistic or threshold) and selects a matching transformation. Threshold attributes use a Gaussian target-proximity function whose tolerance is fixed by a half-membership calibration rule. We prove its algebraic properties and define intuitionistic and interval-valued extensions. It is applied to antihypertensive regimen selection in type 2 diabetes, using illustrative assessments from three expert panels, and to a non-clinical example; all results come from deposited code. The case-study ranking is stable under changes of tolerance, weights and input noise, and matches baseline methods once threshold attributes are given their target direction; guidance from the American Diabetes Association and the Eighth Joint National Committee supports only part of it. In about 23, 000 simulated problems with known ground truth, AT-FGSS identified the best alternative more often than six baselines when alternatives straddled the targets (84.9% versus at most 64.9%), in all 15 design variations, but not when the true preference was one-sided.

Article.Title: Influence of injection mode and hydrogen enrichment on in-cylinder phenomena in CNG/HCNG engines: a simulation study
Article.Authors: Zareei J.; Guerrero J.; Prasad K.; Chohan J.; Dixit R.; Ergashev V.
Article.Abstract: This study compares CNG and HCNG combustion under direct and indirect injection using high-fidelity CFD simulations in a standard spark-ignition engine model. The objective is to understand how injection mode and hydrogen enrichment affect in-cylinder thermodynamics, mixture formation, heat release, and emissions in order to identify configurations that improve efficiency while managing nitrogen oxides (NOx) and other pollutants. Four fuel/injection configurations are examined: CNG-DI, CNG-IDI, HCNG-DI, and HCNG-IDI in a 1.6 MPI engine, a compression ratio of 14:1, and a swept volume of 1598 cc. In this engine, we applied CNG mass of 4.96496 mg and hydrogen mass corresponding to 20% in HCNG, i.e., 0.23504 mg. The governing mass, momentum, energy, and species equations are solved with detailed chemistry to capture ignition delay, flame propagation, and combustion stability. Key performance indicators include cylinder pressure and temperature histories, heat release rate (HRR), mean heat transfer coefficient (HTC) at the piston head, combustion fluctuation, and emissions indices (CO₂, NO) across the crank-angle range. The results show that direct injection (DI) yields faster energy release, higher peak pressures, and higher peak temperatures due to improved local mixing and earlier flame development. Hydrogen enrichment (HCNG) amplifies these effects. HCNG-DI exhibits the most significant pressure increase, the earliest and highest peak temperatures (approximately 1900–2000 K), and the highest HRR. Conversely, IDI produces a smoother energy release with lower peak pressures and broader ignition timing sensitivity. This offers enhanced operability and reduced carbon buildup, though it typically results in lower peak efficiency. HCNG-IDI increases NO formation due to extended high-temperature residence and stronger heat release; however, CO₂ production also increases, indicating improved combustion completeness under HCNG. These findings inform engine design regarding injection strategies and hydrogen enrichment, guiding the timing, duration, and spray characteristics for various operating conditions. The study underscores the importance of simulation-driven evaluations in selecting DI or IDI configurations and HCNG blending levels to balance power output, emissions, and reliability in future clean vehicle applications.

Article.Title: Assessing the range expansion of a generalist carnivore by a novel approach combining questionnaires to experts and dynamic occupancy models
Article.Authors: Ferreras P.; Descalzo E.; Delibes-Mateos M.; Díaz-Ruiz F.; Martínez-Jauregui M.; Soliño M.; Jiménez J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, the geographic ranges of many mesopredators are expanding, largely driven by their generalist life histories and the decline of apex predators. Quantifying these expansions and identifying their underlying drivers remain challenging and require innovative methodological approaches. We aimed at quantifying the factors driving the recent spatial expansion of the Egyptian mongoose ( Herpestes ichneumon ) at the European edge of its range. We combined occurrence data from three periods (2000–2009, 2010–2015 and 2016–2018) in the central Iberian Peninsula (Spain), collected via questionnaires to environmental rangers, with Bayesian dynamic occupancy models. Responses were obtained from 66% of rangers, covering 91.6% of municipalities (93.9% of the total area), ensuring broad spatial representation. Detection probability increased with the proportion of time rangers devoted to field work. Initial mongoose occupancy showed unimodal relationships with elevation and scrubland cover, peaking at low to intermediate elevations and at intermediate scrubland proportions. Colonization probability was highest in warmer areas, near already occupied sites, and in areas with higher scrubland cover. The Egyptian mongoose has undergone substantial expansion in central Spain between 2000 and 2018, with an estimated 262% increase in occupied municipalities (from 6.8 ± 1.5% to 24.6 ± 2.7%). Our study suggests that integrating expert-based questionnaires with dynamic occupancy models may be an effective approach for quantifying range expansions and assessing environmental drivers of colonization.

Article.Title: Dynamics of the traveling wave reduction and exact solutions of the date Jimbo Kashiwara Miwa equation for sensor modeling
Article.Authors: Khater M.
Article.Abstract: The \((2+1)\) -dimensional Date Jimbo Kashiwara Miwa (DJKM) equation is an integrable model of multidimensional dispersive waves. A traveling wave transformation reduces it to the planar Hamiltonian system \(u''=v\) , \(v''=au+bu^{2}\) , where the coefficients \(a\) and \(b\) are fixed by the wave parameters and the equation coefficients. This system is a quadratic nonlinear oscillator. Periodically forced oscillators with quadratic and cubic nonlinearities are standard models of MEMS resonators and sensors, so the reduced DJKM dynamics supply a wave based source of this oscillator class. The study classifies the two equilibria as a saddle and a center that exchange type at \(a=0\) , and it links the homoclinic loop to a solitary wave profile. Under periodic forcing, finite-time Lyapunov exponents are positive mainly for trajectories that escape past the saddle, with escape times from 5.5 to 51.6. This escape corresponds to loss of bounded motion in a resonator, and the results do not establish a bounded chaotic attractor. The Khater III method gives three periodic singular solutions, and the enhanced Kudryashov method gives four kink type solutions with bell shaped derivatives. The Vakhitov Kolokolov criterion classifies two kink branches as stable at one parameter value, and one branch is marginal. He’s variational iteration method reproduces the Khater III solution with absolute errors below \(1.4\times 10^{-9}\) at the sampled points. The analysis covers representative parameters of a deterministic, conservative model without damping or stochastic effects.

Article.Title: Quantifying high-LET heavy-ion-induced non-DSB clustered DNA lesions using Geant4-DNA
Article.Authors: Khuong T.; Lim S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ionizing radiation induces complex DNA damage that can challenge repair processes and contribute to genomic instability. In this study, we extend Geant4-DNA to quantify oxidative non-DSB damage containing 8-oxo-7,8-dihydro-2′-deoxyguanosine (8-oxo-dG) and thymidine glycol (dTg) from direct and hydroxyl-radical pathways. Simulations were performed in a reduced-scale human fibroblast chromatin geometry for 12 C, 28 Si, 40 Ar, and 56 Fe ions (LET 13–148 keV/μm). For 12 C irradiation at 94.55 MeV/u, including direct and quasi-direct oxidation raised the simulated 8-oxo-dG yield from 0.0059 ± 0.0002 to 0.0239 ± 0.0005 lesions/Mbp/Gy, approaching published experimental values. Simulated lesion frequencies matched experimental orders of magnitude, although discrepancies remained and the experimental assays and biological conditions were not fully equivalent to the simulated observables. The resulting damage profiles resolved lesion identity and local multiplicity. Clusters containing one single-strand break and one oxidative base lesion were the predominant non-DSB clustered configurations, particularly SSB + 8-oxo-dG (9.4%–13.2%) and SSB + dTg (8.5%–12.8%). This framework extends Geant4-DNA beyond conventional strand-break analysis, offering lesion-resolved inputs for mechanistic base excision repair models under heavy-ion irradiation.

Article.Title: Experiences of nurses in pre-hospital extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a descriptive phenomenological study
Article.Authors: Cheng M.; Wang Y.; Zhang Y.; Yu M.; Bai X.; Wan H.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pre-hospital extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) requires coordinated work under severe time and environmental constraints, yet nurses' lived experiences remain poorly understood. We explored how nurses experience this work, the challenges they encounter, and the support they consider necessary.We conducted a single-center descriptive phenomenological study in China. Purposive sampling recruited 14 emergency nurses and seven extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) specialist nurses. Data from face-to-face semi-structured interviews were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method.The 21 participants included 11 men and 10 women, with a mean age of 32.2 years (range 24-49). Three interrelated themes captured the experience: dual emotional experiences, challenges in the treatment process, and demands for improving treatment quality. Both professional groups contributed to all themes, while describing role-related emphases in scene-based emergency work and ECMO activation, equipment, and transport.The findings show how emotional strain, technical and organizational constraints, and perceived support needs intersect in one Chinese pre-hospital ECPR program. They support locally adapted training, team protocols, communication support, and staff well-being measures, while requiring cautious transfer to other settings.

Article.Title: Evaluation of zeolitic imidazolate frameworks as catalyst in hydrothermal reduction of CO2
Article.Authors: Pourbagherian E.; Mehrdad A.; Noorani N.
Article.Abstract: Rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration has intensified the global climate crisis that necessary to urgency attentions. In this research, Co:Mn-ZIF-4 and carbonized Co:Mn-ZIF-4 with various ratio of Co:Mn were synthesized by a simple one-step chemical method and characterized with XRD, BET TGA , EDX and Raman analysis. The catalytic activity of Co:Mn-ZIF-4 and carbonized Co:Mn-ZIF-4 were investigated for carbon dioxide reduction in hydrothermal conditions. The experimental results reveals that Co:Mn-ZIF-4 and carbonized Co:Mn-ZIF-4 had catalytic activity for carbon dioxide reduction for formic acid and acetic acid. The effect of reaction temperature and reaction time were evaluated for reaction yield. The obtained results reveal that Mn-ZIF-4 and carbonized Co:Mn-ZIF-4 (2:2) had the beast catalytic activity with respect others catalysts. The obtained results from various reaction temperature shows that the 250 °C was optimum temperature for reduction of carbon dioxide in hydrothermal conditions. Also the obtained results from various reaction time shows that the 3 h at 250 °C was optimum time for reduction of carbon dioxide in hydrothermal conditions. The maximum reaction yield for carbon dioxide reduction in hydrothermal conditions was obtained 28% for carbonized CO:Mn-ZIF-4 (2:2) at temperature 250 °C and 3 h.

Article.Title: A hybrid deep learning framework with domain-adapted embeddings for regulatory violation classification
Article.Authors: Li S.
Article.Abstract: Regulatory violation classification encounters fundamental challenges arising from the lack of domain-specific knowledge in general-purpose language models, insufficient multi-granular feature representation in single-architecture frameworks, and severe class imbalance characteristic of real-world regulatory datasets. This study introduces a hybrid deep learning framework integrating three synergistic innovations to address these limitations through domain-adapted embedding fusion, hierarchical feature extraction, and class-aware contrastive learning mechanisms. The domain-adapted dual-layer embedding fusion (DA-DLEF) dynamically combines general linguistic knowledge, specialized legal understanding, and regulatory-specific terminology through attention-based integration, while the Hierarchical Hybrid Feature Extraction Network (H2-FEN) captures discriminative patterns across local n-gram sequences, bidirectional temporal dependencies, and global contextual relationships through multi-scale convolutional processing, recurrent modeling, and regulatory-biased self-attention mechanisms. The class-aware contrastive fusion classifier (CA-CFC) optimizes inter-class separability and intra-class compactness through supervised contrastive learning combined with focal loss and multi-expert fusion strategies. Comprehensive evaluation on a constructed dataset of Chinese administrative penalty decisions demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, particularly for minority violation categories, validating the effectiveness of domain adaptation, hierarchical architecture design, and contrastive learning in enhancing classification performance. The framework provides practical solutions for governmental regulatory agencies requiring automated violation categorization with enhanced accuracy and equitable treatment of underrepresented categories.

Article.Title: Functional dependence, cognitive function, and nutritional status are independently associated with oral health in care-dependent older residents in integrated medical and nursing care institutions
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Huang Y.; Wang T.; Dai H.; Peng C.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the oral health of older inpatients with disabilities and its links to functional dependence, cognitive function, and nutritional status in medical-care institutions. This study utilized a cross-sectional design between June and December 2025 and recruited a convenience sample of 150 older inpatients with disabilities from two comparable medical-care institutions in terms of care level and patient characteristics. Data collection involved oral examinations, which included the Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index, Gingival Index (GI), and assessment of prosthetic status (classified as ideal or non-ideal). Additionally, evaluations were conducted using the Barthel Index, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score, Mini Nutritional Assessment Short-Form (MNA-SF) score, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and medication count. Data analysis was carried out using multiple linear regression for continuous outcomes (DMFT index and GI) and logistic regression for the binary outcome (prosthetic status). The study population demonstrated significant systemic health challenges, with a mean age of 82.79 ± 8.32 years. Severe functional dependence was observed in 72.7% of participants, cognitive impairment in 68.7%, and a risk of malnutrition in 63.3%. The mean Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index was 25.17 ± 6.55, and 77.3% of participants exhibited non-ideal prosthetic status. The mean Gingival Index (GI) was 1.39 ± 0.73 among 139 participants with natural teeth, as 11 edentulous participants were excluded from GI analyses. Multiple regression analyses identified distinct association patterns: the DMFT index was independently associated with a lower Barthel Index (B = − 0.099, 95% CI − 0.154 to − 0.044, p < 0.001) and a lower MNA-SF score (B = − 0.778, 95% CI − 1.173 to − 0.383, p < 0.001). The GI was independently associated with an increased number of medications (B = 0.109, 95% CI 0.013 to 0.204, p = 0.026) and a lower MNA-SF score (B = − 0.121, 95% CI − 0.168 to − 0.074, p < 0.001). Non-ideal prosthetic status was independently associated with a higher CCI score (OR = 2.762, 95% CI 1.287 to 5.927, p = 0.009), a lower Barthel Index (OR = 0.946, 95% CI 0.908 to 0.987, p = 0.010), and a lower MMSE score (OR = 0.803, 95% CI 0.696 to 0.928, p = 0.003). Older inpatients with disabilities in medical-care institutions exhibit significant oral health challenges. Distinct core health dimensions are associated with dental caries, gingival inflammation, and prosthetic status. Given the cross-sectional design, these associations should not be interpreted as causal. Nevertheless, the observed patterns suggest potential targets for comprehensive oral health strategies that may incorporate nutritional support, functional rehabilitation, medication management, and cognitive care.

Article.Title: A catalogue of solar rotation-scale variations in the first Schumann resonance frequency at high latitudes, 2004–2024
Article.Authors: Tacza J.; Bozoki T.; Satori G.; Neska A.; Raita T.; Bor J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Schumann resonances (SR) are extremely low-frequency (ELF) electromagnetic resonances of the Earth–ionosphere cavity, excited primarily by global lightning activity. Their modal frequencies can vary with the effective electrical properties and dimensions of the cavity, including lower-ionospheric conditions. Solar-rotation-scale variability has been reported in SR parameters, but its appearance in long-term SR frequency time series has not yet been systematically studied. We analyzed daily peak-frequency measurements of the first-mode SR (F1) from Hornsund (Svalbard), Ivalo, and Rovaniemi (both in northern Finland) from 2004/2005 to 2024. The north–south and east–west component time series were examined for time-localized wavelet power in the predefined 25–29-day, 12–15-day, and 8–11-day bands. Temporally overlapping detections in the same target band were grouped across the six F1 time series and labeled as events. Events detected at two or more stations were defined as multi-station events. For these events, we estimated band-limited F1 amplitudes and examined their relationships with solar-wind speed, geomagnetic indices, solar-radiation proxies, and lightning counts using the cross-wavelet transform and wavelet coherence. We identified 8, 29, and 68 time-localized events in the respective bands, of which 2, 4, and 25 were multi-station events. The 25–29-day activity was episodic rather than persistent, with the clearest case occurring across all three stations in late 2020. Same-band, phase-stable coherence was found mainly with solar-wind speed and the AE and Kp geomagnetic indices. Many events coincided with high-speed streams, stream interaction regions, or ICME/sheath intervals, although only a subset showed same-band, phase-stable coherence in individual F1 time series. After correction for multiple comparisons, the timing tests did not establish individual event–driver associations or an excess of solar-wind event overlaps. Comparisons with simulated records provided limited statistical support for an excess of events, with results depending on the assumed background. No single driver could be established. Within these statistical limits, the findings indicate that solar-rotation-timescale variability can appear in high-latitude SR F1 as small, time-localized modulations rather than as a persistent 27-day oscillation.

Article.Title: Colonic fermentation-derived metabolites of bread crust melanoidins modulate oxidative and inflammatory responses in a 3D neuronal OGD/R model
Article.Authors: Gerardi G.; Salazar G.; Muñiz P.; Cavia-Saiz M.
Article.Abstract: Bread crust melanoidins are high-molecular-weight Maillard reaction products that generate bioactive metabolites during colonic fermentation. This study evaluated the effects of the colonic fermentation-derived melanoidin fraction (CFM) on redox homeostasis and HIF-1α/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling in a three-dimensional neuronal model of oxygen–glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Bread crust melanoidins were isolated and subjected to standardized in vitro gastrointestinal and human fecal colonic fermentation. The dialyzed CFM was characterized by HPLC-DAD, GC-FID, and antioxidant assays. Its biological activity was evaluated in differentiated 3D SH-SY5Y neuronal spheroids exposed to OGD/R. Chemical characterization of CFM, a complex fermentation mixture, revealed phenolic compounds and short-chain fatty acids. OGD/R increased cell death and intracellular ROS significantly whereas CFM pretreatment reduced these responses by 41.9% and 21.6%. Notably, CFM attenuated OGD/R-induced oxidative damage, reducing 8-OHdG levels by 57.0%. CFM also modulated HIF-1α/NF-κB/NLRP3-associated responses, including reductions of 42.6% in NLRP3 and 47.2% in caspase-1 protein, together with a 51.3% reduction in the p-NF-κB/NF-κB ratio. In parallel, CFM modulated Akt/p38 MAPK/Nrf2-associated signaling, increasing the p-Nrf2/Nrf2 ratio by 44.5% relative to OGD/R. CFM also attenuated OGD/R-induced antioxidant gene expression, particularly GPX2 and HO-1, by 39.1% and 60.6%, respectively. These findings suggests that CFM modulates redox and inflammatory responses under hypoxic stress in vitro, including changes in HIF-1α/NF-κB/NLRP3- and Nrf2-associated signaling.

Article.Title: Decoupling flash drought frequency, intensification rate, and persistence across Iran’s heterogeneous hydrological basins
Article.Authors: Shafizadeh-Moghadam H.
Article.Abstract: This study quantified three distinct characteristics of flash drought (FD) ​across Iran’s major hydrological basins during 2003–2023. The analysis used pentad-scale, 0–100 cm depth-averaged soil-moisture percentiles derived from ERA5-Land and GLDAS-2.1. Events were detected using a continuous pentad sequence when soil moisture declined from above the 40th to below the 20th percentile within four pentads at a mean rate of at least five percentile points pentad⁻¹. Robust-scaled long-term means of event rate, intensification rate, and restricted persistence were classified using partitioning around medoids (PAM). The analysis identified 7,044 rapid-onset pixel events; 1,188 (16.9%) continued beyond 90 days, and 88 right-censored candidates were excluded from completed-event persistence. Basin means ranged from 0.004 to 0.707 events pixel⁻¹ yr⁻¹, 12.33 to 17.72 percentile points pentad⁻¹ for intensification rate, and 33.56 to 54.78 days for restricted persistence. A three-group PAM typology (13, 12, and 5 basins) revealed substantive within-country heterogeneity, although its silhouette score (0.254) and bootstrap Jaccard values (0.591–0.627) indicate an exploratory rather than definitive partition. Five basin–metric trends had raw p < 0.05, but none remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. These results demonstrate that recurrence, onset rapidity, and subseasonal persistence are related but non-interchangeable dimensions of FD behavior.

Article.Title: Podophyllotoxin disrupts the XIAP–caspase-9 interaction to promote apoptosis: insights from a quantitative split-luciferase complementation assay
Article.Authors: Ebrahimi K.; Ataei F.; Hosseinkhani S.
Article.Abstract: Podophyllotoxin (PTOX), a plant-derived lignan with potent anticancer properties, is hypothesized to mimic Smac activity by interacting with Inhibitor of Apoptosis Protein (IAP) BIR domains. However, the precise molecular mechanisms governing these interactions remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed and validated a highly sensitive, cell-free split-luciferase complementation assay designed to quantify the real-time interaction dynamics between the BIR2–BIR3 domains of XIAP and its key targets, caspase-3 and caspase-9. Our results demonstrate that the BIR2–BIR3–NLuc/caspase-9-CLuc interaction is significantly more robust and stable than the BIR2–BIR3–NLuc/caspase-3-CLuc interaction, highlighting a preferential binding mechanism at the initiator caspase level. Utilizing this platform, we investigated the effects of PTOX in modulating this interaction. Consistent with in silico docking predictions, PTOX disrupted the XIAP–caspase-9 complex in a concentration-dependent manner, leading to a marked reduction in luminescence and a subsequent restoration of caspase-9 enzymatic activity. While PTOX showed a minor inhibitory effect on the XIAP–caspase-3 interaction, its impact on the caspase-9 axis was markedly more pronounced. Furthermore, Carboplatin, a DNA-crosslinking agent, exhibited no significant impact on these protein-protein interactions, confirming the specificity of the observed PTOX-mediated effects. These findings establish a sensitive, real-time platform for monitoring the XIAP–caspase axis and provide compelling evidence that PTOX acts as a targeted modulator of the apoptotic pathway, warranting its further development as a pharmacological agent.
