Article.Title: Psychometric assessment of visual enclosure and walkability in intermediate urban spaces through virtual reality
Article.Authors: Belkacem M.; Abdelhakim H.; Nadia L.; Aya A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban environments are complex systems influenced by spatial, visual, and functional factors. Walkability assessments often depend on subjective opinions and symmetric distance-to-height ratios, assuming that streets are framed by similar surfaces on both sides. This study used immersive virtual reality (VR) to examine visual enclosure in intermediate spaces, while maintaining a consistent stimulus for all participants and a 360° experience. Fifty-nine panoramas, taken at twenty stations along a 1.5 km route in Batna, Algeria, were converted into achromatic line images. Each station was coded for boundary type and two signed asymmetry indices, geometric and material. Ninety-six architecture students completed a twenty-item questionnaire at each station; fifteen items formed five reliable sub-scales, and the medium was widely accepted (92.7%). Participants reported both enclosure (80%) and openness (96%), which seemed to coexist, but rated legibility poorly. In an ordinal mixed model, greater permeability asymmetry between the two boundaries was linked to less favorable ratings (OR = 0.597, 95% CI 0.393–0.906), while geometric indicators were not; 3.5% of the variance was between stations. These exploratory findings, from a single route and a student sample, suggest that boundary permeability may deserve attention alongside height in street design, and that immersive assessment provides a practical way to study how urban space is experienced.

Article.Title: Structural insights into bromodomain-containing complexes from Trypanosoma cruzi revealed by proximity labeling and stoichiometric space exploration
Article.Authors: Rodríguez Araya E.; Martínez Peralta G.; Alonso V.; Serra E.
Article.Abstract: Trypanosoma cruzi , the etiological agent of Chagas disease, remains a major health concern due to the limited efficacy and toxicity of current treatments. Bromodomain factors (BDFs), which recognize acetylated lysine residues, are key components of epigenetic regulatory machinery and represent promising therapeutic targets. Despite their importance, structural organization of bromodomain-containing complexes in trypanosomatids is poorly understood. In this study, we combined experimental and computational approaches to investigate the composition and stoichiometry of BDF-containing complexes in T. cruzi . Using TurboID-based proximity labeling, we mapped interaction networks for five BDFs (BDF3, BDF4, BDF5, BDF6 and BDF8) and identified two major complexes, CRKT and NuA4. To further resolve their architecture, we applied structure prediction methods that explore multiple stoichiometric configurations. Our analyses indicate that CRKT is organized into three modules with distinct interaction dynamics, whereas NuA4 comprises two modules. The CRKT core module displays a symmetric arrangement containing two copies of BDF3, BDF5, and BDF8. Its catalytic module contains three subunits including HAT2, while the BET module contains BDF4 and BDF1. In NuA4, the catalytic module resembles the yeast piccolo-NuA4 complex and includes HAT1, with the TINTIN module associating via BDF6. These findings provide structural insights into epigenetic complexes in trypanosomatids and support their potential as drug targets.

Article.Title: Aster-derived biogenic silver nanoparticles for multifaceted study on antioxidant, para-nitrophenol catalysis, cytotoxicity, and in silico molecular docking evaluation
Article.Authors: Thahir A.; Kandiah M.; Gunaratne B.; Perera O.
Article.Abstract: Advancements in nanotechnology have expanded its prospects as a promising avenue for addressing concerns over environmental remediation, sustainability, and industrial waste management through the development of metal-based nanoparticles. This study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using four varieties of Aster flowers (white, pink, lavender, and violet) and their potential for antioxidants, catalytic, cytotoxic, and in silico molecular docking activities. The UV–Vis spectral analysis confirmed successful AgNP formation under optimal conditions of 90 °C for 30 min. Comprehensive characterization of A_Whi_AgNPs using scanning electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, X-ray diffraction, and energy-dispersive X-ray analysis confirmed crystalline face-centered cubic structures, spherical morphology and 61.0% Ag. Catalytic degradation of p-nitrophenol demonstrated concentration-dependent catalytic activity; complete degradation within 25 min for 10 µL of 4000 ppm AgNPs and instantaneous degradation with 50 µL, with A_Vio_AgNP achieving the highest rate constant ( k = 0.4346 min⁻ 1 ). The AgNPs showed high Artemia salina viability at 200 ppm and 800 ppm, whereas zebrafish embryo exposure revealed model- and exposure-time-dependent toxicity. In silico molecular docking studies revealed a stable interaction with the Ag 3 cluster and amino acid residues in the epidermal growth factor receptor (PDB: 1M17), yielding the highest binding energy (-1.24 kcal/mol). These findings indicate that Aster -derived AgNPs possess multifaceted properties and strong catalytic activity, with effective applicability in bioremediation and industrial wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Polymetallic nodules provide a distinct habitat for abyssal meiofauna
Article.Authors: Diaz-Recio Lorenzo C.; Stratmann T.; de Wilt M.; Radhakrishnan R.; Macheriotou L.; Pape E.; Hoogerdijk L.; van den Hooven-Iza N.; Krüger J.; Kaspersmeier L.; Neuser M.; Klöckner M.; Lauth M.; Schaper M.; Patel T.; Gollner S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep-sea abyssal plains harbour extensive biodiversity, much of which remains undocumented. Polymetallic nodules in the abyssal plains of the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), Central Pacific, harbour diverse meiofaunal communities within their crevices, representing an understudied habitat. Given their high concentrations of nickel, copper, and cobalt, nodules are currently one of the primary targets for the extraction of deep-sea mineral resources. Here, we characterise the physical properties of polymetallic nodules, quantify their meiofaunal crevice communities, and compare them to those from the nearby sediments. We show that nodules contain internal cracks and microfossils, that their crevices harbour meiofaunal communities dominated by nematodes and copepods, and that faunal abundance increases significantly with nodule volume. Foraminifera were also a recurrent component of nodule-crevice assemblages. Nodule-crevice nematode and copepod abundances were equivalent to approximately 10% and 25%, respectively, of those recorded in nearby sediments across the two exploration contract areas in the eastern CCZ. Based on 18S rRNA data, nematode and copepod assemblages recovered from nodule crevices differed from those recovered from nearby sediments collected during the same expedition and within the same exploration contract areas. Our findings, therefore, demonstrate the presence of nodule-associated crevice fauna and the consequent risk of biodiversity loss associated with nodule removal through potential future commercial mining.

Article.Title: A novel fluorescent ocular tracer enables detection of TDP-43 pathology in ALS and related TDP-43 proteinopathies using retinal imaging
Article.Authors: Pilotte J.; Mandel Z.; Sharma S.; Khoury S.; Huang A.; Tafreshi A.; Vanderklish P.; Weinreb R.; Reiman E.; Frosch M.; Svendsen C.; Ly C.; Harris B.; Berry J.; Cudkowicz M.; Sarraf S.
Article.Abstract: Molecular biomarkers of neurodegenerative disease are positioned to facilitate earlier diagnosis and treatment, therapeutic development, and define disease heterogeneities that inform precision interventions. The retina, an optically accessible extension of the central nervous system, manifests biomarkers for many neurodegenerative diseases, providing an opportunity for simple, non-invasive detection. This study evaluates a new method to fluorescently label retinal deposits associated with TDP-43 pathology, a key biomarker of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy (LATE), using a prototype of a clinical-stage small molecule, AMDX-8050. In cadaveric ALS retinas, AMDX-8050 labeled cytoplasmic retinal deposits that co-localized with TDP-43 pathology and revealed a dense and spatially varied distribution of deposits resembling those observed in matched spinal cord and motor cortex cadaver tissues. Additionally, AMDX-8050 labeled deposits that co-localized with TDP-43 pathology in retinas from FTD-TDP-43 and LATE cadaver tissues. These results support the potential of a new class of retinal tracers with broad utility for the TDP-43 proteinopathies.

Article.Title: Mechanistic sensitivity analysis of musculoskeletal factors affecting dropped-head syndrome-like sagittal alignment using a human finite-element model
Article.Authors: Nakahira Y.; Iwamoto M.; Igawa T.; Urata R.; Ishii K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dropped-head syndrome (DHS) is characterised by excessive head and neck flexion, impaired horizontal gaze and sagittal imbalance, particularly in older adults. Although rehabilitation targeting muscle function has shown clinical benefits, the underlying biomechanical mechanisms remain unclear. We conducted a mechanistic sensitivity analysis using a human finite-element model with a muscle controller to quantify how changes in passive muscle and tendon elastic moduli and hip-muscle activation affect sagittal alignment. Adult and elderly model conditions were compared. Reductions in passive elastic moduli increased the chin–brow vertical angle (CBVA) and decreased the C2–7 angle most prominently without active muscle force, whereas these effects were limited when muscle activation was retained. Reduced hip-muscle activation decreased the C7–S1 sagittal vertical axis and sacral slope. However, CBVA generally remained below the clinical DHS range when muscle activation was retained. The simulations represented transient responses to gravity rather than stable DHS standing posture. These findings identify model-predicted biomechanical responses and generate hypotheses concerning interactions among cervical muscle activity, passive musculoskeletal properties and trunk–pelvic alignment. Further experimental and clinical validation is required before these hypotheses can inform rehabilitation strategies.

Article.Title: Association between low muscle mass and hearing impairment in older adults: results from a national cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wu C.; Zhang T.; Liu Y.; Pan X.; Qin J.; Li M.; Cai X.
Article.Abstract: Hearing impairment is a prevalent and debilitating condition with limited established modifiable risk factors. The specific association between muscle mass, as a modifiable component, and hearing impairment remains underexplored. Data from 13,532 participants in the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS) were included in the analysis. A body composition estimation formula was employed to estimate muscle mass. Hearing status was evaluated by trained interviewers. Multivariable logistic regression models were employed to estimate odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression was used to examine a non-linear association between muscle mass and hearing impairment. In the fully adjusted model, participants without low muscle mass (LMM) had a significantly reduced likelihood of hearing impairment (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.45–0.67, P < 0.001), using individuals with LMM as the reference group. This association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses. RCS regression indicated a generally linear inverse relationship between muscle mass and the likelihood of hearing impairment. This study found that LMM is associated with hearing impairment in older adults, demonstrating a consistent pattern across both sexes. Improving muscle mass may be associated with hearing health. Subsequent research can develop targeted interventions and validate their effectiveness.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving clinical data exchange using an AI-enabled zero-trust framework for Internet of Medical Things and cloud healthcare
Article.Authors: Chauhan V.; Arya N.; Soni G.; Amhia H.; Rani M.; Roy V.; Ojha S.
Article.Abstract: The growing proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoMT) and cloud-based health care services has highlighted the demand for clinical data sharing in various heterogeneous platforms via secure and privacy-preserving communications. The paper presents an AID-based Zero-Trust solution combining behavioral anomaly detection, fuzzy trust evaluation, RL-based adaptive access control, federated learning, privacy-preserving computation and blockchain-based auditing. CNN–BiLSTM is used to detect behavioral threats, and fuzzy trust/policy optimization is applied to access decisions, with consideration for context. Collaborative analysis is achieved without directly sharing sensitive information by utilizing federated learning and secure computation, while blockchain offers tamper-resistant auditability. The proposed framework is evaluated by using data from intrusion detection systems of the health care sector to show its effectiveness for both classification and security purposes. The integrated architecture offers a holistic way of continuous verification, adaptive authorization, privacy protection, and accountable clinical data exchange in the distributed environment of IoMT and cloud-based healthcare.

Article.Title: Comprehensive taphonomic study of the surface and histology of Pleistocene fossils from a fluvio-lacustrine system in the Humid Pampas
Article.Authors: Marin-Monfort D.; Fernández-Jalvo Y.; Fernández F.; Tomassini R.; García-Morato S.; Garrone M.; Montalvo C.; Gómez G.; Bonini R.; Bellinzoni J.; Steffan P.; Alberdi M.; Prado J.
Article.Abstract: Fluvio-lacustrine environments preserve abundant vertebrate fossil assemblages and provide valuable settings for investigating the biological, physical and chemical processes involved in fossilisation. However, integrated taphonomic studies combining macrotaphonomic observations with histotaphonomic and mineralogical analyses remain scarce. Here, we apply a multiproxy approach to reconstruct decomposition, transport, burial and fossildiagenesis within a well-constrained fluvio-lacustrine succession, using the Salto de Piedra Palaeontological Locality in the Argentine Pampas as a case study. Carnivore modifications recorded throughout the fossil-bearing sequence indicate that predation and scavenging were the principal drivers of carcass accumulation, disarticulation, bone fragmentation and skeletal dispersal. The absence of microbial bioerosion is consistent with rapid skeletonisation, suggesting that early carnivore activity limited bacterial degradation of bone tissues during decay. Despite deposition in an open-air fluvio-lacustrine setting, the fossils exhibit minimal evidence of subaerial exposure, including low levels of weathering and abrasion. Permineralisation is likewise limited and involves predominantly iron oxides and carbonate minerals. These findings support the formation of mainly autochthonous to parautochthonous attritional assemblages under low-energy depositional conditions. Our results demonstrate the value of integrating multiple taphonomic proxies to reconstruct fossil preservation pathways and improve palaeoenvironmental, palaeoecological and biochronological interpretations of Quaternary continental vertebrate assemblages.

Article.Title: Enhanced jellyfish search-optimized cascaded fuzzy-FOPI control of a three-phase dynamic voltage restorer for power quality improvement
Article.Authors: Kotb H.; Fawzy H.; Hassan H.; Khairalla A.; Khouj M.; AboRas K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Power quality disturbances, particularly voltage sags and swells, pose significant challenges to modern distribution networks with increasing penetration of nonlinear loads and renewable energy resources. Dynamic voltage restorers (DVRs) are highly effective custom power devices for mitigating such disturbances; however, their performance depends strongly on the employed control strategy. This paper proposes an advanced hybrid control framework for a three-phase DVR based on a cascaded fuzzy logic controller (FLC) and fractional-order proportional-integral (FOPI) controller, optimally tuned using the Enhanced Jellyfish Search (EJS) algorithm. To overcome the limitations of conventional trial-and-error fuzzy tuning, EJS is employed to optimize 34 hybrid controller parameters (encompassing both the fuzzy membership functions and FOPI gains) by minimizing the integral squared error (ISE) in the synchronous dq reference frame. The proposed controller is validated in MATLAB/Simulink under severe symmetrical and asymmetrical faults, including LLLG, LLG, LL, and LG conditions. Comparative results against conventional PI and non-optimized fuzzy controllers demonstrate superior transient response, voltage restoration, and harmonic suppression. The proposed EJS-optimized Fuzzy-FOPI DVR achieves near-zero overshoot, reduced settling time, and a low total harmonic distortion of 0.76%, satisfying IEEE standards and providing a reliable, high-performance solution for power quality enhancement.

Article.Authors: Ryu J.; Moon S.; Yoo H.; Yi J.; Kim S.; Yoon H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We aimed to develop a transformer-based model to predict kidney outcomes from longitudinal electronic health records (EHR) of patients with diabetes and normal kidney function, and compared it with. logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), LightGBM, and XGBoost. Using EHR data from 8,772 patients (Seoul National University Bundang Hospital, 2003–2014), we predicted ≥ 30% estimated Glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline and advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years (event 1.2–8.4%). ForeGFR decline, LightGBM and XGBoost both outperformed the transformer at every horizon (AUROC 0.68–0.80 vs. 0.56–0.75), for advanced CKD, the transformer-based model achieved AUROC of 0.77–0.85, comparable to the trees. At a matched operating point (recall 0.8), F1 scores were comparable across models. The transformer was overconfident and, unlike the trees, did not exceed treat-all net benefit in decision-curve analysis. It was, however, more robust to input degradation: retaining only 25% of laboratory values reduced AUROC by 0.03 versus 0.23–0.30 for the trees. Under temporal validation (training ≤ 2009, testing 2009–2016), AUROC fell by an average of 0.09. These findings support the technical feasibility of sequence models for EHR data while highlighting the need for recalibration and external validation before clinical use.

Article.Title: Synergistic effect of XYL-1 and Olaparib in BRCA-proficient TNBC cells is associated with RAD51 and BRCA1 downregulation
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Zhu Q.; Du Y.; Huang L.; Qian B.
Article.Abstract: Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase1/2 (PARP1/2) inhibitors are approved for HER2-negative breast cancer harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations, including TNBC. However, the majority of patients with BRCA-proficient derive limited benefit from these agents. In this study, we demonstrate that the efficacy of the PARP1/2 inhibitor Olaparib in BRCA-proficient TNBC cell lines can be markedly enhanced by co-treatment with the PARP7 inhibitor XYL-1. Our results demonstrated that the combination of Olaparib and XYL-1 significantly inhibited the proliferation of BRCA-proficient MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468 cells compared with either monotherapy, with the strongest synergistic effect observed at a 1:1 molar ratio in MDA-MB-231 cells. Furthermore, the combination of Olaparib and XYL-1 significantly increased cellular ROS levels, induced DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), and ultimately promoted apoptosis. In vivo , the combined treatment significantly suppressed MDA-MB-231 tumor growth compared with either monotherapy, while exhibiting a favorable safety profile. Mechanistically, co-treatment with XYL-1 and Olaparib significantly downregulated RAD51 and BRCA1 expression, which may be associated with impaired homologous recombination (HR)-mediated DNA repair. Collectively, these findings suggest that dual targeting of PARP7 and PARP1/2 represents a promising combination strategy for the treatment of BRCA-proficient TNBC.

Article.Title: An integrated framework combining interpretability and exploratory dependency analysis for flood susceptibility assessment in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region
Article.Authors: Yan F.; Wang J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Flood susceptibility in rapidly urbanizing regions is shaped by terrain, infrastructure, land cover and climate variability, yet modelled spatial associations remain difficult to interpret. We assessed urban inundation susceptibility in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region using 895 Amap inundation locations, 895 sampled background locations and 17 conditioning factors. After feature screening, eight machine-learning algorithms were compared. Random Forest was selected by validation ROC-AUC (0.9476), closely followed by Extra Trees (0.9469). Its independent-test AUC was 0.9447 (95% CI 0.9218–0.9645), with accuracy of 0.8743, precision of 0.8807, recall of 0.8659 and F1 score of 0.8732. Lower scores occurred in the northwestern mountains and higher scores in the central, southern and southeastern plains, reflecting the distribution of reported urban inundation. SHAP and generalized additive models identified land cover and road-related variables as leading predictors and described their nonlinear contributions. LiNGAM summarised joint dependencies among predictors and spatially cross-fitted scores. All 15 residual-independence tests rejected independence, limiting the graph to exploratory interpretation. Future maps varied five precipitation predictors under three SSP pathways while holding 2020 land cover and other static factors fixed. The four 30-year climate windows are illustrative snapshots; 94.72–100% of future cells fell outside the central training range (1st–99th percentiles) for at least one continuous predictor. The maps estimate relative susceptibility to reported urban inundation, not annual flood probabilities or flood risk.

Article.Title: Deptor deficiency protects against acute lung injury through autophagy regulation
Article.Authors: Pan R.; Mao J.; Wang C.; Zheng Y.; Wang L.; Chen W.; Guo J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute lung injury (ALI) is characterized by damage to alveolar epithelial and capillary endothelial cells, resulting in respiratory failure. The mTOR pathway plays a critical role in the progression of ALI, where its dysregulation leads to excessive autophagy activation and exacerbates cellular injury. Notably, Deptor has been identified as a key endogenous regulator of mTOR signaling. To investigate the role of Deptor in ALI pathogenesis, we used type II alveolar epithelial cell-specific Deptor knockout mice subjected to hemorrhagic shock and intratracheal lipopolysaccharide (LPS) instillation as an in vivo model, and employed LPS-stimulated MLE-12 cells for in vitro mechanistic exploration. Pathological changes, inflammatory responses, apoptosis, and key molecules of the mTOR signaling pathway and autophagy-related proteins were evaluated. Comparative analysis showed that Deptor knockout (Deptor⁻/⁻+ALI) mice exhibited significant alleviation of ALI-associated pathology. Deptor deletion markedly suppressed alveolar epithelial cell apoptosis and restored mTOR signaling. These protective effects were consistently observed in MLE-12 cells following Deptor knockdown. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of autophagy by 3‑MA reversed the detrimental effects of Deptor overexpression in LPS‑stimulated MLE-12 cells, reducing apoptosis and improving cell viability. Our study indicate that Deptor is upregulated in ALI and LPS‑stimulated cells, and that its elevation exacerbates injury via mTOR inhibition and autophagy hyperactivation, while its deficiency alleviates ALI by restoring mTOR signaling and limiting excessive autophagy. These results suggest Deptor as a potential therapeutic target for ALI.

Article.Title: MOSAIC (morphology-oriented spatial attention for inferring cell expression)
Article.Authors: Fernandes T.; Vesco M.; de-Mira G.; Fernandes D.; Morais M.; Simizo A.; Nakaya H.; Camilo C.
Article.Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression in tissue, but cost and throughput limit large studies of ulcerative colitis and related disorders. Here we present MOSAIC, a two-phase computational framework that predicts single-cell gene expression from routine H&E histology and then assigns cell lineages using only those predicted profiles. Phase A uses each cell’s image together with six spatially nearest neighbours; Phase B classifies nine curator-defined in-house lineages (integrative clustering of challenge expression; not supplied as challenge annotations) without further use of images. On inflamed colon tissue from the Autoimmune Disease Machine Learning Challenge, with training and test on different patient sections, mean agreement between predicted and measured expression was modest (Pearson 0.22 and Spearman 0.17 across 460 genes) with heterogeneous recovery across genes, and lineage accuracy reached 63%—well above chance (11%) and a majority-class rule (14%), though below a control trained on measured expression (95%). Predicted profiles therefore retain usable lineage structure on a held-out section. These findings support a proof-of-concept under conservative evaluation; they do not establish clinical utility or generalisation beyond this dataset.

Article.Title: Ca2+ signaling through the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor α5 subunit in human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells
Article.Authors: Nakahama K.; Yamamura A.; Kondo R.; Suzuki Y.; Yamamura H.
Article.Abstract: In pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), elevations in cytosolic Ca 2+ concentration ([Ca 2+ ] cyt ) are essential for physiological processes such as cell contraction and viability, suggesting the importance of Ca 2+ signaling in PASMC function. In the present study, the functional expression of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) in human PASMCs was investigated using quantitative real-time PCR, Western blotting, whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, cytosolic Ca 2+ imaging, and cell viability assays. Expression analyses revealed that the α5 subunit of nAChR (nAChRα5) is abundantly expressed in human PASMCs. At a holding potential of -60 mV, nicotine evoked rapidly activating and inactivating inward currents in human PASMCs, which were markedly suppressed by hexamethonium, a nonselective nAChR antagonist. Similar nicotine-induced and hexamethonium-sensitive currents were observed in HEK293 cells expressing human nAChRα5. Nicotine also induced a concentration-dependent increase in [Ca 2+ ] cyt (EC 50 = 395 µM), which was inhibited by hexamethonium. Both nicotine-induced inward currents and [Ca 2+ ] cyt elevations were attenuated by siRNA-mediated knockdown of nAChRα5. Furthermore, knockdown of nAChRα5 significantly reduced PASMC viability. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nAChRα5 is highly expressed and functionally active in PASMCs, where it mediates nicotine-induced Ca 2+ signaling and regulates cell viability, suggesting a physiological role for this subunit in pulmonary vascular function.

Article.Title: Determination of excitation energy transfer efficiency in individual artificial light-harvesting complexes mimicking chlorosomes
Article.Authors: Malina T.; Hancock A.; Meredith S.; Kapusta P.; Kaftan D.; Adams P.; Psencik J.
Article.Abstract: Artificial light-harvesting antennas inspired by chlorosomes, the main light-harvesting complexes of green photosynthetic bacteria, represent self-assembling model systems for applications in solar energy conversion. They contain bacteriochlorophyll aggregates with remarkable light-harvesting properties. The pigments are purified from chlorosomes, thus avoiding an expensive chemical synthesis. Here we present results obtained on individual artificial light-harvesting complexes containing bacteriochlorophyll c as the main light-harvesting pigment, β-carotene as an aggregation-inducing agent, and bacteriochlorophyll a as an acceptor of the harvested energy. We combined multiple microscopic and macroscopic techniques to study free-floating and surface-deposited individual antennas which revealed their structural and functional properties on a single-complex level. The main output is a method which allows the assessment of excitation energy transfer efficiency in individual particles from a small number of detected photons (less than 20 in this work). The data allowed the correlation of the efficiency with the content of β-carotene. Additionally, we determined the size and arrangement of the self-assembled structures, which proved to form rather monodisperse aggregates clustering on the surface. Our method is generally applicable to other types of donor-acceptor systems, from inorganic nanoparticles to molecular assemblies, allowing the study of exciton dynamics in real time at the single-particle level.

Article.Authors: Yang T.; Wen T.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Most studies rely on single-time-point anthropometric measurements to assess abdominal adiposity, leaving the longitudinal association between cumulative exposure and incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) unclear. This study examined the association between the cumulative conicity index (Cum-CI) and incident CMM across three international ageing cohorts. We included participants from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n = 1700), the Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n = 1620), and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; n = 3526). Using a landmark design, three prespecified survey waves with valid conicity index measurements were used to define the cumulative exposure period, and the third measurement wave was designated as the landmark time and time zero for follow-up. Participants who developed CMM before or at the landmark time were excluded. Cum-CI was calculated using the trapezoidal area-under-the-curve method and standardized separately within each cohort. Cohort-specific Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for incident CMM per 1-standard-deviation increase in Cum-CI. Restricted cubic spline, subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses were also conducted. During follow-up, 253 participants in ELSA, 332 in HRS, and 485 in CHARLS developed incident CMM. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-standard-deviation increase in cohort-specific Cum-CI was associated with a higher hazard of incident CMM in ELSA (HR 1.28; 95% confidence interval 1.10–1.49), HRS (HR 1.11; 95% confidence interval 1.03–1.20), and CHARLS (HR 1.31; 95% confidence interval 1.18–1.45). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses showed no statistically significant evidence of nonlinearity in any cohort. Subgroup analyses showed limited evidence of effect modification, with a significant age interaction observed only in ELSA. Higher cohort-specific standardized Cum-CI was associated with a higher subsequent hazard of incident CMM across all three cohorts. Repeated assessment of the conicity index may help identify middle-aged and older adults with a greater cumulative burden of abdominal adiposity and a higher risk of developing CMM.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial diversity and population structure of Matsucoccus matsumurae across South Korea
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Kim J.; Nam Y.; Jung J.; Kim S.; Lee W.
Article.Abstract: Matsucoccus matsumurae is an important pine pest in East Asia, but its mitochondrial diversity and population structure across South Korea have not been assessed nationwide. We analyzed mitochondrial ND5 (603 bp; n = 356) and CytB (550 bp; n = 329) sequences from 24 populations to evaluate haplotype diversity, population structure, and isolation by distance. We identified 27 ND5 and 24 CytB haplotypes; concatenated sequences (1,153 bp) from 320 individuals yielded 55 composite mitochondrial haplotypes. For both markers, nucleotide diversity was low, dominant haplotypes were shared among distant localities, and haplotype networks showed shallow sequence divergence. Nevertheless, substantial differentiation occurred between many population pairs, with pairwise F ST reaching 0.953 in the concatenated dataset. This differentiation showed no consistent regional arrangement, and BAPS clusters were not geographically restricted. Mantel tests for the individual markers detected no significant isolation by distance. Neutrality tests were largely non-significant, but did not exclude recent expansion. The observed patterns are compatible with long-term establishment and secondary redistribution, but cannot distinguish this scenario from repeated introductions or other demographic histories. Because ND5 and CytB are linked and maternally inherited, these results describe maternal lineage structure and cannot establish contemporary gene flow or genome-wide population structure. This study provides the first nationwide mitochondrial baseline for M. matsumurae in South Korea, supporting future geographic comparisons and coordinated pest monitoring.

Article.Title: Federated IoMT-assisted ensemble learning for automated pulmonary CT analysis
Article.Authors: Deshwal D.; Sangwan P.; Bohra N.; Das N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pulmonary diseases such as COVID-19, pneumonia, and tuberculosis continue to impose significant challenges on global healthcare systems, emphasizing the need for rapid, reliable, and privacy-aware diagnostic frameworks. Chest computed tomography (CT) imaging has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in the early screening and assessment of pulmonary abnormalities. In recent years, the integration of deep learning and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-enabled healthcare technologies has emerged as a promising solution for automated medical image analysis and intelligent remote healthcare services. This study proposes a Federated IoMT-Assisted Ensemble Deep Learning framework for automated pulmonary CT analysis. The framework integrates an IoMT-enabled healthcare deployment architecture, federated learning mechanisms, and heterogeneous ensemble transfer learning models to facilitate secure, scalable, and privacy-preserving pulmonary disease diagnosis. A Federated Averaging (FedAvg)-based distributed learning strategy is implemented to support privacy-preserving collaborative model training across multiple healthcare institutions without directly sharing sensitive patient data. The proposed ensemble architecture utilizes three state-of-the-art pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) models, namely ResNet152V2, DenseNet201, and InceptionResNetV2, for robust feature extraction and multi-class pulmonary disease classification. Transfer learning, adam optimization, dropout regularization, and early stopping mechanisms are employed to improve model convergence, reduce overfitting, and enhance generalization capability. The framework is evaluated using a multi-class chest CT dataset consisting of COVID-19, pneumonia, tuberculosis, and normal cases collected from multiple publicly available datasets. Extensive experimental analysis is conducted using several performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Curve (AUC). Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed federated ensemble framework consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art pulmonary disease classification approaches. The proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 98.96%, with precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC values of 98.55%, 98.57%, 98.56%, and 98.56%, respectively. Furthermore, the federated learning-assisted framework demonstrates the feasibility of privacy-preserving distributed pulmonary disease diagnosis while supporting secure healthcare communication and collaborative intelligence across IoMT-enabled healthcare ecosystems. The obtained results indicate that the proposed framework can serve as an efficient, scalable, and reliable decision-support system for next-generation intelligent pulmonary disease screening and remote healthcare applications. The proposed framework contributes to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) by supporting early and accurate pulmonary disease diagnosis, improving access to intelligent healthcare services, and facilitating privacy-preserving remote healthcare delivery. Furthermore, the integration of federated learning and IoMT-enabled infrastructure aligns with SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) by promoting secure, scalable, and innovative digital healthcare solutions.

Article.Title: Exploratory assessment of soil–water quality and microbial indicators across land-use conditions in a rural watershed of India
Article.Authors: Gautam S.; Rakshith B.; Min B.; Jose D.; Mathew J.; Subith D.; Harani P.; Asirvatham L.; Joy J.
Article.Abstract: An exploratory assessment of soil quality, water quality, and microbial indicators was conducted at 15 independent paired sites in the rural watershed of Madavarayapuram, Tamil Nadu, India. At each site, 15 soil and 15 adjacent water samples were collected across agricultural, habitation, and fallow land-use settings. Physicochemical variables, culture-based microbial indicators, acid phosphatase activity, and phosphate-solubilizing activity were measured. Inverse Distance Weighting and Getis-Ord Gi* were used only for exploratory spatial visualization, whereas Spearman rank correlation and principal component analysis (PCA) were used as statistical analyses. The qPCR component was limited to four selected samples and is presented only as exploratory amplification evidence rather than as a watershed-wide quantitative estimate of bacterial abundance. Agricultural sites showed the highest observed water electrical conductivity, nitrate, and phosphate values, reaching 382 µS/cm, 7.37 µg/mL, and 0.34 µg/mL, respectively. Across the 15 paired sites, presumptive E. coli showed a moderate positive soil–water association (ρ = 0.64, p = 0.010), whereas total coliforms (ρ = 0.86, p < 0.001) and total heterotrophic bacteria (ρ = 0.89, p < 0.001) showed stronger positive associations. The first two PCA axes summarized 72.9% of the observed multivariable variation, while Global Moran’s I did not identify statistically significant global spatial autocorrelation for the measured variables. The main finding is that land-use-associated physicochemical conditions covaried with microbial indicators at the sampled locations, but the paired-site associations do not demonstrate directional microbial transfer or direct hydrological connectivity. Future work should use repeated seasonal sampling, source-stratified designs, direct hydrological measurements, and fully validated molecular assays.

Article.Title: Development of a species-specific real-time PCR assay for the detection of Eucoleus aerophilus – the first molecular survey in dogs in Poland
Article.Authors: Samorek-Pieróg M.; Bilska-Zając E.; Bełcik A.; Korpysa-Dzirba W.; Sroka J.; Cencek T.; Karamon J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dogs are hosts to numerous helminth species, including the respiratory nematode Eucoleus aerophilus (syn. Capillaria aerophila ), which infects domestic and wild carnivores and has zoonotic potential. E. aerophilus has been reported in dogs from 24 European countries, with an average prevalence of 3.5%. In Poland, however, molecular data confirming the occurrence of E. aerophilus in dogs have been lacking, and previous investigations relied primarily on coproscopic detection and morphological identification of Capillariidae eggs. The aim of this study was to develop a species-specific real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay for the detection of E. aerophilus and to apply the assay to estimate the prevalence of this parasite in dogs from selected regions of Poland. A total of 198 faecal samples were examined. The newly developed qPCR demponstrated high sensitivity and species-specificity for E. aerophilus . The prevalence determined by qPCR was 7.6%., compared with 4.0% by conventional PCR. Sequence analysis identified four E. aerophilus haplotypes: EaPL1, EaPL1A, EaPL6, and EaPL10. Three of them had previously been reported from red foxes in Poland, whereas EaPL1A was detected for the first time in the country. Coproscopic examination revealed Trichuris vulpis eggs as the most frequently detected parasite (10.5%), followed by Capillariidae eggs (7.0%). Eggs of Taeniidae, Toxocara spp., and hookworms were also identified. This study provides the first molecular evidence of E. aerophilus infection in dogs in Poland and confirms its occurrence in the investigated dog population. The findings contribute to a better understanding of the epidemiology and genetic diversity of E. aerophilus and highlight the value of molecular diagnostics for accurate species identification.

Article.Title: Evaluation of extracellular vesicle-enriched fraction-derived miR-105, miR-1908, and miR-122 expression profiles in prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia
Article.Authors: Yagci E.; Kurt H.; Ozen A.; Ozbayer C.; Metintas S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a critical challenge in oncology. There is a need to explore novel, minimally invasive indicators to help evaluate differences between PCa and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), which often mimics PCa symptoms and whose clinical evaluation is complicated by overlapping PSA levels. This study exploratively investigated the expression profiles of extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction-derived miR-105, miR-1908, and miR-122 miRNAs previously associated with epithelial-mesenchymal transition, metastatic signaling, and metabolic reprogramming to evaluate their potential associations with urological malignancies. EV-like particles were isolated from the plasma of 25 patients with BPH, 50 with PCa (25 localized, 25 metastatic), and 21 healthy controls. Transmission electron microscopy characterized the morphology of EV-like particles and revealed a significant increase in particle size within the PCa cohorts compared to the BPH and control groups ( p < 0.05). Following cDNA synthesis and miRNA profiling, miR-1908 expression was significantly downregulated in the PCa groups (LPCa and especially MPCa) relative to the BPH group ( p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in the expression levels of miR-105 and miR-122. These results suggest that miR-1908 levels may be associated with prostate pathological status. While miR-1908 warrants further investigation as an exploratory candidate, large-scale studies are necessary to validate these preliminary associations and determine their potential clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Experimental characterization of light penetration in animals and human-head simulation for photocatalytic therapy in the brain
Article.Authors: Kawai Y.; Kuriyama M.; Torii S.; Chambers J.; Uchida K.; Sohma Y.; Yamanashi Y.; Kanai M.; Hori Y.; Tomita T.
Article.Abstract: Photoexcitation of chemical compounds, together with the light transmittance of the biological window, enables targeted phototherapy. We have developed a photocatalyst-based therapeutic approach for Alzheimer disease and demonstrated amyloid-β reduction in a mouse model. However, it is unclear whether sufficient light energy can be delivered transcranially to target amyloid fibrils in the brains of larger animals, such as humans. Therefore, in this study, we measured the light energy from the body surface, through the skull, to the brain in mice in vivo and in dog head specimens in mortua , focusing on the short-wavelength side of the biological window. We then constructed an optical simulation model based on these measurements, and estimated the light energy reaching the brain from the human body surface. Our results show that only a small fraction of the light applied to the human body surface reaches the brain, with most energy loss occurring in the skin. In contrast, attenuation by the skull was relatively modest. These findings suggest that sufficient light energy can be delivered to the human brain surface through an appropriately designed delivery route and device that bypasses the skin, supporting the translational potential of photocatalytic therapy.

Article.Title: Green gradient RP-HPLC with variable flow rate for simultaneous analysis of paracetamol and ascorbic acid in pharmaceuticals
Article.Authors: Peng H.; Shi T.; Ma J.; Darwish A.
Article.Abstract: Paracetamol and ascorbic acid are widely incorporated into combination pharmaceutical formulations for the symptomatic treatment of cold and influenza. The present study reports the development and validation of a green, stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for the simultaneous quantification of these active pharmaceutical ingredients in bulk drug materials, intravenous infusion preparations, and effervescent tablet formulations using a microscale sample preparation strategy. Method validation was conducted in accordance with the ICH Q2(R2) guideline. Separation was achieved on a C18 chromatographic column using gradient elution with 0.015 M potassium dihydrogen phosphate buffer (pH 3.0) and methanol as the mobile phase components. A variable flow program ranging from 1.0 to 1.2 mL/min was applied, and analytes were monitored at 245 nm using a diode array detector maintained at 25 ± 2 °C. The method showed excellent linearity within concentration ranges of 3.2–29.3 µg/mL for ascorbic acid and 5.5–48.5 µg/mL for paracetamol. Forced degradation studies demonstrated effective separation of both analytes from degradation products, confirming the stability-indicating nature of the method. Green analytical assessment using AES, AGREE, MoGAPI, BAGI, and RGB12 yielded scores of 78, 0.60, 74, 80, and 96.7%, respectively.

Article.Title: Protein modifications associate with idiopathic membranous nephropathy diagnosis and pathogenesis
Article.Authors: Chen F.; Xue X.; Liu D.; Zhang L.; Yang J.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Idiopathic membranous nephropathy (IMN) is an organ-specific autoimmune disease. However, the pathogenic causes and risk factors underlying its molecular mechanism remain unclear. In this study, we aimed to characterize the differentially expressed protein modifications in the circulating blood of IMN patients to identify potential risk factors associated with the pathogenesis and progression of the disease. Serum samples were collected from patients with IMN (N = 40) and healthy controls (N = 48) for the analysis of protein modifications through label-free proteomic profiling using LC–MS/MS. Subsequently, open search and bioinformatics analyses were carried out. The proteins present in the bloodstream of patients with IMN exhibited extensive post-translational modifications, with several showing significant differential expression. The most prominently up-regulated modification was the cysteinylation of haptoglobin at residue 266, a cysteine residue (Cys + 119.006, > 17-fold increase, p = 0.0002). Among the most significantly down-regulated modifications were the deamidation of the fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) at residue 296, an asparagine residue (Asn + 0.984, > 98-fold increase, p = 0.005), and an unidentified modification of the fibrinogen beta chain at residue 30, a serine residue (Ser − 104.057, > 108-fold increase, p = 0.01). Proteins exhibiting differentially expressed modifications were significantly enriched in pathways associated with thrombosis. Additionally, the modification of haptoglobin (Cys266 + 119.00692) was identified as the top discriminatory marker (AUC = 0.8188) according to the Mann–Whitney U (MWU) test. Our data revealed up-regulation of haptoglobin cysteinylation at Cys266 and down-regulation of FGA deamidation at Asn296. The cysteinylation of haptoglobin is associated with oxidative stress, while the deamidation of fibrinogen is linked to thrombosis. Further investigation into these post-translational modifications may facilitate the identification of potential risk factors for idiopathic membranous nephropathy (IMN) and its associated hypercoagulability complications.

Article.Title: Optimizing sap sampling methodologies for nutrient diagnostics in lettuce and tomato grown under controlled environment agriculture
Article.Authors: Rauf H.; Jackson D.; Lessl J.; Ferrarezi R.
Article.Abstract: Effective nutrient management is crucial for maintaining growth and yield in controlled environment agriculture (CEA). However, nutrient interpretation depends on sampling methodology, and standardized sampling protocols for sap analysis remain inconsistent. This study evaluated five key sap-sampling methods: leaf number, tissue age, tissue part (only for tomatoes, Solanum lycopersicum L.), collection time, and sampling frequency, to establish sampling protocols for hydroponic lettuce ( Lactuca sativa ) and tomato in CEA. A split-plot design with repeated measures was employed using three cultivars per crop, and nutrient concentrations were analyzed within each cultivar using linear mixed-effects models with treatment, stage, and their interaction (treatment × stage), with rep included as a random effect. Two sap-extraction methods were employed: mechanical tissue crushing (TC) and potassium chloride (KCl) extraction. Nutrient leaf analysis (NLA) was subsequently used as the comparative reference method representing total tissue nutrient status. In lettuce, sampling effects were generally modest and nutrient- and cultivar-specific, and responses were frequently not conserved between TC and KCl. Effects of leaf number were more evident under KCl extraction than under TC. Tissue-age effects were present but expressed differently by extraction method; time-of-collection effects were small and inconsistent, and stage effects over the short cycle, 12 vs. 24 days after transplantation (DAT), were limited and method-dependent. In tomatoes, sampling effects were stronger and more structured. The number of leaves interacted with the developmental stage, and sap inorganic N consistently showed a leaf number × stage interaction across cultivars under both TC and KCl, indicating that leaf number must remain constant across DAT for valid interpretation. Tissue age produced strong separation with cultivar-specific age × stage interaction patterns across methods, and in tissue part, we found part × stage interactions, confirming that blade and petiole sap are not interchangeable. Sampling frequency affected tomato sap nutrient profiles across 63–253 DAT, with TC capturing short-term nutrient pools and KCl more clearly reflecting long-term enrichment patterns.

Article.Title: Proteogenomic analysis identifies cell wall-associated signatures linked to oxacillin susceptibility in oxacillin-susceptible mecA-positive Staphylococcus aureus
Article.Authors: Suresh A.; Roy S.; Brahma U.; Bhandari V.; Sharma P.
Article.Abstract: Oxacillin-susceptible mecA -positive Staphylococcus aureus (OS-MRSA) presents a therapeutic challenge because it retains susceptibility to oxacillin despite harbouring the mecA gene. Here, we used integrated genomic, proteomic, expression, and phenotypic analyses to identify molecular features associated with this unusual phenotype. OS-MRSA isolates exhibited impaired biofilm formation and reduced fitness under oxacillin exposure. Whole-genome comparison of human and animal OS-MRSA isolates with MRSA identified 1,357 non-synonymous mutations across 498 genes, including 11 genes associated with cell wall-related functions, cell adhesion, and quorum sensing. Secretome analysis revealed reduced abundance of SceD and LtaS in OS-MRSA relative to MRSA, highlighting these cell wall-associated factors as candidate correlates of oxacillin susceptibility. In addition, a conserved upstream mutation in ltaS was identified across all OS-MRSA isolates, suggesting possible transcriptional modulation, and quantitative PCR confirmed differential expression of sceD and ltaS following oxacillin induction. Taken together, these findings support a model in which altered regulation of cell wall-associated processes may be linked to the OS-MRSA phenotype. However, because the study is based on comparative omics, expression profiling, and indirect phenotypic observations, these associations should be interpreted cautiously in the absence of direct lipoteichoic acid quantification and targeted mutant validation. Overall, this study provides a hypothesis-generating framework for understanding OS-MRSA adaptation to oxacillin exposure and identifies priorities for future functional investigation.

Article.Title: CA-DTNet: a trace-driven communication-aware digital twin network for robust high-resolution traffic forecasting under heterogeneous V2X conditions
Article.Authors: Chauhan S.; Roy S.
Article.Abstract: Reliable high-resolution traffic forecasting is essential for connected intelligent transportation systems, where observations are delivered through heterogeneous vehicular networks. Most forecasting models assume clean, immediately available measurements, although operational inputs can be stale or incomplete. This paper proposes CA-DTNet, a communication-aware digital twin network for robust short-term traffic forecasting. One-second pNEUMA traffic states are combined with ordered CICV5G and SEE-V2X trace segments through a deterministic replay protocol. Packet loss directly produces sample-and-hold observations and increasing Age of Information (AoI), while latency, jitter, load, throughput, and radio-quality measurements condition a learned reliability gate. CA-DTNet uses a shared spatiotemporal representation for clean-state reconstruction and quantile forecasts of speed, vehicle count, and flow at 5-, 10-, and 30-second horizons. Across three seeds, the model obtains the lowest mean absolute error and weighted absolute percentage error in 24 of 27 domain–horizon–target combinations. Its reconstruction $$R^{2}$$ exceeds 0.985 in both communication domains. Exact matched-window analysis yields a mean absolute cross-domain MAE shift of 0.20% and a significant domain effect in only one of nine forecasting tasks. With 71,203 trainable parameters and approximately 0.393 ms inference latency per sample, CA-DTNet improves forecasting accuracy without relying on greater capacity than DCRNN or Graph WaveNet. The results support trace-driven, uncertainty-aware traffic digital twins while also delimiting the current evidence to one traffic source and two replay domains.

Article.Title: Engineered cationic methacrylated chitosan hydrogels as multifunctional biocompatible platforms for robust tyrosinase immobilization
Article.Authors: Mahdavi A.; Kiyani T.; Mohamadnia Z.; Hanifeh F.
Article.Abstract: Despite the broad potential of tyrosinase in biocatalysis, its practical application remains limited by poor operational stability and restricted reusability. Here, we developed two engineered cationic methacrylated chitosan-based hydrogels as biocompatible platforms for immobilization of highly purified Agaricus bisporus tyrosinase. The enzyme was purified to near homogeneity through sequential gel filtration and ion-exchange chromatography and subsequently immobilized using a combined adsorption-entrapment strategy within positively charged hydrogel networks. The cationic matrices were designed considering the net negative surface charge of tyrosinase to enhance enzyme retention while physically entrapping the enzyme within the hydrogel network. The physicochemical properties of the hydrogels were characterized before and after enzyme immobilization to assess the impact of enzyme incorporation. Both hydrogel formulations exhibited enzyme loading capacities of 42.02 and 39.37 μL g⁻ 1 , respectively, while retaining 94.56 and 90.46% of the free enzyme’s diphenolase activity, respectively. Comparative evaluation identified one formulation as the optimal hydrogel, exhibiting superior overall catalytic performance, operational stability, and storage stability, and was therefore selected for further biological characterization. Kinetic analysis revealed negligible changes in substrate affinity together with approximately 90–95% retention of the maximum catalytic activity (V max ), indicating preservation of the enzyme's catalytic function after immobilization. Compared with the free enzyme, the optimized immobilized tyrosinase exhibited a shift in the optimum pH from 6.5 to 5.5 and an increase in the optimum temperature from 30 to 50 °C, retained 81% of its initial activity after five consecutive catalytic cycles, and maintained approximately 82% residual activity after 28 days of storage at 4 °C. Furthermore, the optimized hydrogel demonstrated pronounced antibacterial activity against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus while exhibiting negligible cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity, confirming its high biocompatibility. Collectively, these findings establish engineered cationic methacrylated chitosan hydrogels as multifunctional and biocompatible platforms for tyrosinase immobilization, providing high immobilization efficiency, enhanced operational stability, antibacterial activity, and favorable biological compatibility, with promising potential for industrial biocatalysis and biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Electrospun pectin/polyvinyl alcohol smart nanofiber indicators incorporating red radish peel extract for real-time monitoring of rainbow trout freshness
Article.Authors: Heydarian A.; Hosseinzadeh S.; Bazargani-Gilani B.; Zebarjad S.
Article.Abstract: A colorimetric indicator based on electrospun orange-peel (OP) and banana-peel (BP) pectin/PVA nanofibers incorporating red radish peel extract (RRPE) was developed to monitor rainbow trout freshness under refrigeration. In agar well diffusion assays, RRPE exhibited 25.2–27.8 mm inhibition zones against four common foodborne pathogens. FTIR confirmed RRPE incorporation, XRD showed a predominantly amorphous structure, and TGA showed pectin-source-dependent effects of RRPE on thermal stability. RRPE enhanced moisture barrier properties, hydrophobicity, flexibility, and antioxidant activity (74–75%). The two smart indicators showed different color changes across a broad pH range and achieved RGB sensitivity values of 64.51% (OP/PVA/RRPE) and 63.96% (BP/PVA/RRPE) after 24 min of ammonia exposure. Visual color changes agreed with increases in pH (6.27–7.47), TVB-N (10.73–26.13 mg N/100 g) and TBA (0.15–1.06 mg MDA/kg). The two pectin-based indicators exhibited statistically equivalent sensing performance (Fisher’s r-to-z, p > 0.05), providing flexibility in feedstock selection based on economic or yield considerations. Although OP/PVA/RRPE had finer fiber morphology and better moisture-barrier performance, both systems performed with comparable efficiency in real-time monitoring of fish freshness. The developed bio-based indicator provides a natural and promising platform for real-time monitoring of rainbow trout spoilage.

Article.Title: Performance and cost efficiency of plastic-modified asphalt pavements: a multi-criteria approach
Article.Authors: Somani P.; Lalsotia A.; Mathur N.; Anand S.; Sain A.; Gaur A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The utilization of post-consumer plastic waste in asphalt pavements offers a sustainable alternative to conventional materials. This study evaluates the mechanical performance, moisture resistance, and economic feasibility of incorporating polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), and low-density polyethylene (LDPE) as waste plastic modifiers in asphalt mixtures using the dry process. In this approach, shredded plastic particles coat the heated aggregates before bitumen addition, enhancing aggregate–binder interaction and mixture performance. Modified mixes were assessed for volumetric properties, Marshall stability and flow, indirect tensile strength (ITS) under dry and wet conditions, and tensile strength ratio (TSR). PET- and HDPE-modified mixes showed improved density and reduced air voids, with maximum Marshall stability values of 14.9 kN and 16.1 kN, respectively, compared to 12.1 kN for the control mix. LDPE-modified mixes exhibited superior moisture resistance, achieving TSR values above 89%, while all modified mixes satisfied the minimum TSR requirement of 80%. Economic analysis indicated cost savings ranging from 4.7 to 8.0%. Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) confirmed the significant influence of plastic type on stability and TSR, and multi-criteria decision-making analysis identified the HDPE-modified mix as the optimal solution. The results support the sustainable and cost-effective use of waste plastics in asphalt pavement construction.

Article.Title: Evacuation behaviour under smoke conditions in a real-scale road tunnel experiment in Poland
Article.Authors: Schmidt-Polończyk N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Road tunnel fires pose a serious safety challenge because smoke, reduced visibility and limited escape options can strongly affect evacuation behaviour. This study presents a real-scale evacuation experiment conducted in the road tunnel under the Dead Vistula River in Gdańsk, Poland. Participants entered the tunnel in a city bus, which stopped in a smoke-filled tunnel tube, after which an emergency scenario was initiated and tunnel safety systems were activated. The analysis combined chip-based time measurements, movement observations and post-experiment questionnaires from two evacuation trials. The total evacuation time was similar in both trials: the last participant completed evacuation after 378 s in Trial 1 and 376 s in Trial 2. Mean total evacuation time also did not differ significantly. However, participants spent significantly less time in the smoke-filled section during Trial 2, with the mean time decreasing from 60.32 ± 18.73 s to 40.09 ± 10.69 s. A dominant route-choice pattern was observed, with most participants selecting E2 in both trials, despite this emergency passage being located farther from the bus. The results show that total evacuation time alone does not fully describe tunnel evacuation performance and should be complemented by staged movement analysis, route-choice data and subjective perception.

Article.Title: Assessing children’s perceptions of school-route streets using child-height street-view imagery and explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Lei M.; Jiao H.; Mao L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract School-route streets shape children’s experiences, yet street-view assessments may miss children’s eye-height environments and conflate direct ratings with model-inferred perceptions. Our framework combined reconstructed 1.00 m imagery, children’s ratings, and explainable machine learning at nine primary schools in Harbin, China. Reconstruction was compared with real 1.00 m photographs at 45 sites. Seventy-two children rated 150 scenes for safety, accessibility, comfort, and interest; associations with 15 environmental indicators were analysed separately from proxy-model results. A frozen SigLIP–SVR model generated perception-proxy scores at 1,908 sites, analysed with spatially blocked XGBoost and out-of-fold SHAP across three urban spatial types. Reconstruction performance was mixed; only sky proportion showed a supported improvement under a validity mask. Green View Index had the highest predictive importance (20.26%), while indicator rankings and responses varied by dimension and spatial type. Among the 60 direct-rating tests, 25 remained significant after global BH-FDR correction. Permutation-based hotspot analysis identified six persistent Tier I hotspots and 22 non-persistent Tier III cells, with six Tier I hotspots in the New Planned Large-Block Area. Findings support context-sensitive street assessment, but turning points and hotspots are model-derived screening signals, not validated thresholds or confirmed deficiencies.

Article.Title: MAMDC2 suppresses gastric cancer cells but promotes progression through cancer associated fibroblasts
Article.Authors: Huo Y.; Chen X.; Huang M.; Zhou J.; Liu Y.; Wu T.; Jiang L.
Article.Abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets are urgently needed. MAMDC2 has been implicated in several malignancies, but its biological function and cellular origin in GC remain largely unknown. We integrated bulk RNA-seq data from GEO and TCGA databases to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of MAMDC2 in GC. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics were used to delineate its cellular origin within the tumor microenvironment. In vitro functional assays, including CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, wound healing, and Transwell assays, were performed to assess the effects of MAMDC2 overexpression in GC cell lines. Conditioned medium (CM) experiments using MAMDC2-overexpressing fibroblasts were conducted to evaluate the paracrine effects of fibroblast-derived MAMDC2 on GC cell migration, invasion, and EMT-like changes. Western blotting was used to explore the underlying signaling pathways. MAMDC2 was downregulated in GC tissues and cell lines and showed diagnostic value. Clinically, high MAMDC2 expression was associated with poor overall survival and independently predicted adverse prognosis. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses consistently revealed that MAMDC2 is predominantly expressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) rather than in malignant epithelial cells. Functional experiments showed that forced MAMDC2 overexpression in GC cells suppressed proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Notably, conditioned medium from MAMDC2-overexpressing CAFs enhanced MGC-803 cell migration and invasion, accompanied by EMT-like marker changes (E-cadherin downregulation, Vimentin and N-cadherin upregulation), suggesting that CAF-derived MAMDC2 may promote GC progression in a paracrine manner. These paracrine findings are proof-of-concept, as they were obtained using one commercial CAF line and one recipient GC cell line. Western blotting further showed that MAMDC2 overexpression was associated with altered MAPK pathway activation, including decreased p-JNK and p-p38 and increased p-ERK, although these changes are correlative and require functional validation. MAMDC2 plays context-dependent roles in GC. At the cancer cell-autonomous level, MAMDC2 overexpression suppresses proliferation, migration, and invasion. However, MAMDC2 is predominantly expressed in CAFs, and CAF-derived MAMDC2 may promote GC cell migration, invasion, and EMT-like changes through paracrine signaling, offering a plausible explanation for the association between high MAMDC2 expression and poor prognosis. These findings suggest that MAMDC2 may act as a context-dependent regulator and a potential stromal-derived modulator of the GC microenvironment, rather than a classical cell-intrinsic tumor suppressor. Further validation using additional GC cell lines, primary CAFs, and in vivo models is warranted.

Article.Title: Virtual non-calcium subtraction values enable accurate osteoporosis diagnosis via quantitative CT
Article.Authors: Nie S.; Li X.; Fan B.; Lan M.; Deng W.; Liao Y.
Article.Abstract: Virtual non-calcium (VNCa) imaging derived from dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) is increasingly used in the diagnosis of spinal disorders.However, the effectiveness of VNCa technology in assessing vertebral bone status is unclear, especially across different levels of calcium suppression. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of VNCa imaging for osteoporosis using quantitative CT (QCT) as the reference standard.196 patients were selected for chest CT energy spectrum mode scanning. The images were transferred to the quantitative CT (QCT) workstation, and the vertebral bodies were divided into osteoporotic and non-osteoporotic groups with reference to the QCT diagnostic standards. The diagnostic performance of osteoporosis was evaluated by comparing the vertebral CT values when calcium suppression index (CaSI) was 25, 50, and 75 and the subtraction value between it and the conventional CT plain value. All ROC analyses were performed within a cluster-adjusted framework to account for the within-patient correlation among the three vertebrae contributed per patient. A total of 587 vertebral bodies (129 osteoporotic and 458 non-osteoporotic) from 196 patients were analyzed. After adjusting for within-patient clustering, the AUC values for diagnosing osteoporosis using VNCa CT values at CaSI 25, 50, and 75 were 0.928 (95% CI: 0.901–0.955), 0.841 (95% CI: 0.801–0.880), and 0.680 (95% CI: 0.629–0.730), respectively. The corresponding AUC values for the subtraction values were 0.960 (95% CI: 0.941–0.979), 0.964 (95% CI: 0.948–0.980), and 0.963 (95% CI: 0.948–0.978). The subtraction value significantly outperformed the corresponding VNCa CT value at all three CaSI levels (all P < 0.0001). Conventional CT values alone yielded an AUC of 0.980 (95% CI: 0.970–0.990). Spectral CT calcium suppression imaging can effectively evaluate bone status. Within a cluster-adjusted analytical framework, the subtraction value demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance among all VNCa-based metrics, with an AUC of 0.964 (95% CI: 0.948–0.980) at CaSI 50, significantly outperforming VNCa CT values at all CaSI levels. Conventional CT values also showed excellent diagnostic performance, supporting their potential as a widely available opportunistic screening tool. External validation in multi-center cohorts is warranted to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Orthodontic extraction decision-making under standardized clinical conditions: a case-based study
Article.Authors: Agha F.; Ibrahim A.; Al-Taai N.; Almuzian M.
Article.Abstract: Determining whether to extract teeth remains one of the most challenging aspects of orthodontic treatment planning as it requires consideration of multiple dental, skeletal, and soft-tissue factors. Although established diagnostic criteria and predictive models are available, considerable variation in extraction decisions persists, particularly in borderline cases. To examine how orthodontists make extraction decisions when assessing the same standardized clinical cases, focusing on variation in their recommendations and the clinical factors associated with these decisions. Orthodontic specialists and postgraduate trainees completed an electronic cross-sectional survey. They assessed 20 standardized cases with complete diagnostic records and selected either extraction or non-extraction treatment while identifying the factors that influenced each decision. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cochran’s Q test, Fleiss’ kappa, and cross-classified mixed-effects logistic regression with random intercepts for orthodontist and case. A total of 104 orthodontists completed the survey, providing 2,080 clinician–case decisions across 20 standardized cases. Profile concerns, crowding severity, and incisor inclination were the most frequently reported factors influencing extraction decisions. Inter-rater agreement was fair (Fleiss’ κ = 0.303). In the cross-classified mixed-effects model, none of the six case-level cephalometric measurements showed a statistically significant association with extraction recommendations (all p > 0.05). The estimated random-intercept standard deviations were 0.451 for orthodontist and 1.262 for case. Extraction recommendations varied considerably among orthodontists, particularly for borderline cases, despite assessment of the same standardized clinical information. Within this sample, no statistically significant adjusted associations were detected between the six cephalometric measurements examined and extraction recommendations after accounting for differences between orthodontists and cases. However, the limited number of unique cases and uncertainty in the estimates warrant cautious interpretation and limit generalizability.

Article.Title: Optimization and modeling of rare earth element leaching from Khouribga phosphate rock using response surface methodology
Article.Authors: Taoufik S.; El Farrouji A.; Mallouk S.; Azzaoui K.; Jodeh S.; Hammouti B.; Rhazi L.; Abuelizz H.; Arshad M.; Samhan M.; Boualy B.
Article.Abstract: In Khouribga (Morocco), about 7.2 Mt of phosphate rock is mined annually, and most is used to manufacture fertilizers, phosphoric acid, and for exports. Extracting rare earths elements (REEs) from phosphate rock enhances their supply, improves the quality of phosphoric acid, protects the environment, and adds value to this crucial natural resource. In this regard, we are interested to develop efficient, selective, and applicable methods for processing phosphate in order to extract rare earth elements. Here, we report the characterization of Khouribga phosphate rock and the response-surface optimization of bench-scale hydrochloric-acid of its rare earth elements leaching. HCl concentration (3.7–37.0% w/v), temperature (50–100 °C), and contact time (5–45 min) were studied. The Phosphate rock contained 633 ppm total REEs, with yttrium as the dominant quantified element (427 ppm). The model identified 75 °C, 25 min, and 20.35% HCl as a predicted operating point; the six design center-point runs at these conditions gave a mean measured yield of 86.86 ± 2.05% ( n = 6). These results demonstrate the feasibility of a laboratory-scale leaching process under the conditions examined; which could be applied, after further verification, to rare earth element extraction at a phosphate rock beneficiation.

Article.Title: Multimodal pill image recognition in natural environments using context-aware cross-modal attention
Article.Authors: Nguyen Thi My L.; Vo T.; Truong Hoang V.
Article.Abstract: Medication errors remain a major source of preventable harm, and identifying a pill from a photograph taken in an uncontrolled setting is still difficult because the informative cues-color, shape, surface texture, and imprinted text-are unequally reliable from one image to the next. We present a recognition framework for natural environments in which a fusion module, context-aware cross-modal attention (CACMA), weighs these four modalities separately for every image using a query formed from their joint global context, an explicit confidence branch that estimates per-modality reliability, and a three-way integration of attended, confidence-weighted, and residual features, on top of \(\hbox {U}^2\) -Net segmentation (98.06% validation IoU) and connected-component localization. All results follow a unified end-to-end protocol, with segmentation, localization, OCR, and fusion executed at inference time, over three random seeds on two real-world datasets. On CURE (196 classes) CACMA attains 91.13±0.27% Top-1 accuracy and \(95.50\pm 0.16\%\) mAP, exceeding the published results of Ling et al. and Rádli et al. by 22.83 and 5.41 pp and summation fusion by 3.15 pp ( \(p<0.001\) ); the 0.76 pp margin over weighted summation is not statistically significant, which we report as parity rather than superiority, while CACMA attains the smallest across-seed variability of any method evaluated ( \(\pm 0.27\) pp). On OGYEI-v2 (112 classes) it reaches \(83.23\pm 0.73\%\) Top-1 accuracy. What fixed-weight fusion cannot reproduce is directly measurable: the confidence assigned to the text modality rises from 0.362 to 0.602 when an imprint is legible ( \(p = 1 \times 10^{-55}\) ), with the released weight redistributed to the visual modalities. A fully fine-tuned ViT-B/16 is not significantly more accurate ( \(92.07\pm 0.64\%\) ; McNemar \(p=0.32\) ) while using 6.4 \(\times \) the parameters and offering no modality-level explanation, placing CACMA at a favorable accuracy-efficiency-interpretability operating point. Paired significance testing applied to the ablations shows that no individual component accounts for the result on its own under this segmentation quality; together with calibration, saliency and failure analyses, these tests delimit where multimodal attention fusion helps and where it does not.

Article.Title: An interplay of bricks and emotions- Role of job crafting and emotional intelligence in determining self-perceived productivity in the construction industry
Article.Authors: Dixit A.; Tomar D.; Tomar R.; Gulati C.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to examine the role of emotional intelligence (EI) and relational job crafting and their association with self-perceived productivity among employees working in the construction sector. The study particularly emphasizes Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) theory by considering EI and relational job crafting as important resources for employees. The primary objective is to examine the role of EI and relational job crafting in enhancing employees’ psychological and social well-being and, ultimately, their self-perceived productivity. The study is explanatory and cross-sectional in nature thus the study captures only association among variables. Data was collected from construction workers using standardized scales. A sample of 689 respondents was selected using a stratified sampling technique. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was employed using AMOS to analyze the data. The findings indicate that employees working in the construction industry is linked to emotional intelligence and relational job crafting abilities to reframe their perspectives towards job demands. These abilities assist employees to maintain greater psychological and social stability, which is further found to be positively associated with self-perceived productivity. The findings suggest that construction organizations could support emotional intelligence training and encourage relational job crafting, particularly for workers experiencing physical exhaustion. Relational job crafting and emotional intelligence may help employees to cope with job demands, experience greater psychological relief, and develop a more positive outlook. This study contributes to the understanding of employee well-being in high-risk occupational sectors and advocates a shift from a purely mechanistic model towards more human-oriented management practices. Further, the study provides insights into emotional and behavioral resources associated with well-being and self-perceived productivity in a physically demanding occupational context.
