Article.Title: Hybrid attention and learning mechanism-based deep learning model for crop yield prediction
Article.Authors: Ingle A.; Dhawale D.; Kanekar K.; Waghmode U.; Kale R.; Puri D.; Solanki S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An accurate crop yield prediction is necessary for augmenting farming practices and guaranteeing the security of food. Several approaches have been developed to predict the yield of crops. The conventional approaches were incapable of discovering non-linear relationship amid the data, and they exhibit several drawbacks, such as computational overhead, false errors, overfitting issues, limited resources, poor generalizability and computational complexity, which lead to inaccurate predictions. To overcome these limitations, the research proposed a Multi-Attention and Distilled Task Learning enabled Weighted Decision tree based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (MA-DTL-WDBiLSTM) model to predict the crop yield accurately. The model’s performance in forecasting the crop yield is enhanced due to the incorporation of multi attention mechanism and Distilled Task Learning, which distilled the gained knowledge from the teacher model to the student model and split the tasks into subtasks, respectively. Additionally, the integration of the weighted decision tree in the Bi-LSTM model offers an improved prediction accuracy by handling the intricate data and concentrating on the relevant features. The model is evaluated using the Crop yield prediction dataset and the Agricultural Crop Yield in Indian States Dataset, which enhances the interpretability and better generalizability. Specifically, the proposed MA-DTL-WDBiLSTM model achieved a minimum correlation of 0.884, MAE of 1.759, MSE of 6.536, and RMSE of 2.556 using the Agricultural Crop Yield in Indian States Dataset, showcasing high performance in crop yield prediction and outperforming other existing models.

Article.Title: Simulation of subtropical courtyard microclimate evolution and optimization algorithm for landscape design based on multi-source remote sensing data fusion
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subtropical courtyards temper heat and admit light, yet their thermal performance has been hard to quantify at a scale fine enough to guide design. This study builds an end-to-end pipeline, resting on freely distributed satellite products and open code, that fuses multi-source remote sensing, simulates courtyard microclimate evolution, and optimises landscape configuration; it is applied to twenty-four courtyards in Guangzhou, southern China, a humid subtropical (Köppen Cfa) city, observed between 2021 and 2024. Complementary open products—Landsat-8/9, Sentinel-1/2, MODIS and SRTM/ASTER elevation—were harmonised through a weighted wavelet spatiotemporal fusion whose variance-driven weights marry Sentinel-2 spatial detail to MODIS temporal density, with residual-conserved downscaling holding the land-surface temperature field to its calibrated coarse-scale mean. Because that constraint alone cannot demonstrate microscale accuracy, the nominal 10 m thermal product was tested against twelve campaigns of UAV thermography: it reached a spatial RMSE of 1.62 °C and outperformed bicubic interpolation, vegetation-index sharpening, STARFM and ESTARFM, while ablation identified residual conservation as the component that matters most. From the fused fields a seven-parameter feature system was derived, and correlation screening isolated vegetation cover and impervious fraction as the dominant thermal controls. A hybrid simulator then coupled a physics-constrained convolutional–recurrent network to a ventilation-weighted cellular automaton. Validated separately for surface temperature, air temperature, humidity, mean radiant temperature and physiological equivalent temperature under a leakage-controlled spatiotemporal hold-out, it reproduced air temperature with R 2 of 0.87–0.92 and RMSE near 1.2–1.6 °C, humid-season humidity remaining the softer spot. Model development drew on eighteen courtyards and 11 916 twelve-step training sequences against 5 850 validation and 5 868 test sequences, with six further courtyards and the twelve thermography flights held outside every calibration step; the learner carries 95 778 trainable parameters, and training, test and transfer errors of 1.11, 1.26 and 1.74 degrees Celsius bracket the cost of moving to unseen geometry. Wrapping this evaluator inside a three-objective optimisation—cooling, comfort, greenery—an improved evolutionary algorithm with adaptive weighting and archive elitism attained a larger hypervolume than NSGA-II, NSGA-III, MOEA/D and SPEA2 across thirty independent runs, and needed roughly two fifths fewer simulator calls than the standard elitist baseline. Applied to one representative paved courtyard, the balanced scheme was predicted to lower mean floor temperature by 3.8 °C (95% CI 2.6–5.0 °C) and to raise in-band comfort hours by 27% points (95% CI 17–37), with relief tracking connected planting; these are model-conditioned predictions, not measured outcomes. The work delivers a transparent, auditable route from open imagery to quantitatively comparable subtropical courtyard design.

Article.Authors: Yağcıoğlu S.; Arıcı R.; Ersoy N.; Büyükipekci İ.; Karaağaç İ.; Gün G.; Bakırer Öztürk G.; Eser A.; Kırbaş O.; Sağraç D.; Candangelen P.; Demir K.; Evecen M.; Solakoğlu S.; Şahin F.; Pabuccuoğlu S.; Birler S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seminal plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (SP-EVs) are emerging as bioactive regulators of sperm function; however, their application during semen cryopreservation remains poorly defined. In contrast, the 1× treatment yielded the highest cleavage and blastocyst development rates and was associated with distinct expression patterns of NANOG , GLUT , and IFNT . Overall, SP-EV supplementation improved several post-thaw sperm functional parameters and was associated with higher subsequent cleavage and blastocyst development rates. Importantly, the supplementation level associated with the most favorable post-thaw sperm parameters differed from that associated with the highest cleavage and blastocyst development rates, indicating distinct concentration-dependent responses across reproductive outcomes.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning and multi-objective optimization for forecasting corporate SDG performance
Article.Authors: Mustafa S.; Altrad A.; Awain A.; Ibrahim Hussein I.
Article.Abstract: The current practice of sustainability assessments in the corporate world is based on backward-looking ESG scores, which offer limited insight into dynamic, non-linear and multi-objective sustainability transitions. This study proposes an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Decision Intelligence Framework for predicting and optimizing corporate Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) performance. The framework leverages 4,000 firm-year observations from 12 industrial sectors across the globe from 2016 to 2023, incorporating hierarchical imputation, winsorisation, lead alignment, machine learning, TreeSHAP, Partial Dependence Profiles and Pareto optimisation. Out-of-sample evaluation across four sequential expanding-window forecast periods identifies Ridge Regression as the champion forecasting benchmark (mean OOS R² = 0.8949; RMSE = 2.6884; MAE = 2.1374), while LightGBM is retained as the nonlinear analytical surrogate (mean OOS R² = 0.8787; RMSE = 2.8871; MAE = 2.3124). TreeSHAP identifies concentrated model-specific predictive attributions, while the partial dependence analysis indicates heterogeneous nonlinear response patterns within the analytical surrogate. The sectoral Pareto frontiers clearly show a range of trade-offs, with frontier scores ranging from 81.71 to 89.36, depending on the sector. Small negative or near-neutral changes are simulated in selected sectors under the + 25% Green R&D scenario. Overall, the framework facilitates sustainable decision-making on an explainable, forward-looking and sector-sensitive basis. It offers corporate managers, investors and policy-makers interpretable evidence to allocate resources, plan for transition and implement sector-specific sustainability interventions.

Article.Title: Stress loading following a Mw7.8 megathrust earthquake in the northern Ecuadorian forearc
Article.Authors: Wickham-Piotrowski A.; Meltzer A.; Ponce G.; Garcia A.; Vaca S.; Segovia M.; Beck S.; Ruiz M.; Hernandez S.
Article.Abstract: Whether driven by fluids or aseismic slip, seismic swarms release stress. In the Ecuadorian subduction zone, the 2016 Pedernales Mw7.8 megathrust earthquake caused aftershocks associated with afterslip. It also triggered distant seismic swarms several months after the mainshock. 82 stations were temporarily deployed following the megathrust earthquake. Stress and fluid-pressure changes following the Pedernales earthquake could have triggered a seismic swarm, approximately 60 km north of the 2016 epicenter 8 months after the mainshock. This upper plate swarm consists of three bursts, each larger in terms of number of events and magnitude. The observed migration of seismicity is consistent with pore-fluid diffusion. The third burst of seismicity initiated with the largest event (Mw5.4) of the swarm. Modeled stress change supports nearby triggering of seismicity and enhanced fluid diffusivity. We interpret a pressure back front following this event preventing the occurrence of seismicity near its hypocenter. In northern Ecuador, several Mw5.9 + megathrust events between 2015 and 2025 have loaded the region where a Mw7.7 megathrust earthquake occurred in 1958. Although large megathrust ruptures may result from stress release due to accumulated slip deficit on the plate interface, loading caused by intermediate-sized earthquakes may also contribute to the triggering of larger events.

Article.Title: The evolution of hourly strombolian cycles towards paroxysmal activity at Etna volcano
Article.Authors: Zuccarello L.; Gheri D.; De Angelis S.; Sciotto M.; Badi G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lava fountains are typical of basaltic volcanic eruptions, especially during paroxysms when activity shifts from intermittent Strombolian explosions to sustained high lava discharge often accompanied by ash emission. Cyclic eruptive behaviour –marked by regular variations in explosive intensity and lava fountaining over periods of minutes to hours– has been observed before but rarely captured in the geophysical record. In November 2023, Mt. Etna (Italy) exhibited cyclic Strombolian activity, which culminated in a paroxysm on 1 December, 2023. Over 10 days, clusters of frequent explosions recurred on an approximately hourly timescale from multiple vents within the volcano’s South East Crater (SEC). Infrasound data recorded by the INGV permanent network show repetitive waveforms, indicating consistent eruption dynamics and stable source characteristics. Seismic tremor locations point to a shallow source within the uppermost kilometer beneath the crater. The observations are consistent with episodic gas accumulation and release within the shallow plumbing system, potentially modulated by transient changes in near-vent conditions, and gas transfer through multiple dynamically connected pathways. These observations provide new insights into shallow eruptive processes at Mt. Etna, and, more generally, support models that link cyclic eruptive activity at basaltic volcanoes to near-surface gas accumulation and release.

Article.Title: The effect of normal gait on acromion trajectory quantification
Article.Authors: Guan L.; Zhao N.; Zeng Z.; Shi Y.; Feng L.; Liu J.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: Shoulder motion is key to gait, and its quantitative trajectory offers insights for biomechanical evaluation and gait-based identification. This study explored how 3D acromion (SAE) trajectories affect intra-individual gait stability, inter-individual variability, and person identification. Using motion capture, 65 subjects’ SAE trajectories (normal walking) were projected onto sagittal and horizontal planes and analyzed via sway mode (α, vertical symmetry) and torsional mode ( β , horizontal symmetry). A gait-specific dynamic time warping algorithm quantified trajectory similarity. Sagittal analysis identified 3 sway types ( α < 1.00, = 1.00, > 1.00), and horizontal analysis distinguished 3 morphological patterns. Sagittal-plane SAE trajectories exhibited significant inter-subject variability, with Rank-1 recognition rates of 84.62% (L_SAE) and 81.54% (R_SAE), AUC values near 0.993 and EER below 5.00%. In contrast, horizontal-plane SAE trajectories had weaker discriminative capacity, with Rank-1 rates of 39.85% (L_SAE) and 39.54% (R_SAE), and EER of 20.61% and 22.11%, respectively. SAE analysis captured unique upper-body gait features, aiding identification or biomechanical interpretation and supporting multimodal gait analysis, clinical assessment, and surveillance.

Article.Title: Self-reported knowledge, practice, and associated factors in pre-referral ocular injury management among nurses in Syria
Article.Authors: Alkhoder A.; Nabelsi N.; Zeid M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ocular injuries require prompt and appropriate management to prevent further damage; nurses often play a key role in early assessment before referral. This study assessed nurses’ knowledge and practice in initial ocular injury management and associated factors. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 373 nurses in seven Syrian hospitals from February to April 2026, using a 20-item knowledge questionnaire and a 25-item practice questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using non-parametric tests, correlation, and regression analyses. The mean knowledge score was 75.06 ± 14.16 (good level), while the mean practice score was 113.08 ± 11.85 (90.5%, excellent level); 83.9% demonstrated excellent practice. Although 61.1% reported no previous ophthalmic training, training was associated with higher knowledge (P < 0.001) and practice (P = 0.002). Knowledge was positively correlated with practice (rₛ = 0.455, P < 0.001). Previous ophthalmic training was independently associated with knowledge (β = −0.301, P < 0.001), while knowledge was independently associated with practice (β = 0.330, P < 0.001). Nurses reported good knowledge and excellent practice; however, self-reported measures and the cross-sectional design preclude inference of objective clinical competency. Targeted education and standardized protocols may strengthen preparedness.

Article.Title: Observation of surface frequency doubling in Si(111) mediated by a $$\chi ^4$$ process
Article.Authors: Pires H.; Gomes H.; Priebe C.; Figueira G.; Silva A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nonlinear optical processes such as second-harmonic generation (SHG) provide powerful probes of the structural and electronic properties of semiconductor surfaces and interfaces. While SHG in centrosymmetric materials like silicon has been extensively investigated, higher-order nonlinear contributions remain largely unexplored. Here, we report for the first time the observation of a $$\chi ^4$$ -mediated contribution to SHG from Si(111)– $$SiO_2$$ interfaces, revealed through intensity scaling and azimuthal anisotropy measurements. The frequency-doubled signal exhibits both quadratic and quartic dependence on the incident intensity, with the quartic term displaying a distinct threefold symmetry superimposed on the conventional sixfold SHG pattern. This identifies a previously unreported pathway for nonlinear emission at silicon surfaces. These results were enabled by high-intensity excitation near the laser-induced damage threshold, combined with automated high-sensitivity detection.

Article.Title: Blockchain-enabled depth-wise separable dual convolutional neural network for reliable scheduling to maximize network lifetime in wireless sensor network
Article.Authors: Sundaramoorthy R.; Raja R.; Seerangan K.; Natarajan S.; Mohanamoorthy J.; Das S.; Kumar G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are a well-known and common deployed network in the field of monitoring and data collection in distributed systems, but the network has many difficulties including limited energy resources, reduced lifetime of the deployed network, inefficient scheduling, and unreliable communication. In this paper, the authors proposed a Blockchain based Dual Convolutional Neural Network (DS2CNN) approach to address the above issues, which is designed to effectively schedule tasks in WSNs and optimize the network lifetime. The proposed approach begins by a corona based zone partitioning model which organizes the network to enable its efficient management of data and reduces communication overhead. A Self-Guided Deep Clustering Network (SeGDCN) is proposed to learn discriminative representations and generate compact and balanced clusters out of the collected data. To perform energy-efficient and load-balanced operation of the network, cluster head (CH) selection using Improved Exponential Distribution Optimizer (I-EDO) is then carried out. The node activity scheduling is completed after clustering, using the DS2CNN model combined with a Dual Attention Transformer Network (DATN) to make intelligent judgments on the activity and sleep states under the condition of the network. To ensure security and trustworthiness, a Weighted Byzantine Fault Tolerance Consensus Algorithm (WByFTCA) is validated of the scheduling and control decisions by a mechanism based on blockchain, so that the integrity and bad behavior resistance is guaranteed. Finally, the optimal routing is done by implementing a Delay-sensitive Energy-Efficient Routing Scheme (DEERS), which uses residual energy, link quality and delay to select optimum routing. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework over the conventional approaches which are potentially suitable for energy efficient and secure WSN application in terms of achieving an increase in network lifetime and decrease in energy consumption and latency.

Article.Title: Core activation patterns across different figure skating jumps
Article.Authors: Nikelova P.; Hlavsa V.; Magiera M.; Uchytil J.; Ladrova M.; Cenkova S.; Martinek R.; Vala R.; Rypar T.; Jaros R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a quantitative analysis of core muscle activation patterns across six distinct figure skating jumps: single/double axel, double/triple salchow, and double/triple loop. While previous research has focused primarily on lower-limb kinematics, the role of the trunk in maintaining a rigid rotational axis remains underexplored. We utilized a synchronized sensor framework comprising torso-mounted accelerometers, bilateral electromyography (EMG) of the m. obliquus externus abdominis and m. rectus abdominis, and skate-mounted inertial measurement units to monitor 12 adolescent female athletes. The EMG signals were segmented into the preparation, flight, and landing phases and subsequently normalized to the percentage of inter-trial maximum (%ITM). Our findings reveal a consistent shift from right-side dominance during the preparation phase to left-side dominance during the flight phase (for counter-clockwise rotators). Triple jumps exhibited higher integrated ITM in the obliquus externus compared to double jumps, despite minimal differences in airtime. This suggests that increased rotational velocity ( $$\approx$$ 1570 °/s) necessitates higher muscular tension rather than a longer duration in the air. Furthermore, the landing phase was characterized by a powerful bracing mechanism, with the co-contraction index exceeding 80% in high-rotation jumps. This study provides an objective framework for evaluating jump technique and optimizing strength training in competitive figure skating.

Article.Title: Sex-modulated heterogeneity in frontotemporal dementia spans clinical phenotypes and anatomical substrates
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Ruan Y.; Han P.; Su L.; Wu X.; Li X.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) exhibits profound inter-individual heterogeneity that complicates diagnosis and intervention, yet the factors that modulate this variability remain poorly understood. Here, we examined whether biological sex serves as one such modulator, from clinical phenotypes to anatomical substrates. Using a well-characterized cohort from the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative (108 FTD patients and 67 healthy controls enrolled at the first visit), we quantified multidimensional heterogeneity and assessed sex effects across FTD subtypes. Permutation testing revealed that both phenotypic and anatomical heterogeneity significantly exceeded random expectation across the FTD spectrum, confirming heterogeneity as a core disease feature. Critically, heterogeneity was selectively modulated by biological sex in clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD): males exhibited greater dispersion in phenotypic profiles and atrophy patterns, alongside stronger phenotype-anatomy coupling, effects not observed in other subtypes. Further analysis anchored this male-enhanced heterogeneity in bvFTD to a confined set of regions, whose atrophy patterns reliably discriminated sex via a logistic classifier that outperformed null models (accuracy = 72.73%, AUC = 0.821). Together, these findings position biological sex as a robust and anatomically specific modulator of heterogeneity, with effects most pronounced in bvFTD. This work advances our understanding of individual differences, providing a foundation for sex-stratified biomarkers and precision-medicine strategies.

Article.Title: Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling of height to live crown base in natural and plantation Jack Pine stands
Article.Authors: Eslamdoust J.; Stratton C.; Vasiliauskas S.; White A.; Rafieijahed R.; Little T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Height to live crown base (HCB) is a key indicator of crown architecture, influencing growth allocation, timber quality, and stand dynamics in boreal forests. Accurate prediction of HCB is essential for growth and yield modeling and silvicultural planning. Using measurements from 5973 jack pine trees across 515 permanent sample plots distributed throughout Ontario, Canada, we developed and evaluated nonlinear mixed-effects models for HCB separately for natural- and plantation-origin stands. Three model families (exponential, logistic, and generalized logistic) and five predictor combinations integrating tree-level and stand-level variables were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. The exponential model with diameter at breast height–DBH, stand height–SHT, stand basal area–BAH, and stand density–TPH provided the best fit for natural-origin stands, whereas the logistic form was optimal for plantation-origin stands. Incorporating intercept-only random effect yielded the most parsimonious mixed-effects structure for both stand origins. Final mixed-effects models substantially improved prediction accuracy, reducing RMSE by approximately 23–25% relative to fixed-effects baselines. Subsampling analysis showed that RMSE decreased sharply with additional calibration trees, stabilizing at approximately 5–6 trees per plot in natural stands and 8–9 in plantations. Model-based sensitivity analysis indicated that HCB varied with stand structural conditions, with greater predicted HCB associated with higher stand basal area, whereas the effect of stand density was negative after accounting for DBH, stand height, and stand basal area. Plantation-origin stands however exhibited stronger sensitivity to structural variables (particularly stand basal area) than natural stands. These findings improve the understanding of crown base development in jack pine and provide actionable insights for thinning strategies to optimize merchantable stem length and stand productivity.

Article.Title: Biomolecular evidence reveals site-specific embalming recipes for ancient Egyptian crocodiles
Article.Authors: Koch T.; Phillips E.; Vandenbeusch M.; Stacey R.
Article.Abstract: Animal mummification, which was central to ancient Egyptian religious practices during the second half of the 1st millennium BC, broadly followed similar principles to human mummification. During this period, crocodiles, often associated with the god Sobek, were mummified in great numbers. Some crocodiles were believed to be living manifestations of the god (sacred mummies), and mummified after their natural death, while others served as votive offerings with large numbers deposited in dedicated burial complexes. Prior research on embalming recipes for crocodiles is limited, but has revealed the use of resins, tars, waxes and bitumen. However, it remains unclear whether embalming recipes varied across mummy types, periods or sites. To investigate this, we analysed seven crocodile mummies from the Late to the Graeco-Roman Periods using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry and correlating molecular profiles with radiocarbon dates and provenance. Our results show that the crocodiles were embalmed with different combinations of beeswax, pine (Pinaceae Pinus ) resin or tar and cedar (Pinaceae Cedrus ) tar. When integrated with previously published data, these results reveal a consistent embalming recipe at Kom Ombo, used over several centuries. This combined dataset highlights the continuity and transmission of embalming knowledge, and the existence of site-specific embalming traditions not documented before.

Article.Title: Andrographolide from Andrographis paniculata as a potential inhibitor of the novel malarial drug target PF11_0189: a comprehensive in silico approach
Article.Authors: Mahanta P.; Ansary A.; Lhouvum K.
Article.Abstract: Malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum still claims more than 600,000 lives every year, and the spread of partial artemisinin resistance across South and Southeast Asia now threatens the only first-line therapy available, making antimalarials with genuinely new mechanisms of action an urgent global priority. PF11_0189, an essential M16 insulinase-family metallopeptidase of P. falciparum with no significant human homolog, is a validated yet pharmacologically unexploited drug target. Here we combine the ethnopharmacological heritage of Northeast India (where Andrographis paniculata (Kalmegh) is the most consistently documented antimalarial herb across twelve tribal communities) with a statistically validated, multi-layered computational pipeline to identify putative PF11_0189 inhibitors in silico. Docking of ten A. paniculata phytochemicals, benchmarked against property-matched decoys (ROC-AUC = 0.81; enrichment factor at 1% = 12.4), ranked andrographolide as the top hit, outscoring the reference antimalarial chloroquine by 1.5 kcal/mol (− 8.4 vs. − 6.9 kcal/mol). Andrographolide paired a clean, alert-free drug-likeness profile (zero Lipinski violations; non-hERG; non-P-glycoprotein substrate; PAINS/Brenk-negative) with triplicate 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations that indicated a stable complex (backbone RMSD < 2.5 Å), a single dominant free-energy minimum, and a binding free energy of − 42.3 kJ/mol anchored by five energetic hotspot residues (Glu-203, Thr-89, Phe-116, Trp-214, Ser-112) independently corroborated by hydrogen-bonding and cross-correlation analyses. This convergence of five independent computational lines of evidence nominates andrographolide as a computationally prioritised, mechanistically testable candidate inhibitor of PF11_0189 and provides a hotspot-guided blueprint for structure-based antimalarial development. This is a purely computational study without wet-lab validation: the receptor is an AlphaFold2 model, and enzyme-inhibition, biophysical binding and in vitro antiplasmodial assays are still required before andrographolide can be considered a validated PF11_0189 inhibitor.

Article.Title: Extended antimicrobial use and its associated factors among patients admitted to surgical wards of public hospitals, Harar, Eastern Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Redwan H.; Jambo A.; Mohammed A.; Sisay M.; Edessa D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial agents are more likely to be misused than other drugs in hospitals. However, there are limited studies addressing the extended antibiotic use in surgical wards in Ethiopia, particularly in the study area. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the magnitude of extended antimicrobial use and its associated factors at public hospitals in Harar, Eastern Ethiopia from June 10 to October 10, 2021. A cross-sectional study was conducted at Haramaya University Hiwot Fana Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (HUHFCSH) and Jugal General Hospital (JGH). A total of 423 patients were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using a structured quantitative abstraction tool and analyzed using SPSS version 22. Bivariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were conducted. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to assess associations, and P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The overall prevalence of extended antimicrobial use was 73.0% (95% CI 69–77%). Extended prophylaxis was observed in 293 (69.3%) participants, including 258 (60.9% of the total cohort) post-operative, 33 (7.8%) pre-operative, and 2 (0.5%) medical prophylaxis cases. Extended treatment duration was observed in 16 (3.8%) participants. Male sex (AOR: 2.88, 95% CI 1.44–5.76), prophylactic antibiotic use (AOR: 20.62, 95% CI 8.19–51.95), and 1–10 days of hospital stay (AOR: 0.27, 95% CI 0.15–0.48) were significantly associated with extended antimicrobial use. Extended antimicrobial use was high, driven primarily by prolonged post-operative prophylaxis. Targeted stewardship interventions addressing surgical prophylaxis duration, disease prevalent to the male sex, duration of hospital stay, and availability of appropriate first-line prophylactic agents are needed.

Article.Title: Association of glycemic index and glycemic load with multiple myeloma: a case–control study
Article.Authors: Abdolkarimi M.; Shadnoush M.; Jowshan M.; Lesani A.; Khandaei S.; Rasekhi H.; Mehdizadeh M.; Parkhideh S.; Hamedi-Shahraki S.; Zahedi H.; Hajifathali A.
Article.Abstract: Dietary factors, particularly those affecting insulin resistance and inflammation, may influence multiple myeloma (MM) risk. Evidence regarding the relationship between glycemic index (GI) and glycemic load (GL) and MM is still inconclusive and shows mixed results. We investigated this relationship in an Iranian population. This case–control study included 141 newly diagnosed MM patients and 348 healthy controls (ages 20 to 75 years). Dietary intake was evaluated through a validated 154-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ). Dietary GI and GL were calculated based on participants' food intake. Binary logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) across quartiles of GI and GL. Models were adjusted for potential confounders, including age, sex, total energy consumption, and other lifestyle factors. Participants in the highest quartile of dietary GI had significantly higher odds of MM compared with those in the lowest quartile (OR 3.92, 95% CI 1.84–8.34; P-trend < 0.001) after fully adjusting for potential confounders. In contrast, dietary GL was inversely related to MM only in the crude analysis, and this association disappeared after adjustment for energy intake; GL was not associated with MM in the fully adjusted model (OR 1.37, 95% CI 0.51–3.63; P-trend = 0.45). Higher dietary GI was independently associated with increased odds of MM, whereas dietary GL was not associated with MM after adjustment for energy intake and other confounders. Further large-scale prospective studies are warranted to elucidate the role of dietary carbohydrate quality in MM development.

Article.Title: Influence of social support on kinesiophobia in patients with primary liver cancer after interventional therapy
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Deng X.; Wei Y.; Wu Q.
Article.Abstract: This study explored the factors associated with the occurrence of kinesiophobia in patients with primary liver cancer after interventional therapy, analyzed the correlations between the occurrence of kinesiophobia in patients with social support, psychological resilience, and rehabilitation self-efficacy, and conducted path analysis. This study adopts a parallel mediation model. A total of 209 patients with primary liver cancer who received interventional therapy in the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangnan University were recruited as research objects. The general data questionnaire, Self-Efficacy for Rehabilitation Outcome Scale (SER), Connor–Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC), Social Support Rate Scale (SSRS), and Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia (TSK) were used to conduct a cross-sectional investigation. Rank sum test and multiple linear regression statistical analysis were performed on the data, and model 4 of Hayes’ SPSS Process program was used to assess the intermediary effect. A total of 105 patients (50.2%) in the study population suffered from kinesiophobia. Age, liver cirrhosis, and severe anemia were the covariates associated with kinesiophobia. Correlation analysis revealed that patients’ social support was positively correlated with resilience scores and rehabilitation self-efficacy scores, and negatively correlated with kinesiophobia. Bootstrap mediation pathway analysis demonstrated that the total association magnitude between social support and kinesiophobia in patients with liver cancer after interventional therapy was − 0.524. Rehabilitation self-efficacy and psychological resilience showed a partial mediating association between social support and kinesiophobia, accounting for 18.5% and 5.2% of the total associated pathway proportion respectively. The observed chain association pathway indicates a direct relevant association between social support and kinesiophobia, with psychological resilience and rehabilitation self-efficacy showing a partial mediating association pathway between social support and kinesiophobia. Therefore, targeted strategies for managing kinesiophobia in patients with liver cancer after interventional therapy can be considered by optimizing patients’ social support status and promoting their psychological resilience and rehabilitation self-efficacy.

Article.Title: Trade-offs in deep learning approaches for precipitation downscaling across weather regimes
Article.Authors: Damiani A.; Ishizaki N.; Cordero R.; Feron S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate high-resolution precipitation information is critical for assessing hydrological extremes and climate change impacts in complex topographic regions. While machine learning-based downscaling provides a computationally efficient alternative to dynamical models, its performance can depend on regional climate characteristics and terrain complexity. In this study, we systematically benchmarked representative deep learning approaches for daily statistical downscaling over Japan, including quantile-based and stochastic CNN formulations, two- (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) U-Net variants, and a diffusion-based generative model, alongside conventional baselines. Model performance was evaluated using comprehensive statistical and spatial metrics under both climatological and typhoon-affected conditions, enabling us to assess model robustness under extreme precipitation regimes. We further developed a proof-of-concept forecasting configuration for 3D U-Net prediction of next-day precipitation from short predictor sequences, together with an extreme super-resolution experiment to assess scalability to very high target resolutions. The results revealed clear trade-offs: quantile mapping best reproduced distributional properties, deterministic CNNs performed particularly well for standard deterministic metrics, the stochastic CNN achieved the highest average neighborhood-scale skill, and the diffusion model best reproduced the spatial power spectrum, while U-Nets tended to smooth small scales. Nevertheless, the asymmetric-loss U-Net provided the most robust performance during typhoon conditions. These findings provide practical guidance for model selection in complex climatic regions and illustrate how inductive biases interact with regional climate dynamics.

Article.Authors: Ravitheja D.; Shanmugam Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper investigates accurate electrochemical parameter identification in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems (PEMWES), which is essential for multiphysics digital twins and dynamic control. Conventional analytical and metaheuristic methods may suffer from numerical instability, parameter coupling, and high computational latency under coupled thermal and pressure variations. Purely data-driven models may lack physical interpretability and electrochemical consistency, motivating the proposed BO-LSBoost framework for parameter identification and residual correction. Five core parameters ( $$\:\varDelta\:G,\:J₀,\:\alpha\:,\:r,\:\:{J}_{L}$$ ) are identified for a 160 cm² single-cell electrolyzer operating at 50–80 ( $$\: {}^{ \circ }C $$ )and pressures up to 30 bars. Bayesian Optimization (BO) estimates global thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, while Least-Squares Gradient Boosting (LSBoost) compensates for unmodelled multiphysics residuals. The model achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 0.0006% and 0.0014% for thermal and pressure sweeps, respectively. Dynamic cycling yields an average absolute voltage error of 0.01 V. Increasing the sample size from N = 60 to 239 reduces MAPE from 0.0335% to 0.0028%, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy for real-time load emulation.

Article.Title: Prognostic significance of immunohistochemical expression of chemerin and CD34-assessed microvessel density in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Velusamy P.; Mathew M.; Chandrashekar C.; KenniyanKumar S.; Kudva A.; Ragunathan Y.; Gadicherla S.; Guddattu V.; Solomon M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), the most commonly diagnosed oral cancer, has a poor prognosis, especially in the advanced stages. Chemerin, an adipokine that plays a significant role in inflammation and adipogenesis, has emerged as a prognostic biomarker in OSCC. The study evaluates immunohistochemical expression of chemerin and CD34-assessed microvessel density, and investigates their association with clinicopathological parameters and disease-free survival (DFS) in OSCC patients. The study consisted of tissue sections from 184 histopathologically diagnosed cases of OSCC stained by immunohistochemistry for chemerin. Microvessel density (MVD) was assessed using the hotspot method based on CD34 immunostaining. For survival analysis, three separate Cox regression models were constructed for chemerin expression, CD34-assessed microvessel density, and a composite score combining both to assess their effect on DFS. Composite scoring was based on chemerin expression and MVD. Group 1 includes low chemerin + low MVD; Group 2: low chemerin + high MVD; Group 3: High chemerin + low MVD; Group 4: high chemerin + high MVD. Kaplan–Meier survival curves were used for survival analysis, and the Cox regression model for risk assessment. p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. High chemerin expression was associated with advanced histopathological grade ( p < 0.001) and TNM stage (III-IV) ( p = 0.013), the presence of perineural invasion ( p = 0.022), increased depth of invasion (> 5 mm) ( p = 0.002), and tumor size (pT) (> 4 cm) ( p = 0.016). A statistically significant positive correlation was observed between high chemerin expression and increased microvessel density (MVD), highlighting its role in tumor angiogenesis ( p < 0.001). Advanced TNM stage (III-IV) was an independent predictor of reduced DFS in all three models. Model 1 involving chemerin showed significance only in the univariate analysis ( p = 0.001). Whereas model 2, involving CD34-assessed MVD, showed statistical significance only in the univariate analysis ( p = 0.007). In the multivariate analysis involving model 3, the composite groups (2–4) showed higher hazard ratios for reduced DFS than the reference group 1. Chemerin overexpression is associated with tumor angiogenesis, and its combined evaluation helped in improving the prognostic value compared to individual marker analysis. These findings suggest that chemerin, when combined with other prognostic biomarkers, can help with risk stratification in OSCC, which further require external validation.

Article.Title: The serial mediating effects of mindfulness and anxiety in the relationship between physical exercise and smartphone addiction among college students
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Gao W.; Zhu J.; Wang Y.; Ke F.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Physical exercise is associated with lower levels of smartphone addiction among college students, but the psychological pathways underlying this association and potential gender differences warrant further investigation. Between October 11 and 21, 2025, 1795 questionnaires were collected from ten higher education institutions in Fuzhou, China. After screening, 1670 students aged 18–22 were included. Physical exercise, mindfulness, anxiety, and smartphone addiction were measured using scales. PROCESS Models 6 and 90 were used to examine indirect associations and gender moderation. Higher levels of physical exercise were associated with lower smartphone addiction. The indirect associations through mindfulness, anxiety, and the sequential mindfulness–anxiety pathway were all statistically significant. Gender significantly moderated the adjusted direct association between physical exercise and smartphone addiction, with a stronger negative association among female students. However, gender did not significantly moderate the association between anxiety and smartphone addiction or the corresponding indirect pathways. These findings suggest that mindfulness and anxiety are closely related to the association between physical exercise and smartphone addiction, although the cross-sectional design does not support causal inference.

Article.Title: Water-rich glassy states from mixed sulfate salts
Article.Authors: van Campenhout C.; Castell R.; Heeremans T.; Hunger J.; Woutersen S.; Bonn D.; Shahidzadeh N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glasses exhibit unique mechanical and physicochemical properties distinct from crystalline solids, with relevance to biomineralization, solid-state physics, pharmaceutical chemistry, and planetary science. However, despite their widespread occurrence and fundamental importance, simple chemical rules that predict when an amorphous rather than a crystalline phase forms from solution remain scarce. Here, we exploit the complexity of mixed-salt crystallization to show the spontaneous formation of amorphous glassy states from a wide variety of mixed sulfate solutions. Isothermal evaporation of sulfate solutions containing specific ratios of mono- and multi-valent cations yields an amorphous glassy state. We find that this state is soft, viscoelastic, X-ray amorphous, and retains up to 40 wt% water. Spectroscopic analysis further reveals that disordered and immobilized ionic species trap bulk-like water. By modulating composition and ambient relative humidity, we show that the temporal stability of the glassy state can be tuned from seconds to months. Our findings help uncover fundamental mechanisms governing the formation and stability of amorphous phases, with direct relevance to complex biomineralization processes on Earth, and offer a compelling explanation for the widespread occurrence of amorphous sulfate materials in Martian mineralogy. Moreover, the ability to precisely control the synthesis of these metastable amorphous states and tune their lifetime opens opportunities for the design of next-generation materials, particularly in advanced drug delivery applications.

Article.Title: Synthesis, characterization, and anticancer effect of nanoformulated Zataria multiflora Boiss. extract against prostate and breast cancer cells in vitro
Article.Authors: Khazaei M.; Bozorgi M.; Alizadeh S.; Shahna G.; Bozorgi A.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effect of nanoformulated Zataria multiflora Boiss. (Shirazi thyme) extract on inhibiting the growth of PC3 prostate and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines by regulating autophagy. The hydroalcoholic extract of Zataria multiflora Boiss. (ZM) was prepared by ultrasonic-assisted maceration in 70% ethanol. Blank (Gel NP) and extract-loaded gelatin nanoparticles (ZM.Gel NPs) were synthesized via a two-step desolvation method and characterized in terms of size, surface charge, morphology, chemical structure, loading parameters, and in vitro release kinetics. PC3 and MDA-MB-231 cell lines were treated with various concentrations of the free extract, Gel NPs, and ZM.Gel NPs (with equivalent encapsulated ZM extract) for 48 and 72 h. Cell proliferation was evaluated using the MTT assay, and IC50 values were calculated. The expression of apoptosis- and autophagy-related genes was determined using Real-Time PCR. Gel NPs and ZM.Gel NPs exhibited spherical morphology, with smooth surfaces and suitable physicochemical properties, while providing sustained release of ZM extract over time. ZM.Gel NPs significantly enhanced the antiproliferative potential of the free extract, thereby reducing the IC50 value. ZM.Gel NPs significantly upregulated TP53 and BAX and downregulated BCL2 , while decreasing Beclin-1 , ATG5 , ATG7 , and LC3A expression compared with the free extract. Gel NPs enhanced the antiproliferative and cytotoxic effects of ZM extract, upregulating pro-apoptotic genes and downregulating autophagy-driven genes in prostate and breast cancer cell lines.

Article.Title: Seroepidemiology of dengue and chikungunya viruses in Chabahar city, southwestern Iran-2025
Article.Authors: Salehi-Vaziri M.; Jalali T.; Eybpoosh S.; Asadi L.; Tavakoli M.; Hosseini Z.; Arbabi F.; Sajadi S.; Noori E.; Mobaraki F.; Moghaddam M.; Mashayekhi M.; Moradi G.; Pouriayevali M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dengue and chikungunya viruses (DENV, CHIKV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, pose significant public health challenges in tropical and sub-tropical regions. This study investigated the seroprevalence of DENV and CHIKV in Chabahar city, an area in which Aedes aegypti has been established and local transmission of DENV reported since 2023. From January to February 2025, a total of 650 serum samples were collected from the catchment area of eight health centers in the city and tested for DENV and CHIKV IgG using ELISA kits. The overall ELISA‑defined DENV IgG seropositivity was 14.3% (95% CI 11.7–17.3%) and for CHIKV was 0.9% (95% CI 0.4–2.1%). The highest prevalence of DENV was observed in the urban areas of Zibashahr and urban-2 Districts (25%), and the lowest in Kambel Soleiman (4%). Men had a significantly higher DENV seroprevalence (17% vs. 10.8% in women, p = 0.012), and seroprevalence decreased with increasing education level ( p = 0.021). Older age was associated with increased DENV seropositivity ( p = 0.040). Occupation was not significantly associated with DENV seropositivity. No significant association was found between mosquito bite reports and seropositivity. These findings provide evidence of ELISA‑defined DENV IgG seropositivity in the general population of Chabahar, suggesting previous exposure to DENV. The high seropositivity in certain districts highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and targeted vector control measures in high risk groups and areas with high Aedes mosquito density.

Article.Title: Analysis of incidence and risk factors for intra-abdominal hypertension in critically Ill neurosurgical patients: a prospective-observational study
Article.Authors: Li L.; Wang Q.; Zhang F.; Li Y.; Sun X.; Sun X.; Sun J.; Li S.; Fan M.
Article.Abstract: Intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is associated with high morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients. However, its characteristics in critically ill neurosurgical cohort remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, risk factors, severity and outcomes of IAH in this specific population. This prospective observational study was conducted in a Neurosurgical Intensive Care Unit (NICU) between Apr 2022 to Apr 2024. All eligible critically ill neurosurgical patients had their intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) measured three times daily via a urinary catheter with 25 mL of saline; the mean daily value was recorded. IAH was defined as IAP ≥ 12mmHg. Demographic data, clinical parameters, and potential risk factors for IAH were analyzed. A Total of 283 patients were enrolled. Among them, 53 (18.73%) developed IAH during their NICU stay, and two (3.78% of IAH patients) progressed to abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS). The 180-day all-cause mortality was significantly higher in patients with IAH than those without IAH (33.96% vs. 12.17%, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that Glasgow Coma Scale scores (GCS) (OR, 0.733; 95% CI, 0.567–0.947; P = 0.018), Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores(SOFAs) (OR, 1.830; 95% CI, 1.280–2.616; P = 0.001), positive fluid balance (PFB) (OR, 3.855; 95% CI, 1.485–10.004; P = 0.006), tracheotomy (OR, 3.283; 95% CI, 1.241–8.681; P = 0.017), platelet count (OR, 1.006; 95% CI, 1.001–1.010; P = 0.010) and invasive Mechanical Ventilation (IMV) (OR, 5.915; 95% CI, 1.481–23.624; P = 0.012) were significant associations with IAH in critically ill neurosurgical patients. IAH occurred in 18.73% of critically ill neurosurgical patients and was an important associated factor for 180-day mortality. Associated factors independently associated with IAH in this cohort included lower GCS, higher SOFAs, IMV, PFB, tracheotomy, and platelet count. Moreover, IAH was identified as a associated factor for elevated intracranial pressure in these patients.

Article.Title: In-situ load testing and finite element analysis of a damaged reinforced concrete flat plate slab in a tall building
Article.Authors: Majumdar M.; Ahsan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study provides a detailed case analysis of a reinforced concrete flat plate slab with localized damage in a 25-story high-rise. A poorly hardened concrete layer under the soffit raised immediate concerns about structural safety, prompting a thorough evaluation in accordance with ACI 318-25. A controlled 24-h monotonic load test was conducted using sandbags, with real-time deflection data recorded. Results indicated a maximum deflection of 5.70 mm and a residual deflection of 0.62 mm—both within acceptable limits per code. No crack growth or signs of ongoing deterioration were seen during visual checks after the test. Nonlinear finite element analyses in ABAQUS used the concrete damaged plasticity model with test-based concrete properties and no calibration. On the actual supports, the analysis gave 4.66 mm at full load against 5.12 mm measured, whereas clamped panel edges gave only 0.89–2.19 mm. Although the slab performed well during testing, repair of the deteriorated soffit is advised to address possible long-term issues. This case study offers insights into evaluating flat plate systems with localized damage, linking field diagnostics with analytical models.

Article.Title: Cost-calibrated decision rules for small-sample experimental screening pipelines
Article.Authors: Hackenberger B.; Hackenberger D.; Djerdj T.
Article.Abstract: Small-sample experiments (n = 3–10) dominate preclinical and pilot research, yet, to our knowledge, no closed-form decision-theoretic framework links experimental costs, base rates and error control for small-sample screening pipelines. We present a cost-calibrated framework for pipelines in which initial screening precedes downstream confirmation, unifying frequentist testing, Bayesian posterior thresholding and Bayes-factor analysis as special cases of a single cost-parameterised family. Under a conjugate normal model we derive an analytic false-positive bound, a Bayes risk decomposition with a closed-form crossover condition, and a pipeline optimality theorem with controlled false discovery rates. Simulations and analyses of 248 effects from four domains, three of which provide replication or independent-confirmation data, show improved expected utility for moderate-to-large effects, moderate-to-high base rates and available confirmatory follow-up, and no benefit in low-base-rate or single-stage settings. Open-source R and Python implementations enable direct use without decision-theoretic expertise.

Article.Title: Well-aware stacking ensemble machine learning framework for oil production prediction in gas-lift wells: leakage-aware validation in the Halewah Field
Article.Authors: Hamid A.; Mohyaldinn M.; Lathbl M.; Alameen M.; Adamu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lift-gas decisions in the mature Halewah Field, Yemen, require fast, well-specific oil-rate predictions. PIPESIM models of wells H-06 and H-09, each calibrated to a stabilized field operating point, were evaluated at 350 operating scenarios in each well. Six learners and 22 ensemble configurations were compared, including WellAware_Stack, one six-learner stack per well. On a 105-record holdout, WellAware_Stack reached R² = 0.996 (RMSE 42.0 STB/d), against 0.949 (155.1 STB/d) for the best pooled stack. Repeated scenario-grouped nested cross-validation of these two finalists gave R² = 0.994 and 0.857, exposing a cross-well information path in row-wise splits. A controlled comparison attributed the gain to well information rather than stacking: supplying it reduced the error of every model family five- to tenfold, a well-specific Gaussian process was more accurate than WellAware_Stack (RMSE 23.6 against 44.9 STB/d), and standardizing the Gaussian-process target stabilized the stack. On 60 fresh PIPESIM scenarios simulated after the models were frozen, WellAware_Stack reached R² = 0.995 and 0.999 for H-06 and H-09, and the well-specific Gaussian process 0.999 for both; at the calibrated operating points their errors were 10–17% and below 4%, respectively. The study quantifies surrogate-to-simulator fidelity and provides a leakage-aware protocol for paired simulation data.

Article.Authors: Aydoğdu A.; Karaca T.; Yalcin Kavus B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an explainable hybrid artificial neural network (ANN)–multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework for wildfire susceptibility prioritization and preliminary response-center candidate generation in Muğla, Türkiye. Predictive performance was evaluated using leakage-safe nested spatial validation, repeated 5-, 10-, and 20-km block settings, calibration analysis, and spatial-supergroup bootstrap confidence intervals. The ANN achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.6601 and a mean PR-AUC of 0.6191, remaining competitive with random forest, penalized logistic regression, and LightGBM, but showing no decisive superiority over random forest. Cross-fitted grouped permutation importance and SHAP analyses for both ANN and random forest identified daily minimum relative humidity, daily maximum wind speed, and daily maximum temperature as the dominant predictive-relevance core, jointly accounting for 67.76% of the four-source mean relevance mass. MCDM robustness was assessed across 144 prespecified weight, utility, normalization, TOPSIS, and VIKOR scenarios. The representative consensus TOPSIS and VIKOR rankings showed strong global agreement but only moderate overlap in the extreme upper tail, indicating non-redundant and scenario-dependent reprioritization. Temporal-to-spatial aggregation identified 117 robust 1-km priority blocks within 28 connected hotspot components. Priority-weighted clustering then generated ten hotspot-based screening points for subsequent response-center planning. These outputs support transparent spatial screening, but do not constitute calibrated wildfire probabilities or final facility-location decisions.

Article.Title: PA-SBR: student behavior recognition based on parallel convolution and attention mechanism
Article.Authors: Lu L.; Wu D.; Yang J.; Chen Y.; Zhang Z.; Liu Z.; Liu T.; Tang Z.
Article.Abstract: Student behavior recognition is an important part in smart classrooms. There are two main problems with existing student behavior recognition methods. Firstly, it is easy to overlook the behavior of students who are seated densely; Secondly, it is difficult to recognize the behavior of students who sitting in the back row or being partially obstructed by the students in front row. To address these two issues, a new university classroom student behavior recognition method named PA-SBR was proposed. Firstly, a university classroom student behavior dataset named UCSB was constructed, which consists of 1200 images sourced from real university classrooms. Secondly, C3K2-PC and SPPF-PA modules were designed to form the backbone network, and a joint loss function was designed to recognize student behaviors. Parallel convolution in C3K2-PC module is beneficial to obtain behavioral features of occluded students. Pixel-level attention mechanism in SPPF-PA module helps to focus more on key information at different scales and improve the recognition precision of multi-scale targets and student behaviors with small sample size. Meanwhile, the joint loss function can effectively cope with situations where students sit densely and some students are obstructed. Subsequently, a structured pruning technique was utilized to streamline the model, in order to achieve a certain balance between recognition accuracy and time efficiency. Finally, comparison and analysis between PA-SBR and other excellent methods was performed on UCSB and SCB-Dataset3-S datasets. PA-SBR achieved the best performance on both UCSB and SCB-Dataset3-S datasets, with mAP50 values of 0.538 and 0.757, respectively. Compared with YOLO V11 and YOLO V12 with mAP50 value of 0.517 and 0.482 on UCSB and DB-SBR with mAP50 value of 0.729 on SCB-Dataset3-S, the performance of student behavior recognition has improved.

Article.Title: Cross-channel color image encryption scheme using a novel 3D neuron model and fast Josephus traversal
Article.Authors: Ouyang L.; Yang Y.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: As digital communication continues to advance rapidly, ensuring the security of image data during transmission has become increasingly vital. To overcome the inherent limitations of traditional chaotic image encryption schemes, this paper introduces an innovative color image encryption algorithm that combines a Memristive Hindmarsh-Rose (MHR) neuron model and a Cyclically Maintained Josephus Algorithm (CMJA). Initially, the MHR model incorporates a magnetic flux variable and an adaptive control framework, employing a state-dependent switching mechanism to adjust feedback strength. This closed-loop behavior enhances the system’s nonlinearity and offers a wider range of tunable chaotic oscillations as a highly sensitive source of entropy. Next, to address the efficiency challenges of traditional Josephus scrambling in high-resolution scenarios, a novel CMJA is introduced. By utilizing “head-tail coverage and boundary contraction” strategies, the algorithm mitigates performance overhead from frequent element movement, effectively reducing the time complexity of index maintenance. In addition, a SHA-512 hash-based plaintext-dependent, one-cipher-per-image key generation mechanism and a cross-layer composite scrambling architecture are implemented, resulting in a highly nonlinear redistribution of pixels across the three-dimensional color components. Finally, experimental results show that the chi-square test values for all ciphertext channels remain below the critical threshold of 293.2478. When compared with state-of-the-art schemes, the proposed algorithm improves encryption efficiency while maintaining competitive security, indicating its potential applicability in secure communication.

Article.Title: Integrated control and power system engineering for Thailand Plasma Focus-2
Article.Authors: Bor-in P.; Tamman A.; Wonghabut P.; Lekchaum S.; Locharoenrat K.
Article.Abstract: Plasma physics and nuclear fusion research in Thailand are entering a significant phase at the Thailand Institute of Nuclear Technology (Public Organization) (TINT), which operates the Thailand Plasma Focus-2 (TPF-2) and has received, for the Thailand Tokamak-1 (TT-1) project, major equipment from the HT-6 M machine through cooperation with the Institute of Plasma Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ASIPP), People’s Republic of China. The efficient operation of the TT-1 device primarily depends on the development of four main systems, of which the Plasma Control System (PCS) and Data Acquisition (DAQ) systems are considered critical systems that must be learned and newly developed to support future technologies. This research, therefore, aims to develop and integrate the PCS and DAQ systems on the LabVIEW platform combined with National Instruments (NI) PXIe hardware using the TPF-2 as an engineering testbed that may inform future TT-1 development. The focus is on solving electromagnetic interference (EMI) and severe ground potential rise (GPR) phenomena from discharges at the hundreds-of-kiloamperes level that distort control signals and cause damage to electronic equipment. We developed a multi-tiered grounding architecture according to IEEE Standard 1100 in order to isolate the sensitive diagnostic loops from high-current return paths. This setup includes the diagnostic (DG), working (WG), and shielding networks, and uses optocoupler-based galvanic isolation to protect low-voltage electronics. The transient WG–DG potential difference was not measured. Original signal recovery is handled by a dual-stage technique that combines amplitude limiting with Savitzky-Golay filtering. After the modification, the recorded transient noise within the 10–60 MHz band was more than tenfold lower. The 5 V-referenced interference ratio at the HVPS analog input of the microcontroller rose from − 4.78 ± 2.21 dB to 13.09 ± 1.68 dB (mean ± sample standard deviation, n = 40 shots per configuration; operating points not matched). The clean signal path was used to capture the plasma pinch dynamics at an operating voltage of 11 kV and a peak current of about 120 kA, on a current scale that relies on an uncalibrated coil mutual inductance and unverified equal current sharing, so its dominant uncertainty is unquantified. The measured current waveforms were used to calibrate Lee Model Code simulations, with which they are consistent. Up to 465 shots per day were recorded without observed malfunction. These integration techniques yield a potential technical reference for developing control architectures for the TT-1 device.

Article.Title: Geostatistically resolved PCA and fuzzy C-means clustering based delineation of multi-nutrient soil-fertility management zones for site-specific nutrient management in maize
Article.Authors: Pandit V.; Anjaiah T.; Ravali C.; Venkateswarlu M.; Sivaranjani C.; Chatterjee S.; Noorzai A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sustainable maize production in spatially heterogeneous smallholder fields requires nutrient recommendations that reflect within-field variation in soil fertility and its spatial structure, particularly where micronutrient constraints can coexist with adequate macronutrient supply. This study aimed to convert dense field-scale soil information into operational management zones (MZs) linked to soil-test target-yield fertilizer prescriptions, maize yield, and profitability in a farmer-managed field in the northern Deccan Plateau (Telangana, India). Two hundred georeferenced composite topsoil samples (0–15 cm) were analyzed for 11 indicators (pH, EC, OC, available N, P 2 O 5 , K 2 O, S, and DTPA-extractable Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu). After integrity checks and property-specific transformations, each attributes spatial dependence was modeled via semivariograms and mapped by ordinary kriging, standardized variables were reduced by PCA and clustered using fuzzy C-means with multi-index validation. All attributes showed strong spatial dependence (nugget to sill < 25%), with effective ranges of 24.99–41.22 m and cross-validation R 2 of 0.67–0.87. Variability was low for pH (CV 3.55%) but high for S and micronutrients (CV 34.17–48.78%). Correlations revealed a dominant positive fertility network (e.g., N–S r = 0.96; P 2 O 5 –K 2 O r = 0.93), while Zn opposed this gradient (e.g., Zn–pH r = − 0.81). PCA retained two components explaining 90.2% variance (PC1 86.9%), preserving the antagonistic Zn signal. Validity indices supported three contiguous MZs with significant interzone differences for all indicators ( p < 0.05) and within-zone CV reductions up to 35.30% (pH) and 28.87% (Zn), Zn decreased from 4.7 to 2.9 mg kg −1 from MZ-1 to MZ-3 despite higher macronutrients in MZ-3. Zone prescriptions rebalanced fertilization versus farmer practice (N 249–251 vs 175 kg ha −1 ; P 2 O 5 44–45 vs 60; K 2 O 78–82 vs 40), increasing yields to 70.42–74.14 vs 68.29 q ha⁻ 1 and improving profitability most in MZ-2 (net return ₹85,921 ha −1 ; B:C 2.58). The results show that an integrated geostatistical—PCA—fuzzy zoning framework can translate multivariate soil gradients into actionable nutrient decisions, while highlighting that enriched zones may still require micronutrient-specific diagnosis (Zn) and response validation through replicated trials.

Article.Authors: Gao G.

Across 100 repeated 300-patient samples, logistic updating yielded median slope 1.086 (empirical 95% interval 0.792–1.804) and modest median Brier improvement of 0.0037. Five alternative target partitions gave median slopes 0.90–1.09. Source calibration did not ensure external calibration. Article.Title: Evolution of mechanical response and failure modes in small-spaced tunnels subjected to progressive lining removal
Article.Authors: Ji Z.; Han Y.; Li Z.; Wang Y.; Xiao F.; Hu M.
Article.Abstract: Partial lining removal during tunnel maintenance and widening can alter load transfer between adjacent openings, yet its influence on the mechanical response and damage evolution of small-spaced twin tunnels remains insufficiently understood. A mechanism-oriented investigation was conducted using uniaxial compression tests, two-dimensional digital image correlation (DIC), and three-dimensional LS-DYNA simulations. Six finite-thickness sandstone twin-tunnel specimens with gypsum linings were prepared, with one specimen assigned to each axial lining-removal ratio. The axial lining-removal ratio was defined as η = Lr/La × 100%, where Lr is the removed axial length of the left-tunnel lining and La = 50 mm is the total specimen length along the tunnel axis. Removal covered the full lining thickness and complete horseshoe-shaped circumference within that interval; the right-tunnel lining remained intact. Specimens S1–S6 corresponded to η = 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100%, respectively. The nominal peak axial stress decreased from 37.94 MPa for S1 to 24.33 MPa for S6, and the overall elastic modulus of the composite specimen decreased from 4.54 to 2.28 GPa. The crown-displacement histories of the two openings separated progressively earlier as the axial lining-removal ratio increased. DIC fields and post-peak photographs indicated tunnel-perimeter localized damage at η = 0–40%, asymmetric multi-zone damage at η = 60–80%, and removal-side concentrated crushing at η = 100%. These findings clarify how progressive lining removal weakens coordinated load sharing and promotes asymmetric damage concentration in small-spaced twin tunnels, providing a mechanistic basis for targeted monitoring and support during tunnel maintenance and widening.

Article.Title: Edaphic and seasonal variation in multifloral honeys composition
Article.Authors: González-Porto A.; Martín-Arroyo T.; López-Pérez J.; García-Cardo O.; Bartolomé-Esteban C.
Article.Abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate how the soil substrate and harvest season influence the characteristics of multifloral honeys from the Alcarria region (Spain). This region is a plateau shaped by the uplift of the Iberian System and is characterized by extensive limestone and gypsum formations. For this study, 172 honey samples collected in spring and summer from two types of soil, gypsum and limestone, over a period of eight consecutive years were analyzed. Spring honeys were associated with greater total phenolic content (TPC) and vitamin C and increased total antioxidant activity, whereas summer honeys presented slightly increased electrical conductivity, free acidity, and color (Pfund and chroma). Compared with limestone substrates, gypsum soils produced honeys with greater electrical conductivity, free acidity, and color (Pfund and chroma). Honey originating from limestone substrates contained relatively high concentrations of the main sugars. The differences between the two substrates are less pronounced in the summer season. Overall, both the soil type and harvest season associated with significant variation in the physicochemical and antioxidant profiles of multifloral honeys from La Alcarria. These findings highlight the influence of environmental factors on the composition and quality of honey and underline the importance of conducting further studies on its role as an environmental biomarker.

Article.Title: Deep learning model based on dynamic contrast-enhanced ultrasound to predict thyroid malignancy and BRAFV600E mutation
Article.Authors: Tang J.; Sui E.; Tian Y.; Liu R.; Liu X.; Wang J.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: To develop a video vision transformer (ViViT) model based on thyroid contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) video, applying it to distinguish malignant thyroid nodules and predict BRAFV600E mutation in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). We retrospectively collected thyroid nodules with CEUS videos and divided them into training, validation, and testing sets in a ratio of 4:3:3. The ViViT-CEUS diagnostic model was developed and validated. Its performance was compared with two-dimensional convolutional neural networks (2D-CNN), three-dimensional convolutional neural networks (3D-CNN) and traditional radiomics models. Radiologists with different levels of clinical experience were served as the comparator group. 428 thyroid nodules were included (69 benign, 359 malignant). All malignant nodules were PTC, comprising 267 BRAFV600E mutated and 92 non-mutated cases. The AUC of ViViT-CEUS for diagnosing malignancy was 0.938, which was significantly higher than that of 2D-CNN (AUC = 0.767), 3D-CNN (AUC = 0.790), and radiologists (AUC range : 0.617–0.815). The AUC of ViViT-CEUS for predicting BRAFV600E was 0.865, outperforming 2D-CNN (AUC = 0.704), 3D-CNN (AUC = 0.597), and traditional radiomics models (AUC = 0.682). The ViViT-CEUS model demonstrated high accuracy in identifying malignant thyroid nodules and improved prediction of PTC BRAFV600E mutations compared to alternative methods, providing a basis for identifying molecular features based on dynamic CEUS videos.

Article.Title: A multi-trait genotype–ideotype distance index identifies cold-tolerant bread wheat ideotypes using novel winter survival and freezing tolerance indices
Article.Authors: Haliloğlu K.; Kartay H.; Türkoğlu A.; Işık M.; Bolouri P.; Alipour H.
Article.Abstract: Cold and freezing stress remain among the most economically damaging abiotic constraints on winter wheat production in continental climates, yet the multi-trait genotype–ideotype distance index (MGIDI), a powerful multivariate selection tool recently applied to drought, heat, salinity and waterlogging tolerance, has not, to our knowledge, been applied to cold or freezing stress in any crop. We examined whether combining yield, winter survival and laboratory freezing tolerance within MGIDI could identify lines with a favorable balance of these traits. Here we evaluated 180 F 12 recombinant inbred lines (RILs) from a Norstar (freezing tolerant) × Zagros (freezing sensitive) cross, plus both parents, at two contrasting Turkish environments during the 2022–2023 season: Erzurum, a cold effective site with severe natural winter stress, and Konya, a low stress comparison site. A Freeze Intensity Index (FII = 0.549, based on winter damage) confirmed severe, discriminating cold stress at Erzurum. We computed five classical stress indices adapted from drought physiology (Cold Tolerance Index, CTI; Cold Yield Index, CYI; Cold Relative Stress Index, CRSI; Cold Stress Susceptibility, CSS; and Tolerance Index, TOL) alongside two indices introduced here: a Winter Survival Index (WSI, derived from pre-/post-winter plant stand ratios) and a Freezing Tolerance Index (FTI, derived from laboratory LT 50 (lethal temperature for 50% mortality) values normalized to the freezing sensitive parent). A comprehensive evaluation value (D) and MGIDI, computed via factor analysis (5 factors, 76.3% cumulative variance) at 10% selection intensity, jointly identified 17 superior lines. Selected lines showed substantial selection gains relative to the population: grain yield + 39.3%, winter damage − 39.6%, visual cold damage − 38.7%, absolute LT 50 +14.2%, and WSI + 13.9% (all trait differences significant at p < 0.01). WSI correlated moderately with a Cold Damage Resistance Index (CDRI) for winter damage ( r = 0.621), but only weakly with the yield-based CTI ( r = 0.239), indicating that survival and yield capture different aspects of cold response. These results show that MGIDI can integrate complementary cold response measures to identify productive, winter hardy wheat lines for further evaluation across seasons and cold environments.

Article.Title: Comparative characterization of monosodium iodoacetate-induced osteoarthritis in rat and rabbit models using micro-computed tomography and histology assessment
Article.Authors: Umran N.; Akmal M.; Abu J.; Abas F.; Madzuki I.; Yahya R.; Sulaiman S.; Fong L.; Song L.; Fauzi A.; Ajat M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration and subchondral bone remodeling. Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced animal models are widely used for investigating OA pathogenesis and evaluating potential therapies; however, standardized comparative evaluations of commonly used rat and rabbit models using identical structural outcome assessments following species-specific validated MIA induction protocols remain limited. This study compared structural alterations in MIA-induced OA in rats and rabbits using identical macroscopic, micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), and histological assessments. Twelve male Sprague Dawley rats and twelve male New Zealand White rabbits were randomly allocated to sham or OA groups (n = 6/group). OA was induced by intra-articular injection of MIA (3 mg in rats; 8 mg in rabbits), and knee joints were evaluated at a predefined 12-week endpoint. Both species developed characteristic OA pathology, including cartilage degeneration, osteophyte formation, subchondral bone sclerosis, and trabecular microarchitectural alterations. Quantitative micro-CT demonstrated significant OA-associated increases in bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular separation (Tb.Sp), and total porosity (PO) in both species compared with their respective sham controls ( p < 0.05). Under the present experimental conditions, OA-related structural changes were consistently more pronounced in rats, with greater subchondral bone remodeling and more severe cartilage degeneration than in rabbits, as confirmed by micro-CT and histological grading. Although both models successfully reproduced key features of OA, their disease severity differed substantially. These findings provide standardized comparative evidence demonstrating that validated rat and rabbit MIA-induced OA models exhibit distinct structural responses under their respective experimental protocols and may therefore be selected according to specific research objectives rather than assumed biological equivalence.

Article.Title: SCADA-based thermal degradation prognostics for hydropower step-up transformers: a case study of Nam Theun 2 hydropower plant
Article.Authors: Simphilavong N.; Khunkitti P.; Khunkitti S.
Article.Abstract: Continuous quantification of transformer thermal-aging indicators is vital for risk-informed asset management and maintenance planning in major hydropower facilities, particularly those operating under demanding tropical ambient conditions. However, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA)-only applications for transformer prognostics remain underexplored, while conventional approaches often rely on offline chemical diagnostics or invasive sampling, limiting their suitability for continuous real-time monitoring within SCADA environments. This study presents a non-intrusive, data-driven framework for predicting an IEEE Std C57.91-derived equivalent transformer loss of life (LOL) indicator using routinely available operational SCADA parameters, validated on continuous multi-year data from Nam Theun 2 hydropower plant (HPP) in Lao PDR (capacity 1,080 MW). By bridging the IEEE C57.91 thermal-aging formulation with dynamic temporal feature engineering, including differential aging states and autoregressive thermal lags, the proposed methodology captures nonlinear aging dynamics associated with rapid load variations and tropical ambient thermal fluctuations. Twelve generator step-up (GSU) transformers and seven regression paradigms under chronological partitioning strategies, tree-based ensemble models generally provided strong performance. Specifically, the Random Forest model under a 70:30 train–test split ratio achieved a fleet-wide Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.00 and an R 2 of 0.9865 without requiring offline diagnostic data as model inputs. The developed framework provides a cost-effective, scalable basis for continuous SCADA-based thermal-aging monitoring and condition-based maintenance (CBM) across large-scale renewable energy infrastructure.
