Article.Title: Can internal load associate with adaptation? A comparison of 1v1 and 3v3 basketball training in physically inactive female college students
Article.Authors: Li L.; Wang Y.; Zhou H.; Chen J.; Matta Mello Portugal E.; Trybulski R.; Clemente F.
Article.Abstract: This study compared internal-load profiles between 1v1 and 3v3 basketball training and examined whether accumulated internal load was associated with changes in estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) in physically inactive female college students. The longitudinal estimated VO₂max analysis included 63 randomized participants allocated to 1v1 basketball training, 3v3 basketball training, or a non-exercising control condition. Internal-load and dose-response analyses were restricted to the 42 exercisers because the control group had no training-load exposure. Participants in the exercise groups completed three supervised 60-min sessions per week for 8 weeks. Internal load was quantified using accumulated session-RPE (ΣsRPE) and mean peak heart rate (HRpeak), with CR10 expressed as the algebraic equivalent of ΣsRPE divided by the fixed total training duration. Compared with 3v3, 1v1 produced higher ΣsRPE (12,174 ± 203 vs. 11,351 ± 229 AU; mean difference, 823 AU; 95% CI, 688 to 958; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 3.80). Mean HRpeak was also higher in 1v1 than in 3v3 (178.33 ± 0.83 vs. 177.49 ± 0.50 bpm; mean difference, 0.83 bpm; 95% CI, 0.40 to 1.26; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 1.22), although the absolute difference was physiologically small. Estimated VO₂max increased in 1v1 by 1.97 mL kg −1 min −1 (95% CI, 1.40 to 2.55; p < 0.001) and in 3v3 by 2.45 mL kg −1 min −1 (95% CI, 1.60 to 3.31; p < 0.001), whereas the control group showed no clear change (0.07 mL kg −1 min −1 ; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.24; p = 0.348). The group difference in pre-to-post change was statistically clear (F(2,60) = 18.93, p < 0.001, η² = 0.387), with greater improvements in both exercise groups than in control and no clear difference between 1v1 and 3v3. Among exercisers, ΔVO₂max was not clearly associated with ΣsRPE ( r = -0.050, 95% CI, -0.348 to 0.258; p = 0.755) or mean HRpeak ( r = -0.130, 95% CI, -0.418 to 0.181; p = 0.411). Neither association met the prespecified two-sided α = 0.05 criterion, and both 95% confidence intervals included the null value ( r = 0). These findings indicate that both basketball formats improved estimated aerobic fitness compared with control, while 1v1 imposed greater global internal load than 3v3. In this sample, and using the available global load indices, no statistically clear dose–response association was detected. Registration: The study protocol was registered in the ISRCTN (24697262).

Article.Title: A two-stage cascade framework for traffic sign detection: reproduction and boundary analysis
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Xiang Z.; Huang H.; Li M.; Guo H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traffic sign detection in adverse conditions remains difficult because small, distant signs and degraded illumination act together. This paper reports a reduced-scale reproduction and boundary analysis of a cascade framework for traffic sign detection, comprising multi-dimensional preprocessing, a fast-screening / fine-recheck cascade, and a rule-based semantic gate. We characterise the framework by condition, showing where it works and where it fails. On TT100K (45 classes; 3016-image official test split), a YOLOv8n screening stage trained for 20 epochs reaches mAP@0.5 of 0.187 ± 0.005 over three seeds. Component ablations show that the full pipeline does not outperform a confidence-only cascade on clean data, and that preprocessing yields no measurable benefit in clean conditions. Cross-dataset evaluation on CCTSDB reveals monotonic degradation with sign size (recall 0.323 for XL, 0.002 for XS) and pronounced weakness at night and in rain; preprocessing improves F1 by 30% at night but is ineffective in rain and for small signs. A rule-based semantic gate modifies only 0.66% of detections and loses true positives in 29% of its changes. End-to-end latency on our hardware is 239 ms (median), dominated by CPU preprocessing, giving a single-stream capacity of 1.6 frames/s. We conclude that the cascade skeleton is implementable and that small-sign detection and preprocessing cost are the binding constraints.

Article.Title: Social status and status loss do not influence alcohol-related behaviors in rats
Article.Authors: Coppola A.; Verma A.; Augier G.; Holm L.; Augier E.; Heilig M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impoverished social conditions have been reported to shape the vulnerability to develop alcohol use disorder in humans. However, how social environments mediate their effects on addictive behaviors is not known. In this study, we established a rat model to investigate the role of social status in alcohol-related behaviors, using operant self-administration paradigms. We screened male ( n = 76) and female ( n = 88) Wistar rats for dominance-like behavior using the tube test. Then, we forced half of the “dominant” animals to lose their social status to their subordinates while leaving the remaining animals’ social status unchanged. Finally, we tested the effects of social status and social status loss on emotional behaviors, including anxiety-like behavior and social preference and on addiction-like behaviors, including motivation for alcohol self-administration and resistance to foot-shock punishment. Both male and female rats showed a stable winning phenotype in the tube test that was predicted by social preference in males but not in females. Despite finding robust sex differences, with males being more motivated to get alcohol than females and females being more resistant to punishment than males, neither social status nor social status loss affected any of the alcohol-related behaviors or emotional behaviors.

Article.Title: Real-world analysis of machine learning and Pi-model techniques for SoC prediction in urban electric buses
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Pal K.; Vishwakarma C.; Aldobali M.; Soni A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of the State of Charge (SoC) of electric vehicle (EV) batteries is important for efficient energy management, battery safety, and reliable range prediction. This is particularly challenging for urban electric buses, where battery operation varies continuously with changing driving and operating conditions. Conventional model-based methods can face difficulties in such conditions because of parameter variations and limited adaptability to real-world operation. In this study, six months of real-world operational data from PMI electric buses running on the Meerut–Sardhana route in India are used to evaluate different approaches for SoC estimation. A Battery Equivalent Circuit (BEC) Pi-model is developed and its performance is compared with six machine learning approaches: Random Forest, XG Boost, Light GBM, Support Vector Regression, Linear Regression, and a hybrid K-Means-assisted regression approach. The models are evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), coefficient of determination (R 2 ), and correlation coefficient. The results show that the Pi-model and the ensemble-based ML models provide accurate SoC estimates under real-world operating conditions. Among the methods studied, the Pi-model provides the best overall performance while also offering better physical interpretability and a closer connection to the actual battery behaviour. The study also identifies challenges related to auxiliary load estimation and the practical implementation of SoC estimation in real-time Battery Management Systems (BMS). The results demonstrate the potential of combining physics-based and data-driven methods to develop reliable SoC estimation techniques for electric bus applications.

Article.Title: Vulnerable road user involvement is associated with higher alleged injury odds in reported automated driving crashes
Article.Authors: Viktor P.; Kiss G.
Article.Abstract: Public crash reports can identify injury patterns within reported automated driving system (ADS) incidents, but cannot establish exposure-normalized safety. We analyzed the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ADS file released on 15 July 2026, covering reports received from 16 June 2025 to 15 June 2026. After version selection, incident deduplication, engagement restriction and exclusion of unknown injury outcomes, 1,148 incidents remained. Any alleged injury occurred in 116 (10.1%); 39 (3.4%) involved hospitalization or fatality. Injury was alleged in 13 of 28 incidents involving vulnerable road users (46.4%; 95% confidence interval 29.5–64.2%) and 95 of 807 involving light motor vehicles (11.8%; 9.7–14.2%). The adjusted odds ratio was 6.48 (2.96–14.18). Repeated nested cross-validation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.605 and an area under the precision recall curve (AUPRC; average precision) of 0.161, compared with a no-skill AUPRC of 0.101. Class weighting did not materially improve discrimination. These incident-level associations support further investigation of vulnerable road user scenarios, but do not identify who was injured, establish causation, quantify crash incidence or demonstrate deployment utility.

Article.Title: Characteristics of needlestick injuries and post-exposure practices among healthcare workers in private hospitals in Alexandria, Egypt
Article.Authors: El-Zoghby M.; Hammouda A.; Omran E.; Aboelsaad E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Needlestick injuries (NSIs) are a major occupational hazard among healthcare workers (HCWs), with potential exposure to blood-borne pathogens and associated health consequences. A retrospective record-based study was conducted using 318 records of HCWs who experienced NSIs during 2023–2024 in four private hospitals in Alexandria, Egypt, all with standardized NSI reporting systems. Data included demographic and occupational characteristics, injury circumstances, safety practices, hepatitis B vaccination status, infection prevention and control (IPC) training, and post-exposure management. Most NSIs occurred among female HCWs (61.6%), and nurses represented the largest affected occupational group (63.5%). Syringes were involved in 65.1% of NSIs, while sudden patient movement was the most frequently reported contributing factor (26.1%). Among records with documented IPC training status, 79.8% indicated no prior training, while training status was missing in 36.2% of records. Overall, 16.0% of HCWs were documented as unvaccinated against hepatitis B. Post-exposure actions were not documented in 30.8% of records, and only 29.6% of HCWs underwent documented post-exposure testing for hepatitis C virus, hepatitis B, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). These findings highlight gaps in IPC training, hepatitis B vaccination, and post-exposure management and underscore the need for standardized reporting, timely post-exposure care, and improved occupational safety practices.

Article.Title: Aptamer-engineered extracellular vesicles enable targeted celecoxib delivery for in vitro breast and colon cancer therapy
Article.Authors: Abd-Rabou A.; Kishta M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, largely due to limitations in current therapies that often suffer from poor selectivity, systemic toxicity, and drug resistance. Innovative drug delivery platforms that can selectively target tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue are urgently needed to improve treatment outcomes. In this study, we address these challenges by developing a novel targeted delivery system using extracellular vesicles (EVs) loaded with celecoxib (Cel), a potent anti-inflammatory drug with anticancer properties, and functionalized with DNA aptamer AS1411 (Apt) to enhance tumor targeting. Celecoxib was efficiently encapsulated into EVs derived wharton’s jelly (WJ) mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) via sonication. Subsequently, the EV surfaces were chemically conjugated with amine-modified Apt using EDC/NHS chemistry, creating a targeted nanosystem (Cel-apt-EVs) designed for enhanced recognition and uptake by cancer cells. Comprehensive in vitro analyses demonstrated that Cel-apt-EVs significantly improved cellular binding affinity and cytotoxicity in MCF-7 and HCT116 cancer cell lines compared to free celecoxib and non-functionalized EV formulations, while exhibiting minimal toxicity towards normal WI38 fibroblasts. Cell cycle analysis revealed that Cel-apt-EVs induced significant G0/G1 phase arrest in cancer cells, indicating inhibition of cell cycle progression. Furthermore, Annexin V/propidium iodide (PI)-based flow cytometry confirmed enhanced apoptotic cell death, with a marked increase in early and late apoptotic populations following Cel-apt-EVs treatment. Cel-apt-EVs effectively inhibited cancer cell migration in wound healing assays and markedly suppressed angiogenesis in the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model. These results highlight that aptamer-functionalized EVs provide a promising and biocompatible platform for precision delivery of celecoxib, improving anticancer efficacy while reducing off-target effects. This strategy offers new avenues for the development of safer and more effective targeted therapies in oncology.

Article.Title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for 28-day mortality in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding and chronic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Huang H.; Zheng J.; Yang Y.; Kou Y.; Liang M.; Huang Y.; Zhang Q.; Ye S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with disproportionately high morbidity and mortality, yet no specific risk prediction tool exists for this comorbid population. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a machine learning model for predicting 28-day all-cause mortality in GIB patients with coexisting CKD. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-IV (v3.1) database, identifying 926 adult patients with concurrent GIB and CKD. The cohort was randomly split into a training set ( n = 648) and an internal validation set ( n = 278). An independent cohort of 1,000 patients from the Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University(GDMUAH) served as external validation. Forty-five clinical variables were extracted, covering demographics, comorbidities, vital signs, laboratory tests, medications, and interventions. Feature selection was performed using LASSO regression and Boruta algorithm. Six ML algorithms—XGBoost, CatBoost, AdaBoost, LightGBM, Logistic Regression (LR), and Random Forest (RF)—were trained and tuned via grid search with 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by discrimination (AUROC), calibration (Brier score), and decision curve analysis (DCA). The best-performing model was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Eight overlapping predictors were selected: red cell distribution width (RDW), serum chloride, anion gap, prothrombin time (PT), partial thromboplastin time (PTT), Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP), sepsis and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). In internal Test, LR achieved the highest AUROC 0.734 (95% CI 0.666–0.802) and the most balanced performance (Sensitivity 70.3% (95% CI 0.547–0.891), Specificity 69.2% (95% CI 0.505–0.832),Brier 0.160 (95% CI 0.145–0.178)). External validation of the LR model yielded an AUROC of 0.732 (95% CI 0.689–0.774), accuracy 0.773 (95% CI 0.746–0.799), sensitivity 0.455 (95% CI 0.382–0.531), specificity 0.840 (95% CI 0.819–0.869) and a negative predictive value of 0.88. Calibration and DCA confirmed good agreement and net clinical benefit across a wide threshold range. SHAP analysis identified anion gap, SBP, PTT, and sepsis as the most influential contributors to mortality risk. The LR model showed acceptable discrimination and calibration for early risk stratification of 28-day mortality in GIB patients with CKD; its low external sensitivity and modest PPV indicate that it should be considered a preliminary decision-support tool requiring prospective multicenter validation.

Article.Title: Fatty acid characteristics of high-fat diet-induced tumor tissue in the liver of mice
Article.Authors: Iwasaki M.; Horii N.; Mori A.; Takahashi T.; Umezawa M.; Kamiya T.; Ohtani N.; Soga K.
Article.Abstract: Recent studies have highlighted the potential involvement of hepatic lipid characteristics in the development of liver cancer. Using a non‑invasive approach that integrates near‑infrared hyperspectral imaging (HSI) with machine learning, we previously established a method to visualize total lipid concentration, saturation level, and hydrocarbon chain length of fatty acids within a three‑dimensional feature space in mouse liver tissue. In the present study, to further elucidate the mechanisms underlying tumorigenesis, we expanded our dataset by adding eight additional tumor‑bearing mouse samples and separately analyzed cancerous and non‑cancerous regions within each hepatic lobe. Both gas chromatography and HSI consistently demonstrated that cancerous tissues exhibited elevated total lipid concentrations and were characterized by a notably higher abundance of oleic acid.

Article.Title: Prediction of the self-association of the nuclear inhibitor of DNA-binding and differentiation proteins
Article.Authors: Ahmed Y.; Mo’men S.; Ali E.; Shaker H.; Sayed S.; Elbendary N.; Hassan R.; Elfiky A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The inhibitor of DNA binding and differentiation (ID) proteins (ID1–ID4) are members of the helix-loop-helix (HLH) family of transcriptional regulators that play a critical role in regulating cell cycle progression and cell differentiation. Their overexpression in various cancer types makes them promising therapeutic targets. It has been reported that ID4 acts as a tumor suppressor, as ID4 heterodimerizes with ID-1, -2, and -3 and promotes bHLH DNA binding, essentially acting as an inhibitor of inhibitors of differentiation proteins. In this work, we utilize advanced computational biophysics and bioinformatics tools to map the structural foundations of ID protein self-association. High-resolution models were generated and subjected to 100 ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations to capture their conformational dynamics in physiological environments. Through protein–protein docking (HADDOCK) and interface analysis, aiming to characterize the binding hotspots of both homodimers and heterodimers, facilitating the development of inhibitors that can disrupt its pathological interactions. Results revealed that ID1 can self-dimerize and form a stable dimer with ID4. The dimerization is exerted by the HLH domain, and the dimers are stable compared to the monomeric isoforms. The ID1-ID4 dimer formation has an important role in lowering their concentration in the nucleus and hence affecting their function. Hence, the identified interaction pattern may have important implications for regulating their activity.

Article.Title: Long term survival after mesometrial resection for cervical cancer from the Mesometrial Resection (MMR) Study
Article.Authors: Weydandt L.; Wolf B.; Dornhöfer N.; Hering K.; Martin M.; Höckel M.; Aktas B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Leipzig School Mesometrial Resection Study (MMR Study) investigates whether surgical treatment based on stage-associated ontogenetic cancer fields and their corresponding lymphatic compartments can achieve durable locoregional tumor control without adjuvant radiotherapy. This ongoing, prospective, single-center observational cohort study enrolls patients with primary cervical cancer. Depending on ontogenetic tumor stage, patients undergo total mesometrial resection (TMMR) or extended mesometrial resection (EMMR) with therapeutic lymph node dissection. As all locoregional at-risk tissues are surgically removed, adjuvant radiotherapy is omitted. This long-term follow-up analysis included patients FIGO 2009 stages IB1–IIB. Between 1999 and 2020, 543 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 104 months. Disease stages were IB1 (60%), IB2 (11%), IIA1 (4.4%), IIA2 (1.7%), and IIB (23%). Nodal status was pN0 in 72.4% and pN1 in 27.6%. Ten-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were 84.0% and 84.1%, respectively. Stratified by nodal status, 10-year RFS was 92.6% for pN0 and 60.8% for pN1, while OS was 90.9% and 65.6%, respectively. Multivariable Cox regression showed favorable prognostic stratification for ontogenetic tumor staging compared with conventional pT staging (AIC 928.78 vs. 939.23). TMMR or EMMR with therapeutic lymph node dissection was associated with favorable long-term oncologic outcomes in this cohort. Ontogenetic tumor staging may improve prognostic assessment in cervical cancer.

Article.Title: Coal mine drill pipe detection algorithm integrating large-kernel separation and coordinate locking mechanisms
Article.Authors: Xiao C.; Jiang Z.; Wang C.; Yang J.; Zheng S.; Li Y.; Chen D.; Xie S.
Article.Abstract: Underground coal mine operating scenes feature complex working conditions such as significant dynamic variations, frequent target occlusions, intense exposure interference, localized low illumination, and high concentrations of pervasive dust. Conventional object detection models tend to suffer from severe overfitting, leading to a substantial degradation in generalization performance for detecting slender drill pipes. To overcome the deficiencies of conventional models, this paper proposes a drill pipe detection algorithm based on the lightweight YOLO11n network, integrating large-kernel separation and coordinate locking mechanisms. At the end of the backbone network, Large Separable Kernel Attention (LSKA) and Coordinate Attention (CA) are integrated to construct the LSCA feature enhancement module; this module uses large-kernel convolutions to connect fractured features and alleviate frequent occlusions, and employs orthogonal pooling to precisely lock onto the physical edges of drill pipes against intense light, darkness, and dust interference. At the detection head, an interpolation-based flexible regression loss (InterpIoU) is introduced to reconstruct the bounding box localization mechanism; by establishing a transitional interpolation buffer, it suppresses gradient oscillations caused by extreme aspect ratios and effectively reduces the short-edge divergence sensitivity in slender drill pipe regression. At the validation stage, a validation set is constructed based on an Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) strategy with physical isolation in time and space. Experimental results demonstrate that: (1) The improved model exhibits superior generalization at unknown operating sites, where mAP@50 increases by 2.0% over the baseline (reaching 88.7%) and mAP@50-95 increases by 2.2% (reaching 43.7%); (2) The improved model demonstrates stronger anti-interference capability under complex conditions, with the miss rate reduced by 1.4% over the baseline (to 18.3%) and the recall increased by 1.4% (to 81.7%); (3) The improved model maintains lightweight characteristics, with parameters reduced by 0.029 M relative to the baseline (reaching 2.561 M) while maintaining high real-time inference speed (reaching 1303.8 fps); (4) When coupled with the ByteTrack tracker at the back end, the counting accuracy on five challenging video cases is improved by 9.1 percentage points over the baseline.

Article.Title: Matrix-based computational photonics with applications in beam propagation and Mach–Zehnder interferometric design
Article.Authors: Naik S.; Hamdani M.; Pradhan A.; Singh G.; khursheed S.; Chhipa M.
Article.Abstract: Computational photonics demands efficient numerical techniques to handle high-dimensional field evolution with strong coupling. This work presents a hierarchical matrix-pairing framework for N-dimensional numerical integration, combined with a branching-matrix coarse-to-fine optimization strategy, applied to beam propagation method (BPM) simulations of tapered waveguides and Mach–Zehnder interferometer (MZI) design. In BPM simulations, replacing element-wise Python loops with vectorized NumPy array operations for the transverse-plane power and mode-overlap integrals yields a per-simulation analysis-stage speedup of approximately 91 × on a 128 × 128 grid with 50 propagation steps (Python 3.11/NumPy 1.26/Intel Core i7-12700H CPU). This speedup is specific to the pure-Python execution environment; JIT-compiled or compiled-language baselines would reduce the relative gain. Both implementations apply the same trapezoidal quadrature rule to identical discrete field arrays and agree to within 2.5 × 10⁻ 13 in the power and overlap integrals; these values represent mutual agreement between the two implementations and are not errors relative to an independent reference or ground truth. In MZI optimization, the branching-matrix coarse-to-fine search recovers the target differential arm length ΔL in under 60 iterations for the single test case demonstrated; a systematic comparison with gradient-based and derivative-free optimizers shows that its advantage lies in global-search reliability on a multimodal cost surface rather than in speed. These results demonstrate that vectorized integration provides a computationally efficient alternative to loop-based integration in Python-based BPM workflows, with performance gains that are environment- and grid-size-specific.

Article.Title: A hybrid neural deep belief networks-gated recurrent unit algorithm with a leakage-aware evaluation protocol for ECG-HRV-based cognitive load classification
Article.Authors: Keikhosrokiani P.; Wang N.; Shi J.; Liu W.; Fadilah S.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive underload and overload can impair knowledge workers’ performance. Electrocardiogram-derived heart rate variability (HRV) offers a practical signal for assessing cognitive demand. However, sample-wise evaluation may reward participant recognition rather than cognitive-state classification. This study proposes and evaluates a hybrid deep belief network–gated recurrent unit (DBN–GRU) algorithm on WESAD and SWELL. The model combines restricted Boltzmann machine pre-training with a gated classifier head. The primary WESAD evaluations use participant-disjoint protocols and validation-based model selection. Under leave-one-subject-out validation, the model achieves 68.4% accuracy, 62.8% balanced accuracy and 0.614 macro-F1. A majority-class predictor achieves 52.8% accuracy and 0.230 macro-F1. Participant-relative features improve performance for 13 of 15 participants ( p = 0.0015), whereas adversarial suppression of participant identity does not improve classification. Participant-relative features require unlabelled calibration data from each new participant. None of the eight alternative architectures differs significantly from the proposed model. Zero-shot cross-dataset transfer falls below the target majority-class baseline in both directions. Fine-tuning underperforms direct training on the target dataset. These results indicate a larger effect of participant-relative features than of architectural choice under the evaluated conditions as a quality assurance metrics.

Article.Title: CAD-YOLO11: a lightweight class-aware dynamic optimization framework for pipeline defect detection
Article.Authors: Dang H.; Ge J.; Meng H.; Zhang Y.; Zhou J.; Jin J.; Xian Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pipeline defect detection is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of industrial infrastructure. However, lightweight object detectors often suffer from insufficient feature representation and category-specific optimization capability when dealing with small-scale defects, weak textures, and visually similar defect categories. This paper proposes CAD-YOLO11, a lightweight class-aware dynamic optimization framework based on YOLO11 for accurate and efficient pipeline defect detection. The framework incorporates an adaptive downsampling strategy to improve fine-grained feature preservation during feature compression, while introducing a DetectAux_ClsEnhance branch to provide additional category-level supervision for enhancing semantic discrimination. Furthermore, a Class-aware Weighted Dynamic Optimization (CWDO) strategy is developed, including Class-Aware Dynamic Top-k Assignment (CADT) and Class-Aware Coordinate Optimization (CA-CN), to achieve category-adaptive positive sample selection and bounding box optimization according to different defect characteristics.Experiments conducted on the Daji pipeline defect dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of CAD-YOLO11. Compared with the original YOLO11n, the proposed method improves mAP50 from 88.64% to 91.13% and mAP50-95 from 66.52% to 69.90%, while reducing computational complexity from 6.3 GFLOPs to 5.3 GFLOPs. The proposed framework achieves a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency, providing an effective solution for real-time industrial pipeline defect inspection.

Article.Title: An interpretable machine learning model for predicting 28-day in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with sepsis and atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Sun F.; Xu C.; Gao J.; Zhang J.; Xiao M.; Shi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early prediction of prognosis is critical for optimizing care in intensive care unit (ICU) sepsis patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study aims to develop explainable machine learning (ML) models to predict 28-day in-hospital mortality risk for sepsis patients with AF. Data from sepsis patients with AF were extracted from three datasets: the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV database, the MIMIC-III database, and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU). The study endpoint was 28-day in-hospital mortality following ICU admission. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Boruta and recursive feature elimination (RFE). We developed eight distinct ML models and evaluated their performance comprehensively using various metrics. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to interpret the optimal predictive model. A total of 11,740 sepsis patients with AF were included in this study, with 8,374 from the MIMIC-IV database, 1,669 from the MIMIC-III database, and 1,697 from the eICU database. 18 variables were selected to construct prediction models. The Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) model demonstrated robust predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) and 95% confidence interval (CI) of 0.770 (0.749–0.790) in the internal validation set, 0.781 (0.756–0.807) in the MIMIC-III cohort, and 0.721 (0.691–0.750) in the eICU cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that respiratory failure, urine output, and RDW score were the three most important features for predicting 28-day in-hospital mortality risk in sepsis patients with AF. The simplified model containing only 12 features demonstrated comparable performance, achieving an AUC of 0.756 (0.735–0.777) in the internal validation set, 0.776 (0.750–0.802) in the MIMIC-III cohort, and 0.715 (0.685–0.745) in the eICU cohort. The final streamlined model was deployed on a dedicated website ( https://ml-model.shinyapps.io/gbmapp/ ) to assist physicians in clinical decision-making and timely intervention.

Article.Title: ZeroSEC: hybrid optimized stacked deep learning framework for zero-day anomaly intrusion detection for host system
Article.Authors: Singh M.; Patra J.; Choubey S.; Choubey A.; Shukla P.; Mallick S.; Shingne H.
Article.Abstract: Unseen attacks are still a challenge for the day-to-day users of computers. To guard our digital assets from zero-day attacks is almost impossible due to their unknown pattern of attack. To solve this problem, a more effective approach has been developed to identify and categorize them. A novel integrated framework developed by combining an optimized feature pipeline, an enhanced autoencoder, and a deep learning stacking ensemble to detect and categorize zero-day. The Adam optimizer and Keras tuner were used to optimize the autoencoder. A novel exploration–exploitation-diversification (EED) hybrid optimization method based on spider monkey optimization (SMO) and particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been used to optimize the entire stacking ensemble model. The gated recurrent unit (GRU) as a meta classifier, long short-term memory (LSTM), and a bi-directional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU), which is the base classifier for this deep learning zero-day stacking ensemble classifier (ZeroSEC). The combined approach ZeroSEC evaluated on two of the latest datasets. On the UNSW ToN IoT 2020 dataset, the model produced the best results, achieving a 99.35% recall with a 0.64% false negative rate and an overall accuracy of 99.74% and 0.05% false alarm. The statistical results show the suggested model outperforms earlier research.

Article.Title: AutoSNAP enables automated nerve segmentation and morphometry quantification
Article.Authors: Chakladar S.; Lee O.; Hunter D.; Boukind A.; Dy C.; Brogan D.
Article.Abstract: Accurate morphometric analysis is essential to studying nerve development, injury, and regeneration, but current approaches are inefficient, inconsistent, or inaccessible. Here, we present AutoSNAP, a deep learning framework for automated nerve morphometry assessment. AutoSNAP employs a custom convolutional neural network trained on both injured and non-injured murine nerve cross sections. Segmentation performance is enhanced by the incorporation of confidence-weighted patch restitching and geometry-informed separation algorithms, both tailored specifically to nerve morphology. When compared to manual annotation, AutoSNAP demonstrated pixel-wise segmentation accuracy of 98.6% for myelin sheaths and 96.7% for axons. AutoSNAP also provides a comprehensive set of fiber-, axon-, and myelin-level morphometric characteristics. These metrics showed strong agreement with manually obtained metrics, as evidenced by inter-class correlation coefficients and Pearson correlation coefficients > 0.9 for almost all metrics. The complete pipeline is deployed as a publicly accessible web application available at https://autosnap-7cia.onrender.com/ .

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of face mask: from textile filtration determination to air leakage minimization
Article.Authors: Orjuela-Garzón I.; Fernández-Calderón I.; González-Carvajal L.; Pérez-Cualtán C.; Rojas-Neisa D.; Moreno Á.; Castro-Paez C.; Suárez D.; Morales-Betancourt R.; Varon-Vega F.; Navarro J.; Briceño J.
Article.Abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic emphasized the critical role of face masks in preventing the transmission of respiratory viruses, especially in medical settings. Respiratory viruses, including SARS, influenza, and adenoviruses are primarily transmitted through the respiratory pathways, making face masks the primary barrier for protection. This study aims to evaluate and compare the filtration efficiency and pressure differentials of different face masks to contribute to the development of a comprehensive test bench for medical textiles. Unlike prior fit-testing approaches that assess mask fit only as a wearing condition, this study introduces a test bench that independently quantifies nasal and oral air leakage under controlled sealing configurations, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating custom sealing accessories. The design of a sealing device is also evaluated to assess the effectiveness of a physical external sealer. The study focuses on designing and evaluating accessory seals for face masks to determine air loss percentages in areas where the mask is not in complete contact with the face. The creation of a test bench for textiles in medical use is intended to contribute valuable insights into mask performance, addressing both filtration efficiency and pressure differentials. The study evaluates different face masks including N95, surgical, and newly developed fabrics. Results revealed that N95 masks consistently demonstrate superior filtration efficiency and acceptable pressure differentials across specific flow rates. Thus, understanding face mask efficacies is crucial for optimizing mask designs, contributing to the advancement of protective measures against respiratory diseases.

Article.Title: Advanced optimization of drug solubility through statistical analysis using machine learning
Article.Authors: Obaidullah A.; Alhowyan A.; Mahdi W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predictive modeling of scientific systems is often difficult due to limited data, impaired bias due to shifts in the data, and commonly applied techniques used to model data for generalized solutions. A proof of concept for the aforementioned problem is provided by utilizing a new approach to data analysis and modeling development that results in more accurate solubility predictions from a physics-constrained, hybrid machine learning (ML) and statistical modeling method with added value of embedded constraints into a well-defined, flexible model. A quantitative evaluation of the methodology discussed will be conducted via interpolation, extrapolation, and noise scenarios using realistic datasets to evaluate the performance of the framework. Traditional modeling methods have provided accurate predictions but exhibited unstable and non-physical behaviors during the extrapolation and interpolation process. In contrast, the proposed approach is able to predict solubility accurately, maintain a physical relationship between pressure and solubility, and produce more accurate and robust predictions while prioritizing predictive utility instead of statistical accuracy. A predefined λ weighting factor will adjust the extent to which the methodology incorporates data-driven methodology versus physics-based guided solutions into the models.

Article.Title: Explainable AI-based disease diagnostics using real-time plasmonic biosensor data and blockchain technology
Article.Authors: Indupalli M.; Gera P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a secure and decentralized framework for biomedical diagnostics using plasmonic biosensor data by integrating federated learning, blockchain, post-quantum cryptography, meta-learning, and explainable AI (XAI). The proposed system addresses key limitations of centralized healthcare models, including data privacy risks, vulnerability to cyberattacks, and lack of transparency. A federated meta-learning approach is employed to improve model adaptability and accuracy across heterogeneous institutional datasets, while blockchain ensures secure data sharing, auditability, and resistance to model poisoning attacks. Additionally, a post-quantum cryptographic layer is incorporated to enhance long-term data security against emerging quantum threats. Experimental results demonstrate improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced security, and scalable performance with acceptable latency overhead. The findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed framework in enabling secure, collaborative, and trustworthy AI-driven healthcare systems.

Article.Title: CLNA: controllable latent space of non-prompt attributes for enhancing diversity in text-to-image synthesis
Article.Authors: Park K.; Chae J.; Kweon J.; Ahn J.
Article.Abstract: Text-to-image synthesis in medicine remains challenging because clinically relevant visual attributes are often not fully specified by text prompts, which can limit the controllability and diversity of generated images. We propose Controllable Latent Space of Non-Prompt Attributes (CLNA), a framework that models non-prompt visual attributes within a continuous latent space for diagnosis-conditioned image synthesis, implemented with a style encoder and dual cross-attention within a Stable Diffusion backbone. We evaluated CLNA on otoendoscopic image synthesis for three diagnostic classes: normal tympanic membrane, otitis media with effusion, and chronic otitis media. Compared with the baseline Stable Diffusion model, CLNA improved image fidelity in the domain-adapted feature space, reducing Fréchet Inception Distance from 52.91 to 10.11 against the held-out internal test set, and improved feature-space recall from 57.67% to 90.22%. In classification experiments, replacing 10–40% of the real training data with CLNA-generated images at $$\:\gamma\:=0.5$$ gave F1 scores of 93.57–94.08% on the internal test set (vs. 94.46% averaged across 10 real-only runs) and 84.81–85.30% on the external test set (vs. 83.76% from a single real-only run). With complete replacement of the training data by generated images, CLNA outperformed the baseline model on both the internal test set (78.53% vs. 70.25%) and the external test set (72.37% vs. 54.26%). When the synthetic-only training set was increased 10-fold, CLNA further improved F1 scores to 83.21% on the internal test set and 76.77% on the external test set. These findings suggest that CLNA can control the magnitude of sampled latent variation through a style parameter, thereby improving diversity in otoendoscopic text-to-image synthesis. CLNA-generated images could support downstream classifier training under reduced use of real images.

Article.Title: Extreme temperature exposure and incident chronic lung disease among middle-aged and older adults in china: a longitudinal cohort study
Article.Authors: Mi F.; Qi X.; Zhang N.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: To examine the associations of cold spell and heat wave exposure across varying intensities and durations with incident chronic lung disease among middle-aged and older adults in China. This prospective cohort study used data from five waves (2011–2020) of CHARLS (N = 9,458). Fifty exposure metrics were constructed by crossing temperature percentile thresholds (cold spells: P2.5–P10; heat waves: P85–P97.5) with duration windows (≥ 1 to ≥ 5 days). Associations were analyzed using GLMMs with BH-FDR correction, restricted cubic spline models, subgroup analyses, and comprehensive sensitivity analyses including Cox, Fine-Gray competing risk models, and fixed exposure window validation. Over a median 7.0-year follow-up, 1,562 cases occurred (incidence: 16.51%). All 50 metrics were significantly associated with increased risk (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.01). At ≥ 5 days, P10 cold spells (OR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.27–1.42) and P85 heat waves (OR = 1.32, 1.25–1.40) exceeded more extreme counterparts (P2.5: 1.13, 1.07–1.20; P97.5: 1.20, 1.13–1.27). Cold spells exhibited nonlinear exposure–response patterns (P5: P-non-linearity < 0.001), while heat waves showed linear patterns (P90–P97.5: all P-non-linearity > 0.50). Residence was the only effect modifier identified in the reported FDR-adjusted interaction results for cold spells (adjusted P-interaction = 0.042). Cox (HR = 1.28, 1.22–1.35) and Fine-Gray (sHR = 1.26, 1.20–1.33) models yielded directionally consistent associations. Both cold spells and heat waves were associated with increased chronic lung disease incidence. Frequent moderate events may impose a greater cumulative burden than rare extreme events, while the association with cold spells was stronger among rural residents. These findings highlight the need for climate-health assessments and adaptation strategies to address cumulative exposure and population-specific differences.

Article.Title: Hybrid nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization of artificial neural networks for mustard leaf health classification
Article.Authors: Sharma A.; Sharma C.; Tripathi S.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent and effective agricultural methods that reduce crop losses and enhance yield quality are necessary to meet the growing need for food production worldwide. The production of mustard, a crucial oilseed crop, is greatly impacted by a number of bacterial, viral, and fungal diseases. There is an obvious need for automated and trustworthy health detection techniques because manual disease diagnosis is laborious, inconsistent, and highly dependent on the availability of experts. In this regard, the current study suggests employing image analysis to perform binary mustard leaf health classification by distinguishing healthy and unhealthy leaves using a Hybrid Yellow Saddle Goatfish–Jellyfish Search Optimizer Artificial Neural Network (HY-JANN). In addition, the proposed HY-JANN approach integrates Otsu-based image segmentation and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM)-based texture feature extraction with a hybrid nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization strategy to effectively optimize ANN weights and enhance classification accuracy. The hybrid optimization mechanism improves convergence behavior and mitigates premature stagnation commonly observed in conventional training methods. Comparative analysis against conventional machine learning classifiers (DT, J48, RF, SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression), ensemble methods, and standalone ANN demonstrates that the proposed HY-JANN consistently achieves superior performance across all evaluation metrics giving an Accuracy of 91.878%, Precision of 90.563%, Recall of 91.562%, F-score of 91.021% and Specificity of 91.349%. The results validate the model’s effective convergence and promising classification performance on the evaluated dataset. However, further validation using independent field datasets and computational-time analysis is required before real-time deployment can be established.

Article.Title: At-home colorectal cancer screening participation, persistency, and connection to follow-up care: insights from a large multi-state system
Article.Authors: Gronowski B.; Jones K.; Vartanian K.; Roth S.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common sources of cancer incidence and mortality in the United States. Early detection is crucial for positive outcomes, but screening rates persistently fall short of public health goals. Low-barrier screening options like fecal immunochemical tests (FITs) have the potential to increase screening and reduce disparities across demographic groups, but they require annual testing and follow-up for abnormal results. The study used a retrospective, observational design to assess screening patterns for three types of FIT participation (i.e., initial, continued, and connection to follow-up care) in a multi-state health system. All age-eligible adult patients mailed a FIT from January 2019 to March 2025 were included ( n = 158,128). The main measure for initial and continued participation was FIT return; the main measure for follow-up participation was having a colonoscopy within 12 months of receiving an abnormal FIT result. The majority (59%) of patients who received a FIT participated, and 73% of eligible patients participated in a second test. Among those with abnormal results, 59% had follow-up testing within a year. Initial, continued, and follow-up screening rates varied by race/ethnicity, language, payor, and geography. Findings highlight the potential benefits of low-barrier CRC screening like FIT for certain groups, as well as opportunities to engage all eligible patients across the CRC screening paradigm.

Article.Title: PWTSI-Net: a progressive wavelet-refined and transformer-enhanced semantic interaction framework for infrared and visible image fusion
Article.Authors: Priya B.; Suryanarayana G.
Article.Abstract: Infrared (IR) and visible (VIS) image fusion focuses on merging complementary thermal and structural information into a single informative fused image. IR images effectively highlight salient thermal targets, whereas VIS images preserve abundant texture and structural information. However, existing fusion methods often suffer from insufficient frequency representation, loss of fine details, and limited semantic understanding. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PWTSI-Net, a novel framework for IR and VIS image fusion. The framework integrates frequency-aware feature enhancement and semantic-guided contextual refinement within a unified encoder–decoder architecture. Initially, a coarse fused representation is generated from the source modalities and progressively refined using the proposed adaptive wavelet attention refinement block (AWARB). The AWARB consists of an adaptive wavelet enhancement block (AWEB) for multi-frequency feature enhancement and an attention-guided feature refinement block (AGFRB) for adaptive feature recalibration. Furthermore, a context aware transformer fusion module (CATFM) is introduced to enhance semantic representation by incorporating segmentation-guided semantic priors, modelling long-range feature dependencies through transformer-based attention, and adaptively regulating feature interactions via gating mechanisms. Experimental results demonstrate that PWTSI-Net effectively preserves thermal targets, structural details, and texture information while producing visually consistent and information-rich fused images with improved contrast and semantic consistency.

Article.Title: Channel spatial semantic attention and grouped dilated fusion for real-time steel surface defect detection
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Wang B.; Chen X.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Reliable detection of steel surface defects is essential for ensuring product quality and production safety. However, existing detectors struggle to jointly handle complex-background interference, weak responses to small targets, and spatial information loss under lightweight downsampling. We propose Steel-CGA, a YOLO26s-based detector that addresses these challenges for steel surface defect recognition. Steel-CGA integrates three complementary components: (1) a Channel-Spatial-Semantic Attention Module (CSSAM) appended to the backbone, which reorganizes channel, spatial, and semantic attention as three parallel branches-departing from the sequential pipeline of SE and CBAM-and couples them through residual multiplication, to suppress complex-background interference; (2) a Grouped Dilated Residual Fusion (GDRF) module redesigned from the dilation-wise residual idea of DWRSeg with an asymmetric squeeze-and-dilate channel allocation and SiLU activations, embedded in the C3k2 blocks of the neck, which enlarges the receptive field to enrich multi-scale context and strengthen responses to small defects; and (3) an Adaptive Downsampling (ADown) module adopted directly from YOLOv9, which replaces the conventional downsampling layers in the backbone, reducing spatial information loss while preserving inference efficiency. On NEU-DET and GC10-DET, Steel-CGA achieves 76.6% and 62.0% mAP@50, outperforming YOLO26s by 3.5 and 3.6 points, while reducing parameters by 26.0% and FLOPs by 23.7% and running at 134 FPS.
Article.Topic: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Optimized selenium and cysteine concentrations for improving CO2-to-CH4 conversion by hyperthermophilic methanogens
Article.Authors: Calegari R.; Schutgens M.; Ottosen L.; Kofoed M.
Article.Abstract: The growing need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions has driven interest in CO₂-based fuels as sustainable energy solutions. Biological CO₂ biomethanation represents a promising approach for converting CO₂ and H₂ into renewable methane, supporting carbon recycling and energy storage. Hyperthermophilic methanogens represent potential microbial catalysts for high temperature biomethanation; however, knowledge on factors influencing their growth and longevity remains scarce. Here, selenium and L-cysteine supplementation were systematically evaluated in Methanocaldococcus lauensis , Methanocaldococcus bathoardescens , Methanocaldococcus jannaschii , Methanotorris igneus , and Methanothermus fervidus across 0.46 nM–61.8 µM Se and 0.69–11.35 mM L-cysteine. Significant response-surface models were obtained for four species, with model-selected supplementation conditions of 330–452 nM added Se and 1.00–2.49 mM added L-cysteine and predicted increases in maximum methane production rate (Rm) of 51–131% relative to DSMZ supplementation levels. Experimental validation confirmed significant R m increases of 33.9% for M. bathoardescens and 19.3% for M. jannaschii , accompanied by faster growth. M. jannaschii also showed higher total methane production and sustained methanogenic activity for one additional H 2 /CO 2 headspace cycle. The contrasting responses of M. fervidus (Methanobacteriales) and the Methanococcales species were consistent with evolutionary differences in selenium utilization among methanogenic lineages. The species-dependent supplementation responses identified here provide quantitative targets for improving high-temperature CO 2 -to-CH 4 conversion.

Article.Title: Extreme value combination prediction of summer–autumn drought–flood abrupt alternation in the upper Hanjiang River based on multiple machine learning ensembles
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Chen Y.; Ma Y.; Qiu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Summer-autumn drought–flood abrupt alternation (DFAA) event in the upper Hanjiang River significantly impacts regional water resources regulation and flood control safety. This study aims to improve seasonal prediction of the summer-autumn modified standardized drought-flood abrupt alternation index (MSDFAI). Key influencing factors were identified using the maximal information coefficient. Three machine learning models-random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and long short-term memory (LSTM))-were optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO) and evaluated via expanding window cross-validation. Nine ensemble members were constructed by combining three models and three factor schemes. To mitigate the systematic underestimation of extreme values in ensemble predictions, an extreme-value combination strategy was proposed to improve prediction performance. Results show that the extreme-value combination achieves a test-period NSE of 0.62 and RMSE of 0.17, outperforming the ensemble mean (NSE 0.56, RMSE 0.18), Bayesian model averaging (NSE 0.36, RMSE 0.22), best single member (NSE 0.48, RMSE 0.20), quantile regression (NSE 0.33, RMSE 0.23), and stacking (NSE 0.12, RMSE 0.256), with particularly pronounced improvements particularly in extreme years. This study provides an effective technical approach for seasonal DFAA prediction in the upper Hanjiang River.

Article.Title: AI features and social influence affect Gen Z purchase intention and behavior through trust in an extended SOR model
Article.Authors: Ma L.; Zheng S.
Article.Abstract: Driven by digital transformation in the global retail sector, this study investigates the psychological and behavioral mechanisms underlying Generation Z college students’ AI-assisted shopping experiences. It examines how four stimuli—AI algorithm transparency, user-friendliness, internet word of mouth (IWOM), and trust propensity—influence consumer trust and purchase intention, alongside the moderating effects of privacy concern and information collection behavior. Drawing on an extended Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, the research empirically validates the proposed framework using 979 valid online survey responses analyzed via SPSS 32. Results reveal that the four antecedents exert significantly positive effects on both consumer trust and purchase intention, with trust serving as a significant mediator between these antecedents and purchase intention. Additionally, information collection behavior positively moderates the relationship between IWOM and consumer trust, while privacy concern negatively moderates the relationship between AI algorithm transparency and consumer trust. This study offers novel theoretical insights into Gen Z’s AI shopping behaviors and provides practical implications: retailers should enhance AI algorithm transparency, optimize user interfaces, cultivate positive IWOM, and strengthen privacy protection to foster Gen Z’s trust and facilitate purchase conversion.

Article.Title: Genotype specific polyphenism in pea aphids is associated with reproductive trade-offs, distinct gene expression patterns and limited DNA methylation differences
Article.Authors: Yim Z.; Murgatroyd C.; Hager R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polyphenism occurs when a single genotype produces multiple discrete phenotypes in response to environmental cues and is widespread across many animal taxa. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying polyphenic development and the associated life-history trade-offs remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that environmentally induced changes in DNA methylation are associated with altered expression of genes involved in polyphenic development. Using two different pea aphid ( Acyrthosiphon pisum ) lineages that differ in their life history and polyphenic response to crowding, we found that the two genotypes showed divergent phenotypic responses to crowding: N127 produced a high proportion of pale morphs, whereas N116 preferentially produced winged morphs. Crowding-induced morphs also produced fewer offspring than their corresponding non-crowding induced morphs. Furthermore, the F 1 offspring produced by these morphs (N116 winged and N127 pale), also produced fewer offspring than the F 1 offspring produced by the corresponding non-crowding induced morphs (N116 wingless and N127 red). We further examined the expression and DNA methylation of 14 candidate genes associated with stress responses and polyphenic development. While 12 genes were differentially expressed between morphs in at least one genotype, only four genes ( Dmap1 , Rpd3 , Hsp83 and Mad) also showed significant differences in DNA methylation. These findings suggest that the different polyphenic responses of the two genotypes are associated with distinct patterns of candidate gene expression, whereas DNA methylation differences were comparatively limited and were not consistently associated with differences in gene expression.

Article.Title: Heritage-aware visual representation learning with layout and motif relation modeling for Nanjing Yun brocade image classification
Article.Authors: Liu W.; Shi W.; Chen C.; Liu K.; Zou C.; Hou S.; Song Y.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent classification of Yun brocade images is of great significance for the digital organization of traditional brocade resources, the preservation of intangible cultural heritage, and intelligent analysis of cultural images. To address the challenges of complex motif structures, subtle category differences, and the difficulty of jointly modeling global layout and local motif relationships in Yun brocade images, this paper constructs a Yun brocade image classification method that integrates layout priors and motif relation modeling. The proposed method adopts the visual Transformer as the basic framework, designs the Brocade Layout Weaver (BLW) module to model Yun brocade craft layouts such as central regions, boundary regions, corner regions, and warp-weft structures, and further designs the Motif Structure Relation Composer (MSRC) module to enhance the model’s representation ability for repeated motifs, symmetric structures, and local compositional relationships through motif anchor extraction and spatial structural relation modeling. This paper constructs a self-built Yun brocade image dataset containing three sub-datasets for temporal classification, variety classification, and motif classification, and conducts comparative verification with multiple mainstream visual models. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an Accuracy of \(91.72\%\) , an F1-Score of \(91.20\%\) , and an AUC of \(98.64\%\) on the temporal classification sub-dataset; an Accuracy of \(81.38\%\) , an F1-Score of \(73.03\%\) , and an AUC of \(94.12\%\) on the variety classification sub-dataset; and an Accuracy of \(91.01\%\) , an F1-Score of \(93.64\%\) , and an AUC of \(97.98\%\) on the motif classification sub-dataset, all outperforming the comparison models. Ablation experiments further demonstrate that BLW and MSRC can respectively enhance the model’s representation ability for the global craft layout and local motif structural relationships of Yun brocade, and their joint use can form more discriminative visual representations of Yun brocade images.

Article.Title: Comparing the effects of HIIT and MICT on body composition, cardiometabolic health, and gut microbiota in prediabetes: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Liang Y.; Wu L.; Zheng Y.; Ye J.; Ni X.; Chen L.; Zhuang X.; Hu Q.; Yin L.
Article.Abstract: The study aimed to compare the effects of a 12-week, high-intensity interval training (HIIT) versus moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) on body composition, glucose and lipid metabolism, and cardiopulmonary function in adults with prediabetes, and to explore gut microbiota composition as an exploratory outcome and its associations with these exercise-induced changes. Sixty-four participants with prediabetes were randomly allocated to a 12-week (three times weekly) program in either a HIIT group (10 × 1-min intervals at 75–90% HR peak interspersed with 10 × 1-min at 45–60% HR peak recovery) or an MICT group (30-min at 55–70% HR peak ). This trial assessed changes in body composition, glycolipid metabolism, cardiopulmonary function, and gut microbiota composition. Gut microbiota composition was assessed using 16 S rRNA gene sequencing, and dietary education was provided throughout the study period. The study was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300072936) on June 28, 2023. Following the intervention, compared with the MICT group, the HIIT group exhibited significant reductions in fat mass ( P = 0.046), body fat percentage ( P = 0.045), estimated visceral adipose content ( P = 0.044) and estimated subcutaneous fat content ( P = 0.047). Both the HIIT and MICT groups exhibited significant increases in HDL and VO 2peak , and significant decreases in Lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 (Lp-PLA2) ( P < 0.05) after 12-week intervention, but with no significant difference between the two groups. The α-diversity in the HIIT group increased significantly compared with the MICT group, after 12 weeks of exercise ( P < 0.05). In adults with prediabetes, HIIT produced a greater reduction in body fat percentage, estimated visceral adipose content, and estimated subcutaneous fat content than MICT. Exercise training altered the composition of the gut microbiota. HIIT was associated with a higher increase in gut microbial α-diversity than MICT. Post-training changes in gut microbiota composition may correlate with alterations in blood lipid profiles.

Article.Title: Ice–ocean albedo feedback as a key mechanism driving recent Antarctic summer sea-ice decline
Article.Authors: Nihashi S.; Ohshima K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antarctic summer sea-ice extent has exhibited a remarkable declining trend since 2016, reaching a record minimum in February 2023. This decline could accelerate regional warming, disrupt deep water formation and carbon cycling, and negatively affect Southern Ocean ecosystems. However, the mechanism driving this decline remains incompletely understood. Our analyses of satellite sea-ice data and heat flux calculations suggest that the ice–ocean albedo feedback is one of the key contributing processes to the recent decline. During the early ice-melt season, wind-forced divergent ice motion increases the fraction of low-albedo open water. This enhances anomalous solar heating of the upper ocean, accelerating sea-ice melt and further expanding the open water fraction, creating a positive feedback loop. Additionally, we propose a simplified coupled model that captures the key aspects of the feedback process. This model qualitatively reproduces some of the observed variability, such as the recent declining trend, and the year of the record minimum. These findings demonstrate that wind-forced ice motion during the early melt season (early to mid-November) plays a key role in initiating this feedback mechanism, which should be considered in future sea-ice predictions.

Article.Title: Machine learning–based multiphase CT radiomics for differentiating hepatocellular carcinoma from hepatocellular adenoma in dogs
Article.Authors: Choi M.; Yoo J.; Chae S.; Jee H.; Kim B.; Jeon S.; Yoo G.; Chang D.; Choi A.; Lee N.
Article.Abstract: Noninvasive differentiation between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and hepatocellular adenoma (HCA) is clinically important. Although computed tomography (CT) is widely used to evaluate hepatic masses, these entities often exhibit overlapping imaging features, limiting differentiation based on conventional CT findings alone. Given this limitation, we evaluated conventional CT features and developed radiomics-based machine learning (ML) models to differentiate HCC from HCA in dogs. Seventy-five dogs with histologically confirmed HCC or HCA that underwent triple-phase CT were retrospectively included. For conventional CT evaluation, regions of interest (ROIs) were manually segmented for each hepatic mass across all phases. In addition, 1,316 radiomic features were extracted from the segmented ROIs. SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations)-based feature selection was applied, and the selected features were evaluated using multiple ML classifiers. Conventional CT analysis demonstrated limited qualitative differences between HCC and HCA. In contrast, radiomics-based ML analysis showed high cross-validated classification performance, particularly with random forest and boosted tree-based models. Washout-related intensity and texture features in the delayed phase were the most informative, and multiphase feature integration achieved the highest performance. In summary, radiomics-based ML analysis of triple-phase CT showed promising potential for differentiating HCC from HCA, suggesting that it may serve as a noninvasive adjunct for the preoperative diagnosis of canine hepatocellular tumors.

Article.Title: Cerium-quercetin nanoparticles: antioxidant properties and therapeutic performance in sepsis
Article.Authors: Song L.; Huang X.; Xuan Z.; Jin C.; Jia L.; Dong M.; Zheng N.; Mei Y.; Shen J.; Liang H.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome driven by dysregulated inflammation, excessive oxidative stress, and progressive organ injury, yet therapies that concurrently control these interconnected processes remain limited. Restoring redox homeostasis while suppressing NF-κB-mediated inflammatory activation and correcting macrophage dysfunction therefore represents a key therapeutic objective. However, conventional antioxidant and anti-inflammatory agents are often constrained by limited stability, bioavailability, nonspecific distribution, and insufficient coordination of redox and immune regulation. Here, cerium-quercetin nanoparticles (CQ NPs) were prepared by combining cerium species with quercetin. CQ NPs exhibited concentration-dependent scavenging of ·OH and O 2 · − , reduced intracellular ROS level and apoptosis, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, increased Nrf2 and HO-1 expression, decreased p-p65/p65 and p-IκBα/IκBα ratios, and altered CD86/CD206 expression. In mice with CLP-induced sepsis, CQ NPs reduced circulating TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, attenuated pulmonary histopathological injury, and were associated with improved survival. These findings suggest that CQ NPs exhibit antioxidant and inflammation-associated effects in experimental sepsis, warranting further investigation into their underlying mechanisms and therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Preparation-dependent catalytic performance of magnetic MWCNT–Fe3O4 aerogels in nitroarene reduction by isopropanol-mediated transfer hydrogenation
Article.Authors: Arastofar A.; Tavakol H.
Article.Abstract: In this work, four types (A-D) of magnetic MWCNT–Fe 3 O 4 aerogel catalysts were synthesized using four different preparation methods through the incorporation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles into a chitosan- or PVA-crosslinked carbon nanotube network and applied to the transfer hydrogenation of nitroarenes using isopropanol as a liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC). The structure and properties of the prepared catalysts were characterized by FTIR, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, FESEM, EDS, BET, TGA, contact angle measurements, and VSM analysis. For the selected catalyst (D), the catalytic activity was evaluated for the reduction of nitrobenzene under a nitrogen atmosphere, and an aniline yield of 72% was obtained under the optimized conditions with 20 mg of catalyst, 3 equivalents of NaOH, and 5 mL of isopropanol under reflux conditions. The applicability of the catalytic system was further investigated using 24 nitroarene derivatives, affording moderate to good yields, particularly for halogen-substituted substrates. Furthermore, the catalyst could be readily separated from the reaction medium using an external magnet and reused for four consecutive cycles, exhibiting only a slight decrease in catalytic activity.

Article.Title: Autoadaptive medical segment anything model
Article.Authors: Ward T.; Owen M.; Coleman O.; Noehren B.; Imran A.
Article.Abstract: Medical image segmentation is a key task in the imaging workflow, influencing many image-based decisions. Traditional, fully-supervised segmentation models rely on large amounts of labeled training data, typically obtained through manual annotation, which can be an expensive, time-consuming, and error-prone process. This signals a need for accurate, automatic, and annotation-efficient methods of training these models. We propose ADA-SAM (automated, domain-specific, and adaptive segment anything model), a novel multitask learning framework for medical image segmentation that leverages class activation maps from an auxiliary classifier to guide the predictions of the semi-supervised segmentation branch, which is based on the Segment Anything (SAM) framework. Additionally, our ADA-SAM model employs a novel gradient feedback mechanism to create a learnable connection between the segmentation and classification branches by using the segmentation gradients to guide and improve the classification predictions. We validate ADA-SAM on publicly available computed tomography (CT) datasets as well as real-world clinical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data collected during rehabilitation trials, and demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms both fully supervised and semi-supervised baselines by double digits in limited label settings.

Article.Title: The dual cognitive pathways linking speed-watching short-form videos to self-efficacy and academic burnout among Chinese University Students
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Liu A.; Liu T.; Li F.; Yan J.; Lu Q.; Xu C.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: As short-form videos become widely used in higher education, speed-watching has become a common self-directed learning strategy, yet the cognitive mechanisms linking it to learning outcomes and psychological states have not been systematically examined. Grounded in Cognitive Load Theory, this study proposes and tests a dual-pathway moderated mediation model using a sample of 3,000 Chinese university students. The results reveal that speed-watching exhibits countervailing associations. It is positively associated with perceived knowledge acquisition, with lower extraneous cognitive load serving as a parallel mediator of this association, yet is also associated with information overload when input exceeds working memory capacity. These two cognitive states serve as parallel mediators linking speed-watching to academic psychological outcomes. Perceived knowledge acquisition shows correlations with higher self-efficacy and lower academic burnout, whereas information overload is associated with lower self-efficacy and higher burnout. Cognitive failure functions as a boundary condition. Students with high cognitive failure are more susceptible to information overload and less able to convert speed-watching into knowledge gains, thereby experiencing stronger adverse psychological outcomes. These findings clarify the dual mechanisms of accelerated video-based learning and provide theoretical and practical guidance for designing digital learning strategies that account for individual cognitive differences.

Article.Title: A study of multifilament yarn microstructure effects on polyester harp fog collection efficiency
Article.Authors: Karimi F.; Gharehaghaji A.
Article.Abstract: Fog harvesting is an effective and low-cost strategy for meeting part of the water demand in fog-prone areas. However, the efficiency of conventional fog collectors is compromised by limitations in the effective collection and drainage of droplets. In this study, the fog collection efficiency of harp-based polyester multifilament fog collectors fabricated from partially oriented yarns (POY) and fully drawn yarns (FDY) was evaluated. The fog collection efficiencies of the harp structures were compared with those of three commercial fog collectors: Aqualonis (Cloudfisher), Ditf (FogHa-Tin), and Knitwire. The results revealed that polyester harp collectors exhibited a relative increase of 37–54% in fog collection efficiency compared with the Aqlo-back sample under the full-output condition. The structure based on 300 denier/48-filament FDY yarn exhibited the highest fog collection efficiency of 39.33% and the shortest onset time of 35 s. Capillary rise measurements showed that the initial water imbibition in the yarns follows the Lucas–Washburn model, whereas the equilibrium contact angle did not follow the scaling predicted by Jurin’s law. In addition, the dynamic contact angle was found to depend on the effective pore radius. The spatial arrangement of filaments in the FDY yarns resulted in loop-shaped filaments, which provide suitable sites for coalescing water droplets. Overall, the results demonstrated that FDY yarn-based harp structures, produced through a single-step draw-winding process, showed higher fog collection efficiency than the commercial samples.

Article.Title: Adaptive metaheuristic-optimized PID controllers for closed-loop blood glucose regulation in type-1 diabetes
Article.Authors: Dubey V.; Sharma P.; Goud H.; Das N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Type-1 diabetes mellitus requires continuous regulation of blood glucose through appropriate insulin administration, making the development of reliable closed-loop insulin-delivery control strategies an important research problem. This study proposes an intelligent Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) control framework for closed-loop blood-glucose regulation based on the Bergman Minimal Model. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA), and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) are employed for PID parameter tuning, with adaptive modifications introduced into their search mechanisms to improve the exploration–exploitation balance and convergence characteristics. A unified optimization framework is established in which each optimization agent represents the PID parameter vector [Kp​,Ki​,Kd​], while its fitness is determined from the closed-loop glucose-regulation performance. The proposed controllers are evaluated through time-domain and frequency-domain analyses and compared with conventional and non-adaptive metaheuristic-tuned PID controllers. Among the investigated approaches, the Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimization-based PID (AGWO-PID) controller demonstrates the most favorable overall performance. For the ISE-based design, AGWO-PID achieves a rise time of 0.296 s and an ISE of 0.235, whereas the ITAE-based design achieves a rise time of 0.315 s, settling time of 0.958 s, and ITAE of 1.066. In addition, descriptive analysis are conducted to account for the stochastic nature of the metaheuristic algorithms, with mean, standard deviation, median, and coefficient of variation used to assess performance consistency. The results demonstrate that adaptive metaheuristic tuning, particularly AGWO-PID, can substantially improve the transient response, tracking performance, and stability of the simulated insulin-delivery system. The findings provide a control-oriented basis for further validation using higher-fidelity physiological models and virtual-patient environments. Ultimately, this research directly supports UN SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) by providing a scalable framework that can contribute to improved healthcare outcomes, enhanced well-being, and broader access to effective health-related solutions.

Article.Title: Dimethyl fumarate ameliorates imiquimod-induced psoriasiform inflammation and suppresses melanogenesis
Article.Authors: Hyun H.; Jung J.; Choi J.; Choi M.; Won C.; Song Y.; Chang S.
Article.Abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by IL-23/Th17 axis dysregulation. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an oral small-molecule fumaric acid ester as a NF-κB suppressor, is approved for the treatment of multiple sclerosis and psoriasis. However, oral DMF is frequently limited by gastrointestinal adverse effects reported, underscoring the necessity of investigating topical DMF. First, we performed a retrospective chart review and oral DMF was associated with significant improvement in PASI and BSA in patients with mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis. Therefore, we evaluated the efficacy of DMF administered topically in a 4-day imiquimod-induced psoriasiform mouse model compared to intraperitoneal administration, finding that both routes comparably and significantly reduced clinical severity, inflammatory cell infiltration, and epidermal hyperplasia. Mechanistically, DMF suppressed the mRNA expression of TNF-α, IL-17 C, and S100 families induced by M5 or IL-36γ stimulation in human keratinocytes. STAT3 phosphorylation as well as NF-κB p65 phosphorylation was significantly reduced. In contrast to most anti-psoriasis medications that aggravate hyperpigmentation, DMF reduced melanin content and tyrosinase activity in mouse melanocytes. Furthermore, DMF attenuated UVB-induced melanogenesis in an ex vivo human skin model, accompanied by the suppression of MITF and tyrosinase expression. In conclusion, DMF exerts anti-melanogenic effects in addition to its anti-inflammatory effects. In a short-term, preventive-application mouse model, topical DMF reduced psoriasiform inflammation to an extent comparable to systemic DMF, supporting further investigation of topical DMF as a candidate strategy for psoriasis and associated hyperpigmentation.
