Article.Title: Long-COVID: Ultrasensitive multiplex protein biomarker profiling reveals subclinical neuroinflammatory and innate immune dysregulation without correlation to symptom severity
Article.Authors: Austdal M.; Grimstad T.; Lenning O.; Zetterberg H.; Di Molfetta G.; Tan K.; Benedet A.; Ashton N.; Kvaløy J.; Jonsson G.; Braut G.; Omdal R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Routine laboratory tests are consistently normal in long-COVID, yet patients suffer persistent and debilitating symptoms. Whether subclinical inflammatory and neurological dysregulation underlies this discordance remains unclear. Ultra-sensitive multiplex proteomics may detect low-abundance biomolecular signals invisible to conventional methods, and alternative mechanisms such as central sensitization may be operative. In this single-centre, age- and sex-matched case–control study, plasma from 48 Long-COVID patients and 48 recovered controls was analysed using the NULISAseq™ CNS Disease Panel 120, quantifying 123 biomolecules with attomolar sensitivity. The median interval from SARS-CoV-2 infection was 65.5 weeks in patients and 72.5 weeks in controls. Differentially expressed proteins were identified using Mann–Whitney U test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Principal Component Analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis, and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) were used to characterize biological subgroups and activated pathways. Despite no separation between patients and controls on conventional PCA, 19 proteins were significantly dysregulated, with CCL22, IL-6R, and CST3 being prominently upregulated. IPA revealed activation of the Pathogen-Induced Cytokine Storm, Neuroinflammation, and IL-10 Signaling pathways. Hierarchical clustering identified two biologically distinct patient subgroups—one characterized by metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction, the other by neuroinflammatory pathway activation—yet neither cluster differed in fatigue, depression, cognitive symptoms, or any other patient-reported outcome measure. Long-COVID harbors subclinical innate immune activation and neuroinflammatory dysregulation detectable only at attomolar sensitivity, with no direct mapping to clinical symptom profiles. This biological-clinical dissociation suggests that additional mechanisms—including central sensitization or epigenetic dysregulation—may translate peripheral immune signals into the symptom burden experienced by patients.

Article.Title: Simultaneous retrieval of sea-surface waves and winds from high-frequency radar using a convolutional neural network
Article.Authors: Kataoka T.; Tamura H.; Fujiki T.; Fujii S.
Article.Abstract: High-frequency (HF) ocean radar is a powerful land-based remote sensing technique, yet extracting wave and wind parameters from Doppler spectra remains challenging. Conventional inversions struggle with spectral saturation, low signal-to-noise ratios, and directional ambiguity, traditionally necessitating dual-station networks. This study proposes a unified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework to concurrently extract directional wave spectra and sea-surface wind vectors directly from entire Doppler spectra. We evaluated Single and Quad Point Selection (SPS/QPS) in single- and dual-station setups using datasets from the Hyuga-nada Sea (13.5 MHz) and Kii Channel (24.515 MHz). The CNN was less affected by the numerical instabilities of nonlinear inversions: compared with a Bayesian inversion method, it yielded more stable directional wave spectra and required two orders of magnitude less computation time (CPU versus GPU). In the validation phase, single-station QPS achieved directional accuracy comparable to dual-station networks by leveraging spatial continuity among adjacent radial beams, suggesting that the 180° directional ambiguity can be mitigated without supplementary constraints. Identical model architectures with normalized variables also operated across disparate radar frequencies. These findings could reduce the reliance on dual-station geometry and expand operational coverage, although wind-speed retrieval remained only partially resolved and generalization depends heavily on training dataset diversity.

Article.Title: One-day-ahead photovoltaic power prediction based on local weather properties analysis
Article.Authors: Parczyk P.; Szyc K.; Burduk R.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of Renewable Energy Sources, particularly photovoltaics ( PV ), presents significant challenges to energy systems. Due to their dependence on weather conditions, PV outputs are inherently unpredictable, leading to instability in energy supply. This paper proposes a novel day-ahead PV production forecasting method based on Local Weather Properties Analysis, introducing a new feature: the Angular Cloudiness Index ( ACI ). ACI is incorporated into state-of-the-art machine learning models and tested across a wide range of architectures. A total of 1260 models were prepared and distributed across 18 groups. In 83% of the test cases, models augmented with ACI achieved better metrics than the reference configurations. The highest quality improvement was 23%, while the average improvement in quality reached 6% for Mean Absolute Error. These results demonstrate that ACI is an effective, lightweight enhancement for accurate and resilient PV forecasting in scenarios where external data is limited or unavailable. Moreover, the research has shown that using the proposed features enables replacing complex architectures with simpler ones, gaining processing time without losing forecast quality.

Article.Title: Inverse correlation between a putative surrogate marker reflecting aldehyde oxidase activity and urinary hypoxanthine/xanthine ratio in Xdh knockout mice
Article.Authors: Terada K.; Watanabe T.; Yasuno N.; Hosoyamada M.
Article.Abstract: Type 1 xanthinuria is characterized by elevated levels of xanthine in blood and urine but near absent amounts of uric acid. In humans, xanthine oxidoreductase (XOR) gene ( XDH ) mutations in type 1 xanthinuria do not affect lifespan whereas Xdh knockout ( Xdh KO) mice die young. High activity allele of hypoxanthine phosphoribosyl transferase (Hprt(high))- Xdh KO- Slc23a4 knockout ( Slc23a4 KO) mice survive to adulthood but exhibit renal damage with a low urinary hypoxanthine/xanthine ratio. Aldehyde oxidase (AOX), a homolog of XOR, is encoded by four genes in mice compared to a single gene in humans. If mouse AOX oxidizes hypoxanthine to xanthine, it could contribute to the observed species differences. Here, DBA/2 background Xdh KO mice with low AOX activity were generated, which exhibit reduced urinary N 1 -methyl-2-pyridone-5-carboxamide (2-Py) excretion and increased urinary hypoxanthine/xanthine ratios. Male C57BL/6 background Hprt(high)- Xdh KO- Slc23a4 KO mice were mated with female DBA/2 mice to obtain 48 DBA/2 background Xdh KO mice. Urine samples were analyzed. In 16 Xdh KO- Slc23a4 KO mice, distribution of the urinary 2-Py/Cr ratio versus the hypoxanthine/xanthine ratio showed an inverse correlation. Future work will involve disrupting Aox2 , Aox3 , and Aox4 , leaving only Aox1 functional in a Hprt(high)- Xdh KO- Slc23a4 KO background to establish a mouse model for human xanthinuria type 1.

Article.Title: Semantic token sparse selection and a three-dimensional semantic occupancy completion framework under bandwidth constraints
Article.Authors: Wen K.; Ye S.
Article.Abstract: Cooperative perception can extend the visible range of autonomous vehicles, but dense raw-data or feature exchange is difficult to sustain under vehicular bandwidth and latency constraints. This paper proposes a bandwidth-budget-constrained sparse semantic Token framework for collaborative 3D semantic occupancy completion. Multimodal observations are encoded as candidate Tokens carrying content, spatial indices, timestamps, and predicted code lengths. A semantic-utility and redundancy score identifies Tokens that are informative for occluded, uncertain, and long-range regions. During training, differentiable soft gates and rate-distortion-aware bit allocation are optimized jointly with the completion task, during inference, the gates are converted into hard selections by a utility-per-bit ranking and a budget-feasible greedy/local-swap procedure. The implemented communication cost includes entropy-coded Token values, delta-coded spatial indices, timestamps, source identifiers, quantizer identifiers, packet headers, CRC, and byte padding. At the receiver, an asynchronous Token memory performs pose compensation, temporal decay, and contextual retrieval before a dual-path 3D backbone and a progressive generative decoder complete occupancy and semantic categories. All quantitative results are reported on one V2X-Sim-derived semantic occupancy benchmark, and every compared method uses the same split, sensor inputs, voxel grid, training schedule, hardware, asynchronous link protocol, and serialized communication budget. Under a total budget of 0.36 Mbit/frame, the proposed method achieves a geometric occupancy IoU of 51.04% and a semantic mIoU of 31.42%, with an end-to-end computational latency of 44 ms and 14.9 FPS. Compared with Early Fusion, communication is reduced by 98.06% while semantic completion accuracy is improved.

Article.Title: A reproducible breast mass segmentation pipeline using an improved crested porcupine optimizer with domain shift analysis
Article.Authors: Majdar R.; Kamel M.; Jafarzadeh A.; Razmjooy N.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a new method for reproducible breast mass segmentation from mammograms in computer-aided diagnosis. The study develops a robust, reproducible U-Net segmentation model optimized with a novel Improved Crested Porcupine Optimizer (ICPO) for robust and clinically interpretable cross-domain segmentation. The framework utilizes patient-wise splitting, 256 × 256 ROI extraction consistently applied to both INbreast and CBIS-DDSM and equalized preprocessing across both INbreast and CBIS-DDSM datasets. A two-phase training strategy is employed with composite loss function, which is optimized with ICPO instead of traditional gradient-based methods to conquer non-convex loss landscape and get rid of local minimum. Dice Similarity Coefficient and IoU values obtained are 0.8721, 0.9623 and 0.9187, and 0.7704, 0.9289 and 0.8452 respectively in three case studies: INbreast, CBIS-DDSM and mixed training, improving from the state-of-the-art (AdamW optimizer) by 0.9–2.3%. Validation curves also illustrate the convergence of the networks without any catastrophic overfitting. These outcomes verify the generalizability to heterogeneous mammography domain and reproducibility with explicit random seed, manifest file and freely accessible practices.

Article.Title: The FMR1 isoform landscape reveals new spliced variants in women’s blood and ovarian tissues
Article.Authors: Ingravidi M.; Fernández C.; Caviglia E.; Dain L.; Kamenetzky L.; Ferder I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract FMR1 encodes fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMRP), an RNA-binding protein involved in post-transcriptional regulation and highly expressed in ovarian tissue. Although extensive alternative splicing of FMR1 has been described, the full-set transcript landscape in ovarian cells remains incompletely characterized. Here, we used Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read amplicon sequencing to characterize full-length FMR1 transcripts spanning exons 1–17 in human blood and ovarian granulosa cells. We identified 30 high-confidence isoforms accounting for 95% of amplicon-captured FMR1 expression. The predominant transcripts lacked exon 12 and retained exon 14, consistent with previous reports. Long-read sequencing also resolved previously uncharacterized splicing events, including infrequent splice-site usage in exons 15 and 17, exon 11 skipping, and partial retention of introns 2 and 7. Several transcripts preserve the open reading frame, whereas others introduce premature termination codons and may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce truncated FMRP isoforms. Notably, the FMR1 expression profile was conserved between blood and granulosa cells, indicating that blood may serve as an accessible proxy tissue for studying FMR1 isoform expression. These findings expand the known FMR1 transcript repertoire and demonstrate the value of long-read sequencing for resolving complex splicing, providing a basis for investigating these isoforms’ role in ovarian function.

Article.Title: Achieving resistivity and thermal stability balance in Cu‑xMn‑3Ni-based alloy resistors for smart energy meters
Article.Authors: Hu T.; Liu W.; Yu M.; Li Z.; Pei M.; Lv W.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: High-stability precision resistance alloys are core functional components for DC shunts and high-end smart energy meters. The synergistic control of low resistivity and low temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) is critical for their service performance under high power conditions. Cu‑Mn‑Ni‑based alloys offer a balanced combination of electrical conductivity and thermal stability, and alloying and heat treatment are the key technical approaches for optimizing their properties. In this work, the effects of Mn content and quenching process on the microstructure, electrical resistivity and TCR of hot‑rolled Cu‑ x Mn‑3Ni-based alloys were investigated. With increasing Mn content, the preferential orientation of the (311) plane becomes stronger, while that of the (111) crystal plane weakens, and the resistivity increases whereas the TCR decreases. As the quenching temperature rises from 500 to 800 °C, the dominant factor governing texture in the Cu-17Mn-3Ni-based alloy evolution changes from internal‑stress‑driven thermodynamic stability to kinetic resistance of grain boundary migration, and the (220) plane becomes the dominant preferred orientation. After quenching at 750 °C followed by aging at 260 °C, the effective elimination of residual stresses enables the alloy to possess both appropriate electrical resistivity (0.46 μΩ m) and excellent thermal stability (TCR = 29 ppm/°C). This work highlights that the composition synergistic heat treatment provides a feasible strategy to develop precision resistance alloys with balanced resistivity and temperature stability.

Article.Title: Geological and climatic controls on landslide susceptibility and hazard along the Amarnath pilgrimage corridor, Kashmir Himalaya
Article.Authors: Mir R.; Thapa D.; Dar S.; Kumar A.; Yunus A.; Sarif M.
Article.Abstract: Landslides are a recurrent and increasingly consequential hazard across the Himalaya, where steep terrain, tectonically weakened lithologies, climatic variability, and expanding anthropogenic activity interact to destabilize slopes. This study assesses landslide susceptibility along the Baltal-Amarnath-Panjtarni-Poshpathri pilgrimage corridor in the upper Sind catchment, Jhelum basin of the Kashmir Himalaya, India, using an integrated framework that combines high-resolution remote sensing, field-based geological mapping, geotechnical investigations, and climate-data analysis. We developed a meso-scale landslide susceptibility model at 1:10,000 m using 18 conditioning factors and evaluated against field-verified landslide events. The model achieved AUC values of 0.80 for the success-rate (training) curve and 0.86 for the prediction-rate (validation) curve, indicating good model fit and predictive capability, respectively. About 16% is classified as highly susceptible and 68.1% as moderately susceptible to slope failures along the corridor. Landslides are concentrated primarily on steep, structurally deformed lithological formations, debris-mantled slopes modified by road cuts, and active drainage lines. Structural and kinematic analyses indicate that slope instability is strongly influenced by discontinuities and weak lithological units associated with the Main Central Thrust zone in the area. Climate analysis indicates a warming trend of nearly 2 °C in recent decades, substantial interannual variability in snow cover, and an increasing influence of extreme precipitation events, including cloudbursts and intense monsoonal rainfall. During the annual Amarnath pilgrimage season, rainfall-driven hydrological forcing emerges as a major trigger of debris flows, rockfalls, and flash floods, particularly within weak and structurally controlled lithological assemblages. These findings demonstrate that landslide activity along the high-exposure corridor reflects the coupled influence of geological structure, climatic variability, and anthropogenic slope modification. Our study provides a scientifically grounded basis for scale-appropriate susceptibility assessment and risk reduction through the integration of Earth observation, field validation, geotechnical characterization, and real-time hydro-meteorological monitoring to improve the safety and resilience of pilgrimage infrastructure in the rapidly changing Himalayan environment.

Article.Title: In2O3/CuWO4 nanocomposites for enhanced visible-light-driven degradation of safranin t: kinetic and thermodynamic insights
Article.Authors: Rahman S.; Noor A.; Qayyum S.; Muhammad N.
Article.Abstract: Herein, In 2 O 3 /CuWO 4 nanocomposites (IC-10, IC-20, and IC-30) were successfully prepared through a sonication-assisted method. The morphological, optical, and structural characteristics of the as-synthesized materials were evaluated using XRD, FT-IR, UV-Vis DRS, PL and SEM analysis, together with BET analysis of the best-performing sample (IC-30). The calculated band gap values were found to be 2.63, 2.21, 2.47, 2.34, and 2.29 eV for In 2 O 3 , CuWO 4 , IC-10, IC-20, and IC-30, respectively. Similarly, the IC-30 nanocomposite exhibited a BET surface area of 35.1 m 2 g − 1 . The as-fabricated IC-30 exhibited superior photocatalytic activity under the illumination of visible-light, achieving 93.35% degradation of Safranin T dye (15 mg L − 1 ) within 90 min, using 0.5 g L − 1 of the IC-30 nanocomposite at pH 7, approximately 2.54 times higher than pristine In 2 O 3 . The thermodynamic study demonstrated that the degradation process is endothermic and follows pseudo-first-order kinetics. The scavenging study confirmed the key role of •OH radicals in Safranin T (ST) degradation. Moreover, the IC-30 nanocomposite retained 87.39% of its initial photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles, demonstrating satisfactory reusability under the investigated conditions. The study highlights the potential of In 2 O 3 /CuWO 4 nanocomposites as efficient and visible-light responsive photocatalysts for water treatment applications.

Article.Title: Clustering and degree homogeneity govern reservoir computing performance
Article.Authors: Kitayama K.; Uchida A.
Article.Abstract: Reservoir computing exploits fixed recurrent networks as computational substrates, and the choice of network architecture shapes performance. Because biological brains are sparse, clustered, and small-world networked, connectome-derived reservoirs are often expected to be computationally favorable. However, its computational capability has not yet been fully explored. Here we examine this expectation by benchmarking reservoirs constructed from a human structural connectome against Watts–Strogatz‘s small-world networks and random networks, matched for size and mean degree. The benchmark tests are two standard tasks: human-activity classification and Mackey–Glass chaotic signal prediction. On both tasks the small-world reservoir attains the highest performance, while the connectome performs comparably to a random network on prediction. Sweeping the small-world rewiring probability, we find that performance on both tasks is associated with high clustering and low degree heterogeneity and is largely insensitive to characteristic path length, with an optimum in the small-world regime. The connectome, characterized by relatively low clustering and high degree heterogeneity, sits away from this optimum, which is occupied by the small-world networks. These findings identify network properties associated with reservoir performance and indicate that connectome-based connectivity is not, in itself, advantageous for the tasks examined.

Article.Title: Chromium trichloride impairs oocyte maturation by inducing oxidative stress‑mediated mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Sun Z.; Jiao A.; Gao Q.; Guo P.
Article.Abstract: Oocyte quality is a core determinant of mammalian reproductive outcomes. While hexavalent chromium is well documented to exert reproductive toxicity, trivalent chromium (CrCl 3 ) is generally regarded as a low-toxicity trace nutritional element, and its potential adverse impacts on female germ cells remain poorly understood. This study investigates the effects of CrCl 3 using a short-term acute high-dose intraperitoneal exposure mouse model with gradient concentrations (0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 mmol/kg) administered for three consecutive days to evaluate oocyte meiotic maturation and subsequent preimplantation embryonic developmental competence. Our results indicate that CrCl 3 exposure markedly impaired mouse oocyte meiotic maturation, manifested by a reduced first polar body extrusion rate and disrupted spindle-chromosome organization. This phenotype was accompanied by significant redox imbalance, including excessive intracellular ROS accumulation and GSH depletion, as well as mitochondrial dysfunction featured by decreased mitochondrial membrane potential and abnormal mitochondrial distribution. Further experiments revealed that CrCl 3 exposure induced DNA damage, upregulated apoptotic and autophagy-related markers, and increased the protein level of NF-κB, together with elevated global H3K27me3 fluorescence intensity in oocytes. Collectively, these data demonstrate that acute high-dose intraperitoneal CrCl 3 exposure disrupts oocyte quality via oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, providing experimental evidence for understanding the reproductive risks of excess trivalent chromium exposure.

Article.Title: Bayesian-optimized machine learning models for state of charge estimation of lithium-ion EV batteries: sensitivity analysis and XAI via SHAP
Article.Authors: Raman M.; Nandhakumar V.; Abdissa C.
Article.Abstract: Precise state-of-charge (SOC) estimation is essential for reliable battery management systems (BMSs) in electric vehicles (EVs). This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of four advanced ensemble machine learning (ML) models, namely CatBoost, Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGBoost), LightGBM, and AdaBoost, for SOC estimation using a real-world dataset acquired from a BMW i3 EV equipped with a 60 Ah lithium-ion battery pack. Model hyperparameters were optimized using Optuna-based Bayesian optimization, while model generalization capability was assessed through cross-validation and holdout testing. Performance of the investigated ML models was evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), standard deviation of residuals (STD.DEV), maximum error (MAX), coefficient of determination ( \(R^2\) ), distribution-based error analysis, and noise sensitivity assessment. All investigated boosting models outperformed conventional benchmarks such as random forest and extreme learning machine. Among them, CatBoost achieved the highest prediction accuracy with an RMSE of 5.0386% and an MAE of 3.7333%, whereas AdaBoost demonstrated superior robustness with the lowest MAX error. Furthermore, Explainable Artificial Intelligence was incorporated using SHapley Additive exPlanations to quantify feature importance and enhance the transparency and interpretability of SOC prediction mechanisms.

Article.Title: Associations of early-pregnancy maternal thyroid hormones with fetal growth trajectories
Article.Authors: Liao Y.; Dong T.; Zhang L.; Wang H.; Hu H.; Chen Y.; Yu C.; Xiao C.; Zhou W.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: While overt thyroid dysfunction is a known risk factor for fetal growth restriction, the impact of subtle variations in early-pregnancy thyroid hormone levels remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether such variations in women without diagnosed thyroid disease affect fetal growth trajectories. Using a prospective birth cohort at Chongqing Maternal and Child Health Hospital, we constructed three analytical sets based on early-pregnancy measurements of free thyroxine (FT4), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb). Fetal growth parameters, including biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, and estimated fetal weight, were repeatedly measured by trained sonographers. Linear mixed models were applied to examine the associations. Among 556 – 601 mother – infant pairs, each interquartile range increase in maternal FT4 was nominally associated with a change in fetal abdominal circumference of − 0.91 mm at 30 weeks and + 0.09 mm at 37 weeks. Higher TSH was nominally associated with a change in biparietal diameter of − 0.08 mm at 30 weeks and − 0.29 mm at 37 weeks. Neither primary association remained statistically significant after false discovery rate correction. In sensitivity analyses, the TSH–BPD association was not observed after restricting TSH concentrations to the cohort-specific 2.5th–97.5th percentile range. No associations were observed for TPOAb positivity. Early-pregnancy FT4 and TSH showed nominal gestational age-dependent associations with selected fetal biometric measures among women without diagnosed thyroid disease; however, none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. These findings are exploratory and require replication to evaluate their potential implications for fetal growth assessment.

Article.Title: Microscopically identified tick-borne hemoparasites in cattle and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus in Hyalomma ticks in northern Côte d’Ivoire
Article.Authors: Achi L.; Kouadio J.; Houngbedji C.; N’Guessan A.; Akoto P.; Coulibaly J.
Article.Abstract: Ticks and tick-borne diseases are major One Health threats, affecting animal and human health and imposing substantial economic burdens. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of tick-borne hemoparasites in cattle and to assess Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) in ticks in three departments of northern Côte d’Ivoire. A cross-sectional survey was conducted to collect whole blood from cattle and ticks removed from the same animals. Giemsa-stained blood smears were microscopically examined for the detection and morphological identification of hemoparasites, while tick pools were tested for CCHFV RNA by RT-qPCR. In total, 96 cattle were sampled, yielding 561 ticks (7 nymphs and 554 adults). Five tick species were identified: Amblyomma variegatum , Hyalomma rufipes , Hyalomma truncatum , Rhipicephalus annulatus , and Rhipicephalus microplus . Amblyomma variegatum was the predominant species. Five hemoparasites were microscopically identified, including Babesia bovis , Babesia bigemina , Anaplasma marginale , Anaplasma centrale , and Theileria annulata , with an overall prevalence of 34.38% (95% CI: 25.48–44.52%). Babesia bovis was the most prevalent species (18.75%, 95% CI: 12.07–27.94%), whereas Babesia bigemina was the least frequently detected (2.08%, 95% CI: 0.51–8.08%). CCHFV was detected in 2 of the 9 Hyalomma tick pools analyzed. These findings provide updated epidemiological data on tick infestation, tick-borne hemoparasite infections, and CCHFV RNA detection in Hyalomma tick pools from sampled cattle herds in northern Côte d’Ivoire. Further molecular and longitudinal studies are needed to better characterize the epidemiology of these pathogens and their potential impact on animal and public health.

Article.Title: Pathways of cross-modal access to the visual cortex in late blindness
Article.Authors: Paré S.; Lubell J.; Baillet S.; Kupers R.; Ptito M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated how auditory and tactile inputs reach the visual cortex in late-blind (LB) adults, a population for whom the neural mechanisms supporting cross-modal plasticity remain incompletely understood. Using magnetoencephalography (MEG), we measured neural responses to tactile finger stimulation and preceding auditory cues in LB and sighted controls (SC). When analyses were time-locked to the tactile stimulus, LB individuals showed markedly earlier and stronger activations in primary visual cortex (V1) than SC, with responses emerging at 35 ms versus 59 ms, suggesting the recruitment of a fast, likely monosynaptic thalamo-cortical, pathway in LB but not in SC. In contrast, analyses time-locked to the auditory cue revealed a common sequence in both groups: activation of the thalamus (~ 20 ms), followed by primary auditory cortex (A1, 35–38 ms), and then V1 (49–53 ms), consistent with direct A1-to-V1 transmission. Connectivity analyses showed enhanced thalamus-to-V1 alpha-band connectivity in LB for both auditory and tactile inputs, and increased beta-band connectivity only in the auditory modality. These effects did not correlate with duration or onset age of blindness. Overall, the findings indicate that auditory and tactile signals reach V1 through distinct but complementary pathways in late blindness, highlighting substantial cross-modal reorganization in adulthood.

Article.Title: Mapping hydrothermal alteration zones associated with known Pb–Zn potentials in central and southern Afghanistan: an application of ASTER data
Article.Authors: Ahmadi H.; Rahmani N.
Article.Abstract: Hydrothermal alteration mapping is an important tool for early‑stage mineral exploration, particularly in regions where field access is limited. This study systematically applies established ASTER‑based band ratio (BR) and Selective Principal Component Analysis (SPCA) techniques to map hydrothermal alteration zones potentially associated with Pb–Zn occurrences in two contrasting geological settings in Afghanistan: a carbonate-hosted setting in Bamyan (Central Afghanistan) and a skarn setting in Kandahar (Southern Afghanistan) The integrated spectral indices delineated iron oxide, carbonate, phyllic, argillic, and granitic‑related alteration zones that spatially coincide with known Pb–Zn occurrences, mapped lithologies, and major structural features. Comparison with USGS‑defined Pb–Zn halos and published geological maps showed good spatial agreement, with 77% (Bamyan) and 79% (Kandahar) of reference points falling within the mapped alteration zones. The results provide a preliminary basis for prioritizing targets for field verification in remote and mountainous terrains of arid and semi‑arid regions.

Article.Title: Distribution of carbapenemase-encoding genes (blaIMP, blaNDM, blaKPC, blaVIM, and blaOXA-48-LIKE) in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from Yemen
Article.Authors: Al-Kassar W.; Bahaj S.; Al-Jaufy A.; Noman A.; Fuad A.; Alkhateeb R.; Alsharafi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing spread of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) has become a serious global health concern, as it significantly restricts available treatment options and is associated with poor clinical outcomes. The purpose of this research was to determine the prevalence of blaKPC , blaNDM , blaIMP , blaVIM , and blaOXA-48-LIKE in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa obtained from hospitals in Sana’a, Yemen. This study was carried out in Sana’a, Yemen, between October 2023 and December 2024. Eighty-six non-duplicate clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa showing resistance to carbapenems, imipenem, and meropenem were obtained from sputum, blood, pus, wound, and urine specimens collected at two private hospitals and the National Center of Public Health Laboratories. In accordance with CLSI 2024 guidelines, antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated via the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method, while colistin minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) were determined using broth disk elution. Genotypic detection of blaKPC , blaNDM , blaIMP , blaVIM , and blaOXA-48-LIKE was performed by real-time PCR. DNA was extracted via the boiling method. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26. Among the 86 clinical isolates of carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa analyzed, 56 (65.1%; 95% CI: 55.0%–75.2%) were confirmed to harbor at least one carbapenemase-encoding gene. blaOXA-48-LIKE was the most prevalent (60.5%), followed by blaVIM (16.3%) and blaNDM (11.6%). A significant association was found between gene carriage and specimen type ( P = 0.003), with pus specimens showing the highest positivity (100.0%), whereas no statistically significant association was observed with the type of healthcare facility ( P = 0.701), with comparable positivity rates between private hospitals and the public referral laboratory (63.6% vs. 67.7%; OR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.33–2.12). Co-occurrence of multiple genes was observed in 20 isolates (23.3%), with 16 (18.6%) harboring two genes and 4 (4.7%) harboring three genes. All isolates (100.0%) were resistant to carbapenems and most β-lactams, with high resistance to ciprofloxacin (93.0%) and amikacin (86.0%), while 95.3% of isolates exhibited colistin MICs of ≤ 2 µg/mL (categorized as intermediate susceptibility per current CLSI guidelines).The genes for carbapenemase, specifically blaOXA-48-LIKE , blaVIM , and blaNDM , are prevalent in carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Sana’a, Yemen, with extensive multidrug resistance and significant associations with pus specimens. The equivalent distribution of carbapenemase genes across both public reference and private hospital sectors indicates a high local distribution across the sampled facilities. These findings highlight the urgent need for aggressive antimicrobial stewardship and infection control to limit the further dissemination of these carbapenem-resistant isolates.

Article.Title: Flow-dependent TGF-β1 secretion from HCT116 cells following constriction-based microfluidic passage
Article.Authors: Mashhadi Keshtiban M.; Asgari F.; Kavand H.; Sattari A.; Herland A.; Javdansirat S.; Haghighipour N.; Hadi A.
Article.Abstract: Transforming growth factor β1 (TGF-β1) is a multifunctional cytokine involved in tissue remodeling, mechanobiological signaling, and cartilage-related cellular responses. In this proof-of-concept study, we developed and evaluated a constriction-based microfluidic platform for rapidly modulating TGF-β1 secretion from HCT116 cells through short-duration mechanical perturbation. Suspended cells were passed through repeated constrictions under different flow conditions, and a simplified droplet-based numerical model was used as a device-level framework to compare apparent deformation behavior, pressure amplification, transit time, and simulation-derived shear exposure descriptors. The model was used to describe relative passage trends and was not intended to represent living-cell viscoelastic mechanics, intracellular stress transmission, or mechanotransduction pathways. Experimentally, constriction-based microfluidic passage produced a clear flow-condition-dependent TGF-β1 response. Among the tested conditions, the intermediate flow condition, Case 3, showed the highest net TGF-β1 concentration in the culture supernatant, with TGF-β1 secretion increasing by up to approximately 250% compared with the negative control. Consistently, TGF-β1 mRNA expression increased by approximately 3.5-fold in Case 3. Lower-flow/high-resistance conditions were associated with reduced cell viability, indicating that cytokine output depends on a balance between microfluidic stimulation and post-processing cell survival. Conditioned medium collected from Case 3 enhanced COL2A1 and SOX9 protein expression in a simplified two-dimensional AD-MSC bioactivity assay, supporting the biological activity of the microfluidic-conditioned medium and its ability to promote early chondrogenic marker expression under the tested culture conditions. Overall, this study presents a compact constriction-based microfluidic approach for rapidly modulating TGF-β1 secretion and generating biologically active conditioned medium, while establishing a foundation for future studies incorporating straight-channel controls, time-resolved HCT116 imaging, improved cell-mechanics modeling, and three-dimensional AD-MSC assays.

Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Zhang J.; Yang Z.; Wang X.; Wu D.; Xu Y.; Wang P.; Fu H.; Ma Y.; Zhang Q.; Yin W.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury is a critical condition marked by uncontrolled inflammation and immune imbalance. Here, we investigated the role of extracellular matrix components derived from adipogenically differentiated adipose-derived stem cells in regulating macrophage polarization and lung injury. We found that type III collagen was significantly upregulated in the extracellular matrix after adipogenic induction. Treatment with COL-3 alone enhanced M2-like phenotypic features in macrophages, and pharmacological intervention results supported the involvement of AKT signaling in COL-3-associated responses. Article.Title: Development of real-time forecast modelling for lumpy skin disease outbreaks
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Hayama Y.; Theng M.; Baker C.; Sellens E.; Bradhurst R.; Stevenson M.; Breed A.; Roche S.; Laidlow T.; Matsuyama R.; Kondo S.; Yamaguchi E.; Kamata Y.; Yamamoto T.; Firestone S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lumpy skin disease (LSD) is an emerging transboundary and vector-borne disease of cattle that has spread rapidly across East Asia and Europe. Generating reliable forecasts during the early stages of an outbreak remains challenging because of limited epidemiological data, uncertainty in vector transmission, and differences in livestock production systems across countries. The infection probability approach had higher spatiotemporal accuracy than the infectious pressure approach. This study demonstrated how this model can accurately capture LSD outbreak dynamics while flexibly accommodating structural differences in national livestock husbandry systems. The framework provides information and insights for rapid outbreak response and serves to guide strategic decision-making across diverse national contexts.

Article.Authors: Cummins T.; O’Connell I.; Schuler A.; McGuire D.; McCarthy M.; King C.; Free P.; Cao X.; Walsh L.; O’Driscoll J.; Oshaben K.; Aherne M.; Walshe J.; Dalton T.; García F.; Fuentes A.; Appella D.; O’Farrell B.

The CMOS sensor is leveraged for the detection of beads specifically tethered to PNA probes on the sensor surface. This system provides a manufacturable, compact, low‑cost platform for digital biosensing, and eliminates the need for optical detection. Article.Authors: Frank Ikechukwu A.; Onyelowe K.; Kamchoom V.
Article.Abstract: This study developed and applied two complementary numerical–analytical frameworks to evaluate the behaviour of rigid retaining walls, one incorporating expanded polystyrene (EPS) geofoam and the other without geofoam. Both frameworks employ finite-difference simulations in FLAC2D; the initial phase of the study validates the numerical implementation by comparing model predictions with measurements from a small-scale laboratory experimental setup. Close agreement between simulated and experimental results demonstrates the fidelity of the modelling approach. The subsequent parametric study investigates how EPS geofoam properties and configuration influence the structural response of the retaining system. Variables considered include geofoam density, compressible-layer thickness, and imposed surcharge magnitudes. Response metrics comprise lateral earth pressures, bending moments, shear forces, and wall displacements. Results indicate that increasing the thickness of the geofoam layer substantially reduces lateral pressures on the wall, while lower-density EPS (with reduced stiffness) further diminishes lateral loading. Consequently, bending moments, shear forces, and wall strains are markedly reduced when geofoam is used as a compressible inclusion. The findings underscore the effectiveness of EPS geofoam in mitigating earth pressures and enhancing the performance of rigid retaining walls under a range of loading scenarios.

Article.Title: Pan-cancer expression and clinical associations of HSD11B2 and its functional role in breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Gou Y.; Wang Y.; Lu G.; Zhao J.; Zhang W.; Han Y.; Guo C.
Article.Abstract: Although HSD11B2 serves as a crucial enzyme governing glucocorticoid metabolism, its systemic roles across human malignancies have not been fully elucidated. Current evidence remains fragmented, and integrative pan-cancer investigations covering its expression control, clinical relevance, immune correlates and influence on breast cancer aggressiveness are still lacking. To fill this gap, we integrated multi-omics bioinformatic analyses with experimental validation at both the cellular and animal levels, thereby systematically assessing the diagnostic and prognostic significance, underlying molecular mechanisms and tumor-promoting activities of HSD11B2 in breast cancer. Our ultimate goal was to establish HSD11B2 as an indicator usable for pan-cancer diagnosis and prognosis, and to explore its potential as a candidate therapeutic target in breast oncology. Publicly available transcriptomic and clinical datasets, chiefly from TCGA and GTEx, were collected and merged. Using the R computing environment together with multiple multi-omics bioinformatics platforms, we characterized the HSD11B2 expression landscape, its prognostic and diagnostic significance, genetic alterations, epigenetic control, immune infiltration patterns and associated functional pathways across pan-cancer cohorts. How HSD11B2 regulates the proliferative, migratory and invasive behaviors of breast cancer cells was then examined experimentally, using qRT-PCR, Western blotting and immunohistochemistry together with CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell and wound healing assays and a nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model. HSD11B2 showed broad expression disturbance across the pan-cancer spectrum, being markedly elevated in tumors such as BRCA, CHOL and LIHC but evidently reduced in COAD, KIRC, THCA and additional malignancies. Its transcript level showed significant prognostic associations in eight cancer types and acted as an independent outcome predictor in five of them, and the nomogram built on these variables achieved satisfactory predictive accuracy. Moreover, HSD11B2 transcripts distinguished malignant from normal tissues with excellent accuracy (AUC > 0.9) for CHOL, COAD, KIRC, KIRP and READ. At the regulatory level, HSD11B2 abundance was associated with copy number gain, promoter hypomethylation and m6A regulatory signatures. Tumors with abundant HSD11B2 displayed an immune-desert “cold tumor” phenotype, tightly linked to an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Enrichment analyses connected HSD11B2 predominantly to steroid hormone metabolism, cell-proliferation and immune-regulation pathways. Cellular and animal experiments consistently demonstrated that silencing HSD11B2 markedly weakened the proliferative, migratory and invasive capacities of breast cancer cells in vitro, and xenograft tumors in nude mice grew more slowly upon HSD11B2 knockdown. HSD11B2 holds important clinical significance for prognosis assessment and diagnosis across pan-cancer settings. Through multi-dimensional regulatory control it participates in tumor progression and displays oncogenic activity in breast cancer. Collectively, HSD11B2 represents a promising indicator for pan-cancer diagnosis and prognosis, as well as a potential therapeutic target against this malignancy.

Article.Authors: Ochiai S.; Takizawa T.; Takashiri M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water-floating single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) thermoelectric generators (TEGs) raise their own temperature gradient by evaporative cooling and therefore run without a heat source or a heat sink. Sunlight also warms the cooling regions, so reflecting it away opens a second route to a larger gradient. We compared four devices covering combinations of reflectivity and water permeability on the cooling regions: an unmasked reference, a white acrylic resin mask, a two-layer acrylic + diatomite mask, and a diatomite mask. Under artificial sunlight of 1000 W/m 2 , the diatomite-masked device gave an output voltage of 0.50 mV, against 0.25 mV for the unmasked device. Two thickness-matched device pairs locate the origin of this gain. Covering the bare film with a thin reflective mask raised the output voltage by 0.09 mV, net of the evaporation it costs. A water-permeable diatomite mask raised it by a further 0.16 mV over a sealed one. Junction thermocouples on replicate devices agree with the derived temperature differences. A cooling-side layer that reflects sunlight and conducts water thus offers a route to larger gradients in devices that raise their own.

Article.Title: Context-dependent alarm calls in the Mauritian flying fox, an island-endemic fruit bat
Article.Authors: Yinon O.; Krivoruchko K.; Eitan O.; Janoo I.; Naujeer H.; Oleksy R.; Yovel Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Alarm calls enable animals to warn conspecifics of imminent threats and coordinate collective responses. Despite bats’ rich social vocal behaviour and the predation pressures faced by many species, no experimental evidence of such calls has been reported in this order. Here, we report alarm calls in Chiroptera, in the Mauritian flying fox ( Pteropus niger ), an island endemic species that evolved without natural predators yet now faces intense anthropogenic pressures. In captive colonies, an experimenter entered the enclosure either empty-handed ("No-Net") or carrying a capture net ("Net"), a more salient threat cue. The calls emitted in both conditions were distinguishable from other social calls and likely represent alarm calls. Alarm calls from the two conditions were also acoustically distinguishable, and in one colony bats called twice as often under "Net". Alarm call production was context-dependent: calls were more frequent during the day, when roosting bats are less mobile and potentially more vulnerable, whereas at night the same stimuli mostly elicited flight. Alarm calls emerged only when group size reached at least four individuals. These findings broaden the known communicative repertoire of bats, highlight the need to reassess alarm signalling across Pteropodidae , and provide a basis for comparative work on its origins.

Article.Title: Development and psychometric validation of the Diabetic Retinopathy Psychosocial Adjustment Questionnaire (DRPAQ) in Iranian patients
Article.Authors: Salehnezhad A.; Mahdizadeh M.; Jamali J.; Shoeibi N.; Sedghi F.; Vahedian-Shahroodi M.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision impairment in adults with diabetes and is associated with substantial psychosocial stressors, including progressive vision loss, high treatment costs, and reduced personal and social functioning. These challenges can impair adaptive coping, exacerbate emotional distress, and worsen clinical outcomes. Although several instruments assess vision-related quality of life in DR, none specifically measure broader psychosocial adjustment processes in culturally diverse settings. This study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate a new questionnaire—the Diabetic Retinopathy Psychosocial Adjustment Questionnaire (DRPAQ)—grounded in Lazarus and Folkman’s transactional model of stress and coping, for use in Iranian patients with DR. This cross-sectional psychometric study was conducted in 2025 at a tertiary eye hospital in northeastern Iran. An initial 65-item pool was generated from prior qualitative data and refined using DeVellis’s eight-step approach. Face validity (qualitative and quantitative), content validity (CVR and CVI with 12 experts), and construct validity (exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis on 364 patients) were assessed. Reliability was evaluated through internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha) and test-retest stability (intraclass correlation coefficient) in 30 patients. Analyses were performed using SPSS 25 and AMOS. The final 35-item DRPAQ demonstrated a clear six-factor structure corresponding to the transactional model constructs, explaining 62.4% of variance. Confirmatory factor analysis showed excellent fit (χ²/df = 2.14, RMSEA = 0.056, CFI = 0.95, TLI = 0.94, NFI = 0.92, SRMR = 0.045). Cronbach’s alpha ranged from 0.971 to 0.995 across subscales (overall 0.992) in the full validation sample ( n = 364), and test-retest intraclass correlation in the pilot subsample ( n = 30) was 0.89. The DRPAQ demonstrates promising psychometric properties and appears to be a culturally relevant instrument for assessing psychosocial adjustment in diabetic retinopathy. It may offer a potentially valuable tool for clinical screening and research, enabling early identification of adaptation barriers and facilitating targeted interventions to improve coping and quality of life in this population.

Article.Title: Development of a whole workflow for multiplexed diagnosis of viral respiratory infections
Article.Authors: Hardt M.; Voss T.; Langthaler S.; Sprenger-Haussels M.; Kaiser F.; Oelmüller U.; Zatloukal K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Endemic cold waves caused by SARS-CoV-2, Influenza and RSV challenge global health systems by co-circulation in the population. This requires appropriate pre-analytical workflows that obtain valid multi-virus diagnostic test results and ensure the reliability of downstream molecular analyses. Various pre-analytical parameters like specimen stabilization, virus infectivity inactivation and nasal sprays as interfering substances were examined. The BD transport swab system including the UVT medium was able to stabilize the nucleic acid copy numbers of the tested viruses at 37 °C for up to 96 h, even when supplemented with the virus inactivating reagent transport medium additive-P (TMA-P). Viruses infectivity were inactivated by TMA-P, TMA-D and benzalkoniumchloride (BAC). However, only BAC is usable in combination with the QIAprep&amp high-throughput system. Furthermore, TMA-P and BAC are compatible with sequencing. Additionally, external substances like nasal sprays used prior to sample collection may interfere with test results. The BD system supplemented with inactivating substances reduce the biosafety requirements for transport and analysis while ensuring valid test results including sequencing. The use of the direct PCR QIAprep&amp system in combination with the multi-target detection assays minimizes the specimens processing time. Overall, a rapid and reliable detection workflow of respiratory viruses was developed for clinically relevant pre-analytical scenarios.

Article.Title: Design and performance analysis of optimized and unrolled Grain-80/128 stream ciphers on FPGA and ASIC platforms
Article.Authors: R A.; B S.; P R.; Ekpo S.; V K J.; C S A.; Tupe-Waghmare P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stream ciphers that are both lightweight and high-throughput are crucial for contemporary embedded, Internet of Things (IoT), and hardware designs with limited resources. Grain-80 and Grain-128 are two of the most popular solutions now in use because of their robust cryptographic capabilities and compact construction. However, for high-performance and real-time systems, conventional solutions are not adequate, because of their low throughput and significant initialization latency. In this work, we present optimized and unrolled hardware architectures of Grain-80 and Grain-128 stream ciphers for Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) and Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) platforms. The proposed designs are based on scalable unrolling techniques and architectural changes to improve throughput without sacrificing cryptographic accuracy. FPGA implementations on Spartan-6, Artix-7 and Virtex-7 devices show nearly linear throughput scaling, up to 10.67 Gbps for Grain-80 and 11.40 Gbps for Grain-128 at 16 $$X$$ unrolling on Virtex-7. The proposed architectures achieve single-cycle latency and increase the maximum operating frequency by more than 30% over conventional architectures. Significant improvements in energy efficiency are demonstrated by ASIC implementations generated with the Cadence Genus at 180 nm and normalized to 90 nm, 45 nm, and 28 nm technologies. At 180 nm, energy usage decreased from 2.005 pJ/bit to 1.267 pJ/bit for Grain-80 and from 2.210 pJ/bit to 1.978 pJ/bit for Grain-128. These findings demonstrate that the suggested architectures are appropriate for both lightweight and high-performance cryptographic tasks since they provide a balanced trade-off between throughput, latency, area, and energy savings.

Article.Title: Effect of different therapeutic approaches on quality of life of patients with Graves’ disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Mossavarali S.; Vaezi A.; Ghorban Sarvi D.; Mirdamadi N.; Mohseni S.; Pejman Sani M.
Article.Abstract: Graves’ disease (GD) impairs quality of life (QoL), and the effects of different treatments, including antithyroid drugs (ATD), radioiodine (RAI), and surgery, on QoL remain unclear. This study aimed to assess and compare QoL outcomes following these therapies. We conducted a PRISMA-based systematic review and meta-analysis, searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science to July 30, 2025, for studies assessing QoL after GD treatment using generic SF-36 or thyroid-specific ThyPRO questionnaires. Mean scores were pooled using random-effects models. Sixteen studies were included. Among SF-36 domains, physical functioning had the highest scores for ATD (66.24 [43.97–88.50]) and RAI (84.02 [78.53–89.52]), while social functioning was highest after surgery (72.32 [55.62–89.01]). Vitality was among the lowest-scoring domains for ATD (55.90 [44.63–67.16]), RAI (59.35 [50.35–68.34]), and surgery (55.41 [47.10–63.71]), while bodily pain was lowest for surgery (51.11 [22.70–79.51]). In ThyPRO, tiredness was the worst-scoring domain for all treatments (ATD 40.04 [31.31–48.78]; surgery 32.50 [21.05–43.95]; RAI 41.90 [39.49–44.31]). The most favorable outcomes were observed for goiter symptoms after surgery (7.08 [0.42–13.74]) and RAI (12.03 [5.94–18.12]), and for sex life after ATD (11.59 [6.49–16.69]). Surgery showed significantly better QoL scores than RAI for depression and emotional susceptibility, while ATD was significantly better than RAI for sex life. All treatments were associated with improvements in QoL, with differences across specific domains. These findings may help clinicians and patients understand treatment-related QoL outcomes and support informed treatment decisions.

Article.Title: Data driven solid propellant grain tailoring using surrogate optimization and ensemble machine learning
Article.Authors: Adel H.; Mustafa E.; Ahmed M.; Khalil M.; Belal H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Solid propellant rocket motors (SPRMs) play a crucial role in diverse aerospace applications, with their performance intricately linked to propellant grain design. This study introduces an innovative grain tailoring approach for a highly parameterized, five-slot axisymmetric solid propellant grain. To achieve a target pressure-time history, an automated inverse design framework is developed, coupling the level set method (LSM) for robust topological burnback analysis with a well validated internal ballistic prediction module (IBPM). To investigate the most suitable data-driven strategy for inverse grain design, the study evaluates and compares two advanced data-driven optimization techniques: a Kriging-assisted Genetic Algorithm (GA) and a Random Forest Regression (RFR) machine learning model, both trained on a dataset generated via Latin Hypercube Sampling. In addition, two state-of-the-art machine learning regression models, namely XGBoost and LightGBM, are employed as benchmark models to validate the selection of Random Forest Regression for the proposed inverse design framework. While both approaches successfully navigate the 20-variable design space, the RFR model significantly outperforms the Kriging-assisted GA. Among the investigated machine learning models, Random Forest Regression consistently achieved the highest predictive accuracy and was therefore selected as the surrogate model for the proposed framework. Specifically, the RFR approach achieved a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 3.24 bar compared to the Kriging model’s 11.8 bar, representing a substantial improvement in accuracy while drastically reducing computational overhead. The results demonstrate that integrating ensemble machine learning techniques like RFR overcomes the curse of dimensionality inherent in traditional surrogate models, offering a highly efficient, accurate, and automated pathway for mission-specific grain tailoring. The proposed framework therefore establishes a practical and computationally efficient methodology for high-dimensional inverse solid rocket motor grain design.

Article.Title: Experimental optimization and machine learning-based prediction of warm incremental sheet forming of AZ31 magnesium alloy
Article.Authors: Khot A.; Magdum R.; Shirguppikar S.; Ganachari V.; Chinnaiyan P.; Barah O.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates the warm incremental sheet forming (WISF) behavior of AZ31 magnesium alloy through variable wall angle experiments, with the aim of improving formability and reducing forming force. Four process parameters forming temperature, step-down, spindle speed, and tool diameter were investigated at three levels using a Taguchi L27 orthogonal array. Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) was employed to evaluate the experimental results and identify the optimal combination of parameters for multi-response performance, while Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) was used to determine the contribution of each process parameter. The findings indicate that a high forming temperature and low step-down have the greatest influence on increasing the achievable wall angle and reducing forming force. Random Forest-based machine learning models were employed as supplementary predictive tools for both responses. The Random Forest models showed promising preliminary predictive performance for maximum wall angle and moderate performance for forming force. Feature-importance analysis provided supplementary insights into parameter influence within the investigated experimental domain. However, given the limited dataset of 27 experimental runs, further validation using additional experimental data is required to establish the models’ generalizability. The optimum condition identified by Grey Relational Analysis was a forming temperature of 250 °C, a step-down of 0.2 mm, a spindle speed of 250 rpm, and a tool diameter of 8 mm, under which a maximum wall angle of 66.5° and a forming force of approximately 0.639 kN were obtained. These results demonstrate that the combined experimental, statistical, and data-driven framework can effectively identify favorable WISF conditions for AZ31 magnesium alloy within the investigated process window.

Article.Title: Microplastic exposure reduces plant biomass and chlorophyll content with no detectable safety advantage for biodegradable polymers
Article.Authors: Yuksel B.; Eryilmaz N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biodegradable plastics are increasingly promoted as environmentally preferable substitutes for conventional polyethylene, yet whether the microplastics they release are less harmful to plants remains unresolved. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed 31 studies (323 effect sizes) comparing biodegradable and conventional microplastics for effects on terrestrial plant growth, chlorophyll content and genotoxicity, using random-effects models with robust variance estimation. Microplastic exposure significantly reduced plant biomass and growth (− 19.2%, 95% CI [− 29.5, − 7.3]) and chlorophyll content (− 19.5%, 95% CI [− 30.4, − 6.8]). Reductions were numerically larger for biodegradable than for conventional microplastics (biomass − 22.1% vs. − 13.3%; chlorophyll − 26.8% vs. − 10.1%), but the between-class difference was not statistically significant. Co-exposure with heavy metals or other stressors more than doubled the biomass reduction (− 40.1% vs. − 16.2%). Aged biodegradable microplastics showed a non-significant trend towards genotoxic and cytotoxic responses, based on only two to three studies. Heterogeneity was extreme (I 2 ≈ 96–100%), but effects were robust in sensitivity analyses. These results provide no evidence that biodegradable microplastics are safer for plants than conventional ones, although a non-significant difference is not evidence of equivalence; co-occurring stressors intensify phytotoxicity, and ageing may introduce genotoxic potential, pending confirmation. These findings bear directly on environmental evaluation of biodegradable mulch films.

Article.Title: Toxicity of immunosuppressive drugs on human fetal kidney development ex vivo
Article.Authors: Babin P.; Boulay H.; Desdoits-Lethimonier C.; Toupin M.; Fernández Prieto F.; Lesné L.; Lavoué V.; Vigneau C.; Mazaud-Guittot S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immunosuppressants, including calcineurin inhibitors and corticosteroids, are used during pregnancy to treat autoimmune diseases and prevent transplant rejection. Their use requires balancing maternal benefits against potential fetal toxicity, as calcineurin inhibitors are nephrotoxic in adults and cross the placenta. This study investigated whether immunosuppressants induce toxicity or affect early differentiation of the human fetal kidney. Human fetal kidneys (7–14 weeks of development) obtained following elective abortions were analyzed for gene expression patterns. Kidney fragments were exposed for seven days to increasing concentrations of immunosuppressants, alone or in combination. Toxicity and developmental effects were evaluated by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative PCR. We first characterized the expression of genes encoding proteins of the calcineurin signaling pathway by in situ hybridization. Although expression signatures differed, most genes were detected in interstitial cells. High concentrations of cyclosporine impaired cell viability, proliferation, differentiation, glomerular density, and depleted renin-positive cells. Tacrolimus and prednisone, alone or combined, produced subtler effects, mainly on differentiation. Their combination slightly decreased proliferation and glomerular density. Overall, immunosuppressants did not induce acute toxicity at biologically relevant concentrations. However, the sensitivity of renin-positive cells warrants further investigation, including cardiovascular and renal follow-up in experimental models and mother–child cohorts.

Article.Title: Liver-derived extracellular vesicle proteomics reveals mechanisms and potential biomarkers of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
Article.Authors: Donoso-Quezada J.; Mellergaard M.; Lai A.; Scholz-Romero K.; Christiansen G.; Stensballe A.; Salomon C.; Handberg A.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves disturbances in hepatic metabolism, inflammation, and extracellular matrix remodeling, yet minimally invasive biomarkers for early detection and monitoring remain limited.We profiled the proteome of putative liver-derived extracellular vesicles (L-EVs) isolated directly from plasma using ASGR1/CYP2E1 immunocapture in a clinically characterized cohort including lean controls, obesity control group, and individuals with obesity and MASLD undergoing weight-loss intervention. L-EV preparations were characterized and their hepatic association assessed using nanoparticle tracking analysis, high-resolution flow cytometry (hFCM), CD9 immunogold transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Western blotting, and mass-spectrometry–based proteomics.Exploratory analyses suggested L-EV proteomic differences associated with obesity and MASLD, affecting metabolic, inflammatory, extracellular matrix, and fibrogenic pathways. Several MASLD-associated proteins, such as cathepsin L (CTSL) and the tumor protein D52-like 2 (TPD52L2), correlated strongly with liver fat, insulin resistance, and fibrosis indices. Weight loss induced dynamic shifts in L-EV proteins, most notably between one and five months, accompanying metabolic improvement and changes in fibrosis-related biomarkers. Biomarker analysis identified two combinatorial protein panels with moderate discriminatory performance for MASLD (AUCs 0.702–0.724). Three candidate proteins, SerpinE1, GNA13, and CTSL, were also detected in plasma L-EVs using hFCM, supporting their potential as biomarkers of MASLD within the ASGR1-positive circulating EV population. Overall, L-EV proteomics provides molecular insight into MASLD and its changes during weight loss, with potential applications in biomarker discovery and longitudinal monitoring.

Article.Title: Mineralogical and geochemical fingerprinting of Lower–Middle Eocene carbonates at Umm Russeies area, north Galala Plateau, Egypt
Article.Authors: Abd-Elhameed M.; Attia G.; Mahmoud A.; El-Moghazy A.; Salama Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Lower–Middle Eocene carbonates of Egypt’s Northern Galala Plateau preserve a critical, yet geochemically underexplored, archive of southern Tethyan paleoenvironmental change. This preliminary integrated mineralogical and geochemical screening study of the Minia, Gebel Hof, and Observatory formations in Umm Russeies reveals a dynamic depositional history. The Minia and Gebel Hof limestones consist of high-purity calcite (95–98 wt%) with elevated bulk Sr concentrations (1180–1560 ppm), above typical values for stabilized low-Mg calcite (200–400 ppm), consistent with retention of originally Sr-rich carbonate components that experienced limited meteoric alteration. Phase-specific analyses (e.g., sequential leaching, Sr isotopes, SEM-EDS/EPMA) are recommended to confirm Sr partitioning and further constrain preservation potential. In contrast, the Observatory formation exhibits pronounced heterogeneity, defined by three distinct geochemical suites: (i) Fe-rich dolomites; (ii) siliceous rudstones documenting a major terrigenous pulse; and (iii) rudstones with anomalously high Sr concentrations reaching 2200 ppm. The stratigraphic distribution of selected geochemical parameters is presented for the Wadi El-Qanaa succession, providing a foundation for future chemostratigraphic investigations. Trace elements (V, Cr, Ni) show strong correlations with Al₂O₃, consistent with a dominant detrital association and unsuitability as redox proxies in this dataset. The high-purity limestones are compositionally comparable to chemical-grade resources, warranting industrial qualification testing. The newly identified Sr-rich horizons define a high-priority target for mineralogical investigation to identify Sr host phases and evaluate their potential as a future by-product recovery opportunity.

Article.Title: Rapamycin attenuates renal ischemia–reperfusion injury and early profibrotic responses
Article.Authors: Yuan B.; Fan Z.; Liang C.; Jia Y.; Tang Q.; Liu T.; Zhang M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Renal ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major cause of acute kidney injury and contributes to subsequent renal dysfunction and profibrotic responses. Rapamycin, an Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin inhibitor, has been reported to modulate autophagy and inflammatory responses; however, its effects on renal I/R injury and early profibrotic signaling remain incompletely understood. In this study, a rat renal I/R injury model was established by 45 min ischemia followed by 3 or 7 days of reperfusion. The experiment utilized 6- to 8-week-old male and female Sprague–Dawley rats, with a sample size of n = 6 in each group, comprising 3 males and 3 females. Starting one day prior to modeling, the rats received daily gavage of rapamycin at low (1 mg/kg) or high (2 mg/kg) doses. Renal injury was assessed through renal histopathological staining, TUNEL apoptosis detection, and the measurement of oxidative stress, inflammatory factors, and fibrosis markers. Additionally, the molecular mechanisms underlying the renal protective effects of rapamycin were investigated using RNA sequencing. Rapamycin treatment significantly reduced tubular injury and apoptosis following renal I/R injury. In addition, rapamycin decreased oxidative stress markers (ROS and MDA) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6), while enhancing antioxidant defenses (SOD and GSH). Expression of profibrotic markers was also reduced after rapamycin treatment. Rapamycin treatment resulted in alterations in the expression of autophagy-related markers, such as LC3B. RNA sequencing and subsequent validation experiments revealed a correlation between the expression level of Col6a6 and the aforementioned protective indicators. In conclusion, the current findings suggest that rapamycin can mitigate renal ischemia–reperfusion injury, accompanied by changes in autophagy, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses, and is linked to the attenuation of early activation of pro-fibrotic signaling pathways in the kidneys. However, the causal relationship of this association and whether Col6a6 directly mediates the protective effect necessitate further experimental validation.

Article.Title: Common balance tests and their association with falls
Article.Authors: Grgic J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Semi‑tandem, side‑by‑side, and full‑tandem balance tests are commonly used to evaluate balance performance. This study aimed to examine their associations with self-reported falls using nationally representative data from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (wave 1), including up to 57,720 adults aged ≥ 45 years. Balance performance was assessed using the 10‑second semi‑tandem and side‑by‑side tests, as well as the 60‑second (≤ 70 years) and 30‑second (> 70 years) full‑tandem tests. In the crude model, gender‑stratified weighted logistic regression examined the cross-sectional association between falls and ability to maintain balance for the full duration (yes/no). The weighted multivariate model was adjusted for age, grip strength, body mass index, activities of daily living, dementia diagnosis, and physical activity. In the crude analyses, significant associations were observed between falls and semi‑tandem, side‑by‑side, and 60‑second full‑tandem test completion ability (Odds ratio [OR]: 0.418–0.771). In adjusted analyses, significant associations with falls were found for male and female side‑by‑side test (OR = 0.527–0.622) and 60‑second full‑tandem test (OR = 0.784–0.856), as well as female 30‑second full‑tandem test (OR = 0.833). In summary, the 10-second side-by-side test and the 60-second full-tandem test showed the most consistent association with self-reported falls within the subgroup in which they​ were​ administered.

Article.Title: Dynamic role-based optimal playing XI generator for T20 cricket using match context and MLP model
Article.Authors: Pathak O.; Dey T.; Chatterjee A.; Roy S.; Dey N.; Roy S.; Sen S.
Article.Abstract: Cricket, is played in multiple formats and generates a large amount of data which makes it highly suitable for analysis. Among all formats of the game, Twenty20 International (T20I) is the most dynamic which needs quick decision making, dynamic strategies and strong overall performance. This study introduces a machine learning-based, context-aware system that analyzes and evaluates players beyond the traditional statistics by considering match-specific factors such as the pitch conditions, opposition strength and pressure situations with the intention to assist selectors and analysts to form a balanced Playing XI. The research used overall statistics and the ball by ball data from 2022-2024 to capture recent player trends. The Iyengar-Sudarshan method (a statistical technique used to create a composite index when there are several indicators with unequal importance) was used to assign appropriate feature weights. Then, multilayer perceptron (MLP) and light gradient boosting Machine (LightGBM) models were used to predict player performances on the basis of contextual parameters such as pitch conditions, opposition strength, location and pressure situations. The system generated role-constrained lineups that ranked the players with reliability-weighted composite scores. The experimental results clearly showed consistency between the predicted teams and the actual playing XIs in the latest International Cricket Council (ICC) events and series. These findings validated the efficiency, accuracy and applicability of the proposed model. The decision-making in T20I team selection is improved by incorporating predictive analytics, weighted scoring and contextual modeling. The platform provides a simple interface that allows both manual and automated team composition selection. Overall, it provides a data-driven intelligent approach to modern cricket analytics and player evaluation.

Article.Title: ATIC: a closed-loop, migration-aware tiering controller for cloud and edge NVMe storage
Article.Authors: Hamarsheh A.; Kamel El-Taj H.; Al-Qerem A.
Article.Abstract: Tiered cloud and edge storage pairs a small, fast tier with a larger capacity tier, but traditional storage replacement policies can allow for the admission of large or sequentially accessed objects whose migration cost is greater than the object’s reuse value. This paper introduces an online admission and eviction controller, ATIC, that combines interpretable benefits per byte of decayed frequency, compactness based on reuse-gap (rather than reuse-size), sequentially, read propensity, object size, device service-time savings, and promotion cost. A quantile gate dynamically tunes the admission selectivity every 750 requests, based on the ratio of promoted bytes to requested bytes. ATIC is benchmarked in a disclosed object-level queueing simulator with five business-intelligence and five artificial-intelligence workload families, 30,000 requests per workload and 20 paired seeds. Relative to GDSF, ATIC saves 41.3%–80.3% of promoted bytes and 2.9%–10.5% of modeled active-I/O energy at 10% capacity for all workloads (one-sided paired Wilcoxon p < 10⁻⁴). With the best latency baseline, ATIC reduces the latency for AI training by 0.5%, and checkpoint traffic by 2.6%, outperforming effectively tied for ETL, and 10.5% and 3.6% slower for locality-dominant BI and mixed analytics, respectively. Ablations reveal that size normalization keeps latency failure from becoming widespread, while the adaptive gate mostly restricts migration. ATIC thus offers a clear migration-energy-latency trade-off, instead of a general latency improvement. Before deploying, hardware and production-trace validation is still required.

Article.Title: Integrated utilisation of multiple industrial byproducts in eco friendly masonry mortar development
Article.Authors: Manoharan V.; Sreevalli Y.
Article.Abstract: The utilization of industrial byproducts in masonry mortar provides a sustainable measure for increased natural resource consumption and environmental pollution caused by conventional cement mortars. Studies that aim to integrate multi source industrial wastes in mortar development and simultaneous replacements of cementitious and fine aggregate component in mortar are not much explored. This study investigates the integrated utilization of multi source industrial byproducts in masonry mortar development. Mortar proportions with progressive replacements for manufactured sand (M-sand) with construction demolition waste(CDW) and waste foundry sand(WFS) upto 100% and cementitious replacement by flyash(FA) and waste marble powder(WMP) upto a maximum proportion of 30% was done. The mortar specimens were evaluated for their mechanical properties, pozzolanicity, microstructural behaviour, durability, environmental performance, cost analysis and bond behaviour with bricks. 20 mixes were formulated using industrial byproducts and the results were analysed using one-way ANOVA and linear regression. Results reveal CDW exhibited enhanced mechanical and durability performance than WFS as fine aggregate replacement due to its uniform gradation and interfacial behaviour with cement paste. FA exhibited enhanced cementitious performance than WMP because of its particle shape and enhanced pozzolanic reactivity. Mix MM6C50F50-FA30 containing cement, CDW and WFS in the proportion of 1:3:3, with cementitious replacement of FA by 30% gave compressive strength of 19.82 MPa achieving the limits for various masonry applications. Mechanical, durability and environmental parameters of the ecofriendly mortar mixes were comparable with conventional mortar. This integrated utilization of multi-source industrial byproducts in masonry mortar development fosters circular economy and enhances waste reuse in construction.

Article.Title: Process optimization and thermodynamic analysis of ultrasonic-assisted extraction of peanut meal protein
Article.Authors: Dabbour M.; Hamoda A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study optimized the ultrasonic-assisted extraction (UAE) of protein from peanut meal (PMP). The operational ranges for the key variables, pH (9–11), temperature (25–45 °C), time (10–30 min), and ultrasonic power density (100–300 W·L⁻¹), were established through single-factor experiments. A Box-Behnken design, centered on a four-factor-three-level, was subsequently employed to simultaneously maximize protein yield and solubility while minimizing energy consumption. The developed models demonstrated a significant fit to the experimental data ( p < 0.0001), as validated by a non-significant lack-of-fit ( p ≥ 0.055) and high coefficients of determination (R 2 ≥ 0.975 and adjusted R 2 ≥ 0.953). The optimized extraction conditions for all responses were pH 10, 39 °C, 19 min, and 172 W·L⁻¹. Under these conditions, the observed values for protein yield (35.81%), solubility (62.49%), and energy consumption (121.06 kJ) were in close agreement with the predicted data. Furthermore, thermodynamic analysis showed that UAE significantly lowered the energy barrier for PMP extraction, thereby augmenting process efficiency. Notably, ultrasonication substantially improved PMP yield and solubility by 44.21% and 25.08%, respectively, relative to the control ( p < 0.05), supported by particle size distribution and zeta potential outcomes. SEM and AFM analyses revealed that the sonicated isolate exhibited dissociated microstructures with smaller particles, irregular fragments, and disordered lamellar structures, indicating the disruption of crosslinking and molecular bonds. UV-Vis spectroscopy and DSC thermograms further indicated that sonicated PMP possessed higher peak absorption and greater thermostability than the control. This study highlights the potential of UAE to enhance the yield and solubility of PMP, providing an efficient and industrially scalable strategy for the food sector.
