Article.Title: Identification and validation of potential biomarkers associated with RNA modification-related gene signatures in intervertebral disc degeneration
Article.Authors: Shi B.; Li J.; Qian H.; Yang X.; Fei X.; Wu H.; Chen L.; Li L.; Lin S.; Xie W.
Article.Abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) represents a prevalent degenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates the involvement of RNA modification-related genes in IDD pathogenesis, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study integrated public IDD datasets with RNA modification-related genes from existing literature and key module genes identified through weighted gene co-expression network analysis, yielding 105 candidate genes. Of these, 102 exhibited protein-protein interactions, with core genes primarily enriched in protein processing and axon guidance pathways. Further screening using Boruta and XGBoost identified seven candidate biomarkers.​ Among the seven candidate biomarkers, TFPI and TNFAIP6​ were consistently upregulated in IDD samples across datasets. A nomogram constructed from these potential biomarkers achieved an AUC value of 0.953 in the GSE70362 dataset, and independent external clinical validation is still needed to verify its diagnostic performance prior to clinical application. Functional enrichment analysis suggested that TFPI and TNFAIP6 are potentially associated with mismatch repair, cytokine interactions, and immune-related processes. Finally, reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in a small clinical cohort provided supportive experimental evidence for the upregulation of TFPI and TNFAIP6. Collectively, these findings suggest that TFPI and TNFAIP6 may serve as potential biomarkers for IDD, while their biological functions necessitate further in-depth investigation specific to IDD.

Article.Title: Hybrid transformer-augmented convolutional network for robust plant disease recognition from leaf images
Article.Authors: Ramzan Z.; Iqbal A.; Din I.; Trabelsi Z.
Article.Abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) capture long-range spatial context only indirectly, whereas vision transformers need large training sets. We ask whether adaptively fusing local convolutional and global self-attention features at several depths of a pre-trained CNN improves accuracy and cross-domain robustness. We present HTA-ConvNet, which inserts a Dual-Branch Spatial Attention (DBSA) block after three intermediate stages of EfficientNet-B4. Each block processes the same feature map with a depthwise separable convolution branch and a multi-head self-attention branch and fuses them through a learned channel-wise convex gate with a residual connection. All baselines, including hierarchical vision transformers (Swin, Focal) and hybrid CNN-transformer models (CoAtNet, CvT, ConvNeXt, EdgeNeXt), are re-trained under one protocol. On PlantVillage (54,309 images, 38 classes), HTA-ConvNet attains 99.61% accuracy and 99.58% macro-F1. Because this benchmark is near-saturated, the main evidence comes from near-duplicate-controlled splits, multi-seed confidence intervals, and field data: zero-shot accuracy is 88.34% on PlantDoc (macro-averaged) and 82.47% on Plant Pathology 2020, and we quantify how far fine-tuning and domain adaptation close the remaining gap. Efficient-attention variants, uncertainty-based rejection, and error analyses quantify the cost, reliability, and failure modes of the design.

Article.Title: Semantic complexity estimation and price-based multi-agent negotiation reduce tail latency and energy in edge-cloud generative inference
Article.Authors: Chen T.; Zi B.; Rhee M.; Teng D.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Serving large language models across mobile devices and cloud servers is hard because the cost of a generative query cannot be read off its input: a short prompt may trigger thousands of decoding steps. Schedulers therefore commit resources before knowing what a query will cost, and in a shared network many congest one server at once. In MAGS, each device runs a small probe that forecasts a query’s token count and generation entropy before decoding begins, then bids for cloud capacity against a congestion price broadcast by the server, selecting its per-token privacy parameter in the same bid under a metric differential privacy mechanism with explicit clipping. Two design choices follow from measurement. Splicing an 8B model’s lower layers into a 70B model’s upper layers destroys accuracy even with a trained adapter (24.7% versus 82.4% Pass@1 on GSM8K), so activation exchange stays within one model and the larger model is reached by prompt-level offload; and because migrating a key-value cache costs between 2.0 and 16.0 MB per decoder layer, the partition is fixed at prefill. Randomising the packet header cuts an eavesdropper’s identification of the source corpus from 71.1 to 24.7%. Across ten seeds MAGS lowers 99th-percentile latency by 17.1% and energy per token by 13.6% against a reactive PPO baseline given identical observations, and raises throughput by 20.7%; hardware testbeds reproduce the latency gain to within 0.6 percentage points on a single device and cut the correlation between eight devices’ offload decisions from 0.41 to 0.08. Beyond roughly 500 devices per server performance converges to the local-execution bound; doubling server capacity moves that point by the same factor, placing the limit in the shared server rather than in the pricing rule or the learner.

Article.Title: Preliminary clinical evidence on the efficacy of topical cannabidiol in the management of myogenous temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Sobhy Y.; Elmaghraby S.; El-Din M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the current preliminary clinical efficacy of topical cannabidiol (CBD) in managing myogenous TMDs. A literature search was performed through MEDLINE (via PubMed), Scopus, Web of Science, and Clinical trial.gov databases. In addition to citation chasing of the included studies, focusing on studies published in English up to September 2026. This review was prospectively registered (Prospero, No. CRD420261293459). This systematic review was carried out independently by three researchers in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, utilizing both controlled vocabulary terms (such as MeSH) and free-text keywords related to Cannabidiol (e.g., “Cannabidiol,” “CBD,” or “Cannabis”). A modified PICOS framework was applied to address the research question: What evidence currently exists regarding the efficacy of Cannabidiol in managing myogenous temporomandibular disorders? Heterogeneity was evaluated through visual inspection of the forest plots and quantified using the I² and Chi-square tests, in case of heterogeneity, a random-effect model was used, otherwise a fixed-effect model was used. The pooled result was judged as heterogeneous when the Chi-square P-value was less than 0.1. A total of 744 records was identified through the preliminary search. After resolving 176 duplicates, 568 articles were included in the title and abstract screening phase, followed by the full-text screening phase. Finally, two studies were included in this review as they met the eligibility criteria. The two randomized studies included were assessed for risk of bias using the RoB 2 tool. Both studies demonstrated a low risk of bias across all domains. The overall effect of the VAS, righ sEMG, left sEMG, favored CBD with mean difference of -2.89 [-3.58, -2.21], -0.06 [-0.09, -0.04], -0.07 [-0.12, -0.02] respectively. The certainty of evidence for pain intensity, right and left masseter muscle activity was rated as low due to imprecision and indirectness. Topical CBD significantly reduced masseter muscle activity and pain intensity in myogenous TMD patients. However, the current evidence remains limited by the small number of studies and short follow-up periods. Further large-scale randomized clinical trials are required before routine clinical recommendation.

Article.Title: Robust depth–yaw control of autonomous underwater vehicles under disturbances and parametric uncertainties
Article.Authors: Eissa A.; Mohamed S.; Awad M.; Munim H.; Emad D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents a simulation-based comparative investigation of four control strategies for depth and yaw regulation of a nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) operating under external disturbances and parametric uncertainties. Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) control, Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control (ST-SMC), and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) are implemented within a unified MATLAB/Simulink framework and evaluated under three operating scenarios: nominal conditions, external ocean-current disturbances, and hydrodynamic parameter uncertainties. Controller parameters are held fixed across all scenarios to ensure a consistent comparison. Performance is assessed in terms of trajectory-tracking accuracy, root-mean-square error (RMSE), robustness, control effort, and computational execution time. The results show that ST-SMC provides the most consistent tracking performance among the four controllers. For depth regulation, ST-SMC achieves RMSE values of 0.0920 × 10⁻², 0.9903 × 10⁻², and 0.1819 × 10⁻² m under nominal, disturbed, and uncertain conditions, respectively, with corresponding yaw RMSE values of 0.0250 × 10⁻², 0.3276 × 10⁻², and 0.0270 × 10⁻² rad. These results indicate improved tracking accuracy and robustness relative to PID, FLC, and NMPC across the scenarios considered. Real-time computational performance was profiled at the common 1 ms sampling period used throughout the simulation campaign. PID exhibits the lowest computational cost, with an average execution time of 0.0011 ms per call. ST-SMC also shows very low computational demand, with an average execution time of 0.0142 ms, satisfying the 1 ms deadline in 99.903% of the 100,001 profiled samples. In contrast, FLC and NMPC require substantially higher computational effort, with average execution times of 11.37 ms and 11.0057 ms, respectively, exceeding the 1 ms deadline in all profiled samples; their practical deployment therefore presupposes slower control-update rates or more capable embedded hardware. All four controllers achieved a 100% feasible-solution rate throughout the simulation campaign. Overall, ST-SMC offers the most favorable balance between tracking accuracy, robustness, and computational cost among the investigated strategies, providing a consistent benchmark of the four control approaches within a unified simulation framework. As the reported computational measurements were obtained in a Software-in-the-Loop environment, further Hardware-in-the-Loop and experimental validation on physical AUV platforms is required to confirm real-time performance under operational conditions.

Article.Title: Multifunctional phenyl piperidinyl triazoles targeting cholinesterase: toward next-generation Alzheimer’s therapeutics
Article.Authors: Amjad H.; Rahman R.; Javed S.; Rehman A.; Nadeem M.; Zhao Y.; Zhu Y.; Zulfiqar H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with no disease-modifying therapy. Inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) remains a validated strategy for improving cognitive function. Here, nineteen piperidinyl-triazole derivatives ( 9a-9s ) were synthesized, characterized by IR and NMR spectroscopy, and evaluated as dual cholinesterase inhibitors against eserine. Most were active in the micromolar range. Compound 9h was the most effective AChE inhibitor (95.26 ± 1.12% inhibition; IC 50 18.24 ± 0.68 µM) and 9c the most active against BChE (84.51 ± 1.24%; IC 50 82.36 ± 1.15 µM), although both remain considerably less potent than eserine. Electron-donating para substituents on the propionamide-linked phenyl ring enhanced inhibition, whereas electron-withdrawing groups reduced it. Compound 9s was the most effective anti-biofilm agent against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus , and most derivatives caused negligible hemolysis of bovine erythrocytes, with 9j showing no detectable lysis. Density functional theory indicated stable frontier orbital gaps and favourable reactivity descriptors, and molecular docking placed the compounds within the catalytic and peripheral anionic sites of both enzymes. Predicted physicochemical, CNS-permeability and toxicity profiles were largely favourable. These results identify the piperidinyl-triazole scaffold as a starting point for the development of dual cholinesterase inhibitors.

Article.Title: Forecasting radial head arthroplasty in Germany through 2045
Article.Authors: Krane F.; Klug K.; Klug A.; Müller L.; Leschinger T.; Babasiz T.; Sarter M.; Leyendecker J.; Heck V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, we aim to estimate the expected growth in radial head arthroplasties (RA) in Germany through 2045. To do this, autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA), Error-Trend-Seasonality (ETS), and Poisson models were used to forecast trends in RA. Official data on demographics and procedures were used, provided by the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Statistisches Bundesamt). The models project an increase in the number of radial head arthroplasties through 2045. Specifically, the incidence rate is expected to increase by around 80% to 2.56 per 100,000 inhabitants by then. The projected total number of RA in 2045 is 2,098. Based on our projections, this increase is mainly driven by a rising number of male and female patients aged 65 years and older, leading to a 2.1-fold increase in procedures performed for these patients in 2045 compared with 2023. In total, radial head arthroplasties are projected to be performed approximately three times more often in women than in men, corresponding to a projected total number of 1,574 radial head arthroplasties for women and 524 for men in 2045. Our results emphasize the need to improve implant development, surgical expertise, and training in this specific procedure.

Article.Title: Transglutaminase 1 is conserved in amphibians and required for membrane-associated transglutaminase activity in the epidermis of clawed frogs
Article.Authors: Sachslehner A.; Christiaens A.; Carron M.; Steinbinder J.; Golabi B.; Vleminckx K.; Eckhart L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transglutaminase 1 (TGM1) plays a central role in the cross-linking of proteins during the cornification of the epidermis in mammals. Mutations of human TGM1 lead to TGM1-nonsyndromic epidermal differentiation disorder (TGM1-nEDD), and the deletion of Tgm1 is lethal in the mouse. Here, we investigated whether the role of TGM1 is conserved in the western clawed frog ( Xenopus tropicalis ), a model species for amphibians. We found that a tgm1 gene is conserved in the three main clades of amphibians, namely anurans, caudates and caecilians. The amino acid residues implicated in catalytic activity and palmitoylation-dependent membrane anchorage are conserved in amphibian Tgm1 proteins. tgm1 is expressed besides multiple homologs of tgm3 in the skin of X. tropicalis . CRISPR-Cas9-mediated disruption of tgm1 abolished the cell membrane-associated TGM activity in the epidermis of X. tropicalis . In contrast to mosaic mutants and heterozygous mutants of tgm1 , compound heterozygous frogs carrying two predicted loss-of-function alleles of tgm1 died around metamorphosis. In conclusion, Tgm1 is catalytically active at keratinocyte cell membranes during epidermal cornification of X. tropicalis . The conservation of this role of Tgm1 in frogs and mammals supports the hypothesis that Tgm1-dependent cornification evolved in a common ancestor of amphibians and amniotes.

Article.Title: d-Phenothrin exposure alters protein abundance in human HaCaT keratinocytes
Article.Authors: Kwon Y.; Kim H.; Lee S.; Ryu S.; Park D.; Park C.; Hyun M.; Park D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract d-Phenothrin is a type I pyrethroid insecticide widely used in household and public-health applications; however, its effects on protein abundance in human keratinocytes remain poorly characterized. We used label-free quantitative proteomics to characterize abundance changes in HaCaT keratinocytes exposed to nominal d-phenothrin concentrations of 0.05 and 0.1 mg/mL for 24 h. Proteomic profiling yielded 1987 proteins, and differential abundance analysis identified 216 unique proteins across the two treatment-versus-control comparisons. MTT reduction decreased with increasing exposure concentration. At 0.1 mg/mL, the mitochondrial respiratory proteins NDUFS1, NDUFV1, and SDHA showed lower abundance, whereas the molecular chaperone HSPA6, the proteostasis-associated protein SQSTM1, and the cell-death-associated protein CASP8 showed higher abundance. Functional enrichment analysis of the 216 proteins identified terms related to RNA processing and cell-cycle regulation. Concentration-response classification further distinguished monotonic, concentration-specific, and reversed abundance patterns. Together, these findings define a proteomic response involving mitochondrial metabolism, proteostasis, and genome maintenance, providing a molecular basis for investigating the effects of d-phenothrin in human keratinocytes.

Article.Title: Co-infection with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus and Rickettsia monacensis in Korea
Article.Authors: Chatterjee S.; Kim C.; Kim D.; Seo J.; Kim D.; Yun N.; Jung S.; Kim U.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Kim E.; Hur J.; Kim Y.; Jeong H.; Heo J.; Lee H.; Park S.; Kwak Y.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) and Rickettsia monacensis , transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicornis and Ixodes spp. ticks respectively, are endemic to East Asia and can cause overlapping febrile illnesses. Despite their shared ecological niches, co-infections remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the prevalence of R. monacensis co-infection in patients with SFTS in Korea using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and sequencing. Clinical samples were collected from 129 patients with SFTS. One-step reverse-transcription PCR was performed to identify the SFTS virus (SFTSV), and rickettsial nested PCR testing targeted outer membrane protein A ( ompA) . Phylogenetic analysis was conducted to confirm the evolutionary relationships among the different species. Among the 129 SFTS cases, nine patients with SFTSV were positive for R. monacensis , with a prevalence rate of 7.9%. Phylogenetic tree analysis revealed that the seven sequences identified in the present study clustered closely with R. monacensis. This is the first study wherein 7.9% of patients suspected of having SFTS were also found to be co-infected with R. monacensis based on molecular testing. We believe that these findings highlight the need for the differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illnesses and raise awareness of the potential co-infection impacts on disease severity and management.

Article.Title: Computational analysis links methylparaben responses in colonic cell models to MAOB and Hippo/Wnt signaling
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Deng Y.
Article.Abstract: Methylparaben (MP) is a widely used preservative in personal care products, foods, and pharmaceuticals, resulting in widespread human exposure through dermal contact, dietary intake, and pharmaceutical use. Although the gastrointestinal tract represents a major site of MP absorption following oral exposure, its effects on colonic epithelial homeostasis and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. We employed an integrative approach combining network toxicology, bulk transcriptomic analysis ( N = 685 from four GEO datasets), weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), systematic evaluation of 101 machine-learning strategies, molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and single-cell transcriptomic analysis (GSE132465, 33 samples) to investigate MP-associated molecular alterations in colorectal cancer (CRC). The biological effects of MP were further evaluated in normal human colonic epithelial NCM460 cells and colorectal cancer RKO cells using colony formation, wound-healing, and Transwell assays. MP exposure reduced colony formation, wound closure, and invasion in NCM460 cells, whereas the opposite responses were observed in RKO colorectal cancer cells under the tested in vitro conditions. Integration of computationally predicted MP targets with CRC-associated transcriptomic alterations identified 52 overlapping candidate genes. Among 101 machine-learning strategies, the LASSO–Random Forest (LASSO–RF) model showed the best predictive performance for CRC classification and identified six feature genes, including monoamine oxidase B (MAOB), which emerged as a candidate molecular feature. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations suggested a potentially stable binding conformation of MP within the MAOB catalytic pocket. Single-cell analysis revealed relatively higher MAOB expression in normal colonic epithelial cells than in inferred aneuploid malignant cells. In silico MAOB perturbation further suggested associations between MAOB-related transcriptional changes and Hippo/Wnt-associated signaling pathways. MP exposure was associated with distinct phenotypic responses in non-transformed colonic epithelial cells and colorectal cancer cells under the tested in vitro conditions. Integrative computational analyses identified MAOB and Hippo/Wnt-associated signaling as candidate molecular features for further investigation. However, the proposed molecular relationships remain hypothetical, and their causal roles in MP-associated cellular responses require direct experimental validation.

Article.Title: Entropy-resolved q-rung orthopair hypergraph diffusion enables robust structural sensor fusion
Article.Authors: Yogeesh N.; Almakki M.; Ganati G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Higher-order sensor groups and incomplete reliability evidence are usually modelled separately, preventing unified analysis of topology, ambiguity and adversarial corruption. This study introduces entropy-resolved q-rung orthopair hypergraph diffusion (ER-qROHD). Residual q-power mass and binary entropy define evidence-gated incidences. The resulting transition is row-stochastic, reversible and similar to a positive-semidefinite matrix. An anchored iteration has a unique fixed point, geometric convergence and a strictly convex energy representation. Median-centred clipping yields bounded contamination influence. An operator-specific Green-kernel analysis further partitions source influence, proves distance-decaying locality and certifies perturbations on specified sensor subsets. In a fully specified 12-sensor synthetic computational benchmark with 400 replicates per missingness condition, ER-qROHD achieved the lowest reconstruction error from 0 to 40% missingness. At 20% missingness, RMSE was 0.219 versus 0.288 for crisp diffusion and 0.385 for median-filled observations; the paired crisp reduction was 0.069 (95% interval 0.065–0.073). Ablation attributed the material gain to clipping and evidence-weighted transport; removing residual allocation changed RMSE by only + 0.0001 and removing the entropy penalty by -0.0003, so this benchmark does not identify an independent entropy benefit. A 20-cell stress analysis identified attack multiplicity as the dominant degradation mechanism; at four attacks RMSE rose to 0.2756–0.2831, while q-entropy sensitivity changed RMSE by only 0.30%. Primary benchmark data, numerical results and executable code are included, with an accompanying deterministic script for the added validation. Additional 24- and 48-sensor synthetic tests covered two hypergraph structures, clustered missingness, altered attack magnitude, ambiguity-enriched evidence, and graph-Tikhonov and Huber-graph baselines. The study still uses fixed synthetic topologies and edge weights, random-sign attacks with at most four attacked sensors, and no physical SHM data; the median guarantee requires fewer than half of the observed values to be contaminated, and paired intervals quantify computational replicates rather than population uncertainty.

Article.Title: Grey epistemic-trust QUALIFLEX framework for software platform vendor selection under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Esangbedo M.
Article.Abstract: Virtual industry-education collaboration platform procurement requires combining judgments from stakeholders whose expertise varies by criterion while retaining bounded uncertainty in both criterion importance and vendor performance. This study develops a grey-epistemic-trust (GET) weighting rule and integrates it with the established permutation-based Grey–QUALIFLEX ranking procedure. GET operationalizes epistemic reliability using three observable signals: criterion-specific domain-expertise rating, experience-based credibility proxy, and interval-width confidence proxy. The conjunctive product determines criterion-specific decision-maker influence. The empirical case contains six vendors, 18 criteria, and eight decision-makers. Interval grey importance assessments were elicited directly on a 0–10 scale; vendor performance was rated individually on a 0–100 scale and aggregated into group interval grey performance values using the observed minimum and maximum ratings after restoring canonical vendor identities. The analysis identifies the fourth vendor ( \(A_4\) ) as the top-ranked alternative and the fifth vendor ( \(A_5\) ) as the lowest-ranked alternative, with \(\textrm{Net}(A_4)=2.431\) and \(\Phi (\pi ^*)=5.210\) . Weighting ablation shows that the empirical ordering is stable across GET, equal, midpoint-mean, grey-geometric, and domain-expertise-only weights. To evaluate decision quality beyond rank correlation, a fixed-seed 1000-replication controlled experiment with known latent weights and oracle rankings was added. Under a reliability-aligned data-generating regime, GET reduced mean absolute weight-recovery error from 0.0037 (midpoint mean) to 0.0030 and increased oracle top-choice agreement from 93.5 to 95.0%; under a reliability-neutral regime, midpoint averaging performed better, showing that GET’s advantage is conditional rather than universal. This study contributes a transparent reliability-weighting mechanism, a reproducible grey outranking integration, and an empirical vendor-selection application.

Article.Title: A super learner ensemble machine learning model with SHAP-based explanations for pneumonia detection based on routine hematological markers
Article.Authors: Xu J.; Yang C.; Chen L.; Xu F.; Chen J.; Qin Y.
Article.Abstract: Low-cost and accessible tools for preliminary pneumonia screening remain particularly important in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a machine-learning model with post-hoc SHAP-based explanations using routine hematological markers to distinguish patients with pneumonia from healthy controls. We retrospectively analyzed data from 4,389 participants, including 1,671 patients with pneumonia and 2,718 healthy controls, from two medical centers. The cohort was partitioned at the patient level into training, validation, and held-out testing sets. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used for initial feature reduction, after which 15 candidate machine-learning base learners were developed, tuned, and evaluated. Four class-balancing strategies—synthetic minority oversampling technique, random oversampling, random undersampling, and random over-sampling examples—were compared within the training workflow in terms of feature-distribution preservation and downstream predictive performance. Entropy-weighted TOPSIS was used to rank the base learners, and TOPSIS-weighted averaging, stacking, and Super Learner strategies were compared across progressively expanded combinations of top-ranked learners. An outer five-fold cross-validation analysis was performed to assess robustness. Model performance was further evaluated using calibration and decision curve analyses, while post-hoc model explanations were generated using SHapley Additive exPlanations and a SHAP-informed surrogate nomogram. Synthetic minority oversampling technique showed the strongest overall downstream performance and was retained for the final modelling workflow. Among the candidate ensemble strategies, the Super Learner with a random forest meta-learner achieved the highest validation AUC of 0.9749 and was selected as the final model. On the held-out testing set, the final model achieved an AUC of 0.9822 (95% CI, 0.9744–0.9891), accuracy of 0.9431 (95% CI, 0.9282–0.9579), sensitivity of 0.9401 (95% CI, 0.9143–0.9641), specificity of 0.9449 (95% CI, 0.9253–0.9631), positive predictive value of 0.9128, negative predictive value of 0.9625, F1-score of 0.9263, and Brier score of 0.0450 (95% CI, 0.0360–0.0549) at the Youden-index-derived threshold of 0.50. In outer five-fold cross-validation, the prespecified final workflow achieved a mean AUC of 0.9612 ± 0.0077 and an accuracy of 0.9071 ± 0.0172. SHAP analysis identified mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration, lymphocyte percentage, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, platelet distribution width, and mean platelet volume as the most influential predictors. The Super Learner demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration for distinguishing patients with pneumonia from healthy controls using routinely available hematological markers. The model may provide a low-cost tool for preliminary pneumonia screening and risk stratification in resource-limited settings. However, because the comparator group consisted of healthy controls, prospective validation in symptomatic patients with clinically relevant non-pneumonia respiratory or inflammatory conditions is required before the model can be applied to differential diagnosis.

Article.Title: Knowledge distillation with lightweight peer branches for learning diverse representations
Article.Authors: Kim D.; Pyo S.; Go J.; Ryu J.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a novel online knowledge distillation framework that enables various vision models to generate and transfer knowledge from multiple perspectives using only lightweight additional networks. Previous online distillation studies have focused on a self-guided paradigm without pre-trained teacher models, aiming to generate and transfer new knowledge on their own. However, they suffer from several limitations arising from duplicating portions of the backbone stages to create peer branches for self-guided distillation, including high computational overhead and redundant representations. To address these issues, we propose a method that creates multiple lightweight peer branches on a single shared peer stage instead of duplicating backbone stages for each branch, and introduces a learning algorithm that encourages the peer branches to produce distinct prediction distributions, thereby increasing the diversity of the knowledge transferred to the backbone network. As a result, the backbone network can effectively learn from the diverse predictions of the peer branches while using fewer additional resources than existing multi-view distillation methods, and the peer branches are removed during inference, preserving the original model’s inference speed. Moreover, unlike previous studies that mainly demonstrated improvements on basic models such as ResNet, we validate the effectiveness of our approach on modern architectures such as ConvNeXt and CSWin.

Article.Title: Integrated computational biology approaches provide insights into the potential mechanisms underlying arrhythmias induced by anthraquinone-related antitumor drugs
Article.Authors: Meng J.; Su X.; Yu L.; Meng X.; Yang Y.; Cheng A.; Zhang C.; Li X.; Li S.; Liu B.; Wang Z.; Shan P.; Ding K.; Chu Y.; Hu Y.; Hu X.
Article.Abstract: Despite the significant cardiac toxicity and arrhythmia-inducing potential of anthraquinone-related antitumor drugs (including anthracyclines and anthracenediones) in clinical practice, the underlying common systemic molecular mechanisms remain unknown. Therefore, this study aims to systematically elucidate the multi-target and multi-pathway arrhythmogenic mechanisms of seven representative drugs, with the expectation of providing theoretical support for safe clinical use and the development of related toxicity intervention strategies. This study first employed network toxicology techniques to screen out potential arrhythmogenic targets of seven representative drugs from databases such as PubChem, Novo Pro, and SwissTargetPrediction. Subsequently, based on the STRING database and with the aid of Cytoscape 3.10.1, protein-protein interaction networks and a multi-dimensional “arrhythmia-drug-target” network were constructed. Further, GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were conducted to explain the toxicity-related biological processes and key signaling pathways, and their roles in immune infiltration were explored. Finally, molecular docking was used to assess the potential binding interactions between drugs and core targets. Two drug–SRC complexes were selected for further molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate the stability. Combined with ADMET assessment, these computational analyses provide a comprehensive and hypothesis-generating assessment of the potential toxicological profiles and underlying mechanisms of anthraquinone-related antitumor drugs. Through network pharmacology, 195 potential toxicity targets (such as AKT1, SRC, TNF, TP53) were identified, and they were significantly enriched in key signaling pathways such as PI3K-Akt and MicroRNAs in cancer. Immune infiltration analysis further suggested that this process might be related to the regulation of immune cells such as Mast cells activated, T cells CD8 and B cells memory. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions between the drugs and the core target, while dynamic simulations further evaluated the stability of the SRC complex of the two selected drugs. Finally, ADMET predictions indicated that Mitoxantrone and Losoxantrone might block the cardiac hERG potassium channel, prolong the QT interval, and thereby may contribute to arrhythmia. This study provides insights into the potential mechanisms by which anthraquinone-related antitumor drugs induce arrhythmias.

Article.Title: Cation distribution effect in spinel (Mg1−xFex)[MgxFe2−x]O4: a density functional theory study
Article.Authors: Alavisadr S.
Article.Abstract: The structural, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of MgFe 2 O 4 were investigated using density functional theory. To reconcile the discrepancy between experimental reports favoring an inverse spinel structure and prior theoretical studies focused mainly on the normal spinel configuration, we modeled (Mg 1−x Fe x )[Mg x Fe 2−x ]O 4 in normal ( x = 0), mixed ( x = 0.5), and inverse ( x = 1.0) states. The GGA + U approximation, with an optimal Hubbard parameter of U = 6.5 eV, was employed to correct the band-gap underestimation typical of standard DFT. Structural optimization identified the ferromagnetic inverse spinel phase as the thermodynamic ground state, with a calculated equilibrium lattice parameter ( a = 8.3410 Å) showing better agreement with experiment than previously reported theoretical values. Within GGA + U scheme, all three configurations exhibit semiconducting behavior with direct band gaps of 1.83, 1.68, and 1.87 eV for the normal, mixed, and inverse structures, respectively, consistent with experimental data. The total magnetic moment remains constant at 10.0µ B across all cation distributions. Charge-density analysis reveals pronounced covalent character in Fe–O bonds, arising from Fe(d)–O(p) hybridization, while Mg–O bonds are predominantly ionic. The optical properties reveal significant optical activity within the visible-to-ultraviolet (UV) spectrum, highlighting the potential of MgFe 2 O 4 for photocatalytic and optoelectronic applications.

Article.Title: Development of a modular light-up aptamer platform for selective fluorescence detection of chloramphenicol
Article.Authors: Sai L.; Nguyen T.; Nguyen T.; Van Nguyen K.; Pham H.; Vu D.; Nguyen M.; Chu T.; Pham T.; Pham B.
Article.Abstract: Chloramphenicol (CAP) is banned in food-producing animals, yet illicit use persists in aquaculture, where LC-MS/MS confirmation is too costly for routine screening. We report a label-free light-up aptamer sensor, S-CAP (Sulforhodamine B-reporting chloramphenicol aptamer): a single unmodified DNA strand carries a CAP-binding module, a Sulforhodamine B (SRhB)-binding signaling module, and an engineered transducer stem, so CAP binding raises SRhB emission without label, quencher, nanomaterial, or enzyme. Stem length and G/C content were varied systematically to select the transducer, and circular dichroism together with a Stem-1 mutant retaining only about one third of the response showed that the signal depends on that transducer rather than on a generic folding event. Fitting the fluorescence titration with a binding model that accounts for ligand depletion at the 2.5 µM aptamer concentration used gives an apparent dissociation constant of 1.27 ± 0.13 µM after 30 min at 25 °C, which together with a docking estimate of 6.2 µM and the 9.8 µM reported calorimetrically for the parent CAP1 aptamer places the interaction in the low micromolar range. With 2.5 µM aptamer the response was linear from 16.2 to 646 µg/L CAP (0.05 to 2 µM), with a detection limit of 4.4 µg/L and a quantification limit of 14.7 µg/L. Recoveries were 91.2 to 107.4% (RSD below 9%) across three aquaculture water samples, three shrimp samples and one human serum sample, and results agreed with LC-MS/MS to within ± 8%.

Article.Title: Effects of repeated ice massage, percussive massage, and combined recovery on 72-h calf muscle–tendon recovery after eccentric exercise in recreational runners: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Ryszkiel I.; Pilis K.; Stanek A.; Olchowy C.; Bjelica D.; Trybulski R.
Article.Abstract: To compare the short-term effects of repeated ice massage, percussive massage, combined ice-plus-percussive recovery, and passive recovery during the 72 h after eccentric calf exercise in recreational runners. The active interventions were initiated immediately after exercise and repeated twice daily, providing seven treatment sessions over 72 h. Recovery was analyzed using repeated-measures models and Holm-adjusted contrasts. All participants completed follow-up. Muscle soreness decreased more from immediately post-exercise to 72 h after active recovery than passive recovery (− 1.20 to − 1.35 points; all adjusted p < 0.001). Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of base editor sgRNA fitness score
Article.Authors: Orro A.; Consiglio A.; Curci M.; Scichilone M.; Hasin F.; Minervini M.; Mencar C.; De Bellis G.; Cocola C.; Pelucchi P.; Selmi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pooled CRISPR base-editing screens enable the functional assessment of large numbers of genetic variants at scale. Predicting whether a selected sgRNA-Base Editor combination will produce a robust fitness effect could support sgRNA prioritisation and reveal features that are transferrable across screening experiments. However, this remains challenging due to the number of molecular and biological events taking place in a screening experiment. Here we investigated whether sgRNA fitness effect can be predicted by Machine Learning from a set of biological and sequence-specific features using a published Base Editing screening dataset. Decision Tree based models showed AUC-ROC ranging from 87 to 94% and AU-PR ranging from 53 to 75% using a gene-held out validation. Feature interpretability analysis revealed that sgRNA sequence, in particular PAM-proximal nucleotides, were the most predictive features. Gene essentiality and Predicted Variant Effect also carried predictive weight albeit to a more marginal extent. Analysis of matched Cas9 and base-editing data further identified gene essentiality as the feature most strongly associated with the different fitness score among base editing and Cas9. Our results confirm the feasibility of predicting fitness effect of a selected base editor-sgRNA combination using sequence as the primary feature, opening the way for future studies to incorporate additional biological features to enhance model interpretability and transferability.

Article.Title: Towards automated multilingual autobiographical interview scoring: a machine translation approach
Article.Authors: Groer G.; Külpmann A.; Zlomuzica A.; Plank L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Autobiographical Interview (AI) is one of the most used method for quantifying episodic memory from memory narratives. Its manual scoring, however, is limited and demands considerable time and effort. These issues have been recently addressed by the use of natural language processing (NLP) allowing for automatic, unbiased and less time-consuming scoring of memory performance in the context of the AI. Since existing NLP models for AI analysis are primarily designed for English narratives, this study investigated whether machine translation could enable their effective use on German narratives without significantly reducing classification capability. We evaluated model performance on a total of 1920 German narratives generated by 258 individuals across two datasets. We further provided an open-source analysis code. We demonstrate that correlations between predicted and manually rated internal and external details were highly significant and comparable to existing studies performed with English narratives. Machine translation of German narratives allows for high classification performance and low frequency of misclassification without a meaningful impairment of model performance compared to English narratives. We observed no performance differences across translation models, indicating lightweight models perform equally well. Our findings support the use of NLP as an alternative cost- and time-efficient approach for automated AI scoring in non-English-speaking populations. Our results highlight the potential of language models for large-scale memory research across languages. We conclude that NLP enables more detailed analyses of episodic memory narratives beyond traditional manual scoring.

Article.Title: Repurposing expired Colistin as a sustainable corrosion inhibitor for API 5CT P110 steel tubing in hydrochloric acid medium
Article.Authors: Motawea M.; Elabbasy H.; Al-Subaie N.; Shanab M.; Younes A.; Satti A.; Daoub R.; Atia M.
Article.Abstract: Corrosion causes extensive damage to property, human life, and the environment, underscoring the urgent need for effective prevention. Hence, eco-friendly inhibitors are essential. Green corrosion inhibitors present a viable alternative, and their importance is growing from both environmental and economic standpoints. Expired Colistin Drug (ECLD) was evaluated as a green corrosion inhibitor for API 5CT P110 Steel Tubing (CS-​P110) in 1 M HCl solution. Its inhibitory performance was assessed using multiple techniques, including gravimetric mass reduction (MR) measurements and electrochemical techniques, including potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and surface characterization methods such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX), and atomic force microscopy (AFM). The inhibition efficiency (IE%) increased with increasing inhibitor concentration and decreased with increasing temperature, reaching a maximum of 97.1% at 50 ppm from WL measurements at 298 K. Electrochemical analysis revealed increased charge-transfer resistance (from 19 to 540 Ω·cm 2 ) and reduced corrosion current density, consistent with mixed-type inhibition. The adsorption behavior was best described by the Langmuir adsorption isotherm, while the calculated thermodynamic parameters, ΔG ads values ranged from (− 24.4 to − 26.6 kJ·mol⁻ 1 , indicative of physical and chemical adsorption, with mainly physisorption, Moreover, Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirmed the strong adsorption affinity of the ECLD derivatives toward the Fe (1 1 0) surface. Overall, the chemical and electrochemical findings were in good agreement, providing strong evidence that ECLD forms a protective layer on the steel surface, thereby reducing the corrosion rate of CS-P110 in acidic medium.

Article.Authors: Alshammari S.; Alghamdi B.

The results indicate that performance expectancy (PE) and effort expectancy (EE) significantly predict CTAI, while CTAI significantly predicts behavioral intention (BI). However, the direct effects of PE and EE on BI are not significant. Mediation analysis using bootstrapping reveals that CTAI fully mediates the relationship between PE and BI, whereas the indirect effect of EE on BI is not significant. These findings suggest that students’ perceptions of performance benefits are associated with their behavioral intention to use ChatGPT through confidence and trust in AI, whereas this mediating mechanism was not supported for effort expectancy. The study contributes to technology acceptance research by conceptualizing CTAI as an integrative higher-order construct and providing initial empirical evidence of its mediating role specifically in the relationship between performance expectancy and behavioral intention.

Article.Title: Does land transfer-in promote pesticide reduction? Evidence from Chinese rice farmers
Article.Authors: Yan A.; Luo B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pesticide reduction is an important means of achieving sustainable agricultural development and promoting the green and low-carbon transformation of agriculture. Previous studies have generally emphasized the pesticide-reduction effects of farm scale and land transfer, but differences in the pesticide-reduction potential of different land transfer-in models have not been fully explored. Using survey data from 1,130 rice farmers in China, this study examined the effects of land transfer-in, including decentralized and contiguous transfer-in, on pesticide use and further analyzed the mechanisms and heterogeneity underlying the effects of contiguous land transfer-in. The results showed that, first, different modes of land transfer-in had significantly different effects on farmers’ pesticide use. Contiguous land transfer-in significantly reduced pesticide use, whereas decentralized land transfer-in was associated with an increasing trend in pesticide use. Second, the pesticide-reduction effect of contiguous land transfer-in was more pronounced among farmers who signed written land transfer contracts, those operating on a large scale, and lower transaction cost groups. Third, the mechanism analysis showed that contiguous land transfer-in primarily reduced pesticide use by changing farmers’ pesticide application methods and regulating their pesticide-use behavior. Therefore, government departments should fully realize the pesticide-reduction potential of contiguous land transfer-in by promoting contiguous land transfer, standardizing land transfer contracts, cultivating large-scale farm operators, and improving pesticide application technologies, thereby contributing to the achievement of pesticide-reduction targets.

Article.Authors: Delshad B.; Lindberg E.; Andersson A.; Blomberg A.; Engvall J.; Eriksson M.; Grote L.; Hedner J.; Holmgren E.; Janson C.; Malinovschi A.; Mannila M.; Prakash A.; Sköld M.; Spaak J.; Tanash H.; Ulander M.; Zaigham S.; Zhou X.; Zou D.; Franklin K.; Ljunggren M.

Long sleep showed stronger inverse associations: FEV₁ % predicted (− 1.82; −2.68 to − 0.96), FVC % predicted (− 1.21; −2.01 to − 0.40) and D LCO % predicted (− 2.71; −3.62 to − 1.79). DIS was associated with lower FEV₁ % predicted (− 0.74; −1.21 to − 0.27) and D LCO % predicted (− 2.19; −2.69 to − 1.70), and with higher odds of CAL (OR 1.22; 95% CI 1.09 to 1.37). Article.Title: Cortical proteomic alterations and exploratory glycopeptide profiling of Parkinson’s disease frontal cortex
Article.Authors: Daramola O.; Fowowe M.; Nwaiwu J.; Adeniyi M.; Solomon J.; Galbreath D.; Bennett A.; Mechref Y.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by complex molecular alterations involving changes in protein abundance, cellular pathways, and post-translational regulation. However, molecular changes associated with PD pathology in cortical regions remain incompletely characterized. Here, we performed global proteomic profiling of post-mortem frontal cortex tissue from individuals with PD and neurologically normal controls. As a complementary exploratory analysis, detected glycopeptides were evaluated to identify candidate glycosylation-associated features associated with PD. Global proteomic analysis identified 73 significantly altered proteins following covariate adjustment and multiple-testing correction, with affected proteins associated with mitochondrial energy metabolism, intracellular signaling, cytoskeletal organization, and neuronal structure. Exploratory glycopeptide profiling identified a limited subset of altered glycosylation-associated features. Candidate glycosylation-associated differences were observed among glycopeptides assigned to extracellular matrix and synaptic-associated proteins, including Versican, Neurocan, and Plasma Membrane Calcium-Transporting ATPase 2. Integration of proteomic and exploratory glycopeptide profiling identified candidate molecular changes that warrant validation using dedicated glycoproteomics workflows. Limited overlap between protein abundance alterations and glycopeptide-level observations suggest that glycosylation-associated changes may involve regulatory mechanisms beyond protein expression differences. Collectively, these findings define proteomic alterations associated with PD frontal cortex pathology and provide preliminary insights into glycosylation-associated features that require validation in larger cohorts using dedicated glycoproteomics approaches.

Article.Title: Antigenicity in mice of multiple antigen peptides containing B-cell/T-cell epitopes of the Neisseria gonorrhoeae MafA 2/3 protein
Article.Authors: Girgis M.; de Oliveira D.; Kant R.; McCormick C.; Machado-de-Avila R.; Christodoulides M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract There are no prophylactic vaccines for the sexually transmitted disease gonorrhoea, caused by infection with the Gram-negative pathogen Neisseria gonorrhoeae . In this pilot study, we examined the antigenicity in mice of two synthetic multiple antigen peptides (MAP) containing B- and T-cell epitopes of the MafA 2/3 outer membrane protein. The B- and T-cell epitopes were identified in silico and synthetic MAP octamer peptides synthesized. The peptides were docked in silico with mouse and human MHC II complexes to examine binding properties. Mice were immunized with MafA 2/3-MAP-A and MafA 2/3-MAP-B peptides with different adjuvants. Antisera were tested in ELISA against homologous and heterologous MAP peptides, against recombinant MafA 2/3 protein and outer membranes (OM) from strain P9-17, and two other strains (FA1090 and 12CFX_T_039; AR205). Antisera were also examined by flow cytometry against whole bacteria, and for their ability to induce complement-mediated killing of gonococci. Our data generated showed that immunization with MafA 2/3 MAP-A and MAP-B in saline, on alum and in SAS and TitreMax emulsions induced antibodies that reacted with peptides and OM in ELISA but showed low levels of binding to whole bacteria in flow cytometry. Antibodies were of the IgG1 subclass and weak bactericidal activity was observed only with anti-MAP-A sera against strain P9-17 (50% titres of 4), and not against the two other strains. Thus, MafA 2/3 MAP peptides were antigenic in mice, and this synthetic approach joins a limited list of previous attempts to create experimental epitope-based gonococcal vaccines. The ability to induce functional, albeit weak antibody responses, merits their further development.

Article.Title: Exploratory derivation of a clinicoradiologic model for splanchnic vein thrombosis in acute pancreatitis
Article.Authors: Xiang H.; Che J.; Wang C.; Lv J.; Jiang H.; Tao Y.; Fang Z.; Chen Z.; Yang X.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: To derive and internally evaluate an exploratory clinicoradiologic model for splanchnic vein thrombosis (SVT) detected on index contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) in acute pancreatitis (AP), and to assess its association with pancreatic necrosis volume (PNV). This single-center retrospective study included 360 adults with AP. Non-contrast CT (NCCT) preceded index CECT in all patients. SVT detected on index CECT was considered prevalent rather than incident. A ten-predictor elastic-net logistic model was evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. Its performance was compared with PNV-only models using ordinal and nominal coding. Among 360 patients (276 men; median age, 41 years [IQR, 34–50]), 47 (13.1%) had SVT. The ten-predictor model achieved an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI 0.679–0.838; bootstrap-corrected AUC, 0.762) and a Brier score of 0.099. At a training-derived threshold of 0.14, mean sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 0.66, 0.77, 0.31, and 0.94, respectively, with 15.9 missed SVT events per 360-patient validation repeat. Across matched folds, mean AUCs were 0.772 for the ten-predictor model and 0.763 for ordinal PNV-only (paired ΔAUC, 0.009; 95% CI − 0.027 to 0.046; P = 0.608). With nominal PNV coding, the paired ΔAUC was 0.013 (95% CI − 0.027 to 0.053; P = 0.510). Brier scores and decision-curve net benefit were similar, whereas mean average precision was higher for the ten-predictor model under both codings (ΔAP, 0.074 and 0.089; unadjusted secondary P = 0.006 for both). The ten-predictor model showed moderate internal discrimination but no clear advantage over PNV-only models in AUC, Brier score, or decision-curve net benefit. Higher average precision is hypothesis-generating. Independent validation is required before clinical application. In this exploratory cohort, PNV was associated with SVT detected on index CECT. Its descriptive discrimination was higher than that of the recorded composite imaging scores, but this finding does not establish clinical superiority. The results are hypothesis-generating and require independent validation.

Article.Title: Delayed radiation-induced epigenetic remodeling is associated with enhanced somatic cell reprogramming
Article.Authors: Kang M.; Park H.; Lee J.; Jang H.; Yoo K.; Kim J.; Jang W.; Park S.; Lee S.; Kim J.; Choi S.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Ionizing radiation triggers targeted responses in directly irradiated cells and non-targeted responses in several cell generations after the initial exposure. A delayed non-targeted response to radiation enhances the efficiency of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) generation. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated the molecular mechanisms by which delayed radiation responses enhance somatic cell reprogramming. Fibroblasts irradiated with 5 Gy exhibited phenotypic recovery, including cell proliferation and altered global histone modifications. Transcriptomic profiling revealed distinct gene expression signatures in post-irradiated cells, including the upregulation of proliferation-related secreted factors, such as growth/differentiation factor 5 (GDF5), WNT1-inducible signaling pathway protein 1 (WISP1/CCN4), and interleukin-34 (IL34). Integrative analysis of RNA-seq and chromatin modifications further demonstrated the enrichment of activation-associated histone marks at the promoters of CCN4 and IL34, indicating radiation-induced epigenetic remodeling. Functionally, exogenous recombinant CCN4 or IL34 enhanced iPSC generation efficiency, producing cells with the typical characteristics of pluripotent stem cells, including trilineage differentiation capacity. Moreover, iPSC (rCCN4) displayed higher differentiation efficiency toward the endodermal lineage than iPSC (control) and iPSC (rIL34). Together, these findings suggest that delayed radiation responses are associated with an epigenetically altered cellular state and increased expression of secretory factors that may contribute to enhanced susceptibility to somatic cell reprogramming.

Article.Title: Analytical formulation and dynamic response investigation of a 3D vehicle-pavement-bridge coupled system
Article.Authors: Ren J.; Qiu H.; Li S.; Wang L.; Qin Z.
Article.Abstract: The three-dimensional vehicle-pavement-bridge coupled system (3D-VPBS) exhibits significant coupling and time-varying characteristics. Constructing a refined vehicle-bridge coupled system model is crucial for enhancing the accuracy of dynamic interaction simulations between vehicles and bridges. In this study, an analytical model of the 3D-VPBS is developed to investigate its dynamic response. A two-axle full-vehicle model with seven degrees of freedom is adopted to represent the vehicle, the bridge is modeled as a simply supported Kirchhoff plate, and the pavement layer is characterized by a continuous distribution of springs and dampers. The vehicle’s suspension and wheel systems are modeled using spring-damper elements, and the connection between the bridge and pavement layer is also represented by spring-damper components. Correlated left- and right-wheel road surface irregularities are introduced as external excitations to the system. The equations of motion are derived using D’Alembert’s principle and Kirchhoff plate theory and solved numerically via the Newmark-β method. Based on the proposed model, the effects of pavement layer properties, vehicle speed, traffic lane position, and road surface roughness on the dynamic behavior of the 3D-VPBS are systematically analyzed. The results indicate that incorporating the pavement layer effectively reduces the dynamic response of the vehicle body and enhances ride comfort. An increase in vehicle speed leads to intensified system responses and deteriorated ride quality. The traffic lane position has an impact on the partial dynamic responses of the system, with the maximum vibration occurring when the vehicle travels along the driving lane. Additionally, road surface roughness has a pronounced effect on vehicle dynamics, with deteriorating surface conditions resulting in amplified vehicle responses and reduced ride comfort.

Article.Title: Design and implementation of a tube nonlinear model predictive controller for quadcopter trajectory tracking
Article.Authors: Kahrizi M.; Kamali P.; Nikoofard A.
Article.Abstract: Trajectory tracking of quadrotors is conventionally addressed by a range of control strategies, including cascade Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) loops, linear Model Predictive Control (MPC) designed around a hover-linearized model, feedback linearization, sliding-mode control, and nominal nonlinear MPC (NLMPC). Each of these approaches, however, suffers from inherent limitations: linear schemes lose accuracy under aggressive maneuvers, large attitude excursions, and strong nonlinear couplings; feedback linearization relies on exact cancellation of the nonlinear dynamics and degrades rapidly when the dynamic model is not precisely known; sliding-mode controllers are prone to chattering and require conservative disturbance bounds; and nominal NLMPC offers no guarantee of constraint satisfaction in the presence of disturbances and model uncertainty. To overcome these limitations, this article develops a robust Tube-based NLMPC for the full nonlinear 12-state quadrotor model, explicitly accounting for inertia uncertainties along the x , y , and z axes as well as bounded additive disturbances acting on the states. The tube-based formulation optimizes a nominal disturbance-free trajectory online while an ancillary feedback law confines the true state within a robust invariant tube around it, thereby guaranteeing robust constraint satisfaction. Recursive feasibility, asymptotic stability of the nominal closed loop, and input-to-state stability of the perturbed system are formally established. The proposed controller is benchmarked against a conventional cascade PID scheme in constant-reference and helical-path tracking scenarios under injected disturbances. Simulation results show that the Tube NLMPC achieves lower tracking error, faster settling, reduced oscillations, and markedly superior disturbance rejection, while its average per-step computation time of 3.86 ms-well within the 100 ms sampling interval-confirms its real-time feasibility and practical suitability for deployment in unpredictable operating environments.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: quadrotor trajectory tracking; input-to-state stability; robust constraint satisfaction; disturbance rejection; recursive feasibility; inertia uncertainty

Article.Title: Stochastic birth-death dynamics of insect outbreaks: finite-time extinction and quasi-stationary distribution
Article.Authors: Rao Y.; Lan G.; Wei C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper constructs a stochastic extension of the classic deterministic Ludwig–Jones–Holling (LJH) model for spruce budworm population dynamics. We propose a continuous-time Markov chain model whose mean-field limit coincides with the LJH model, leading to a stochastic differential equation (SDE) with an absorbing boundary at extinction. We establish the well-posedness of the SDE and, using Feller’s boundary classification, prove that extinction occurs almost surely in finite time—a fundamental departure from deterministic predictions. Conditioned on non-extinction, the process converges exponentially to a unique quasi-stationary distribution (QSD), which characterizes the metastable outbreak state observed in nature. The associated Q -process is shown to be exponentially ergodic, providing a formal framework for analyzing recurrent outbreak statistics. We further obtain an asymptotic extinction rate and a scaling function for local extinction resistance, offering practical metrics for resilience assessment. Extensive numerical simulations validate the theoretical results.
Article.Topic: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models

Article.Title: Mining pressure law and strata movement of thick coal seam mining in isolated panel with multiple adjacent goafs
Article.Authors: Sun Q.; Han Y.; Lei X.; Chen K.
Article.Abstract: The law of mining pressure and the characteristics of strata movement are the key factors affecting the safe and efficient mining of coal mines. Using numerical simulation via the Mohr–Coulomb model in FLAC3D and physical analog modeling, the mining pressure and strata movement of the mining area during the mining process of five adjacent goafs in the case study (Yangchangwan Coal Mine, China) was comprehensively evaluated. The stress distribution characteristics and the laws governing overlying rock movement and failure during the panel’s mining process were investigated. The research results indicate a clear pattern of complex, asymmetric mining pressure during the panel’s mining process. When the panel was close to the 1202-1 goaf, energy accumulation led to a significant increase in mining pressure intensity, with the maximum stress reaching 28 MPa and a stress concentration factor of up to 4.48. The lower area of the 1202-2 panel, along the dip direction, experienced overall pressure relief, with a stress peak of 50% of that in the upper area, while the transition area showed stress-concentration characteristics. The stress variations in the 14 m coal pillar (where the headgate was located) were complex, manifested as stress concentrations in the area of coal seam thickness variation, in the coal pillar area between the 1201 and 202-1 goafs, and in areas of high mining pressure. Based on the research results, the key influencing factors of the law of mining pressure and strata movement in the isolated panel were discussed and analyzed. The results obtained provide theoretical substantiation for the study of mining pressure laws and control in similar isolated panels.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: strata movement; mine pressure; thick coal seam; coal pillar; stress concentration

Article.Title: Orthodontic tooth movement-induced acute referred pain is associated with pain intensity but not psychological and behavioural factors: a prospective study
Article.Authors: Chuinsiri N.; Thammanichanon P.; Puttaravuttiporn P.; Mongkolchart W.; Chudet C.; Thongraksri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This prospective study investigated acute referred pain following orthodontic appliance insertion by examining the association between dental pain intensity (DPI) and orofacial musculoskeletal pain assessed using the TMD pain screener, while accounting for psychological and behavioural factors as potential confounders. Participants aged 18–44 years receiving fixed edgewise appliances ( n = 121) and controls ( n ​ = 120) were recruited. Most included participants had mild psychological and behavioural profiles according to Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7, Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ)-9, PHQ-15 and Oral Behaviour Checklist-21. Follow-up was conducted via telephone on post-operative day 1, week 1 and week 4, during which participants rated DPI and completed the TMD pain screener. Fixed edgewise appliances induced greater DPI on post-operative day 1 compared with controls ( p < 0.001), with no differences observed at later time points. TMD pain scores were positively correlated with DPI (Spearman’s rho = 0.21, p = 0.03) but showed no correlation with psychological or behavioural variables. Multiple logistic regression demonstrated that DPI was the only variable significantly associated with TMD pain score ≥ 1 (OR = 1.27, p = 0.047). Fixed edgewise appliances may induce transient dental pain associated with intensity-dependent referred pain in the orofacial musculoskeletal region. Clinicians should recognise this phenomenon to avoid misdiagnosis and provide appropriate management.

Article.Title: Directed resting state BOLD dependencies change after learning a novel foot drawing motor task
Article.Authors: Rezaei M.; Bahrami F.; Tahmasebi Boroujeni S.; Talesh Jafadideh A.
Article.Abstract: Learning a motor skill makes movements more accurate and faster, but whether the same circuits support both gains remains unclear. Thirteen adults learned a novel foot-drawing skill over seven sessions. Nine had usable resting-state fMRI and matched behavioural data for the pre-to-post brain analysis. We used PCMCI to estimate directed, time-lagged BOLD dependencies between 112 cortical and subcortical regions and related their change to behavioural gains. Inference used small-sample resampling with family-wise error control. The primary direct change-score analysis yielded no family-wise-error-corrected accuracy or speed association. In the complementary longitudinal interaction analysis, one network-level Post \(\times \) accuracy association from VisCent to LimbicA survived maxT correction across 361 blocks ( \(p=0.020\) ), and one Post \(\times \) speed edge from left retrosplenial cortex to left putamen reached the maxT threshold across 12,432 edges ( \(p=0.047\) ; Monte-Carlo 95% interval 0.043–0.051). Broader accuracy- and speed-related maps are exploratory. We report the complete \(2\times 2\) interaction results, direct accuracy-versus-speed contrasts, nested cross-validation of the baseline analysis, and model-matched sensitivity. These preliminary findings provide replication targets for larger studies of learning-related changes in directed resting-state BOLD coupling.

Article.Title: Trophic guilds overpower microhabitat in the dispersal traits of saproxylic beetle
Article.Authors: Martínez-Pérez S.; Aguirrebengoa M.; Pérez-Sánchez D.; Galante E.; Micó E.
Article.Abstract: The study of flight morphological traits in insects provides an opportunity to understand species dispersal patterns and predict species vulnerability to different scenarios. Theoretical hypotheses predict poorer dispersal for species living in persistent habitats and for generalists than for those of ephemeral habitats and specialists, yet this has rarely been explored in insects. Saproxylic beetles were chosen to empirically evaluate the habitat persistence hypothesis. Three flight traits (body length, wing loading and abdomen-to-elytra ratio) and two microhabitats with different spatio-temporal dynamics (tree hollows and dead wood on ground) were used. We tested trophic guild and microhabitat specialisation effects on flight traits using phylogenetically corrected regressions. Results showed differences in flight traits according to microhabitat type, specialisation and trophic guild. Trophic guilds seemed to more strongly impact dispersal traits than microhabitat type. We conclude that while tree-hollow assemblages harbour larger species, they do not necessarily exhibit morphological traits indicating lower dispersal compared to those in dead wood, at least when focusing on flight traits. Additionally, body length as a surrogate for dispersal in saproxylic beetles is questioned, as wing loading generally showed opposite trends. Future research should focus on defining specific dispersal syndromes to better predict the vulnerability of saproxylic communities.

Article.Title: Metabolomic rewiring of energy, structural and signaling networks underlies triple negative breast cancer aggressiveness
Article.Authors: Barry N.; Michel M.; Djité M.; Sow M.; Baldé S.; Ngom N.; Sy M.; Kandji P.; Thioune N.; Thiam J.; Tall F.; Ndour E.; Bissan A.; Dial C.; Dem A.; Ka S.; Simard G.; Chao de la Barca J.; Gueye P.; Reynier P.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly prevalent in West Africa and associated with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Targeted quantitative metabolomic and lipidomic profiling was performed on pretreatment tumor biopsies from Senegalese women with TNBC ( n = 40) and hormone-dependent breast cancer (HDBC; n = 40). After exclusion of two PCA outliers, 39 samples per group were analyzed. Using the Biocrates MxP Quant 500 XL platform, 1019 analytes were assayed, and 655 metabolites were retained for statistical analysis. Sixty-nine metabolites differed significantly ( p < 0.01, fold change ≥ 1.2), including eight after FDR correction (q < 0.05). OPLS-DA showed robust group separation (Q 2 cum = 0.56; CV-ANOVA p < 2.62 × 10 −12 ). Machine learning classifiers achieved consistent discrimination (AUC ≥ 0.70), with Ridge regression performing best (AUC = 0.79). TNBC showed metabolic patterns consistent with increased glycolysis, fatty acid oxidation, glutaminolysis, and branched-chain amino acid catabolism, together with alterations potentially related to angiogenesis and extracellular matrix remodeling. Lipidomic differences included phosphatidylethanolamines, sphingolipids, and phosphatidylinositol species. Overall, tumor metabolomic and lipidomic profiling discriminated TNBC from HDBC and identified metabolic features associated with aggressive tumor biology in West African patients.

Article.Title: An AI-powered trisomy 21 Research Assistant
Article.Authors: Nandi S.; Sundararajan Z.; Subirana-Granés M.; Espinosa J.; Pividori M.; Sullivan K.; Galbraith M.; Costello J.
Article.Abstract: Down syndrome, caused by trisomy 21, increases diverse co-occurring conditions, and with nearly 35,000 publications indexed in PubMed as of late 2026, keeping pace with this literature is challenging. General-purpose large language models are widely used for information retrieval but rely on broad training data rather than specific evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves rigor by linking outputs to source texts, but standard implementations rank background text as highly as experimental results. We developed the T21 Research Assistant, a section-aware RAG system that prioritizes Results sections to ground responses in primary experimental evidence. The system draws exclusively from 1,594 open-access original research articles on Down syndrome from PubMed Central, including 158 NIH INCLUDE-funded studies, and uses a multistage pipeline for query validation, retrieval, reranking, synthesis, and citation verification. Built on open-source NVIDIA-Nemotron models, it returns structured, cited responses. Across 30 expert-curated questions, no statistically significant differences were detected between the T21 Research Assistant and leading proprietary and open-source models or two published biomedical RAG baselines on most metrics. The T21 Research Assistant delivered traceable, citation-anchored answers and significantly outperformed its standalone generator model on Recall. The interface is accessible online, and the open-source platform can be deployed locally.

Article.Title: Blockage mechanisms of suspended particles in fractured ultra-low permeability reservoirs and optimization of water quality standards for post-fracturing injection
Article.Authors: Li P.; Ren P.; Mu Q.; He Z.; Chen Z.; Li H.; Li Y.; Jiang J.; Liu F.; Luo J.
Article.Abstract: The ecological and environmental management department require the treatment of oilfield produced water to comply with the "Technical Requirements and Analytical Methods for Water Quality Indicators of Clastic Rock Reservoir Water Injection" SY/T 5329-2022. This standard imposes strict limits on injected water quality indicators, including suspended solids concentration, median particle size, and oil content, which are generally determined according to reservoir permeability. However, Hydraulic fracturing creates complex "pore-fracture" dual-media systems in ultra-low permeability reservoirs and the blockage mechanisms of suspended solids during post-fracturing water injection remain unclear-rendering conventional homogeneous-media water quality standards inadequate. In this study actual cores from the Ansai and Jiyuan oilfields, Brazilian-split fracture analogues, proppant-filled fractured cores, and controlled water-quality variations were combined to investigate blockage behavior after hydraulic fracturing. The main novelty of this work is the establishment of a fracture-specific blockage framework: an experimentally observed transition near PC = 1.059 separates internal throat plugging from inlet-face filter-cake formation in the tested cores. Fractures exhibit a dual effect: they mitigate overall permeability damage as preferential flow pathways, while simultaneously facilitating the invasion of solids and oil, complicating subsequent removal. Water-quality optimization tests with 40-70 mesh ceramic proppants showed that Class IV water (particle size < = 5 μm, suspended-particle concentration < = 25 mg/L, and oil content < = 30 mg/L) kept core-scale permeability loss below 25% under the tested conditions. By clarifying fracture-induced blockage mechanisms and validating relaxed standards, this study provides theoretical insights and practical guidance for cost-effective water injection in fractured ultra-low permeability reservoirs.

Article.Title: Unlocking unconventional organic-rich tight carbonate reservoir potential of the Lam Carbonate Member (LCM) in the Shabwah depression, Southeastern Yemen
Article.Authors: Al-Matary A.; Hakimi M.; Alaydrus A.; Alawdi A.; Rahim A.; Abdulfarraj M.; Ghurab A.
Article.Abstract: Organic-rich tight carbonate reservoir potential of the Lam Carbonate Member (LCM) across the Shabwah depression, southeastern Yemen has received limited investigation, particularly regarding its integrated source-rock and reservoir properties. In the current work, a comprehensive assessment combining organic geochemical, mineralogical, and petrophysical analyses of the organic-rich carbonate facies of the LCM encountered in three exploration wells, along with one-dimensional basin modeling analysis, was undertaken to investigate the suitability of the LCM as unconventional oil-tight carbonate reservoir system. Organic-rich carbonates of the LCM exhibit high total organic carbon (TOC) values up to 8.4 wt%, and contain mainly hydrogen-rich Types II and II/III kerogen, implying a strong basis for oil-and gas-source rock charactestics, with mainly oil generating and accumulation potential. The organic geochemical results also reveal that the LCM is interpreted as an oil-saturated source rock with a probability of oil production, as supported by high oil saturation index (OSI) values greater than 30 and up to 145.66 mg HC/g TOC. One-dimensional basin models of three exploration wells also show that the LCM has high oilholding capability, as indicated by transformation ration (TR) values of kerogen from 32% to 50%, and likely resulted due to thermal maturity of peak mature stage of the oil window, with modeled Easy%Ro values of approximately 0.80%–1.00%. The LCM is characterized by high abundance of calcite mineral and favorable silicate and clay mineral, resulting in a high brittleness index of more than 0.80 and up to 0.88, may have contributing to create efficient micro-fracture pores during hydraulic-fracture susceptibility. Moreover, the LCM exhibits limited pore development, with low porosity and very low permeability values, ranging from 0.36% to 7.00%, and from 0.01 to 2.91 mD, respectively, suggesting poor to fair reservoir quality. Consequently, the highlighted results in the current research reveal that the LCM in the Shabwah depression can be considered as an oil-bearing tight carbonate reservoir potential that hydraulic fracturing may be required to facilitate economically viable unconventional hydrocarbon production.
