Article.Title: NGU-Net: a modified U-Net with feature refinement block for accurate medical image segmentation
Article.Authors: Hassan E.; Ghadiri H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is essential for medical diagnosis and treatment planning, enabling automated and reliable analysis of complex imaging data. Despite the widespread use of U-Net and its variants, challenges remain, including internal covariate shifts and suboptimal feature extraction, which can limit performance on complex datasets. NGU-Net builds on the U-Net encoder–decoder and introduces a Feature Refinement Block (FRB) that keeps the two-convolution structure of the standard block. In each FRB, a 3 × 3 convolution with ReLU is followed by a second 3 × 3 convolution, batch normalization, and a final ReLU. This ordering stabilizes the internal feature distributions and training, with only a negligible increase in parameters. These modifications contribute to faster convergence during training and improved segmentation performance. Experimental results on brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) datasets demonstrate that NGU-Net outperforms the original U-Net and several of its variants, achieving higher accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed framework provides an effective architecture for brain tumor segmentation, demonstrating promising performance on The Cancer Genome Atlas Lower-Grade Glioma (TCGA-LGG) dataset that warrants further multi-center external validation.

Article.Title: Molecular adaptations and metabolic reprogramming of Priestia megaterium KW16 in response to fungal pathogen-derived filtrates
Article.Authors: Pinski A.; Nowak B.; Żur-Pińska J.; Beckmann M.; Mur L.; Hupert-Kocurek K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Priestia megaterium KW16 is an endophytic bacterium with broad-spectrum antifungal activity, but its molecular response to phytopathogens remains unknown. Here, we combined transcriptomics, metabolomics, RT-qPCR, and fatty acid profiling to characterise the response of KW16 to cell-free culture filtrates of pathogenic fungi: Colletotrichum dematium , Fusarium avenaceum , Rhizoctonia solani , and Sclerotinia sclerotiorum . KW16 inhibited the growth of all tested fungi, with the strongest effect observed against S. sclerotiorum (> 50%), followed by C. dematium, R. solani, and F. avenaceum . Transcriptomic analysis identified 2440 unique differentially expressed genes, with S. sclerotiorum inducing the largest response (1149 upregulated and 1058 downregulated genes). A conserved response across all treatments included repression of sporulation-associated genes and induction of genes involved in iron acquisition, acetate utilisation, stress adaptation, and cell wall remodelling. Our results demonstrated that exposure to fungal filtrates upregulated the genes encoding gas vesicle biosynthesis, competence-associated functions, and lasso peptide biosynthetic genes, particularly in response to S. sclerotiorum . The fungal-derived metabolites could serve as both nutritional resources and ecological signals, driving extensive physiological reprogramming in KW16 and revealing molecular mechanisms that may underlie its persistence and biocontrol activity in competitive plant-associated environments.

Article.Title: Thermodynamically constrained exclusive occupancy of p65 Cysteine 38 resolves the persulfidation–overoxidation competition in neuronal oxygen–glucose deprivation
Article.Authors: Singh D.; Juvvanapudi S.; Jabbar M.; Heera M.; Sree S.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemic injury is described through a therapeutic window whose molecular content has never been specified, and the candidate switch, the redox state of a reactive cysteine, is measured only as a population average over whole proteins. Modifications of one cysteine are alternative fates of a single sulfur atom, yet no kinetic representation treats them as competing occupants of one site. Cysteine 38 of the NF-κB p65 subunit is represented here as a point on a probability simplex whose six vertices are its chemically distinct states, evolving under a generator whose rate constants are produced from state free energies, edge barriers and cosubstrate free-energy changes, so that every cycle affinity depends on chemical potentials alone. The residue layer is coupled to the bioenergetic collapse of oxygen–glucose deprivation and to a bistable survival decision. Cycle affinities proved invariant to the state free energies to $$\:4\times\:{10}^{-15}RT$$ , and detailed balance was recovered exactly, with net cycle flux below $$\:{10}^{-18}{min}^{-1}$$ . Persulfide occupancy rose to 0.44 while oxygen was absent and collapsed on restoration, when sulfinate occupancy reached 0.33, identifying restoration rather than deprivation as the vulnerable interval. Only representations enforcing exclusive occupancy reproduced the reported reversal of the sulfide effect with concentration, raising survival from 0.53 to 0.57 before falling. The thermodynamic constraint removed exactly the six parameter directions the observations cannot constrain, improving identifiability from 9 of 22 directions to 11 of 16 without altering any trajectory. Results are computational; no experimental measurement is reported.

Article.Title: Critical comparison of storage strategies for oral metagenomics
Article.Authors: Rehner J.; Förster M.; Rupf S.; Becker S.; Keller A.; Molano L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The salivary microbiome is increasingly recognized as a diagnostic resource for oral and systemic health, offering a noninvasive alternative to stool sampling. However, pre-analytical factors, including collection and storage conditions, may influence microbial nucleic acid stability and sequencing results, particularly in resource-limited settings where immediate freezing is impractical. We evaluated ten storage conditions across 50 saliva samples collected using sterile Falcon tubes, ZymoBIOMICS DNA/RNA Shield tubes, and Oragene ® Discover kits. Samples were processed immediately, frozen at − 80 °C, or stored at room temperature or 30 °C for up to three days, and were analyzed by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Most core oral taxa were detected across conditions but their relative contribution showed method-dependent abundance. Sequencing yield and Shannon diversity did not differ significantly from fresh samples. In contrast, both preservation buffers reduced observed richness by 16–25% and shifted community composition. These shifts reflected a selective loss of Gram-negative taxa such as Neisseria and Porphyromonas , which fell from 59% to 6–15% of reads in every participant. Unpreserved storage for more than two days instead increased the proportion of Gram-negative and anaerobic bacteria. Notably, nucleic acid from the bacterium Klebsiella pneumoniae was detected only in Oragene ® Discover and sterile falcon samples stored at 30 °C. Overall, freezing or storage in sterile tubes for up to two days best preserved the fresh salivary profile, supporting saliva-based metagenomic studies in decentralized and resource-constrained environments.

Article.Title: Design of an ultra low voltage VDBA using bulk driven quasi floating gate techniques for high order biosignal processing
Article.Authors: Kumngern M.; Khateb F.; Kulej T.; Arbet D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents a high-performance ultra-low-voltage (ULV) voltage differencing buffered amplifier (VDBA) operating from a 0.5-V supply. Consisting of an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) followed by a voltage follower (VF), the proposed VDBA combines bulk-driven (BD) and bulk-driven quasi-floating-gate (BD-QFG) MOS techniques to overcome threshold-voltage limitations and enhance the performance of subthreshold circuits. Designed in the Cadence Virtuoso environment using the TSMC 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed VDBA consumes only 370 nW and occupies 0.022 mm 2 area. Its applicability is demonstrated through a fifth-order Butterworth low-pass filter for ECG signals, achieving an electronically tunable cutoff frequency from 73.65 to 557.8 Hz, 1.1% THD for a $$\:100{\text{}\text{mV}}_{\text{p-p}}$$ input signal, and a 44 dB dynamic range. Monte Carlo and PVT analyses confirm the robustness of the proposed design, while experimental implementation using the commercially available LM13700 further validates the proposed filtering approach.

Article.Title: Composition- and temperature-controlled architecture of pluronic F127–miltefosine mixed micelles
Article.Authors: Carriles J.; Aydillo C.; Smith G.; Nguewa P.; González-Gaitano G.; Dirany Z.
Article.Abstract: Polymeric micelles have been long used as nanocarriers to improve the solubility and delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs. However, the incorporation of amphiphilic drugs introduces an additional level of complexity, where the drug can contribute directly to the self-assembly process, giving rise to mixed micelles whose structure and properties are determined by the cooperative interactions of both components. Here, we investigate this concept using Pluronic ® F127, a thermoresponsive triblock copolymer, and miltefosine (MF), an amphiphilic drug currently used for the treatment of leishmaniasis. By combining small-angle neutron scattering with complementary light scattering, fluorescence, and NMR methods, we establish a quantitative structural description of F127-MF mixed micelles over a range of polymer-to-drug ratios. MF promotes the formation of mixed micelles by facilitating micellization at lower F127 concentrations and below its critical micellization temperature, while preferentially partitioning into the hydrophobic core. Through manipulation of the polymer-to-drug ratio, the properties of these mixed micelles can be tuned. At high F127 content, the mixed micelles closely resemble those of the pure surfactant, whereas increasing MF fraction induces a transition from polymer-rich to drug-rich aggregates characterized by changes in aggregation number, hydration, and internal organization. Overall, this work establishes an exhaustive characterization of F127–MF mixed micelles as a versatile and tunable colloidal system, providing valuable insights into the design of pharmaceutical formulations based on amphiphilic block copolymers as drug carriers.

Article.Title: Governance capacity determines food security resilience across Arab sub-regions (2016–2025)
Article.Authors: Abdelmagid S.; Abdelgadir H.; Qurtam A.; Ali A.; Elsayed A.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the evolution of food security across the Arab region from 2016 to 2025, addressing three research questions: trends in key food security indicators, differential impacts of major shocks across sub-regions, and conditions under which shocks become persistent versus transitory. Using triangulated data from AOAD, FAO, World Bank, GHI, and GFSI with panel regression (2016–2022, N = 98), we find that while the pan-Arab food gap increased from $34.5 billion to $43.3 billion, the aggregate trend masks a four-tier resilience hierarchy. Persian Gulf countries showed strong negative correlation between food prices and hunger (− 0.741), while conflict-affected regions showed very strong positive correlations (0.71–0.92). Panel regression shows a statistically significant positive association between SDG progress and food security outcomes (Fixed Effects β = 0.255, p = 0.001). The analysis indicates that governance capacity, not strategy availability, is the strongest predictor of resilience. A central contrast emerges between sub-regions. The Persian Gulf maintains undernourishment below 5% despite 94.6% import dependence, whereas the Maghreb, Mashreq, and Central regions face rates of 6–8%, 12–15%, and over 20% respectively. This shows that the same import dependence amplifies vulnerability when fiscal buffers are absent. We propose a differentiated implementation model where AOAD coordinates region-specific programs tailored to sub-regional capacities. Without targeted interventions addressing these gaps, regional food security will remain fragile, poorly governed, and deeply unequal.

Article.Authors: Moradzadeh M.; Nikokar I.; Roshani M.; Mobayen M.; Roushan Z.; Parast K.
Article.Abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a opportunistic pathogen and common cause of nosocomial infections. Article.Title: Decoding the night: a machine learning approach to diagnose and predict the severity of obstructive sleep apnea through clinical parameters
Article.Authors: Özçelik N.; Bendeş E.; Özçelik A.; Şentürk Topaloğlu E.; Özyurt S.; Karadağ M.; Güçlü Ö.; Yıldız M.; Selimoğlu Şen H.; Yetkin N.; Baran B.; Öztürk Ö.; Erçelik M.; Türkmen Kaya H.; Sarıoğlu N.; Çolak M.; Akkoyunlu M.; Kansu A.; Kotan A.; Karakaş F.; Bülbül Y.; Doğru S.; Gümüş A.; Özçıbık Işık G.; Topaloğlu Ö.
Article.Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep-related disorder associated with cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities. Early diagnosis is essential; however, access to polysomnography is limited. Machine learning approaches may support clinical decision-making by predicting OSA using easily obtainable variables. This study aimed to develop an artificial neural network (ANN) model to predict the presence and severity of OSA. This multicenter study included adult patients who underwent diagnostic polysomnography at ten different sleep centers. Eighteen demographic and clinical parameters were used as input features, and four OSA severity categories served as output classes. The ANN architecture consisted of one hidden layer with 50 neurons (ReLU activation) and a Softmax output layer. The dataset was randomly divided into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. A total of 1,954 participants (70.2% male) were included. Polysomnography classified 39.2% of participants as severe OSA, 29.4% as mild OSA, 15.0% as moderate OSA, and 16.4% as non-OSA. The ANN model demonstrated good discriminative performance across OSA severity categories, with class-specific AUC values ranging from 0.89 to 0.96. These findings support the potential utility of ML-based tools for screening and early risk stratification, particularly in resource-limited settings.

Article.Title: Intracortical recordings in human lateral occipital complex support the biased-competition model of spatial attention
Article.Authors: Vanhoyland M.; Ramirez J.; Janssen P.; Theys T.
Article.Abstract: Spatial attention is fundamental for prioritizing relevant information in complex visual environments. Yet, the neural mechanisms underlying this process in humans remain elusive, given the spatiotemporal constraints of noninvasive functional imaging. Here we present multi-unit spiking activity from the human lateral occipital complex (LO) during a covert spatial visual attention task. Spatial attention strongly modulates neural activity when two competing stimuli fall within the receptive field, but not when only one of them does, supporting the biased-competition model of attention. This model suggests that spatial attention reduces interference between stimuli by favoring the attended one. We further found that, under competition, attended, task-relevant objects are selectively maintained. This is, to our knowledge, the first demonstration of the neural effects of spatial attention in human visual cortex at the level of multi-unit spiking activity, offering a more naturalistic view of human visual attention, as participants received no prior training, unlike electrophysiological studies in trained macaques. Our study bridges human neuroimaging and primate electrophysiology, providing insights into the neural basis of attention.

Article.Title: Lie group error state representation and analysis in earth-centred earth-fixed coordinate system
Article.Authors: Mingming L.; Jinlai L.; Ke Z.
Article.Abstract: To address navigation accuracy degradation caused by error accumulation in traditional Strapdown Inertial Navigation Systems (SINS), this paper systematically investigates error state representation and analysis methods for SINS in the earth-centered earth-fixed (ECEF) frame based on Lie group theory. The SINS mechanization in the ECEF frame was established, embedding attitude, speed, and position states into the extended special Euclidean group, and deriving both left-invariant and right-invariant error representations for non-group-affine and group-affine Lie group error models. By introducing auxiliary speed vectors, a SINS mechanization satisfying group-affine dynamic characteristics was constructed. Given the time-varying characteristics of measurement noise in SINS/DVL integrated navigation, the Sage-Husa Adaptive Kalman Filter (AKF) was employed for real-time estimation and adjustment of measurement noise. Five algorithms were compared through shipboard experiments: traditional error model (ESINS), non-group-affine left error model (LSE), non-group-affine right error model (RSE), group-affine left error model (LSEGA), and group-affine right error model (RSEGA). Experimental results showed that under small misalignment angles (e.g., [0.1° 0.1° 0.1°] and [1° 1° 1°]), RSEGA-AKF and RSE-AKF perform comparably to the other algorithms, with only marginal differences in yaw and position accuracy. Their distinct and measurable superiority is exclusively demonstrated under large misalignment angle scenarios. Under [0.1° 0.1° 0.1°] misalignment, yaw RMSE and MAE differ by only 1 × 10 −3 ◦10 −30 , while position RMSE and MAE differences are within 0.7 m and 0.5 m respectively, which are negligible for practical navigation. Under large misalignment angles ([10° 10° 10°] and [30° 30° 30°]), however, the advantages of RSEGA-AKF and RSE-AKF become prominent and clearly measurable: under [30° 30° 30°] misalignment, yaw RMSE and MAE are superior by up to 0.3° and 0.1° respectively, while position RMSE and MAE are reduced by up to 15 m.

Article.Title: NSFA AQE CenterOBB detects oriented SAR ships using frequency domain noise suppression and angle quality estimation
Article.Authors: Roohi S.; Akbarizadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery underpins maritime surveillance, traffic monitoring, and safety-of-navigation applications, yet high-quality detection in real-world SAR remains difficult. Multiplicative speckle and sensor-dependent noise degrade contrast, sea clutter and strong land or shore backscatter confuse inshore scenes, and elongated ships need reliable orientation estimates that a horizontal bounding box simply cannot give. We present NSFA–AQE CenterOBB, an end-to-end, anchor-free, one-stage detector built to address these three problems within a single oriented-detection pipeline. Its backbone is lightweight and includes Noise Suppression and Feature Amplification (NSFA) blocks that modulate the spectrum of intermediate feature maps, designed to attenuate clutter while preserving ship-discriminative structure; a Sobel-derived edge enhancement module adds boundary cues intended to support localization under weak contrast. Building on a CenterNet-style objects-as-points formulation, a probabilistic angle head predicts both an orientation mean and an uncertainty estimate, trained with a periodic negative log-likelihood loss that respects the π-periodic symmetry of ship orientation. At inference, this uncertainty drives an Angle Quality Estimation (AQE) mechanism that recalibrates detection scores during decoding and oriented non-maximum suppression. A symmetric Kullback–Leibler divergence regularizer maps predicted and ground-truth oriented boxes onto two-dimensional Gaussians and enforces geometric consistency across center, size, and orientation. On SSDD + , the rotated-box relabeling of the SAR Ship Detection Dataset, the detector performs competitively across both offshore and challenging inshore scenes, and our cumulative ablation shows that adding a geometry-consistency term to the training objective gives the numerically largest single step in mean average precision (part of which offsets a preceding drop at the probabilistic-angle stage); a controlled comparison across four geometry-consistency loss formulations shows the symmetric KLD variant we adopt achieves the highest mAP50, although the differences among the geometry losses are within run-to-run variation, and it is not the best in mAP75 or angular accuracy. The predicted angle uncertainty is, however, only weakly informative at the evaluated checkpoint, so AQE does not improve AP in our controlled comparison.

Article.Title: Enhancing ultrasonic spot weldability of aluminum-copper alloy through surface modification techniques
Article.Authors: V. S.; Pattanaik A.; Satpathy M.; Debebe S.
Article.Abstract: Ultrasonic welding is a solid-state technique that is increasing​ly employed to join Li-ion battery interconnections in electric automobiles. Understanding the joint microstructure is essential for evaluating the performance and joint integrity. Surface modifications play a crucial role in affecting the friction and contact behavior at the joint interface. This investigation describes the effects of surface treatments and various welding energies on the ultrasonic weldability of aluminum/copper alloy joints using lubricated, normal, electrolytic, and emery-polished surfaces. The results demonstrated that lubricated surfaces facilitated improved plastic flow and mechanical interlocking, resulting in elevated tensile shear and T-peel failure loads of 642.37 N and 280.86 N, respectively, at a welding energy of 1950 J. The interface temperature of 420.66 °C was attained at this optimum weld energy. Microstructural analysis indicated that the lubricated surfaces exhibited a ductile fracture mode characterized by dimples, signifying mechanical interlocking and interface diffusion. Emery-polished surfaces exhibited the lowest mechanical performance. This decline is attributed to mixed-mode fracture, adhesive wear, and poor metallic bonding. Restricted interfacial sliding is considered responsible for the weakened bond. X-ray diffraction verified the existence of Al 2 Cu, Cu 5 Zn 8 , and Al 4 Cu 9 intermetallic compounds at the edge of the aluminum/copper alloy joints.

Article.Title: Feature guided prompting distorts synthetic fake news corpora without improving detection
Article.Authors: Wani S.; Zangana H.; Gulzar Y.; Alkanan M.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly applied for generating synthetic training data to address class imbalance problems in fake news detection. Existing approaches commonly apply multiple stylistic constraints in generation prompts to control the characteristics of generated samples and evaluate their overall compliance. However, the contribution of individual constraints to synthetic data augmentation performance remains unclear. This research investigates whether any single stylistic constraint is necessary or sufficient to improve LLM-based data augmentation effectiveness. A single-feature ablation analysis was conducted using an LLM-based augmentation pipeline with the GossipCop–PolitiFact headline dataset containing 23,196 samples and 15 stylistic constraints adopted from previous research. The Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model was used as the primary generator across 26 prompt conditions. Phi-3.5-mini-instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B were used for cross-model validation on three key conditions (full, naive, F5-only). Three independently generated corpora, each containing 5,000 headlines, were produced for every condition and evaluated with six classical classifiers (30 seeds each), three fine-tuned transformers (3 seeds each), and one zero-shot LLM classifier. The results indicate that no individual stylistic constraint is necessary, as all 15 ablation settings achieved statistical equivalence under a two-one-sided equivalence test with δ = 0.02. Although three features (F1, F7, F9) produced statistically detectable changes after FDR (false discovery rate) correction, their magnitudes remained within the equivalence margin. Furthermore, the F5-only prompt achieved performance within δ = 0.02 of the full prompt across the three evaluated generator families. The maximum within-family F1 difference among the full, naive, and F5-only conditions was 0.0088. Although F5-only achieved numerically higher F1 scores than naive prompting, the differences remained below the predefined practical margin. In the Qwen experiments, the F6-only and F12-only prompts also matched the full prompt within δ = 0.02, as did the F6 + F4 condition (Δ = −0.0037). In the primary Random Forest evaluation, the Qwen full, naive, and F5-only conditions achieved lower fake F1 scores than the no-augmentation baseline of 0.6034. Random oversampling and class-weighted Random Forest achieved higher scores of 0.6324 and 0.6452, respectively. The findings indicate that the stylistic constraints may introduce distributional distortions rather than improve alignment with real fake-news characteristics. The full prompt increased question mark frequency by 5.3× and reduced ALL CAPS usage by 12.5×, while the F5-only prompt increased exclamation mark frequency by 15×. The direction of question-mark distortion is partly model-specific: Qwen and Phi over-comply (5.34× and 4.51×) while DeepSeek under-complies (0.66×), confirming that the misalignment is a joint property of the prompt and the generator. These findings indicate that synthetic data quality evaluation should consider feature-level distributional alignment rather than relying solely on aggregate prompt compliance, particularly within the scope of the English-language headline generation setting evaluated in this study.

Article.Title: TraCo-CLIP: transition-conditioned CLIP adaptation for static-bias-robust open-vocabulary video action recognition
Article.Authors: Zhuang J.; Zhang Y.; Bao F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adapting image–text pretrained models to video action recognition requires learning temporal information while preserving transferable visual–textual representations. However, global category-level supervision can favor class-correlated static cues over localized temporal evidence. We propose TraCo-CLIP, a transition-conditioned CLIP adaptation framework for static-bias-robust open-vocabulary video action recognition. A lightweight controller combines semantic change, frame-level ambiguity relative to the source action vocabulary, and their interaction to estimate transition-sensitive routing scores. Temporal non-maximum suppression with fallback selection and confidence-weighted local aggregation construct transition anchors. Two auxiliary objectives supervise the same anchors: transition-centered visual–textual alignment provides inter-class discrimination, while static counterfactual contrast compares transition-oriented and static textual descriptions within the same action category. Both objectives regularize the shared visual representation during training. We evaluate TraCo-CLIP under base-to-novel, cross-dataset, cross-domain open-vocabulary, and out-of-context static-bias protocols. On XOV-Action, the reported controlled comparisons improve $$\mathrm {AVG\text{- }A}$$ by $$2.61$$ and $$2.60$$ percentage points under K150 and K400 source training, respectively. On UCF101-SCUBA/SCUFO, SCUBA accuracy increases by $$8.3$$ points, SCUFO accuracy decreases by $$6.4$$ points, and contrasted accuracy increases by $$11.9$$ points. Controlled ablations and representation-level analyses support the usefulness of the auxiliary learning framework under the evaluated settings. The auxiliary components introduce computation and text-bank storage during training. They are removed for recognition inference, leaving the same deployed architecture and inference operations as the controlled baseline.

Article.Title: Descriptive comparison of fatigue performance in asphalt mixtures containing reclaimed asphalt pavement using combined activation treatments
Article.Authors: Ma W.; Chen S.; Fazli A.; Khairy Y.; Ghoniem R.
Article.Abstract: This study examined fatigue damage evolution in asphalt mixtures containing 48% Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement to determine how RAP material characteristics and combined activation treatments influence dry and moisture-conditioned fatigue performance. Three RAP materials, Urban Arterial, Highway Corridor, and Industrial Pavement, were each combined with Low, Medium, and High activation treatments that simultaneously varied rejuvenator dosage, mixing temperature, and compaction temperature, producing nine formulations. Dry specimens were tested at 400 and 500 microstrain, while freeze-thaw-conditioned specimens were tested at 500 microstrain. RAP characterization included binder content, penetration, softening point, viscosity, carbonyl index, sulfoxide index, and fine fraction. Performance evaluation included volumetric properties, Indirect Tensile Strength, Tensile Strength Ratio, Retained Modulus, fatigue life, dissipated energy, normalized stiffness damage, Fatigue Life Retention, and Normalized Fatigue Loss. The Medium treatment produced the highest fatigue life within each RAP material. HC_M achieved the highest N₅₀ values of 81,726 cycles at 400 microstrain, 28,451 cycles under dry conditions at 500 microstrain, and 22,983 cycles after freeze-thaw conditioning. HC_M also achieved a Tensile Strength Ratio of 90.1%, Retained Modulus of 87.5%, Fatigue Life Retention of 80.8%, and Normalized Fatigue Loss of 19.2%. Increasing strain from 400 to 500 microstrain reduced fatigue life by 65.2% to 70.3% across the tested formulations. These results indicate that moderate combined activation provided the most favorable balance of moisture resistance and fatigue durability among the tested 48% RAP mixtures.

Article.Title: QbD-optimized novel oral nanoemulsion for co-delivery of capecitabine and morin for colorectal cancer to overcome monotherapy limitations
Article.Authors: Khan M.; Hassan M.; Rahman N.; Ahmad A.; Mushtaq H.; Othman R.; Zeb A.; Alsayed S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading global health concern. Capecitabine (CAP) demonstrates limited clinical effectiveness due to intestinal mucositis, cachexia, chemoresistance, and organ toxicities. Morin posses modulating properties for such effects; however, no Quality-by-Design (QbD) optimized nanoemulsion has co-delivered CAP and Morin for CRC. Morin was initially computationally assessed against cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), P-glycoprotein (P-gp), and CYP3A4 using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. A QbD-based O/W nanoemulsion was optimized using Design Expert software ( p-value < 0.05). CAP and Morin were incorporated into the aqueous and oily phases, respectively, using olive oil selected through preformulation studies. The nanoemulsion was characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) Spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy-Energy Dispersive X-Ray (SEM-EDX) spectroscopy, particle size, Polydispersity Index (PDI), zeta potential, entrapment efficiency, stability, and ex vivo release studies, followed by an in vivo evaluation in a DMH-induced CRC rabbit model. Morin exhibited strong binding affinity toward COX-2 (-9.0 kcal/mol), P-gp (-7.9 kcal/mol), and CYP3A4 (-7.5 kcal/mol), with stable molecular dynamics profiles. The optimized nanoemulsion (F10) showed a particle size of 131.7 nm, PDI of 0.157, and zeta potential of -13.1 mV. Furthermore, SEM revealed spherical nanosized droplets. In addition, ex vivo NE release was pH-dependent, reaching 66.9% at pH 1.2 and 89.1% at pH 7.4 after 24 h, following Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetics (R² = 0.987). Furthermore, in vivo studies revealed attenuation of mucositis, cachexia, cardiotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and nephrotoxicity compared with CAP alone. The QbD-optimized nanoemulsion demonstrated favorable formulation characteristics and showed potential as an oral nanotherapeutic co-delivery strategy for CRC management.

Article.Title: Probabilistic health risk assessment of caffeine intake from milk tea among college students in Wuhan, China by Monte Carlo simulation
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Zhang H.; Zhou Y.; Ge L.; Zhou X.; Wu X.; Ming F.; Zhao Z.; Xin J.; Hu S.; Guo Y.; Liu J.; He Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Milk tea has become increasingly popular among young Chinese consumers, yet caffeine exposure through this beverage has not been systematically quantified. This study conducted the first probabilistic risk assessment of daily caffeine intake from milk tea among college students. Caffeine concentrations were measured in 154 freshly prepared milk tea samples across five tea base categories using HPLC. Consumption data were obtained from a cross-sectional survey of 1,495 college students in Wuhan, China. A Monte Carlo simulation was applied to characterize variability in caffeine concentration and milk tea consumption and to estimate daily caffeine intake. Caffeine exposure was additionally expressed on a body-weight basis for habitual intake (mg/kg bw/day) and single-occasion intake (mg/kg bw), and compared with the corresponding EFSA reference levels. Uncertainty in the summary exposure estimates was quantified using bootstrap resampling. The overall median caffeine concentration in milk tea was 178.2 mg/kg (range: 30.7–476.9 mg/kg), with borderline differences across tea bases ( P- value = 0.057). Monte Carlo simulation yielded a median daily caffeine intake of 13.1 mg/day (95% CI 12.9–13.3) and a P95 of 29.0 mg/day (95% CI 28.2–29.7), with no simulated intake exceeding 400 mg/day. The median body-weight-normalized habitual exposure was 0.21 mg/kg bw/day (95% CI 0.21–0.21), with a P95 of 0.50 mg/kg bw/day (95% CI 0.49–0.52), and no simulated exposure exceeded the EFSA adult reference level of 5.7 mg/kg bw/day. For single-occasion exposure, the median was 1.45 mg/kg bw (95% CI 1.42–1.48), while the P95 was 3.35 mg/kg bw (95% CI 3.25–3.45), with 7.7% of simulated exposures exceeding 3.0 mg/kg bw. Overall, caffeine exposure from milk tea was low on a habitual basis, although higher exposure levels were observed for some simulated single-consumption occasions. These findings provide a more comprehensive characterization of milk–tea-derived caffeine exposure among college students.

Article.Title: Differential landscape evolution in the Himalayan Piedmont zone across Kopili Fault Zone, NE India from InSAR, geomorphic and sedimentological analysis
Article.Authors: Rajkhowa S.; Jaiswara N.; Sahadevan D.; Pandey P.; Pandey A.
Article.Abstract: The seismically active NNW-SSE-trending Kopili Fault Zone (KFZ), a transverse basement fault buried beneath thick Brahmaputra alluvium, partitions deformation across the southern part of the Himalaya in NE India. The northern segment of the KFZ in the Himalayan Piedmont zone experienced an Mw 6.0 earthquake in 2021, with a dominant reverse-fault component that produced extensive coseismic liquefaction in the epicentral area. The time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) analysis suggests a 5–10 mm/yr uplift rate in the epicentral area during the 2017–2021 period in the eastern block of the KFZ. The time-lapse Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from Landsat images over the past 40 years reveals an eastward deflection of channels. The tectonic-geomorphic proxies, such as mountain front sinuosity (Smf), normalized steepness index ( k sn ), river sinuosity, and drainage deflection, combined with sedimentation patterns and OSL dating of younger terraces, suggest differential uplift in the eastern block of the KFZ over the past millennia. These geomorphic expressions and sedimentological evidence are discussed to elucidate neotectonic growth along the northern high-angle reverse-fault segment of the KFZ and to highlight its heterogeneity.

Article.Authors: Severs T.; Gebbink A.; Gard L.; Rossen J.; van Alphen L.; Koeck R.; Smit P.; Yahiaoui R.; Matamoros S.; van den Bosch B.; Koopman P.; Cartuyvels R.; Dingemans J.; Ivens M.; Pas S.; Boers S.

In addition, EasySeq-GD identified 92 unique bacterial taxa, whereas comparator workflows identified 32 unique taxa. These findings resulted in clinically relevant discrepancies in eight and three samples, respectively. Overall, EasySeq-GD demonstrated good interlaboratory reproducibility. Taxon-level results were concordant with comparator workflows in 107/151 samples (70.9%), while 140/151 samples (92.7%) showed no clinically relevant discrepancies.

Article.Title: Myopic patchy atrophy differs from geographic atrophy in retinal pigment epithelium appearance and intraretinal hyperreflective foci
Article.Authors: Jonas J.; Jonas R.; Bikbov M.; Kazakbaeva G.; Wang Y.; Panda-Jonas S.
Article.Abstract: To assess clinical-histological characteristics of myopic patchy atrophy (PA) and geographic atrophy of age-related macular degeneration (GA). Participants of population-based studies (Ural Eye and Medical Study (n = 5899; age: 40 + years), Ural Very Old Study (n = 1526; age: 85 + years), Beijing Eye Study (n = 3468; age: 40 + years) were clinically examined. We additionally assessed histologically human globes (n = 446) enucleated due to clinical reasons or enucleated post mortem. In the population-based studies, GA and PA were detected in 79 eyes (age: 81.9 ± 12.0 years;axial length: 23.0 ± 0.9 mm) and 59 eyes (age:70.1 ± 12.3 years;axial length: 28.2 ± 2.2 mm), respectively. The GA group versus PA group had a higher degree of intraretinal hyperreflective foci (iHRFs) (3.6 ± 1.1 versus 0.2 ± 0.7; p < 0.001) and para-lesional retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) irregularities (3.9 ± 1.0 versus 0.1 ± 0.6; p < 0.001), higher prevalence of outer nuclear layer thinning (72/79 (91.1%; 95% CI 79,100) versus 36/59 (61.0%; 95% CI 41,82); p < 0.001),and lower prevalence of Bruch´s membrane (BM) defects (0% versus 35/59 (59.3%; 95% CI 40,78)). PAs showed BM defects with absence of choriocapillaris, while in GAs, BM and choriocapillaris were intact. In all eyes with GAs and PAs, the ellipsoid zone and external limiting membrane were defect or absent. Similar findings were obtained upon histology, with intraretinally located RPE cells in GAs in contrast to PAs as additional finding. PA and GA have in common the presence of an RPE-layer opening, and they differ in continuity of BM and adjacent choroidal structures, RPE appearance and prevalence of iHRFs. PAs may be due to an axial elongation-related expansion opening in the RPE layer without marked RPE reaction, while GAs may be associated with a primary RPE reaction including intraretinal RPE cell migration.

Article.Title: Microplastics inhibit macrophage bioenergetics impairing homeostatic function and immune responsiveness
Article.Authors: Dhupar R.; Udoh H.; Noureen N.; Bardawil C.; Zhao X.; Cheema M.; Tuli S.; Shields D.; Mats K.; Al-Bataineh O.; Golla L.; Wang A.; Pineda R.; Königshoff M.; Uttam S.; Gau D.; Soloff A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Since the 1950s, microplastics (MPs) have become omnipresent, representing a novel environmental hazard which continually deposits in our airways. Pulmonary macrophages (pMacs) orchestrate the balance between inflammation and tolerance required for homeostasis of the lung and are among the first immune cells to encounter inhaled MPs. Yet, how pMacs react to plastic deposition in the lung and implications for disease remain unknown. Here, we exposed mice in vivo, human precision-cut lung slices (hPCLS) ex vivo, and monocyte-derived macrophages and cell lines to polystyrene MPs in vitro. MP deposition in the lung and extrapulmonary tissues was determined over a 1-week period and pMacs from MP-laden lungs isolated for RNA-sequencing. Macrophage phagocytosis was impaired through decreased mitochondrial function which could be rescued pharmacologically. MPs inhibited the ability of macrophages to effectively present OVA-antigen preventing TCR-specific activation, an effect that could be restored by blocking PD-1/PD-L1. These findings indicate that MPs impair macrophages via unique mechanisms linking phagocytic and bioenergetic dysfunction. Loss of antigen-presenting capabilities in MP-laden macrophages may compromise immunosurveillance. As such, MPs have the potential to increase susceptibility to lung disease independent of the conventional mechanisms of inflammation and oxidative stress.

Article.Title: Comparing FTIR spectra of goethite, hematite, and ferrihydrite and testing a semi-quantitative approach
Article.Authors: Ellerbrock R.; Bhattarai N.; Schaller J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Iron-(oxyhydr)-oxides like goethite, hematite and ferrihydrite affect soil properties like sorption capacity and can be distinguished by their properties like color, crystal structure (XRD), and spectroscopic data like FTIR. During dissolution–precipitation processes the iron (oxyhydr)-oxides can convert from one into the other. Some studies used Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to analyze hematite and goethite. The objective of this study was to identify absorption bands in FTIR of synthetic (oxyhydr)-oxides that allow to distinguish hematite, goethite, and ferrihydrite and to compare the FTIR of iron (oxyhydr)-oxides synthesized in the laboratory with soil born ones. Additionally, we test a semi-quantitative approach to estimate goethite/hematite weight ratios from FTIR of goethite-hematite mixtures. Comparing the FTIR spectra indicate that all studied synthetic iron (oxyhydr)-oxides show absorption bands located at wavenumber (WN) region from 1180 to 400 cm − 1 typical for each of them. Especially goethite shows characteristic absorption bands in FTIR. Hence, FTIR might be a suitable method to distinguish goethite from the other iron (oxyhydr)-oxides. Our analysis also suggests that binary mixtures of goethite and hematite can be semi-quantitatively quantified using characteristic absorption bands from FTIR. However, when analyzing soil samples such identification may become complicated by overlapping bands caused by other minerals and/or soil organic matter.

Article.Title: The gap between elite female and male runners continues to shrink in the 21st century
Article.Authors: Jucker T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In 1992 a controversial analysis of historical trends in world record performances raised the question of whether women would one day run faster than men across a whole range of athletic disciplines. Since then, however, the consensus has been that the gap between male and female runners stabilised towards the end of the 20th century and has since remained unchanged. Here I analyse running performances by elite athletes since 2001 to show that contrary to this widely held belief, women have in fact continued to close the gap on men across all distances from 60 m to the marathon. Women made the biggest gains relative to men in middle and long-distance running disciplines, and this occurred despite the fact that men too have continued to improve significantly in these events over the past 25 years. The jury is still out there as to whether women will one day run faster than men, but what does appear more certain is that women will continue to push the boundaries of running performance over the coming decades.

Article.Title: Synchronous oscillation characteristics and finite time projection synchronous control method of DC microgrid
Article.Authors: Qiu N.; Wu L.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: In response to the nonlinear, strongly coupled, and time-varying synchronous oscillation phenomena in DC microgrids, traditional methods cannot accurately describe the characteristics of synchronous oscillations. Based on the idea of synchronous control and finite time theory, this paper proposes an effective method for analyzing the synchronous oscillation characteristics of microgrids and a finite time projection synchronous control method. Firstly, establish a dynamic model of the DC microgrid and analyze its synchronous oscillation characteristics. Then, a small world network model is established using complex network theory to analyze node synchronization characteristics. A finite time projection synchronization control method is proposed to quickly achieve synchronization of microgrid small world network nodes, avoid system oscillation, and suppress the oscillation state of the microgrid within a limited time, and quickly achieve complete synchronization. Finally, a DC microgrid simulation experimental platform based on MATLAB/Simulink software and far-width controller is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve synchronization of all nodes in the microgrid more quickly and has better adaptive regulation capability.

Article.Title: Development and external validation of an immediate-postoperative prediction model for high hidden blood loss after PFNA in older intertrochanteric-fracture patients
Article.Authors: Lei Z.; Che C.; Ren H.; Yu H.; Cao H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hidden blood loss (HBL) is a frequent and clinically important complication after proximal femoral nail antirotation (PFNA) for intertrochanteric fractures. A practical immediate-postoperative prediction model with independent external validation may support individualized postoperative blood management. This retrospective prediction model study included a development cohort of 186 older patients who underwent PFNA and an independent external validation cohort of 84 patients. High HBL was defined as HBL > 650 mL based on an X-tile-derived cutoff using postoperative anaemia as clinical endpoint. A main immediate-postoperative model was developed using predictors available before and during surgery, with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator screening and multivariable logistic regression. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples where full modelling workflow including LASSO tuning was repeated within each bootstrap sample. High HBL occurred in 99 of 186 patients (53.2%) in the development cohort and 27 of 84 patients (32.1%) in the external validation cohort. The final immediate-postoperative model included preoperative anticoagulant use, preoperative albumin, and operation time. The apparent development AUC was 0.715 (95% CI, 0.640–0.790); full-workflow bootstrap validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.660, an optimism-corrected Brier score of 0.239, and an optimism-corrected calibration slope of 0.735. In external validation, the AUC was 0.894 (95% CI, 0.826–0.963), Brier score 0.165 (95% CI, 0.109–0.229), calibration intercept − 1.806 (95% CI, -3.006 to -1.244), and calibration slope 1.026 (95% CI, 0.688–1.821). Intercept-only recalibration reduced the Brier score to 0.121 while leaving AUC unchanged. The supplementary preoperative model had an external AUC of 0.839. A parsimonious immediate-postoperative model showed moderate optimism-corrected discrimination and high discrimination in an independent external cohort. However, non-negligible internal overfitting and substantial external absolute-risk overestimation were observed. The model is intended only for immediate-postoperative risk stratification; local recalibration and prospective multicentre validation are required before broad clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Women on the move and the emergence of Etruscan urban polities (Veii, Italy, first millennium BCE)
Article.Authors: Motta L.; Cangemi I.; Bernardini S.; Silvestrini S.; Higgins O.; Magri S.; Terlato G.; Armaroli E.; Coppa A.; Bondioli L.; Nava A.; Pacciarelli M.; Terrenato N.; Lugli F.; Benazzi S.; Esposito C.
Article.Abstract: Veii was an emerging urban center in Tyrrhenian Central Italy, playing a crucial role in the development of the Etruscan society at the beginning of the first millennium BCE. Strategically situated close to the Tiber River, Veii controlled extensive trade networks and prospered through economic and cultural exchanges with Italic and Mediterranean groups. This study investigates human mobility and gender at the Quattro Fontanili necropolis (ca. 820–730 BCE), using strontium isotope ratio ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) and proteomic analysis of dental enamel (amelogenin) for sex determination of 44 inhumed individuals. Results reveal a good correlation between biological sex and funerary gender indicators, particularly in high-status burials. Evidence of non-local individuals at Veii is limited, lower than at comparable sites, and predominantly associated with medium to lower-status women, while elite burials with imported grave goods belong consistently to 87 Sr/ 86 Sr isotopically local individuals. These findings illuminate the social and economic strategies underpinning early urbanisation and polity formation in Etruria.

Article.Title: Extreme heat scenarios and door-to-door operational emissions of metro travel in Jinan
Article.Authors: Guo X.; Gao M.; Ren G.; Jiang J.; Wang H.; Han C.
Article.Abstract: Extreme heat may erode the door-to-door low-carbon advantage of metro travel by changing first- and last-mile choices. We combine grid-scale heat exposure at 159 Jinan station locations with 9,600 randomised stated-choice tasks completed by 1,200 adult recent metro users recruited through convenience sampling. Discrete-choice models describe preferences, and mixed logit predictions support per-trip operational carbon accounting. XGBoost provides supplementary predictive and policy comparisons. From 28 to 40 °C, predicted full-trip metro retention declines from 96.47% to 90.91%, while expected emissions rise from 956.5 to 1,054.2 gCO 2 e/trip, approximately 10.2%. Access and egress changes narrow the retained-metro chain’s emissions advantage over the fixed substitute chain from 43.0% to 39.0%. All paired temperature increments are positive in 2,000 accounting-input simulations with behavioural parameters fixed; three illustrative station-weight scenarios give the same direction. Under central assumptions, both model families give the highest retention for the four-policy package and the lowest emissions for the five-policy package. These conditional scenarios inform access design and subsequent benefit–cost assessment; they do not establish population-wide impacts, realised effects, or cost-effectiveness.

Article.Title: Pore–throat and fracture structures control heterogeneous fluid transport in volcanic reservoirs of the southern Songliao Basin
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Gao X.; Li M.; Yu X.; Liu N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep volcanic gas reservoirs are widely distributed in the southern Songliao Basin, yet their exploitation is severely constrained by pronounced heterogeneity and complex pore–fracture architectures. To address this challenge, we developed an integrated approach combining multi-scale, high-resolution computed tomography (CT) modeling and grey relational analysis to quantitatively characterize the three-dimensional structures of total pores, connected pores, pore–throat networks, and fracture systems in representative volcanic samples. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity, with porosity ranging from 2.3% to 29.3% and permeability spanning six orders of magnitude (0.00017–9.25 mD). Flow simulations demonstrate that coupled fracture–pore–throat systems form continuous, low-resistance flow pathways, whereas dispersed pore structures exhibit pronounced bottleneck effects and reduced transport efficiency. Grey relational analysis further identifies the dominant controls on permeability, showing that fracture attributes predominate in high-permeability samples, whereas pore–throat characteristics dominate in low-permeability samples. Accordingly, two distinct seepage regimes are identified: fracture-enhanced flow with pore–throat synergy and pore–throat-dominated flow. This study establishes a microstructure-based framework for classifying and evaluating heterogeneous tight reservoirs, providing insights into the pore–fracture controls on fluid transport and technical guidance for efficient gas development.

Article.Title: Transcranial alternating current stimulation for Parkinson’s disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of motor outcomes
Article.Authors: Mai T.; Gjishti T.; Witt K.; Roheger M.; Herrmann C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is a promising noninvasive intervention for modulating pathological brain oscillations in Parkinson’s disease (PD). To evaluate its clinical and neurophysiological efficacy, we searched five databases (Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar and APA PsycInfo) up to August 31, 2025, for trials employing tACS in patients with idiopathic PD. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools. Random-effects meta-analyses were used to calculate standardized (SMD) and unstandardized mean differences (MD) with 95 % confidence intervals (CIs). We included 10 studies (184 patients with PD, mean age: 64.9 years, mean disease duration: 5.2 years) in the qualitative review and seven trials (146 patients with PD, mean age: 65.6 years, mean disease duration: 5 years) in the meta-analysis. No statistically significant differences favoring active tACS over control were found in overall motor severity (Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS): SMD = 0.21, 95 % CI [−​0.10, 0.52],​ p = 0.097), tremor (SMD = −​0.40, 95 % CI [−1.97, 1.17],​ p = 0.478), or a neurophysiological marker of inhibitory response, represented by short-interval intracortical inhibition (MD = 0.00, 95 % CI [−​ 0.40, 0.41],​ p = 0.971). The prediction intervals indicated substantial uncertainty, and significant between-study heterogeneity was observed, particularly for tremor outcomes​​ (I 2 = 86.1 %). This variability and limitation in evidence quality is largely driven by small sample sizes, highly heterogeneous stimulation protocols, and varying outcome assessments. Overall, tACS was generally well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported across the included studies; however, formal safety assessment was beyond the scope of this review. Current exploratory evidence shows a lack of consistent improvements in motor symptoms or functions in PD largely due to protocol-level heterogeneity. Future studies should consistently assess the​ ​MDS-UPDRS III post-tACS and report its specific subscores alongside neurophysiological measures to enable robust meta-analyses.

Article.Title: COVID-19 vaccination and patient-reported health one year after SARS-CoV-2 infection
Article.Authors: Förster C.; Napierala H.; Schrimpf A.; Joos S.; Blaschke S.; Hanses F.; Idris R.; Hamelmann E.; Schmidt J.; Scheer C.; Römmele C.; Vetter M.; Göpel S.; Almahfoud M.; Dahl E.; Hamprecht A.; Friedrichs A.; Butzmann J.; Erber J.; Lücke T.; Wendel J.; Jensen B.; Tepasse P.; Dashti H.; Vehreschild J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract COVID-19 vaccination reduces the risk of symptom-defined post-COVID syndrome (PCS), but its association with patient-perceived health and health-related quality of life remains insufficiently understood. We aimed to evaluate the association between pre-infection vaccination and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) across multiple health domains. We analyzed data from the prospective nationwide German NAPKON cohort, including adults infected with SARS-CoV-2 between July 2020 and May 2023. PROMs were assessed over 12 months and included EQ-5D-5L​ , PHQ-4 , PROMIS Cognitive Function , PROMIS-29 , and PROMIS Global . Associations with vaccination status were estimated using multivariable linear regression models. Among 2,680 COVID-19 patients in the NAPKON cohort, 660 adults with documented vaccination status were included; 464 (70.3%) were unvaccinated, 91 (13.8%) fully vaccinated (2 doses), and 105 (15.9%) booster vaccinated (≥ 3 doses). WHO-defined symptom-based PCS was more frequent in unvaccinated patients (70.7%) than in fully vaccinated (45.6%) and booster vaccinated patients (52.4%). In adjusted analyses, booster vaccination was associated with better EQ-5D-VAS at end-of-acute COVID-19 (β = 10.72, 95% CI 1.55 to 19.90). At 3 and 12 months, between-group differences were small and no longer significant after adjustment, while selected within-person changes were greater among unvaccinated patients. Using multiple validated PROM domains, this exploratory study provides a patient-centered perspective on vaccination-related post-COVID recovery, showing limited, domain-specific differences that largely attenuated by 12 months. Larger within-person improvements among unvaccinated patients may reflect poorer post-acute health status. Generalizability to the broader population, particularly individuals with mild COVID-19, is limited by the predominantly hospitalized cohort (85%); nevertheless, these findings suggest that symptom-based PCS definitions alone may insufficiently capture patient-perceived health burden, supporting PROMs as complementary measures in post-COVID research and care. Trial registration : NAPKON is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier NCT04768998).

Article.Title: Farm size and tillage technology reveal contrasting modelled patterns in fuel consumption and machinery-related greenhouse gas emissions in Lithuanian crop production
Article.Authors: Lekavičienė K.; Šarauskis E.; Romaneckas K.; Naujokienė V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fuel use and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with mechanised agricultural operations depend on both production technologies and farm characteristics, yet these factors are often analysed separately. This study developed an integrated deterministic modelling framework to evaluate fuel consumption and machinery-related GHG emissions from diesel fuel combustion across five tillage systems—conventional plowing (PL), minimum tillage (MT), deep strip-till (DST), shallow strip-till (SST), and no-till (NT) across multiple crop groups and five farm size groups ranging from 30 to 50 ha to > 500 ha under Lithuanian conditions. Fuel consumption was calculated for all mechanised operations using predefined tractor–implement operating parameters, field performance, coefficients, input requirements, crop yields, and transport distances. Machinery-related GHG emissions were estimated from diesel consumption using IPCC emission factors. Soil-derived emissions and upstream emissions associated with the production of fertilisers, pesticides, fuels, and machinery were outside the system boundary of the present study. The results identified contrasting area- and yield-scaled patterns. Fuel consumption and machinery-related GHG emissions per unit area increased across the predefined farm-size scenarios, partly reflecting the assumed transport distances and machinery configurations, whereas fuel use and machinery-related GHG emissions per unit of production decreased as a result of the predefined yield and operational-efficiency assumptions. Across all farm sizes, NT showed the lowest fuel consumption and machinery-related GHG emissions, while PL consistently produced the highest values. Compared with PL, NT reduced fuel use and associated machinery-related GHG emissions by 35–58%, depending on crop type and farm size. The principal contribution of the study is a harmonized scenario-based comparison of tillage intensity, crop group, farm size, machinery configuration, operational logistics, and machinery-related GHG emissions within a single deterministic framework using both area- and output-scaled indicators. This approach enables the magnitude and consistency of machinery-related fuel and GHG differences to be evaluated across production scenarios under a common set of assumptions. The results demonstrate the importance of reporting both area- and output-scaled indicators when evaluating technological scenarios in crop production.

Article.Title: Hardware reconfigurable secure data acquisition system of a shared ADC in heterogenous multi-channel inputs with automatic sampling frequency configurations
Article.Authors: Alkelany O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multi-channel Data Acquisition (DAQ) Systems can use a single multiplexed analog to digital converter (ADC) to reduce system cost. But this ADC must be configured to proper sampling rate for each channel. In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed to automatically generate ADC configuration, and improve the ADC’s utilization and utility, reduce the number of redundant bits, and reduce cost. This proposed algorithm is mathematically formulated, and numerical examples are given. The research methodology involves using FPGA board with analog to digital and digital to analog conversion card, and synthetic wave form is generated and captured for verification. In this phase, a single channel is investigated, as the investigation of multi-channel DAQ requires the integration and scheduling of the ADC with an external analog multiplexer. In prior work, a custom computer board is designed to implement the HTMS algorithm for 32 analog channels. To effectively demonstrate the previously proposed HTMS superiority against other approaches, new performance metrics were defined, namely the ADC’s utilization, utility and efficiency using two different heuristic analog input sets. These metrics show that the HTMS-based DAQ outperforms relevant systems as it reaches 100% of ADC’s utilization and utility, while other systems have 75% utilization, and 6.25% utility. By devising a unified figure of merit for multiple DAQ systems, it is shown that the proposed system is higher by 218% compared to the baseline multi-channel DAQ system. Furthermore, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) has been extensively investigated for cryptographic applications. A given pipelined 54-cycle AES-256-bit key core is considered for enhancement. With a single cycle design approach, the given core is successfully implemented in FPGA device using only 14-cycles / round, and generating a maximum encryption throughput of 12.8 Gb/s, with an FPGA utilization of only 9% Cyclone V SX SoC 5CSXFC6D6F31C6N, with speed up factor of 7 times is reported, compared to recent results, operating at a maximum clock frequency of 100 MHz. The proposed system will have a broader impact, particularly in medical diagnosis and prognosis, where multiple sensors of heterogenous types are used simultaneously, and the collected data must be secured to protect subjects’ privacy.

Article.Title: Risk assessment of coal mine water inrush based on AHP–entropy weight matter-element extension model
Article.Authors: Jing G.; Yang D.; Qin R.
Article.Abstract: This study focuses on the risk assessment and prevention of coal mine water inrush, aiming to reduce accident incidence through proactive prevention. Based on water inrush accident statistics from 2011 to 2025, the distribution patterns of water inrush accidents are revealed across regional, temporal, and ownership-structure dimensions, and an accident causation model is established by integrating accident causation theory. Furthermore, by incorporating the human–machine–environment–management framework and deep-mining characteristics, a water inrush risk evaluation index system comprising 6 first-level indicators and 30 s-level indicators is constructed through the screening of 68 cases and literature sources. A water inrush risk assessment model is developed based on Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and matter-element extension theory. Indicator weights are determined by combining the AHP with the entropy weight method, and the correlation degree is computed using MATLAB to determine risk grades. Taking Pingmei J Coal Mine as a case study, the results indicate that the comprehensive risk of the mine falls between medium and relatively low risk, leaning toward the latter. Accordingly, targeted water prevention and control measures are proposed, providing a scientific basis, decision-making reference, and actionable prevention and control countermeasures for mine water inrush risk management.

Article.Title: Magnetite records high-δ18O fluid evolution in the Shinyemi Fe skarn deposit, South Korea
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Kim C.; Yi K.; Kim J.; Ryu J.; Oh J.; Park C.; Kim H.; Kang P.; Lim C.
Article.Abstract: Carbonate-hosted Fe skarn deposits form through reactions between magmatic-hydrothermal fluids and carbonate wall rocks, but the effects of magmatic input, wall-rock interaction, and later hydrothermal modification are difficult to separate. Here we combine zircon U–Pb geochronology, phlogopite 40 Ar/ 39 Ar dating, magnetite trace-element chemistry, Ti + V-in-magnetite thermometry, and Fe–O isotopes to examine fluid evolution in the Shinyemi Fe skarn deposit. Zircon U–Pb ages indicate Late Cretaceous emplacement of quartz monzonite and granite at ca. 84–81 Ma, followed by emplacement of an intermediate dyke at 80.4 ± 0.8 Ma. A phlogopite 40 Ar/ 39 Ar weighted mean apparent age of 84.6 ± 2.5 Ma provides a constraint on hydrothermal cooling or alteration. Magnetite has low Ti–V contents and variable Mg, Mn, Al, Si, and Ca contents, consistent with skarn-type hydrothermal magnetite. Ti + V-in-magnetite thermometry yields a median temperature of 385 °C ( n = 304). Magnetite δ 56 Fe values range from − 0.12 to + 0.31‰, and δ 18 O values range from + 2.6 to + 4.4‰, whereas calculated apparent δ 18 O fluid values range from + 11.1 to + 12.8‰. Together, the trace-element and isotope data are consistent with magmatic-hydrothermal Fe input and subsequent oxygen-isotope modification during interaction with carbonate wall rocks and later hydrothermal processes.

Article.Title: Projected Amazon forest loss alters tropical Atlantic circulation and surface heat exchange through reduced freshwater input
Article.Authors: de Almeida Gouveia N.; Wongchuig S.; Espinoza J.; Aragão L.; Paes E.; Santos R.; Gherardi D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deforestation alters the terrestrial water cycle, with consequences that can extend to the ocean. In the Amazon Basin, projected forest loss is expected to substantially modify river discharge, yet how these hydrological changes affect tropical ocean circulation and surface heat exchange remains poorly understood. Here we ran an offline hydrological simulation with the MGB (Modelo de Grandes Bacias, or Large-Basin Model) to produce river outflow for a business-as-usual deforestation scenario projected for 2050, that was fed into the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) to simulate the ocean for the period 1992–2015. This setup isolates the influence of changes in freshwater export on the western tropical North Atlantic. Simulations of a business-as-usual 2050 scenario (~ 45% forest loss) show dry-season discharge reductions exceeding 50% in southern tributaries and ~ 12% at Óbidos, increasing surface salinity and reorganizing the Amazon River plume. These changes intensify the North Brazil Current and its retroflection by ~ 14%, deepen the mixed layer by up to ~ 6 m, thin the barrier layer by up to ~ 8 m, and alter surface heat exchange, warming the surface by up to 0.4 °C along the retroflection and North Equatorial Countercurrent corridor during boreal summer and autumn. Sustained Amazon forest loss can therefore drive persistent changes in the upper-ocean circulation and heat distribution of the tropical Atlantic.

Article.Title: From projected phase to surface-state electrostatics in FIB-prepared semiconductor lamellae
Article.Authors: Çelik H.; Fuchs R.; Häusler I.; Lehmann M.; Koch C.; Busch K.; Wagner T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Off-axis electron holography provides quantitative access to projected electrostatic potentials in semiconductor devices. However, focused-ion-beam (FIB) preparation can substantially modify the near-surface electrostatics of transmission electron microscopy lamellae. These effects redistribute the internal potential through surface-state charging, band bending, and screening, making the measured phase difficult to interpret in terms of the crystalline device core. Here, we establish a physical interpretation of the multilayer Simple and Intuitive Model for Potentials (SIMP), a three-dimensional forward-modeling framework for reconstructing electrostatic potentials from projected electron-holographic phase images, by relating its phenomenological parameters to effective screening lengths, near-surface band bending, electric fields, and charge carrier densities. As an illustration, the framework is then applied to symmetrically doped Si p-n junction lamellae prepared at final FIB acceleration voltages of 2 kV and 30 kV. The results show that reduced projected fields can arise primarily from averaging over preparation-modified near-surface regions rather than from intrinsically weak junction electrostatics. This advances multilayer SIMP from an empirical reconstruction method towards a physically anchored framework for quantitative electrostatic characterization of FIB-prepared semiconductor nanostructures.

Article.Title: Handling techniques of an unbalanced stick tool in Goffin’s cockatoos (Cacatua goffiniana)
Article.Authors: Nasa Ö.; Folkertsma R.; Auersperg A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Parrots (Psittaciformes) exhibit unique morphological and behavioral traits that enable flexible, dexterous tool use, often comparable to that of apes. In tool-using species, attending to weight-related cues can enhance foraging efficiency by minimizing the energetic costs of tool manipulation. Previous research has shown that Goffin’s cockatoos ( Cacatua goffiniana ) can detect and utilize weight cues, but their sensitivity to unbalanced objects remains unexplored. This study examined how Goffin’s cockatoos managed an unbalanced stick tool and the individual strategies they used to complete a stick-tool box task. We carried out a series of experiments using a setup with different levels of difficulty, focusing on variations in insertion techniques and the birds’ ability to distinguish unequal weight distributions. At the group level, the cockatoos tended to handle the stick with the center of mass positioned closer to their grip. The birds also demonstrated highly individualized adaptations in their techniques when solving unfamiliar problems. We suggest that individuals that did not modify their techniques in this setup may still be capable of doing so under greater task constraints. Overall, these findings provide the first evidence that Goffin’s cockatoos can detect and adjust to uneven weight distribution in tools, underscoring their behavioral flexibility and sensitivity to physical tool properties.

Article.Title: Research on the surface settlement regularity induced by tunnel construction and operation in saturated loess strata
Article.Authors: Wei Z.; Sen P.; Caihui Z.; Haoding X.; Zhiqiang Z.; Xingxing G.; Xing L.; Guohua D.; Xinyi T.
Article.Abstract: The surface settlement (SS) caused by shield tunnel in the loess strata of the northwest region is significant during the construction and operation periods. Taking a metro section tunnel as an example, using the Fast Lagrangian Analysis of Continua in 3D(FLAC 3D ) software, the parameters n and α that affect the constitutive model of the soil layer were inversely analyzed. This study deeply explored the influence laws of various factors on surface settlement during the shield construction and operation periods, and conducted sensitivity analysis on these factors. The results show: (1) The modified Mohr–Coulomb model (MMC) better reflects the SS caused by shield tunneling. To reduce the impact of SS, it is recommended to control the soil chamber pressure ratio between 1.0 and 1.2, the grouting pressure ratio between 0.9 and 1.2, and the shield thrust ratio has little effect. This method not only meets the settlement requirements but also reduces economic losses and construction risks. (2) To ensure the long-term safety of the shield segments, the number of leakage blocks should not exceed 3. The groundwater recharge and elevation in the loess layer can help reduce SS, but it should be controlled within 3.0 m. It is recommended that the groundwater level should be controlled 2 m below the initial water level. (3) Through the sensitivity analysis of SS, the sensitivity of each influencing factor to SS from high to low is as follows: the number of leaking segments Q SS ( N ) > the falling height of groundwater level (FHGL) Q SS (△ h F ) > soil chamber pressure ratio Q SS ( λ ) > grouting pressure ratio Q SS ( δ ) > the rising height of groundwater level (RHGL) Q SS (△ h R ) > shield thrust ratio Q SS ( ψ ). In the later stage of construction, first focus on the waterproof measures of the lining segments, which is a key issue to be concerned about in the later stage. Secondly, the change of the groundwater level is controlled as much as possible to keep the groundwater level of the soil layer unchanged. During the construction period, the main control is the change of the grouting pressure. On the basis of the grouting pressure, the grouting pressure and the shield thrust should reach the soil pressure balance.

Article.Title: MER-CycleGAN: memory-embedded residual learning for brain MRI synthesis and harmonization
Article.Authors: Tavse S.; Bachute M.; Ankam J.; Bhoi A.
Article.Abstract: Variations in imaging modality, scanner field strength, and acquisition conditions can introduce substantial heterogeneity in brain MRI data, affecting the robustness and generalizability of automated image analysis. This study proposes MER-CycleGAN, a memory-embedded residual learning framework that integrates memory modules within intermediate residual representations of the CycleGAN generator to enhance feature processing during image synthesis. The framework was evaluated on two complementary unpaired MRI domain translation scenarios: T1-weighted-to-T2-weighted cross-modality synthesis and 1.5T-to-3T cross-scanner harmonization. Performance was assessed using MAE, MSE, PSNR, SSIM, paired statistical tests, effect-size analysis, qualitative evaluation, and spatial error maps. Additional downstream evaluation of the 1.5T-to-3T harmonization task was performed using hippocampal segmentation and CN-versus-AD classification. MER-CycleGAN consistently outperformed the fixed baseline CycleGAN on the primary cycle-reconstruction metrics and showed greater similarity to real target-domain images in the evaluated feature space. The reconstruction improvements were statistically significant with large effect sizes, and were accompanied by reduced spatial reconstruction errors. In the downstream evaluation, hippocampal segmentation showed modest and metric-dependent differences between the two models. None of the segmentation measures remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing, while CN-versus-AD classification showed modest numerical improvements in balanced accuracy and AUC for MER-CycleGAN. The findings demonstrate that explicit memory interaction within the generator feature space provides an effective strategy for improving cycle-consistent unpaired brain MRI domain translation across cross-modality synthesis and scanner harmonization scenarios. However, the downstream findings do not establish clinical superiority, and further validation using larger independent multi-site cohorts, paired target-domain data, and expert clinical assessment is required to confirm broader generalizability and clinical applicability.

Article.Title: SiamDUKF: RGBE Siamese tracking with a differentiable unscented Kalman filter
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Qiu J.; Li P.; Lu Y.; Fang Y.; Zheng K.
Article.Abstract: In practical UAV tracking, performance is often degraded by nonlinear maneuvers, abrupt illumination changes, and occlusion. Single-modality trackers therefore struggle to maintain robust performance in complex environments. To address this issue, we propose SiamDUKF, a Siamese-network-based tracking framework that integrates RGB and event information with a differentiable unscented Kalman filter (Diff-UKF). Built upon SiamFC, the framework adopts a dual-branch backbone with unshared weights to extract modality-specific features and employs CBAM for adaptive cross-modal refinement and fusion. In addition, a lightweight MLP predicts the process and measurement noise covariance based on tracking confidence and motion nonlinearity, enabling end-to-end joint optimization of multimodal feature learning and state estimation. Experimental results on the VETD220 dataset show that SiamDUKF achieves a success rate of 62.2%, a precision rate of 83.0%, and a tracking speed of 82.7 FPS, indicating competitive accuracy, robustness, and real-time performance.

Article.Title: Association of first-row local minimum burden dispersion with surface oversize counts in open-pit bench blasting
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Mao Y.; Zhen S.
Article.Abstract: Surface oversize counts can vary markedly among production blasts even when design and construction conditions are comparable and the first-row mean burden is close to the design value. We established a database of 100 production blasts from the same mining area of the Yulong Copper Mine. A field-validated point-cloud method provided the first-row local minimum burden sequence \(\:{B}_{i}\) ; \(\:{B}_{\text{m}\text{e}\text{a}\text{n}}\) represented the overall burden level and \(\:{B}_{\text{s}\text{t}\text{d}}\) its within-row dispersion. Surface fragments larger than 1.0 m were counted throughout loading and haulage as \(\:{N}_{o}\) . \(\:{B}_{\text{m}\text{e}\text{a}\text{n}}\) (3.86–4.10 m) was unrelated to \(\:{N}_{o}\) ( r = 0.004), ( p = 0.966), whereas \(\:{B}_{\text{s}\text{t}\text{d}}\) (0.017–0.324 m) was strongly positively correlated with \(\:{N}_{o}\) ( r = 0.961), (rho = 0.958), ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.924\) ), ( p < 0.001). Six field-derived equal-mean, variable-dispersion numerical cases showed an overall increase in strip-scale response heterogeneity with \(\:{B}_{\text{s}\text{t}\text{d}}\) ( r = 0.829), ( p = 0.041); high-dispersion cases also showed spatial correspondence between large local burden deviations and weak-response strips. Mesh assessment supported comparisons of spatial heterogeneity. The combined evidence identifies \(\:{B}_{\text{s}\text{t}\text{d}}\) as a useful pre-blast geometric indicator of surface oversize risk under comparable production conditions and supports coordinated control of \(\:{B}_{\text{m}\text{e}\text{a}\text{n}}\) and \(\:{B}_{\text{s}\text{t}\text{d}}\) .
