Article.Title: Laccase assisted gallic acid functionalization of corn straw fibers and their reinforcing effects on SBS modified asphalt binder
Article.Authors: Huang M.; Dai W.; Guo W.; Yuan S.; Cao G.; Gu K.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the regulatory effects of differently modified corn straw fibers (CSF)—a green fiber material derived from agricultural waste—on the mechanical properties, rheological characteristics, and molecular structural evolution of asphalt binders. Although plant fibers have been widely used in asphalt modification, natural CSF remains difficult to apply directly because of its insufficient toughness, poor structural stability, and weak interfacial compatibility. To address these limitations, CSF was modified using NaOH, tannic acid, and a gallic acid–laccase synergistic system. The effects and reinforcement mechanisms of different modification methods were revealed through fiber mechanical tests, abrasion tests, SEM, FTIR, XPS, dynamic shear rheological tests, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that the gallic acid–laccase synergistic modification exhibited superior overall performance. Compared with unmodified fibers, the tensile strength, elastic modulus, and elongation at break of the modified fibers increased by 127.51%, 154.00%, and 45.97%, respectively, while the abrasion loss rate decreased by 56.85%. Microscopic characterization indicated that the gallic acid–laccase modification formed a functionalized layer rich in oxygen-containing functional groups on the fiber surface, enhancing fiber surface activity and interfacial bonding potential. Rheological tests showed that GA-CSF significantly improved the high-temperature stiffness, elastic recovery ability, and resistance to permanent deformation of SBS-modified asphalt. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that GA-CSF increased the cohesive energy density and elastic modulus of the system while reducing the free volume fraction, suggesting enhanced intermolecular interactions and restricted molecular motion in asphalt. These findings demonstrate that gallic acid–laccase synergistic modification is an effective approach for improving the reinforcing potential of corn straw fibers and enhancing the high-temperature rheological performance of SBS-modified asphalt binders.

Article.Title: Student technology self-efficacy statistically mediates the associations of institutional and online instructor support with AI literacy in AI-mediated online learning
Article.Authors: Song L.; Wang W.; Xu J.
Article.Abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has transformed how students learn and interact with knowledge, making AI literacy an essential competency in the digital age. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, this study examined the associations of institutional support and online instructors’ support with AI literacy and the mediating role of student technology self-efficacy among Chinese university students in AI-mediated online learning environments. AI literacy was conceptualised as a multidimensional construct comprising Technical Understanding, Critical Appraisal, and Practical Application. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 603 Chinese university students aged 18–26 years in Shanxi Province, China. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM). Institutional support and online instructors’ support significantly predicted both student technology self-efficacy and AI literacy. The standardised association between online instructors’ support and AI literacy was numerically larger than that between institutional support and AI literacy. Student technology self-efficacy partially mediated the relationships between institutional support, online instructors’ support, and AI literacy. These findings support the application of an SCT-informed framework to AI-mediated learning environments, showing that environmental support is statistically associated with AI literacy, both directly and indirectly through student technology self-efficacy. The study contributes to AI education research by clarifying the statistical relationships through which institutional support and online instructors’ support are associated with AI literacy.

Article.Title: Illumination-guided and reliability-aware YOLOv11 for low-light object detection
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Huang K.; Zhan Y.; Yang M.; Hao J.; Che W.; Zheng J.; Qin X.; Ning Y.
Article.Abstract: Target detection in low-light environments has wide applications, but it faces challenges due to extremely weak photon responses, severe sensor noise, and broken target geometry. We propose a target detection architecture based on feature-level physical prior decoupling–Illumination-Guided and Reliability-aware YOLO (IGU-YOLO). First, we design a reliability-aware illumination gating module (UIG-Block) in the shallow backbone layers. It estimates illumination priors and learns a feature-reliability map for confidence-guided suppression of unreliable responses. To further separate illumination from noise, we design a self-supervised illumination consistency loss (SIC Loss). Together, these two designs encourage the model to learn physically consistent illumination distributions without real illumination labels and to reduce unreliable feature injection through confidence gating. Second, to address broken target contours in extremely dark regions, we deploy an illumination-guided deformation refinement module (IGD-R) in the backbone. This module uses shallow illumination priors to guide deformable convolution for spatial structure reconstruction and introduces a frequency-domain mechanism to suppress secondary semantic artifacts. Experiments on the extremely low-light benchmark dataset ExDark show that IGU-YOLO improves \(mAP_{50}\) , \(mAP_{75}\) , and \(mAP_{50:95}\) by 2.6%, 2.7%, and 2.1%, respectively, over the baseline, demonstrating its effectiveness under low-light conditions.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: low-light object detection; YOLOv11; deformable convolution; self-supervised learning

Article.Title: Risk of groundwater loss from an ecologically vital aquifer induced by bed separation: an assessment using strain‑softening numerical simulation
Article.Authors: Fan L.; Fan K.; Xue S.
Article.Abstract: The groundwater stored in the Cretaceous strata constitutes a vital water resource for maintaining ecological stability in the Ordos Basin. This study assesses the risk of groundwater loss induced by coal mining, with particular emphasis on the influence of rock strain-softening behavior. Using the Yingpanhao Mining Area as a case study, the water-conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) was characterized using underground borehole measurements. A three-dimensional distinct-element model was developed to simulate the response of overlying strata to mining, employing both the conventional Mohr–Coulomb (MC) model and a strain-softening (SS) constitutive model. The simulation results indicate that the SS model more accurately captures progressive failure and the connectivity of plastic zones in key lithological units, including the medium sandstone within the Zhiluo Formation. The SS model predicted a WCFZ height of 124 m, in reasonable agreement with the measured height of 115.5 m. In contrast, the MC model predicted a WCFZ height of 57 m, corresponding to a relative error of 50.6%. The evolution of bed separations with increasing mining advance was also simulated, revealing four distinct separation zones. Based on the simulated WCFZ heights and protective-layer thickness distributions, a water-inrush coefficient map was generated, revealing pronounced north–south spatial heterogeneity in the evaluated water-inrush hazard, with localized areas of relatively high coefficient values concentrated in the southern region. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating strain-softening behavior when evaluating mining-induced overburden failure and provide a numerical basis for identifying areas potentially vulnerable to mining-related groundwater loss.

Article.Title: Land fragmentation and agricultural commercialization: New insights from Cameroon
Article.Authors: Ndip F.; Nzira J.; Kambiet P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Land fragmentation (LF) is a salient feature of smallholder agriculture. However, its implications for agriculture and the livelihoods of smallholders remain ambiguous as studies report both negative and positive effects. In this study, we add to the literature by analyzing how LF is associated with agricultural commercialization, which has not been studied so far. This is important because commercialization is an essential facet of agricultural transformation with several implications for the livelihood of smallholders. Specifically, we hypothesize and test a potential non-linear relationship between LF and commercialization, using unique survey data from Cameroon. Estimating non-linear models, we find a robust non-linear (inverted U-shape) relationship between LF and commercialization. As LF starts increasing, it is initially associated with higher commercialization up to a threshold beyond which further increases in LF are associated with lower commercialization. We further show that the possible mechanisms through which LF operates are crop diversification and the use of modern inputs like pesticides and inorganic fertilizers, where we also find these inverted U-shape patterns. In addition to different U-shape tests that confirm these results, the results are also robust across different indicators of LF, different estimators, and are unlikely to be driven by unobserved factors. These findings suggest that LF could also have positive benefits and thus these patterns may be relevant for policy makers when designing consolidation policies. In addition, modeling the relationship between LF and other outcomes would provide more insights for targeted policies.

Article.Title: Assessing nursing and midwifery students’ knowledge, attitude, and preparedness in managing intimate partner violence
Article.Authors: Almegewly W.; Khedr M.; Hendy A.; Hussien R.; Amodi R.; Aleanzi A.; Alfaifi R.; Alshamari J.; Almalki N.; Alkhars F.; Alghmlas N.; Dator W.
Article.Abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a global public health concern that requires healthcare professionals, including nurses and midwives, to be prepared to recognize, assess, and respond to affected individuals. However, limited evidence exists regarding nursing and midwifery students’ preparedness to manage IPV. This study aimed to assess nursing and midwifery students’ knowledge, attitudes, and preparedness in managing IPV and to identify factors associated with preparedness. A descriptive, cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted among 309 nursing and midwifery students at a selected university in Saudi Arabia. Data were collected using the modified Physician Readiness to Manage Intimate Partner Violence Survey (PRIMS). Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, Pearson correlation analysis, mediation analysis, and multiple linear regression were performed to examine relationships among study variables and identify factors associated with IPV management preparedness. Nursing students reported significantly higher perceived knowledge, more positive attitudes toward IPV, and greater perceived preparedness than midwifery students, whereas actual IPV knowledge did not differ significantly between groups. Significant positive correlations were observed among actual knowledge, perceived knowledge, attitudes, and perceived preparedness. The exploratory mediation analysis revealed a small but statistically significant indirect association between actual knowledge and perceived preparedness involving attitude toward IPV (indirect effect = 0.042, bootstrap 95% CI [0.002, 0.101]). The direct association remained significant (B = 0.283, p = 0.019), consistent with a pattern of partial statistical mediation rather than evidence of a causal pathway. In the multiple linear regression model, perceived knowledge (β = 0.301, p < 0.001) and specialty (β = 0.147, p = 0.006) were independently associated with perceived preparedness. Actual knowledge, attitude toward IPV, academic year, age, and IPV-related training were not significantly associated with perceived preparedness after adjustment. The model explained 18.3% of the variance in perceived preparedness (R 2 = 0.183; adjusted R 2 = 0.158), indicating that much of the variability remained unexplained. Nursing and midwifery students reported an overall perceived preparedness score of 49.37 ± 10.36. Nursing students reported significantly greater perceived preparedness than midwifery students. Perceived knowledge and specialty were independently associated with preparedness, while attitude toward IPV showed a significant indirect association between actual knowledge and preparedness.

Article.Title: Nested association mapping (NAM) reveals genetic architecture of agronomic traits in quinoa
Article.Authors: Lozano-Isla F.; Munoz-Salas M.; Vidal-Villarejo M.; Haussmann B.; Mujica-Sanchez A.; Schmid K.
Article.Abstract: Quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is a stress tolerant pseudocereal recognized for its nutritional value and adaptation to marginal environments. However, breeding progress for yield and resilient cultivars remains constrained by limited knowledge of the genetic architecture of agronomic traits. To address this gap, two nested association mapping (NAM) populations were developed using the recurrent parents Salcedo INIA, a high-yielding cultivar, and Kancolla, a traditional highland landrace, crossed with four diverse founder cultivars from the Peruvian Altiplano. Previously collected multi-environment phenotypic data from 125 recombinant inbred lines were integrated with low coverage whole-genome resequencing, from which 5’803 high-quality SNP markers were retained in 118 individuals for genomic analyses. Population structure analyses showed differentiation between Salcedo and Kancolla families, with limited differentiation among families. Genome-wide association analysis identified 29 significant SNPs involving 21 unique SNPs across eight agronomic traits, including flowering time, physiological maturity, plant height, panicle morphology, and yield. Candidate genes analysis identified 38 genes located within genomic regions surrounding significant SNPs. Genomic prediction showed trait and population dependent performance, with accuracies ranging from − 0.11 to 0.79 and the highest values observed for phenological and selected panicle traits. This study establishes a NAM resource for quinoa and provides genomic insights that can support genetic dissection and efficient selection for adaptation and productivity in Andean breeding programs.
Article.Topic: Genetic Mapping and Diversity in Plants and Animals

Article.Title: Evolution of non-metallic inclusions in an Al-killed, Ca-treated, low-S steel during industrial secondary refining
Article.Authors: Musi R.; Thiele K.; Ilie S.; Rössler R.; Michelic S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evolution of non-metallic inclusions during secondary refining of an Al-killed, Ca-treated, low-S steel was characterized at eight stages from deoxidation to the tundish. Automated SEM–EDS analysis was applied down to an equivalent circle diameter of 0.5 μm. The modification path proceeded from alumina via spinel to Ca-aluminates. Ca-treatment affected the pre-existing oxides differently: within approximately 85 s of CaSi wire injection, the spinel inclusions were consumed, whereas a small alumina population persisted. A predominantly submicroscopic, transient CaO–CaS population formed and converted to Ca-aluminates within minutes, with the CaS component consumed preferentially. During subsequent ladle holding, reoxidation generated new Ca-poor spinel and alumina alongside the modified inclusions, as the Ca fade progressed from 32 to 17 ppm. Between the final ladle sample and the tundish, the mean number density decreased from 291.4 to 96.4 mm - ², the size distributions shifted toward larger diameters in every heat, and the total O content decreased from 29 to 13 ppm, indicating agglomeration-assisted removal. Despite differences during treatment, all four heats converged at the tundish, centered on the low-melting 12CaO·7Al 2 O 3 composition. For the investigated steel and process route, tundish samples therefore provide a reliable basis for cleanness assessment, whereas single ladle samples may not be representative.

Article.Title: EffiThy-Net: a lightweight lesion-calibrated and boundary-preserving network for thyroid nodule segmentation
Article.Authors: Shi Z.; Wu W.; Liu J.; Hu H.; Tao J.; Guo S.; Li P.
Article.Abstract: Accurate thyroid nodule segmentation is important for ultrasound image analysis, yet low contrast, blurred boundaries, and heterogeneous background responses jointly affect lesion recognition, contour localization, and mask generation. More specifically, lesion structures and irrelevant high-frequency background patterns may produce similar local responses, deep and shallow features are prone to semantic-contour misalignment in weak-boundary regions, and classification, localization, and mask prediction may compete when they share the same features. To address these issues, this paper proposes EffiThy-Net, a lightweight lesion-calibrated and boundary-preserving segmentation network that establishes a coordinated processing pipeline for lesion-aware feature calibration, lesion-contour semantic alignment, and boundary-preserving prototype-decoupled mask decoding. First, the Lesion-Aware Alternating Calibration Block (LAC-Block) alternates feature propagation and response calibration to suppress irrelevant high-frequency background responses while preserving lesion-related structures. Second, the Lesion-Contour Semantic Alignment Module (LCSA) uses deep lesion semantics to constrain shallow contour details, thereby alleviating feature misalignment in weak-boundary regions. Third, the Boundary-Preserving Prototype Decoupling Head (BPD-Head) reduces interference among prediction branches through task decoupling and prototype-based mask reconstruction. Experiments on the TN3K and TNUI-2021 datasets are conducted under a unified pixel-level mask evaluation protocol. The results show that EffiThy-Net achieves a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency under the current setting. Compared with DeepLabv3+, the proposed method improves DSC by 3.1 percentage points on TNUI-2021 while reducing the number of parameters by 92.5% and GFLOPs by 91.4%. Additional controlled additive Gaussian perturbation experiments show that, on TN3K, when the perturbation level reaches \(\sigma =20\) , the drops in mAP@50 and DSC for EffiThy-Net are 2.5 and 2.3 percentage points, respectively, which are smaller than those of the included YOLO baselines. These results indicate lower sensitivity to the evaluated additive Gaussian perturbations, but they do not establish robustness to physical multiplicative ultrasound speckle.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy trajectories and their associated factors in patients with gastrointestinal tumors: a cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen Q.; Zhu H.; Bao H.; Nie L.; Peng Y.; Qiu J.; Zhou Y.; Huang W.; Jiang L.; Ren X.; Ren L.
Article.Abstract: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common and important nerve-related side effect of chemotherapy. However, researchers still know little about how CIPN changes over time in patients with gastrointestinal tumors. This prospective cohort study aimed to identify different CIPN patterns during chemotherapy and to examine factors related to these patterns. We recruited 233 patients with gastrointestinal tumors from a tertiary cancer center. All patients had a pathological diagnosis and received first-line chemotherapy with drugs known to cause peripheral nerve damage. At baseline, we collected demographic and clinical data. We also measured cancer-related fatigue with the Revised Piper Fatigue Scale, physical performance with the Short Physical Performance Battery, and self-management efficacy with the Strategies Used by People to Promote Health scale. We assessed CIPN symptoms with the Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy Assessment Tool after the 1st, 3rd, 5th, and 7th chemotherapy cycles. We used latent class growth modeling to identify CIPN trajectory patterns. We used chi-square tests, analysis of variance, and logistic regression analyses to examine factors related to these patterns. We identified four CIPN trajectories: worsening CIPN symptoms (71 patients, 30.5%), mild stable CIPN symptoms (81 patients, 34.8%), improving CIPN symptoms (42 patients, 18.0%), and severe stable CIPN symptoms (39 patients, 16.7%). Age, smoking history, number of chronic diseases, chemotherapy regimen, standardized cumulative neurotoxic exposure index, cancer-related fatigue, physical performance, and self-management efficacy were related to CIPN trajectory membership. These findings highlight the heterogeneity of CIPN trajectories during chemotherapy and the factors associated with trajectory membership.

Article.Title: Nonlinear association between baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and severe acute pancreatitis in the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the association between baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) in patients with acute pancreatitis (AP) using MIMIC-IV data. Adult patients with index AP admission and NLR measured within 24 h were included. The primary outcome was severe AP, defined by the Revised Atlanta Classification as Modified Marshall organ failure persisting beyond 48 h; in-hospital mortality was the key secondary outcome, with prolonged ICU and hospital stay evaluated as additional secondary outcomes. Mechanical ventilation and vasopressor use were retained as descriptive endpoints because they contributed to the EHR-based operationalization of organ dysfunction. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were performed with adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, etiology, and APACHE II score; subgroup analyses were also conducted. Among 1,044 patients, 200 (19.2%) developed severe AP and 106 (10.2%) died in hospital; ln(NLR) was independently associated with severe AP (OR = 1.329, 95%CI:1.129–1.566, p < 0.001). RCS revealed a significant nonlinear relationship ( p < 0.001), with a steeper increase in the odds of severe AP around NLR values of 8–9 and a flattening thereafter. High NLR was associated with higher odds of in-hospital mortality compared with low NLR (OR = 2.300, 95%CI: 1.340–3.949, p = 0.003), and continuous ln(NLR) was also associated with mortality (OR = 1.420, 95%CI: 1.129–1.785, p = 0.003), although the nonlinear component was not significant for mortality ( p = 0.063). Baseline NLR shows a nonlinear association with severe AP in MIMIC-IV, with a steeper increase in the odds of severe AP around NLR values of 8–9. NLR may serve as an accessible early risk stratification tool, though external validation is needed.

Article.Title: Research on the spatial characteristics of traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi corridor of China under geospatial technology approaches
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Zhai S.; Guo Y.
Article.Abstract: The article takes 267 traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor region as the research object, the spatio-temporal differentiation and influencing factors of the traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor were analysed with the help of ArcGIS software. And their relationships with the natural environment, humanities and social factors were explored, in an attempt to provide a theoretical foundation and technical support for the development and conservation of the traditional villages in the area in the future.The results show that: (1) The spatial distribution of traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor is of agglomerative structural type, with Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture of Ganzi and Lijiang City are the two places with the highest number of traditional villages. (2) The nearest-neighbour index R value of the 267 traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor is 0.524, indicating that the traditional villages are in a clustered state. (3) A variety of factors combine to create the spatial agglomeration characteristics of traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor, factors such as topographical features, hydrology and socio-economics may combining to affect the distribution characteristics of traditional villages.

Article.Title: Sequence stratigraphy, sedimentary systems and implications for hydrocarbon exploration in the Qaidam Basin, Northern China
Article.Authors: Song F.; Liu Y.; Su N.; Jin Z.; Yuan J.
Article.Abstract: The Qaidam Basin is endowed with abundant Paleogene–Neogene hydrocarbon resources and possesses major exploration potential. Lacking an overall understanding on sequence stratigraphy and sedimentary facies of the basin is not favorable for making new progress in hydrocarbon exploration. In this study, using outcrop, core, well logging and seismic data, the Paleogene–Neogene strata of the Qaidam Basin was divided into 7 second-order sequences, 12 third-order sequences and 24 system tracts. In addition, 7 sedimentary facies types were identified, i.e., alluvial fan, braided river, flood plain, fan delta, braided river delta, lacustrine deposit and turbidite fan. Six single sedimentary factors were selected for analysis, and with third-order sequences as the unit, the distribution and evolution of sedimentary systems were defined. For the controlling factors of lithofacies paleogeography, “snow mountains controlling lakes” and “fault steps control basins” were proposed. It is believed that under a compressional tectonic setting, lake level fluctuation is closely related to elevations of peripheral mountains, and lake water is sourced principally from mountain snowmelt. A higher structural uplifting amplitude will result in a larger area of mountain snow, a greater water supply and a larger lake area. Boundary faults of the basin retreated towards the mountains in a step way, resulting in an expanded basin. However, the faults advancing towards the center of the basin aroused basin shrinkage. From a sedimentary view, the distribution characteristics of Paleogene–Neogene source rocks and reservoirs of the Qaidam Basin were analyzed; it is proposed that the periphery of the hydrocarbon generation center of the Shizigou–Mangya sag is the present-day optimum exploration zone, and the periphery of the hydrocarbon generation center of the Yiliping depression center is a potential favorable exploration zone.

Article.Title: Persistence of the bar transgene during recurrent backcrossing between GM Brassica napus and Brassica rapa subsp. narinosa
Article.Authors: Pandian S.; Shin E.; Sohn S.
Article.Abstract: Interspecific hybridization between cultivated crops and their wild or closely related species is a major route for transgene escape and remains an important concern in environmental biosafety assessment of genetically modified (GM) crops. In this study, we evaluated the potential for bar transgene introgression from GM Brassica napus line TG#39 into Brassica rapa subsp. narinosa ‘Dachae’ (DC) through reciprocal hybridization and recurrent backcrossing. Although both reciprocal crosses produced viable F₁ hybrids, reproductive performance declined markedly in the F₂ generation and varied between the two backcross lineages; nevertheless, viable BC₁ and BC₂ progenies were obtained. Morphological analyses showed that F₁ hybrids displayed paternal- or intermediate-like characteristics, while BC₁ progenies showed substantial phenotypic variation. BC₂ progenies showed reduced within-group dispersion for some traits, although the direction and magnitude of variation differed among traits and lineages. Morphological and SSR analyses provided complementary evidence: morphological traits revealed generation- and lineage-dependent segregation, whereas SSR markers showed lineage-specific similarity to the corresponding recurrent parents. In the DC × TG#39 lineage, the bar transgene remained detectable in tested BC₂ progenies despite increased SSR-based similarity to the DC recurrent parent. These findings show that the bar transgene remained detectable through two successive backcross generations in this controlled crossing system, supporting consideration of subsequent backcross generations in GM Brassica biosafety assessment.

Article.Title: A new approach to recognize performance deviation pattern of a micro gas turbine under different degradation factors
Article.Authors: Talebi S.; Madadi A.; Tousi A.
Article.Abstract: The pivotal role of micro gas turbines (MGT) as backup power sources for renewable energy systems and distributed power generation has significantly increased the importance of condition monitoring. Fouling and erosion are two main factors of gas turbine deterioration. Gas path parameter analysis is a popular way to carry out more accurate and robust diagnostics. Due to the high nonlinearity of the MGT dynamics, this analysis is a challenging process that consumes high computational costs. This study proposes a new approach to recognizing the faults’ signatures. A performance adaptation approach is proposed to generate off-design operating conditions for the MGT. The similarity method is applied to consider component degradation. Both clean and faulty operation modeling are validated against available experimental data. The analysis of parameters shows fault detection is obtainable by monitoring shaft speed versus output power; however, any other decision to isolate faulty components or identify fault origin is impossible due to the confusing pattern of variations. To solve the problem, A set of derived variables is formulated using the original parameters. The results show that using shaft speed, Compressor Exit Pressure (CEP), Compressor Exit Temperature (CET), and Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT) to define three transformed variables enables fault diagnosis under off-design operating conditions.

Article.Title: Prognostic role of 18FDG-PET/CT based biomarker, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer survival
Article.Authors: Fatima N.; Zaman M.
Article.Abstract: To determine prognostic strength of 18 FDG PET/CT based glucose metabolism, tumor grading and immunohistochemical markers in breast cancer (BC) patients. The cohort study conducted at PET/CT Section of one of the tertiary care hospitals in Karachi, Pakistan. A total of 110 patients with advanced-stage breast cancer (predominantly stage II or higher) who underwent baseline 18 F-FDG PET/CT between April 2017 and July 2020 were included. Patients were followed for up to five years from date of baseline 18 FDG PET/CT, and metabolic progression-free survival (mPFS) was assessed using serial 18 FDG PET/CT findings. Tumor demographics (type, grading, staging) and immunohistochemistry (estrogen receptor ER, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 HER2/Neu, progesterone receptor PR, Ki-67) were also recorded. Using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analysis, the significant predictors of complete metabolic response (CMR) based on binary outcome (CMR achieved and not achieved) were analyzed. Kaplan Meier’s survival plots were analyzed to measure mPFS against ROC derived cutoff values of significant predictors. The median age of study group was 57 years (25–86 years), significantly obese and 85% invasive ductal CA with 97% grade II-III on Bloom-Richardson classification and stage IV disease (74%). The significant association of maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and Ki-67 index were found in CMR on logistic regression while no significant association of patients’ age, BMI, tumor grading, ER, PR, HER-2/neu status were found in CMR in BC. SUVmax > 5.4 and Ki-67 > 30% were found to have significant association with failure to achieve CMR (AUC 0.729 and 0.759; p = 0.0002* and p = 0.0001* respectively). The mPFS was significantly shorter in patients with SUVmax > 5.4 (29 vs. 45 months; Logrank = 16.356; p = 0.0001*) and in patients with Ki-67 > 30% index (27 vs. 48 months; Logrank = 14.901; p = 0.0001*). Higher baseline SUVmax (> 5.4) and Ki-67 index (> 30%) on baseline 18 FDG were associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CMR and significantly shorter mPFS in breast cancer patients. Integration of metabolic and proliferative biomarkers may improve prognostic risk stratification, particularly in advanced breast cancer.

Article.Title: Efficient greybox fuzzing framework with tabu search
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Niu Z.; Xiao K.
Article.Abstract: Recently, fuzzing has emerged as a prominent technique for automatically detecting a wide range of security vulnerabilities in cybersecurity. Nevertheless, existing fuzzers remain limited in seed scheduling and energy allocation, as they typically rely on coarse-grained criteria or computationally intensive methods to evaluate seed quality. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive fuzzing framework, namely TabuFuzz, which aims to prioritize seeds with a higher likelihood of generating interesting variants through mutation and allocate more energy to that seed. Specifically, TabuFuzz utilizes a tabu search (TS) algorithm to model seed scheduling, enabling the precise selection of promising seeds. In addition, we design an adaptive energy allocation strategy that exploits fine-grained dynamic execution information, thereby enhancing overall fuzzing efficiency. We implement TabuFuzz on top of AFL and evaluate it on nine widely-used real-world programs. Across six independent 24-hour trials, TabuFuzz achieved higher observed path exploration and crash discovery than the evaluated baselines on most target programs, with improvements of 19.89% and 160.87% over AFL, respectively. Comparative analyses further show that TabuFuzz recorded higher numbers of paths and crashes than representative fuzzers such as FairFuzz, MOPT, EcoFuzz, and AFL + + under the reported experimental setup.

Article.Title: Specifics of the growth of lithium-doped KCl single crystals by the Bridgman method in an argon atmosphere
Article.Authors: Shunkeyev K.; Sagimbayeva S.; Kenzhebayeva A.; Ubaev Z.; Beketova G.; Zhumabayev D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A purification and growth process for alkali halide crystals (AHCs) is demonstrated using KCl: Li as a model system and employing an experimental crystal growth setup manufactured by Across International, USA. The process involves the following sequential stages: (i) deposition of a thin pyrolytic carbon coating (pyrolysis) onto the inner surface of a quartz ampoule in order to suppress the adhesion of molten alkali halide compounds (AHCs) to the ampoule walls; (ii) generation of a high vacuum (10 –6 Тоrr) inside the quartz reactor to purify the alkali halide raw materials from oxygen-containing impurities; (iii) establishment of an argon atmosphere (1.1–1.3 bar) and the quartz ampoule shielding as a technological approach for suppressing the evaporation of aggressive halogen vapors. Flame photometry, absorption spectroscopy, and luminescence spectroscopy analyses demonstrate that the KCl crystal matrix was purified from oxygen-containing impurities (OH) down to 0.2 ppm, divalent impurities (Me 2+ ) down to 0.1 − 0.3 ppm, and alkali-metal homolog cations (Li + , Na + ) down to 1–3 ppm. Unique capabilities of the facility were further realized in the growth of KCl single crystals doped with hygroscopic lithium ions. Enhanced scintillation and dosimetric properties of KCl: Li crystals were demonstrated.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation and numerical modeling of the behavior of sandwich panels with grooved PVC foam cores and CFRP/GFRP facings
Article.Authors: Aribi C.; Houari A.; Djellab A.; Chellil A.; Lecheb S.; Safi B.; Nekkaa B.; Amroune S.; Hakizimana E.
Article.Abstract: This work presents a thorough experimental and numerical investigation into the mechanical behavior of sandwich panels subjected to three/four-point bending, as well as flatwise and edgewise compression. The studied structure is designed for aerospace and marine applications, aiming to optimize the trade-off between weight and stiffness. The core consists of a 10 mm thick, grooved, closed-cell Airex C70.55 PVC foam. The skins are formed by three-layer laminates combining carbon fiber (CFRP) and glass fiber (GFRP) fabrics of various areal weights. The panels were manufactured using the vacuum resin infusion process with an epoxy matrix. Experimental results reveal that failure initiation consistently manifests as localized compressive wrinkling of the upper skin, which subsequently progresses into direct crushing beneath the load application points. These tests highlight the critical influence of the facing material and the orientation of the grooved core face relative to the loading direction. The sandwich panel with carbon skins (BMS 9 − 8 3 K-70) outperforms all glass fiber configurations, while the “Up” orientation (grooved face positioned in the upper zone) yields the highest flexural strength. This configuration increases the failure load and the apparent ultimate core shear stress by 24% to 38%, an effect attributed to the resin ribs formed in the grooves during infusion, which raise the local indentation resistance of the loaded face by about one order of magnitude. The experimental flexural stiffness ( \(\:{D}_{exp}\) ) also exceeds the classical sandwich-theory prediction based on the facing modulus ( \(\:{E}_{f}\) ). In parallel, a 3D implicit numerical model was developed in Abaqus. The Hashin progressive damage criterion was implemented to predict composite skin failure, while a Cohesive Zone Model (CZM) based on COH3D8 elements was used to model skin–core interface behavior and delamination. The resin-filled grooves are represented explicitly and the core is described by a hyperfoam model calibrated on compression tests. For the reference configuration (BMS 9 − 8 3 K-70 facings, “Up” orientation, three-point bending), the predicted load–displacement curve agrees with experimental data within 3% for the peak load and 6% for the initial stiffness, with predicted damage localizing at the observed transverse compressive failure of the upper skin.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation of undrained and drained shear behavior of fat clay stabilized with industrial sewage sludge ash and reinforced with PVA fibers
Article.Authors: Jalali J.; Noorzad R.; Ta’negonbadi B.
Article.Abstract: The mechanical properties of industrial sewage sludge ash (ISSA) stabilized and PVA fiber-reinforced fat clay were studied with special reference to the trade-off between strength improvement and brittleness enhancement by stabilization. The experimental program included a complete set of Atterberg limits, standard Proctor compaction, unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial, consolidated-drained direct shear tests, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP) analysis. In the study, the effects of ISSA content (0–15%), PVA fiber dosage (0-0.5%), curing period (14–42 days), and moisture condition were examined. The results show that the ISSA stabilization significantly improved the shear strength of the fat clay and also significantly increased its brittleness. Under a confining pressure of 400 kPa, the maximum deviatoric stress increased from 553 kPa for untreated clay to 1602 kPa for soil stabilized with 5% ISSA. Increasing the ISSA content to 10% resulted in only limited additional improvement. The PVA fiber reinforcement improved the post-peak strength, the deformation capacity, and the resistance to shear localization. Within the investigated range, 5% ISSA, 0.3% PVA fibers, and 42 days of curing provided the most balanced performance. SEM observations showed particle aggregation, structural modification, and stronger interaction between fibers and matrix. TCLP results showed that heavy-metal concentrations were below regulatory limits for the tested conditions. The results suggest that ISSA stabilization with PVA fiber reinforcement is a promising method to improve high-plasticity clay and to reduce the brittleness caused by cementitious stabilization.

Article.Title: Thermal transport and crystallisation in octadecane composites with porous framework coatings and graphene
Article.Authors: Albalawi H.; Mukhtar A.; Jafarov S.; Sotvoldiav D.; Abdullayev A.; Abduvokhidov A.; Yadav B.
Article.Abstract: Low thermal conductivity and leakage limit the use of organic phase change materials for latent heat storage. Confinement can also delay crystallisation. Polyurea capsules containing n-octadecane were coated with either zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) or Universitetet i Oslo-66 (UiO-66) and embedded in a polyurethane matrix containing graphene nanoplatelets. Modulated differential scanning calorimetry characterised heat-flow components, while fast scanning calorimetry examined cooling-rate dependence. At a graphene loading of 5 wt%, the ZIF-8-coated composite had an effective thermal conductivity of 0.78 ± 0.04 W m −1 K −1 at 25 °C and an onset-based supercooling of 1.2 ± 0.2 °C. Corresponding values for the UiO-66-coated composite were 0.72 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 and 2.4 ± 0.3 °C. Control composites containing only the coating or only the graphene reached 0.31 ± 0.02 and 0.44 ± 0.03 W m −1 K −1 , so neither component accounts for the transport of the complete formulation. The ZIF-8-coated composite retained 98.2 ± 1.1% of its initial melting enthalpy after 1000 cycles between 10 and 60 °C, losing 0.34 ± 0.08% of its mass and showing unchanged infrared and diffraction signatures. Values are means and standard deviations across three independently prepared batches. The two coatings differ in thickness, crystallite size, surface area and growth conditions, so the measurements compare complete formulations rather than isolating a topology-dependent nucleation mechanism. Discharge power at device scale remains untested.

Article.Title: Embedded sensing telemetry and a validated explicit finite element digital twin of pressurised uPVC pipe under low velocity impact
Article.Authors: Ahmed H.; Kibria G.; Raphi S.; Benta Bashar J.; Afroz M.
Article.Abstract: Polymeric pipelines are increasingly used for pressurized fluid transport, yet their behavior under accidental low-velocity impact, and the means to monitor it in service, remain underdeveloped relative to metallic systems. This study recasts a combined experimental and numerical investigation of clamped unplasticized poly(vinyl chloride) (uPVC) pipe as the first building block of a physics-based digital twin for polymeric utility pipelines. A drop-weight rig was instrumented with a purpose-built ESP32-S2 sensing unit, using infrared timing gates and a pressure transducer, that streams real impact telemetry: the hammer velocity and the transient internal pressure pulse. Five water-pressurized specimens, spanning 689.48 to 2068.43 kPa, were struck at mid-span by a 4 kg hammer at 5.56 m/s, and a high-fidelity ABAQUS/Explicit counterpart was synchronized against the measured response. As internal pressure rose, the peak contact force increased from 3527 to 4174 N, the permanent deformation fell from 15.1 to 7.0 mm, and the pressure pulse grew while the contact period shortened, all consistent with pressure-induced wall stiffening. The contact-force response was linear up to about 1379 kPa before plateauing at the onset of the burst-pressure regime. Experimental and numerical plastic-zone areas agreed to within 16.9%, a conservative over-prediction the twin corrects during synchronization. On this validated basis, a conceptual digital-twin framework is proposed, enabling real-time damage identification and predictive, surrogate-driven structural health monitoring of polymeric pipelines.

Article.Title: A systematic review and meta analysis of early exercise based cardiac rehabilitation in patients hospitalized with acute heart failure
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Luo Z.; Yang M.; Huang W.; Wang Y.; Yu P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (ExCR) has been increasingly investigated in patients hospitalized with acute heart failure (AHF), but its effects on functional recovery and whether these effects vary across selected study-level characteristics remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of ExCR initiated during hospitalization on functional capacity in patients with AHF and to explore potential differences according to rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, and study-level mean age. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI were searched from inception to May 2026. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if they enrolled adults hospitalized with AHF, initiated a structured ExCR program during hospitalization, compared ExCR with usual care or no structured exercise intervention, and reported 6-minute walk distance (6MWD). The primary outcome was 6MWD, secondary outcomes included health-related quality of life (HRQoL), clinical events and safety. Random-effects models were used, and subgroup analyses were considered exploratory. Twelve independent randomized controlled trials were included. Early ExCR significantly improved 6MWD compared with control group (mean difference [MD] 54.44 m, 95% CI 35.62 to 73.26; I² = 60%). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed no statistically significant differences according to rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, or study-level mean age. ExCR also showed potential benefits for disease-specific HRQoL, whereas evidence for HF-related readmission and all-cause mortality remained inconclusive. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the primary 6MWD finding, although the certainty of evidence was rated as low because of risk of bias and inconsistency. Early ExCR initiated during hospitalization may improve functional capacity in patients with AHF. Exploratory subgroup analyses did not identify significant effect modification by rehabilitation delivery model, World Bank country income classification, or study-level mean age. However, the exact magnitude of benefit should be interpreted cautiously, and larger, methodologically rigorous trials are needed to clarify optimal delivery strategies and long-term clinical effects.

Article.Title: Estimating dispersal, survival and population size of wild Aedes aegypti in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania using self-mark-release-recapture method
Article.Authors: Tenywa F.; Makame H.; Moore J.; Dogan O.; Mapipi H.; Smith T.; Chitnis N.; Moore S.; Felber L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aedes -borne arboviral diseases represent a major global public health challenge, with vector control remaining the primary preventive strategy because there are no available antivirals or universal vaccines for most of these infections. This study quantified dispersal, survival time and population size of Aedes aegypti using a mosquito mark-release-recapture (MMRR) approach to generate ecological parameters required for implementing a release-based approaches for Ae. aegypti control. Wild Ae. aegypti pupae were placed beneath a marking unit covered with fluorescent dust-coated cloth-grids. Marked mosquitoes were recaptured within a 250 m radius using BG-sentinel traps, Prokopack aspirators, resting buckets and gravid traps. The overall mean distance travelled (MDT) was 94.5 m (95% CI 83.4–105.7) and the maximum distance travelled was 156 m. The average life expectancy (ALE) was 13.5 days (95% CI 12.2–14.8), with an average probability of daily survival (PDS) of 0.93 (95% CI 0.92–0.94). Survival analysis showed that approximately 80% of male and female Ae. aegypti survived up to 10 days. The estimated population size was 1195 mosquitoes/ha. These findings demonstrate that Ae. aegypti exhibit limited dispersal and survive beyond dengue virus’ average extrinsic incubation period (EIP) of 7–12 days, providing ecological conditions conducive to sustain arboviral transmission. The results also provide critical parameters for optimizing release-based control strategies.

Article.Title: Outcomes of surgically treated type a aortic dissection with malperfusion syndrome: an asian multi-institutional cohort study
Article.Authors: Cheng T.; Chen S.; Hsieh S.; Hsieh M.; Lin C.; Chen D.; Tung Y.; Hsiao F.; Chu P.; Cheng Y.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated mortality in surgically treated type A aortic dissection with malperfusion (mTAAD), identified malperfusion types associated with 30-day mortality, and assessed whether its prognostic impact persists beyond the early postoperative period. Among single-organ malperfusion, cerebral malperfusion was associated with 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.25; 95% CI 1.08–4.70). Compared with no malperfusion, 30-day mortality was higher with single-organ involvement (aOR, 1.86; 95% CI 1.23–2.86), but not significantly with two organs (aOR, 1.66; 95% CI 0.76–3.66). In surgically treated mTAAD, the prognostic impact of malperfusion is concentrated in the early postoperative period. Cerebral malperfusion is associated with high 30-day mortality, supporting its emphasis in preoperative risk stratification.

Article.Title: Effects of an intensive firefighter training program on a simulated fire-escape staircase climb
Article.Authors: Sanchis C.; Martí-Martí J.; Miñana J.; Navarro-Martínez D.; Zahonero J.; Monleón C.
Article.Abstract: We examined changes in weighted stair-climb performance, its physiological and neuromuscular correlates, and attentional function in firefighters and firefighter candidates across a four-week intensive training program. Eighteen participants (17 men, 1 woman) completed baseline testing and 16 training sessions combining strength, power and endurance work; 17 completed post-intervention physical testing. Assessments included a loaded fire-escape staircase climb, an incremental VO₂max test, a 30-s Wingate test, a two-load squat test, anthropometry and the ANTI-Vea attentional task. Changes were estimated with linear mixed models and effect sizes were expressed as Cohen’s d . Stair-climb time was 1.26 s lower after training ( d = − 0.88). Post-intervention stair-climb time was best explained by a composite Strength Score (β std = − 0.65) and a Wingate Score (β std = − 0.37; R ² = 0.86). High-load squat velocity and power, estimated 1RM and Wingate mean power were higher after training (all d ≥ 0.67), whereas VO₂max, ventilatory thresholds and body mass were unchanged. ANT-I mean reaction time was lower ( d z = − 0.59); executive and arousal vigilance did not change. In this single-group design, changes were consistent with neuromuscular and anaerobic rather than aerobic adaptation, and suggest that preparation for this test should emphasize strength at task-relevant loads and anaerobic endurance.

Article.Title: Application of spectral preprocessing and machine learning models for discriminating nitrogen levels in cucumber production
Article.Authors: Sabzi S.; Azadbakht M.; Vahedi Torshizi M.; Pourdarbani R.
Article.Abstract: Nitrogen is one of the most essential macronutrients for plant growth, and its improper management can reduce fertilizer use efficiency while causing significant economic and environmental consequences. In this study, a hyperspectral imaging–based machine learning framework was developed and evaluated to classify different nitrogen fertilizer levels in cucumber leaves (cv. Super Arshiya-F1). Nitrogen treatments consisted of 30%, 60%, and 90% additional nitrogen applied to a nutrient solution with a base concentration of 2 g L⁻¹. Seventy-two hours after treatment application, a total of 300 leaves were collected from the treated plants, and hyperspectral images were acquired in the spectral range of 400–1100 nm, producing 327 spectral bands for each sample. To enhance signal quality and examine the influence of spectral preprocessing on class separability, three preprocessing techniques—Savitzky–Golay filtering, Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC), and Gaussian normalization—were applied exclusively to the training dataset and subsequently transferred to the independent test set. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Decision Tree (DT), were evaluated using a 75/25 training–testing split along with five-fold cross-validation for model optimization. The results demonstrated that SVM consistently achieved the highest classification performance across all scenarios. The best results were obtained without preprocessing and with Gaussian normalization, both reaching an overall accuracy of 94%, an F1-score of approximately 0.94, and a ROC–AUC exceeding 0.98. In contrast, LDA showed moderate performance, while DT yielded the lowest classification accuracy. These findings highlight the strong potential of integrating hyperspectral imaging with SVM for accurate discrimination of nitrogen levels and for supporting efficient nutrient management in crop production systems.

Article.Title: Profilin-regulated actin polymerization dynamics at high monomer concentrations
Article.Authors: Heydenreich L.; Funk J.; Bieling P.; Kierfeld J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Actin polymerization in the cytoskeleton drives crucial dynamical biological processes such as cell motility and morphogenesis. Recent experiments 1 show that binding to profilin plays a crucial role in controlling the maximal polymerization speed of F-actin at cellular actin concentrations. These experiments are successfully described by a four reaction kinetic model, which predicts a Michaelis-Menten-like saturation of growth speed at high profilin-actin concentrations. In this work, we further analyze the four reaction model in terms of master equations and using the concept of two polymerization cycles, a pure actin cycle and a profilin-actin cycle and propose further experimental setups to gain access to all kinetic rates of the model. We find that varying the profilin excess leads to a profilin-dependent Michaelis constant for the growth speed. For polymerization against an external force, we identify a unique stall force as an indicator of energetically balanced profilin-driven polymerization, i.e., for the absence of coupling to other chemical processes providing energy input. Calculating length diffusivity (or Fano factor) we show that actin growth becomes much more precise by profilin-regulation and almost reaches precision bounds set by thermodynamic uncertainty relations.

Article.Title: Maternal autophagy contributes to grain yield in maize
Article.Authors: Tang J.; Wan X.; Myers A.; Avin-Wittenberg T.; Vollbrecht E.; Bassham D.
Article.Abstract: Maize ( Zea mays ) is an important crop species that is cultivated worldwide, and increasing maize yield is one of the major goals of plant breeding. Here, we demonstrate that maize autophagy-defective atg10 mutants have delayed flowering and reduced kernel size, weight and number, leading to reduced grain yield. Reciprocal crosses between mutant and parental lines indicate that, in contrast to the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana , the maternal maize plant genotype is the major contributor to the kernel phenotype in atg10 mutants, rather than the seed genotype.

Article.Title: Expression patterns of Slc38a4 and mmu-miR-6948-3p in a murine model of metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Farzamfar P.; Salehi Z.; Mashayekhi F.; Khodayari S.
Article.Abstract: SLC38A4 (SNAT4), a system A amino acid transporter, contributes to nutrient uptake and metabolic regulation, but its role in the progression of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is unclear. RNA-sequencing data (GSE150928) from primary mammary tumors and lung metastases were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by functional enrichment, protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and miRNA–mRNA target prediction. Eighteen female BALB/c mice implanted with 4T1 TNBC cells were grouped into those with primary mammary tumors and those with lung metastases. Levels of mmu-miR-6948-3p did not differ significantly between groups. Article.Authors: Knowles E.; Danzi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Disasters are a significant source of stress for parents, and people of color (POC) are disproportionately negatively impacted. It was hypothesized that FOC would report greater distress compared to White families and that ERI would mitigate distress in FOC. Parents ( N = 218) exposed to a hurricane reported on their family’s hurricane experiences, ERI, and parent and child psychological functioning. FOC parents reported greater hurricane-realted distress compared to White parents. ERI did not diminish the association between hurricane adversity and distress in parents. FOC children experienced greater distress compared to White counterparts. Child and parent distress were positively associated with one another. ERI was found to buffer the relationship between parent distress and child distress, such that these symptoms were mitigated. These findings highlight the impact of disaster exposure on FOC and describe how ERI may diminish negative outcomes for these families.

Article.Title: Parent-metabolite PBPK model of methotrexate to inform pediatric extrapolation, transporter-mediated drug–drug interactions, and renal impairment
Article.Authors: Dette C.; Marok F.; Alberg V.; Dings C.; Selzer D.; Schwab M.; Kotnik B.; Dolžan V.; Yildiz D.; Bittenbring J.; Remke M.; Lehr T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Methotrexate (MTX) is widely used in treating chronic inflammatory diseases and in chemotherapy for both adult and pediatric patients. Its pharmacokinetics are complex, as MTX is a substrate of multiple transporters. Particularly during high-dose chemotherapeutic use, it is associated with severe toxicities including reversible kidney impairment and hematological toxicity. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling offers a mechanistic approach to predict drug pharmacokinetics and guide dosing, especially in pediatric applications where clinical data is limited. A whole-body parent-metabolite PBPK model of MTX and 7-hydroxymethotrexate was developed in PK-Sim ® (version 12.1) for intravenous and oral administration in adults and children. Model development used 42 MTX and 16 metabolite plasma concentration-time profiles and showed strong predictive performance, with 53/58 area under the plasma concentration-time curve and 38/39 maximum plasma concentration values within a 2-fold range of observed data. Pediatric extrapolation incorporating transporter ontogeny yielded adequate predictions. Drug-drug interaction simulations for five perpetrator drugs met established acceptance criteria, and renal impairment simulations revealed markedly increased exposure in the high-dose setting. The model will be made publicly available to support dose optimization across clinical scenarios.

Article.Title: Effects of maximum teleportation distance on wayfinding in virtual reality: the role of optical flow cues
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Instantaneous teleportation reduces simulator sickness risk by omitting continuous viewpoint motion but may impair spatial orientation. Sketch-map scores were lower at 25 m than at 5 and 15 m. Navigation time was longer at 5 m than at 25 m, and mean navigation time per teleportation increased across the 5-, 15-, and 25-m conditions. No significant between-type differences or type × distance interactions were detected for sketch-map or navigation measures. Simulator sickness scores were low across conditions. The aligned rank transform analysis indicated effects of teleportation type, distance, and their interaction that were not consistently reproduced by other approaches, leaving insufficient evidence for a stable simulator-sickness effect. Interview responses suggested that shorter-distance teleportation facilitated environmental observation, whereas longer-distance teleportation was perceived as easier to operate. The 25 m condition combined shorter navigation time with lower sketch-map scores. Distance conditions were paired with fixed scene variants, and the fixed 0.3 s transition coupled displacement with translation speed. The possible trade-off between traversal efficiency and environmental learning therefore remains specific to the tested configurations.

Amrapali/Olour produced the highest total flower number (1,077.33 per panicle), whereas Amrapali/PAM-2 exhibited the greatest hermaphrodite flower number (372.67 per panicle) and proportion (38.78%). Exploratory correlations associated bud zeatin with male flower number in Amrapali (r = 0.963, P = 0.037) and bud ABA with panicle length in Dashehari (r = 0.962, P = 0.038). Article.Authors: Asmeen S.; Chenam V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer is still a major cause of cancer mortality in women, and the development of efficient, reliable and explainable diagnostic systems capable of inter-hospital data sharing while maintaining privacy of data is essential. This study proposes a Hierarchical Window Pattern Cognition Network for breast cancer diagnosis using the Breast Histopathology Images (IDC Regular Patches) dataset. The framework uses CLAHE and data augmentation, image normalization and image resizing to enhance the image consistency. A federated learning framework with five clients uses Federated Averaging (FedAvg) to aggregate models and share model updates securely. The security layer uses an AES-256-GCM encryption algorithm, a SHA3-512 hashing algorithm, and a mechanism simulating those of CRYSTALS-Kyber and CRYSTALS-Dilithium for cryptographic security. Record-integrity verification is supported by a local hash-chain audit log, and predictions of the model are explained with visual and feature-level explanations by using GradCAM + + and SHAP. Article.Authors: Oliveira T.; Basile R.; Souza B.; Vicentini Y.; Barbosa A.; Baccarin R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to describe and compare the electroencephalographic patterns of sleep in horses during recumbent and standing positions, identifying the cortical dynamics and spectral characteristics associated with each stage. REM sleep was posture-dependent, with complete paradoxical patterns observed only in recumbent horses. In standing animals, a REM-like state was identified, marked by rapid eye movements but cortical hypoactivation and absence of muscle atonia. Quantitative analysis revealed that N1 and N2 accounted for approximately 90% of total sleep duration, while N3 and REM represented smaller fractions. Standing horses exhibited longer light sleep stages and a smaller proportion of N3 sleep. These findings demonstrate that equine sleep architecture is highly posture-dependent, and behavioral postures such as sternal or lateral recumbency cannot be reliably used as proxies for specific EEG sleep stages. Article.Title: A Bayesian Functional Kriging framework for spatial interpolation of PM2.5 concentration profiles
Article.Authors: Baseer A.; Khalefa M.; Ismael W.; Hussain I.; Basheer A.
Article.Abstract: Air pollution, especially fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), is a major global public health problem, causing breathing difficulties, lung disease, heart problems, and premature death. This study introduces a new Bayesian Functional Kriging (BFK) model to predict PM 2.5 concentration profiles across Pakistan’s most populous province, using MERRA-2 reanalysis data at 17 city locations across Punjab. The BFK framework combines three methodologies: Functional Data Analysis (FDA), where continuous temporal curves model discrete PM 2.5 concentration profiles through B-spline smoothing; Functional Kriging (FK), in which functional data are used for spatial prediction of curve-valued observations; and Bayesian hierarchical modeling using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for parameter estimation. Prior empirical distributions are assumed for all parameters of interest: mean, partial sill, nugget effect, and spatial range, while posterior estimates are derived via a hybrid Gibbs-Metropolis algorithm within Gibbs sampling. In addition, we used the proposed model to estimate temporal variation in PM 2.5 concentration at five locations not sampled during data collection: Vehari, Sialkot, Attock, Khanewal, and Okara. We found that pollution is much higher in the southern areas than in the northern ones. These findings underscore BFK’s utility as a statistically principled and practically effective tool for air quality monitoring and environmental policy.

Article.Authors: Redwan M.; Belete B.; Abdeta G.; Gebremeskel T.; Demissie A.
Article.Abstract: Severe pneumonia remains a primary driver of pediatric morbidity in Sub-Saharan Africa. The proportion of prolonged hospital stay (> 7 days) was 42.0% (95% CI 37.2–46.8). The multivariable explanatory model demonstrated good discriminative performance (AUC = 0.804, 95% CI 0.759–0.848) and good model calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.612). Article.Title: Hidden baseline heterogeneity can mask treatment effects in randomized xenograft studies
Article.Authors: Gül N.; Hekim N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Randomization and standardized analytical workflows are central to preclinical oncology, yet they do not necessarily ensure biological comparability at baseline. Using a real-world xenograft efficacy dataset generated under standard CRO conditions, we show that biologically meaningful treatment effects can remain statistically undetected when baseline heterogeneity is not explicitly considered. Although treatment groups appeared balanced at study entry by conventional summaries, baseline tumour volume exhibited latent structure within the cohort. Pooled group-level analyses reported no significant treatment effect, whereas baseline-aware evaluation of tumour growth trajectories revealed a responder subpopulation whose signal was masked by aggregation. This discrepancy did not arise from deficiencies in experimental conduct or data quality, but from limitations of pooled inference in the presence of structured baseline variability. Extending this framework to publicly available xenograft datasets, we observed that baseline tumour volume heterogeneity is common under routine preclinical workflows and can similarly alter efficacy interpretation. Together, these findings indicate that baseline tumour burden represents a biologically consequential source of hidden heterogeneity and that baseline-aware analytical strategies can improve the sensitivity and interpretability of preclinical efficacy assessment without deviation from standard experimental practice.

In addition, cochlear inflammation in virus-infected mice resulted in the loss of barrier functions of the SV that have also been linked to SNHL. Decreased expression of these DRG in infected animals was associated with SNHL that was similar to that observed in genetically engineered murine models with deletion of these DRG. Together, these results argue that virus-induced inflammation can lead to dysregulation of host genes associated with barrier and ion transport function of the SV, thus providing further insight into potential mechanisms of SNHL that follow virus infections during early auditory development.

Article.Authors: He Y.; Ding C.; Bai C.; Yan D.; Hu M.

Utilizing the geographical detector model, it identifies key factors associated with their spatial distribution, quantitatively assessing their explanatory power and interaction patterns among natural, economic, and cultural dimensions. The study also suggests strategies for the protection and sustainable use of traditional villages in the QRB. The research findings reveal that traditional villages in the QRB exhibit a clustered distribution pattern, characterized by a spatial structure of “two cores and multiple clusters”. This agglomeration tendency is observed at the county level, with a distinct pattern of concentration in the southwestern mountainous regions and sparsity in the northeastern plains. Various factors such as slope, altitude, per capita disposable income, road network density, and the proportion of the primary industry play significant roles in shaping the spatial distribution of these traditional villages. A multifactor detection model demonstrates that the distribution pattern of traditional villages in the QRB is a result of the dynamic interplay between natural features and human influences. The impact of each factor varies across different stages, highlighting the complex nature of village distribution. This quantitative analysis assesses the varying degrees of influence exerted by the natural environment, socioeconomic conditions, and historical heritage on the distribution of traditional villages, addressing limitations of previous qualitative studies. This study not only enhances our understanding of the factors driving the distribution of traditional villages but also provides a scientific foundation for the strategic conservation of these villages in the QRB and the management of cultural heritage on a basin-wide scale.

Moreover, pre-reactivation administration of an M1 muscarinic cholinergic receptor agonist appeared to promote memory destabilization in middle-aged mice, enabling memory updating. Finally, a brief period of enrichment yielded behavioural effects consistent with enhanced memory updating, and these were associated with elevated expression of hippocampal VAChT. This research expands our understanding of the critical involvement of cholinergic system changes in age-related cognitive deficits, highlighting an underappreciated role for cholinergic transmission in memory updating functions distinct from merely learning and remembering.

The results showed that the younger nymphs were, the higher proportion that shifted from solitary to gregarious phase, whereas adults never switched; a density of 60 insects produced the highest transition rate, whereas lower or higher densities resulted in fewer gregarious individuals. RNAi silencing of JHAMT , Hn , DDC or CSP resulted in a major decrease of phase transition occurrence while JHAMT , Hn and DDC knock-down caused partial albinism. The research demonstrates that population density functions as the key trigger for phase transition while gene interactions with their respective metabolites undergo central regulatory functions. Nonetheless, since the locusts used in this study were field-collected and reared for less than two generations, the results should be interpreted within the context of environmentally induced plasticity rather than genetically fixed phase differences.

Article.Abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) provides a privacy-preserving and contactless sensing modality for human activity recognition, but practical CSI recognition remains challenged by limited labeled data, heterogeneous motion dynamics, and signal perturbations. The encoder models motion evolution at multiple temporal receptive fields and complementary frequency-selective responses across OFDM subcarriers, while Efficient Multi-Scale Attention is used only as a lightweight feature-refinement component rather than as the primary methodological novelty. Experiments were conducted on the public UT-HAR and NTU-Fi HAR benchmarks using the SenseFi data partitions. Main recognition and low-label experiments were repeated five times with random seeds 42–46, and low-label subsets were independently sampled by stratified class sampling in each run. CSI-MSRNet achieved 98.76 ± 0.18% accuracy on UT-HAR and 99.85 ± 0.21% on NTU-Fi HAR. With only 1% labeled data, the corresponding accuracies were 73.6 ± 2.4% and 77.8 ± 2.8%, respectively. Controlled synthetic tests further indicated improved tolerance to amplitude noise and random subcarrier loss. These results should be interpreted as benchmark-level behavioral recognition rather than evidence of subject-independent generalization, clinical monitoring effectiveness, or embedded-device deployment. The framework therefore provides a computationally lightweight approach with potential applications in smart-home and health-related behavioral sensing.

Article.Title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal a senescence-associated lipid-metabolic macrophage phenotype driving immunosuppression and poor prognosis in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhao B.; Liao Y.; Ye S.; Jiang N.; Lu W.; Chen Y.; Chen W.; Huang Y.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their functional heterogeneity remains poorly understood, especially regarding the interplay between cellular senescence and lipid metabolism. We integrated multi-omics and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize a novel macrophage subpopulation termed senescence-associated lipid-metabolic (SALM) macrophages. Using eight machine learning algorithms, a prognostic model based on SALM signatures was developed and internally evaluated via nested cross-validation in a combined TCGA–GSE39582 cohort. Spatial multiplex immunofluorescence and qPCR were employed for experimental validation. SALM macrophages exhibit elevated IL-10/STAT3 signaling, terminal differentiation, and a core gene module enriched in senescence and lipid metabolism pathways. They interact strongly with T cells via immunosuppressive ligands IL-10 and MIF. Spatial analysis confirmed p16 + CD68 + IL-10 + cell enrichment at the tumor front. The SALM-based prognostic model achieved high accuracy (AUC = 0.972), and a corresponding nomogram showed potential for personalized prognosis prediction. SALM macrophages drive immunosuppression in CRC through a senescence-lipid metabolism axis, serving as a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Design and characterization of beta-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 to enhance luteolin solubility and anticancer efficacy: bioinformatic and biologic assessment
Article.Authors: Kharazmi F.; Homayouni Tabrizi M.; Jafarinia M.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a cause of cancer-related mortality, while luteolin, a flavonoid, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, and low bioavailability. This study developed a luteolin-loaded β-cyclodextrin/chitosan-coated zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8) nanocarrier intended to improve drug retention, pH-responsive release, and anticancer activity against colorectal cancer cells. ZIF-8 nanoparticles were synthesized by room-temperature precipitation, coated sequentially with β-cyclodextrin and chitosan, crosslinked using sodium tripolyphosphate, and loaded with luteolin by post-synthetic incubation. Molecular docking using MOE 2024 investigated luteolin interactions with KRAS (PDB 6MBU), chitosan-binding protein (4ZXE), and VEGF (2VPF), with 5-fluorouracil as a computational comparator. FTIR, dynamic light scattering, zeta-potential analysis, pH-dependent surface-charge measurements, and FESEM characterized the formulation. Encapsulation efficiency and loading capacity were quantified spectrophotometrically; release was assessed by dialysis at pH 7.4, 6.5, and 5.5. HCT116 colorectal carcinoma and normal human dermal fibroblasts underwent MTT testing. Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, AO/EB microscopy, SOD activity, FRAP, and qRT-PCR for CASP3, SOD1, and IL6 evaluated cell-death and stress responses. The particles showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 228.95 ± 2.7 nm, a PDI of 0.139 ± 0.04, and a zeta potential of − 27.24 ± 0.32 mV, indicating a uniform nanoscale dispersion. Synthesis yield was 78.5 ± 3.2%. Measured luteolin retention increased with feed concentration, reaching 83.5 ± 1.44% encapsulation efficiency and 16.1 ± 1.53% loading capacity. Release was slower under physiological conditions and accelerated in acidic media, supporting pH-responsive behavior; model fitting was descriptive, with Higuchi favored at pH 7.4, Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 6.5, and the lowest AIC assigned to Korsmeyer–Peppas at pH 5.5. In HCT116, free luteolin produced an IC 50 of 166.5 ± 12.3 µg/mL, whereas Lut@β-CD/CS/ZIF-8 reduced the IC 50 to 45.96 ± 2.3 µg/mL (approximately 3.6-fold greater potency; p < 0.001). The formulation IC 50 in HDF cells was 128.7 ± 8.4 µg/mL, yielding an HCT116/HDF selectivity index of 2.8. At 66 µg/mL, total apoptosis reached 48.9 ± 2.9%, compared with 1.3 ± 0.3% in controls. FRAP antioxidant capacity decreased to 0.578 ± 0.015 versus 0.801 ± 0.022 in controls. CASP3 and SOD1 transcripts increased 4.98-fold and 4.10-fold, respectively, while IL6 peaked at 10.92-fold at the intermediate dose. The dual-coated nanocarrier enhanced luteolin potency and apoptosis-associated responses in HCT116, with selectivity relative to HDF cells. Docking and characterization findings are supportive, not proof of KRAS inhibition, tumor targeting, or in vivo efficacy; validation remains necessary.

Article.Title: Physical literacy and health-related quality of life: the serial mediating role of resilience and positive mental health
Article.Authors: Mumu S.; Reena I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical literacy (PL) is recognized as a multidimensional construct that supports physical activity and health. Beyond physical competence, PL includes motivation, confidence, knowledge, and understanding. However, the role of positive psychological resources in explaining the relationship between physical literacy and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among university students has received limited empirical attention. This study examined whether resilience and positive mental health (PMH) mediate the relationship between PL and physical and mental components of HRQoL. In this cross-sectional study,159 undergraduate and graduate students from a single university in Louisiana, US completed the perceived physical literacy instrument, adult resilience measure-revised, positive mental health scale, and short form 12 health survey online. PROCESS Model 6 was utilized to analyze the mediation model. Age and sex were added as covariates. PL is positively associated with resilience, PMH, and both physical and mental HRQoL. PMH significantly mediated the relationship between PL and mental HRQoL, and a significant serial indirect association through resilience and PMH was identified (B = 0.227, 95% bootstrap CI [0.109, 0.403]). In contrast, no significant indirect effects were observed for physical HRQoL. The final model explained 35.1% of the variance in mental HRQoL. These findings suggest that physical literacy is associated with mental HRQoL through a psychosocial pathway in which resilience supports positive mental health. Findings from this study can be utilized to inform policy that seeks to identify modifiable psychological and behavioral determinants of HRQoL and meaningfully enhance the university health promotion program to support health outcomes of students in higher education.
