Article.Title: Experimental and finite element analysis of coupled electro-thermal responses of concrete-encased grounding electrodes under lightning impulses
Article.Authors: Sarker M.; Zubair H.; Algarni S.; Alqahtani T.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: Grounding systems are critical for maintaining the safety and transient stability of high-voltage and smart-grid infrastructure subjected to lightning-current impulses. This study presents an integrated experimental and three-dimensional finite element method (FEM) investigation of conventional copper-bonded steel rod and concrete-encased grounding electrodes under standardized 8/20 µs impulse-current conditions. Laboratory experiments were conducted using an impulse-current generator with a maximum current capability of 1.5 kA, while a COMSOL Multiphysics model was developed and validated against the experimentally accessible current range and subsequently used to investigate higher-current conditions numerically. Three representative soil types of clay, sandy loam, and gravel were considered to evaluate transient impedance, ground potential rise (GPR), current-density distribution, soil-ionization behavior, and electro-thermal response. Experimentally, the concrete-encased configuration reduced impulse impedance by approximately 33–49% across the investigated soils. FEM analysis showed a reduction in peak current density from 69 to 43 A/m², corresponding to approximately 38%, together with a larger effective current-conduction region. Numerical predictions at higher current levels indicated delayed soil-ionization onset and lower temperature rise for the encased configuration compared with the conventional rod. These high-current results are identified as FEM predictions rather than direct experimental measurements because they exceed the 1.5 kA capability of the laboratory generator. The validated experimental numerical framework demonstrates the potential of conductive concrete encasement to improve impulse-current dispersion and reduce localized electrical and thermal stress in grounding electrodes. Further high-current experimental validation is required to confirm the predicted behavior beyond the laboratory test range.

Article.Title: Urinary metal exposure and type 2 diabetes mellitus: the potential mediating role of biological aging in older adults
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Chen F.; Ren H.; Zhang X.; Zhuo L.; Guo X.; Cui C.; Zhang P.; Zhang Y.; Zhang Y.; Ding L.; Lei L.
Article.Abstract: The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasing, and environmental exposures may contribute to diabetes susceptibility. Metals are widespread environmental contaminants associated with metabolic disorders; however, the role of aging-related processes in this association remains unclear. A total of 843 participants were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of six metals (Pb, Zn, Mn, Cr, As, and Co) were measured, and phenotypic age was calculated based on nine biomarkers. Multivariable regression models were used to assess individual-metal associations, while weighted quantile sum regression was used to evaluate mixed-metal exposure; mediation analyses were conducted as exploratory analyses. Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr exposures were significantly associated with T2DM ( P < 0.05). Mixed-metal exposure was also associated with higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.515, 95% CI: 1.277–1.884). Additionally, Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr were positively associated with phenotypic age, and each one-year increase in phenotypic age was associated with higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.391, 95% CI: 1.319–1.466). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that phenotypic age may partially account for the associations between metal exposure and T2DM, with estimated mediation proportions of 10.9%–22.2%. Phenotypic aging may represent a potential pathway linking environmental metal exposure with diabetes susceptibility.

Article.Title: Relationships between reproductive steroids, glandular microbiota, and volatile chemical signals in naturally cycling versus hormonally contracepted female lemurs
Article.Authors: Grebe N.; Boulet M.; Bornbusch S.; Greenwald L.; Dimac-Stohl K.; Grady J.; Drea C.
Article.Abstract: Olfactory communication directs socio-reproductive interaction in animals, but underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Endocrine action and microbial fermentation both influence the manufacture, composition, and expression of vertebrate chemosignals, involving volatile organic compounds (VOCs); however, there has been no integrative investigation of a putative tripart relationship between reproductive hormones, microbes, and VOCs. Our longitudinal experimental study of normative and contracepted females characterizes pairwise and tripart relationships in two scent-marking primates: ring-tailed lemurs ( Lemur catta ) and Coquerel’s sifakas ( Propithicus coquereli ). We used (1) serum enzyme immunoassays to quantify progesterone (P 4 ), estradiol (E 2 ), and the synthetic progestogen, medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA), (2) Illumina sequencing of the bacterial 16 S rRNA gene to identify microbiota in genital (labial) secretions, and (3) gas chromatography-mass spectrometry to characterize labial VOCs. Despite species differences in hormone concentrations, contraception expectedly muted natural variation in the E 2 /P 4 ratio and introduced initially supraphysiological MPA concentrations. Normative and induced hormonal variation was reflected in the microbial and/or chemical composition of labial secretions; however, predictive power varied by species, potentially reflecting socioecological variation or differences in glandular specialization. These results highlight the importance of cyclical endocrine variation in female reproductive signaling and the overriding effects on VOC manufacture of a disturbed glandular microbiome during contraception.

Article.Title: Forecasting legal coastline based on highest astronomical tide as a predictive model for land–sea integration
Article.Authors: Setiyadi J.; Pratomo D.; Sukotjo B.; Pranowo W.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a highest astronomical tide (HAT)-referenced legal coastline framework to support the integration of terrestrial and marine cadastre in Bekasi Regency, Indonesia. Six Landsat image epochs acquired between 2015 and 2024 were processed and normalised to HAT derived from an 18.6-year tidal record at Pondok Dayung Tidal Station, selected as a regional reference because of its comparable tidal characteristics with the study area. Water bodies were delineated using the modified normalized difference water index (MNDWI), with scene-specific thresholds determined by the Otsu method and refined through morphological post-processing. This procedure produced a vertically consistent legal coastline for each selected observation epoch. The bounding-box area of the coastline decreased by 6.33 km 2 between 2015 and 2024, indicating a net contraction of the coastal spatial envelope despite localised erosion and accretion. A random forest regression model was used to hindcast the 2024 coastline and achieved an RMSE of 12.8 m, a mean displacement of 9.6 m, an MAE of 10.7 m, and an R 2 of 0.84. The resulting six-epoch dataset provides a consistent geospatial record of coastline change over a 10-year calendar period and supports scenario-based projections of future HAT-referenced coastline positions. The proposed legal coastline is intended as a scientific spatial reference for future harmonisation of land–sea administration, spatial planning, and coastal risk management; it does not replace existing statutory boundary definitions in Indonesia.

Article.Title: Effects of bonded rapid maxillary expansion and miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion on craniocervical posture, sagittal pharyngeal airway dimensions, and hyoid bone position
Article.Authors: Tuhan Kutlu E.; Baser B.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to compare the effects of bonded rapid maxillary expansion (RME) and miniscrew-assisted rapid palatal expansion (MARPE) on skeletal measurements, craniocervical posture, sagittal pharyngeal airway dimensions, and hyoid bone position using lateral cephalometric radiographs. This retrospective cohort study included 60 patients with transverse maxillary deficiency treated with bonded RME or MARPE. The bonded RME group included 30 patients (17 females and 13 males) and the MARPE group included 30 patients (16 females and 14 males). Lateral cephalometric radiographs obtained before treatment (T0) and 6 months after completion of active screw activation (T1) were analyzed using ImageJ software. Generalized estimating equation models were used for repeated-measures comparisons, and chronological age was included as a covariate. After adjustment for age, no significant group × time interaction was observed for any skeletal measurement. ANB showed a significant time effect, whereas SNA, SNB, SN–GoGn, NSL/NL, and FH/ML did not show significant time-dependent changes. No significant group, time, or group × time interaction effects were detected for sagittal pharyngeal airway or hyoid measurements. Significant group × time interactions were observed for NSL/OPT, NSL/CVT, and CVT/HOR, indicating different craniocervical postural change patterns between the groups. In skeletal Class I patients with transverse maxillary deficiency and normal vertical growth patterns, bonded RME and MARPE showed comparable skeletal, sagittal pharyngeal airway, and hyoid outcomes after age adjustment. The absence of significant sagittal airway and hyoid changes should be interpreted within the limits of two-dimensional cephalometric assessment. The craniocervical posture findings should be considered exploratory and interpreted cautiously.

Article.Title: Selectively VO2-loaded terahertz metasurface for dual-state broadband polarization conversion and near-unity absorption
Article.Authors: Nipun M.; Islam M.; Arifuzzaman M.; Haque M.; Naidu R.; Rifatur Rana S.; Khan H.
Article.Abstract: A selectively VO 2 -loaded terahertz metasurface is studied for dual-state polarization conversion and absorption. The ground-backed unit cell consists of a broken diamond-shaped Au resonator, two square VO 2 loading regions, a circular VO 2 ring, and a polyimide spacer. With VO 2 in the insulating conductivity state, the structure operates as a reflective cross-polarization converter. PCR x remains above 0.90 from 1.5150 to 2.5849 THz, while PCRγ exceeds 0.90 from 1.5270 to 2.6726 THz. In the metallic conductivity state, A x remains above 0.90 from 1.5700 to 1.9970 THz and reaches 0.9997 at 1.8050 THz. At this frequency, the normalized impedance is 0.970 − j 0.014, and VO 2 accounts for 97.14% of the dissipated power. The conversion mechanism is supported by polarization-resolved reflection, rotated-axis phase response, and asymmetric current paths. The absorber state is associated with reflection suppression, resonator-ground coupling, and loss in the metallic VO 2 regions. Four-pass and six-pass mesh solutions differ by less than 1% in the principal response measures. Angular and tolerance analyses further show that the main features of both operating states are retained under the investigated conditions. The results numerically demonstrate dual-state terahertz operation through conductivity-state switching of selectively loaded VO 2 within a single planar unit cell.

Article.Title: The mediating role of depression, anxiety, and stress between health literacy, life satisfaction, and psychological maladjustment in young Turkish adults
Article.Authors: Mert A.; Sarigül A.; Turan M.
Article.Abstract: The present study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Turkish version of the Mini-DASS and to test the mediating role of depression, anxiety, and stress in the association between health literacy and both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment. Two consecutive studies were conducted. Study 1 evaluated the psychometric properties of the Turkish Mini-DASS using item analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), criterion validity, and internal consistency reliability. Study 2 tested a proposed mediation model. Participants were Turkish young adults recruited online (Study 1: N = 460; Study 2: N = 905). In Study 1, EFA supported the original three factor structure of the Mini-DASS with acceptable factor loadings, and all subscales demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency. CFA indicated good model fit indices, supporting the validity of the three-factor model. In Study 2, mediation analysis revealed significant indirect effects of depression, anxiety, and stress in the association between health literacy and both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment. The Turkish Mini-DASS is a brief, reliable, and valid measure of psychological distress, encompassing depression, anxiety, and stress. The mediation findings indicated that health literacy is associated with both life satisfaction and psychological maladjustment, and that depression, anxiety, and stress functioned as mediators in this association, highlighting the potential relevance of psychological distress in explaining how health literacy relates to individuals’ broader psychosocial functioning.

Article.Title: Performance enhancement of electrohydrodynamic thruster using sub unit electrode configuration
Article.Authors: Jiang X.; Tsubata H.; Shimizu S.; Nozaki T.
Article.Abstract: Electrohydrodynamic (EHD) propulsion has garnered significant interest as a lightweight and silent thrust generation technology, owing to its lack of moving parts and low vibration characteristics. However, enhancing the thrust output and energy efficiency of EHD thrusters remains a key challenge. This study introduces a novel thrust enhancement electrode configuration that incorporates a sub unit for an EHD propulsion system. Experimental results demonstrate that the introduction of the sub unit substantially increases thrust generation compared with the conventional electrode system without a sub unit. At an applied voltage of 22 kV, the conventional configuration generates a thrust of 50.23 mN, whereas the sub unit electrode system achieves 64.09 mN, representing an approximate 27.59% increase in thrust. To further enhance thrust generation, an additional structure, termed the sub unit plus, is implemented beneath the original sub unit electrode system. This enhanced configuration optimizes aerodynamic interactions within the investigated range, resulting in a thrust output of 68.70 mN. The sub unit plus electrode system delivers an additional 7.19% increase in thrust over the sub unit configuration alone, and a total improvement of 36.77% relative to the conventional system. These results indicate an engineering trade-off between maximizing absolute thrust and maintaining thrust to power ratio of the configuration. Overall, the incorporation of sub unit structures is crucial in enhancing thrust output. The proposed design strategy provides a promising pathway for improving thrust performance in EHD propulsion systems and provides valuable insights for the development of higher thrust output EHD thrusters.

Article.Title: Clinical and imaging characteristics of difficult-to-treat patients with rheumatoid arthritis and peripheral psoriatic arthritis with ultrasound-confirmed inflammation
Article.Authors: Omaña-Iglesias O.; Novell G.; Azuaga A.; Frade-Sosa B.; Sarmiento-Monroy J.; Cuervo A.; Ponce A.; Corzo P.; Farietta S.; Ruiz-Esquide V.; Gómez-Puerta J.; Cañete J.; Ramírez J.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the proportion of Difficult To Treat (D2T) disease according to three operational definitions in a population of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and peripheral Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA) with ultrasound (US)-confirmed inflammation, and to characterize its clinical, structural, and therapeutic features. Cross-sectional study involving RA or peripheral PsA who had active disease, established through both clinical and US examination. D2T disease was categorized according to three criteria: an operational treatment-failure-based D2T definition, requiring inadequate response or failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and ≥ 2 b/tsDMARDs with different mechanisms of action (MOAs); a time-dependent criterion, defined by failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and two or more b/tsDMARDs with different MOAs over a period of less than 12 months and a very refractory criterion, requiring failure to ≥ 1 csDMARD and ≥​ 3 b/tsDMARDs with different MOAs. A total of 148 patients were included. Overall, 31.7% fulfilled the treatment-failure-based D2T definition, 12.1% the time-based definition, and 18.2% the very refractory one. Treatment-failure-based D2T disease was more frequent in RA ( p = 0.033) and associated with longer disease duration ( p < 0.001), cardiovascular comorbidity ( p = 0.037), US proliferative synovitis ( p = 0.034), erosive disease ( p < 0.001), combined therapy (csDMARD + b/tsDMARD) ( p < 0.001), and prior tsDMARD ( p < 0.001). Time-based D2T disease was equally present in both RA and PsA, associated with combined therapy ( p = 0.008), tsDMARD use ( p = 0.002), and nail involvement ( p = 0.019). Very refractory D2T disease was more prevalent in RA ( p = 0.029) and associated with longer disease duration ( p = 0.014), erosive disease ( p < 0.001), US proliferative synovitis ( p = 0.046), combined therapy ( p = 0.003), and tsDMARD exposure ( p < 0.001). D2T disease defines a severe phenotype characterized by cumulative disease burden, structural damage, comorbidities, and treatment refractoriness. Erosive disease, combined therapy, and tsDMARD exposure emerged as associated factors across definitions, emphasizing early disease control and comprehensive management.

Article.Title: Exploring sustainable use intention of AIGC image enhancement technologies among designers
Article.Authors: Zhou B.; Wan B.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates designers’ sustainable use intention toward AIGC-assisted image enhancement technologies in low-light mural design. An extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework was developed to examine how image-related performance perceptions, facilitating conditions, and effort-related factors influence designer experience and sustainable use intention. Survey data from 557 designers were analyzed using a two-stage Structural Equation Modeling–Artificial Neural Network (SEM–ANN) approach. The SEM results indicate that facilitating conditions exert the strongest direct influence on sustainable use intention, while performance expectancy substantially influences designer experience. Resource and organizational support significantly contribute to facilitating conditions, whereas technological accessibility shows no significant effect. Designer experience and sustainable use intention are also positively associated with social influence. These findings highlight the importance of organizational and resource support alongside perceived technological performance, extending the application of UTAUT to AIGC-assisted creative design and providing practical guidance for image enhancement tool adoption.

Article.Title: Hierarchical graph attention and memory-augmented learning for spatio-temporal network intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Nune S.; Moka D.; Jerith G.; Srinivas P.; Udata S.
Article.Abstract: Graph neural networks are increasingly used for network intrusion detection, but their reported advantages often depend on evaluation choices. We present STAR-IDS, which builds a graph from every window of ten consecutive network flows, applies two-level graph attention and a prototype memory bank, and estimates prediction uncertainty with Monte Carlo Dropout. STAR-IDS was evaluated on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v3, with real IP-address nodes and flows ordered by start time, and on the IoT dataset NF-ToN-IoT-v2, using block-wise splits that prevent leakage, temporally blocked cross-validation, five paired seeds and controlled baselines (E-GraphSAGE, GAT, GCN, GraphSAGE and a graph-free MLP) trained under identical conditions. On NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, STAR-IDS achieved 87.61% ± 1.22% accuracy and 86.41% macro-F1, and no difference from the baselines or ablations was statistically significant after Holm correction; on NF-ToN-IoT, the graph-free MLP was the most accurate model (81.10% vs. 77.21%). The uncertainty estimates separated erroneous from correct predictions with an AUC of 0.89, and on that dataset flagged predictions were 16–25 percentage points less accurate than auto-accepted ones. Control experiments show that shuffling flows before windowing, synthetic node identifiers and forward-in-time splits change accuracy by up to 68 percentage points.

Article.Title: High-throughput mineralogical characterization using automated in-situ microscopy and Raman spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Stigliano L.; Cosmidis J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation in natural and engineered systems is controlled by complex interactions among physicochemical variables and organic molecules, making large-scale systematic exploration of mineralization pathways challenging. Here we present a high-throughput experimental and analytical workflow that enables rapid, particle-resolved characterization of mineral formation. The platform integrates miniaturized mineralization experiments in multi-well plates with automated optical microscopy, particle detection, morphometric analysis, machine-learning classification, and targeted Raman spectromicroscopy. Applied to calcium carbonate precipitation mediated by organic additives, the workflow enables particle-resolved morphological analysis and mineral phase identification. Across 307 experiments involving 23 organic additives, automated imaging revealed ten reproducible particle morphologies. Raman spectromicroscopy showed that each morphotype consistently corresponds to a single mineral phase, either calcite or vaterite. A Random Forest model trained on morphological descriptors classified particle types with a mean accuracy of 97 ± 1%, enabling automated quantification of morphotype populations across experimental conditions. Systematic screening showed that organic additives strongly influence particle populations, modifying particle number, size distributions, and accessible particle morphologies. Time-lapse imaging further enables rapid estimation of particle growth rates, providing a practical metric to identify conditions that promote or inhibit mineralization. This integrated workflow provides a scalable framework for mapping mineralization pathways across multidimensional chemical spaces.

Article.Title: Synergies in streamlining: AI and Lean Management in Polish healthcare administration
Article.Authors: Garski J.; Walkowiak D.
Article.Abstract: Administrative tasks consume 15–30% of healthcare budgets, and applying artificial intelligence (AI) tools within Lean Management (LM) is theorized to yield substantial efficiency gains, yet professional perceptions of this integration remain largely unexamined. In this exploratory cross-sectional survey of 330 Polish healthcare professionals across five role groups (April–September 2025), we introduce the AI-Lean Synergy Index, an exploratory formative composite measure of perceived AI-LM synergy pending confirmatory validation, derived from a 39-item instrument grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (average Cronbach’s α = 0.844). The Index yielded a median of 0.60 (interquartile range 0.30), with 88.9% of respondents ( n = 244) perceiving moderate to very high synergy. A 41.8-percentage-point perception–application gap separated belief that AI can improve healthcare quality (69.1%) from conscious application of AI to administrative efficiency (27.3%), while perceived implementation barriers were uniformly high (median 4.0/5.0 across 11 categories). Healthcare managers scored significantly higher than physicians (median 0.60 vs. 0.50; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.045, post-hoc p = 0.0304), a difference consistent with a champion–skeptic dynamic and, alternatively, with role-specific referents for administrative efficiency. We propose an evidence-informed priority framework: governance, competency development, pilot projects, and change management for translating perceived synergy into administrative practice in centrally financed health systems.

Article.Title: Evaluating the decomposition of agricultural legume species to estimate nutrient recycling in Mediterranean climates
Article.Authors: De Prato L.; Harrison R.; Scanlan C.; Howieson J.; Steel E.; Yates R.
Article.Abstract: Legumes enhance the sustainability of Mediterranean farming systems by increasing soil nutrient levels, improving soil water and carbon retention, and reducing reliance on synthetic fertilisers through biological nitrogen fixation. However, the environmental and biological complexity of residue decomposition necessitates a clear understanding of how different crop residues decompose in synchrony with the nutrient requirements of subsequent cereal or oilseed crops. To address this, litterbag experiments were conducted at two distinct agroecological zones within the Western Australian Wheatbelt (Kendenup: 730 mm rainfall, Brown Gravelly Chromosol; Konnongorring: 350 mm rainfall, Grey Chromosol sandy duplex). Residues from nine legume species (grain legumes: Lupinus angustifolius, Vicia faba ; traditional pastures: Trifolium subterraneum, Vicia sativa, V. villosa ; novel ley legumes: Ornithopus sativus, Trigonella balansae, Trifolium spumosum ) and wheat ( Triticum aestivum ) were monitored from summer to winter (60 weeks) to assess decomposition patterns and associated C and N dynamics. Decomposition rates were significantly higher at the high-rainfall Kendenup site, with all species showing 70–85% biomass loss by 60 weeks compared to 50–75% at Konnongorring, reflecting moisture as the primary driver of decomposition. Across both sites, T. aestivum exhibited the slowest decomposition and highest N immobilisation (final C:N ~ 35), followed by grain legumes L. angustifolius and V. faba (final C:N 30–40). Vetch species ( V. sativa, V. villosa ) and T. spumosum decomposed most rapidly, achieving final C:N ratios of 11–19. Novel ley legumes O. sativus and Trig. balansae displayed intermediate decomposition rates and achieved a C:N ratio of 25–35, potentially optimising N release synchrony with subsequent crop demand. These findings provide the first comparative assessment of second-generation ley legumes ( O. sativus , Trig. balansae ) alongside traditional pasture and grain legumes under field conditions in Mediterranean environments. Results demonstrate that novel pasture legumes provided sustained N release, potentially optimising nutrient synchrony with subsequent cereal crops better than either fast-decomposing traditional pastures or low N fixer grain legume residues. This species-specific decomposition information addresses a critical knowledge gap in managing N cycling in evolving Australian farming systems, where increases in N harvest index and changes to ley systems have altered N dynamics. This study demonstrates that, while edaphoclimatic conditions were strongly associated with residue decomposition in the Mediterranean environments of Western Australia, species selection substantially influenced the timing of N release. Novel ley legumes offer intermediate decomposition patterns that may better balance availability and consistency of N release compared to traditional legume options, with potential implications for managing nutrient synchrony, cereal biomass, and grain quality (protein and grain size) in evolving rotational systems.

Article.Title: Virtual screening of Withania somnifera phytochemicals identifies scopoletin and linoleic acid as predicted dual-target AChE/BACE1 candidates for alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Alsrhani A.; Riaz S.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder driven by interlinked pathological processes, including cholinergic deficit and amyloid-β accumulation, limiting the efficacy of single-target therapies. Multitarget-directed ligands capable of simultaneously modulating acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and β-secretase 1 (BACE1) offer a promising but underexplored strategy, particularly from natural product sources. Although the withanolides of Withania somnifera have been extensively studied for neuroprotection, its non-withanolide phytochemical fraction remains largely unexplored as a source of dual-target anti-AD agents. Here, from 129 initially retrieved non-withanolide phytochemical entries, duplicate removal across plant parts yielded 80 unique compounds, of which 76 returned valid SwissADME outputs; these compounds, derived from W. somnifera were evaluated using an integrated in silico pipeline comprising ADMET and toxicity profiling, molecular docking against AChE (PDB: 7E3H) and BACE1 (PDB: 7F1D), PASS-based bioactivity prediction, BioTransformer metabolite profiling, and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, with donepezil as the reference inhibitor. Twelve compounds satisfied pharmacokinetic filtering criteria, and this screening identified scopoletin and linoleic acid as the leading dual-target candidates, showing computationally predicted binding affinities toward AChE (− 7.7 and − 7.9 kcal/mol) and BACE1 (− 5.2 and − 5.8 kcal/mol) respectively, together with favorable blood–brain barrier permeability and low predicted toxicity. Molecular dynamics analysis further showed that the AChE-linoleic acid complex maintained conformational stability comparable to the AChE-donepezil reference complex over the full 100-ns trajectory, supporting a physically stable binding mode. These findings identify scopoletin and linoleic acid as predicted dual-target AChE/BACE1 candidates from W. somnifera , offering a computational foundation for their experimental validation as multitarget neuroprotective candidates against Alzheimer's disease.

Article.Title: Genomic analysis links phage susceptibility to the K5 capsule in uropathogenic Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Nagano D.; Hanawa T.; Tanaka M.; Tanji Y.; Matsuda T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) is the leading cause of urinary tract infections, which can progress to bloodstream infections, while the increasing prevalence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing strains limits treatment options. Here, 49 ESBL-producing UPEC clinical isolates and 42 phages were analysed to investigate bacterial genomic features associated with the phage susceptibility. The K5 strains were broadly susceptible, whereas three strains remained nonsusceptible; genome analysis revealed mutations in capsule biosynthesis genes linked to reduced capsular polysaccharide levels. Phage adsorption assays using the K5 capsule fraction supported the K5 capsule as a receptor for these phage clusters. Furthermore, phages associated with K5 susceptibility were predicted to encode putative depolymerases similar to K5 lyase, extending this mechanism to phages effective against ESBL-producing UPEC. These results support the K5 capsule as a receptor for phages targeting ESBL-producing UPEC and highlight its potential as a predictor of phage susceptibility.

Article.Title: Dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network for spatiotemporal correlation modeling of mine microseismic events and intelligent rockburst risk level reasoning
Article.Authors: An J.; Zhou J.; Li H.; Wang X.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Deep mining releases accumulated strain energy violently, and microseismic arrays record the fracturing that precedes rockbursts. Graph neural networks have already been applied to seismic and microseismic tasks such as phase association, source characterisation and event forecasting; what those graphs share is a topology anchored to a fixed sensor array and a single edge semantics, so they cannot follow an event field that turns over as the working face advances. This paper proposes a dynamic heterogeneous graph attention network (DHGAT). Every event enters as a node that retains four feature channels — waveform, source parameter, spatial and temporal — and three edge types (spatial proximity, temporal sequence, feature similarity) are rebuilt inside a 48 h sliding window. Relation-specific multi-head attention aggregates neighbours separately for each edge type, a semantic-level layer learns how much each relation contributes, and a gated recurrent encoder tracks the evolving graph embedding before four risk grades are assigned: no risk, low, moderate and high. On a 24-month catalogue of 7956 events from one deep metal mine, DHGAT reached 91.9 ± 0.4% accuracy, 0.853 ± 0.008 macro-F1 and 0.887 ± 0.006 quadratic weighted Kappa over ten runs, ahead of the strongest static heterogeneous baseline (HAN, 89.2% and 0.788) and of every other baseline at p < 0.01; recall on high-risk events reached 80.0%. Relation weights migrate from spatially dominated during gradual stress build-up to temporally dominated in the final hours before failure, which mirrors the shift from distributed microcracking to localised coalescence, and a perturbation test confirms that the attention carries the discriminative signal. Inference costs 46 ms per window on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. All data come from one mine, so the reported thresholds require recalibration before transfer.

Article.Title: Network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of dioctyl terephthalate in systemic lupus erythematosus pathogenesis
Article.Authors: Fang T.; Long S.; Wang T.; Chen T.; Yang H.; Zhong F.
Article.Abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dioctyl terephthalate (DOTP) may serve as an environmental risk factor for multiple diseases. Here, we explore potential molecular associations between DOTP exposure and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and identify candidate targets and pathways that may underlie these associations. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses revealed underlying mechanisms. Machine learning was used to prioritize candidate DOTP–SLE targets. CIBERSORT assessed target-immune cell infiltration relationships. Molecular docking evaluated DOTP-target binding affinities. We identified 39 DOTP-associated SLE targets. Enrichment analyses linked them to inflammatory cytokine production and immune activation. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) and machine learning prioritized six key targets (NFKB1, TLR4, CASP9, CDK5, DNMT1, PRKCD). Exploratory CIBERSORT analysis described associations with LM22-derived reference profiles, while ROC analysis characterized within-cohort discrimination and an exploratory nomogram summarized the combined candidate-gene pattern. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and these key targets. Our research results suggest a potential link between DOTP exposure and SLE progression through specific genes and pathways, and molecular docking predicted favorable binding interactions between DOTP and the relevant SLE targets. The ROC and nomogram analyses provided supplementary within-cohort characterization of the prioritized candidate genes. This study provides mechanistic insights into DOTP-associated SLE and supports the development of targeted prevention strategies.

Article.Title: ChGBO_QRNN: chronological gooseneck barnacle-based quantum recurrent neural networks for intrusion detection in IoT-SDN
Article.Authors: Jyothi B.; Thaiyalnayaki S.
Article.Abstract: There has been significant growth in the number of heterogeneous components configured within the Internet of Things (IoT) to allow effective data communication. However, IoT components are resource-constrained, and there are no standardized security procedures for communication within IoT platforms. While various solutions have been developed to secure communication in the IoT ecosystem, the existing approaches are not always reliable enough to address cyber threats and unwanted intrusions originating from IoT endpoints. Thus, this research presents a Chronological Gooseneck Barnacle Optimization-based Quantum Recurrent Neural Network (ChGBO_QRNN) for intrusion detection in SDN-IoT. Here, the proposed system contains three phases, which include a sniffer, a detector, and a sensor phase. In the sniffer phase, the features are extracted from the packets, and the extracted features are utilized for intrusion detection. In the detector phase, intrusion detection is carried out by the Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks (QRNN), and ChGBO is employed for training. In the sensing phase, the boundary of the attack is checked. If any concept drift is detected, the identification of a new attack is done using the proposed ChGBO_QRNN. Furthermore, the ChGBO_QRNN has gained weighted Accuracy, weighted True Positive Rate (TPR), weighted True Negative Rate (TNR), weighted F1-score, and weighted precision as 91.868%, 90.134%, 92.894%, 92.072%, and 92.978%.

Article.Title: Experimental study on corrosion mitigation and shear behavior of novel repairable rock bolts
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Qian S.; Lin Z.; Cai Z.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Based on the concept of repairable anchorage for post-damage performance recovery and corrosion protection in jointed rock masses, this study develops novel repairable structures in the form of rock bolts: the extrusion-crushing repairable (ECR) bolt and the hot-melt repairable (HMR) bolt. Chloride wet–dry cycling tests and double-shear tests were conducted on separate groups of double-jointed rock mass specimens to investigate their anticorrosion effectiveness and restoration capability. Preliminary results indicate that both repairable bolts can release repair materials after damage to partially restore sealing conditions, suppress corrosive ingress, and enhance shear resistance. Specifically, the ECR bolt demonstrated the potential for superior corrosion resistance, achieving higher peak shear load and greater external work to peak load under the tested conditions. This improvement may be associated with the infiltration and adhesion of the released polyurethane–ethyl acetate repair agent, which helps seal damaged regions and restore grout integrity over a wider area. In contrast, the HMR bolt provides localized sealing and partial reinforcement through thermally activated melting of EVA adhesive, leading to comparatively moderate enhancements in corrosion resistance and shear capacity. Observations of the failure characteristics further elucidated the reparative mechanisms and the differences in mechanical responses among the bolt systems. This work suggests that integrating repair functionality into rock bolting systems may provide a promising approach for mitigating damage and corrosion in rock engineering.

These findings identify a consistent pattern of adjusted between-group differences associated with instructional mode among advanced female Iranian EFL learners. They do not establish comparative efficacy or causal superiority of blended instruction. Pending replication using randomized designs, objective measures, and more diverse samples, the findings may inform further investigation of blended instructional arrangements and the specific pedagogical features associated with learner outcomes.

The accuracy of questions with a picture was significantly worse than those with no picture (69% vs 91%, respectively). Inter-model agreement was moderate (κ = 0.497–0.613). Contemporary LLMs show high accuracy on ID coursework, with weaknesses in chemistry/microbiology content, higher-order reasoning, and image interpretation; careful integration and guidance are warranted.

With regard to AHEI, we found no significant association between AHEI score and odds of breast cancer either before or after controlling for potential confounders. This association remained non-significant either in pre-menopausal or post-menopausal women. We found that adherence to a diet with high diversity was associated with decreased odds of breast cancer. Article.Title: Multiscale damage evolution mechanisms and life-cycle performance prediction modeling of asphalt pavement for resilient infrastructure
Article.Authors: Ju D.; He P.
Article.Abstract: Asphalt pavements deteriorate under heavy loading, thermal extremes and freeze–thaw cycling, yet damage physics, life-cycle prediction and resilience assessment are still handled as separate problems. This study joins them. We define damage at the micro, meso and macro scales through a single effective-bearing-area variable, and we link the scales with viscoelastic-damage constitutive relations, a cohesive interfacial criterion and representative volume element homogenisation. Scale-separation limits are stated explicitly: a convergence study fixes the representative volume element at four times the nominal maximum aggregate size, and the homogenisation integral is restricted to meso damage below 0.4. Characterisation combines openly accessible condition, climate and traffic records with a laboratory programme of 216 independent specimens covering dynamic modulus, four-point bending fatigue, wheel tracking and interleaved freeze–thaw plus ultraviolet conditioning, supported by image-based mesostructural reconstruction that we validate against expert annotation and against a learned segmentation baseline. A hybrid model embeds the damage evolution equation and a monotonicity requirement in the training objective of a gated recurrent network with attention, and an adaptive weight keeps the data and physics gradients comparable. On a test partition isolated by section, by period and by region, the model reached a coefficient of determination of 0.91 ± 0.01 for rut depth and 0.87 ± 0.02 for cracking ratio over five seeds; the physical constraint raised extrapolation trend consistency from 0.79 to 0.93 and cut monotonicity violations from 11.6 to 0.3%, while keeping the empirical coverage of the nominal 90% interval at 89.4%. Cross-scale transfer was nonlinear in temperature for all three gradations tested, amplifying below freezing and above about 45 °C, although the magnitude was gradation-dependent and we do not claim generality beyond the materials examined. Maintenance strategies separated clearly across resistance, recovery and adaptation. Data, code and configuration files are provided with the paper so that the workflow can be rerun without licensed components.

Article.Title: Spinal analgesia during childbirth in Sweden: a nationwide survey of midwives´ perspectives
Article.Authors: Bjurström M.; Fahlbeck H.; Skalkidou A.; Asif S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pain is a central symptom during childbirth. Compared to epidural analgesia, labour spinal analgesia (LSA) has received little attention, and no study has previously examined midwives´ attitudes toward LSA. This nationwide, mixed-methods survey study explored Swedish midwives´ experiences, perceptions, and use of LSA during vaginal childbirth. A 16-item questionnaire was distributed to 1,756 midwives, of whom 943 (53.7%) responded; the largest proportion was from the Stockholm–Gotland region (67.7%). Most midwives with LSA experience perceived it as effective (96.0%). Experience (number of women assisted with LSA) was categorized as none (4%), low (34.6%, 1–9 women), moderate (38.5% 10–49 women), or high (22.9% ≥ 50 women). Common indications included multiparity, previous rapid labour, and difficult-to-manage pain; the most common limiting factor was concern that the analgesia would wear off before birth. In multivariable penalized logistic regression analysis, working in a university region was associated with lower odds of LSA experience (aOR 0.09, 95% CI 0.01–0.39). Reflexive thematic analysis of 791 free-text responses resulted in two themes: Effective pain relief within limits of progress and Critical timing as a clinical concern . Respondents expressed strong interest in education on LSA. Further research and interprofessional collaboration are warranted to clarify LSA´s role in obstetric analgesia.

Article.Title: Understanding barriers to clinical trial participation among U.S. women: a national survey study
Article.Authors: Fida D.; Rajasekera T.; Roy A.; Wilson J.; Petro G.; Wiley A.; Lederman R.; Spagnolo P.
Article.Abstract: Women—particularly those from racially and ethnically minoritized groups—remain underrepresented in clinical research, yet their perspectives on participation are not well characterized. We conducted a national cross-sectional online survey of 5,301 U.S. women aged 18–70 years to assess willingness to participate (WTP), experiences with clinical trials, and awareness of sex-based differences in relation to research engagement. Because participation is shaped by social and structural determinants, we examined racial differences alongside socioeconomic status, healthcare access, and self-reported health to delineate intersecting contributors to disparities. Among 4,987 respondents reporting race (77% White, 14% Black, 7% Asian, 2% Other), most expressed at least tentative interest in participating (23% “definitely”, 60% “maybe”), yet only 11% had ever been invited and 7% had enrolled. In adjusted models, WTP was lower among Black women (β=−0.4; P = 0.0003) than among White women, whereas higher educational attainment and multimorbidity predicted greater WTP. Preferred resources, motivators, and perceived barriers also differed by race, which may inform tailored engagement strategies. Finally, most respondents (88%) endorsed women’s inclusion and sex-specific reporting in clinical research, suggesting that emphasizing the sex-specific relevance of research merits evaluation as an engagement strategy. Our findings suggest that limited invitation, together with structural and informational barriers, may contribute to women’s low participation, and support the evaluation of trust-building, burden-reducing, and culturally responsive strategies centered on women’s needs and perspectives to improve equitable representation.

Article.Title: Hand-washing frequency, gastric histopathology, and depressive symptom burden in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: a structural equation modeling study
Article.Authors: Owais M.; Aziz S.; Gul S.; Ijaz U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common among patients referred for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but their relation to mucosal pathology is unclear. We examined whether gastric histopathological severity links lifestyle exposures to depressive symptom burden in 442 adults undergoing endoscopy at two tertiary care hospitals in Pakistan, 320 of whom had gastric biopsies. Depressive symptom burden (five DSM-5-derived items) and gastric severity (four Updated Sydney System markers) were modeled as latent variables using structural equation modeling. An abrupt shift in patient characteristics and histology grades during recruitment was identified and adjusted for. In the primary model (CFI = 0.971; RMSEA = 0.040), less frequent hand washing was associated with higher depressive symptom burden (β = 0.23, 95% CI 0.06–0.39) but not with gastric severity (β = −0.11, 95% CI − 0.25 to 0.03). Gastric severity was not associated with symptom burden (β = 0.14, 95% CI − 0.06 to 0.35), and the indirect effect through gastric severity was null. The hand-washing association persisted in all six sensitivity analyses, whereas an apparent hand-washing–pathology association appeared only without adjustment for recruitment period. Depressive symptom burden in these patients was unrelated to mucosal pathology but tracked reduced self-care, supporting symptom screening irrespective of endoscopic findings.

Article.Title: Assessment of moisture availability and dryness during the growing season in the almaty region
Article.Authors: Akshalov K.; Zhunissova M.; Baisholanov S.; Zhumabek B.; Baimukanova O.
Article.Abstract: The novelty of this study lies in the integrated assessment of moisture availability and dryness during the growing season in the Almaty region over 1990–2024 using SPI-6 and SPEI-6 indices combined with NDVI-based vegetation response, providing new insights into climate-driven agricultural vulnerability in Central Asia. Under recent climate variability, an analysis of moisture availability and aridity and their distributions during the growing season in the Almaty region was conducted based on long-term data (1990–2024) on temperature, precipitation, moisture coefficient, hydrothermal coefficient (HTC), standard precipitation index (SPI-6), standardized precipitation-evapotranspiration index (SPEI-6), and NDVI satellite observations. It was found that the region is characterized by high spatial and temporal variability of climatic parameters. The average long-term temperature deviation during the growing season was 1.2 °C (maximum 1.8 °C in Kegen), the greatest precipitation variability was recorded in Esik and on the Almaty Kamensky Plateau, and the least in arid areas (Aul 4, Bakanas). The humidity coefficient varies from 0.33 (severe aridity) to 2.0 (excessive humidity), with HTC indicating non-arid conditions in the mountains (≥ 0.8) and severe aridity in desert areas (≤ 0.4). The SPI-6 and SPEI-6 indices revealed an increase in the frequency and intensity of droughts, especially in flat areas, while the NDVI confirmed vegetation stress during dry periods. The region's climate variability is manifested in both a trend towards aridification and short-term phases of excessive moisture (2016), with 2021 being the driest year on record. The results confirm the high climatic vulnerability of the Almaty region and the need for adaptation measures in the agricultural sector.

Article.Title: Network-based SEIVQHR modelling with optimal mobility control and QUBO reformulation
Article.Authors: Ramesh R.; Kannan M.; Chandrasekran K.; Zhan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human mobility between interconnected geographical regions can substantially influence the spatial transmission of infectious diseases, motivating epidemic-control strategies that account for both disease dynamics and regional interactions. In this study, we develop a network-based discrete-time SEIVQHR model comprising susceptible, exposed, infectious, vaccinated, quarantined, hospitalized, and recovered compartments, with inter-regional transmission represented through a normalized mobility matrix. The formulation incorporates vaccination, quarantine, hospitalization, and mobility-dependent infection within a unified metapopulation framework. A key feature of the model is the explicit representation of breakthrough infection among vaccinated individuals. Vaccine efficacy $$\epsilon $$ determines the residual susceptibility $$1-\epsilon $$ , and breakthrough infections enter the exposed compartment before progressing through the infectious pathway. We establish positivity, boundedness, and positive invariance of the discrete-time system under admissibility conditions involving the time step $$\Delta t$$ . The basic reproduction number $$R_0$$ is derived using a next-generation matrix formulation that accounts for both vaccination coverage and network connectivity. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be locally asymptotically stable for $$R_0<1$$ and unstable for $$R_0>1$$ . We further formulate a finite-horizon optimal-control problem with binary regional mobility restrictions and continuous vaccination allocation subject to vaccine-supply constraints. For a prescribed vaccination trajectory, the binary mobility-control component is approximated locally by a quadratic objective and reformulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. The resulting QUBO is mapped to an equivalent Ising Hamiltonian, enabling solution using simulated annealing, greedy heuristics, or quantum-annealing platforms. The framework is calibrated using COVID-19 surveillance data from India for 2021, with selected epidemiological parameters fixed at literature-based values to reduce overfitting and maintain biological plausibility. Numerical experiments examine parameter sensitivity, reproduction-number behaviour, admissible parameter regions, QUBO construction, and solver performance. The results identify the transmission rate as the dominant sensitivity factor and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed QUBO-based formulation for binary mobility-control optimization. Overall, the proposed framework provides a mathematically consistent decision-support methodology that connects network-based epidemic modelling, continuous vaccination allocation, binary mobility intervention, and QUBO/Ising optimization while retaining the nonlinear epidemic dynamics for validation of the resulting intervention strategies.

Article.Title: Deep-learning surrogate modeling for rapid design of high-sensitivity terahertz metasurface sensors
Article.Authors: Ahmadi E.; Mirshekari N.; Taghadosi M.; Mohammadi Pouyan S.; Askari M.
Article.Abstract: The design of terahertz metasurface sensors commonly relies on extensive full-wave electromagnetic simulations, making systematic exploration of high-dimensional design spaces computationally demanding. In this work, a deep-learning-assisted surrogate modeling framework is proposed to accelerate the design and optimization of refractive-index-sensitive metasurfaces. A dataset comprising 2048 distinct CST-simulated metasurface configurations was generated over the frequency range of 1.0–1.4 THz. With 1001 frequency points evaluated for each configuration, the pointwise regression dataset contains 2,050,048 input–output samples of the complex transmission response. A multilayer neural network was trained to predict the real and imaginary components of the transmission coefficient as a function of geometric parameters, operating frequency, and analyte refractive index. The trained surrogate achieved strong predictive performance on an independent test dataset, yielding a mean squared error of \(4.12\times 10^{-3}\) , a mean absolute error of \(4.27\times 10^{-2}\) , and a coefficient of determination of \(R^{2}=0.9792\) . The model accurately reproduced the spectral features governing resonance-based sensing and enabled rapid evaluation of candidate metasurface designs without repeated full-wave simulations. The surrogate model was subsequently employed to screen thousands of candidate geometries and identify promising sensing configurations. Selected candidates were validated through full-wave CST simulations, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed screening strategy. The best-performing design exhibited a refractive-index sensitivity of approximately \(0.2~\mathrm {THz/RIU}\) ( \(232~\mathrm {GHz/RIU}\) ), which is roughly 2.5 times higher than the baseline value of \(80~\mathrm {GHz/RIU}\) reported for closely related metasurface geometries. The observed resonance shifts and the agreement between surrogate predictions and CST results demonstrate the capability of the framework to guide the discovery of high-performance sensor designs. The results highlight the potential of surrogate-assisted electromagnetic design as an efficient and scalable alternative to conventional parameter-sweep-based optimization. The proposed framework substantially reduces computational cost while enabling systematic exploration of complex metasurface design spaces, providing a practical route toward data-driven development of terahertz sensing devices.

Article.Title: Beyond formal institutions: informal governance and farmer cooperation in a transition economy
Article.Authors: Skreli E.; Xhoxhi O.; Valentinov V.; Imami D.; Zhllima E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Friedrich Hayek distinguished the small-group logic of local norms, interpersonal trust, and reciprocity from the impersonal rules of the Great Society. In transition settings, however, these forms of governance may coexist rather than follow a simple sequence of replacement. Using a cross-sectional Albanian orchard farm survey, we estimate OLS models, bootstrapped product-of-coefficients paths, and an exploratory interaction to examine associations among local informal-rule enforcement, interpersonal trust, reciprocity, institutional trust, and willingness to cooperate. Stronger perceived local-rule enforcement is positively associated with interpersonal trust and willingness to cooperate; interpersonal trust is strongly associated with reciprocity, and reciprocity with willingness to cooperate. Institutional trust has no statistically significant direct association with willingness to cooperate in the fully specified model, although the local-rules/cooperation association is modestly stronger at higher levels of institutional trust. Indirect-path estimates are consistent with a sequence linking local rules, trust, reciprocity, and cooperation, but the cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal or causal ordering. The study therefore provides exploratory, single-setting evidence compatible with complementarity between informal and broader institutional governance.

Article.Title: Clinical classification of multiple sclerosis by machine learning
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Liu H.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that affects many adults and causes substantial neurological disability. Its clinical presentations are highly heterogeneous, and distinguishing clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing-remitting MS and progressive subtypes remains difficult, even though subtype determines treatment. Machine learning offers a way to address this difficulty: it identifies subtle patterns in high-dimensional biomedical data and has shown promise for MS classification from neuroimaging, whereas its performance on transcriptomic data has received less attention. To examine this question, we benchmarked three ensemble classifiers, AdaBoost, Random Forest and XGBoost, on 594 peripheral-blood mononuclear-cell transcriptomes from three public datasets, using a shared 6,033-gene matrix for four binary tasks: MS versus non-MS, CIS versus non-CIS, primary progressive versus relapsing-remitting MS, and secondary progressive versus relapsing-remitting MS. Models were evaluated on a 3:1 training/held-out split after standardization and two-component principal component analysis. All three classifiers achieved high held-out performance across the four tasks. These results indicate that ensemble machine learning can effectively classify MS and its clinical subtypes from blood transcriptomic profiles.

Article.Title: An intent aware framework for semantic edge intelligence in autonomous 6g UAV and vehicular networks
Article.Authors: Begum S.; Khan M.; Babu G.; Raghavi S.; Sakri S.
Article.Abstract: In autonomous communication between unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and vehicles in emerging sixth-generation (6G) networks, intelligent edge computing is essential for reliable decision-making under rapidly changing network conditions. This paper presents SEM-EDGE-X, a semantic edge intelligence framework integrating semantic feature extraction, Bayesian priority prediction, adaptive edge-to-cloud routing, semantic memory-assisted decision-making, dynamic resource management, adaptive cold-start semantic fusion, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) validation, dynamic trust refinement, and Digital Twin simulation. Performance is evaluated using Python and SUMO mobility modelling with the KITTI and UAVDT datasets under varying channel conditions and network densities, in terms of semantic accuracy, simulated communication latency, throughput, energy consumption, scalability, computational cost, and robustness. The results indicate a favourable trade-off among communication efficiency, energy consumption, and semantic performance, with 95.76% semantic accuracy (transmission fidelity under channel noise, not correctness against ground-truth labels), approximately 1.04 ms simulated communication latency (propagation, transmission, and queueing only), throughput above 25 Mbps, and energy consumption below 0.006 mJ. The separately measured software execution time of the pipeline is approximately 109.6 ms and is not included in the simulated latency.

Article.Title: Evaluating weakly supervised deep segmentation trained on radiometric pseudo labels for thermal fault screening in electrical substations
Article.Authors: Ekici S.; Uyar M.; Kabir M.
Article.Abstract: Fixed radiometric rules often supply training labels for infrared inspection of substations, where dense expert masks are rarely available. We examined what segmentation networks learn from such a rule and whether the result supports fault screening. On 193 calibrated FLIR frames, pixels exceeding the frame’s 30th-percentile temperature by more than \(16^{\,\circ }\) C served as pseudo labels for U-Net, DeepLabV3 and a compact attention-based network under five-fold cross-validation; outputs were assessed against held-out expert labels and independent field notes. With per-frame min–max input normalisation, agreement with the rule was low (Dice 0.34–0.44), and two networks ranked expert-positive frames below expert-negative ones (area under the curve 0.26 and 0.30). Supplying the temperature difference on a fixed physical scale raised agreement to Dice 0.78–0.81 and removed this inversion, whereas architecture had no significant effect. The pseudo labels encoded the extent of warm equipment rather than faults (labelled-area AUC 0.40), and the rule’s maximum temperature difference remained the best screening signal (0.75 against expert labels, 0.91 against field notes). A local thermal reference made labelled area informative (0.60–0.69). Network inputs should preserve the physical units in which supervision is defined, and radiometric pseudo labels benefit from local rather than frame-level references.

Article.Title: AI-driven HR service quality and organisational citizenship behaviour in the Indian IT sector: the mediating role of organisational commitment
Article.Authors: Priya K.; Muddhangala N.
Article.Abstract: In the modern world, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource Management (HRM) is changing the landscape of service delivery in Knowledge-Based Organisations (KBOs). While there is an increasing trend in investing in HR processes powered by AI, there is not enough empirical research exploring how perceived AI-HR service quality relates to employee behavioural outcome through psychological mechanisms, especially in the Indian information technology (IT) industry. The study uses Social Exchange Theory (SET) as its primary lens and non-measured, but secondary, lens is Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to analyse the impact of AI-based HR service quality on Organisational Citizenship Behaviour (OCB) which is in turn mediated by Organisational Commitment (OC) which is operationalised as a second-order reflective construct with three sub-constructs namely affective commitment, continuance commitment, and normative commitment. A survey of IT professionals drawn from major technology hubs across India was conducted and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The results demonstrate that AI-driven HR service quality exerts a significant positive influence on organisational commitment, which in turn meaningfully predicts organisational citizenship behaviour. Furthermore, AI-driven HR service quality also directly influences citizenship behaviour, and organisational commitment partially mediates this relationship. Individual and organisational boundary conditions, including AI literacy, technology anxiety, organisational AI support, and job role complexity, were found to moderate key relationships in the model. Theoretical and practical implications for AI-HRM system design and IT workforce management are discussed.

Article.Authors: Han Y.; Cheng D.
Article.Abstract: Traditional music generation models suffer from error accumulation and degraded quality in long-sequence generation, limiting their potential applications in intelligent music education. This study proposes a Long-term Memory Variational Generative Adversarial Network (LM-VGAN) by integrating long short-term memory and gated feature selection modules. We constructed multiple baseline models, including VAEGAN for comparative experiments, and adopted both objective quantitative metrics and subjective auditory evaluation to assess model performance. Experimental results show that after 50 iterations, LM-VGAN achieves a scale consistency of 89.15, pitch range of 1055, and note quality of 0.391, which outperforms mainstream baseline models and approaches real music standards. In subjective evaluation, it scores 8.30 in pleasantness and 7.77 in naturalness. The proposed model effectively solves the long-term dependency problem of music sequences. It provides a reliable technical solution for content creation, personalized training, and innovative development in modern potential applications for music education.

Article.Title: A privacy aware lightweight edge intelligent framework for real-time lethal threat interception and risk assessment
Article.Authors: Saha H.; Banerjee U.; Ghosh A.; Mattar E.; Bhattacharya P.; Shieh C.
Article.Abstract: Real-time intelligent surveillance systems require a careful balance between predictive reliability, computational efficiency, energy consumption, inference latency, and privacy preservation. However, existing vision-based approaches often achieve high detection accuracy at the expense of computational complexity, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this challenge, we propose a privacy-preserving, lightweight edge intelligence framework guided by a multi-objective architectural design methodology that jointly balances accuracy, computational efficiency, energy efficiency, real-time responsiveness, and on-device privacy.​ The proposed framework combines hybrid local-global representation learning with a lightweight multi-scale spatial attention mechanism to enhance the recognition of small and partially occluded lethal threats. A lightweight Temporal Threat Validation Module suppresses transient false alarms through temporal consistency analysis, while a context-aware Threat Assessment Network transforms validated detections into quantitative threat intelligence for priority-based decision-making. The complete pipeline executes locally on a Raspberry Pi 5 integrated with a Hailo-8L neural accelerator, transmitting only encrypted threat metadata to ensure low-latency, privacy-preserving operation.Experimental results demonstrate a Precision of 95.36%, Recall of 93.74%, an F1-score of 94.54%, and an mAP@0.5 of 96.58%. The proposed framework reduces localization error by 34.1%, decreases false alarms by 60.9%, and increases actionable alerts to 92.8% while sustaining 31.8 FPS, 31.4 ms inference latency, and an average power consumption of 9.1 W on the edge platform. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively unifies lightweight representation learning, temporal reasoning, contextual threat intelligence, and privacy-preserving edge computing, providing an energy-efficient and practically deployable solution for next-generation real-time intelligent public safety systems.

Article.Title: Design, implementation, and deployment of a machine vision-based dimension measurement system for steel slabs using deep neural networks
Article.Authors: Mazandarani M.; Akbarizadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Accurate measurement of steel slab dimensions is important for quality control and process monitoring in hot rolling. This study presents an automated machine vision system for measuring slab length, width, and thickness under real production conditions. The system combines a dual-camera imaging setup, controlled illumination, DeepLabV3 + semantic segmentation with an EfficientNet-B5 backbone, RANSAC-based boundary fitting, and a height-dependent calibration strategy for pixel-to-millimeter conversion. The software is integrated with the plant’s SQL-based network to compare measured dimensions with Product Data Information (PDI) and provide operator feedback. The system was evaluated on 65 previously unseen steel slabs that were independent of the 1,514 slabs used for network training and validation. Mean absolute errors were 2.56 mm, 1.84 mm, and 1.04 mm for length, width, and thickness, respectively, with corresponding RMSE values of 3.15 mm, 2.39 mm, and 1.35 mm. Using plant-specific tolerance bands of ± 5 mm, ± 3 mm, and ± 2 mm, within-tolerance agreement rates were 98.5%, 96.9%, and 95.4%. The complete measurement cycle takes approximately 4.2 s per slab and the system is currently deployed on a production line.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based PM2.5 estimation using NASA’s MERRA-2 and comparison of ML- and SHAP-based meteorological normalization in Thailand
Article.Authors: Aman N.; Torsri K.
Article.Abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) poses severe health risks in Thailand; however, sparse ground monitoring has left long-term trends poorly quantified. This study utilizes NASA’s MERRA-2 reanalysis to estimate historical PM 2.5 levels across Thailand through two approaches: an empirical formulation based on PM 2.5 chemical components (MERRA2_EF) and a machine-learning model (MERRA2_ML) utilizing the Light Gradient Boosting Machine algorithm. Validated against 58 reference air quality stations across Thailand (2012–2022), the MERRA2_ML model significantly outperforms the MERRA2_EF, increasing temporal correlation from 0.48 to 0.84, while reducing MAE from 14.99 to 8.64 µg m⁻³ and RMSE from 24.95 to 13.39 µg m⁻³. Similar improvements in model performance were also observed across the different regions of Thailand, with the MERRA2_ML estimates generally showing stronger temporal agreement and lower errors than the MERRA2_EF. MERRA2_ML substantially improved the representation of observed PM 2.5 variability across Thailand, accurately capturing diurnal peaks, dry-season enhancements, and interannual fluctuations, particularly in biomass-burning- and urban-influenced regions, compared with MERRA2_EF. Long-term analysis revealed significant increases in PM 2.5 across Thailand (1.97 µg m ⁻3 per decade) and most regions from 1981 to 2022, with MERRA2_ML showing consistently lower and more moderate trends than MERRA2_EF, highlighting substantial spatial heterogeneity in long-term PM 2.5 changes. By employing Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) for meteorological normalization, this study isolated emission-driven PM 2.5 variations. Overall, decreasing trends in emission-related PM 2.5 were observed across Thailand and several regions; however, statistical significance varied by region and method, and the non-significant national trends do not provide sufficient evidence to attribute the observed decline to a sustained nationwide reduction in emissions or policy interventions. These findings demonstrate that ML-enhanced reanalysis provides robust, spatially explicit data to support evidence-based public health decisions and air quality management throughout Southeast Asia.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation of blade-tip leakage flow control in a low-speed axial compressor using natural aspiration through casing wall slot

Article.Abstract: Mitigating rotor blade tip leakage flow in axial compressors is crucial for improving aerodynamic performance and extending the stable operating range. This study experimentally evaluates natural aspiration through a circumferential casing slot upstream of an isolated rotor blade row, with the configuration informed by previous numerical studies. The treatment passively admits ambient air without an external compressed-air supply. Experiments at 1600 rpm compared plain and treated casings using performance measurements, casing-wall static pressures, and single-wire hot-wire anemometry. Fourier-based spectral analysis was used to examine the measured flow unsteadiness. The performance curves indicated an approximately 1.2% increase in the pressure-rise coefficient. The reported operating points extended to an inlet-flow coefficient of 0.28 for the treated casing and 0.32 for the plain casing. Wall-pressure distributions and velocity spectra provided complementary information on the near-tip flow response, without independently establishing vortex weakening or a specific stall-inception mechanism. The admitted mass flow and overall efficiency were not quantified, limiting conclusions about rotor-throughflow-based stability improvement and efficiency. The results provide an experimental basis for evaluating passive air admission as a compressor casing treatment.

Article.Title: Computational evaluation of pongamol interactions with potential molecular targets of Blastocystis hominis
Article.Authors: Subramaniyan V.; Kumarasamy V.; Osman E.; Rajamanikam A.; Ashok C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pongamol, a bioactive substance that occurs naturally, shows promise as a treatment that targets several molecular pathways associated with Blastocystis hominis infection. Its binding affinity, pharmacokinetic behaviour, and protein-chemical interactions were examined in this work using molecular docking, ADMET profiling, and STITCH network analysis. Docking analysis predicted favorable binding of pongamol to eight selected protein targets, with the lowest docking scores observed for squalene epoxidase (− 9.7 kcal/mol), dihydrofolate reductase (− 8.9 kcal/mol), adenosine deaminase (− 8.6 kcal/mol), and thioredoxin reductase 1 (− 8.2 kcal/mol). These findings indicate that pongamol may interact with proteins involved in processes related to sterol metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and redox regulation. However, the docking results represent predicted binding interactions and do not establish enzymatic inhibition or biological efficacy. The ADMET analysis predicted high gastrointestinal absorption, blood–brain barrier permeability, and favorable drug-likeness, but also indicated inhibition of CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, and CYP3A4, as well as potential hepatotoxicity and reproductive toxicity concerns. These in silico results support further investigation of pongamol as a computationally prioritized multi-target candidate against Blastocystis hominis . However, experimental studies are required to determine whether pongamol truly inhibits these targets or exhibits antiparasitic activity.

Article.Title: Chromatin-associated miRNAs in PANC-1 cells: strong chromatin abundance of miR-21 and candidates with RNA–DNA triplex-forming potential
Article.Authors: Martin M.; Jalife C.; Méndez C.; Montecinos C.; Brown-Brown D.; Díaz-Tejeda F.; Caffi V.; Zavala K.; Kugler F.; Molina-González L.; Valenzuela-Nieto G.; Längst G.; Mardones G.; Munita R.; Opazo J.; Maldonado R.
Article.Abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are best known for their role in post-transcriptional gene regulation in the cytoplasm. However, a subset of miRNAs has been detected in the nucleus, suggesting additional regulatory functions. Here, we systematically characterize chromatin-associated small non-coding RNAs in the human pancreatic cancer cell line PANC-1. Using chromatin RNA immunoprecipitation coupled with small RNA sequencing, we show that the chromatin-associated small RNA population differs markedly from the bulk nuclear RNA pool and is strongly enriched in miRNAs. Among these, miR-21 represents the most abundant chromatin-associated species. In parallel, sequence analyses further revealed that a distinct subset of chromatin-associated miRNAs fulfills sequence requirements compatible with RNA–DNA triplex formation at genomic regulatory regions. Gel-shift assays demonstrate that Argonaute2 (Ago2) can interact with triple-helical structures in vitro, providing biochemical support for Ago2 recognition of such triplex substrates. Evolutionary analyses indicate that triplex-forming chromatin-associated miRNAs show a restricted phyletic distribution, with the full complement observed only in anthropoid primates, in contrast to the much broader conservation of non-triplex-forming miRNAs. Together, our results define a chromatin-associated miRNA landscape in PANC-1 cells, highlight miR-21 as the most abundant chromatin-associated miRNA, and identify candidate triplex-forming miRNAs and Ago2-triplex interactions that outline a testable hypothesis for an additional mode of miRNA-chromatin communication.

Article.Title: Cognitive impairment is associated with lower extremity function among community-dwelling older adults in Taiwan
Article.Authors: Liang I.; Lin L.; Tseng W.; Lin T.; Shen Y.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment is associated with poorer physical function in older adults, yet its relationship with different dimensions of lower-extremity function remains underexplored in community-dwelling populations. This study examined associations between cognitive status and lower-extremity function among community-dwelling older adults in Taiwan. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 82 adults aged 60 years and older. Cognitive status was assessed using the Saint Louis University Mental Status Examination (SLUMS) together with physician assessment, with participants classified as having normal cognition, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Lower-extremity function was evaluated using standardised measures of lower-body strength (30-second chair stand), flexibility (chair sit-and-reach), agility and dynamic balance (8-foot up-and-go), and postural stability (Biodex BioSway system). Significant differences in physical performance were observed across cognitive groups, with participants with dementia demonstrating poorer lower-body strength, flexibility, agility/dynamic balance, and selected measures of postural stability compared with those with normal cognition and MCI ( p < 0.05). Higher SLUMS scores, indicating better global cognitive performance, were associated with better lower-body strength and flexibility, faster 8-foot up-and-go performance, and better performance on several postural stability measures ( p < 0.05). These cross-sectional findings demonstrate associations between cognitive performance and multiple dimensions of lower-extremity function in community-dwelling older adults. Performance-based assessment of lower-extremity function alongside cognitive assessment may help characterise functional differences across levels of cognitive impairment, although longitudinal studies are required to determine whether these measures have value in predicting subsequent functional or cognitive decline.
