Article.Title: Simultaneous extraction of cocoa butter and antioxidants from defective cocoa beans by natural deep eutectic solvents
Article.Authors: Makhotkina D.; Tuntiwiwattanapun N.
Article.Abstract: Defective purple cocoa beans from incomplete fermentation are an underutilized source of cocoa butter and phenolic antioxidants. Natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) are used to extract polar bioactives, but their role in non-polar oil recovery through plant-matrix disruption remains underexplored. This study developed a NADES-assisted single-step extraction process for simultaneous cocoa butter and phenolic antioxidant recovery and examined whether oil release was associated with cell-wall disruption. Among six oil-immiscible NADES, choline chloride–lactic acid (ChCl–LA, 1:2) was selected for high cocoa butter recovery while retaining phenolic extraction. ChCl–LA recovered 63.02% of total extractable oil, exceeding anhydrous ethanol and acidified water but not screw pressing. Its oil showed a peroxide value (1.80 meq O₂/kg), lower than that obtained by Soxhlet, ethanol, and pH control extractions and comparable to screw-pressed oil. The aqueous NADES fraction showed a total phenolic content of 45.17 mg GAE/g dry weight, 44.46 mg TE/g dry weight DPPH activity, and 57.79 mg TE/g dry weight FRAP capacity. Reduced relative hemicellulose and lignin contents and SEM-observed morphological changes were consistent with cell-wall modification that may have contributed to oil release. These findings demonstrate the potential of oil-immiscible NADES for dual recovery of cocoa butter and phenolic antioxidants.

Article.Title: Interpretable and lightweight multimodal Transformer assessment of English education ecosystem health
Article.Authors: Lv M.; Wang Y.; Han D.
Article.Abstract: How can the health of an English classroom ecosystem be assessed from routine recordings in a way that is accurate, traceable to observable behaviour and inexpensive enough to run inside a school? The question is harder than it looks, because what is taught, how it is delivered and how learners respond are dynamically coupled: the difficulty of the material shapes delivery, and delivery in turn shapes learner behaviour. Single-modality models and shallow feature concatenation capture only fragments of that interplay. To answer the question, we build a multimodal Transformer that encodes textual, acoustic and visual streams through modality-specific front ends, learns their mutual dependence through bidirectional cross-modal attention, and merges them through a learned gate to predict a five-dimensional Ecosystem Health Index whose scoring rubric, rater protocol and entropy-based weighting are fully specified. A gradient-weighted attribution scheme turns attention into modality-decomposed, temporally localised explanations, which show textual features dominating healthy sessions and video-based disengagement cues taking over in degraded ones. A joint distillation and structured pruning pipeline compresses the network from 23.8 M to 2.9 M parameters, an 8.2-fold reduction that retains 88.2% of the teacher model’s RMSE-based performance. On 6,142 sessions recorded in 20 institutions the full model reaches an RMSE of 0.0431 ± 0.0009 and a coefficient of determination of 0.923 ± 0.004 across five random seeds, ahead of unimodal, early-fusion and prior cross-modal baselines under paired significance testing. Error rises by 13.5% to 34.1% once instructors, institutions, provinces, course types or educational levels are held out, and we treat that gap as the honest boundary of the present evidence rather than as noise. Device-level benchmarks on Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi hardware, together with an explicit responsible-use protocol that rules out punitive teacher evaluation, complete the account.

Article.Title: Exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability of the conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
Article.Authors: Rimu N.; Islam M.; Hossain M.; Akbar M.; Dey P.; Afikuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (CNLSE) serves as a robust mathematical model for understanding nonlinear wave propagation across various media, including optical fibers and plasma. This study introduces a cohesive analytical-computational framework to explore exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability associated with the CNLSE. By applying a conformable fractional traveling-wave transformation, the governing equation is transformed into an equivalent nonlinear ordinary differential equation. Utilizing the Modified Sardar Sub-Equation Method (MSSEM) and the Extended Generalized Riccati Equation Mapping Method (EGREMM) in conjunction leads to the derivation of extensive families of exact 21 solutions from Modified Sardar Sub-Equation Method and 27 from Extended Generalized Riccati Equation Mapping Method expanding the prior knowledge base significantly. The solutions encompass various wave structures, such as bright, dark, singular, periodic, rational, trigonometric, kink, and anti-kink forms. Notably, the integration of Hamiltonian phase-plane analysis, bifurcation theory, and dynamic stability through Hyers–Ulam stability assessment, alongside verification via the Differential Transform Method (DTM), enhances the study’s depth. The phase-plane analysis reveals critical dynamics such as equilibrium states and bifurcations, while perturbation analysis showcases transitions toward chaotic behaviors. The findings have profound implications on optical-pulse control, plasma-wave regulation, and quantum-wave transport, ultimately providing a comprehensive solution catalogue and deepening the understanding of nonlinear fractional-wave propagation mechanisms and their stability considerations.

Article.Title: Agentic AI for inverse design in nanophotonics and meta-optics
Article.Authors: Kang C.; Bae J.; Bae M.; Han J.; Suk H.; Kim J.; Jang I.; Chung H.
Article.Abstract: Nanophotonic inverse design requires coordinated choices about geometry, optimization, and electromagnetic simulation. We present an agentic AI framework that combines literature-based reproduction, human-approved optimization strategies, adjoint optimization, and separate forward evaluation of binary candidates. Four metagrating strategies tested from a common initialization yield final diffraction efficiencies of 79.4–90.9%. Selecting by peak optimization objective and by final binary efficiency produces different rankings. A separate metagrating redesign increases diffraction efficiency from 81.2% to 94.6%. For a two-dimensional metalens, the minimum focusing efficiency across three visible wavelengths increases from 40.0% to 65.2% relative to a symmetrized reproduced reference under matched lossless evaluation. A Bayer color router improves mean channel routing from 50.3% to 54.7% under a 125 nm minimum-feature criterion. Separate workflow evaluations include five reproducibility-screening examples, seven literature-to-simulation cases, and repair outcomes across five solver errors. Solver-specific retrieval resolves an interface error left unresolved by every tested standalone configuration. These results demonstrate agent-assisted exploration of nanophotonic designs and show why candidate selection must use the optical performance of the final binary structure.

Article.Title: Computational discovery of lead natural compounds targeting the HPV16 E6–E6AP–p53 interaction
Article.Authors: Alanazi A.; Ibrahim S.; Ejaz H.; Alruwaili I.; Chohan T.; Riaz S.; Eltayeb L.; Mazhari B.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) contributes to malignant progression by recruiting host E6-associated protein (E6AP), which facilitates ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the tumor suppressor protein p53.This study employed an integrated computational strategy to screen natural compounds for their potential to bind HPV16 E6 binding pocket and disrupt​ its interaction with the E6AP, thereby potentially preserving p53 function. The HPV16 E6–E6AP–p53 complex (PDB ID: 4XR8) was retrieved, assessed for structural quality, and analyzed for binding pocket identification. GO and KEGG were performed to explore associated biological functions and pathways. Pharmacophore-based virtual screening and molecular docking were conducted to screen high-affinity compounds, followed by ADMET, toxicity prediction, density functional theory (DFT) analysis, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation. Finally, protein–ligand interactions were analyzed to characterize key binding residues. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that the E6–E6AP–p53 gene set is associated with apoptosis, DNA damage response, and viral carcinogenesis pathways. Structural validation showed acceptable stereochemical and structural quality metrics. Pharmacophore-based screening of ​511 natural compounds followed by molecular docking identified several molecules with favorable binding affinities (−​11.0 to −​11.7 kcal/mol). The six top-ranked compounds were then filtered by ADME and toxicity predictions, and C-12 and C-17 were prioritized because they combined high docking affinity (−​11.4 kcal/mol) with acceptable pharmacokinetic properties and safety profiles. Interaction analysis confirmed stable binding within the E6–E6AP–p53 pocket. DFT calculations revealed that C-17 exhibited the smallest HOMO–LUMO energy gap compared with the luteolin and C-12, indicating a distinct electronic profile. Molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA analyses indicated greater stability and a more favorable binding free energy for C-17, followed by C-12, over the reference inhibitor, luteolin. Overall, C-12 and C-17 emerged as promising candidates for inhibiting the E6–E6AP–p53 interaction, which may help restore p53 function in HPV-driven tumor biology, and warrant further experimental validation.

Article.Title: Enhanced labor activity recognition via wearable physiological signals: a comparative machine learning study
Article.Authors: Ali L.; Kuruvachalil L.; Parambil M.; Masoud A.; Alam M.; Alnajjar F.; Bouktif S.; AlJassmi H.
Article.Abstract: Labor activity recognition using wearable physiological signals can support safety, productivity monitoring, and human-centered decision-making in industrial workplaces. This study presents an exploratory comparative benchmark of twenty machine learning and deep learning models for two labor activity-recognition tasks: binary productive/non-productive recognition and multiclass recognition of specific productive tasks. The raw data comprised 29,187 synchronized one-second physiological readings collected from four workers during three shifts in a stone prefabrication facility using Empatica E4 and Zephyr BioHarness 3 wearable devices. Blood volume pulse, electrodermal activity/galvanic skin response, heart rate, respiration rate, and skin temperature were transformed into 35 physiological statistical features per labeled analysis window; an additional activity-window Duration predictor yielded 36 predictors per modeling window. The final binary dataset contained 400 windows (200 productive and 200 non-productive), and the multiclass dataset contained 393 windows (131 oiling, 131 moving, and 131 cleaning). All models were evaluated using a stratified 80/20 train-test split, with standardization fitted only on the training data. The MLP Classifier achieved the highest binary performance (accuracy = 0.8625, support-weighted precision = 0.8646, support-weighted recall = 0.8625, and support-weighted F1-score = 0.8623). For multiclass recognition, CatBoost, Extra Trees, and Bidirectional LSTM each achieved accuracy = 0.9873, support-weighted precision = 0.9878, support-weighted recall = 0.9873, and support-weighted F1-score = 0.9873. These findings demonstrate strong within-dataset classification performance while emphasizing the need for future worker-independent and multi-site validation.

Article.Title: A unified model embedding MCC-MLD constitutive laws in Biot’s framework for settlement of Weinan interbedded clay-sand loess foundations
Article.Authors: Yang W.; Lu Q.
Article.Abstract: Consolidation settlement prediction in interbedded clay–sand loess foundations is complicated by stratigraphic heterogeneity and hydromechanical coupling that homogeneous-soil models cannot capture. This study presents an integrated elastoplastic framework combining the Modified Cam-Clay model for loessial clay, the Wright–Duncan model for sand with particle breakage, and Biot’s consolidation theory in a unified implementation for the Weinan plain, China. Parameters for clay, sand, and transitional interlayers came from 20 borehole samples. Although each component is established, their integration with site-specific enhancements—a structure-dependent yield surface for shallow clay and a breakage-dependent hardening law for deep sand—constitutes a practical advancement. The numerical implementation via Python-Matlab, validated against borehole data from the same site using a reserved validation set (6 boreholes not used in calibration), reveals settlement in three stages—elastic rebound, primary consolidation (70–80% of total), and secondary creep—peaking at the 20–30 m clay–sand interface, where sand dilatancy transfers 12–18% of stress to clay, quantified by the proposed γ–μ interface parameter system. Spatially, settlement is shallow-dominated with deep-layer lag; temporally, sand accelerates clay pore-pressure dissipation by 35–40%. The model attains ± 5% accuracy versus ± 25% for homogenization and establishes a closed-loop monitoring–inversion–updating workflow. Assuming full saturation, it neglects matric-suction effects in the vadose zone, including water-table fluctuations and dry–wet cycles. At the Weinan site (water table 15–25 m), the model applies directly to deep saturated strata, contributing most (70–80%) of consolidation settlement; the shallow unsaturated zone requires caution and further characterization.

Article.Title: Association between maxillary labial frenulum morphology and gingival health, midline diastema and anterior caries in children
Article.Authors: Aşık A.; Sağlam C.; Acar S.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the distribution of various morphological types of the maxillary labial frenulum in children between 2 and 13 years of age and to evaluate the association between frenulum morphology and dentition stage, gingival health, presence of midline diastema, and caries in the maxillary anterior teeth. This cross-sectional study enrolled 381 children aged 2–13 years from the Pediatric Dentistry clinics of Izmir Tınaztepe University and Ege University Faculty of Dentistry. Parental written informed consent and ethical approval were obtained. Frenulum morphology was classified according to Mirko (mucosal, gingival, papillary, or papilla penetrating). Dentition stage (primary, mixed, or permanent), gingival health (Löe & Silness Gingival Index), and the presence of midline diastema and maxillary anterior caries (present/absent) were recorded. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27.0, with associations between categorical variables examined using Pearson’s chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests ( p < 0.05). The study sample of 381 children consisted of 51.4% girls and 48.6% boys, with a mean age of 7.58 ± 2.46 years. Primary dentition was present in 29.9% of participants, mixed dentition in 63.8%, and permanent dentition in 6.3%. The most common frenulum types were papillary (37.2%) and gingival (36.5%), followed by mucosal (17.2%) and papilla penetrating (9.1%). Maxillary midline diastema was detected in 47.1% of children, and caries in the upper anterior teeth in 28.1%. The most frequent gingival index score was 1 (58.3%). Frenulum type was significantly associated with dentition stage ( p = 0.006) and the presence of midline diastema ( p < 0.001). Specifically, the papilla penetrating frenulum type was significantly more common among children with midline diastema ( p < 0.001). Different frenulum types were most frequently observed during the mixed dentition stage. No significant association was found between frenulum type and gender ( p = 0.470), gingival index ( p = 0.748), or maxillary anterior caries ( p = 0.120). A significant association was also observed between higher gingival index scores and increased caries prevalence ( p < 0.001). This cross-sectional study demonstrated a significant association between maxillary labial frenulum morphology and both dentition stage and the presence of maxillary midline diastema in children aged 2 to 13 years. The papilla penetrating frenulum type was significantly more common among children with midline diastema. Different frenulum types were most frequently observed during the mixed dentition stage. However, no significant association was found between frenulum type and gingival index scores or the presence of caries in the maxillary anterior teeth. These findings indicate that frenulum morphology is associated with certain clinical parameters, particularly dentition stage and midline diastema, but not with gingival inflammation or anterior caries in this study population.

Article.Title: Epidemiological patterns and inequalities of emergency department visits for self-harm and interpersonal violence before and after the first COVID-19 lockdown
Article.Authors: Sartini M.; Pessano S.; Ottria G.; Schinca E.; Dupont C.; Orgiana A.; Romairone P.; Paoli G.; del Puente F.; Carbone A.; Cristina M.
Article.Abstract: Violence is a major public health concern associated with substantial health burdens and social inequalities. Routinely collected healthcare data can support surveillance and prevention strategies. We conducted a retrospective study of all Emergency Department visits for violence and self-harm recorded in a North Italian Region between January 2016 and September 2025 using the regional healthcare data warehouse. Descriptive analyses were performed to characterize temporal and sociodemographic patterns. An Interrupted Time Series based on a negative binomial regression model assessed changes associated with COVID-19 lockdown measures. Among 5,409,509 ED visits, 53,086 (0.98%) were related to violence or self-harm. Rates varied across provinces. Foreign nationals accounted for approximately one-third of visits, with an increasing trend overtime, suggesting possible inequalities in ED attendance. Visits were more frequent among males, during evening and nighttime hours, on weekends, and in the summer months. Among Italian residents, interpersonal violence-related ED visits decreased by approximately 55% during the lockdown period (IRR 0.449, 95% CI 0.365–0.552; p < 0.001), while self-harm-related visits decreased by approximately 25% (IRR 0.750, 95% CI 0.571–0.985; p = 0.039). Trends among foreign residents were in the same direction for both outcomes but for self-harm did not reach statistical significance, likely reflecting smaller event counts in this subgroup. Violence- and self-harm-related ED visits showed marked temporal and sociodemographic disparities. Changes observed during pandemic-related restrictions are consistent with altered exposure opportunities and may reflect underlying inequalities, providing evidence to guide targeted prevention and surveillance strategies.

Article.Title: Interpretable soil thickness mapping with nested and spatial validation in the Angulinao semi-arid lake basin
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Zhang Q.; Li W.; Liu J.; Zhu Z.; Zhang G.; Li T.; Zhao J.; Zhao D.
Article.Abstract: Soil thickness varies markedly across semi-arid basins, yet sparse profile observations make these spatial patterns and their environmental controls difficult to resolve. We mapped soil thickness in the Angulinao semi-arid lake basin using 92 profiles and 27 environmental covariates. Twelve feature-selection and regression pipelines were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation. Boruta-random forest achieved the lowest mean root mean square error (RMSE; 25.941 ± 0.859 cm), while elevation, slope, relief, topographic position, wetness and precipitation recurred most consistently across training subsets. A fixed seven-variable XGBoost model achieved the lowest RMSE in the five-zone internal spatial comparison (26.358 cm; R² = 0.716) and was used for regional mapping. Thicker soils were concentrated across broad basin lowlands, whereas dissected terrain showed greater spatial heterogeneity; the > 100–150 cm class covered 48.30% of the 3318.773 km² mapped domain. SHAP analysis identified elevation as the dominant model contribution and revealed conditional effects across topographic scales. Bootstrap refits produced a mean pixel-wise standard deviation of 10.072 cm, and 3.16% of the mapped area fell outside the model-defined area of applicability. The resulting maps characterize basin-scale soil-thickness patterns, their environmental associations and priority areas for field verification, providing spatial information for regional soil-resource assessment.

Article.Title: Trends in one-year survival and pregnancy termination in congenital heart defects in 1994–2024: a population-based registry
Article.Authors: Derridj N.; Monier I.; Wojciechowski M.; Goffinet F.; Bonnet D.; Lelong N.; Khoshnood B.
Article.Abstract: To assess trends in one-year survival among infants with congenital heart defects (CHD) and in termination of pregnancy for fetal anomaly (TOPFA), with particular attention to isolated and severe isolated CHD. 5,898 CHD from the Paris Registry of Congenital Anomalies (1994–2024) were included. Isolated CHD were defined as CHD without associated genetic or extracardiac anomalies, as opposed to non-isolated CHD. One-year survival was estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Temporal trends in survival and TOPFA among pregnancies with a recorded prenatal diagnosis of CHD, were analyzed using logistic regression. Non-linearity (fractional polynomials) and slope changes (segmented models) were assessed. Among 5,898 CHD cases, 4,391 were live births, 1,361 TOPFA and 146 stillbirths. One-year survival was 91.0% (95% CI 90.1–91.8), reaching 95.0% (95% CI 94.2–95.7) in isolated CHD and 84.0% (95% CI 81.4–86.2) in severe isolated CHD. Overall survival improved significantly over time (p < 0.001), with a change in slope around 2007–2009; the absolute annual gain decreased from approximately + 0.5% (95% CI 0.26–0.68) at the beginning of the study period to + 0.2% (95% CI 0.16–0.23) in recent years. Similar improvement was observed in isolated CHD, with smaller gains after approximately 2009, and in severe isolated CHD (+ 0.56% per year; 95% CI 0.28–0.84). Among prenatally diagnosed pregnancies, TOPFA decreased in isolated CHD (− 0.50% per year; 95% CI − 0.74 to − 0.26) and severe isolated CHD (− 0.36%; 95% CI − 0.69 to − 0.03). One-year survival improved over three decades, although gains became smaller over time rather than showing a uniform plateau across CHD subgroups. Improvement extended to severe isolated CHD and occurred alongside declining TOPFA among prenatally diagnosed isolated and severe isolated CHD.

Article.Title: The amplification effect is not driven by perceptual sampling bias
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Liu W.; Li Y.; Lu N.; Fu J.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract When observers are confronted with a set of stimuli of varying sizes, the relatively salient large stimuli among them tend to influence their judgments, leading them to overestimate the average size of the set of stimuli—a phenomenon known as the "amplification effect." This effect is a prevalent phenomenon in the research on ensemble perception, yet its mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to address this issue by manipulating stimulus presentation and introducing adaptation to distinguish between early perceptual encoding and later responding as potential loci of the effect. Firstly, comparing multiple stimuli of varying sizes with a single stimulus produces an amplification effect, resulting in the overestimation of the average size of multiple stimuli, which is in line with the former theory. However, this bias disappears when comparing the sizes of multiple stimuli of varying sizes and multiple stimuli of uniform size. Secondly, the adaptation paradigm provides converging evidence in support of this hypothesis. Adaptation to both multiple large stimuli and a single large stimulus induce adaptation aftereffects, whereas adaptation to multiple stimuli of varying sizes does not, suggesting that stimulus salience does not bias the perception of average size during the adaptation period. Experiment 1 was conducted in the central visual field, and Experiment 2 replicated these findings in the left and right hemifield fields. In conclusion, the amplification effect does not constitute a stable bias arising at the perceptual sampling stage, which is driven by stimulus size salience. Instead, it likely emerges during intermediate processing or the subsequent response selection stage after initial perception. These findings suggest a reassessment of the perceptual saliency-based weighting theory.

Article.Title: Computational and experimental screening identifies 6-chloro-2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde derivatives as disruptors of the HEG1–KRIT1 protein–protein interaction
Article.Authors: Kamel E.; Bin-Jumah M.; Alfassam H.; Alotaibi R.; Alammari B.; Alshabrmi F.; Alkhayl F.; Lamsabhi A.
Article.Abstract: The HEG1–KRIT1 protein–protein interaction is a central regulatory interface in cerebral cavernous malformation signaling and represents a potential target for small-molecule modulation. Compounds were prioritized through drug-likeness filtering, PAINS/reactivity assessment, diversity and purchasability evaluation, AutoDock Vina docking, short molecular dynamics refinement, and MM/PBSA rescoring. Among the tested compounds, HN1 yielded a modest positive ΔΔG PPI estimate of + 2.66 kcal/mol, whereas HKi2, HN2, and HN3 yielded negative estimates; these values were interpreted descriptively as approximate indicators of ligand-dependent changes in the HEG1–KRIT1 interface. Experimental testing showed concentration-dependent inhibition of EGFP–KRIT1 FERM binding to HEG1-coated beads. Under the applied assay conditions, HN1 produced the numerically lowest IC₅₀ estimate at 3.51 ± 0.14 µM, compared with 3.90 ± 0.13 µM for HKi2, while HN2 and HN3 produced IC₅₀ estimates of 24.12 ± 1.59 and 31.63 ± 1.99 µM, respectively. These numerical differences do not establish superiority or equivalence among the compounds. Collectively, the computational and experimental findings support HN1 as a preliminary hit that warrants further target-engagement, mechanistic, and cellular validation.

Article.Abstract: This study introduces a novel multi-waste binder design approach for high-strength alkali-activated concrete (HSAAC), in which ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) content was reduced to only 20%. The results show that the steam-water treatment system produced higher compressive strengths for all mixtures after 28 days compared to the other curing systems. The WCA20 mixture showed a 3.5% improvement in workability. The control, MK40, and WCP20 mixtures achieved high-strength concrete requirements, with compressive strengths of 87, 75, and 70 MPa, respectively. The QP20 and WBP20 mixtures exhibited enhanced flexural strength, with increases of up to 44% and 25%, respectively, and achieved tensile strengths of 7.16 MPa and 6.21 MPa, respectively. MK20 and QP20 exhibited superior resistance to both sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄) and magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) attack. Microstructural analysis further confirmed the strength enhancement observed after sodium sulfate exposure. The SEM–EDS results revealed denser reaction matrices and increased Ca/Si ratios of 0.31 and 0.27 for MK20 and QP20, respectively, suggesting the formation of additional Ca-bearing reaction products and continued matrix densification. Environmental assessment revealed improved sustainability across all mixtures, with WCP and WBP showing the highest environmental performance among the multi-waste blends.

Article.Title: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma pretreatment as a novel tool to tailor the functional properties of quince seed mucilage biopolymer-based edible films
Article.Authors: Karimi J.; Sohrabi S.; Rad M.; Sharifian M.; Zare L.; Meybodi N.
Article.Abstract: Quince seed mucilage (QSM) is a promising polysaccharide for the fabrication of biodegradable edible films; however, its relatively limited functional performance restricts broader food-packaging applications. The present study investigated the effects of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) treatment applied to quince seed at 6, 7, and 8 kV for 1, 3, and 5 min, then mucilage extraction was performed, followed by a comprehensive evaluation of the physicochemical, surface, barrier, mechanical, and thermal properties of the resulting films. CAP treatment did not significantly affect film thickness regardless of the applied processing conditions. Contact angle analysis demonstrated that the highest surface hydrophobicity was achieved under a 7 kV for 3 min plasma treatment. Water vapor barrier measurements revealed that films treated for 3 min exhibited the lowest permeability, irrespective of the applied voltage. Surface topography analysis indicated that 6 kV for 1 min plasma exposure generated the greatest surface roughness, whereas increasing either the treatment duration or applied voltage produced a denser, more homogeneous, and compact film microstructure. Compared with the untreated control, CAP treatment significantly enhanced the mechanical performance of the films, with the optimum tensile properties obtained following treatment at 6 kV for 1 min. Thermal characterization by TGA and DSC further demonstrated that 5 min plasma exposure time adversely affected the thermal stability of the films, while optimized CAP conditions (3 min) provided the most favorable thermal performance. Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriately optimized CAP treatment effectively improves the structural integrity and functional performance of QSM-based biodegradable films.

Article.Authors: Hamim O.; Gazmeh H.; Reimer T.; Loaiza-Ramírez J.; Qian X.; Ukkusuri S.
Article.Abstract: Currently, electric vehicle (EV) adoption in the United States is transitioning from early experimentation to stabilized adoption. However, barriers to mass adoption remain, particularly related to user perceptions and behavioral differences between non-EV and EV users. This study analyzes survey data from 996 US adults, including non-EV, plug-in hybrid EV (PHEV) and battery EV (BEV) users, using an econometric model that accounts for self-selection bias in evaluating users’ perceived importance of charging time-related features at EV charging stations (EVCSs). The estimated treatment effects for current PHEV and BEV users are -0.920 and -0.975, respectively, indicating lower perceived importance under their observed EV adoption states relative to their estimated counterfactual non-EV states. In contrast, perceived importance among non-EV users slightly decreases by 0.016 under the PHEV adoption counterfactual and increases by 0.913 under the BEV adoption counterfactual. On average, transitioning from non-EV status to PHEV or BEV status significantly decreases perceived importance by 0.442 and 0.076, respectively, with these shifts larger than or comparable to corresponding observed simple differences. This suggests that charging-time concerns may be less salient under the estimated EV adoption states after accounting for self-selection. Our results indicate that self-selection bias can impede EV adoption by amplifying perceived barriers among non-EV users. Furthermore, by identifying and adjusting for self-selection effects, this research offers insights for designing targeted outreach strategies and infrastructure policies to support mass diffusion of EVs.

Article.Authors: Orsi L.; Lajunen T.; Madore A.; Hamilton F.; Margaritte-Jeannin P.; Vernet R.; Bouzigon E.; Granell R.; Jaakkola M.; Laprise C.; Jaakkola J.; Nadif R.; Dizier M.

Applying this approach and accounting for the phenotypic heterogeneity of asthma, we identified three new genes PTPRE , FZD7 and SASH1 associated with asthma, and not detected before by classical approach of GWAS. They play a crucial role in key biological processes involved in asthma development, suggesting potential new targets for asthma prevention.

Article.Title: Bacterial etiologies, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and multidrug resistance trends among patients with sterile body site infections in Northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Assefa M.; Tigabie M.; Tesfa A.; Smineh F.; Worku T.; Shferaw Y.; Worku M.; Mesfin Y.; Girmay G.; Almagharbeh W.; Cherie N.
Article.Abstract: Sterile body site (SBS) bacterial infections are one of the most critical problems in hospital settings. The rise of antimicrobial resistance and empirical treatment of SBS infections without local up-to-date evidence have led to higher patient mortality, representing a research gap in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the bacterial distribution, their antimicrobial resistance patterns, multidrug resistance (MDR) trends, and associated factors in SBS infections at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia. A retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with SBS infection at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized and Referral Hospital. The Kobo data collection tool was used to extract laboratory records from September 2021 to May 2026 (five years) using a consecutive sampling technique. Sterile body fluid samples were collected and inoculated onto blood agar, chocolate agar, MacConkey agar, and mannitol salt agar plates. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the modified Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion method. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26 software. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test assumptions, and logistic regression models were applied. Bivariate logistic regression results with a p-value < 0.25 were entered into multivariate analysis to control for potential confounding factors. To assess associations between dependent and independent variables, a p-value < 0.05 in multivariate analysis was considered statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. Study findings were presented using tables and charts. A total of 1,368 study participants were included in this study, consisting of 678 (49.6%) males and 690 (50.4%) females. The prevalence of culture-confirmed bacterial SBS infection was 5.48% (95% CI: 4.38%-6.83%), with 75 bacterial isolates identified. No mixed bacterial infections were detected in any patient. There was a high prevalence of Gram-negative bacteria (88.0%, n = 66), while 12.0% ( n = 9) were Gram-positive bacteria. E. coli (33.3%, n = 25) and K. pneumoniae (26.7%, n = 20) were the most predominant pathogens causing SBS infection. Gram-negative bacterial isolates demonstrated resistance to commonly used antibiotics such as ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and ampicillin. An overall prevalence of MDR was 17.3% (13/75), with K . pneumoniae (35%, n = 6), Non-Lactose Fermenting Gram-Negative Rods (28.6%, n = 2), and E. coli (16%, n = 4). Being male ( p = 0.011) and study years 2025/26 ( p < 0.001), 2024/25 ( p < 0.001), and 2023/24 ( p = 0.020) were significantly associated with bacterial SBS infection. In this study, Gram-negative bacteria were the most common cause of SBS infection, with MDR E. coli and K. pneumoniae being frequently identified isolates. Over the five-year trend, a higher MDR rate was observed in 2024/25 (46.2%), with K. pneumoniae exhibiting a high MDR rate in 2024/25 (71.4%); p = 0.03, and the prevalence of MDR E. coli peaked at 50% during 2022/23 and 2024/25 tracking periods. This study highlights the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance surveillance and molecular detection of resistance mechanisms.

Article.Title: Complementary spectroscopic methods for simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide and olodaterol hydrochloride with analytical performance and environmental sustainability assessment
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Taha E.; Soliman S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly analytical methods for drug quality control is essential in modern pharmaceutical analysis. This study presents, to the best of our knowledge, two independent and complementary analytical strategies for the simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide (TBM) and olodaterol hydrochloride (OLH) in laboratory-prepared mixtures and the pharmaceutical formulation Stiolto ® Respimat. The first strategy employed UV–Vis spectroscopy combined with Partial Least Squares (PLS), Genetic Algorithm-PLS (GA-PLS), and Multivariate Curve Resolution–Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS), whereas the second employed first-derivative Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy using zero-crossing wavenumbers. Validation mixtures were designed using Latin Hypercube Sampling to provide systematic coverage of the investigated concentration space. First-derivative preprocessing was applied to enhance spectral resolution and minimize baseline effects. The UV–Vis spectra in the range of 222–263 nm and FTIR spectra in the range of 4000–400 cm⁻¹ were used for quantitative analysis. Among the investigated UV–Vis chemometric models, MCR-ALS provided the lowest root mean square errors of calibration and prediction, with RMSEC and RMSEP values of 0.0359 and 0.0329 for TBM and 0.0622 and 0.0375 for OLH, respectively. The developed models provided recoveries of approximately 100%, with precision expressed as RSD values below 2%. Application to the commercial formulation produced satisfactory recoveries ranging from 98% to 101% for both drugs using the developed techniques. Statistical comparison with the reference HPLC method showed no significant differences at the 95% confidence level. Overall, the complementary UV–Vis chemometric and ATR-FTIR approaches provided satisfactory quantitative performance for the simultaneous determination of TBM and OLH within the investigated analytical ranges.

Article.Title: Field-compatible tissue cryopreservation enables delayed endothelial cell culture
Article.Authors: Allen K.; Burns J.; Vázquez-Medina J.; den Heyer C.; Shero M.
Article.Abstract: Decades of biomedical research have developed robust tools in molecular and cell biology, including cell culture systems, for model vertebrate species. Logistical constraints associated with remote fieldwork limit the application of these techniques to non-model species. Traditionally, cell culture requires tissue collection from live or very recently deceased animals, followed by immediate sterile processing and cell isolation, but these requirements are often impractical in field settings. To address this limitation, we developed a field-compatible method to cryopreserve arterial tissue from pinnipeds for delayed endothelial cell isolation. Grey seal placentae were opportunistically collected, and arteries were preserved using benchtop blunt dissection and a portable ​​-80 °C freezer with a standard cell freezing medium. Samples were held in a portable ​-80 °C freezer for ~ 2 months before transfer to LN 2 vapor storage for ~ 1 month, followed by endothelial cell isolation. Cells isolated from cryopreserved arteries are phenotypically endothelial, proliferate in culture and are the first endothelial cell cultures derived from grey seals. Grey seal endothelial cells respire after culture expansion, and ATP production rates are ~ 1.5×​​ greater than those in freshly derived endothelial cell cultures from a related species, though the relative contributions of OXPHOS and glycolysis were comparable between cell preparations. This method is practical for field researchers and supports the generation of primary cell cultures weeks-to-months after initial tissue collection with minimal resources, strengthening the ability to investigate the cellular basis of physiological phenomena in the natural world.

Article.Authors: Mao Y.; Xu R.; Lu H.; Zhou Y.; Bao L.; Zhong L.; Wang P.; Ren C.; Feng X.

Article.Title: Storying digital well-being and quality of life in Ghanaian adult learners’ use of generative AI
Article.Authors: Adarkwah M.; Kayi E.; Oduro F.; Osei-Tutu A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in higher education; however, little is known about what its use means for adult learners’ digital well-being (DWB) and quality of life (QoL). This mixed-methods study, which leaned towards a qualitative design (qualitative dominant), investigated these issues among adult learners at a university in Ghana. The quantitative phase involved 212 randomly selected respondents, while six (6) participants were purposively selected for the qualitative phase. The survey findings showed that overall DWB was above the midpoint of the 7-point Likert scale (M = 4.58, SD = 0.76). The mental (M = 4.09, SD = 1.12), emotional (M = 4.51, SD = 1.29), and reverse-coded physical (M = 5.14, SD = 1.45) subscales indicated generally positive perceptions of digital well-being. However, item-level responses showed that a notable minority of participants still reported physical challenges, including disturbed sleep, changes in eating habits, physical discomfort, and reduced physical exercise associated with GenAI use. QoL was measured using a 3-point substantive scale, with two non-substantive response options excluded from scoring. The QoL mean (M = 2.06, SD = 0.94) indicated modest gains in safety, control, activity engagement, and time efficiency. A digital storytelling analysis of the participants’ experiences revealed that the adults held ambivalent views about GenAI, reflecting both appreciation for its efficiency and anxiety over its encroachment on human creativity and authenticity. The coping strategies adopted included developing a critical distance and self-awareness, re-engaging human connection and support networks, mindful regulation and intentional use, and transforming frustration into learning. It is recommended that adult educators prioritise the digital safety of adult learners.

Article.Title: NPSBZn fertilizer rate and variety effects on carrot yield, quality, and soil acidity in the central highlands of Ethiopia: a two-year field trial
Article.Authors: Manore D.; Watumo T.; Bosha A.
Article.Abstract: Carrot (Daucus carota L.) is a valuable vegetable crop in Ethiopia, yet national average yields remain low due to soil nutrient deficiencies, unbalanced fertilizer use, and limited access to improved varieties. Most existing research is single-season, which limits the robustness of fertilizer recommendations across varying climatic conditions. Additionally, the recently introduced blended NPSBZn fertilizer lacks crop- and site-specific recommendations. To address these gaps, a two-year (2020–2021) field experiment was conducted in the Hadiya Zone, central Ethiopia. Increasing NPSBZn rates from 0 to 150 kg ha⁻¹ steadily improved all yield and quality parameters, with no plateau observed at the highest rate. Marketable yield reached 38.5 t ha⁻¹ in Nantes at 150 kg ha⁻¹, with marginal returns exceeding 1200%. However, soil pH declined from 5.94 to 5.56, indicating progressive acidification likely due to nitrification of ammoniacal nitrogen from urea and NPSBZn fertilizers. We conclude that NPSBZn fertilization at 150 kg ha⁻¹ combined with the Nantes variety is economically viable and agronomically superior in the short term, but integrated soil management including liming or organic amendments is required to mitigate long-term acidification and sustain soil health.

Article.Authors: Zhe Z.; Han S.; Kim S.

These findings suggest that a PLVAP promoter–driven reporter can be used to refine and functionally evaluate iPS-derived endothelial-like cell products with strong pro-angiogenic properties in ischemic models and to support the development of cell-based therapies for ischemic cardiovascular disease.

Article.Title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
Article.Authors: Kodukhov A.; Pastushenko V.; Pflitsch M.; Vinokur V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel. In this study, we demonstrate that additional quantum effects and techniques can improve the performance of quantum cryptography while maintaining everlasting security. In particular, we study the recently introduced loss control-based QKD approach, which relies on the physical properties of optical fiber channels associated with Rayleigh scattering and on continuous monitoring of channel integrity. We show that achieving everlasting and future-proof security requires an additional assumption concerning the completeness of the mathematical description of the devices and, consequently, of the eavesdropper’s ensemble. Furthermore, we introduce a security statement framework that combines physical assumptions about a cryptographic implementation with formal mathematical security proofs. Applying this framework to loss control-based QKD, we derive the eavesdropper’s ensemble for an arbitrary number of local attack points and define channel-dependent QKD as a new class of QKD protocols. Finally, we propose a general criterion for identifying quantum cryptographic solutions based on whether the physical mechanism underlying security disappears in the classical limit.

Overall reliability showed moderate values (mean ICC = 0.566) with significant network-specific variation. Salience Network regions, particularly the supramarginal gyrus, and lateral parietal regions of the Default Mode Network demonstrated the highest stability (ICC > 0.600). Matrix-wide analyses indicated high consistency in connectivity rankings (Kendall’s W = 0.798). Among the 23 most temporally stable regions, five connections showed systematic associations with reactive aggression across sessions; none survived FDR correction, consistent with the non-aggressive nature of the cohort. These findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in rsfMRc reliability across brain networks and measurement intervals, providing empirical guidance for researchers planning longitudinal connectivity studies. Network-specific considerations are critical in study design, and importantly, reliability estimates from this healthy homogeneous sample represent upper-bound values not directly transferable to clinical populations, where greater symptom heterogeneity and state fluctuations are expected to reduce temporal stability. Within these constraints, identifying stable connectivity patterns through reliability-informed frameworks provides a proof-of-concept for future individual-differences research, while regions with poor reliability require methodological optimization before serving as measurement targets.

Article.Title: DnaB mutants suppress DciA essentiality in Thermus thermophilus and uncover its role in recombination-dependent replication
Article.Authors: Gost M.; Failde-Soler M.; Silva de Sousa B.; Quiles S.; Herrero P.; Gómez-Campo C.; Carrasco B.; Blesa A.; Alonso J.; Mencía M.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial DNA replication is initiated by assembling two hexameric replicative DnaB helicases at the DnaA-unwound oriC region, a process that requires a cognate helicase loader, DciA, DnaC, or DnaI. Members of the phylum Deinococcota encode a DciA-type helicase loader composed of an N-terminal DUF721 domain, an intermediate lasso-like region (IR), and two specific domains: a Zn-finger (ZnF) and a replication-recombination domain (RRD). Here, we show that deletion of the Thermus thermophilus dciA gene is lethal, but viability is restored by a dnaB M375I extragenic suppressor. DnaB M375I expression is necessary and sufficient to sustain replication in otherwise wild-type Δ dciA cells. In vitro, DciA interacts with DnaB and its mutant variants. DnaB efficiently unwinds 3’-forked DNA and this activity is restrained by DciA through inhibition of DnaB’s ATPase and helicase functions. Cells lacking DciA, or specifically the RRD, fail to grow at the optimal temperature (70 °C) but grow at lower temperatures (60–65 °C). Notably, the combined loss of the RRD and the recombination proteins RecO or RecR is lethal. Together, these results establish DciA as the replicative helicase loader in Deinococcota and reveal a functional link between DNA replication and homologous recombination.

Article.Title: Design-oriented comparison and load adaptability of deep cement mixing columns with different cross-sectional geometries for soft-soil bridge foundations
Article.Authors: Jiang S.; Za’ba N.; Hussin T.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a capacity-equivalent framework for selecting circular, square, and rectangular deep cement mixing (DCM) columns for a soft-soil bridge foundation when pier load varies in service. Unlike equal-length shape comparisons, the required column length was determined separately for each geometry and area replacement ratio under the same 240 kN bearing-capacity criterion. Sixty-three three-dimensional ABAQUS cases covered replacement ratios from 0.30 to 0.50; selected circular and rectangular cases were then evaluated at five loads from 180 to 240 kN. The model used Mohr-Coulomb soil and linear-elastic DCM and cushion idealizations and was checked against a layered-summation solution and one field settlement measurement at 196 kN. The finite-element settlement differed by 3.4% from the analytical value and by 14.5% from the field measurement. At m = 0.30, circular, square, and rectangular configurations produced settlements of 25.44, 27.78, and 32.41 mm, respectively; the rectangular configuration used the least cement-treated soil (3.60 m³). Increasing m generally shortened the design-dependent column and reduced equivalent-stress demand but increased cement-treated volume, so settlement did not change monotonically. Range-averaged normalized settlement sensitivities were 0.454 and 1.109 for the circular and rectangular cases, while the corresponding equivalent-stress sensitivities were 0.877 and 0.638. The framework shows that capacity compliance, settlement, relative stress demand, material use, and load adaptability can favor different geometries. The findings remain site- and model-specific because groundwater, consolidation, nonlinear DCM behavior, and full mesh and boundary sensitivity studies were not included.

Article.Title: Exact nonlinear wave structures in the conformable time-fractional Vakhnenko equation via bilinear neural networks
Article.Authors: Zidan A.; Shafee A.; Sanaee H.; Iqbal N.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a conformable bilinear neural network framework for constructing exact nonlinear wave solutions of the conformable time-fractional Vakhnenko equation (CTFVE), a model of high-frequency wave motion in a relaxing medium in which the fractional order acts as a tunable time-scale parameter. By introducing a logarithmic dependent-variable transformation and a generalized Hirota bilinear operator compatible with the conformable fractional derivative, the governing fractional equation is recast in bilinear form. Several feedforward neural network structures with one and two hidden layers are then employed as structured ansätze for the bilinear auxiliary function, and the resulting algebraic systems are solved in closed form. This yields the integrable solution families of the Vakhnenko equation—the one-soliton, the two-soliton with its exact phase shift, the breather formed from a complex-conjugate soliton pair, and the cnoidal periodic wave—each verified symbolically against both the bilinear form and the original nonlinear equation. We show that the fractional order is physically equivalent to an algebraically time-varying relaxation rate of the medium, which makes the wave structures propagate with a power-law (decelerating for \(\epsilon <1\) ) speed while preserving their amplitude and width, and a numerical perturbation analysis confirms that the soliton is orbitally stable. Because the solutions are obtained in closed algebraic form, the method avoids the discretization and convergence errors of iterative schemes. The framework offers a flexible analytical route to coherent structures in fractional evolution equations and extends naturally to related nonlinear wave models.

Article.Title: DirectHF-DA integrates a lightweight network and multi-resolution STFT-RGB for edge-deployable cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhu C.; Yu K.; Zheng L.; Wu M.; Ruan C.; Tie J.
Article.Abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions is challenged by domain distribution shifts and the high computational cost of deep models on resource-constrained edge devices. To address these coupled challenges, this study proposes DirectHF-DA, a directional high-frequency domain-adaptive network for lightweight cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis. First, a compact multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform representation (MR-STFT-RGB) is constructed by deterministically organizing short-, medium-, and long-window STFT spectrograms into a standard three-channel tensor, enabling complementary transient, modulation, and harmonic information to be jointly processed by a single lightweight backbone. Next, a lightweight feature extractor, DirectHF-Net, is developed by integrating directional depthwise separable convolution (DDSConv), directional residual refinement and transition blocks (DRRB/DRTB), and a high-frequency enhancement block (HFEB), thereby preserving fault-sensitive directional textures and high-frequency impact features with low computational complexity. Joint maximum mean discrepancy (JMMD) is further introduced to align the joint distributions of the source and target domains, enabling effective adaptation to unlabeled target operating conditions. Experiments on 12 cross-domain transfer tasks using the CWRU and HUST bearing datasets achieve average diagnostic accuracies of \(99.70\pm 0.05\%\) and \(92.31\pm 1.02\%\) , respectively. DirectHF-DA contains only 1.6 M parameters, requires 0.22 GFLOPs, and has a model size of 6.22 MB. When deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super, the proposed model achieves real-time inference throughputs of 60.54 FPS and 61.71 FPS on the CWRU and HUST tasks, respectively. These results demonstrate that DirectHF-DA achieves a favorable balance among cross-domain diagnostic accuracy, computational efficiency, and real-time edge inference capability.

Article.Title: Sustainable AC/ZIF-67 hybrid adsorbents derived from agricultural waste for rapid dye removal from water
Article.Authors: Alsaidy M.; Tahmasebpoor M.; Ateeq A.
Article.Abstract: Activated carbon (AC) derived from a mixture of walnut and almond shells was prepared via phosphoric acid activation (ACA) and subsequently combined with ZIF-67 to fabricate a series of ACA/ZIF-67 composite adsorbents for removing dye contaminants from water. Comprehensive characterization (including FESEM, EDS, FTIR, XRD, and N 2 adsorption–desorption) confirmed the integration of ZIF-67 within the carbon matrix. The results demonstrated that the highest BET surface area (592.43 m 2 . g − 1 ) belongs to the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite with a hierarchical porous structure. The effects of operational parameters, including ACA/ZIF-67 ratio, pH (1–11), amount of adsorbent (0.1–2 g/L), time (5–60 min), initial dye concentration (10–100 mg/L), and operational temperature (25–45 °C), were systematically investigated. Under the optimum conditions of pH 7, temperature of 25 °C, and the amount of adsorbent 1.5 g/L, the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite achieved more than 98% removal of 10 mg/L MB within only 5 min. Equilibrium and kinetic data were satisfactorily well-fitted to the Langmuir isotherm (R² > 0.99) and the pseudo-second-order kinetic (R 2 = 0.9999) models, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 35.95 mg/g. This adsorption behavior can be attributed to the combined effects of pore filling, electrostatic attraction, π–π interactions, and hydrogen bonding between dye molecules and the ACA5/ZIF-67 surface. Consequently, these outcomes highlight the potential of biomass-derived AC/ZIF-67 composites as favorable adsorbents for the simulated removal of dyes from aqueous solutions, subject to further assessment in real industrial effluents.

Article.Title: Deciphering salinity tolerance during germination in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L) through systematic phenotypic screening
Article.Authors: Teku T.; Mekonnen T.; Bayissa K.; Hora O.; Woldesemayat A.
Article.Abstract: Wheat is the major staple crop contributing about 20% of global calorie intake and ranks second to maize in worldwide production. It is vital to increase the production of wheat by about 70% by 2050 to feed world population. However, soil salinity is a critical constraint that impairs plant growth and development during germination stage. Therefore, identifying salt-tolerant bread wheat genotypes at germination stages is critical for mitigating yield losses. This study aimed to evaluate and identify wheat genotypes with superior germination performance under salinity stress. To achieve this objective, a comprehensive study was performed on 153 Ethiopian bread wheat genotypes obtained from Holeta agricultural research center. Seeds of each genotype were treated under four salinity levels for eight days. The results demonstrated that salinity stress had a significant effect on all measured 17 traits. Salinity markedly reduced growth parameters (SL, RL, SH, SFW, SDW, RFW and RDW), physiological traits (SRWC and RRWC), and germination indices (GP, GVI, SI), which showed strong correlations with salt tolerance. In contrast, mean germination time (MGT), time to 50% germination (T50), and shoot height reduction (SHR) increased under salinity stress. The substantial genotypic variation observed among the 153 Ethiopian bread wheat genotypes under salinity stress indicates the presence of valuable genetic diversity for salinity tolerance at the germination stage, providing promising resources for breeding salt-tolerant wheat cultivars.

Article.Title: Deep learning–based object detection for automated classification of ripe and unripe tomatoes in field conditions
Article.Authors: Hassanzadeh L.; Pourdarbani R.; Sabzi S.; Daliran O.; Molina-Martínez J.; García-Mateos G.; García-Berná A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate detection of tomatoes at different ripening stages from close-range remote sensing imagery acquired under real field conditions is a key enabler for yield estimation, harvest scheduling, and selective robotic picking in precision agriculture. However, achieving reliable performance is challenging due to occlusions, variable illumination, dense foliage, and the limited size of domain-specific datasets typically available to small farms and research teams. In this work, we present a controlled comparative study between two representative object detection paradigms, Faster R-CNN with a ResNet-50 FPN backbone (two-stage) and YOLO26s (single-stage), on a curated dataset of 367 high-resolution images acquired in a commercial cherry-tomato greenhouse under natural illumination, containing more than 8,900 manually annotated tomatoes across three classes: blossom, premature, and ripe. Both models were trained for 100 epochs under a controlled protocol sharing the same data, stratified 70/15/15 split complemented by 5-fold cross-validation, and evaluated using COCO-style AP/AR together with per-class precision–recall and ROC analyses. YOLO26s achieved a macro-average AP of 0.741 and ROC AUC of 0.954 on the held-out test split, substantially outperforming Faster R-CNN (macro AP 0.241; ROC AUC 0.836), particularly under stricter localization thresholds, and qualitative examples confirm that localization rather than classification is the main bottleneck of Faster R-CNN. These results provide actionable guidelines for deploying detectors on small agricultural remote sensing datasets in fixed monitoring stations and on ground or aerial autonomous platforms, where tighter bounding boxes and a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off are decisive for reliable operation.

Article.Title: Coupling between structural evolution and glass transition in supercooled water
Article.Authors: Kocherbitov V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water exhibits unique structural, thermodynamic, and dynamic anomalies, particularly in supercooled states where structural evolution between high- and low-density liquid environments occurs alongside kinetic arrest. Here we use molecular dynamics simulations of TIP4P/2005 model of water with cooling and heating scan rates from 10 to 3000 K µs⁻¹ to investigate equilibrium and nonequilibrium behavior. Above ~ 220 K, properties are scan-rate independent, indicating equilibrium, while below this temperature kinetic effects dominate on the simulations time scale, reflecting glassy dynamics. In the liquid regime, the temperature dependence of viscosity reveals two relaxation mechanisms with distinct activation energies. The rapid slowing down of the lower-temperature mechanism leads to the onset of the glass transition. At the cooling and heating rates accessible to the present simulations, the glass transition occurs in the same temperature range as the heat-capacity maximum associated with the gradual structural evolution between high- and low-density liquid environments. By integrating a two-state thermodynamic model with the Tool–Narayanaswamy–Moynihan glass-transition framework, we separate equilibrium anomalies from kinetic glass-transition effects. This combined structural evolution – glass transition (SE-GT) approach provides a consistent description of water’s coupled thermodynamic and dynamic behavior across a broad temperature range.

Article.Title: A fuzzy DEMATEL–ISM framework for unpacking barriers to digital twin adoption in high-density crowd management
Article.Authors: Miski A.; Bafail O.
Article.Abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology promises to revolutionize the management of large gatherings by coupling physical assets with their virtual counterparts to enable real–time situational awareness. However, adoption in safety–critical crowd scenarios remains limited. This work introduces a hybrid framework combining fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (FDEMATEL) and Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) to systematically identify, interrelate, and prioritize the obstacles to DT deployment for hyper–dense events such as Hajj and Umrah. By embedding fuzzy logic, the method captures the vagueness and variability of expert assessments, while ISM organizes barriers into a hierarchical structure. Analysis of ten barriers (BR1–BR10) identifies the nascent stage of domain implementation (BR10) as the deepest root cause, occupying the base of the interpretive structural hierarchy and exhibiting the largest net causal effect. The shortage of specialized expertise (BR6) occupies the second hierarchical level, mediating between domain immaturity and the remaining barriers. Crowd dynamics and behavioral diversity, legacy system integration, and regulatory and governance frameworks are net causes in the DEMATEL sense but occupy the upper hierarchical level as members of a mutually reinforcing cluster. Infrastructure requirements and cost emerge as the most strongly dependent barriers, followed by resistance to change and privacy concerns. The findings invert the intervention priorities transferred from industrial digital twin deployment, where cost and infrastructure are treated as binding constraints, and provide a cause-and-effect roadmap for policymakers and technology providers.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-driven computed tomography analysis of upper airway morphology in patients undergoing multilevel sleep surgery
Article.Authors: Moon S.; Ryu S.; Jeong Y.; Lee J.; Cho H.
Article.Abstract: Anatomical information for planning sleep surgery is limited. We conducted an exploratory analysis to quantify upper airway morphology before and after multilevel sleep surgery and to examine whether preoperative measurements were associated with surgical response. In this post hoc analysis of a prospective cohort, 25 adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea underwent expansion sphincter pharyngoplasty, tonsillectomy, and single-port transoral robotic tongue base resection, with nasal surgery when indicated. Preoperative and postoperative computed tomography scans were segmented using a previously developed deep-learning pipeline. Surgical response was defined a priori as a postoperative apnea–hypopnea index below 15 events/h. Eighteen patients (72.0%) met the definition of response. Segmentation agreed with manual ground truth (mean Dice coefficient 0.868 ± 0.034). Surgery was associated with significant change in 8 of 13 morphological parameters, including uvula area (+ 140.2 mm²; 95% CI 109.2–171.3) and uvula–tongue volume (+ 2270.5 mm³; 95% CI 1166.6–3374.3). No preoperative parameter distinguished responders from non-responders (all p > 0.05), and preoperative tongue–epiglottis volume showed no discrimination. No drug-induced sleep endoscopy finding differed by response status. Automated computed tomography analysis reliably quantified upper airway remodeling after multilevel sleep surgery, but no preoperative morphological parameter predicted surgical response. These exploratory findings require independent confirmation.

Article.Title: PrivLightScreen: a privacy-preserving lightweight multitask AI framework for operational millimeter-wave airport security screening
Article.Authors: Adil M.; Ullah S.; Sajid M.; Aburaed N.
Article.Abstract: Airport passenger security screening is both a public-safety control and a performance-critical node in the airport supply chain, yet most artificial-intelligence studies on millimeter-wave (MMW) screening optimize detection accuracy without explicitly modeling false alarms, queue delay, privacy risk, resilience, or deployment cost. This paper presents PrivLightScreen, a unified multitask framework for privacy-preserving concealed-object detection in MMW screening, together with an Operational Performance Evaluation Framework (OPEF) that translates inference-level measurements into checkpoint-level performance indicators. PrivLightScreen combines physics-informed adaptive preprocessing, zone-guided self-supervised contrastive pretraining, a lightweight multitask module with an inter-zone Zone Transformer detection head, a representation-level anatomical abstraction layer, and a four-tier knowledge-distillation hierarchy spanning server graphics processing units (GPUs) to embedded processors. On the public Transportation Security Administration (TSA) passenger screening dataset, evaluated with a subject-disjoint protocol, the full model achieves a zone-level F1-score of 0.978 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.974–0.982), a log-loss of 0.0498 (95% CI 0.0476–0.0521), and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.983 (95% CI 0.979–0.987), giving the best result among the compared baselines under this protocol. Auxiliary keypoint and segmentation performance is evaluated against weak labels derived from the TSA body-zone metadata and a quality-audited pseudo-mask pipeline, reaching a percentage of correct keypoints normalized by head size (PCKh@0.5) of 99.81 percent and a weak-mask mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 85.7 percent. The smallest distilled student retains 98.3 percent of teacher F1 with a 3.1 MB footprint and an $$8.0\pm 0.6$$ ms batch-size-one forward-pass latency on commodity embedded hardware. Under OPEF, this edge model is the only tested configuration to satisfy all deployment-readiness thresholds, reaching a modeled 353 passengers per hour per lane (95% interval 345–361), a mean resilience index of $$0.82\pm 0.03$$ across six stress conditions, and a design-time Privacy Compliance Score of 0.95. The results show that detection accuracy, operational throughput, resilience, privacy, and hardware efficiency can be evaluated jointly in a single deployable MMW-screening framework, while regulatory deployment still requires site-specific validation and formal certification.

Article.Title: Depression, anxiety, and stress among Polish optometrists: a cross-sectional study conducted two years after legal regulation of the profession
Article.Authors: Garaszczuk I.; Zielonka S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health among healthcare workers is a major concern, as depression, anxiety, and stress contribute to burnout, medical errors, and suicide risk. In Poland, optometrists combine healthcare responsibilities with commercial pressures related to optical retail. In 2023, optometry was formally regulated under the Polish Act on Certain Medical Professions, introducing legal protections as well as new professional obligations that may increase occupational stress. Despite international evidence of elevated psychological distress among optometrists, no prior studies have examined mental health in this professional group in Poland using validated clinical screening instruments. A cross-sectional online survey using the DASS-21 questionnaire was conducted among 276 practising Polish optometrists between August and November 2025. Demographic and professional data were collected, and open-ended responses on occupational stress and burnout were analysed using conventional content analysis. Moderate-to-severe symptoms were reported by 44.9% of respondents for depression, 42.4% for anxiety, and 41.6% for stress. Female gender and lower income were associated with higher DASS-21 scores. Key stressors included excessive workload, inadequate salary, commercial pressure, and lack of professional recognition. Polish optometrists reported levels of depression, anxiety, and stress that exceeds rates observed in the general Polish population and among optometrists in several other countries. Targeted mental health support and workplace reforms are urgently needed.

Article.Title: Monsoon rainfall prediction using a BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism: a case study of Odisha state
Article.Authors: Sahu B.; Panigrahi A.; Pati A.; Sahu S.
Article.Abstract: Effective water resource management and disaster mitigation require accurate rainfall prediction for planning purposes. Forecasting of rainfall is a difficult time series problem as it is highly non-linear and non-stationary, and dependent on season. This study suggests a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) with Transformer Architecture and Attention, as well as the ensemble based on meta-learning. This framework employs CNN layers to gather temporal local patterns, BiLSTM networks to shape sequential dependencies, and transformer blocks to embrace the self-attention mechanism to formulate long-range patterns. An attention mechanism is used to dynamically weigh relevant time steps to achieve higher accuracy and interpretability in predictions. Moreover, various forecasts from LSTM, CNN–BiLSTM–Attention, CNN–Transformer–Attention, and XGBoost are fused together using a Random Forest-based meta-learner for enhanced robustness and generalization in the ensemble model. The proposed method utilizes Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty estimation, enhancing the trustworthiness of the aforementioned approach by providing confidence intervals. The model undergoes assessment through a variety of performance metrics such as RMSE, MAE, R², MAPE, and NRMSE. Experimental results show that the ensemble framework consistently outperforms individual models, achieving better predictive accuracy and greater stability than individual models for a variety of rainfall, including extremes. The proposed model combines attention-based interpretability, transformer-based global learning, and ensemble meta-learning for rainfall forecasting, which is robust and scalable.

Article.Title: Integrative multivariate analysis of Pisum sativum L. genotypes using agro-morphological traits under contrasting semi-arid highland agro-ecosystems
Article.Authors: Mareai M.; Zaid N.; Al-Omri T.
Article.Abstract: Understanding yield formation and environmental adaptation in pea ( Pisum sativum L.) is essential for improving productivity under semi-arid highland conditions. This study evaluated eleven pea genotypes using morphological characterization and multivariate analyses across contrasting Northern and Central Highland environments of Yemen. Qualitative and quantitative descriptors revealed clear phenotypic variation among genotypes and successfully distinguished improved cultivars from local landraces. Analysis of variance showed significant differences ( P ≤ 0.05) among genotypes for all measured traits, indicating substantial genetic variability. Grain yield ranged from 0.40 to 1.20 t ha⁻¹ in the Northern Highlands and from 0.50 to 1.80 t ha⁻¹ in the Central Highlands, with Yahsb and Amran consistently exhibiting superior performance across environments. Principal component analysis indicated that yield variation under favorable conditions was mainly associated with seed weight (SW) and number of pods per plant (NPP), whereas phenological traits contributed more strongly under Northern Highland conditions. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations of grain yield with seed weight, pod length, pod width, and number of pods per plant, although the magnitude of these relationships varied between environments. Path coefficient analysis showed that seed weight exerted the greatest direct effect on grain yield in the Central Highlands (0.703), while pod length had the strongest direct effect in the Northern Highlands (0.568). Hierarchical clustering and heatmap analyses consistently grouped Yahsb, Amran, YG50075, and YG50083 into a distinct cluster across both environments, reflecting their close phenotypic similarity and superior agronomic performance. These findings demonstrate that yield determination in pea is environment-dependent and highlight Yahsb and Amran as promising genotypes for breeding and cultivation in semi-arid highland agroecosystems.

Article.Title: Association of the TyHGB index with hyperuricemia in adults aged 65 years and older
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang Z.; Wu T.; Ma J.; Zhang R.; Yu Z.
Article.Abstract: The triglyceride high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose body index (TyHGB) is a newly proposed metabolic marker. Our objective is to investigate the association between TyHGB and hyperuricemia prevalence in the elderly population. Data were analysed from 5730 adults aged 65 years or older in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), with an external validation sample from Kunshan Jinxi People’s Hospital, China. Logistic and linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were employed to evaluate the associations between TyHGB and hyperuricemia. TyHGB levels were significantly higher in participants with hyperuricemia ( P < 0.001). After adjusting for covariates, TyHGB remained significantly associated with hyperuricemia (OR: 1.141, 95% CI: 1.105–1.178, P < 0.001) and with increased serum uric acid (SUA) levels (β: 4.798, 95% CI: 3.759–5.836, P < 0.001). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship. ROC analysis further demonstrated that TyHGB had better discriminatory ability compared to other metabolic measures. These associations were also confirmed in the external Kunshan Chinese elderly sample. TyHGB is significantly associated with hyperuricemia, suggesting its potential utility in evaluating the role of metabolic disorders in hyperuricemia.

Article.Title: Motor imagery EEG signal classification using SAGAN-based data augmentation and ResNet-18 for brain–computer interface applications
Article.Authors: Jaipriya D.; Sriharipriya K.
Article.Abstract: Electroencephalogram signals are an important basis for motor skill rehabilitation and motor control in brain–computer interface (BCI) research. However, the limited labelled EEG data may limit the development of effective motor imagery (MI) classifiers. To address this limitation, this study presents a data augmentation framework using an improved Synaptic Augmented Generative Adversarial Network (SA-GAN). The EEG signals of the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset were transformed into two-dimensional time–frequency representations from one-dimensional time-series signals using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). The resulting representations were augmented using SA-GAN to generate synthetic MI samples and used to train ResNet-18 under augmented and non-augmented conditions. The proposed SAGAN-ResNet18 framework achieved better classification performance than the considered GAN-based augmentation approaches for all the evaluated subjects. The results show that the generated samples can provide valuable extra training information and reduce the negative impact of limited training data in within-subject MI classification. The results show that the proposed augmentation strategy is effective for the conditions evaluated in the BCI Competition IV-2a experiment.
