Article.Title: Improved YOLOv7-based surface defect detection method incorporating feature retention and densely-scale spatial attention mechanisms
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Ko C.; Chang Y.; Chang H.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to automated defect detection. However, the feature information of small defects is easily lost during feature extraction, and as the network deepens, the increased computational burden and the insufficient utilization of existing features also affect detection performance. In addition, when the model is trained using stochastic gradient descent (SGD), it may converge to a local optimum, which limits its detection performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a method based on YOLOv7-tiny that integrates feature retaining blocks (FRBs) and densely-scale spatial attention (DSSA) blocks into the backbone network and incorporates a cosine annealing (CA) learning rate schedule during training. The proposed method, termed Cosine Annealing Learning Rate Scheduled YOLOv7 with Densely-Scale Spatial Attention and Feature Retaining Block (CA-YOLOv7-DF), is applied to surface defect detection. Experiments were conducted on the public NEU-DET dataset, and the components were analyzed through gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), confusion matrices, and training convergence analysis. Under a unified training protocol with three random seeds, CA-YOLOv7-DF achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 71.9 ± 1.2%, compared with 70.9 ± 1.0% for YOLOv7-tiny; the FRBs provided the largest average gain, whereas the effects of the DSSA blocks and the CA schedule were within the run-to-run variation. Moreover, the proposed method achieves a detection speed of 11.6 frames per second (FPS) on the Jetson Nano embedded device, which makes it applicable to low- to moderate-speed or sampling inspection. On the GC10-DET dataset, the method did not improve on YOLOv7-tiny, indicating that its benefit depends on defect scale and the amount of training data.

Article.Title: Asymmetric visible-infrared cross-fusion for robust bolt localization and missing detection
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Chen X.; Xie K.; Sang J.; Wen C.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Accurate and reliable detection of missing bolts remains challenging under exposure anomalies, low illumination, and cluttered backgrounds. Visible images are sensitive to illumination changes and may lose texture and detail, whereas infrared images are more illumination-robust but lack the detail and resolution required for accurate standalone detection. Existing general multimodal fusion models are primarily designed for universal detection scenarios, which fail to adapt to the unique feature distribution characteristics of bolt targets with weak textures and easily degraded deep features. Such methods cannot effectively extract critical fine-grained target features, leading to prominent performance limitations in industrial bolt detection tasks. To address these complementary limitations of dual-modal data and the drawbacks of existing fusion methods, we propose Dual-modal Asymmetric Cross-Fusion YOLO (DACF-YOLO), a lightweight network for bolt localization and missing detection. Modality-specific asymmetric branches and bidirectional shallow high-frequency feature injection exploit cross-modal complementarity and compensate for information loss. A Shallow Feature Screening and Enhancement module suppresses redundant texture noise and background interference, improving early feature quality. A Cross-Modal Guided Fusion mechanism dynamically assigns weights according to modality-specific feature quality, enabling adaptive complementary enhancement. A parameter-shared Lightweight Detail-Enhanced Detection Head preserves critical bolt textures and contours while reducing model complexity. Experiments on a registered visible-infrared bolt dataset show that DACF-YOLO achieves 95.3% mAP50 and 63.2% mAP50-95 with 3.28 M parameters and 9.7 GFLOPs, demonstrating a favorable balance between detection accuracy and computational cost under challenging industrial conditions.

Article.Title: Prediction of the maximum available traction boundary for HST-based agricultural tractors
Article.Authors: Ahn H.; An S.; Choi C.; Kim S.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: The traction force of an agricultural tractor with a hydrostatic transmission (HST) is governed jointly by the engine, the hydrostatic unit (HSU) and the gearbox; when these are not matched, part of the engine power cannot be converted into traction within the working speed range. This study proposes a method for determining the boundary of the traction available from an HST-based tractor at the component-matching stage. The boundary was constructed from four limits: the engine power and torque-rise characteristics, the maximum allowable pressure of the HSU with its experimentally measured efficiency map, the gearbox ratios, and tire slip. The workable area was derived for three gear ranges of a 43.3 kW tractor, selected so that the governing limit differed between cases, and verified by measuring the traction force during plowing with a six-component load cell. Where each limit governed, the measured traction force reached 86–96% of the predicted boundary on average and exceeded it only transiently, whereas the predicted vehicle speed deviated by up to 22.7% at high HSU pressure owing to a pressure-dependent loss of volumetric efficiency that a single coefficient corrected. The method allows the engine, HSU and gearbox to be matched to a target traction force.

Article.Title: Horizon-dependent level–shape decomposition for multihorizon ERA5-Land temperature-field forecasting in the Lanzhou–Xining region
Article.Authors: Wang X.; He A.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Monthly regional temperature fields combine a stable seasonal–spatial background with forecast-origin-dependent regional displacement and within-domain reorganization. We developed RegimeTransfer-DCSF (Deep–Causal Shape Fusion), which separates a forecast-causal regional level from median-centred spatial shape and transfers shape responsibility from a learned fine–coarse branch to a stable anchor as lead increases. Using 12-month histories of 12 ERA5-Land variables, the model forecast ERA5-Land 2-m air-temperature fields at one-, three-, and six-month leads (h1, h3, and h6, respectively) over 39 counties in the Lanzhou–Xining region. Across two rolling-origin selection-and-evaluation folds, 114 horizon-specific cases yielded 114,114 county-domain grid-cell predictions. The selected DCSF fit achieved a pooled MAE of 1.131 °C, RMSE of 1.494 °C, and R² of 0.977, with 83.677% of errors within 2 °C. Across 114 county-area-weighted cases, MAE was 9.952% lower than seasonal climatology and 20.345% lower than TimeFilter. During 25 h1 thermal-state changes, DCSF reduced area-weighted MAE by 0.301 °C (19.795%) relative to TimeFilter, with a fold-stratified three-month moving-block bootstrap interval of 0.073–0.526 °C. A separate retrospective ERA5-Land analysis found that annual mean warm-area fraction increased by 9.29% points per decade during 2000–2024 (three-year block interval, 2.72–15.52). In the Lanzhou–Xining ERA5-Land experiment, explicit separation of domain-level temperature displacement from median-centred spatial shape, followed by horizon-dependent responsibility allocation, yielded lower rolling-validation MAE and clearer short-horizon transition gains than the evaluated comparators.

Article.Title: Novel formula for improving the oral bioavailability of paclitaxel using P-glycoprotein inhibitors
Article.Authors: Gupta A.; Kunkalienkar S.; Saha M.; Rajora A.; Soman S.; Marwaha D.; Moorkoth S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Paclitaxel (PCL), a taxane derivative with potent antimitotic properties, is ubiquitously utilized as a remedy for various cancers. PCL’s therapeutic utility via the oral route is limited by poor water solubility and low permeability, resulting in inadequate bioavailability. This limitation restricts the development of effective oral formulations, particularly for conditions such as gastric cancer. The current research aimed to evaluate the effects of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors, specifically piperine (PIP) and silibinin (SBN), on the pharmacokinetic parameters of orally administered PCL. An in-silico drug-protein docking study was performed to evaluate interactions between PCL and selected P-gp inhibitors. PCL was administered orally at a dose of 40 mg/kg, either as a single treatment or in combination with PIP or SBN at 10, 20, and 40 mg/kg. Plasma samples were obtained at predetermined sampling intervals, followed by Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis using an H-ESI source. Compared with PCL administered alone, combination treatment significantly enhanced key pharmacokinetic indices, including peak plasma concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration–time curve (AUC). After administration of PCL with 10 mg/kg of PIP 1.67 and 1.09 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, 20 mg/kg of PIP 1.79 and 1.16 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, and 40 mg/kg of PIP 2.04 and 1.51 fold increases in Cmax and AUC. After administration of PCL with 10 mg/kg of SBN 1.36 and 1.03 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, 20 mg/kg of SBN 1.73 and 1.69 fold increases in Cmax and AUC, and 40 mg/kg of SBN 2.29 and 2.22 fold increases in Cmax and AUC. Additionally, the elimination half-life (t1/2) of PCL was extended, indicating prolonged persistence of the drug in circulation. It can thus be concluded that PCL, along with PIP or SBN, exhibits increased absorption through P-gp modulation. These findings emphasise the promising potential of incorporating such bioenhancers into the development of effective oral PCL formulations to improve cancer therapy. An AGREE score (0.69) indicates the eco-friendliness of the bioanalytical method.

Article.Title: Exploring the sustainable scaling of AI dilemma: a projective study of corporations’ AI environmental impacts
Article.Authors: Desroches C.; Chauvin M.; Ladan L.; Vateau C.; Gosset S.; Cordier P.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), raises environmental concerns extending beyond greenhouse gas emissions. Limited transparency from major providers hinders companies’ ability to evaluate their AI-related environmental impacts and achieve their net-zero targets. This paper proposes a methodology to estimate the environmental impact of a company’s AI portfolio, delivering actionable insights without requiring deep AI or Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) expertise. Using a modeling approach that incorporates increased AI usage, hardware efficiency, and electricity mix changes aligned with IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) scenarios, we forecast AI impacts through 2030. Under a high adoption scenario, driven by complex generative AI models and frameworks, AI electricity consumption could rise by a factor of 24.4. Mitigating this impact by 2030 demands coordinated efforts across the AI value chain. Isolated measures like hardware or model efficiency alone are insufficient. We call for standardized environmental assessment frameworks, increased transparency, and a “Return on Environment” metric to align AI development with sustainability goals.

Article.Title: Rigosertib promotes expression of the antimicrobial peptide beta-defensin-3 in human cells
Article.Authors: Wozniak W.; Sagnat D.; Dautreppe R.; Bourumeau W.; Khazaal S.; Kurowska A.; Bournet B.; Buscail L.; Buscail E.; Le Cosquer G.; Alric L.; Navarro L.; Vergnolle N.; Sperandio B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial defense in the human gut relies on innate immune recognition of microbes via pattern recognition receptors, triggering antimicrobial peptide (AMP) expression and immune cell recruitment. Among AMPs, beta-defensins are crucial defense effectors, exhibiting broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and immunomodulatory functions. Their inducible expression makes them attractive targets for therapeutic modulation, particularly given the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. Through the evaluation of clinically approved or investigational compounds, we identified the multi-kinase inhibitor Rigosertib as an inducer of the human beta-defensin-3 (HBD3) in colon epithelial cell lines and in organoids. Notably, Rigosertib robustly induced HBD3 even at the lowest concentration tested in vitro, whereas proinflammatory cytokine expression increased only at the highest concentration and to a substantially lesser extent. Mechanistically, Rigosertib-triggered induction of HBD3 expression was found to be primarily dependent on the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and downstream P38 pathway, with ERK1/2 and JNK contributing to a lesser extent. Functionally, Rigosertib enhanced the antimicrobial activity of colon-derived cells and organoids against intestinal bacterial pathogens. Moreover, Rigosertib induced AMP expression in a range of non-intestinal cells from different tissues, including hepatic cells. Collectively, these findings support the potential of Rigosertib to enhance endogenous antimicrobial defense while limiting excessive and potentially detrimental inflammatory responses.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning for postoperative atrial fibrillation after noncardiac surgery
Article.Authors: Zhu S.; Gao Y.; Li L.; Wang P.; Zhang C.; Li Y.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is an important complication after non-cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Accurate perioperative risk stratification remains challenging because POAF risk reflects both baseline atrial substrate and dynamic perioperative physiologic stress. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the INSPIRE perioperative database to develop interpretable prediction models for clinically documented postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after non-cardiac surgery. POAF was defined as new-onset AF captured during the index hospitalization by electrocardiography or rhythm-monitoring documentation; because a uniform cohort-wide measure of monitoring intensity was not available, the endpoint was interpreted as clinically detected POAF. Candidate predictors were grouped by acquisition window into preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative (≤ 24 h) variables to support dynamic perioperative risk assessment rather than a purely preoperative screen. Feature selection was performed with Boruta, model explanation with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and classifier comparison with LASSO logistic regression, AdaBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Because POAF was uncommon, performance was evaluated with AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and F1 score after stratified splitting and threshold evaluation; synthetic resampling was not used in the primary analysis. Among 99,887 patients, 1,058 (1.1%) developed clinically documented POAF. Compared with controls, POAF cases were older (median 70 vs. 55 years) and showed substantially greater burdens of hypotension and hypoxemia, including more frequent and prolonged MAP < 65 mmHg and SpO₂ <90%. Boruta retained average diastolic blood pressure, average heart rate, and left atrial enlargement as informative features. SHAP identified valvular disease, surgical duration, cardiopulmonary instability, and related early postoperative events as major contributors, consistent with a dynamic perioperative risk model. Discrimination was good across classifiers, with AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.85. AdaBoost and CatBoost achieved the best overall performance (both AUC 0.85), while CatBoost showed higher specificity and PPV. In a large non-cardiac surgical cohort, clinically documented POAF was associated with both baseline atrial substrate and perioperative cardiopulmonary stress. Interpretable ML models, particularly boosting-based methods, showed good discrimination and may support dynamic perioperative risk updating and targeted postoperative surveillance, although monitoring heterogeneity, class imbalance, calibration, and external validation remain important considerations.

Article.Title: Proposal for new cut-off points for vital signs used to identify at-risk patients over 65 years old in Emergency Departments
Article.Authors: Pérez-Valencia D.; Barrio I.; del Castillo J.; Fernández-Alonso C.; Miró O.; Larrea N.; Legarreta M.; García-Gutiérrez S.; N/A N/A.; Lamberechts J.; Villalibre A.; Lobé S.; García L.; Blázquez B.; Molina E.; Cuchillo J.; Rebollal M.; del Rio J.; Izquierdo S.; Arrizabalaga O.; Arretxaga Z.; Cantón E.; Bello M.; Perestelo L.; Cabrera C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency Department (ED) overcrowding and non-age-adapted triage criteria increase the risk of delayed recognition of critical conditions in older adults, who face higher morbidity, atypical presentations, and poorer short-term outcomes. We conducted a retrospective multicentre cohort study including 23,278 ED visits (patients ≥ 65 years) from 52 Spanish hospitals, drawn from the EDEN (Emergency Department and Elder Needs) cohort. Thresholds were selected to maximise the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). External validation was performed in an independent cohort. Compared with conventional values, these adapted cut-offs classified as alarm a greater proportion of patients at risk who would not have been classified as high priority according to traditional criteria: 66.1% for RR, 28.2% for SBP, 14.8% for HR, 8.6% for SatO2, and 6.6% for DBP. Findings support the identification of candidate age-adapted thresholds for older ED patients and motivate future predictive models incorporating vital sign interactions to enhance early warning systems in EDs.

Article.Title: Inflammatory biomarker profiles and their associations with Nordic dietary habits and metabolic outcomes in adults affected by MAFLD
Article.Authors: El-Sehrawy A.; Kandil I.; ELmazny G.; Salah A.; Abohassan M.; Alanazi M.; Elzayyadi I.; Ibrahim R.; Gameil M.; Hamed M.; Rozaik S.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is commonly accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation. The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) is an accessible inflammatory marker, while the Healthy Nordic diet may have favorable metabolic effects. This study investigated relationships among AISI, healthy Nordic Food Index (HNDI), and metabolic health in adults with MAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 253 adults with MAFLD were evaluated. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire and HNFI using a composite score. Anthropometric, biochemical, and hematological variables were assessed. Higher AISI was associated with lower apple/pear intake (adjusted P = 0.034) and root vegetable intake (P-trend = 0.029). The HNFI score (β=−0.149, P = 0.020) and root vegetable intake (β=−0.154, P = 0.016) were independently associated with lower AISI. Higher AISI was associated with an unfavorable lipid and inflammatory profile and lower adherence to the HNFI. Greater Nordic diet adherence and root vegetable intake were independently associated with lower AISI. Causal relationships cannot be inferred.

Article.Title: Phytotoxicity and germination responses of Zea mays L. to anaerobically digested liquid biofertilizers derived from cattle manure and fish-processing sludge
Article.Authors: Linares-Nima L.; Huaytalla-Galindo B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Valorization of cattle manure and fish-processing sludge as liquid biofertilizers may contribute to waste valorization and potential agricultural reuse within a circular bioeconomy. This study evaluated four formulations (GC, T1, T2, and T3) produced in three biodigesters per formulation and anaerobically digested for 15 weeks. The three biodigesters within each formulation were pooled before preparation of the 5, 10, and 100% (v/v) bioassay dilution levels. Distilled water was retained as an external reference and excluded from factorial inference. Final formulation-level composite samples showed near-neutral pH and formulation-specific nutrient profiles; the measured nitrogen concentration in the analyzed liquid fraction was higher at the final sampling point in all four composite samples, whereas P, K, organic matter, and C/N ratio showed formulation-specific variations. Most final microbiological determinations were lower than their corresponding initial measurements, although variability remained in some T2 and T3 determinations. In Zea mays L. bioassays, germination percentage and germination rate showed significant formulation × dilution-level interactions ( p = 0.0065 and p = 0.015, respectively). Root length differed significantly by formulation ( p = 0.0145) and dilution level ( p = 0.0013), without a significant interaction. The germination index (GI), used as a phytotoxicity indicator, was evaluated descriptively; T2 maintained GI > 1 and comparatively high root length across all evaluated dilution levels, whereas T1 and T3 showed lower GI and root-length responses at 100%. Overall, responses were formulation- and dilution-level dependent, supporting soil-based validation of selected combinations before field recommendation. Because biodigesters were pooled at the formulation level before downstream analyses, these findings characterize the specific composite samples tested and do not represent independent reactor-level replication.

Article.Title: Combining rather than selecting multi-horizon forecasting of an agricultural commodity price index
Article.Authors: Malla S.
Article.Abstract: Wholesale food prices in emerging economies move sharply, with direct consequences for farm incomes and food security. Individual commodity series are short, gap-ridden and shock-dominated, so this study forecasts a composite instead: the Agricultural Commodity Price Index, an inverse-volatility weighted aggregate of 135 daily wholesale series from Nepal’s Kalimati market, 2013–2023, with 55 strictly causal predictors including Nepali festival windows. Twelve architectures spanning penalised linear models, tree ensembles, recurrent networks and direct neural forecasters are compared under a protocol that fits on 2013–2020, chooses every configuration on 2021 to mid-2022 by blocked cross-validation, and reads July 2022 to September 2023 only for reporting. A shrunk combination improves on the model that validation would have selected by 1.3, 1.5, 2.0 and 11.2 %, and on a no-change benchmark by 2.1, 3.2, 7.8 and 22.2 %. The models that proved best on the test window ranked third, seventh, fifth and fourth on validation, so none could have been chosen in advance. A supporting result explains why these models work at all: the recursive, level-target strategy common in this literature caps tree ensembles at their training range and compounds recurrent error, and a direct change target reduces error by 33-53 %.

Article.Title: Dingxiang Guanshitong suppresses ESCC progression by modulating TAK1/NF-κB/GLUT1-associated glycolytic reprogramming
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Wang S.; Li J.; Sun X.; Chen X.; Zheng Y.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive tumor with poor clinical outcomes and limited treatment options. Dingxiang Guanshitong (DGST), a traditional Chinese herbal formulation, has shown potential activity in ESCC, but its molecular mechanisms require further clarification. The current study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic impact and underlying biological actions of DGST on ESCC. Network pharmacology was used to identify candidate DGST constituents and targets, followed by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. Antitumor effects of DGST was examined in a 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (4NQO)-induced ESCC mouse model using H&E staining, immunohistochemistry, TUNEL assay, and flow cytometry. Proteomics analysis identified differentially expressed proteins and enriched pathways. In TE-1 cells, TAK1 knockdown/overexpression stable lines were constructed by lentiviral transduction, and pathway involvement was evaluated using immunofluorescence, luciferase reporter assays, CCK-8, Transwell, scratch assays, qRT-PCR, western blotting, and metabolic indicator assays. DGST showed dose-associated suppression of ESCC tumor progression, cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while promoting apoptosis. Proteomics suggested that DGST affected glycolysis and NF-κB-related pathways. DGST treatment was associated with reduced phosphorylation of TAK1, IκBα, and p65, lower GLUT1, HK2, PFKP, and LDHA expression, decreased ATP levels, and increased MPC1 as well as mitochondrial complex indicators. TAK1 knockdown enhanced the effects of DGST, whereas its overexpression reversed these effects. DGST may inhibit ESCC progression by modulating TAK1/NF-κB/GLUT1 axis-mediated glycolytic reprogramming. The findings elucidate the potential therapeutic value of DGST in the treatment of ESCC and provide mechanistic insights for its clinical application.

Article.Title: Inverse-distance weighting alignment-diversity attention transformer for days ahead particulate matter concentration forecasting
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Loskot P.; Lin Y.; Gao Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate forecasting of particulate matter (PM) concentrations including PM \(_{2.5}\) and PM \(_{10}\) is vital for the public health as well as the environmental management. Forecasting highly non-stationary PM data remains challenging due to their complex spatial dependencies, irregular local correlations as well as periodic variations. It is also useful to constrain the predictions by the actual Air Quality Index (AQI) while maintaining the model interpretability. In this paper, an adaptive Inverse-Distance Weighting (IDW) framework referred to as the IDW-ADAFormer is devised for the medium-term forecasting of multi-sensor PM data. Its two main components are iTransformer and a newly designed Alignment-Diversity Attention (ADA) module. In particular, the adaptive IDW first separates the spatial trends from local temporal variations. The separated components are processed by a kernel-based ADA module in order to extract and align the spatial patterns. The signal components and the raw inputs are then adaptively fused using learnable weights. The model training minimizes a multi-objective AQI-aware loss function, which jointly improves the prediction accuracy and the output AQI-level classification. Numerical experiments were performed for a public dataset of hourly PM \(_{2.5}\) and PM \(_{10}\) data. Assuming one- to three-days-ahead forecasting, the proposed IDW-ADAFormer is found to consistently outperform and is more interpretable than other existing methods.

Article.Title: Multi-window HRV and temporal context for sleep staging from ECG and smartwatch PPG-derived intervals
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Peng Y.; Li J.; Zhang Z.; Cao C.; Chai Y.; Cai Z.; Zou Y.; Yan Z.; Tao Z.
Article.Abstract: Sleep staging is essential for evaluating sleep quality, yet conventional polysomnography is costly, intrusive, and difficult to deploy in everyday settings. This study presents an HRV-centered sleep-staging framework for ECG-derived RR intervals and smartwatch PPG-derived IBI sequences. Rather than introducing a new Transformer architecture, the study systematically evaluates multi-window HRV representation and sleep-progress context for four-class sleep staging, while examining demographic information and feature-interaction strategies as auxiliary components. The framework extracts time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features from multiple temporal windows, combines them primarily with sleep-progress context while optionally incorporating demographic context, and uses a lightweight Transformer encoder as a temporal integration module for classifying Wake, Light sleep, Deep sleep, and REM sleep. In the final baseline comparison, the proposed configuration achieved accuracies and Cohen’s Kappa coefficients of 0.6988/0.5326 on the SHHS 1000 subset, 0.6958/0.4830 on Huami ECG, and 0.6915/0.4615 in the Huami smartwatch PPG setting. Ablation analyses showed that multi-window HRV representation and temporal sleep-progress information provided the most consistent contributions, whereas demographic variables and feature-interaction strategies had auxiliary and dataset-dependent effects. For practical interpretation, configurations without the future-context 300-s feature are considered the relevant setting because they exclude explicitly post-epoch information, whereas configurations containing this feature are treated only as offline retrospective analyses. Further validation across independent datasets, wearable devices, prospective deployment settings, and external PPG interval-estimation pipelines is needed before broader real-world use.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal variation of gravity field and inter-seismic correlation analysis of the 2021 Maduo and 2022 Menyuan earthquakes
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Zhu Y.; Zhao Y.; Wei S.; Lv H.; Cao C.
Article.Abstract: The spatiotemporal evolution of the gravity field is a comprehensive response to deep crustal material migration and tectonic deformation processes, and contains key precursory information for the seismogenic stage of earthquakes. Based on mobile gravity observation data collected in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2015 to 2021, this study obtained multi-spatiotemporal-scale gravity field changes before and after the earthquakes through classical adjustment. In light of the regional tectonic framework and deep dynamic background, we systematically analyzed, from a gravity perspective, the relationship between the spatiotemporal dynamic gravity changes and the preparation and occurrence of the 2021 Maduo M S 7.4 earthquake and the 2022 Menyuan M S 6.9 earthquake, and explored the possible association between the two earthquakes. The main findings are as follows: (1) The significant gravity changes observed before the 2021 Maduo M S 7.4 earthquake and the 2022 Menyuan M S 6.9 earthquake are closely related to regional tectonic activity, and these changes may have mainly originated from deep crustal material adjustment and migration processes. (2) The pattern of gravity changes in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau has a clear spatial correspondence with the locations of strong earthquakes. Both the Maduo and Menyuan earthquakes occurred near the turning points of gravity high-gradient zones and around the centers of the four-quadrant pattern. (3) The gravity changes in the Menyuan seismic region were significantly enhanced following the Maduo earthquake, We inferred that the Maduo earthquake may have caused some perturbation to the tectonic stress state in the Menyuan region, indirectly influencing the occurrence of the subsequent Menyuan earthquake. (4) The gravity change maps show that the gravity anomaly areas and gravity gradient zones before the Maduo and Menyuan earthquakes are highly correlated, possibly implying a close relationship between the two events in terms of deep-seated tectonic processes.

Article.Title: Application of the rigid finite element method to modeling multibody systems with redundant constraints
Article.Authors: Tański M.; Wojtyra M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The research aimed to investigate the applicability of the Rigid Finite Element Method (Rigid-FEM), which is an alternative to the classical Finite Element Method, for modeling multibody systems with redundant constraints. The investigation focused on resolving problems with determining reaction forces. Such problems are encountered in classical rigid multibody dynamics formulations. The methods used include the development of an underlying theory, diverse simulations, and experimental verification. Specifically, the theoretical foundation of the Rigid-FEM method—discretizing rigid bodies into smaller rigid finite elements interconnected by spring-damper elements (SDEs) with appropriately defined stiffness and damping properties—was supplemented by proposed methodological modifications that significantly reduce the number of required SDEs and improve computational efficiency. To perform a variety of tests, a spatial parallelogram benchmark mechanism was used. Results from both Rigid-FEM and classic FEM models were analyzed. A comprehensive parametric study was conducted to assess the influence of selected modeling parameters on accuracy and computational efficiency, including the placement of elastic elements, discretization density, and the introduction of a shear coefficient. Ultimately, the simulation results were compared with experimental data obtained from measurements conducted on a hardware mechanism. The findings demonstrate that the modified Rigid-FEM achieves accuracy comparable to the regular FEM model, yet requires significantly fewer elements and delivers results in substantially reduced computational time. Although the Rigid-FEM is limited to plate- and beam-like structures, these components constitute the primary structural elements of many mechanisms, such as parallel robots, where constraint redundancy is frequent and renders classical rigid multibody dynamics formulations incapable of determining reaction forces. The results, validated against experimental data, confirm the suitability of Rigid-FEM as a highly efficient and accurate computational tool for analyzing overconstrained multibody systems.

Article.Title: Sustainable bioactive membranes based on κ-carrageenan and açaí seed extract for potential topical application
Article.Authors: dos Santos É.; de Souza Pagani L.; Dotoli G.; de Andrade G.; da Silva Pinhal M.; Cogo-Müller K.; Rosa P.; Paiva-Santos A.; Fardim P.; Mazzola P.
Article.Abstract: Açaí ( Euterpe oleracea Mart.), an Amazonian fruit widely exported worldwide, generates seeds corresponding to approximately 85% of the fruit weight, which are commonly discarded despite their valorization potential. In this study, κ-carrageenan bioactive membranes containing açaí seed extract were developed and characterized as candidate materials for topical applications. The açaí seed extract showed antioxidant capacity in chemical assays, with a DPPH radical-scavenging activity of 95.75 ± 0.75% at 10 mg/mL and an EC₅₀ of 7.78 ± 0.41 mg/mL, while ferric reducing capacity was 0.19 ± 0.02 mg GAE/g (EC₅₀ = 1.49 ± 0.01 mg/mL). The açaí seed extract showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 3.13 mg/mL. HPLC analysis confirmed the presence of catechin (0.03 mg/mL) and epicatechin (0.01 mg/mL). Membranes were prepared and mechanical analysis showed tensile strength of 3.63 ± 0.34 MPa and elongation at break of 35.97 ± 2.19%. Adhesion force was 26.35 ± 5.53 g and the membranes remained structurally intact for up to 7 days under the evaluated PBS conditions. FTIR analysis showed preservation of the characteristic functional groups of κ-carrageenan after extract incorporation, while SEM revealed increased structural heterogeneity in the açaí membrane. Cytotoxicity assays demonstrated that the extract and membranes were non-cytotoxic at most tested concentrations. The membranes exhibited water vapor permeability of 1.05 ± 0.75 g·mm/kPa·day·m² and swelling capacity of 0.42 ± 0.08 g/g. Overall, the developed membrane showed promising potential as a sustainable platform for topical applications, although further biological studies are required to establish its antimicrobial performance and wound-healing potential.

Article.Title: Little effect of further aging on soil-weathered plastics
Article.Authors: Forsyth H.; Gnoffo C.; Stoll R.; van der Zee M.; Frache A.; Bigalke M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plastic waste accumulates in soils, impacting structure, biota, and ecosystem functioning. Understanding the persistence and aging of plastics in soil is therefore important. However, aging occurs over timescales which cannot be covered in conventional experiments. Many studies therefore focus on simulated weathering of pristine polymers over short timescales, but these experiments do not consider potentially different aging behaviour after extended environmental exposure. To address this, we investigated the continued aging of naturally weathered macroplastics sampled from agricultural soils by reburying them under field conditions for 19 months and comparing properties before and after. Samples of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, and polyethylene terepthalate were analysed for chemical structure, surface oxidation (carbonyl index), crystallinity, molecular weight, thermal stability, and surface morphology. All samples showed signs of oxidative aging and aging-related surface alterations before and after reburial. After reburial, most samples had little to no change in carbonyl index, with several showing significant decreases, likely due to loss of highly oxidised surface layers through fragmentation. Crystallinity, thermal stability, and molecular weight remained largely unchanged. Overall, our results suggest that the further aging of weathered polymers does not follow the same trajectory as the initial aging and that conventional plastics degrade very slowly in soil.

Article.Title: A self-healing secure group communication framework for resource-constrained IoT devices using decentralised key management and trust-based voting
Article.Authors: Patil P.; Ravi Teja S.; Praveen Kumar Y.; Bulagouda R.; Anitha H.; Nalina V.
Article.Abstract: Group communication in resource-constrained IoT deployments still lacks a dependable answer to insider misbehaviour. Sensor networks that grow to hundreds of heterogeneous nodes cannot always afford the memory and CPU budget that conventional cryptographic machinery demands, and Group OSCORE, while shown to be hardware-feasible, offers little protection once a malicious node has already been admitted to the group: a compromised member can quietly drop everything it is asked to forward and the rest of the network has no built-in way of noticing. We present SecureGroup-IoT , which closes this gap through three components working together: (1) a server-coordinated logical key hierarchy giving \(O(\log N)\) re-keying along with forward and backward secrecy; (2) a BLET-IoT-style trust layer that uses subjective logic to turn raw forwarding observations into calibrated, uncertainty-aware opinions about each node; and (3) a multi-watchdog consensus mechanism that automatically evicts a misbehaving node and triggers the corresponding key rotation. We built and ran the protocol in Contiki-NG 4.0 on emulated Zolertia Zoul hardware inside Cooja. Against an active blackhole attacker, the framework pulled packet delivery ratio back up from 43.7% to 93.4%, with a median isolation time of 22.4 seconds, while adding only 6.4% energy overhead. Total memory footprint came to 17.9 kB, leaving 45% headroom on Class 1 hardware.

Article.Title: Cross-site pooling with feature harmonization for small-for-gestational-age (SGA) prediction across heterogeneous feature spaces
Article.Authors: Lim J.; Nirmalan P.; Choorakuttil R.; A/P Naresh Sethi N.; Kamar A.; Saaid R.; Jalil N.; Ng K.; Saw S.
Article.Abstract: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) neonates face health risks when undetected, yet machine learning (ML) models are difficult to apply across sites with heterogeneous feature availability. We developed a cross-site pooling framework, incorporating feature-specific imputation and leakage-safe five-fold partitioning, for SGA prediction using Malaysian ( n = 18,582) and Indian ( n = 1,760) antenatal data. The framework is evaluated on a held-out partition of 853 complete records including 184 SGA events. Three training strategies were evaluated: (i) country-specific training using common features (baseline), (ii) pooled training with feature harmonization, and (iii) cross-country transfer using common features. In the Malaysia test set ( n = 807, 169 SGA), the AUROCs were 0.825, 0.823, and 0.606, whereas in India test set ( n = 46, 15 SGA), they were 0.553, 0.673, and 0.695. The feature-harmonized approach showed results similar to the country-specific baseline in Malaysia (0.823 vs. 0.825) and numerically higher than the India-only baseline in India (0.673 vs. 0.553) with wide overlapping CIs on 46 scans (15 SGA). In a training size-matched analysis, pooling Malaysian data raised India AUROC from 0.573 to 0.653 (95% CI 0.604–0.706) while adding the harmonized feature gave 0.655 (95% CI 0.608–0.706), no measurable difference. Compared to clinical diagnosis using EFW<10th centile, the model achieved slightly lower AUROC (Malaysia: 0.823 vs. 0.838; India: 0.673 vs. 0.695). We showed that cross-site pooling was feasible despite heterogeneous feature availability. Feature harmonization enabled integration of datasets with differing feature spaces rather than providing discriminative gain. Independent validation on unseen sites, clinically justified operating thresholds, and prospective evaluation are required before clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis exacerbates radiation brain injury after FLASH whole-brain irradiation: insights from the microbiota-gut-brain axis
Article.Authors: Yuan Y.; Wang N.; Li L.; Li C.; Dong J.; Cheng J.; Guo Y.; Dang X.; Ning K.
Article.Abstract: The microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA)plays a critical role in neurological injury and repair, but its involvement in FLASH radiotherapy, a modality that minimizes radiotoxicity to normal tissues, remains unexplored. We found that FLASH irradiation alone injured the brain (neuronal necrosis, elevated TNF-α and IL-1β, oxidative stress) and disturbed the gut (colon shortening, colonic inflammation); however, the microbiota was remodeled, with increased diversity and expansion of Akkermansia and Muribaculum , and the serum metabolome was barely affected. In contrast, Antibiotics alone collapsed microbial diversity and reduced differential serum metabolites, yet the brain remained normal by all pathological, cytokine, oxidative and metabolic measures. When dysbiosis preceded FLASH irradiation, however, radiation brain injury was amplified and sustained: neuronal necrosis and edema extended into day 9, ZO-1 remained reduced, cerebral IL-1β and colonic TNF-α remained elevated, and early oxidative stress was aggravated. The serum metabolome was remodeled, with microbiota-driven bile-acid and kynurenine changes. Taken together, these findings indicate that gut dysbiosis exacerbates radiation brain injury after FLASH irradiation mainly by altering the composition of the blood reaching the brain, making the MGBA a candidate target for improving radiotherapy outcomes.

Article.Title: Biomechanical effects of fixed retainer designs under different labiolingual alveolar bone loss conditions: a finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Tuhan Kutlu E.; Carkaci T.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical effects of three different fixed retainer designs in the mandibular anterior region under different labiolingual alveolar bone loss conditions using finite element analysis. Three alveolar bone models were created for the mandibular anterior region: intact alveolar bone, labial one-third–lingual two-thirds alveolar bone loss, and labial two-thirds–lingual one-third alveolar bone loss. Three different retainer designs were applied to each bone model: a multistranded stainless steel retainer, a rectangular dead-soft stainless steel retainer, and a CAD/CAM NiTi retainer, resulting in a total of nine finite element models. To simulate incisal edge loading, a total vertical force of 285.3 N was applied to the mandibular anterior teeth. Tooth displacement, maximum and minimum principal stresses in the periodontal ligament, von Mises stress in the retainer wires, and maximum principal stress distribution in the adhesive composite were evaluated. As alveolar bone support decreased, tooth displacement and stress concentrations in the periodontal ligament, retainer wire, and adhesive composite increased. The most pronounced biomechanical changes were observed in the labial two-thirds–lingual one-third alveolar bone loss models. Labiolingual displacement was the dominant movement component. Although differences were observed among the retainer designs, alveolar bone morphology had a more pronounced effect than retainer type. In patients with reduced periodontal support, fixed retainer selection should not be based solely on material or design. The degree and labiolingual distribution of alveolar bone loss should also be considered during retention planning.

Article.Title: Northward shifts and range contractions: future distribution of Plicosepalus acaciae in Vachellia woodlands of AlUla, Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alshahrani T.; Kassem H.; Assaeed A.; Patko L.; Abdulkareem A.; Nasser M.; Abd-ElGawad A.
Article.Abstract: Parasitic plants such as Plicosepalus acaciae act as keystone species but can exacerbate host stress under warming and drying conditions. To inform adaptive woodland management, this study models the current and future potential distribution of P. acaciae under climate change scenarios in AlUla, Saudi Arabia. The maximum entropy model was used to analyze a dataset of 124 georeferenced occurrences collected between March 2023 and April 2024. Nineteen bioclimatic variables were used as predictors of habitat suitability. Additionally, these variables, together with topographic factors and host preference, were employed to generate a most limiting factor map using DIVA-GIS. The model performed strongly (AUC = 0.847; TSS = 0.66), identifying annual mean temperature (17–19 °C), precipitation in the wettest month (> 18 mm), and altitude (200–800 m) as key determinants of current habitat suitability. At present, P. acaciae predominates in wadi and mountainous habitats, while sandy areas and high-elevation plateaus remain unsuitable. Future projections under RCP 2.6 and RCP 8.5 scenarios show pronounced range contractions across central and southern AlUla by 2050 and 2070, accompanied by a potential northward shift. These findings underscore P. acaciae ’s vulnerability to increasing aridity and thermal stress, with its survival dependent on microclimatic stability, host availability, and disperser behavior. Results offer valuable insights for developing climate-resilient management strategies aligned with the Royal Commission for AlUla’s ecological restoration goals—such as prioritizing high-suitability subregions, establishing host-specific monitoring programs, integrating avian disperser ecology into management planning, and incorporating trait-based variables and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) into future modeling.

Article.Title: Non-prescription antibiotic dispensing in community drug retail outlets in Central Gondar, Ethiopia: a mixed-methods study
Article.Authors: Mengesha A.; Gebyiaw S.; Tessema T.
Article.Abstract: Antibiotics are prescription-only medicines in Ethiopia, yet community drug retail outlets may provide an important route of access without a valid prescription. Evidence on observed non-prescription antibiotic dispensing in Central Gondar is limited. To quantify non-prescription antibiotic dispensing in community drug retail outlets in Central Gondar, Ethiopia, and explore contextual factors that may help interpret observed dispensing practices. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods study was conducted from March to May 2024. The quantitative component used standardized simulated-client encounters in 120 of 134 eligible community drug retail outlets. Each outlet received one encounter involving one of three standardized clinical scenarios: acute uncomplicated cough/upper respiratory symptoms, non-bloody diarrhea, or mild urinary symptoms. A structured questionnaire assessed pharmacy personnel’s knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions. The qualitative component comprised interviews with 25 participants, including pharmacy professionals, clinicians, and regulatory officials. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression were used to examine factors associated with observed non-prescription antibiotic dispensing. Because only 29 outlets were outcome-negative, Firth penalized logistic regression was additionally used as a sensitivity analysis. Antibiotics were supplied without a valid prescription in 91 of 120 assessed outlet encounters (75.8%). A total of 116 antibiotic items were supplied during these 91 encounters; amoxicillin accounted for 49 (42.2%), ciprofloxacin for 26 (22.4%), and metronidazole for 14 (12.1%). Patient assessment occurred in 24/120 (20.0%) encounters, while counseling was provided in 11/91 (12.1%) encounters in which antibiotics were supplied. In conventional multivariable logistic regression, non-prescription dispensing was associated with unlicensed outlet status (AOR 3.45, 95% CI 1.64–7.29), peri-urban location (AOR 2.21, 95% CI 1.04–4.71), and absence of a licensed pharmacist (AOR 2.76, 95% CI 1.32–5.74). Firth penalized logistic regression was used as a sensitivity analysis because of the sparse outcome-negative category. The Firth estimates were similar in magnitude and direction to those from the conventional model: unlicensed outlet status (AOR 3.32, 95% CI 1.55–7.25; p = 0.002), peri-urban location (AOR 2.16, 95% CI 1.00–4.76; p = 0.050), and absence of a licensed pharmacist (AOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.24–5.67; p = 0.012). The fourth covariate showed no evidence of an association (AOR 1.18, 95% CI 0.56–2.49; p = 0.660). Overall, the Firth analysis yielded findings consistent with the conventional regression model, supporting the robustness of the observed associations despite the sparse outcome-negative category. Qualitative findings highlighted perceived regulatory challenges, economic and competitive pressures, and customer expectations for antibiotics. Non-prescription antibiotic dispensing was frequently observed during standardized simulated-client encounters in community drug retail outlets in Central Gondar. The findings identify regulatory oversight, professional staffing, and community expectations as potentially relevant areas for future antimicrobial stewardship research. The study did not evaluate interventions, and the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal.

Article.Title: A federated learning-based globally coordinated cyber hygiene framework for individual users
Article.Authors: Gupta A.; Singh J.; Gupta S.; Gupta S.; Magotra B.; Ali F.; Kwak D.
Article.Abstract: Cyber hygiene refers to the policies and practices governing the access, retrieval, and consumption of data and information by individual users, small and medium businesses, and large corporations. However, users, both individual and corporate, have been guilty of not practicing basic cyber hygiene, resulting in inadvertent financial losses, data theft, and security breaches. Thus, cyber hygiene enforcement is non-trivial, as poor cyber hygiene can potentially compromise even sophisticated security frameworks and tools. For a large number of individual users, the challenge is severely exacerbated, as they remain outside the scope of sophisticated security frameworks, making them susceptible to incidents of ransomware and other cyber attacks. Existing research has not adequately addressed the security concerns for individual users, focusing on simple tools, awareness, and advisories to address the security challenges. This research paper proposes a comprehensive cyber hygiene framework, focusing on real-time advisory for better cyber hygiene, combined with a globally coordinated federated learning framework for real-time threat detection and response formulation. The framework ensures that individual users stay protected from new emerging threats on a continuous basis. Experimental results establish the efficacy of the proposed framework.

Article.Title: MSCs-derived exosomes attenuate cadmium-induced hepatotoxicity by suppressing mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis
Article.Authors: Zhu X.; Zhang H.; Yang P.; Tian M.; Xin M.; Wang R.; Wang T.; Han X.; Wang B.; Yan J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a ubiquitous environmental toxicant that poses a persistent threat to the liver. Although Cd exposure has been closely linked to various liver diseases, effective and safe therapeutic interventions remain lacking. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSCs-Exos) against Cd-induced hepatotoxicity. Mechanistically, we​ identified​ that Cd triggers mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis, characterized by mitochondrial fragmentation, loss of membrane potential, and depletion of key antioxidant defenses. MSCs-Exos effectively reverse these alterations by restoring mitochondrial integrity, reducing reactive oxygen species and iron accumulation, and rebalancing the expression of ferroptosis regulators and mitochondrial integrity-associated factors. In vivo, systemically administered MSCs-Exos home to the injured liver, alleviate Cd-induced elevations in liver enzymes, and attenuate hepatic inflammation, necrosis, and ultrastructural mitochondrial damage. Together, these results indicate that MSCs-Exos protect against Cd-induced liver injury by suppressing mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis, highlighting their therapeutic potential for Cd-associated hepatotoxicity.

Article.Title: Silibinin enhances the antitumor effect of radiotherapy in melanoma cells and potentiates immunogenic cell death-associated markers
Article.Authors: Moridikia A.; Jafari S.; Pourfarshid A.; Montazersaheb S.; Molavi O.
Article.Abstract: Melanoma is an aggressive skin malignancy with limited response to radiotherapy (RT). This study investigated whether silibinin enhances RT-induced cytotoxicity and immunogenic cell death (ICD) in melanoma cells. Apoptosis was quantified by flow cytometry, and caspase-dependent apoptosis was further investigated by measuring cleaved caspase-3 levels using ELISA with or without Z-VAD-FMK. ICD induction was evaluated by calreticulin (CRT) surface exposure and extracellular release of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) and heat shock protein 70 (HSP70). Combination of silibinin with RT exhibited moderate synergistic anticancer effects in A375 and B16-F10 cell lines, as indicated by CI values < 1. Combination treatment significantly decreased cell viability and increased apoptosis compared with monotherapies. Increased cleaved caspase-3 levels were attenuated by Z-VAD-FMK, confirming caspase-dependent apoptosis. ICD markers, including CRT exposure HMGB1/ HSP70 release, were elevated in both cell lines and further enhanced by combination therapy. Silibinin promotes RT-induced apoptosis and ICD-associated markers. These finding support further investigation of silibinin as a potential adjunct to RT in melanoma cell lines.

Article.Title: Mathematical spectrophotometric determination of ibuprofen and paracetamol in the presence of 4-aminophenol: AI-assisted comparative assessment
Article.Authors: Gomaa Y.; Lotfy H.; Badawey A.; Nessim C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simple mathematical filtration-based spectrophotometric methods were developed for the selective and accurate simultaneous determination of ibuprofen (IBU), paracetamol (PAR), along with the toxic impurity 4-aminophenol (4-AP) without prior separation. The procedures were implemented using built-in spectrophotometer software through a stepwise approach involving the removal of 4-AP by the ratio subtraction technique, followed by spectral processing of the resolved binary mixture of IBU and PAR. Three spectrophotometric strategies, namely ratio subtraction–constant multiplication (RS-CM), ratio difference (RD), and derivative ratio (DD¹), were established and validated for the quantitative determination of IBU and PAR. The concentration of 4-AP was also quantitatively determined and validated using the concentration-value method (conc. value), with wavelength selection optimized through Artificial Intelligence (AI). The proposed methods exhibited excellent linearity over concentration ranges of 4.0–40.0 µg/mL for IBU, 1.6–16.0 µg/mL for PAR and 1.0–10.0 µg/mL for 4-AP were successfully applied to laboratory prepared mixtures and pharmaceutical formulations. Statistical comparison with reference methods using Student’s t - and F -tests confirmed the accuracy and precision of the proposed procedures. The principal novelty of the study lies in the integrated comparative assessment of the three analytical strategies using the newly introduced Method Performance Score (MPS) and Method Performance Ranking (MPR) systems, which provide quantitative benchmarking of analytical performance. This framework was further complemented by an Environmental, Performance, and Practicality Index (EPPI) and an extended Sustainability of Analytical Methods Index (SAMI) mapped across all 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), enabling a multidimensional assessment of analytical performance, practicality, environmental impact, and sustainability. The proposed integrated framework provides a comprehensive basis for selecting an appropriate analytical strategy for routine pharmaceutical quality control.

Article.Title: Puerarin alleviates cerebral ischemic injury by modulating PINK1-mediated mitophagy and NLRP3/GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis: an integrated in silico and in vitro study
Article.Authors: Wu Q.; Dong P.; Zhao X.; Lu W.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: CIRI is characterized by severe oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, fundamentally driven by the pathological interplay between defective mitophagy and robust pyroptosis. While the natural isoflavonoid puerarin exhibits neuroprotective potential, its precise atomistic interactions with targeted biological macromolecules remain elusive. In this study, we employed an integrated computational biophysics and in vitro approach to explore the multiscale mechanisms by which puerarin modulates PINK1-mediated mitophagy and NLRP3/GSDMD-dependent pyroptosis. ADMET profiling and DFT calculations initially confirmed puerarin’s favorable pharmacokinetics and intrinsic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging capacity (Bond Dissociation Energy = 89.68 kcal/mol). Extensive 100 ns MD simulations and MM/GBSA analyses suggested that puerarin could act as a structural modulator. It was computationally predicted to anchor stably within the functional cavities of the PINK1, NLRP3, and GSDMD monomers and act as a steric hindrance, theoretically attenuating the binding free energies of the native NLRP3-ASC and Caspase-3-GSDMD macromolecular assemblies. These thermodynamic predictions were empirically supported by an in vitro OGD/R model using HT22 cells, with nimodipine included as a reference comparator. At the protein level, puerarin significantly upregulated markers of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy while profoundly suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and subsequent GSDMD cleavage. Furthermore, the application of the autophagy inhibitor 3-MA exacerbated OGD/R-induced pyroptotic marker expression, experimentally validating the intrinsic biological crosstalk between defective mitophagy and pyroptosis. Collectively, our findings propose that puerarin may mitigate CIRI through a dual-pronged mechanism: the computationally predicted thermodynamic destabilization of pyroptotic machineries, coupled with the in vitro modulation of mitophagy-related proteins to potentially clear upstream oxidative triggers.

Article.Title: Distal electrical stimulation produces facial nerve regenerative and anti-synkinetic effects comparable to proximal electrical stimulation
Article.Authors: Nakao K.; Sakuma H.; Yamaga M.; Sugimoto H.; Ikuta H.; Kamikawa Y.; Tanaka K.; Miki N.; Kishi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Several reports indicate that electrical stimulation (ES) promotes peripheral nerve regeneration, primarily when applied proximal to the site of injury. However, when considering its application in facial nerve palsy, which is most commonly of viral origin, the lesion is typically located within the temporal bone, rendering proximal stimulation challenging. Therefore, despite its therapeutic potential, ES has not been successfully translated into clinical treatment for facial nerve palsy. The present study investigated whether distal ES could achieve regenerative and anti-synkinetic effects comparable to those of proximal stimulation using a rat facial nerve crush model. The animals were divided into three groups: no stimulation, proximal ES, and distal ES. Functional recovery was assessed using the eye blink reflex and whisker movement, whereas synkinesis was evaluated using electromyography and retrograde labeling. Both proximal and distal ES significantly promoted functional recovery and reduced synkinesis compared to controls. Importantly, the effects of distal stimulation were comparable to those of proximal stimulation across all assessments. These findings suggest that stimulation applied at a site distal to the injury—which, unlike proximal stimulation, does not require surgical exposure of the lesion itself—can achieve regenerative and anti-synkinetic effects comparable to proximal stimulation. This proof-of-concept evidence, while not a direct demonstration of clinical efficacy, supports further preclinical evaluation of distal ES as a potential therapeutic strategy for facial nerve palsy.

Article.Title: CT radiomics for predicting thoracic vertebral compression fractures after radiotherapy in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a two-center retrospective study
Article.Authors: Pang C.; Wang L.; Tang Y.; Jiang S.; Su K.; Xiang Y.; Han J.; Yang Z.; Du G.; Zhao Y.; Li R.
Article.Abstract: To develop and externally evaluate an exploratory CT radiomics-based model for patient-level risk stratification of thoracic vertebral compression fracture (VCF) after radiotherapy in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). This retrospective two-center study included 551 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent radiotherapy. Patients from institution 1 were randomly assigned to a training cohort ( n = 321) or an internal validation cohort ( n = 138), whereas patients from institution 2 were included in an external validation cohort ( n = 92). Radiomic features and CT attenuation values were averaged across all eligible irradiated thoracic vertebrae on pretreatment CT for each patient. Candidate predictors were identified using univariable Cox regression, followed by Akaike information criterion–based Cox model selection in the training cohort. Six prediction models were developed: vertebral CT attenuation, radiomics, radiotherapy, clinical–radiotherapy, clinical–radiotherapy–CT attenuation, and radiomics-integrated models. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (time-dependent AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. During a median follow-up of 0.92 years (interquartile range, 0.58–1.50 years), 77 of the included patients developed post-radiotherapy thoracic VCFs, including 47, 21, and 9 events in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Age, alcohol consumption, radiotherapy fractions, vertebral CT attenuation, and Radscore were retained in the final radiomics-integrated model. The integrated model demonstrated discrimination for patient-level VCF risk, with C-index values of 0.888, 0.796, and 0.847 and 24-month AUCs of 0.903, 0.716, and 0.863 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Bootstrap validation yielded an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.854. Although the external C-index comparison between Models 6 and 5 was statistically significant ( p = 0.018), the 24-month NRI and IDI were not ( p = 0.186 and p = 0.067, respectively). Calibration and decision-curve findings warrant cautious interpretation given the limited number of external events. CT radiomics showed promising predictive performance for post-radiotherapy VCFs in patients with ESCC and may provide additional information for individualized risk stratification. The radiomics-integrated model may have potential to support the identification of patients at higher VCF risk, although its incremental value and clinical utility require further validation in larger independent cohorts, particularly given the nonsignificant 24-month NRI and IDI results in the external validation cohort.

Article.Title: High-dose vitamin D supplementation alters peripheral blood mononuclear cells transcriptomic in preschoolers with moderate to severe asthma
Article.Authors: Hosseini B.; Mailhot G.; Grenier J.; Tse S.; Longo C.; Morin G.; White J.; Fernandez I.; Ducharme F.
Article.Abstract: Several studies have highlighted the potential role of vitamin D in modulating asthma severity, yet the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of high-dose vitamin D3 supplementation on the transcriptomic-wide changes in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of children with moderate to severe asthma. As part of an ongoing randomized controlled trial of children aged 1–5 years with asthma, we conducted an exploratory genetic study. Participants were allocated to receive either an oral bolus dose of 100,000IU vitamin D3 followed by daily supplementation of 400IU or placebo for 3.5 months. Blood samples were collected at baseline, 10 days, and 3.5 months; PBMCs gene expression profiling was performed using bulk RNA sequencing. The primary outcome was the change in PBMCs gene expression at 10 days. Forty-six children (54% male, median age: 2 years) were enrolled (vitamin D3: 24; placebo: 22). Furthermore, KEGG pathway analysis highlighted enrichment in immune and inflammatory pathways, including cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction, chemokine signaling, and antigen processing and presentation. However, after correcting for multiple testing, none of these changes remained statistically significant. Our findings provide a clear direction for further exploration in large-scale in vivo studies.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning prediction of interlayer bond strength in self-consolidating concrete using multiple bond test methods
Article.Authors: Ahari R.
Article.Abstract: The interlayer bond performance of self-consolidating concrete (SCC) strongly influences the structural integrity of multilayer concrete elements, particularly under delayed casting. Accurate assessment of interlayer bonding is challenging due to time-dependent rheology and stress-dependent failure mechanisms. This study combines experimental and machine learning (ML) approaches to investigate SCC incorporating supplementary cementitious materials (SCM), including Class F fly ash (FAF), ultra-fine Class F fly ash (UFAF), Class C fly ash (FAC), and granulated blast furnace slag (GBFS) at 15–60% replacement. Altogether, 2295 specimens were tested using slant shear strength (SSS), direct shear strength (DSS), and splitting tensile strength (STS) methods under five interlayer intervals and three curing ages. Results showed that longer interlayer intervals reduced bond strength, while extended curing enhanced bonding due to pozzolanic reactions. The SSS test showed limited sensitivity to interface degradation, whereas DSS was highly responsive to delays and SCM type, detecting weak interfaces. STS exhibited intermediate sensitivity, with UFAF providing the greatest tensile bond improvement. Five ML models Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), Multilayer Perceptron, Extreme Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Decision Tree were developed to predict bond behavior, with GBR achieving the highest accuracy (R2 > 0.96). Comparative analyses indicated that dominant predictors varied across tests: curing age governed SSS, interlayer interval influenced DSS, and UFAF content affected STS. SHAP and partial dependence analyses confirmed these trends, emphasizing the stress-dependent nature of interlayer bonding. The proposed experimental-ML framework offers a reliable basis for performance-based SCC mix design and prediction of interlayer bonding in multilayer construction.

Article.Title: A hybrid AI-IoT framework for predictive conservation of tropical heritage façades: empirical validation from a multi-site study in Indonesia
Article.Authors: Gbran H.; Rukayah S.; Suprapti A.; Setyowati E.; Setiawan I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predictive conservation for tropical built heritage is hindered by the persistent separation of continuous environmental sensing from computational deterioration diagnostics. We address this gap through a fourteen-month hybrid AI-IoT deployment across three heritage sites in Semarang, Indonesia (Lawang Sewu, Pasar Johar, and Tawang Railway Station), integrating unsupervised HSV-space hierarchical clustering with Random Forest classification and a derived Humidity Stress Factor (HSF). The framework was evaluated using 48,686 expert-labelled pixels, achieving a macro-F1 of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.85–0.89) and pixel accuracy of 91.2% (95% CI: 89.4%–93.0%), with inclusion of the HSF producing a 9.2-percentage-point increase in macro-F1 ( p < 0.001). Cumulative exposure to RH > 85% showed a strong association with deterioration (Spearman’s ρ = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.71–0.89, p < 0.001), while leave-one-site-out cross-validation yielded F1 scores of 0.79–0.82 (95% CI: 0.76–0.84), providing evidence of spatial transferability within the study region. Retrospective testing detected 79% of impending high-risk events and yielded conditional technical lead-time estimates of 4.8, 9.2, and 16.7 h for the 6-, 12-, and 24-hour horizons, respectively (expected: 3.8, 7.3, and 13.2 h after accounting for missed events). These lead-time estimates are technical and require operational validation before integration into management practice. The study advances prior work through three methodological refinements: direct integration of environmental sensing as a predictive input, prevention of data leakage through training-set-only clustering, and quantitative estimation of early-warning lead times from retrospective analysis. The resulting workflow provides a reproducible basis for risk-prioritised intervention planning. However, generalisation beyond the tropical coastal context requires independent cross-site validation and operational piloting. The findings therefore provide an empirical basis for further development of anticipatory conservation approaches for tropical heritage façades.

Article.Title: Detector-optimized wavelength-hybrid entangled photon source for scalable fiber quantum key distribution
Article.Authors: Dosan V.; Lagarrigue A.; Zannotti A.; Parab T.; Folwill Y.; Steinlechner F.; de Vries O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Practical deployment of entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires photon sources that simultaneously address fiber transmission loss, detector performance, and system cost–constraints that are individually well-understood but collectively unresolved in current source designs. Here we present a detector-optimized, wavelength-hybrid entangled photon source (EPS) that resolves this trilemma by design and show its performance in a QKD system. The source uses type-0 spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a crossed-crystal periodically poled KTiOPO $$_4$$ (ppKTP) configuration pumped at 473 nm, generating polarization-entangled photon pairs at 680 nm and 1550 nm. This highly nondegenerate wavelength combination is engineered to route the 680 nm photon to a high-efficiency, low-cost Si-SPAD detector while transmitting the 1550 nm photon through standard telecom fiber with minimum attenuation. The source achieves a spectral brightness of (1.9 × 10 3 )s −1 mW −1 GHz −1 pairs over a 300 GHz phase-matching bandwidth, with polarization entanglement visibilities of (97.3 ± 1.0)% and (94.9 ± 1.6)% in the H/V and D/A bases, corresponding to a state fidelity of $$\ge $$ (96.1 ± 1.3)%. These results establish the wavelength-hybrid approach as a scalable and cost-effective building block for deployed entanglement-based QKD nodes and future quantum network infrastructure.

Article.Title: Integrated optimization of thermal and mechanical properties of electrical insulation paper based on APTES modification
Article.Authors: Fan X.; Wang J.; Bi H.; Wang H.; Lyu F.
Article.Abstract: Crepe insulation paper serves as the core insulation material for dry-type high-voltage bushings rated 110 kV and above, where integrated optimization of thermal and mechanical properties is critical for high-end product development. The intrinsic performance of flat-sheet insulation paper, as the basis of crepe insulation paper, directly determines the overall properties of the final product. Here, we employ a multiscale approach combining molecular simulations and experimental validation to systematically investigate the effects of APTES modification on the thermal, mechanical, and electrical properties of flat-sheet insulation paper. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that a grafting ratio corresponding to 7% APTES treatment concentration achieves optimal modification, with thermal conductivity of 0.351 W/(m K), glass transition temperature of 455 K, Young’s modulus of 3.91 GPa, dielectric constant of 3.95, and hydrogen bonds increasing to 351 per unit cell. Experimental studies on modified base papers with 0%, 3%, 5%, 7%, and 10% doping confirm that the 7% sample exhibits superior overall performance, including glass transition temperature of 418.98 K, thermal decomposition temperature of 585.95 K, tensile strength of 6.902 N/mm, elongation at break of 1.492%, Young’s modulus of 3.602 GPa, dielectric constant of 4.25, breakdown strength of 42.1 kV/mm, and contact angle reduced to 63.7°. Further fabrication of epoxy resin/7% APTES-modified base paper composites demonstrates enhanced interfacial compatibility, with glass transition temperature of 398 K and breakdown strength of 68.2 kV/mm. These results reveal a coherent mechanism involving hydrogen-bond network reconstruction and enhanced interfacial interactions, which contribute to improved wettability with epoxy resin and strengthened interface bonding, thereby leading to elevated macroscopic properties. For dry-type bushing applications, the ~ 27.7% enhancement in thermal conductivity is particularly advantageous as it facilitates more efficient heat dissipation from winding hot spots, thereby reducing thermal stress and potentially extending service life. This mechanism offers theoretical direction and experimental support for the targeted design and development of high-performance insulation papers.

Article.Title: Identifying Brachyura in tidal flats using UAV imaging and a deep-learning approach: a republic of Korea west coast case study
Article.Authors: Kim D.; Shin D.; Son S.
Article.Abstract: Brachyura taxa serve as key bioindicators of tidal flat ecosystems, yet traditional monitoring methods are labor-intensive, ecologically invasive, and subject to access constraints. Here, we present a non-invasive monitoring approach combining unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a U-Net semantic segmentation model to detect and classify Brachyura species directly on the tidal flat surface. High-resolution images (~ 0.2 cm ground sampling distance) were acquired over the Baramarae tidal flat (Taeanhaean National Park, Republic of Korea), and a dataset of 103,792 images was used to train and evaluate the model for four species: Austruca lactea (nationally endangered), Tubuca arcuata , Macrophthalmus japonicus , and Scopimera globosa , including sex-level discrimination for the first two species. Population estimates were within 18% of manual counts for all taxa. These results demonstrate that UAV-based deep learning can provide rapid, non-contact population assessments of tidal flat Brachyura, with accuracy sufficient for ecological monitoring while minimising habitat disturbance. Future work should focus on expanding training data for underrepresented taxa and integrating multi-temporal imagery to track population dynamics.

Article.Title: MnOx nanoparticles cause broad transcriptomic deregulation in A549 cells, unlike graphene-MnOx composites
Article.Authors: González-Plaza J.; Fernández-Pampín N.; García-Gómez A.; Peña E.; Rumbo C.; Martel-Martín S.; Barros R.; Aparicio S.; Suarez-Diez M.; Tamayo-Ramos J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nanomaterials (NMs) pose significant, yet unknown, occupational health risks owing to their nanoscale size and reactivity, particularly through inhalation. MnOx NPs (GNA35) caused broad and extensive transcriptomic deregulation across multiple pathways, including significant enrichment in processes related to cellular stress, and apoptosis. Conversely, pristine and degraded graphene-MnOx nanocomposites (GNA15 and GNA15d) induced only minimal and limited transcriptional responses, indicating a substantially reduced toxicity profile. This transcriptional evidence demonstrates that the metal immobilization of MnOx NPs on a graphene surface effectively mitigates their intrinsic toxicological activity. Furthermore, the lack of enhanced toxicity upon degradation suggests that the composite maintains its protective capacity. These findings strongly indicate that incorporating metal-based NMs, such as MnOx, into a graphene composite notably enhances their safety profile for occupational handling.

Article.Title: From digital to green: the effect of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity
Article.Authors: Xu B.; Liu M.; Xie H.; Xu K.; Liang L.
Article.Abstract: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly enhances corporate pollution emission intensity. The effect is more significant for enterprises in labor-intensive enterprises, and heavily polluting enterprises. Management efficiency, green technological innovation, and total factor productivity are important mechanisms through which digital transformation improves pollution emission intensity. This study provides empirical evidence and policy references for China to explore new paths for green and transformative development.
