Article.Title: An integrated in silico and in vitro approach to optimize Aspergillus niger xylanase using agricultural wastes for bioethanol production
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; Amin S.; Abou-Taleb K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungi and agricultural waste have drawn more attention as a source of xylanase enzyme synthesis recently. In this study, fungal isolates able to produce xylanase were isolated from the soil sample. Within the 19 isolates, three exhibited the highest activity as determined by the Dinitro Salicylic Acid (DNS) method. These isolates were cultivated using various agricultural wastes as cheap carbon sources (xylan), including corn cob, maize straw, sugar cane bagasse, wheat straw, wheat bran, rice husk, and sawdust. Out of the three isolates, the most effective one (WA7) and three agricultural wastes (rice husk 167 U mL −1 , corn cob 159 U mL −1 , wheat bran 154 U mL −1 ) were chosen based on the highest xylanase activity. Using Design-Expert, the optimization of xylanase production occurred in two phases. The first step was screening the essential fermentation parameters affecting xylanase production using the Plackett–Burman design. For the second step in optimization using a definitive screening design, the most important factors for enzyme synthesis from the fungal isolate were further investigated. The maximum xylanase yield after optimization was 242 U mL −1 . Based on genotypic characterization, the fungal isolate was identified as Aspergillus niger 28S ribosomal rRNA. Xylanase enzyme was used in four different processes to produce ethanol on various substrates. The fourth simultaneous saccharification and fermentation technique, which used rice husk as an environmentally friendly waste, was shown to be the most effective, with ethanol yields reaching 40 g L −1 . Further, A. niger xylanase showed optimal molecular interaction and binding affinity toward xylan: −8.00 kcal/mol. Based on these results, A. niger xylanase showed a promising perspective for xylan hydrolysis to produce ethanol.

Article.Title: Transformer-based endoscopic polyp detection with structural reparameterization and dynamic upsampling
Article.Authors: Ren X.; Tang Y.; He Z.; Lu D.; Xie X.; Wang M.; Li Z.; Liang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate polyp detection is important for colorectal cancer prevention, while practical deployment requires reliable localization, manageable model complexity, and robust detection performance. This paper presents an improved RT-DETR-r18 detector for endoscopic polyp detection. The proposed C2f_RCB backbone construction embeds a UniRepLKNet-derived large-kernel reparameterization transformation within the C2f hierarchy, while the original DySample operator replaces the two nearest-neighbor upsampling layers in the top-down neck. A source-code audit shows that the K = 7 DilatedReparamBlock contains one 7 × 7 depthwise main branch and three auxiliary depthwise branches, namely 5 × 5 with dilation 1, 3 × 3 with dilation 2, and 3 × 3 with dilation 3. During deployment, these spatial branches are merged into an equivalent 7 × 7 depthwise convolution, and compatible normalization/affine terms are further folded into adjacent operators by the UniRepLKNetBlock deployment routine; SE, GELU, GRN normalization/scaling, channel projections, residual operations, and DySample remain explicit in the inference graph. Under the archived evaluation protocol, the complete model achieves 96.8% precision, 93.0% recall, 97.1% mAP@0.5, and 79.5% mAP@0.5:0.95, with 13.90 million parameters and 46.6 GFLOPs. These values were obtained from an expanded-file split later found to contain augmented variants of the same original samples across subsets and should therefore be regarded as preliminary until leakage-free retraining is completed. The current evidence supports a compact, localization-oriented trade-off, but not a standardized runtime advantage, clinical readiness, or leakage-free generalization.

Article.Title: China’s elite championship output during and after the COVID-19 disruption: competition opportunities and Olympic/Paralympic cycle structure, 2013–2025
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Gong S.; Xu Y.; Zhou S.
Article.Abstract: Annual world-champion counts indicate elite sporting output, but they are constrained by the international competition calendar. This study examined China’s non-disabled and para championship output from 2013 to 2025 in relation to competition availability and Olympic/Paralympic cycle structure. Official annual data on world-champion counts and world-record items were combined with an 11-series selected World Championship calendar and official cancellation, postponement, and event-opportunity records. Primary analyses described annual output and ratios relative to group-specific 2013–2019 means. A calendar-sensitivity proxy was calculated for 2021–2025, when selected-core availability was non-zero. Mean pre-pandemic output was 115.43 championships for non-disabled athletes and 231.43 for para athletes. In 2020, output ratios fell to 0.035 and 0.104, while selected-core calendar availability fell to 0. In 2021, availability was 0.636 and the sensitivity proxies were 0.912 and 0.747. Mean output ratios across 2023–2025 were 1.458 and 1.070, respectively; the 2025 ratios were 1.265 and 0.773. World-record items fell from 16 in 2019 to 1 in 2020 and reached 17 in 2025. These findings describe substantial disruption and heterogeneous subsequent output patterns but do not isolate a causal COVID-19 effect or directly measure organizational resilience. Competition opportunity and cycle position should therefore be considered when interpreting national elite-sport output.

Article.Title: Association of the planetary health diet index with overweight and obesity among patients with diabetes mellitus in a cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Moradi Baniasadi M.; Nasli-Esfahani E.; Khakbaz M.; Azadbakht L.
Article.Abstract: The Eat-Lancet diet, which encourages a shift towards plant-based foods and reduced intake of animal products, has been proposed as a solution to improve both human health and environmental sustainability. This study explores the association between Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) adherence and the risk of overweight or obesity in type 2 diabetes (T2D) residing in Tehran, aiming to determine whether this diet can serve as a dual-purpose strategy for managing weight and promoting planetary health. A total of 210 participants were recruited in this cross-sectional study. Dietary information was gathered via a validated 168-item food frequency questionnaire, and PHDI score was derived from 16 food groups. Anthropometric assessments were performed following standard procedures to identify overweight or obesity. Associations between PHDI and outcomes were examined using logistic regression and restricted cubic spline models. Study participants had a mean age of 62.15 ± 8.60 years, and 70% were female. PHDI was categorized into tertiles, with 33.3% of individuals in the highest tertile. In fully adjusted logistic models, high PHDI adherence was associated—though not significantly—with lower odds of overweight/obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.42, 1.95) and obesity (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.37, 2.20) compared to low adherence. Additionally, we did not observe any non-linear association between PHDI and odds of overweight/obesity in T2D patients, after adjustments for potential confounders. Given the absence of a statistically significant link between PHDI and the likelihood of overweight or obesity, which may reflect insufficient statistical power, future studies incorporating larger cohorts and diverse populations are needed to assess the generalizability of these findings.

Article.Title: Effect of Al3+ on low-salinity water flooding in carbonate reservoirs: a comparative study with Ca2+, Mg2+, and SO42−
Article.Authors: Ghalamizade Elyaderani S.; Saeedi Dehaghani A.; Razavinezhad J.
Article.Abstract: In low salinity water flooding (LSWF), oil–brine and rock–brine interactions are strongly influenced by potential determining ions (PDIs), which have been predominantly studied for divalent ions such as Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , and SO 4 2− . However, the performance of trivalent ions remains poorly understood. This study investigates whether Al 3+ is more effective than conventional PDIs under the tested conditions and elucidates the underlying enhanced oil recovery (EOR) mechanisms using carbonate rock samples. Interfacial tension (IFT), contact angle, zeta potential, and calcite-coated micromodel flooding experiments were conducted using individual ions in distilled water and low concentrations in low salinity water (LSW). Al³⁺ exhibited the strongest IFT reduction (Ca 2+ < Mg 2+ < SO 4 2− < Al 3+ ) and altered wettability to strongly water-wet conditions, achieving a minimum contact angle of 18.4°, whereas divalent ions resulted only in neutral wettability. At 100 ppm in LSW, Al 3+ reversed both oil–brine and rock–brine zeta potentials to positive values, while Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , and SO 4 2− remained ineffective. Wettability alteration was primarily driven by calcite dissolution and the high charge density and small ionic radius of Al 3+ . Micromodel flooding confirmed that Al 3+ increased oil recovery from 50.6% to 57.7%. These findings suggest that Al 3+ , at the tested concentration of 100 ppm in LSW, is a promising low-concentration additive for improving LSWF performance in carbonate reservoirs. Future studies can use this research to improve ion-tuned water flooding and develop new models for IFT and wettability alteration, ultimately enhancing oil recovery.

Article.Title: Factors associated with TyG-BMI among pre-frail older adults: a cross-sectional study using multiple linear regression and decision tree analysis
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Pang L.; Chen M.; Liu L.; Qin Y.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: TyG-BMI is a surrogate marker associated with insulin resistance and metabolic status. Characterizing its associated factors among pre-frail older adults may help describe metabolic variation in this population. Using baseline data from the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 2249 adults aged ≥ 60 years classified as pre-frail. We aimed to examine factors associated with TyG-BMI using multiple linear regression and to explore subgroup patterns using classification and regression tree analysis. Univariate analyses and multiple linear regression (MLR) were used to examine associations between participant characteristics and TyG-BMI. CRT analysis was used to identify subgroups defined by combinations of demographic, residential, family, and social characteristics. For an exploratory discrimination analysis, participants were classified into high- and low-TyG-BMI groups according to the sample median, and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate discrimination between these groups. In the MLR model, weight, waist circumference, gender, and C-reactive protein were statistically associated with TyG-BMI. Weight had the largest positive standardized regression coefficient. The decision tree identified seven terminal subgroups, with gender as the root node and residence, number of living children, and social interaction appearing in subsequent splits. The PCOA-6 subgroup had the highest observed mean TyG-BMI (243.77), whereas the PCOA-2 subgroup had the lowest (194.92). The apparent area under the ROC curve was 0.873 (95% CI 0.859~0.888) for MLR and 0.605 (95% CI 0.582~0.629) for the decision tree. These AUC values describe discrimination between groups defined by the sample median and should not be interpreted as evidence of prediction of future clinical outcomes. This cross-sectional study characterizes factors associated with TyG-BMI and exploratory subgroup patterns among pre-frail older adults. Independent validation and longitudinal studies are needed to assess the reproducibility and clinical relevance of these findings.

Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Xu Q.; Shi X.; Sun Y.; Zhang M.; Wang L.; Zheng J.; Ma J.; Gu Q.; Chen S.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and structural and functional brain MRI alterations in Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients with REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD). PD-pRBD patients exhibited elevated plasma NfL and GFAP, which were positively associated with RBDQ-HK scores. They also showed right caudate atrophy, which was negatively correlated with RBD severity and with both plasma biomarkers. Additionally, this group exhibited altered ALFF in the occipital pole, anterior cingulate cortex and brainstem, along with disrupted frontotemporal, visual and auditory network connectivity. In conclusion, greater RBD symptom severity was associated with right caudate atrophy and distributed cortical functional anomalies correlated with plasma NfL and GFAP, offering exploratory clues for PD-RBD neuropathology and candidate biomarkers requiring further validation.

Article.Title: Photolithographic patterning and mechanical characterization of electrodeposited cellulose nanofiber composite microstructures
Article.Authors: Kikuchi K.; Van Toan N.; Kumar R.; Kao Y.; Sakamoto K.; Sakakibara K.; Fukuhara M.; Hashida T.; Ono T.
Article.Abstract: Cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) have attracted considerable attention as sustainable materials for microsystems and microdevices owing to their low density, high mechanical strength, and biodegradability. However, integrating CNFs into such systems requires patterning techniques compatible with photolithography. In this study, we present an electrodeposition-based “electroforming” method for fabricating free-standing CNF microstructures. Mechanically fibrillated CNFs were co-deposited with carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), producing dense composite films. Nanoindentation measurements revealed a Young’s modulus of 4.2 GPa for the CNF/CMC films. Photolithography-enabled patterning produced CNF composite micropatterns and suspended CNF composite bridges with thicknesses as low as 300 nm. Mechanical vibration measurements under vacuum revealed a fundamental resonance at 23.34 kHz with a quality factor of 39. The high resonance frequency is consistent with an effective tensile stress likely introduced by constrained shrinkage during the pre-release hot-plate drying steps. These results demonstrate a scalable microfabrication approach for CNF-based microdevices, paving the way for biodegradable resonators, sensors, and electronic components.

Article.Title: Cumulative and persistent glycemic–renal burden and incident cardiovascular disease in the Health and Retirement Study
Article.Authors: Chen D.; Xie Z.; Hu N.; Yu Y.; Luo S.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Sustained glycemic and renal abnormalities may contribute to cardiovascular disease (CVD), but evidence from repeated joint assessment remains limited. We analyzed 2,867 Health and Retirement Study participants with three measurements of glycated hemoglobin and cystatin C who were free of heart disease and stroke at the third assessment. Standardized glycated hemoglobin and log-transformed cystatin C were averaged to construct a joint glycemic–renal burden score, with high burden defined by the pooled first-assessment median. Incident CVD was analyzed using interval-censored proportional hazards models. During follow-up, 411 incident CVD events occurred. In the prespecified primary Model 3, each 1-standard-deviation increase in time-averaged cumulative burden was associated with higher CVD risk (hazard ratio [HR] 1.14, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02–1.26), as was each additional high-burden assessment (HR 1.18, 95% CI 1.07–1.31). Participants with high burden at all three assessments had higher risk than those with none (HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.17–2.37). Cumulative burden was strongly correlated with third-assessment burden and provided no clear independent information beyond it. Persistent glycemic–renal burden was associated with subsequent CVD, while repeated measurements may primarily characterize longitudinal exposure rather than distinct incremental risk information.

Article.Title: Deep learning-based binary classification and probabilistic calibration of navicular bone pathology in equine radiographs
Article.Authors: Nasiri Dashtaki F.; Javdani M.; Javdani Gandomani T.
Article.Abstract: Radiographic assessment of the equine navicular bone is challenging because pathological changes may be subtle, surrounding anatomical structures can overlap, and image interpretation may vary among observers. This retrospective single-center study developed and evaluated deep learning models for the binary classification of equine navicular bone radiographs as radiographically normal or pathological. The dataset comprised 528 radiographs from 176 horses. ResNet-50 was used as the primary classifier, while Xception and VGG-16 were evaluated as comparator architectures. All data partitions were created at the horse level to prevent subject leakage. The development dataset included 140 horses and was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, while a temporally separated internal hold-out set containing 36 horses and 108 radiographs was reserved for final testing. ResNet-50 achieved a mean AUROC of 0.893, an accuracy of 79.6%, and an F1-score of 85.5% across the cross-validation folds. On the hold-out test set, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.905, an accuracy of 82.4%, a sensitivity of 90.5%, a specificity of 71.1%, and an F1-score of 85.7%. Temperature scaling produced modest improvements in probability calibration, reducing the Brier score from 0.1582 to 0.1533 and the expected calibration error from 0.1639 to 0.1595 without altering discrimination. Qualitative Grad-CAM analysis was additionally used to illustrate image regions associated with model predictions. These findings support the feasibility of deep learning for automated classification of navicular bone radiographic appearances. However, the model does not diagnose clinical navicular syndrome, assess lesion severity, or replace veterinary interpretation. Prospective external validation using multi-center datasets is required before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of pulmonary aspergillosis information generated by large language model-based chatbots
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Li J.; Zhong J.
Article.Abstract: Chatbots powered by large language models are increasingly used for medical information retrieval, yet pulmonary aspergillosis presents complex diagnostic and therapeutic information needs. This comparative cross-sectional study evaluated the information quality, transparency, and readability of responses generated by four chatbot platforms. On 6 August 2026, 31 search terms derived from five-year worldwide Google Trends data were submitted to Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT (GPT-5.5), Perplexity, and Gemini 3.6 Flash, yielding 124 first-response texts. Quality and transparency were assessed using JAMA, GQS, EQIP, and DISCERN, and readability using SMOG, Coleman-Liau, FKGL, GFI, FRES, and ARI. Friedman tests accounting for matched queries showed significant platform differences for all four quality and transparency measures. Median DISCERN scores were 43 for Copilot and Perplexity, 36 for ChatGPT, and 33 for Gemini. None of the 124 default responses met the prespecified sixth-grade threshold for any of the six readability measures. Copilot and Perplexity achieved higher scores on several measures of written-information quality and transparency, while responses from all four platforms remained textually complex. Chatbot-generated information should serve as a supplementary resource following professional verification.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware lung CT slice classification using a lightweight CNN with selective referral
Article.Authors: Khalid A.; Abdel-Moniem S.; Lashin N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lung CT slice classification may support image-level decision assistance, but deterministic neural networks do not explicitly indicate when a prediction is unreliable. This study presents a lightweight uncertainty-aware convolutional neural network (CNN) for three-class classification of benign, malignant, and normal CT slices, integrating Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, validation-selected selective referral, and Grad-CAM visualization. After removing 43 exact duplicate files, 1,054 IQ-OTH/NCCD images were analyzed using an image-level split of 842 training, 106 validation, and 106 test images (seed 42). Because reliable patient identifiers could not be recovered, the study is considered an internal image-level proof-of-concept rather than patient-independent diagnostic validation. With 50-pass MC Dropout, the model correctly classified 105/106 test slices, achieving 99.06% accuracy (exact 95% CI: 94.86–99.98%) and a weighted F1-score of 99.04%. The single misclassified benign slice was predicted as normal and exhibited high predictive uncertainty. Selective referral was based on the scalar uncertainty score $${\text{U}} = {\text{max}}\left( {1 - {\text{Confidence}},\,{\text{H}}_{{{\text{norm}}}} ,\,{\text{MI}}_{{{\text{norm}}}} ,\,{\text{VR}}} \right)$$ , with a threshold selected as the 80th percentile of validation-set U values $$\left( {\tau_{U} = 0.174166} \right)$$ , without using test labels or test performance. This operating point accepted 88/106 slices (83.02% coverage) and referred 18/106 (16.98%), with an observed accepted accuracy of 100% (95% CI: 95.89–100%) and an observed selective risk of 0% (95% CI: 0–4.11%). Calibration analysis yielded a 10-bin equal-width expected calibration error of 0.0295, a multiclass Brier score of 0.0137, and a negative log-likelihood of 0.0385. Deep Ensemble and Ensemble MC Dropout each correctly classified all 106 test slices, although these results remain subject to the same image-level data limitation. Simulated low-contrast and Gaussian-noise perturbations reduced accuracy and increased referral, indicating responsiveness of the uncertainty score to distributional degradation. A separately retrained binary lightweight CNN variant on the Chest CT-Scan Images Dataset correctly classified all 286 Cancer-versus-Normal test slices (100%; 95% CI: 98.72–100%), but its validation-selected referral rule accepted only 134/286 slices (46.85%) and referred all 25 Normal test slices. Therefore, the second-dataset experiment should be interpreted as a dataset-specific image-level benchmark rather than direct external validation of the primary three-class model. These findings support further patient-wise, multi-center evaluation of uncertainty-aware CT-slice classification and selective referral.

Article.Title: AI-integrated multi-omics fusion for precision cardiovascular diagnostics
Article.Authors: Xiao S.; Gao D.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and early diagnostic systems for effective intervention. Traditional prediction approaches relying only on clinical data often fail to capture complex biological interactions underlying disease progression. This study proposes CardioPrecision-BioFusion, an AI-driven framework that combines clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, and simulated proteomic representations. The clinical and omics datasets were obtained from independent cohorts and were not patient matched; consequently, the framework performs cohort-level latent representation integration and does not claim patient-level multi-omics fusion. Modality-specific encoders, target-blind prototype retrieval, multi-head attention, transformer-based learning, an autoencoder, and stacking were used to model heterogeneous feature interactions, while masked attention handled structurally unavailable modalities without imputing unobserved patient-level omics measurements. On the internal held-out constructed fusion test set, the model achieved 97.96% accuracy (95% CI, 97.14–98.55%), 98.05% precision, 98.05% recall, and a 98.05% F1-score. In a source-disjoint, transcriptomics-only external evaluation using 332 samples from GSE141910, the frozen transcriptomics branch achieved 84.64% accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 91.20%. SHAP analysis identified influential clinical and molecular features. These findings support the framework as an exploratory multimodal methodology, but prospective validation in patient-matched multi-omics cohorts is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Adaptive reconstruction mechanism for enterprise collaborative networks based on multi-agent reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Peng J.; Li M.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Enterprise collaborative networks must reorganise as markets shift, partners fail and demand changes. This study develops an adaptive reconstruction mechanism in which each firm acts as an autonomous agent that adds, terminates or reweights collaborative ties within a bounded candidate set. The Multi-Agent Deep Q-Network with Prioritized Experience Replay (MADQN-PER) combines attention-based coordination, a dynamic learning rate and rewards that mix firm-level and network-level objectives. Graph operations have explicit enterprise meanings, authorising parties and cost components; action masks enforce feasibility before selection. Across synthetic networks of 50 to 200 nodes, the reported efficiency gains range from 34.7% to 41.2%, with 78.3% performance retention under 15% random node failures. Attention and the shared reward are associated with the largest component differences in composite score. A calibrated supply-chain simulation reports a 41.7% reduction in delivery time and a 53.2% robustness gain. Quantitative comparisons are restricted to the five baselines with documented configurations. Conservative bounds derived from ten-run summaries distinguish gains in efficiency, robustness and adaptability from the reconstruction-cost trade-off. The evaluation schedule supports finite-budget comparisons but does not establish convergence times.

Article.Title: Social–ecological dual-network patterns and coupling characteristics in Gannan Prefecture from a complex network perspective
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Yang X.; Su J.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Under the tide of globalization, ecological fragmentation and imbalanced urban development have emerged as two major global challenges. In recent years, facing dual pressures of social governance and ecological protection, Gannan Prefecture has encountered separate issues in both social and ecological systems, further impeding their coordinated coupling development. This study proposes an optimization method integrating social-ecological dual networks with coupling coordination to achieve balanced eco-social integrated development. Using ENVI, ArcGIS, UCINET, and MPNET, we established an “ecological network-social network-interlayer network” framework. The ecological network was constructed through three steps: selecting comprehensive source points, building ecological resistance surfaces, and identifying ecological corridors. A township evaluation system covering population-industry-land-transportation was developed, employing an advanced gravity model to build social networks. Both networks were abstracted as undirected, unweighted complex networks for metric measurement. Coupling degree between social and ecological networks was quantified, while interlayer network stability and dual-network dependency were assessed by measuring module proportions in both networks. Key findings include: (1) Western Gannan shows better ecological conditions while eastern areas exhibit superior social development; (2) Ecological networks demonstrate higher stability and balance than social networks, though with lower network efficiency; (3) 91% of townships display coordination imbalance, including 13% with moderate or severe imbalance; 4) Minimal proportions of stable modules A3 and C2 indicate unstable social-ecological dual networks. Analyzing influencing factors of network balance, coordination, stability, and dependency, we propose ecological functional zoning and spatial planning aligned with national territorial spatial planning principles, aiming to support high-quality development and ecological civilization construction. This study not only enriches the theoretical knowledge base of complex network research but also offers new perspectives for research on social and ecological networks. At the same time, it provides planning methodology references for regions with similar ecological environments and social development characteristics, thereby accelerating the construction and development of ecological urbanization nationwide.

Article.Title: Sensitivity to chunk order in a premotor song nucleus of canaries
Article.Authors: Cazala A.; Giret N.; Hinaut X.; Del Negro C.
Article.Abstract: Sequences of distinct, ordered elements can be organized hierarchically across multiple levels. Representing such sequences in the brain may require extracting information about transition probabilities and chunks. How these processes are implemented at the neuronal level and the extent to which they are intermingled remain unclear. To address these questions, we took advantage of the multilevel structure of domesticated canary song, which comprises syllables, phrases, and chunks, as well as the selective auditory responses of neurons in the premotor HVC nucleus to playback of the bird’s own song. Neuronal activity was recorded in response to a selected song bout and to variants of that song bout generated by altering the sequential organization at either the phrase or the chunk level. Reordering chunks could strongly affect responses to one or more phrases. Moreover, the lower the transition probabilities due to chunk rearrangement, the weaker the responses. In contrast, reordering phrases within a given chunk had little impact on responsiveness, despite a dramatic decrease in transition probabilities. The present study also suggests an encoding of chunk sequencing through the integration of information provided at chunk boundaries and over a preceding period of several seconds.

Article.Title: Effective source selection of solar-grid powered electric vehicle charger circuit using machine learning algorithm
Article.Authors: Shanker N.; Sridevi R.; Harika S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for charging systems integrated with renewable energy sources for efficient operation. Solar-grid integrated systems offer a promising solution; however, photovoltaic (PV) fluctuations and varying grid conditions reduce power efficiency and increase battery stress. To address these challenges, a machine learning-based source selection method for a Quasi-Z-Source Network Converter (QZNC) used in EV charging is proposed. Different machine learning algorithms, including Fine Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Weighted KNN, and Random Forest, are implemented and analyzed. Simulations are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink under different load and power conditions to evaluate system performance. Under the considered MATLAB/Simulink simulation scenarios, the Random Forest classifier achieved the best performance with a classification accuracy of 99.67% and an AUC value of 1.0 on the generated test dataset. The proposed system attains a maximum efficiency of nearly 90%, maintains voltage fluctuations below 2.5 V, and reduces charging cost by about 13% compared to conventional methods. In addition, the use of a fast-recovery diode minimizes switching noise and enhances converter performance while supporting bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operation.

Article.Title: Carbon monoxide accumulation and oxygen depletion during butane heater operation in an enclosed tent
Article.Authors: Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) accumulation in a heated tent can expose occupants to different concentrations at different locations. Three full-scale trials used a liquefied-butane heater and tent submitted after a fatal incident. CO and oxygen (O₂) were measured at 0–100 mm and 1400–1500 mm above the floor, with paired observations analyzed every 180 s from 180 to 2340 s. Mean CO rose from 40.33 to 93.33 ppm at 1400–1500 mm and from 8.67 to 101.67 ppm at 0–100 mm. Descriptive fitted slopes were 0.02515 and 0.04473 ppm s⁻¹, respectively. At 1800 s, upper-minus-lower differences were − 2, −2 and + 4 ppm despite a mean of zero; all three differences were negative from 1980 s onward. The time-weighted mean over 180–2340 s nevertheless remained higher at 1400–1500 mm (62.99 versus 51.10 ppm). Mean O₂ declined from 20.03 to 16.80 vol% at 1400–1500 mm and from 20.90 to 17.97 vol% at 0–100 mm. Conditions deteriorated at both monitoring locations, but the CO ordering changed. The reconstruction shows why measurement height and the concentration history should be considered together when interpreting conditions in a tent incident.

Article.Title: Proton pump inhibitor/histamine-2 receptor blocker exposure and ocular toxoplasmosis: a nationwide claims-based study
Article.Authors: Park H.; Ro J.; Jung W.; Kim J.; Lee C.; Park T.; Han J.
Article.Abstract: This nationwide, population-based, retrospective case-control study investigated the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) and histamine-2 receptor blocker (H2B) use and recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis using Korean National Health Insurance Service data (2002–2021). Among 7,411 patients diagnosed with toxoplasmosis, 3,353 had recorded ocular involvement and 4,058 did not; PPI/H2B exposure during the preceding year was compared between groups. In multivariate logistic regression, older age (40–69 years: odds ratio (OR) = 2.74; ≥70 years: OR = 6.17), hypertension (OR = 1.63), hyperlipidemia (OR = 1.18), and PPI/H2B use for ≥ 8 weeks (OR = 1.50) were associated with higher odds of this diagnosis, while female sex was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.36; all P < 0.05). Propensity score–weighted analyses confirmed this duration-dependent pattern, with higher odds at longer PPI/H2B exposure durations, particularly ≥ 8 weeks. Self-controlled case series analysis showed an increased relative risk (RR) of recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis during PPI/H2B exposure (RR = 8.26). These findings suggest a possible association between longer PPI/H2B use and recorded ocular toxoplasmosis diagnosis among patients with toxoplasmosis.

Article.Title: The effects of fabricated polycaprolactone/gelatin nanofiber scaffolds via various organic solvents and Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) on the metabolic activity of fibroblast cell line L929
Article.Authors: Karimi S.; Mirzaei-Parsa M.; Vahidi R.; Sadeghi Dousari A.; Farsinejad A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrospun Polycaprolactone (PCL)/gelatin(Gel) nanofibrous scaffolds can provide a biomimetic fibrous environment for cell–material interactions. This study investigated how acidic and emulsion solvent environments and platelet-rich plasma (PRP) loading affect fiber morphology, physicochemical characteristics, and the metabolic activity of L929 fibroblasts. PCL/Gel nanofibers were fabricated using acidic and emulsion electrospinning formulations, with 0%, 10%, or 20% PRP. A Trifluoroacetic acid(TFA)-based formulation was evaluated during formulation screening. Scaffolds were cross-linked using 25% glutaraldehyde vapor, and L929 fibroblasts were cultured on selected scaffolds. Scanning electron microscope (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), and simultaneous thermal analysis (Thermogravimetric Analysis—Differential Thermal Analysis) (STA/ TGA-DTA) were used for physicochemical characterization, and Methyl Thiazolyl Tetrazolium (MTT) assay was used to evaluate cellular metabolic activity. Statistical comparisons were performed using two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak multiple-comparisons testing. Emulsion electrospinning produced smaller fibers than the acidic formulation. PRP incorporation was associated with a further reduction in mean fiber diameter. The 10% PRP formulation showed a favorable overall cellular metabolic response, although the emulsion scaffold containing 20% PRP showed the highest numerical metabolic activity in a specific comparison. FTIR supported the presence of PRP-associated chemical functionalities, while STA/TGA demonstrated differences in the thermal behavior of PRP after exposure to the acidic and emulsion solvent systems. Within the conditions tested, solvent environment and PRP loading influenced scaffold morphology and L929 cellular metabolic activity. The emulsion formulation with approximately 10% PRP showed a favorable combination of fiber morphology and cellular response. These findings support further investigation of PRP-containing PCL/gelatin electrospun scaffolds, while additional studies are required to establish PRP growth-factor bioactivity, release behavior, residual cross-linker content, and quantitative cell proliferation.

Article.Title: Micro-needle-dispenser-based direct writing of optical microlenses on optical fiber facets for visible-range applications
Article.Authors: Das S.; Karunakaran Nair N.; Waldhauer S.; Spengler F.; Rüßeler A.; Kaierle S.; Kracht D.; Hinkelmann M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a droplet-based micro-dispensing technique for the fabrication of photopolymer microlenses directly on the end facets of optical single-mode fibers. The process is based on a layer-by-layer droplet stacking approach, where each deposited droplet is individually cured with ultraviolet light to achieve precise control over the microlens height, curvature, and geometry. In contrast to traditional fabrication techniques, this method removes the need for lithographic or molding processes and allows rapid and customizable fabrication. Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD)-based optical simulations agree with the experimental results, confirming accurate control over the beam shaping properties of the fabricated lenses. A focal beam radius down to approximately 1.7 μm with a working distance of 38 μm at a wavelength of 635 nm has been achieved. This facilitates potential applications e.g. where coupling from single-mode fibers to photonic chips with smaller mode field diameter (MFD) is required. The developed approach provides a scalable method for directly integrating microlenses into photonic integrated circuits and other optical platforms for sensing, imaging, and biomedical single-fiber probing applications.

Article.Title: Exosomes from adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells ameliorate bladder dysfunction in diabetic rats by attenuating oxidative stress via the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; Zhang D.; Li H.; Chen H.; Jin R.; Zhao Y.; Sun X.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetic bladder dysfunction (DBD) is a common urinary system complication in diabetic patients, with oxidative stress (OS) being a key factor in its onset and progression. Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes (ADSC-exos) hold potential for treating OS-related diseases. In this study, we established high glucose-induced cell models and diabetic rat models to investigate the role and molecular mechanisms of ADSC-exos in mitigating OS in DBD. The results demonstrated that ADSC-exos inhibited intracellular ROS generation, downregulated PTEN expression, activated the PI3K/AKT pathway, promoted GSK-3β degradation, reversed NRF2 suppression, and enhanced the expression of downstream antioxidant proteins. In diabetic rats, ADSC-exos improved bladder function by reducing maximum voiding pressure, prolonging voiding intervals, and decreasing bladder tissue fibrosis and apoptosis. Further analysis revealed that miRNA-21-5p is highly enriched in ADSC-exos. Bioinformatics predictions identify PTEN as a target of miRNA-21-5p. Overexpression of miRNA-21-5p reversed PTEN-mediated suppression of the antioxidant stress system. In summary, ADSC-exos alleviate OS and improve bladder function in diabetic rats via the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/GSK-3β signaling pathway, in which miRNA-21-5p may play a certain role.

Article.Title: Erector spinae muscle fibre size estimation using high-density surface electromyography in people with and without non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Purushotham S.; Casolo A.; Arvanitidis M.; Grison A.; Gardner A.; Falla D.
Article.Abstract: There is limited evidence on whether lumbar erector spinae (ES) fibre morphology is altered in people with low back pain (LBP), due to the inherent challenges with biopsy studies. High-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) provides an opportunity to assess motor unit properties, allowing non-invasive estimation of muscle fibre morphology. This cross-sectional study compares estimates of ES muscle fibre size and activity in people with and without non-specific chronic LBP and examines correlations with clinical features in those with LBP. HDsEMG data was acquired from the ES from people with and without non-specific chronic LBP (28/group) during isometric lumbar extension at maximum and submaximal levels (10%, 30%, 50%, 70%). HDsEMG signals were decomposed to estimate motor unit conduction velocity (MUCV), fibre diameter (FD), and fibre cross-sectional area (CSA). Additionally, global estimates from topographical HDsEMG amplitude maps were assessed including amplitude, entropy and y- and x- barycentre locations. There were no significant differences between the groups for MUCV ( p = 0.1310), FD ( p = 0.1310), or CSA ( p = 0.2875). Differences in the regional activation of ES along the y-axis ( p = 0.009) and entropy ( p = 0.023) were observed between groups. In conclusion, estimated ES fibre morphology did not differ between people with and without chronic LBP. However, an alteration of the spatial distribution of ES activity was observed for those with chronic LBP. These findings suggest that alterations in neuromuscular function may occur in individuals with non-specific chronic LBP in the absence of detectable differences in estimated ES muscle fibre size.

Article.Title: fNIRS and eye tracking reveal observation-practice ratio-dependent neural efficiency in multi-level 24-style tai chi learning
Article.Authors: Guo C.; Hong Y.; Jiang E.; Long Y.; Wei C.; Liu C.; Shi B.
Article.Abstract: Observation and physical practice are the most frequently used methods in learning 24 Style Taichi. The effective ratio of these methods for enhancing skill acquisition remains unclear. This study aimed to identify effective Observation-Practice Ratios for novice college students learning movements of varying difficulty, and to elucidate associated differences in cognitive neural activity and eye movement performance. A two-factor mixed design was employed. The between-subjects factor was Observation-Practice Ratio (1: 3, 1: 1, 3: 1), and the within-subjects factor was Task Difficulty (Easy, Medium, High). During 24-Style Tai Chi learning, hemodynamic signals were recorded via wearable functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and eye movements were tracked using eyeglass-type eye tracking. Data were analyzed using Three-way ANOVA and Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA. The O1P3 and O1P1 groups exhibited lower oxy-Hb concentration compared to O3P1. They also showed reduced fixation, saccade, and blink counts alongside better motor performance. Taken together, the combination of lower neural activity, improved oculomotor control, and comparable motor performance suggests that the O1P3 and O1P1 ratios may promote more efficient neural processing during learning, consistent with the Neural Efficiency Hypothesis. Additionally, oxy-Hb concentration was higher in the parietal area than in the frontal area, with the premotor cortex (PMC) and supplementary motor area (SMA) regions showing particularly strong activation patterns compared to other measured fronto-parietal regions during Tai Chi learning. O1P3 and O1P1 ratios show better learning efficiency for beginners. These ratios achieve comparable performance with reduced neural resource allocation and improved oculomotor control. These findings collectively provide fNIRS and behavioral support for the Neural Efficiency Hypothesis. Additionally, parietal regions, particularly PMC and SMA, show substantial involvement in the motor learning process for 24-style Tai Chi.

Article.Title: Lesion-aware prototype contrastive learning for port-wine stain classification
Article.Authors: Xiang F.; Yu S.; Xu C.; Qu Y.; Zhang X.; Ding Y.; Kang X.
Article.Abstract: Image-based classification of pink-red and purple-red port-wine stain (PWS) subtypes is a fine-grained visual recognition task. However, subtle chromatic differences, blurred lesion boundaries, and heterogeneous acquisition conditions make this task challenging. To address these issues, we developed LAPC, a lesion-aware prototype contrastive framework that combines dual-statistic channel-spatial attention with prototype-discriminative representation learning. The attention branch combines average and maximum feature statistics with learned directional spatial responses through residual channel and spatial recalibration. The contrastive branch mines lesion representations through supervised contrastive learning, class-prototype aggregation, and inter-class margin separation. On an expanded internal cohort of 887 PWS images, five-fold evaluation showed higher mean Accuracy, Recall, AUC, and BACC for LAPC than the compared methods under both backbones; these numerical comparisons do not establish statistical significance. Ablation experiments evaluated the individual and combined effects of lesion-aware attention and prototype contrastive learning across two backbone architectures, with supplementary experiments conducted on PH2 in a separate dermoscopic setting.

Article.Title: Sex differences in inflammation, mitochondrial function and energy sensing during early recovery from COVID 19 in older adults
Article.Authors: Temp J.; Estepa M.; Nnaji M.; Haritonow N.; Marx L.; Vakhrusheva O.; Wu H.; Ladilov Y.; Barcena M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 infections induce mitochondrial dysfunction and exacerbate systemic inflammation. In the present study, sex differences were investigated among post-COVID-19 patients during the early recovery phase, as emerging evidence indicates that sex critically influences post-COVID-19 outcomes, particularly in older adults. Mitochondrial dysfunction, energy stress signaling through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), and inflammatory dysregulation represent pathogenic mechanisms implicated in prolonged recovery. In this study, we analyzed peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and plasma from aged male and female patients during early post-COVID-19 recovery (1–4 weeks after obtaining a negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR test), comparing them to an inflammatory control group. Female post-COVID-19 patients exhibited elevated circulating TNF-α levels and a trend toward increased mRNA levels of proinflammatory interleukins IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs, accompanied by enhanced acetylation and decreased activity of mitochondrial superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2). Both sexes displayed increased phosphorylation of AMPK, suggesting altered energy-sensing pathways. Mitochondrial gene expression was upregulated in female post-COVID-19 patients, potentially indicating compensatory responses to energy deficits. These findings reveal sex-dependent inflammatory and mitochondrial alterations during early recovery, suggesting a mechanistic link to the higher prevalence of long COVID-19 in women. These findings emphasize the need for sex-specific therapeutic approaches targeting mitochondrial and immunometabolic dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients.

Article.Title: Insights into CO₂ adsorption on zeolite ZSM-5: an experimental and advanced modeling approach

Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate CO₂ adsorption on ZSM-5 zeolite. The adsorbent was characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The correlation coefficients (R²) obtained from the isotherm models indicate that the classical Langmuir model provides a good fit to the experimental data across different temperatures. In addition, the physicochemical parameters of the advanced multilayer model were examined in detail. Key isotherm parameters, including the number of CO₂ molecules per site (n), receptor site density (Dm), and energy parameters (ΔE₁ and ΔE₂), were also analyzed. The results suggest that CO₂ adsorption on ZSM-5 is spontaneous, exothermic, and governed by physisorption. Overall, the model outcomes can be applied to the design and optimization of a pilot-scale CO₂ adsorption system.

Article.Title: Threat adaptive trust weighted federated learning for Byzantine resilient cybersecurity across healthcare edge networks
Article.Authors: Dalal S.; Kundu S.; Kaushik J.; Alqaisi O.; Rajkhan N.; Dahiya P.; Nirkhi S.; Rakesh S.
Article.Abstract: The rising adoption of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices, edge computing, and distributed healthcare platforms brings with it a host of cybersecurity threats, whereas the centralized learning approach also brings with it privacy, communication, and single point of failure concerns. This study introduces the threat-adaptive Trust-weighted Federated Optimization (TrustFedHealth) framework for Byzantine-resilient healthcare cybersecurity, which combines the multi-signal client reliability estimation, temporal trust updating, norm clipping, error-feedback Top-k compression, and threat-guided Multi-Krum aggregation, with trust-weighted FedYogi optimization. The experiments were run on 15 k healthcare records with 52 attributes, with 12 k of them used for training and 3 k of them being future-held-out for testing, in 60 edge-node clients. Three tasks were assessed: security-risk classification, health-risk classification and health-risk regression. FedAdam showed the best security classification, with 93.67% accuracy, 0.9028 Macro-F1, 0.8867 MCC and 0.9898 ROC–AUC, while FedYogi attained the best ROC–AUC of 0.9904 and regression performance with 0.0516 MAE, 0.0651 RMSE and an R 2 of 0.6562. Multi-Krum has 0.8892 ROC–AUC and 75.77% security-classification accuracy when the attack rate is less than 20% malicious-client participation. A gender Macro-F1 gap of 0.0089 was achieved in the subgroup analysis and the expected calibration error was reduced from 0.0274 to 0.0185 by temperature scaling. The highest compressed checkpoint's accuracy is 90.46% and the highest Macro-F1 score is 0.8480, with a 22.25% cumulative communication reduction. The results show the promise of TrustFedHealth for secure, calibrated, equitable and communication efficient collaborative intelligence in the healthcare domain.

Article.Title: Reward-related memory benefits cannot be explained by post-encoding stimulus-related thought
Article.Authors: Chaloupka B.; Fain M.; Cowan E.; Tambini A.; Murty V.
Article.Abstract: There is an active debate regarding whether rehearsal drives memory benefits associated with awake post-encoding consolidation. In the current study, we manipulated conditions designed to encourage or discourage rehearsal during post-encoding wakeful rest to characterize downstream effects on associative memory in the context of a reward-motivated memory paradigm. To manipulate rehearsal during the post-encoding period, participants in the rehearsal group were explicitly instructed to rehearse high-reward memoranda for 15 min and then completed an incentivized mini-retrieval test. In contrast, participants in the rest group completed an incentivized mini-retrieval test immediately, eliminating the need for post-encoding rehearsal, then were instructed to rest for 15 min. A surprise memory test occurred approximately 24 h later. We found that reward significantly enhanced item memory, replicating a large body of work. Importantly, we found that neither encouraging post-encoding rehearsal nor self-reported time spent thinking about high-reward stimuli during the post-encoding period were related to reward memory enhancements. These findings suggest that explicitly encouraging rehearsal during post-encoding rest cannot fully explain consolidation-related memory benefits, consistent with the notion that spontaneous processes support reward memory benefits on long-term memory.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-assisted ECG interpretation for identification of occlusive myocardial infarction following cardiac arrest: a multi-reader, multi-case study
Article.Authors: Silwanis C.; Groche M.; Neunteufel A.; Huss M.; Eder J.; Kirchweger B.; Bruckner M.; Lindner G.; Fellner A.; Nahler A.; Rechberger S.; Blessberger H.; Kellermair J.; Maier J.; Steinwender C.; Lambert T.

In this multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study​, 69 real-world post-ROSC ECGs were evaluated by 15 physicians from five groups at two timepoints (T1 [without AI] and T2 [with Queen of Hearts (QoH) neural network support]), yielding 2,070 interpretations. At T1, sensitivity/specificity were 77.97%/84.64% (LR + 5.08, LR − 0.26); at T2, 78.55%/90.43% (LR + 8.21, LR − 0.24). For the primary endpoint, MRMC AUC increased from 0.882 to 0.912 (Δ 0.030, 95% CI 0.008–0.058; p ​=0.018). The error rate fell by 2.32% (95% CI − 0.9 to + 5.6; p ​=0.156); odds of correct identification were numerically higher at T2 (aOR 1.29, 95% CI 0.98–1.69). Of 66 changed decisions, 64 (97%) followed QoH: the error rate fell by 5.03% where QoH was correct and rose by 10.56% where it was not. Sensitivity for non-STEMI high-risk OMI did not improve. Confidence increased, and within-group agreement rose through convergence on the algorithm output. The benefit of AI support is tied to algorithm accuracy.

Article.Title: Temporal trends and disparities in cardiac arrest and co-listed acute myocardial infarction-related mortality in the United States, 1999–2025: Insights from CDC WONDER database
Article.Authors: Arsheen F.; Fatima S.; Shaheer M.; Asif A.; Fatima A.; Fareed M.; Farooq A.; Khalid N.; Naz A.; Safeer H.; Khan S.; Aminpoor H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiac Arrest (CA) and Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) are closely linked cardiovascular conditions and major contributors to global mortality. We evaluated national trends in mortality associated with CA co-listed with AMI among United States (U.S) adults from 1999 to 2025 and assessed demographic and geographic disparities. There were 747,073 reported deaths due to CA and co-listed AMI. The AAMR decreased from 22.06 in 1999 to 7.37 in 2025 (AAPC: −4.28; p ≤ 0.000001). Men had higher mean AAMRs than women (mean AAMR: men 16.38; women: 9.77). Among races, Non-Hispanic (NH) Black individuals had the highest mean AAMR (17.14). Mortality burden was greatest among older adults aged ≥ 65 years (mean AAMR: 51.35). Regionally, the Northeast had the highest mean AAMR (16.29), and rural areas showed slightly higher mortality compared with urban areas (14.29 vs. 13.53). Most deaths (69.22%) occurred in medical facilities. Mortality associated with CA and co-listed AMI has declined substantially in the U.S over the past two decades, with significant disparities. These findings highlight the importance of improved risk stratification and targeted preventive strategies in high-risk populations.

Article.Title: Hexamerin contributes to nutrient-driven metamorphosis in Anopheles stephensi
Article.Authors: Srivastava V.; Rohilla P.; Saini V.; Yadav P.; Singh T.; Sankhala N.; Sharma G.; Tevatiya S.; Tandon G.; Kumari S.; Kaur J.; Dixit R.
Article.Abstract: The mosquito life cycle involves a rapid transition from aquatic larvae to non-feeding pupae, requiring precise synchronization between nutrient allocation and development. While macronutrients are known to drive metamorphosis, the molecular mechanisms that link amino acids to this transition remain poorly understood. This study investigates the impact of branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) supplementation on the growth and metamorphosis of Anopheles stephensi . We found that BCAA supplementation to standard insectary food accelerated larval growth, enabling larvae to reach the pupal stage approximately 1.5 days earlier than unsupplemented controls. Next, we evaluated a possible association between AsHex and the nutrient-sensing TOR pathway. Rapamycin treatment delayed the larval-to-pupal transition, similar to AsHex knockdown, suggesting a possible association between AsHex and TOR-dependent developmental regulation. Collectively, our results indicate that AsHex plays a role in coordinating nutritional status with developmental progression during the larval-to-pupal transition. This discovery provides new insights into mosquito growth regulation and identifies AsHex as a potential physiological target for innovative vector control strategies.

Article.Title: Investigation on mechanical and thermal behavior of geopolymer phase change concrete
Article.Authors: Qin Z.; Liu Z.; Zhang X.; Lin J.; Zhang L.; Liu S.; Yang N.; Tian Y.
Article.Abstract: Phase change concrete (PCC) is gradually gaining traction in engineering applications owing to its superior thermal regulation capabilities. This study investigates the effects of varying paraffin microcapsule (PM) replacement levels on the mechanical and thermal properties of geopolymer-based phase change concrete (GPCC) and ordinary Portland cement-based phase change concrete (CPCC) through macroscopic physical and mechanical testing, complemented by microscopic characterization techniques. The results demonstrate that the compressive strength of both GPCC and CPCC decreases progressively with increasing PM content, accompanied by a continuous rise in porosity. Under identical PM replacement levels and curing ages, GPCC consistently exhibits higher compressive strength than CPCC, despite possessing a relatively looser microstructure. The incorporation of PM enhances the structural integrity and ductility of the failure modes observed in both concrete types. PM addition induces a concurrent increase in porosity and reduction in matrix densification for both GPCC and CPCC. While maintaining a compressive strength threshold of no less than 25 MPa, GPCC-20 achieved a latent heat of phase transition and specific heat capacity that were 2.0 and 1.1 times those of CPCC-10, respectively, with its thermal conductivity being 40.1% lower than that of CPCC-10. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the further research and engineering implementation of phase change concrete.

Article.Authors: Olono A.; Ogunsanya O.; Sijuwola A.; Saibu F.; O’Donnell V.; Lakin S.; Parker E.; Barette R.; Xu L.; Adedokun O.; Fadele J.; Abiola J.; Tchokote E.; Park D.; Mboowa G.; Tomkins-Tinch C.; Faburay B.; Brown C.; Happi C.; Happi A.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever is a viral disease with major socioeconomic consequences in countries including Nigeria, where pig farming sustains many livelihoods. Here, we report the first comprehensive whole-genome sequencing and genomic analysis of ASFV, conducted entirely within Nigeria, using both Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing platforms. Notably, we report novel large deletions in variable regions, which may affect genes linked to virulence and host adaptation. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that the Nigerian ASFV genomes form a divergent clade within genotype II, which also differs considerably from the genome backbone currently used for vaccine design, highlighting the impact of viral divergence on current control measures.

Relative to the matched backbone, FCD/Test improved from 0.57250 to 0.55633 and scaffold similarity from 0.90221 to 0.91031, whereas validity changed from 0.87756 to 0.87488 and novelty from 0.94076 to 0.93936. Article.Authors: Gömöryová E.; Pichler V.; Leuschner C.; Gömöry D.
Article.Abstract: Close-to-nature silvicultural systems are increasingly applied as an alternative to intensive forest management, but their effects on soil microbial communities remain insufficiently understood. We investigated whether shelterwood management affects soil microbial properties in comparison with old-growth beech forests in three national nature reserves in eastern Slovakia: Havešová, Kyjov and Stužica. In each reserve, data on soil properties and microbial activity were collected from a network of sampling points covering both the core of the reserve and the managed stands (146 plots in total). CLPP was used to assess the responses of soil microbiota to environmental conditions and stand management. While microclimate and vegetation were similar in all three reserves, significant variation was observed among the reserves in soil chemistry and the diversity and activity of soil microbiota. In contrast, differences between old-growth forests and managed stands were few and not consistently statistically significant across the three sites. Substrate availability was the most important determinant of microbial activity in the organo-mineral A-horizon, while soil moisture was the sole factor influencing soil microbiota in the litter O-horizon. Our results suggest that when management mimics natural ecosystem processes, as in the shelterwood system applied in the studied forests, the effect on soil microbial processes need not to be negative.

Article.Authors: Miura F.; Shibata Y.; Miura M.; Shibata T.; Suzuki Y.; Ito T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) ligation is required for library preparation from fragmented, chemically modified, and naturally occurring ssDNA. SDL-m5 retained efficient AppDNA ligation while markedly reducing AppDNA-to-pDNA conversion under the tested conditions. Wild-type SDL and SDL-m5 displayed distinct pH optima, and ligation efficiency across these conditions was inversely associated with sequence bias at the ligation junction. In cfDNA, replication-associated ssDNA, and bisulfite-converted DNA library workflows, SDL-m5 frequently yielded more library than wild-type SDL under AppDNA conditions. These results establish SDL-m5 as a practical variant for AppDNA-dependent ssDNA ligation and provide guidance for choosing ligation conditions in ssDNA library construction.

Article.Abstract: Dimensional synthesis of multi-loop mechanisms requires adequate task-envelope coverage and transmission performance while maintaining usable task paths in the active-input domain. A disclosed two-input planar surrogate enables comparison with four multi-objective optimization methods under a common budget of 200 charged candidate-design requests per run. In one representative case, FCD-MOPSO reduced the dimensionless kinematic transmission proxy by 15.60% and increased task coverage by 0.154 percentage points, with 10.50% more raw loop-closure solves. In another case, it was the only method to return an independently qualified design within the budget. A separate paired guidance study confirmed changes in leader selection and evaluated successor positions in same-pool replays. The results illustrate trade-offs among design quality, task recovery and computational cost in connectivity-aware dimensional synthesis.

Article.Title: Generational differences in mediterranean diet adherence: associations with hedonic hunger and the obesogenic environment
Article.Authors: Mengi Çelik Ö.; Güler Ü.; Samanci M.; Özer H.; Acar Taşkaya M.; Akçakaya S.; Akay G.; Sözen R.; Yilmaz B.
Article.Abstract: Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet may show intergenerational differences in its association with hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environment. This study aimed to examine the relationship between adherence to the Mediterranean Diet, hedonic hunger, and perceived obesogenic environment among adults in Türkiye from an intergenerational perspective. This cross-sectional intergenerational study was conducted among 1176 adults (845 women, 331 men) aged 18–58 years living in Ankara, Türkiye. Data were collected via a web-based survey using the snowball sampling method. Sociodemographic characteristics and self-reported anthropometric measurements were recorded. Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet (MEDAS), hedonic hunger (Power of Food Scale), and perceived obesogenic environment (Obesogenic Environment Scale) were assessed. Participants were classified into Generations X, Y, and Z based on age groups. Correlation analyses, group comparisons, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed. Adherence to the Mediterranean Diet differed significantly across generations, with the highest adherence observed in Generation X and the lowest in Generation Z ( p < 0.001). Levels of hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environment were significantly higher in Generation Z ( p < 0.05). MEDAS scores showed significant negative correlations with the total and subdimension scores of both the Power of Food Scale and the Obesogenic Environment Scale across all generations ( p < 0.001). Generation-stratified multiple linear regression analyses showed that age and income level were positively associated with MEDAS scores within each generation, whereas men sex, higher hedonic hunger, and greater perceived obesogenic environment were negatively associated with MEDAS scores ( p < 0.05). This study shows that hedonic hunger and perceived obesogenic environmental factors are inversely associated with adherence to the Mediterranean Diet across all three generations. These findings highlight the potential relevance of considering behavioral and environmental factors in the development of generation-specific public health interventions aimed at promoting diet quality and sustainable healthy eating patterns.

Article.Authors: Gupta K.; Ashma R.; Jonnalagadda M.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains a challenging chronic disease as despite adherence to known therapeutic guidelines nearly half of patients experience persistent moderate to severe disease activity. Pathogenesis is driven by multiple pro-inflammatory signalling pathways that includes Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), NF-κB, Notch and MAPK, thereby driving macrophage polarization toward the pathogenic M1 phenotype. JAKis modulate different cytokine pathways at once causing both benefits and risks, such as improved outcomes in hyperinflammatory conditions and increased susceptibility to certain infections. However standard JAKis’s show adverse side effects motivating the search for safer alternatives. In this study in-silico molecular docking, ligand efficiency and selectivity index (SI) analyses was performed for 10 ligands to identify phytochemicals with high binding affinity to JAK family proteins, to recommend potential safer plant derived alternative inhibitors for RA therapy. Quercetin showed the strongest affinity toward JAK2 (− 9.3 kcal/mol), comparable to the reference drug baricitinib (− 8.2 kcal/mol), and peficitinib against JAK1 and JAK3 (− 9.0 kcal/mol). Similarly, kaempferol and catechin exhibited strong binding to JAK2 (− 8.9 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, respectively) and JAK3 (− 8.5 kcal/mol, − 8.8 kcal/mol, respectively), indicating their potential as pan-JAK inhibitors. SI analysis indicated marginally favourable target-engagement profiles for quercetin (SI = 1.18), naringenin (SI = 1.15), and kaempferol (SI = 1.14) relative to standard JAK inhibitors. In spite of lower SI (1.08), catechin has high absolute binding affinities for all four JAK isoforms, which supports its candidature as pan-JAK modulator. Together, these four phytochemicals warrant further preclinical evaluation as candidate modulators of the JAK/STAT pathway in RA, potentially expanding the therapeutic options available for managing this disease.

Article.Authors: Ukubuiwe C.; Abalaka M.; Ukubuiwe A.; Ossamulu I.; Adabara N.; Olayemi I.

These results demonstrate enzyme modulation by these metabolites and indicate that K. pneumoniae (PX652414) metabolites may serve as promising agents for integrated vector management.

Article.Title: Improved genetic algorithm based intelligent scheduling model and efficient solution method for green financial resources
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Tang X.
Article.Abstract: Green financial resource scheduling must reconcile heterogeneous project requirements, time-varying capital availability and tail risk exposure within a single allocation decision. Manual review and static rule-based procedures coordinate these dimensions poorly once the number of candidate projects and financial instruments grows. This research formulates the problem as a constrained multi-objective programme in which a continuous decision vector specifies the fraction of each project’s financing demand routed through each eligible instrument, and twelve instrument-by-quarter capital ceilings together with priority-dependent minimum funding requirements define the feasible set. Economic cost, environmental benefit and conditional value at risk at the 95 per cent level are optimised jointly. An improved multi-population genetic algorithm, denoted IMaPGA, integrates subpopulation co-evolution, elite migration, state-dependent crossover and mutation, crowding preservation, reference-direction selection and feasible neighbourhood refinement. Comparative experiments against NSGA-II, MOPSO, SPEA2 and NSGA-III at scales from 50 to 400 projects use an identical budget of one hundred thousand objective-function evaluations with three repetitions per instance and scale, while MOEA/D and an epsilon-constraint sweep are evaluated in a separate comparison under a reduced verification budget. IMaPGA attains the highest hypervolume and the lowest inverted generational distance throughout the tested scales, and paired significance testing identifies the comparisons in which that advantage is statistically reliable. The framework converts green financial scheduling into a quantitative multi-objective decision process.

Article.Title: Explainable vision Mamba–Kolmogorov–Arnold learning for multi-temporal monitoring of vegetation stress and land degradation in drylands
Article.Authors: Almalki S.; Alshari E.; Almuntashiri A.; Alghamdi T.; Senan E.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Monitoring vegetation stress and land degradation in dryland environments is challenging because short-term spectral variability can obscure persistent ecological change. Complex deep-learning architectures also do not necessarily provide higher predictive performance or independently validated explanations. The study developed and evaluated an explainable Vision Mamba (VMamba)–Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) framework for multi-temporal vegetation monitoring in Badr Al-Janub, Saudi Arabia, using Landsat observations from 2015 to 2025. Multi-temporal vegetation and moisture indices were integrated with terrain variables, while a geographic partition defined training, validation, and locked independent-test subsets. On the locked independent-test set, VMamba–KAN achieved an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 78.76%, frequency-weighted Intersection over Union (FWIoU) of 71.28%, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 20.06%, and Macro-F1 of 25.11%. The CNN baseline achieved higher OA, FWIoU, mIoU, and Macro-F1 values than VMamba–KAN. Cohen's Kappa was 0.424 for VMamba–KAN and 0.404 for the CNN baseline. The Kappa difference is reported separately and is not interpreted as evidence of overall or class-balanced predictive superiority. Temporal analysis identified broad improvement in vegetation condition toward 2023 followed by partial deterioration in 2025 rather than continuous landscape-scale degradation. Integrated Gradients provided descriptive attribution patterns associated with VMamba–KAN predictions. Full-scene softmax probabilities provided descriptive predictive-confidence information and were not interpreted as calibrated uncertainty estimates. The results emphasize temporal persistence, geographic evaluation, class imbalance, predictive performance, and cautious interpretation of attribution evidence.

Article.Title: Ultrasound-responsive erythrocyte-fused vesicles for targeted theranostics of Wilms’ tumor
Article.Authors: Meng K.; Gao Y.; Zhao Z.; Liu W.; Zheng Y.; Ma Q.; Zhang Y.; Wang Y.; Sun X.; Liu Y.; Zhao W.; Wang B.
Article.Abstract: Wilms’ tumor (WT) is the most common renal tumor of childhood. Despite clinical chemotherapy and radiotherapy showed favorable treatment-response, serious side effects caused by the absence of efficient targeted therapeutic fumulations remain a major challenge in clinical practice. Here, we identified neural cell adhesion molecule 1 (NCAM1) as a potential delivery target by bioinformatic analysis and selected an NCAM1-targeting peptide (NTP) as its specific ligand. Then, we prepared NTP-modified vesicles loaded with doxorubicin (DOX) and perfluorohexane (PFH) (NDP), which were fused with red blood cell (RBC) membranes to obtain NDP@RBC, where “@RBC” denotes fusion with RBC membranes. After administration, the RBC membrane prolonged the circulation time of NDP@RBC, with 10.95% of baseline fluorescence retained at 48 h, compared with undetectable levels for free DOX and NDP. The NTP significantly facilitated WT cell recognition and cellular uptake, with the mean fluorescence intensity at 2 h reaching 0.95 × 10 5 compared with 0.62 × 10 5 or the non-targeted DP@RBC group. PFH encapsulated in the vesicles enhanced the ultrasound (US) imaging signal and mediated ultrasound-responsive drug release, with cumulative DOX release reaching 85% under ultrasound versus 13.3% without ultrasound at 60 min. In vivo animal experiments showed that NDP@RBC + US suppressed tumor growth, with a tumor growth inhibition rate of 80.22% compared with the PBS group and 19.27% compared with NDP@RBC alone. In summary, this work highlights the importance of targeted theranostics of WT.

Article.Title: Technical validation of a regional landslide forecasting system in the Eastern Himalayas
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Mishra A.; Singh G.; Karmakar R.; Ghosh S.; Bahuguna H.
Article.Abstract: Rainfall-induced landslides pose a recurrent threat in the Darjeeling–Kalimpong Himalaya, India. The Geological Survey of India developed a prototype Regional Landslide Forecasting System (RLFS) that issued daily experimental forecast bulletins during the 2020–2023 monsoon seasons. Here we present the first systematic evaluation of an Indian regional landslide early warning system using the EDuMaP framework. Performance was assessed over 2,316 block-days spanning 373 monsoon days across 11 administrative units. Of 521 landslides analysed, 96.50% of block-days recorded no or only minor activity. Aggregated validation yielded 361 correct predictions, 1,862 true negatives, 19 missed alerts, and 74 false alerts. Green and yellow grades together represented 95.60% of forecast–observation pairs, with a mean combined efficiency index of 0.86 across the nine non-overlapping forecast zones. The system’s error structure was dominated by overwarning rather than catastrophic missed events. A stakeholder-driven transition to finer administrative forecast zones improved skill scores. Because the forecasts combined an automated rainfall-threshold model with expert review, the reported skill reflects this hybrid system, not the model alone.

Article.Title: Early longitudinal lactate-to-albumin ratio and mortality in critically ill adults: a temporally aligned multicohort study
Article.Authors: Chen D.; Su M.; Wang Z.; Xie Z.; Ye T.; Fan S.; Wu Y.; Luo S.
Article.Abstract: The prognostic value of longitudinal lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) patterns in critically ill adults remains uncertain. In this retrospective multicohort study, we evaluated early LAR dynamics in MIMIC-IV and independently assessed them in eICU using temporally aligned exposure and landmark definitions. In MIMIC-IV, LAR was assessed during 0–<96 h, with mortality follow-up beginning at 96 h. Among 1,456 landmark-eligible patients, higher mean LAR was associated with 30-day and 365-day mortality (adjusted risk ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.11–1.34] and 1.09 [1.02–1.17], respectively), but associations were similar for mean lactate. A descriptive three-class trajectory model identified stable-low, moderate-declining, and high-increasing patterns; neither non-reference trajectory was associated with increased mortality after adjustment. Trajectory structure changed under alternative temporal definitions. In eICU ( n = 1,181), independently estimated trajectories differed, although a stable-high class was associated with higher hospital and ICU mortality. Secondary prediction analyses showed only modest incremental performance for mean LAR and little contribution from trajectory class alone. In this selected population with sufficient serial measurements, longitudinal LAR provides prognostic information but does not establish superiority over lactate, a universal high-risk trajectory phenotype, or clinical utility.

Article.Title: Insulation failure and partial discharge mechanisms of BOPP films under complex electrical stresses
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Zhu M.; Zhu Q.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Parallel capacitors across the interrupter contacts of circuit breakers in ultra-high voltage (UHV) converter stations are continuously subjected to complex electrical stresses from the superposition of harmonics and power-frequency voltage, alongside high operating temperatures, making their insulation failure a critical constraint on the safe and stable operation of power grids. Existing research mostly focuses on insulation properties under low-frequency harmonics or room temperature, with insufficient systematic studies on the coupled effect of temperature and high-frequency harmonics. Taking biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) films, the core insulating material of such capacitors, as the research object, this study established an electro-thermal test platform to conduct breakdown and partial discharge (PD) experiments under power-frequency, characteristic-harmonic-superimposed, high-frequency harmonic and multi-temperature coupling conditions, and analyzed the influences of harmonic frequency, harmonic ratio and ambient temperature on insulation failure. Results show that harmonics significantly degrade BOPP film insulation performance, with high-frequency harmonics causing more severe deterioration than characteristic harmonics. Rising temperature synchronously reduces both breakdown field strength and PD inception field strength, and PD phase distributions differ notably across voltage waveforms. These conclusions provide a solid theoretical reference for insulation condition assessment and fault prevention and control of converter station parallel capacitors.
