Article.Title: Mortality and survival rates following lower limb amputation: a national observational cohort study in Sweden
Article.Authors: Jansson S.; Johannesson A.; Carlberg M.; Hiyoshi A.; Jarl G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare the association between initial lower limb amputation (LLA) and mortality risk compared with matched controls, and to determine whether this association varies by amputation level and by region of residence by comparing individuals with and without LLA within each region. We also assessed temporal trends in 1-year post-amputation mortality. This matched cohort study used population-based national registers in Sweden to identify initial LLAs performed from 2008 to 2017. Individual with LLA was matched by age-, sex-, and county with up to 10 individuals without an LLA. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). A total of 16,757 people with LLA and 165,555 without LLA were included, of whom 76.1% and 37.6%, respectively, died during follow-up (until December 31, 2018). LLA was associated with a 4.48-fold higher mortality risk (95% CI 4.39–4.57), after adjusting for age, sex, marital status, education, and birth in Sweden (yes/no). HRs for specific amputation levels were 5.19 (5.05–5.33) for high proximal, 4.05 (3.94–4.16) for low proximal, and 3.93 (3.69–4.19) for partial foot amputations. LLA was associated with higher mortality compared with individuals without LLA within each of Sweden’s 21 regions, HRs ranged from 3.67 (CI 3.26–4.12) in Kalmar to 5.16 (CI 4.56–5.83) in Södermanland. The association varied significantly by regions (global test of interaction, p < 0.001). One-year mortality remained largely stable during the study period, although a small declining trend was observed following high proximal amputation (mortality rate ratio 0.986, 95% CI 0.972–0.999). Lower limb amputation was strongly associated with increased mortality compared with matched individuals without LLA, with poorer survival following more proximal amputation. The association was observed across all Swedish regions, although its magnitude varied significantly between regions. One-year mortality remained largely stable between 2008 and 2017, with a small declining trend following high proximal amputation. Exploratory analyses identified chronic kidney disease and heart failure among the comorbidities associated with increased mortality. These findings highlight the substantial mortality and systemic disease burden among individuals undergoing LLA.

Article.Title: Soil erosion response to future climate variability and best management practices in the Kesinga catchment, India
Article.Authors: Vani P.; Ravali C.; Pandit V.; Mahapatra S.; Chatterjee S.; Noorzai A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil erosion poses a growing threat to watershed sustainability under changing climatic conditions, particularly in monsoon-dominated regions. This study integrates the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) with bias-corrected CORDEX–South Asia climate projections to quantify present and future sediment yield and to evaluate the effectiveness of structural best management practices (BMPs) in the Kesinga catchment, eastern India. The watershed was delineated into 33 sub-catchments, and model calibration and validation (2003–2020) demonstrated very good performance for streamflow during calibration (NSE = 0.86) and good performance during validation (NSE = 0.72). Sediment-yield performance was satisfactory during calibration (NSE = 0.52) but unsatisfactory during validation (NSE = 0.49), according to the performance criteria adopted in this study. Future projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios indicate increases in streamflow (26–73%) and sediment yield (5–36%), with the greatest amplification under end-century RCP8.5 conditions; these sediment projections should be interpreted in light of the unsatisfactory validation performance. Spatial analysis revealed persistent sediment hotspots in central and eastern sub-catchments, where high slope gradients and projected precipitation intensification interact to enhance erosion risk. Across the future periods and scenarios, 40.2–51.2% of the catchment area was projected to fall within the severe-to-extreme erosion categories, with the highest proportion occurring under end-century RCP8.5. Structural BMPs, including grassed waterways (GWW) and vegetative filter strips (VFS), were implemented in priority sub-catchments. Under historical conditions, VFS and GWW reduced soil loss by 13% and 25%, respectively, while their combined application achieved up to 38% reduction. Although absolute sediment loads increased under future climates, combined BMP implementation consistently mitigated erosion by 27–36%, demonstrating potential for reducing sediment losses under intensified rainfall regimes. By explicitly linking projected climatic changes with sediment response and BMP performance at the sub-catchment scale, this study provides a spatially targeted framework for climate-resilient watershed management in monsoon-driven agro-ecosystems. The results highlight the need for proactive and spatially targeted implementation of integrated soil and water conservation measures in erosion-prone sub-catchments.

Article.Title: Multi-task learning for multi-goal path planning with path-cost estimation and heuristic-guided RRT sampling
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Lin W.; Zhai J.; Chen R.; Sun J.
Article.Abstract: Multi-goal path planning (MGPP) requires identifying a closed, collision-free trajectory that visits a set of goals in an optimal sequence. This is typically formulated as a Physical Traveling Salesman Problem, where the quality of the visiting order depends on an undirected complete graph with precise edge weights representing inter-vertex path lengths. However, calculating these weights efficiently in obstacle-rich environments remains a challenge, often leading to a trade-off between sequencing optimality and computational overhead. To address this, we propose a multi-task learning model termed Prior Information Extraction (PIE). The PIE model concurrently estimates inter-vertex path lengths for graph construction and generates “promising regions” and “search guidelines” to serve as low-level heuristics. These outputs are integrated into a sampling-based framework, PIE-MGPP, which bridges high-level sequencing with low-level motion planning. Specifically, PIE-MGPP utilizes the model-generated weights to determine a prioritized visiting order, while the predicted regions and guidelines focus the RRT-based search toward high-probability configuration spaces. Extensive numerical experiments based on training-source and unseen maps demonstrate that PIE-MGPP achieved high planning success rates and shorter paths among successful cases, while using fewer samples than evaluated baselines.

Article.Title: Research on the dimension reduction of the partial discharge feature space for oil-paper insulated power transformer
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang P.; Chu Z.; Gao C.; Fan X.; Du Z.; Zhang Y.; Peng G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Oil-paper insulation condition directly affects transformer reliability. This study evaluates how dimensionality-reduction performance varies with feature type and diagnostic task using laboratory-simulated gas-gap, column-to-plate, pin-to-plate, and inter-turn partial discharges. Statistical (67-dimensional), waveform (13-dimensional), dissolved-gas-analysis (17-dimensional), and combined (97-dimensional) feature spaces were reduced using KPCA, CCMDR, and RST. RST produced the greatest separability improvement for statistical, waveform, and combined features, whereas CCMDR performed best for DGA. With BPNN, combined features with CCMDR achieved the highest defect-type accuracy (93.02%), and combined features with RST achieved the highest severity accuracy (91.86%). Matched RBF-SVM and Random Forest experiments preserved the ordering of all 16 feature-space/reduction configurations (Spearman rho = 1.000 for both tasks). In sequential type-severity recognition, combined CCMDR-RST achieved the highest joint accuracy (90.70%), while waveform RST-RST had a lower normalized batch-processing time (0.228 versus 0.923 s per test sample); both were Pareto-efficient. The results provide feature- and task-specific selection guidance among the evaluated methods. Because the evidence is limited to laboratory single-source defects, field validation is required before deployment.

Article.Title: Development of fertilizer spreading mechanism for UAV-based fertilizer applicator
Article.Authors: Soni S.; Singh S.; Sahni R.; Kumar S.; Agrawal K.; Babu V.
Article.Abstract: Efficient fertilizer application is vital for crop productivity, but conventional broadcasting is labor-intensive, time-consuming and often leads to uneven distribution, whereas UAVs offer a precise alternative. This study developed and evaluated a UAV-mounted spreading disc mechanism for urea application to improve distribution uniformity and optimize operational parameters. The system comprises a rectangular hopper (39° slope), a flow control unit, and interchangeable discs with 2–6 vanes. Laboratory trials followed a factorial design with flight height (1–3 m) and vane number (2–6), assessing fertilizer deposition using tray collectors and evaluating uniformity via coefficient of variation (CV). Deposition patterns were consistently right-skewed. Increasing vane number improved uniformity, reducing CV from 55.80% (2 vanes) to 38.21% (6 vanes). Higher flight height and lateral distance decreased uniformity, with CV increasing from 36.04% at 1 m to 56.03% at 3 m, and from 21.08% at 2 m to 70.83% at 20 m. Optimal performance occurred at 2 m flight height with 6 vanes, achieving a CV of 30.37% at 4 m lateral distance. The study demonstrates that UAV-mounted spreading disc mechanisms can effectively complement conventional ground equipment by enhancing efficiency and precision in fertilizer management.

Article.Title: YOLO vs. diffusion networks for underground pipe detection: a case study using ground penetrating radar data
Article.Authors: Senousy D.; Saad O.; Ebrahim S.; Abbas A.; Gody A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The accurate detection and mapping of underground pipelines are critical for urban planning and infrastructure resilience. This process is critical to prevent catastrophic failures, minimize service disruptions, and maintain the structural integrity of public works projects. Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a prominent technology for the automated detection and precise localization of subsurface utilities. However, the current dependence on manual data interpretation is a major bottleneck, often resulting in high temporal and operational costs. Consequently, this research addresses these limitations by presenting a performance analysis of two distinct deep learning architectures–YOLO (You Only Look Once) and Diffusion-based neural networks–for automated underground pipe detection. Utilizing a specific dataset of GPR scans, the models were evaluated using a robust five-fold cross-validation framework to assess mean Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (mAP50) and inference latency. The experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-based architectures provide a superior balance between detection precision and real-time processing efficiency. While five-fold cross-validation established a mean mAP50 of approximately 80% for the YOLO models, the YOLOv12n architecture exhibited superior performance on the independent test set, achieving an mAP50 of 94%. In contrast, DiffusionDet models were characterized by lower precision and significantly higher latency. While this study focuses on a single-site case study, the findings establish a foundational baseline for the selection of deep learning architectures and provide a framework for future research into the adaptation of these models across varying geological conditions.

Article.Title: Cumulative exposure to TyG-BRI and risk of incident cardiovascular disease across CKM syndrome stages 0–3: evidence from the CHARLS Prospective Cohort
Article.Authors: Chen L.; Chen Q.; Fang H.; Zheng H.
Article.Abstract: Despite advances in cardiovascular risk stratification, tools that adequately capture cumulative cardiometabolic burden remain limited, particularly in non-Western populations. The association between cumulative triglyceride–glucose index and body roundness index (cumTyG-BRI) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) across the spectrum of Cardiovascular–Kidney–Metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains to be elucidated. We conducted a prospective cohort analysis of 3,367 adults aged ≥ 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) spanning CKM stages 0–3 (follow-up: 2015–2020). CumTyG-BRI was computed via the trapezoid method. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for incident CVD, with restricted cubic splines assessing nonlinearity and Kaplan–Meier curves illustrating cumulative risk. Robustness was confirmed via subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses. Among 3,367 participants, 638 CVD events occurred (18.9%). Higher CumTyG-BRI was associated with greater CVD risk in a threshold-dependent rather than linear manner (Q4 vs. Q1: HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.19–2.02; P for trend < 0.001), with risk elevation concentrated at the highest exposure quartile and corroborated by restricted cubic spline analysis. Kaplan-Meier curves showed progressively diverging survival probabilities (log-rank P < 0.0001). In this prospective cohort of Chinese adults aged ≥ 45 years, cumTyG-BRI showed a threshold-dependent association with incident CVD risk. Given that its constituent measures require only readily available metabolic parameters, cumTyG-BRI warrants further investigation as a potential index for CVD risk stratification, particularly in populations with high cardiometabolic burden.

Article.Title: Petroleum systems and hydrocarbon prospectivity of the offshore Garad Basin, north-central Somalia
Article.Authors: Ali M.; Hussein H.; Abdelmaksoud A.; Ali M.; Jabir M.
Article.Abstract: The petroleum potential of the offshore Garad Basin in north-central Somalia remains poorly constrained. This study provides an integrated reassessment of the basin’s structural framework and petroleum system using 2D seismic reflection and well data, and 1D/2D basin modeling. Seismic interpretation reveals coast-parallel culminations, tilted fault blocks, and rollover structures at shelf-to-upper slope depths, with several closures identified within the Upper Cretaceous interval. The Upper Jurassic Uarandab marine mudstone is identified as the main source rock in the offshore Garad Basin, with an average thickness of approximately 95 m. Basin modeling results, calibrated to vitrinite reflectance data, indicate that the Uarandab source rock entered the oil window during the Oligocene and reached the main oil window by the Middle–Late Miocene beneath the shelf and upper slope. Transformation ratios increase basinward and approach expulsion thresholds in depocenters during the interval of Oligocene–Miocene trap formation. The Upper Cretaceous Gira rudist-shoal carbonates constitute the main reservoir targets, with dolomitized Hamanlei stringers representing secondary prospects. Key exploration risks include pre-Aptian truncation of the Uarandab source, trap breach during Oligocene–Miocene reactivation, and depth conversion uncertainty. Future work should include long-offset 2D/3D seismic acquisition, checkshot/VSP data, and geochemical calibration to better constrain source kitchens and structural closures.

Article.Title: Creep deformation until failure under constant water content in sandy model slope
Article.Authors: Sasahara K.
Article.Abstract: The measurement of displacement on slopes under excavation or rainfall revealed that the displacement increased not only during excavation or rainfall but also afterward. The increase in displacement after stress loading can be identified as creep displacement under constant stress. However, the conditions for the generation of creep displacements are still unknown. To this end, inclined direct shear tests were conducted under constant stress and rainfall infiltration, and the measured data were analyzed to examine the conditions for creep displacement generation under rainfall infiltration. In some cases, shear displacement grew under constant volumetric water content (VWC) just prior to failure, but not in other cases. In the latter cases, shear displacement grew with increasing VWC. An accelerating increase in shear displacement just prior to failure—referred to as tertiary creep—could be observed in all cases in which shear displacement increased under constant VWC; meanwhile, a decelerating increase in shear displacement just after the start of the constant VWC duration—referred to as primary creep—could not be observed in some cases. The creep displacement normalized by all shear displacements until failure was larger when the increase in VWC corresponding to the shear displacement during soil absorption was greater. Thus, a larger increase in VWC corresponding to shear displacement during the absorption process is a condition for the generation of creep displacement under constant VWC. Primary creep displacement developed under the condition of no normal displacement, indicating a steady state in the shear zone. The primary creep displacement was greater for cases with a higher initial velocity at the start of the constant VWC duration. Thus, the absence of an increase in normal displacement under constant VWC may be a condition for the generation of primary creep, and a larger primary creep might be generated with a larger initial displacement velocity at the start of the constant VWC duration. The relationships between velocity and acceleration derived from the measured shear displacement during both the primary and tertiary creep stages are identical and linear on a logarithmic scale for each case. A future study will establish methods for predicting creep shear displacement based on the simple relationships between the velocity and acceleration derived from the measured displacement.

Article.Title: Association between serum uric acid and elevated blood pressure among pregnant women in Bangladesh: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ali N.; Begum J.; Mou A.
Article.Abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy remain a leading cause of maternal and fetal morbidity worldwide. Serum uric acid (SUA) has emerged as a potential biomarker of endothelial dysfunction and cardiometabolic risk during pregnancy, yet evidence from Bangladesh is scarce. This study investigated the association between SUA concentrations and elevated blood pressure among pregnant women in Bangladesh. This cross-sectional study included 194 pregnant women attending antenatal care in two districts of Bangladesh. Serum SUA and cardiometabolic biomarkers were measured using standard laboratory methods. Participants were categorized into SUA quartiles, and multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between SUA and elevated blood pressure. The mean age of the participants was 25 ± 5 years, while 16.9% had hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and 12.4% had preeclampsia. Women in the highest SUA quartile (≥ 5.5 mg/dL) had significantly higher systolic blood pressure (129.4 vs. 113.5 mmHg), diastolic blood pressure (81.8 vs. 71.4 mmHg), and mean arterial pressure (97.7 vs. 81.3 mmHg) than those in the lowest quartile (all P < 0.01). Increasing SUA levels were also associated with higher TG, TG/HDL-C ratio, and LDL/HDL-C ratio, whereas HDL-C levels decreased significantly ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of elevated blood pressure increased across SUA quartiles. In multivariable analysis, each 1 mg/dL increase in SUA was associated with a 38% higher odds of elevated blood pressure (adjusted OR: 1.38, 95% CI 1.03–1.86; P < 0.05). Compared with women in the lowest SUA quartile, those in the higher quartiles had approximately three- to four-fold greater odds of elevated blood pressure after adjustment for potential confounders. Overall, in all models SUA showed a significant association with elevated blood pressure. In conclusion, higher SUA concentrations were independently associated with elevated blood pressure and an adverse cardiometabolic profile among pregnant women in Bangladesh. However, due to the cross-sectional design, modest sample size, and lack of temporal assessment, the study findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality or prospective predictive ability. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine whether SUA measured earlier in pregnancy provides additional value for identifying women who subsequently develop gestational hypertension or preeclampsia.

Article.Title: EEG network features and APOE ε4 for amyloid classification in mild cognitive impairment
Article.Authors: Kong J.; So M.; Lee I.; Park H.; Kim Y.; Kim H.; Kim H.; Kang S.; Do S.; Lim D.; Lee C.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) may provide information complementary to apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) for identifying amyloid pathology in mild cognitive impairment. We evaluated this hypothesis in an exploratory cross-sectional study of 93 patients, including 54 with amyloid-positive positron emission tomography, using EEG functional connectivity, graph features and 11 classifiers under nested cross-validation. In the original partition, extreme gradient boosting with all domains achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.806 versus 0.682 for its APOE-only model (paired difference 0.124, 95% confidence interval 0.010–0.238). The median paired difference across 30 additional partitions was 0.088. Among non-carriers, the combined model identified 11 of 16 amyloid-positive patients, with 10 false positives among 31 amyloid-negative patients. The gain was smaller against carrier status used directly (difference 0.057, −0.043–0.157). Nesting classifier selection reduced the median AUC to 0.734, and alternative EEG epoch samples yielded AUCs of 0.571–0.773 on the original partition. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of complementary EEG and genetic information, while demonstrating dependence on the comparator, model selection and epoch sampling. Reliable EEG estimation and external validation are required before clinical use.

Article.Title: Genetic Characterization, phytochemical analysis and evaluation of the antioxidant and wound healing activities of Phyllanthus angustifolius Sw. and Phyllanthus emblica L
Article.Authors: Gabr S.; Bakr R.; Okba M.; Elshishtawy H.; ElFishawy A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phyllanthus species are widely recognized for their medicinal value, with Phyllanthus emblica being extensively studied, whereas Phyllanthus angustifolius remains comparatively under-investigated. This study aimed to comparatively characterize the genetic and phytochemical profiles, antioxidant capacity, and in vitro scratch closure activity of P. angustifolius and P. emblica . Genetic characterization was performed using primers targeting chalcone synthase (CHS), cinnamate 4-hydroxylase (C4H), phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL), and D-galacturonate reductase (GalUR). While both species yielded positive amplicons for key biosynthetic genes, distinct differences in the PCR amplification patterns for the phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL) locus were observed. These variations reflect genetic diversity rather than functional gene absence, underscoring the need for sequencing and expression analyses to clarify metabolic regulation. Colorimetric assays showed that P. angustifolius had a higher total flavonoid content, whereas P. emblica had a higher tannin content. HPLC-DAD analysis identified several phenolic acids and flavonoids, with gallic acid and quercetin among the predominant identified constituents. P. emblica exhibited higher antioxidant activity across the DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP assays and showed greater scratch closure than P. angustifolius under the tested conditions. Notably, the stronger antioxidant and scratch closure responses of P. emblica coincided with differences in its overall phytochemical profile, including its higher tannin content and markedly higher gallic acid content, whereas the higher total flavonoid content of P. angustifolius did not correspond to greater antioxidant or scratch closure activity. These findings suggest that the observed biological differences may reflect the combined contribution of the overall phytochemical composition rather than the abundance of a single compound class. Further mechanistic and in vivo studies are required to determine the constituents and pathways contributing to these activities.

Article.Title: Integrated computational pipelines using machine learning and deep neural networks for modelling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease classification
Article.Authors: Kondapaneni V.; Melkani Y.; Melkani G.
Article.Abstract: High-speed optical microscopy of Drosophila hearts has become an essential approach for modelling cardiovascular disease and aging. However, manual evaluation of cardiac function is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to error, highlighting the need for reliable computational frameworks. Here, we present computational pipelines that combine segmentation-derived cardiac parameters with ensemble machine learning and raw video-based representations with deep convolutional neural networks, enabling the development of new predictive models while extending our previous framework. This integrated approach enables automated and quantitative phenotyping of cardiac function across both aging and cardiovascular disease contexts. We evaluated the performance of the pipelines across three biological problems relevant to cardiovascular systems biology: distinguishing between young (1-week-old) and aged (5-week-old) Drosophila hearts, classifying healthy hearts from those carrying the lamin C mutation ( LamC G489V ), and identifying phenotypes associated with Ogdh knockdown. Ensemble learning with Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost (age classification) and Random Forest ( LamC G489V and Ogdh classification) applied to segmentation-derived features achieved accuracies (mean ± standard deviation across 5-fold cross-validation) of 83.7% ± 5.2% for aging classification, 78.2% ± 8.2% for L amC G489V mutant detection, and 98.5% ± 3.1% for Ogdh knockdown identification. In parallel, video-based modelling using a custom dual-input convolutional neural network and 3D residual networks (R3D-18 and MC3-18) achieved accuracies of 89.5% ± 4.3% for age classification, 75.6% for lamin C mutant detection, and 90.8% ± 6.0% for Ogdh knockdown classification. By integrating classical feature-based machine learning with modern deep learning architectures, this work provides a scalable computational framework for modeling Drosophila cardiac aging and disease. More broadly, the study demonstrates how multimodal machine learning can enhance quantitative phenotyping, reduce human error in analysis, and accelerate the application of models in systems-level investigations of cardiovascular health and aging.

Article.Title: MGS-DETR: a multi-granularity spatial representation learning framework for joint driver fatigue and distraction detection
Article.Authors: Kong L.; Zhang Y.; Qiu Z.; Wang Z.; Qin H.; Xie K.; Wen C.; Liu S.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Driver fatigue and distracted driving are major causes of traffic accidents, yet existing vision-based detectors often suffer from imbalanced feature modeling, insufficient cross-layer fusion, and loss of fine-grained spatial details under complex in-vehicle conditions. To address these issues, we propose MGS-DETR, a multi-granularity spatial representation learning framework built upon RT-DETR for joint driver fatigue and distraction detection. In the encoding stage, we develop a Multi-scale Spatial Awareness Encoder (MSAE) to balance local fine-grained fatigue cues and global distracted-action context. In the feature-fusion stage, we design Global-guided Cross-Modulation Fusion (G-CMF) to enhance the interaction between shallow spatial details and deep semantic features under pose variation and occlusion. In the multi-scale transmission stage, we construct a Spatial-Detail Enhanced Feature Pyramid Network (SDE-FPN) to preserve fine-grained spatial details during feature transmission and improve the localization of annotated regions for fatigue-related visual signs. Experiments are conducted on the Composite Distraction and Fatigue Dataset (CDFD) and the self-collected Real-World Fatigue and Distracted Driving Dataset (RWFDD). On CDFD, MGS-DETR achieves 0.9628 precision, 0.9618 recall, 0.9708 mAP50, and 0.8159 mAP50-95, improving mAP50-95 by 5.44 percentage points over RT-DETR-r18. Under the source-video-group-disjoint RWFDD split, it obtains 0.8868 precision, 0.8946 recall, 0.8907 F1-score, 0.9123 mAP50, and 0.8501 mAP50-95. Bidirectional transfer experiments are reported separately under the stated nine-class protocol. The full model runs at 164.50 FPS with 21.90 M parameters and 64.0 GFLOPs on the desktop test platform; embedded-device throughput is measured separately on Jetson Orin NX.

Article.Title: Microwave coherent addition in waveguides by berry phase locking
Article.Authors: Goldstein G.; Oppenheim Y.; Kleiner V.; Hasman E.; Maguid E.
Article.Abstract: Coherent addition of electromagnetic sources is essential for scaling radiation power and brightness beyond the limits of individual emitters. Yet achieving robust, continuous phase control in waveguide systems at high power remains a major challenge. Here, we demonstrate coherent combining of microwave sources in metallic waveguides using geometric (Berry) phase locking. By controlling the polarization evolution of circular-waveguide modes on a generalized Bloch sphere, we realize a compact, passive phase shifter based on a rotated dielectric birefringent metamaterial implemented with subwavelength gratings. The device provides deterministic, continuous phase control via Berry-phase accumulation while sustaining high electromagnetic fields. We experimentally demonstrate stable phase shifting up to 2.3 MW peak power and near-ideal coherent combining, achieving simultaneous doubling of output power and brightness. This work establishes a geometric-phase paradigm for high-power microwave control and coherent addition, providing a scalable route to phase-stable, high-brightness microwave systems.

Article.Title: Coevolution of heterogenous traits stabilizes predator–prey dynamics
Article.Authors: Mougi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ecological interactions are often mediated by multiple traits with distinct interaction structures, yet most eco-evolutionary models assume homogeneous interactions across traits. I developed a predator–prey model combining matching interactions, where trait similarity promotes successful interactions, and difference interactions, where trait divergence enhances prey defense, to examine how heterogeneous interaction architectures influence ecological stability. Although rapid prey evolution destabilized systems when either interaction evolved alone, simultaneous evolution of both traits frequently stabilized population dynamics more strongly than either trait alone, generating a synergistic stabilizing effect across broad parameter ranges. Unlike homogeneous multi-trait systems, where stabilization emerges through compensation among structurally equivalent traits, stabilization in the hybrid system arose through rapid switching between distinct coevolutionary modes, preventing prolonged dominance of either mismatch-driven escape or escalation dynamics. Despite the underlying asymmetry of the interaction architecture, rapid prey evolution generated more dynamically symmetric switching trajectories, suggesting that emergent dynamical symmetry may represent a more general route to eco-evolutionary stabilization across both homogeneous and heterogeneous interaction systems.

Article.Title: General-purpose LLM versus knowledge-base-grounded AI for real-world medical questions: a paired evaluation
Article.Authors: Russ P.; Einloft J.; Bedenbender S.; Armbruster N.; Wenzel L.; Ganser A.; Hirsch M.; Grgic I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to answer clinical questions, but comparisons by clinicians of general-purpose and knowledge-base-grounded systems remain limited. We conducted a non-blinded, paired evaluation at the 2026 congress of the German Society of Internal Medicine. Sixty-four physicians and medical students each assessed paired responses from LiSA, a knowledge-base-grounded clinical AI system developed by AMBOSS, and ChatGPT to one of 15 real-world internal medicine questions. Participants rated perceived quality, trust, and safety concerns. LiSA received higher ratings for overall quality (3.96 ± 1.20 vs. 3.48 ± 0.93; p = 0.002) and trust (5.11 ± 1.73 vs. 3.67 ± 1.39; p < 0.001). Safety concerns were reported in 15.6% of LiSA evaluations and 26.6% of ChatGPT evaluations ( p = 0.143). Clarity ratings did not differ significantly between systems, whereas LiSA was rated higher for completeness, actionability, and perceived medical accuracy, suggesting that the perceived advantage extended beyond linguistic clarity. In post hoc analyses, differences in quality and trust were greater among current than non-current AMBOSS users. These findings reflect perceived rather than objective performance, are susceptible to bias from non-blinding, question selection, and prior familiarity, and do not isolate the effect of knowledge-base grounding. Prospective, blinded studies are needed to determine clinical implications.

Article.Title: LMDE-UNet: local multi-directional state space modeling with dynamic edge enhancement for building extraction from remote sensing images
Article.Authors: Huang H.; Huang Z.; Ren C.; Zhang W.; Zhao G.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate building extraction from remote sensing imagery requires both contextual information and local structural detail. This paper presents LMDE-UNet , an encoder–decoder network that combines window-based local multi-directional scanning (WLMS), a bottleneck feature aggregation module (BFAM), and an edge enhancement module (DEEM) in the skip connections. Each local visual selective scan block models global context before applying local scanning within non-overlapping windows. Experiments on three building-extraction datasets show that LMDE-UNet achieves higher intersection over union (IoU) and F1-scores than the evaluated baselines, with competitive precision and recall. On the Typical Chinese Urban Building Dataset, LMDE-UNet achieves an IoU of 73.47% and an F1-score of 85.16%, exceeding the corresponding SwinUNet scores by 0.99 and 0.63 percentage points, respectively. Its precision reaches 86.73%. The ablation results suggest that WLMS provides larger IoU gains when combined with BFAM and DEEM than when added alone.

Article.Title: Comparison of four insulin resistance surrogate indices for incident MASLD in Chinese and prevalent MASLD in Japanese nonobese adults
Article.Authors: Mao J.; Kang J.; Han B.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) is central to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but head-to-head comparisons of IR surrogate indices in nonobese populations are scarce. We compared the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR) and single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) in relation to incident MASLD in a longitudinal Chinese cohort and prevalent MASLD in a cross-sectional Japanese cohort of nonobese adults. We analyzed two Dryad health examination datasets with different designs. The Chinese cohort ( n = 16,172) was longitudinal: participants free of hepatic steatosis at baseline were followed for a median of 35.8 months (interquartile range [IQR] 23.4–47.3), the outcome was incident MASLD, and entry was restricted to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) ≤ 3.12 mmol/L. The Japanese NAGALA cohort ( n = 12,932) was cross-sectional: prevalent MASLD was ascertained at the baseline examination, and entry was restricted to fasting blood glucose (FBG) < 6.1 mmol/L. The Japanese cohort was used for replication rather than harmonized external validation, and all participants had BMI < 25 kg/m². Steatosis was defined by ultrasound and MASLD by the 2023 multisociety criteria. Associations were examined with multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic splines, together with a Cox proportional-hazards sensitivity analysis of the Chinese follow-up data; discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), DeLong tests, category-free net reclassification improvement (NRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), decision curve analysis and bootstrap validation. Sensitivity analyses addressed the overlap between index components and the MASLD criteria by using steatosis alone as the outcome and excluding cases qualifying only through shared criteria. Incident MASLD developed in 2,114 (13.1%) Chinese participants during follow-up, and prevalent MASLD was present in 1,132 (8.8%) Japanese participants. Fully adjusted odds ratios per standard deviation increase in TyG, TyG-BMI, METS-IR and SPISE were 2.39, 5.09, 3.65 and 0.15 in the Chinese cohort and 2.19, 3.71, 2.90 and 0.18 in the Japanese cohort (all P < 0.001); the corresponding hazard ratios in the Cox sensitivity analysis were 1.83, 3.25, 2.10 and 0.24 (all P < 0.001), and associations were attenuated but persisted in sensitivity analyses. TyG-BMI had the highest AUC (0.8755 and 0.8865), and TyG-BMI, METS-IR and SPISE each outperformed BMI (0.8248 and 0.8404; DeLong P < 0.001), whereas TyG did not. Adding each index to a baseline model of total cholesterol, triglycerides, FBG and BMI improved NRI and IDI but increased the AUC by at most 0.0078, a gain that became negligible when HDL-C was added to the baseline model and when the components were modeled flexibly; decision curve analysis showed no clinically meaningful difference in net benefit, and NRI gains should therefore be interpreted cautiously. In nonobese adults, BMI-integrated IR indices, particularly TyG-BMI, were associated with incident MASLD in the longitudinal Chinese cohort and with prevalent MASLD in the cross-sectional Japanese cohort, and discriminated both outcomes better than single anthropometric or biochemical markers (BMI, fasting glucose and triglycerides), whereas TyG alone did not outperform BMI. Because the two cohorts differ in design and outcome, their estimates should not be compared numerically. Shared diagnostic variables may inflate these estimates, and the incremental gains were small, so prospective external validation is required before any clinical use.

Article.Title: Benchmarking latent-space reasoning abilities in large language models through forced response-language selection
Article.Authors: Hagendorff T.; Fabi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) can perform reasoning computations both internally within their latent space and externally by generating explicit token sequences like chains of thought. Significant progress in enhancing reasoning abilities has been made by scaling test-time compute. However, understanding and quantifying model-internal reasoning abilities – the inferential “leaps” models make between individual token predictions – remains crucial. This study introduces a benchmark (n = 4,000 items) designed to quantify model-internal reasoning in different domains. We achieve this by having LLMs indicate the correct solution to reasoning problems not through descriptive text, but by selecting a specific language of their initial response token that is different from English, the benchmark language. This not only requires models to reason beyond their context window, but at the same time to overcome their default behavior to respond in the same language as the prompt, posing an additional cognitive strain. We evaluate a set of 18 LLMs, showing significant performance variations, with GPT-4.5 achieving the highest accuracy (74.7%), outperforming models like Grok-2 (67.2%), or Llama 3.1 405B (65.6%). Control experiments and difficulty scaling analyses suggest that while LLMs engage in internal reasoning, we cannot rule out heuristic exploitations under certain conditions, marking an area for future investigation. Our experiments demonstrate that LLMs can “think” via latent-space computations, highlighting model-internal inference processes that need further understanding, especially in view of safety-related aspects like covert planning, goal-seeking, or deception emerging without explicit token traces. Significance Statement – Large language models (LLMs) often appear to "reason" only when they show step-by-step chains of thought. We introduce a benchmark that instead measures reasoning carried out silently in a model’s latent space. Tasks require models to infer the correct answer and indicate it solely by choosing a pre-specified non-English response language—preventing them from "thinking in the context window." Across eight reasoning domains, models show wide variation, with some large dense transformer models substantially outperforming others. Control studies and difficulty scaling suggest genuine internal computation, while also revealing potential heuristic shortcuts. By isolating model-internal "reasoning leaps," our approach helps quantify hidden inferences and highlights oversight and safety risks from capabilities that leave no explicit token trace.

Article.Title: Monitoring initial dose to navigate ARPI treatment outcomes (MINATO study)
Article.Authors: Kawahara T.; Hashizume A.; Yamazaki M.; Takamoto D.; Ito H.; Takeshima T.; Kuroda S.; Ito Y.; Uemura H.; Makiyama K.; Teranishi J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs: apalutamide, enzalutamide, darolutamide, abiraterone) are central to the first-line treatment of castration-sensitive prostate cancer (CSPC). Although their efficacy has been established in large-scale clinical trials, real-world evaluations of drug tolerability and related outcomes remain scarce. Using a large prescription database, this study analyzed the continuation of ARPIs in CSPC and the impact of dose reduction on time to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). This was a retrospective cohort study using a medical information database (MDV). Among patients with prostate cancer, those who initiated a first-line ARPI while in the CSPC state (no CRPC diagnosis) were included. First, as indicators of treatment continuation, same-drug dose reduction among patients starting at the standard dose and switching to another agent were evaluated from the date of first-drug initiation using the Kaplan-Meier method and the log-rank test; the timing of dose reduction and the distribution of the final administered dose were also described. Next, as an indicator of prognosis, the time from first-drug initiation to the first CRPC diagnosis was evaluated by first-line agent using the Kaplan-Meier method and the log-rank test. Time to CRPC was examined in two cohorts: a full-period cohort and a post-approval cohort comprising patients who initiated treatment on or after the approval date of darolutamide plus docetaxel (February 24, 2023). In addition, for apalutamide and enzalutamide, time to CRPC was compared by starting dose (full dose vs. reduced-dose start) and by the presence or absence of on-treatment dose reduction. The first-line agents were enzalutamide in 8,254 patients (50%), abiraterone in 4,896 (30%), apalutamide in 2,318 (14%), and darolutamide in 951 (6%). Regarding dose reduction, the proportion of patients reducing the dose among standard-dose starters was highest for apalutamide (28%), versus 10% for enzalutamide, 12% for darolutamide, and 7% for abiraterone (log-rank P < 0.001). Apalutamide dose reductions were concentrated within the first 0–6 months. The proportion maintaining the standard dose as the final dose was only 52% for apalutamide, compared with 70–87% for the other agents. In contrast, switching was infrequent for all agents, with no significant difference among them (P = 0.060). Next, in the full-period cohort, the time to CRPC differed significantly among the agents (overall log-rank P < 0.001) and was longest for apalutamide; the same ordering was observed in the post-approval cohort, in which all four agents were simultaneously available ( P < 0.001). Of note, apalutamide had the highest proportion of censoring (76% in the full-period and 90% in the post-approval cohort), and follow-up was uneven across agents. With respect to dose, apalutamide showed no significant difference in time to CRPC by either starting dose or the presence or absence of on-treatment reduction (starting dose P = 0.74; 6-month landmark P = 0.12). Enzalutamide showed a difference by starting dose ( P < 0.001) but no difference by the presence or absence of on-treatment reduction (landmark P = 0.72). Because the four agents are prescribed to different patient populations under Japanese reimbursement rules, these between-agent differences are descriptive and are not efficacy comparisons. This study evaluated the continuation and dose-reduction patterns of various ARPIs as first-line treatment for CSPC. It also evaluated the association between dose reduction and time to CRPC.

Article.Title: LDUnet: a lightweight deep unfolding framework for video snapshot compressive imaging reconstruction
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Dong K.; Wang C.; Fu Q.; Zeng Z.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Video snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) enables high-speed video acquisition by encoding multiple temporal frames into a single coded measurement. However, recovering the original video sequence from compressed observations remains a challenging ill-posed inverse problem, requiring effective integration of physical measurement constraints and spatio-temporal prior learning. In this work, we propose LDUnet, an efficient lightweight deep unfolding framework for video SCI reconstruction. LDUnet incorporates the SCI measurement model into the unfolding process through a measurement-normalized fidelity update and employs a compact spatio-temporal prior with parameter sharing across unfolding stages. Extensive experiments on simulated grayscale and color SCI datasets demonstrate that LDUnet achieves competitive reconstruction performance with substantially reduced model complexity. Additional ablation experiments verify the contribution of measurement normalization and show that stage-wise parameter sharing substantially reduces model size with only a marginal change in reconstruction accuracy. Evaluations under unseen masks, different measurement noise levels, and real SCI measurements with different compression factors further characterize the reconstruction behavior of LDUnet under varying sensing conditions. These results indicate that LDUnet provides an efficient measurement-consistent unfolding solution for video SCI reconstruction, achieving a favorable balance between reconstruction quality, model complexity, and computational efficiency.

Article.Title: Spatial distribution, pollution assessment, and controlling factors of heavy metals in tropical agricultural soils of Hainan Island, China
Article.Authors: Cao Q.; Fu C.; Zhang Z.; Lei F.; Wu Y.; Zhang W.; Nicholas O.; Meng L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hainan Island is China’s largest tropical crop-production base, making its agricultural soil quality important for national food security. We determined total concentrations of eight heavy metals (Hg, As, Cd, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn, Ni) in 300 surface soils collected across the island in late 2025. Soils were predominantly acidic (mean pH 5.18; 77% below pH 5.5), and mean concentrations were low to moderate (e.g., Cd 0.21, Pb 58.19, and Ni 28.50 mg kg⁻¹). Against pH- and land-use-stratified GB 15618 − 2018 screening values, single-metal exceedance was most frequent for Pb (28.0%) and Ni (14.7%); separately, the Nemerow comprehensive index exceeded its pollution threshold ( P n > 1.0) at 23.7% of sites. The geo-accumulation index ( I geo = log 2 [ C i /(1.5 × B i )]) showed the strongest enrichment for Cd (mean 1.48; 99.3% above 0), moderate enrichment for Pb (0.33), and at or below background levels for the remaining metals. Soil pH correlated negatively with total Cd, Cr, Hg, and Pb ( r = − 0.47 to − 0.28). Parent material, land use, and pH jointly explained about 45% of the variance, separating lithogenic Ni-Cu-Zn from mixed Cd-Pb-Hg-Cr associations. Together, these results show that fixed-threshold assessment understates contamination in acidic tropical soils, providing an island-wide baseline for targeted risk management.

Article.Title: Comparative effects of nanoalumina and nanosilica on the mechanical, morphological, and thermal performance of additively manufactured PLA composites
Article.Authors: Budak S.
Article.Abstract: The effects of nano-Al₂O₃ and nano-SiO₂ at 2 and 3 wt% on the mechanical, thermal, and morphological properties of polylactic acid (PLA) fabricated by fused filament fabrication (FFF) were investigated. Neat PLA and four nanocomposite formulations were produced and characterized by tensile, flexural, and compression tests, together with Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric/differential thermogravimetric (TGA/DTG) analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX). The mechanical results showed that the effect of nanoparticle addition depended on filler type and loading level. S3 (3 wt% SiO₂) showed the highest mean tensile strength (38.23 ± 1.77 MPa), an 11.75% increase relative to neat PLA; however, differences in tensile strength among formulations were not statistically significant ( p = 0.442). A2 (2 wt% Al₂O₃) exhibited the highest flexural and compressive strengths, reaching 122.76 ± 1.89 MPa and 99.10 ± 1.47 MPa, corresponding to increases of 55.77% and 10.60% relative to neat PLA, respectively. The flexural differences were statistically significant ( p < 0.001), whereas the overall compressive ANOVA was significant ( p = 0.033). DSC results showed formulation-dependent changes in crystallization and melting behavior, while TGA/DTG analysis revealed variations in thermal degradation parameters among the formulations. FTIR showed the characteristic absorption bands of PLA, while SEM provided qualitative morphological observations and EDAX indicated the presence of the corresponding elements in the analyzed regions. Overall, the results demonstrate that the effects of nano-Al₂O₃ and nano-SiO₂ are property- and formulation-dependent rather than universally beneficial.

Article.Title: Four resistance training protocols for upper-body strength and punch performance in elite female boxers: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Tian T.; Liu X.; Yu F.; Bao S.
Article.Abstract: Blood flow restriction training (BFRT) and cluster set training are effective for strength and power, but their comparative and combined effects in female boxers remain unclear. To compare four interventions—conventional high-load training (CON), cluster set training (CS), BFRT, and combined BFRT + CS—on upper-body strength, anaerobic capacity, and punch performance in elite female boxers. Forty elite female boxers were randomly assigned to four groups ( n = 10): CON (70% 1RM), CS (50–60% 1RM), BFRT (20–30% 1RM, 40–60% limb occlusion pressure, intermittent), and BFRT + CS (same load with cluster sets). Training lasted 8 weeks, twice weekly. Outcomes included straight punch force and velocity, bench press 1RM, bench press throw peak power and height, 30-s punch count and mean velocity, and Wingate peak and mean power. Analyses used one-way ANCOVA with pre-test covariates and Bonferroni post hoc comparisons. All groups improved significantly ( p < 0.01), and all three active interventions outperformed CON in multiple outcomes. Task-specific differences emerged: BFRT was best for bench press 1RM; CS for straight punch velocity and throw height; BFRT + CS for punch force, 30-s punch count and velocity, throw peak power, and Wingate power. No single intervention was universally superior. The three alternative training protocols (BFRT, cluster set training, and their combination) deliver distinct performance advantages relative to conventional high-load training in elite female boxers. These findings reflect comparisons of four complete training packages; the independent contributions of external load, set structure, rest intervals and blood flow restriction cannot be disentangled in the present design. Findings are limited by the absence of a non-exercise control group and punch force measurement validity. Coaches may select among these training protocols based on specific performance goals.

Article.Title: Consideration of sex and gender in routine research data: results from an online survey across German medical data integration centers
Article.Authors: Schindler L.; Beelich H.; Gütebier L.; Katsari E.; Liprandi D.; Stracke S.; Waltemath D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Medical Data Integration Centers (DIZ) have been established at German university hospitals to collect, transfer, consolidate, and process routine clinical data and make it available for health research. Because the consideration of sex and gender benefits research and enhances the quality of medical care, DIZ staff members need to be well-informed and knowledgeable about sex and gender aspects in clinical data, so that they can advise researchers on the thoughtful selection of study cohorts, the appropriate encoding of sex and gender information, and the benefits of considering gender distributions. In this work, we systematically analyze the awareness of sex and gender among technical and scientific staff members at DIZ using an online survey, which was distributed in February 2024 to all 38 DIZ in Germany via a national mailing list. The survey was structured into three topics: (1) perception of sex and gender in medical research, (2) consideration of sex and gender during data collection, and (3) consideration of sex and gender in data use and reuse. We analyzed the collected data with descriptive statistics and checked for correlation within the dataset. After a four-week response period, 74 current employees had fully completed the questionnaire and an additional 62 had partially completed it. The survey results show a lack of knowledge and awareness regarding sex and gender aspects among DIZ employees, indicated by a high amount of “No” and “I don’t know” answers, specifically regarding sex- and gender-specific training, official recommendations, and team policies. As essential links between clinics and researchers, DIZ employees need targeted training on sex and gender aspects to better support and advise research efforts. We provide first recommendations for the different levels of administration to improve knowledge and awareness of sex and gender aspects in medical research data, which will guide future recommendations for handling sex and gender aspects in clinical research.

Article.Title: Machine learning-driven reverse prediction of concrete mix design: a comparative study of twelve algorithms
Article.Authors: Nadimalla A.; Mydin M.; Masjuki S.; Sattar A.; Awoyera P.; Fadugba O.
Article.Abstract: Concrete mix design is usually treated as a forward, iterative task: proportions are adjusted until the required compressive strength is met. Here, we work in the reverse direction. From a target 28-day compressive strength and curing age, the model estimates seven proportions directly: cement, blast furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate. The workflow combines machine learning with a deterministic physics-informed correction layer. Twelve algorithms from six model families (linear, instance-based, tree-based, ensemble, kernel, and deep learning) were trained on the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength dataset 1 ( n = 1,030). For a fair comparison, each model used the same multi-output regression wrapper, hyperparameters were tuned with 30-iteration RandomizedSearchCV and 5-fold internal cross-validation, robustness was assessed by 10-fold cross-validation, and pairwise differences were tested with paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. The study contributes a tuned twelve-algorithm benchmark with statistical comparisons, a per-component analysis linked to concrete-material mechanisms, and a post-processing layer that enforces 0.30 ≤ W/C ≤ 0.80, cement ≥ 200 kg/m³, supplementary cementitious replacement ≤ 50% of binder, and non-negative superplasticizer dosage. After tuning, Extra Trees gave the highest test-set R² (0.341), while Gradient Boosting gave the highest 10-fold CV R² (0.262 ± 0.041). The leading four models were not significantly different (paired t-test, p > 0.05). Per-component R² ranged from about 0.52 for superplasticizer and 0.46 for cement to below 0.16 for fine aggregate and slag. This pattern is consistent with concrete chemistry: hydration-controlled components can be partly inferred from strength, whereas aggregate proportions are set largely by grading and workability. For a 15 MPa target, the unconstrained model returned a W/C of about 1.0; the physics layer corrected it to 0.80 with only a modest test-set R² reduction (0.341 to 0.302). The full pipeline was then applied to an independent ultra-high-performance concrete dataset (863 mixtures, 17 variables). The algorithm ranking was preserved and the best inverse R² increased to 0.608, indicating that input dimensionality strongly affects inverse predictability. A conditional-variance analysis shows the tuned models operate near the upper bound of the two-input formulation: mixtures with the same strength form several distinct design families, so the prediction is best read as a screening anchor within a family of valid designs. The proposed framework should be used as a screening tool, not as a replacement for ACI 211.1 design or laboratory verification.

Article.Title: Optimal allocation of electric vehicle charging stations and renewable energy resources using a modified version of walrus optimizer
Article.Authors: El-Ela A.; Elbanna S.; Ebeed M.; Nagem N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Decarbonization policies aim to electrify the transportation sector by increasing the use of Electric Vehicles (EVs); consequently, Electric Vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are widely integrated into distribution systems (DSs). EVCSs can be considered a significant additional electrical load on DSs, leading to negative effects such as increased system power losses and reduced voltage profile and voltage stability. In this regard, the negative effects of adding EVCSs can be mitigated through optimal integration of EVCSs and renewable energy resources (RERs), such as wind turbines (WTs), photovoltaics (PVs), and biomass units. This paper aims to optimize the planning of integrating the EVCSs and RERs into multi-microgrid-based DSs (IEEE 33-bus, 69-bus, and 94-bus) to reduce the total voltage deviations (VDs), the total costs, and improve the total voltage stability index (VSI). A modified version of Walrus Optimizer (MWO) is proposed and applied to solve this problem. MWO is based on enhancing the search capability of the conventional WO algorithm and avoiding its stagnation at local optima using three approaches, including a hybrid chaotic mutation (HCM), Fitness Distance Balance (FDB), and Quasi-opposition-based learning (QOBL). The performance and capability of the MWO are tested and verified using standard benchmark functions, and the obtained results are compared to other metaheuristic optimization methods. The simulation results reveal that the proposed MWO is an effective optimizer for optimal planning solutions in which the overall cost was reduced by 21.36%, 28.25%, and 29.9% for the IEEE 33-bus, 69-bus, and 94-bus systems, respectively, while the system total VDs were reduced by 70.93%, 65.26%, and 82.3% for the IEEE 33-bus, 69-bus, and 94-bus systems, respectively. In addition, the total VSI was improved by 21.41%, 8.47%, and 58.34% for the IEEE 33-bus, 69-bus, and 94-bus systems, respectively.

Article.Title: Characterization of corynacin K411, a leaderless bacteriocin from Corynebacterium jeikeium
Article.Authors: Albright C.; La J.; Buragina J.; Ignacio M.; Magpusao A.; McArthur S.; Sadiq N.; De Buck J.; Acedo J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides that are emerging as natural preservatives and alternatives to conventional antibiotics in response to the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. Here, we provide a comprehensive experimental characterization of corynacin K411, previously reported as K411/AucA. The corynacin K411 biosynthetic gene cluster encodes a set of proteins that support a coordinated system for peptide production, secretion, and self-immunity. Corynacin K411 exhibits potent activity against various bacteria, including the foodborne pathogen Listeria monocytogenes . It demonstrates stability across acidic and alkaline pH (pH 2 to 10) and high temperatures (37 °C and 60 °C). It exerts bactericidal activity by disrupting membrane integrity, causing leakage of nucleic acids, proteins, potassium and magnesium ions. Importantly, corynacin K411 is non-hemolytic and non-cytotoxic to human keratinocytes. In addition, it inhibits L. monocytogenes biofilm formation, reduces the biomass of pre-formed biofilms, and lowers bacterial cell counts in a milk preservation model system. Structural analysis of the AlphaFold-predicted three-dimensional structure indicates a saposin-like fold, consistent with other characterized saposin-like leaderless bacteriocins.

Article.Title: Riverscape genetics of a limnophilic fish in a near-natural river system reveal implications for conservation management
Article.Authors: von Spinn D.; Meulenbroek P.; Curto M.; Shumka S.; Schiemer F.; Hein T.; Meimberg H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract River-floodplain systems are among the most impaired ecosystems globally, with severe impacts on associated biota. A key challenge in restoration is the limited understanding of natural metapopulation dynamics. The aim of the present study is to describe how a near-natural river network shapes the population structure of a limnophilic model fish species, the Southern-Balkan endemic Pelasgus thesproticus . Specifically, we aim to (I) infer population connectivity among floodplain habitats and (II) test environmental resistance driving metapopulation dynamics. Utilizing 30 anonymous nuclear markers and mitochondrial cytochrome b sequences, we genotyped 474 specimens from 13 sites in the Vjosa River system in southern Albania, one of the last free-flowing rivers in Europe. Population structure was inferred using clustering and distance-based approaches. The effects of riverscape properties on population connectivity were tested within a riverscape genetic framework. We found evidence for a strongly connected metapopulation linked to river network structure and flow. Gene flow was primarily directed downstream, and genetic differentiation increased with increasing distance to the mainstem. Restoring suitable habitats and hydrological connectivity are essential targets to re-establish functional metapopulations in impacted river-floodplain systems. Moreover, our study underscores the value of the few remaining near-natural rivers as reference conditions for studying natural ecological processes.

Article.Title: A Fermatean fuzzy CRITIC WASPAS framework for conflict detection in autonomous drone navigation
Article.Authors: Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: The fast growth of autonomous drone activities in urban airspace poses major challenges in real-time conflict detection during uncertain and dynamic conditions. The current models of decision making usually employ simplistic representations of uncertainty and less objective weighting models, which restrict their efficacy in safety–critical settings. In order to fill this gap, this research will introduce a new multi-criteria decision-making model using Fermatean fuzzy set (FFS) combined with CRITIC (Criteria Importance through Intercriteria Correlation) and WASPAS (Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment) models. FF environment can model higher order uncertainty and hesitation in a better way, and the CRITIC approach can offer objective criteria weight that takes into consideration inter-criteria conflict and variability. The WASPAS approach is used to obtain a strong and stable ranking of conflict-resolution options by aggregating both additively and multiplicatively. The suggested framework is justified in a simulation-based case study and a comparison to benchmark methods like TOPSIS and VIKOR. The findings indicate that there is a consistent behavior in the ranking and better stability under changing conditions as attested by the sensitivity analysis, which underscores the soundness of the proposed method in dealing with uncertainty and inter-criteria relationships. The research adds to the structured and objective decision-making model in detection of conflict in the face of uncertainty and serves as a foundation of real-life application in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles UAV systems.

Article.Title: Oak and sumac gallnut polyphenol extracts attenuate aluminum-induced inflammation and oxidative stress in a human intestinal cell model
Article.Authors: Lambert D.; Lemaire C.; Billamboz M.; Jawhara S.
Article.Abstract: Chronic intestinal inflammation associated with inflammatory bowel diseases arises from dysregulated immune signaling, epithelial barrier dysfunction, oxidative stress, and sensitivity to environmental toxicants. Polyphenol-rich natural extracts represent promising modulators of these processes, yet their mechanisms of action remain incompletely characterized. Following an initial screening of multiple natural extracts, two polyphenol-rich candidates, oak gallnut extract (OGNE) and sumac gallnut extract (SGNE), were selected for further investigation using in vitro and in vivo models. OGNE and SGNE decreased NF-κB activation and downregulated key components of the TLR/NF-κB signaling axis, including TLR2, Dectin-1, and MyD88. This was accompanied by reduced expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines and increased PPAR-γ expression. Both extracts attenuated reactive oxygen species accumulation and preserved epithelial barrier integrity in dextran sulfate sodium-treated intestinal Caco-2 cells, with OGNE displaying cytokine modulation. Chemical profiling revealed polyphenolic signatures dominated by glycosylated gallates (OGNE) or pentagalloylglucose (SGNE). Both extracts reduced intracellular aluminum accumulation and mitigated aluminum- and LPS-induced oxidative stress. In vivo, treatment with OGNE or SGNE improved nematode survival during C. albicans infection, reduced pathogen burden, and induced the antimicrobial gene lys-1.These findings highlight the complementary anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and aluminum-detoxifying activities of OGNE and SGNE.

Article.Title: Development of an evaluation system of neighborhood culture based on multi-source data
Article.Authors: Guo L.; Gao Y.; Qiao Y.; Zeng L.
Article.Abstract: In the process of rapid urban development, neighborhoods, as spatial units for residents’daily lives, work, and leisure, are an important part of urban renewal. However, the lack of awareness of local regional history and neighborhood culture among developers has resulted in homogenous appearance and lack of cultural presence in many neighborhoods. The present study aimed to protect and optimize neighborhood culture and used public perception as the research perspective to evaluate the cultural perception of the neighborhood, to clarify the perceived strength of each cultural element and provide a scientific basis for cultural conservation. Considering the Da Zhao Historical District of Hohhot as an example, a cultural perception evaluation system was developed by integrating subjective perception analysis and objective spatial data measurement. Drawing on existing literature to identify evaluation factors and criteria, the system was grounded in multi-source data by obtaining field research, geospatial, and online text data to analyze the public’s cultural perceptions of the built environment and subjective perceptions of the neighborhood’s architectural style, street space, and environmental atmosphere. The present study provides a scientific and effective method for evaluating the cultural perceptions of neighborhoods with a view toward promoting the construction of a better life.

Article.Title: STK33 is required for the differentiation of spermatocytes and spermatids in male mice by maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis
Article.Authors: Zhang W.; An Z.; Zhang C.; Tian Q.; Wang Y.; Li X.; Tian P.; Wan N.; Yuan Y.; Yuan J.; Du J.; Huang X.; Yu Y.; Ren L.
Article.Abstract: Spermatogenesis is a highly intricate and tightly regulated cell development process, involving mitosis, meiosis and spermiogenesis. STK33 , a member of the serine/threonine kinase family, is prominently expressed in testicular tissue, particularly in spermatocytes. In male mice, STK33 is essential for the spermatid differentiation and male infertility. However, the role of STK33 in spermatocyte cell development in males has remained unexplored. To further elucidate the exact role of STK33 in mouse reproduction, we generated STK33 −/− mice using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Deletion of STK33 resulted in complete infertility in male mice, and STK33 −/− mice displayed reduced sperm count compared to wild-type (WT) mice. Single-cell cytometry results of testes show that the differences between STK33 −/− and WT mice mainly concentrate at the spermatocyte stage, with differentially expressed genes primarily focusing on metabolic pathways. STK33 −/− mice manifested mitochondrial abnormalities and heightened apoptosis compared to WT mice. Furthermore, there were notable irregularities in the expression of proteins associated with apoptosis and mitochondrial function.In conclusion, our findings unveil a novel role for STK33 in germ cell development in male mice, whereby knockout of the STK33 gene leads to disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis and increased cell apoptosis in mouse spermatocytes and spermtids.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic responses of Botrytis cinerea under L-carvone fumigation
Article.Authors: Ren Z.; Lu Q.; Yang C.; You W.; Wang C.; Zhi Y.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Botrytis cinerea , a necrotrophic phytopathogenic fungus with a wide host range, causes severe postharvest gray mold and huge economic losses worldwide. Conventional chemical fungicides easily induce multidrug resistance in field isolates, while the natural monoterpene volatile L-carvone exhibits broad-spectrum antifungal activity. However, the comprehensive molecular mechanism by which L-carvone suppresses B. cinerea remains unclear. In this study, mycelia of B. cinerea were treated with L-carvone at EC 50 concentration with sterile water as blank control. RNA-seq transcriptome and HS-SPME-GC-MS widely-targeted volatile metabolome profiling sequencing were performed to systematically dissect molecular responses via combined transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis. A total of 1,531 DEGs were identified, including 347 upregulated and 1184 downregulated genes. Upregulated DEGs were enriched in sulfur metabolism, cysteine and methionine metabolism involved in transient antioxidant response, whereas downregulated DEGs mainly participated in cell membrane lipid biosynthesis, carbon energy metabolism, phytotoxin synthesis and conidiation. A total of 246 DAMs were screened. Antioxidant terpenoids including γ-cadinene, carvacrol and camphene were significantly accumulated, while lipid precursors for cell membrane assembly and toxic botrydial-derived aldehydes were drastically reduced. L-carvone simultaneously blocked phytotoxin biosynthesis, ergosterol membrane formation, vegetative growth and asexual reproduction of B. cinerea . The fungus only activated short-term ROS scavenging and xenobiotic efflux pathways, whereas the long-term glutathione-dependent antioxidant system was suppressed, leading to irreversible oxidative damage. This study reveals the multi-target antifungal mechanism of L-carvone at transcriptional and metabolic levels, providing theoretical support for green control of gray mold and the development of botanical fungicides with novel modes of action.

Article.Authors: J V.; A V.
Article.Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram monitoring in the Internet of Medical Things requires arrhythmia classifiers that run on resource-constrained devices and learn across hospitals without pooling patient data. We propose FedIoMT-RPM, a split federated learning framework in which each device trains only a 28.4 KiB client-side network, 6.8 times smaller than in full-model federated learning, while a bounded adaptive weighted aggregation adjusts each client''s contribution to its smoothed validation performance. Under the patient-independent inter-patient protocol of the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, with five clients holding complete patient records and six seeds per method, its detection performance was statistically comparable to that of the best federated baselines, with an accuracy of 93.97 ± 1.72%, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.731 ± 0.039 and a macro-F1 score of 60.07 ± 2.41%. This macro-F1 reflects limited detection of supraventricular beats, with a sensitivity of 64.8%, and near-zero detection of fusion beats, and 1,381 of the 1,781 supraventricular test beats come from a single record. Among the split methods, FedIoMT-RPM averaged 18.9% less communication than SplitFed. Zero-shot INCART and PTB-XL benchmarks gave results comparable to the federated baselines. Reconstruction attacks recovered the ECG from the transmitted activations, which need protection before clinical use; membership inference stayed near chance.

Article.Title: Optimizing NPK fertilization for Se enrichment and Cd reduction in selenium-rich rice
Article.Authors: Su Y.; Huang F.; Li X.; He N.; Yu D.; Zhao Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Selenium (Se)-enriched rice fields encounter a risk of cadmium (Cd) contamination, which reduces the quality of rice safety. This study aimed to investigate the impact of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) fertilizers application ratios on rice yield and the coexistence issue of Se and Cd in Se-rich paddy fields. And to explore the possibility of achieving high yield of rice with low Cd and high Se. An innovative “3517” fertilization experiment was conducted to explore the effects of N/P/K application on Se/Cd levels in the soil, stems and grains of rice at different growth stages, and to investigate the correlations among them. Furthermore, the multi-objective optimization model was adopted to analyze the optimal fertilization for the first time. Yield was significantly positively correlated only with N application, and the Se content in the soil was negatively correlated with the Cd content in grains. Regarding Se, N inhibited Se accumulation in grains, while P has a threshold effect and is positively correlated with Se in grains; K increases Se in grains to a certain extent. For Cd, an N application increased in content of Cd in grains, while P and K delayed the migration of Cd into grains and were positively correlated with Cd in straw. Optimal N/P/K combinations (codes 211 and 220) were identified, which can regulate the Se and Cd contents in rice with less fertilizer application. This provides feasible technical guidance for the safe production of Se-enriched rice.

Article.Title: Effects of dietary iron restriction on Junín virus disease in a humanized transferrin receptor 1 mouse model
Article.Authors: Wasson S.; Li M.; Bailey K.; Westover J.; Davies C.; Daniels-Wells T.; Penichet M.; Gowen B.
Article.Abstract: Five New World mammarenaviruses (NWM) cause severe hemorrhagic fever and threaten human health in South American communities where they are endemic. No FDA-approved antiviral drugs exist to treat these viral infections, and treatment options are urgently needed. Laboratory mice genetically modified to express human transferrin receptor 1 (huTfR1 Tg mice) are susceptible to Junín virus (JUNV), which, like other pathogenic NWMs, enters cells by attaching to the receptor’s apical domain. However, these mice exhibit physiological abnormalities, thereby limiting the model’s utility. In contrast, transgenic mice that express a murine TfR1 with a human apical domain (huApTfR1 Tg mice) are physiologically normal but more refractory to JUNV disease. Here, we investigated whether dietary iron restriction increases huApTfR1 expression, thereby promoting greater JUNV entry and more severe disease in response to reduced iron bioavailability. While a significant increase in huApTfR1 expression in target tissues was observed in mice raised on a low-iron diet, it did not confer greater susceptibility to severe JUNV disease. Notably, the low-iron diet resulted in iron-deficiency anemia and significantly lower body weight in the mice. Although our findings indicate that dietary iron restriction upregulates huApTfR1 expression and induces iron-deficiency anemia, it does not enhance mortality following JUNV challenge.
