Article.Title: Dependency-aware evolutionary search using population representation learning for large-scale many-objective optimisation
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Khan W.; Singh S.; Siddiqui S.; Joshi U.; Wanjale K.; Chauhan A.
Article.Abstract: Many-objective optimisation problems characterised by large decision spaces and complex objective interactions remain challenging for conventional evolutionary algorithms. Existing approaches primarily rely on predefined variation operators and dominance-based selection mechanisms, which often struggle to exploit latent structural relationships among candidate solutions. This study introduces a representation-guided evolutionary optimisation framework that learns population-level dependencies during the search process and incorporates the acquired knowledge into evolutionary variation and selection. The proposed framework employs a population encoding mechanism based on self-attention to capture global interactions among candidate solutions and generate latent representations describing the evolving search landscape. These representations are subsequently utilised to guide adaptive crossover, mutation, and diversity preservation strategies, enabling a more informed exploration–exploitation balance. Unlike conventional learning-assisted evolutionary algorithms that use machine learning models as external predictors, the proposed method integrates representation learning directly within the optimisation cycle. Experimental evaluation was conducted on selected configurations from the DTLZ, WFG, MaF, and CEC 2020 MMOP benchmark families, involving up to 20 objectives and 1000 decision variables. On the evaluated configurations, MOEA-T achieved improved mean convergence and diversity indicators compared with the considered Pareto-based, decomposition-based, reference-vector-based, and learning-assisted algorithms. These findings provide evidence of the potential effectiveness of representation-guided evolutionary search under the tested high-dimensional and many-objective conditions. However, they do not imply uniform superiority across every problem instance in the complete benchmark families. Additional ablation and scalability studies confirm the effectiveness of dependency-guided search and population representation learning in addressing the challenges associated with high-dimensional many-objective optimisation. The findings suggest that integrating population-level structural learning into evolutionary search provides a promising direction for next-generation large-scale optimisation frameworks.

Article.Title: Causal machine learning reveals heterogeneous effects of loss versus gain framing on retirement savings
Article.Authors: Bösch K.; Müller O.; Weinmann M.; Feuerriegel S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abstract: As Western countries face rapidly aging populations, insufficient retirement savings threaten individual financial security and the sustainability of social welfare systems. Behavioral interventions such as loss–gain message framing are often proposed as scalable solutions, yet evidence on their effectiveness is mixed, largely because little is known about when and for whom they work. We analyze heterogeneity in the effects of loss–gain framing on real-life, high-stakes retirement saving decisions. In a large-scale randomized field experiment ( $$N = 22{,}919$$ ) with a European retirement savings company, individuals were randomized to loss- or gain-framed reminders designed to increase participation (extensive margin) and savings amount (intensive margin). Using causal machine learning, we estimate heterogeneous treatment effects across socioeconomic characteristics and validate them in a second, independent experiment ( $$N = 18{,}288$$ ). In this validation experiment, for the 25% most responsive to loss framing, conversion is estimated to rise by 9.4 percentage points relative to gain framing, whereas for the 25% most responsive to gain framing it is expected to fall by 8.4 points. For savings amount, we estimate that loss framing raises contributions for 64% of contributors (by €737 on average) but backfires for the rest (by €615 on average). Overall, a personalized targeting policy based on causal machine learning is expected to increase participation by 51% (from 4.53% to 6.86%) and average savings by 18% (from €2,062 to €2,442 per converted customer) relative to uniform loss framing.

Article.Title: Modeling afforestation suitability in the Cross-Niger transition forest through remote sensing and analytical hierarchy process to advance global goals
Article.Authors: Enoh M.; Enoh E.; Chiemelu N.; Okereke C.
Article.Abstract: Afforestation is a crucial strategy for conserving biodiversity, mitigating climate change, and preventing land degradation to accomplish Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.2. It is the process of establishing forests in previously unforested areas. Accordingly, the study integrates remote sensing and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP) to identify optimal sites for afforestation suitability that support SDGs within the Cross Niger transition forest. It combined sustainable factors or criteria such as land use/land cover, erodibility, soil, rainfall, aspect, slope, elevation, distance to river, distance to road, NDVI, land surface temperature, drainage density, and human disturbance index to model afforestation suitability maps. AHP was employed to assign weights to these factors, for normalization and validation with the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The final afforestation suitability map was classified as very low (1501.503 km 2 ), low (5297.648 km 2 ), moderate (6971.094 km 2 ), high (5178.869 km 2 ), and very high (2640.442 km 2 ) afforestation suitability. The AUC-ROC value of 0.970 demonstrates that the model has excellent predictive accuracy for afforestation suitability. The study emphasizes the relevance of integrating remote sensing and AHP for well-informed decision-making for afforestation initiatives, thereby supporting global goals including SDG 15.2 within the study area.

Article.Title: Optimizing environmental sensing on public transport to cover broader demographics in Amsterdam
Article.Authors: Koljenšić P.; Venverloo T.; Vrijhoef R.; Duarte F.; Ratti C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban senrsing systems often have uneven spatial coverage, with sensors concentrated in few areas, reinforcing social and environmental inequalities. This study explores how public transport vehicles can serve as mobile environmental sensors not only to increase the spatial coverage of sensing strategies but also to create a fairer and adaptive monitoring system. Using Amsterdam as a case study, we combine GPS locations of public transit vehicle data with 100 × 100 m sociodemographic data to assess and optimize fair sensing coverage. Our method selects the minimum number of vehicles to balance demographic fairness, spatial reach, and temporal frequency. Results show that six vehicles operating during one day can ‘fairly’ represent 17.6% of residents within the applied direct-sensing range, compared with 0.2% for the six static PM₂.₅ sensors deployed in Amsterdam. By redistributing mobile sensors, cities can move from unequal monitoring toward an equitable, city-wide environmental sensing framework.

Article.Title: Heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia incidence in a Chinese cohort
Article.Authors: Fei Z.; Zhang Y.; Pan Y.; Jin X.; Li F.; Luo T.; Shi L.; Zeng J.
Article.Abstract: Heatwaves are increasingly frequent due to climate change, yet their association with respiratory sarcopenia remains underexplored. We aimed to examine the association between heatwave exposure and incident respiratory sarcopenia in a Chinese cohort, identify potentially susceptible subpopulations, and evaluate the robustness of the findings across alternative exposure definitions. In a prospective cohort study of Chinese adults from 2011 to 2015, heatwave exposure was assessed at the city level as the difference in heatwave frequency and days between 2011 and 2015 across 12 definitions (HW01-HW12). Participants free of respiratory sarcopenia at baseline were followed to identify incident cases. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for the association between heatwave exposure and respiratory sarcopenia. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, BMI, geographic region, and chronic lung disease status, and sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the results. Among 1984 participants, 15.7% developed respiratory sarcopenia by 2015. Greater heatwave frequency was associated with higher odds of respiratory sarcopenia in five definitions, and more heatwave days were associated with higher odds across eleven definitions. Associations appeared stronger among participants with BMI < 23 and those with chronic lung disease, while no clear effect modification was observed by age, sex, or region. Sensitivity analyses yielded broadly consistent results. Heatwave exposure was associated with higher odds of incident PEFR-based respiratory sarcopenia in Chinese adults, particularly among those with low BMI or chronic lung disease. These findings support further research on environmental heat exposure and respiratory muscle-related health, while limitations related to exposure misclassification, residual environmental confounding, and indirect outcome measurement should be considered.

Article.Title: Cervical cancer on-site mass-screening device utilizing multiple biomarkers in Swab samples for surveillance in the resource limited areas of India
Article.Authors: Chowdhary R.; Khurana U.; Halder A.; Dwarakanath S.; Kumar S.; Kaore S.; Jadhav A.; Goel S.; Kapoor N.; Lokhande S.; Rozatkar A.; Kumar A.; Mukherjee D.; Nagar N.; Purohit R.; Yadav M.; Patil V.; Ray S.; Kanwar J.
Article.Abstract: At the World Health Assembly in August 2020, a target was set to eradicate cervical cancer globally by 2030 (incidence < 4/100,000) with 90% vaccination coverage, 70% screening coverage, and 90% treatment coverage. India has a worrying prevalence of between 6 and 30 percent, due to HPV infections and low awareness in rural areas. HPV infections and cervical cancer disease development window period is anytime between 6 and 20 years. Thus mass screening of the population will play a very crucial role. KayaCervi, a lab-free, point-of-care mass screening device based on fluorescence EEM technology, consisting of a cartridge, a reader and a microchip was clinically validated in the study. Initially, ten biomarkers were compared using ELISA and Pap smear. Four (p16INK4a, Ki 67, HPV16, HPV18) were selected. Swab validation was performed with cohorts’ of 200 hospital patients and 800 healthy community females, benchmarked against LBC to optimize sensitivity and ensure high specificity. The community-based validation study was to evaluate the performance of the device as a mass-screening tool among apparently healthy women. In such settings, the majority of participants are disease-negative, and high specificity is essential to minimize false-positive results, unnecessary referrals, psychological distress, and healthcare costs. Sensitivity was measured during the standardization phase by screening participants and confirmed positive cases. Initial findings used biomarkers p16NK4A, Ki67, HPV16, and HPV18 to categorize women into high, moderate, and low risk. The design of the cartridge ensured efficient sample capture and quantification, integrating mechanisms to correct for various light wavelengths during analysis. In community-based evaluation (N = 801), the device demonstrated an overall agreement of 98.0% with the reference standard. Cohen's kappa coefficient was 0.545, indicating moderate agreement beyond chance. The device achieved 100% sensitivity, 98.0% specificity, 38.5% positive predictive value, 100% negative predictive value, and 98.0% overall accuracy and identified high percentage of infections in the apparently healthy women comparable to the liquid based cytology reading done for the relative cellular changes. This study validated KayaCervi, a portable, laboratory-independent point-of-care diagnostic device developed to address India's high burden of cervical cancer. The device integrates a fluorescence-based detection platform with a four-target biomarker panel comprising p16INK4a, Ki-67, HPV16, and HPV18, achieving a specificity of 86–90% in community-based rural screening. As a rapid, low-cost, and user-friendly screening tool, KayaCervi has the potential to democratize access to cervical cancer screening by overcoming barriers related to laboratory infrastructure, trained personnel, and patient follow-up. Further, it include the need for larger, prospective, multicenter studies involving geographically diverse populations, with the biomarker panel and diagnostic thresholds predefined before evaluation and with an appropriate independently established reference standard. Such studies will be essential to confirm the reproducibility, generalizability, diagnostic performance, clinical utility and implementation feasibility of KayaCervi before large-scale deployment. Its suitability for decentralized, large-scale population screening is particularly important given the prolonged natural history of cervical carcinogenesis, where persistent HPV infection may take 15–20 years to progress to invasive cancer, providing a critical window for early detection and timely intervention. This highlights the public health significance by emphasizing the long preclinical phase and the opportunity for early intervention.

Article.Title: Training-corpus overlap and evaluation protocol constrain measured gains in a fine-tuned clinical language model
Article.Authors: Agha A.; Anwar E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned medical language models are frequently assessed using public question-answering benchmarks, which may overlap with their training data. We re-evaluated an 8.2-billion-parameter QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-8B under a fixed generative chain-of-thought harness and compared eight benchmarks against its 97,041-item fine-tuning corpus using 13-gram, exact-stem and longest-common-subsequence matching. Exact-stem overlap exceeded 70% for PubMedQA, MedQA and MMLU Professional Medicine, making those scores unsuitable for capability claims, while MedMCQA, evaluated on a held-out split, was effectively unflagged. On several overlapping benchmarks the unmodified parent checkpoint matched or exceeded the fine-tune, significantly so on MedQA. On the 1,838 MedXpertQA items not flagged by exact-stem matching, the fine-tune scored 20.8% against 15.6% for its parent, a paired gain of 5.2 percentage points (McNemar exact P = 7.9 × 10⁻⁷), against an originally reported 7.1. A bundled ablation, in which reasoning traces, sampling weights, curriculum staging, token exposure and output-format supervision differed simultaneously, preserved approximately 70% of the observed improvement. The remaining 1.6-point difference was not statistically significant ( P = 0.175) and cannot be attributed to any single component. The evaluation protocol and the overlap of the training corpus limit the scope of measurable outcomes in these benchmarks.

Article.Title: Identifiability assessment and physics-informed residual machine learning for calculated Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X thermodynamics (X = Mo, Hf)
Article.Authors: Yasin M.; Yahya A.; Bulay-Og L.; Quimada N.; Albina D.; Bajuyo J.; Muhammad Y.; Assiimwe E.; Badruddin I.
Article.Abstract: Calculated alloy properties can produce misleading measures of machine-learning accuracy when the prediction target is generated by the same equation used as the model prior. This study examines that dependence in 140 Ti–Zr–Nb–Ta–X records (X = Mo, Hf), reduced to 129 unique compositions. The tabulated mixing enthalpies agree with a fixed regular-solution prior to within rounding precision. With complete elemental-enrichment trajectories withheld in turn, the prior and a regularized residual learner both give an RMSE of 0.00285 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) ; the maximum learned correction on the candidate grid is \(1.18\times 10^{-6}\) kJ mol \(^{-1}\) . This agreement will be inherited from the analytical prior and will not be an independent physical validation or measurable improvement in accuracy of machine learning. In the other hand, the composition-only support vector regression changes from the RMSE of 0.0202 (shuffled validation) to 1.5687 kJ mol \(^{-1}\) (omitting a complete enrichment trajectory). The features of each pair are ranked with 12 for 15 in post hoc singular-value analysis. There are two null directions, one being the absence of the Mo–Hf interaction, and two others being sampled interaction. There are 3051 possible compositions of the grid, of which 3005 satisfy the empirical thermodynamic criteria, 126 satisfy both proposed geometric restrictions, and 36 satisfy both restrictions and the empirical thermodynamic criteria and form a resulting Pareto set. The global equal-weight compromise is Ti \(_{15}\) Zr \(_{15}\) Nb \(_{25}\) Ta \(_{15}\) Mo \(_{30}\) . The fact that the calculations were performed with fixed priors is reflected in the results of the sensitivity tests and in the 300 interior compositions separately produced, which indicate that the geometric restrictions do not guarantee the reliability of the calculations. Controlled synthetic tests distinguish a learnable smooth deviation from unpredictable point offsets. The contribution is a reproducible assessment of analytical dependence, validation design and coefficient identifiability in a deterministic dataset. Biomedical suitability is not evaluated.

Article.Title: Proteomics-identified serum ROBO4 and VCAM-1 enable robust diagnosis and prognosis-associated biomarkers in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Lin H.; Geng L.; Li M.; Zhang Z.; Wu X.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: Early diagnosis and prognosis assessment of colorectal cancer (CRC) require more effective biomarkers. Using data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, we analyzed serum samples from CRC, colorectal adenoma, and healthy control groups, identifying 50 differentially expressed proteins including ROBO4 and VCAM-1. These candidate biomarkers were further validated by ELISA in an independent cohort of 300 participants (100 per group). Serum levels of ROBO4 and VCAM-1 were significantly elevated in CRC patients, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance (AUCs: 0.886 and 0.871, respectively) compared to conventional markers CA199 (AUC = 0.757) and CEA (AUC = 0.808). Both markers were significantly associated with clinical stage and lymph node metastasis. A nomogram integrating all four markers achieved excellent diagnostic ability (AUC = 0.969). Public database analysis confirmed that high expression of ROBO4 and VCAM-1 significantly correlated with poor overall survival. This study identifies and validates serum ROBO4 and VCAM-1 as promising diagnostic and prognosis-associated biomarkers for CRC through proteomic screening and large-scale cohort validation, supporting their potential utility for CRC detection and risk assessment.

Article.Title: Characterization of plasmodium SEY1, an essential dynamin-like GTPase and potential anti-malarial druggable target
Article.Authors: Carolino K.; Blauwkamp J.; Bottome A.; Ghidelli-Disse S.; De Souza M.; Harmon E.; DeRocher A.; Morano A.; Chen D.; Farringer M.; Farre J.; Lafuente-Monasterio M.; Wirth D.; Van Voorhis W.; Absalon S.; Gamo F.; Dvorin J.; Winzeler E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In some species, SEY1 is a predicted essential dynamin-like GTPase that is implicated in homotypic fusion of endoplasmic reticulum membranes. SEY1 family members are conserved among eukaryotic pathogens, but they show minimal similarity to human atlastins. Here, we characterize Plasmodium SEY1 proteins. Through conditional knockdown and epitope tagging studies in P. falciparum, we demonstrate that SEY1 is essential, localizes within the endoplasmic reticulum, and its disruption leads to defects in endoplasmic reticulum morphology. We show that P. vivax SEY1 can be recombinantly expressed as a soluble truncated isoform. This protein maintains its catalytic activity and ability to dimerize. It also possesses a moderate K d for GTP and is amenable to high throughput inhibition studies. Our data show that SEY1 is a new and attractive druggable and assayable target that is conserved across Plasmodium species.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanism of preoperative autologous blood donation and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients
Article.Authors: Chen X.; Tao H.; Xu J.; Wang J.; You L.; Wu M.; Zhang Y.; Guo J.
Article.Abstract: Type-2 diabetes (T2D) is prevalent and significantly impacts the people’s health. At present, there is no specific treatment to prevent the progression of T2D. Furthermore, the clear mechanism of T2D remains unknown. The present study aims to clarify the mechanism of preoperative autologous blood donation (PABD) and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients through regulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. The present study was conducted to clarify the molecular mechanism of T2D. The general data and blood specimens were obtained from T2D patients. Then, the apoptosis and viability were evaluated. Finally, western blot, flow cytometry assay, immunofluorescence assay, and CCK-8 assay were performed to determine the molecular mechanisms of PABD and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution in improving blood-derived PBMCss in diabetic patients through regulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. The present study revealed that PABD and the modified blood-derived PBMCs preservation solution improved T2D patients by downregulating the ChREBP-HMGB1-Nrf2 pathway. This potential target would be of value in alleviating T2D progression. Our findings suggest that dysregulation of the ChREBP–HMGB1–Nrf2 axis may be associated with diabetic pathophysiology, although the precise role of Nrf2 appears to be context-dependent.

Article.Title: Reinforcement learning based predefined-time synchronization control for competitive neural networks
Article.Authors: Yin C.; Saleem N.; Riaz S.; Afzal F.
Article.Abstract: To optimize the comprehensive performance of competitive neural networks while strictly prescribing the transient behavior and upper bound of the synchronization error convergence time, this paper proposes a performance-guaranteed optimal synchronization control strategy based on reinforcement learning. Initially, a prescribed performance constraint function is employed to confine the synchronization tracking error within desired bounds. Balancing the minimization of synchronization errors and energy consumption, a performance-guaranteed optimal controller is formulated. To accelerate convergence, an approach law featuring predefined-time convergence characteristics is integrated into the controller framework. Furthermore, to address model uncertainties embedded in the synchronization error dynamics, a neural network approximator is utilized, thereby broadening the controller''s applicability. A reinforcement learning algorithm is then deployed to approximate the gradient function within the optimal controller, significantly reducing computational complexity. Theoretical analysis rigorously establishes the predefined-time convergence of the closed-loop system. Distinct from conventional RL methods, an adaptive law with predefined-time convergence is constructed for updating the RL network weights, thereby enhancing algorithmic efficiency. Finally, numerical simulations validate the efficacy and superior performance of the proposed control scheme.

Article.Title: Absent vestibular evoked myogenic potentials and graviception cofactors in adults with diabetes
Article.Authors: Jáuregui-Renaud K.; Miguel-Puga J.; García-López A.; Tirado-Mondragón M.; González-Carrasco L.
Article.Abstract: This study was designed to explore the clinical characteristics (including quadriceps strength) of 166 adults (28–80 years old) with diabetes who have either present or absent bilateral otolith reflex responses by Vestibular Evoked Myogenic Potentials (VEMPs), and its relation to graviception by the Subjective Visual Vertical (S.V.V.). After retinoscopy, electromyography, audiology, vestibular function and quadriceps strength evaluations, assessments were performed on ocular and cervical VEMPs, and estimation of S.V.V., during static condition and on-axis/ off-axis rotation (utricle/ semicircular canal stimulation). 43.9% participants had absent ocular VEMPs, which were not related to on-axis/ off-axis estimations, but to the quadriceps strength; 5.4% participants had absent cervical VEMPs. The S.V.V. during on-axis and off-axis rotation showed no linear relation to present/absent VEMPs, but to static S.V.V. standard deviation (precision), and to an interaction among gender, high blood pressure and dyslipidemia. In conclusion, in adults with diabetes, metabolic compromise and macrovascular factors might contribute to otolith dysfunction; while the presence/absence of ocular VEMPs can be dissociated from the presence/absence of cervical VEMPs and from graviception during utricle/semicircular canal stimulation.

Article.Title: Insecticidal activity of the alkaloid oxymatrine on Atta sexdens workers (Hymenoptera: Formicidae)
Article.Authors: de Melo Souza T.; Castellani M.; Forti L.; da Silva Camargo R.; de Matos C.; da Silva E.; Sabattini J.; dede Cássia Antunes LimaPaula R.; Moreira A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Leaf-cutting ants of the genus Atta are traditionally controlled using synthetic insecticides, which raise environmental concerns. Botanical compounds have therefore been investigated as alternative control agents. Four concentrations (0.01%, 0.03%, 0.05%, and 0.1%) were tested, along with a negative control and a positive control (0.1% sulfluramid). Oxymatrine induced delayed mortality in A. sexdens workers; however, none of the tested concentrations reached the regulatory efficacy threshold required for bait-based control. Article.Authors: Zhu H.; Zhang J.; Xu X.; Lv Y.; Lu C.; Hao Q.; Huang J.; Peng M.; Wang J.; Ouyang K.; Shu Z.; Song S.; Li X.; Xiao M.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexists with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but hepatocentric case-finding remains underexplored. Eight predictors selected by Boruta and LASSO were used to compare logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and XGBoost. XGBoost was retained as the reference implementation for TreeSHAP interpretation and probability presentation, not because of demonstrated algorithmic superiority. The model incorporated age, triglycerides, controlled attenuation parameter, liver stiffness measurement, ALT, AST, hsCRP, and eGFR. This framework may help prioritize confirmatory glycemic testing but requires external validation and recalibration before clinical use.

Article.Title: Comprehensive genome-wide identification and expression profiling of WRKY transcription factors in Avena sativa under abiotic stresses and phytohormone treatments
Article.Authors: Waswani H.; Jha D.; Dey N.; Ranjan R.
Article.Abstract: WRKY transcription factors are key regulators of plant stress responses and phytohormone signaling; yet, their involvement in stress response in Avena sativa L. is still insufficiently explored. We found 167 WRKY genes ( AsWRKYs ) in the oat genome. Phylogenetic analysis categorized these into three primary groups (I–III), with Group II further subdivided into five subgroups (IIa–IIe). Chromosomal mapping revealed an unequal distribution across the 21 chromosomes, with chromosome 5 harbouring the most genes. Analyses of gene structure and conserved motifs confirmed the presence of the WRKY domain and revealed subgroup-specific diversification. The promoter study revealed various stress- and hormone-responsive cis-regulatory elements, including ABRE, CGTCA, TGACG, MYB, and W-box motifs. Collinearity research revealed that segmental duplication is the principal driver for the proliferation of AsWRKY genes, with duplicated gene pairs demonstrating significant purifying selection. Expression profiling revealed tissue-specific patterns, with several AsWRKY genes ( AsWRKY19 , AsWRKY66 , AsWRKY92 , AsWRKY98 , AsWRKY125 , AsWRKY146 , and AsWRKY156 ) showing significant induction under abiotic stress and in response to phytohormones, including abscisic acid, methyl jasmonate, salicylic acid, and gibberellic acid. Structural modelling validated the conserved β-sheet-rich WRKY structure, whereas protein-protein interaction research indicated their participation in stress-responsive regulatory networks. These findings elucidate the evolution and functional roles of WRKY transcription factors in oats.

Article.Title: Growth and nutrient uptake enhancement of Bambara groundnut under drought stress as impacted by Bradyrhizobium japonicum and Bacillus subtilis co-inoculation
Article.Authors: Udeh E.; Nyila M.; Kanu S.; Kalu C.; Tekere M.; Mohale K.
Article.Abstract: Although Bambara groundnut (food security crop) is relatively drought-tolerant, water stress can still adversely affect its growth, physiological performance, and nutrient uptake. Enhancing nutrient acquisition under drought conditions is therefore essential for improving its productivity. This study evaluated the effects of B. japonicum and B. subtilis BD234 co-inoculation on growth, biomass production and nutrient uptake by landraces of Bambara groundnut under simulated drought conditions. A greenhouse experiment was conducted using a completely randomized design in a 5 × 3 × 2 factorial arrangement with four replicates. Treatments included i) inoculation with B. subtilis BD234 alone, ii) inoculation with B. japonicum alone , iii) co-inoculation with both microbial strains, iv) ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃) as a positive control, and v) a non-inoculated control. The drought stress treatment was imposed at three levels: 100% field capacity (well-watered), 50% field capacity (moderate stress), and 25% field capacity (severe stress), using two Bambara groundnut landraces (red and cream). Co-inoculation with B. japonicum and B. subtilis BD234 had a significant effect ( p < 0.05) on growth, biomass production and nutrients accumulation in shoots of Bambara groundnut under drought stress and landrace response was significant, with the red landrace showing superior adaptation compared to the cream landrace. Co-inoculated plants were taller with more leaves, longer roots, and higher biomass production. Additionally, drought stress influenced nutrient uptake and the associations among them and landrace response was also significant. Under well-watered conditions, co-inoculation enhanced phosphorus (P) uptake by 67% and 61% in the red and cream landraces, respectively, compared to their respective uninoculated controls, while under severe drought stress, increases of 14% and 17% were recorded for the red and cream landraces, respectively. Likewise, under moderate drought conditions, co-inoculation enhanced Ca absorption by 65% and 64% in shoots of the red and cream landraces (respectively) compared to uninoculated controls. Co-inoculation markedly improved uptake of both macro-nutrients (P, K, Ca, Mg) and micro-/trace elements (Na, Cu, Mn, Fe, and B) in shoots of Bambara groundnut landraces subjected to simulated drought stress. These findings imply that combined microbial inoculation can be a viable, sustainable strategy to improve drought resilience and nutrient use efficiency in Bambara groundnut cultivation, particularly when selecting drought-tolerant landraces.

Article.Authors: Sawaragi E.; Akita R.; Yamanaka H.; Sakamoto M.; Miwa S.; Kato S.; Yamada Y.; Nagatani S.; Yamaoka T.; Demura S.; Morimoto N.
Article.Abstract: High hydrostatic pressure (HHP) is a non-thermal cell-inactivation method that may permit reuse of anatomically matched autologous tissues. We investigated whether selected biological, histological, surface-morphological, and local mechanical properties of bone remain measurable after HHP processing. Recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 (rhBMP-2) was subjected to HHP, heat, or liquid-nitrogen treatment, and its activity was assessed by alkaline phosphatase staining in MC3T3-E1 cells. In two independent experiments, normalized ALP-positive areas after HHP or liquid-nitrogen treatment were numerically similar to those obtained with untreated rhBMP-2, whereas lower values were observed after heat treatment, particularly at 80 °C. In a rat calvarial reimplantation model, HHP treatment showed no consistent adverse pattern across mineralized tissue volume, graft mobility, graft–host fusion, histomorphometric, or CD31-based vascular measurements. A time-specific difference in red-stained bone area was detected at 12 weeks. Qualitative scanning electron microscopy showed no apparent surface alteration after HHP, whereas the fibrillar surface architecture appeared less distinct after 80 °C heating and autoclaving. Vickers microhardness did not differ significantly among the principal treatment groups. These findings provide preclinical feasibility data supporting further evaluation of HHP as a non-thermal processing approach for anatomically matched autologous bone, while further studies are required to establish oncologic safety and clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
Article.Authors: Nejat H.; Westerberg J.; Maier A.; Spencer-Smith J.; Bastos A.
Article.Abstract: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve. Here, we describe a local multi-LLM pipeline for ontology-constrained literature synthesis. The pipeline reads papers, extracts evidence, incorporates figure descriptions, assembles constrained prompts, and validates outputs against an expert glossary. We defined a predictive-coding glossary of thirty-six concepts grouped into three hypotheses: predictive suppression, feedforward error propagation, and ubiquity. A council of ten local language models scored 31 studies across local and global oddball contexts. This enabled pairwise study-agreement analysis, cross-model comparison, and three-dimensional hypothesis-space mapping. Agreement was stronger for local than global oddball contexts, particularly for feedforward error propagation. Hypothesis-space temperature was lower for local oddball contexts and higher for global oddball contexts, indicating greater dispersion in the latter. These results show that local multi-LLM councils can produce auditable disagreement measurements that map heterogeneous literatures into quantitative evidence spaces.

Article.Title: Assessing household resilience to climate change using resilience index approach in southwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Abafogi M.; Kebebew Z.; Gemeda D.
Article.Abstract: Climate change significantly affects rain-fed dependent economies, particularly those of smallholder farmers. This study evaluates climate-resilient approaches among smallholder farmers in south-western Ethiopia using a composite climate resilience index (CRI). A mixed-methods approach was used, combining household surveys (n = 381), key informant interviews (KIIs), and focus group discussions (FGDs) in Chora Boter and Limmu Seka districts. Chi-square tests and principal component analysis (PCA) were used to calculate the CRI across five pillars: income and food access, assets, access to basic services, social safety nets, and adaptive capacity. Results showed that 42.3% of households had low resilience, 32.0% moderate resilience, and 25.7% high resilience. Adaptive capacity and asset ownership were the strongest predictors of household resilience. Multiple regression showed that education levels (β = 0.234, p < 0.001); access to climate information (β = 0.212, p < 0.001); landholding size (β = 0.198, p < 0.001); contact with extension officers (β = 0.186, p < 0.001); social networks (β = 0.167, p < 0.001); and credit availability (β = 0.145, p = 0.002) significantly increased resilience ( p < 0.001). Female-headed households were significantly less resilient (β = − 0.134, p = 0.002). Thus, targeted interventions should strengthen adaptive capacity and asset ownership.

Article.Authors: da Silva A.; de Oliveira Pereira M.; Pereira L.; da Silva Lima J.; dos Santos Lucas P.; Cabral J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seed dormancy occurs as a mechanism of adaptation to the environment. Dormancy can be exogenous and/or endogenous, making it difficult to obtain high-quality seedlings, as occurs in the Passiflora genus. Therefore, the objective of this study was to evaluate methods for overcoming dormancy in sour yellow passion fruit seeds of BRS Sol do cerrado cv. BRS SC1. The hybrid seeds were subjected to the following treatments: (1) control; (2) immersion in distilled water at 5 °C for 10 min; (3) immersion in distilled water at 80 °C for 10 min; (4) immersion in Stimulate ® at 40 mg L −1 gibberellic acid for 2 h; and (5) immersion in Stimulate ® at 50 mg L −1 gibberellic acid for 2 h, with and without manual scarification, in a 2 × 5 fatorial arrangement with each treatment containing 3 replicates, consisting of thirty seeds each. The following variables were evaluated: germination percentage, time to 50% germination (T50), germination speed index (GSI), average shoot length, roots and index of developed seedlings. Manual scarification of sour yellow passion fruit seeds Sol do Cerrado cv. BRS SC1 results in dormancy breaking, with a relatively high germination percentage (64%), germination speed index (1.2) and seedling development, therefore, it is recommended for improving the performance of seeds from this cultivar, as it accelerates and standardizes germination.

Article.Authors: Shadbolt J.; Schreiber M.; Russell J.; Waugh R.; Houston K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heavy metals act as essential metalloprotein cofactors in numerous physiological processes but can become toxic when non-essential metals accumulate or when essential metals are in excess. As plants continuously encounter heavy metals through their roots, they have evolved complex homeostatic mechanisms to regulate metal uptake and distribution. The Heavy Metal ATPase ( HMA ) gene family encodes a group of heavy metal transporting P-type ATPases that have been linked to stress resistance and nutrient supply. Here, we used a bioinformatics approach to identify and characterise 13 HMA genes containing characteristic P 1B -type ATPase domains and motifs in the barley Morex V3 reference genome. The genes are located on five of the seven barley chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that they cluster into five sub-clades, including one clade containing only barley. Expression profiling across multiple datasets showed distinct temporal and tissue-specific expression patterns among HvHMA s, with several members exhibiting significant transcriptional responses to specific biotic and abiotic stresses. By utilising recently available pan-transcriptomic and pan-genomic resources, we have identified substantial allelic diversity and inter-accession variation in HvHMA s. Our findings suggest that HvHMA s have functions extending beyond canonical heavy metal homeostasis and warrant further investigation for their potential roles in broader physiological and stress-related processes.

Article.Title: Implementation methodologies and socio-technical dynamics as drivers of analytics adoption in ERP systems
Article.Authors: Solano M.; Cruz J.
Article.Abstract: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems increasingly embed Business Intelligence and Analytics (BI&A) capabilities, including real-time dashboards, key performance indicators, and predictive and artificial intelligence (AI) functions. These capabilities often remain underused in implementation projects that prioritize transactional stabilization. Prior studies have explained ERP and analytics adoption mainly through the Technology, Organization, and Environment (TOE) framework and Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory, with limited attention to how implementation processes shape analytical activation. This study examines how implementation methodologies and socio-technical dynamics influence BI&A adoption in ERP systems. Drawing on TOE, DOI, and Actor-Network Theory (ANT), it uses a qualitative multiple-case design based on 43 semi-structured interviews with ERP partners, client organizations, vendors, and industry association representatives in Colombia, combining thematic analysis, theory-based pattern matching, and exploratory network modeling of two partner cases (15 and 14 nodes). The findings suggest that agile and hybrid methodologies, as enacted by implementation partners, are associated with earlier BI&A integration, whereas waterfall-oriented sequencing tends to defer analytical activation. Analytical roles showed limited brokerage over key implementation decisions. The study extends ERP adoption research by showing how methodological sequencing and actor positioning shape whether embedded analytics are activated or remain dormant.

Article.Title: Hybrid feature selection for dimensionality reduction while preserving predictive performance in breast cancer diagnosis
Article.Authors: Mishra S.; Dhakad B.; Ojha S.; Sharma K.; Singh V.; Sharma C.; Tiwari V.
Article.Abstract: Globally, Breast Cancer (BC) is the most common type of cancer among women, which is growing at a high rate. Recently, AI/ML-assisted algorithms have most frequently utilised to accurately, efficiently, and early detection of diseases in healthcare. Though many existing techniques rely on high dimensional features and analysis of performance-feature trade-offs are rarely addressed. This work proposes a novel Hybrid Machine Learning (HML) framework to address three key contributions. Firstly, a unified framework is proposed which integrates filter and wrapper-based Feature Selection (FS) approaches to enhance their feature relevance and subset optimization. Secondly, it presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of diverse hybrid FS models to identify optimal solutions for efficient and high-performance models. Third key contribution of this work demonstrates a quantitative analysis which clearly presents that optimized FS can significantly reduce dimensionality while preserves or gives comparable model predictive performance. Experimental results reveal that the proposed RF hybrid models give comparable performance with significant features reduced from 30 to 10. In the same manner, DT with hybrid models give comparable performance by using only 6–8 significant features i.e., 73 to 80% feature reduction. It is demonstrated that RF based approaches achieves accuracy nearly 98% whereas DT based approaches obtain accuracy nearly 95% in a single split test. Moreover, the reliability of results is assessed by using 10-fold cross-validation with 95% confidence interval and Wilcoxon statistical test. Feature importance analysis is demonstrated to strengthen interpretability as significant features contributes more into model decisions and accuracy. Consequently, the proposed hybrid framework achieves an optimal balance between performance, interpretability, and computational efficiency thereby offers a scalable and practical solution for BC diagnostics. However, this work is limited for subgroup specific performance and needs validation on large, independent, and diverge datasets.

Article.Title: Association of admission acid-base phenotypes with delirium in cardiac critical illness: a multicenter cohort study
Article.Authors: Hwang J.; Jang W.; Kim B.; Chun K.; Kim J.; Park I.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: Acid-base disturbances frequently complicate cardiac critical illness. Although their associations with mortality have been described, their relationship with neurologic complications, particularly delirium, remains poorly defined. We analyzed data from 1259 adults with cardiac critical illness enrolled in an eight-center intensive care unit (ICU) registry (2011–2025). Using a physiological Boston approach, admission arterial blood gas profiles were categorized into six mutually exclusive phenotypes. Sequentially adjusted logistic regression models assessed associations with delirium, and separate adjusted models assessed associations with short-term mortality. Delirium was documented in 555 patients (44.1%). Compared with no acid-base disorder, admission respiratory alkalosis was associated with higher odds of delirium after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.76; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.67–4.54; p < 0.001). The association remained statistically significant after accounting for center-level clustering and ICU admission year (adjusted OR, 2.33; 95% CI, 1.20–4.52; p = 0.012). Each 5-mmHg decrease in PaCO₂ was associated with higher odds of documented delirium in Model 3 (adjusted OR, 1.07; 95% CI, 1.02–1.12; p = 0.004), but the association was not statistically significant after additionally accounting for center and admission year (adjusted OR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.99–1.14; p = 0.078). No other phenotype remained significantly associated with delirium after full adjustment. Although metabolic acidosis had the highest crude ICU (22.6%) and in-hospital (29.8%) mortality, no acid-base phenotype remained significantly associated with mortality after adjustment for illness severity and mechanical circulatory support. Admission respiratory alkalosis was associated with delirium documented during the ICU stay in patients with cardiac critical illness. The continuous PaCO₂ association was less consistent across adjustment models. Residual confounding and uncertainty regarding the temporal sequence preclude causal inference.

Article.Title: Enhancing soil creep index prediction accuracy using optimized XGBoost and LightGBM models with bio-inspired optimization algorithms: SHAP- and LIME-based explanation methods
Article.Authors: Ikram R.; Alizamir M.; Heddam S.; Gholampour A.; Kim S.; Yun S.
Article.Abstract: Soil creep, as a form of long-term deformation, significantly influences the performance of foundations and earth structures. As this deformation develops over time, it can lead to major geotechnical issues such as slope failures, differential ground movement, and excessive settlement. Consequently, accurate estimation of the soil creep index is essential for informed geotechnical decision-making. To address this, the primary aim of this study is to develop precise models for estimating the soil creep index using modern machine learning methods. This study develops fourteen predictive models, including seven based on XGBoost and seven based on LightGBM. These include the standard XGBoost and LightGBM models, as well as their optimized variants enhanced using grey wolf optimizer (GWO), whale optimization algorithm (WOA), bat algorithm (BAT), dragonfly algorithm (DOA), crayfish optimization algorithm (COA), and grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA). To assess the reliability of creep index prediction, the models were evaluated under four separate sets of input variables. In addition, SHAP, LIME, and SelectKBest methods were applied to explore the influence of individual input factors on the prediction outcomes. Each model’s effectiveness was assessed through four principal statistical indicators: the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), correlation coefficient (R), and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE). Based on the RMSE values, the top three hybrid XGBoost models were XGBoost-GOA (RMSE = 0.002259), XGBoost-GWO (RMSE = 0.002273), and XGBoost-COA (RMSE = 0.002316). Among the hybrid LightGBM models, the best performers were LightGBM-BAT (RMSE = 0.003813), LightGBM-GWO (RMSE = 0.003884), and LightGBM-COA (RMSE = 0.003885). For the standalone models, XGBoost (RMSE = 0.003084) outperformed CART (RMSE = 0.003398) and LightGBM (RMSE = 0.003972). The testing results indicate that XGBoost-based models provide a reliable and accurate approach for predicting the soil creep index.

Article.Title: Regional covariation between climate-normalized storm rarity and landslide magnitude in Taiwan is sensitive to rainfall timing
Article.Authors: Liou J.; Chen C.; Tung Y.; Chu F.; Saito H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate-normalized rainfall rarity may facilitate comparisons across climates, but pooled rainfall–landslide associations can obscure regional structure and rainfall timing. We examined 994 reported rainfall-induced landslides in Taiwan (1987–2018) using 2-km hourly precipitation and generalized extreme-value climatologies for 1980–2019. Rainfall rarity ( T max ) was defined as the maximum of 1–72-h duration-specific return periods, not the recurrence interval of an entire storm. Retrospective whole-storm T max was available for 912 records, including 708 with estimated volume. Within 18 selected spatial cells, 16 contained 393 volume-bearing records. Contextual decomposition yielded a positive between-cell rarity–volume coefficient ( β between = 0.945, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.642–1.248), but no detectable positive within-cell association ( β within = − 0.105, 95% CI = − 0.288–0.078). Cell-clustered inference was less decisive. The between-cell coefficient decreased to 0.279 after adjusting for absolute 24-h rainfall and to 0.317 after excluding Typhoon Morakot. When rarity was calculated using only rainfall preceding recorded failure, the positive between-cell association was not recovered ( β between = − 0.276, 95% CI = − 1.115–0.563; 361 volume-bearing records), although analytical populations differed. These findings identify a Morakot-anchored, inventory-specific association that is sensitive to absolute rainfall and exposure timing.

Article.Title: Integrating graph neural networks with urine metabolomics for non-invasive detection of bladder cancer: a multi-centre case–control diagnostic study
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Xu Z.; Zheng S.; Li K.; Wu Q.; Luo Z.
Article.Abstract: Bladder cancer remains a major global health burden, and the stage at which a tumour is found largely determines what follows for the patient. Cystoscopy and urine cytology, the current mainstays, are invasive or insensitive, which keeps the search for accurate non-invasive alternatives open. We therefore asked a narrower question than a screening trial would ask: can a graph-based model separate treatment-naive bladder cancer patients from healthy controls using urinary metabolomic profiles alone? Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry data were acquired for 338 participants (186 patients, 152 controls) at three centres, and 847 reproducible metabolite features passed quality control. Metabolite interaction graphs encoding partial correlations and KEGG pathway co-membership were estimated on training participants only, and a graph attention network (GAT) fusion architecture was trained on the resulting patient-level graphs. Every data-dependent step—quality-control filtering, normalisation, graph estimation, hyperparameter search and selection of the operating threshold—was confined to training and validation data, so that the internal test set and the external cohort were touched once. At the prespecified threshold the model reached an AUROC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.887–0.987), with sensitivity 0.919 (0.781–0.983) and specificity 0.900 (0.735–0.979) in 67 held-out participants, and an AUROC of 0.931 (0.873–0.977) in an independent cohort of 89 participants from a fourth centre. The model ranked above all conventional baselines, although with this sample size none of the pairwise differences survived correction for multiple comparisons, and a control model trained on randomised graph topology performed almost as well. Attention weights, permutation importance, integrated gradients and feature ablation converged on tryptophan catabolism, nucleotide biosynthesis and lipid remodelling. Because cases were histologically confirmed and controls were disease-free volunteers, these results describe case–control diagnostic discrimination; they do not establish detection before clinical presentation, and prospective enrolment of asymptomatic individuals remains necessary before any screening claim can be made.

Article.Title: Effects of corneal cap thickness on corneal morphological and biomechanical properties of rabbits in vivo following SMILE
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Bai H.; Tian M.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the effects of 100 μm and 160 μm corneal cap thicknesses on corneal morphology, endothelial cell density, biomechanics and epithelial thickness in rabbit eyes after SMILE, and to provide experimental reference for clinical surgical parameter selection. Twenty-four New Zealand white rabbits were randomly allocated to a 100-μm corneal cap group (group A) and a 160-μm group (group B), with 12 rabbits in each group and balanced sex distribution (6 males and 6 females in each group). SMILE was performed on the right eye of all rabbits using a uniform VisuMax program with programmed refractive correction of − 4.00 D, an optical zone of 6.50 mm, a cap diameter of 7.60 mm, and an incision at the 120° position with a 45° angle. Corneal morphology (Pentacam), endothelial cell density (specular microscopy), biomechanical properties (Corvis ST), and epithelial thickness (anterior-segment OCT) were measured preoperatively and at 1 week, 1 month and 3 months postoperatively. Between-group comparisons at each time point were performed with independent-samples t-tests; longitudinal trajectories were analyzed with a two-way mixed-design analysis of variance (group as the between-subjects factor; time and the group × time interaction as within-subjects effects). Multiplicity was controlled using the Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure for secondary outcomes. Baseline central endothelial cell density was significantly higher in group B than in group A (2994.42 ± 237.96 vs 2693.60 ± 345.72 cells/mm 2 ; P = 0.021); baseline anterior and posterior Km and anterior chamber volume also differed between groups ( P < 0.05), reflecting imperfect baseline balance in this small randomized cohort, whereas the remaining baseline indicators were comparable. Both groups demonstrated comparable postoperative corneal flattening, with comparable central endothelial cell density throughout the 3-month follow-up. Early postoperative intergroup differences in corneal asphericity and Corvis ST parameters were observed but were largely nominal after false-discovery-rate adjustment. Group B had lower Def Amp Max and higher SSI at 1 and 3 months (FDR-corrected). The group × time interaction was significant for Def Amp Max, IR, SP-A1, SSI, ARTh, and corneal epithelial thickness, indicating different postoperative remodeling trajectories between the two caps. No significant intergroup differences in corneal morphological parameters were detected at 3 months. In this rabbit SMILE model, both 100-μm and 160-μm caps produced comparable postoperative corneal flattening and no significant reduction in central endothelial cell density over the 3-month follow-up. Cap thickness was associated with different postoperative biomechanical and epithelial remodeling trajectories (significant group × time interactions for Def Amp Max, SSI, and epithelial thickness), without affecting corneal morphological outcomes at the final follow-up.

Article.Title: The association between cardiovascular disease and cognitive decline varies by long-term depressive symptom trajectories in older adults
Article.Authors: Bao Y.; Wang S.; Lu Y.; Chang F.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depressive symptoms are established risk factors for cognitive decline in later life, but it remains unclear whether long-term depressive symptom burden modifies the association between CVD and cognitive ageing. We used data from 5423 adults aged 50 years and older in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing between 2004 and 2018. Depressive symptoms were assessed repeatedly using the eight-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, and growth mixture modelling was used to identify long-term symptom trajectories. Linear mixed-effects models examined associations between baseline CVD, depressive symptom trajectories, and changes in global cognition, memory, semantic fluency, and orientation. Three trajectories were identified: low-stable, moderate-stable, and high-stable. Participants with moderate-stable and high-stable depressive symptoms had poorer baseline cognitive performance and faster decline in global cognition, memory, and semantic fluency than those with low-stable symptoms. Baseline CVD was associated with faster cognitive decline, but the CVD-related difference was most evident in the low-stable group and attenuated among participants with higher depressive symptom burden. These findings suggest that persistent depressive symptoms may shape the observable association between CVD and cognitive ageing, highlighting the importance of considering long-term mental health burden in cognitive risk assessment.

Article.Title: Bone age estimation from lateral cephalograms using cervical vertebrae–centered ROIs: a multicenter deep learning study
Article.Authors: Seo H.; Shin J.; Hwang J.
Article.Abstract: This multicenter retrospective study compared cervical vertebrae (CV)-centered region-of-interest input strategies for bone-age estimation from lateral cephalograms and evaluated whether incorporating upper-airway regions provides complementary information, with emphasis on cross-site generalizability. In total, 1,100 paired lateral cephalograms and hand–wrist radiographs (ages 4–18 years) from two institutions were analyzed. The second to fourth cervical vertebrae and upper airway were manually delineated to generate three input strategies: CV masking, combined CV and airway masking, and CV-centered cropping without masking. Reference bone ages were AI-derived surrogate labels obtained from commercial hand–wrist bone-age software. A deep-learning regression model was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, an internal test set, and an external test set. Performance was comparable across strategies under internal evaluation but differed under external validation. Although overall errors increased substantially in the external test set, CV-only masking showed the largest degradation (mean absolute error, 1.91 years); airway-inclusive masking (1.72 years) and unmasked CV-centered cropping (1.67 years) yielded significantly lower errors. Interpretability analyses highlighted mainly cervical vertebral structures. However, Grad-RAM showed prominent airway activation for airway-inclusive inputs. Together, these findings suggest that CV-centered inputs preserving surrounding anatomical context are more robust for cross-site bone-age estimation than strictly vertebra-only masking.

Article.Title: Boundary-weighted supervision and multi-scale context enhancement for greenhouse tomato instance segmentation using YOLO11n-seg
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Xiong J.; Yang M.; Che W.; Wang S.; Zheng J.; Zhan Y.; Ning Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate tomato instance segmentation in greenhouse scenes remains challenging because of fruit occlusion, instance contact, ambiguous boundaries, and the visual similarity between green fruits and leaves. This study presents a lightweight YOLO11n-seg framework that combines a morphology-based shape-boundary-driven (SBD) weighting strategy with the previously proposed CMPRD multi-scale context module. SBD constructs a narrow contour band for each ground-truth instance and increases the contribution of boundary pixels to the mask loss during training without altering the inference graph, whereas CMPRD replaces SPPF near the end of the YOLO11n-seg backbone to enhance multi-scale contextual representation. Across five independent runs on the 128-image validation split (mean ± standard deviation), the combined model increases Mask Recall from \(0.7656\pm 0.0046\) to \(0.7726\pm 0.0039\) and Mask mAP50–95 from \(0.6587\pm 0.0025\) to \(0.6812\pm 0.0026\) relative to YOLO11n-seg, while Mask Precision changes from \(0.7989\pm 0.0037\) to \(0.7961\pm 0.0035\) . In the fixed seed-0 comparison with additional baselines, the larger YOLOv8s-seg and YOLO11s-seg models achieve Mask mAP50–95 values of 0.69161 and 0.69434, respectively, whereas a literature-guided reimplementation of Enhanced YOLO11n-Seg achieves 0.67840 under a comparable lightweight computational budget. On the untouched 161-image official test set, the primary Mask mAP50–95 results, reported as the mean ± standard deviation across all five runs rather than the best-performing run, are \(0.6529\pm 0.0016\) for YOLO11n-seg and \(0.6782\pm 0.0016\) for the proposed model, corresponding to a mean gain of 0.0252 and a paired 95% confidence interval of [0.0227, 0.0277]. Among successfully matched instances with mask IoU \(\ge 0.5\) , Boundary IoU increases from \(0.612\pm 0.004\) to \(0.651\pm 0.003\) , and Boundary F-score increases from \(0.744\pm 0.003\) to \(0.779\pm 0.002\) . On the same validation split and seed-0 development run, a parameter/FLOP-matched convolutional control achieves a Mask mAP50–95 of 0.66530, compared with 0.67007 for CMPRD. The effects of spatial boundary weighting and overall mask-loss scaling are not isolated, and cross-dataset generalization remains unverified.

Article.Title: Lanxangia tsaoko sesquiterpenes inhibit methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by targeting the arginine biosynthesis pathway
Article.Authors: Gu Y.; Tang J.; Chen S.; Dai M.; Pu Z.
Article.Abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), pose a major global health challenge as a difficult-to-treat pathogen. Lanxangia tsaoko is a well-known aromatic herb traditionally used in Chinese medicine. Historically, it has been applied for its antimicrobial and antiparasitic properties, including the treatment of malaria. L . tsaoko essential oil (LEO) exhibit potent anti-MRSA activity both in vitro and in vivo; however, its active components and mechanisms remain unelucidated. We investigated the inhibitory effect and mechanism of bioactive components from LEO on MRSA infection. Bioactive constituents of LEO were retrieved from the literature, and the major bioactive constituents responsible for the anti-MRSA activity were identified through network pharmacology. The antibacterial efficacy of the predicted constituents was subsequently evaluated using in vitro experiments and a mouse model of MRSA infection. Untargeted metabolomics and molecular docking identified potential targets and pathways, which were validated by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting (WB). Notably, five constituents predicted by network pharmacology were all sesquiterpenoids, with trans-farnesol (FAR) exhibiting the strongest anti-MRSA activity (minimum inhibitory concentration = 0.039 mg/mL; minimum bactericidal concentration = 0.078 mg/mL). FAR showed additive effects with antibiotics, inhibited MRSA biofilm formation, and showed preventive efficacy in MRSA-infected mice in vivo. Metabolomics revealed disruption of the arginine biosynthesis pathway, with molecular docking indicating strong binding of FAR to argG and argH. This interaction was further confirmed with RT-qPCR and WB confirming downregulation of argG/argH mRNA in MRSA and upregulation of argininosuccinate synthase (ASS1)/argininosuccinate lyase (ASL) proteins in infected mice. The findings of this study present FAR as the primary active component of LEO, highlighting its potent anti-MRSA effects via the arginine biosynthetic pathway, argG/argH mRNA downregulation in MRSA, and ASS1/ASL upregulation in infected mice.

Article.Title: Modular urban furniture design for young adults’ fragmented time use
Article.Authors: Wu F.; Li C.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: At present, the function of urban furniture is relatively single, which cannot meet the needs of people. In this study, 180 young adults (aged 18–35 years) were interviewed by questionnaires and structured interviews. According to the survey, 86.7% of them want to be configurability, 74.4% focus on the environmental integration, and 76.7% need to use multi-activity support. Based on the above requirements, the study followed the five principles of practicality, economy, aesthetics, modularity and sustainability, and produced a modular urban furniture with a flexible size of 400–500 mm - intelligence landscape seat, and the landscape seat is made of sustainable materials. According to the results of semi-structured interviews, the device can improve the retention intention of users. Through semi-structured interviews, it was found that the retention intention of users was increased compared with that of ordinary seats. Sustainable materials promote the effective implementation of the concept of circular economy in production, procurement and recycling. This study provides theoretical and practical reference for urban furniture design and promoting the sustainable development of public space.

Article.Title: Field-deployable hybrid gravimetry: projecting absolute accuracy across a remote 24 km2 survey via daily quantum calibration
Article.Authors: Shettell N.; Lee K.; Oon F.; Maksimova E.; Chen H.; Dumke R.
Article.Abstract: Hybrid gravimetry combines the mobility of relative gravimeters with the long-term stability of an absolute reference. Following our previous demonstration of this concept under controlled field conditions, we investigate whether quantum-assisted hybrid gravimetry retains its calibration performance during an extended survey under realistic operational constraints. A transportable atomic gravimeter provided routine \(\upmu {\textrm{Gal}}\) -level calibration of two mobile spring gravimeters throughout a seven-day survey spanning 24 km \(^2\) of dense tropical terrain. Despite rainfall, dense canopy, and limited field infrastructure, the atomic reference enabled high-precision asynchronous comparison of relative measurements while suppressing instrumental drift in regions where GPS positioning remained reliable. These results demonstrate that transportable atomic gravimeters can provide practical calibration references for extended geophysical surveys, extending hybrid quantum gravimetry beyond controlled demonstrations toward realistic field deployment.

Article.Title: Magnetic targeting of autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells for knee osteoarthritis: a first-in-human exploratory study
Article.Authors: Kamei N.; Ochi M.; Adachi N.; Ishikawa M.; Nakamae A.; Nekomoto A.; Kawano R.; Tanaka Y.; Hirami N.; Yanada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Knee osteoarthritis lacks disease-modifying therapies, and poor retention of intra-articularly injected mesenchymal stromal cells at cartilage lesions may limit their therapeutic potential. We conducted a physician-initiated, single-center, open-label, first-in-human exploratory trial to assess the safety and feasibility of magnetic targeting–guided delivery of autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells in symptomatic knee osteoarthritis. Five female patients with Kellgren–Lawrence grade 3 osteoarthritis underwent arthroscopic microfracture in areas of full-thickness cartilage loss, followed by intra-articular injection of magnetically labeled autologous bone marrow–derived mesenchymal stromal cells under a ring-shaped electromagnetic device. All patients completed 48 weeks of follow-up. No serious adverse events, tumor formation, abnormal tissue proliferation, or device-related complications were observed. Knee joint effusion was the only adverse event considered potentially related to the investigational cell therapy and resolved without additional treatment. Clinical outcomes showed exploratory improvement trends, including an increase in the mean Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score Quality of Life from 15.0 to 50.0 at 48 weeks. Magnetic resonance imaging showed variable structural changes, whereas second-look arthroscopy demonstrated cartilage-like repair tissue in evaluated cases. These findings indicate that magnetic targeting–guided delivery is a feasible cell-delivery strategy for knee osteoarthritis, with no major safety concerns and exploratory signals of therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Interpretable AI for echocardiography-based early screening of rheumatic heart disease in Ethiopia: a cost-effective strategy to tackle a persistent global health disparity
Article.Authors: Tadesse D.; Mekonnen D.; Gonfa O.; Kebede S.; Waldamichael F.; Debele T.; Mekonnen H.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is a serious condition that develops from untreated streptococcal throat infections and causes long-term damage to the heart valves. Although it is become rare in wealthier countries, it still affects many people in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), like sub-Saharan Africa, where fragmented healthcare infrastructure and limited access to specialized diagnostics exacerbate diagnostic delays. This study presents an interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) framework designed to automate early RHD screening using echocardiographic imaging, with a focus on addressing critical diagnostic gaps in resource-constrained settings such as Ethiopia. Our study explores how Interpretable AI based approach can help identify early signs of RHD using echocardiographic images, primarily mitral regurgitation (MR). Specifically, we focus on detecting mitral regurgitation in two views (A​pical​ ​five chamber (AP5) and Parasternal long axis (PSLAX) views) during the heart’s systolic cycle and measuring the thickness of the anterior mitral valve leaflet (AMVL) from the PSLAX view as part of the old criteria. To do this, we trained and compared two AI models to segment the left atrium (LA) and mitral valve (MV) using annotated echocardiographic datasets. By tracking vol​ume changes in the segmented LA, we identified the frames corresponding to the systolic cycle. To detect MR, which is a key pathological hallmark of RHD, we then overlaid Color Doppler blood flow information on the segmented LA regions of the systolic frames. Additionally, the MV segmentation model was used to measure the AMVL thickness during systole, a critical morphological indicator of chronic valvular damage which was not part of our primary focus. Importantly, this AI framework was developed primarily for the detection of World Heart Federation (WHF) significant MR. While AMVL thickness was examined as an additional morphological parameter, its measurement was performed during sys​tole for methodological convenience and has not been validated for the assessment of mitral stenosis. Furthermore, the framework does not evaluate restricted mitral leaflet motion. Therefore, leaflet thickness measurements should be regarded as exploratory findings and not as diagnostic outputs of the proposed system. Trained on annotated echocardiographic datasets and tested on an independent pilot test set of real-world scans from Ethiopian regional hospitals (patients not seen during training or validation), the AI model demonstrated promis​ing results, achieving precision (1.0), recall (0.7), F1-score (0.82), and accuracy (0.7) metrics that underscore its potential for reliable deployment in low-resource environments. The system’s interpretable design, which visualizes segmentation boundaries, Doppler flow patterns, and anatomical measurements, prioritizes clinical transparency, enabling healthcare workers to validate AI outputs against familiar diagnostic benchmarks. By automating labor-intensive echocardiographic analyses, this AI-driven strat​egy could revolutionize early RHD detection in LMICs, reducing reliance on scarce specialist expertise and paving the way for scalable, cost-effective screening programs. Our findings highlight the transformative role of context-specific AI solutions in bridging global health inequities.

Article.Title: A COI barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods supports biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe
Article.Authors: Sulikowska-Drozd A.; Proćków M.; Kuźnik-Kowalska E.; Maltz T.; Hofman S.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial molluscs are important components of terrestrial ecosystems, yet they remain poorly represented in molecular biodiversity assessments. Although they occur in a wide range of habitats, their inclusion in such studies is constrained by the lack of reliable genetic reference data, particularly in Central Europe. In Poland, despite a well-documented malacofauna comprising approximately 179 species, genetic data remain scarce. At the beginning of our study, 43 species lacked COI sequences in public repositories, while COI sequences from Polish specimens were available for only 11 species. Here, we present the first comprehensive COI DNA barcode reference dataset for Polish land gastropods, supported by expert morphological identification. We analysed 857 sequences representing 177 species occurring in Central Europe, including 21 species not yet recorded from Poland. The BIN approach yielded 291 molecular operational taxonomic units, 105 of which were unique to our dataset. Among putative species represented by at least five sequences, 83% exhibited a barcode gap, although its position varied considerably among the infraorder-level groups. For example, it occurred at approximately 11–20% K2P divergence in Clausilioidei and 5–10% in Limacoidei. This barcode reference dataset provides a valuable resource for land-gastropod identification and DNA-based biodiversity monitoring in Central Europe, including the detection of non-native species and lineages warranting further taxonomic investigation.

Article.Title: Integrated coffee husk biochar and NPSB fertilizer improve bread wheat productivity in acidic soils
Article.Authors: Bekele K.; Zewide I.; Wato T.
Article.Abstract: Bread wheat is an important cereal crop worldwide, but its productivity in acidic soils is constrained by low soil fertility and limited use of effective soil amendments. This study evaluated the agronomic and economic performance of combined coffee husk biochar (CHB) and NPSB blended fertilizer for bread wheat production under limed and unlimed conditions during the 2023 main cropping season. The experiment comprised three CHB rates (2.5, 5, and 7.5 t ha − 1 ) and three NPSB fertilizer rates (50, 100, and 150 kg ha − 1 ), together with positive and negative controls. Treatments were arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications. The interaction between CHB and NPSB significantly affected grain yield. Under limed conditions, the highest grain yield (3.99 t ha − 1 ) was obtained from 5 t ha − 1 CHB combined with 100 kg ha − 1 NPSB, representing a 149% increase over the unfertilized control (1.60 t ha − 1 ). This treatment also resulted in the highest net benefit (276,280 Birr ha − 1 ) and marginal rate of return (22,076%). Under unlimed conditions, the same treatment combination provided the highest net benefit (197,080 Birr ha − 1 ). These findings indicate that the integrated application of 5 t ha − 1 CHB with 100 kg ha − 1 NPSB has promising potential for improving bread wheat productivity and economic returns under the conditions of the study area, particularly when combined with lime. However, because the experiment was conducted at a single location during one cropping season, further multi-location and multi-year studies are needed to validate the consistency and broader applicability of these findings.

Article.Title: Metabolomic profiling and pathway level multiomics integration identify shared stress associated and drug specific responses in the parasitic nematode Anisakis simplex s.s.
Article.Authors: Łopieńska-Biernat E.; Maździarz M.; Polak I.
Article.Abstract: Anthelmintic exposure can perturb multiple cellular processes in parasitic nematodes, but the metabolic response of Anisakis simplex s.s. remains poorly characterized. Here, we generated untargeted metabolomic profiles of L3 larvae exposed for 12 h to albendazole, ivermectin, or pyrantel and integrated these new data at the pathway level with previously reported transcriptomic and treatment-associated single-nucleotide variant (SNV) datasets generated under matched experimental conditions. Fourteen unique LC–MS features were consistently differentially abundant across all three treatments. One shared feature had two alternative Compound Discoverer annotations (5-hydroxylysine and 4-methoxyestrone) and was counted once at the feature level. Shared changes involved membrane lipids, select amino acid related features, folate/one carbon associated metabolites, and ribose 1-phosphate. These patterns were accompanied by treatment specific quantitative differences; under the concentrations and exposure conditions used, albendazole was associated with the broadest metabolomic alteration. Curated, treatment matched pathway level co-mapping identified convergence in amino acid, purine, tryptophan, and arachidonic acid pathways. No direct gene metabolite correlations were calculated, and annotation dependent low confidence connections were excluded from the curated integration. Overall, the data identify a shared metabolic phenotype together with treatment specific molecular perturbations, involving lipid homeostasis, select amino acid and nucleotide pathways, and redox associated processes, rather than a coordinated hierarchical detoxification or resistance program.
