Article.Title: A lightweight dual-domain attention YOLO for small object detection in remote sensing images
Article.Authors: Qingxue L.; Guoming W.; Wen X.; Dongyan W.
Article.Abstract: Small object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging due to limited pixel representation, complex background interference, and the requirement for computationally efficient lightweight models. To address these issues, this paper proposes LDA-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework built upon YOLOv8 that integrates adaptive refinement of multi-level features and dual-domain attention to enhance fine-grained perception while maintaining low computational cost. Specifically, we design a Selective Gated Convolution (SGConv) module that adopts a multi-branch convolutional structure with ECA-based channel reweighting to selectively emphasize informative feature responses while suppressing redundant activation. An Improved C2f (IC2f) block is further constructed to strengthen short-range feature reuse and preserve detailed structures during feature refinement. To further refine the multi-level features aggregated by the neck, a Dynamic Convolutional-attention Fusion Module (DCFM) combines lightweight attention with depthwise convolutional enhancement to integrate long-range contextual cues and local structural features with complementary receptive fields. In addition, a Dual-Domain Attention Module (DDAM) is introduced in the prediction stage, where spatial- and frequency-domain responses are jointly modeled to highlight small-object structures and suppress cluttered backgrounds. Extensive experiments on three widely used remote sensing benchmarks, including VisDrone2019, DIOR and DOTA, demonstrate that LDA-YOLO achieves competitive SOD accuracy compared with existing lightweight detectors, while maintaining a compact model size and low computational cost, indicating its potential for resource-constrained deployment.

Article.Title: Towards optimising the combination of non-thermal plasma therapy with immune checkpoint inhibition in melanoma
Article.Authors: Van der heyden L.; Privat-Maldonado A.; Berghmans Y.; Peeters E.; Baroen J.; Hermans C.; Lau H.; Brants L.; Marcq E.; Lardon F.; Vanlanduit S.; Bogaerts A.; Smits E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-thermal plasma (NTP) is a promising cancer therapy that induces immunogenic cell death and may complement immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI). We evaluated NTP as monotherapy and in combination with different ICIs in a syngeneic murine melanoma model. Immune checkpoint-associated ligand and receptor expression was assessed in vitro and in vivo following clinically relevant treatment conditions. NTP largely preserved baseline checkpoint expression, with only limited, treatment-dependent modulations, while maintaining overall immune cell presence within the tumour microenvironment. NTP monotherapy significantly inhibited tumour growth, with the strongest effect observed at 120 s, and was associated with a modest survival benefit in the initial treatment-duration experiment. However, combining NTP with single-agent ICI did not improve tumour control or survival compared to monotherapies, while dual PD-1/CTLA-4 inhibition extended survival independently of NTP. These findings demonstrate that NTP is immunologically compatible with ICI and represents an alternative local therapy for melanoma, although further optimisation is required to unlock its full combinatorial potential.

Article.Title: Kinematic validation of an IMU-based 2-segment foot model using optical motion capture and the oxford foot model
Article.Authors: Bauer L.; Woiczinski M.; Seehaboot K.; Yotnuengnit P.; Vitoonpong T.; Baumbach S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) have emerged as a promising alternative to Optical Motion Capture (OMC) systems. However, many applications simplify biomechanical models, particularly for the foot and ankle, by representing them as a single rigid segment. To address this limitation, a 2-segment Foot Model was developed and validated against the Oxford Foot Model using OMC. Twelve participants were equipped with both systems, and their kinematics were measured during overground walking. The data were compared using statistical parametric mapping (SPM), Pearson correlation, and range of motion (ROM) analysis. The results revealed significant differences in some aspects of the curves according to SPM, but the overall shape demonstrated very high correlation values. Additionally, ROM was not significantly different in six out of nine cases. These findings indicate that, while absolute values were not identical, the IMU-based system provides a valid representation of foot and ankle kinematics when analyzed as two distinct segments.

Article.Title: Intelligent clinical decision support system for intracranial aneurysm lesion-based detection using biomedical imaging data
Article.Authors: Praveena S.; Murali Krishna V.; Sonthi V.; Gottumukkala D.; Pattanaik C.; Behera N.; Bansal K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a type of cerebrovascular condition that occurs due to focal bulging or expansion in the wall of a cerebral artery, most frequently affecting the internal carotid artery. An IA is seemingly connected with conditions such as fibrous dysplasia, adult-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and coarctation of aorta. A ruptured brain aneurysm can result in a severe and life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage if not treated early, often leading to long-lasting neurological damage and a higher chance of death. However, the traditional diagnostic technique is time-consuming, and it necessitates a trained and skilled medical practitioner. Hence, building an automated model to help physicians precisely detect IA can reduce the clinicians’ burden. Recently, deep learning has gained significant interest in the domain of medical imaging as it automatically learns patterns and accurately detects several types of diseases, such as IAs. Therefore, this article introduces a Clinical Decision Support System for Intracranial Aneurysm Lesion-Based Detection (CDSS-IALD). The main purpose of this work is to develop a robust system that can automatically detect and identify intracranial aneurysms using medical imaging data to assist clinicians with treatment decisions. Initially, the proposed CDSS-IALD model pre-processes the input biomedical images using image normalization, noise reduction, contrast improvement, and skull stripping to refine image quality and consistency for subsequent analysis. Following that, a ConvNeXt hierarchical model is employed for feature extraction, which effectively extracts local details and global context from pre-processed images. Finally, these extracted representations are then forwarded to a spiking neural network, which performs accurate aneurysm detection and classification. To ensure the enhanced performance of the CDSS-IALD system, extensive experiments were conducted on the benchmark Intracranial Aneurysm Dataset. The experimental outcomes clearly demonstrate the betterment of the proposed CDSS-IALD system over the other approaches in detecting and localizing intracranial aneurysms from biomedical imaging.

Article.Title: Surveillance epidemiology and an open machine-learning benchmark of antimicrobial-resistant healthcare-associated infections in a Chinese district hospital
Article.Authors: Han D.; Hu Y.; Shu X.; Zou H.; Wang C.; Peng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) drives a growing share of healthcare-associated infection (HAI) mortality; however, data resources from Chinese hospitals outside university referral networks remain scarce. We conducted a retrospective analysis of 39 months of prospectively collected, hospital-wide HAI surveillance data (February 2023–April 2026) from a 1,100-bed district-level general hospital (accredited Class III Grade A) in Chongqing, China, comprising 1,240 episodes among 1,054 patients across 256,993 admissions and 1.14 million patient-days. The hospital-wide episode incidence was stable at 0.48 per 100 admissions and 0.82 per 1,000 patient-days, with no seasonal pattern or residual autocorrelation. Acinetobacter baumannii was the leading pathogen (19.4% of isolates), with carbapenem resistance reaching 92.0% hospital-wide and 98.5% in the intensive care unit, exceeding national benchmarks. Mechanical ventilation, bedridden status, central venous catheterization, and stroke were enriched among resistant infections (odds ratios 2.4–5.2; all Bonferroni-adjusted p ≤ 0.001). We then benchmarked three transparent machine-learning baselines on routinely collected, pre-infection variables using patient-grouped, 10 × 5-fold repeated cross-validation. AMR phenotype prediction achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.74–0.75 (area under the precision–recall curve 0.55–0.56 against a prevalence of 0.31) for logistic regression and random forest, whereas infection-site classification was not clinically useful (accuracy 0.39–0.52 versus a 0.46 majority-class baseline). A previously reported AUROC of 0.91 was traced to two forms of leakage (patient overlap between partitions and inclusion of total length of stay) and is corrected here. The de-identified dataset, bilingual codebook, and complete reproducibility pipeline are deposited under permissive licences, providing an open, leakage-audited benchmark for AMR prediction research in an under-represented hospital tier.

Article.Title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
Article.Authors: Zahrani A.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming human resource management (HRM) by supporting recruitment, training, performance management, workforce planning, talent analytics, and employee engagement. Nevertheless, limited evidence explains how different AI-enabled HRM practices contribute to process efficiency, decision-making, workforce agility, and overall HRM effectiveness. This study examined six AI-enabled HRM capabilities through an integrated Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory framework. The proposed model included AI in Recruitment and Selection, Training and Development, Performance Management, Strategic HR Planning, Talent Analytics and Retention, and Employee Engagement and Wellbeing. HR Process Efficiency, Decision-Making Accuracy, and Workforce Agility and Innovation were examined as organizational mechanisms contributing to Enhanced HRM Effectiveness. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 256 h professionals from public-sector, private-sector, and higher-education settings in Saudi Arabia and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings showed that recruitment and performance-management AI were positively associated with HR process efficiency, while strategic-planning and talent-analytics AI were positively associated with decision-making accuracy. Employee engagement and wellbeing AI was positively associated with workforce agility and innovation. However, training and development AI was not significantly associated with process efficiency, and decision-making accuracy was not significantly associated with enhanced HRM effectiveness. The study demonstrates that the contribution of AI to HRM effectiveness depends on the HR function and the organizational mechanism involved. The findings provide theoretical and practical guidance for integrating AI with HR expertise, organizational routines, workforce capabilities, and responsible governance.

Article.Title: An AI–IoT enabled upgraded industries framework for sustainable business operations and intelligent decision management
Article.Authors: Kasat K.; Raman M.; Roy D.; Talele G.; Patel V.; Santhosh A.
Article.Abstract: With the advent of Upgraded industries, the shift in focus is now towards an intelligent, human-centric and environmentally-conscious business ecosystem. But the current Upgraded industries approaches are not always very effective in supporting strategic decision making and real-time company operations, as they do not fully include the full integration of AI, IoT, sustainability assessment, and intelligent decision management. This study offers a framework for sustainable business operations and intelligent decision management enabled by AI and IoT to tackle these difficulties. A unified architecture is achieved via the framework’s integration of edge-cloud computing, sustainability assessment, intelligent decision support, AI-driven analytics, and data collecting based on IOTs. A new HLX-DOM is presented to further enhance operational efficiency, decision-making towards sustainability and predictive accuracy. A number of industrial datasets, such as AI4I Predictive Maintenance, Smart Manufacturing, Appliances Energy Prediction, and Industry 4.0 Production, were used to validate the scheme. In the experimental evaluation, efficiency in operations, use of resources, energy consumption, sustainability and accuracy of predictions were some of the performance indicators used. The results demonstrate the optimization of resources (92.3% efficiency), energy saved (91.8% efficiency) and the sustainability increase (91.8% efficiency). The proposed HLX-DOM model outperformed the other models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, XG Boost, ANN, and a single LSTM model, achieving the highest accuracy of 98.7%, precision of 98.1%, recall of 97.9%, and F1-score of 98.0%. The framework’s scalability and resilience are further confirmed by studies of real-world case studies, ablation, sensitivity, and computational complexity. Intelligent, sustainable, and human-centric Upgraded industries ecosystems can be implemented in corporate, healthcare, supply chain, and industrial settings with the help of the suggested solution.

Article.Title: Design and implementation of an industrial software cloud platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Liu H.; Bai Y.; Yang L.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Industrial software is evolving from standalone tools toward collaborative services, increasing the need for heterogeneous resource coordination and industrial knowledge reuse. Integrating knowledge-based planning with shop-floor execution remains a challenge in complex manufacturing workflows. To address this challenge, this study presents the design and engineering implementation of an industrial software cloud platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs). Deployed in a private cloud, the platform comprises resource, enabling, driving, and application layers within a cloud-fog-edge-endpoint framework. A knowledge-model-data-resource operational loop connects data governance, knowledge retrieval, task planning, verification, execution, and feedback. Knowledge graphs provide domain evidence and constraints, LLMs generate candidate plans, and mechanistic models and deterministic software services support verification and execution. Agents coordinate service invocation and feedback across these stages. Two engineering applications demonstrate the platform’s implementation in five-axis blisk computer-aided manufacturing (CAM) and CNC machine-tool prognostics and health management (PHM). Existing CAM records show reductions of 40.27% in aggregate programming and preparation time and 12.29% in single-piece machining time. The PHM application demonstrates the functional integration of data acquisition, fault reasoning, maintenance planning, and knowledge updating. These cases demonstrate the platform’s engineering implementation in manufacturing and maintenance workflows. The current evaluation is based on case-specific CAM records and PHM functional demonstrations, with broader performance and cross-enterprise validation remaining outstanding.

Article.Title: Effect of a Zr seed layer on agglomeration phenomena for Ag nanostructure formation
Article.Authors: Park Y.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Oh D.; Kang H.; Kamiko M.; Ha J.; Rho J.
Article.Abstract: The morphological characteristics of Ag nanostructures strongly influence their plasmonic properties, making morphology control through processing conditions important for optical applications. In this study, Ag nanodots were formed on MgO(001) substrates using a seed-layer-assisted agglomeration (SLAA) process with a Zr seed layer. The effects of Zr seed-layer thickness, Ag deposition thickness, and annealing time on nanodot formation were investigated. Variations in the processing conditions resulted in systematic changes in nanodot density, surface coverage, and three-dimensional morphology, while the introduction of the Zr seed layer influenced the agglomeration and separation behavior of Ag. After annealing, Zr was found to exist predominantly in an oxidized state, suggesting the formation of a ZrOₓ-based interfacial region between Ag and MgO. In contrast, no distinct difference in the crystallographic orientation of Ag was observed with or without the Zr seed layer. These results suggest that the Zr seed layer primarily contributes to modifying the interfacial state and Ag nanodot morphology rather than controlling crystallographic orientation, indicating its potential as a seed layer for process-based morphology control of Ag nanostructures.

Article.Title: Development and external validation of a predictive model for epithelial ovarian tumors based on MRI features and serum tumor markers
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Niu Z.; Qi L.; Mao S.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a major threat to women’s health, and early-stage disease is often asymptomatic, making timely diagnosis difficult. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and serum tumor markers to distinguish benign from malignant epithelial ovarian tumors. A total of 222 patients from Huzhou Maternity & Child Health Care Hospital were included as the training cohort, and 102 patients from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital served as the external validation cohort. Independent predictors were identified using multivariate logistic regression, and a predictive model was constructed based on regression coefficients and externally validated. In the training cohort, 168 patients were benign and 54 were malignant. Tumor morphology, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) signal intensity, ascites, carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125), and human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) were independent predictors (AUCs: 0.748–0.876). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.965, with 94.4% sensitivity and 84.5% specificity, and showed good calibration ( P = 0.870). In the validation cohort (80 benign, 22 malignant), the model yielded an AUC of 0.972, with 90.9% sensitivity and 95.0% specificity. The proposed model integrating MRI features and serum tumor markers demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance and robust external validity. This practical and easily applicable tool may assist in preoperative risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: A lightweight multi-task transformer for joint classification and priority ranking of community service requests on edge devices
Article.Authors: Deng Q.; Suo L.
Article.Abstract: Urban community service platforms receive thousands of textual requests every day, yet most deployed systems still run two separate pipelines: one for category classification and one for urgency ranking. The duplication wastes computation and sits poorly with the memory and power envelope of a community-level edge gateway. We address this gap with EdgeCSR-Net, a multi-task transformer that couples a depth-wise separable encoder, a grouped-query attention block and a convolutional positional encoding, so that thirty-six-way classification and four-level urgency ranking emerge from a single forward pass. Ranking is trained as a pairwise comparison and the resulting score is mapped onto the four operational levels by thresholds fixed on the validation split. The uncompressed encoder carries about 2.02 million parameters; a task-aware pipeline of structured pruning, distillation from a BERT-base teacher and INT8 quantization-aware training trims this to a 1.43-million-parameter, 1.5 MB deployable model. Rather than hand-setting the balance between the two objectives, we weight each loss by a learned task-noise term, an arrangement usually called homoscedastic uncertainty weighting, and pair it with a gradient-projection rule that suppresses conflicting updates on the shared encoder. Evaluated on a corpus of 47,832 requests from three metropolitan districts, EdgeCSR-Net reaches 88.1% macro-F1 and 0.897 NDCG@10. Against BERT-base it gives up 1.4 macro-F1 points and 0.015 NDCG@10 while carrying 77 times fewer parameters; against RoBERTa-base the corresponding figures are 1.8 points, 0.019 and 87 times. Under a matched INT8 pipeline it is significantly more accurate than TinyBERT and DistilBERT, statistically tied with MobileBERT, and six to ten times faster than all three. On an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX the quantized model finishes inference in 7.6 ms per request while occupying 34 MB of peak memory; on a Raspberry Pi 4B it takes 52.3 ms. Temporal and leave-one-district-out protocols cost only 1.7 and 0.8 macro-F1 points respectively, which indicates that neither the joint architecture nor its compression schedule buys real-time latency at the price of cross-region robustness.

Article.Title: Deciphering morphometric and terrain-driven controls on groundwater recharge and agricultural suitability using geospatial and multivariate modeling
Article.Authors: Abishek S.; Pitchaimani V.; Sidhu N.; Singh K.; Sharma A.; Sharma S.; Kaliraj S.; Senagah A.; Thakur C.; Mattar M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of basin morphometry, groundwater recharge potential, and agricultural suitability in the Lower Thamirabarani River Basin, Tamil Nadu, using geospatial datasets and statistical analyses. The morphometric results indicate an elongated basin (Rf = 0.268; Re = 0.584) with a moderate drainage density (1.4 km/km 2 ), reflecting a balanced runoff response and a reduced tendency toward flash flooding. High relief (820 m), steep terrain (17.23%), and a high Melton Ruggedness Number (0.0333) signify strong erosional forces in the western highlands. Flow accumulation analysis shows that 18.7% of the basin experiences concentrated runoff, while curvature mapping identifies concave surfaces that enhance infiltration. Land-use and land-cover mapping indicates agricultural predominance (59.9%) and highlights the influence of expanding settlements on hydrological processes. The Recharge Potential Index (RPI) mapping reveals that moderate recharge zones cover 67.6% of the basin, with high recharge areas primarily located in the eastern floodplains. The Agricultural Suitability Index (ASI) indicates that over half of the basin is of low to moderate suitability, and unsuitable areas coincide with rocky, saline, or steep landscapes. A strong positive correlation exists between ASI and RPI ( R = 0.78, p < 0.001), indicating a close relationship between agricultural potential and groundwater recharge conditions. Principal Component Analysis and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis identify relief-related parameters as the major contributors to spatial variability. The novelty of this study lies in the development of an integrated framework that links basin morphometry, recharge potential, and agricultural suitability, supported by multivariate validation. The results support the prioritization of watersheds, erosion control, and sustainable land and water management practices.

Article.Title: Facial expression recognition based on multi-scale dual-channel attention mechanism
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Ma X.; Yang J.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, with the continuous advancement of artificial intelligence technology, the way humans interact with computers has undergone significant changes. Facial expression recognition technology for human faces has increasingly become a hot research topic in computer vision. However, traditional facial expression recognition models are based on deep neural networks, which have problems such as insufficient extraction of image details, poor generalization ability of the model, and low utilization rate of key feature information. To address these issues, in this paper, a Multi-scale Dual-channel Attention Mechanism Facial Expression Recognition Network (MDAMNet) is proposed. Firstly, a Multi-scale Feature Extraction Block with Dilated Convolution (DMFE Block) is designed, which uses ordinary convolution and dilated convolution to form different receptive fields. The model can focus on and extract feature information at different scales at the same time. Then, a Dual-channel Attention Mechanism (DAM) combining channel attention and spatial attention is designed, which can enhance the perception ability and extraction ability of key features, and effectively suppress redundant information. Finally, Focal Loss is employed to dynamically adjust the loss function, with the aim of enhancing the accuracy and stability of the system. During the experimental verification stage, experiments were conducted on three publicly available classic datasets (FER2013, CK + and JAFFE). The final accuracy rates reached 76.87%, 97.52% and 98.34% respectively, effectively demonstrating the feasibility of this method.

Article.Title: Fresh and mechanical properties of hemp fiber-reinforced concrete: an experimental dosage study with multi-output artificial neural network modelling of mechanical strength
Article.Authors: Rajkumar K.; Anandaraj S.; Awoyera P.; Fadugba O.
Article.Abstract: The construction sector’s dependence on carbon-intensive binders and synthetic reinforcement has intensified interest in plant-based fibers as sustainable crack-control reinforcement for concrete. This study experimentally characterises the fresh and 28-day mechanical properties of hemp (Cannabis sativa bast) fiber-reinforced concrete (HFRC) and develops a multi-output Artificial Neural Network (ANN) that predicts its compressive, splitting tensile and flexural strength from fiber dosage. The physical programme comprised eleven dosage levels (0–2.0% by volume in 0.2% steps) of 5% NaOH-treated fiber (aspect ratio ≈ 235) in a fixed M30 base mix (cement 340 kg/m³, water–cement ratio 0.45, superplasticizer 7.48 kg/m³). Slump, compaction factor and Vee-Bee time were measured in triplicate, and three cubes, cylinders and prisms per mix were tested to IS 516; dosage effects were assessed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey and Dunnett comparisons. The 33 physical specimen results per property were kept distinct from 1,100 augmented rows generated from truncated-normal distributions bounded by each mix’s measured mean, standard deviation and range. A 64–32 ReLU multi-output perceptron was evaluated by leave-one-dosage-out cross-validation over ten seeds and benchmarked against polynomial, spline, ridge, tree-ensemble and single-output models. Fiber dosage significantly affected all three strengths ( p < 0.001). Compressive strength peaked at 0.6% (32.8 MPa, + 5.8%), statistically indistinguishable from 0.4 to 0.8%, while splitting tensile and flexural strength peaked at 1.2% (3.95 MPa, + 33.9%; 5.50 MPa, + 31.0%) within statistically equivalent plateaus. On unseen dosages the ANN reproduced the experimental means with RMSE of 0.36, 0.09 and 0.13 MPa, respectively, and outperformed three single-output networks, although a cubic smoothing spline was equally or more accurate. Slump fell from 95 mm to 40 mm and Vee-Bee time rose from 3 s to 20 s across the dosage range, confirming a workability–reinforcement trade-off. The results support hemp fiber dosages of about 0.6–1.2% and show that, for a single-variable dosage study, the multi-output ANN is best used as an exploratory response-curve model rather than as a substitute for physical testing.

Article.Title: Hard attention mechanism integrated with VGG16 for high-precision tomato leaf disease classification
Article.Authors: Laatiri Y.; Mahjoub M.
Article.Abstract: Tomato diseases represent a major threat to agricultural productivity and global food security. Early and accurate identification of these diseases is essential for effective crop management and yield preservation. In this study, we propose a hard attention–enhanced VGG16 model for automatic tomato leaf disease identification. By integrating a hard attention mechanism into the VGG16 architecture, the proposed model is able to focus on the most informative regions of the input images, thereby improving its capability to discriminate between healthy and diseased tomato leaves. The proposed approach is evaluated using a publicly available dataset of tomato leaf images. Experimental results demonstrate that the hard attention–based VGG16 model significantly improves classification performance compared to the standard VGG16 architecture and several existing deep learning models. In particular, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 96.0%, outperforming the baseline VGG16 model, which achieves 92.3% accuracy on the same dataset. Furthermore, the integration of the attention mechanism enhances the interpretability of the model by highlighting the image regions that contribute most to the prediction process. This explainability provides valuable insights into the model’s decision-making process, making it a reliable and transparent tool for intelligent plant disease identification systems.

Article.Title: Evaluation of large language models’ responses to patient questions about avascular necrosis of the femoral head
Article.Authors: Gokalp A.; Cakar A.; Issiz H.; Tepeoglu T.; Erturk S.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence chatbots are rapidly gaining popularity for acquiring health information, but the quality of responses seems to differ between platforms. This study investigated the responses of ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, and DeepSeek to 15 frequently asked questions regarding femoral head avascular necrosis. Each platform answered each question once, for a total of 75 responses. Four orthopedic surgeons assessed the response using the JAMA benchmark criteria, DISCERN, an adapted five-point scale of clinical accuracy, and a binary safety score. Readability was measured by Flesch reading ease score (FRES) and Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FKGL). Models were compared by using Friedman tests and Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Claude ranked the highest by JAMA and DISCERN scores and that DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot in terms of DISCERN. Clinical accuracy differed significantly among the models ( p < 0.001). Claude and DeepSeek were rated higher than ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, with no significant difference between Claude and DeepSeek. All responses were rated safe by all four raters. Readability performance scores of the models achieved significant differences on FRES ( p = 0.043) and FKGL ( p < 0.001) measures. The average FKGL score (10.85–13.93) was higher than the grade scores recommended for patient education information. There was heterogeneity in the platforms ability to report on aspects of transparency, information quality and clinical accuracy while consistently failing on readability. Patient comprehension was not evaluated.

Article.Title: A lightweight closed-loop adaptive intrusion detection framework for cyber resilience in critical infrastructure
Article.Authors: Al Ghamdi M.; Alghamdi I.; Alzahrani R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most operators of energy, health, or transport facilities do not have at their disposal the kind of computational resources that large-scale deep-learning detectors require. Being energy and health care and transportation facility operators, they seek an intrusion detection approach that is responsive to environmental changes. We present one such lightweight alternative. At the core of such an approach is a regularized Logistic Regression-based detector, with the closed loop comprising context-aware thresholding, behavioral profiling, recent error-rate feedback, budget-limited incremental updates, and deception-derived observations from outside. None of these approaches is, in itself, novel. Our contribution lies in the coupling of these mechanisms to displace the decision threshold using contextual and behavioral signals and in detecting confirmed outcomes that are then fed back to update the classifier, the behavioral baseline, and future decisions. We conduct the model evaluation on two levels of abstraction. The confirmation dataset includes 39,919 SWaT instances segmented into 40 nonoverlapping time windows, validated over StratifiedGroupKFold with a per-instance allowance of no more than 256 analyst-validated instances. In an ablation study over 25 such splits comparing the full model to the Logistic Regression with the static threshold, the full model achieved an F1 of 0.7526 ± 0.1074 compared with only 0.5719 ± 0.1578 for the latter (Holm adjusted p < 0.001). Most of the contribution came from budgeted incremental learning; without it, F1 dropped by 0.1704. Feedback using error rates was less important but still significant, returning 0.0048 in F1 together with a lower false positive rate. Behavioral profiling did not affect the F1 and improved specificity. Context-aware thresholding increased the false positive rate while yielding no improvement in the F1; thus, this is reported as a trade-off rather than an improvement. There were no significant contrasts with respect to the Holm correction; hence, we do not claim any synergy. Batch Logistic Regression with matching scored 0.7065 ± 0.1254 in terms of F1 score compared with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Linear SVM, Extra Trees, and MLP, none being significantly different from batch Logistic Regression. Because the labels were equally split among 256, all feedback mechanisms outperformed the case with no feedback, going from an F1 of 0.5845 ± 0.1495 to between 0.7292 and 0.7676. The deception-prioritized proxy did not make it into the winners. It beat no feedback but lost to random sampling on all the metrics that we examined. We have, therefore, referenced the previously published simulation and emulation figures as exploratory studies illustrating the behavior of this architecture. In toto, the framework is efficient and competitive under the tested conditions, and nothing herein suggests classifier superiority or a deception-specific advantage or true zero-day detection or readiness for a live plant.

Article.Title: FS-VMADW: a frequency–spatial vision mamba framework for dual watermarking of medical MRI images
Article.Authors: Ur Rehman A.; Lee C.; Li L.; Khan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Secure transmission and copyright protection of medical images require watermarking methods that preserve image quality and enable reliable payload recovery. However, the currently available deep watermarking architectures either encode only a single watermark or use convolutional networks with inherently restricted receptive fields, which limits their ability to capture long-range anatomical dependencies in medical images. Moreover, spatial modeling alone does not explicitly capture the frequency characteristics that influence watermark imperceptibility and robustness. This work proposes FS-VMADW - a Frequency-Spatial Vision Mamba Dual Watermarking architecture for abdominal MRI security. The proposed encoder combines the Vision Mamba spatial branch with a four-direction selective scan of state-space models applied with linear complexity, along with a two-stage Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform frequency branch, which are fused with a gating module generating location-specific weighting of spatial and frequency feature maps. Two independent spread-spectrum carriers encode two 64-bit binary watermarks, while an adaptively generated Vision Mamba mask controls their embedding. A two-phase training curriculum mitigates the gradient conflict between imperceptibility and extraction fidelity by decoupling the two objectives across successive training phases. Experiments on the CHAOS abdominal MRI benchmark demonstrate PSNR = 42.37 dB, SSIM = 0.9557, NC = 0.9511, BER = 0.0491, and BitAcc = 0.9509 under clean conditions. Controlled backbone comparisons further show that Vision Mamba outperforms CNN and Transformer alternatives, while the addition of DWT provides further improvements in both imperceptibility and watermark recovery. These results demonstrate that long-range spatial modeling and multi-scale frequency information provide complementary benefits for dual watermarking of medical images.

Article.Title: Serial multi‑time‑point assessments of well‑defined somatosensory domains and their associations with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke
Article.Authors: Jing J.; Du R.; Wen L.; Fang Y.
Article.Abstract: The association between post-stroke somatosensory deficits and limb spasticity has been reported. This study aimed to assess patients at multiple time points to further investigate relationships between well-defined somatosensory domains and the occurrence of limb spasticity following ischemic stroke. Briefly, the study enrolled 514 patients with ischemic stroke. Post-stroke proprioceptive deficits, pain-temperature deficits, sensory extinction, and stereognosis deficits were evaluated at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge. Limb spasticity was assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale at 30 and 90 days post-discharge; a score ≥ 1 was defined as spasticity. Multivariate logistic regression models were applied to examine relationships between these variables. The results showed that proprioceptive deficits and pain-temperature deficits at 10, 20, and 30 days post-discharge were associated with limb spasticity and moderate-to-severe limb spasticity (relative to mild spasticity), and an interaction was observed between these two deficits. Only post‑stroke sensory extinction and stereognosis deficits assessed at 10 days post‑discharge were associated with spasticity, but these associations were attenuated to non‑significance upon additional adjustment for admission affected‑limb muscle strength. In conclusion, proprioceptive and pain-temperature deficits at all three time points were associated with limb spasticity after ischemic stroke in this cohort. These findings guide future stroke‑somatosensory research.

Article.Title: Analysis of a reaction-diffusion SVEIR model for measles geographic spread
Article.Authors: DarAssi M.; AbuHour Y.; Almuneef A.; Alqahtani Z.
Article.Abstract: We formulate and analyze a deterministic reaction-diffusion SVEIR model for the geographic spread of measles, explicitly incorporating vaccination, vaccine efficacy, latency, recovery, demographic turnover, and spatial diffusion. The disease-free equilibrium and the basic reproduction number $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ are obtained using the next-generation matrix, and linear stability analysis identifies the invasion threshold and the critical spatial mode. Because the critical wavenumber is zero, a long-wavelength analysis is used to characterize slow spatial variation near the invasion front. A mathematical consistency check shows that the common-diffusion formulation does not support a finite-wavenumber Turing instability; the roll, square, and hexagonal modes are therefore presented only as generic pattern-theory modes rather than as patterns proved to arise from the present model. Numerical simulations illustrate spatiotemporal propagation and quantify the effects of vaccine efficacy, vaccination rate, and transmission intensity.
Article.Topic: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models

Article.Title: Sleep disturbances and their association with quality of life and depressive symptoms among elderly residents of long-term care facilities: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wójcik-Pędziwiatr M.; Kontowicz E.; Dębska G.; Rudzińska-Bar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleep disturbances are common in later life and may be particularly relevant among residents of long-term care facilities, where multiple clinical and functional factors can affect sleep and well-being. Evidence concerning the relationship between sleep disturbances, depressive symptoms, and quality of life among institutionalized older adults in Central and Eastern Europe remains limited. This cross-sectional study included 80 residents aged ≥ 60 years from two long-term care facilities in Poland. Sleep was assessed using the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Depressive symptoms, functional independence, cognitive functioning, and quality of life were evaluated using the 30-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-30), Barthel Index, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and WHOQOL-BREF, respectively. Associations were examined using Spearman’s rank correlations and multivariable regression models accounting for available potential confounders. Insomnia symptoms (AIS ≥ 6) were present in 50 participants (62.5%), poor sleep quality (PSQI > 5) in 42 (52.5%), and increased daytime sleepiness (ESS ≥ 10) in 21 (26.3%). Depressive symptoms above the adopted GDS-30 cut-off were identified in 37 participants (46.3%). Greater insomnia severity and poorer sleep quality were associated with more severe depressive symptoms and lower scores in several WHOQOL-BREF domains in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment for depressive symptoms and available clinical and functional covariates, the associations between sleep measures and quality-of-life domains were attenuated. Sleep disturbances were common in this selected sample of long-term care residents with relatively preserved cognitive functioning and were associated with depressive symptoms and poorer quality of life in cross-sectional analyses. However, these relationships were attenuated after accounting for relevant covariates. Given the cross-sectional design, selected study population, and potential residual confounding, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships.

Article.Title: Evaluation of performance and emissions of a diesel engine using dual aqueous ammonia -diesel fuel
Article.Authors: El-Fakharany M.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The carbon footprint of fossil fuel application is a crucial indicator of the overall quantity of greenhouse gases discharged into the atmosphere. Sustainable replacements, such as aqueous ammonia, are viewed as a good approach to solve the shortage of conventional fuel, low-carbon fuels and address climate change. Emissions and performance of diesel engine running on dual fuel of diesel and aqueous ammonia were investigated. Ammonia and water were combined in volumetric amounts of 5, 10, and 15% to get around these adverse effects. Adding aqueous ammonia of 5, 10 and 15% to diesel boosted brake specific fuel consumption by 4, 7, and 13% at 75% of engine output power. Thermal efficiency of diesel and aqueous ammonia were decreased by 4, 7 and 13% when aqueous ammonia was added by 5, 10 and 15%. Aqueous ammonia of 5%, 10% and 15% demonstrated increases of 17, 32 and 42% in CO emissions about diesel, whereas the decreases in nitrogen oxides were 5, 10 and 15% in relation to diesel, respectively. At 100% of output power, increases in hydrocarbon emissions for 5%, 10%, and 15% aqueous ammonia were 10, 23, and 31% but carbon dioxide values were decreased by 6, 12, and 17% for diesel with aqueous ammonia compared to diesel oil. Increases of oxygen concentrations for 5%, 10% and 15% aqueous ammonia were 6, 8 and 10%, respectively at 75% of output power. Engine performance penalties and emissions issues limit the use of aqueous ammonia, despite its potential as a carbon-reducing supplemental fuel.

Article.Title: Changes in breast cancer management and care infrastructure in Turki̇ye: a ten-year multicenter comparison, 2009–2019
Article.Authors: Canturk N.; Erkek A.; Güler S.; Şimşek T.; Gulluoglu M.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate changes in breast cancer management infrastructure, diagnostic approaches, and treatment practices in tertiary breast centers in Turkiye between 2009 and 2019 and identify areas requiring further development. This repeated cross-sectional multicenter institutional survey compared aggregated center-level data from 2009 to 2019. Data included pathologically confirmed breast cancer cases, diagnostic sampling, stage at diagnosis, breast and axillary surgery, neoadjuvant therapy, imaging availability, and specialized multidisciplinary and supportive-care services. Individual recurrence and survival outcomes were unavailable. Thirty-eight centers contributed data in 2009 and 44 in 2019, with confirmed cases increasing from 4,808 to 6,550 (p < 0.001). The number of specialized breast surgeons increased. Core needle biopsy largely replaced excisional/incisional diagnostic procedures (p < 0.001), while neoadjuvant therapy use increased (p < 0.001). Surgical management shifted toward breast-conserving surgery. The reported proportion of sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) increased from approximately 48% to 55%; however, the aggregated dataset did not include clinical nodal status or patient-level indications for SLNB, so appropriateness of axillary staging cannot be assessed. Availability of diagnostic imaging, medical oncology/chemotherapy units, and lymphedema services also improved, although progress remained uneven across multidisciplinary and supportive-care domains. Participating Turkish tertiary breast centers demonstrated substantial structural and procedural changes between 2009 and 2019 that were broadly consistent with evolving breast cancer care. Because patient-level treatment indications and longitudinal outcomes were unavailable, the appropriateness of individual axillary procedures and effects on disease-free or overall survival cannot be determined.

Article.Title: Formulating a training strategy for tactical swimmers: an integrated approach using the modified Delphi method and an intuitionistic fuzzy three-dimensional eight-octant distribution
Article.Authors: Zheng C.; Lin K.; Chang K.; Tsai W.; Chu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tactical swimming enhances the operational effectiveness of military personnel in diverse maritime missions. Compared with conventional swimming, tactical swimming places greater demands on endurance, speed, and load-bearing capacity. Inadequate warm-ups or improper daily training may result in sports injuries, thereby compromising combat readiness. This study employed the modified Delphi method to develop stretching exercise evaluation indices specifically tailored to tactical swimming. Eighteen cadets from a Taiwan military academy were recruited as participants and provided intuitionistic fuzzy evaluations of stretching exercises, along with assessments of their swimming abilities. A three-dimensional eight-octant distribution was subsequently applied to formulate tactical swimming training strategies. The results identified 11 key stretching indices and revealed that two participants (M2 and M4) demonstrated the highest performance. This study identified inter-individual differences and provided recommendations for improving group performance and guiding future tactical swimming training.

Article.Title: Vision-semantic alignment with hierarchical consistency constraints for multi-attribute museum artifact classification
Article.Authors: Luo F.; Lu Q.; Meng C.
Article.Abstract: The digitization of museum collections has produced vast multimodal data, yet existing automated classification methods treat classification attributes as independent flat categories and overlook the hierarchical taxonomic structures embedded in museum cataloging systems, frequently yielding predictions that are taxonomically illegitimate. We present a multimodal hierarchical learning framework for multi-attribute museum artifact classification that combines vision-semantic alignment with hierarchical consistency constraints. The framework extracts visual and textual features through a ViT and BERT dual-encoder, aligns the two modalities in a shared space via a contrastive objective trained on cultural-heritage data, adaptively fuses them through a gating mechanism, and performs joint hierarchical prediction across multiple taxonomy trees using cascaded conditional classification heads. The core contribution is a hierarchical consistency loss that explicitly penalizes incompatible prediction distributions between adjacent levels during training, complemented by a constrained decoding strategy that guarantees the structural legitimacy of output paths at inference. On the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access dataset, the framework achieves an average hierarchical F1 of 85.2%, a gain of 6.9 percentage points over the strongest multimodal baseline, and reduces the model’s learned hierarchical violation rate to 2.8%, with constrained decoding eliminating the remaining violations at inference. On the SILKNOW silk textile corpus, ten epochs of fine-tuning surpass the reported baselines under the evaluated transfer setting. Ablations and visualization analyses further clarify the contribution of each component and the model’s internal decision-making behavior.

Article.Title: Silencing of LOXL4 inhibits colorectal cancer progression via regulating GLS1-dependent glutamine metabolism
Article.Authors: Qu P.; Wang M.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lysyl oxidase-like 4 (LOXL4) is frequently overexpressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and associated with poor clinical prognoses. However, the metabolic mechanisms underlying LOXL4-driven CRC progression remain poorly elucidated. This study investigated the biological function of LOXL4 in CRC and its potential as a therapeutic target. We detected LOXL4 expression in paired CRC and normal tissues via western blot, qRT-PCR, IHC and flow cytometry. CRISPR-Cas9 was used to construct LOXL4 knockout SW480 and HT-29 cells, and multiple functional assays assessed cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Integrated proteomics and targeted metabolomics screened glutamine metabolic alterations, with the glutaminase 1 (GLS1) inhibitor CB-839 for functional validation. AOM/DSS-induced CRC mouse models were built to evaluate in vivo tumor growth. LOXL4 was significantly upregulated in clinical CRC samples. LOXL4 knockout suppressed malignant behaviors of CRC cells in vitro. Combined proteomic and metabolomic profiling confirmed GLS1 downregulation in LOXL4-knockout cells, accompanied by glutamine accumulation and glutamate reduction. Exogenous glutamate supplementation enhances the proliferative and migratory capacities of LOXL4-knockout tumor cells. LOXL4-knockout mice developed fewer, smaller intestinal tumors and milder weight loss. CB-839-mediated GLS1 inhibition synergistically strengthened the anti-tumor effect of LOXL4 deletion. LOXL4 silencing restrains CRC progression via a novel mechanism of GLS1 downregulation and intracellular glutamine accumulation. GLS1 pharmacological blockade further potentiates the anti-cancer efficacy of LOXL4 depletion, highlighting complex metabolic dependence in CRC.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a nomogram for screening poor sleep quality among night-shift nurses
Article.Authors: Xing B.; Zhang M.; Wang Q.; Zhang M.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a practical nomogram to screen poor sleep quality among night-shift nurses. A cross-sectional study was conducted involving 595 night-shift nurse s selected between January and March 2026. The nurses were randomly divided into two groups in a ratio of 7:3. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale, and the Fatigue scale-14. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to develop a nomogram model. The performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. The nomogram included eight associated factors: age, marital status, department affiliation, weekly working hours, monthly night shifts, drinking coffee or tea, generalized anxiety disorder, and fatigue. The area under the ROC curve in the training and validation set was 0.856 (95% CI 0.823–0.882) and 0.849 (95% CI 0.821–0.876), respectively. Calibration showed excellent fit across all datasets. The decision curve confirmed that the nomogram offers good clinical net benefits. This study provides a preliminary screening tool for identifying night-shift nurses at high risk of poor sleep quality.

Article.Title: Prevention of parasite infection in birds: adaptive advantages of anting behaviour
Article.Authors: Ohkawara K.; Kamei Y.; Akino T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anting, the application of ants to plumage, has been reported in more than 200 bird species worldwide. The advantage of the peculiar behaviour is hypothesized to be self-treatment against parasites and bacteria because many ant species eject pungent fluids from their exocrine glands, which might help remove ecto- and microparasites from bird’s body. However, this hypothesis has not been well explored. In this study, by using thrush Turdus cardis and two ant species, Lasius spathepus and L. nipponensis , it was tested whether any chemical components on bird’s body surface were altered by anting and whether any ectoparasites were excluded or repelled from the bird’s body. Artificial ant treatments and GC analysis revealed the chemical components on body surface of T. cardis were remarkably altered by anting. Specifically, dendrolasin, a species-specific volatile chemical in the two ants, was added to the body. The anting treatments were significantly effective in removing ectoparasites, louse flies and dipteran insects. Insecticidal effects also were confirmed. Additional experiments showed dendrolasin and some chemical components had directly repellent effects on dipteran insects. It suggests the advantages of anting include the exclusion of harmful dipteran insects and preventive medication for the diseases they introduce, such as avian malaria.

Article.Title: Modeling and optimization of electric smelting parameters for ferrosilicon production from vanadium quartzite leaching residue and coal flotation tailings
Article.Authors: Aitkulov D.; Shevko V.; Badikova A.; Mukhametzhanova A.
Article.Abstract: Silica-rich quartzite leaching cakes and carbon-rich coal beneficiation tailings represent promising technogenic raw materials. Therefore, these cakes and tailings can be considered alternatives to natural raw materials for ferrosilicon production. This article presents the results of a study that examined the feasibility of using coal flotation tailings as a carbon-containing reducing agent for ferrosilicon production from vanadium quartzite leaching cakes. This study was conducted using thermodynamic modeling with the HSC Chemistry software package, electric smelting of the charge in induction and arc furnaces, and second-order rotatable planning. On the basis of these data, vanadium quartzite leaching cakes and coal flotation tailings were found to be suitable raw materials for producing various grades of ferrosilicon. The optimal conditions for the electrothermal production of FeSi45 ferrosilicon with a silicon extraction rate of 71.6–88.5% are a filter cake-to-tailings ratio of 1.0–3.25 and a steel cutting content of 20–32%. For the production of FeSi50 ferrosilicon, the optimal filter cake-to-tailings ratio is 1.0–1.37, with a steel cutting content of 20.0–22.2%. The feasibility of smelting FeSi45 ferrosilicon, containing (by mass) 43.4% Si, 1.54% Al, 0.32% Ca, 0.43% Mn, 0.17% Cr, 0.12% Ti, 0.11% V, 0.5% C, 0.05% Ni, 0.038% P, and 0.034% S, with a silicon extraction rate of 81.6%, was confirmed through pilot-scale electric smelting in an arc furnace.

Article.Title: Groundwater quality dynamics and hydrochemical indicators of water insecurity in the semi-arid Sokoto Basin, Northwestern Nigeria
Article.Authors: Wali S.; Alias N.; Kaoje I.; Ibrahim S.; Umar A.
Article.Abstract: To determine groundwater quality at a basin level in climate-stressed, data-scarce basins, approaches need to be developed that go beyond traditional descriptive hydrochemistry and interpret the data to provide spatial indicators of water insecurity. Groundwater samples were collected from 54 boreholes and hand-dug wells from the Sokoto Basin across the contrasting basement and sedimentary aquifer systems with the aim of providing an integrated assessment of the quality dynamics of the groundwater. The methodological novelty is the simultaneous testing of controlling processes in a hydrochemical and heavy metal characterisation, quantification of spatial dependence through multivariate statistical analysis, variogram modelling, and ordinary kriging, resulting in the identification of contamination hotspots. The findings show significant variation between the different lithologies and different areas, with values being higher in the basement complex aquifers than the sedimentary aquifers, with respect to the concentrations of minerals such as Mn, Cr, Al, Zn and As. The combined investigation suggests that the composition of groundwater is mainly regulated by mineral weathering, rock-water interaction, evaporation-induced concentrations and locally derived human inputs. The geostatistical modelling also identified specific regions of hydrochemical hotspots, which were mainly located in low-lying locations and areas with high evaporative stress, suggesting that climate stress can enhance the accumulation of solutes. The analysis integrates groundwater water insecurity, hydrochemical processes, spatial prediction and geological setting in a single analytical framework, providing a transferable approach to groundwater assessment in poorly monitored semi-arid groundwater settings. The results offer scientific insights for early warning systems for specific monitoring and for enabling adaptive groundwater management, public health protection and progress towards SDG 6.

Article.Title: Healthy diets and heart rate variability in a cross-sectional analysis of over 7000 adults attending the Maastricht study
Article.Authors: Haeri F.; Eussen S.; Schram M.; Yu E.; Seyedhosseini S.; Sarebanhassanabadi M.; Soltani S.; Salehi-Abargouei A.; Zeegers M.; Wesselius A.
Article.Abstract: A limited and conflicting body of evidence exists on the association between adherence to healthy diets and HRV. The current study aimed to investigate the association between the Mediterranean Diet, Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Dutch Healthy Diet (DHD), and the Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet and HRV in adults. The baseline data from the Maastricht study were used for this cross-sectional research. Dietary adherence was assessed via a validated Food Frequency Questionnaire. HRV parameters were measured using a 12-lead Holter system over 24 h. Mean HRV parameters across quartiles (Q4 vs. Q1) of diet adherence scores and their linear associations were assessed using analysis of covariance and linear regression in different multivariable adjusted models. A total of 7,256 participants aged 59.19 ± 8.66 years were included in the analysis. After full confounder adjustment, in the total population, none of the diets were associated with HRV time domains. The frequency-domain analyses showed that the DASH and the DHD diets were significantly associated with higher power in the very-low-frequency (VLF) range (linear association, P ≤ 0.001). A significant interaction effect was observed between beta-blocker use and adherence to the DASH diet in association with VLF ( P < 0.001). After stratification by beta-blocker use, the DASH and the DHD were significantly associated with higher VLF only among non-users (linear association, P ≤ 0.001). In conclusion, the DASH and DHD dietary patterns were significantly associated with a higher VLF. These associations were more evident among participants not receiving beta-blocker therapy. Future prospective investigations are needed to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Red–blue light ratios shape growth, physiological responses and leaf metabolic profiles in tissue-cultured Zingiber officinale plantlets
Article.Authors: Jiao X.; Li D.; Wahyuni D.; Subramaniam S.
Article.Abstract: Light quality regulates in vitro plant development, but the integrated responses of ginger plantlets to different red–blue light ratios remain unclear. Tissue-cultured Zingiber officinale Roscoe plantlets were exposed for eight weeks to white light (W), red light (R), blue light (B), or combined red–blue light at 1:1 (RB11), 1:3 (RB13), or 3:1 (RB31). Morphological traits, physiological and biochemical parameters, and untargeted leaf metabolic profiles were analysed. R primarily promoted stem elongation (mean stem length 46.0% higher than W) but produced relatively fewer buds, leaves and roots. B increased soluble sugar and protein contents and produced the lowest malondialdehyde level (19.7% below W). RB31 showed high catalase and peroxidase activities together with relatively low malondialdehyde. RB13 produced the highest bud and root numbers (root number 21.3% above W), maintained a high leaf number, enhanced carotenoid accumulation, and was associated with candidate responses involving lipid, phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, glutathione, polyamine and carbon–nitrogen metabolism. Only linoleic acid metabolism in B versus W remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Overall, the treatments induced distinct growth, physiological and metabolic response patterns. RB13 showed the most balanced response among the combined red–blue treatments and may be suitable for improving in vitro ginger plantlet quality.

Article.Title: Combined application of nanobiochar, silicon, and iron nanoparticles mitigates multiple heavy metal stress in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum)
Article.Authors: Mustafa R.; Jamal A.; Hamarashid S.; Salih D.; Hamze H.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the efficacy of nanobiochar (NB) and foliar Si/Fe nanoparticles in mitigating multiple heavy metal stress (HMS) in tomato. A three-factor factorial greenhouse experiment (completely randomized design, five replications) was conducted in 2023: soil amendment (control vs. 1% w/w NB), foliar spray (control, Si, Fe, Si + Fe at 2 g L⁻¹), and growth condition (normal vs. HMS from wastewater). HMS induced significant oxidative stress, as evidenced by increased H₂O₂ and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, reduced photosynthetic pigment levels, and lower fruit yield. However, NB plus foliar nanoparticles, especially in combination, markedly alleviated HMS toxicity. The most effective treatment (NB + Si + Fe) increased key antioxidant enzymes (CAT, SOD, APX) and non-enzymatic antioxidants (proline, sugars, phenols, flavonoids), thereby decreasing H₂O₂ and MDA levels. Consequently, chlorophyll a , b , and carotenoid content increased under HMS. This treatment also reduced Cd, Pb, Cr, Cu, and Zn uptake in plant tissues and enhanced fruit yield by more than 57.14% compared to the stressed control. Integrated Biomarker Response version 2 (IBRv2) showed that NB + Fe (I = − 0.01) and NB + Si+Fe (I = − 0.02) produced the smallest negative deviation in growth indices and the greatest increase in antioxidant defense. Co-application of nanobiochar with Si + Fe nanoparticles is a highly effective strategy for sustaining tomato productivity in heavy-metal-contaminated soils, offering a promising nano-remediation approach for sustainable agriculture that warrants field-scale validation.

Article.Title: Behavioral deficits in Caenorhabditis elegans raised for six generations under Mars-analog gravity and hypomagnetic fields
Article.Authors: Akinosho A.; Armstrong N.; Benefield Z.; Dai X.; Stein W.; Vidal-Gadea A.
Article.Abstract: Life on Mars will require organisms to endure sustained exposure to reduced gravity and near-absent planetary magnetism, yet little is known about how these factors combine to affect biology across generations. Here, we investigated the effects of Mars-analog gravity and magnetism on neuromuscular, sensory, and morphological function using Caenorhabditis elegans as a model. Animals were reared continuously under ground-based Mars-analog conditions for six generations and assessed at Generations 2, 4, and 6. We reasoned that developmental disruption could manifest at several levels and assayed body morphology, crawling, swimming, and chemotaxis. Animals remained viable and reproduced in every lineage. Body morphology and crawling behavior remained mostly unaffected whereas chemotaxis was unaffected at first but declined progressively across generations. Swimming frequency was reduced from the earliest generation assayed and did not worsen thereafter. The two deficits followed different time courses suggesting that they arise from different mechanisms. Neither was reproduced by six generations of passive housing in Earth conditions in the unpowered apparatus. Because gravity and magnetic field were varied together, these effects cannot be attributed to either factor alone. Our results show that a Mars-analog environment alters behavior in a terrestrial animal without altering its body plan, and that one of these changes was detected only after several generations. Experiments confined to endpoints that do not challenge the organism would have missed the first deficit, and experiments confined to a single generation would have missed the second.

Article.Title: Performance-based determination of optimal slip force of Pall friction dampers for multiple seismic hazard levels using endurance time method
Article.Authors: Shams M.; Zahrai S.; Shirkhani A.
Article.Abstract: The incorporation of friction damper devices mitigates damage to primary structural members by dissipating seismic energy through controlled frictional mechanisms. Among the earliest and most extensively implemented friction-based devices are Pall friction dampers (PFDs). The endurance time method (ETM) reduces the computational effort required for obtaining structural responses and enables their estimation across multiple seismic hazard levels through a single analysis. The optimal slip force of PFDs is a key design parameter of these dampers. However, the optimal slip force determined for a specific seismic hazard level does not necessarily ensure satisfactory performance of structures equipped with these dampers across multiple seismic hazard levels. Hence, in this study, using ETM, a practical procedure is suggested for obtaining the optimal slip force of PFDs at multiple hazard levels. To this end, cases including 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-story moment-resisting frames are considered. Then, the performance of structures with optimal PFDs and without PFDs is compared at different hazard levels. A comparison between the results of the ETM and conventional nonlinear time-history analysis using far-field ground motion records of FEMA P695 revealed a discrepancy of approximately 10%, indicating that the ETM predicts structural responses with acceptable accuracy. The investigation of PFDs' hysteretic behavior showed a more significant contribution by dampers located on the lower stories.

Article.Title: No detectable BK polyomavirus or JC polyomavirus DNA in FFPE specimens from patients with advanced laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Doulaptsi M.; Tseliou M.; Karatzanis A.; Akoumianakis E.; Tzardi M.; Prokopakis E.; Velegrakis G.; Sourvinos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human polyomaviruses (HPyVs) exhibit oncogenic potential, and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) is an established cause of Merkel cell carcinoma. While BK and JC polyomaviruses possess oncogenic properties, their etiological contribution to head and neck squamous cell carcinomas, specifically laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains highly controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the presence of BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) in advanced LSCC to clarify their potential role. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor specimens were obtained retrospectively from 35 patients with advanced (pT3–pT4a) LSCC treated with total laryngectomy. BKPyV and JCPyV DNA was investigated by real-time PCR, with co-amplification of the human β-globin gene as an internal control for DNA amplifiability and PCR inhibition. Amplifiable genomic DNA was confirmed in all 35 samples. No JCPyV or BKPyV DNA was detected in any specimen (0/35 for each virus; 95% CI 0–10.0%). The absence of detectable JCPyV and BKPyV genomes in the examined specimens does not support a frequent or persistent presence of BKPyV and JCPyV in advanced LSCC. However, we cannot definitively exclude transient early-stage viral involvement, low-level infection or varying prevalence in different populations.

Article.Title: Lyapunov-based adaptive path tracking control of wheeled mobile robots using a self-organizing recurrent Gaussian-gating functional-link fuzzy neural network
Article.Authors: Khater A.; Chen Y.; Maoudj A.; Aouaichia A.
Article.Abstract: A recurrent Gaussian gating functional-link fuzzy neural network (RGFL-FNN) is developed into a two-channel path-tracking controller for nonholonomic mobile robots. The six-layer structure combines Gaussian grade-field gating of fuzzy grades, a first-order recurrent state, and trigonometric functional-link consequents. A normalized descent rule updates the parameters online. On the fully specified discrete-time Pioneer 3-DX study, the controller is compared with three fuzzy-neural networks and an adaptive neural sliding-mode design. On the lemniscate it has the lowest and most consistent error, over twenty noisy trials and wins every paired comparison against the four alternatives. In the noisy run it lowers mean-absolute-error by 51.6% and 66.0% relative to the functional-link and conventional baselines while using three rules instead of five and nine. Ablation results associate the Gaussian grade-field layer with lower error in the tested noisy configuration. Each update executes in 73–146 $$\:\mu\:s$$ within a 10 ms sampling period. An additional MuJoCo run is retained only as an exploratory simulation.

Article.Title: Spatial and temporal context effects in visual perception: crowding, serial dependence, and their interaction
Article.Authors: Cass J.; Jertberg R.; Van der Burg E.
Article.Abstract: Visual perception depends not only on current sensory input but also on its spatial and temporal context. Serial dependence and visual crowding are two well-established phenomena in which perceptual judgments are shaped by recent history and surrounding stimuli, respectively. However, their functional relationship remains unclear. We examined this using orientation and brightness discrimination tasks in which peripheral targets were presented with flankers varying in colour, orientation, and proximity. Robust crowding and reliable trial-to-trial sequential biases emerged in both tasks, with a similar task–stimulus double dissociation, and the two interacted in feature- and location-specific ways. To resolve how crowding shapes serial dependence, we applied a joint logistic decomposition to the two-alternative forced-choice accuracy data, partialling the previous response from the previous stimulus to recover stimulus- and decision-driven contributions separately. The sequential biases were carried predominantly by the previous response, but a reliable stimulus-driven residual remained, particularly for orientation judgments, with opposite sign to the decisional component at both locations: at the same location the decisional was attractive and the residual repulsive; for orientation at different locations both components reversed sign, the decisional becoming repulsive and the residual attractive. Current-trial crowding amplified the decisional carry-over in both tasks. Prior-trial crowding additionally shrank both the decisional and stimulus-driven components for orientation, suggesting that crowding acts upstream of the sequential integration mechanism rather than on the integration itself. Crowding and serial dependence are therefore distinct processes whose interaction is feature-specific and operates through multiple routes: current crowding directly amplifies decisional carry-over; prior crowding both degrades decision reliability and, for orientation only, scales the perceptual representation that sequential integration acts on. These findings recast the link between crowding and serial dependence: rather than parallel manifestations of a single integrative computation, they are dissociable processes whose interaction is asymmetric, feature-specific, and routed through both perceptual and decisional stages.

Article.Title: Community-based RoboGym training improves gross motor function in ambulatory children with cerebral palsy
Article.Authors: Kim C.; Krebs H.; Chung T.; Oh-Park M.; Hallett M.; Choi J.; Kim H.; You S.
Article.Abstract: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) require sustained, intensive, task-specific rehabilitation, yet conventional community-based rehabilitation (CBR) is often limited by insufficient training dose and lack of assistive technologies. In this pragmatic randomized controlled trial, 60 children with CP (mean age 10.4 ± 1.4 years; Gross Motor Function Classification System levels II–III) were allocated 1:1 to a community-based RoboGym (CRG) integrating five robotic modalities in a task-oriented circuit, or to conventional CBR. Both groups received 90-min sessions twice weekly for 6 months. The primary outcome was the Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66); secondary outcomes were the Pediatric Balance Scale (PBS), Functional Independence Measure (FIM), and Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL). Significant Time × Group interactions favored CRG for GMFM-66 ( p = 0.048), PBS ( p = 0.048), and the PedsQL emotional ( p = 0.039) and social functioning ( p = 0.015) domains; differences in FIM ( p = 0.065) and PedsQL physical functioning ( p = 0.076) also favored CRG but were not statistically significant. The CRG mean GMFM-66 percentile advanced from the 36th to the 48th (individual effect size (iES) = 1.14, large), whereas CBR remained near baseline (iES = 0.29). A higher proportion of CRG participants exceeded the minimal detectable change threshold (37–63% vs. 17–27%), a difference that was statistically significant for GMFM-66, PBS, and FIM. Multi-modal robotic circuit training may offer a scalable community-based approach to CP management, although confirmation in larger multicenter trials is required. Article.Title: Landscape heterogeneity is structured by multidimensional components and land-cover proportion interactions
Article.Authors: Bae S.; Westphal C.; Ammer C.; Hostert P.; Hüttel S.; Kis-Katos K.; Kneib T.; Kreft H.; Paul C.; Plieninger T.; Putzenlechner B.; Rötter R.; Schlund M.; Seidel D.; Siebert S.; Wiegand K.; Knohl A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Landscape heterogeneity is a key driver of biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, and resilience. However, its multiple components—compositional, configurational, vertical, and temporal— are rarely analysed together at broad spatial scales. Compositional heterogeneity refers to the number and proportions of different elements, configurational heterogeneity to their spatial arrangement and shape, vertical heterogeneity to variation in vegetation height, and temporal heterogeneity to interannual variation in land cover and management. Here we examine relationships among these components across forests, croplands, and grasslands using nationwide geospatial data from Germany. We show that compositional and configurational heterogeneity (Shannon diversity vs. edge density) are positively correlated, although their relationship varied with land-cover proportions. Contrary to common assumptions, configurational heterogeneity does not enhance habitat connectivity. Vertical and temporal heterogeneity are largely independent from horizontal heterogeneity. Forests are the main contributors to landscape heterogeneity across land-cover types, whereas croplands contribute little or even negatively. These findings highlight the importance of considering land-cover proportions and multi-dimensional heterogeneity when assessing landscape structure. Our results have broad implications for environmental monitoring and planning for biodiversity and ecosystem assessments, offering a framework to avoid hidden collinearity and consider multi-dimensional perspective and socio-ecological context.

Article.Title: Effects of fiber post and restoration type on endodontically treated maxillary premolars: finite element analysis and in vitro study
Article.Authors: Li R.; Xie W.; Peng X.; Gao Y.; Wan Q.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the influence of fiber post and ceramic restoration types (crown/onlay/overlay) on biomechanical behavior of endodontically treated maxillary premolars using finite element analysis (FEA) and in vitro fracture resistance test. A three-dimensional model of an endodontically treated premolar with MOD cavity was generated. Different restoration scenarios were simulated, including CNP (crown with no fiber post), CP (crown with fiber post), OnNP (onlay with no fiber post), OnP (onlay with fiber post), OvNP (overlay with no fiber post), OvP (overlay with fiber post). A force of 300 N was loaded at a 45° angle to the occlusal surface. von Mises stress values were analyzed. Seventy-two extracted human maxillary premolars were randomly divided into six groups (n = 12) and subjected to in vitro testing. Fracture resistance data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA and Tukey’s HSD tests (α = 0.05). Fracture modes were documented and examined by scanning electron microscopy. FEA analysis demonstrated that premolars with ceramic overlays exhibited the lowest maximum Von Mises stress, regardless of fiber post. The insertion of fiber posts resulted in stress dispersion on the cervical segment of premolars, regardless of restoration type. In vitro study indicated that no significant differences existed in fracture resistance among six treatment groups. The proportion of restorable fractures was highest in the OvP group and lowest in the CNP group. Restoration types did not significantly improve biomechanical behaviors of endodontically treated premolars. Placement of fiber post did not significantly increase fracture resistance, although it altered stress distribution and was associated with a numerically higher proportion of restorable fractures in some groups.
