Article.Title: Prevalence of drug-related hospital admissions and associated factors among chronic internal medicine wards in Wolaita Sodo University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital
Article.Authors: Dana D.; Paulos G.; Dawit M.; Toma A.
Article.Abstract: Drug therapy is fundamental to clinical care, aiming to optimize outcomes while minimizing risks. However, increased medication use has raised the prevalence of drug-related problems (DRPs), which may lead to serious consequences, highlighting the need for proper management and monitoring. Therefore, the objective of this study was to assess the prevalence of drug-related hospital admissions (DRHA) among chronic care patients and its associated. An institutional-based cross-sectional study was conducted using a previously validated tool. Descriptive statistics summarized sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, while binary logistic regression identified associated factors. Variables with a p -value < 0.25 in bivariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to control for potential confounders. A p -value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant at a 95% confidence level. Out of 367 patients, 34.6% experienced DRHAs. Significant predictors included comorbidities, chronic kidney disease (CKD), younger age, and urban residence. Patients with ≥ 3 comorbidities had 3.25-fold higher odds (AOR = 3.25, 95% CI 1.75–6.04), 1–2 comorbidities nearly doubled the risk (AOR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.21–3.23), CKD increased risk (AOR = 2.41, 95% CI 1.41–4.13), young adults aged 18–35 had higher odds (AOR = 1.65, 95% CI 1.01–2.69), and urban residents had 54% higher odds (AOR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.01–2.35). DRHAs were considerably high in the study setting. The most common causes were noncompliance, untreated indications, unnecessary drugs, and adverse drug reactions, most of which were preventable.

Article.Authors: Pegoraro S.; Toffoli M.; Balduit A.; Zito G.; Fogar B.; Hervatich G.; Romano F.; Ricci G.; Bulla R.; Agostinis C.
Article.Abstract: Molecular studies of the human placenta may reveal gene expression alterations responsible for impaired placentation and the subsequent development of pregnancy complications ( e.g. , preeclampsia, fetal-growth restriction, pre-term birth) characterised by a significantly increased risk of maternal and newborn mortality. This study systematically evaluated six candidate housekeeping genes ( ACTB , GAPDH , HPRT1 , RPS18 , TBP , YWHAZ ) in human placental tissues (first/third-trimester, preeclampsia) and trophoblast cell lines (BeWo, HTR-8/SVneo, JAR, JEG-3). Strong transcriptional divergence was identified between tissue samples and cell lines; restricting the analysis to placental tissue samples significantly improved stability values. Among the six candidate genes tested, the RefFinder comprehensive ranking identified GAPDH and HPRT1 as the most stable reference pair for placental tissues. Normalization with this pair successfully detected significant differences in CD93 expression across groups, whereas the least stable combination ( TBP/YWHAZ ) failed to do so. The geometric mean of GAPDH and HPRT1 provides a robust normalization strategy among the candidates evaluated here for qPCR studies in human placental tissues across physiological and pathological conditions.

Article.Title: Association of glycemic variability with delirium and mortality in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia: a retrospective analysis
Article.Authors: Li M.; Zhang Y.; Zhang L.; Luo Y.; Tang X.; Dong Q.; Xiao Q.; He Z.; Zhang L.; Ma H.
Article.Abstract: Delirium frequently complicates the course of critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Nursing screening tools such as the CAM-ICU remain subjective and fail to capture underlying metabolic disturbances. Glycemic variability (GV) which can be calculated from routine glucose measurements collected by nursing staff, has been linked to delirium and poor outcomes in general ICU populations but has not been fully explored in CAP patients. This study evaluates whether GV is associated with delirium onset and one-year mortality in ICU-admitted CAP patients, with the goal of informing targeted, evidence-based nursing interventions. This retrospective cohort study analyzed 6,167 ICU patients with CAP from the MIMIC-IV database. GV was measured using the coefficient of variation of blood glucose values and divided into tertiles. The primary outcome was delirium, identified by at least one positive CAM-ICU assessment. Secondary outcomes included 1-year mortality and ICU length of stay. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between GV and delirium, while Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate the association between GV and 1-year mortality. Kaplan–Meier curves and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to examine the associations between GV and clinical outcomes, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory performance of multivariable models incorporating GV and prespecified covariates. A sensitivity analysis using a fixed 72-hour exposure window was performed to assess the robustness of the primary findings. Among 6,167 critically ill patients with CAP, 54.3% developed delirium, the overall 1-year mortality rate was 45.2%, and the median ICU length of stay was 4.30 days (IQR 2.37–9.08). After full adjustment, each unit increase in log-GV was independently associated with higher odds of delirium (OR, 1.328; 95% CI, 1.177–1.499) and a higher hazard of 1-year mortality (HR, 1.081; 95% CI, 1.006–1.162). The highest GV tertile (GV3) exhibited a delirium incidence of 58.40% and significantly greater mortality compared with GV1 ( P < 0.001). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed lower survival in GV3 (log-rank P < 0.001). Restricted cubic splines showed a nonlinear positive association with delirium (P nonlinearity = 0.002) and a linear relationship with mortality (P nonlinearity = 0.65). ROC curves yielded AUCs of 0.82 for delirium and 0.74 for 1-year mortality. GV was significantly associated with delirium and 1-year mortality in critically ill patients with CAP. GV may serve as a potential risk marker for identifying patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes. Further prospective studies are warranted to determine whether targeted assessment or modification of GV can improve clinical outcomes.

Article.Title: Effect of freezing rain-induced changes in dry deposition on particulate matter concentrations in Hubei, China
Article.Authors: Tian T.; Xia X.; Wang L.; Zhu B.; Zhu Z.; Zhang T.; Zhang M.; Huang Y.; Han W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a critical aspect of urban air quality degradation, and vegetation mitigates atmospheric PM concentrations via dry deposition, offering a natural, sustainable, and cost-effective strategy for pollution mitigation. Based on multi-source satellite remote sensing products, this study quantified the dry deposition effect of PM 2.5 and PM 10 on vegetation using a mathematical model, and evaluated its spatial and temporal changes in the long-term series in Hubei province, especially the impact of dry deposition changes induced by the extreme freezing rain process in early 2024 on particulate matter pollution. The key findings are as follows: (1) Leaf Area Index (LAI) showed a significant negative correlation with PM 2.5 and PM 10 , and modeled dry deposition flux (DDF) showed consistent coherence with LAI, Land Surface Temperature (LST), Wind Speed (WS), and Precipitation (PRE) at the one-month scale; (2) The physical damage caused by the freezing rain substantially diminished the vegetation’s capacity for particulate matter deposition, with the reduction of the deposition effect of PM 10 being more pronounced than that of PM 2.5 ; (3) A decadal spatiotemporal analysis of dry deposition on vegetation indicated an overall trend toward improving air quality in Hubei and further revealed stronger spatial heterogeneity in the long-term trend of PM 2.5 dry-deposition reduction than that of PM 10 , partly reflecting differences in regional socioeconomic and industrial activity and background PM concentrations. This study advances a deeper understanding of the influence of extreme weather events on vegetation-driven dry deposition and provides scientific support for air quality management and strategic development aimed at strengthening urban ecosystem resilience.

Article.Title: Pistacia khinjuk oil enhances oxidative stability of a corn-canola-sesame frying oil blend during six months of storage under repeated thermal treatment
Article.Authors: Khajeh-mehrizi R.; Ardakani S.; Alizadeh A.
Article.Abstract: The degradation of frying oils during thermal processing and storage poses a significant challenge to food quality. This study investigated the impact of blending frying oil with Pistacia khinjuk oil at concentrations of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% on oxidative stability and physicochemical properties over a six-month storage under thermal condition. The 20% P. khinjuk oil blend (TK20) exhibited superior oxidative stability, maintaining a high induction period (18.52 ± 0.01 h at month 1; 18.39 ± 0.00 h at month 6). Acid value was significantly reduced in TK20 (0.056 ± 0.001% at month 6, P < 0.05), peroxide values were lower in TK20 (5.30 ± 0.05 meq O₂/kg) compared to the control (7.6 ± 0.11 meq O₂/kg) at month 6, and the Totox values were also reduced in TK20 (16.2 ± 0.00) relative to the control(19.7 ± 0.00), indicating effective inhibition of both primary and overall oxidation. Polar compound formation was inhibited dose-dependently, with TK20 remaining below the 10% safety threshold (9.2 ± 0.00% at month 6). These findings demonstrate that P. khinjuk oil serves as an effective natural stabilizer, increasing frying oil shelf life and safety, offering a sustainable alternative to synthetic antioxidants with potential health benefits.

Article.Title: A garment-integrated shape-changing actuator for facilitating dressing
Article.Authors: Nipatphonsakun K.; Hayashi I.; Watanabe T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dressing is a fundamental activity of daily living that becomes challenging for individuals with motor impairments, particularly when garment twisting, wrinkling, and limited armhole space hinder smooth limb insertion. This study presents a garment-integrated shape-changing actuator designed to increase localized stiffness, preserve garment structure, expand the armhole, and reduce friction between the fabric and skin. Flat-tube pneumatic actuators were embedded into a long-sleeved shirt to dynamically maintain garment geometry during dressing. Mechanical evaluations showed that actuator activation increased armhole resistance and reduced sleeve friction compared with the inactive condition. A user study involving 32 participants under normal and simulated hemiplegic conditions revealed a significant reduction in dressing time when dominant-arm impairment was simulated, alongside improved subjective ratings of dressing ease (p < 0.001). Although objective improvements were not observed for non-dominant impairment, participants consistently reported enhanced perceived ease. These findings suggest that actively maintaining garment shape can facilitate dressing motions and reduce interaction barriers between the wearer and clothing. By supporting user participation rather than replacing it, the proposed approach highlights the potential of garment-integrated soft actuators as an interaction-level assistive technology to support independent dressing while preserving residual functional abilities.

Article.Title: Adaptive fuzzy fault-tolerant PID controller design for a single-tank level process in the presence of sensor faults and disturbances
Article.Authors: Barzgar F.; Azmi H.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the implementation and evaluation of a water level control system using Arduino and MATLAB. The main objective is to analyze and compare the performance of different controllers in a real experimental setup. The dynamic behavior of the system is identified based on experimental data, and the system transfer function is approximated as a first-order model. Based on this model, the PID controller parameters are designed and tuned in the Simulink environment. The controller performance is then evaluated in real time through direct communication with the Arduino platform. In this study, manual control is completely eliminated, and MATLAB/Simulink fully undertakes the control task of the system. Furthermore, various types of potential sensor faults are systematically implemented, and their effects on system performance are analyzed. To improve the response of the classical PID controller, a Fuzzy-PID controller is employed. This improvement is particularly evident in reducing overshoot and shortening the disturbance-recovery time. In addition, the system response is examined under both disturbed and disturbance-free operating conditions.

Article.Title: Calcium oxalate crystals provide a supporting matrix for the leaf structure
Article.Authors: Brumfeld V.; Sui X.; Wagner H.; Shtein I.; Karimov T.; Feiguelman G.; Cohen M.; Klein T.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the structural role of calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystals within leaf tissues, proposing that they act as a mechanical supporting matrix for leaf structure. Across plant species, CaOx crystals are preferentially positioned around the leaf veins, but their precise architecture is species- and developmental stage-dependent. We focus on leaves of the Mediterranean evergreen tree species carob ( Ceratonia siliqua L.), applying a combination of micro computed tomography (micro-CT) imaging and mechanical testing. We provide data showing that the presence of CaOx crystals increases leaf stiffness. Specifically, we demonstrate the link between CaOx crystals distribution and leaf stiffness across three approaches: (1) among different plant species. (2) Among plants grown with or without Ca. (3) among leaves of the same plant but at different ages. Our data shows that CaOx crystals are not merely metabolic byproducts but are designed to form a mineral-organic structure which specifically enhances the resistance of the midrib and secondary veins to buckling forces. We propose that CaOx acts as a tunable stiffening agent of leaves that plants can modulate based on nutrient availability.

Although multi-teacher distillation has been exploited elsewhere, we quantify teacher complementarity and introduce a mask-boosted feature distillation objective tailored for cattle faces. Without architectural novelty, the pipeline delivers competitive accuracy-efficiency trade-offs on three public datasets, underscoring its practical value.

Article.Authors: Beam C.; DiMeglio L.; Speake C.; Boest-Bjerg K.; Pearce O.; Almutairi B.; Evans-Molina C.; Wong F.; Long A.; Gillespie K.; Pearson J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diurnal islet autoantibody (Aab) variation in type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains poorly understood and could hinder efforts to develop, test and refine new therapies. We also found that, in clinical settings, time-restricted sampling can lead to increased IA-2A and ZnT8A detection within specific age-groups. We conclude that time-restriction can potentially improve the use of Radiobinding-measured Aabs as biomarkers for the development and monitoring of disease-modifying therapies and in developing islet transplantation strategies in established T1D. Article.Title: Disorientation as a marker of neurotrauma in an animal that uses shock waves as weapons
Article.Authors: Mierow T.; Harris K.; Speiser D.; Kingston A.
Article.Abstract: By snapping their claws, snapping shrimp create cavitation bubbles that release supersonic pressure waves when they collapse. Shock waves such as these are dangerous to animals because they can cause blast-induced neurotrauma by transferring kinetic energy to neural tissues. To learn how effectively orbital hoods function, we need to be able to compare levels of blast-induced neurotrauma in snapping shrimp. In humans, spatial disorientation is a behavioral hallmark of blast-induced neurotrauma. Here, we develop methods for assessing spatial disorientation in snapping shrimp and ask if shrimp, like humans, demonstrate disorientation following shock wave exposure. Shock wave exposure caused snapping shrimp without orbital hoods to travel longer, slower, and more tortuous paths compared to shrimp with unaltered orbital hoods. Article.Title: Document world models: a cognitive-inspired auxiliary training framework for document-level relation extraction
Article.Authors: Wei F.; Yang W.; Gu T.; Gu B.; Lv H.; Jia L.
Article.Abstract: Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) requires models to integrate relation evidence scattered across multiple sentences. Yet existing encoder-based methods perform relation classification in a single pass over a static final representation, causing long-range evidence to decay before it can inform the classification decision. Inspired by theories of incremental reading comprehension, we introduce the Document World Model (DocWM), a lightweight training-only auxiliary framework that encourages progressive entity-state maintenance and relation-belief stabilization in standard DocRE encoders. DocWM introduces two auxiliary training objectives. Entity State Tracking (ES) maintains an entity-specific recurrent hidden state, updated sentence by sentence and aligned with entity embeddings pooled from mentions up to each sentence to preserve early evidence. Relation Belief Dynamics (BD) supervises relation predictions at each reading step via a temporally weighted loss, guiding relation beliefs to stabilize progressively toward the correct label. Article.Title: Genetic diversity of the endangered saproxylic beetle Boros schneideri and preliminary insight into its associated bacterial and fungal communities
Article.Authors: Kaczmarczyk-Ziemba A.; Wagner G.; Pietrykowska-Tudruj E.; Staniec B.
Article.Abstract: Boros schneideri is a rare and endangered saproxylic beetle associated with old, dead trees. We investigated its genetic diversity in Western Polesie, Poland, and assessed larval microbiota and mycobiota. COI sequences were additionally compared with records from Poland, Finland, and Mongolia. Both mitochondrial and nuclear datasets revealed high haplotype diversity and moderate nucleotide diversity, while phylogenetic trees and haplotype networks showed shallow relationships without distinct, well-supported geographic lineages. Shared COI haplotypes occurred among geographically distant populations. Negative Tajima’s D and Fu’s Fs values, together with the diversity pattern, were consistent with a possible recent demographic expansion. No Wolbachia infection was detected. High-throughput sequencing targeting the bacterial 16 S rRNA V3–V4 region and fungal ITS1 revealed diverse bacterial communities in 11 larvae, dominated by Proteobacteria, particularly Burkholderiaceae and Yersiniaceae. Preliminary mycobiota profiling of one larva identified predominantly Ascomycota, including Ophiostoma , previously suggested as a potential food resource. Despite limited sampling, these findings provide a baseline for understanding the genetic and microbial diversity of B. schneideri and support integrating population genetics and microbiome research into future conservation studies.

Article.Title: Perfusion-guided virtual element analysis for biomechanical diagnosis of breast cysts and tumors
Article.Authors: Mohana R.; Chandru M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the most common cancers in the world. There is a pressing need for sophisticated diagnostic techniques that can identify anomalies in their earliest, benign stages. Although infrared thermography provides a non-invasive way to monitor surface temperature distributions, the lack of quantitative, parameter-based markers limits its clinical utility. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations of the model, such as the derivation of optimal convergence rates, error estimates in the $$L^2$$ -norm, and demonstrations of existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution, in order to guarantee the robustness of VEM. Our methodology incorporates the Pennes bioheat equation into the virtual element method to determine blood perfusion ranges from thermal profiles corresponding to healthy, cystic, and malignant tissues, in contrast to traditional approaches that assume constant perfusion. By methodically mapping these thermal signatures against the selected perfusion ranges, pathological zones are identified, offering a diagnostic approach comparable to the application of biochemical markers in clinical settings. By creating perfusion-based quantitative markers, this framework enhances thermo-graphic diagnostic potential and opens the door to better early identification and characterization of breast tissue abnormalities.

Article.Title: A Caputo fractional physics-informed neural network for Lorenz chaotic systems
Article.Authors: Baskar A.; Naveen S.
Article.Abstract: Fractional-order dynamical systems provide an effective mathematical framework for describing nonlinear processes with memory and hereditary effects. The reference solutions are generated using the Caputo Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM) predictor-corrector method to ensure an appropriate numerical treatment of the fractional derivative. The proposed framework is evaluated for several fractional orders over the considered simulation interval, and its predictive performance is assessed using quantitative error metrics, including mean squared error, mean absolute error, sum of squared errors, and the coefficient of determination. The numerical results demonstrate that the FPINN accurately reconstructs the fractional Lorenz trajectories while maintaining good agreement with the ABM reference solutions. Furthermore, the study investigates the influence of the fractional order on prediction accuracy and computational performance, providing a systematic numerical assessment of the proposed framework. The results indicate that FPINNs constitute an effective and data-efficient approach for approximating nonlinear fractional dynamical systems within the investigated computational setting.

Article.Authors: Ekrami Kakhki S.; Kheyroddin A.
Article.Abstract: The bond behavior of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) and steel rebars in advanced cementitious composites is governed by a complex interplay of rebar type, concrete matrix, confinement, embedment length, and geometric parameters, yet it remains insufficiently understood. Bottom concrete cover, transverse reinforcement, and fiber-induced confinement critically enhance stress transfer and mitigate splitting failures. Steel and glass fibers significantly improve bond performance via crack bridging and confinement, whereas polypropylene fibers mainly reduce shrinkage-induced cracking. The findings advance understanding of size effects, stress redistribution, and confinement efficiency in SCC and FRC systems and provide a robust experimental basis for developing improved bond models and design guidelines for FRP-reinforced concrete structures.

Article.Authors: Hussain I.; Badar H.; Alhwikem F.
Article.Abstract: Federated learning (FL) trains shared models on consumer IoT devices without moving raw data off the device, but poisoning can compromise it. It has the highest mean accuracy, or matches it, in 9 of 15 attacked settings, and is within one percentage point of the best in 13. Ablation shows that the norm clip provides most of this robustness. The trust layer excludes every Gaussian noise adversary, excluding at most 2.9% of benign clients, but no sign flipping or ALIE adversary. Article.Authors: Khodaei S.; Sarvari M.; Sajadi E.; Asadzadeh F.; Ebrahimian H.; Rahgozar M.; Kavousi K.
Article.Abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, affecting millions of people each year. There are many different types of cancer, including breast cancer, colon cancer and endometrial cancer, each with its own unique characteristics and challenges. One of the most crucial aspects of cancer management is early detection. Detecting cancer at an early stage significantly increases the chances of successful treatment and survival. In recent years, much research has been conducted to accelerate the diagnosis and prediction of cancer, especially by examining the role of genes, their effectiveness, and especially the sequence of changes in their activities in relation to this disease. An important part of the results of these studies has been related to KEGG signaling pathways. Many studies have also been conducted to model these signaling pathways via Petri net tools, which have shown good capabilities in this field. This article reveals in part some of these capabilities observed in a recently developed tool that provides a means for diagnosing breast cancer by modeling the related signaling pathway via Petri nets. The proposed method provides high accuracy and precision (95–99%) on most related GEO datasets. Similar promising results have been reported in various cancers and will be published soon. With this method, blood samples, which are less expensive and easier to obtain for earlier detection, perform as well as tissue samples.

Article.Title: Eigenmodes of synthetic antiferromagnetic skyrmions
Article.Authors: Zulfiqar K.; Lang M.; Holt S.; Pathak S.; Bruckner F.; Fangohr H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate the excitation modes of confined synthetic-antiferromagnetic (SAF) skyrmions using micromagnetic eigenvalue and ringdown simulations. We consider several geometries: single SAF skyrmions in square and rectangular confinement, unequal layer thicknesses, and strips containing multiple skyrmions. The antiferromagnetic coupling strongly modifies the low-frequency dynamics. The square geometry exhibits two nearly degenerate gyrotropic modes, where in each both layers have the same rotation sense. In rectangular geometries, we instead find nearly linear SAF skyrmion translation emerging from opposite gyration sense in the two layers. These translational modes become the characteristic low-frequency excitations of SAF skyrmion chains. For skyrmion chains, we identify collective translational and breathing modes with standing-wave-like spatial profiles. Beyond ferromagnetic-like breathing modes, the SAF geometry supports breathing oscillations in which the two layers oscillate out of phase. We further demonstrate signal propagation along extended SAF skyrmion chains with propagation velocities about 15% larger than in ferromagnetic skyrmion chains. These results provide a systematic description of the collective dynamics of SAF skyrmions arising from the interplay of geometric confinement, intralayer, and interlayer coupling.

Article.Authors: Ti Y.; Cheng R.; Wei S.; Huang W.; Yu C.
Article.Abstract: The limited energy capacity of sensor nodes remains a central constraint on the operational longevity of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs)-a challenge that is more critical in Rechargeable Wireless Sensor Networks (RWSNs), where sustaining long-term functionality depends on delaying the First Node Death (FND), a key point that often signals the beginning of network problems. While prior research has extensively explored heuristic algorithms coupled with energy-aware routing mechanisms to reduce transmission energy consumption and extend network lifetime, these methods typically require repeated iterations to converge. Such computational demands render them unsuitable for real-time applications. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a hybrid optimization framework that integrates Genetic Algorithms (GA) with Deep Learning (DL). This framework can run quickly to improve energy efficiency and extend network lifetime in RWSNs. The proposed approach builds upon an energy-aware clustering architecture that incorporates a lightweight version of the Residual Neural Network (ResNet) model. This clustering strategy promotes a more balanced distribution of energy consumption across the network, delaying early node failures caused by localized energy depletion. Based on this setup, we create an optimization scheme using a novel version of GA that helps the ResNet model-simplified for use on regular CPUs-learns an optimal CH selection policy. The GA component employs a custom fitness function designed to maximize the time to FND latency. The synergy between the clustering method and the GA-DL hybrid selection mechanism enables rapid and effective CH assignment without the iterative overhead typical of heuristic algorithms. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only reduces energy consumption and extends the time to FND but also achieves near real-time performance. This makes it a promising alternative to traditional heuristic-based approaches, particularly in latency-sensitive RWSN applications. Together, these contributions mark a significant step toward the development of scalable, efficient, and resilient RWSN architectures.

Article.Authors: Cosemans S.; Heirman E.; Broux H.; Volders J.; Leufkens L.; Ghogare D.; Verheijen M.; Paez J.; Elen K.; Mann D.; Hardy A.; Van Bael M.; Buskens P.

The influence of tungsten incorporation on phase formation and on the thermodynamics and kinetics of the SPT was investigated. Structural and morphological analyses show that W 6+ promotes the formation of phase-pure monoclinic and rutile VO 2 . Differential scanning calorimetry revealed switching enthalpies between 15 and 36 J g –1 and a decrease in phase transition temperature with increasing W content. Isoconversional kinetic analysis demonstrated that the SPT is governed by nucleation kinetics, resulting in a temperature-dependent activation barrier that increases strongly as the temperature approaches the critical switching temperature. Article.Title: Ontogenetic gains in photosynthetic capacity and winter–summer photoprotective contrasts in wild Camellia formosensis across light environments
Article.Authors: Shen J.; Wang C.; Jhou H.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Camellia formosensis , Taiwan’s only native tea-producing tree, is near-threatened and increasingly cultivated as a forest-understory crop, yet light-management guidance derives largely from nursery seedlings. Light-adapted photosystem II efficiency was markedly lower in winter than in summer in both light environments, coinciding with a site minimum temperature of 5.4 °C; non-photochemical quenching was higher under shade in winter but under full sun in summer. SPAD and PRI were consistently higher under shade. Wild-tree Amax (6.1–14.2 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1) was two- to three-fold that of one-year-old seedlings measured with the same protocol, consistent with an ontogenetic increase in photosynthetic capacity. Article.Title: Spatial multi-omics identifies regional immunometabolic remodeling and macrophage PCK2-associated T-cell activation in lupus nephritis
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Li A.; Guo Q.; Wen M.; Zhao L.; Tan S.; Peng M.; Kong M.; Xu Z.; Zheng L.; Tang Y.
Article.Abstract: Poor response of lupus nephritis (LN) to conventional therapies frequently results in persistent renal inflammation and progression of chronic renal insufficiency. The complex pathogenesis of LN, characterized by microregional immune heterogeneity and interregional crosstalk, greatly hinders identification of the core immune network initiating disease and development of effective therapeutic strategies. Given that metabolic reprogramming drives immune cell activation, exploring region-specific immunometabolic characteristics of LN kidneys is critical for clarifying disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets. This study integrated spatial proteomics, spatial metabolomics and multiplexed immunofluorescence to map the spatial immune landscape of three key regions (glomerulus, renal tubules, medulla) in LN kidneys and analyzed their distinct metabolic profiles. Significant region-specific immunometabolic dysregulation was observed. The glomerular region was enriched with neutrophils and exhibited purine metabolism disorder with upregulated ADCY4; the renal tubules showed obvious T cell aggregation and glycerophospholipid imbalance with elevated Shmt1; the medulla was characterized by macrophage accumulation and increased PCK2 expression within a pyruvate associated metabolic signature. In an inflammatory macrophage–T-cell co-culture model, PCK2 knockdown in macrophages reduced macrophage and T-cell activation readouts. This study delineates distinct region-specific immunometabolic landscapes and key regulatory molecules across different renal compartments in LN. Functional perturbation in vitro further indicated that macrophage PCK2 contributes to T-cell activation under inflammatory co-culture conditions. These findings reveal the heterogeneous immunometabolic pathogenesis of LN and provide promising region-specific metabolic targets for the precise treatment of refractory LN.

These findings support selecting augmentation according to the intended representation task and reviewing intermediate drawings alongside final layouts. A Morgan ECFP4 random-forest comparator gave the best compound-grouped regression result ( \(R^2=0.739\pm 0.065\) ), but its performance declined under scaffold separation ( \(R^2=0.472\pm 0.303\) ). The connectivity-index blocks did not significantly improve the RDKit-only models after Holm adjustment. Article.Authors: Dickinson M.; Duval M.; Penkman K.

Consequently, this supports cautious reuse of irradiated ESR powders, preferably those exposed to low laboratory doses, enabling effective reuse of finite fossil tooth enamel resources.

Article.Authors: Bertho A.; Martinez Vicente P.; Fernandez Rodriguez A.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Moros M.; Prezado Y.

Article.Authors: Pavez V.; Melgar-Rodríguez S.; Selman J.; González-Osuna L.; Díaz-Zúñiga J.; Cafferata E.; Carvajal P.; Bravo D.; Vernal R.
Article.Abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a keystone periodontal pathogen whose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contributes to immune dysregulation during periodontitis. Article.Authors: Kabtyimer A.; Jemil H.; Endalkachew A.; Mankelkl G.; Kassaw A.; Abeje E.

The observed improvements in performance metrics confirm a well-balanced trade-off between sensitivity and specificity. Further, Area under the Curve and radar analyses confirm enhanced discriminative capability which highlights the consistent advantage across architectures and datasets for hybrid optimization techniques. Article.Authors: Sridhar J.; Unnissa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blockchain technology has emerged as an innovative digital solution aimed at enhancing transparency, traceability, and trust within closed-loop supply chains, particularly in the domains of remanufacturing and recycling operations. This study formulates a Blockchain-enabled Closed-Loop Supply Chain model that incorporates an original equipment manufacturer $$(M-R)$$ , a retailer-third party $$(R-3p)$$ , and a manufacturer-third party $$(M-3P)$$ . In light of Blockchain investment costs, privacy concerns, information transparency, and competitive dynamics in recycling, a Stackelberg game framework is developed to analyze optimal pricing strategies, collection decisions, and overall profitability. The research investigates the impact of collection competition and Blockchain-related parameters on supply chain performance. Through numerical analysis and sensitivity assessments, the findings reveal that the adoption of Blockchain technology enhances acceptance rates for remanufactured products and influences channel decision-making, whereas intensified competition in collection efforts tends to diminish individual collection performance. The results indicate that the $$M-R$$ model exhibits superior economic performance, while the $$M-3P$$ model demonstrates greater recycling efficiency in the context of intense competition. This research contributes theoretical insights and practical guidance for the design of sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chains through the strategic integration of blockchain technology and optimized recycling channel selection.

Article.Title: Control of source–migration–trap coupling on hydrocarbon accumulation in the Shahejie Formation, Qikou Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Liu W.; Fu G.; Liang M.; Zhang D.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of hydrocarbon accumulation in continental rift basins remains a major challenge in petroleum geoscience because the relative roles of hydrocarbon supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness are often poorly constrained. Focusing on the lower section of the first member of the Shahejie Formation (Es 1 L ), this study formulates a hierarchical control framework that synthesizes source supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness to elucidate the mechanisms of hydrocarbon accumulation. Integrating three-dimensional (3D) seismic, well logging, and geochemical data, this study delineates the distribution of effective source rocks, systematically characterizes vertical and lateral hydrocarbon migration pathways, and identifies the development locations of effective traps in the target interval combined with the evaluation of fault lateral sealing capacity to carry out coupled hydrocarbon accumulation analysis of source-migration-trap. A total of 18 migration pathways and 24 effective trap locations were identified. The hierarchical framework identifies source-rock expulsion intensity as the first-order control, defining the upper limit of hydrocarbon supply; migration-pathway architecture as the second-order control, regulating hydrocarbon focusing, dispersion, and charging efficiency; and trap effectiveness, particularly fault sealing capacity, as the third-order control, governing hydrocarbon preservation and final filling degree. The results indicate that hydrocarbons mainly accumulate in zones with optimal matching of source-migration-trap elements, characterized by sufficient hydrocarbon supply from source rocks, unobstructed migration pathways and effective trap conditions. Production-testing results from Well BS-4, located within one of the predicted favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones, provide field-based support for the proposed coupling framework. The proposed hierarchical source-migration-trap framework provides a process-based approach for evaluating favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones in lower-source upper-reservoir petroleum systems of mature faulted basins.

Article.Title: Multi-omics profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in mouse hippocampal CA1 following adolescent social isolation
Article.Authors: Kubota A.; Shinohara Y.; Goto A.; Tajima A.
Article.Abstract: Social isolation (SI) during adolescence is associated with neurobiological alterations; however, its effect on the hippocampal epigenome and transcriptome remains unclear. We performed ATAC-seq and RNA-seq of hippocampal CA1 in an adolescent mouse SI model, with single-cell RNA-seq reference mapping and cell type deconvolution. ATAC-seq identified candidate SI-associated chromatin accessibility alterations, with nominal functional enrichment linking increased enhancer-associated regions to calcium transport and decreased promoter regions to synaptic organization. Motif analysis showed enrichment of the activator protein 1 (AP-1) motif among candidate regions with reduced accessibility. RNA-seq identified 106 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including upregulated Fosl2 and Hdac9 and downregulated Fbxw7 , with enrichment of myelination-related pathways. Although global concordance between chromatin accessibility and transcriptional changes was limited, integrated analysis showed directional concordance between expression and nearby candidate accessibility changes for a subset of DEGs. Cell type analyses suggested that SI-downregulated transcriptional signatures were linked to excitatory neurons, whereas SI-upregulated signatures were enriched in non-neuronal populations, particularly oligodendrocytes. Deconvolution suggested higher estimated oligodendrocyte representation and lower estimated excitatory neuron representation in isolated mice. These findings suggest that adolescent SI is associated with significant transcriptomic remodeling and candidate chromatin accessibility changes within hippocampal CA1, accompanied by distinct neuronal- and glial-associated transcriptional signatures.

Article.Title: Comparative detection of multielement geochemical anomalies using PCA and Mahalanobis distance in artisanal gold mining soils in eastern Ghana
Article.Authors: Kazapoe R.; Kwaw A.; Sagoe S.; Sagru-Larr P.; Adam A.; Amoah B.; Fynn O.
Article.Abstract: Elemental concentrations in artisanal and small-scale gold mining environments reflect overlapping geological and anthropogenic controls, complicating the identification of multielement geochemical anomalies. This study analysed 665 B-horizon soil samples for 14 elements using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) and applied principal component analysis (PCA), Classical Mahalanobis distance (MD), robust MD, and spatial autocorrelation. PCA retained three components explaining 62.89% of the total variance and identified 60 anomalies (9.02%), compared with 51 (7.67%) for Classical MD and 120 (18.05%) for robust MD. Overall, at least one method identified 164 samples (24.66%), at least two methods identified 57 (8.57%), and all three methods identified 10 (1.50%). PCA showed the strongest spatial dependence, with a Global Moran’s I of 0.1474 (p = 0.002). Local spatial analysis corroborated 25.00% of PCA, 13.73% of Classical MD, and 10.00% of robust MD anomalies. The results indicate that PCA identifies more spatially coherent anomalies, whereas robust MD detects a broader range of unusual multielement compositions. Integrating these methods provides complementary evidence for prioritising locations for field verification and environmental monitoring in mineralised and mining-affected areas.

Article.Title: Interplay between immune cell damage and depletion, population size, ecological factors and Picornavirus infection in the Venice Lagoon (Italy)
Article.Authors: Carella F.; Feola A.; Romano G.; Aceto S.; Garcia-March J.; Tena-Medialdea J.; Prado P.; Mazzero G.; Sabino A.; Sigovini M.
Article.Abstract: We monitored the mortality of the fan mussel Pinna nobilis (L.) in the Venice lagoon (North of Italy) during a period of one and half year (2023–2024) in two areas named Ottagono Alberoni (OA) and Coffa Val Grande (CV) reporting the disease condition for the period time 2024. Host and environmental factors (e.g. pen shell state of infection, size, immune cell depletion with activation of caspase-3, oxygen, temperature, salinity) were investigated and shown to influence morbidity and mortality progressiveness in the two areas. During the study period, Pinna nobilis Picornavirus ( PnPV ) caused systemic hemic infections in all examined individuals (100%) compromising the organelle compartment of the cells activating cell death. Ultrastructure revealed widespread viral replication organelles (vROs) occupying most of the host immune cells that arose from a total rearrangement of cell cytoskeleton that were dedicated to the virus machinery. Our results show a positive correlation between mortality rates and host size, with higher mortality affecting bigger/older individuals, although with local differences. CV pen shell population was characterized by smaller/younger individuals affected by milder viral infections and suffering lower mortality rates. Conversely, OA population presented larger individuals (adults) of P. nobilis affected by heavy viral infections that suffering a 100% mortality rate, leading to the extinction of that population by October 2024. Total Hemocyte Count (THC) was lower in OA (1.77 × 10 4 ±0.16 cell/ml) compared to CV (1.65 × 10 5 ±0.8 cells/ml) showing a negative correlation with viral load, connected with percentage of dead cells percentage, in turn correlated with animal size, suggesting that number of immune cells is regulated by the level of infection, and also age. Collection of hemolymph from the adductor muscle is safe practice for P. nobilis and should be explored to the evaluation of PnPV presence in the fan mussel residual population in the Mediterranean Sea.

Article.Title: The spirometric blind spot: oscillometry identifies a tobacco-dose-associated small-airway signal in community case-finding
Article.Authors: Kotsiou O.; Passalidis K.; Gouta E.; Perlepe G.; Barkas G.; Kirgou P.; Papagiannis D.; Fotiou M.; Diakomanoli K.; Albanou M.; Dimtsi V.; Liaros T.; Karanikola E.; Tsiatsiou X.; Feizoula E.; Gkouletza K.; Laki E.; Nari C.; Koukousa M.; Fanara C.; Litso A.; Plessa A.; Nikolaou A.; Liaskou P.; Rousi S.
Article.Abstract: Small-airway dysfunction (SAD) may precede fixed airflow obstruction, but the clinical meaning of increased oscillometric detection in community settings remains uncertain. In this cross-sectional study, we evaluated an oscillometry-defined SAD phenotype, its concordance with spirometric indices, and its association with cumulative tobacco exposure within an open-access community respiratory case-finding programme. Adults attending nine healthcare sites in Greece underwent structured questionnaire assessment, respiratory oscillometry and spirometry. Oscillometric SAD was defined as any abnormal R5–R19, X5, AX or Fres z-score, whereas spirometric SAD was defined as FEF₂₅–₇₅ <65% predicted. Oscillometric SAD was present in 145/533 (27.2%), spirometric SAD in 71/504 (14.1%), and fixed-ratio airflow obstruction in 18/504 (3.6%). Among 468 participants with complete paired oscillometric and spirometric classifications, positive agreement was low (22.8%; Cohen’s κ = 0.055). Each additional 10 pack-years increased the adjusted odds of oscillometric SAD by 19% among ever-smokers (aOR 1.19, 95% CI 1.05–1.36; p = 0.007) and by 18% among ever-smokers with FEV₁/FVC ≥ 0.70 (aOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.03–1.36; p = 0.020). SAD was also observed in 15/56 participants with asthma (26.8%) and 57/191 never-smokers without a prior chronic respiratory diagnosis (29.8%). Oscillometry therefore identified a tobacco-dose-associated mechanical phenotype that was incompletely captured by spirometric criteria, but its substantial prevalence outside COPD limits disease-specific interpretation.

Article.Title: Physical exercise and interviewer-rated appearance: longitudinal evidence from the China family panel studies, 2010–2022
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical appearance is an important form of social capital, yet limited longitudinal evidence exists on whether it can be shaped by modifiable behaviors such as physical exercise. Using seven waves of data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) collected between 2010 and 2022, this study examines whether changes in exercise behavior are associated with changes in interviewer-rated physical appearance. We construct an unbalanced individual-level panel and estimate fixed-effects models to exploit within-person variation over time while accounting for time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity and survey-year effects. Physical appearance is measured using interviewer evaluations on a 1–7 scale, and physical exercise is primarily measured by weekly exercise frequency. The results show that exercise frequency is positively and significantly associated with appearance ratings: each additional exercise session per week corresponds to a modest increase in interviewer-rated appearance. This positive association remains stable across sequentially adjusted model specifications. However, when total weekly exercise duration is used as an alternative measure, the estimated coefficient is no longer statistically significant. The estimated association is somewhat larger among women than among men, although the gender difference is not statistically significant. In addition, lagged exercise frequency is not significantly associated with current appearance ratings, suggesting that the appearance-related benefits of exercise may be more immediate than persistent. This study contributes to the literature by improving identification relative to prior cross-sectional research through panel fixed-effects estimation and by using interviewer-rated appearance. The findings provide longitudinal evidence that physical exercise is associated with external appearance evaluations in a manner that is relevant to real-world social interactions.

Article.Title: High stimulation rate ABR reveals auditory brainstem conduction abnormalities in vestibular migraine
Article.Authors: Li C.; Huang Y.; Wang Y.; Yang S.; Yu W.; Pan Q.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: To explore the application value of high-stimulation-rate auditory brainstem response (ABR) in evaluating auditory pathway conduction in vestibular migraine (VM) patients and to analyze its correlation with clinical symptoms. A prospective case-control study was conducted, including 56 VM patients (56ears) and 56 healthy controls (56 ears). All subjects underwent acoustic immittance testing, pure-tone audiometry, and ABR testing at low (11.1/s) and high (51.1/s) stimulation rates. The interpeak latency variance of wave I–V (ΔI-VIPL) between high and low stimulation rates was calculated, and ≥ 0.28 ms was defined as the abnormal threshold. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) were used to evaluate headache intensity and dizziness-related handicap, respectively. The correlations between these scores and ΔI-VIPL were also analyzed. At the low stimulation rate, no significant differences in ABR parameters were observed between the control and VM groups ( P > 0.05). At the high stimulation rate, the latencies of waves III and V, as well as the I–III, I–V and ΔI-VIPLs, were significantly prolonged in the VM group ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of abnormal ΔI-VIPL was 69.64% (39/56), which was significantly higher than that in the control group 12.50%(7/56), P < 0.05. ROC curve analysis for discriminating VM patients from healthy controls showed that the optimal cutoff value of ΔI-VIPL was 0.265 ms (AUC = 0.791, sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 87.5%, P < 0.05). Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples supported its stability (bootstrap median 0.265 ms, 95% PI 0.215–0.285 ms). Spearman correlation analysis demonstrated that ΔI-VIPL was significantly positively correlated with the total DHI score ( r s =0.623, P < 0.05) and VAS score ( r s =0.534, P < 0.05). High-stimulation rate auditory evoked potential (ABR) can effectively identify abnormal auditory brainstem pathways in VM patients. The ΔI-VIPL parameters show differences among different clinical subtypes, and are closely related to dizziness-related handicap and headache intensity; however, these associations are cross-sectional and should not be interpreted as causal or independently predictive.Therefore, ΔI-VIPL may serve as an auxiliary electrophysiological metric reflecting brainstem auditory conduction stress in VM patients, although further studies with disease controls are required to confirm its clinical utility.

Article.Title: Generative AI-assisted design problem exploration in interaction design: response disclosure, prompt initiative, and cost-sensitive prompting behavior
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Ibrahim F.; Wang Y.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Zhao S.
Article.Abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in early-stage design exploration, yet experimental evidence is limited on how system-side response disclosure and user-side prompt initiative jointly shape the exploration of design problems that are not yet well defined. In a 2 × 2 within-subject experiment, 48 design students completed four interaction-design tasks involving unfamiliar user groups under one-time versus progressive response disclosure and low versus high prompt initiative, with the composition time of every submission logged. Progressive disclosure was associated with greater perceived understanding change, higher self-reported engagement and germane cognitive load, lower extraneous cognitive load, and more prompts. High prompt initiative showed the same pattern on these four self-reported measures but significantly fewer prompts, reversing the predicted direction; composition time accounted for 18% of the exploration window under high initiative and under 2% under low initiative. Both sets of main effects held after multiplicity correction and adjustment for task and period. An exploratory interaction for germane cognitive load did not survive correction. These findings extend a mixed-initiative view of AI-assisted exploration by identifying response structuring and question formulation as separable design levers. They also indicate that prompt frequency should be interpreted together with the cost of producing a submission.

Article.Title: Comparative benchmarking of the small and nano versions YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 for FDM 3D printing fault detection
Article.Authors: Hany H.; Elashry A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printing is widely used in industrial and consumer applications, but printing failures are often detected only after substantial material and production time have been lost. This study presents a controlled benchmark of four lightweight YOLO object detectors, YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s, YOLOv11n, and YOLOv11s, for in-process FDM fault detection. All models were fine-tuned under identical conditions on 5793 annotated images covering six fault classes. Performance was evaluated on clean test images and under three types of synthetic camera degradation: Gaussian blur, directional motion blur, and additive Gaussian noise. Deployment-related metrics, including parameter count, GFLOPs, ONNX model size, GPU latency, and CPU inference latency, were also measured. On clean images, YOLOv8s achieved the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.7905, while YOLOv11n provided comparable nano-scale accuracy with 14% fewer parameters. Stringing remained the most difficult fault class, with AP@0.5 values of approximately 0.45–0.48. The robustness experiments showed that blur caused a gradual reduction in detection performance, while directional motion blur was more severe than Gaussian blur. Additive Gaussian noise produced the largest performance degradation. Across the extended degradation grid, YOLOv11n achieved the lowest Degradation Sensitivity Index (DSI) of 28.80%, and also provided the fastest CPU inference at 48.11 ms/image and the smallest model footprint at 10.61 MB. These results provide a practical benchmark for selecting lightweight YOLO models and designing robust FDM monitoring systems.

Article.Title: Phase-matched ion pre-acceleration by upstream magnetic dipole vortices in relativistic collisionless shocks
Article.Authors: Naseri N.; Turkakin H.; Shvets G.
Article.Abstract: Collisionless shocks are among the most efficient particle accelerators in the Universe, yet the physical mechanism responsible for energetic upstream seed ions remains poorly understood. Using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of unmagnetized relativistic electron-ion shocks, we investigate ion pre-acceleration by self-generated magnetic dipole vortices (MDVs) in the upstream region of the shock. We identify two distinct ion populations: one remains phase-matched with the moving MDV, undergoes considerable energization, and returns toward the shock, whereas the other escapes upstream after gaining only modest energy. We show that the magnetic component of the Lorentz force reduces the ion’s longitudinal velocity relative to the moving MDV, extending the interaction time and allowing the transverse electric field to perform sustained positive work. Decomposition of the electric field shows that both the motional electric field associated with the moving MDV and plasma-generated fields contribute to the observed ion energization. Repeated interactions with successive MDVs can increase ion energy before the particles return to the shock transition region. These results identify MDV-mediated upstream ion pre-acceleration as a candidate mechanism for producing energetic seed ions that may facilitate subsequent shock acceleration.

Article.Title: Interpretable prediction of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis
Article.Authors: Meng S.; Yu S.; Zhu X.; Zhou S.; Zhu S.; Yu Y.; Xie Y.; Huang Z.; Xiang M.; Ma H.
Article.Abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a concern among critically ill patients with heart failure receiving early thromboprophylaxis, yet individualized risk stratification in this population remains limited. We developed nine prediction models using 8,825 patients from MIMIC-IV and externally validated them in 5,425 eICU records. Fifteen predictors were identified through combined least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and Boruta feature selection. XGBoost achieved the highest observed discrimination, with ROC AUCs of 0.764 (95% CI, 0.723–0.805) internally and 0.731 (95% CI, 0.676–0.786) externally. SHAP analysis identified atrial tachycardia/fibrillation, respiratory failure, previous thromboembolism, antiplatelet therapy, and mechanical ventilation within 24 h as the leading contributors to model predictions. External validation highlighted the value of recalibration, with exploratory five-fold cross-fitted intercept recalibration improving overall calibration and predictive accuracy. Decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit at selected low-risk thresholds following recalibration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of an interpretable prediction model based on routinely available clinical data, with potential for integration into ICU workflows to support individualized VTE risk stratification and targeted surveillance.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a multidimensional scale for heat-related health behavior across domains of everyday life
Article.Authors: Schmid-Ellinger J.; Bachner J.; Blaschke S.; Mess F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heat is an escalating global health risk, yet how populations adapt behaviorally remains poorly understood. We developed and psychometrically evaluated a novel instrument to assess heat-related health behavior (HRHB) across domains of everyday life and along a continuum from reactive to anticipatory responses in a large population-based sample in Germany ( N = 3,351). Factor analyses supported a multidimensional structure capturing both domain-specific (diet, housing, clothing, activity/change of location) and temporal adaptations. HRHB showed good reliability and moderate associations with heat-related health literacy and knowledge, indicating related but distinct constructs. Higher levels of reported behavior were associated with greater symptom burden, consistent with behavior being partly driven by experienced heat strain. HRHB explained additional variance in symptoms beyond sociodemographic and cognitive factors, supporting its incremental validity. These findings identify behavioral adaptation as a distinct and measurable dimension of population-level heat resilience, enabling improved identification of vulnerable groups and more targeted public health interventions.

Article.Title: Phytochemical profiling and computational analysis highlight anabsinthin as a potential ligand of coronavirus main protease
Article.Authors: Loukman S.; Hadad S.; Mesrar F.; Talha A.; Tachallait H.; Benmrid R.; Bouchmaa N.; Daoud R.; Fatimy R.; Benhida R.
Article.Abstract: Natural products remain an important source of diverse structures for antiviral drug development, but pinpointing and prioritizing bioactive metabolites from complex plant extracts remains challenging. We developed an integrated approach combining phytochemical analysis and computational methods to identify sesquiterpene lactones from Artemisia absinthium L. as potential candidates for interaction with the conserved coronavirus main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), a crucial target for viral replication. Using a central composite design, we optimized ultrasound-assisted extraction, followed by GC–MS and LC–MS profiling to analyze solvent-dependent phytochemical profiles. Ethanol yielded the highest extraction efficiency and enabled the enrichment of constituents tentatively assigned to absinthin/anabsinthin-type dimeric sesquiterpene lactones, followed by chromatographic purification. These compounds were assessed through molecular docking, ADMET and toxicity predictions, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations with trajectory-based Prime MM-GBSA calculations. X77 served as the crystallographic non-covalent reference, and nirmatrelvir was examined only as an additional MD benchmark. Both lactones were predicted to fit within the Mpro active site, with anabsinthin showing a more favorable computational profile than absinthin. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the anabsinthin–Mpro complex displayed lower backbone deviations, reduced residue fluctuations, and persistent interactions with key residues, including Glu166 and Gln189. Prime MM-GBSA estimates also favored anabsinthin over absinthin, although the energetic difference relative to X77 was sensitive to the sampled trajectory window. In silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity predictions suggested generally favorable early drug-like characteristics without prominent predicted toxicity alerts. This integrated workflow combining extraction optimization, phytochemical profiling, purification, and computational assessment provides a rational strategy for prioritizing natural products for further investigation. Among the compounds examined in this study, anabsinthin emerged as the most promising A. absinthium -derived lactone candidate for subsequent experimental evaluation against Mpro. However, these computational predictions require confirmation through biochemical and cellular assays before direct Mpro inhibition or antiviral activity can be established.

Article.Title: Normative OCT-derived ocular measurements in rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Lester J.; Barron Arrambide A.; Burgos-Rodriguez A.; Schwantes G.; Ede E.; Nepal P.; Fasih-Ahmad S.; Huynh L.; Zambrano R.; Lee T.; Kim B.; Schuman J.; N/A N/A.; Antón S.; Brent L.; Higham J.; Martinez M.; Melin A.; Montague M.; Platt M.; Sallet J.; Snyder-Mackler N.; Melin A.; Higham J.; Danias J.
Article.Abstract: To define normative OCT-derived measurements of the retina, optic nerve head (ONH) macrostructure, and lamina cribrosa (LC) microstructure in a large cohort of healthy, predominantly youngadult rhesus macaques, and to investigate their association with demographic traits and image quality. Macular and peripapillary scans were segmented to measure the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL), and total retinal thicknesses. ONH macrostructure and LC microstructure were quantified using software of our own design. Linear mixed-effects modeling was used to assess association between demographic features, image quality, and OCT-derived ocular measurements. Average macular GCIPL and peripapillary RNFL thicknesses were 80.6 ± 6.4 and 96.8 ± 8.9 µm, respectively. Average cup-to-disc ratio and cup depth were 0.46 ± 0.18 and 75.6 ± 50.3 µm, respectively. Average LC beam-to-pore-ratio was 2.06 ± 0.37. Significant associations existed between LC OCT quality and most LC microstructural parameters. We present robust normative ocular measurements of the healthy rhesus macaque eye and demonstrate LC microstructural measurements are sensitive to image quality, which should be considered in any future analysis of these parameters.

Article.Title: Industrial defect image generation via structured latent-space interpolation
Article.Authors: Cang Y.; Rong H.; Zou R.; Ma J.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial visual defect detection suffers from scarce defect samples, limiting generalization. We propose a novel image generation framework that synthesizes diverse and realistic defect images through three sequential innovations. First, we introduce UMAP-based dimensionality reduction to project VAE latent features onto a low-dimensional manifold while preserving local neighborhood structure, thereby enabling artifact-free sampling in the subsequent stage. Second, we design a PSO-optimized Gaussian mixture model to capture the sparse, multimodal distribution of defect features within this manifold, and sample new coordinates from high-likelihood regions to generate diverse yet realistic defect representations. Third, we employ a non-parametric radial basis function interpolator to map these sampled coordinates back to the original VAE latent space, preserving geometric continuity and restoring high-frequency defect details before decoding. Experiments on bearing-defect and public industrial datasets show that detectors trained with a synthetic-to-real ratio $$\le 1:3$$ achieve superior accuracy and robustness, validating each innovation’s effectiveness.

Article.Title: Simulation-based implementation of the developed system dynamics model for sustainable urban water supply systems
Article.Authors: Hassan Z.; Rehan R.; Khan F.; Khan M.; Ali A.; Nasery M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water is an indispensable resource, underpinning not only domestic livelihoods, but also the social and economic fabric of nations. Climate change serves among the most formidable threats to the world’s freshwater reserves. Naturally, potable water serves as a finite and precious commodity, merely, 3% is fresh, 2% locked within glaciers and polar ice caps, leaving only 1% accessible for human use. As global water consumption increases at an average rate of 1% annually. Projections alarms need of adopting robust and advanced water management policies, as only 60% of the world’s required water supply will be available by 2030. This crisis is most acutely felt, in developing nations with rapid population growth and pervasive poverty compounds water scarcity. In Pakistan, groundwater serves as the cornerstone of the national domestic water supply infrastructure approximately, meeting 70% of drinking water demands nationwide. Moreover, the widening chasm between water demands and supply urgently required, innovative water management strategies. At present, in Pakistan, urban water supply planning, development, and maintenance remain heavily anchored in conventional engineering and demand-driven frameworks. This study develops the first tailored System Dynamics decision-support model for Peshawar’s urban water system, introducing a novel coupling of an age-band leakage formulation with proactive pipe replacement policies tailored for intermittent, groundwater-dependent utilities. At its foundation, lies meticulously on a constructed Causal Loop Diagram, serving as a comprehensive visual map. To capture, the intricate interdependencies in social, financial, and physical/technical sectors of urban water supply systems. The framework was operationalized and demonstrated on Tehsil Peshawar over a 50-year simulation horizon. Currently, the public water supply system in Peshawar, comprising of tube wells collectively discharging approximately 2 million gallons per hour. However, at baseline static conditions, the total water demand is 6.01 MGH with an estimated leakage rate of 1.703 MGH (28.3%). Crucially, comparing these requirements against the actual municipal abstraction capability of 2 million GPH reveals a 3-fold supply deficit. This structural gap highlights the disparity between standard design benchmarks (250 LPCD) and real-world supply capacities, demonstrating how operational intermittent supply acts as a forced rationing mechanism under current system constraints. Critically, energy costs constitute nearly 80% of total tube well operating expenses, positioning energy optimization as a linchpin of financial sustainability. The study advocates for solar-based energy alternatives, demand management interventions and proactive groundwater replenishment strategies as transformative interventions. This paper makes a compelling case of holistic and systems-thinking approaches, embracing full complexity of sustainable water governance, offering a replicable and scalable model for developing nations confronting analogous of water security challenges.

Article.Title: Predicting the number of infant deaths per woman in ethiopia using complementary count regression and machine learning approaches
Article.Authors: Aga M.; Dugasa S.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infant mortality remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding factors associated with cumulative infant deaths and improving their prediction may help identify populations with higher infant-death burdens. This study examined maternal-level counts of infant deaths ever experienced by women in Ethiopia using complementary count-regression and machine-learning approaches. Data from the 2019 Ethiopia Mini Demographic and Health Survey were analyzed among 5,846 women with complete birth histories. The outcome was the cumulative number of infant deaths experienced by each woman. Because the outcome is mechanically related to the number of births, the logarithm of the number of children ever born was incorporated as an exposure offset in the count-regression models and excluded from the machine-learning predictor set. Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP), and zero-inflated negative binomial models were compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. Poisson Random Forest, Extreme gradient boost (XGBoost)-Poisson, and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-Poisson models were evaluated using 70% training and 30% independent testing split, with five-fold cross-validation for hyper-parameter tuning. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). The ZIP model provided the best fit among the evaluated count-regression models, with the lowest AIC (2503) and BIC (2544). In the count component, maternal age, household wealth, postnatal care, child vaccination status, maternal education, and place of delivery were statistically associated with the expected number of infant deaths. In the machine-learning analysis, XGBoost-Poisson achieved the best test-set predictive performance, with an MAE of 0.320 and RMSE of 0.570. Region had the largest relative predictive contribution (gain = 0.190), followed by marital status (0.167), maternal age (0.136), education level (0.125), and wealth index (0.117). These variable-importance measures represent predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Cumulative infant-death counts among women in Ethiopia were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and maternal and child healthcare characteristics. The ZIP model provided interpretable adjusted associations, whereas XGBoost-Poisson provided the best out-of-sample prediction among the evaluated machine-learning models. The findings support the value of combining inferential count regression with count-specific machine-learning methods while emphasizing that predictive importance does not establish causality. Continued attention to maternal education, socioeconomic disadvantage, postnatal care, immunization, and access to appropriate delivery care may help inform child-survival strategies in Ethiopia.

Article.Title: Multi-environment evaluation of finger millet genotypes for agronomic traits, yield stability and adaptability for summer cultivation
Article.Authors: Mishra S.; Rajendran A.; Kumar S.; Thakur M.; Kishor K.; Singh M.; Chandra M.; Banoriya R.; Shivraj G.; Mundakochi M.; Dash P.
Article.Abstract: Identification and advancement of high yielding and early maturing finger millet genotypes for summer season is essential for crop diversification in the Indo-Gangetic flood plains to enhance food security and production efficiency. The current experiment studied 145 finger millet genotypes under six contrasting environments namely: E2, E4, and E6 (summer) and E1, E3, and E5 (rainy) in three consecutive years (2021–2024) to identify parents suitable for the development of specific varieties and superior genotypes for summer cultivation. An integrated analytical framework combining AMMI, GGE biplot, BLUP, WAAS and MTSI were employed to reveal greater insights. REML/BLUP analysis was employed to enhance the reliability of selection, which revealed that genotypic variance accounted for a larger proportion of the phenotypic variance (49.5%) than genotype × environment interaction variance (24.3%), coupled with moderate broad-sense heritability (0.49) and high selection accuracy (0.95). AMMI found C3, C2, C1, G120 and G11 to take the top high yielding genotypes and G111, G12, G7, G65 and G81 were the most stable. GGE mean vs. stability biplot indicated G120, G80 and G29 as broadly adapted and high-yielding, G120 topped as the best performer and G52 and G68 summer-specific adaptors (E2 and E4). BLUP predicted results with re-affirmation of G120, G29 and G80 as the good performers. C3, C2, C1, G120, G29, G28 and G85 were grouped by the WAAS index as ideal (high yield and stable). Multi-Trait Stability Index (MTSI) also identified eighteen genotypes that could be improved simultaneously for multiple traits. Overall, the elite genotypes (G120, G80, G29 and the check varieties C1, C2, and C3) are useful as parents for breeding climate resilient finger millet varieties adapted to summer climatic conditions in the Gangetic plains of India.

Article.Title: Bhallatakadi modaka induces apoptosis of cancer cells via activating ROS/p-ERK pathway
Article.Authors: Dixit A.; Mishra S.; Ghosh D.; Shrivastava N.; Sarkar M.; Paul M.; Bose S.; Kumar D.; Basak S.; Dey R.; Roy S.; Saha S.; Jagtap C.; Nair P.; Bora M.; Babu G.; YR S.; Srikanth N.; Acharya R.; Srivastava A.
Article.Abstract: Bhallatakadi modaka (BM) is an Ayurvedic formulation that has been traditionally used for various therapeutic purposes, but its anticancer effects and underlying molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized.This study aimed to investigate the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of BM in cancer cell lines and a xenograft mouse model. In vitro assays, including MTT and clonogenicity assays, revealed that BM inhibited cancer cell growth and induced apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Flow cytometry, DAPI/PI staining, and Western blotting further confirmed apoptosis induction. Additionally, BM treatment reduced the cancer stem cell population, evidenced by a decrease in CD44+CD117+ cells and reduced sphere formation. Mechanistically, the formulation induced the generation of ROS, which activated the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) pathway, culminating in apoptosis. Increased expression of apoptosis markers such as cleaved caspase-3 and decreased total PARP1 further confirm the apoptotic effect. In vivo, treatment with BM in OVCAR-3 xenograft-bearing mice led to a significant reduction in tumor size compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry showed a marked decrease in Ki-67 expression, indicating suppressed tumor cell proliferation. Overall, the data suggest that BM may inhibit cancer cell growth through mechanisms involving ROS accumulation, p-ERK activation, and induction of apoptosis.

Article.Title: Formononetin-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles attenuate inflammatory signaling in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes
Article.Authors: Faheem M.; Ahmad A.; Munawar N.; Ali M.; Akhtar B.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with persistent synovial inflammation induced by pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases. Formononetin (FN), a plant isoflavone, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties with therapeutic potential for RA. This research aimed to prepare FN-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (FN-SLNPs) and determine whether nanoencapsulation preserves chemical identity, increases antioxidant potential, and enhances anti-inflammatory activity in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes. FN-SLNPs were characterized by particle size and zeta potential analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), UV-visible spectroscopy, and antioxidant profiling, including total flavonoid content, total phenolic content, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity. In vitro biological activity in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A cells was evaluated using cytotoxicity analysis by MTT assay, protein quantification by ELISA, and gene expression analysis by qRT-PCR. FN-SLNPs showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 148 ± 42 nm and a zeta potential of − 27.3 ± 1.3 mV. SEM revealed crystalline lipid domains. FTIR confirmed the chemical retention of isoflavone functional groups. Flavonoid content and total phenolic content increased with FN-SLNP loading compared with pure FN. DPPH radical scavenging activity was highest for FN-SLNPs at 20 mg compared with pure FN. TNF-α increased MH7A cell viability to 145.2 ± 5.8%. FN-SLNPs at 100 µg/mL reduced viability to 85.4 ± 3.1%, decreased interleukin-1β (IL-1β) protein levels from 0.0182 ± 0.0015 to 0.0035 ± 0.0003 µg/mL, and reduced IL1B gene expression from 18.50 ± 1.20 to 2.90 ± 0.25. These findings indicate that FN-SLNPs preserve the chemical identity of FN, enhance its antioxidant activity, and potentiate anti-inflammatory responses in MH7A synoviocytes.
